reviews.comment: People seem to have mixed feelings about AR but I really think he wants the best for all his students and I am a better engineer because of him. Is the class hard? yes. Is he also fair? yes. If that is a problem I am not sure why you decided to become an engineer.

This professor tries to make the course bearable; however, I do not trust him to help be because he said at the beginning of the semester not to use Chegg, AI, or any related outside source, and these outside sources explain calculations to me so much better than humans and textbooks do.

He is a great guy and I am taking him for other classes so I'll be back to update! Very helpful during office hours. His lectures are kind of boring and a little difficult to keep up with, though he tries his best and is super enthusiastic :) Get help from TAs for homeworks, ask questions, actually do the zybooks and you'll do good!
reviews.rating_tags: EXTRA CREDIT--Clear grading criteria--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: This class is heavily frontloaded towards the beginning of the semester. The ZyBooks are tedious, but as time goes on the homework assignments and mini projects are a fun challenge. Prof R. was very helpful during office hours and offered tons of extra credit. He is an enthusiastic lecturer.

This is a coding class and half the time he spends in lecture solving integrals. It feels more like I am taking two calc classes. He always front loads the beginning of the semester with all of our text books readings. About 2 or 3 readings a week and each takes about 2 hours if you actually want to learn anything.
great guy! fun class!

Beginning of the semester is dense, after that you have a few somewhat reasonable homework assignments, two very challenging mini projects, and a midterm, no final. Go to lecture because there are in class assignments due at the end of the class. Prior coding knowledge is very helpful. Expects you to know a lot once through but overall not bad.

CLASS: MIE 124 | SEMESTER: SPRING 2024 -- Professor Ramasubramaniam is interesting. He is not the most helpful person, but he is nice. A zyBook (interactive textbook) is required [~$77]. There are many required readings. The MATLAB homework is lengthy and very challenging, and the mini-projects are even worse! Prior coding experience is beneficial!

Don't take this class unless you are required too. Learned everything by myself by reading mat lab forum. Ta's grade everything hopefully you have a good one or your GPA will suffer. Does in class assignment's posted on moodel for attendance you can do them from your bed.

The class is only graded based on homework. Textbook hw is hard. These are difficult but can be fun once you get into them. If you have prior programming experience, even a little, you will do much better in the course. Go to the TA help sessions if you are struggling

Lectures were a little confusing but office hours were very good.  This class will take all your time away.  The class is very front loaded, be prepared to have like 1 day to read like four chapters along with practice problems.  Later in the course it get's better.  Start work early and go to all help sessions and you'll be okay. Hard material.

Great Prof.! The entirety of the grade is based on the homework which is great. As long as you work hard and go to office hours when stuck you will be fine (the TAs and Prof are very helpful). A good thing to note is the class is heavily front-loaded. No previous coding experience is required. I got an A and had basically no prior coding knowledge.

An amazing professor that is excited to teach and is very available outside of class and answers emails incredibly fast. The course work is very challenging and its very easy to fall behind but the professor makes available the resources to succeed

This class is not fun and difficult. Find good friends that are good at coding so they can help you. The lectures are boring, confusing, and dry. The professor is nice but other than that this class is terrible. But if you want to be an ME you have to take this class and this professor. Weekly homework gets harder and harder but no exams.
This guy sucks, tough grader, very unforgiving. Grade for him: F

I only did well in this class because I programmed in high school. The lectures were pretty bad, and tended to be very confusing. He has office hours and is willing to work with students, but how helpful they are seems to depend on the day. Sometimes he helps you through a big error, sometimes he just tells you to debug the same line 100 times.
reviews.rating_tags: Accessible outside class--Graded by few things--EXTRA CREDIT

reviews.comment: The class is easy if you don't rush the entire homework a night before the due date. Planning ahead and scheduling when to the do the homework is the key to getting 100 in the class. I didn't watch the online lectures and only looked at prof's lecture notes. the assignments become easy if you can find his pseudocode and adapt it to your code.
Nice guy, confusing class. I'm just gonna be a farmer and drop out of college so MatLab has no purpose for me. I was too busy watching Anime during the lectures.

This class is not for the faint of heart. For a while, I had to sit with TA's for a long long time. The homework is a big struggle and took many many hours over a few days. His lectures are not very informative towards the end, and at times, the class seems pointless when you write codes for codes already in Matlab. Make use of EC and TA's!

Beware Prior coding knowledge is basically needed. Due to covid, I had to take this class online which definitely hindered the learning experience of the class. Had a hard time trying to connect with TA's and the Professor. DO NOT WORK WITH OTHER PEOPLE if you work with other people you will get flagged and your grade will tank. Good Luck

Don't expect any feedbacks. Youll be working on HW 5 when hw 2 ,3, and 4 arent even graded. That way, you will be constantly making stupid mistakes that the professor doesnt like. You will receive a zero if he doesnt like what you submitted. Major points are deducted from the DUMBEST thing like having too many variables or no "clear, close, clc'

Do not take his courses. the only source of help in this class that is ACTUALLY helpful is your classmates. The help sessions from UTAs are utter garbage and waste of time. These sophomores don't know how to even help you most of the time. Help session with the professor is even worse. His answers to all coding related question r conceptual. useles

He is probably one of the WORST instructors I have every encountered in my 7 semesters at UMAss. He gives out zeros all the time for being creative in HW, tough grader that barely gives any information on the HW, and his way of "helping" students is to criticize them and telling them to just read the HW that is filled with typos. This man is full

I have attended all the lectures and almost all of available office hours (Not that there were that many available). The class is taught through lectures where the professor explains algorithms for certain problems. However, the professor does not actually teach you how to code, he expects you to know it or to research. Office Hours not helpful!!!
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Get ready to read--Skip class? You won't pass.

reviews.comment: he's easily the best professor i've had so far. this man cares a lot about his student's learning and is very nice. the class itself was pretty easy and with extra credit its very easy to get over a 100. the class is based entirely off weakly homework assignments that are all pretty fun.

No tests which were nice but front-loaded the class with confusing textbook work when no one knew how to code yet. Before taking this class try and get a basic understanding of Matlab and you'll do great. He and the ta's are extremely helpful and make sure to go to their office hours and you'll be fine.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Lots of homework--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Really nice guy, good lecturer. Made class really reasonable in terms of the workload, clear in terms of deliverables. Grade was based on three group lab reports and two more heavily weighted individual reports, as well as some in-lab 10-minute quizzes and a "final quiz" worth 20%. Was accommodating when I had to miss lab and let me take it ahead.
He is an excellent teacher and communicator. Don't miss his course while your are in UMass Amherst.
reviews.rating_tags: Respected--Skip class? You won't pass.--LOTS OF HOMEWORK

reviews.comment: I don't want to say hot, but he is attractive, you know the difference. The discussions held are well conducted and interesting. No textbook is needed.

This class requires a lot work.  The HW help sessions are optional but I went to everyone because each homework involved a derivation that was impossible without getting help.  He is a very nice guy that is wants to help his students succeed.  You have to put the work in his class.  Each test was 2 hours 2 questions and the average was very low.
Good teacher. Cares about his students. Super nice, down to earth guy.
One of the better, more helpful teachers at UMass amherst. Friendly and willing to explain ideas. This class is a killer - go to office hours!

First year that the professor decided to have in-person exams and it shows in the class average. All of my friends consistently do poorly on homeworks and have gotten 50s on exams. Class is poorly structured and grading is harsher than necessary for an introductory statistics class.

Class is really easy, I barely went. Attendance not mandatory, exams online, and 9/10 coding assignments on R Studio are the large majority of your grade. I completed homework outside of class/lab, went to TA office hours if I had questions, and that worked well for me.

There are 10 HWs (with the lowest grade dropped) and 2 exams, and a final, all open note and online. There are optional labs where you can ask questions about the homework. All notes were posted online, and all classes were recorded. 

I definitely recommend this teacher. He taught a very straightforward class.

There are 10 coding assignments on R, 2 multiple choice online midterms and a final that is online as well. Learning to code is a bit tricky but if you read the slides you can get by. I didn't go to lectures that often and I still ended out well. Great professor though and explains things beautifully.

This is a decently soft class in terms of difficulty. I kinda enjoyed the HW although I understand why some people dislike it. The Lab block has optional attendance and is office hours. Lectures are engaging and this is a fantastic professor. I have no points of criticism.

The hardest part about this class was learning the functions in R. The lectures were great and fostered a lot of engagement and the professor was very open to questions and helping people grasp all the concepts. The homeworks, quizzes, and exams were all online which I prefer as I have really bad test anxiety and it's more comfortable at home.

Attendance is not mandatory for lectures/labs but go to the labs for the coding homework it will help a lot! Lectures always recorded on echo 360. 2 midterms exams and 1 final exam & they are all online open note. 10 coding homework assignments with R programming (not as bad as it sounds) but lowest grade is dropped. SONA extra credit offered too.
reviews.rating_tags: EXTRA CREDIT--Clear grading criteria--Lots of homework

reviews.comment: Dr. Staub was a great professor for Psych240, the lectures are clear and concise, and he loves what he does. Discussion is optional, but really good to get homework help. Learning to code with R is 70% of your grade, but he gives the code to you and the workload isn't bad at all, you just have to learn analysis.
reviews.rating_tags: Clear grading criteria--Caring--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: I had him for Statistics in Psychology and it was such a good class! Attendance was optional and he provided the textbook for us for free. All exams were online and there was just one weekly homework assignment :)

He definitely made the course content more interesting by using real-life examples. Homework on R was a little difficult and intimidating at first, but you're talked through it in the instructions and TAs are there to help during discussions. 2 midterm exams and the final are all online and open note, pretty easy overall. SONA extra credit offered.

He is a good lecturer. I hate math and didn't understand most things, so having friends in the class really helped me. Exams are online open-note and there are HW assignments through a coding system called R (it's scary at first but alright). The discussion section attendance is optional. Overall easy but not my favorite.

Honestly one of my favorite professors I have ever had. Though I didn't have much one-on-one time, he was always accessible and willing to help through email and didn't make lectures feel long and monotonous. As long as you review the material and attend labs for help in R Studio, you will be golden.

You don't need to go to class, just go to the discussion. The disc is for help with the homework which is basically  the only grade for the class. Exams are online, everything is online. Super easy class, the homework can be challenging so discs help more than the class.

Great professor. Lecture material is incredibly organized and clear for beginners in statistics. He gives examples and is good at answering questions. 
To get a good grade, just have a decent grasp on the topics in class, don't worry about crazy calculations. 
R can be difficult if you're a beginner but is fun when you get the hang of it.

It seems like a stupid class & I stopped going.  But eventually I forced myself to start going to the lectures and labs. It is pretty easy to understand if you pay attention during lectures. Exams are online, open notes. HW is coding which saves time, so you do not need to do any equations/math. Its difficult but with patience it gets easier.
Worst class ever. Very rude and doesn't respond to emails

Genuinely a great professor. This course can be difficult and surprising because a lot of psych majors seem to be a little wary of coding. However, all the instructions are clear and Prof Staub is a great teacher. If you put away some of the anti math bias, the course material is very interesting and helpful.
reviews.rating_tags: Amazing lectures --Clear grading criteria--Lots of homework

reviews.comment: Adrian is an amazing teacher and I honestly learned more in this class than I did in any other. He uses R for the HWs (there is one HW for each Unit) and that saves you a great deal of effort in calculating complex statistical problems. The TAs are super helpful in guiding you through the homeworks and teaching you R. Overall a great class and prof
reviews.rating_tags: Amazing lectures --Clear grading criteria--Lots of homework

reviews.comment: Nice professor, but attending class is not mandatory or needed as it's just reading off of slides. Easier to just teach yourself. Use office hours to work on your homework, it basically makes up your grade. Exams are not challenging. Make sure your grad TA knows who you are.

I love adrian, hes a great teacher.  I honestly stopped showing up for class, though, because he basically just read off the slides and it was easier/faster just to teach it to myself.  His slideshows made stats super easy to understand and I feel like he did a really great job with the class! Super nice guy as well :)

It was hard to do well in this class at first because you had to learn how to code, you use R Studio. The homework is worth a good amount of your grade(10 HW a sem) and two take home tests&a cumulative final. The material wasn't bad, but the homework was graded pretty hard and the exams were confusing at times. He tended to be passive aggressive.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Graded by few things--Online Savvy

reviews.comment: He is a bit monotone. Lectures are boring but the material is boring so it's not his fault. Homework is hard at first. Attend discussions please they will help you so much with homework. My exams were open-note and online. Homework will help you understand the material

the homework are pretty easy, my issue was with the exams. they aren't worth much of your overall grade (37%) but some of the questions are worded strangely or are different to what was taught in class. he speeds through lectures so if you want to go at a slower pace watch the recorded lectures and don't go to class

solid prof but I had trouble paying attention in his lectures, could barely retain any info. He posts his slides, 10 hw assignments which are the bulk of your grade, 3 exams open note + mc, sona credit, I recommend going to the lab to get help w hw, first couple assignments are intimidating but you eventually get the hang of it, you use R studio.

Staub sucks in lecture. I lead a study group because I'm the only person in my friend group who knows what's going on, so we teach ourselves. Light on work, one assignment per unit, plus two multiple choice open note exams. Lab goes over homework.

I learned things, but at what cost?

He also made me feel bad for asking too many questions. Big ego.

Grading is based on 10 homeworks and a few moodle quizzes. You have to download a free system to do the homeworks, which get easier as you go. Grading is not harsh, lectures are recorded but you don't really need to go as he posts notes and the homeworks can usually be done with notes and common sense. Textbook is free, not necessary to read.
reviews.rating_tags: Lecture heavy--Graded by few things--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: This was a solid class and Professor Staub did a solid job leading it. I had no background in statistics or using tools like R Studio before, but he made everything simple and easy to understand. All lectures were recorded as well. As long as you follow the lectures well, homework and exams will be no trouble. He also offered some extra credit.

Class was interesting. Didn't go to any lectures but could watch them online and that was really helpful. Definitely watch the lectures because they will help you understand the homework. TAs were very good and helpful, go to lab and they will tell you exactly what to do. Exams were ok and mainly based off lectures.

Adrian is a decent professor, but I often lost focus during his lectures. My tips for success in this class is to utilize your TAs and attend lab! If you do that, homework will be a breeze. R is used for coding on the homework. It is daunting at first, but with some dedication, you will get the hang of it in no time. Exams are fair too.

Key to succeed in this class attend/review lectures, go to every lab, do ALL homework. There's only 2 test and 1 final. HW can be tough, if you're like me and are unfamiliar with programming language. The lab is a huge help with hw & R Program. Lab TA has been great (Anna) made herself available beyond her office hours to help me. Lectures recorded
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Test heavy--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Professor Staub is great! He explains the material very well and is easy to understand. The tests are all open note and online. There is 1 HW assignment per week which at first seem difficult because he uses a coding program called R. If you put in the effort and go to your TA labs it is not hard to succeed in this class.

At first I thought this class was hard, but if you put in minimum effort its easy fr and I regret not realizing this earlier on into the class bc I got a few bad grades for no reason. TAs are is SO helpful and valuable, join the discord too!! If you go to lecture and take notes the exams aren't that hard either. Very easy and forgiving class.

Prof. Staub is absolutely amazing ! Attend his lectures and take really good notes for the quizzes and tests. But your R homework can make or break your grade ! Attend the labs because the TAs usually help A LOT with the homework. Homework is mostly copy-paste with few changes. Using R can seem difficult in the beginning but it gets easier !!
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Skip class? You won't pass.--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: Professor Staub is the best. He is a really, really nice guy who genuinely wants his students to do well. If you go to class and do the homework, the class should not be a problem. The tests were really straight forward, no surprises or tricks. I would take him again for sure.

I never went to a single class and got an A in the class. The grade is mainly coding assignments on R, where you just gotta copy and paste the code from the assignment and change a few things. (10 HWs, 1 dropped). Exams were open notes and extremely fair. It's not a hard class, but joining a group chat helps a lot w/ small questions for HW & Exams!

Most of the time, you have to do a lot of reading, along with either completing assigned reading questions or posting your comments in a discussion forum on Moodle. Other than that, you are expected to conduct a presentation and talk about what research paper you are assigned to is about. I find the workload kinda heavy but it's worth it!
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Get ready to read--Inspirational

reviews.comment: He's such an amazing professor. He constantly engages our attention during lectures and pays lots of efforts in order to make lecture less boring (cuz it's statistics), for example, adding aliens between lecture slides. 49% Homework, 28% Quizzes & 23% Final Exam Many ways to earn extra credits, such as iClicker participation & SONA experiments.
Great teacher and always willing to help, super strict on late homework which accounts for 50% of the grade, definitely have to pay attention during lecture

Statistics can be boring and scary for us, Professor Staub's definitely one of the best professors I've ever met at UMass. His lecture slides are filled with aliens in order to make it interesting at least and he always ensures that everyone's on track. Yeah, maybe one homework & quiz per week, but they're manageable and I learnt a lot from him )

Decent prof, just really boring material. Homework is pretty easy, it's just annoying because of how repetitive it can get. Weekly timed quizzes on moodle. Showing up and using your iClicker gets you extra credit. Only one test, the final, and counts for a good chunk of your grade. Definitely attractive which can get distracting in class... ;)
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Skip class? You won't pass.--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: Staub is a pretty good teacher go to class to get participation points. HW can be pretty hard and doesn't really have anything to do with the final go to lab and you should be fine. Final is hard but depending on grades will be scaled.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--EXTRA CREDIT

reviews.comment: The subject is pretty boring, but Adrian tries to make it better. You need to go to lecture for the clicker answers and clicker points. Labs are an easy way to get homework answers. Homework takes a long time but isn't extremely difficult. The final was really similar to the weekly quiz questions so use that to test yourself without notes.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--LOTS OF HOMEWORK--LECTURE HEAVY

reviews.comment: Prof Staub is excellent. Stats isn't always super straightforward but he does a great job of explaining the material in manageable chunks. I think the structure of the class is fantastic and if you do all of the work, the A will follow. His TAs are phenomenal as well.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Skip class? You won't pass.--Caring

reviews.comment: The homeworks and the actual class/quizzes feel like two different courses. The final is multiple choice which is only beneficial if you actually understand the material, which is hard to do when the homeworks don't seem to prepare you very well. Overall confusing and dry. Go to class for iClicker questions. Go to discussion to get homework help.

Professor Staub's lectures are clear, he gives useful homeworks, and there are many opportunities for grades. If you go to class and do your homework carefully, this class will be no trouble and you will learn a lot.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--LOTS OF HOMEWORK--LECTURE HEAVY

reviews.comment: Homework was 36% of our grade and uses RStudio which is basically compsci that you have to learn on your own. There's only 7 graded homeworks and one gets dropped. They take long and apparently are harder than other Psych 240 teachers RStudio HWs. Nothing to do with psychology at all which sucks
reviews.rating_tags: LOTS OF HOMEWORK--GRADED BY FEW THINGS--Caring

reviews.comment: Professor Staub really cares about what he teaches and wants his students to be successful. He tries to make stats as interesting as possible, but the R program can really suck the fun out of the course. Start your homework early, print out the lecture slides + take notes on them, and make your own guide for each unit-this helped me ace the final!

Adrian was pretty solid, part of why people don't give him high grades here is because stats is boring as all get out for most of us. He's pretty sweet, tries to make the material less horrible. Its nice that he really likes what hes doing. Clicker attendance. Moodle HW and quizes, lowest of each is dropped. HW is kinda CompSci because of R.
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--LOTS OF HOMEWORK--Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: I thought Professor Staub was great, the material is dry & it can get confusing. I thought his lectures were very clear, & he does a great job at explaining things. He seems like a nice guy & has a good sense of humor. There isn't a ton of homework, the lode itself is manageable however the homework takes a LONG time! Start it before it's due date!
reviews.rating_tags: ACCESSIBLE OUTSIDE CLASS--Clear grading criteria--EXTRA CREDIT

reviews.comment: Good class, the teacher was really helpful and spelled out the statistics well enough that had I not taken a stats class already, I could have learned this from him. We use R which is a coding software, but is ultimately not too hard to figure out. His homeworks are long and he has periodic quizzes, but you learn a lot and it's not too painful.

Homework takes fooorrreeevvveeerrr! I usually spend nine hours in one day to complete them. However, if you pay attention in class and google  how to do certain R Studio commands you should be okay. There was a final which got scaled since most students ended up getting in the high 70s. Staub's not a bad teacher, it's just a hard subject.

Staub is a good guy, the subject itself is extremely dry, that's just the nature of it, but staub does his best to make bearable. that being said, the homework can take days to complete (and do it right) but if you take the class seriously, and go to his office hours if you're confused, you should be fine.  There's also, no book, which is a plus.

He is a nice guy and likes what he teaches, but I found myself falling asleep during his lectures. It is a hard class, the homework takes days and is very confusing. LOVED my TA. He was always so helpful and I went to office hours often. Not a horrible class but not the best. NEED A CLICKER. no textbook, no tests, just the final. Work hard!!

No textbook and just have you learn the material from his notes from lectures (post lecture slides online). Answers q's as much as possible. One assignment a week and they take at least 2 hours (in my opinion). Exams are good. TA's are helpful. MUST HAVE A CLICKER SO GO TO CLASS.

Staub was a decent professor, you can tell he possesses a wealth of knowledge but he doesn't really know how to teach that knowledge. Homeworks are the majority of the grade, though they are time consuming because R is cumbersome to use, but once you get used to it there should be no problem. Also, he scales final grades about 5 points!

He is a really nice guy. The homework, as many have said, takes a while but is pretty easy. The tests are the toughest part of this class. There are some concepts that are difficult to understand, so you are gonna have to study. He really knows his stuff, but doesn't always explain it well. So wave your hand like crazy or else he won't see it.

1. He is so hot 2. He cares about all of his students and wants EVERYBODY to do well 3. Homework takes time to get used to but once you master R, you'll be fine 4. Discussion is pointless because stats is only enjoyable because Adrian is a sex god 5. He has a sense of humor that makes class time fly by

Adrian Staub is the chillest professor out there. He's a little hottie, too! ;) You're going to love him -- he's a really nice guy, and he gives every one of his students a great opportunity to learn.

Worst part about this class is the homeworks - they are extremely time consuming but not necessarily hard. Staub is a pretty good professor. He does his best to make lecture interesting and will clarify information if you ask for help. No textbook required. Go to lecture (and pay attention) and you'll get an A

Very clear professor if you listen to him and follow his slides. His slides are very easy to follow and he'll clear up any points of confusion if you ask about it. Easy A if you pay attention and seek help from TA's during discussions if needed (they are very helpful). Only 2 midterms worth 10% of your grade each, and a final. No problems here!

I was nervous going into this class, but if you have to take PsychStats, I'd recommend Adrian.  He is extremely clear in lecture and while R was kind of a pain at first, if you follow his super detailed instructions for homework, you should do just fine.  There are 3 tests and they're pretty straightforward if you reread lectures and understand hw

Professor Staubs PSY240 is a difficult class for those who already struggle with math concepts. He knows the subject matter very well; however, he is almost to proficient with it. I would suggest Prof. Staubs class in an honors setting, or if you are mathematically inclined, but seek another prof. if math is not your strongest subject.

This is a very easy class.. The homework assignments are very time consuming but are extremely manageable. If you're having trouble in the case, confront your TA or friends, the professor isn't the best at elaborating his methods. I would suggest this class.

Really nice guy and knows a lot about the material, however he doesn't know how to teach at all. Talks in circles and never understands people's questions. 40% of grade is hw and he barely explains how to do it. Every hw takes hrs to do and is basically impossible. Only one exam that's 30 pages long. Definitely take this class with another prof.

He's organized and overall a good teacher. Slides are up online and clear/thorough. Stats is straightforward but not particularly easy. Only thing is that homework is SO time consuming and tedious so it gets annoying - it uses R & R skills aren't even tested in the final. Material gets tricky toward the end of the sem but it's not that difficult.
homework's are very time consuming and the quizzes get trickier as the semester goes on. his slides and lectures are clear, but this class is not an easy A

I would absolutely recommend taking this class with Adrian. He is easy going and really enjoys what he's teaching, and it shows. You have to put the effort in, but this is true regardless of the teacher. Stats isn't an inherently easy class, so just be prepared to work for it if you're not a math person. He genuinely wants his students to succeed.
expects you to know everything. you use this weird program call R where you actually type in code, its weird. exams are nothing like homework. take this course with a different professor

Honestly, I had very little trouble with this class. I didn't read the FREE ONLINE textbook EVER. Go to lab. Go to class, there are easy in-class quizzes. Do all the homework. I never got lower than a 90 all class. Staub is very willing to help out if you need help. I'm hoping to TA for this class in the future.

Professor Stuab is pretty cool. Stats is a difficult class on its own, but he really tries to make it simple. He's very willing to help with something you don't understand, so just speak up. Exams (2) are challenging but homeworks and daily quizzes give you a nice cushion. I would recommend Staub if you have to take stats.

We all know that this is a hard class..however, if you attend the lectures, go to his office hours, do the work, this class is really do-able. he's a really good professor and is quite passionate about what he is teaching.  i highly recommend this class, but know its not an easy a..,you have to put your effort in and you'll do just fine

Adrian is wonderful, his lecture style extremely lucid, his selection of reading excellent, and his grading and comments extremely helpful and fair. Genuinely great guy, and encouraging. Like grad work tends to be, you gotta go and work your ass off or else you will absolutely not do well. However, it was a pleasure doing the work. Great class.
very arrogant.  Not helpful at all
Definitely worth taking.
He has a way of making difficult material accessible and interesting. If you go to class and pay attention you will do well!
Really tough class, but great TA! Staub isn't really great at explaining the material, but if you go to class, lab sections, and do the homework you'll do fine.

nice guy. awful class. terrible teacher. makes the material harder to learn than it should be with his rambling explanations. gets flustered easily. homework takes forever and is really hard. the only reason i'm passing is because of the TA. if you want an easy A, don't expect it from this class. DO NOT TAKE THIS CLASS!

Clear and entertaining lecturer, really knows his subject...his genuine interest in his field and in teaching is apparent. Assignments are manageable and grading is reasonable. And, as several people have mentioned, he's extremely attractive as well!
Hot Geek! Statistics... his classes were useless and boring, homework was hard, but the TA was very helpful, in fact, the TA was more of a teacher the the Professor.
Hot Professor, but can be a little dull and geeky. He gets really excited about some things that are just mathmatical... good professor.
Nice guy, okay teacher.  He can get a little bit confusing when he explains things.

I am a senior in college and this professor straight up made me want to drop out!
