reviews.comment: 3 Exams and a final with iclicker make up your whole grade. The material isn't hard to learn, but her exams make it so complicated. She asks questions that are not related to what you learn in class. Teaching online she will ghost you and only email with when you have an exam. Try to contact her and you will get a condescending email. Not worth it.

Exams are worth a large portion of your grade and so is participation. If you don't go to class to get the notes you really won't pass because lectures are not recorded and notes are not posted. She is a nice woman and is willing to explain things further if you just ask.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Graded by few things--Test heavy

reviews.comment: Would not recommend. She is condescending and wastes class time by calling out students who use their phones, and sneaks up on students who have their laptop open on something other than class material. Also, her exam questions are confusing and unfair. She seems to be annoyed by students very easily.

The laziest professor I have ever had, tried to guilt trip my class into opting out of the final so she doesn't have to make one. Don't get the textbook. All the exams are based on lectures ONLY. Doesn't record lectures or post full slides so you have to go to class. Grade is based on exams and participation only, aka no homework.
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Skip class? You won't pass.--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: Seriously. Like so serious. Do not take Cognitive Psych with Jesse. She is such a hardo about any form of things "distracting"... but only to her- not the class (she will walk back to you or call you out on the mic lol). She's condescending and passive, along with boring. She has 3 attendance methods EACH lecture. Take Learn&think. Trust me plz.

Very condescending, will cut students off mid-sentence when they talk (whether they're asking a question or answering one.) If you go to her class and take notes, you'll be fine. But she is not an easy teacher and not a nice one, as much as she tries to act like she is.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough Grader--Skip class? You won't pass.--LECTURE HEAVY

reviews.comment: This professor was pretty dry and the material didn't help either. This is a Psych requirement, but the Learn and Think is a much better choice of the two. The professor posted pretty bare slides and mostly talked the useful information at you. There was absolutely no need for the textbook. Participation was a big chunk of your grade.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--LECTURE HEAVY

reviews.comment: Class material is pretty dry and somewhat boring, but Dr. Jesse cares about the success of her students and puts in an effort to make class engaging including attendance note cards and iclickers. Really enjoy her class and as long as you understand the slides you'll be fine
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Caring--LECTURE HEAVY

reviews.comment: Her lectures were very dry and boring; I found it hard to maintain attention. But if you go to class (attendance counts) and study for the exams you'll be fine. I didn't buy the textbook and I never felt like I needed it.

Professor Alexandra Jesse is horrible at giving lectures. You can hardly understand her, she has some accent and it's very hard to understand what she is saying in a huge lecture hall. When people ask questions she seems to not like being interrupted. Someone had a question at hooking their iclicker and she was annoyed. Very boring..
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Skip class? You won't pass.--LECTURE HEAVY

reviews.comment: Lectures are extremely dry and boring, but she attempts to make it engaging by giving you participation credits. Her tests are very specific-- MC questions to make SURE you understand the material and SA to make sure you can explain details of the studies mentioned in her class. Missed class once and was completely lost. Don't buy the book.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Skip class? You won't pass.--LECTURE HEAVY

reviews.comment: Don't take this course with Alexandra. Her lectures are so dry and her policies for absences and make ups are so unfair it isn't even funny. Try finding 315 with another professor or avoid it as a whole.

DO NOT TAKE THIS CLASS WITH JESSE. just don't do it. She may be a very talented researcher, but a terrible lecturer. this is one of the earliest credits for the psych major and there was NO REASON it had to be this difficult. I put in the effort and she wrecked my GPA. Methods was easier than her class. Jesse is the worst prof i've had at UMass.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough Grader--GRADED BY FEW THINGS--LECTURE HEAVY

reviews.comment: Really boring class and lectures are really dry. You have to pay very good attention in class and when reading the book if you want to do well. Crutches are there to help (drop the lowest test grade.. etc) but still tests and in class writing assignments are really tough. Definitely need to drop the lowest grades and do all SONA extra credit.

Seriously don't waste your time with her class. She's impossible to understand because of her and because people talk a lot in her class. You can never hear what she's saying! Tests are all multiple choice and are so unnecessarily hard and specific to the textbook and they're the biggest part of the grade. Class was stressful for no reason.

Professor Jesse really wants her students to succeed and makes that clear. This class is not an easy A, you definitely need to study for the exams, but she does her best to help and genuinely wants her students to succeed

Professor Jesse is amazing. Her class on the Psychology of Language is so interesting and she truly tries to make it so. There are tons of grades to get a good average with, and she truly gives the class all she's got. She gives you so many opportunities to succeed in this class. I think shes awesome- i would definitely take another class with her!

She is so sweet and eager to help her students learn. Definitely sit towards the front. She will never pick on someone who doesn't raise their hand, but sitting in the front helps you hear her better, as she's really soft-spoken and has a hard time keeping the class' attention.

Alexandra is my favorite professor at UMass so far. She is such a genuinely sweet woman with a cute accent. She constantly says she's willing to give extra help to those who need it. She tries to be funny, sometimes she succeeds. As long as you pay attention this class isn't hard. I only used the book for the tables in the back.

She is really enthusiastic about Stats, and is really sweet, but her accent is a little hard to understand. She's also very dry and doesn't explain to clearly. But the TA was fantastic and very helpful. But the material was easy, its very simple math. And she provides a ton of ways to practice, which is awesome.

Although she seems to have the best of intentions, if you can avoid taking this class with her, avoid it at all costs. If statistics isn't hard enough to understand as it is, her thick German accent and inability to keep the classes attention or make people stop talking makes this class terrible.

Jenafer is a great professor and super flexible. The lab is 5 hours long with a 45 min lecture which is a bit long especially if you have been a server before. The homework isn't bad and the exams are easy if you go to class
She is a sweetheart and very passionate about her work. She will help you with anything you need outside of class and she is always accessible by email. I highly recommend you take her class.
Love Chef Jen. This class is time consuming but if you show up and put in effort its an easy A.

One of the greatest professors I have ever had in my life (not even just college). She cares so much about her students, she is an awesome teacher and she truly just wants her students to succeed. the class may seem intimidating w a 5 hr lab, but it goes by fast and its actually really fun!! 355 is my favorite class so far at umass
Super easy all you have to do is show up and care about what your doing. Exams are straightforward and shell let you retake the quizzes if you ask

Jenafer is the kindest, most genuine professor you'll probably ever have at UMass. She truly cares and wants you to succeed and is REALLY quick at responding to emails. She doesn't judge at all so literally ask her any questions you have- she'll never leave you hanging. Class is fun & you learn a lot! And "Family"meals are the best!
Jenafer is the best!

She is awesome! She gets back to your emails very quickly and does not give up on answering your questions. The discussions are an easy 100 points, so do not skip these! She gives study guides for both tests, which help out a ton. Also, the pro sim helped me connect what I learned for the textbook. Put in the effort & you will get 100 on pro sim.

Awesome professor. She really doesn't care if you mess up in class because she knows you're learning. So much better than 150. Definitely take the dinner Labs because it's less busy than lunch. The project is a lot of work but she helps every step of the way. Attendance is mandatory in Lecture & Lab. Exams are easy if you do the study guides before

Jenafer is amazing!  She genuinely cares about all of her students & wants to you succeed.  This course is nothing like 150 with Linda, it's fun, informative, & you meet a lot of great people in it. You can email her whenever & she gives great feedback on everything.  Theres work to do in this class, but Jenafer won't let you drown.

Jenafer is literally the nicest, most understanding teacher you will ever have at Umass. I cannot emphasize enough that she answers emails back faster than anyone on the planet!!!!!!!! How refreshing compared to everyone else!!!!! The class is a restaurant that you run during your lab, and every week you rotate positions. You get to eat too.

Jenafer is the best. Hates being called Professor. Values communication and will answer ALL emails ASAP. The class takes up alot of time so don't skip a class or a lab (more importantly) or you will fall behind very quickly and fail. Keep up to date with Manager meetings. Ask her anything. She never judges.

Jenafer is a great professor. Easy to work with and always happy to help. Small homework assignments once a week, management project and two exams (midterm and final) are what makes up the grade. Don't bother buying the textbook - can help on tests but I got an 87.5 on the first and a 98 on the second without having it.
Jen is awesome. By  far the best professor in the HTM department. She is so helpful and actually enjoys teaching. You will learn so much while having a great time!

GREAT CLASS! much better than 150. Jen is a great person to learn from she has so  so so much experience and she is always there if you need help. Labs are mandatory or else you loose a letter grade on final, but the labs are fun and go by fast and you get to eat really good food after!! all the better!
This is a really fun class. I think the 5 hour lab makes everyone nervous but she really does help you the whole time. Definitely take this class with Jen, she was fun.

This class is a lot of fun. The lecture if pretty useless but the lab is great, all five hours of it. Jenafer is a good teacher and really down to earth. You get a lot of experience and should end up with a good grade.
No Comments

I enjoyed this class. The 5 hour lab goes by fast and she's really lenient with handing stuff in late. You don't have to buy the book but you do need the lab manual. This class was much better than 150.

I really liked this class. i was scared about the five hour lab, but it actually goes by really fast and is great experience. she helps you with everything. you have to go to all the labs, but you can miss two lectures.buy the lab booklet, but not the textbook, because i honestly didn't open it once.
i love you benjamin bailey
I disagree with some of the people on here. I think he is whimsy and he makes me laugh every class. Not everyone gets his humor but I do and I recommend. He does cold call though.

On a power trip and refuses to admit he's ever wrong. The professor does nothing but repeat the readings and make you teach yourself as opposed to him teaching. Take it if you want an easy A, but don't expect an enjoyable time.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Lots of homework

reviews.comment: Such a good professor. He engages the audience and does funny, light-hearted demonstrations. Simple assignments, but exams are all open-response. Attendance is definitely important but you can watch the Echo360 and get away with it. Overall, as someone who loves an engaging class and a passionate professor, this was a great experience!

Such an amazing professor but SO MUCH WORK! Beware there's 2 assignments, 2 readings and 2 quizzes on the readings every week. My heaviest class this semester. Such interesting topics though and he's a nice guy. Just so much work...
reviews.rating_tags: Amazing lectures --Lots of homework--So many papers

reviews.comment: Professor Bailey's lectures were always entertaining! He does cold call, which I was nervous about because I am shy, but you can always say pass. I'm not sure why people said the essays were graded harshly, as long as you follow the prompt and provide detail, you'll be fine. I would suggest studying for the quizzes as they are all open response.

Able to retain my attention which is uncommon for me. 2 papers, 3 quizzes and no tests/final. Only issue was how he used students races as examples for class. He'd say "and to the Chinese students" and put a mic in one of their faces. He'd ask a question and often they would be too shy to respond and he would say "Okay I'll go to the other Chinese"

Overall good class if you pay attention and understand the material. There are frequent lecture and reading quizzes, however if you keep track of them they aren't bad. In-class tests are definitely worth studying for, and papers are graded harshly. As for the professor, he is great overall and does a good job at trying to keep the class engaged.

Professor Bailey was a very good professor who enjoys what he teaches. Funny guy, the work is not hard, you just have to do some pre and post class quizzes, and some easy papers. The in class quizzes are slightly harder, definitely study for them.

Prof. Bailey has to be the best professor I have right now. He makes effort to know the students in his class. There are small quizzes on lectures and readings but they are very easy if you pay attention. Paper exams are not bad at all if you pay attention and study before it. I'd take his class again, I never got bored of his lectures!

Professor Bailey is easily one of the best lecturers I've encountered at UMass, I have never heard classrooms erupt with laughter like how they did in his class. The exams can be tricky and there are online quizzes after every class which can be a blessing or a curse depending how you score on them.
Grading responses and paper has no leniency. If its not exactly what the rubric says then it is wrong.

probably my favorite professor at umass! lecture quizzes are easy if you show up but the reading quizzes are a little more challenging but not bad. lots of in class discussions about the readings and analyzing conversations, he will cold call on you but you can skip it and he wont ask you about it again which is nice!

The classwork isn't crazy, just busy work. There is two papers and 3 in class quizzes. The only negative thing is that for quizzes and papers, you need to be specific with details or else they take points away. There's a lecture quiz after every lecture. Attendance isn't mandatory but some questions on the lecture quiz are very specific to lecture.

Bailey is great & one of the few professors who is very dedicated to what they teach. The homework for this class was a lot of readings, but few were challenging. Two essays and three tests, all of which are gone over step by step in lecture or section. He does cold call but gives option to pass and not answer the question. Def take his classes

Set us up for failure on the last exam- only reviewed the final paper, no review for exam and combined different aspects of concepts together for questions making it so hard. Never went to class because I was scared of getting cold-called on (he does it all the time). Way too much work for a comm gen ed. Don't take this class
L

Great professor, makes lectures really interesting even though you might not have any interest in social science (coming from a stem elitist), a lot of reading, average amount of writing (if you can a write an average college paper while putting in some effort you will be fine in this respect), super easy to talk to, give 100% on every online quiz

Great professor and makes sure u understand the material. Weekly readings and a short open note/book mini quiz (usually 3 Mcg) about it. If you do the reading it's easy. Lectures are not mandatory but there is an open note after lecture quiz (3-4 mcg). If you pay attention to the lecture the quizzes are easy. He's passionate abt the class. Take it
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Amazing lectures --Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: one of the best comm classes I've ever taken. bailey's funny, engaging and kind and despite teaching a huge lecture class, remembers kids names and gives attention to everyone. lots of reading but they're super interesting, you're quizzed on all of the readings, but it's not that bad, it pushes you to actually read

Prof Bailey is my king. Great guy, really funny, and gets to know people in his class. There is a lot of quizzes, but they encourage you to do the readings (which can be long), but these quizzes helped me so much with the in class tests.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Lots of homework--Respected

reviews.comment: professor Bailey is one of my favorite professors at Umass. He is smart, organized, clear and funny. I actually looked forward to his class because it was so well done. He doesn't do exams, instead does lecture quizzes and reading quizzes so prepare for a lot of material. If you actually do the required work, you will do really well in the class.

Bailey's class was one that I genuinely enjoyed and looked forward to every week. He's super witty and his genuine passion for the subject makes the lectures even more engaging. The TAs were super helpful and accessible outside class as well (shoutout to Val :)!). The only downside IMO was the readings before every lecture.But 11/10 would recommend

It is clear that professor Bailey really likes his job and want's whats best for his students. He is very funny and outgoing. The class material is very interesting although he give out a lot of quizzes. The quizzes might seem overwhelming at first but I promise it does get easier. I really reccomend this class!

Prof. Bailey obviously enjoys his job and makes lectures interesting and engaging. He makes sure to get to know as many students as possible (by name too). There are a lot of quizzes (like ALOT) but they are relatively easy as long as you do the readings and watch the lectures (always has online recordings)

Prof Bailey is a funny guy and gives great feedback on assignments while still giving good grades. All the work leads to the final paper which makes it awesome and you know what is expected. This was one of the most entertaining classes and easy to pass because everything you do goes into your final paper basically.

I enjoyed Prof. Bailey's lectures over zoom, but his TA Eean Grimshaw was awful. Eean's grading is nitpicky & he is very critical, even if you do the entire assignment according to the rubric you'll probably get a 75. He also is not understanding and comes off as rude in discussion/over email. I don't recommend taking the class if Eean is your TA!

Professor Bailey is my favorite professor at UMass so far. His class (212) was very engaging, and would be even better in person. He was also my section instructor, and he presented the material in a very interesting way. He tries to get to know all of his students and will know everyone's name. Lots of small quizzes that make it less stressful. :)

One of my favorite professors I've had. Despite Covid, his lectures were extremely engaging, the material was very interesting, and he gave clear instructions on grading. Lots of very short online quizzes, but if you keep up with the material, you'll do fine. Definitely recommend!

Prof Bailey has done a great job online during corona. Classes are spent engaging in the material and he is an entertaining prof. You most likely will need to share an example to the class, so if you don't like that don't take this class. Also be aware that you will have an online quiz (usually multiple choice) or assignment due before every class.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Lots of homework--Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: Has done the best job with online lectures. Really makes you engaged with the course and has past recordings of in person lectures so you feel like you're really there. Loved all of the material and was the most interesting class I've taken in a while. Can be tedious, but kept me engaged. Would take again 100%
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Get ready to read--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: This class is really eye opening and I really enjoyed taking it. That being said, it is a decent amount of work, it isn't too bad if you have good time management skills, I just don't and found that a little challenging, but all in all it wasn't bad at all, and the interesting topics of study definitely keep you interesting.
reviews.rating_tags: Accessible outside class--Get ready to read--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: One of the most inspirational and eyeopening teachers. Great professor, really eccentric and caring. Does hilarious stuff in class to make a point he's trying to underline. Small quizzes for readings that appear tedious but are super easy and helpful. Do his work and he will like you, he's a great guy who's trying to make the world a better place.

Professor Bailey makes his class very interesting by engaging various students in the audience through different examples and questions, making the material more memorable and interesting. He gives an online quiz before and after each lecture, with the one before requiring reading. The quizzes tend to be pretty easy and short though.

lectures are very informative and help for daily quizzes. Bailey is soo funny and runs around the the class and has high energy that really keeps you interested even though i would try to sit on my phone. he also has tenure and tells you day 1 that reviews dont matter but he is really nice and my favorite even though im gonna fail his class
best class I've taken at UMass. Ben is a great professor and very well liked by his students. He really explains his assignments and make them enjoyable to complete. 10/10 recommend

VERY interesting class. Am now a senior, but took this class as a freshman. One of the most challenging classes I've ever taken at UMass and that is solely because there is just so much work you need to be accountable for. Keep up with EVERY assignment and youll do alright. I got a C in it because i was having difficulty managing it all. try it out
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Get ready to read--Skip class? You won't pass.

reviews.comment: Class isn't hard if you put in the work. Very interesting topics and readings. Hybrid class one lecture in class one, online. There's a lot of short quizzes really easy though if you read and listen in class. My favorite comm class I've taken at UMass so far.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Participation matters--LOTS OF HOMEWORK

reviews.comment: As a gen ed, the class had more readings than I would've liked. Prof. Bailey only gives a lecture once a week, then there's a discussion, and an online lecture. He gives 2 online quizzes per week which are pretty easy and 3 in- class quizzes which are graded fairly harshly. 2 papers graded easily. Not a terrible class, but too much work for a gened
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: THIS CLASS IS A JOKE, DO NOT TAKE THIS CLASS FOR YOUR GENED, PICK SOME OTHER CLASSES HE HAS NO MERCY FOR HIS STUDENTS
reviews.rating_tags: Tough Grader--LOTS OF HOMEWORK--BEWARE OF POP QUIZZES

reviews.comment: Dont take this class, its a joke

Prof. Bailey will attempt to complicate the simple action of talk. He does so by making you do a research paper and having you complete many assignments along the way. His lectures were mostly irrelevant to what the course was supposed to be about or what I expected the integrated experience to be.  Take the music I.E- its easier and a lot more fun
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--LOTS OF HOMEWORK

reviews.comment: Bailey is a nice guy and it was easy to talk with him about the final paper.  His class is just really boring.  Wouldn't recommend unless you're super dedicated to doing his assignments.

I agree with other reviews about his 414 class. Don't take it. It's not practical material and there are too many assignments.  His lectures are boring to sit through and I ended up with no useful knowledge.  If recording and transcribing conversations and doing pointless work sounds interesting to you then go for it.  If not, avoid at all costs.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--LOTS OF HOMEWORK

reviews.comment: Avoid Bailey if you're looking for an IE requirement.  His class is boring and not worthwhile to students.  If you want to do lots of pointless work, then take his class.  If you're interested in media/video, this class will make you want to give up on life.  His lectures are not engaging and you won't learn much from this course.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--LOTS OF HOMEWORK

reviews.comment: Professor Bailey is a boring professor and his class-The study of everyday talk was the most worthless class ever took at UMass.  It was a requirement and I should've taken an I.E. class earlier because COMM only offered Bailey's class as the single IE requirement for the semester.   There is so much work every week and its all worthless in the end
reviews.rating_tags: Tough Grader--Get ready to read--LOTS OF HOMEWORK

reviews.comment: Professor Bailey is a very interesting guy. 212 is a really cool class that made me think differently. A lot of the assignments are the same, which got pretty annoying. There are moodle quizzes every week for online lectures and in-class lectures. There are no exams, but there are in-class quizzes that were all short answer. Make sure you study.

Fantastic and respected professor. Lectures are interesting and although there is a lot of reading/quizzes they are interesting and doable. You need to make sure you are organized and plan out your reading time because there is a reading for each quiz. You will get an A if you do all the work. You will also learn a lot and enjoy the class.

Very good class. He gives small online quizzes that are very easy if you did the reading or lectures that are only 3 questions long. No final, only three in class quizzes and two papers. Highly recommend!

A LOT of pointless work. You don't learn anything. Extremely repetitive. A lot of reading. Worst TA's ever. You don't have to go to class, but you have to go to discussion. SO many online quizzes. Two papers. Three tests with all short answer questions. TOO MUCH WORK for 200 level class. His voice is also really annoying and you have to listen.

Hybrid course, one lec in person, one lec online. 3 short quizzes per week (3 ? each) on the readings, and the 2 lecs. A lot of information but if you have a good TA and actually pay attention to the reading you should do fine. Don't miss too many of the quizzes, individually they're not worth much, but they can start to count against your grade

His class is so boring do NOT take it. "Studying everyday talk" may sound interesting, it is not. This class is nothing but him boring you, you talking to your partner about nothing, and doing assignments twice a week.

I had Bailey for 3 courses (118, 212, 414) and I thought he was awesome in all of them! He is not necessarily easy but if you go to class and put some effort in you will get an A. The material is easy to understand and he is very thorough. If you need anything he is so helpful and also emails back in 5 minutes or less. Great professor!

There is a lot of work involved in this course on a variety of different topics. While there are a lot of small, 3 question quizzes online, the in-person questions are really difficult and he does not prepare the students well. Basically, if you do not get a good TA for discussion, you will get lost amongst the material.
Love Professor Bailey! He's funny and engaging and always asks the class for feedback. Class was pretty easy, just be prepared for (easy) pop quizzes

Overall loved the class. He prepares you for exams very well if you go to class. There are three exams, 1 paper and no final. Attending class is not mandatory but he attempts to learn most people's name in the class so he'll know. reading and online quizzes can be a pain as some questions are worded weird and are only 3 questions long

Each week you have about three online reading quizzes and three lecture quizzes. Each quiz has three questions so if you get one wrong you have a 67. those were annoying. make sure you get a good TA because they grade the papers. overall easy class but online quizzes were very annoying

He always made sure we understood the material. There were a lot of unannounced quizzes so you should really go to class. He shows funny video clips in class. There is a midyear and a final but he gives you a question bank before the tests. Great professor and great class!
he is one of the best professors at the school. he really knows his stuff and genuinely enjoys it. he give unannounced quizzes so its usually a good idea to go to class

I feel bad for Bailey, he obviously has very good views on education, but they don't work with classes the size of his. The "talking with your partner" exercises are about obvious questions. He would be great with a small class. His teaching is pretty clear, a little redundant. Don't take notes, he puts all powerpoints online. fairly easy A.
class was pretty boring, but he was a nice guy. does pop quizzes sometimes so have to go to class. tries hard to make the class interesting, just doesn't always work.

Good professor. He prints out your pictures and brings them to class to make sure your attending. Its nice to see a teacher try to learn everyone's name in a big lecture. You need to go to class to understand concepts but discussion helped too. Also he likes to shoot down answers he doesn't like.
Incredible teacher! Plus, he helps me with my math homework...
Great Overall! Definitely my favorite teacher EVER! He knows his stuff.
Extremely helpful, always happy to discuss things with students and work out problems.
really approachable and knowledgable

He seemed very interested in what he was talking about. he knew his stuff. He put up many videos that were sometimes boring sometimes interesting. There are a lot of pop quizzes, mainly on reading or class material. If you do the reading you'll be fine. The class was sometimes boring, but it was interesting as well. Do the reading! Go to class!
The material is interesting but he can be very monotonous at times. Unannounced quizzes are his way of taking attendance, lots of reading. Overall, I enjoyed what I learned in this class.

Benjamin Bailey may be the worst professor I have taken at UMass.  He may be good in a small setting, but he cannot teach a large class.  He gives pop quizzes, and even if you show up after doing the reading, its hard to get better than a 1 (if not a 0) out of 3 on the quizzes. Exams were hard. Talk to Bailey 1 on 1, and he may raise your grade tho

this class is so boring and not interesting at all. A lot of people in my class failed the midterm and he would not scale the test therefore a lot had to drop the class...think before you take this class with him
No Comments

This is a decent communication course. He seemed pretty helpful and he usually made class lively. He knew what he was talking about, so no confusion. There's constant homework reading and discussions in every class. If you take this class, expect to read at least the majority of the assigned readings because there are some unannounced quizzes, lol.
No Comments
he is an awesome teacher. he is funny n kind of witty. some of the remarks he makes takes ppl a while to get. quirky sense of humor. class content is really interesting too.
Very funny, kind of a hard grader, but class is small enough to figure out what he wants to see on his tests. Pop quizes but as long as you read  you'll be fine. Content in class is interesting.
No Comments
Prof. Bailey is helpful and inspiring.  A favorite!  He's great, but spacey.
No Comments
Prof. Bailey is always concerned about how the students feel about his classes

Great guy cares about student success. The class is less than helpful, learned more from my 310 jr year writing class. assignments are not well described, canvas so confusing, putting in WAY too much effort for a one credit class

I loved this professor, he really helped our class feel more conversational and would ask us questions to help engage in glass. He helped us really think about our professional development and how to excel in the business world. I don't like how the grading system changed though but what can you do. Assignments were very helpful too.

Prof. Bowse genuinely wants his students to succeed, and the class itself is helpful for making a resume and cover letter. Attendance is mandatory since it's once a week, but what else do you expect? TA's are kind and give good feedback.

The class has WAYYYY too much work for a 1 credit course. To add insult to injury the work is graded obscenely harshly. If you are able to take this class with anyone else do it. In terms of how he actually is as a professor he's actually not bad, very clear and engaging, just assigns way too much work.

The course is divided into two sections, and you need to earn 50 points in each section. The great thing about it is that you can choose which assignments to complete, as long as you earn the required 50 points. Professor Bowse is fantastic!

It's a 1-credit class with attendance on TopHat and about one assignment a week. It's easy career prep and Bob is nice, but my TA (Ailene) graded harshly. There are a lot of out-of-class tasks, so doing work early helps. Overall it was super helpful for resumes, LinkedIn, and interview advice.
Professor Bowse is super nice and respected. He wants everyone to do well. Definitely take a class with him if you can.

Professor Bowse is a good professor in a very useful class. No exams, just weekly assignments which make up for 80% of your grade. Class is pretty useful in getting you prepared for internships, as you work on resumes/cover letters. Some assignments are longer than others, but nothing too bad. Do the assignments and show up, and you will get an A.

Class is insanely easy. Literally show up, do the homework and online quizzes, and you'll get an A. It's also incredibly helpful for building a great resume and making your LinkedIn professional. It's worth paying attention and putting effort in too, as most of the material is applicable to real life
Funny and knowledgeable guy and this class actually helped me get a pretty solid resume prepared. Some assignments were annoying and involved but overall useful material.
Bob and his TA are nice and answer emails quickly. Attendance is worth 15% of your final grade so go to class. The work is light and you only meet once a week, overall not a difficult class.

Overall, this was an okay class. Consistent class structure and a decent amount of work to do outside of it, but it was manageable. Sometimes Bob can be a bit cold and abrasive, but his class was fairly informative. Not very responsive through email

Bob is lovely, but he is a very tough grader. His lectures were rather nice, but it was really difficult to stay engaged and to follow along. I am so grateful that I got to take the class with him, but found it difficult at times to pay attention. Have have heard that he can be rather harsh and dismissive. Great class and really enjoyed taking it!

Genuinely useful career advice! I'm glad this course is a requirement. Some of the assignments get a bit involved, but it's all very manageable. He makes his lectures engaging, and he's very approachable. Super nice guy. He let students connect with him on LinkedIn which was very helpful.
reviews.rating_tags: Clear grading criteria--Accessible outside class--Online Savvy

reviews.comment: You just meet once a week and usually have assignments you could finish an hour before class starts. It's a one credit class so it was made to be an easy A and the material we go over is pretty useful career wise.

Class is only once a week with assignments that you have to stay on top of, but manageable if you keep ahead of it. Some assignments are very easy but some would be out of the blue take a couple of hours so make sure you plan ahead.
Really nice professor, this class was only 1 credit so easy A, does have weekly assignments but they are all really easy, no worries.
His feedback is alright but he gives so much unnecessary busy work compared to other professors you can take. I would recommend someone else.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough Grader--Skip class? You won't pass.--LOTS OF HOMEWORK

reviews.comment: This class will definitely keep you busy, but his grading is fair and the feedback he gives you is valuable.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Skip class? You won't pass.--LOTS OF HOMEWORK

reviews.comment: Great professor, I actually learned so much from him. He does tend to give a lot of busy work and is pretty particular when it comes to grading. But I feel like I learned so much in this class, and it is a useful topic that everyone will need in business. My writing definitely improved and I would definitely recommend him.

Professor Bowse has quite a deceptive rating of 4.3. His grading is extremely picky and assignments must be completed HIS way or no way. In terms of workload, this Junior year writing class has considerably more work than other professors.

Bob gives lots of work and can be a strict (but fair) grader, but gives a lot of useful feedback and makes his expectations for each assignment clear. Grade is mostly based on 4 major assignments at the end of each section. There is a conference before every deadline where Bob gives feedback for the final version. Not hard to get an A if you listen

Great class! He is very inspiration. I'm taking it at 8:30 a.m. and I actually don't dread going to it. Fair grader and learned a lot because he gives extensive feedback. Divided into 4 sections: a cover letter, a brand analysis report, proposal and a group presentations.
Way more work than you sign up for.  More work than all my other classes combined
reviews.rating_tags: Tough Grader--Skip class? You won't pass.

reviews.comment: One of the best professors I've ever had. He's a fair, if not lenient, grader. He teaches Business Communications extremely well. If you attend every single lecture you get an additional 2 points on your final grade. He cancels a couple classes for individual 'conferences' to help give feedback. This class really helped my writing.

Lots of dad jokes! Assignments require a lot of work but he has conferences so that you can get feedback. Grading criteria is really clear and he is a straightforward grader. Lots of little, easy assignments to keep your grade up & extra credit for perfect attendance.

Professor Bowse's class is well-structured. Unfortunately, he is not the most pleasant human being. The class can be dry, attendance is basically mandatory, and he has a heavy personality. I would NOT recommend people to take his class, not because it's a "bad" class, but because there are more favorable alternatives at UMass. Take my advice.
Actually learned a LOT in this class. Bowse is super funny and helpful. The assignments are a lot of work but not impossible. Attendance is mandatory though but no book you have to buy!

Great professor, he really wanted to help us learn to be better working professionals. I thought his resume-workshop class was amazing as it really helped clean up my resume. We gave a presentation at the end which helped me earn some skills, and he gives 7 extra credit pts for coming to class. No exams just 4 big projects and little hw. Take it.

AWESOME CLASS. Not mandatory, but professor is so helpful in every way possible. No tests, only projects, and you will get A's if you re-read his power points he posts online. Also,  submit assignments for feedback and you are not only guaranteed to get a good grade, but you will also learn a lot.

I took the half-online, half in class format they offered as a test. how to get an A: go to lecture+ iclicker, submit draft for review from online professor, get it read by bowse too and fix whatever he says, do the moodle homework on time. That's it. They'll tell you what parts of your paper suck and you fix it. Do exactly what the sample does.
Great teacher. Very smart. Very easy on the eyes. Not hard to get me to go to this class at all. Oh and he's really funny.

I can sum it up by saying he is tough, but fair. It's not a ton of extra work but a decent amount, and NO BOOK and HARDLY EVER ANY READINGS! Especially in the beginning of the semester he is EXTREMELY helpful because he completely helps fix your resume and cover letter, which helps you in the job market! He really does care about helping you.

Smart guy! We did a lot more work than other junior writting classes but I am a better business communicator because of it. He gives excellent feedback and will give you ideas if you go to his office. Bob is down to earth and funny it was my favorite class this semester. Take this class to learn how to write professional cover letters & resumes.
Good professor. Very blunt when grading, which turns out to be extremely helpful. The projects and activities are good. Fair grading system.

Extremely good teacher who made writing fun!!! He gave really good feedback on papers and allowed for multiple peer-editing during class. He told you common mistakes before you started writing so that you didn't make the same ones. I would definitely take another class with him.
amazing teacher and i learned so much from him. and hes super hot :)
cool guy, doesnt expect too much, go to class, 5 essays, could have a much worse teacher

he's a fun prof and a good guy, but he expects a lot out of his students, especially in the honors section. he will not hesitate to tell you if your essays...well suck. but in the end, his sheer honesty makes for easy corrections.

gives alot of B+'s. alot of 1 page writing assignments for homework - pretty easy to do though. have to really work on editing your paper and improving it - can sometimes be unclear in what he wants but that's just writing. good guy
Open minded teacher who listens to students.
He grades pretty easy and all you have to do to get a good grade is improve on your essays, the final product doesnt even have to be that great.  Classes are a little dull though.
Really easy class. Grades easily, and not a lot of work.

Honestly Lori is best professor I have had thus far. She makes seemingly tough concepts so easy to understand, and gives 5 easy exams with a cheat sheet allowed. Not a lot of work outside class. So many opportunities for extra credit, including an optional discussion once a week which is super easy and helpful. Love Lori and this class!

there are not a lot of assignments to help you if you dont do well on the 5 exams we have. she talks so fast, the only plus is that you can do the class on zoom. The exams were kinda hard and i would not recommending taking this if you are a normal psych student.
Lectures, top hat attendance, no quizzes, easy small assignment every week, very easy A+ as long as you complete all assignments on time and go to each lecture

Dr. A explains the material clearly and makes sure to clarify anything people ask about. She encourages questions and answers in easy to understand ways. Assignments: weekly 15 min or less surveys and one final project.

Honestly just a really great professor. Very clear and informative lectures. Its clear she cares about her students doing well. It is a very content heavy class with very difficult concepts. Also exam heavy, 5 midterms, optional final. Although this class was hard Dr. A had lots of extra credit, and lots of help opportunities.
reviews.rating_tags: EXTRA CREDIT--Clear grading criteria--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Truly the best professor I've ever been blessed to have. PLEASE attend the most lectures you can because they are the most comprehensive and engaging hours of my college experience so far. She has so much extra credit that it is hard to not get an A in this class. Attendance is through TopHat and you can join from zoom if needed, but go in person!!

She is amazing. Dr. A offers a zoom link to watch class live while not attending in person. Quizzes are take home and multiple choice. She is very passionate about neuroscience. The class is very big but she does encourage participation and talking with people near you. She is amazing, even if science is not your thing you can do great.

Dr. A is one of the best professors I've had. She is very passionate, funny, and makes going to lectures worth it (even in lousy weather!). Go to lectures, takes notes, and you will pass no problem. She teaches such complex material in way that any student can understand. Tests are easy and fair, and everything you need are on the slides!

Just an amazing professor overall! Lori makes the content super understandable and really cares about your understanding. She is guaranteed to make you laugh atleast a few times during the semester, and good notes are key to doing well on the mini exams, (they are open note :)

I took Psych 330 with Dr. Astheimer Best. I'd say that she's the best professor I've had at this school. She does such a good job of making the content digestible and interesting. perfectly compliments the course content, and the amount of extra credit provided is insane. We have no exams, only mini-exams that are open note and online.
One of the best professors I've had! She's so enthusiastic about the material and makes it so exciting to learn. She's very understanding and helpful outside of class too!

Lori is one of the best professors I've had at Umass. She makes class so enjoyable and interesting. There are 5 mini exams, unfortunately I think this semester is the last time they will be take home, but take good notes and you will be fine. There are 5 other small assignments. There is really no way you could fail the class.

The best professor I have had at umass. She talks fast but she is so energetic and funny and you can tell she loves the subject, which makes her lectures enjoyable. There are five assignments, five open-note multiple choice mini-exams, and the final is optional. The textbook and top hat are free and she gives so much extra credit.

Great prof. Has SONA and discussions for extra credit. She is funny and great at explaining. Available slides, readings, open note exams. I like going to class and even has a zoom to join from home is needed. Clicker questions but not graded intensely --> 1/2 credit = full credit for them. She is intelligent and informative, kind, and enjoyable.
Best professor I've had.

She was so great and super inspiring! Homework, quizzes, and exams are all offered online and during office hours so you can Zoom in with any questions. The SI sessions were super helpful and fun too.

One of the best profs I've ever had. I believed that I hated neuro until I took her course. Funny and engaging lectures, clearly is passionate and cares about students. Mandatory attendance but you get 10 opportunities to miss. Optional (extra credit) discussions. 5 online open note mini exams. 5 simple hw assignments. TAKE THIS COURSE!!
One of the best profs I've had - super engaging lectures, makes learning fun with puppy breaks and great analogies. Exams are online open-note, and unstuckstudy was a big help for study prep.
My most favorite professor I have ever had

Please take a class with Lori if you can! Really engaging lectures and makes complicated topics easy to understand. Online & open note exams, 5 very short writing assignments (like 4 questions about an article you choose), extra credit discussions, and iClicker based on completion not correctness. She really cares about the students and it shows.

Great prof. Took intro neuroscience which was hard. But her lectures were recorded, and all tests were online. IClicker points can be done on the app outside of class but I did 50% of them and still got a B. I wish I had attended class more because I would have had a better understanding of the material. She has accessible class material so 10/10.

Lori is an absolutely PHENOMENAL professor, possibly the best I have had at UMass. She is knowledgable and cares about the content that she is teaching and her students. Lori is very accessible outside of class and is always willing to answer questions. All exams were online and open note and the final was optional, making it a very easy A.

One of the nicest professors I've ever had; her exams were online open-note, she really just wanted you to learn the content and not worry about your grade on exams. She offered extra credit for going to TA discussions and dropped your lowest exam. Also super accommodating and provided live Zoom lectures to still get attendance credit if you're ill

Prof. AB's flexibility allowed for an open learning environment that worked for everyone. You could participate as much or as little as you wanted in discussions, she provided in person or zoom options for class, and dropped lowest grades.

I absolutely ADORE Lori. I'm not a science person in the least but she sparked my interest in neuroscience. Lectures have a zoom option and she has made all textbooks free for students thru the library. Tracks attendance through iClickers but you would want to go to class bc of how good she is. Super helpful in office hours. 11/10.

LOVED this class. The extra credit discussion was great for studying help and test prep. AND its extra credit so go! All the exams are online and you have writing assignments with questions to answer. Shes super passionate about her class and it really shows. She has a zoom option which is great when your sick and iclicker bonus points as well.
reviews.rating_tags: EXTRA CREDIT--Gives good feedback--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: One of the best prof I've had and know. She makes lectures very interesting and has great jokes and puppy breaks. Mini exams are online. Attendance is mandatory but you can miss up to 11 classes. Neuro discussions are extra credit.
She was just amazing I loved having her as a teacher!

Very engaging class and professor. She was always well-prepared to answer all questions and cover all subjects thoroughly. She also inspired great interest in the class because her lectures were fantastic. Grading policy is clear and fair, as long as you attend lecture you'll do well and probably even enjoy yourself.

This class was by far my favorite. Dr. A's course was very interesting and she managed to make every difficult topics easy to digest. Her assignments aren't too hard and there's plenty of feedback available if you need it

Dr. Astheimer was the best professor! I really enjoyed her teaching style and the way that she got me interested in Neuroscience. Her lectures were very informative and she made it easy to do well in the course. There were 5 mini exams, an optional final, and so many extra credit opportunities. 10/10 rating for Dr. Astheimer!!
reviews.rating_tags: Amazing lectures --Clear grading criteria--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Lori is the best! I haven't taken a bio related class since high school but she made it fun and accessible. All you really need is to come to lecture, either in person or online, and you're set for the course.

Dr. Astheimer is a phenomenal teacher. She makes lectures super engaging and interesting and always has funny analogies/ways to help you remember information. She shows clear passion for what she is teaching and brings energy to class each day. This is my favorite course I've taken at UMass so far. 5 "mini-exams" and 5 discussion-esque assignments

Professor A is the best! Has 5 mini exams that are all open note and online. Optional final that can replace two of these mini exam scores. IClicker attendence but also offers class over zoom. Can miss 10 classes without penalty. 5 Neuro Newsroom assignments which you pick an article and answer a few questions about. Various extra credit given.

Even though the class material is extremely hard for me and I don't understand it, I still enjoyed this class. She is a really accessible and caring professor. I can tell how passionate she is about the things she teaches. Classes are very engaging. She is also extremely accommodating to any extenuating circumstances. One of the best professors.

I love Dr. A!! She is so engaging and makes lecture pretty interesting. 5 "mini-exams" and they were all online/open note + 5 "newsroom" assignments (usually 1-2 pages, easy). Even though the material can be super sciencey I thought it was very interesting. No need to read the textbook.
Dr. Astheimer is one of the best psych professors I've had so far. I also took her PSYCH191B before 330 and she was equally great. If you are able to take a class with her as a professor do it!

She's so passionate about the subject that it makes you want to learn. She does iclickers every class, but I always wanted to attend her lectures so I never found it tough to go. Hands down one of my favorite professors. All psych majors should try to take a class with her at some point!

Really good teacher and very interesting class. Attendance is not mandatory, but she does use iclicker to take participation points but she drops a lot of the missed grades. You can also join iclicker from home and watch the lecture on zoom which is really helpful.

I am by no means a biology person, but she made me enjoy this class much more than I would've expected. She's great at explaining, her teaching and slides are engaging. You can miss up to 12 classes without penalty & plenty extra credit. Some exams were tough, but not the worst, homework assignments help engage material with the real world.

I LOVE Lori. She was by far my best professor at umass this far and you could tell she really cared about all the students even though this was a big class. Some of the material is hard but she makes it super engaging. If you can take a class with her, DO IT! So happy to know there are still professors like this.

Best professor I've had at UMass. Engages students in the course material, ensures it is easy to understand. Wants you to succeed. HW assignments (10 total) are simple. Discussion sections optional. Opportunities for extra credit.

I love Lori!! This class was pretty easy. She allows you to miss around 12 lectures which is really nice. She does IClicker, but she drops the amount of lectures you are allowed to miss. Not a lot of outside work too. She does around 5 mini assignments. All the exams are online as well, even the final. There is no required textbook as well.

The material can be tough but Dr. A structures class so you have what you need to do well. In person study groups go over material and test prep (ech attendance worth .5 extra credit points) Lectures are key for course. All lectures recorded & Zoomed w/ iClicker app access (that's been a life saver when sick). Lectures key for tests.

Lori is by far the best professor I have ever had. She is so smart and super helpful, I have nothing but respect for her. She will always make time for her students and she loves to answer questions about the content. She makes the neuro major a lot less scary and her lectures are straightforward and easy to understand. Take her class if you can.

Dr.A is an excellent instructor and actually cares about her students doing well, and learning. There are barely any homeoworks, and 5 mini-exams, so each one doesn't jeapordize your grade too much if you do poorly. Definetly reccomend this class, especially as a tech elective for BME.
Dr. A is a fantastic teacher. This class was super easy with very straightforward expectations, so it was easy to stay on top of things. 10/10 recommend.

Cannot say enough good things about Professor Astheimer. She is amazing! Introduction to neuro content is biology heavy, but her lectures make it manageable. Her lectures are engaging, and her expectations are reasonable. You have a weekly quiz that is solely based on iClicker questions in class. Exams are straightforward and totally doable.

Lori is amazing ! She is extremely organised and so kind to talk to. Her material is so amazingly interesting. Attend her lectures, take good notes - class is divided into 5 mini exams that are pretty straightforward if you took good notes and studied well. She is absolutely wonderful. Take it
reviews.rating_tags: Clear grading criteria--Lecture heavy--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Lectures were very organized, so easy to follow, and always stops to answer questions and provide clarity. Assignments are very straightforward and not hard. There are 5 mini exams, which are low stress and make it so if you don't do well on one you can still get a good grade. She is funny and makes it enjoyable to attend class.
Wish I could have her for every Psych class I take. Easy to do well if you pay attention and make use of the many resources. Shes an understanding person too so dont be afraid to reach out.

Psych 191B was only 1 credit so it was already an easy class but Lori taught it beautifully. She uses PowerPoints which she also posts on Moodle and included handout versions that you could easily print and write on. She was really sweet, tried her best everyday + she cares about you passing as a student. Will never give you a hard time, 10/10
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Skip class? You won't pass.--Caring

reviews.comment: I absolutely loved her lectures. She makes a lot of difficult content easy to digest. Highly recommend taking a class with her.

I cant say enough good things. Her lectures are extremely interesting and even as a person with ADHD I find myself paying attention the entire class. Shes very fair with assigning work  its very manageable. Shes also very understanding and generously changed all the exams to online when covid numbers on campus started rising. 10/10.

Dr. A is wonderful professor! Neuroscience is content heavy but the course is divided into 5 mini-exam making it easier to follow. All the answers to the weekly quizzes are in the lectures. Shes easily accessible outside of class! Watch all the lectures, take notes, and youll do great!
reviews.rating_tags: Accessible outside class--Clear grading criteria--EXTRA CREDIT

reviews.comment: Very straightforward class, and Dr A is a very caring professor. Super recommended. I just found the concepts of Neuroscience being taught a little tricky since I have never taken CHEM or BIO. If you pay attention you will do great.

She was the best! There is a lot of material but it is broken down into 5 sections (with a mini-exam at the end of each)so it's manageable. Def attend/watch every lecture and take good notes! 5 easy hw assignments. Weekly quizzes but she gives you the answers in class! No textbook/extra reading needed. I'd recommend taking this before 315
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Amazing lectures--Caring

reviews.comment: Professor AB is a great professor! She explains everything super well and the exams are open notes. She has weekly quizzes but they're all questions from lectures so if you just take a picture you'll get an easy 100 on them. There are 5 exams and a final which covers 2 exam scores if it's a higher grade, this helps if you mess up an exam.
Lori is the best. Great professor, clear explanations, and offers extra credit. The mini exams are doable, as long as you study, you can get an A
reviews.rating_tags: Respected--Skip class? You won't pass.--EXTRA CREDIT

reviews.comment: Professor Astheimer has been my favorite psych professor so far! Her lectures are engaging and clear, she's understanding and sympathetic to student needs. Assignments and grading are straightforward, and she's very passionate about student understanding. I was scared to take neuro, but I learned a lot and felt pretty confident during the class.

I loved Dr. A. I was really nervous for neuroscience, but she made the information accessible and easy to understand. Her lectures were engaging and she makes sure that her students are following the material. She really cares for her students and is genuinely a very good person.

This class was really easy. You can easily just learn from the slides she uploads to Moodle. Once a week, you just need to do a small quiz or assignment on Moodle, and there's an open-notes final. It's a P/F class that I mostly took for an extra credit and to get ready for Psych 330. She also teaches 330, so it's a good way to get to know her

Dr. A is an incredible professor. I have struggled with every science class I have taken since high school so I was really intimidated by taking behavioral neuroscience but I ended up understanding the material, ending with an A, and actually enjoying myself! She explains things in a way that makes complicated material seem really easy. 10/10 prof

Wrapping up my semester with Prof A. Best and she was absolutely wonderful. Neuroscience is definitely a difficult subject but she explains everything really clearly and effectively despite the remote learning format. She really, genuinely cares about her students and wants us to succeed.

I wouldn't consider myself an exemplary student, so this class was pretty difficult. Prof Best makes the class as easy as possible, but your grade entirely depends on your personal effort. If you don't show up to class, you will fail. If you don't study hard before each exam, you will fail. If you do those two things you will be completely fine.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Test heavy--Caring

reviews.comment: Amazing professor. Extremely fair. You must actually study before the exams to do well, but if you put in the effort you can get an A. Helpful weekly discussions and extra credit options.

The most amazing professor. I wish she taught every class. The lectures are very dense, but she breaks it up into 5 mini exams so each exam doesn't have too much on it. The clickers in class help prepare for exams so much by testing how well you can apply the knowledge, not just knowing information. You learn a lot. I except an A in this class.
She's just a good teacher

Please take this class! Professor A is by far the greatest teacher on campus. She explains everything so clearly and is absolutely hilarious. 5 "mini exams" are the bulk of your grade with an optional final to replace the 2 lowest grades. Lots of extra credit available as well. Just pay attention in lecture and you'll do great.
In the past I have struggled with neuroscience but Professor Astheimer made it easier for me to understand. As long as you try to follow along and review discussion notes, you should be ok.

Lori is amazing. The course is very dense & a lot of information. Not work heavy at all but 5 mini exams that you really need to study hard for. She wants you to do well & gives you the chance to replace your two lowest exams with the final which is huge. Shes a great professor. Attendance is key, allowing 5 absences. Assignments are an easy 100.
reviews.rating_tags: Respected--Skip class? You won't pass.--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: Dr. A was an overall good teacher. If you try to skip her lectures you are F#cked. Even with echo 360 to catch up after her lectures are HEAVY.

reviews.comment: Attendance iClicker: 30 points, 5 Moodle assignments (really easy): 25 points total, 5 MINI-Exams (they are really specific, but if you make quizlets and study for them they are an easy A): 150 pts total. Optional final exam replaces 2 Mini exam grades. Extra credit: SONA + Surveys Go to all classes, and study effectively-- EASY A
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Graded by few things--Test heavy

reviews.comment: Lori is an amazing professor and the material she teaches is very interesting and relevant. The class is pretty easy as long as you study the material a couple of days leading up to the exams (there are 5 in total) and the final is optional. There is a lot of memorization in this class but flashcards help a lot.

Lori is a great teacher who is really invested in what she teaches. There isnt really a lot of homework which is good. I clicker definitely plays a big part in your grade but you get a certain amount of free absences. The exams can be tough but she the final is optional and can replace your two lowest exam grades.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Skip class? You won't pass.--ACCESSIBLE OUTSIDE CLASS

reviews.comment: Lori is absolutely amazing. Best professor I've had at UMass, and also a great advisor. Puts a lot of care into her lectures, and can answer any question she's asked. I wouldn't take Psych 330 with anyone else. Pay attention in class, and you'll be fine. 5 easy mini-exams and lots of extra credit. It's pretty hard not to do well.

The best professor I've had at UMass so far! She explains things so well and gives amazing lectures. There are 5 mini exams, an optional final, and some moodle assignments. There are so many ways to earn extra credit, and the exams are super easy. Honestly, I think it would be hard not to get an A.
Lori is amazing! She is super knowledgable and while the information is not the easiest, Lori explains it really well and gives the class good ways to remember info.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Hilarious--TEST HEAVY

reviews.comment: She is legit one of the best (pun intended) professors that I have had. All of the lectures were great. I didn't read the textbook, but through the lectures I did well. You would have to pay attention, but she will explain everything well and gives great ways to remember the material. I would definitely recommend her as a professor for any class.

Lori is one of the best professors I've had at UMass. Attendance for the class is mandatory and taken through iClicker questions, but lectures are very interesting anyway. There are 5 mini-exams, an optional final, and 5 Newsroom posts through moodle. I'd highly recommend.

One of the best classes I've taken at UMass. Super clear and easy to understand. Makes the material really interesting. Makes you laugh with her funny analogies and ways to remember things. Overall just an awesome class that isn't really that difficult if you pay attention and study for the exams. I would take every class she teaches, she is so rad
reviews.rating_tags: Respected--Skip class? You won't pass.--Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: Very engaging and amusing and tries to keep you from getting bored. Moves through material at a good pace to make class fly by half the time. A lot of your grade is tests (multiple choice) but there are several and she posts the slides. Clicker attendance is part of your grade as well as some relatively minor homework every-other week.

I loved this class. As long as you read over the slides and actually study for the exams, you will get an A. She says you need the textbook but you definitely don't. 100% of her exam questions come from her lecture slides, which she posts on Moodle. She also gives extra credit. One of my favorite classes at UMass.

Graded on 6 mini exams with an optional final that replaces your two lowest exam grades if you do better on the final. Iclicker points in class, and she posts the lectures on Echo360 if you miss one (I think you can miss 2 no penalty) Option discussions for extra credit. Overall she clearly knows what shes talking about.
reviews.rating_tags: Respected--Skip class? You won't pass.--TEST HEAVY

reviews.comment: Dr. A has been my favorite professor thus far. She is super funny and going to lecture is actually enjoyable. The class consists of 5 newsroom articles, 5 mini exams and an optional final. There's tons of extra credit and if you show up to every class and pay attention you should have no problem getting an A especially if you've take bio or psych.

This was a really great course and that was completely due to Lori. Her lectures were really clear and comprehensive. She explained concepts multiple different ways and gave you fun ways to remember kind of confusing material. There were 5 exams, but they were each only 25 questions and completely based on lecture so a quick review is all you need!
Lori is a great teacher and is so nice. There is not a lot of work for this class but she does not prepare you for exams that well in my opinion.

Dr. A really cares for her students and is one of the best professors I've ever had! Take this class if you ever get the chance, she makes it really interesting and she is extremely knowledgeable and offers a lot of extra credit opportunities! (Plus she puts in puppy videos when she changes topics)

Lori is an AMAZING professor. Neuroscience can be hard, especially if you haven't taken any extensive bio classes, but Lori makes it manageable. The units are blocked in helpful ways, her iclicker questions prepare you well for exams, and she explains things in the best way possible.

This class is fantastic- it is properly difficult without being impossible and you will learn so much if you go to class and put the effort into it. Professor Astheimer is passionate lecturer, provides clear explanations, and puts in a ton of effort to ensure your success. This class is a must if you are interested in psychology!

Lori is the best professor I have ever had! She is funny, intelligent, and makes every lecture super interesting. The grading criteria is clear, and there are many opportunities for extra credit. 5 exams, 5 newsroom assignments that take 30 mins a piece, and iClicker. Up to 16 points of EC between optional discussion and SONA.

Lori is hands down best professor I have ever had. she's so young and funny and really makes class interesting and entertaining. optional discussion that gives you 10 extra credit points if you go. tests are kind of difficult if you don't study. her clicker questions basically tell you what is on the exam. love her so much

Lori is one of the best professors I have ever had.  She makes the material super fun and easy to memorize. Go to the optional discussion for tons of extra credit. Highly recommend taking this class to someone who isn't a psych major, but is interested in the subject. Great intro to the field.
A lot of extra credit opportunities. Lori is very nice and always answers questions. She makes corny jokes in class and it's pretty funny! Definitely a good professor.
Best person to have. 6 exams might be a lot, but they are only 25 multiple choice questions.

Lori is one of the best professors I've ever had. Grading criteria is simple, and there is no homework. There are six mini exams, note-card quizzes that serve as attendance and plenty of extra credit opportunities. As long as you attend lecture and optional discussions (which count for extra credit and prepare you for exams) you can get an A!
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--ACCESSIBLE OUTSIDE CLASS--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: Lori is one of the best and most reasonable psychology professors at UMass. Her lectures move pretty fast and there are writing assignments that measure your attendance and comprehension but they're usually answered by the material she covers. She's hilarious and loves showing you dog pictures but make sure you study for the exams; notes are a MUST

Lori is easily one of the best professors at UMass. It's so evident that she cares for all of her students and their success. This class has optional discussions, but they're helpful and make up a TON of extra credit. Definitely go to lectures, but with no homework you just have to study the lecture slides,discussion worksheets and you'll do great!

She is a goddess. You'll have to put in a fair amount of effort, but all in all the course isn't very stressful.  The exams are not only fair but also kind of fun, and she really wants everyone to succeed.
It was not easy to get an A. But her office hour was very helpful. She truly helps out her students a lot. Go to the lecture and take a notes.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Respected--Skip class? You won't pass.

reviews.comment: LOVE LOVE LOVE Lori. Honestly if you have the chance to take a class with Lori do it! It's challenging but shes the best professor at UMass hands down. You have to study and go to class but it's not hard to do because everything is clear and interesting! I want to take more classes with her!
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--TEST HEAVY--Caring

reviews.comment: Lori Best is the best Lori at umass.  Seriously, her teaching style keeps your attention even though the material can be quite difficult.  Its worth it for how awesome she is.

She's the best! Dr Astheimer is incredibly passionate about neuroscience and wants you to be too. Attendance is taken so you do need to go to class, but it is extremely helpful to go and take notes. There are 6 tests throughout the semester and optional final, plus lots of extra credit if you want it. Definitely take this class with her if you can!
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Inspirational--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: The material is pretty straightforward as long as you go to class and take notes. She makes it interesting and easy to remember with acronyms and memory tricks. Her mini exams were sooo much better than having evening exams, and writing assignments weren't bad at all. Book completely not necessary. Go to discussion!!! Every week.

Dr. Best is great. She tries to make lectures fun and exciting and she does. She is clear about what you need to know and she provides everything in the lecture slides. Really easy to get an A if you put in the time to study the lecture slides. She also gives you many chances to get extra credit so take advantage of that!

Neuroplasticity Seminar is a wonderful seminar and Lori does a great job engaging students in a cool area of study by making this class similar to a journal club. One main project + moodle participation and a final paper. Not too much work. Lori really gets to know the students and makes it an enjoyable class.

This class is really a pretty easy A.  She is really clear and does not try to overcomplicate anything like some professors might.  If you attend lecture you will get at the very least a B+.  She also gives enough extra credit that you will do really well.  6 mini exams that are fairly easy because they are shorter.  The final is optional.

I absolutely love her!!! She is really interested in the subject matter, and she tries to make it funny and engaging for everyone, even if you're not super into science. The course itself is certainly rigorous but as long as you pay good attention in class and study the review worksheets, tests will be absolutely fine.

Dr. Best is probably one of the best professors I've had. The material can be confusing but she does an AMAZING job of explaining everything. Textbook really isn't mandatory. Grading is based off 6 multiple choice exams and handing in a short response every lecture, so no homework. If you need to take Psych 330, I highly recommend Dr. Astheimer.

Lori is one of my favorite professors at umass. she cares about her students and is a great lecturer. She moves a little quickly but her study guides are really helpful. She says you need the textbook and for someone who has a hard time with the material it may help, but her exams come straight from her lectures that she posts online.

Lori is one of the best professors I have ever had. She's  clear and concise with all of the information presented. Lori's also funny  and loves what she studies which makes the class way more engaging. Going to class is a must bc of in-class writing assignments and exams can be tricky, but there's an optional final (replaces lowest 2 mini-exams).
Lori is an incredible teacher. Definitely recommended. Don't buy the book.

Dr. A is one of my favorite professors I've had so far at UMass. If you don't go to class, expect your grade to reflect that. Paying attention to lecture slides is critical, but she is extremely generous with extra credit. Don't bother buying the book, as it was an expensive waste.

Lori is such a nice person! Lectures were super long and condensed with a ton of info.  As long as you study her slides, and her pre-test wkshts you should be fine. If you can do high school bio you should do fine. Psych majors strug hard though. 6 exams, that sometimes test random stuff, and in class writing asmt, lots of EC. No need for book IMO.

Lori is a great teacher because she really cares about her students. Sitting in her lectures you can tell she wants every person in the room to understand what she is trying to teach. Yeah, behavioral neuroscience is a confusing subject for some people, but she makes it as simple as she can. I am so glad I took this class; I wish she had more!

If you're not good at science, you'll have to work hard to do well in this class. At the same time, it is possible to succeed if you go to class and study for the tests. Lori is funny and wants her students to do well and to be engaged. She's understanding, but not by any means a pushover.

Lori's test were almost impossible... she would jumble up everything you learn in lecture and throw it on the test in a completely different context. I would study for 3 days straight for these tests and still get high D's on them. Tests are really unfair. She does give extra credit though, which is the only reason I got a B.
There's a lot of material in her slides, but focus on the study guide that she hands out and you should do fine on the mini-exams. The mini-exams are tough but a lot of extra credit is offered.

Prof. Astheimer makes class interesting because she is actually interested in her subject. The material can be hard at times, but she will clarify any questions and is good about taking time to make sure that everyone understands. Also she has a good sense of humor.

While the material in Behavioral Neuro is pretty tough, Astheimer does a great job clarifying the information and you can tell she loves what she teaches.  6 mini-exams and an optional "for extra credit" discussion that I found super helpful. Exams are just 25 multiple choice each and there's an optional final that can replace your two lowest exams

LOVE HER! 6 "mini exams" instead of one or two really big ones makes it easy to save your grade and retain material. Her sense of humor is great and she's very interested in student success.
