Offers extra credit, only complaint is that the material can be tough but she honestly makes it so easy to succeed if you put in the effort.

pI just started Behavioral Neuroscience and I can already say this woman is amazing.  She makes difficult material manageable and interesting. Just the way she talks about it inspires interest in the class. Plus she's pretty funny! Love her! Great class so far, she seems really understanding!

Professor Best was absolutely amazing. I love Neurosicence already and she just made me want to learn even more. She is extremely clear and concise. She lets you know what exactly is going to be on the exam. Study her slides and you will be golden for the exam. 6 easy mini exams! little 3 point index card question at end of class. A must take!!!!

Dr. Astheimer tries to makes the material interesting even when most psych majors hate this topic. She flies through the notes but willing to answer questions. Attendance is taken through daily writing assignments. Mini Exams about every two weeks are moderately hard but there's plenty of opportunities to get a good grade.

This was a super easy class if you attend lectures. She explains everything clearly and puts that information on the exams. She gives plenty of opportunities for extra credit. You don't need to buy the book if you go to class. Easy A.

Easiest Class of my college career. Then again...I major in a science related field, which I will not disclose in order to prevent bias opinions. Just read the book for this class. The lectures are tedious, if you are smart.

Dr. A is awesome! Sometimes test questions are confusing, but she's willing to give half credit. She's very passionate. Attendance mandatory, 6 mini-exams, optional final, extra credit. If you're struggling, go to the discussion sections and test reviews. Reading the book definitely helps. Lori makes this topic as easy as it can be.

I'm a business major with no science background at all and I just got an A in this class.  Buy the book, go to EVERY class, take notes on a laptop (to keep up with her fast paced lectures,) study hard for each exam, and do the extra credit discussion section.   I also took this class at the same time as Developmental and there was some nice overlap

If you are a psych major and need to take Psych 330 for your major eventually, take this class! I had already taken Psych 330 before I took this so it was really easy, but I wish it was offered before I took 330 because it would have helped ALOT. Five 10 minute in class quizzes, weekly 2 minute online "quizzes", Easy extra credit & take home final.

She's clear with material, but fast. And it's all incredibly dense. I didn't buy the textbook, and didn't need to. Everything is in lecture notes. But if you stop her, she'll make sure you understand. I didn't do so hot earlier on in the semester, but she offers SO MUCH EXTRA CREDIT.

This class is interesting, but her exams are hard. If you are looking for an easy A, don't take this class. A lot of studying for the 6 mini exams, which are tricky. Class average right now is a C- and she still won't scale at all. Also, make sure you have the book for a reference.

Good teacher and a very interesting class, but material moves very quickly and in force. Six MC "mini exams", do the readings and/or take good notes (also online). One quirk, a question on an exam about MDMA's "harm" was bias. She used a study where monkeys had 40mg/kg of MDMA in their system for 2 days, which would be 2.72g in a 150lb human.

Lori is a fantastic teacher. I'm a psych minor and I have trouble with science but she clarifies everything and makes it understandable. You have to go to class and study to do well. Don't bother buying the textbook, she only tests on her lectures.

She goes through the material really fast, so you have to attend and pay attention in lecture to do well.  An exam every other week, but if you can stay on top of the work you should be able to do well. A bit science-y but very interesting. Would recommend.

Attendance is mandatory every class because of writing assignments. Opportunity for extra credit (definitely should take advantage of, you'll probably need it). Exams are hard, but simply because of the crappy word choice she uses and there's 6 of them. If you study, you should be fine but to get the A is a challenge. No book needed. Optional final

I had her for behavioral neuroscience which is challenging if you don't have any background in life sciences. It heavily relies on biology and chemistry. Mostly psych majors take this class, so no offense, but they often struggle. She's a great professor and very clear and approachable. Her tests are simple as long as you understand the material.

Coming from a strong science background, I didnt find this all that difficult. She teaches this class at a level that is simple for anyone to understand and enjoy. She has six small exams and an optional final with two ways to gain extra credit. Easy to get a high grade. Highly recommended!

You can expect any hard science course to be a little challenging, but this Professor definitely makes it interesting and somewhat easy to understand. Attendance is mandatory, & you have to really pay attention in the lectures to do well. Also, I bought the book to clear up points of confusion. Very helpful when you don't fully understand something

Flies through too many slides in a single class session. Material is difficult, exams, are tricky, and reviews are useless. Mandatory attendence because there is a writing assignment at the end of every class and even if you go, you won't get the full 3 points for the assignment. Tough class.

Dr. Astheimer tries to get through 50-75 slides in one lecture. She talks so fast that the material makes no sense. Her tests are ridiculously hard and you have to attend every class because of the writing assignments. She doesn't use the book at all, so do not bother buying it. The TA's are useless and the reviews just make you more confused.

This class is really difficult. I enjoy the professor because she's really into it and up-beat, but the material is complicated as ever. The tests are difficult, so definitely study. She allows you to record lectures (I RECOMMEND YOU DO THIS!!). There is one extra credit paper, and a writing assignment each class.

Really interesting class! Attendance is mandatory every class because of writing assignments, and lots of extra credit! Exams are a bit hard, and there's 6 of them. If you can put in work, you'll be fine

i'm a second semeseter senior, so it's really hard to care about my classes. i started off doing just that and sitting in the back, but honestly, she's interesting and makes neuroscience easy to understand! also, if you get there a few minutes early, she'll bump good music, which gives her points in my book. all in all, she rocks. take this class

She would  go on random tangents and constantly asking the class unrelated questions; this would force her to rush through the hardest material at the end of each lecture..she improved on this towards the end of the course though. Good prof otherwise. Interesting material & tons of EC which really really boosts your grade. Take this class.
Lori was hilarious. I looked forward to going to every class and she made an extremely difficult topic understandable and even fun!
Awesome teacher! I highly recommend this class! I actually looked forward to going!

Dr. AB makes a difficult topic very understandable, even if the material has a tendency to be a little dry.  6 "mini exams" every 2 to 3 weeks and in class writing assignments every class, so attendance is mandatory (and she doesnt allow cell phones)  I was dreading this class at first but it turned out to be very interesting and enjoyable

Although she is new, she is an AMAZING professor. This is the only class I actually looked forward to going to! She honestly made me consider a neuroscience track. I would recommend her and this class 100%!!!

She is new to the teaching world but I think she did a pretty good job this semester. She has a lot of knowledge on the subject of behavioral neuroscience. She is the advisor for the Neuroscience department after all. Her exams are fair for the most part and she gives an optional final that will replace two of the 6 lowest exam scores.
Really great professor! I hate science and she made me want to consider a neuroscience track!

I didn't take bio ever and got an A. Her exams are small and easy to study for if you actually care. Don't buy the book. She has a great personality and made neuroscience interesting for me, which is something I never thought I would say. This woman knows her stuff, this might not be her concentration but who cares? She explained it well.

my favorite class at umass. i definitely recommend taking a class with her! mini exams are easy as long as you study her lecture slides, which she posts online. textbook not mandatory. TAs suck and are not helpful at all, but other than that, i would definitely recommend this class and professor!

One of the best classes I've taken. If you need to take this class because you're a Psych major don't worry. She gives 6 mini tests that are 25 multiple choice questions each. Going to class is mandatory since she gives an inclass writing assignment every class She's very good at presenting the material. Do not buy the book and study off the slides

Great teacher who cares makes time for every question asked in a large lecture hall. mini exams more manageable than big ones and are ALWAYS on lecture slides so they're easy to study for. interactive online forum for sharing vids and ideas. also her syllabus says she doesn't answer emails  just read it and you'll do well. good professional humor.

Very fun and scatterbrained. Would be a great aunt or drinking buddy, but very difficult to follow in a classroom setting. Great at clarifying when you see her one-on-one, but mini-exams are extremely difficult and circuitous. If you're interested in science, Great class. If not a science person, it's very hard. She could definitely make it easier!

Such a fun professor, really makes class interesting. The 6 mini-exams make studying much more manageable, and there are small open responses and lots of extra credit to boost your grade. It helps to have taken Bio 100 but she understands that some students don't have a science background. Highly recommend, her personality alone makes it worth it!

She goes off on tangents all the time and constantly asks the TA's to clarify what she's teaching. She seems like she doesn't have full knowledge of the subject. Hasn't responded to any of my e-mails when I ask questions about tests or grades. Really confusing teacher because she goes off subject so frequently. I personally don't reccomend it.

She is so amusing. She really knows her stuff, and cares about what shes teaching. She really wants you to understand everything and makes herself available for the students. 6 "mini exams" every 2 weeks or so, and an open response question at the end of each lecture. She made a hard subject really fun to learn.

Absolutely amazing, funny professor, so glad I took the class with her. 6 small exams, relatively easy, all from lectures.  Attend class, pay attention, and you will do well.  There are plenty of opportunities for extra credit.  She really makes this class interesting!

Probably one of the easiest classes I have taken, just applied myself a day before the exams and got 110% on both. the exams are 12 multiple choice (which are pretty straightforward) and only your best 10 count and anything over that is a bonus 10%. Would recommend even though a lot of people dont like the team oriented learning that goes on

I don't think the problem is with Paul, but with how Phys 131 is structured as a whole. The whole team based learning thing is a mess and it didn't work for me at all. The TA's along with Paul honestly weren't the best as well, and Paul expects you to know the material based off the textbook instead of him actually doing his job and lecturing.
you'll do good if you put in the effort, kids get bad grades because they don't put in effort. Paul is amazing i highly recommend him.
Not a bad professor, but is very stingy on due dates and lab grades. stick close to the rubrics and submit labs on time and you should be ok.

12 exam questions total, only counts 10 questions. Exams are worth a decent portion of the final grade.TBL = ok, definitely a learn outside of class thing. The physics lab is definitely one of the most useless labs I've ever attended(arguable that Bio 153 is worse time-wise) as it did not deepen my understanding. Have over 100%, do well on exams

There isn't much to say about Bourgeois himself because he does not teach. TBL does not work and the class was extremely reliant on TAs, which were good but a lot of confusion came from having a lot of different people trying to help. I would do anything you can to try and take this class over summer or winter since it does not use TBL or take 151.

This guy didn't do a single thing all semester. The class is team base learning which means you teach yourself while he sits on his phone and if theres ever a question the TA's answer it. He didn't even watch the final presentation himself. With that being said the material is manageable imo and there were only in class tests and no final.

Paul can be so condescending to students, and considering this is a class for non-engineering majors, a lot of students haven't taken a physics class before. He is not accessible outside of class and seems disorganized. TAs do everything. TBL is hard for a professor to get involved, but he sure didn't try.

TBL is the worst learning model UMass could have done, combined with Paul, the class is near impossible. Exams are brutal and everyone does bad. Only way students can somewhat exceed is if he curves grades at end of the semsester, which he has yet to mention...

I liked Dr. B! Not a huge fan of TBL, but he was helpful when I had questions or when he was introducing topics. Could get carried away talking about stuff, eating into TBL time. Exams are not bad at all, just make sure to study and do the practoce problems in class.
L professor
I would take this class at another school. Maybe another country. Get as far away as possible.
worst professor ive had here

It's unfortunate that I have to give him a not so great rating. He is a great person and I feel like would be a great professor in a traditional lecture. The thing is that TBL SUCKS. The homework has very little to do with anything. You learn only from the textbook and if you have a bad group, you're kind of in the deep end.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Group projects--Lots of homework

reviews.comment: As this class uses TBL, Paul often faded to the background and we mainly relied on ourselves and our TA for guidance. The few I interactions I had with him were nice and he was helpful when he came around. Best way to succeed is to go to SI and do the practice problems before class, especially if your group isn't the best.

You better start praying that your groupmates are physics geniuses because team-base learning is the pitfall of this class. You're better off going to the physics help sessions or learning yourself because on the rare chance Professor Bourgeois lectures, he tends to skip steps because physics is second nature to him and he forgets he teaching.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Group projects

reviews.comment: Truly terrible at teaching.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: He is terrible at teaching. He can be mean and condescending to students and is not flexible to the needs of the class. You will not learn one thing from him, but from the SI leaders, TAs, and other professors instead. Mr. B's combination of lazy teaching style, poor course structure, and degenerate attitude leads students towards failure.

The class structure was very confusing and set up to make student's lives harder. I appreciate that we use a free textbook resource that was written by the professor. They had to scale almost every assignment to help students pass.
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Group projects--Beware of pop quizzes

reviews.comment: This guy was one of the worst professors I've ever had. He would talk to students like he was trying to teach physics to 5 year old's, but not in the helpful way, in the condescending way. Additionally, for my final, he made no major comments during the presentation, yet my group got a 76 on it. No explanation given.

Doesn't teach, TAs do all the work, very not lenient (was violently ill so submitted lab a few hours late, gave a 0), provide little to no resources and homework and test questions are completely different. Not impressed, would give lower than 1 if possible.

Exam and quiz grades matter a lot, but you get to take team quizzes and exams afterward that can help boost your grade. Most of the class is solving problems with teammates randomly selected by the professor.

A lot of this class is heavy on group work but doesn't have required attendance. That doesn't make a lot of sense to me. Your grade could be improved or destroyed by your group. The final was a group project that my teammates did not contribute to, which seriously hurt my final grade. The class structure is strange and feels very disconnected.

Paul is a good enough guy and tries to make things interesting. However, team-based learning is the downfall of this course. It seemed like an excuse for Paul to simply not teach concepts. Chances are if you take this class it's not because you're a physics major and you have little background knowledge, so it's super inaccessible.

I don't think Paul is the problem with this class: Physics 131 itself is set up poorly. The emphasis on team-based learning is way to high. You are expected to figure things out on your own way too soon. Exam and homework questions were worded poorly and coded with the wrong answers, which lead to lots of issues. The course needs a makeover.

This is the worst class I have taken. Team based learning is an excuse to teach yourself the course. SI sessions are the only reason I understood material. Paul is nice, but he is extremely unclear and does not specify anything. All the material is made by the other teacher, and exams and homeworks have a lot of mistakes and unclear questions.

Dr. Bourgeois seems like a really wonderful and smart guy... It's just that I learned more from the 2 hour long exam review sessions than any of the actual coursework. 
Poorly executed "team based learning" and do-it-yourself teaching style. 
Expect *multiple* apologies about "weird wording" and lack of coherency in exam questions.
HE CANNOT WORD HIS QUESTIONS PROPERLY! get ready to get many points off for unclarity of homework and quiz questions and in class questions and anything for that matter
Very easy going and genuinely a fun teacher. Practice exams are exactly like actual exam and are easy. He clearly cares about his subject and is kind, understanding, and down to earth

Overall, Dr.B was an average professor. He made lectures interesting, but I didn't end up retaining much of the material. Exams were super easy though, as long as you can do the practice exam you'll easily get an A! Homework was way harder than the exams, but other than that 152 was a relatively easy class, as long as you pay attention

Dr. Bourgeois is awesome! He makes lectures interesting and tries to get students engaged. There's a lot of chances to work with other students in lecture. Exams are super easy; do the practice exam and you'll get an A. There are a lot of opportunities for extra credit. Definitely take Physics 2 with Dr. B!

Paul is by far the best physics professor I've ever had. His lectures are entertaining and involving, he will stop the class completely if you do not understand the topic. Very easy class, very easy homework, very easy exams. Definitely recommend taking his class

I don't know why everyone hates on Paul. He is a beast. An excellent, lively teacher who keeps the class engaged. They redid the tests for Spring 2023 so they have been extremely easy. Hopefully, it stays that way. 0 complaints about Paul, best physics teacher I have had and most people in my CURRENT class/semester agree

If you're in PHYS152 - dont worry, he's actually a pretty good lecturer and the grading is reasonable. Tests are fair and similar to the practice exams. His overall ratings are low because PHYS131 is a self-taught class (for some reason) and is very challenging - which isn't his fault, rather the Physics department's fault for setting that up.

He's honestly way better than the other reviews make him seem & a great prof. Almost didn't sign up for 152 in his section, but I'm so glad I did. Lectures are entertaining & he's a very funny/captivating professor who really cares about answering questions. I think this semester the physics department revamped their teaching style and it's great.
He is clearly a smart guy who knows a lot about physics, but he doesn't really explain anything and his handwriting is pretty bad. Just rubs off as super messy and rushed through lectures

Paul is certainly not a bad professor; he has an interesting ability to make lectures that would normally be boring fun. The main criticism is that his lectures weren't a big help on the exam, and almost felt unrelated to the TBL material. The lecture portion of this class feels insignificant; you don't need to attend if you use the practice exams.
reviews.rating_tags: Clear grading criteria--Lecture heavy--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: "Team-based learning" is an excuse for you to teach yourselves. Maybe 2 lectures given throughout the semester- the rest were old videos from ANOTHER professor. My TA, who was a sophomore helping a bunch of juniors/seniors, was a better professor than Paul. He's a nice guy but this class is a disaster.
The team based learning structure was really challenging for me since I am taking physics for the first time and he never posted any answer sheets even before the exams.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Test heavy

reviews.comment: it is so bad. i want to give you a zero. but thats not possible. so i give you a one. this class was horrendous gave me too many mental breakdowns, i have no words to explain how awful the exams were. the downfall of physics 131 at umass is the team based learning style. it needs to be abolished expeditiously.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Group projects

reviews.comment: he is, definitely a professor

paul is a nice guy. i really like him actually. but there is a fundamental issue with the physics 131 classes at umass. the team based learning format does not work. they do not teach you any of the basics and a lot of students fail. exam average was consistently a D. no scale. also unorganized when it comes to labs. be prepared to teach yourself.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Get ready to read--Group projects

reviews.comment: Dont take his class. Hate this guy
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Get ready to read--Inspirational

reviews.comment: PLEASE avoid his class if possible. He's extremely strict and not a good teacher. Taking his class is equivalent of having no teacher at all. If there is another option, please take it.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Beware of pop quizzes--Tough grader

reviews.comment: literally the worst class I have taken in my life and has 0 structure. be prepared to get a lab 3 days before it's due and have 0 class time to work on it. everything is group work and you never learn anything. you don't get lectures and your only resource for information is the textbook. exam questions are so ambiguous. would rate 0 if i could

He makes physics hard for no reason! A great guy but his exam questions are WAY too ambiguous. The homework is not like the exam at all. Youre going to see things on the exams that you've never seen before. Theres also a quiz every class. I wish he would treat this class like a normal physics class instead of trying to put a twist on the subject.
He cares students.

Paul manages the lab section for my class. While I've heard from other students about how awful he is with lab I have never experienced it myself. He ignores emails, will post an entire lab three days before it is due and generally is an awful professor.

He's absolutely horrible. He's a nice guy, but the class is only working through problems with other group members. You're never given clear answers, or strategies to solve the problems. All the problems are way too open to interpretation, and the class itself is really hard. It's heavily scaled though, because everyone does so horrible.

The way the class is set up is that you pretty much have to go to class but you won't learn anything because he doesn't teach The practice exams are useless for than actual exam because they are always way easier. I'm beyond upset with this class and hope he gets fired and yes I got an A in the class it was just ridiculous I am also a physics majo

Don't believe him if he tells you 'it's not true that you have to learn everything by yourself'. IT IS! He hardly lecture anything but to ask your group to do question on the board. Quiz on the beginning of units with actual calculation problems which are completely self-taught . Ok if you have good teammate. Finally TeamBaseLearning is the WORST.

this was a team based learning class. luckily my team was good, but if you end up in a bad team then it will be a terrible class. be prepared to figure things out on your own - people are there to help but mostly it felt like i was teaching myself
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--GROUP PROJECTS

reviews.comment: Physics is a hard enough subject as is, but is made even harder by the way this class is set up. Team learning is awful when nobody has any idea whats going on since he rarely teaches how to do anything. Be prepared to see things on the exam that youve never seen before in class. However, lots of extra points, so its still possible to get an A

This class was the worst I've taken at UMass. The TBL format is not conducive to learning and Paul doesn't teach anything ever. The only way you will learn is if you watch the YouTube videos he posts and even then you won't be prepared for the exams. The review sessions help sometimes but he structures the exams to be on material you've never seen.

This class seemed like it was going to be helpful and student centered, however the TBL format is an incredibly useless teaching tactic under this Professor. He expects you to understand the subject matter on your own and tests your knowledge before he teaches you anything. It seems like there are good resources at your disposal, but there aren't.

He's a really nice/funny guy and passionate about physics but a HORRIBLE teacher. He never actually teaches you how to do problems because its TBL he just makes you try to figure out how to do things as a group which is just impossible. You have a quiz on the FIRST DAY of the new unit on material he has never even talked about. Go to exam reviews!!

As an upperclassman, I have a suspicion a lot of the high reviews are due to recency bias. Kathleen is often passive aggressive and not very understanding of personal circumstances, yet demands you be completely understanding of hers. Trust me - you will not like this professor.

I think her classes are very chill and enjoyable. The content of this course is helpful beyond college life, and she's a nice professor, too. I'd recommend reading the material (she doesn't assign much) and trying to participate in class discussions. Fair grading with clear criteria, you will do well as long as you care.

Very great teacher. She knows her stuff and it is a very fascinating class. There are a lot of reading assignments each class, but it is easily spark notable. During her classes, she talks the majority of the time, strictly no technology, tough grader with papers, but easy class if you maintain good attendance and ask questions.

Professor Brown-Perez was one of the most effortlessly charismatic and helpful professors I've had at UMass. She is incredibly passionate about what she teaches, and the more that you're interested in the material, the exponentially more you'll get out of her instruction and feedback. Also super funny!
She honestly grew on me. I would be lying if I said I didn't walk away from the class having learned a lot from her.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Gives good feedback

reviews.comment: I would absolutely recommend Kathleen Brown-Perez's Ideas that Change the World class to any UMass Honors student. Both she and her class were very interesting. I learned a lot and thoroughly enjoyed the assigned readings and discussions.
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Amazing lectures --Graded by few things

reviews.comment: She was very kind and funny. She made so many topics very interesting and added humor to help us learn. Participation was super important and was most of our grade. Otherwise there were 3 reflection essays throughout the semester that were very easy. There were very few assignments but I still felt as though I learned a lot.

If you can, take her class for Ideas that Change the World! It's almost completely discussion-based, so attendance and participation are critical. There are 3 graded reflection essays that are super manageable. Getting an A is easy if you just attend class.
Dont be fooled by her high rating, you will not like this professor

We watched videos and talked about them. There is a lit review we write but she has assignments that lead up to it. She's very understanding if you tell her your situation or what you need help with. There are discussion times, but she does the talking mostly. She's nice. No electronics, no noise, no vibration (except when watching videos)
Wonderful teacher and a diverse array of topics. The best honors seminar available.

Prof Brown-Perez is so funny that I forgot that I was in an 8:30am class with her. When she teaches, she uses examples mixed in with humor, which really breaks down topics that would otherwise be complicated and instead makes them easy to understand. You can tell she wants everyone to learn and succeed, and even makes quizzes open book!
fun interesting class
Interesting class with cool material, her "discussions" are just her talking for the entire class period. She wants you to succeed so just try.
This class was awesome, mandatory freshman year but I actually liked it. Kinda a lot of reading but they are easy, one research paper at the end and not many other assignments. Mostly discussion
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Gives good feedback

reviews.comment: very easy class. barely any assignments. nice woman.

Would def recommend this class. Very fair in grading and I learned a lot abt citing and overall paper formatting stuff. This class can be frustrating as it will make you think abt social issues. Don't take any other 201H prof.
reviews.rating_tags: Clear grading criteria--Gives good feedback--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: Very manageable 201H class. Everything is discussion based besides one research paper due at the end of the semester. Kathleen is a very fair grader and gives good feedback. Boring at times, but would overall recommend this class
By far one of the best 201H teachers you will ever have. Gives good feedback and an extremely forgiving grader as long as you put in the effort. Do not take 201H with another professor.

Kathleen is a very sweet woman, although her classes are always early in the morning. If you simply put all the effort and participate consistently, you'll do well. Getting an A in her class is a walk in the park, but it can be frustrating if you're a night owl.

Solid class overall- it was very easy and relatively light on work, and the topics covered were thought-provoking and interesting. However, the topics eventually became a little repetitive, but other than that, good class.
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Clear grading criteria--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Kathleen is your best bet if you're a freshman CHC taking the 201H class. You won't be bored in her class (because her personality). Also, her lectures are genuinely inspiring. I can confidently say that I gained a lot from her class. Best of all, she gives the option of a final exam instead of a research paper (tip: opt for the exam!)

Kathleen is amazing. She provides great insight in discussions and actually inspires us. I got so much out of this class and it wasnt too difficult at all. There are only 12 open note quizzes based on readings that she gives you. She is so understanding and genuinely cares about her students. Take her!!

made us think critically and ask questions about the everyday systems we function within, didn't assert her opinion as fact and encouraged us to form our own opinions. she's a great teacher and will expand your mind.

intimidating at first but really nice! she recently stopped taking attendance bc this is a weird year for everyone but participation still matters. very chill class tho, usually have to do some readings the night before, go to class and discuss or watch a video. grade mostly based on moodle quizzes from reading (easy), participation, final paper
reviews.rating_tags: Respected--Participation matters--Skip class? You won't pass.

reviews.comment: She makes waking up at 8:30 am to learn Criminal Law worth it. Kathleen is an amazing professor, truly inspirational, extremely smart, and caring too. You can tell she truly cares about the course content and her students. I would definitely take the class again and my major isn't even related to criminal law.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Get ready to read--Inspirational

reviews.comment: Prof is nice and understanding. Classes are interesting and easy. She gives a lot of chances to get extra credit. Homeworks are a total of 5 1-2 page essays on given topics. One of the few classes which didn't stress me out. You don't have to work too hard to get an A.
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Graded by few things--EXTRA CREDIT

reviews.comment: Taken Zoom Fall 2020. Kathleen is kind & funny. I appreciated her organization. Classes scheduled for MWF, but Fridays asynchronous 1-2pg reflection on a reading/video. Basically for completion. Largest assignment was an annotated bib. There was supposed to be a final essay but it was cancelled bc of all the writing w reflections. Def recommend!

Classes/lectures were mainly discussions on social issues and we watched a lot of videos. Homework consists of 1 page reflection papers on videos or topics covered in class. Super easy course work. Definitely would recommend her for a first year seminar, super interesting!

Never had a Kathleen do me wrong. I had her for a mandatory seminar class and even though I slept through every zoom meeting for the second half of the semester, she was really nice and clearly cares about what she's talking about. Very detail oriented but honestly the class was easy. Show up, do the writing assignments, and maybe say 1-2 things.

Prof is extremely nice, but completely all over the place. Though this class was "Ideas that Change the World" you will spend 90% of your time discussing how climate change is real and plastics are bad. Nothing was enlightening, nothing mind changing--though it should said the professor cares about her students and facilitates conversation well.
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Graded by few things--Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: BEST professor on campus. She gave minimal homewok, no tests/quizzes during semester, Cares about your success, and basically gives everyone A's

My favorite professor so far at UMass. Genuinely cares for students and tries to make it as easy as possible to get an A while still learning. Participate in class and read the minimal readings she assigns and you got yourself a GPA booster.

LOVED this class! No essays and instead of essays we had one test that I didn't find to be too difficult. She graded us using notes that we took on nightly online readings, no textbooks needed. She truly cares about her students and classes. I learned a lot about contemporary issues in the world. Attendance is mandatory and part of the grade.

Kathleen's expectations are explicit- her syllabus is detailed & well organized. No books need to be bought. All readings are online. Readings are due most days, but you simply need to take notes & be prepared for discussions. She tweaks her course from semester to semester, so not everything on here might be correct. Overall, I learned a lot!
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Clear grading criteria--Caring

reviews.comment: Brown-Perez is a great professor who made Ideas 201H interesting and fun. She always adds funny stories or points into our discussions and the readings she assigns are pretty easy to understand as well.
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--ACCESSIBLE OUTSIDE CLASS--GRADED BY FEW THINGS

reviews.comment: Great professor! Made the class so easy and somewhat fun!

Love, LOVE Kathleen, she's super nice. I took honors crim law with her and learned so much. She's more than willing to help you if you ask for it, or even talk to you about anything. Knows her stuff and is extremely intelligent. One of the best professors I have ever had. If you have the chance, you have to take a class with her!
reviews.rating_tags: ACCESSIBLE OUTSIDE CLASS--Clear grading criteria--EXTRA CREDIT

reviews.comment: Kathleen is the best Ideas professor out there. She does not require you to buy any textbooks, and you only write one thesis-driven paper, which is helpful in teaching you to use databases and scholarly articles only for research and citing. She really cares about her students and makes sure you do not stress too much; even the discussions are nice

Kathleen is a great professor for Criminal Law. I took this class as an elective and was a little nervous about its difficulty going into it but as long as you care and are willing to put a little effort in, no one should have a problem getting a good grade. This class is at 8:30 and I have no problem getting up for it because its so interesting!

Kathleen is great and does not require you to purchase ANY textbooks unlike other professors in this course. Replies quickly to emails and is always prepared for class. Has plenty of movie days in class but she gets mad if you go on your phone. Class is discussion based so participation is key.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Clear grading criteria--EXTRA CREDIT

reviews.comment: Great professor with a love for teaching and the course material. She was an excellent instructor to have for my first semester of college. Her course was mostly rooted in group discussion. One of the few instructors for 201H that does not require you to buy any materials. I wish I could have her again.

She is one of the most inspiring professors that I met. She doesn't give too many readings. As long as you participate in the discussions it'll be one of the best classes.   She's very helpful in writing papers, she's funny, and the material is interesting.

Kathleen is literally one of the best professors I've ever had. To pass, all you really need to do is show up and participate in the discussions. She even bought our class donuts. I highly recommend her and respect her as a professor.

Professor Brown-Perez is the best! Homework is readings and taking notes, which is super easy. Class is discussion-based, led by the students. She respects all of our viewpoints and brings up a lot of interesting questions and points about society. She doesn't make you buy any books for this class either. I would definitely take this class again!

Best professor ever. The classes included movies, ted talks, and class discussions; there were no exams, only four in-class essays. There was a lot of reading, but not around midterms or finals, and the only HW was to take notes.

Kathleen is an amazing professor and I'm so glad I took her class. She encouraged class discussion of the materials which brought interesting viewpoints to our society. The final project is to write a research paper which was challenging, but so rewarding because she really helped you write it every step of the way.

A nice and caring person but not a good professor. His slides are just copy paste from the textbook, he takes all class to give you the one equation that you needed all along and it's very confusing. Instead he takes forever with theory and context. He'll do daily quizzes call that his “attendance”. Be ready for a lot of work outside class
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Caring--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Really like his teaching style, I normally never go to lectures because the professors are so hard to follow, but I can actually follow what is happening in class. Very nice guy who is accessible outside of class. Lectures are pretty engaging

Lectures are really hard to follow. He heavily relies on the textbook and can't explain the content on his own, as he "haven't taught the class in 10 years". His completion and assignments homework are all from the textbook and are 5x harder than what you learn in class. Would not recommend taking Hari, basically taught myself the whole course.
great experience
Good Professor.
Highly highly recommend Professor Hari. He was really the first professo

One of the best classes I have taken so far at UMass. Hari is a wonderful professor who cares about his students. Group projects are pretty tricky and require a lot of work but they are super interesting. All real world applications. Would definitely recommend!!
Learned a lot in his classes. Very interesting.

One Of Umass engineering's best professors. One of the first professors i have had who has inspired me to apply my learning to real life problems and other applications.  Many time consuming projects throughout semester, however grades are based upon effort and doing your best to find a creative solution to a problem, often using code.
Class is pretty slow and boring (I guess that's the subject matter though). He uses PRS, so you have to go to class, although I bet you could pass the class by learning through the textbook.

I love KB, genuinely one of the best teachers I've ever had. Super passionate about what she teaches and takes the time to learn the names of students & hear their feedback or contributions to discussions. Exams are memorization heavy, make flashcards for the sections of lecture slides written in red/highlighted. Labs are super fun and engaging

Dr Beltaire is such a kind, caring professor with a deep passion for what she teaches. Her lectures are entertaining and she's always enthusiastic to answer questions. I can't say enough positive things about her.

Dr. Beltaire is very kind and caring about her students. The only thing I dislike about this class is that she goes through slides quickly, and doesn't record lectures-- so if you miss class it kinda sucks. Lowkey old school.

Probably the best professor you could have at UMass. She really loves the topics she teaches about, and it shows during lectures. I was never bored during lectures, and the labs are engaging and fun most of the time. The only downside is that she mainly teaches about livestock, which may not be a downside to others!
I love this woman so much - I never once felt bored in her lectures, she makes everything so interesting. She LOVES veterinary medicine and it shows, I would recommend her every day.

Dr. Beltaire is hands down on the of the best professors I've ever had. Her lectures were engaging and very interesting. She's very passionate and knowledgeable and easy to talk to. Go to class and the labs! It does make a difference in your grade and understanding the material. Don't bother with the textbook, we never used it even once.

She is AMAZING! Her teaching style is very easy to follow and it is clear that she is passionate about what she teaches. I did fine without reading the textbook, the textbook is good for reinforcement. The class is easy to study for because it is a lot of terminology, so Quizlet will be your best friend.
Great lecturer, very interesting and cares about her students learning. She is funny and knows what she is talking about. Exams were off the lectures with no homeworks or quizzes

Great ansci professor, lectures are very easy to understand and she makes everything relatively clear. Exams were not that hard, everything came from the lectures. No quizzes or homework which is really nice. Attendance helps your grade

Dr. Beltaire is very passionate about what she teaches, having lectures filled with personal experiences tied to the slides. All of the information is as straight forward as possible-- you're tested on just what comes off of the slides. After finishing this course, I am very inspired to continue learning on my Animal Science/Pre-vet major track.

She is an amazing person. She is very caring and inspiring. You can tell she really loves what she does and wants her students to succeed. If you have any questions, she is extremely easy to talk to. Her tests were not hard, but there was a good amount of memorization. If you stay on top of things, you will do really well in her class.

LOVE Dr. Beltaire, such a kind person who makes note heavy lectures fun and engaging. Lots of notes, but no homework and exams are very easy if you study a few days in advance. Says you should use a textbook but honestly I never needed it. Loved this class!

I love KB! She's so nice and she weaves personal experience from being a vet into lectures. The exams are very easy! Just make flashcards based on the slideshows and you'll ace them. Yes, memorization is required, but what else did you expect from a 101 class? Don't buy the textbook, I didn't use it at all!!!!!
This class is a lot of memorizing!

Approachable, very smart, in-depth fast lectures. Read the slides before and after class. Just the slides are on the exam, not the (unnecessary) textbook or her extra stories (although those are interesting). A bit memorization-heavy. Exams are tough but match what she teaches. Labs are fun but you only 3x per semester.

Amazing professor! She really cares about student success and enjoys teaching. Lots of lecture material, but that's to be expected. You have a lot of time to prepare for exams and they are all fair. She takes the time to get to know everyone. Labs with her were also fun!
She is a great professor and great person. I had her for 101 and 103 and she will make an effort to remember you're name and details about you. Don't be afraid to talk to her!

I had the opportunity to be a TA for KB as well as have her as an academic advisor and she is easily one of the sweetest and most caring human beings you will ever meet. She takes time the time to get to know you on a personal level and it really shows. Take every class you can with this woman.
Basically the best ansci professor at umass. Get close to her so she will write you a fire recommendation.

KB is literally the best teacher I have ever had. She has so much knowledge that she truly wants to share. Her lectures are dense but she explains things super well, giving real life examples from her experience as a Vet. Attendance is mandatory and phones can't be out but you really want to pay attention in her class. Literally 10/10.

KB is such an amazing lecturer. She is incredibly thorough with what you need to know, and adds her own life experiences as a vet to her lectures. I have gotten so many 'fun' facts from her to torture friends and family with. There are also lots of opportunities to boost your grade if you aren't great on tests. I love Dr. Beltaire.

Beltaire's teaching style is great. There is a textbook you can buy, but there is no need to because her exams come straight from what is on her lectures. She explains material very, very well, and is always open to answering questions. She does not give homework or quizzes usually.

Pros: Amazing professor and clearly cares about her students. Cons: Attendance is taken at every lecture, the class is extremely lecture heavy and the slides are loaded with information so it's important to study in advance or you will be sorry come exam time, two times during the semester you have to get up at 6am for barn chores.

Dr. Beltaire was the best teacher I had at Umass. She provided all of the resources to succeed and get an A. The labs are a great grade booster because it's easy to get 100s. The exams I found a little challenging, though, since there were many slides to memorize. Study for the lab practical very far in advance; you'll thank yourself later.

This class is disorganized & way too much work for 2 credits. U need to complete 10 hours outside of class at the farm, which doesn't sound bad until you remember that it's a 30 min drive there and hours are only offered at a few inconvenient times each week. I
reviews.rating_tags: Clear grading criteria--Lots of homework--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Dr. Beltaire was by far one of the best professors I had. Her lectures were very well formatted, but they were pretty loaded with material. During each lecture, attendance was taken every time. Dr. Beltaire's labs were also really enjoyable. Her grading is fair, and she is very kind. Overall, she is a very organized and likeable professor.
I genuinely have nothing bad to say about KB, I wish she taught all the ansci courses. Labs offer amazing hands on experience and her lectures are awesome she's a great person, love her!

KB is the best professor on this campus hands down. I wish she could teach every course I have to take. Her slide decks and exams are well-written and correlate well with each other. Exams are fine as long as you know the material from the lecture. The lab practical final was a stressful event but other than that the course is amazing.

KB is very charismatic and kind! As long as you go over the slides, exams will be fine. Things written in a different color on the slides will most likely be on the exam! Quizlet helps a TON (a lot of small percentages to remember.) For the lab practical USE THE STUDY GUIDE, it was exactly the same. Textbook not required.

KB was amazing. She was enthusiastic about what she teaches which just motivated me to do well. There was a lot of memorization in this class, she is definitely a numbers and percentages person. If you study for exams, you will be fine. The text book is not required, everything is on the lecture slides.

Prof. Beltaire is so knowledgeable and is good at simplifying difficult topics. You have to study for the exams but the content isn't difficult. Its a class that is very easy to get an A in and is very entertaining. The lecture material is easy to study from and you know what to expect on the exams.

I genuinely have no bad things to say about Dr. Beltaire, she is very passionate and cares about what she is teaching. Textbook is optional, I bought mine so don't make that same mistake :) Material for lab practical is available on moodle and is that exact material. Final exam is not cumulative but definitely study those powerpoint slides.
reviews.rating_tags: Amazing lectures --Clear grading criteria--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Dr. Beltaire is such a great lecturer. She does go quite fast though, I recommend taking notes on the slideshow before class if possible. She will emphasize things you need to know for the exam in class, and she LOVES questions about reproduction. All in all she is so great and really cares about her students and wants them to succeed.

KB is one of the best professors here. The textbook is useless, never used it as all the information needed is presented on the slides. The exams are straightforward, and she typically throws in an extra credit question. You can tell she cares about her students and is passionate about what she is teaching.
LOVE KB! She is so passionate and the most amazing person ever please notice me KB i will be so happy shes like a celebrity like pls :DDDDDD
Very kind and easy

Hands down one of the best professors and instructors I have ever had. I also have the benefit of having her as an academic advisor and have her for my Cattle Management class. She is very down to earth and approachable and genuinely seems to care about her students and the topics that she teaches. Wish I could take a class with her every semester.
I love her SO much!

I've only taken Animal Science 101 so far but Dr. Beltaire's lectures have been fantastic & very engaging.  She explains material very thoroughly and clearly but keeps it interesting by including personal stories related to content & answering any questions that students may have.  It's clear she really cares about what she's teaching.

Best professor I've had by far! She's always passionate about the material that she is teaching. There's a lot of material covered, but with quizlets and studying it's very easy to understand. She uses her own personal experiences as cases to cover during class to help us engage with the content. Lots of hands on experience in labs/barn chores.

KB is the best professor I've had at UMass. She's so knowledgeable and experienced, yet she's so easy going and absolutely lovable. You'll make wonderful memories with her. Her exams are straightforward and her lectures are fantastic. She wants you to succeed. I've had her for two semesters and she's the best professor ever.

Doctor Beltaire is the best professor ive had so far at Umass. She cares so much about her students and always answered my emails when I had any issues. She is the most understanding professor ive ever encountered. She is extremely passionate when she speaks about animals and it is made very clear through her lectures. She is awesome.

Ever since I joined this class with this professor, I instantly knew I would succeed in it. She encourages engagement in her class and really cares about her students! 101 is a difficult class because there's a lot of numbers and terminology to remember but I think she does a really good job with teaching it! If you listen, you will succeed!

Great professor to teach this class! Really gets down to the nitty gritty of each topic. 103 is a little easier because its all management based and she uses her own experiences to teach the class as well! Highly recommend this class if you're going into the animal science major!

I am scared of Dr. Beltaire but also in the I respect her a lot kind of way. As long as you study and attend classes/labs/barn chores/etc. you will get a good grade. Hardly any homework. You don't need the textbook but it can help since her lectures do go fast. She is very passionate about the subject. Love the hands-on experience.
reviews.rating_tags: Respected--Skip class? You won't pass.--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: As long as you study and show up to lab, this class is an easy A. The exams are strictly memorization, you never have to apply any concepts or anything. She does flyyyy through lectures but she always posts the notes. DO NOT GET THE TEXTBOOK. I wasted my money and never used it, all the info needed is in her lecture notes.

Prof. Beltaire is so kind and flexible. Her lectures go extremely fast and she tests on what she goes over in class. She does assign a textbook but mainly as a supplemental so it is not required. Definitely study for the lab practical ahead of time! It is a lot of content and doesn't use a normal test structure.

KB is fantastic. Inspiring, very well respected, funny (without knowing it), and down-to-earth. Does not assign busywork. All exams are very fair as long as you study her material. She goes above and beyond to help students when they seek her out. I can't recommend her enough!
reviews.rating_tags: Respected--Skip class? You won't pass.--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: Katie is amazing. She is extremely understanding and caring. I loved her class and learned a lot even in the online circumstances. She really does go the extra mile fore her students.
reviews.rating_tags: Respected--Skip class? You won't pass.--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: KB is the best! Most of the class is memorization and very straightforward. She is my favorite professor.

One of the best professors I've ever had. She sparks students' interest and explains concepts very clearly and at a basic level. Very willing to chat outside of class, clear assignments, tests, and grading.

This class was amazing. No homework, tests were pretty easy, and the labs were super fun for the most part. The only reason I didn't get an A was because I didn't prepare enough for the lab practical. But she is a great prof, being a vet herself she is so knowledgeable and understanding, even funny. Show up to class and you'll be fine.
Not to be dramatic or anything but I'd die for KB

Not only an awesome professor but a great person as well. Very knowledgeable, kind and takes every opportunity to teach her students. She cares about her students' success' in and out of the classroom. Attendance is taken, but nearly all notes are posted online. Exams and lab practicals are extremely fair. A great course!

Dr. Beltaire has to be one of my favorite instructors of all time. She is so clearly passionate about what she teaches and so well-versed in every topic. She puts in a lot of work for her slideshows and lectures, and always answers any questions. Lectures do move quickly because of how much material there is, but she's very clear and concise.

KB is wonderful! I've taken 101, 103, and two semesters of Belties with her. Her lectures are interesting, and as long as you actually want to be there you won't have a problem. She is clearly so passionate, and it really translates into her teaching. Her tests for 101 and 103 are easy as long as you went to class and studied.
I would take every single class with KB if that were an option.

KB is an amazing professor who obviously cares about both the subject matter and her students. Shes hilarious and makes the class really enjoyable. You will learn a lot from her, just take good notes (she loves percentages as exam questions!) and stay on top of things to get an A.

KB is one of those professors where you can tell she's extremely passionate and knowledgable about the subject. She not only cares about the material she's teaching but cares about her students too; always taking the time to answer questions the best she can and writing up review sheets for exams. Make sure you attend class and take good notes.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Hilarious--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: Love KB!!
She makes the lectures really enjoyable and durable during an hour span of class.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Clear grading criteria--Caring

reviews.comment: Dr. Beltaire is by far one of my favorite professors at UMass. She's super kind, smart, and passionate about what she does and it definitely shows in every class. Her tests aren't too bad, definitely study though, and she is always around if you need help or just have a question for her. 10/10 would recommend, everyone I've talked to loves her.

KB's a really good professor. She goes really fast in lectures, so be ready to write, but her tests are pretty easy if you know your vocab. You don't need the textbook. Gives a lot of information about the subject in general, but you won't need all of it for the exams (Don't worry too much about the specifics of history, just the trends).

Katie is an amazing teacher! She cares so much about each of her students and even learns their names! You have to go to each and every single class in order to get everything you need for the exams but the exams are straight forward and exactly hat you would expect. Labs are also fun and easy. There is no homework.
The nicest teacher I think I have ever had. She truly cares about the veterinary field, and my passion to become a vet has truly grown since having a class with her.

Dr. Beltaire is not only an amazing professor, but she really cares about her students. Her background in veterinary medicine allows us to go much deeper into what we are learning. If you put the time in and study the lectures, you will do well on the exams. I personally never used the book, so wouldn't suggest buying it. Great class to take!
This woman is amazing, the classes have a lot of lectures and information to memorize but it is still enjoyable for any AnSci major.
Best lectures! Very dense and fast paced but always interesting and comprehe

She knows everything about veterinary medicine and animal science. She is the veterinarian for UMass farms. Her lectures are easy to follow, but heavy on material. Always answers emails. Very respected. She hates when students are late to class! She expects students to be responsible adults. Attend barn chores and don't miss any labs!

Lectures are easy to follow, all the material you need are on the slides. If you know the slides, you'll ace the tests. Attend barn chores and anything in the barn for credit. Labs are easy 20 points, no homework, participation matters but not counted. Learned a lot from this class, always would recommend.

One of my favorite professors on campus! KB's always there to help and will go to great lengths to make sure her students succeed. Very clear lectures, great examples from her own experience, fair exams as long as you put in the effort, and she's pretty funny too! You'll do great as long as you show up to lectures and participate actively in labs!!

Great teacher. Charismatic, occasionally funny. Keeps you engaged in class and is probably the most responsible teacher I have ever met. Always uploads grades on time, and gives you everything you need to do well in her class.
Dr. Beltaire is the greatest professor you will EVER HAVE (point blank)!!! That is all that needs to be said :)

Dr. Beltaire is super sweet and very straightforward. Not very concerned about dressing  up her lectures or herself! She's very laid back and her lectures are enjoyable. I love going to her class and I love learning from her. She's definitely one of my favorite professors in the VASCI program.

Absolutely loved this class so much, Dr. Beltaire is one of my best professors yet. Tests were not that hard, do expect a practical at the end of the semester but it really isn't bad if you study. She knows all of her students and wants you to succeed.

Loved taking ANSCI 101 during my first semester. The lectures were very interesting but had a lot of info in them. Her exams aren't too hard but you will have to study in order to pass them. If I had to redo my first semester again, I would definitely sign up for a class with her.

Love Dr. Beltaire! Her lectures are great and she really sparks your interest on different animals. The two mornings of barn chores sound terrible, but they aren't bad at all. Exams aren't too hard and she doesn't do quizzes. The labs are super easy too. You really get all of your info from her lecture slides and what she says in class.
Has clear-cut powerpoints that you should take notes on. Loved her so much. My favorite professor so far.

Katie Beltaire is an excellent professor. Her lectures are as clear as possible and she posts the lectures on Moodle before class. He exams are very straightforward and usually gives review sheets for them. She is very passionate about what she teaches and is actually perfect and an inspiration. Favorite professor in college so far.
Animal science 101 was by far my favorite class of the semester! Dr. Katie Beltaire is an amazing professor. Can't wait for 103 this spring !!!!

Dr. Beltaire is a wonderful teacher! It amazes me how she knows the entire class by name after a week or two of classes and she will remember you years later. Her power points covered everything on her exams and she gave study guides. If you are interested in the material, show up, and put in some effort, you will get an A.

Lectures are very, very clear. She will help you if you ask, however, sometimes I felt like when I asked questions she got somewhat annoyed with me. Other than  that, she is a wonderful professor and person. She is very passionate about her work and seems to genuinely enjoy teaching it as well.

Dr. Beltaire is such a nice and understanding person and is really dedicated to helping her students learn. She's super approachable but also kind of intimidating because she is so perfect. Her perspective as a veterinarian when teaching the class is also really unique and makes you apply what you learn to real life cases.

Dr. Beltaire is an awesome professor and person. She takes time after class to answer any questions you have if you go up to her. Her powerpoints are all you need for the exams. She gives you review sheet that tells you everything to study. I definitely recommend. I loved it and learned a lot. My favorite class by far.

Dr.Beltaire is such a sweetheart. I couldn't imagine a better person for her job. She is always prepared and really enjoys teaching. She is very fair as far as testing, grading and attendance and clearly wants the best for her students. Not only a great professor, but a role model too!

Dr. Beltaire is an amazing professor and veterinarian. She loves what she's doing and it shows! Her power points are everything you need to know for the exams. Even if you have a disability she will do anything in her power to help you . Couldn't of asked for a better professor for my first semester.

I absolutely adore Dr. Beltaire. She has so much experience in the field and so much passion for what she is doing that it makes the class that much better, and makes me that much more eager to attend. Can't wait to take 104 with her!

Dr. Beltaire is an awesome professor and veterinarian.  She is very enthusiastic and very "into" what she is teaching. She encourages hands-on learning, which is exactly what an ansci/prevet major needs! Do not hesitate to ask questions in class, there are no stupid questions in her class.

Everyone should take one of Cynthia's classes!!!! She is a great lecturer and is very knowledgeable about everything she teaches. She makes every class feel comfortable and is so friendly to each student. Also the projects are not super challenging, but feel very useful and rewarding. Love her, love her classes.

Influencer Marketing - Do not take this class. She is SO unclear about every assignment and whined and audibly sighed when people asked her for a rubric or guidelines of any kind for projects. All of the due dates on Canvas/syllabus were wrong. She very clearly picks her favorites and shows it.

I took Professor Barstow's Advertising and Promotional course this spring and I loved it! She is a creative spirit and has a true and clear passion for what she does, which is refreshing in an undergrad professor. A lot of the class is based in creativity, but she gives deep and specific feedback to help improve. I loved this class!

Advertising & Promotion became one of my favorite classes thanks to Professor Barstow. She's incredibly knowledgeable, on top of marketing trends, encourages AI use, and truly cares about her students. No textbooks either, just real & authentic content! No textbooks & a lot of real world examples. I couldn't recommend her classes enough!

MRKT422 - Advertising and Promo - Do not take this professor. She is extremely unclear about what she wants and added another slideshow and paper the day the project was due. We exactly followed the rubric and she said we were missing so much. She is so unclear and picks favorites I'm extremely disappointed with this class.

Gave assignments with no submission on the class platform, over break, and graded harshly with zero feedback. After saying that she's an easy grader and just wants to see effort. Seriously? I had an easier time in Corporate Finance.
Doesn't explain rubrics or what she wants to see. I wouldn't be surprised if she graded on if she liked you or not.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Group projects--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Although tough, you will learn a lot outside of the classroom if not as much and more as you learned inside the classroom. I did not like her course in the beginning because of its trajectory, but by the end I probably raised my hand the most. She was very understandable and took every interjection with humility. Ask Questions! She loves it!
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Gives good feedback

reviews.comment: Cynthia is not the best teacher, but makes class enjoyable. Grading is based on 2 quizzes, a 3-4 person semester-long group project, and an AI hubspot activity. This class is easy and fun if you make a strong connection with Cynthia. She is not a bad person, just disorganized and busy. You need to go searching for answers and information at time.
reviews.rating_tags: Group projects--Gives good feedback--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: This is one of the worst professors I have had in the four years I have been at UMass. I took her Sustainability Marketing class and there were no rubrics for our project, no clear direction, and I had to constantly ask her clarifying questions on what we were suppose to do. I do NOT recommend taking this class.
I say Cynthia is a good person, but I wouldn't say she's a good professor. The entire class is based on group projects.

This was the worst instructor i"ve encountered at UMASS. Lectures are highly disorganized. What makes it worse is having to listen to audio clips in her powerpoint lectures with her grating condescending voice. Truly hard to pick out what information truly matters. Many hours spent figuring out what she wants. Group project lacks a Rubric.
reviews.rating_tags: Graded by few things--Group projects--Tough grader

reviews.comment: Most of your grade is dependent on a semester-long group project with no rubric that tells you what she wants.
reviews.rating_tags: Graded by few things--Group projects--Tough grader

reviews.comment: RUN. This is the least helpful professor I've ever experienced. Almost your entire grade is dependent on a group project where there is no rubric or clear direction. If you ask questions, she will refer you to the lecture slides (which you obviously already viewed). She will literally not answer any questions OR give any clarification on anything.

Cynthia is an amazing and passionate professor. Grading is dependent on some quizzes and a 2-4 person semester-long group project where you create your own sustainable business. The only downfall to this class is the possibility of getting in a bad group. Gives real-world experience. All learning material videos are prerecorded.

I sincerely enjoyed Prof. Barstow's classes! She does not teach directly from the textbook, but instead assigns in-class projects to work on so that we are able to experience assignments that we would be responsible for in the "real-world." I have work to show at interviews, which is also extremely helpful thanks to her style of teaching!

Prof. Barstow is awesome. She does a good job of inspiring students and keeps the class interesting. Of the three profs that teach MKTG 301, she is definitely my favorite. Easy lectures, easy test questions (directly from TopHat) and very helpful. Definitely take a class with her if you can.

I had Professor Barstow for Sustainability Marketing and it was hands down the best class I've ever taken. Unlike classes where you cram text book information into your head and spit it out on exams, you gain real-life business experience by crafting a marketing plan around a product, system, etc. that can solve a sustainability issue- AMAZING.

My only issue here is that a major percentage of your grade is based on a group project. This was very disappointing. There were few examples of what the project should look like and often our grade was less than expected considering the level of effort. There was no extra credit either to make up for the short fall.

Now there were many important things I learned when taking this course, so I don't want this to come across as completely negative. However, the group project has a lot of components, and there is not a clear-cut rubric to follow. Understandably businesses, and sustainability especially are complex, however there needs to be a well laid out plan.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--GRADED BY FEW THINGS--GROUP PROJECTS

reviews.comment: Cynthia is an amazing educator and wants the best for her students. Her sustainability class is extremely interesting and inspiring. There are no exams, just short quizzes, and the one group project is a lot of work but really allows you to think about all the ins and outs it takes to start a business. Best professor I've ever had!

Cynthia's course was quite challenging, and that is what made it so fun. Cynthia knows how to keep her students engaged and interested in the material, while inspiring them to learn as much as they can. Cynthia is also the most kind, and understanding professor here. I would recommend to all, her course is an experience I will never forget.

I've heard she's a great teacher for smaller classes, but for a big lecture she's not great.  She flies through slides, and the tests are vastly harder than you think they'll be.  The class is very long and boring, but the mastering marketing sections with Matt Glennon are great.  Lots of projects though, would not take again.

Cynthia inspires her students to think compassionately. Her class revolves around the creation of a comprehensive marketing plan for an entirely sustainable business. Pieces of the group project are due throughout the course and offer a chance to receive useful feedback. Truly the MOST valuable class I have ever taken.

A truly passionate professor, but it is hard to understand what exactly she wants for things because of the lack of guidelines. Explanations of expectations would be very helpful. Her feedback can be very helpful, but also unclear at times so you can't be afraid to ask her for more information. Her love for sustainability is obvious. Participate!

Her class is pretty out there, she brings in speakers and musical guests and lots of things to the class, so sometimes it feels like sort of a waste of time. But the exams are pretty straight forward and the group projects are easy.
The material is stupid simple you feel stupid reading the textbook its so simple. Tests seemed a little more tricky, overall easy class for requirement

Professor barstow is amazing. She truly cares for her students. One of the best professors in Isenberg. Take a class with her or you will regret it!!! Shes awesome and such an easy, laid back type of teacher.

She is very good at what she does and keeps her lectures interesting but the class overall is a burden, frankly.  The concepts are so broad and almost common sense but the tests are based on memorization and are very specific.  I went to the lectures just for the iclicker but was on my phone the entire time and still did great.

I'm a Marketing major and this was my least favorite class all semester. Attending these  lectures somehow managed to confuse me even more. The grading for the class was easy, but I struggled to follow her thought process in class. The exams are REDICULOUS. They make NO SENSE at all. Take with a different professor. I was disappointed.

Cynthias lectures are both eye opening and inspirational. You have to watch 8 documentaries and read 3 books to educate yourself on the most up to date sustainability issues in the business world. Semester long group project is intense, but she gives great feedback and helps you create the best possible marketing plan.

Consumer Behavior is made interesting by Cynthia! She makes you read 3 REAL books about CB making the class fun and interesting. You take super easy quizzes on the book once you finish. She hardly refers to the textbook. She always uses real-world examples in class making you look forward to her lectures. Exams are easy because she prepares you!
Unclear, unrealistic, and unprofessional.  Stay away!

Cynthia is such a nice professor. She's definitely my favorite of the three professors for this course. Her exam was based totally on what was covered in class, so you definitely need to go to her lectures.

Cynthia is awesome! She's the only teacher i can listen to in this class because she has real world experience. She keeps the material new and exciting by comparing it to her past work. She also provides great in class examples of the material. Cynthia has a niche for teaching!

Best professor I have experienced at umass. I will get behind anyone who expresses their passion as much as Cynthia does. She is truly an amazing professor and makes marketing interesting and applicable. Everyone should take her sustainability course if you want to be creative and change the world.

Cynthia Barstow made learning Marketing fun and interesting. She's hip and entertaining to listen to. Her classes involve a lot of group work, but it's easy to do and takes no time at all. Hands down best business course I've taken so far.

Amazing and interest provoking teacher. All you really need to do is read 3 books over the semester and study the study guide the night before any test. The projects are easy and this class is perfect to take with a group of friends. Gotta say, if I didn't know anybody in the class I probably would have hated it. Group work everyday

Professor Barstow is hands down one of the best professors I have had in college. She makes class interesting by using real world examples. Her exams are easy as long as you know the vocab and study her slides. If you can definitely take a class with her she is so outgoing and fun that her class is enjoyable to go to.

Cynthia Barstow is an amazing professor.  She is compassionate and knowledgeable in Marketing.  She has real world experience in agencies and marketing, unlike most of the professors.  She provides a unique and refreshing exposure into the field of Marketing.  She is a rock star being open to student feedback in an engaging and open-minded way!

second time i took this class, MUCH better than the other class taught by three professors. easy to talk to, encourages students, and the tests are so much easier than the other class. read the book if you want, but just stare at the powerpoints a bit and you'll win. her other classes are much better though

Cynthia is one of the best marketing professors at UMASS.  Her classes are engaging and her passion really resonates with her students.  Her exams are so easy so long as you study her slides. Very vocab based.  Love her.

I'm a straight A marketing student- she did not give me a good taste of this major. Tests were random, never knew what to study, questions worded oddly, and trade show grading policy makes no sense. With that said, class is an easy B, but trying to get an A is impossible and all based on luck in guessing on tests. Wouldnt recommend yet its bearable

Professor Barstow is a very caring professor who has a lot of passion for what she does. This is a class that will require a decent amount of work to get an A. Learn all the terms in the book and take careful notes on what she and the guest speakers say in class and you will be fine. She could give more clarity for what to focus on for exams.
