Alright, after taking her final I realized there is not point in even studying. All the stuff is common sense, and she only asks a few things from the book. Pretty much you study all the vocab (800-words total) and shell quiz you on 1% of that. The rest is all stuff she talks about in class. Also the trade show grading is ridiculous!!

this pitiful psychotic professor is the worst out there. her class is a 100% waste of life where she tells obnoxious moronic stories and then tests you on it without ever mentioning it because shes offended that nobody cares to sit through her ridiculous class. also, the trade show is just a way for her to steal students ideas for her own career

Cynthia's passion for teaching this class is infectious. She is a pioneer in the natural and organic food industry and has immense marketing and business experience. She treats you like an adult and expects you to do the work but you will get A LOT out of her assignments and just having a relationship with her in general. One of the best teachers!

She is not a good professor. She spends little time talking about relevant material in class and instead tells meaningless stories for most of the time. I found that I relied on the book when studying for the exams. She gives no indication of what is on the exams and everything from the book is fair game, leading to way too much info on exams.

Her class wasnt that hard HOWEVER she messed up peoples grades multiple times & its just unprofessional & rediculous we had to deal with it all semester and even now AFTER final grades are in. Completely unfair and inexcusable and frustrating for students. Overall, you can teach youself the class considering all the notes are based on a textbook.

By far the WORST teacher I've ever had.  Extremely disorganized, and even though she knows what she's talking about, she has NO CLUE how to teach it, you have to go to class then watch e-lectures, test comes from book and e-lectures, class time is pointless but she shows useless youtube videos that she asks about on the test. AVOID AT ALL COSTS!!!

Class is her using the books notes and then talking about how great she (thinks) she is. Ta's always seem disinterested in her and the students maybe they learn from her, exams ARE easy however.  But we only got 2 weeks to do the trade show which is WAY less than we should've had and groups suffered for it.

Cynthia is definitely a great teacher and knows her stuff. She is in her late 50s but acts like a 30 year old. She owns her own business and is always telling stories and how she dealt with problems. Don't be fooled tho, her tests are tricky, there designed to make you think. Go to class, even when somedays you think your going to die. its worth it

SHE NEVER STOPS TALKING ABOUT SUSTAINABILITY AND BEING ECO-FRIENDLY! You need to go to class because she shows youtube videos that she then asks questions about on the exams. She has 3 exams and a final, and she drops the lowest out of the 3 exam grades. She rushes through slides in class!! She makes you rely on the e-book and materials.

Had Cynthia in 241 and 343. I don't think she is teaching either next semester. For you future students that see her name in either one of these classes don't hesitate to add it to your schedule. GPA booster and can be used in THE RES EC MAJOR...

Very into herself.  Class can be fun and she's really excited about the subject she teaches, but when I was in her class she confronted the whole class to try to find out who posted something negative about her on ratemyprofessor and made the class very uncomfortable.  Definately says something about her.

Takes deans book way to seriously, and her grading reflects her twisted idea that honors kids are only out for A's, so she makes it a point to not give people the grade the deserve .. I did all the work, participated EVERY CLASS, did her messed up reflections and still couldnt pull off an A. I tried so hard in this class and now my gpa is ruined!

she is the worst dean's book prof.She expects A LOT more than any dean's book professor.Unless you BROWN NOSE you won't get an A. DO NOT take her if u value your GPA. She doesn't care about effort she only cares about her own experience.  It is her way or your gpa will get it. You'll have to do something retaining ur major or you won't get an A.
A little loofy but a pretty easy A. Will make you follow the Dean's Book class rules by doing "reflections."

Interesting class.  Cynthia is INCREDIBLY pationate and excited about her subject matter, sometimes a bit crazy in fact, but definately a fun class.  Don't let her outgoing personality scare you, she's actually really fun and engaging.
dried up
by far and a way the best class I have ever taken at umass. I wish all my teachers cared as much about there subjects and students as cynthia does. A GREAT CLASS that everyone should take
I love this professor. She is great.
Best professor I've had...incredibly helpful and fair. extremely intelligent and interesting. By far my favorite class!!!
Awesome awesome teacher. take this class just for the experience
Awesome teacher. Her class was tough in the beginning but she was alway helpful. I loved the class.
No Comments
Professor Bock is super nice and this class isn't bad. It's almost all group projects but the lectures can be boring but sometimes she will let you out early

Kristin Bock is a great professor! She really cares about her students and is very understanding. I have learned a lot in her class and if anyone is looking to take Business Comm I highly recommend her!

I thoroughly enjoyed Professor Bock's class this semester! She always gave insightful feedback on assignments and since it's a workshop class, she would give time to work on the assignments (definitely take advantage of that time). She has a respectful and kind approach to her teaching, but is also very direct which made it easy to follow along!
reviews.rating_tags: Group projects--Clear grading criteria--Gives good feedback

reviews.comment: Prof. Bock is a great instructor who genuinely cares about her students and their success. The course is well-structured, and work is applicable to real-world business communication. She provides fair grading and is approachable if you put in the effort. Highly recommend for anyone looking to improve professional writing and presentation skills.

Class was on-ground but Professor would join through Zoom. Not ideal, but Bock was lovely and the course did give valuable skills. Lectures were on business/professional writing, doing research, gaining PowerPoint skills, and speech presenting. Bock was available for students through Zoom Appts. & provided feedback as well as extensions on work.
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Clear grading criteria--Gives good feedback

reviews.comment: Really nice professor.  Class material helped me learn a lot and gave me skills for the business world.  Good lectures on business formatting, professional writing, research, and PowerPoint skills.  Accommodates student needs well and provides flexible due date extensions.  Also, feedback provides explanation for any points taken off.

Professor Bock provided more feedback on assignments than any other teacher has in my college experience, and this feedback was very thoughtful and helpful. Professor Bock was extremely accommodating to her student's needs, allowing an extension on basically any major assignment (with a few exceptions). I would highly recommend this class and prof.
reviews.rating_tags: Clear grading criteria--Gives good feedback--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Professor Bock was very helpful throughout the semester. We met once a week online, but the other days were open if you wanted to meet with her to get feedback before submitting our weekly assignments. She taught us how to make a very professional looking PowerPoint presentation which is very helpful. Would recommend taking JYW with Professor Bock.
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Gives good feedback--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Professor Bock is a very nice professor and you can tell she truly enjoys her classes. Saying that I personally wouldn't suggest taking this class unless you have to. A lot of homework seemed more like busywork rather than something that actually needed to be done. A couple of projects seemed that I was teaching myself.

Professor Bock was wonderful. The class was held online and majority through recorded lectures. I learned a significant amount through each project. She was very understanding for both grading and other circumstances, and she gives the best feedback of any professor I've had. I would highly recommend taking SCH-MGMT 310 with her.

Actually I took this class while we have class on-line during the pandemic. It was such a great experience for me to have this professor since she is so caring and flexible. We don't have too many homework like once a week and you can always ask for advices for editing our paper. She taught us how to make PPT, write business letter, presentation.

Professor Bock runs a strictly online class even though we are back to in person. Most classes are recorded, but there are some mandatory zoom classes every once in a while. You are pretty much just turning in the work on your own every week with little help or feedback. If you are a good writer you will be fine.

Kristen is super sweet, but it can be to a fault. She wants you to succeed, so she over explains inforamtion as well as explains the same thing 10 times in a class. Sometimes it feels like the material she teaches could be put in an email that would take 5 minutes to read, but she manages to make it last 1.5 hours, and drages it on.

She is the best. The workload is appropriate for a 300 level course. I took this class remotely and attendance was required only 4 times throughout the semester at the beginning of each section. The class is an easy A as long as you complete all the assignments by the deadline. She is also a great professor, clear & concise, and very understanding.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Accessible outside class--Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: She's super sweet! Her bubbly attitude makes class fun like elementary school in a good way. Transition to virtual learning was extremely organized with clear expectations and feedback. Pay attention to details in assignments. The standard 310 topics can drag if you've had internships; you'll still learn, it's just more time-consuming vs difficult.

Toughest grader Ive ever met. There is a civility policy, where she takes off points if you come to class late or take papers out too loudly. 5 assignments make up 90% of your grade. Forgot a couple commas in your otherwise perfect paper? Expect no more than a 90. I recommend you take 310 with someone else.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Group projects--Tough grader

reviews.comment: Professor Bock obviously cares abouts students doing well and the class a lot. The issue is not her teaching but the class itself since it is mostly covering the same material as SCHG-200 and SCHG-100. That being said you have to take the class so with that in mind Professor Bock does a good job..
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Skip class? You won't pass.--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Ignore the negative reviews of this class. Prof. Bock is excellent. She's clear about her expectations and fair--even generous if you display effort--when grading. Her class is easy, and yet, still full of useful tips and tricks that will immediately elevate your writing style. Take this class if you want to have an edge over other job applicants.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Accessible outside class--Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: One of the assignments she gave our class was to draft up a cover letter. My paper came back as 33% plagiarized which I wasn't surprised because all cover letters are drafted similarly "look forward to hearing from you" ..." thank you for your time and consideration" etc. Useful class but not in the way she was teaching it or lack of.
reviews.rating_tags: Accessible outside class--Participation matters--Skip class? You won't pass.

reviews.comment: The class itself is a waste of time.

Get ready to talk in front of your table group and your whole class! it's not too bad though, just do your work, come to class and you should get an A. She knows it's a 2 credit course so it is not too intense and she tries to prepare you for the "real world." Overall, she's pretty good.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--GROUP PROJECTS

reviews.comment: Easy A- go to class & do the homework assignments & it's hard not to get an A. Class can be annoying because you are forced to read your resume aloud, are recorded on presentation, and do a mock interview in front of the whole class. Assignments were not easy necessarily, but very helpful such as editing your resume, Linkedin & interview prep
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Skip class? You won't pass.--LOTS OF HOMEWORK

reviews.comment: Bock is so sweet and really wants her students to learn. About 50% of your grade is group projects so try to take the class with a friend or two. All group members are liable for the other members, so avoid slackers. The material isn't hard especially if you go to her office hours because she will tell you exactly what to change.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--GRADED BY FEW THINGS--GROUP PROJECTS

reviews.comment: Don't know why she has a 4.3 rating. Most useless class at Isenberg and she grades unreasonably hard. The same cover letters and writing style that has gotten me high-level internships was a 80% in this class. Make sure not to use the word "not" or else you'll lose 20 points! Wow I wrote Dear ______ to start a letter. Too bad that was -10 points
reviews.rating_tags: Tough Grader--Skip class? You won't pass.

reviews.comment: Super straightforward course; show up do the work and you'll get an A. Shes a little annoying with the grading criteria for assignments but as long as you double check before you turn stuff in youll be fine
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Skip class? You won't pass.

reviews.comment: You learn a lot in her class but she grades stupid hard. Put in so much work on every assignment and especially the last project to get my grade up to an A in the class just to not get it. Take this class with Schurter, Bock's Rate My Professor is so misleading.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough Grader--Skip class? You won't pass.--GRADED BY FEW THINGS

reviews.comment: Great professor.  Her class really helped me become a better public speaker.

This was a very straightforward and easy class. It seems intimidating to do public speaking but its a small class with no pressure at all. As long as you put in a little effort you will get an A. Speeches are short and everyone in the class is just as nervous, really loved this class! It's definitely helpful for the future.

Public speaking sounds scary but it's really not horrible in this class. It's great for all levels of public speakers and Kristin just wants you to improve and feel relaxed. There are five speeches you make throughout the entire course and one of them is the elevator pitch which is quite helpful. Take this class!

TAKE THIS CLASS. Kristin Bock is one of my favorite professors at Umass and is so sweet and kind. The class is made up of 5 speeches and class participation, and is essentially based on effort. If you try to succeed, you will get a good grade. You also get CLASS TIME to write your speeches. I have learned so much! Highly recommend!

Take this class with Professor Bock!!!! Not only is the workload very reasonable, but Professor Bock creates an environment that is extremely beneficial for students hoping to improve their public speaking skills. I've made noticeable improvement throughout the semester without getting stressed out. 11/10 would recommend, would take again.
Great teacher! Will help anyone who has trouble talking in front of a group. Easy grader, but you will definitely benefit either way
Professor Bock was an excellent teacher with great attitude. Taught with purpose and grades extremely fairly. One of my favorite classes taken at UMass.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Skip class? You won't pass.--ACCESSIBLE OUTSIDE CLASS

reviews.comment: Bock was kind of a scatterbrain but a good teacher. Not much actual work done but what we did do was helpful. Easy A.

Took public speaking with Professor Bock this semester and it was a great class.  I was really nervous to start presentations in front of the class, but the environment is very friendly and she is always smiling at you while you are at the front of the class.  Definitely would recommend this for anyone who wants to come out of their shell!

The class is a great way to  improve your speaking skills whether you are a gifted speaker or one who's shy.  There are multiple presentations throughout the class each with its own theme and designed to help you feel comfortable to various situations.  I would 100% recommend this class to anyone who needs helpis interested in public speaking!

Kristin is extremely nice and her feedback is very helpful on the presentations. If you follow the instructions for each presentation and present it with confidence (or at least fake your confidence) you will 100% get an A in this course.

Great teacher to have for junior year writing. Definitely knows what she's talking about and really shows an interest in helping her students learn. Very fair grader and if you put in the effort you'll end up happy with your grade. Going to miss this class!

Absolutely incredible teacher!  I have learned so much more in her class than any other and she makes the material interesting.  The assignments aren't difficult and she gives you time in class to work on them. Also, if you go to her office hours she will correct them for you.  No textbook required.  Genuinely one of the best professors at UMass.

She's nice, but if you're a girl, she wont like you as much.  She did not like me, but she LOVED my friend who happened to be a guy. If you wanna do good in her class, bring your papers to her before handing them in.  She'll give you a better grade for doing that.

Best professor at Umass! There is work for the class but it is very manageable; no useless busy work. She always wants to help her students and will show you exactly what needs to be done to get a good grade. An A is doable if you put in the effort
Prof Bock is awesome. from what i heard best jryr writing prof to get. Interesting and fairly easy assignments, good grader, and gives up a lot of class time to work on her assignments.

Professor Bock is definitely the teacher you want to have for 310.  She is very nice, clear (shows examples) and helpful if you have questions. You will get the grade you deserve if you put in the effort. Attendance is mandatory and important to your grade. Classes are a mix of learning about your next assignment and working on your papers. No book

Professor Bock was one of the best professors I had at UMass. Most of her assignment requirements are flexible and allow you to pick your own topic.  On graded papers, she takes the time to read every sentence and write thoughtful comments.  Going to her office hours were very helpful.  She cares about her students and even learns your name.

Professor Bock is a very helpful and insightful teacher. Her material was clear and the subjects covered were extremely relevant to the business writing world. The assignments were straightforward and designed to help you improve skills and become a better communicator. Overall I learned a lot and am a better writer.

One of the best profs @ UMass! On top of managing a business, Prof. Bock has an extensive writing background. Provides extra help during class and office hours. She's caring, helpful, smart, approachable and patient. Makes class fun to attend, where students want to participate. Class is tough, but you will get good grades if you put in the effort.
class is boring but as a teacher I think that she's pretty good at giving feedback. definitely recommend her

Very nice lady. Business writing can be monotonous, but she would always try her best to inspire interest in the subject. Workload is very manageable compared to other writing courses, and she grades very fairly, rewarding those who obviously put in more time and effort than the average student does. Go to class, do your work, and you'll do well.

Easy B.  No matter how hard you try you get a B on your paper.  Took a paper to the writing center, rewrote it, got a B. Assignments are easy though, not a lot of writing at all and it's a writing class!

SCH-MGMT 310 - Management Communications. Professor Bock is a great teacher. The class was cool and not to hard.  As a senior it was a good class to take to end my schooling here at Zoomass.  Professor Bock is hot, fair, nice, sweet, and the class work is moderate.  It was a good experience and I suggest you take Jr Year writing with her.
Prof. Bock was amazing! She is so helpful and will make the class time go by quickly. Shes pretty hot too! Take this class, you will not be disappointed.
Vey Helpfull... always willing to talk and help you through problems... a great teacher
Prof. Bock is really cool, nice and understanding. Class is not as hard as it seems at first, as long as you go to class.

She's a really nice teacher and one of the best 310 teachers in my opinion.  The class is intimidating at first but there are 4 major assignments and 3 quizzes.  Have to go to class or it really hurts your grade.
at first the class seemed a little intimidating but work is manageable and she is very helpful.  there are 4-5 major assignments during the class.  just make sure you participate and you'll be fine.
Better class than I expected! =) I think she the best SOM 310 professor compared to the other one
Professor Bock is a kind teacher who makes class time fun.

I loved Professor Bock, she is the nicest lady, and the amount of work was fair and gave plenty of helpful feedback on papers. she did give us three quizzes and two were easy but one was really hard. she cancels class a lot and never made us stay the full hour and 15 min. such a good teacher!

Prof. Bock is a nice woman, and clearly an English teacher, and it shows. However, she remembers her time in college well, and sympathizes with students. She gave a rewrite for one of our assignments for anything less than a B; it was amazing. I recommend her for the DBC, she asks a lot but she is sympathetic and helpful.
Even though she doesn't have any experience with graphic novels, she is understanding and enthusiastic about writing and literature in general.
No Comments
Bock is one of the very very best!
No Comments
not sure how I feel about this class. Definitely structured great and her slides are great but lots of assignments and lectures can be boring. Exams are essay questions but not bad

The workload was very manageable even if accelerated (6 wks due to summer). There's a mix every week. You have “Exercises” due weekly that are essentially small papers - can be a reflection or training. You get good feedback! My favorite assignments were the self-assessments. I genuinely enjoyed the class and plan to take Professor for HR too.

I took this class as a Finance major and it was the best decision I could have made. Professor Baker is awesome and is the best professor I have ever taken a class with in all the time I have been in Isenberg. Please, if you have the opportunity, take a class with her. You will not regret it.

Professor Baker is one of the best professors at Isenberg. During the two semesters I took this course, she took us to MGM Springfield for a field trip to see how they operate. She is caring and will accommodate you if you ask. I highly would recommend you take any class with her.

It has been an absolute pleasure taking a class with Professor Baker. She is one of the best professors I have ever taken a class with; this is my second one with her. Yes, there is a group project. But she gives you a whole semester to do it with specific deadlines to ensure you won't fall behind. Pay attention, go to class, and you will do well.

Great personality & lectures. Don't take if you're not an HTM major bc you'll be doing so much work and it's not worth it. The exams are hard, open-response & handwritten. There is a group project you do all semester, but she grades it so harshly. The final grade for the project is not as harsh, but overall, the project is 30+ pages & hard.
Great Professor, teaches the class from a management perspective, I appreciate the approach.

HTM 386 actually was the class I took but there was no option for it. She's a great professor, but definitely need to show up to class but she makes them entertaining. Only problem is there is a group project the whole semester and my group barely helped.

Love her, but she is one of the harshest graders I have ever had. She is very kind though and will help with career networking as well. Exams are heavily weighted, in-person, hand written, and all open response. Must study a lot to succeed.

I took this class in my first semester (and second in a continuation of the class) as part of the Isenberg RAP. She is one of the most caring and professional professors I have ever had while at UMass. She is very funny and we did a field trip to the MGM Springfield Casino as part of the course. IF YOU CAN, TAKE A CLASS WITH PROFESSOR BAKER!

Participate, do the homework, join the Zoom sessions and Prof. Baker will make sure you maximize what you take away from this course.  The level of effort required is what I would expect for a graduate-level class.  Would recommend.

Doctor Baker makes class extremely straight forward. There is no miscommunication on whats required for work/on the exams. One of the most interesting classes I have taken - htm 386. She wants everyone to do well, and have extensive knowledge in the field. Amazing professor and a great resource. Love her.

Professor Baker has been by far the best professor that I have had at UMass so far. She has an immense amount of industry knowledge and is always available to speak outside of class. People will say that she is a tough grader but as long as you show that you have put effort into the assignment and follow the rubric you will be fine. THE BEST!!!

AVOID THIS PROFESSOR and any of her classes. Doesn't post her slides and expects you to keep up with her fast-paced lectures, unreasonably difficult. The lecture itself is vague, boring and repetitive. Loves talking about herself during lectures and how well she did when she was in the industry, one of the most bizarre classes I have ever taken.

The information taught in this course was terrific! One of my favorite MBA courses, as far as material is concerned. The professor's communication style is much harsher than any other I have encountered and difficult to follow. This should not be the hardest course in an MBA program. This was one of the most stressful courses I have ever taken.

Melissa is one of the hardest professors I have ever taken at UMass and she has no reason to be so difficult. She does not lay out her grading criteria until you submit an assignment and get a bad grade. Her lectures are fine, but she makes us write 2 pages every week for a question that could be answered in a paragraph. She makes me want to cry.

Melissa Baker is an OUTSTANDING professor and one of the best in Isenberg. She truly cares about the students and will offer resources that yield success. Interactive group projects, guest lectures, and field trips make each class a great opportunity to grasp the concepts. You'll definitely have to work for an A+ but her expertise makes it worth it
LOVEE MELISSA BAKER, one of my favorite professors ever. She is personable and you can tell she really enjoys what she's teaching

Human Resources should not be the most difficult class in an MBA program, but Professor Baker seems determined to make it so. Class requires reading an entire (poorly written) textbook cover to cover, 5 medium-length papers (a.k.a. "exercises"), numerous graded discussions, weekly quizzes on book material, and a very long final paper. Just say no.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough Grader--Get ready to read--SO MANY PAPERS

reviews.comment: This professor is one of the best professors at UMass. Doctor Baker it's an A+ profesor. Her classes are so rich and interesting. She has �� % full class attendance. Nobody's miss her classes. Her class projects are amazing. She is very sweet and fear. I like her teaching and her exams are very avanced. She has an innovatived teaching style ����

Heavy workload with weekly hard deadlines. Read 700 pg text. 11 quizzes-get electronic version of text to help. 5 exercisesmini 2-3 pg papers. Mandatory discussion posts every other week with firm 3 post min and length rules. One 8 pg paper. Limited guidance on exercises. Only interaction with class was feedback on asgmts. Quick but tough grader.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough Grader--Get ready to read--Participation matters

reviews.comment: After taken the class in the Fall 2017, I STRONGLY recommend going to class (nothing posted online and no book so all the information is taught in class), attending guest lecture presentations (she asks questions on exams based of the presentations), and not waiting until the last minute to do the assignments. She such is a caring professor!
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Inspirational--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: Although Melissa is a great lecturer, she is an extremely hard grader and she doesn't lay out the criteria or expectations clearly enough for the students when it comes to projects and exams, hence why this course is so difficult. If you want to keep up your GPA I would not recommend.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough Grader--Skip class? You won't pass.--LECTURE HEAVY

reviews.comment: Her lectures are very clear ad you learn a lot from her. She is a harsh grader, you have to elaborate a lot on your answers on her exams. You really have to work for that A in her class, not like other HTM courses.

Melissa is the best! Her classes aren't easy but you actually learn something. I've learned so much from her this semester & can't wait to take more of her classes. She's an inspirational professor and gives incredible lectures - she makes you love your major even more and has great stories! Hands down best professor of the HTM department A+++

I took Foodservice Mgt with her, and it was by far the best class I've taken. She is engaging and animated during her lectures, using lots of real-world examples to get her point across. Her personality IS  a little strong, but she's very nice and helpful whenever you ask her for it.  This is not a class to half-ass it in, she loves to see effort.

I took Food Service as a Senior expecting it to be an easy class. VERY HARD. Exams are all easy questions so you need to go to class to pass. Love her as a professor, best I've had but it's not easy to pass her classes. The project is long and she grades it tough.

She was a great teacher. she always has office hours right after class, gives good lectures and is willing to answer any questions you may have. PARTICIPATE AND SHOW UP OR ELSE YOU WILL NOT DO WELL, or have a friend who takes reallly good notes and study like hell the night before test. the project final project isnt bad but it does take time.

Haven't had a better professor. Very invested in her students, and will help you through everything. Projects are long and tough, but everything is due piece-wise (little bit at a time), and you get very good feedback. No attendance, but you should go to class for the in-class assignments and to take notes. no lectures online. took HTM 350,353,455

Professor Baker is really interested in what she does which makes you want to learn. She makes class interesting and tells stories that relate to the lecture so you have real examples to go along with the material. There isn't much homework but there are mini in class assignments that really help so go to class. No textbook for this class either.
By far best class ever taken. No textbook necessary and you'll want to go to class. You actually learn about fun things and Baker is really cool. Definitely take this class if you like to eat.

Caroline Winter's class was an exceptional experience for me. After initially feeling unprepared for her class, I took it again a year later and encountered so many opportunities for personal growth. She's detail-oriented, understanding and applies concepts in her teachings to help students become more intentional with their own writing.

Caroline is an incredible professor. Her class is super interesting and easy to keep up with. The readings are long but it's easy to get through them because they're entertaining. She's super helpful with her feedback and always makes sure you're doing okay. 10000% would take again.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Gives good feedback--Caring

reviews.comment: The class starts out very reading heavy, but all the texts are beneficial in improving your writing. Caroline is very understanding, and gives a ton of helpful guidance and feedback.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Gives good feedback--Caring

reviews.comment: Caroline was an absolute joy to learn from, she really cared about making our writing better and helping us create and execute our ideas. I'm taking another class with her already because I liked her first one so much. She is very engaging and the workload is more than manageable.

Caroline Winters is an absolute gem in the Journalism Department. She's an incredibly talented writer who's published in The New Yorker, GQ, Bloomberg, and every other prestigious magazine you could think of. Despite this, she's humble, caring, and dedicated to helping her students succeed in their writing and in the industry. Take her class.

Professor Winter is the best educator within the Journalism department at UMass. She's incredibly intelligent, engaging and truly cares about her students. The work load is medium, but actually interesting/helpful  (descriptive passages, reading articles, and one big piece on whatever you want at the end). Don't debate it--take it!
Uncompromising. Doesn't help students who have a valid need - an uncaring attitude.

He is very nice but he is not good at explaining things clearly. His instruction made this class so much more difficult than it had to be. The lecture slides are mid at best and hard to understand without context. Go to labs and study the worksheets and Canvas quizzes for exams and you should be fine. There's also tons of office hours and SI.
explained concepts decently but would often make mistakes or skip over seemingly important points/clarifications/fixes (in the recordings which he could have fixed!)

Course seemed overwhelming at first but the structure ended up working well for me. It kind of forces you to stay organized. There were async, remote, and in-person options for lecture. Do the lesson quizzes mid lecture and worksheets with a couple friends/at the optional labs. The exams are pretty similar to the quizzes.

The concepts taught are not hard, but the class is structured to make it feel as hard as possible. Exams are fair.
There are no reliable lecture notes. They look chaotic without context. And when you need to listen to lecture, he is pretty hard to understand.
You want to learn, but you need to dig your way through. You're on your own, use YouTube.

This class was very straight forward in material & how to succeed. Understood everything easily. All the material u would need to ace the exams are given to u and frankly just do the homework as assigned & you will barely need to study for exams. Exams will be almost exactly like what you practice in homeworks and there are no tricks or surprises.
reviews.rating_tags: Clear grading criteria--Lots of homework--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: Unorganized class, practice test was nothing like the final. Likes to ask super arbitrary things and is very difficult to understand. Homework had little guidance and his videos are useless.
For the life of me, I couldn't understand a word he said, take anyone else.
avoid for your mental health

I'm not gonna lie Joe is a great guy, he is just really bad at lecturing. This was his first semester teaching CS326 and boy was it alright. All the work is ChatGPT and it is extremely easy to get an A is this class but the group project has you complete milestones almost every other week which is annoying as its around 5-6 slides of writing

Teaching style: Your choice of synchronous or asynchronous. 
Weekly activities: 2-4 short lesson quizzes, 1 weekly quiz, 1 worksheet. 
Projects: 5 total, due every other week. 
Workload is 100% manageable. Being able to do work asynchronously is great. Joe cares a lot about student success. All projects/activities reinforce concepts well.

This is also not Joe, Joe is the goat. The worksheets are helpful. Do the work and pass the class. Everyone says if you don't like Marius it's an intelligence issue, no way. If you don't like Joe that is an intelligence issue he genuinely teaches. Marius is essentially giving a podcast each lecture with a single slide the length of the book of John
Very fun projects, decent lectures, and easy exams. If you review the slides and/or videos and make a genuine effort to understand the content, the course is not that difficult.

worst class ever. do not take it with him. i'd rather switch majors than take this class if i were you right now. it's structured in the worst way any class could be structured. worst class at umass undergrad.

Too much for this class. 2 exercises due each week, bigger projects due every two weeks, mandatory attendance, mandatory lab attendance, mandatory group-meeting at office hours attendance, semester-long group project that forces you to use Github, for this week's "milestone" we have to not only code front-end but make a 20-slide presentation.

I took CICS 110 with Joe, overall he is a nice guy and he's passionate about the subject which is shown by his efforts to make people interact and discuss in class, however, his teaching simply just isn't the best.

Took CICS 110 with Joe, overall he does seem really passionate about the subject and tries his best to push in class discussions and interaction, however, his teaching simply just isn't great and he could work on explaining things more clearly.

Had this guy for CS110.Terrible system, barely responded to emails. SO MUCH HOMEWORK. I got 100%s in all assignments, 93% on the midterm but failed the final miserably (was egregiously ill the entire week of finals). This man calculated my final grade to 66% and then curved it DOWN to 60%?? Attendance weighs A LOT so show up (or don't, better off)

Joe Chiu is maybe the worst professor I've had at UMass. His teaching and course set up is decent at best, but his attitude is horrible. He seems to find joy and glee in rooting out academic dishonesty. Collaboration on projects (which is encouraged on the syllabus) is treated like a life sentence. Take 230 with anyone else.

For some reason, this was my least favorite 200-level class. I enjoyed 220 more than this. Honestly, I had no idea what was going on at the end. Chill guy, but I'm not a big fan of how the course was organized. Felt like I was constantly sprinting, and the topics were of very little interest to me.

I found the subject boring in general, but the way the lectures were done did not help. He is a good guy and it seems like he tries. I watched the lectures they had little relation to the homework and weekly assignments. I'm a senior now and this is still the most poorly taught class I have taken.

I think Joe Chiu gets more hate then is deserved. Yes his slides and lectures are at times bad, and the general course structure can be all over the place, but it wasn't terrible. Projects ranged from easy to difficult and the exams were almost identical to the weekly quizzes (although sort of an unusual format). Language barrier can be difficult.
Horrible class, I hate CS 230. and I am very disapointed in the way this class is set up and taught. thanks for nothing

Great and very caring professor. CS230 is set up with so much care. You can attend lectures, watch them through Zoom in real time, watch the recordings, or watch his pre-recorded videos. His analogies are great and I've learned the most through his class! His teaching style really supports good coding practice and gives you a strong knowledge base.
I hated CS 230. Horrible class.

I know there is a lot of debate on what the hardest 200 level at UMass CS is but I honestly hate CS 230. I think Joe Chiu is funny and he tries, but the class is horribly set up. The asynchronous work just is set up horribly along with weekly quizzes and worksheets, then the very poorly instructed projects and exams.
Great Class, good teacher. Gets a lot of hate but if you actually show up to class and put in the effort it is an easy A. 4/5 difficulty for a 200 level but if it was a 400 level it would be 2/5.
Bad lectures where Joe often just rambles. Projects aren't good either.

Marius cares about his students' learning, puts in effort to make sure his projects/expectations are clear, and is very approachable. Joe Chiu cannot do any of these things. CS230 is a chaotic mess of unclear, fuzzy instructions with equally chaotic grading criteria. Projects are bad and you don't learn much. Worst 200-level I've taken.

guys useless. he designed the class to be totally doable just from his lecture slides, but then his lecture slides are just a bunch of random pictures and diagrams. specifically the cache lesson makes absolutely 0 sense. 230 is super easy though, projects are light. can fail everything else and still pass. overall kind of annoying class
He is a terrible speaker and very unclear about assignments, really impossible to listen to.
I love this guy

Overall, I did like Joe has a professor. Like many others have said though, he does have a thick accent that doesn't incline me to take the class again, but he was extremely caring and nice, making jokes throughout class and leaving some time for questions even bringing candy for when the class is over. Great professor, accent is not his fault.
I did not attend lectures.  Joe builds the entire course so that you have the option to take it asynchronously, and most students take advantage of that.

Pre-recorded lectures strayed very far from quiz questions and exam content. In-person lectures were boring and not very helpful. Often left class feeling just as confused as I went in. The only learning I actually did was through the projects. Worst instructor I've had at UMass so far imo.

Joe is super sweet, and really wants his students to do well. CS230 is quite easy at this point, so much so that the lectures aren't really needed, but I still found them useful, especially the class Kahoot reviews at the end of lecture. Make sure to have a good understanding of C going in, as their isn't much review.

Attendance is optional but weekly quizzes can be difficult if you don't attend, keep in mind he does have heavy accent. Projects are biweekly and I found them to be quite easy with one or two office hour visits. Exams are only 30% of your grade so it easy to do well in class, however the exams are mostly multiple choice thus no partial credit

Firstly, he has a thick accent that makes him hard to understand. Additionally, the recorded videos on Moodle are 480p and lack most info present on the slides, info that's also tested. Lastly, exams are graded out of 40 points, so slight mistakes compound into significant underperformances at the class level. Not the worst, but avoid if possible.
This class has too much workload for a 1 credit class, its unacceptable. its almost like 220 but less workload

The lectures were quite boring, but it's easy enough to get by with just his YouTube videos and the slides. 230's content is pretty foundational but honestly not very interesting. Using C can be very annoying, and the projects are substantially more challenging than 187. Exams and quizzes weren't bad, but make sure to be careful on the worksheets.

Walked into class day 1 and had a horrible impression: plagerism policies seemed way too strict, very thick accent, and RateMyProf reviews were not very positive. Nearing the end of the semester, I couldn't say enough good things. If you attend his lectures, follow his directions carefully for graded assignments, and put the work, you will succeed.
Joe has got to go.
Just overall poor. Boring lectures, unclear projects, etc.

Lectures arn't even worth going to, just study the material on your own and it would be better. I also had him for CS187 and remember him yelling at me when I went to his office hours to ask for help on a project. Not a pleasurable experience taking any of his classes.

He was one of 3. Provides entertaining lectures that I found the most engaging. Often, he would simplify ideas well. I preferred him to Elliot Moss, although he sometimes simplifies too much, to the detriment of learning. Overall good, but he seems disorganized, which could be catastrophic in a higher level course, so I wouldn't take him again.

187 with Joe is one of the worst classes I have ever taken. In lectures, he is not motivated or good at teaching. His pronunciation of some words made this class even harder for me. It took me a couple of classes to understand what word he was talking about. Also, the projects were super hard compared to what he thought during the class.

He is absolutely one of the most unforgiving and uncooperative professors I have had the displeasure of having in my lifetime. 

Going to his lectures are the largest waste of time. Even if you could understand the words coming out of his mouth, his methods of explanation and lecture are horrible. 

He NEVER gives extensions. Period. 0 forgiveness.

Professor Joe was honestly one of the worst professors I have ever had. His lectures don't offer any help with the difficult exams and overwhelming projects. And anytime you ask for help he comes off as rude and makes you feel stupid for asking any questions. He only knows how to teach people who already know how to code. This class was the worst.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Lots of homework--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Oftentimes very difficult to understand. I did not find his lectures to be particularly useful or interesting after doing the Zybook, which does a much better job of explaining concepts. He is fairly responsive on Campuswire, but sometimes his responses do not help much with your question.

I grew up in a country where Chinese was spoken. You would think I'd get used to hearing a Chinese accent by now but I still have trouble understanding what he says. He's a nice guy and the topics in this class are interesting, but he's not a great teacher.

If you are not a CS major, do not take this class because the professor only knows how to speak to CS majors, who already know the material, which messes up the grading curve. The class moves incredibly fast so much that the dep't is getting rid of this class next semester. Example problems are NOTHING like the exam problems.
Lectures are so boring I can't even pay attention (even recorded ones on moodle). I can't really tell if we are learning anything either?
5 words: a lazy CICS faculty member.

For my year, Joe decided to screw everyone up and redo the course content that was not reviewed by the board. The content was not something that could be covered in one semester. Additionally, Joe, TAs and the student volunteers were not on the same page and would give confusing answers to literally everything. Different answr for the same question

The Labs with the right lab group are manageable, while the Zybooks will carry you through the class. Joe's a very caring and honest guy, he brings candy to lectures, tries to answer questions quickly, and works hard to make sure everyone can pass. His accent can be a bit hard to understand at first but is easy to get used to.

230 under Joe is a class that is just poorly structured with an incompetent teacher. Joe makes no effort to teach his students, his projects have unclear documentation, and he was even called out for not running his classes well. If you can, just take 230 with either Marc Liberatore or Tim Richards. They do a better job running classes.

Joe is a prime example of someone who recently began his villain arc. He doesn't listen to students or care about them anymore, he's being super lazy when it comes to running a class, and his Piazza posts fail to clarify information or fill important knowledge gaps. Good thing he's going to be on sabbatical for the fall of 2022.

Solid professor who does a good job lecturing and explaining the content to students. Attendance isn't mandatory but kahoots and in-class coding walkthroughs help a lot. Projects are solid difficulty but definitely doable.
Joe is solid, a nice guy who cares about his students and very helpful in office hours. The course material is not too difficult.

Extremely difficult for a 1 credit class. Requires 10+ hours per week. The recorded videos are insufficient and you will need to teach yourself C and EdLab. Don't be fooled by the simplicity in the first few weeks - it gets VERY hard. Joe is disorganized and never answers questions well. Had to withdraw for mental health.
Good professor, answers your questions well

reviews.comment: Joes lectures were never really helpful. Most of the time it would just be explaining concepts through zybooks that's you can easily just read yourself. In addition, I went to officer hours one time and asked how something was supposed to work and he ended up just yelling at me for not knowing how it should work. I never went again.

This course section taught by Joe is down right awful. I thought Joe's teaching style for 121 was mediocre, but his 187 lectures were so bad I went to the first 2 and then NEVER AGAIN. The course is run at an unrelenting pace so you're always doing the projects back to back... it's a truly miserable experience. Beware taking 187 with Joe!

Watching Joe Chiu's recorded lectures for 198c is an absolute blast. He uses a Snorlax stuffed animal to pose clarifying question, and ends every lecture with "(lecture topic) isss awesome" and then a transition. I love his clear passion for teaching and it makes all the difference in keeping students engaged.

He doesn't know the material and doesn't know how to explain it. No effort is put for students to succeed. Isn't helpful in his responses when you ask him or reach out to him. UCA's are incompetent and the TA's as well. The whole structure of the class needs some change.
Joe Chiu is a mixed bag. He seems like a nice person, but his CS230 class has the worst structure when compared to the other instructors who taught it.

I think Joe is a nice guy but 230 under him just has a horrible structure, basically just an online course and you only have to show up for the exams. Projects are cool but stressful because Joe's responses on piazza are unclear and not helpful. Exam is just reused quiz questions too, very lazy.

Joe Chiu must quit his job as not only did he get a bad name from students for his poor management of 230 in-person, but after the switch to in-person learning, he’s also a perfect example of a professor who has zero respect towards students with disabilities. Good thing he's on leave for the fall of 2022.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Participation matters--Beware of pop quizzes

reviews.comment: Joe Chiu used to be the sweetest professor during COVID, but his recent inability to take criticism after the switch from online to in-person learning and the lack of physical in-person lectures really darkens the respect I have for him as a professor. It sucks because he was very nice and helpful when he co-taught 220 with Marius in spring 2021.
Very poor course management alongside lack of physical lectures should make 230 a hard pass if Joe teaches it. Take 230 with Tim if he’s teaching.

One lecture a week, and it was solely for Kahoot/worksheets; no content. Discussions were just us sitting in silence in a room taking ONLINE quizzes with questions we've never seen. Projects were marred by project quizzes that were 40% of our project grade. The final exam was just the removed quiz questions; average was a 59. Terribly run course.

reviews.comment: Does not provide specificity with how he wants work done. Unnecessarily rigid and a poor explainer. Taking his class means relying on zyBooks in order to learn anything, and his Kahoots do absolutely nothing for anybody. I've never been so dissatisfied with a teacher as I have with Chiu, and I would never recommend him to anybody. You can do better

The first 1/3 of 121 is pretty easy with Joe. After that, you will need to put more effort into the class to get good grades. He uses kahoots to quiz students on coding problems, which is kind of hit or miss. He is hard to understand sometimes. If youre struggling in 121 go to his office hours!! He is rlly helpful outside of class.

I believe that Joe is genuinely a nice professor, but he's being super lazy!!! He is reusing old video lectures, has converted one of our 2 lecture sessions to an office hour WHICH SOLVES NOTHING, doesn't even teach in the other lecture, and has us take way too many quizzes each week (project, weekly, lesson). Has a minimal curve to the grade.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--So many papers--Tough grader

reviews.comment: Fantastic projects that truly illustrate the essence of the course to the student and completion ensures good fundamental understanding and intuition for similar material (more advanced). But pushing more on tests these days, early morning labs and quizzes, projects given over a short timeline which is not very conducive all things considered.

reviews.comment: He is a super caring professor, but the class set up sucks. You have to watch recorded lectures then during lectures/discussions take quizzes or graded worksheets. Tough class overall.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Accessible outside class--Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: Instead of lecturing, he uses old and outdated lecture videos that are either in low quality (480p) or riddled with mistakes (which he never address). Moreover, he couldn't even speak English properly, therefore his videos are extremely hard to follow. He gets defensive and would clap bank at students who express doubts or question his teaching.

CS230 is about making projects. Projects need documentation (guide of what you need to do) so he can grade it. If not, you will create arbitrary projects yourself. Joe's doc are often missing things. In short, he deducts your score based on what he hides/forget to add to doc.
Very bad professor. Don't take him.
Dead from the class. My GPA will not recover from this blow! The class is not hard, but he did not teach anything throughout the semester.

What a hilarious prof. Tries to cover up for his incompetency with a soft animals like people will not find out he's not doing anything and reusing recorded videos from the summer. Truly a letdown for Robert and Donna Manning College Of Information and Computer Sciences.

The fact that a "flipped classroom model" was implemented after this class was taught online is not lost on me. It seems like he was able to cut down how much he actually contributes to the course by having students learn on their own and pretending that a single synchronous meeting in which you are quizzed is called teaching. I call it lazy.

Great professor; really knowledgeable about the material, responds quickly to questions on Piazza, wants everyone to succeed, and actively asks for our feedback. The only reason I didn't give 5 is that his accent and assignments can be hard to understand, but it's not too much of a problem, I've gotten better at understanding him.

Professor Joe is a great professor. The projects are hard, but they will make you learn. The format of the class works well for but I can see how others could struggle. He cares about his students and wants us to succeed.
Joe is a terrible professor and this class has been awful.

Great professor. Took his 220 with Marius Minea. Lighthearted, cute, a bit cringe, good slides and videos. His quiz is often confusing due to the accent. Sometimes he may sound ironic, but actually it's him being chilled.

Level of difficulty is 4 on the basis of 198c being a 1 credit class, but felt like 3 credit class workload. I've had Prof. Chiu for 198c during the summer along with 220 in spring 2020, and it is safe to say he is the most passionate and caring educator in my entire scholastic career. He explains complex concepts in a very easy to understand way.

Joe is quite a passionate professor. You can tell that he puts a lot of effort into his lectures, and he answers Piazza almost instantly, even when it's late at night. The only one down side of Joe is that his accent is a bit hard to understand, but if you can get used to it he is quite a good professor.

Combo of lesson vids w live lectures was perfect. KAHOOT was the best idea ever. Live lectures were very well organized: summary -> Kahoot (with thorough explanations) -> class activities. Very helpful during OH. Class is one of the best and one of the hardest ever. Does not repeat stuff, but rather explains material in new ways.
Joe is a great professor. Very caring, tries really hard to make the course fair for us. Always cleared up confusion, and answered questions extremely fast. Could not recommend enough.

Joe is a very nice professor. However, beware of this class. CS220 is awful and very annoying. The average on the weekly quiz is an F. And the average on the final exam was 19/65 (also an F). This class is much worse than CS187.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Skip class? You won't pass.--Test heavy

reviews.comment: Joe is one of the kindest professors in the CS department. He really truly cares about his students and he wants you to succeed. He will do his absolute best to help you. The classes can be hard, but none of that falls on Joe imo. Great prof.

Yeah, definitely had to work hard to get my grade in the course. Concepts aren't bad, but C in general isn't the easiest to pick up for me to be honest. Joe is nice and caring. You can succeed, but you need to put in the work and stay on top of things.

Joe obviously cares about his students and wants to help them pass. It seems like the course guidelines the CS department gives him are rigid, though he tries to be as helpful as he can. The switch to remote learning was bumpy and he made a few mistakes, but he obviously had the students' best interests at heart.

Joe clearly knows the subject well but he is not suited to be a professor, at least at this level. His accent is extremely hard to understand, and the slides and posts that he writes are riddled with mistakes. I learned almost everything in this class from the projects, which are a lot tougher than the CS121 projects.

JOE IS AMAZING and cares about his students. One time he stuck around for AN HOUR after class ended to give me help on a challenge (I ended up getting it). He brings candy too to class! NOTE: 230 starts off with an intense worked, then tapers off by spring break (or mid semester). First project took 20h, last took 5h #covid19semester
I think the guy is really smart but it's impossible to understand him because of his thick asian accent. I'm trying to learn and I can't understand him. Take another comsci professor if possible.

Joe Chiu is one of the worst professors Ive ever had. Hes not helpful at all and those who say he is most likely have prior knowledge about C programming or are overconfident in their abilities. He isnt lenient with most things like due dates and hes very cynical towards you when you try to ask simple questions. Dont take his class.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Graded by few things--Tough grader

reviews.comment: He has the absolute worst English and doesn't deserve to teach this course. There are SO MANY mistakes in anything he writes. He wrote one new project for our semester and it had the WORST documentation ever. He wrote a midterm with an unholy amount of mistakes and ambiguities. His accent is bad. One has to scout Piazza for everything.

While Joe himself is pretty good at explaining, his accent makes him hard to understand in lectures. The CS department, made this the hardest class you can take, putting in measures to intentionally lower your grade, like trick questions in exams, graded iclicker answers, and lab assignments with varying due dates. I'd still recommend Joe though.

The only downfall of Joe is his English ability, especially when he writes exams. I have found him to be really caring in office hours, and he is a fairly good professor in my experience. Just be wary of what he says during exams in terms of corrections; many times his questions are poorly worded, so ask him directly, NOT the TA's.

Joe is a good professor. Yes, his accent is kinda heavy but you can still clearly understand him. He is also very helpful in office hours. 187 is one of the project heavy class so be ready to do work in it.

reviews.comment: Joes is so kind and he is so helpful at office hours. He always wants to make sure that students are understanding material. Yes, his accent is a little difficult to understand but just ask and he can rephrase what he is saying. Also, don't buy into the hype of 187. Yes it is difficult, but treat it as another hard class to succeed in!
Joe is literally a god. If you don't take Joe for 187 you are betraying god himself.
Joe is literally a god. If you don't take Joe for 187 you are betraying god himself.
I made the mistake of choosing the other professor for this class. Switched lectures to Joe's after dropping in once. Best decision I've ever made.

Horrible accent that makes understanding him hard. Lousy at communicating. Teaches purely from the slides. Offers nothing beyond that I can get a Coursera or edX now. I can't believe I'm paying this much in tuition and have such poor quality professor.

I took CS 187 with him in the fall and I wasn't too much of a fan. However, taking 220 in the spring, he made major improvements as a lecturer and overall is extremely caring and nice to his students. He is a great professor and I hope to have him in CS 230!
Awesome and funny teachers. It is quite hard to listen to what he said at first because his English accent is not so good but the lecture is still amazing.
Best instructor ever despite his English accent is a little bit hard to hear but you will get used to it. He is always passionate about the lecture materials, and he is also funny.
his accent is a little hard to hear but the slide is very helpful and he eager to explain everything you ask. His lecture is very inspirational and hilarious.
Although his accent is a large barrier, if you are focused in class, you can pass the class effortless. If you have any question after class, he's always available.

reviews.comment: A gem of an instructor. I have had him for two classes, TA for CS187 and now CS220, will sign up for his CS230 section as well! Very accessible and doesn't have the inflated ego seen in many CS students and some profs. CS courses are difficult.

Joe cares a lot about his students and wants them to learn the material. He uses in class group activities a lot. Nice guy, but one of the worst teachers ever. Can barely read off of the slides.
He was an okay teacher. His lectures were okay, but he struggled to explain concepts well in his lectures. He is a very nice guy though :)

reviews.comment: I honestly believe that he is a smart guy, but I learned absolutely nothing from his lectures. Practice exams were just spreadsheets of student submitted questions that weren't checked for accuracy.

For the past three classes, we've been getting lectured by the graduate TA, and she is so much more engaging. This is a hard class, and Kyle Cave is able to make an otherwise interesting topic convoluted and boring.

Pop quizzes contain the most random material from past and upcoming lectures, you can never be prepared for this class.

I took his class for studies of consciousness and loved it, Some students dont like it simply because he expects what a college professor should expect, If you go to class and take notes you will be fine on the exams. Horrible, I was warned, and I took the class anyways

95% of grade is quizzes and exams. Nothing due at a normal time. Quizzes and exams are extremely difficult. Won't allow any leniency in the course. Apathetic to disability. Just so so bad. Like I saw the reviews and was like "I'll be fine! im smart!" girl do not fool yourself. This man does not care about your success in the slightest. He takes every opportunity to decrease your grade with garbage. He unjustly accused me of plagiarism on an exam open response. Not even my advisor agreed with him. Take 315 ONLINE.

reviews.comment: It is easy to do well if you go to class and do the readings. There is multiple quizzes due every week. The lectures tend to be boring but the professor is nice and does seem to care about his students.
Its bad and he doesnt care

Read text, attend lecture, keep up w assignments and you'll be fine. Cave is really knowledgeable and answers questions well IF you put in the effort to ask/clarify. He makes this class more difficult than it needs to be but in the end you get what you put in. Overall i learned a lot just sucked to be in the thick of it - so power through!!

I never went after the first day. Not once. I never watched a lecture or studied for an exam. I used the textbooks to help with the exams and would check for "in-class assignments" after class because you have 24hrs to submit them. And, I did SONA extra credit. His voice is incredibly monotone and lectures are hard to follow, so I chose not to!

absolutely awful lecturer, very boring & just reads off the slides & doesn't actually teach or clarify anything. I put a good amount of effort into this course & still ended up with a bad grade, it is not worth it, do not take

Don't be scared away by the bad reviews! I found the content to be fascinating, and Kyle is clearly passionate about it. There are a lot of readings/quizzes, but if you do the readings and go to class you will be fine. reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Test heavy

reviews.comment: I almost didn't take this class because of all the bad ratings, but I'm glad I did. Prof Cave is definitely not as bad as all the reviews say, and if you pay attention in lecture and do the assigned readings, you will be just fine. He was really nice and lectures were pretty easy to understand. If you're worried about this class, don't be.

He is a nice guy, but he makes the class tough. 30% of your grade is the after-class quizzes, which are some multiple-choice questions and an essay response. 4 open-book exams (lowest gets dropped). Lectures are really boring and the material is not particularly interesting. Be prepared to read the textbook every week

He seems like an ok guy but man this class makes you work. Super lecture heavy with so many notes to take and he goes so fast. Multiple quizzes a week and the readings matter a lot on the tests. The tests are on like 6-7 chapters of material but there is only 27 questions so it makes studying so hard as you never know what to focus on.

Not as hard as I thought it would be based on these reviews, but the way Cave teaches is soul crushing. The material is so unbelievably boring. Exams are open note which is nice, but you have to do the readings to do well on them. After class quizzes are worth 30% of your grade and require you to go through hundreds of lec. slides which takes HOURS

This class is insane. Especially towards the end of the semester - SO much material and it gets so complex. I feel like I'm drowning. So much textbook reading required (doesn't go over some stuff in lecture from text that is on exams), assignments and quizzes every week. I've done EVERYTHING I can to stay on top of the work - avoid, avoid, avoid.

reviews.comment: Kyle Cave goes out of his way to make this class difficult, you know how I know this? Don't waste your money lining his pockets by taking his class. AVOID CAVE AT ALL COSTS

Prof.Cave is passionate about cognitive psychology but makes it hard. Lectures are verbatim from slides - not mandatory, but they should be because exams/quizzes are very difficult and nit-picky for the 1hr time limit. Open-note, but worded very confusingly-you will be between 2+ answers every time, and essays (100 words) are graded very harshly.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: Trust me don't take it. Hardest psych class I've taken by far. The exams are worded completely different and we only have 60 mins to complete it. MAKE SURE to do the after-class quiz it makes up 30% of your grade. Reading the textbook will help you better than attending lectures.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Group projects

reviews.comment: This class was slightly better than I expected. Open book exams that weren't hard if you paid attention in lecture. Material could get boring, Prof Cave can be robotic and monotone, but he knows what he's talking about and answers ?s. Reading quizzes with unlimited attempts and after class quizzes with 24 hour deadlines were the entire workload.

One of the hardest classes I've taken so far as psychology major. The content is easy to understand it is more that Kyle makes the class hard. There are multiple weekly quizzes before and after class and the exams are the hardest thing about the class. It is definitely a manageable class if you put the work in but Kyle does not make it easy.
not the most understanding, if you dont go to class you wont pass, make sure to buy the textbook. Really tough exams.

reviews.comment: Never take this class. You will regret it.

Accused me of cheating on the 1st exam because of a technological error out of my control, purposely makes exam and quiz questions extremely hard, completely disorganized class, random assignments presented in class on top of the other 2 quizzes and chapter readings due each week, lectures hardly on exam, all knit picky stuff from text, ETC ETC ETC

Kyle Cave shows no mercy when it comes to grading or extension and eventuating circumstances. He purposefully makes exams extremely difficult. He randomly posts in class assignments due the next day and he will not give an extension. He also has random after class quizzes posted on Wednesdays and due on Wednesdays. If you it miss it no extension.

Kyle Cave is really a great guy. You can tell he is passionate about the subject. But this class is very robotic and not interesting at all. You will have a google doc with 20+ pages of notes before an exam. So much information and he lectures very fast. Do good on the paper that's worth 30% and you'll be okay.

Let me say this first: Professor Cave is well knowledgeable, is receptive to questions, and is available for extra help.

But there's asense of "I don't care about you" in his teaching style. It's robotic, textbook heavy, and mundane. He gives quizzes after exams like it's nothing. Has a friendly tone, but does not exemplify it with self awareness.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Beware of pop quizzes--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: There is a decent amount of work required for this class but Dr. Cave is pleasant, engaging, and extremely knowledgeable. He begins every class by asking if anyone has any questions and appears genuinely happy to answer questions/review material. If you are willing to do the work you will do well.

Effort doesn't matter because he is just an unempathetic and mundane professor. No regard during COVID when asked for extra help, accused me of plagiarism on a paper just because I used a long quote, then unnecessarily emailed me saying I wouldn't have gotten a good grade in the class anyway regardless of the paper.

Prof.Cave is well-knowledgeable and that is unquestionable, however, his lecture is very robotic and very unmotivated/boring. He's not enthusiastic at all! Knowledgeable is not the same as being engaged. He acts as if he doesn't like teaching, and that can impact the way students perceive and engage in his class.Don't take him if you don't have to!

reviews.comment: I almost didn't take this class because of the rate my professor reviews but just took it and i was pleasantly surprised. literally, you just have to try. Dont let low ratings scare u out of taking this class. Prof Cave is VERY nice in office hours+cares about u learning the material+ offers many chances in lecture to ask Qs. SO BORING

Ok, this class is definitely difficult but I enjoyed it. Exam 1 grades came back lower than he expected so instead of looking over the exam and perhaps looking at the ways it was flawed he gave us an assignment to read suggesting our bad grades where the result of cell phones. The exam questions are just needlessly wordy and overcomplicated.

This class is literally the most boring class I've ever taken at UMass. It's truly painful to sit through. I do think that professor Cave is a nice man and he seems like he genuinely cares about his students. But, his lecturing is literally so boring. And the classroom is flipped so you read textbook at home and then learn in lecture which I hate.

I like Professor Cave as a person, but not as a professor. The description for this course (psych 391SC: study of consciousness) is extremely misleading. It is very science heavy and difficult. Professor Kyle Cave is a wonderful professor! His classes are so lively and he makes lectures enjoyable and easy to follow along. His exams are fair as long as you study and go to lecture.
