Do not take this!!! So stressful and for what! Class was built to be incredibly difficult, and not at all rewarding. I really tried in this class, studied for everything, never missed a lecture and always look notes. This was one of the most unenjoyable class I've ever taken. Thank god for P/F. My first review for him got taken down.... awful sus
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Beware of pop quizzes--Tough grader

reviews.comment: I took psych315 as part of my secondary psych neuro track (i am a bio major primary) and i still found the course to be very difficult. The content seems like it could be interesting, however Kyle did a pretty poor job making it enjoyable to learn. Almost feels like it was intentionally made to be difficult for no reason. Would not recommend.
reviews.rating_tags: Test heavy--Clear grading criteria--Beware of pop quizzes

reviews.comment: If you have a choice, DON'T TAKE THIS CLASS. Dr. Cave is still leading class as if there isn't a pandemic and we are not juggling 658734 things at once. For exams, there is no clear answer on material, just says maybe or maybe not. A student had some conerns about the exam (hoping he would make adjustments) and he just said to study better. -100/10
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Skip class? You won't pass.--Beware of pop quizzes

reviews.comment: Pop quizzes practically 1/3 of classes, and they are based on the material LEARNED ON THAT DAY!!! We get 50 minutes to do multiple-choice exams with 45 questions, and all these questions are super hard with no easy answers (even if you studied). He is rude over email, and so are his TAs. He goes through the slides super fast. Theres also an essay.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Beware of pop quizzes--Tough grader

reviews.comment: y'all, im not even done with the semester and yet im here. NEVER take a class w this man. NEVER. if you ever have any type of issue big or small he will NEVER help you out he is actually the most inconsiderate man I have ever met in my life. Even with the majority of the class struggling with exams he ignores everyones cries for help anddoesnothing

kyle cave does not know how to control and maintain the attention of a lecture hall. cognitive is already a tough enough subject and his trick exam questions, harsh grading on a mandatory paper, and dry lectures make this class much more difficult than it needs to be. do not take 315 with him.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Beware of pop quizzes--Tough grader

reviews.comment: My problem with this class is that you are set up to fail! Lectures are dry, and you literally have to read the entire 600 page textbook if you want to do remotely well. A 600 word "essay" that is graded way too hard for what it is, and exams ask for specific, obscure knowledge. I would stay clear! Find another way to fulfill your requisite.

Lectures are extremely dry and not super useful, but he does have pop quizzes in class every so often that count towards your grade to make you go. I honestly think you could read the textbook (though chapters are dense) / study info on lectures slides to pass. Questions on exams include stuff from the textbook that are never mentioned in class.

Professor Cave is a great guy, but I did not find his lectures to be particularly helpful. The exams are very specific and he expects you to know everything covered in lecture and from the textbook. The fourth exam is on the same day as the final and you have to take both. The lowest exam grade is dropped, but the exams aren't easy.

Professor Cave is one of the worst professors I have ever had. He is extremely boring in lectures and expects you to know everything he says as well as everything in the textbook. He has the final and 4th exam in the same time period. This is extremely unfair and unnecessary. If you can avoid it do not take this class!
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Graded by few things--Tough grader

reviews.comment: He generally cares and really does try his best to engage, but he picks his favorites and leaves lectures much to be desired. His lectures are a very odd layout and have left many confused. Exams are 50/50 writing and multiple choice. The writing, he's really tough and is looking for very particular info that is failed to be mentioned. Hard class.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Skip class? You won't pass.--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Pros: Kyle is amazing and really knowledgeable. Every class I learned something new. Answers questions in class and regularly checks in to make sure everyone understands. Cons: Lots of work! Weekly quizzes, papers, and exams are not easy. Stick to it, it's worth it though.

Professor Cave is a good guy, but it takes a lot of work to get an A. His lectures were never clear to me, but reading the entire textbook was extremely helpful. He has a lot of assignments, but when he likes your class he'll scale his exams and such.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Get ready to read

reviews.comment: Nice professor, passionate about subject. My advice: for exams, know the main experiments/studies discussed in class well. Most of his multiple choice questions are something like "Which of the following is NOT true about so-and-so's experiment." You do have to put effort into this class but Professor Cave is fair.

Took him last semester. Very nice guy, and interesting class. Read the book and remember the important research he discusses in class (as well as how it is in the book). Did take a lot of effort (reading, 3 exams, participation, final group project and long paper) but if you do put in effort you will succeed (he does pay attention to who's trying).
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Skip class? You won't pass.

reviews.comment: A lot of work for honors: 20 min presentation, online debates, 12 page paper (ew) on top of readings. Classes were pretty boring if you don't care much about cognitive psych. In terms of kindness and explaining material: not bad but not great. He gave no criteria for the paper and can be very vague/unhelpful if you ask questions outside of class.
Great teacher. There was a fair amount of work, but I learned alot and it was pretty easily graded. Smart guy.

Great class! The material can be a little dry, but I learned so much. Professor Cave expects a lot, but if you put in the effort he will reward you. LOTS of information, but an easy grader, so it balances out. Nice guy who really wants everyone to succeed. He is very fair.

Pretty much the worst class I've ever taken. He couldn't make a straightforward exam to save his life. Refused to give me the extra credit points I rightfully earned. Only one grade that isn't a test, and it's only worth 10%. Don't take this class unless you're awesome at multiple choice tests and decoding mysterious questions.

Tough at first, and the material is a bit dry but hang in there! class becomes incredibly interesting, shows great videos and you learn a lot. make sure you do the reading before the first test, you are more likely to do well
Great professor! You WILL learn if you put the effort in it.
Fun & Fair

Easy class if you attend lecture.  Exams based directly from lectures, I hardly read the book and still did very well in the class simply from taking notes and following lecture closely.  Definitely recommend this class to anyone with an interest in cognition and/or neuroscience.
really nice and good guy.

Go to Class. It's the only way to figure out his exams.  They are ridiculously wordy and confusing.  He does not know how to ask straightforward questions about complex ideas, which *really* sucks. As a lecturer, quite boring, but maybe that's because the class barely ever responds. scheduled our last exam and final exam on the same day. no makeups
Very clear, very helpful, an overall nice guy

Did well in the class.  Go to lecture, read the text (even though it sucks, it does help) and you'll do fine.  Not his fault that most students aren't interested in the material.  It's a requirement.  But he's not bad.  Just boring and doens't give ANY make up exams.

He really knows his stuff for this class. His lectures are very organized and thorough. He posts some notes on the web, but I'd recommend going to the lectures. The tests were multiple choice and a short essay question. They're not too hard if you know lecture material and stuff from the textbook.
Exams are ridiculously hard multiple-choice that cover way too much material and try to trick you.  Don't take this course unless you adapt well to old-school teaching and exam methods.

Nothing to learn in the homework, very poorly design structure and description for homeworks. It takes a lot of time but you will learn nothing meaningful. The lecture are boring. The class is a waste of time and energy. Don't take this meaningless class.
She is okay but her course are poorly structure. The homework are too much and you don't learn much in the course. It is all buzz word description.

It's clear that Prof. Conboy cares about good coding practices and preparing students to be effective engineers. The lecturers aren't super engaging but most of the course is based on the group project. She gives rubrics for each assignment so expectations are clear although grading can be a bit harsh

All of the assignments are badly specified, there are many minor deductions you'll get for asinine criteria that were unspecified in the instructions. The assignments themselves aren't ridiculous, but the grading is. Plus they never take student feedback into consideration. All of mine has led to nothing. Dissapointing class.

Professor Conboy is a kind and understanding instructor who cares about her students and the material she teaches. However, she has high expectations for grading. While the workload isn't terrible, it can be very easy to lose a lot of credit on the homework assignments due to unclear instructions.
She is a down-to-earth professor who is helpful in office hours, but the grading policy is overall too harsh. Would not recommend unless you're a graduate student. (coming from an undergrad student)

Homework instructions are lacking. I've consistently lost marks for tiny details unmentioned throughout assignment descriptions. She fights tooth and nail for regrades, as if she has a deduction quota. She makes no effort to space out assignments. Overall her teaching was mediocre, her instructions poorly described, and assignments poorly graded.

Won't recommend the course. The worst part is the grading, not at all clear and will cut marks on any silly trivial thing. Supposed to be not heavy but there are 8 heavy assignments apart from the weekly participation quiz and a big project. No extra credits. Recorder lectures are inaudible and teaching is superficial.

The professor will not teach you anything but expect pristine code from you. I will never recommend anyone to take a class with her. She does not specify how she is grading home-works and then deducts marks for absolutely foolish reasons. I had a perfect GPA, but she is the reason my GPA will go down. RUN!
Most down-to-earth professor in the software engineering field of the CS department. If you are stuck drop by her office hours anytime!

Severely underrated professor. Professor Conboy is super accommodating, which is very rare in many CICS professors. Very willing to clarify, and if you have reasonable extenuating circumstances, she'll grant you an extension.

The labs are fairly easy and if you're confused, she'll always clarify for you. She wants to make sure you understand each lab and the science behind it. She understands that most students are not bio majors, so she doesn't grade them too harshly.
Smart dude, but cannot teach well.

This man does not know what he is doing. He's brought his kid to class multiple times, which is fine, but then he lets the child distract students during lectures. He brushes past material and expects you to just know everything, while always going off topic and stroking his ego. The guy also makes off putting comments, or personal comments a lot.
BEST TEACHER EVER PLEASE DONT HESITATE TO TAKE HIS CLASS

Being a young "professor" and former UMass CS undergrad, Cooper excels at being relatable and adjusting the course based on student experiences. For someone so new to teaching, he is a natural at building CS course curricula, though he does make them difficult. I learned so much, and he is one of the most effective teachers I have had.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Hilarious--Beware of pop quizzes

reviews.comment: Cooper Sigrist is an easy grader and super nice, really chill. But he hardly gives lectures; his class feels more like a study hall. Not very beginner-friendly. He had us do a final project, but he didn't provide a clear rubric for it.

I feel bad giving a 3 cause Cooper is honestly a really cool guy. I think he's probably an amazing professor for upper levels, but for 110 the class was way too fast paced. He kind of brushed past the basics and expected us to know them when we did not. If you're looking for a challenge or already know basic CS then I would recommend.
Makes class way harder than it should be.

Does way too much, expects a lot out people just starting off with CS. Do the labs yourself because the lab TA's are AWFUL. Nice guy overall but seems a bit egotistical in his teaching style and just expects for things just to click the first time around.

As a person, Cooper is a good guy. However, his biggest flaw is that his teaching style for 110 is fast paced. He finished the bulk of the 110 curriculum in 1 month when this class is an intro class, which is wrong to do. He expects most people to just know things and when you ask him for help, he just loops what he says, leaving you confused.

He is an excellent teacher, he knows the course material very well. But sometimes go over the course difficulty in my opinion. The homework can sometimes be a rollercoster ride, as it takes 20 min to 6h to complete. We do get a lot of collaboration time for team work and sharing ideas.
THE KING OF ML, THE SAVIOUR OF FRESHMAN, THE GLORIOUS KING OF CS110 AND FINALLY THE MAN AMONG BOYS
THIS IS THE BEST GUY EVER. TAKE HIS CLASS. DON'T THINK ABOUT IT, JUST TAKE IT

Cooper is an amazing and interesting professor. However, the jump from the lecture content to the often bug-filled homework is pretty big. If you have no ML experience be very wary of this class. That being said Cooper is a pretty lenient grader so if you try in this class your grade should be no issue.

First of all, I am someone with no prior ML experience. Cooper not only made the class super enjoyable for me, but also inspired me to study more about the field. He is friendly, knowledgeable, and overall a really wholesome guy. Definitely would recommend.

389 is definitely a tough class if you haven't done any ML before. However, I think Cooper does a great job at teaching this difficult material, especially near the start of the semester where it's more ML theory related. Quizzes are free points which is cool, homework is difficult but doable with dedication and office hours help.
Cooper is incredible! If you can, get him! Really knows how to connect w/ students.
Awesome. Clearly knows what he's doing. Best to have some prior coursework about the same subjects, though!

Cooper seems knowledgeable in ML but I wish he didn't gloss over the math for backpropagation at the start of the semester since I feel like it would've been really nice to know. His slides are also not the best at conveying conceptual stuff, but it's to force you to write down notes (which I really dislike because I can't write everything down).

Ignore the 1/5, it was some kid who had beef with him. Course was challenging, but awesome! He knows what he's doing and is passionate about it; you will struggle if you have no background in the subject. Teaches well and knows how to engage! 10/10!

Cooper is awesome. He is very passionate in machine learning and it makes his class very enjoyable. Some of his assignments are really hard, and he doesn't give extra resources so you kind of have to go to OH to get help. If you are interested in ML I highly recommend taking this class with him.

This class is very difficult if you don't have any previous ML experience. That said, Cooper is still good at teaching the material, difficult as it may be, to those of us without prior experience. He's pretty forgiving on grading projects, except he won't tell you that until after you've spent several days struggling. Overall positive experience

Cooper is a great dude, not only is he extremely sympathetic towards people with no machine learning background, but he teaches difficult material well and is always willing to explain further. When it comes to course management, Cooper knocks it out of the park.
He's a really nice dude who teaches well.
Cooper is a GOD. If you're into ML, I highly recommend 389 with him.

He is a really nice dude but he has no idea how to teach. These people that are saying he is good they have a strong background in machine learning but this class is an intro class and requires no prior background. No resources available and the lecture are insanely hard to understand even if you watch them multiple times. Only take with background
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Graded by few things--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: Cooper is just a good dude.... it's only a few weeks into the semester yet and it's already clear that he cares about his students, the material, and teaching the students without killing us. One of the best (if not the best) Professors at umass. He's young, and thats a good thing. Imagine a professor who is actually in touch with his students....

Expects strong background but if background is weak, will teach everything and gets really invested in the students' learning because instructor was an undergrad not too long ago and knows the struggle. Course nature requires a lot of reading or extensive learning from experience (by trying it yourself). Math-heavy but come on it should be for ML.

One of the worst professors i've had. Rushes every topic and he thinks you know as much as he does so lectures are extremely fast and confusing. You'll be better off learning by yourself because Cox won't do that for you and you'll be lost with so much content. Avoid him at all cost, i taught myself everything.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Lots of homework--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: He is very nice and always willing to help if you ask
I really liked his lectures; I felt he explained concepts well without just jumping straight into problems. Other than that, very similar to other calc courses.

Genuinely do not take 223 with him. He is a nice dude, but his lectures do not help at all. He goes off topic every 5 mins and does not focus on the stuff we're learning right now. 90% of the time, his examples don't make sense, and he doesn't really explain the concepts first. Homework is a lot at times. You're better off taking another professor.

The most annoying professor I've ever had. Went on some BS tangent in between every step of every single problem in class, and would skip necessary sections to make up for time lost yapping about the University of Delaware. I spent most classes going through the textbook version of what he was "teaching" and did fine, get ready to teach yourself.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Lots of homework

reviews.comment: He is very sweet and kind. Go to SI sessions as those are very helpful. Some of the homework and quizzes are different than what he says in class but if you took calculus in highschool its basically all the same things.

Great man, but terrible professor. Lectures don't really give insight into how to understand the concepts and most of the time I don't understand what he's talking about when going through the examples. The discussion sessions are a lifesaver though, but otherwise, I'd choose a different professor for multi.
His lectures do not help you learn at all. He does not explain things well and gets off topic a lot. Everything is online until the final exam. I feel like I barely know anything. Do not recommend.

I was signed with disability services to take my chem exam the same time as his class and he threw a temper tantrum and refused for me to take my chem exam the same time as his and in fact blamed it on me while it was disability services who picked that time for me. he also took forever to respond to my emails. HAS THE BIGGEST COMPLEX EVER.

He's very passionate and he cares about teaching the students, but sometimes the content of his lectures doesn't align with what we need for the class. His lecturing skills are solid, but you can tell many people get bored in class.

Moderate homework, weekly quiz in discussions, and pretty fair exams. It's definitely a course you can self study.

Mr. Cox is a great professor and the nicest dude ever. He wants all his students to succeed and always responds to emails in a timely manner. Attendance is mandatory but I found his lectures incredibly easy to understand and he explains things very well. Homework can be long at times but really help you understand the topic and do well on exams.

He's a nice guy, but not a good lecturer. His lectures are boring, and the examples shown in class aren't useful for homework and exams. Moreover, this is a mandatory attendance class. I learn more from the discussion session than the lecture itself. He responds to emails quite fast and is also accessible.

I went to a few classes at the beginning of the semester and then never went again. He isn't even talking about math most of the time. I have no idea what he's talking about. It's a waste of time. There's ALWAYS math homework due...but at least it's open note and quite easy.

The quizzes are online and you are given a second attempt for mini quizzes but the final exam is in-person. The TA sessions are useful if you're struggling but go slow. His way of teaching math isn't super clear because he just does example after example and the mini quizzes and chapter quizzes test more than just how to solve the equations.

Chris Cox is the funniest professor I will probably ever have. His lectures are very easy to listen to, and he is always willing to help students after class and in office hours. His lectures were also recorded and posted on canvas, which made it very nice.

Not a good teacher in the slightest. He doesn't use slides instead writes everything on his iPad and his handwritings hard to read. If you want to learn anything I don't recommend. Either skipped class or used the time to just learn the material on my own. Only good part is all the tests and homework are online except for final exam.

he was a nice prof but class taught me nothing. did fine on homework but them quizzes made no sense. only three questions on them too. textbook unhelpful. taught myself the class and I don't even like math. i feel like everybody struggled on final.

I took AB calc in high school so I thought the course wouldn't be bad, but prof. Cox doesn't explain anything clearly and would always go on stupid tangents in the middle of class. The mini quizzes were so random and the lectures did not help at all with getting a good grade on the homework or exams. My advice would be go to the TA office hours.

Not helpful at all, the lectures were long and usually he would go on tangents and never actually explain the topic clearly. Had to teach myself almost everything and the text book was not that helpful either.

As someone who had only taken a pre-calc class prior to this one, this was a very stressful class. I attended every lecture and never felt like I gleaned much from them. He's poor at describing concepts and he gets distracted mid lecture making them even more confusing. I ended up teaching myself most of the content. The textbook was also terrible.

Harder class if you don't have any calc background. I did end up teaching myself a lot of the material, but the textbook was kinda awful at explaining concepts. Still attended lecture despite not paying that much attention after the midpoint of the year. Notes are not posted until like the day before chapter quizzes. He seems like a great guy tho.

DO NOT TAKE!! Pros: everything is online except for the final exam, graded by many things: 15% mini quizzes, 40% chapter quizzes, 25% homework, and 20% final exam.
Cons: examples in class are limited and don't help you with hw or quizzes, final exam review sheet isn't helpful at all; class average was 60%. Professor doesn't explain concepts.

He's not a good lecturer for this class. You'll learn more on your own or by going to Cahill's lectures. Don't know how accessible or helpful he is outside of class. However, the class is very well structured, and the exams & written hw easy enough to get through if you watch the video notes on canvas and do the Wiley HW due same day as the final.

Professor Cox is a nice guy but the way he explained things made it more confusing. Additionally, there are 5 chapter tests worth 10 points each and getting a 7 or 8 can swing your grade by 5%; you basically need to ace every chapter test to get an A in the class.
he is a good teacher

do not take this professor if you didnt take calc in highschool. he is a very sweet guy and a nice person but a horrible teacher, esp if you dont know anything. i learned everything on my own. go to the si sessions because they teach you more in 30 mins than he does in a month.

Professor Cox is a great guy. He is super accessible outside of class and will email you back pretty quickly. The content of 331 is hard, however, I found the videos that Cahill makes (linked for every 331 section) to teach the content way better than any lecture from any teacher of 331. Lecture isn't mandatory, so I didn't go, but Cox seems good.

Nice guy but terrible lecturer, going to class made everything more confusing. Definitely don't recommend if you have no calc background. I learned everything from the textbook which also sucked, but still better than lecture. All homework and tests online except for the final which is the one in person assignment
This class was really difficult for me and pretty much everyone i knew in the class. i have been struggling through it but what i will say is professor cox is a really good guy.

Professor Cox's lectures tend to make the content more confusing. Had I not had a previous understand of the main concepts of calculus, I would be totally lost in the class. Also, often times he'll spend up to 15 minutes talking about the upcoming schedule. I stopped going to lecture, and found it more informative to take notes from the book.

Good guy, just a terrible lecturer. I took AP Calc and found myself more confused from his lectures than before. He seems to skip around and go on tangents. I missed quizzes many times and he always let me redo them with no penalty. If you have no calc background, i'd recommend a different professor. No regular exams so HW and quizzes really matter
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Caring--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: I'm sure he is a good man but he is not good at explaining concepts. Do not take this course if you haven't taken calculus in high school. If you took calculus in high school it will be easy to teach yourself the material.

He is a very kind professor, and very understanding if you talk to or contact him. That being said, he is sort of bad at teaching so I stopped going to lecture. They weren't helpful and I coasted on my previous knowledge. There are weekly quizes and chapter tests every few weeks all online. Careful though, one bad assignment can cost your grade.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Caring--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: While Professor Cox is such a caring and nice man, I personally didn't feel as if his lectures helped a whole lot. What mainly carried me was my previous knowledge in AP Calc during high school. If you don't know calc that well, honestly skip the lectures and just learn on your own. Other than that, there was weekly homework and quizzes.

He is not the best at teaching any of the material. If you've done Calc in Highschool it will be easy; if you haven't you will have to teach yourself. The class is easy though because attendance doesn't matter, quiz/test are all online, and multiple attempts on online quizzes. There is weekly homework though.

talked about nonsense, seems like nice guy but never on topic, i dropped the class because i wasnt learning actually anything. def need a tutor if hes ur professor. he talked about the wasp issue in the room for like 10 mins then killed one like tf.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Hilarious--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Prof. Chandramouli is one of the most dedicated and kind professors I have encountered at UMass, incredibly accessible, and very helpful in class and even more so in office hours. If you put interest and effort into the class, you will learn a lot from him.

explained in thorough detail and paid attention to problem areas. offered extra office hours and taught outside of class when we needed to make up time. sometimes a bit bland lecturing but still a very good teacher! ta was unfortunately not very good at explaining and would sometimes mess up or get bored and stop in the middle of a problem lol

He is a nice guy and really tries to make sure he goes over things but there's just so much content in 233 that it always felt like things weren't clearly explained. Attendance isn't mandatory always just once in 2 weeks (he will specify when) he took attendance for participation grade. If you can take the course chair or Cahill for this course.

He is actually a great professor and the TA's are really helpful as well you will just sadly get your s*** rocked by the exams. Attendance is mandatory every other Monday and you just sign a sheet. There is a lot of homework but that is the whole department, so like the exams, he can't do much about it. The quizzes help keep your grade up.
reviews.rating_tags: Clear grading criteria--Lots of homework--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Best math professor! He always will get back to you in a ridiculously small interval if you email him with a question and will fairly consider any disagreement with his lecture material and correct himself if even slightly wrong. That being said, he is very knowledgable. Intentionally searched this professor out for 331 as well.

M132, M233: Goes above and beyond to make sure all students understand and are provided for. Extremely detailed lectures, always gauges whether students are following, and responds to emails (typically very helpful and does whatever he can to meet request/answer question) almost immediately. Will be going out of my way to have him 3 sem.s in a row.

He made lectures worth going to because I felt as though I learned a lot in the lectures. Exams were most of the grade so it is important to study and go to extra help if necessary. Overall, he was good at teaching but the class was difficult so either pay attention or be ready to learn by yourself outside of class.
reviews.rating_tags: Clear grading criteria--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Great professor who goes above and beyond to make sure students understand him. He also does a nice job of defining what counts for what in our grades since the weekly quizzes didn't count for much of the grade, allowing students to calmly learn the material. Bear in mind, the course is difficult and will certainly require a lot of effort.
Best professor i've ever had. Always eager to answer questions and really cares that students understand the root of the material.

One of the better professors that you will have for Calculus at UMass. He presents the material well and provides examples that can be used to solve homework problems. Unfortunately, the bulk of your grade is with exams that are in the hands of unnamed TAs, who are some of the most unfair and unreasonable graders you will ever experience here.

Sathya was a great professor communicatively. He always replied to my emails within MINUTES, and was very helpful and caring when it came to issues I came to him for. I spent weeks with him doing out-of-class work to prepare for the final (about 3 weeks). The class was very hard though. The grading was harsh on tests. Do the homework truthfully.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Really nice prof who really wants you to do well. Lectures are well structured and you get a pretty decent understanding of the material by the end of the lecture.

Sathya is a really sweet professor who is very accessible via email and is willing to make extra office hours to accomodate students that have questions or need extra help. His lectures are taught pretty well; unfortunately they are not recorded but he does post notes so if you miss a class you can still catch up. Homework is very reasonable.

The lectures were good, and the TA was all right. If you do your homework, attend every lecture before the exam, and do every problem in the SI Session. The class is not that super difficult, but if you put in enough work(average 5 hours per week) and spend 20 hours studying before the test, you will get an A.
Not the most engaging lecturer, but definitely cares and puts in a lot of effort to make sure everyone understands!

Class material is dense and difficult but Sathya does his best in making it understandable and enjoyable. He is not responsible for making the class so he can't control the homework or exam content but is always suber helpful after class.

One of the best professors I've had so far at Umass. He is very kind and considerate of students and takes the time to answer every little question that is posed during the lecture. He makes this difficult course much easier. He is very helpful during office hours as well and is very understanding.

Sathya was by far the best lecturer I had for any math course. He was very willing to help students in need, and understood the struggles they went to. The class itself is very difficult, but Sathya was able to make it a bit easier to understand as the course progressed. He helped me understand Stoke's  Theorem during office hours very quickly.

Sathya is cares a lot to help his students understand. Out of all the math professors I've had, he's definitively one of the better ones. Calc 3 is a very hard class but he really helps you work through the problems and can answer any question you ask. He is very accessible outside of class.

Very understanding professor who was willing to move HW deadlines, posted extra practice questions that helped with homework, and was very accessible outside of class. You can tell he cares about how well the class grasps the material. The class is tough but I think every Calc 3 professor here is plagued by how difficult the material is to teach.

Great Professor with detailed lectures, will definitely help to attend and be attentive while he teaches, especially when he goes over Greens, Stokes and Divergence Theorems. Tough material, but he makes it pretty easy to understand the concept, although you still need practice.
reviews.rating_tags: Amazing lectures --Gives good feedback--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: He's a great professor! Very detailed lectures with tons of examples, and he posts all of his notes in case you can't make it to lecture. The way the course is designed kind of sucks and is really hard, but he really tries to get us to understand the concepts. Great guy, but tough material.

Teaches well. He posts handwritten notes that help immensely in homework. The exams are difficult even otherwise but I don't think it's upto him coz there are way too many instructors for this course so not sure who sets the exams. But overall a nice guy. Explains concepts well.

He is a really great professor. However, the way the course is designed is horrible. The work load is almost impossible to complete weekly. It almost like they designed it specifically for students to fail.

Really great professor is very empathetic, explains things well, often extends homework deadlines and genuinely cares about students and teaching. Attendance is not mandatory and detailed notes containing solutions to homework problems are posted.
Tests and quizzes are online and open-note at home. She does "in-class writing" once a week for attendance, but you can usually get someone to send the prompt to you if you aren't there
Love professor norton!! She is a great lecturer. Awesome if you just want to take a class to learn about nutrition and not be stressed about exams and coursework because it's very manageable.

Great professor! Easy class. Attendance not mandatory but there are random in-class writings, not difficult but annoying if you're looking to skip class. Online quizzes and exams, open notes. I recommend attending class as her slides tell you what are on the quizzes and you don't have to deal with missing a in class writing.

A great class to take for an easy gen-ed. Her class was honestly super easy but very interesting. The discussion assignments were kinda annoying but honestly super light. She had tests but online so super easy.

She was such a funny and chill professor def take this class. The only thing was the discussions and TA classes had a lot of work but it wasn't bad, those are mandatory but not lectures. Take this class lowkey easy just lots of online hw and you cant miss any or else your grade will tank. Professor is super nice class was never boring, useful too.
Easy. A bit of work but mainly doable and busy work. Not very accessible outside of class.
reviews.rating_tags: EXTRA CREDIT--Clear grading criteria--Lots of homework

reviews.comment: This was a very good and interesting class to take. Professor Norton teaches each concept very well. There are weekly quizzes that you can do on your own time. There are exams but they are take-home. There are also opportunities for extra credit if you need it. She is so understanding and a good/ personable professor.

Claire is very knowledgeable, passionate, and cares very much about what she teaches. A lot of topics are covered but the material is very easy to digest. Gives extra credit opportunities and exams are take home and open note with answers to questions in her class slides. Overall, a great course to take to learn a lot about nutrition.

This class is super easy, if you go to class you get an A+. She puts the test question answers on the slides and puts a little sun on the questions you should write down so you make sure you have all the right notes, and she doesnt just read off of the slides, she is educated. discussions are annoying but easy, arent they all tho.

Professor was rude to me when explaining something. I have a pretty severe disability that makes material pretty difficult to understand. Disappointed in how that affected how she treated me. Overall, it was a pretty decent class though.

This class is one of the easiest 3 credits you can get. Prof Norton is hilarious and she explains well what shes teaching and makes directions clear for exams tests etc. Tests are online and the only work assigned are work from the discussion portion (which you have time to do in class), weekly in class writings, and end of the week lecture quizzes

Prof Norton is a great teacher and this class is easy and low stress. She made learning about nutrition interesting and enjoyable and clearly cares about her students. Grade is mostly made up of a lot of small assignments that don't take long and all answers are in the lecture slides.

I had a heavy course schedule in terms of difficulty, and this class definitely helped me balance my demanding classes. Exams are easy, as the answers are in the slides. Very stress-free environment and super sweet professor.
Professor Norton makes the lectures engaging. With no need for a textbook and easy online exams, this is a great gen-ed class. I found unstuck ai helpful for quick review before tests.

Nice professor; clearly very passionate and knowledgable about her field and the topics that she teaches. Crams a good amount of information into the lectures, but posts majority of the slides. Online quizzes and tests. Overall, a really good intro class to learn about the topic without being overwhelmed by work.

This class was an easy gen ed, but watch out because she might make it harder. 4 online exams, and quick mini quizzes every week. The discussion class was kind of annoying, but overall easy work, Claire is super nice, just show up to class and you'll be fine. Easy A.

Easy class and Gen Ed. Take this if you want something easy. You have to be in class most days, but she drops two in-class writings and 10 absences. She is a bit political honestly, especially given current events... But if you can ignore that, it's fine.
Claire is so passionate and caring. I highly suggest this course. It is pretty easy.

Claire is so sweet and funny! The class is super interesting and easy. No essays, a few online tests that are open note, and some homework/discussion assignments with plenty of extra credit opportunities.

Such a good professor makes the lectures engaging. If you go to all the lectures and take notes you will get a good grade, the exams are online and take questions directly from the lecture slides. Weekly discussion activities for homework but they're easy and won't take more then an hour per week. Great class great professor would recommend

Claire wants you to understand the material in a stress free environment. That is why she is an easy grader - exams are all online. The discussion assignments are very straightforward and all take less than an hour to do.
No complaints, interesting material and all relevant.
Really solid class. Enjoyable and informational. Optional attendance, but definitely helps to go! Not a hard class, but busy with little assignments often. Easy to listen to during lectures.

Prof. Norton's lectures are both engaging and inherently useful. She makes clear the distinction between fact and speculation, and she will stop everything to make sure everybody understands an important concept. Her ideology is that "Students learn best when they are not stressed" which shows in her lax grading and straightforward assignments.

Professor Norton keeps the lectures entertaining. You don't need to buy the textbook and she gives Moodle quizzes that count for IClicker credit. She goes over the answers of the quizzes in class as well. Exams are online and pretty easy.

Pretty easy class. For me, all exams were online and pretty easy. The only thing is that you do not want to switch between the physical iClicker remote and the app, or you may not receive credit for your attendance. Professor is really nice.

Claire is an amazing Prof. I have to say this is the best prof in my whole life so far, she knows some of us only take the class for the sake of GenEd credits so she made the course as easy as possible for everyone. And indeed it is so easy. I am a slow learner but I got A+ in her class it is incredible.

Easiest gen-ed ever. Only mandatory thing are the discussions which are helpful bc you just do the weekly assignment during them. The lectures are on echo 360 and she literally marks the slides you need to write down/know for the exam. 4 online exams total, no cumulative final, all open note & found in slides/notes. There's extra credit every week

If you're looking for a bio gen ed, take this class! Professor Norton is a great professor and her lectures are pretty interesting, but not mandatory. Online quizzes are easy and she stars the slides that are going to be on them.Go to discussion every week and you'll pass. She makes it very easy to pass this class and there's lots of extra credit:)

This professor is the best. Her lectures are always entertaining and relevant to your own life. Lectures are not mandatory but highly recommend. She is really flexible. Tests are all online and a answers are easily found. Super easy credit and very little homework. All assignments can be done in discussion. Lots of opportunity for extra credit.

I love her teaching style. Many opportunities for extra credit and the homework is automatic 100% if you do the work (same with quizzes). Lectures are super straight forward same with exams. She makes sure you know exactly what will be on the exam and theres no trick questions. Would definitely recommend
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Clear grading criteria--EXTRA CREDIT

reviews.comment: easy Iclicker questions and quick writing responses during lecture for participation points. in lab you basically just do your homework assignments which are easy. exams are open note. she posts her lecture slides. many extra credit opportunities. she's very nice and her lectures are interesting.

The best gen ed! So glad I took this class it was very easy to pass and also super interesting. All in class grades had an online option if you couldn't make it to class, tests were open notes, and we did most of the weekly homework during the discussion. Lectures are also interesting she's a really cool person overall!

Claire is the sweetest professor ever and cares about her students. The class was an easy A if you put in work. Grades were based on 4 exams (40%), iClicker (8%), in class writing (7%), discussion participation (10%), and the rest is based on homework. iClickers could be done through moodle so attendance not mandatory. Would recommend.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Clear grading criteria--Caring

reviews.comment: This is the best class I've ever taken, I genuinely enjoy going to it. Claire is super sweet and a great professor. Her lectures are very interesting and she offers SO many extra credit opportunities. The discussions are fun and the assignments aren't hard. She specifies exactly what is going to be on exams by pointing it out during lectures

If you need a a BS GenEd, this is a no brainer. The class is somewhat interesting and is laughably easy. Lectures were option since you can do online quizzes instead of iClickers with multiple tries. Usually one assignment a week that is done during the discussion section which is mandatory. Exams online, super straightforward, and open note
Take this GenEd, easy A. The professor recorded all the lectures ahead of time and the weekly quiz answers were clearly stated in the videos. The exams were straightforward and easy.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Get ready to read--EXTRA CREDIT

reviews.comment: The class was extremely easy to get a good grade in, which was appreciated especially while learning remotely. She let us learn on our own time at our own pace, and I actually did learn some helpful nutrition tips. This is a great choice for your biological gened.

I took this for a gen ed requirement. I enjoyed the class and felt as though I learned a great deal. It was online due to covid and all of her lectures are uploaded on her Moodle. The homework is very easy to get through. Make sure you review for tests so that you can get an A.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Group projects--Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: by far my favorite class this semester. classes were online and lectures were asynchronous (due to pandemic), but i really did enjoy watching her lectures. there's a mini quiz after every lecture, but they were super easy. exams were easy as well, and were open notes (probably due to the pandemic as well).

Awesome prof! Wants to actually change your life with her class, not just be an "easy gen ed" (although it is that too). She is super interesting and encourages you to be critical and think for yourself - so popular she has to ask students sitting in who couldn't enroll in time to leave as Mahar as it gets too crowded!

easy A for gen-ed. i had her online and this was my fav. class because it was organized very well. asynchronous lectures so you watch whenever you want, she puts stars on what slides you need to write down and easy quizzes on moodle.

This class was so easy I accidentally got a 99 overall because I did more extra credit than I needed to. You'll also learn some pretty interesting things about nutrition. My only complaint is discussion sections were quite useless and an overall waste of time.
EASY A.

You need to show up to class early to get a front row seat to be able to hear her. There are random writing assignments in the middle of the lecture that you get little time to do, and you can't rely on extra credit to get a good grade anymore. The discussion section is where you get nagged by the TA to do meaningless group work.

Easy class to get an A in. Exams are easy if you go to the review session the day before. Lots of easy ways to earn extra credit. Don't really have to pay attention in lecture as they are posted to moodle. Most kids are not focused during lecture. Show up to section and do the homeworks with care. I had a horrible TA and still got an A.

I barely went to lecture and did just fine. Claire is a amazing caring professor who teaches a great class. As long as you do the homework and quizzes (open book) you'll get an A. Lots of extra credit opportunities (take them). Don't buy the textbook or Pearsons. Tests are easy as long as you study the notes and do the quizzes.

This course is super easy A. The moodle practise tests are very helpful for all midterms. There's no final. Attendance for discussion is mandatory, and you can earn 5% extra credit. You should show up for in-class writing assignments. A very fun and light class :)

Keep in mind this is a bio course. I took it expecting to just learn about how to eat healthy but its mainly about the actual biological affects that food has on your body. Overall not a hard course, lots of study guides online and she provides lots of extra credit opportunities. From what I've heard its one of the best bio gen eds offered.

Claire Norton is a FANTASTIC lecturer. She is super organized which is huge for me and explains everything so well. Her exams are so easy, taken right from the lecture notes. She gives SO much extra credit. There's literally no way to fail the class with the amount of extra credit she gives. Go to grocery store tours you'll learn a lot there too.
reviews.rating_tags: Accessible outside class--Participation matters--Beware of pop quizzes

reviews.comment: Pretty easy class and the material is interesting. I really liked learning what to put in my body and understand the topic at a deeper level.

Claire is a great professor and if you study for the exams they are easy. There was a textbook but I never bought it and was fine. There is extra credit iClickers but I also never did those and got an A.

Claire is by far one of the best teachers at UMass. She is funny and caring and really wants all of her students to do well. Even though this class is an easy A, it is very interesting and you will learn a lot. The discussions are dumb but the class itself was enjoyable. I would retake this class if I could.

Claire is by far one of my favorite professors. She is hilarious and tells you exactly what you need to know. She reviews material enough (+ discussions) that you barely have to study for exams. Super easy course, highly recommend.

Claire's class is great. She loves what she does and has an amazing passion for nutrition. Her notes are very clear and she specifies what you should be reviewing for each exam. Tons of extra. Really good Gen-Ed/GPA booster.

Very easy BS gen ed, if you show up to class and put in minimal effort you will get an A. I have always been bad at science but this class was fairly straightforward and is stuff you will actually use in real life. DO THE GROCERY STORE TOUR! Exams are similar to the practice exams and are all multiple choice.
reviews.rating_tags: LOTS OF HOMEWORK--Clear grading criteria--EXTRA CREDIT

reviews.comment: Although the material was pretty interesting and easy to understand, I didn't enjoy Claire as a professor and lecturer. Claire gives a lot of extra credit opportunities to her students and grades are dropped. Attending lectures was extra credit, but there were in-class writing assignments that counted as a grade. Exams were like the practice exams.

Pretty good - the semester I had her she changed some stuff so it was a little bumpy having her needing to iron out some kinks as we went through it, but she does things like drop lowest in-class grades and gives a variety of extra credit options so even if you have a hard time on tests you can get a good grade. Text was mandatory for quiz access.

Claire is very knowledgeable and genuinely cares about her students. She is always open to feedback, and she makes her lectures as relatable as she can. I ended up learning a lot from her lectures. She makes it really clear what is going to be on her tests, and they were all pretty easy and straightforward. Overall a good, fair class.

Not the worst way to get a gen ed. Material is pretty interesting, but I didn't learn much in lectures. The discussion has small projects that are really easy. The best part is that she offers a lot of extra credit! Very easy to pass even if you zone out in class.

Norton changed the curriculum this semester to make it more science-based with a new textbook. Her lectures are dry, preachy, and sporadic. She'll find a way to complain about anything, and is extremely unclear with her grading criteria. This class may have been good before but it has changed for the worse.

Not really sure why people rate her so high, she's fine but nothing special. She comes across as very "mom" to me so maybe that's what I found weird about lecture? I actually would have enjoyed class more if it were more cut and dry info exchange. Easy mandatory discussion, but the book is required now because there is work hosted through that site

I honestly thought I was going to fail the class because I failed my first two exams (76 and 66). However, I somehow passed the last exam with a whopping 94 and enough extra credits to pass the class. This class is interesting and there is a lot of information, but if you study on her slides you would honestly pass. Discussion is so easy.

Highly recommend this class and Claire to literally anyone. Easy to get an A if you pay attention, which is not hard to do. Claire makes the class super enjoyable as she is hilarious and super passionate about nutrition. I enjoyed listening to her lecture and she gives tons of extra credit. Overall a great class and even better professor.

She's greta! I actually learned helpful real world things about nutrition which is amazing considering I only took it for a GenEd. I highly recommend it to anyone who isn't great with science but needs to fulfill the BS requirement. One of the easiest A's I've ever taken while not being a total joke of a class.
Easiest gen ed class you can take. You can get C's on all three exams and still get an A in the class with all the extra credit. Highly recommended

This is honestly one of the best classes I've ever taken. The material is interesting, important and Claire does a fantastic job of making it easy for everyone. It's impossible not to get an A with all of the extra credit offered. Loved it.

This is honestly one of the best classes I've ever taken. The material is interesting, important and Claire does a fantastic job of making it easy for everyone. It's impossible not to get an A with all of the extra credit offered. As long as you do the homework (which is really easy) and go to discussion, it's the easiest class you'll ever take.

She offers a ton of extra credit and as long as you study the starred slides, you'll be fine for the exams. She makes the class interesting and you even get extra credit for using your iClicker in class.

Easiest class you'll take. She gives so many opportunities for extra credit that you would have to try to not pass this class, even just showing up for lecture is extra credit. Discussions are mandatory though.

Claire highlights exactly what will be on the exams in her lecture slides. She gives easy 5 question Moodle quizzes each week, 3 homework assignments, an essay and 3 non-cumulative exams. Most of the discussion section grade is based on attendance, with two group projects.

Professor Norton is wonderful. She is extremely passionate about Nutrition - especially eating disorders - and makes the topic very interesting and accessible. She also even says herself that you basically just have to show up and put in extremely minimal effort to get an A in the class.
reviews.rating_tags: Respected--Skip class? You won't pass.--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: Enjoyable class. Impossible not to get an A if you show up and just pay attention to the lectures.

As long as you pay attention in class and study the material that Professor Norton marks as important, it is very easy to get an A. The final exam is not cumulative and the material is interesting and useful. Great class! The professor is funny and I definitely would recommend taking it with her.

This class is a joke. There is so much extra credit it is almost impossible not to get an A. I failed the final, and got a C and a B- on the two mid terms and still got an A. No other class you should be taking as your BS gen ed.

Easiest A at UMass. Marks slides that pertain to exam questions, followed by sample exam questions. Three non cumulative exams that are no brainers. Exams Qs are also taken directly from exam prep quizzes. Attendance is extra credit. Discussion is attendance based. Take this course if you're looking for an easy 4 credits.
This class was super easy and I learned a lot! Her lectured are very interesting.

Professor Norton is an awesome teacher! She really wants the students to do well. The final isn't cumulative. All of the exams are multiple choice and based on questions we've already gone over in the semester. Definitely take this class if you need an easy A. Plus the material is super interesting. Great class. A lot of extra credit!
great irish lady. easy A!!!!!!! why not take an easy A course? just go to lecture to get extra credit and it's just memorizing common sense material.

Claire is the absolute BEST teacher I've had here. She gives a ton of extra credit, her class is clear and easy to follow, you can skip pretty much whenever you want because what she covers is really easy to catch up on, and on top of it she's so funny and really just wants everyone to understand the material. The exams weren't difficult either.

She is a great professor and the reason why I am now a nutrition major. She cares about her students and her lectures are interesting. The class is an easy A and nothing is too bad. Would definitely recommend her.

She was a great professor, easy A class, long lectures but they were interesting so I would recommend showing up because she stars the slides that will be on the exam. All slides on moodle. The exam is 50 questions multiple choice and there are three of them and a couple readings and homework but nothing too bad.
Easiest gen ed i've ever taken. Mid term and final are both easy, and she gives out in class extra credits.

She is intelligent and passionate about her work. She puts a star on the pages of her power points that you will be tested on, but if you do not come to class you won't know which ones were starred because when she posts them online they do not have stars. Lectures are amazing, discussion sections stink with TAs and are good only if have her!

Claire is so sweet and she really wants you to apply what you learn in class to your life. She realizes that most of us have to be there, so she tries to keep it fun and lighthearted. The class is pretty easy. I went to about half of the classes and I am on track for an A. Attendance helps, especially because she offers extra credit.

The lectures were terrible to get through I would fight to stay awake every time. She is very sweet and hilarious and there is only a midterm and final with 50 mc each. They can be confusing with 5 choices, always with "all of the above" and things like "a and c only." I skipped a lot of classes and did fine. She doesn't check attendance

Definitely my favorite course at Umass thus far. Lectures are sometimes boring, but usually quite interesting and relatable to life. Nicest lady ever and is so passionate about Nutrition. A lot of students skipped a lot of classes and did fine, I did not skip any and got an 100 for the course. Some homework, midterm and final are 50 EASY multiple c

Claire is super helpful. Marks slides that need to be known for the test. 3 homework assignments that are very easy. Weekly readings and mini quizzes that are a breeze & 3 online tests (you can use your notestextbook and have 3 tries) Very easy A,  Need to study to pass the exams. Attendance is suggested but not mandatory.

Professor Norton was very nice, but her lectures were very long. I would suggest attending lecture, especially since she has many extra credit opportunities that she does not announce beforehand. Discussion was great, but sometimes felt too repetitive. I heard this class was easy, which is why I took it, but I definitely worked for that A.

I am a Nutrition major, and taking this class was just a confirmation of why I chose my major. I always got so excited to take this class, I loved it. It really changed the way I look at food and taught me to really pay attention to what I am putting into my body. Easy A. Few Assignments, Easy class.

Easiest class to take if you're looking to fill a Gen-Ed. Only two tests but they are pretty simple if you study. You get a lot of extra credit opportunities so you can easily get over a 100. If you show up to class and discussion there's a really good chance you'll get an  A.

I just finished Claire Norton's Nutrition 130 class. It was, to say the least, one of the best classes that I have even taken. Even if she was teaching dull material, her hilarious sense of humor made it more than bearable. She gives three exams, which can get tricky at times, and a bunch of online quizzes that allow retakes and are fairly easy.
Don't buy the book-you don't need it at all. I thought it was an awesome class that taught useful information I'll use for the rest of my life, but it was also really easy
She is great!. very funny and understanding. just do your work and you will pass. easy A

Claire is super funny. Especially with her cute Irish accent. I learned a lot of stuff that interested me. It was a lot of content, but it was clear cut what we needed to know for exams. I recommend for Biological science gen-ed
If you show up to class she tells you exactly what's on the exam, it's just up to you to memorize it. The final is not cumulative. An easy BS gen ed if you're not a science person.

Super nice professorAlways takes questions and isn't condescending about them. Wants you to actually learn what she is teaching, and knows what she's talking about. Likes to relate to everyday life examples in lectures. There are random in-class extra credit chances so going to class is helpful.
Super easy class. She puts stars on all the important slides to make studying easier.  Easy to listen to.

Super easy class. I took it to fulfill my biological science gen ed and I would definitely recommend it. Easy quizzes online. Attendance not taken but it's pretty helpful especially for extra credit. Must go to your discussion but they aren't bad. Midterm was easy. I would definitely recommend this class for an easy gen ed.
She is just very nice and goes slow for everyone

I LOVED THIS CLASS. I took it to fulfill a gen-ed, but it is also a great life skills sort of class. Lecture is not mandatory, but she gives out 10 pts of extra credit over the term for attending, plus she highlights exactly what she wants you to know on the ppt.  Tests cover a lot of material, so be prepared to memorize. Final was not cumulative.

One of the best class I've taken on campus. I didnt expect much of it but I left the course actually putting label-reading skills and nutritional info to real practice. Prof. Norton is passionate about what she teaches and it shows. Interesting videos are always shown in class. Relatively simple coursework! HIGHLY RECOMMENDED CLASS!
Easiest class on campus. Don't but the book.

Possibly one of the best professors I have ever had. Not only are her lectures extremely clear and engaging, she is always open to answering questions and giving extra credit. TIP: GO TO LECTURE! She stars slides she wants you to know and you will get an A if you go, trust me. Highly recommend, Claire is the BEST!

This class can be very boring and she is all over the place. She is nice and she explains what she wants you to know for the exams, but they are still tough because they are on a lot of information. There is a good amount of work the first couple weeks, but after that there isn't much. Discussion is mandatory. In the end, an easy class.

Claire Norton is a awesome lady. She is always trying to figure out ways to get students to do well, especially the ones who attend classes. Her classes are interesting. I think my attendance helped but a lot of people don't go and still do good. I missed 4 or 5 and still expect an A. Discussion attendance is very important, its work 25% (or 20)!!

Great and relevant intro to nutrition class. A Gen Ed class that I actually felt was relevant and useful, she touches on a broad swath of information and makes it readily available for tests. Somehow 400+ person lectures aren't boring w/ her. Take this class! Thinking about pursuing a nutrition minor after this class
All over the place, but easy. Only a midterm and a final. Online quizzes, but so easy.

I didn't like this class too much at the start but the subject matter became more interesting later in the course. Claire is very nice, and you should attend lecture for the extra credit. Discussion is worth 25%, and is an easy 100 if you go. Two multiple choice exams. Put a good effort in and you shouldn't get less than an A.

Class was so easy. Lecture isn't mandatory. Professor posts all the slide shows online so if you are good at studying on your own then you don't even need to go to class. Only some homework but they are really easy. Professor Norton is really nice and can be funny at times. Sometimes spends too much time talking about material that won't be on exam
Easy class. If you go to lectures, she will tell you exactly whats going to be on the exam. The material is easy and as long as you study you will be fine.

This is a great gen-ed. You don't have to go to class, but her lectures are very clear and she clearly states what is on each exam. Weekly online quizzes, 5 lecture quizzes, and two exams are all very easy. Love her Irish accent, too. Definitely take this class!
Loved her class. She genuinely cares and makes it interesting and easy and enjoyable to learn.
Easy class. Material is easy and common sense. Just go to class for the extra credit, and review all the material before the midterm/final and you will be fine.

She's very clear with what she wants you to know for the exam, the only thing that really sucks is that exams are 50%, so don't screw up. You definitely do not need the book if you go to lecture and you don't need lecture if you have the book.
Professor Norton is the best!

in class she goes over the ppts she puts online but go to class to get the extra credit and the special test questions she doesnt put up.discussion easy, tests little hard but its can get A if you go to discussion+participate. for the tests, look over the review questions. make sure you do the quizzes on time. guaranteed 100 since you get 4 tries

Easy class, lectures are online, exams are easy, attendance for lecture isnâ??t mandatory. Donâ??t buy the textbook. 3 homework assignments, weekly reading quizzes, 5 lecture quizzes, 1 essay. Attendance to discussion is mandatory. Discussion can be good or bad depending on your TA.
Very sweet woman, VERY easy class.  All of the quizzes and slides are online and the exams are almost EXACTLY what is written on the slides.  Great way to fill a gen-ed requirement with an easy A.
Really great teacher, loves what she is teaching and the class is very manageable! If you do the work and go to discussion your golden!

I love her. She is such a good professor. She really shows that she wants us to learn and understand the material. I always went to lecture and I got an A on the midterm. Just go to class, it's easy and interesting, and you'll understand everything. Also, discussion is worth 25% of your grade so GO! It's a really easy way to keep your grade up.

she's probably my favorite professor ever. you don't need to go to class but she gives extra credit to those that do. exams are really easy if you study. go to discussion! i'm a nutrition major so i like this stuff but it's a good gened, and she's funny too. she knows her stuff

EASIEST GENED EVER, easy A, never opened the textbook once at all for the whole entire semester. She gave out 8 extra credits in one semester, just make sure go to the lectures, go there play your phone, study for other class, do whatever you like. exams are easy to study from her online notes, one short essay required only (500 words)

Interesting and easy. Go to class, you get extra credit. Listen when she goes over the review questions- that's all the exams are on. Sometimes confusing in class, but overall, great professor, good class, EASY A if you do your work (DON'T BUY THE BOOK!)

She is SUCH a sweet lady. Class can be boring at times and you will see fewer kids show up as the semester moves forward. However she cracks a few jokes here and there which can make it fun. You often get extra credit for coming to class and her lectures, though right from her notes, are helpful when you start to study for exams.

Claire is the nicest prof ever. I loved her class and she made it really enjoyable. The class and material were wicked easy, but she still made it interesting. If you do all of the (easy) work, you can get A even if you do badly on the exams (also easy though). Go to review sessions they are very useful. DIscussions were pointless but mandatory

Loved this class. extremely easy to understand, and really good, useful information. prof was funny and really nice, and she made lectures entertaining. easy A, just look over the lectures online and take the quizzes till you get a 100- you have 4 chances for most of them. highly recommend this class.

I've been to one lecture, the first one, and I shouldn't have even gone to that one. Literally the easiest Gen Ed out there.. Discussions last about 20 minutes, everything is online, and exams are 50 multiple choice. Just go to the review and you'll be fine. EASY A.. you should def. take it

Wicked easy class. Her midterm and final are based directly off the slides, and the quizzes on spark give you four tries to get all the answers right. when you view your submission it tells you what page of the book the answers on... so easy. as long as you go to discussion and do the work, you'll get an A.

an easy gen ed. you will get an A. you only need to attend the discussions. the topics learned in class are easy and common sense. the professor explains everything clearly and the lecture is based on the slides which are all available on spark.

Class is really easy, professor is nice. Just go to the discussions, the lectures are really not necessary. I didn't go to lecture all semester and still ended up with an A in the class. Class requires little time/effort. Would definately recomend this class. Also, DO NOT buy the textbook...didn't use it once such a waste of money!

Go to the first class and discussion. That's it. If it's required don't worry about it- it's just a pain in the butt. But you can get an A.. easily, study learning outcomes/review questions on the slides before midterm/final, do online stuff. A, done.
It's an easy class. She explains everything exactly how it is on the slides so there really is no use to go to lecture.

Easy A. Professor is extremely nice and goes out of her way to make sure everyone can get all the online quizzes and assignments done. There is a lot little quizzes and assignments but they are EXTREMELY easy and require little effort. Definitely recommend this class.
lol

Literally the worst teacher I have ever had.  She's a complete joke and has no idea how to teach.  However, this class is extremely easy and requires barely any effort.  You can fail the final and still end up with an A.
She is pretty easy. Just do the online quizzes/homework til you get 100. Slides are online. She provides study guides

Easy A. I went to class about 6 times all semester and ended up with a B+. The notes are all online, and she can't figure out how to work PRS so it's not necessary to go. The discussions are every other week and even though the homework seems like a lot most of the TA's give everyone a 90 or above on the assignments.

This is such an easy class. I didn't go all of the time and still got an A. She's very nice and willing t help students with any questions. Exams are easy if you study and tere's a lot of extra credit. Take the class, it's worth it!
Good teacher

the class is pretty easy. at first she used PRS's but then she stopped so a lot of people stopped going to class because she puts the notes on SPARK. the homeworks are easy, shes not a bad teacher, just new at it.

I loved this teacher, she was very nice and understanding. Honestly, I felt bad for her because it is her first year teaching and she is stuck teaching a Freshman class who are very rude and inconsiderate; they are people who really do not care. I would recommend this class, easy GenEd.

She seriously is a joke. She wasn't prepared for our first test in Mahar which is HUGE how didn't she know that. Personally she seems like a nice person but academically she isn't the best. She avoids questions and literally says "i don't want to answer that with the wrong information"  ????

this lady is a joke. she's this little irish lady and i don't think she really knows how to use her computer. anyways, the class is easy, there is extra credit, drops the lowest test, and only 4 HW's. good gen ed to take. study the slides for the tests and youll be good, all the slides are on spark so if she doesnt do PRS dont go to class.

Good gen ed. Lectures are all slide shows,and she puts the slides on SPARK.She used to make attendence mandatory with the PRS, but when people started getting sick with swine she stopped.Discussions are only every other week, and there are a total of 4 easy HWs.There are 4 tests, and she drops the lowest one.The tests are pretty easy,50 multichoice
Disrespectful and discouraging

If you truly want to learn something during grad school, take 689 with this prof. Both the lecture and the homework content were amazing. 689 is definitely going to take significant effort, and it assumes that you cover the necessary basics. However, the delivery of this challenging content was pretty good (provided you know your basics).

Transitioned to a fully online project-based course which helped to focus on core concepts and learning as opposed to exams and quizzes. One TA didn't explain concepts clearly, provided a confusing analogy, and when asked to clarify his explanation: "Sorry, I won't give you the answer. You'll have to figure out the solution for yourself."

Forced students to use his own library, whose syntax and usage weren't clearly explained. One of the TAs was really bad, made you feel dumb, and never told you if your solution was correct. I learned a lot, but I ended up spending significantly more time on this course than you typically would for a 3 credit one.

reviews.comment:
Only take this class if you're very comfortable with statistics and math. I can't emphasize that enough. Also be good at linear algebra and calculus. I'm very well versed in those fields but I can see why others are struggling and I would also personally struggle if I didn't know statistics well

HWs are easy if you know the math. Otherwise, avoid

Made this easy subject insanely difficult for no reason. Great TA, did most if not all of the work for the course. Absolutely unsympathetic to having deadlines extended. Assignments that take tens of hours that need to be completed within deadline or else its all for waste.

People will praise Tim Richards for not giving exams, but when Domke does the same thing but actually makes the assignments require the tiniest bit of effort, they'll scream bloody murder. Not to mention, Pangolin is 10x easier to use than base NumPyro. Be grateful. Your real issue is ChatGPT didn't see Pangolin in its training data.

I like how the course is structured and what materials are covered. However, the assignments often require knowledge not covered or partially covered in the lectures, which makes them time-consuming and sometimes too difficult as you have to learn it yourself. Yes, you learn a lot through the process, but the assignments are 100% of your grade...
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: People are just mad that they actually have to learn because he created his own package and can't use chatgpt. Lectures don't cover enough content though

Contrary to some beliefs - not a skill issue if the course is shambolic. Course staff is very condescending and never make you feel welcome. The instructor is heavily not involved. Questions on the homeworks (which account for all the grade) are dealt with as comments on his Notion page, or office hours with the TA which are full of snappy remarks.
Skill issue if you don't like him. Just adapt not that difficult.

No in-person/zoom lectures at all. He uploades his online videos instead. I never felt like I'm not learning anything to this extent. And I spend a lot of time to do hw. 

We're supposed to learn from office hours which are held by TA's and not him. If I ask a question about my code, I get vague answers instead of a help to find my error.

Forces his students to use the python library he developed in the homeworks, which means we have to learn it. Skims over content expecting students to know it. Not very inspirational. I don't like being a hater but take a different professor

he's a great lecturer and i did learn a lot of ml from him. i do have a feeling that he gave people random grades though. really shady grading policy and never gave back final exams. a lot harder than other professors who teach the same course. would avoid him if possible.

My biggest concern with this instructor is that, unlike most educators I have encountered, he displays utter disregard for his students and their learning experience. Beyond delivering the scheduled lectures which stimulate little participation, he is removed from the learning process and provides no feedback on assignments. Quite disappointed.

One of the worst professors you can take a course under. Never gives any practice problems to learn things. Assignments are not enough for what he asks in the exams. The grading is unfair. The professor keeps telling he cares about students but doesn't even want to share correct solutions of the quizzes so that they can learn from their mistakes.
He's a great prof who gives quality assignments and really makes you think conceptually. His ML course is out of this world!
