He provides study guides outlining the topics for the 3 exams (2 midterms 25% each, and a final 30%) and gives weekly online quizzes that are open note and open book. Attending lecture is important because there is little information on his slides, but attendance for discussions is not mandatory.
reviews.rating_tags: Lecture heavy--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: He's a nice guy and knows what he's talking about, lectures can get boring- I didn't go much- but the discussion was better and the TA was good. There are 2 midterms and 1 final, and then there are weekly quizzes (online you can use the internet). No homework, but overall kind of boring but its a fine class
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Lecture heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: His lectures are good but his slides are a little vague and confusing. He gives you a study guide of exactly what will be on the test. You'll have to study but you can definitely can an A on everything. Sometimes it's hard to figure out what he's talking about in his lecture and its often different from the study guide.

This class is early, but trust me, if you want to do well - GO TO CLASS. He asks questions on the exam based on things he mentioned in class. Probably one of the best Macro professors you will get at UMass. Tests have a lot of material though, so you definitely need to study and use the study guide that he gives you.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--TEST HEAVY

reviews.comment: Dolenc's lectures are great. He truly cares about teaching his students. There are 3 tests and online homework. The tests are challenging but doable. The test usually consist of three open responses and two problem solving questions. Go to class, take good notes, and pay attention and you will do great. Study for every test as well!
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Amazing lectures--Tests are tough

reviews.comment: Dolenc is a great lecturer. He will ask a question on a test that he mentioned in class so go, but he makes it worth while. He gives a study guide that tells you everything you need to know, so dont be dumb and look past things or it will cost you big. Overall, tests are easy and it is an interesting course. Highly recommend.
reviews.rating_tags: Respected--Skip class? You won't pass.--Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: Tests are just a few questions that require a one page essay for each. He gives a list of possible questions beforehand, so the most helpful thing is to go to discussions/review where the TAs go over what to know for each question. He describes material clearly in class, but slides lack detail.
reviews.rating_tags: TEST HEAVY--GRADED BY FEW THINGS--Would take again

reviews.comment: Class is informative, slides are minimal. Tests are hard and specific, essay style.

Really good in lecture, makes it interesting and easy to understand. Slides were minimal, so it is tough to go back and review the slides if class is missed. However, since its my 9am, I've slept throw it 3 or 4 times and every time was able to read the textbook and keep up. My favorite professor freshman year!!

Class can be a bit of a chore but is very manageable. His lectures are a bit all over the place but refrain from skipping class as his slides are bare. I would recommend sharing one textbook copy between a few friends, and ALWAYS do the online homework together. This way you can use trial and error to get 100% because the homework is weighted heavy
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--GRADED BY FEW THINGS

reviews.comment: Was a challenging class with 3 exams being 80% of the grade, but Prof. Dolenc was immensely helpful outside of class and really showed how much he cared for his students. Take him for Econ no question.

This class is most focused on the tests.  You have to study a LOT for the exams and basically pray you have a good TA since they're the ones who grade the exams.  I found discussions really helpful even though my TA didn't make them mandatory.  The online homework isn't bad since it's straight from the textbook.
reviews.rating_tags: Clear grading criteria--TEST HEAVY--GRADED BY FEW THINGS

reviews.comment: He conducts class very clearly and provides all the material you need to succeed. The textbook is required to get the access code for weekly online assignments with the answers easily found in the textbook. Most of your grade depends on three exams, all topics on these exams are provided on a study guide beforehand.
this class has 3 exams, as long as you good at taking exams, you will be fine. Professor Dolenc will sent his slides after class and i really love my TA!!

This is a very basic class, so expect to learn that much. Dolenc definitely know what he's talking about, and the lectures are very clear, if a little simplistic. if you go to the lectures and discussions, you'll be fine. Don't worry about buying the textbook, it's expensive and he doesn't use it. Good professor, not the most interesting class.
reviews.rating_tags: Respected--Clear grading criteria--GRADED BY FEW THINGS

reviews.comment: This guy is the man. Best econ professor ive had so far at UMass. Good lecturer and passionate about the material. Tests are easy.

Dolenc is a nice enough guy. Lectures are kind of pointless because the powerpoints are posted online. The homeworks are really easy and require minimal effort not very often. He also drops the lowest two scores. To do well on the tests, I just studied a ton and taught it all to myself the day before. Easy A.

The Econ 104 with Dolenc is very straight-forward. There are three exams (25%, 25% and 30%) and My Econ Lab assignments worth 20%.  The exams have four short answer questions and two calculation questions. However, he gives you a study guide for every exam and if you listen in class, the exam material is very accessible. I highly recommend Dolenc.

Dolenc is a very good professor. You'll definitely learn A LOT. You have to study for tests a lot too if you want a good grade. 2 midterms (25% each) and a final (30%). Homework was worth 20% and required you to read the book. The tests are mainly on lectures, but he'll definitely stick a question or two from the book or his readings on Moodle.

This class makes you get lots of preparation for the exams. You need to prepare enough before the exams to get good grades. You must go to lectures if you want to understand materials based on professor's lectures. Nothing helpful on PPT.

I had Professor Dolenc in both 103 and 104. He is very clear on the material and gives clear examples to help you understand. He is there to help you learn and warns you about what is most likely to be on the exam and his uses study guides. Homework isn't awful, reading helps.

Professor Dolenc has been one of my favorite professors so far at UMass. He explains concepts in ways that are easy to understand, and clearly outlines everything you will need for exams; just study from the study guide and you'll get an A no problem. Attendance at lectures discussions isn't mandatory, no papers or projects. Learned a lot.

Professor Dolenc is great; He's personable, easy to learn from, and knows more about his subject than a high of majority of teachers will do. If you are taking Micro or Macro, I'd recommend trying to enroll in it with him.
Professor. Dolenc teaches the material very clearly and you do not have to go to class. I went to two class and got an A. Just take notes on his powerpoints on Moodle and you'll be fine.

The tests count for a lot of your grade, so study hard. Also, if you don't do the textbook readings, you'll be lost. That being said, Professor Dolenc is a really nice guy, an engaging lecturer, and a teacher who genuinely wants his students to do well. Don't skip the lecture because the online slides barely have any info, and be nice to your TA!
I won't say you can get A that much easy. But if you work harder before the exam, you will be fine. Only three exams for a semester, no pop quiz, no paper, no project.

His lectures are confusing because he tells random stories but he is a very nice guy and truly wants us to do well. Your TA's are extremely important because they grade and go over your tests with you so create a relationship with them if possible. He posts lecture slides on moodle but they are not detailed at all so attendance is important.

He is a great professor! If you have any interest in Economics you will not get bored in class. He gives great examples in class that really make the material easier to comprehend. Going to class and reading the book is really help with the tests because some of the questions he gives answers to during the class.

Class is very easy. Show up to lectures. Slides are online but contain little to no information. Exams are easy. You just need to memorize notes from class. He gives you a study guide of all possible topics on the exams. Homework is very minimal. Discussions aren't mandatory and are not needed to do well.

Dolenc was an amazing professor to have; his class is engaging and enjoyable. Homework is worth 20%, so it's easy points added to your grade. Lectures are posted online, however he goes much more in depth in class. He truly cares about his students and is very helpful during office hours. Tests are easy as long as you study the study guide!

Great Professor, he is about as straightforward as you can get. Attend class if you can, and try to do well on the homework. I didn't really give it much though when I could have easily done better.   STUDY for the tests too, they're worth most of the grade and he gives fantastic study guides.  Extremely engaging as well.

Professor Dolence was a really great professor to have to learn the basics. He spends time explaining and breaking things down so you're not just mindlessly plugging in numbers. His exams are very straight forward and the online homework is easy. Great professor, but beware of skipping classes, he only puts his guideline notes up on moodle.

His lectures are very interesting, and he can convey the topics with humor and clarity. His slides are posted online, but he gives essential information in lectures, and the discussion sections can help to solidify your understanding depending on your TA. He gives clear study guides for each exam which make studying a world easier. Don't skip.

Lectures help (and has stuff that shows up on the exams), so take notes. Exams are 4/5 open response and 1/5 other, and worth a good chunk of your grade. If you don't understand something, you can google it or ask your TA at discussion. Only get the online textbook if you need it: Ended up paying an extra $60 for nothing. Worth waking up at 8AM.

Tests are very straight-forward and fair, nothing like trick questions. Tests do have at least one question based on the reading, so it is best to read the textbook, but he goes over all concepts clearly in lectures. He presents real life scenarios to help gain understanding of big scale concepts on a smaller scale.

This man turned a dry subject rife with policies and money into an engaging learning experience full of lively examples and inclusion of the students in lecture. Not only does he teach very well, but he displays fantastic people skills like smiling, remembering the names of people in a +300-person class, and much more. Take his class!

Professor Dolenc is a great teacher! He is clear in his lectures, does not assign too much reading/homework and does not surprise you on the exams (he gives a study guide showing about 8-10 topics and picks 4-5 of them to go on the test). Highly recommend taking econ with him

Professor Dolenc gives great lectures, making everything clear and understandable. He is very personable and willing to help his students. Everything you need to know he puts on the study guide and doesn't add in any tricks or surprises to trip you up. You don't really need the book since it comes with the online code. Highly recommend him!

Great professor. He is very jolly and easy going. This class should be super easy as long as you either pay attention during lecture, or read the book. Class isn't mandatory, but discussion sections are and those help your grade just by showing up. Exam material is clearly told and should be easy if you use a study guideslides that are online.
Overall wicked easy, everything is straight forward, take notes in class and remember those for the exams and you're guaranteed and 100

Great class that he makes interesting. You don't have to show up to the lectures, but it will make the course and material much easier. Unfortunately, he no longer allows you to skip a question on his tests (although there is a study guide for each one). Drops some of the homeworksquizzes at the end of the semester.

BEST professor I've had so far. Clear, gives great and memorable examples, doesn't rush through things, interacts with the class in a fun way. Gives good feedback and definitely knows what he is talking about, engaging at all times. Attendance not mandatory but you need it to pass.

GREAT professor. Lectures are engaging and he puts a lot of effort in making key concepts clear with diagrams, real-life examples and mathematical problems. Exams are very fair and manageable as long as you invest some effort in reviewing lectures and reading the book. I wish I'd had him for Econ 103 too!

Took 103 and 104 with him, he's a great prof. If you have a friend in the class, the three hw assignments and studying for the 2 tests and final are a breeze. Everything is clearly explained in the powerpoints, which are online. Don't bother buying the textbook- just attend lecture and discussion and you'll do great
He explains things very thoroughly and in an understandable manner. 3 homework assignments, 3 exams. Great guy, easy class, highly recommend.

Took 103 with him so made sure I had him for 104. He truly does make this course an intro course and tries to make everything as clear as possible for you. Discussions weren't mandatory but were helpful if you didn't understand some concepts. The exams have no surprises because he pulls everything exactly off the study guide.

One of the better professors on campus. All his slides are online and he actually explains clearly what the topics are with good examples. Homework isn't that hard as it's all online but it does take some time to do it though. Exam are all basically straight memorization as he gives a bulleted list of about 10 topics to know for the exam.

He is a great professor! He is engaging and keeps class interesting. Class is not super easy but if you pay attention its not hard. He gives a very helpful study guide and if you actually study you should do well. Going to class is helpful but not necessary. I had him for 103, and he was so good that I made sure I took him for 104. Highly recommend

Great guy, great class.  Has a powerpoint lecture each class, which is also available online.  Homework was through Person MyEconLab.  Provides a complete study guide with 10 or so concepts to master before the test, and only 7 of them are on the test.  Final is cumulative, but its only the bullets on the study guide that weren't tested.

His lectures and explanations are very clean and concise. If it wasn't clear the first time, he'll use some form a metaphor or story to prove his point so that you do get it. Exams were straight off of material summarized on study guide. Discussions aren't really mandatory; they're just  a reiteration of what was said in class, but good for review.

Dolenc is really nice! He made an 8AM less painful. His slides are clear and easy to understand and he posts them all incase you miss class. He gives a study guide for every test thats very straightforward and you will get an A if you study it. LOVE him.

This class could be easy if you just do the work, he explains everything in class and even does problem solving that isn't on the power points which is helpful. He isn't that bad of a teacher but when his voice cracks you want to get up and leave but that can all be ignored with lots of effort and training.

Go to class, use the study guides and go to discussion to pick up tests. This class is incredibly easy. The online homework bears no resemblance to the actual tests. It would be very difficult not to get an A in this class.

He made an 8 AM class pretty easy to go to. Very clear in class and makes the notes as simple as possible to explain the concept. Gives you study guides with everything that will be on the test so there's no surprises. His TA's aren't the best but the class is impossible to fail.

Go to class, do the MyEconLab and you'll be set.  Fairly entertaining and clearly explains concepts.  Gives study guides for exams that make them impossible to fail.  He also posts every powerpoint online.  Overall, great class and professor.

This guy is great, he's entertaining, he delivers the information very clearly, and he's really straightforward about what's going to be on the exams. I wish more professors at this school were like this guy. If you review what's on the study guides, and do your homework, you will definitely get an A.

Makes an 8 AM class bearable and not boring. He is pretty clear in the lectures, and nothing is mandatory, not even the discussions. The online work kind of has nothing to do with the lectures/tests but it's all really easy.

the class is pretty easy for me, as long as you attend the classes and pay attention you will fully understand. the online assignment contains lots of questions and those are the ones he rarely talk in class. there are only 2 exams and a final. study guide is provided and it is very helpful. he will upload the notes on myeconlab as well.
Loved this class! He makes the lecture easy to attend. Study guides tell you exactly what will be on the exam!!

Professor Dolenc is an excellent professor. He is very engaging and makes a fairly dry topic (microecon) interesting and understandable. There are no surprises on the test, which is honestly all you can ask of a teacher. They are fairly challenging test but he does make sure you are fully prepared for them.
Highly recommend gives a study guide and everything no surprises on test
LOVED HIM...even though it was an 8 a.m. :(

Dolenc was a really nice guy. I am not at all interested in economics but I didn't mind going to his class. As long as you go to class and do the homework you will get a good grade. Also his study guides are normally identical to the tests.

Pat Dolenc is a great professor for Econ 104. He explains everything very clearly and keeps the lecture interesting. Study guides given for exams, and the exams themselves are very easy if you study. Discussion sections are unnecessary to attend as long as you go to lecture. Great class.

Pat is one of the better Econ teachers at Umass. Very good, clear lecturer and provides a study guide for exams. As long as you know everything on the study guide, you should do well. The book is needed for the Aplia code and to complete the Aplia assignments, which are fairly easy.
Best econ theory professor.  So clear with his presentations, his exams are easy but you really learn the material.

Pat is a great professor. He explains things very clearly and if you didn't understand anything, he will explain it in another way with examples. Tests were VERY straightforward. Really, as long as you go over the study guide and went to class, you will do great on the exam. Recommend!
Best teacher I have had for Econ. Great Explanations, great guy. Fair exams, no surprizes.

Really good at explaining concepts. Didnt take attendance but if you missed a class it threw you off.  Tests were based on your understanding which was tough but it was all on the study guide if you could figure out how to do it.
homework every week thats online. gives a study guide for every test so basically just find the answers and memorize them and you'll do fine. good teacher for macro

Although going to his 8 am was hard, i definitely recommend going to class because he explains the topics with good relatable examples you can use on the exams. he gives study guides before his exams so there are no surprises. study each topic on them and you will do great

Attendance was very optional for an 8am class. Missed about 60%-70% of the classes and pulled off an A-. Homework and discussions taught me the most, just copied notes from someone who went. Average professor.

Good guy. Gives good real life examples (not to be used on the tests). Aplia assignments don't always give the needed practice, so studying the book is highly recommended. The 8AM lecture isn't necessary, but never hurts.

Explains things really well. Sit in the front. Take good notes. Aplia homework is long but pretty easy. Tests require a lot of writing so you can't really BS your way through. You have to try but it's pretty easy. He never responds to emails. Look at study guide topics...all short answer questions are from there. Reading book is really important.
Do not take a class with him.

He's a pretty good teacher, really nice and explains the material well. The homework on aplia isn't too bad. The exams aren't too hard but you have to actually study for them using the study guide he gives you and notes in class. The discussions don't really help either.

He made the class really interesting.  In terms of exams, I don't think class is really necessary.  He gives a study guide before the exam, just make sure you understand the concepts on the guide, and understand the homework assignment for the math part of the exams. Had him for two semesters the classes were about the same. Light workload.

He's a pretty good teacher but sometimes there's a little bit of bias but this is an econ class so it's expected.  Only went to discussions for the exam portion.  assignments are just like exams so if you do well then your set.
Great teacher and really cool guy def reccomend for an easy class.

Professor Dolenc was a great teacher last semester. He keeps the class basic and easy to follow. Aplia sucks for hw but what can you do. Tests are easy in my opinion. You do have to make every lecture because he outs the slides online. However he can be interesting. I definitely recommend this class and Prof Dolenc as well

MacroEc.-he is very intelligent, however since he knows his material like the back of his hand, he expects you should too. He covers during class, if you skipped you might miss something he will put on a test.My TA was not really helpful but I heard others are. Tests are hard, only about half of what is on the S.G. is on the test. Study w/a partner

He's a pretty good teacher, uses good examples during class. He puts all of his powerpoints online eventually, which is AMAZING because attendance is not necessary.. especially for an 8AM. His test and exams are kind of hard though.. and the short answers are worth alot so you really need to know what you're talking about. Not a bad class choice

Nice guy, gives useful examples. Wants students to do well. Aplia sucks and will bring down your grade. Exams are straight foward and fairly easy to study for (just don't leave it to the last minute). Overall a very interesting class with real world applications. Nice introduction to financial markets.
Friendly guy except for the fact that i hate him due to 4 hours a week of hw
Great professor learned a ton should go to class he explains concepts well and tests are very easy
I didnt think the lectures were helpful.. uses aplia and the questions are straight out of the book.. my TA sucked so it sucked even more... test are difficult to study for.
He is the best professor at umass. I loved this class and thought he did an excellent job teaching it. You need to go to class, because the textbook just does not cut it.

Nice guy. Vague lectures. Wasn't very clear on subject matter. Overall I did not enjoy the class and would not recommend it. If you study its not too difficult to get a good grade but it took forever to get my test grades back.
I hear he is the best for 204.  If you go to every single class, its not that hard to do well.

Didn't go to any classes after Spring Break and still got an A...Lectures are dry, Discs are pointless, exans were do-able and Aplia's were kind of hard. If you take Micro or have had any Macro before you shouldn't have a problem. He cancels a lot of lectures because he teaches at another college. My TA was horrible but I heard that Mark S was good

Guy is a very fair teacher. He left 7 pages of the final out by accident and ended up giving us free points for the sections he forgot and he weighted the easy essay to be worth a lot. Let us drop lowest exam score too. Interesting class.
Worst teacher ever! don't take a class with him, hw is very hard and has nothing to do with class material. Discussions were uselss.
awfulllll teacher. seriously so bad. avoid taking any class with him if you can. he puts materials on the tests that we never went over and the TAs are AWFUL

Go to class, go to class, go to  class. Straightforward and engaging lecturer, and one of the better intro econ classes. Course may be difficult to those who don't attend class, but for those who go, he hints at what readings, notes, etc will be on final, and often gives answer questions to essays in class. Just go!

concidering that the material that a 204 class has to cover (which sucks a phat one...) doc does the best he can, and actually finds a way to make it interesting. if you have to take this stupid class, make sure its with him, and o yea, never take it with karol heim or watever her name is.

Teachers material well. However, essay assignments are flawed and tests formats are bad, it's always 5 general essay questions. Entire grade is based on 3 tests and two essays and discussion participation = hard course to get an A in.
Excellent at realating material, very organized, fair grader.  Expects work but tests are fair.
Highly recommended.  Exam essay questions are given in advance.  Very fair grading system.  Interesting lectures.
Great teacher.  Really knows his stuff and cares if you learn it.  Top notch.
Marxian Economics would have been alot harder with this guy
Test based grade. No homework. lecture was fast, based on examples and kind of unorganized. Lab was easy and fun.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Lecture heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Professor Irschick is a phenomenal lecturer. He is so engrained in the field of mammalian biology, I could not imagine anyone else teaching this course better.

Irshick is an amazing professor.  He really does expect u to work hard and is a one of a kind kind of guy...he really provides the kind of material that one expects when taking a class.  Study hard!!  He will talk to you and does his best!  You should do the same...

This class has 2 parts, the 2nd taught by Irschick. I liked the 1st half & grading was easy however it completely changed when he took over. He gives good feedback on summaries but grades harsh. Showing up is not enough to get a good participation grade from him. He didn't curve the exam (Gerson did). Overcomplicated everything & ruined my grade.

Duncan is super passionate about animals and his research and biology as a whole, which is the main draw of his class. He also stresses how important coming to class and putting in effort is, which it is. This class is deceptively hard. The labs are great and he put a ton of effort into them. Duncan just isn't very personable or human.

Duncan is a fantastic prof. He clearly cares about students and makes the class so fun. He gives a lot of feedback on your primary literature summaries and the lectures are 25 min. The only thing is that his slides are mostly pictures so you have to listen carefully to what he says for the material. The exam was ok(75 min for 10 short answers).
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Get ready to read--Caring

reviews.comment: A great person. Really cares about his students. This guy is a genius and is pretty funny too. Take this class, you wont regret it!

One of the most clear and cogent professors in the department - whats really clear is that he REALLY cares about the students and is willing to spend a lot of time with you to ensure that you fully understand the material. Really an amazing professor and person.

I REALLY liked this class a whole bunch - Dr. Irschick is really amazing, kind and generous - he is clearly one of the bext faculty in the Bio dept and really cares about his students! I highly recommend this class...

Really one of the most amazing professors in the world! I really loved his class - BIO 566 is really incredible and the grading is amazingly fair and well thought out - TAKE this class if its the last thing that you do.

In all my years of taking classes, its safe to say that his are among the best - a real gem - and last of all, his tests are super fair and a real treat to take - its definately an awesome class and one that i would take again anyday

Well all I can say is that its quite clear that this was an incredible and wonderful class with amazing clairty -the professor had remarkable vision and the ability to understand everyone and assign reasonable grades - take! take!
Incredible professor and so helpful
What an incredible class and professor.  He cares so much about the class and the students.  Really amazing person and teacher.

terrible class. Puts stuff on exams never discussed in class. This class used to be super easy but it is now a nightmare considering the only grades are the three exams. So messing up one and your grade is ruined. Also he said we would be graded on attendance even though its not on the syllabus?
reviews.rating_tags: Tough Grader--Skip class? You won't pass.--TEST HEAVY

reviews.comment: the three exams are your only grades.  so screw up one and you may as well drop the class. adds exam questions on stuff never discussed in class.  His research is cool
reviews.rating_tags: Respected--Skip class? You won't pass.--TEST HEAVY

reviews.comment: He is by far the best professor I have taken - and its not even close - his lectures are so interesting and so inspirational - take  this class now!
ONE WORD - incredible!!  AND AMAZING!  Would take him again any time - great person, lectures are so clear and fun!
He is absolutely one of the best professors who has ever walked the planet!!  He does SUCH an amazing job and is a swell person also!  His BIO 105 class is really awesome and he rocks!

All I can Say is he is a really nice guy who works really hard in class - I would say that everyone really seems to like him as a teacher!  His tests are fair and he is an incredibly inspiring professor!  Highly recommend!
The class is really easy but once you get bad points for the exams you loose your A. I wish there could've been more extra credits or in class notes

I could have done better in this class if I studied harder and did all the readings. I expected an easy A and that is not what this class is. I got 100s on all the quizzes and in class writing assignments and even on the essays, but the exams killed me They are so specific and even studying wont help much because there is so much random material.
wow!  I loved him as a teachers!!  He shows great examples and is an awesome person to boot!  Really works well with students and shows great examples...
Irschick is a very impressive teacher and really does an amazing job with BIO 105!  He treats the students well and does a great job!
The class is super easy but he rarely comes prepared. He just babbles through a generic powerpoint and shows videos to pass the time.
Irschick is one part of the professors that teach Bio 105. The guys enthusiasm comes across, he definitely loves what he teaches. Class is super easy too.
Had him for Bio 566. All i have to say, he is an amazing professor. His lectures are so interesting. And talking about exams, easy just study the lectures maybe a day before and you will ace it.
He is an interactive and totally fun guy who rocks like you cannot imagne!!
Amazing guy!  Incredible Professor who does a great job making the class fun and interesting!

Thought this class was going to be an easy A, (no textbook, lots of extra credit) but it was so boring that it could not hold my attention what-so-ever. Don't take it if you're not interested in biology there are other BS gen ed classes that can be taken

Professor Irschick Professor Podos is a really nice guy who, like most scientists, is sometimes a little awkward. His section of Bio 105 was an easy A. He did a great job of making science interesting to non science majors.

One of the best professors I have had at UMass!  He really cares about whether students understand the material and takes time to get to know you. He has so much interesting knowledge to share and an absolutely hilarious dry sense of humor.  Take this class.
Irschik is a really awesome professor who helps his student and knows how to connect.  He takes the time to get 2 know the students and is not too hard - HIGHLY recommend.

Irschick is a great guy, a great professor, brings up interesting real world examples of cool A $ P throughout his lectures. Involves students by having groups perform a lecture. Also has class read scientific papers. Exams are midrange in difficulty, but gives plenty of opportunities to get a good grade. would definitely recommend.

THIS REVIEW IS FOR ECE 529-629, there was no option for that course so I had to select otherwise. I would like to advise everyone to please stay away as far as you can from this guy's course. He will do everything in his power to make students life miserable. The course had 4 mini projects, 2 mega projects, 2 midterms and 1 final.
Worst Prof, will not take it any courses that he teaches.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Group projects--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Is not a goat of ECE - not afraid to dish out the hurt.

reviews.rating_tags: Hilarious--So many papers--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Yes, reviews here are all real. The class that was taught was so bad and infuriating that I ended up switching out of Computer Engineering as whole. I not only completely failed this class, but failed multiple other classes as I struggled for time in this one. A year goes by and I will honestly say that this was the worst class I've ever taken ever
These are real reviews. Worst professor in all of Umass. Its been a year and we are still sitting here ruminating about this class. Avoid him at all costs.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Lots of homework--Beware of pop quizzes

reviews.comment: are these reviews real or just a joke
Honestly a good guy. The course itself was fine, although lectures I would say fell short - more so due to a lack of direct translation between theory and exam questions.

I walked into the first lecture feeling excited that I was going to learn how to code (since I had never coded before). Fast forward, I walked into and out of the final exam with actual depression and anxiety. Eslami does not teach you anything. I had to use ChatGPT for almost every assignment, and the tests were extremely difficult; awful class.

The class was really not as bad as many people set it out to be. 

The exams were tough but I thought if you could do the weekly lab assignments without looking at notes, then you were all set.

They also help you build a conceptual foundation for the exams, which require you to have a firm grasp of the connections between the different units.

Although Professor Taffet's lectures can be fast and dense, he truly cares about each and every individual that takes his class. He uses plenty of references and metaphors to explain chemical concepts, which sometimes work well, but other times make things a bit more confusing (entering class already familiar with the concepts helps this).

Extremely helpful review sessions before exams and always willing to answer students' questions.  Awesome lecturing style that emphasizes active learning with in-class questions.  Good philosophy of Preview, Perform, Review to stay on top of the material and build a solid foundation for chem.
prof taffet went very fast and failed to explain some topics very well. that being said, he was very accessible outside of class time and extremely passionate.

Taffet is extremely passionate about everything. The lectures can be heavy and go fast, but all the material he goes over is given to you and he is VERY accessible outside of class. He has amazing office hours and it is really worth going to them.

AQICs and then OneNote annotations kept me engaged and left me with a sense of how to approach homework problems. There's good correspondence between the questions we have to do for homework and the questions that we focus on in class. I started to preview the content in the textbook and then look for deeper insight from the lectures.

Comes up with nice acronyms like NOF and SRF with a clear ability to break things down along with answering questions. Super helpful during office hours, and I kinda wish I started going sooner. Repetition is key, so make sure to keep reviewing the OWLs and request a timer reset on your practice exam.

He's got lots to say, but there'a a lot to get done in this class. I liked how the Canvas Gradebook was set up so that I could get access to exam scores the night of and figure out how I was doing with all the correct weightings. Grading is clearly structured to help students who struggle with exams but want to do well.
reviews.rating_tags: Clear grading criteria--Gives good feedback--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: There's no limit to the level of detail he's willing to provide, so go to office hours! And there's the instantaneous response to email on weekends! A lot of this class is about staying focused and putting in the work, but Dr. Taffet leads by example through Implicit Office Hours held every morning on Saturday, Sunday, and any day of the week!

If you follow the Preview, Perform, Review mantra, you're golden. Lectures have real-world examples like hydrogen bonding in DNA, and new content is broken up with plenty of practice problems. We even got a couple of extra videos on the hard stuff like ICED-to-ICE tables and names to formulas for acids. The material quickly builds on itself though.

Honestly, the key to this class is OneNote.  There's a ton of practice problems on there, clearly labeled by the OWL unit the question was pulled from on the homework.  After every class, you get a Canvas announcement about what homework assignments relate to the last lecture and what to expect for next lecture.  It really helps you stay on top.

He provides a ton of resources that help you get ahead and stay ready for the exams.  Hands down one of the most intense Lecturers cuz he'll maximize those 75 minutes of class time to give you everything he has to help you understand the content.  Pre-recorded lectures, quizzes, and TA exam reviews are great resources outside of class.

He really goes in-depth on OWL problems, distilling challenging concepts down to their most simplistic elements.  In-class questions keep you constantly engaged, and they give you 15% extra credit on Attendance by just doing them all and attending every class.  He also gives a ton of exam-review problems that help you integrate the concepts.

He's a good professor that really wants all of his students to succeed. If you are coming in with no background knowledge of chem, he is heavily accessible with his office hours in which he will go over concepts. I personally thought that this class and his exams are easy to leverage by just grinding OWL questions (with a few conceptual Qs).

Attendance every lecture. Lectures slides and handwriting are barely understandable. Very nice and forgiving, ALWAYS available for office hours/one-on-one help! Exams have only 20 questions (which is badddd), they're similar to practice, but the final was hard, had unexpected questions we haven't seen.

Elliot was a great teacher for this course! I recommend going to his office hours as he is very accessible, and sometimes lectures can be dense, but he is able to explain well during office hours! Owls due at the end of the semester, attendance counts as 115% if you go to all the classes and the final is based off of practice exam questions!

His slides are so full of needless information that it makes studying for exams more confusing. Lectures aren't too much better either because of his fast pace and tangents. Taffet is an incredibly smart guy within his field and always willing to help students, but his teaching style just wasn't it for me. Teach yourself using OWL to get an A.

His slides are too crowded, over explains things in a way that's confusing, but he's a very smart prof. He also talks very fast, but he's always available to help. If you can do all the owls and have conceptual understanding, you'll ace the class. Exams are 80% practice exams + conceptual stuff. Final exam is the easiest exam from the 4.

Hes very smart but doesnt know how to teach. Slides have too much info, talks fast, confusingly, + complicated. Thought he was a good prof bcuz of these reviews but everyone I talked to doesn't like this class. He's very available outside of class and his OWLS are due at the end of sem, but other than that, take someone else. Lectures are boring.

Dr. Taffet is a very smart guy, one of the smartest people I've ever met. His class can be challenging, however, the exams are 80% of the practice exams. He will throw in a couple of conceptual questions. The final exam is easy. Do the owl homework and get perfect attendance if you can (will result in 115% for attendance portion of the grade).

lectures were genuinely painful to sit through because bro is a yapper and he never even takes a breath to stop yapping. his slides have way too much stuff on it, and while he knows his stuff, concepts are lost amidst challengers references and sex jokes. he thinks he's funny but he's not. honestly don't know how he has so many good ratings.

The lectures are horrible: cramped slides, head-ache-inducing, hard to follow along, talks too fast and too much, and explanations that are overly complicated, making simple concepts confusing. A few questions on the exam were not covered in class. Once he talked in a British accent and a mob boss accent...the entire class. Head-ache-inducing.

He seems like a super nice person who genuinely cares about his students. but he's a terrible teacher. His slides are all over the place and packed w too much info. He's very enthusiastic in his lectures but talks really fast/loud and hard to understand. The exams were alr but I had to teach myself everything through OWL the whole semester.

Very nice guy. Cares a lot about the material and the students. I took TT classes so the lectures felt incredibly boring and long but the practice problems he gave during lecture would help me stay engaged.

Taffet is a bit quirky, but once you overlook that, he's a great prof. He's accessible nearly 24/7 outside of class and clearly wants all his students to succeed. Exams were about 80% copy and paste from the practice test and homework deadlines were very generous.

The first few lectures he was already making sex jokes which was very uncomfortable. He talks in an odd fashion, sort of like a theater kid so he is very hard to understand. There are 3 exams which are 20 MCQs and a final. I gave him a 2 stars b/c his office hours are like 6 hours and he still has zoom available outside of office hours.

I don't know why he has such high ratings. Everybody taking the class disagrees lol. His teaching style is very hard to understand everyone falls asleep in lecture. But if you teach yourself, you can do well on the exams. Owl homework are due end of semester.

Very nice, funny, and caring guy but not for me. Everyone told me to take him but he is very hard to follow, slides are super long and he spends a lot of time showing you how to manipulate formulas even though he provides them on the exam. You might like him if you have ADHD or a shorter MWF class, but I wish I stuck with Mentzen. Beware of exam 2!

Okay I am TERRIBLE at chem and I do not blame Taffet at all. His lectures are pretty wordy but he is amazing at explaining concepts. He responds to emails within an hour and always has office hours. He is SUPER funny (explains concepts with sex jokes) and very caring. He tries to develop 1 on 1 relationships with students which is appreciated
Explains things in weird ways that make no sense if you aren't extremely good at chemistry.

I get a headache from every single class with him. He just talks at you, nonstop, for 75 minutes. The slides are so full of text you don't know what to look at. When he takes notes, his handwriting is completely illegible. If I get distracted for a second I'm completely lost the rest of class. I don't know how he never learned to make slides right.

Take this class if you want to waste your time. He talks for the entire class nonstop and uses ridiculous analogies trying to explain things that could have been explained in one bullet point. I don't even use the notes to study and I've learned everything I know from the homework. The slides are so packed with random stuff they hurt your eyes.

Taffy Bear was very caring and inspirational in his lectures. Had funny analogies and made the lectures more interesting. Also does not require and iClicker which saved me money at least for this semester. 3 exams and 1 final, but the final was easy because it was legit the same questions as on the three previous exams plus the practice.

Taffet's slides are the most confusing, most text filled slides I've ever seen with no actual real notes. These other ratings are straight up lies. He is not funny, talks way too fast, talks in analogies, and teaches like we all already know the content. I learned more from SI sessions than this guy. Take Hanz Mentzen for chem 112.

Daddy Taffy is an absolute gem—goofy, hilarious, and effortlessly engaging. His lectures are packed with witty humor, playful sex jokes, and a lighthearted approach that keeps students entertained while actually learning. He makes even the driest topics fun, and his warm, charismatic personality creates a welcoming classroom vibe.

Dr. Taffet is the boy. He's a little funky but he's the most enthusiastic and caring professor I've had. Though he talks incredibly fast, chemistry is his life, he is available pretty close to 24/7 for office hours and will stop at nothing to ensure that you understand the material. Took him for 111 and 112, and would have taken him for Orgo too.

Professor Taffet is very good at lecturing in a way that is engaging to his students and helps them learn, often coming up with creative ways to help people understand a certain concept. On top of this, he is very flexible and easy to work with if you ever have any scheduling conflicts. Absolutely would recommend.

I definitely recommend taking his class. Professor Taffet does a very good job at explaining the material in an easy to understand method and he is always willing to help you in any way. I would definitely recommend listening to him on how to approach this course as it will help you get an A.

You can tell Taffet cares alot about his students. I never went to lecture because I took AP chem and already knew all the material. Exams very easier than easy, used alot of previous OWL problems. Final exam was identical to the practice final. But, I heard he changed it and he uses previous exams as his final. Have a solid understanding in chem.
reviews.rating_tags: Amazing lectures --Clear grading criteria--Gives good feedback

reviews.comment: His slides are filled with information and he talks very fast. He is very passionate about this course. The homework is honestly a lot. There are three midterms and a cumulative final. He provides a practice exam for each. The final consists of questions from the other three exams. He is easily accessible, especially with emails.

He wants everyone to do well in his class and will work with you. He cares a lot about his students and has office hours every single day. If you do all the homework you should be able to do well in the class.
exam 2 was most difficult, but like he said do all your owls and you will be golden, 3% extra credit of a grade available,  remembered my name first time I went to office hour

He was so amazing and interactive! By far one of the best chemistry courses I have ever taken. I am very bad at chemistry but still managed to succeed in this class because he is clear with material you will be tested on. Can't recommend him enough!

Professor Taffet is one of the best professors I have ever had. I always thought I was not good at chem until I took CHEM 112 with him. You can tell he loves what he does and loves helping students. I would definitely recommend taking this class. The material is hard but if you go to office hours he will explain it very well! GO to class!!

Elliot is a great professor. He explained things really thoroughly and had lots of practice questions. For our final, he gave us questions from previous exams. Can be confusing/fast-paced at times, but has many office hours to help. There are 6(?) unexcused absences, but going to all the lectures gives you extra credit. Would recommend

Elliot is that dude. Easily one of the best and memorable professors I've had so far. Chem is usually a hard subject for me, but I found myself doing way better than I ever thought I would. I will be honest and say that it's kind of hard to follow along with him during lecture but if you put in the work you'll be fine. Definitely reach out too.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Hilarious--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: The ability prof Taffet has to explain information is like no other. I enjoyed his class immensely even though it was difficult at times. Exams are not hard but would highly recommend studying for them. If you are ever confused GO TO OFFICE HOURS. You can tell he loves what he is doing behind the passion he shows.
reviews.rating_tags: Amazing lectures --Clear grading criteria--Gives good feedback

reviews.comment: Elliot Taffet- who by that way has accumulated (soon to be) 2 distinguished teaching awards in his short UMass Career, cares more about teaching than any professor I have ever taken. If you are dedicated even if not naturally gifted Dr. Taffet will go the extra TEN miles to help you understand. Highest recommendation without reservation.
reviews.rating_tags: EXTRA CREDIT--Clear grading criteria--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: He's a bit of an odd man but in an endearing way. I went to lectures purely for attendance points because I'd be lying if I said I understood him more than 25% of the time. However, you can tell he cares deeply for his student. Go to his office hours, he lets you in on a lot if you show your dedication! He purposely makes exam 2 the hardest.
reviews.rating_tags: Clear grading criteria--Lecture heavy--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: I have never met a professor more dedicated to both their students and their craft. Dr. Taffet is extremely dedicated to each and every one of his students and no joke, he wants you to succeed above and beyond, maybe more than you want to succeed tbh. PLEASE take the class with him you'll get an easy A

Take Elliot Taffet, I don't care who says otherwise take this man. The GREATEST thing about this man is that THE FINAL IS THE PRACTICE TEST VERBATIM. I'm talking question and answer is exactly the same. I believe I was out within ten minutes. Also, he will actually learn your name, first and last, before you ever meet him.

Funny guy who does care about his students, but worst lectures I have ever sat through and attendance is mandatory. I have never seen so many words on a slide, and when questions get asked I think he makes it harder to understand than originially explained. Expect to be teaching yourself. Would avoid this class.

Professor Taffet lectures on the problem-solving techniques you need to complete the OWLs efficiently, presents in-class exercises taken straight from the OWL that he goes through in depth, and builds exams based on the OWL homework.  As a result, it is straightforward to succeed in his class.

Professor Taffet is very lively and clearly cares about his student's progress. He really wants you to understand the course material and goes out of his way to answer any questions you may have. However, his teaching style can sometimes get confusing and you need to be able to keep up to his pace. He wasn't terrible but I've had better
Happy to solve problems, there are often extra credit questions, and if you have reviewed thoroughly and completed the homework and practice exam, the exam will be very easy.
Only speaks in analogies, so it's hard to understand some times.
Taffet is definitely knowledgeable in Chemistry and lectures well but can be overstimulating for some with his energy. Would recommend and attending office hours will get you a good grade for sure.

I am someone who HATED chemistry. I was also super bad at it as it never really made sense in my mind. Taffet explains his lectures very well and uses humor to keep you engaged. He takes breaks during class to take questions and make sure you understand what we're going over. He's also never taken more than a couple hours to answer my emails.
He is so incredibly passionate on the topic and teaches extremely well. He always has a smile on his face!
He makes awesome information sheets, which make the math-heavy parts of the class simpler.
I actually had fun taking this class, and that's a credit to Dr. Taffet's teaching style. He's the most enthusiastic professor I've ever met.

This class was a whirlwind, but Dr. Taffet kept everything together. So many topics get covered in this class, so OWL after OWL due date will feel pretty intimidating at first. But Dr. Taffet's availability makes things so much better.
It's pretty amazing to witness how much content and passion he packs into every lecture. I really respect how much energy and effort he puts into teaching us.
So much homework, but he's there for you every step of the way. He'll even meet with you on weekends to go over the homework and practice test. He's a lifesaver.
He's really nice. Some of the sections on OWL were super hard, so I reached out for help. He would spend as many hours as necessary to make everything clear!
He's got lots of interesting takes on complex material and really useful shortcuts on the math.
His lectures have a bunch of practice problems that help prepare you for the test.

Like a lot of the reviews say, he has a ton of energy. Every class has a bunch of problems that break up very thorough slides. The problems are aligned perfectly with the assignments, and the due dates aren't until the end of the semester. He always wants to help in office hours, which you can schedule for whenever works for you.

Filled with energy, he does everything he can to help you. He'll meet with you at 9 pm on a Thursday and then 8 am on a Sunday. His in-class problems have QR codes that you scan on your phone, so you don't need to bring an iClicker. He then thoroughly annotates solutions to these problems, which is really helpful when doing the homework.

He's not your worst option but I don't think he does the best job at explaining chemistry concepts because he gets too conceptual and its hard to understand, even if i was familair with some of it. His exams were pretty managable and I managed to do very well on them with some studying.

Professor Taffet teaches a tough course but makes jokes/adds in pop culture references/sings/etc to keep the class's attention. Attend office hours while doing Owl homework, and ask him to explain what problems mean conceptually! This is the ticket to a good grade! Very understanding professor. Super sweet, but the material is pretty hard.

Personally, I liked 10% grading weight on attendance instead of quizzes. If you're the type of person who attends lecture, take his class. He provides lots of extra-credit (in class Q's, some owl hw, quiz, PLTL). I don't understand why he sent academic alert even though I did good on exam 1, but he cares students and tries to help everyone learn.

I don't understand some of these responses articulating that Prof Taffet is unsympathetic; although I struggled to understand his lectures and Exam 3 was SO TOUGH T^T he was brimming with kindness. Don't expect free handouts (though the bonuses kinda are). It's chemistry, and you get what you get. Just be willing to learn, and you'll be all set.

He responds to emails really fast. cares greatly of his students. I personally did not learn much from his lectures, I learned from the homework instead and that was great. I do recommend showing up to his classes for the majority of the time and doing the homework a lot. Classes sometimes have bonus question

Taffet is such a great person. He's super caring about his students and will instantly answer any emails and is super accessible outside of class if you need help. His lectures go by really fast and he talks fast as well but i'd say his exams are very fair for the most part.

He cares about your success. This class is really easy if you just put in the work to understand the material. Practice exams mirror the real exams, sometimes he might throw some curveballs in there, but it's expected. A lot of homework, it takes time, so don't wait last minute and do ALL of it, because it helps you understand everything.

Very caring persons who really wanted his students to do well but the lectures were very confusing and dense, and the lecture slides provided were just as confusing. He did have lots of opportunities for extra credit and the practice exams were very helpful

This guy might be a lizard person. But he's more genuinely caring than any human professor I've had, and it shows. He talks so fast that lectures aren't worth much, but he is available nearly all the time for office hours either in person or online. He will greet every student by their name and do everything in his power to ensure your success.

He is super knowledgeable and teaches the class as if you are too. Lectures are super dense but he is always available for office hours. He's available in person or on zoom nearly 24/7 and deeply cares about the success of each and every student.

He does really care about your understanding of content. I don't really understand all the bad reviews on here regarding difficulty. This class really isn't hard at all if you put in the work (staying on top of homework) and study practice exams he provide. The only thing I don't like about him is that he isn't accommodating of personal issues.

He really cares about his students, there is not a moment where he will not be available, he holds long office hours, schedules times to help and he responds to emails within minutes, he's patient when explaining the topics. During lecture he can get really excited and use difficult words. He is extremely smart and passionate about what he teaches.
reviews.rating_tags: EXTRA CREDIT--Lots of homework--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Chemistry is something I have taken before and succeeded in, until Dr. Elliot Taffet. At first I thought because I was confused and new to the school this semester. But as the semester went on I was struggling. After he admitted to me that he makes the exams more difficult than any question we have ever been given, I was so concerned for my grade.

Chem is a difficult subject made even more difficult by Dr.Taffet. Exams are tough because the materials given to prepare for them aren't similar to the exams. Be prepared to devote your semester to this class if you don't have a strong background in chem and hope that you don't have anything important on exam day. The extra credit is a lifesaver.
reviews.rating_tags: EXTRA CREDIT--Lots of homework--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Probably one of the most unsympathetic and irritating professors. I know it's unrealistic for a practice exam to mirror the actual exam, but he intentionally tried to screw us over throughout the semester. The most recent exam (Exam 3) was ENTIRELY different from the actual exam, and he knew it too. He also teaches like we already know the content.

He doesn't have any sympathy for students whatsoever. So don't expect any extensions on homework or be able to postpone a test. He rushes through everything way too fast, attendance shouldn't be mandatory. I usually don't find his lectures helpful, the only time I actually understand anything is when I did the OWLS (homework assignments).

Have him for 112 . He is awesome. Attendance is mandatory however halfway thru semester he offers bonus questions in lecture that if you get right make up for missed lectures. Offers optional extra credit quizzes as well. HW all due on the last day of class, but there are lots of OWLs. Exams are exactly like practice. So easily accessibly

Professor Taffet is amazing! His enthusiasm for chemistry makes learning really fun. He cares about building a strong foundation, so DON'T SKIP YOUR OWLS and STUDY FOR EXAMS. Full of energy, sometimes he talks too fast but he's very accessible outside of class and more than willing to go over material with students. Truly an AMAZING professor!

Prof. Taffet is a standout professor who cares about his students more than any other professor I have met. His love for chemistry is palpable and he truly teaches with a passion and even some humour. He is extremely caring to his students and is extremely accessible and responds very quickly.

Professor Taffet's enthusiasm about chemistry is why I'm taking him again for 112. He is always encouraging and motivating. This class requires a lot of studying because not everything is covered in lecture: the OWLs are indispensable and read all of the chapters. Fast lectures, but he clarifies everything you're struggling with in office hours.

The class is difficult but Professor Taffet helps you learn. Explanations are a little difficult to understand so going to the SI sessions is very helpful. He is very energetic and enthusiastic so you can tell he loves Chemistry. Lots of OWL. I emailed him at 7 PM on a Friday and he responded in less than a minute so he cares about student success.

Extremely easy, the practice exams were exactly like the actual exams. He literally replies to emails 1 minute after you send it, even on weekends, even on breaks. He is very passionate about teaching, and will gladly take time out of his day and lecture to make sure you understand. Lectures are admittedly fast-paced, but clear and worthwhile.

His exams are super hard and he does not scale. He goes so fast and uses complex explanations. He is bad at explaining and does not make it understandable. He treats it like a junior and senior class when he is just general chemistry 1. He admitted himself to get an A you have to do gives you even the optional work. Get a different professor.
reviews.rating_tags: EXTRA CREDIT--Graded by few things--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Professor Taffet brings great enthusiasm to every one of his lectures. He is very accessible, will answer your emails quickly, and has incredibly flexible office hours. However, there is a lack of emphasis on important information in his lectures, making his lectures slightly irrelevant to the OWLs and exams.
Literally the goat. Super engaging and caring about each student. Remembers everyone's name by week two. Heavily based on OWL assignments and lectures are on OWL, which helps to practice for exams.

Loved the guy but the material was difficult and not what I was expecting, I thought it'd be more interesting. Stopped going to class because everything was online so it was a very easy A. Reminder: GEN EDS SHOULDN'T BE HARD. I'm a firm believer that I'll put all my effort into my major classes but not gen eds so I didn't have to worry abt this.

Out of the 400 people, maybe 75 students regularly attended class, to start every class he thanked all the students for coming. The last class he spoke about the lack of real world connections. I have never seen more people close their computers and pay attention to a class. He genuinely cares about the students in his class and it shows.

He doesn't take attendance and all exams are online. Really intelligent, funny, and caring professor! Highly recommend! Easiest class I've taken he drops the lowest exam grade and 4 of the lowest quiz grades. Great for a gen ed.

Take this class! Martin is such a sweet prof and the class itself is very easy to do well in. He really cares for his students and wants us all to succeed :) I took this class for Gen Ed and would definitely recommend

Easy gen-ed. Definitely take. Attendance was not mandatory and he never checked however he did mention changing that for future classes because participation was low so beware of that. Martin himself is fantastic and so fun

Martin is an awesome professor, truly very caring and passionate about his lectures. This is a great class to take as a gen-ed because it is easy and informative, I would say even though attendance is not mandatory this professor loves participation and it does not take effort to go to his class because it is non-stressful. Would 100% recommend.

Martin is so kind, and he's such a cutie. He's basically a cute dad. His class is so easy as well. All exams are online, LOWEST EXAM GRADE IS DROPPED. Yeah, EXAM GRADE! Online quizzes after each class with two attempts. It gives you all the answers after the first attempt, so you get 100 every time. He's probably the best professor I've had

Haven't gone to class since syllabus week because attendance isn't mandatory and everything is online. Seems like a great guy. He did get caught using ChatGPT to make his lectures though which is a bit iffy but do with that what you will.

He was really chill and assignments were easy if you paid attention or even just looked at lecture slides. Sometimes lectures were boring but you can tell he's really passionate about his craft and was interesting to listen to.
Martin is such a nice human. He really truly cares about his students, and the class material.
Super considerate and inspiring with his passion for oceanography. Lectures can be pretty information-dense, but it's not particularly difficult to do well.

The worst thing about him was that his voice could lull me to sleep during a lecture. The best thing about him is lots of things. He did, at times, say objectively incorrect things. Like how Sweden is always in the dark, despite midsummer when the sun doesn't set, but it's okay. He loved audience participation and hand-raising.
Professor was hila

This class was the definition of what a gen-ed should be. All online assignments and exams, including the final. Professor is funny, caring and understanding. I came to class every day because I enjoyed his lectures and his jokes, even though I'm a polisci major and just took this for a gen-ed. Exams give you more than enough time. I recommend!

Easy A class. I never went to class and did all my work online. Exams were kind of difficult but gave you more than enough time to complete (3 hours for 30-40 questions). There were weekly mini quizzes that consisted of around 5 or more questions that was homework.

Pretty easy class. All of the exams were online and were split to allow you to basically get a 100 on 25% of the exam every time. It's easy to tell that this is the first time he has taught the class, but he tries his best.

Easy class to get an A. The professor was enthusiastic about the material however struggled to explain and teach in a large lecture, making lectures useless. Lectures felt very disorganized because he jumped around slides that he clearly didn't make. Four exams and a final, as well as two weekly quizzes, easy to score well on but can be tedious

Took for PS Gen Ed. It's clear that Prof. Elizalde is passionate & knowledgeable. He has a great personality, but at times I felt as though assignments & exams were all over the place/confusing/unpredictable despite attending every lecture and studying. This class & the material stressed me out, but I recommend if oceanography is your thing.

Professor was super nice! He cared about us understanding the material and doing well in the course. He offered makeups for every exam. He made it easy to feel involved and gave opportunities to participate in class. Lectures were super fun, although not necessary to attend, I highly recommend going. Would definitely take class again!

Easy A Class! Definitely take for your PS requirement! Weekly online assignments/quizzes (2 per week) with answers from textbook or lectures. Online exams all MC and given an 1 hour and 15 mins with 30 ish questions, super easy and you get 2 tries! Online cumulative final exam, super easy! I 100% recommend! The professor is super sweet and nice!

Never went to class bc it was a waste of time. Graded on weekly online assignments which are easy, 4 online exams, & an online cumulative final. It's not difficult to get an A, but the exams are wordy/hard to finish w/ the time limit. The lectures were so unhelpful but he posts the lecture slides to use for the exams which you get 2 tries on.

This was his first time teaching Oceanography, so he'll probably improve with experience, but he took everything from the previous professor and didn't know what was on his own slides. There are a lot of assignments, but they're really easy and taken right from the textbook/lecture slides. You'll get an A if you read the textbook and lecture slides

This was his first semester teaching intro to oceanography so I do not think he was that familiar with the material, but he is super nice and tries to engage with the class and make lectures interesting. The assignments are super easy, but the tests are difficult if you do not know the material.

Really good and understanding professor. He definitely gets off track sometimes leading to class lectures being 90% off topic and 10% on topic, but that's a rare case. You can tell he genuinely cares for his students.

Martín is an incredible professor. His classes were always interesting and he is so passionate about his work. I genuinely felt interested in the topics presented in class and his homework and readings were also not too bad. He cares a lot about the students and he's really a brilliant and knowledgable guy. Totally recommend 100%.
fluid mechanics (340), so good

I took this (audited because I'm not in engineering dept) as an intro to aerospace engineering and it was the best idea ever. I showed up to every single class that I could, it was a perfect pace for me (a physics major) and Prof Roohi is very sweet and good at drawing out diagrams and noting details. You won't regret taking this class!!!

Super genuine and caring. I took Professor Roohi for 490A and 490F and he was great for both classes. 490F was a solid introduction into aerospace engineering and 490A was a solid opportunity to build on my strength of materials background while introducing aerospace applications. He is super resourceful and easily accessible outside of class.

I took this and MIE490A with professor Roohi and he was great for both, I found 490F more interesting but less challenging being an intro course. He is super accessible outside of class and always helpful. Course has a good blend of math, practical knowledge, and a hands on project. I would definitely recommend him and this course in particular.

Prof. Roohi is a great professor and also a really nice guy. He is extremely knowledgeable and able to explain course material with ease, and he clearly cares a lot about what and who he teaches. The course is made up of 20% homework, a group project worth 20%, and two exams worth 30% each. More difficult than 490F but not a super hard elective.

Professor Roohi truly cares about his students and wants them to learn the material that he teaches. He is trying to establish the Aerospace program at Umass Amherst, and I believe that he will succeed in doing so. Homework and exams are very reasonable, and the glider project is a great way to apply what you have learned.

Great Class with a cool group project making a 3D printed Airplane. Project was rushed due to it being the first time project was done, so it took a while for materials to come in. Lectures were very strength of materials focused initially until the back half where it was all about planes in flight. Fair exams and very passionate professor!

Very accessible outside class (office hours and Discord), lots of example problems done in class. Challenging material at times. The group project was a little chaotic with shipping and printer errors. He's the first professor I ever wrote a review for, really enjoyed teaching us, cares about his students and is super passionate about his material

Interesting but challenging expansion on strength of mats. concepts with some aerospace applications towards the end. Easily accessible. Hard exams, but fair grading. Always kept the mood light in class. Great examples on chalkboard. Unorganized project, but it's his first year here and other circumstances prevented it from being done earlier.

Interesting and fun way to introduce students to aerospace concepts. Very open to feedback regarding teaching style and is accessible outside of class via Discord/Canvas. Fair exams. The project was unorganized, but there were circumstances that caused that, plus it is his first year here. Things always need straightening out after the 1st run.

There were issues with obtaining the materials to complete the final project as efficiently as possible. However, with current materials, it is still possible, and after all, we are engineers, so it's kind of the point. Besides the project, he is a great lecturer, pretty funny, always accessible on Discord, and certainly cares about his students.
He is the first professor to teach the Aerospace program at UMass, and I think he's off to a good start,  just minor organization fixes, and he is a 5/5 prof.

He's one of the best prof's I've had at Umass. He's incredibly nice, cares about his students, and wants to see them do well. Not sure why he's getting so much hate on here. This was his first semester at Umass and yes some things went wrong/were delayed for our group projects, but it wasn't his fault at all. If you can, 100% take a class with him
Great class to satisfy MIE elective.
If you are willing to learn and attend the lectures, you will have no problem.

I think Prof Roohi is a great Professor overall; he genuinely wants his students to do well and does not grade unfairly. It was his first semester, so it's understandable if he was a little unorganized, but overall, he was a great guy, and it's clear he has a passion for the subject.

Same problem as 490A. Very caring and understanding, but super dry hard to follow lectures, bad slides in 490F. Easy and fair exams. Huge group project with no clear expectations with 1.5 weeks to complete before the end of the semester. Uses discord and canvas, so it is confusing and hard to find materials.

Super nice and understanding, however it is the least organized class that I have ever taken. Giant group project that the wrong components were purchased for, and no details or rubric were given- then it was expected to be finished with approximately 7 days left in the semester when materials were finally provided. Easy and fair exams.

PHIL100 is a great class. Prof. Neufeld is well-prepared, givs us lots of preparation for essays, and gives funny lectures. She's upbeat and passionate about philosophy. Flurry of negative reviews within the last days seems suspicious, appearing right after an AI audit where some students were penalized for cheating....

I wholeheartedly believe this class was intentionally designed to be ragebait. Lectures are insufferable, homework is glitchy and can make you do 3-4x as much as you're told, she's constantly in a bad mood, explains everything in about as unclear a way as possible, and the discussion sections are actually just tragic.
Lectures and a discussion section are required. Lots of reading. BORING lectures but discussions are fine and there is no final
The worst ever.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: A lot of reading. Class is more effort than its worth. The lectures are pretty interesting but discussions are a pain to get through. The papers were not graded with feedback and were graded pretty harsh. Take only if you're willing to put in the work and effort you need to get a good grade.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Lots of homework

reviews.comment: EN is a fun professor for sure, she definitely likes and knows what shes talking about. The lectures are somewhat interesting but I often found myself on wordle. There are a bunch of annotation homeworks on confusing philosophical readings that honestley make no sense at all. You have to write 3 philosphical papers that also are confusing. Thats it

Great professor & TA, easy gen-ed for AL as long as you put the min effort. There are three papers you need to write that account for 60% grade, but I was an inexperienced writer and frankly didn't put much effort into the papers and still got a good grade.

I actually took PHIL100 but for some reason I can't rate that. The class is well structured and I loved her lecturing style, it was very clear and easy to understand. There's usually a couple reading assignments every week but they are super easy. You do have to write 3 papers throughout the semester but they're not bad at all Definitely recommend!

Prof Neufeld gave interesting and humorous lectures. She seems newer to teaching but she is a natural, allowing for a lot of dialogue between her and the students in such a lecture heavy class. Her energy is fantastic and she explains more difficult concepts very well.

Eli is awesome, always fun! Clarifies concepts in a fun way, encourages discussions, has creative activities - which helps since bulk of grade discussion/participation and homework (Perusal). There's a couple big tests and papers, which have plenty of review. She makes and keeps time to meet with students and is really understanding and helpful.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: While I unfortunately had to withdraw from completing the semester due to medical issues, this was easily the best teacher I had for this semester. She was super nice, and while the course material could be challenging at times, she made it as easy as possible. I will definitely be retaking this class when I am back to classes.

As an art history major I was excited for this class, he is passionate about what he teaches and is respectful to students. The only thing I have to say for this prof is that his lectures and class structure is sloppy. You need to listen to every word he says in order to get a decent grade on one of the 4 quizzes or 3 exams.

The only good thing about the course is that attendance isn't mandatory, so you don't have to listen to his boring lectures. Exams are centered on the smallest details from lectures, are fully based on memorization, and he shows no leniency in grading—a badly structured class, where the professor doesn't care about how you do.
