The class has a lot of reading and his micro-responses every week. There were also 4 assignments that are very time consuming and challenging and are harshly graded. However, Poehler is a great and understanding professor and he cares about his students. He is always available for help and wants to challenge his students and see them succeed.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Participation matters

reviews.comment: Super interesting and engaging guy! Knows everything about Pompeii, which is what the whole course is about! A few papers, but no tests so just put in the time and you will do really well.

Don't take this course if you get easily bored. Roman classics has no use in the real world and the Professor will tell you that several times. There's 3 exams and 4 quizzes. You don't get any study guides so you kind of have to show up to lectures which is beat. All in all this class isn't worth it, so by all means avoid it for a gen ed.

Prof. Poehler's (online) class has been really good. 4 projects, mostly group work online, and mini essays (10 minutes during class time, turned in) once a week. My class engages with him and he's a pretty jolly guy, so to speak. Tries to keep Zoom engaging as well.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Graded by few things--Group projects

reviews.comment: Show up to class and pay attention and you will not have a problem.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Graded by few things--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: There are no study guides for tests, or outlines so you know whats on the tests/quizzes. Most of what is on the assessments is on random quotes he said in class., if you dont remember them word for word you get the question wrong. He also often has to reward points to the whole class because he puts misleading and unfair questions on the exams.
reviews.rating_tags: GRADED BY FEW THINGS--Tests are tough--LECTURE HEAVY

reviews.comment: I hate history, he made it interesting, easy as that. Great lectures, quizzes sometimes feel disjoint from those said lectures. Has his act together.

Don't get this professor! I had him for Roman Civ and it was harder than some of my chem classes. First, the only thing students can use to study are in class powerpoints which he races through in lecture & the book. Slow note takers? Sucks to be you. Book? Dense. The tests encompass thousands of years, tons of random info.  Overly difficult.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough Grader--Get ready to read--Skip class? You won't pass.

reviews.comment: Real genuine enjoyable guy, but class is kind of boring at parts. There's a lot of reading and some pretty in depth projects. Biggest thing about this class is how time consuming it is.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Skip class? You won't pass.--LECTURE HEAVY

reviews.comment: I took this class as one of my academic requirements. It isn't hard necessarily, but you need to read. He will go over the important things in class, but he will only skim over them because there is a lot of material. You'll have to read  and pay attention to those specific things he talked about in class if you want to do well.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough Grader--Get ready to read--Skip class? You won't pass.

reviews.comment: Great man and teacher but don't take Roman Civilization. Took it as a GEN ED, turned out to be a struggle. Why? Because besides in class notes, we have nothing to study with! His tests are hard too, random info. With hundreds of years of timespans, it's hard to know what he'll include on exams. He doesn't even offer study guides. Very difficult.

Roman Civilization w/ Poehler is extremely hard for a number of reasons. The only resources you have are his powerpoint slides and the book. He doesn't hold study sessions, review sessions, he doesn't give out study guides or outlines, and doesn't even post his powerpoint slides on moodle. Combined with the random information he puts on tests, BAD

I'm warning you! Do not take Roman Civilization with Eric Poehler. Although he is very nice and passionate, his class will set you up for failure. He offers no study guides for tests, does not help students decipher what is important to know and what isn't, and doesn't post lecture slides on moodle. I get constant C's bc his tests are unpredictable

Professor Poehler is very interested in Roman Civ and he tries to engage students in his lectures. His power points are kind of confusing--its a bunch of random information and you never really know what to study for when he gives tests, his tests have insignificant questions on them. The class was harder than it should have been.

Roman Civ was interesting. Poehler had long lectures with a lot of information. You never know what exactly to study because he puts random small information on the tests. Hes really nice and enthusiastic about the subject though. He assigns a lot of readings, if you want an A read, I didn't and I'm getting a B
smoke show. straight dime. so boring it almost cancels it out. physically painful to be in this class.

I have never had a teacher more charismatic and likeable teach such a boring subject. You can tell he loves what he teaches, very passionate guy. However there is a lot of work. Not necessarily difficult just time consuming.
Really tough, and requires you to remember who wrote about what, but has a high passion and shows the real side of archaeology

Awful. Fills a powerpoint with a million notes and moves quickly. Get ready to write. Tests are very hard if you can't remember everything from 300+ pages out of two books- not an exaggeration. This class as a gen ed took more time out of my life than a grad level Neuro course. The secretary said a lot of students had a problem with his class.

Absolutely a great professor. He's pretty funny and you can tell he loves what he's teaching and wants to be there. No study guides but if you can use common sense and can take notes, you'll do fine on the quizzes and exams. Maybe not a good one for freshmen who need to be spoon-fed information, brain power is necessary.

I have NO idea how this guy got such a high rating. This class is so boring and ridiculous for a gen-ed I felt the need to warn everyone here. His tests & quizzes arent bad as long as you study, well...EVERYTHING! dude gives you so much info but wont tell you whats important on the test. Oh and dont buy the books, all the questions are from lecture

Extremely fair. Just go to the lectures and take good notes. He gives extra credit opportunities as well. Interesting lectures. Class grade based on attendance, 2 quizzes, 2 tests. Make sure you have a buddy in the class because if you miss a class, it can really set you back! Getting an A is completely possible in this class!!!

Tough grader, but really good at explaining material. Nice guy and very approachable. Offers extra credit opportunities if you're not satisfied with your original quiz grades. Other that that, just take good notes and you'll be fine.

Professor Poehler is personable and has a sense of humor, but do not expect to receive a good grade!  I worked harder in this class than for those in my major, and received my worst grade ever (by a lot). He gives very difficult quizzes.  No As on the first and only one or two on the second.  Nice guy but avoid his classes for the sake of your GPA!

well prepared, good lectures, tries to get the class to participate. his quizzes are a little wierd, too few questions for too many points, get one question wrong and it's like you are immedietly down to a B. very approachable.

Took Ideas that Change the World with Prof. Ferrari. Super engaging! He keeps things really active with discussions, and I actually got to know my classmates. Didn't love all of the readings, but helps us connect it to our own lives and the real world which keeps it relevant. I also loved his approach to philosophy as a way to live everyday.
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Gives good feedback--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: I'm a freshman and this was one of my favorite classes so far. Visit to Dubois archive and museum were a nice bonus. You read many important texts, and the discussions are interesting. Got tired of talking about technology but it also felt relevant. I was rarely bored. Wasn't into keeping the journal but then it grew on me over time
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Beware of pop quizzes--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Took 201H. He's very big on group discussion and participation, and really tries to get his students to think-- about themselves, life, society, etc. Go to his office hours! He's awesome to talk to, and wants his students to question + reflect on the readings and beyond. He emphasizes keeping a handwritten journal, discourages digital technology.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Loved this class. Ferrari kept us active with different discussion activities and focused on getting us connect readings to our own lives. He's big on small group discussions, so you get to know your class mates. Didn't love all the readings but it moves on to new material quickly. Be warned, no phones and very little laptop use in class though.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Gives good feedback

reviews.comment: Slightly boring, a little uptight, and has a tendency to wait for a student to give the one response he wants to hear rather than letting discussion happen. But does a good job of covering huge time periods over a short period of class time. OK class.

He taught Film Genres, a 400 level course last semester.  Not the greatest lecturer, and often tries to start a discussion with students.  Sometimes is awkward.  Other than that, the assignments weren't very hard and the subject was interesting.  An average class that you can get a good grade in relatively easy.

Matt's class was my favorite by far this year! His movie selections are really interesting, but then the discussion always ends up being about so much more than just the film. Awesome lectures but not too much of it because he really wants to get discussions going. I'd definitely take another class by him!

Refrain from taking Ferrari.  He means well but should learn how to properly give a lecture.  There is no flow to his class and people do take note of it.    His assignments are interesting, but rather  complicated in nature.  My best advice is to take 228 with someone who knows how to interact with college students because this guys doesn't get it

I really loved this class! The material is pretty clear, the professor is always there to clear up questions. Assigns a lot of readings but there not mandatory to pass the class. Interesting material.

I agree with the part about TA's harsh grading, but I find the lectures to be very engaging. For the record, this is the only large lecture class I've had that feels like a dialogue, where students are regularly asked to think instead of sitting there zoning out. Some lectures definitely better than others, but I plan to recommend Ferrari to others

Ferrari is a nice person but his lectures couldn't keep a meth addict awake.  The TA's are the harshest graders I've ever had, and Ferrari does little to combat that despite knowing their expectations are ridiculous.  Took a month to get our first exam grades back.  Really well educated in his field, can't deny that, but the class is miserable

Prof Ferrari does better job of getting students to speak up and discuss in a large class than other teachers in my exp. I've taken other history classes and this is totally different.. keeps relating current issues in media technology to history so we don't get bored just looking at the distant past. Brings guest speakers in which is also great!

Don't know about his other classes but currently loving film history. Some of the films are too arty but he does a great job of making sense of each one for its history and culture. He seems to genuinely care about our thoughts on movies and not just telling us what to think which i appreciate. Not just memorizing. Def recommended class and prof.

I came to Ferrari's office hours and he spent so much time helping me prepare for the exam, which helped so much! I like that he doesn't lecture too long and always stops to ask students questions and try to keep them involved in the class. I'd take another class with him for sure.

The other 3 comments here are pretty harsh. Ferrari isn't so bad, I actually find him to be brilliant. He may not always be clear and he may look for his opinion as the right answer but this forces you to really analyze material and think things through conceptually which is a beneficial skill in life in general. true comm majors would appreciate

The other reviews, while harsh, are pretty much accurate. He is completely arrogant and has absolutely no idea what he is talking about. His lectures are pretty much "What do you guys think?" *Looks really confused* "Okay". If you do part of the homework you'll get a 0. TA's can't grade to save their lives. 13 every time, even if you it right.

Class was very engaging and fun, the readings were also super short. She does a lot of fun activities and makes it really easy to learn. There were 3 take home exams and 3 writing assignments. Very easy to do well and have fun as long as you take notes and occasionally participate.
Good lectures, easy material if you have a good base knowledge of graphs and biology. Just take good notes and you'll have a great time.

Took for BS gen ed, attendance is taken via a survey at the end of lectures, so if you really don't want to go you can show up near the end of class. Grades are online exams and a short essay. Offered extra credit through going to a guest lecture as well as a video presentation. Homework before class was to read articles on canvas, not a grade tho.

I loved Laura! Exams were reasonable compared to lectures and the lectures themselves were always engaging and relevant. I appreciated that she took student concerns to heart and changed things in the course to reflect that. I also loved the guest lecturers she invited. New reading per class but nothing was ever too hard/long. Will miss her :(

Overall, the class was okay, but I definitely wouldn't want to take it again. The grading was a bit harsh, she cold-called quite a lot (felt like I was in high school), feedback wasn't great, and the online exams were way too long. Lecture-wise, she went too fast on many slides and the QR code for attendances were way too overloaded. 5/10 class

Laura has a strong passion for entomology, and it shows in her lectures. Attendance is a big portion of the grade, so be prepared to show up and ready to learn. Students will get the most out of the class by being engaged, but Laura is very caring and kind. Exams are take-home and open note, no graded homework, and one essay. She is wonderful!
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Clear grading criteria--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Kind of condescending and was not a huge fan of her teaching style. Liked to cold-call people sometimes. Lots of readings for HW, no assignment attatched but would ask questions about them in class. Exams were take home/ online, but IMO questions could sometimes be subjective, and they were long. Intersting class in theory, but she made it boring
Engaging lectures and really fun examples. She is very passionate about the material. You actually have to think for the tests, its not enough to just take notes and memorize.

Lecture material is interesting but goes through slides way too quickly even though there is a quiz at the end of each class that counts for participation. Exams are 2 hours and are open note but they are not easy so DO NOT BE FOOLED. Tons of material covered but not much homework. (NRC 261)

Goes through slides very quick, not enough time to take notes. Quiz at the end of each lecture which you cannot do well due to the rushed lectures. Guest lectures were great and taught at a nice speed, regular lectures were not. (NRC 261)

Quizzes are extremely challenging with lecture materials not sufficient to score an A on quizzes. Professor grades essays extremely harsh as well. I made the mistake of risking to take this course with a professor with no ratings on this site and will recommend anyone to NOT TAKE this course from this professor to satisfy the biology requirement!
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: She wants you to do well, all tests are open notes, she explains everything so well, not too much detail. Will help you with anything you need. Very little homework, 2/5 classes each section are mandatory.

Professor Facette is very nice and helpful. the class is interesting and she does a good job teaching it. you have to show up for the worksheet days, but they are helpful because they are very similar to the exams which are open note.
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Clear grading criteria--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Hi love Dr. Facette! She is clearly so passionate about what she does and it makes the students excited about it. If you're at all interested in plant cell bio she's the person to talk to. She's a clear lecturer and takes time to clarify confusing topics. Her portion of BIO335 was manageable and I learned a lot.

Facette taught the second half of this course and was clear with the expectations of what we're supposed to know for exams. Theres 4 exams in total and 6 quizzes (drops 2) that were all online and open book. Your grade is made up of 70% exams and 30% quizzes so be careful not to slip up too much although there were extra credit opportunities.

Dr. Facette is the most straightforward professor I ever had. She has clear guidelines for her exams. If you know the group worksheets, you can guarantee a 90+ on the exam. She also makes plants so interesting. If you put some effort into the class you will do just fine.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Amazing lectures --Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: Dr. Facette is an amazing professor who really cares about her student's success. She makes plant cell bio fun and easy to understand. She is super understanding and an overall great professor. Dr. Facette is also accommodating and really wants you to succeed in her class. Her exams are straight forward, no tricks.

One of the best professors I ever had. Cares about student success!! Graded by group worksheets, press release, exams. Great lectures, exams were not too bad (fair questions). Gave a huge amount of extra credit for exam corrections and had an optional final! She is the GOAT highly recommend; give this woman an award! highly recommend PLANT COURSE
she is very clear in what is expected of you on exams, exam was short and easy, all multiple choice. Very nice and good teacher
reviews.rating_tags: Graded by few things--Clear grading criteria--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: Dr. Facette is ok. She is not very clear and her exams are difficult. Don't take this class because it's not an easy A, it's more trouble than it's worth, and it's pretty boring. There are other plant classes that can fulfill your major requirement and are much more interesting. Avoid the stress and copious amounts of work. 0/10 wouldn't recommend.
Just do the OWLs, lecture would be more fun if it wasn't super technical. would not recommend unless you love hard science.

Great guy! Tests aren't super easy but all students are allowed to take an online version that averages out your grade. So in short, super easy class to get an A in, attendance isn't graded, and overall Justin is just a really cool person

Inspiring lectures. Exams are an average of in class and at home attempts.  His teaching style can seem confusing, but the whole class is designed to get you to actually think and figure out how to do things more independently over time. It's a challenging class w/ plenty of chances to improve your grade. I wish I could take more of his classes.

Lecture heavy class with weekly problem sets. There were no slides and lots of material covered so it was easy to fall behind. Difficult class content wise but there are no exams, the problem sets can be re-done, and the students wrote the take-home final. Justin Fermann really cares about growing student's learning abilities and I learned a lot.

Great professor. practice exams were exactly like the exams, except for the final, which was slightly different. very lenient with homework, accepted late from me many times. lectures were slightly off topic, i had to teach myself sometimes to make it clear. class was enjoyable and engaging. chill guy tbh
Don't go to lecture it's pointless. You learn basically everything through owls. He is super chill tho and lets you get points back on exams

He is a good professor, who really cares about his students LEARNING. Personally, did not like his lectures AT ALL. He doesn't explain the concepts, just jumps into examples so you really rely on OWL for this one. Nice guy.

He is a great guy but not a great professor. His lectures are somewhat fun but unstructured and all over the place. You have to rely on OWL for understanding topics. Focuses on learning, so there is credit claim after all the exams, and there was extra credit in one of them. There are opportunities to get good grades.

Horrendous lecturer, nice guy. I don't understand the people saying he doesn't control the OWLs, he definitely has control over that and he assigned like 8 assignments due 3 days before the due date. He kept assigning homeworks due the day of the exam as well. You can barely take notes on the lecture, use OWL for notes.

Sweet teacher but not a good lecturer. He also doesn't have any control over how many OWLs given, there are a lot but it's not his choice. He is super sweet and accommodating and we can fix 2 questions for full credit. I'd recommend not going to lectures all the time, and instead studying using OWL. Super nice but I don't understand his teaching.

Prof. Fermann is easily the nicest and most knowledgeable professors I've met. He makes class super engaging and clearly puts thought into how his student can learn best. He lets you correct 2 questions back on exams meaning u basically get a free 10% back. He's so nice and I couldn't recommend him more for chem 112!
If you go to class you probably won't have enough time to keep up with the homework. There is like 35 owl questions due every few days

Prof Fermann was so great in lectures I'd recommend CHEM123 to any chem/chem adjacent majors. He was super engaging and would realize where he'd lost the class during a board-wide derivation, then back up to reexplain. Exams can be hard but if you go to his office hours he will help you with the questions you're stuck on. Don't get behind on OWLS!!
reviews.rating_tags: Amazing lectures --Graded by few things--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Grading scale is really nice. OWL homework takes a lot of time but you can do it as many times as you want to get full credit. I really liked this class, especially the way that it was discussed. Would take again!
Lots of homework scattered across three different platforms, which can be hard to keep on top of. Very kind, though, and a great lecturer! Really interesting class.

Professor Fermann was awesome. The way he scales the grading is great so even an 85 is considered an A. The tests are individual and collaborative so you can do well. Hes always making things to give away in lecture. The TAs are super easy graders and let you redo things. There is a weekly homework assignment that you have to pay for though.

An easy and very engaging GenEd for non-STEM majors. There's so much opportunity to bring your grade up, and tests are averaged between an individual and collaborative portion. There's a lot of room to explore with your final paper/experiment, and overall Professor Fermann is very charismatic and seems genuinely passionate about the material.
Be prepared to do several projects and homework assignments on several different websites he makes you buy. Do not even consider this class.

Prof. Fermann's class is engaging and manageable if you stay on top of the work. The tests are doable with preparation, and the ability to retake them helps. Unstuckstudy can complement your study routine.

Chem 190 is worth taking solely because of Justin. He's an entertaining lecturer, although the concepts he teaches are highly theoretical and can be difficult to understand at times. Lots of OWL homework, but the exams are collaborative, take-home, and graded leniently. Overall a great guy who makes chemistry much more interesting.

Justin is really chill, and the tests are pretty easy. You take them twice, and the score is the average of the two. Make sure to take notes on what he says during lecture because the test questions are often based on things he said in class that may not be on the slides.

Justin is a great professor! The class was very interesting, and he's very experienced at teaching it. The homework was some small responses, a few medium-sized assignments, and a big final project and paper. The tests weren't super hard if you study, and he allows you to retake them with any notes or help you need for half credit back.

A LOT of busy work!! The class itself was okay, interesting subjects, and the way the tests are done allows for improvement. Not a bad choice for a Gen Ed, but make sure to stay on top of all the little assignments.

Fermann is an amazing professor who is invested in the success of the class. His lectures consist of derivations that are broken up with group discussions on questions he may pose. Exams are taken home and encouraged to be done with others in the class, however, are difficult and time-consuming. Homework tends to be busy work however still helpful.
take this instead of 112 or 122, if you have ap credit. you will learn a lot and do well in the class. just do all of the owl homework.
He allows you to take every test twice to help with test anxiety

Prof Fermann is just a great chemistry professor. Homework was from the online textbook, but he allowed full late credit and wants his students to learn rather than feel pressured to meet deadlines. His lectures utilize real world applications and were great for learning (beware of chapter 17: buffers if this is your first time taking chem) :D
Great Professor. Good Gen-Ed to take for Physical Sciences. Easy to get an A, but you have to do the work. Tests are done in a group setting, and they are very doable if you study beforehand.

Justin's a good guy but he likes rambling and seems to be determined to only use power point default layout slides which are vague anyways. Pros: due dates are very lenient, extra credit, EASY exams (copy of practice test), attendance not mandatory. Cons: LOTS of homework (he assigns OWL books & prac questions), useless lectures (teach yourself).

Fermann is super caring for his students. You can tell he has his best interest in your success, not just for this class, but outside as well. Exams are pretty easy for this course & he is lenient with the grading & time to complete homework assignments. I think lectures are good for visual learners, but not the most helpful. Highly recommend!

Professor Fermann obviously cares a lot about his students and wants us to do well. However, students pretty much have to teach themselves the material through OWL assignments. His lectures are very theoretical and his slides have no actual information on them, just graphs. He assigns tons of homework, and it takes a very long time to do.

Justin is a great professor he truly cares about his students success. Highly recommend going to office hours. His lectures are very conceptual and most of the math you learn is self taught from owl. Grace period on all homework.
Justin Fermann is awesome, easily one of the best professors at UMass.  I have had him for Chem 111 and now 391AH, he's really good for both.  Very kind and truly cares about his students.

Justin is an amazing professor! His class is work and the concepts are new and difficult, AP Chem will be used and expanded upon. However, Justin is always there to answer questions and will gladly pause the class in order to fully explain a concept so that you are confident in your understanding. His class is more conversation than lecture.

His class was my favorite of the semester. While the theory and conceptual work behind the course content was at a high level, Justin made learning these concepts very engaging. He obviously had a good understanding of the material and was open to fun, spontaneous discussions in class. Attendance wasn't mandatory but I wouldn't recommend skipping.

Super nice but his lectures consisted of him talking and writing with NO notes posted anywhere. No one knew what he was talking because he tries to show the derivation of every equation ever developed and it's really hard to follow. Just take chem112 if you took AP chem to brush up on the harder chem skills because this guy is not good.

DO NOT TAKE THIS CLASS I DONT CARE WHAT YOUR ADVISOR TOLD YOU, THERE IS MATH AND A LOT OF BACKGROUND CHEMISTRY KNOWLEDGE REQUIRED TO DO WELL IN THIS CLASS!!!! I am a 4.0 student, however, I am an SBS major so I evidently don't have a lot of knowledge or experience in STEM. I have consistently received ~70s on all of the exams. this class is so hard

Review for 2022

He's an amazing teacher- intelligent, willing to help, and takes feedback from each class to incrementally improve.  His lectures give most of the info needed, and then some interesting info + in-class experiments.  You'll need to teach yourself rarely using the OWL homework.  Four exams, but they're 1/2 solo 1/2 group w/ notes.
Everyone should take this class,  he makes beer, do blacksmith, blow glass and make ceramic in class. It's the most fun class in umass ithink

Professor Fermann is very knowledgeable and very helpful when you go to his office hours. I'm sure he's a great teacher for science majors and upper level classes but chem103 is a gen ed that is harder that is should be, especially for non-sceince majors. Take another physical science class if you're only looking to take a gen-ed.

Justin is clearly a very knowledgeable professor who has an answer to every question. Great course for chemistry majors who scored a 4 or 5 on the AP Test, which covers the content of both semesters of gen chem at a higher level. Tests were take home.

A really caring and wonderful prof, but he's wayyy too intelligent to be teaching a general chemistry class! Sometimes he goes on tangents about complex concepts. I did have to teach myself using OWL on occasion. Nonetheless, he still is a great teacher and explains concepts well. He just gets ahead of himself. I liked him a lot.

Very nice guy- but Justin is way too smart to be teaching a general chemistry class. His knowledge of the subject is just so far beyond the level you need for this class- during lecture he tends to go on tangents about advanced chemistry topics that don't help you for a test. Solid professor, but there are better options for Chem 111.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Very standard. Very flexible and understanding. Pretty solid, lectures did get boring after a little while

This professor did not lecture well at all. His lectures were unorganized and he would randomly do an experiment that had no correlation to the learning. He does not teach the homework, so it takes quite a long time to finish. The only idea of what is on the exams is by doing the practice exams and if your lucky they might have similar questions.

Dr Fermann (Justin) is one of the kindest professors at UMass. His lectures are very interesting and he is happy to help. Go to his office hours, they are a gem! His exams are hard and can have some unlearned info in them though. The OWL homeworks suck but those are given by the dept so you can't avoid them. I would highly recommend.

Prof. Fermann is funny, knowledgeable, and organized. However, his teaching style can be difficult for some; you essentially teach yourself and his lectures expand on the info you read. Do the OWLs (including optional) and you will be fine. My knowledge from AP Chem made the class quite easy but many people I know struggled. Great Chem111 choice!
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Accessible outside class--Get ready to read

reviews.comment: Class was fine. I did have to teach myself most of the material but I've had to in every science class I've ever taken at UMass. The exams are pyramid style (which is awesome) and his grading scale is 90+ is an A. I thought this class was a lot of fun and interesting. Form a solid group of friends to study with and take exam with and should be good

He is a great person, but his lectures don't really teach chemistry. He is very vague and theoretical with his teaching, leaving you to teach yourself most things. Don't fall behind on the homework, watch YouTube videos and take your own notes, and read the textbook and you will probably do fine.
reviews.rating_tags: Respected--Lots of homework--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: He's a funny guy, nice enough. The class was confusing for me but I'm not great at paying attention in class. You will do fine if you make an effort to review material outside of class.

SofC sounded like it would be a cool way to get the science requirement I needed. I was mistaken. Very test heavy, lectures are very spotty and hard to follow. Questions weren't really clearly answered, and teacher was hard to reach. It was cool to get to see crafts up close, but not worth hurting my grade. Nice, fun person, difficult professor.

Justin knows chemistry like the back of his hand. His lectures are usually full of applications and demonstrations. Although those are helpful, you have to spend a lot of time in the textbook to really understand the material and get the OWLs done. You will struggle if you don't. He is pretty funny and cares about the success of students though.

Justin was an incredible teacher for this class. I think he was wonderful at expressing higher level ideas at a manageable level. Sometimes the information went above my head (integration in chemistry??) but I feel that I really learned a lot. Justin, and Ethan the TA, both really cared about our learning and encouraged us to think deeply.

If you go to lecture, do the homework, and the practice exam... you won't pass the exam. In lecture he talks about things that are not on the exam and does not even acknowledge 70% of the homework problems. Would have been so much easier if all the material was lined up, but it was far from that. He is a wicked nice guy but should not teach intro

Fermann is a really personable guy but his class is so hard to understand. His slides aren't helpful and his lectures are hard to follow. He doesn't teach what is required for the tests and it's difficult to get a passing grade, even with studying.

He is an amazing prof. He is incredibly understanding, and cares that his students understand the material. Very fair and reasonable (especially during pandemic). An amazing lecturer - I left every lecture feeling like I learned something useful. If you're scared to take him at 8am - trust me, this is a professor that is worth waking up early for.
hands down one of the best profs i have had

Professor Fermann is a good and knowledgeable professor, but this class is just too much work for a gen Ed. However, I must say that I barely watched the lecture videos and somehow Im passing with an A. Navigating through the powerpoints was enough for me to make guesses. So I guess this class is doable, but I would look elsewhere for a PSgen Ed.
I do not recommend this class. Ridiculously tough for a gen ed course. Fermann's friendly but he does not realize that most people taking this class are doing it to fill out a gen ed requirement.

I 100% regret taking this class. Tests were unnecessarily hard for a gen ed course. Fermann treats the class like it is an honors level chemistry course. He's a genuinely nice guy but the class is not worth taking. Please do not take this class if you would like to preserve your sanity. Find another Physical Science credit course.
Lots of homework and the exam questions were nothing like we learned in class. Lectures are confusing and he's not very entertaining.

Like others have said already, this class did not transfer to the online format well at all. I honestly feel like the lectures should have been synchronous as there was no reason to go at all. Wait until its in person.

TBH I expected to fail, but he doesn't like to fail people. He's cool guy and he really wants you to succeed but this online school thing went HORRIBLY for this class. It was really hard to follow what was happening and OWL was infuriating (as per usual). As a non sciencey person I wanted to die. There r probs better options for the PS gen ed

This class did not translate well to the online format. I was excited to take this class but was stressed by the number of random assignments. Too much to keep track of each week between discussion, OWL homework, Hmwk Submissions, Tests, project checkpoints, long lecture videos, etc. Just save the hassle and wait until it's in person

I was excited to take this class but it doesn't fit the online format well. The prof is well intentioned but it's very confusing, lectures are asynchronous, and there are too many homework assignments to keep up with. Not an easy A or easy Gen Ed. Nothing against Prof Fermann but I recommend waiting to take this in person.

Science of Crafteasy A. Lectures are all recorded and if you want to show up, and most of the time you don't have to. 4 Exams are 50% group and 50% individual not cumulative. Final project is super easy. Homework isn't hard, just don't forget about it. A lot of extra credit offered. Ask him to change a grade and he will. Most sports teams take it
reviews.rating_tags: Accessible outside class--Clear grading criteria--EXTRA CREDIT

reviews.comment: He is a nice professor and class is always interesting. However he only demonstrates experiments and never actually explains the material. The tests are not based on the book and you just have to know what he's talking about right off the bat. He is very confusing and tests are EXTREMELY hard and difficult to pass. He does not give partial credit.

Fermann can best be described as chaotic. I never knew what was happening in class because he would go off on tangents and talk about chemistry in a way that was above everyone's head. But the exams are just like the owl homework and he gives a practice test so the class is manageable. He is very caring and understanding but he just can't teach.

I rarely attended class because it was an 8:30 AM class. At the end of the semester he really helped out by dropping bad grades, and his office hours were very helpful as well. The classes I attended were interesting and he has great humor.
He's rad

DO NOT TAKE GEN CHEM WITH FERMAN!!! He is traditionally an honors professor where he should stay! During lecture, he goes off on tangents and does demonstrations that are unrelated to the topics. He unexpectedly assigns OWLs with no notice and not enough time to complete them. Be prepared to teach yourself from the book.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Beware of pop quizzes

reviews.comment: This may be because I wasn't in Honors when I took this class, but this guy has never taught a general chemistry course before and it shows. Everyone is teaching themselves, because whatever he mentions in class doesn't connect to the homework. I only showed up for the clickers. Wish he would dumb it down and start from the beginning.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Get ready to read

reviews.comment: If you're going to take an 8 AM take 121H with Ferman, but you do actually have to go to class to pass. While I felt lost at 75% of the lectures, I left each class feeling like I had learned and that I had just done something worthwhile. The take home exam took me 15 hours, but the other exams were very similar in difficulty to the homework.
Im just going to keep this short and sweet, if it is worth it to wake up for a 8 am class then it is this one
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: Prof. Fermann is the best choice for honors chem. He really cares about you and tries to explain everything in a deeper level to make sure you really understand the material and phenomena behind the basics of chemistry. He likes the physical/math side of things and teaches that way the most but he will always try to help your grade whenever he can.

Justin seriously was amazing. I took his chem 101 science of craft class and it was great. He was nice and funny and made an 8:30 lecture not as bad as it should have been. It was hard to do poorly on his tests because it was a 50/50 test where you take it individually and then with a group and he averages it to get your grade.

Fermann is the best choice for honors chem. He really cares about the student and makes you work for your grade, but also you learn a lot. He teaches chemistry from more of the physical and theoretical point of view to apply to general chemistry topics so you get a deeper understanding, and it really makes you question and think differently.

He teaches chemistry from a physics perspective, because he performed chemical physics work in his post-doc. It makes the class a little different, but he gives you a genuine understanding of the world, jumping from model to model of the atom. It can be difficult because this is vastly different than high school AP. Also, the two exams are tough.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--ACCESSIBLE OUTSIDE CLASS--GRADED BY FEW THINGS

reviews.comment: Love this man. He has a heart of gold. Sometimes his lectures may seem unorganized but it all comes together at the end and they way he teaches is actually super helpful once you catch on to his teaching style. Nicest dude ever.

My class was science of craft so we learned 4 amazing crafts that he's actually had experience with. He did a lot of in-class demonstrations. However his tests are VERY difficult. only 4 per sem and he grades 20/22  100%, so 2 freebies. BUT some questions are worded awkwardly/unclear. Final is group proj DIY craft and he gives Extra credit.
Brilliant professor. The course is rigorous (and relatively stressful), but he really cares and you'll end up learning a lot.

Fermann is a great professor and makes his lectures fun and interesting, despite them being at 8am. He can sometimes be difficult to follow, especially if he expects you have already learned about what he is talking about. Exams are tough, but one is a take home, and there are other grades that balance out your overall grade.

Class for me was not great. Have not taken chem is a while and if you think this class is not chem heavy your gonna be surprised. Basically its what you learn in high school but applied into crafts which is confusing and not straightforward if you have no background in chem. if you want an easy class for gen ed take something else.
Really great guy but really not the best teacher. Lecture material completely unrelated to test material and very hard to understand. He's not the most organized

Good professor. If you have to take honors chemistry, definitely take Justin. Funny, tough tests, but if you prepare for them you will do well. Barely any written homework - all online. He wants you to get an A as much as you do.

I took him in both Chem 121H and 122H. He peaks interest in chemistry. he digs in the materials and helps you understand deeper the materials. Exams are fairly hard but you can get a fair grade if you attend lectures, read book, and study the materials carefully

The man is amazing. He was my advisor (and my actual advisor) for NSO. I knew then that I'd be willing to wake up for his 8:00am WMF. He's extremely helpful, always there during office hours, and is just a really cool guy. I'm 100% taking his 122H class next semester. The tests are hard, but he really wants you to succeed and will help you do so.
I found the exams to be pretty hard.

Super helpful guy. This is my second semester with him by choice. If you didn't have a rigorous high school chemistry course, you'll have to put in some serious legwork. The SI was really helpful for condensed studying sessions before tests, but she's leaving next semester. Makes the 8 am worth it.

Fermann is my favorite teacher, always there if you need help, whether with his class or anything you need in general. The class is difficult, but he is there to help if you are willing to put in the effort. 8am class is pretty brutal, but he makes it a lot easier to deal with. Highly recommend him for this course.
He is such a nice guy and really cares about your learning. Attendance isnt mandatory, but you want to go just because he's that nice.
This class was difficult. It actually requires you to study and read the chapters. if you are going to take this class, make sure to do well on the exams!

Didn't follow the textbook/curriculum very closely. Although I found his tangents to be interesting, the nonlinear approach isn't very well-suited for an intro course. That being said, he's very insightful and helpful, and has a rather lenient testing policy.

Rly smart/nice guy! Rly tough class do, not take unless you need to/love chem. Lectures are scattered, he doesn't rly follow the book. Tests are hard, but doing book problems / taking good notes helped. The tests are not based on the owls. Really wanted everyone to do well+graded fairly. Go to class+put in effort and you'll do fine. 8am was a strug

Fermann was a very good teacher. He kept class interesting and engaged students. Very likable and approachable. Homework is not much and easy. Pyramid tests focus mostly on concepts, not as many calculations. SI Sessions were VERY helpful if explaining material. Class notes lack some structure. Looking forward to his 122H course next semester.

Fermann was easily the coolest guy at UMass, but he was absolutely useless as a professor. He was way too smart for the job and would either answer questions very circularly or not at all. I had to learn everything from either the book or OWL. Also his exams were wicked hard. However, he wants his students to do well, and he is a fair grader.

I think he is a great teacher that really tries to make you think. The class is very difficult and the tests are hard too but he is a very fair teacher. He takes the time to go through all of his topic so his students understand what is going on. You need to be good at chemistry to take his class. Great teacher.
very hard class. do not take unless you are very passioante about chemistry. that being said, he is a really nice guy and will help alot if you go to office hours.. very fair/ generous grader

He's not too bad if you're interested in chemistry. If you hate chemistry, it will seriously suck. Exams consist of mostly weird conceptual questions. Doing the questions in the back of the book is recommended, and I don't think I would have passed if I didn't read the book. He's a computer guy, so he won't go over any math, so heads up.
Fermann is an awesome professor. He really gets you to think and to try to figure out things on your own. Really study for the tests because they can be a tad difficult but nothing you cannot handle.

Fermann definitely was not a very straightforward teacher and liked to go off on tangents which did not help those who do not have a firm grasp on chemistry understand the topics. Gives pyramid exams which can really boost your grade. Overall not a bad guy, he just spent too much time expanding conceptual and superfluous examples.

During lecture, Fermann focused a great deal on the concepts behind molecular interaction.  He shows a great interest in helping students learn.  Tests are evenly composed of conceptual questions and math questions and can be difficult but pyramid exam helps.If you go to lecture,pay attention,and read and understand the book you can get an A

He's the better teacher out of the two for this class. He doesn't teach you the material really. You learn how to do all calculations and math from OWL. Do the OWL's over again, they show up on the exams. Final is tricky!!! Pyramid style exams help your grade A LOT.

A conceptual teacher and far different than my Chem 111 teacher. Sometimes you'll spend 20 minutes on one seemingly trivial problem and learn a lot about chemistry. Those who are intuitively good with chemistry will fair the best. Very fair grader and his tests are fair as well. The class flies by, so obviously I'm enjoying it. Recommended!

Not the best teacher I've ever had, but he's very smart and well-backgrounded. Some people just aren't fit for the class, but it's not his fault. The class is by no means easy, but you have plenty of opportunity to learn (SI, office hours, etc). Exams are average. Not too much homework (maybe once ever 1 and a half weeks). I recommend him.

This guy was an awkward teacher, no notes during class, OWLs were crazy because you had to learn the material by yourself. I mean he is a cool guy but his teaching just sucks. If you take this class it is probably a necessity to go to the SI sessions because they clear everything up.

Honestly chemistry is chemistry and it sucks either way. I think Fermann is good he can just get really theoretical sometime. I liked the pyramid style and he can be funny in class sometimes. I would take he's class!

Great Teacher. he is just very tough and expect you to know a lot. Its tough keeping up with him in class but he is pretty helpful when you ask questions. You need to ask questions to pass the course. He make you think outside th box which is something we are not used to doing. You need to read the textbook to do well.
Best teacher I've ever had.  Learned more from this course than any other.

Not sure how he is for 111 but for 112 he was honestly the best.  I took AP chem in high school so i understood some of the material better. Exams have a few trick type questions but are pretty generous to the practice exam. plus the pyramid testing works like a charm.

I had him for 111 and 112. I can honestly say he ruined chem for me. He is so arrogant and rude and talks down to people. I suppose his pyramid grading style is fair, but so few people would pass the class if he didnt do this (even after averaging in a take home test, tests avg around 60). He tests on material not covered. The worst prof I've had.

Not sure if he's best or not for Chem 111, (I had Adams for that and LOVEDDDD his teaching style), but DEF take Fermann for 112. Lets you take exams in class also at home averages the 2, NO reason you should fail, but I did NOT understand his lectures at all, most ppl were lost unless they put in some serious effort.

I had Fermann for both Chem 111 and 112. I got A's in both classes, but I really struggled for them. Yes, his test policy is great and it is fair, but I honestly have no idea what happened in either class. I attended almost all lectures and payed attention. Unless you are obsessed with chem, don't take it with Fermann. He is also arrogant and rude.

I'm glad I'm not the only one who found him attractive... in a nerdy way of course.  Judging the class is hard because chemistry was not a subject I ever would have taken by choice.  But Justin was an entertaining teacher - funny and did some interesting experiments in class.
difficult class. uses PRS for attendance. keep up with textbook readings or you will be completely lost. however, VERY generous with test grading (take home exams).

He speaks and I just don't understand what he's saying. He goes off on tangents so when you take notes they don't make any sense. I was a chem major going into UMass, and I switched after first semester. Horrible teacher.

Fermann is a great professor. I had his for 111 and didn't take advantage of his teaching abilities by missing class but now in 112 i'm almost always in lecture. He explains everything vividly (just make sure your vocabulary is on point) and when it comes to test time he has more than a fair/generous testing policy. The best chem professor
Fermann is the man! All those people who say he is too hard are probably the kids who facebooked in class. He explains the material extremely well and made me love chemistry!
Tests were extremely hard, I was saved by PRS and OWL's. I would avoid this guy at all costs
I want to marry Justin Fermann.
Hard teacher, completely in his own head. Goes off subject all the time and never explained anything too well. I'm not sure if the other Chemistry teacher is any better...
He's freaking awesome.  He teaches the material with a passion and goes out of his way to engage the class.  He inspired my interest in chemistry.

An awful professor! He told us that he designs the tests so that if you come to every lecture, do all homework and reading, you can get a 75 on the tests. to get higher you have to figure out problems that haven't been covered. Tests aren't remotely related class material. He is the most pompous man I have ever met! take chem 111 with someone else!

After taking 112 with Voigtman I miss Fermann. Great teacher, fun to attend class, interesting to listen to. Sometimes he gives the same exams taken in class to take home, and then counts the take home as 25% of the exam. Clear instructions and demonstrations. Definitely take chem with him if you need to take it.

Extremely knowledgeable and one of the best professors I've had.  Makes you think about what you're doing and makes you work for your grade.  Puts extraordinary amount of effort into transferring information to the students in the class, and gives all students an opportunity to succeed.

I came into the school majoring in Chemistry. After taking his class, I immediately changed my major. He's funny and makes the class interesting to attend but there are so many things that was wrong. I worked so hard and learned nothing at all. His lectures are nothing at all related to the book. Exams are crazy hard.  I hated him.

really great professor. at first i didnt know what i had gotten myself into but if you show up for class, put in effort, and study, then you should have no problem. studying is huge with his exams. He's big on understanding general concepts and applying them. awesome class

justin fermann is an AWESOME teacher. if you hate chemistry take it with him..hes really helpful, easygoing, and funny. Tests are very fair and he gives practice ones to help you study. overall, i thoroughly enjoyed this class and am taking chem 112 with him..and realllly cute!!

He makes the class very intereting to listen to. However some of the things he teaches aren't much related to the book. He wants you to learn more than anything. He's fair and funny. He's memorable and it's just not a typical class. That can be a con or pro, depends.
Has a good sense of humor and makes chemistry interesting. He is willing to work with you, though sometimes he isn't very clear. Added bonus, he's really hot.
Hard test but very fair grader. Wants to see student learn more than anything. Great class

he is a difficult professor. Not a memorable professor though who can drill things into your mind for helpful studying. He was a bit funny at times but that has nothing to do w/ anything like exams, etc. I did decent on the exams without the help of a textbook. The class was okay. I can't really trash it.
No Comments

Lectures are really interesting to attend. Not the typical monotone, boring lecturer. Very supportive and speaks in terms students can comprehend. I would go back to him for any Chemistry help in the future. We primarily use OWL for homework.
Fermann is a very charismatic professor.  Personally, however, I had a hard time learning with the way that he taught.

He is a very hard professor but is willing to help you if you go to office hours. I am terrible at chem but he managed to help me through it. Nice guy with a good sense of humor. If you do well in lab and do all the prs and owls you'll do fine.

A nice guy but incredibly hard. I studied for hours for his tests and still managed to get F's on his exams. People say going to him for extra help helps, but every time I go he's swamped with other students. I once waited an hour and a half to talk to him, and my "help" lasted only 5 minutes. This guy has a sense of humor but at the same time teac
He is a very good teacher. The material is hard, but he makes it easy to understand as long as you go to class. LOTS of OWLS, but they really do help you learn. I would definately recommend him

He's amazing, and he definately wants you to be mini versions of himself. Although he may seem tough, the material isn't that hard. Just make sure you always ask him what he's looking for. Doesn't go by the book, but make sure you read it. Teaches it like his 121H. Bonus: not so bad to look at. Just do the work (OWLS PRS ETC) and you will get an A!

This guy is amazing! I have to say, I hated chemistry before and I hate it now, but if you seek his help he will be more than happy to help you. He's hilarious in class, but his exams are hard as hell and you better know your stuff. An 85 is an A but it's still hard to get there. Go to class, do your OWLs, and study! I love him!

His lectures may seem unclear, but much of the time kids don't put in the effort to study when there is not an exam. He is fair, and I've gone to his office hours and he is extremely helpful. Make sure you study his notes, and watch out for the second exam, it's tough. He makes you think, and you are learning more than what you thought. Hes awesome

He is a very funny guy,who tries to make his lectures interesting,but his tests are extremelly hard. The average range b/w the high 50s to mid 60s.He is all over the place with the material, meaning one second he talks about radiactive decay the next he talks about something that has to do with chemistry but not with radioactive decay. DONT TAKE IT

He teaches the 110 series in a unique order which I find better.  He is very kind, and a fair teacher.  First half of 111 is a primer on physics which is helpful for understanding the chemistry that follows.  Gives a LOT of owl's.  Most students find his class tough, yet they are learning more than they think.  Tests are fair.  I recommend him!
He's a great teacher, I hate chemistry but he tries to keep it interesting. He knows his stuff and he's a really nice guy, willing to help you out if you go talk to him

Don't take this class if you do not have a strong chemistry background!! Does not give slides, notes, practice tests that can be used to study, or stay within the book. Class averages on tests are D's or F's. I ended up having to go to a tutor and have him reteach me everything. Common class comment, "I don't understand what you just did."
I would recommend him to anyone taking this class.  Helpful and passionate.

For me, I need lots of hw practice. Thus, I liked having Botch: worksheets, a billion owls, and 2 hour tests intended for 1 hour w/ notecard (you put whatever you want on them). Fermann gives few owls, a couple take HW that are tough, and in-class exams w/out notecard. If you are more of an auditory and visual SELF learner, he's for you.
such a good professor!! take chem 111 with fermann if you can...very intelligent, clear with his explanations, gives practice tests similar to his exams.  go to class and you will do well.

GO TO CLASS!! very nice, helpful, enthusiastic proffessor. but sometimes a little un-clear and gives alot of un-needed info, so its alot to handle at once. and he moves at a fast pace. owl homework is not always the same as his exams. exams are tricky, and puts complicated probs on them. and PURCHASE the book, dont rely on the ebook

Best chem teacher ever.  I usually hate chem, the most tedious of all the sciences.  However, I loved this class.  I feel like I've learned more in this than in any other science class I've taken.  Fermann is funny and will go out of his way to help you.  He is currently up for UMass's yearly 'best professor award,' and I hope he gets it.
Extremly hard class. Smart teacher, but dosent explain the material well.

He is unbelievably intelligent and motivates you to learn the material.  Also if you want a good grade, he will make it so you get one, that is if you want to put the effort in.  He really portrays the subject well, and is great in front of a class.  I would highly suggest him as a teacher.  He can be tricky on exams, but he makes you think!

The class is definitely difficult, but he is very willing to help you understand the material.  He uses a lot of helpful visual demos.  He is very approachable and helpful.  If you make the effort, you will do well in his class.  In general, he is just a very good teacher.

Great Professor.  Very good at explaining the material.  Just make sure you go to class because some of his exam questions can be a little tricky. Going to class will help prepare you for the harder test questions.

He is an awesome teacher. He explains chem so easily and it's hard not to do well in the class. His tests are pretty much the same every year and last years are posted online. so you can get an idea of what the test is going to cover.
He was by far the best professor I had first semester. He is insanely smart and does a great job of explaining even the toughest concepts.
He doesn't explain things well at all and his tests are tricky! I would try to take the class with someone else.

Fermann was the best chem teacher I have had. He incites interest and genuinely loves what he teaches. A good professor to teach a foundation for chemistry- especially if you are going on to more complex chem classes...
awesome teacher. very clear. i loved this class.
Great teacher.  Pick him if you can.
LOVED him LOVED him!! He is super nice,understanding and helpful!!!AWESOME GUY!
Fermann is an awesome teacher.  He is SO funny and is always excited about chemistry.  His tests are tough but fair, just do the owls and the old practice tests and go to his reviews.  Hes hott too.

He's an awesome teacher and explains everything really clearly and stops to answer questions and make sure everyone understands. The class definetly goes at a good pace but you have to attend class to do well. Exams are okay and he grades very fairly. If you don't like chem, take it with him
He's not too clear, and test are pretty hard a lot of work in his class, but with hard work the pay off is good
Fermann is an awesome teacher. He explains everything very clearly and his practice tests are just like the actual tests just a little bit harder. Take this class with him!
He is a good teacher but he is tough. his lectures are sometimes hard to follow but the owls clear it up. exams are tough but if u go to class and do the homework you will be fine.

No doubt he is a hard prof, but it is a foundation course and ferman did an amazing job at teaching it. in order to do good in his class DO THE OWLS, GO TO CLASS, and if u'r aiming for an A than do the problems in the back of the book.
Best Prof at Umass as well
He's HOT
Not a class where you can slack off, but you shouldn't slack in a foundation course anyway, makes you work but isn't that what you're here for? Very helpful, not condesending even though he could be.

this guy has an issue with writing fair exams

way to go Fermann!

nice guy but expecting way too much from an introductory chemistry class for non-majors

I only took his entry-level chem course, none of the harder ones, so I didn't find it too difficult. As long as you show up to class you won't have any trouble (and if you do, it's easy to get help). Definitely on of the best professors i've ever had.
class can be very tough!

His tests are really hard, he even said he wanted to be tricky, but he's so unbelievably intelligent, helpful, and funny. The final was a breeze. Easy to get a good grade if you show you want to put an effort in: curves.

Professor Fermann is an AWESOME TEACHER if ur planning on going to med school and you want to pass orgo take him. you will learn a****load. He's funny and cool. His tests are challenging but study and you'll pass. Plus an 80 is an A. i love fermann

Justin is the coolest professor that I've had so far in college. Although his class is real hard, he really doesn't want to fail any of us and he REALLY tries to help! He's real cool and nice too. If something is unclear, he's more willing to help you out
Justin is a great professor. his class is extremely challenging, but he is willing to take time out of his schedule to meet personally with students and give them the help they need.
Challenging class, yet he makes it interesting. He definitely puts in a great amount of effort, which makes you try harder. I'd recommend him.

Fermann is the best chem proffesor ive ever had. He really knows his chemistry and he actually makes it interesting. One of the few classes I actually looked forward to going to. (Along with Bio 100 with Randall Phillis)

Class was fairly challenging, but he was an excellent teacher and really showed interest in wanting us to learn.Also,one of the only science profs I have had that hand-graded all of our exams w/ comments, etc.  even though it was a big lecture.

You need to go and take notes to do well you will also need to study the text book. Go to class take notes and be engaged and you will do well.

reviews.comment: Be ready for the quizzes and exams. It just a midterm and a final. be sure to take GREAT notes during lecture because the quizzes and exams are very specific. You get a cheat sheet so make sure to put as much as you can. Extra credits are VERY helpful so make sure to do the required assignments. 1 group project, read directions carefully.

reviews.comment: Worst Professor I've ever had. He makes the quizzes and exams so particular and detailed that you look at the paper and say "what am I even looking at." You have so much material to study for yet he chooses the smallest and most random things to test you on

need to take GREAT notes to pass his exams because they were hard, open notes tho. Allowed for 12 pnts of extra credit to be received, missing only 5 classes was 5 extra points, this was slay. only annoying thing is hes very specific. Gave me a .9 on my extra assignment because I didn't capitalize 1 word. Very knowledgeable guy tho, learned A LOT.

Professor Fiocchi is a no-nonsense type of guy, but he does make most expectations extremely clear. Very knowledgeable, slides in class are well thought out and organized. If you pay attention to the lectures and make sure you understand each concept the quizzes/exams are fine. Few assignments/quizzes/exams, so if you miss a deadline its no good.

Great guy, funny, and teaches some really cool stuff. Beware there is a rather difficult project at the end, there's only 6 homeworks, and midterm isn't hard. Pay attention, learn the calculations, download the slides, and you'll do well.

reviews.comment: Fiocchi's class is very content-heavy. Most people complaining about this class flat out don't pay attention or study. This class requires you to genuinely learn what is going on you can't BS your way through the course. Fiocchi's grading format forces you to study a lot since exams/quizzes are the bulk of our grades.

Fiocchi is extremely knowledgeable. You will learn an insane amount in this class. There is no homework in this class so your entire grade is from quizzes and tests that are very very hard and one group project that isn't that hard but the guidelines/format is unclear.
reviews.rating_tags: Graded by few things--Test heavy--Group projects

reviews.comment: Fiocchi is a great guy you should go to his lectures for sure. No HW for 313 so quizzes and exams are huge. Dont leave final project for the end of the class and put some good work into it. Do the extra credit it helps a lot. Overall good class pay attention to the red in the slides and the details, quizzes and exams are very specific.

Professor Fiocchi is a great guy and does seem to care about his students. For some reason though, I am always confused when doing the assignments and exams. Maybe I don't pay enough attention in the lectures but it never seems like I learn much. It might just be me but I've taken 3 classes with Professor Fiocchi and everytime I've struggled. Tough

He is indeed one of the best professors I took. He really cares about his students' improvement in future career. The exam is pretty hard but straightforward but if you pay attention in class you will be fine. There are no recorded lectures and slides are mostly companies' data since it only understandable during lectures. He deserves 5s rating.

Robert Feingold is hands down the best professor I've had through my college career. The topic itself is challenging, but he does a great job breaking down what you need to know. I can't say enough good about him, easy grader, funny guy, easily accessible when you need help, and a caring professor who wants to see his students do well. Love him!

This was a great class to take and Prof. Feingold clearly cares about his students. Exams were hard, but if you genuinely pay attention in class and properly study they will come easy to you. The homework  were relatively straightforward. Group project was not too bad as long as you communicate well with your group.

Robert is a great professor. His class is hard, but he does his best to help you succeed. He gives a decent amount of HW, but its not too difficult and most of it prepares you for real-world work you'll do in the office. His lectures are great. He is entertaining, funny, and gives real world stories from his experiences. His ratings make sense here

Great professor, but he makes you work for a good grade. The midterm & final were long and difficult (if you did not study for them). He randomly sprinkles in HW as you learn new concepts, so they're usually due the next class. Make sure to read the book & watch the movies bc there will be Qs abt them on the exams.
W (I needed to type 10 characters so here more)

The single greatest professor I've ever had. Rob is an absolute legend, Isenberg is extremely lucky to have him. I was absolutely enthralled each and every class. Learned more in one semester (507,509) about finance than I had in all my other courses combined. Running against a world limit but TAKE HIS CLASS. Thanks for everything, Rob - Kyle M

There is always one professor in your major that everyone raves about and Rob is Finance's. Let me be clear: if you can take ANY of his classes, do it. I still regret not taking his Careers In Finance class. He's hilarious, teaches like you'd hope all teachers would, and you come out of the class ACTUALLY HAVING LEARNED SOMETHING.

Rob is seriously the best there is. I've had an extremely rough semester and Rob was very accommodating for everything going on in my life. He's very good at explaining things and is very patient with the class. He's also a very funny guy in general and is one of the few professors here that can keep their class engaged with the material.

Hands down the best professor in Isenberg. The material is definitely not easy, but he prepares you well for the real world. He cares so much more about just the material and teaches you life lessons that are so important. Take every class you possibly can with Rob, he is so smart and cares about the success of his students!

Such a great professor! Not the most exciting material but he makes the lectures great! He's funny and gives great advice. The midterm and final were not easy but he prepares you well. You receive random HW which helps your grade and a big group project that was difficult. Overall, if you pay attention, you'll get a solid grade and learn a lot.

One of my favorite professors of all time. He's engaging, knowledgeable, and very entertaining. You learn a lot. Class which consists of two exams, some assignments, and a big group project. My only problem is his tests include questions about books you must read but those questions are way too trivial and don't show an understanding of the book.

What a professor he is!! An absolute gem and most definitely one of the best classes I have had! he makes classes interesting and relatable to the real world! He always has stories to tell from his hedge fund manager days, makes classes interesting! there is a reason why he is highly rated here! I wish I had taken him more times! it was a pleasure!

Rob is one of the best professors ive ever had. he has so much knowledge from actually working in finance and treats his students like entry level employees who are learning about the industry. this is not the easiest class but rob is understanding and deeply cares about his students. take a class with him if possible!
reviews.rating_tags: Respected--Participation matters--Skip class? You won't pass.

reviews.comment: Rob is awesome and keeps class interesting. I took Fixed Income (509) with him last semester and this class is identically structured. No textbook but he assigns 3 good books to read. Take notes on the slides (& books) and you'll breeze through the exams. They're straight forward and he basically gives you a heads up about what might be on them.

Funny professor and a good class. You don't need the book, just his slides. You read 3 books during the semester that are all good reads and on the exams. One midterm, one group project, and a final exam. A couple short homeworks along the way but he basically just grades for completion and they're to help you with how to do the project

Fixed Income with Professor Feingold is a good class to take if you have significant experience with bond and capital analysis. He explains topics very quickly and assumes that students already know what he's talking about. His lectures are full of unexplained jargon. Don't take classes with him unless you already know much about the topic.

Awesome course. Great introduction to finance and lots of guest speakers. You have to read two books but it's not a lot of work. One paper and one quiz and you just have to show up and pay attention to the guest speakers. I learned a lot and was super easy to pass.
reviews.rating_tags: Respected--Graded by few things--Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: Rob was by far my favorite professor at Isenberg. He has a great sense of humor and awesome stories. He keeps lectures light by showing clips from shows and movies. That said the material is tough, so you're going to have to study quite a bit. Grading criteria is very clear. Midterm, Final, Attendance, and Project. Always accessible and a great guy

Great guy with a ton of industry experience. He keeps lectures light and has a good sense of humor. The work load isn't too bad but his tests can be unpredictable. Material is definitely difficult at times as the class is structured off of real world finance work. Would highly recommend if you want go into the finance/banking/Investment industry.
Is Rob the GOAT? If Tom Brady, Michael Jordan, Wayne Gretzky, Muhammad Ali, and 4 actual goats all had a kid ... his name would be Rob Feingold. Simply put.

Rob's class was truly enjoyable. He worked in finance for over 20 years and has tons of practical industry experience. The work you do in his class is realistic and extremely important for investment related career paths. A couple exciting books, 3 exams, usually an assignment a week, and one group project. Cares if students are really learning.
YOOOOO Feingold is the man brah. PEACE.
He's a great guy, actually cares if students are learning. The most practical finance teacher I've yet to have.
What an amazing professor he truly knows his stuff from his previous professions and uses that practical knowledge to teach his class.

Rob is the smartest and most practical finance professor in Isenberg. If you want to do: Investment Management, Investment Banking, Equity/Credit Research or any of the other top front office roles, he teaches you all of the pre-requisites: DCF modeling, comparable companies, 3 statement model, cap tables, etc. Has incredible industry experience.

One of the best professors I had in college. He has the most real world experience of any of the finance professors and it really shows. In terms of work, you will have a couple of projects, a midterm, and final. He clearly outlines what he wants and how to do it. Personally, I did not find this class to be very hard, but I know a few who did.

Took his LING 201 class. Prof. Faruk plans his lectures very well, and uses class time effectively. As long as you show up to lectures, you'll do fine. He makes sure students understand the class material really solidly, but won't elaborate beyond the scope of the course. However, this keeps class on-topic and on track.
I don't recommend

Great class! Explains the subject matter clearly & is enthusiastic about it too. Communicates well w/ the class & is a good person in general! There's a section where (as it's a gen ed class) we go over the IPA, so if u're alr a LING major & took 201 prior to this, that part'll be pretty easy. If u need to fulfill your HIS gen ed, take this class!
Awful

Professor Akkus is very good at explaining difficult concepts. His syntax class is very informative, and I appreciated the detailed explanations on the slides. It is important to show up to lectures, since he moves quickly through the material. Office hours were at accessible times, as were the TA's.
Fantastic at Explaining Concepts. Would take him many times more. This is from 150 Ling not 401 though. It did not give me the option to chose this class.

He tries his best and he's nice, but syntax is very difficult and I think he struggles to explain it sometimes. If you miss a single class, you MUST rewatch the lectures to catch up. It's not a lot of work, but it's a very challenging class and he grades quite harshly sometimes. He's very nice, though, and willing to help those in need.

What an amazing teacher. I really enjoyed his class. He cares a lot about the students and the subject he teaches. The grading criteria were pretty clear, and you will do well if you show up and put in little effort. The news quiz took some getting used to.
reviews.rating_tags: Amazing lectures --Clear grading criteria--Gives good feedback

reviews.comment: It is just a discussion based class that is worth 1 credit. There were weekly discussion posts due that made up most of your grade. The discussions were fun and Prof. Fox led them well. Overall really fun and easy class.
This guy might be the GOAT of UMass. Incredible guy who feels more like a friend than a professor. Couldn't recommend him enough.

Professor Fox was far and away the best professor I had in my freshman year at UMass, he was funny, knowledgeable, engaging, and you got the sense that he really cared about his field and his students. Take this class if you get the chance, even if you are not studying or interested in journalism directly.

The most challenging part of this class is by far the news quizzes, however, as the semester goes on it is easy to get the hang of what/how much to read. Additionally, if pop quizzes aren't your strong suite, the reaction papers, (open book) midterm, and final paper make up a significant portion of the final grade.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Clear grading criteria
