reviews.comment: Fox was one of my favorite professors at UMass. This class is really just based on engagement. Mostly writing papers, Fox will talk you through and want to be updated on your progress. He is very engaging and not an easy grader, but a fair one. Be ready to be pushed outside your comfort zone and be confused about due dates occasionally.

Most of the class is pretty straightforward and not terribly difficult. He's a pretty lenient grader and papers aren't terribly long, plus Bull Quizzes (textbook) and midterm is open note. However, the news quizzes were the only hard part as questions range from local national and international news. Theyre either general or very specific questions
reviews.rating_tags: Beware of pop quizzes--So many papers

reviews.comment: Took Sports in Film, Literature and Journalism with him. Not my first class with Fox and have always enjoyed them. Aside from a few papers and books to read, the work is not too intense in this class, and he's always flexible about due dates and willing to cooperate with students. Class is heavy on discussions.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Gives good feedback--Caring

reviews.comment: Professor Fox is the best!! I had him for intro to news writing and reporting and it was one of my favorite classes at UMass by far! His lectures are extremely engaging  and he even brings in cool guest speakers. He is also understanding about deadlines and extensions if you shoot him an email or let him know. I would highly recommend  Fox!!

News Quizzes can be tough at times, sometimes having rather obscure topics. His lectures are fairly engaging with many real-world examples, and while the discussions can drag a bit, they often do address important topics. The papers are usually fairly straight-forward, with most being a minimum of 500 words. Took for a gen-ed, would recommend.

Very disrespectful attitude and not flexible about deadlines, absences, or hardships. Prefers you to almost repeat material given instead of actual critical thinking if it does not align with his beliefs or opinions. Is totally unapproachable about issues you may have, personal or professional and gives no guidance. Many assignments are vague.
Be prepared for class and make sure to complete assignments on time. falling behind is not the best idea.
It's a one-credit course so not a ton of work and only one graded assignment. Does his best to check in and get to know his students, I'd love to take another class with him. Talks a lot about Trump

I thought this class was pretty easy: everyone in my class got an A since we showed up and participated in a group discussion every class. Professor Fox mostly just let the discussion go wherever we wanted it to. Not too much work required outside of class.

This is by far my favorite class I've taken at UMass. Professor Fox is an amazing guy and it's evident that he just wants to see his students succeed. Lectures were always very interesting, and the assignments for this class were weekly memos due each Sunday by midnight, and a short news quiz at the start of every class. Couldn't recommend more!

Pretty chill professor, who has a lot of experience and examples to give for what he teaches. The classes were always interesting, and there isn't a ton of work. The news quizzes are tough, but he's a pretty easy grader in everything else, so it balances out. Also seems tough, but he's a pretty nice guy.
Great guy, chill class. Knows his stuff and is super approachable.

Front page was a wonderful class with light work and insightful discussions. Professor Fox was very understanding about how difficult this online semester has been for many, and you can tell he genuinely cares for his students. Definitely take this for the honors contemporary topics rap if he's teaching the course again!

Professor Fox is very knowledgeable and I learned several solid things from his news literacy class. There are 9 500-word-minimum writing assignments that are due at midnight on Sunday. He has a relevant news quiz every class which can be difficult to to get any right or easy to get 6/5 (bonus question each class). There is a 10 dollar book to read

Steve is a good guy. He doesn't have a lot of patience for your mistakes so always be prepared. This class requires A TON of outside work so make sure you have a light semester when you take it. As long as you get all your work done and have some knowledge about sports it isn't too hard to succeed in this class. Lectures are two hours long but fun.

I was assigned to the high school beat, which meant I was out covering football, basketball, hockey games etc. which usually happened on weekends. The class was A LOT of work, I probably wrote close to 10,000 words total. However, he really knows what he's talking about and it is great experience for anyone seriously interested in the industry.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough Grader--LOTS OF HOMEWORK--ACCESSIBLE OUTSIDE CLASS

reviews.comment: Good professor, annoying Sunday deadlines. Class time is well spent. Attendance is mandatory and there are quizzes every class.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough Grader--BEWARE OF POP QUIZZES--SO MANY PAPERS

reviews.comment: This class was my favorite class this semester, and Steve was the reason why. His class uses current events in the world, so I would suggest downloading news apps, reading the local paper, and keeping on top of what's going on around the world. His news quizzes are fair, and his "bull quizzes" (textbook) are open-book, so they're very easy to pass.

Loved this class and Professor Fox - you can tell he has a ton of experience in the field and he has a true talent for passing on his knowledge to his students. Gives great feedback on weekly memos and really gets students involved in the subject matter without being overbearing - for sure looking for more classes with him in the future!

Steve Fox is an extremely enthusiastic professor, always happy to help students and will help them find opportunities in the department.  He gives excellent advice, his class is very helpful to those interested in media and journalism. Make sure to show up to class though, he will take points off if you don't show up.

Quiz every class on the morning's news headlines. Wake up early and look at the news. Occasional quizzes on the book. Weekly 1-2 pg. memo due every Sunday. Great lectures, not too much work, VERY important stuff for journalism students and news consumers to know.

Fox is a great professor, although he isn't the clearest at times, I have gotten a lot of great feedback and skills from his class that I am going to continue to use in future journ classes and careers.  Great guy, great class environment, one of my favorite professors I've had at UMass.

Steves classes are work intensive and require a lot of time, they are more than worth it. I got more experience in his classes than any other, and while grading was tough, it ultimately made me a better writer and reporter. If you're serious about Journalism, then these are the classes that will prepare you for a newsroom.

A LOT of work outside of class, including weekends. Mandatory attendance, usually a difficult grader, not always clear in what he wants in an assignment. If you write sports for the Collegian, don't think you'll get an easy A, he tends to be harder on you guys. Fox does have a lot of experience, so take all the advice you can from him.

Steve is very good journalism teacher and a solid person. I have been a student in his multimedia class as well as a TA for the class. Both experiences have been positive. He is not an easy teacher and requires a lot from his student but that's always better than it being too easy. After taking multiple class with Steve I would recommend him highly

Fox's Multimedia Journalism class should be a requirement for all journalism students. He really know his stuff, so absorb all you can. Workload is more than most classes (reporting outside of class) but not overloading. Don't miss class, don't be late and pay attention!

The class started out with a clear goal in mind. However, as the semester progressed the expectations and the requirements were kind of thrown out the window. I felt that Fox checked out mentally mid way through the semester and didn't really care to give helpful feedback on the majority of work. He makes you question the value of your education.

Steve was one of the best professors I've had at UMass. He completly changed the way I think about sports journalism. The course required a lot of work outside of class, but it was definitely worth it!

I took his multimedia and sports journalism class and they were both awesome. His background speaks for itself, the guy knows his stuff. If your a journalism student take a course with him, he has a lot of connections and he knows the new age of journalism. Going to class is the easy part its what he has you do outside of class that is difficult.

This was a very interesting and fun class. I recommend it to anybody in the journalism department or anybody planning to be. We created several different video pieces of journalism and several audio-slide shows as well. Attendance is mandatory, as Fox said to miss class "either your dead or I'm dead." I think he was joking, but I wouldn't skip.

Attendance isn't mandatory, but usually you have to go in order to pass in assignments or take weekly quizzes. He is strict about arriving to class on time or else you cannot take quizzes. We have lots of little assignments including blogs, current events quizzes and writing news stories. However, I learned a lot in the class.
I would not take courses with her because she was not available most of the time and does not respond to concerns or questions, I was frustrated.

The course felt disorganized at times (e.g., a section lacked an SI leader). The practice midterm was much easier than the actual exam, making expectations unclear. Calculator policies changed multiple times, and students needing accommodations were asked to come to the front during the first quiz, which was uncomfortable.
She is hilarious and the topics are fun. She explains difficult concepts very well. The course is organized and well-structured.

The class is not well structured, and exams test your handwriting speed more than actual knowledge.
She was not reachable outside the class.
She seemed like a good lecturer though, I kinda wish I paid more attention to the lectures.

She's funny and really helps you in her office hours. However, her teaching style is horrendous, like an audio reading of slides. The pace is quite fast, and the lecture is really boring. Attendance is mandatory but all she does was reading off the slides.

Great professor that cares about nurturing  students ability to learn not just reciting the material. Willing to answer any and all questions if you ask so feel free to speak up. She understands the material well and can explain a concept in multiple ways. Bonus she's funny and stays after to help with individual questions or hw. She is fantastic
Great lectures. Reasonable exams. No homework.
I liked the way she teaches.

Explains well and in detail. Sometimes uses the board to go through something step by step. Makes sure everyone learns. The Homeworks are fair. She is funny, kind and caring. Cannot wait to take 311 with her.
Class goes very fast. Very basic explanation of topics, doesn't seems like she really know how to explain. Be prepared to study a lot outside of class
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Lecture heavy--Test heavy

reviews.comment: Lessons are very unorganized, and she wastes a lot of time in class. She adds a lot of extra material, into the syllabus, just to make the class harder. Her voice makes it very hard to concentrate, very tiring. She like minding other's business. You cannot talk in class even if it's a class related discussion.
One of the better CICS profs out there.

Funny professor with clear gift for teaching and explaining complex topics like graph theory, dynamic programming and more in a clear and accessible fashion for students. Plus, lenient grading for exams, challenge sets and such so I ended up learning a lot. Would highly recommend others to take this course with her if possible.

Pretty funny professor, does her best teaching a course that's notoriously known to be hard. She does a pretty good job, all things considered. Covers topics well and tries to keep people involved. The class itself is just hard and tricky if you don't have the logic brain for it, but not Parvini's fault.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Lots of homework--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: Parvini is kind, funny, and pretty. However, she's very unorganized, her lecture slides and homework sheets have multiple typos, and she's unresponsive to emails. This was her first time teaching this course so it might improve in the future. The class was relatively easy, but very boring. I'd still take her over Mark Wilson.

Professor Parvini's course is disorganized and frustrating. The final covers two-thirds of the material, but no proper practice exams are provided. Lecture slides, often error-ridden, are unavailable until three days after class—after homework is due. Frequent mistakes in homework further hinder learning, reflecting poor course management.
I learned a lot in this class. She is nice and funny.

Absolutely loved her. It was her first time teaching the course and she did a great job. She was caring. Explained examples in detail when we had questions. She knows if you are listening or not. 240 was my favorite class because of her.
Only main criticism is that lecture slides, homework, discussion, and exams were littered with typos, often to the point where they would affect your answer.

Parvini's 311 was a fun experience. She's funny and goes through good examples in class. The grading criteria overall was pretty lenient and the exams typically have a few easy questions, few mediums, and one or two hard ones. Better experience than 250 imo

311 with Parvini is alright. She's pretty funny in the lectures and tends to explain fairly well, although the lectures can still be boring. Exams were mixed in terms of difficulty. Textbook is pretty good if you read it. The TAs were good, and the homework load overall was not too bad. Sometimes she moved through the content a bit too slow.

There are a few problems with her as a prof, since it can be hard to reach her outside of class, and communication is not always the most straightforward. However, she is nice and CICS110 with her isn't hard if you pay attention in class.

I have mixed feelings about Prof. Parvini. On one hand I thought her class was pretty disorganized and disliked her lecture style (use of paper notebook on projector). On the other hand she's really nice and also told us how she had a really stressful semester which made me want to cut her more slack. I'd still recommend Barrington for 250.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Very good professor, very clear explanations especially graph theory topics

Professor Parvini explains concepts clearly and gives helpful responses to questions, but her teaching style may come off as disorganized. Some of the content is interesting and useful, but some is miserably annoying. The homeworks were definitely challenging and took quite a bit of time. Quizzes were somewhat tricky, but the exams were very fair.

Took her for 311 (not an option), and her grading was really bad. She also never ever responds to email, so don't even bother. Incredibly frustrating to work with, and lacks lecture enthusiasm, so you end up dreading class. The content could be interesting if you got useful feedback on challenges, which was not the case, just ''major/minor error"

If taking during the summer, she assigns a lot of content, even up to 2 hours of asynchronous videos, in addition to 3 75 minute lectures and a 50 minute discussion per week (plus weekly homework that takes several hours). She is fairly monotone which can make the lectures boring, but she does put in effort and explains well. The TAs were great.

CS250 was an exam-heavy, content-heavy math class with a lot of homework. Professor Parvini explained things well and in detail, but her lectures are not very organized time-wise. Overall ,her lectures were better than just reading the textbook or watching recordings from the other class. She was not that active on Piazza or office hours.

She threw a tantrum over a regrade request in which she failed to acknowledge where she was wrong about my solution. She also tends to arrive late to class and lacks overall time management/organizational skills. Apart from that she seems like a nice woman though, and she at least tries (sometimes).

Her time management is a mess. She uses iClicker questions for attendance and gives them out after class has ended, meaning that in order to be marked for attendance you have to stay late. She has also arrived late on multiple occasions, essentially without warning, and it feels like she's constantly in a rush.

Lectures were fast-paced, disorganized, and not particularly engaging. It's really hard to follow what she's doing and I usually have to self-teach the material. Often she would continue teaching or do a clicker question past when the class is supposed to end.
Great person, just not the best teacher.

She was nice, her notes were enough for me not to have to dig through the textbook constantly, but grading was... odd. Homeworks were kind of crazy, usually not being relevant to exam material. Generous with extra credit on exams, though. Quizzes were like 1/3 material not in lecture/homeworks/exams, she gave extra points on all of them though.

I really tried to like her since she seemed like a sweet woman, but this class just felt boring. I stopped attending her lectures after the second week as she was just regurgitating stuff from the textbook. She is also hard to reach, even TAs and UCAs were frustrated. I do however liked that she was generous with the extra credits on the exams.

Incredibly generous in handing out extra credit, with exams having 10+ points up for grabs. Sure, the course scheduling turned out a mess, but everything you really needed was in the textbook. Unfortunately, the textbook is also awful.

Always behind. Quizzed on content we weren't taught. Disorganized to a point where it seriously compromises your grade. Constantly giving extensions on things, not because she's caring or understanding, but because she is constantly behind content. Does not often respond outside of class on our public forum. Ignores. avoid
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Lots of homework--So many papers

reviews.comment: No PPTs or online resources, although attendance isn't mandatory, she makes it kinda required to go to class

She was not prepared for classes and very disorganized. She didn't pace the class properly and then had us watch several hours of lectures out of class the last week to make up for it. She also moved the final earlier with less than 24 hours heads up. She was decent at explaining the content, but the disorganization outweighs it heavily.

Ghazaleh was nice and knowledgeable, but her lectures were sometimes hard to understand. The pace of the class was also extremely fast, so there was no time to get a grasp on concepts without doing a ton of studying. Assignments were sometimes easy and sometimes close to impossible. The midterm had an incredibly low average, and wasn't curved.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Lots of homework

reviews.comment: She's very knowledgeable, kind, and mostly helps when needed, but if you're a beginner, AVOID. She did not seem to know at all how to pace the class or teach to beginners and it made the class terrible for me. Some tests were overly difficult as were all the projects, but the grading policy is very fair. Overall, good prof, bad for novices.

I went to every lecture and barely retained anything. So nice and will try to answer your question if you have one(I never had any tho bc I was always so confused I didnt know what to ask) Everything I learned was from the ZyBook textbook. Group lab once a week and 6 projects. There are better profs for 121 especially if u dont have prior knowledge
She teaches well, and shes a great person
The best thing about her is she teaches best.

Her voice can be a bit monotone, and she seem to lack energy in teaching. Class can be very boring. I went to few lectures and stop going. The class can be too easy if you already have some knowledge in coding. The exams are not too hard and for the final they dropped the inheritance section compared to previous year.

She is an amazing professor who find creative ways to teach. She is willing to help everyone and explains concepts fantastically. She uses LeetCode as an extra material to help students practice on real stuff. Although the course goes really fast, as long as you study daily and practice, you'll be good.

Too many lecs honestly. It might have been done with the intention of helping students which I appreciate, but there was just too much material to plow through every week. Also, lecs were extremely dense and did not provide overview of topic. Vids often jumped right into proofs at very beginning when idk what we are proving.

She is a great professor. Her asynchronous lectures are amazing and she is very caring. I wish we could get our assignment feedback faster but I understand that it is a big class and grading is heavy. I recommend her and will take again.
She is an extremely caring professor. However, don't take this class with CS220 or else you will suffer like never before. 220 is also a very hard class.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Skip class? You won't pass.--Test heavy

reviews.comment: Professor was always available whenever needed. She is one of the most helpful people I have come across and she explains the course like no one else.

I didn't attend many of the lectures for this class but I did go to most office hours. She is very helpful one-on-one and cares if we do well. She wasn't the best professor I've ever had but if you use the resources she gives you you'll be fine.
She is really nice. Easy to understand and always responsive. She deeply cares about the success of her students. Take a class with her and you definitely won't be disappointed.
awful. cant teach and gets mad when people ask for help. would switch out if I got this professor again.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Skip class? You won't pass.

reviews.comment: Prof. Glennon is such an inspiring, caring guy. I just wish his class wasn't taught at 6 pm while being attendance mandatory lol

I loved this class, it was so interesting and Professor Glennon is so nice, insightful, and inspiring. The group work wasn't my favorite but it helped me learn how to work with others. The class times and classroom wasn't ideal but material wise it was great.

Professor Glennon genuinely cares about students' professional development. One of the biggest strengths of this course is how he connects students with real companies and industry perspectives, which makes the material feel practical and relevant rather than just theoretical.

I definitely recommend this class even if you have no interest in going into sales. Prof Glennon has loads of experience and will teach you so much information that is valuable for any skill or industry. He cares of forming a connection and seeing everyone improve. There are also plenty of chances to meet with companies that speak in class.
Lectures are boring, but good class and the work is manageable.
He's one of the best professors at UMass. He is super caring and replies to emails quickly, always recognizes the work his students and TAs do, and makes the class very interactive.

Prof. Glennon is by far the best professor I've had here at UMass. He cares so much about students and the material he is teaching. He is literally the cutest most wholesome man ever. He brought his dog to class one day - and that tells you everything you need to know about him.

Professor Glennon might be the least engaging professor I've ever had. He treats the class like it is the most important class you will ever take, and peppers you with busy work throughout the semester because of it. He is not engaging in any remote way, he didn't inspire me or my friends in the class to learn. This class was a waste of time.

Professor Glennon was great. Lectures can be boring, but they are informative. He has a lot of guest speakers come in. There are two group project assignments; they are easy if you have a good group and everyone does their portion. There are two exams that are online. There is homework once a week, but it is easy. Great class, definitely take it,

This class is very interactive and is a great learning experience. There are a lot of projects, but they are VERY relevant to what a marketing major would do in their career. There are plenty of extra credit opportunities as well.
Prof. Glennon is a nice guy. Assignments are very straightforward. The main downside is that lectures are really boring and the exams often feel like a series of trick questions.

Glennon is an amazing lecturer. He is funny and he keeps class interesting. Attendance is taken at the beginning of class via TopHat and there are three group projects with random people but they are straight forward. Exams are online and all homework is completion.

Such a sweet man, you can tell he cares about his students and everything he does. Lectures are always interesting and he makes an effort to make everything fun and worth your time. Group projects 2-3 i think, they arent hard if you have a good group, and honestly i think they were interesting and quite useful. Also there is lots of extra credit

Matt Glennon is awesome I love his class. He is very knowledgeable about marketing and I would love to take another class with him. Exams are online and there are 3 case studies that you do with a group you are assigned to. As long as everyone does their work its fine. Attendance is through tophat.
Professor Glennon is amazing. Best professor at Umass, I highly recommend taking his class.
reviews.rating_tags: EXTRA CREDIT--Group projects--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: I like that he actually does marketing outside of teaching, so he can use his real-life experiences as examples. It does get boring and no one ever pays attention during class unless tophat is going on. homework is super easy and the TAs usually grade easy on the assignments

Professor Glennon is a great professor and offers a lot of support outside of class. He's really knowledgeable about marketing and brings in a lot of guest speakers. The class and the material are really easy but the homework and tests are a little time-consuming. Lectures were sometimes boring but that's mostly because of the material.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Clear grading criteria--Caring

reviews.comment: It's an easy A, lectures themselves are very boring. The group case projects are very tedious depending on your group, and hw/quizzes are super easy. Attendance is mandatory but i'd just take this class cause there's no way you get below a B

Matthew Glennon is one of the best professors at UMass. He is passionate about Marketing and does his best to make lectures engaging and interactive. There are 3 main quizzes that are online and easy if you do the homework. I would take this class over and over if I could. He also helped me launch my own soap business.

The best professor I have ever had. Never met a professor who has made themself as available to students as Matt. He will brings in top companies to class to help you network, and will even open up his network to you if you prove yourself.

Professor Glennon is a very good professor. He brings lots of experience to the class and is very passionate. The class has 3 case studies, 2 with groups. 2 exams as well, with TopHat and other smaller assignments to make up the grade. He is willing to help students and tries to make it as interactive as possible. Overall, he is a great professor.

Prof. Glennon is great. He is a very busy guy but loves teaching! Even though attendance in not mandatory it really helps with group projects and content on the final exam. There are 3 main projects and they are graded fairly by the TAs.

Lectures are long and sometimes painful, with Tophats used for attendance. Glennon is super nice and respected, but so much is covered in just one lecture. 2 big group projects with random members, so it can be hit or miss.

Professor Glennon was so sweet! It's a big lecture, but he does his best to keep everyone engaged. We had a lot fo guest speakers, which was nice for net working. Case studies are interesting, but depending on your group it could mean more work for you. Great class though, he also has a lot of personal experience stories from working in field.

Glennon is a great professor. Lectures are attendance mandatory and can sometimes be lengthy. You get assigned a group for a couple of projects. Exams are online, but a bit difficult. Homework is pretty easy.

Professor Glennon is the best! Although the lectures and case studys (3 throughout the semester( were a little tough, the class was pretty easy. Useful material for the future and Professor Glennon is the sweetest guy at UMass. Super easy to reach outside of class, genuine person, and will help you individually if you need it. Great guy overall.

Professor Glennon was a fine teacher. His lectures went on for far too long and I really did not get anything out of them. There are three group projects throughout the class that take up most of the grades and they are not very hard, but make sure to do well on them!

BEST PROFESSOR I'VE EVER HAD! He gives excellent feedback on assignments, emails back quickly, and offers a lot of extra credit. I've never written a review on this app, but people need to know how great of a professor he is!

The class itself was very easy. Need to buy Connect for smart books and exams. If you have a bad group for your case studies immediately tell the TAs. They grade harshly and your grade is highly dependent on it. You will suffer because of other people.

Firstly, the class was super easy and not much work. Attendance was strictly mandatory, but I've never had a course where attending class was more worthless. It mostly consisted of him going on and on about personal experiences, as well as companies trying to recruit us. He was rude and not helpful when my group asked questions.
He's one of the best profs I've taken at UMass Amherst. I really appreciate his sympathy and understanding.

Prof Glennon was pretty good, the lectures aren't the most interesting but attendance is tracked with iclicker questions and often have interesting guest speakers. You also have multiple group projects which affect your grade alot but exams were online so overall wasn't too hard with alot of extra credit opportunities.

Great professor with great people brought in from Target and etc. Need to read because exams are on the reading and not lectures. Exams are online, fairly easy. TAs grade harsh and your grade depends on your case study group. This class requires a lot of work. Lots of extra credit, so don't sweat it if you miss a few points.
reviews.rating_tags: EXTRA CREDIT--So many papers--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Great professor. He gives some extra credit through later smartbooks/surveys. Group projects aren't too hard but don't just fluff it up too much because they do grade thoroughly. 2 exams on topics from the book/companies. I wouldn't take notes in class because it doesn't relate to exams too much. Just look up topics from book and recorded lectures

Great teacher, loves what he does and his students. Night classes are the worst and I probably would not have gone every night if attendance wasn't required. His lectures are pretty interesting and the tone of his voice is captivating. He uses good examples and has real companies come in and present for us. It's a great entry level marketing class

Matthew is a pretty nice guy, he tries to make the lectures interesting and keeps you engaged with TopHat and videos. I wish the group projects were more creative though instead of just writing group papers. You should be good if you are creative and know how to use your Marketing terms. Also feel like the class would be better if it were smaller.

Take 301 with Glennon not Victoria for your own sake. This is an EASY A. Just do homework on time and actually make sure your group projects are good. Be creative and you'll pass the class. All exams online.

He is a great guy and a great resource. If you are not into sales don't take this class because it is just companies coming in, presenting and trying to recruit you 90% of the time. An easy class but can be boring at times and lacks much structure.

He was able to make teaching to a lecture of 200+ people more enjoyable than most. He uses lots of real world examples in his lectures which also is helping in putting things into the bigger picture. Some of the group projects can be difficult especially if you get a bad group, all depends. Easy to talk to professor.

Professor Glennon is one of the best profs in the marketing department. He is caring and is willing to give extensions if you have a valid reason. He also gives a lot of extra credit opportunities. He's nice but his TAs are tough graders, so beware of that.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Group projects--EXTRA CREDIT

reviews.comment: Glennon is a really solid professor. Knows what he's talking about and goes above and beyond to bring great guests to class. I had trouble unexpectedly with the midterm but on the final studied a little harder and got an A. There are in class participation questions.
Good class. Lots of pointless guest lectures that have no relevance to the course and attendance is required.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Group projects

reviews.comment: Prof. Glennon is a great professor but the class was subpar. He knows what he's talking about, but his exams are solely based on the book, which his lectures don't cover. Lectures are mandatory but feel pointless. Exams are difficult if you don't study ahead of time. Not an easy A, more like a B class.
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Skip class? You won't pass.--Group projects

reviews.comment: Glennon really cares about students and tries to make the class as interesting as possible. He's clear about what will be on exams. Participation is annoying because the class is at 5:30pm. The group projects suck, but TAs are reasonable graders. Wish I took this as an upperclassman so I could've had a better shot at job opportunities he brings in.

Professor Glennon is the nicest professor I met that he is always inspirational and wanted all of us succeed. The lecture is about 2 hours and 45 minutes including half lecture and half guest speaking as well as competition exercise. You can definitely meet different companies people and have lots of opportunities to networking. Recommend to anyone

Glennon is a great teacher. He brings in companies that you do projects with and is very specific about what is on his quizzes. Attendance is mandatory and it's fairly interesting because he is very knowledgeable. Internship/job opportunities too.
the labs themselves suck but glennon tries to make them as interesting as he can. he genuinely cares about students and real world marketing. try to take this with him if you can

Glennon is a nice guy who knows a lot about real-world marketing. Discussion can be a drag and the group work is hit or miss but he is willing to work with students. Class is nothing exciting but not hard
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Skip class? You won't pass.--Group projects

reviews.comment: Glennon really makes each semesters content individualized, specific, and relevant. He tries very hard to teach the course in an enjoyable way which is really appreciated. Whole discussion is based around 4 group projects and you can't choose group members but if your team works well together, they should go by smoothly.

Important to listen in class as his portion of exam (esp first exam) is more based off examples he gives out loud rather than material on the slides, but his lectures are easy to listen to as they are engaging. Majority of the work is group projects (randomly assigned teammates) but as long as you really follow the rubrics they're not so bad!

Overall fun class. Downside: too many projects, which are all group projects btw (Groups are randomly assigned at the start of the semester and lasts until the end). His part of the exams has questions that require you to listen to him during lecture because not all the information is available in his lecture slides.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Group projects--So many papers

reviews.comment: Great guy and really helpful when it comes to understanding what he wants. Very practical class and is above and beyond the lecture portion of the class. Only complaint is that your grade is heavily dependent on the work of your teammates, which personally hurt me a lot.
Glennon's marketing 301 discussion is by far the most practical class I have ever taken at UMass. He's genuine and wants his students to succeed. Talk to him during office hours, you'll love the guy.
Professor Glennon is the best. If you're interested in sales, you need to take this class. It is extremely rewarding and class always flies by. Best class/ professor I've had at Umass.

Marketing 425 Sales & Distributions was genuinely the best class I took at UMass. Real practical sales skills taught by Professor Glennon who has decades of sales experience both before & during his time as a professor. I looked forward to this class every week and unlike many other classes feel I gained real life-long skills I can use. Take it!

Prof Glennon is amazing. He clearly cares about what he is teaching, he is very straightforward, and the case studies are very fun and interesting. He gives so many opportunities for extra credit and he is extremely accessible for questions outside of class. I will definitely be taking another class with him!

The discussion section itself is useless but attendance is mandatory. There are 4 case studies that aren't too difficult. He really cares about the class and the students but the hour and fifteen minute class could be said in 20.

Taught the discussion section of mktg301. Boring lecturer and just kind of rambles about companies and trends. Projects are really easy, which helps b/c they're most of your grade. Most helpful with off-subject stuff, like meeting for resume help and such.
reviews.rating_tags: GRADED BY FEW THINGS--GROUP PROJECTS--LECTURE HEAVY

reviews.comment: One time, I was driving on campus, and my car broke down. Mike saved me from a burning car and took out the fire himself with his handy-dandy fire extinguisher. This man is always prepared. Then he brought cookies to calm me down.

Professor Gentile was a very good professor. He made the class easy and engaging. There is a fun group project at the end on the topic of your choice and it was very fun. The readings aren't bad and you have unlimited chances on the quizzes. I would love to have him again as a professor.

This class was so easy, it was graded by weekly discussion posts, online textbook work, attendance, and a group project in place of a final. He knows a lot about the subject and is very passionate, he takes time to answer student questions at the start of each lecture from the previous class attendance form.

Mike is a great professor. His class isn't super difficult and is honestly super interesting. His class is asynchronous on Tuesday and then meets on Thursday. You do have to pay for an online textbook and have weekly textbook readings but honestly this class is SUPER easy. You only have one group project at the end of the semester.

He made me cry on zoom, called me immature, has been rude to my classmates too. Sends passive aggressive emails. Thinks he knows everything and this program is our lives. Talks down to you. I think he is on the spectrum a little. There are social deficits.

hes fine. thinks he knows everything. its his way or the highway. tries too hard to get students to like him. class was fine, understood we had a lot of work and tried to be understanding. just didn't really like his vibe. at all.

I loved Professor Gentile's introductory Special Education course. His "choice assignment" format for projects and grading offered flexibility, and allowed students to tailor the course to their interests, while still gaining a foundational knowledge of the field of special education. This course felt accessible and engaging.
MIKE IS AWESOME! He cares about his students and always checks in on all of his students. He adds humor to the class while still being insightful. Would definitely recommend him to anyone.
Funny guy! Love him

People complaining that Laura is hard seriously just don't want to do any work. Her lectures are clear and don't take that much time outside of class tbh. She discusses problem set Qs in class and gives the answers, and then the tests are exactly like the problem sets. Lectures do a great job teaching concepts and you thoroughly learn the material

SO MUCH HOMEWORK, but in doing it I've never felt more confident about a class. Feel free to complain about the work but she provides you with all the materials you need to succeed, so if you don't that's on you
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Gives good feedback--Lots of homework

reviews.comment: she would give you 15 page problem sets every week and there'd be like two quizzes every week too and the exams were all open response so it was actually hell but i did learn a lot and she's really smart but still she was doing too much for intro bio

"flipped classroom" structure that consists of watching outdated lectures as homework and listening to laura yap in class. weekly problem sets are long but very helpful. tests and quizzes aren't bad either. don't let laura's reviews scare you from doing biotap! the class honestly isn't that bad, there's just a lot of work.

The material covered in 285 is not hard by any means, however Dr. Francis sure tries her best to make this class a living hell. Class is designed in a way where she does absolutely nothing, while students are assigned a ridiculous amount of work, w/ no consideration of other courses. If you're stuck with her, may the odds be ever in your favor

It's a flipped classroom and her video lectures  are not comprehensive for the material she expects you to know. Everything is graded by her TA's and there isn't a rubric so pray that your TA is forgiving. She expects a lot from you but gives nothing in return. There is a lot of work but it does teach you, which you need since Laura never will.

Bio 285 is a very hard class, though I think the way Laura teaches it is very thorough. I have never learned more in-depth from a class so quickly. There is a lot of work outside of class, a few hours worth at least, a week. I really liked her class, but it can be a lot. Tests, quizzes, and homework all require long, detailed answers.

Laura assigns long problem sets, but they help when it comes to the tests. Flipped classroom and her videos are lowk outdated. All tests are open response and have specific criteria for full points. But! she is passionate and is willing to help. She loves to yap. Don't let the other reviews scare you, it's not that bad, just lots of work.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Lots of homework--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: She might as well be the devil. Lot of work in this class like problem sets (10+ pages), handwritten notes. Every week there is a quizzz. The grading system is messed up ( got 95+ in both midterm but needed a 100 in the final to get an A). Your overall grade should be 95+ to get an A. Flipped classroom system so good luck ;)

*391AH* - very chill professor, all you really need to do is read research papers, write a 3 pager, make comments in perusall, a make a few presentations. Everything in this class is participation based not effort, but you will get more out of it if you put effort into it. She loves when you make an effort to participate in weekly discussions.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Gives good feedback

reviews.comment: Yes, the class is a lot of work, but it gives you a deeper understanding of the course material. Do the notes and problem sets, pay attention to clicker questions, and ask questions during office hours. Very kind, caring, and knowledgeable professor if you put in the effort. Loved this class, if you are serious about biology, take Laura
testasdsadssdad

I would not wish this professor on my worst enemy. SHE DOES NOT TEACH. Hours of videos to watch that are from covid when she needed to make them (LAZY!!) that have ads on them, wasting time and she's profiting. Exams are graded HARSHLY all open response. Weekly assignments take10 hours. The class is not that bad if you take literally any other prof

If you want your GPA to get messed up take with her, if not TAKE CALEB ROUNDS. This class ruined my gpa. Super exam heavy, super long weekly problem sets that take 12 hours to complete and are WEEKLY. They are also graded harshly as well as with exams. Exam is only open response and hard. You are also expected to watch 1 hour+ videos before class.

Good class if you're going into a bio-adjacent field (and not just taking it as a req.). Laura gives more work than other Bio151 professors, but she'll make you understand biology, and it will help you later. If you want a prof who will answer in-depth questions, push you, and support your goals, it is Laura! Just prepare for long problem sets.
TAKE CALEB ROUNDS SHE SUCKS

Absolute Worst and if you are a visual learner she is NOT for you. Acts like she is better than other professors in the department but she is by far so much worse. Take 285 with Rounds and save yourself the struggle

I took this class in Fall '24 and Laura is genuinely the best professor I've had thus far. The problem sets take some time, but it really helps you learn the content. I truly felt like I was able to master the material. Best use of a "flipped classroom" style I've ever seen. Lecture videos are good, class time is well spent. Laura is the goat fr
Her materials are outdated. You watch 4 lecture videos (30 minutes long each and were recorded during COVID) every week with a 20 page problem set. Her directions are outdated and very unclear.
does dr. laura francis want to teach? signs point to no.

She tells her students at the end of the semester to rate her well because of how many bad ratings she has. She gave pop quizzes, if you gave to much info on hw you would get marked poorly as well as if you gave too little info, nothing in lecture are on exams but you have to show up, you have to teach yourself. Do not take her, take the class @BCC
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Beware of pop quizzes--Test heavy

reviews.comment: Laura has you learn from pre-recorded lecture videos that she assigns on a weekly basis which are great because nothing outside the vids are on the test. Lectures are basically all review sessions. The expectation that you watched the videos is annoying but if you just do it, lectures reinforce the content really well and guarantee good test grades
Hardest umass course I have ever taken. All of my time and sweat I put into this class barely paid off. Do not recommend.

I don't think she deserves the hate she is receiving. She is an incredible teacher and honestly made me switch my major to biology. I really enjoyed working with her, she always was willing to help outside of class. The class was very hard, but you could always schedule a zoom with her, around your schedule, which most teacher don't do. I love her.
terrible. goes too fast, teaches in a disorganized way, unhelpful outside (or inside) of class. her class is ridiculous for an intro biology class and she does not care. DO NOT TAKE THIS CLASS

Very difficult course, took up most of my time. Hard to adjust to at first because of the amount of homework and studying, but you learn to manage it. If you put in the effort, you will do well, it's just a lot of effort. But Laura is very understanding and kind. Great professor, just the material is tough. Also very hard tests (kind grader tho).

Took this as a gen-ed; one of my favorite classes I have taken! Large volume of work, but I found that there was very little studying needed outside of the provided assignments. There is also lots of opportunity for extra credit and many assignments dropped. Professor Francis is super accessible outside of class and really cares about her students!
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Lecture heavy--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: This class was simple but felt like a lot for a 1 credit course. We had readings and had to write a reflection paper for each. The reading you were assigned, you do a presentation on. We had a group project presentation as well. We also had to go to 2 seminars and write a reflection on them too. You also have to annotate the readings on Persuall.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Group projects

reviews.comment: so bad bro she makes you turn in hella notes and doesn't even teach what u need to know in class, so u need to watch the video lectures as we'll. Her tests are open response too and take forever. and she an A is a 95% or above in her class.

285 with Laura kind of felt like being punched in the stomach over and over again. Despite that I ended up liking her by the end of the course. I feel like I learned a lot + got way more serious about studying. Exams are entirely open response and graded pretty harshly but due to weighting you can mess up on an exam and still get an A.

Witty professor. Nice class because it was more participation and work ethic based rather than tests. I'd recommend taking with the other professor. All quizzes and exams were open response. Be prepared to watch 1+ hours worth of videos before class. TAs were your best help. Hard class, but interesting content.

Would only take this class if you are a Bio/Biochem major. You'll get a lot out of this class if you plan on continuing in bio, but if not then don't take it. Class is hard but you'll get a good grade if you do the work, exams are only like 30% of the grade so doing the other assignments can get you a good grade even with ok exam scores.

I honestly learned in this class which I appreciated. However, the professor actually expects so much out of you. She does absolutely way too much for an intro class. The topic notes that you have to submit every Wednesday she just goes over them in class so there's no point. The lectures were just so unhelpful, but go to discussion, it helps.

If you are a biology major or plan to go to med school or anything related absolutely take this class. It requires full attention but you will learn more from Laura than you will in any other class. If you are taking this as a non bio major, don't. Watch the video lectures - make sure you understand them, take great notes, do the problem sets.

As someone who is taking this class just to cover a Gen Ed, I struggled a lot. Most of the time she seems to assume we have all taken AP Bio in High School and if you haven't it gets really confusing. The class is structured weirdly where we have to watch video lectures and take notes and then go to class where she gives the same lectures.

Honestly such a good professor, lots of work but in the end it just makes you do better on the exams. Lectures are good and she's super nice and accommodating. As long as you do the problem sets and notes you'll get a good grade.

Laura is very sweet and wants her students to learn. This class will take most of your time since  problem sets are long. Grading is clear and pathway copies are given in exams. Exams are based on conceptual understanding so make sure to watch recorded videos before the class, and come prepared. You should be fine if you follow the syllabus.

Hardest class I have taken, AVOID THIS CLASS! Very long and complex problem sets along with challenging weekly quizzes and pre-lectures to take notes on. Exams are all open response. Spent all my time on this class. If you are taking this class I wish you the best of luck.

Do not take this class with Dr. Francis if you value your sanity. You will spend hours and hours doing busy work only to get graded harshly and points taken off for the littlest things, leading you to fail the assignment you spent hours on. Tests are extremely long. Puts things on the test that were never taught in lectures. Don't take this class.

I love Laura Francis, she is very demanding in terms of the workload, but you walk away knowing the content better than other courses. I feel like I learned a ton in this class, and her lectures are interesting.

just a lot of video watching because it is a flipped classroom. lots of problem sets, but I found them helpful to learn subjects. extra credit point available every week in an easy discussion. lots of availability to gets more points. final was hardest exam out of the three. nice professor, I think just a lot of work involved.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Lots of homework--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: I love Laura Francis. This class will probably make you feel like you've been killed and reborn by the end of it and it's so much work it's basically a part-time job, but it will prepare you SO well for upper level cellular bio courses. I learned more in this class than in any other class I've ever taken. DONT TAKE ON TOP OF OTHER HARD CLASSES.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Lots of homework--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: Great person but this class forced me to learn a lot due to the amount of work assigned. I would say only take any of her classes if you have the time, and you are passionate because she'll give you the same passion back. Her final was way too long though.

I do not recommend this class. The assignments are overly lengthy and require way too much work, while the material is confusing and hard to grasp. The workload is overwhelming, and it feels like too much to handle. Look for alternatives that offer clearer content and a more reasonable workload.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Lots of homework--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: Super challenging course, but I enjoyed the teaching style/material and retained more information from this class than anything else at UMass. The final was ridiculously long and should've been shortened, was definitely a little unfair. Be ready to put in the work, but know that if you do it will be rewarded.

She has a "flipped classroom" style of teaching, so you have to teach yourself the material and end up doing nothing during lectures besides occasional presentations and homework. Weekly quizzes, 3 exams. She's also very VERY picky with grading, so don't expect any 100s on assessments. Good person to talk to, but not the best professor.

Laura's class is tough, I don't pretend it isn't. But it's honestly worth it if you're trying to learn biology, because biology really is that hard, and Laura does her absolute best to make sure that you don't get swept away by the current. Put in the time and effort and you will reap the rewards. That's why I chose her as my thesis advisor.

Tough class, but manageable with the right approach. Lots of open-response assignments and exams, so prepare to dedicate significant time. Using unstuckstudy ai and forming a study group helped me stay on top of the workload.
The problem sets can be a little intense, but you can definitely flop a few things and still get an A (case in point: me).

I was extremley intimidated by this rate my professor forum before taking this course, It was very difficult but if you put a good chunk of effort in, you'll do fine. Problem sets were tedious but they are meant to make you think, I would focus on the problem sets when studying as she usually reuses questions from them in exams also a nice person.

she does this flipped classroom thing that does not work for anyone. there is so much homework every week: 15 page problem sets, quiz, discussion and lecture notes. her lectures are useless and she just repeats the slides. she is really good at answering emails. her exams are like the problem sets, they are hard and she tells you to know everything

This is a really difficult class because of the heavy workload and difficult exams. Laura teaches in a reverse classroom style, which wasn't effective for me. The exams are all open response and can take up to 3hrs. The final can take up to 5hrs (scheduled for 2). There are a lot of small assignments to make up for how harshly exams are graded

Laura is sweet and very cool but the setup of the class is grotesque. I understand what she's trying to do and I like challenging and in-depth assignments but the key issue is, she doesn't really back-up what shes looking for in her lectures/notes(she thinks she does and thats the problem)Would be an awesome class if she made some adjustments

Laura is super sweet, understanding, and does a good job of teaching! The online lectures can feel long at times but just put them on 1.5-2x speed! I liked the online lectures because it gave me time to truly understand the content and not feel rushed for notes in class because its a ton of info to take down.

She assigns extremely time-consuming open response homework every week. The answer keys were provided very late so that I would not have enough time to process what I got wrong and what answers she is looking for. The tests had open response questions as well. It was an awful experience and I'm required to retake the class due to my low grade.

The exams are very tough and they are all open response. She gives you a sheet of diagrams but they do nothing to help you. The exams are only worth 18% of your grade. Most of the points come from the problem sets. DO THE PROBLEM SETS! Also, they give no feedback as to why you got an answer wrong. They wrote "look at the answer key".

Reverse classroom structure was not beneficial for me at all. My issue was really the fact that she waits until exams to release answers to problem sets that are extremely long so you really do not have adequete time to go over your work. Also there is really no way to check whether your answers are right or wrong  yet they are graded on accuracy.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Lots of homework

reviews.comment: The class was the hardest class I have taken thus far at UMass. The weekly amount of homework was insane I did not sleep Sunday nights trying to finish my problem set. The exams are all open response and its so hard to prepare because there is so much material. I would recommend taking it with friends to get through this class.

She is a great teacher. The problem is how much work she assigns. I lost my well paying job to focus on her class because her exams will give you nightmares. I still get PTSD when I see her classes, I stay away honestly. If you take her, you will learn a lot but be ready to READ LIKE YOU ARE IN MED SCH OR STH

Laura gives a lot of work in her classes and much prefers open response rather than multiple choice, which really worked for me, since you can receive partial credit. As long as you understand the general concept and can explain it, Laura can help you fill in the finer details. She's really approachable and happy to help people understand.

Took this class in the winter. She's a very tough grader. Each topic has a problem set that ranges from 11-16 pages of a Word document that might take a while to complete. Uses lecture videos that are old, and the method of teaching is ineffective and unstructured. She doesn't teach well but will grade assignments harshly. No extra credit.

Genuinely so stressful I had to withdraw. Don't do this to yourself. Know who you are, know that you can't do this. Be serious. Laura will make you regret being born. Insane expectations for a 3 credit course. Maybe if it was 6 credits it would make sense. The "flipped classroom" concept only makes it easier for her, not you.

If this class is a major requirement, TRY &  AVOID TAKING IT WITH OTHER HARD SCIENCES LIKE ORGO/PHYSICS/PHYSIOLOGY/ETC! I cannot stress that enough. Making this class my main focus allowed me to take the time necessary to do well. It is A LOT of work, but it is completely doable especially if you form a study group and keep each other accountable.

Class time was wasted on dumb I-clicker questions that were multiple choice even though she "doesn't believe in multiple choice." The clicker questions were a waste of time because tests are all open response. Graded on notes from her 3 year old lecture videos. Workload is a lot with notes, discussion posts, and a 10-page problem set every week.
reviews.rating_tags: Lecture heavy--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Took her back in Fall 22, and didn't post a review until now because of how many brain cells I lost and how traumatic the experience was. The workload was beyond comprehensible. Class made me diagnosed with long-term erectile dysfunction. Had multiple brain aneurysms. Will probably have Parkinson's or Alzheimer's or maybe both when I'm 25. Amen

This is the definition of a weed out class. You need to be on point with your intro bio content to succeed, as this isn't (and never was) an intro class. 100s are intro classes. Biochem285 is your other option.. with harder content and a slightly "easier prof." Pick your poison, but if you plan to be a bio major buckle up lol.

This class is hard and Laura's teaching format doesn't help. The other posts will tell you the demanding workload. At least you get points for everything you do, so it can cushion bad exam grades a tiny bit (which are problem-solving short answer). Her lectures are useless. She doesn't cover all the week's content in class. Find a friend.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Lots of homework--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: The final took 5 HOURS! other exams take 3 hours. 2 hours of pre-lecture videos that are super old w/ads + 12-pages long problem set (short answer only)! + 1hr quiz due every sunday + discussion posts... as much as she might seem like she cares, it is not reflected on her grading. Her lecture are practically USELESS. goes on rants for most of class
Do not take this professor under any circumstances. Take Caleb. Or be homeschooled. But not this professor. She took me through hell. I had a 4.0 GPA, but thanks to her, my GPA is ruined.

DO NOT TAKE 391AH WITH LAURA! She assigns multiple 12 page scientific papers every week on perusall and THEN makes you write a 2 page reflection on. You also have to go to 2 seminars and write a reflection on those and present/lead discussion twice during class! She is lazy, inaccessible, and assigns way to much work for a 1 credit class.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Lots of homework--So many papers

reviews.comment: The thing about Laura is you HAVE to go to review sessions. I hated her until I talked to her and while the workload is astronomical, her online lectures are good enough to carry the class.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Lots of homework--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: The class is fine but the workload is intense. Weekly you have lectures to watch outside of class, 10-13 page packet (all short answer), a quiz, and a discussion forum post. In class, all that is done really is clicker questions. Also, the videos that are posted online have ads so she is making adsense off of us using 3 year old Covid-19 lectures.
tests are brutal, homework is wayyy too much do not take
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Beware of pop quizzes--So many papers

reviews.comment: Worst class ever. Grades your notes. Exams are fully short answers and usually take more than 2 hours to write.

Laura Francis serves no purpose in the class. Our lectures consist of maybe 4 iClicker questions that she poorly explains for 50 minutes, we are expected to learn everything through 3-year-old pre-recorded lectures, weekly overly long problem sets of which 2 questions are graded, etc. She is the epitome of a professor who is just here for research.

the TAs don't even know whats going on.... you ask them a question, they give you the wrong answer 25% of the time. Wouldn't be a huge problem, but sometimes you use what they told you on graded assignments and you get screwed.

Very nice lady. Has potential but hasnt quite fine-tuned her method of teaching, that, in theory, works but she really drops the ball with making her lectures watchable. Shes needs to work on the resources she provides and needs to stop taking points off for petty things. Seems like a great, caring person though.
seems like the professor wants to be the "tough" professor that gives a lot of work, problem is, like most professors, she just doesnt teach it well.

I really love that she wants you to know the ins and outs of the material and through open response, you will be able to do this.The resources can be vague and unclear, the lecture videos are boring and unclear. The grading is oftentimes unreasonable and the class is not user friendly overall.

Review for Bio586. Lot's of reading and writing!!!! The exams are all open response questions. The guided reading homework and exams are force! Literally stressing about finishing the assignments. Recorded presentation, a disease mechanism paper, all open response material is ridiculous. Plus, this is a summer course so everything is condensed.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--So many papers

reviews.comment: Professor Francis is an amazing teacher. She prepares her lectures very well and consider a lot of different aspects of effective learning into her teaching. Highly recommend edit to those who have a passion for biology. A lot of effort is needed for this class, though, its totally worth-it with the skills and knowledge you will get from doing so.

391AH is a one-credit course. Laura is a great person and the discussions were great in the course. There is a weekly scientific paper and reflection required before each discussion and every student will pick a disease to lead the discussion on once in the course. Along with presenting a disease at the end of the course.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Clear grading criteria--Caring

reviews.comment: Amazing professor. Make the effort to attend office hours and put in the work. The value in the class is not the material learned as much as how to learn and study. She will most likely change how you view learning, super approachable, has a true idea of education. You can talk to her about anything related to academics/career/goals and even life.

If you want to take a 200 level bio course that is falsely advertised as "introductory to biology" then this is your sign to register for laura francis' class. Way too much work assigned weekly, even the TA's can attest to the rigor of the course. 10+ page problem set, exams are all open response, you can picture what the rest is like.

Laura Francis has the potential to be a great professor. The exams contain a lot of writing so be prepared. Homework consists of lengthy problems sets that if saved until Sunday then your Sunday will be gone. If you don't have to take this class then don't take it.

Reuses the same pre-recorded lectures and wants you to watch them outside of class and just do iClicker in lecture. Teaches the class like an advanced biology course and uses most of the content from her higher level bio class on exams and problem sets. She is a nice lady but the workload and expectations are a lot.

Laura is sweet as a person, but the work overload is too much!! The TAs aren't help at all when you want to discuss about work that you've missed and Laura never responds to emails or if she does its far too late from when I actually needed her. Problem sets are 10 long draining pages of work.

Professor Francis's class is not meant to be an introductory bio class. Every week there is a weekly 10-12 page problem set per topic, pre-lecture quiz to a set of videos, topic assessment quiz&discussion post. Lectures are i-Clicker questions that review the material you learned from the pre-lecture videos. Exams are all open response.

This was my second time taking 151 and my experience with Laura was a major step up. She's a nice person and easy to listen to, making for a relaxed class environment. There is a LOT of homework, but I've taken the class before and that's pretty typical in 151.
reviews.rating_tags: Amazing lectures --Gives good feedback--Lots of homework

reviews.comment: Laura is very nice and very intelligent although she does not know how to teach her life. Her excuse is that she knows too much and doesn't know how to simple her class to an intro class and instead makes the class more of a 200-level course. The grad ta's are also not helpful, if anything the uTA's do a better job at explaining.

Lots of work and long pre-lectures. Reverse-classroom style teaching which might not be preferred. However, she's very helpful and accessible during office hours and is genuinely caring and super funny.

Please DO NOT TAKE THIS CLASS, unless it is for your major. This is the hardest "introductory" course I have ever been in. It requires you to know biology beforehand which is not what the class is supposed to be about. Take easier gen-eds than this or a better teacher. She gives so much homework each week and the quizzes are challenging.

Out of all my classes, this one was my favorite this semester. There is definitely a lot of work, but everything is meant to help you learn and there is no busy work. The other 285 classes have less work, but are much more challenging. Cheat sheets are allowed on exams, and it really is difficult not to do well in this class if you do the work.

This class is not easy and requires lots of work, but it is well structured to make you learn the material. the weekly question sets are worth a large portion of your grade, but the TA's are very helpful if you need help answering them. you are also allowed an 8x11 note sheet for each exam and can use them on the final.

Laura's class is not meant to be an introductory biology. The amount of work she gives and expects students to be on page is concerning. There is a new topic weekly, requiring you to watch pre-recorded lecture videos from covid, complete a pre-lecture quiz, a topic assessment quiz, a discussion post, and 10+ page problem set. Save yourself.

Laura has potential to be a great teacher, but her class will make you miserable. She makes you rely on her problem sets/lecture videos to teach yourself all the content. Her classes is just iClickers not teaching like at that point, why make it mandatory. War cry on her exams because she will say you over explained or didn't explain enough. Help.

Laura has potential to be a great teacher, she is like-able and seems to care about her students but her explanations in the videos provided every week are terrible. They were fine in the beginning (easier topics) but I swear she confuses herself and loses me about a dozen times in each video. She goes too fast for her own good.

My problem is mostly rooted in the 4-5 weekly videos. These need to be updated. Too many times, she speeds over the crucial, complex ideas and makes it so I have to go do my own research about these pathways or mechanisms in order to complete the homework assignment. Everything to complete the problem set should be in those videos.

Not good. Avoid. 
Online lectures: 0/10 
In class lectures: 5.5-6/10
ProblemSets: 5/10 ---- no useful feedback, doesn't make it clear what shes looking for--- grading criteria sucks 
Exams: Good luck--- you can have 90% of the questions correct but if you don't elaborate to every atom, you'll get nickel and dimed for points and end up with a 70%

I loved Laura as a professor! She was engaging, helpful, and approachable both in and out of lectures, and provided more study material than any other professor I've had thus far! Bio 151 is a hard class, but she explains things extremely clearly, and posts resources to help students go through the more complicated topics covered. Laura is awesome!

So there's a bunch of hw, but I learned a ton from it. There were 3 non-cumulative exams & a final. You're allowed to have a full notes sheet (8x11 front & back) for the 3 exams and all 3 sheets for the final. The exams were still tough, but you aren't expected to memorize anything. Also attended, but didn't pay attenntion in lectures.

A lot of work for 1 credit class (weekly Perusall readings, attending 2 department lectures, 2 papers, leading 1 discussion, & presenting once). But, I submitted the 2 papers over a month late w/out asking for an extension and they were still graded for full credit. Only participated when I lead the discussion. Topics were rly intersting too!

Took it over Winter. Lectures were clear, but often needed to do more research on my own to answer the problem sets. Problem sets take forever, but are worth it, they provide a solid way to get a full understanding of the material. Not at all hard, just requires some effort. She's available to answer questions and explain. Get out what you put in.

Professor Laura Francis comes across as lazy and burnt out as she solely uses lecture videos (filmed during COVID) to teach course material. You are better off taking an online course because the level of teaching done inside class is minimal, and you essentially teach everything to yourself outside of class.

no matter how hard you try in this class she will grade you unfairly. she ignored emails asking for help and clarification on homework for me and other students. it seemed like she didnt even read the homework we passed in

My all time favorite professor, it's clear how much she cares ab the subject + her students. This class and content is difficult, but it's doable. The hw is excessive but it's directly helpful for exams if you spend time on it. Weekly lecture videos are a drag but 1000% worth your time. Tough class but amazing professor. Learned good study habits!

I took her for an Honors course 391AH, she was alright no clear grading criteria, the class was simple good amount of homework but as long as you do it you should be able to get a decent grade, she takes forever to grade though, have heard she is not the greatest in other classes, I personally wouldn't take her classes

Laura is an awesome and caring person. She gives clear and helpful feedback and does her best to be accessible and as helpful as she can to her students. I spent more time doing work for the lab than for the actual course component that goes with it. The lab reports were time-consuming and tiresome. You get placed in a group for the semester.

I had Laura for the lab section. While friendly, no clear grading scale was ever given (no lab reports were graded until the end of the semester), and feedback would change based on the day. Communication with the TAs did not seem to be very good, and group work was done in assigned groups that you were never allowed to change.

SHE IS THE GREATEST OF ALL TIME. SHE TEACHES YOU ALL THE BASIC SKILLS. IF YOU WANT TO LEARN, TAKE HER CLASS. YES YOU HAVE ALOT TO DO IN THE CLASS BUT GUESS WHAT? YOU GET A BETTER GRADE AT THE END BECAUSE YOU COULD FAIL ALL THREE EXAMS AND STILL END WITH A C+. I FAILED TWO EXAMS AND ENDED UP WITH A B BECAUSE I DID MY WEEKLY HOMEWORK.

So much work, including the 6-8 pg problem set- which are graded on two questions, and you dont know which ones. Had to watch old lecture videos and take notes before the week starts. Finals are supposed to be 2hrs, but hers is 4hrs in person (Registrar found out recently and she got upset, but no one told her to lie to them and make a 4hr exam).
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--So many papers

reviews.comment: Laura has high expectations but makes EVERY effort to help her students succeed. Long problem sets? Full credit for practice; She walks through each Q in her weekly reviews. Hard essay exams? Cheat sheet (3 for final). 47% of points just from problem sets, attendance, discussion posts, quiz answers in topic notes/videos. Other 3 exams/9 assessments

Doesn't grade anything. The tests are extremely long open responses that aren't worded clearly. Getting the right answer doesn't even matter because she's just going to take points off anyway. She clearly thinks she's incredibly smart but can't even answer students' questions. Basically, she's the worst. Run.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Laura was one of the sweetest professor I've had. She clearly cares about her students, and even though the exams are a big part of the grade, there's a lot of homework that can boost your grade up. However if you're already taking classes that require a lot of time, maybe take this class later because there's a lot of homework.

Dr. Francis is passionate about the material, but often disorganized and overcomplicates topics during her lectures. Be prepared to watch 1-3 hours of lecture videos outside of class, do two quizzes and two discussion posts, and a 4-6 page problem set due every Sunday. Exams are open response and she takes a long time to grade them.

If you have ADHD, avoid Laura Francis like the plague. Absolutely insane amount of work and procrastinating will dig you into a hole you won't be able to climb out of. She is so incredibly nice but holy sh*t. I'm getting B+s to As in all other courses this semester but fighting for my life to hopefully, maybe get a C in this course
I'm typically not a hater, but she really changed that.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Lots of homework

reviews.comment: Really enjoyed the subject matter, but the way she taught it was poor, and her lecture videos are appalling.

Material is very interesting and Laura is very sweet but if youre taking a lot of hard, heavy-load classes, wait till you have a lighter load before taking her class. There is a lot of work and she expects a lot of detail in her exams. The problem sets really push you, which isn't bad but alot of info provided isn't clear. You WILL need outsidehelp

Her class is so DIFFICULT FOR NO REASON! I SHOULD HAVE TAKEN CALEB ROUNDS AGAIN! You have 2 weekly quizzes, VERY TOUGH WEEKLY PROBLEM SET questions, she only grades two questions out of all of that! Her exams are all open response.
PLEASE STAY AWAY! TAKE SOMEONE ELSE. HER LECTURES ARE SO CONFUSING. I SPENT SO MUCH TIME ON THIS CLASS THAT MATHS 127
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Lots of homework

reviews.comment: She's nice, but this class burned me out quicker than a california wildfire. You watch prerecorded lectures on your own time, in-person lecture is just practice. Every week you are expected to do 2-3 hrs of prerecorded lecture, 2 disc posts, 2 quizzes, and an 8-10 page problem set of which only 2 random questions are graded. Don't take her class.
