I had hoped to get an A, but had elected to have my final exam score replace my lowest exam score, and now will likely have a good grade replaced by an F. I hope to god she scales a lot, or I wont be graduating now :(
Nice lady, exams were impossible. Final was unbearable. For a straight A student I am really worried about passing. She says there will be no scale, but I pray to god there will be one.

Laura is a really nice person, but tests largely on material not learned in class. For instance maybe 30% of our final exam was material we did not ever learn (organic chemistry). Grading is abysmal, with the class overall doing very poorly. She says what is on tests is directly from her slides,but in reality a LOT of outside information is needed.

The way she taught thus class(disease based) had the potential to be very interesting, but the way she taught it made it very difficult to pay attention and follow what she was saying. Tests were really confusing. It always seemed that the TA knew more than she did about the given subject.  One does not simply pay attention in Laura Franceis' class

Rambling lectures, vague exam questions (some of which test material that isn't in the book or the lecture slides), seemed satisfied when the class average for an exam was a 66%. On the whole, not a bad person, just lacks experience. Stay away til she gets another couple semesters under her belt and she'll probably be great.

Very unprepared for class, has to figure out the answers to her own clicker questions on the spot. The timer for clicker questions can run for over 5 minutes for no reason. Rambles a lot, spends too much time on material that less significant and rushes through the complicated important stuff. not excited to be in class, hard to follow her lessons.

This is Laura's 2nd Semester teaching. She is very smart but has trouble passing some idea onto students. In office hours, she is amazing at explaining material and is very supportive and helpful. Exams are challenging and require studying and time to think. Overall, she is not bad at all; she just needs a little more experience. I give her a 8/10.

Had to teach myself with the book and online videos. Stay away at all costs. Tests are multiple choice but worded very oddly and are very confusing. Not a lot of homework though, but going to lectures is pointless. Better off teaching yourself all the information. Easy class, hard teacher so stay awayyyyy!

This class was a disaster. Lectures are rambling and confusing, wasting huge chunks of class time going over insignificant details. Tests are confusingly worded and vague. Nice in a one-on-one setting, but can't hack it in a lecture hall at this point. Avoid at all costs or you'll be sorry.

Laura is very nice and intelligent, but she is also disorganized and hard to follow, and not a conventional teacher. She is pretty informal, and once you figure her out and what she expects you can learn a lot from her.

This was the most confusing class I've ever taken. Lectures are unprepared & sometimes it seems she doesn't even understand what she's saying. Even though she seems like a pretty smart lady she has zero ability to teach the material. She always comes unprepared to class and uses other professors materials without even reading through it first.

AVIOD AT ALL COSTS. I did very well in AP Bio, but what we learn in this class makes no sense. She repeatedly corrects herself in class and it makes an already disorganized class impossible to follow. She doesn't use the book, so you can't learn the info on your own. She is very nice, but not a good teacher.

I love Laura. She is a little disorganized at times but it's biology, you need to teach yourself out of the book. It's her first year, yes, but I believe that after a few semesters she will be the professor everyone wants. Laura is a goof but she knows biology. She is helpful during office hours. Do the work, put the time in and you will get an A.

I thought she was very nice but I did not enjoy the class as much as I thought I would. She was confusing in class but I found her helpful at office hours. I found her tests to be a little difficult because the right info wasn't emphasized enough. Overall she is ok but not what I was expecting. You really need to pay attention in class.
worst class

She is a very nice person, but very unclear and confusing. She doesn't make her own slides, and seems like she is learning herself along the way. Always insists that there is never an actual solid answer to anything.  I also find her humor to be very annoying.  Class is easy enough as long as you actually put a little effort in.

On the first day, she stated that she had lost all of her slides. Rather than recreating them, she borrowed slides that she didn't always understand herself. She can't handle teaching a lecture as large as Intro to Bio because she just doesn't have the experience. She is extremely nice and attempts to help, but it is often confusing.

First lecture of the semester: told us her computer had crashed the night before and she'd lost all her lecture materials (her "entire life," actually). Thinks "Science is collaborative, guys!" is a justification for not knowing what the hell she's doing. Malformed tests. Not the smartest + distracted by home life. Fairly nice. Avoid if decent alt.

Francis is a lovely person and ever so nice to go up and talk to. However, she has no teaching experience and though is very intelligent, just out of the lab and her knowledge is specific. Not good Intro Bio teacher! Lectures confusing, tests very difficult (true/false) and she takes other prof's slides and unsuccessfully attempts to explain them.

Her teaching is all over the place. However, she is very helpful if you go in for office hours and she can explain it very well one on one. If you are willing to put in a little extra work outside of lecture, it will be an easy A. The homeworks and weekly quizzes are helpful grade boosters.

While she is a nice person, she is a horrible teacher. All her lectures are disorganized and unclear. She doesnt actually underlying knowledge, so if you dont already have some basic bio knowledge, the difficulty jumps. Tests are confusingly worded and the questions are poorly chosen. She puts up all class notes, but they are largely useless.

Lectures are disorganized and when you read your notes after the class, they will just be a bunch of unanswered questions. Instead, I teach myself everything out of the book. Weekly quizzes are easy, exams are worded confusingly and mostly true/false. DO NOT TAKE UNTIL SHE GETS MORE EXPERIENCE. She is really nice though!

She is a terrible teacher. Her tests are puzzles and her lectures ramble about things you dont need to know. She has quizzes and just tells you to go read some stuff.If you want to learn from the book,too bad.She doesnt even follow it.Her scales are 92=B and 82=C.It was her first year teching so maybe she gets better. I doubt it with her arrogance

She is super nice but is not very good at the subject she is teaching. She once had a student come to the front of the class to do a problem because she didn't know how to do it. Everyone clapped afterwards. Her class isn't too difficult but I would choose a different teacher if i were you.
really nice. answers all questions. but seems to get confused sometimes. weekly quizes. tests are not hard

she is a really funny, nice person who genuinely cares about teaching and her students. it is her first year teaching here, and she has a few issues to work on. She doesnt make any of her own slides, so she is often confused and all over the place during lecture. it is just hard with her teaching style to fully comprehend what she is trying to say
It's difficult to keep track of what she's saying and if you don't ask, she will not explain things.

She is a really nice person and is always willing to help with one on one discussions, but her lectures are confusing. She is new to UMass, and I'm not sure if she knows how to deal with such large lectures. She talks in circles and does not finish lectures a lot of the time. I would wait a year or two before taking her class.

She's new to the university, so I would steer clear of her for at least a couple years. She needs to know how to teach a big lecture first, especially in a lecture hall full of freshmen. She's nice, and will answer questions, however at times she will say she doesn't know or forgot the answer. NOT GOOD for a college professor to say that.

Fairly easy material, especially if you have a background in AP. Extremely nice with helping her students. Only problem is that her wording on tests is horrible, which makes True/False questions harder. Sometimes disorganized during lectures.

Only reads off slides repeating same practice questions and quotes from textbook, no teaching. Discussions are more helpful with TAs. Calls out students and doesn't respect sickness. Not caring or understanding of student difficulties or questions.

Rude when I had to miss class for sickness and classes were fast with little explanation of anything. Same questions with no actual teaching. TA discussion sections are the only reason I did well. God Bless the TAs. Exams super difficult and heavily determine final grade. Just overall a rude guy and not a good professor. Plz don't take.

He is not a great teacher, ESPECIALLY if you are new to the language. He doesn't explain why things are, he introduces new words that utilize different conjugations without explaining what the different conjugations mean, and he can be pretty mean sometimes and blames his students for asking questions. He can be nice outside of class however.

Dr. Gimeno does little to explain well the grammar in the class or the vocab. Despite the fact that I ended the course speaking Spanish better than all but one person in the course I ended up with a B- for many reasons. The assignments are very easy and clear I will say, the exams not so much. This professor also crossed my boundaries once 😬.

liked him a lot not sure why his rating is so low.  lots of homework through a website you have to pay a one time fee of $70 but they're easy and weigh the same as quizzes/exams.  definitely intimidating at the beginning of the year but if u participate in his class and pay attention he's really nice.  (had him for span110 but it wasn't an option)
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Clear grading criteria--Lots of homework

reviews.comment: Very lazy and repetitive professor. The class slides poorly explain content but the curriculum is very high school grammar centric with fancy jargon attached. Unhelpful and boring, did not enjoy the class but had to attend cause attendance is mandatory.

I found this class to be very boring - he used the same slideshow for classes on end, giving the same explanations each time. Couldn't adapt to students' questions. Always looked to TAs for help (admitted they knew more about the grammar than himself). Also rude to many students.

Jorge is a passionate professor and clearly places deep importance in his craft. However, he does not post lecture slides online or answer many questions in class. He is a strict instructor and is upfront about the difficulty of the class, but it can be overwhelming at times. Amazing TAs, who grade all classwork, help alleviate these issues.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Worst Spanish prof ever. He read off the slides during class. Provided weak examples and hard exams. Your grade is determined on your exams, hw and participation does nothing. The discussions with the TA was more helpful. This class is very tough material and he was not a good teacher for this subject. Avoid him if possible.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Awesome guy, knows a lot about finance. the class is just lecture and a few homework assignments, and exams are online. only complaint is the slides can be confusing and word heavy but super chill class

Prof. Griffin is clearly knowledgeable about what he teaches. The course was very interesting and he did a very good job of explaining all of the topics. He grades relatively easy and the homework tend to be pretty simple to get good grades on. If you are interested in what he is teaching this class will be a good one to take.

genuinely my favorite professor ive ever had. took 404 and 402 with him. all assignments are online and does tophat so technically attendance is mandatory but as long as you go to most classes you get full credit. i would go anyway just because class is so chill. TAKE HIM!!

Professor Griffin is a great guy and professor. He is new to it; worked as a consultant for 25 years. Lectures can be dull at times but he is very entertaining and caring. Easy person to talk to and has lots of relevant advice given his recent work experience. Overall, this is a good Finance elective to take and you can learn a lot from him.

Professor Griffin is the best finance professor I've taken at Isenberg. He is funny, engaging and a very easy grader. No attendance but you'll go just cause he is wicked chill. Hw is every other week w/ lowest grade dropped. One online test and final. Super easy course load and great professor. Every finance major should take 506 and 404 w/ him.

No attendance, Bi-weekly homework, 1 online test and final project. Lowest hw grade dropped. Very easy class.  One of the only finance professors I have had at Isenberg that I genuinely enjoyed going to. Attendance not taken but you'll go just to hear his stories/jokes. Funny and personable. Take his 404 and 506 if its there, you wont regret it
KIN236 was the class that I took with him. He cares about students and takes all responsibility for confusion. Highly recommend.

Really just wants to help you, so as long as you do the reflections, grading is not an issue. You'll only get as much out as you put in, so do yourself a favor and really think about the reflections as well as explore the resources he shows. I learned a lot about myself, and felt very confident choosing my major (a huge shift from before).
Adam is so energetic and caring. His class is chill and fun.
He is really nice and supportive. He explained the concept in thee easy way to understand.

He explains topics super well, he clarifies his explanations constantly so everyone can understand and is super kind. Truly a caring professor. If you have the chance to take any of his classes please do so!

Professor Guu is phenomenal. While I heard rumors that Math 154 was a difficult course with low averages, Jin made the concepts simple and easy to follow. He is a great professor and truly helps students succeed in a challenging subject. If you have the choice, definitely take his section.

I loved taking Jin-Cheng's class. He was always available if any extra help was needed, he answered any and all questions asked. He was very clear on what was expected, and was generally a very likeable person.
reviews.rating_tags: Amazing lectures --Clear grading criteria--Gives good feedback

reviews.comment: He's a really nice prof and really cares about his students. His explanations were also quite clear.
He was very kind; I had a reason for needing to defered my final exams, and he was very concerned about it and helped me a lot.
almost good
goodgoodgood
Very responsible, fast email response speed, and timely feedback after class
My Instructor is really kind, nice and helpful. He usually helps us to solve our question clearly. He is really funny too, he really helps us to improve our mood
He is super supportive and friendly
he is nice
He is an easy approaching man, very understandable and chill.

I had him for both calc 131 and 132 and I feel like I didn't learn anything in his class and it was pointless to go to lectures. I had to retake this class and did so much better because his teaching style wasn't great. You must already know the content to do well.

He wants students to succeed he is answers all the q's asked in the class even though the question asked previously or the questions about the content you should know before taking this class. He goes over lots of examples step by step, if someone still don't understand he go over it again. I personally like that his handwriting is easy to read.

Probably best Calc II prof at the moment. He is very blunt lol. Super smart dude though. Lectures end early. I wish there were more examples during lecture but he explains them very enough. Always will answer your question. He wants to help you succeed. Beware he has 0 say as to exam content / etc.
reviews.rating_tags: Amazing lectures --Lots of homework--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Besides being funny at times, he was incredibly helpful in explaining concepts. Very patient with student questions and broke things down fundamentally. Wore a weighted vest once just for fun. He is very frank about how prepared you should be at points in the sem. Guu was a great professor and should you have him for this class, you are in luck.
Funny dude and he tries hard to make sure people understand and breaks down a lot of problems really well that seem confusing at first
Fun guy, Wants to and is willingly to help his students understand the course material clearly. 10/10
Great professor, would highly recommend!

Prof was goated. He clearly explained all concepts thoroughly and was happy to answer any questions even if said question was previously asked by someone else. If someone was having trouble with something, he would break it down to a more fundamental level so that they could understand it better.

Professor Jin really cares about his students doing well. A lot of people come into the class with prior knowledge from AP Calc and he makes sure that students understand the differences between this class and the AP Class, especially on grading criteria.
reviews.rating_tags: Clear grading criteria--Gives good feedback--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment:
Prof. Jin is very entertaining and always ready to help out students. He usually leaves some time after class to help students or to go over more complicated topics related to our current subject.
Very good!

Amazing professor! He genuinely cares about my education beyond the basic material that's in the textbook and is always willing to stop and explain steps in the example problems so I can understand what's going on better. Would definitely take another class with him again.

Loved his lectures. His explanations provide both the exact definition and an easier explanation. He doesn't go over too much theory, like some other professors, and he gives plenty of examples that all vary for great coverage. Highly recommend him, he's hilarious and gives great personality to his lectures!

Great lecturer. He filled in for my TA and was amazing. I wish he was my TA. His presentation skills are great and he answers questions very well. His lessons are very well structured and he will tell you everything that will happen. You can tell he is a jovial guy and sprinkles his lectures with a bit of humor and his past which is great.

The lecture, he does not use this time effectively or connect it to any of the amount of homework we have, then there is the lab, which is basically another class with different topics and its own tests. It is possible to get an A, but it takes a lot of studying. When you do the weekly quiz, put it in a Quizlet, and it will be on the test.
reviews.rating_tags: Clear grading criteria--Lots of homework--Test heavy

reviews.comment: iClickers are worth a relatively high amount of the grade, but what actually sucks is that you have to get the answers right to get most of the credit for them. Lots of work, and pretty notable disconnect between lecture and homework, but the content is taught and he does what he can to make a pretty tough course fun.
Graded iclickers in class to check attendance. Lecture never aligns with textbook or with learning objectives. Deliberately makes trick questions.

Jay Gump is awesome. He likes to help students remember important concepts by doing random things like doing a headstand. Exams are about 75 questions and more than half of the questions are from previous quizzes. You get A LOT. of extra credit by doing the iClicker in class, and attendance is not mandatory. HW is easy but takes a while to finish.

Professor Gump is very passionate and interesting, but the class can feel disorganized with scattered notes. Exams are mostly familiar questions (70%), which makes them easier if you study, and SI sessions help a lot. Chill professor overall, just a bit confusing at times.

Great guy with a good personality and funny jokes. Clearly knows the material but the lectures didn't really make sense to me. Plus, the slides aren't suited for taking notes. Make sure you have a good understanding of the McGraw assignment before coming to class, because the lectures will not clear up anything and you'll leave even more confused.

Kin 270's lab portion is much more engaing and hands-on than the lecture, which feels slow and isconnected. Jay Gump speaks very slowly, making it hard to stay focused. About 70% of midterm exam and 40% of final exam questions come directly from the quizzes.

Professor Gump is quite the lighthearted and funny guy, and a genuinely great person. The class definitely requires a lot of effort (McGraw Hill assignments can be very tedious), but it is not hard to excel as long as you study regularly. Go to open lab hours, mock practicals, and take the weekly quizzes over and over (make quizlets for them too)
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Lots of homework

reviews.comment: class was fine. exams mostly old weekly quiz questions w some new stuff. McGraw Hill for hw, sometimes took a long time. Labs were easy and but take good notes and diagrams for everything for exam quizzes. The biggest issue was lab practicals. 45sec to write answers and spelling counts. I missed some answers by 1 letter and he did not care.

The class itself is VERY content-heavy. Dr. Gump is an amazing, caring professor, but the class is a challenge regardless. I HIGHLY recommend going to mock practicals and open lab hours. I learned most of the info from the McGraw-Hill textbook, not lecture. Use Quizlet to study for practicals and lecture exams

Very caring and funny guy. Grading is transparent and he owns up to his mistakes w extra credit points which is nice. Lecture exams take 70% of the questions from the practice exam, then 30% new ones. On the final there are ~73.33% from the practice exam. Practicals are very easy if you make/find a quizlet, and I recommend going to mock practicals.
reviews.rating_tags: EXTRA CREDIT--Clear grading criteria--Lots of homework

reviews.comment: Anatomy and Physiology I and II with Jay Gump were my two favorite classes as a kin student. I would agree with others that the material is difficult, but not that the class is difficult. There are tons of grading opportunities making an A very attainable, just study the quizzes and make sure to read smartbooks thoroughly. Lab practical is easy.
Professor Jay Gump is very nice! I enjoy listening to his lectures. The contents of the exams were complicated, and you had to put a lot of your efforts into studying.

Jay gives a lot of chances for extra credit and points, which is nice. Lab exams are doable, but lecture exams are pretty difficult. Smart guy and kind, but I definitely would not take this class again.

Great guy and great professor. Does takes a little extra work, but PREPARE FOR LECTURES! Use the guidelines he posts and plug them into AI. Helps understanding physiology so much easier when you are introduced to it before listening to the lecture. Go to class as well, he gives so much extra credit from iclicker participation.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--EXTRA CREDIT--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: The contents of this class is incredibly dense and in order to stay caught up you would need to put a lot into paying attention to the lecture slides and homework assignments. If you pay attention to the lectures, look over the readings, and study the quizzes frequently, you'll pass the lecture portion. Jay is good at what he does though!

Going to lecture isn't too helpful for me, but 70% of the exam comes from weekly quizzes like word for word so as long as you memorize those you'll get at least a 70 on the exams. The lab is harder and more dense where you have to memorize a lot of info but if you don't do well it won't ruin your grade. Very easy to pass with a good grade.

I like Professor Gump as a person, but it's tough seeing so many students struggle. Exams used to be open-note online, so take old reviews lightly. The first exam average this semester was ~60%. Great guy, but poor lecturer—his brain's on another level. Not ideal for healthcare-bound students passionate about the subejct, but he's the only option.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--EXTRA CREDIT--Test heavy

reviews.comment: Same thing as 270 except lab practicals are cumulative. TAs run a review on the new questions seen on exams which is helpful.

Manageable course, coming from someone who typically struggles with lecture-heavy courses and took 20 credits this semester. While not the easiest, you should be able to pass with a good grade as long as you focus on memorizing the answers for weekly quizzes (70% of exam content) & memorize lab assignments for practicals! Iclicker=extra credit!
reviews.rating_tags: EXTRA CREDIT--Clear grading criteria--Lots of homework

reviews.comment: This class was a lot. I probably spend most of my time on this class and it somehow still wasnt enough. Professor Gump is very strict in his ways so make sure you know his policies well. You get extra credit for showing up and 70% of the exam questions are from the weekly quiz. Practicals were annoying as labs weren't that helpful.

Gump is a really great professor. Very engaging in lecture and gives a lot of extra credit. The grading system helps students who don't test well as long as they do the other work. There are a lot of materials to learn from. SmartBook homework can be a chore and long. Expect to know what the textbook said for the lecture its on. Just show up.

Prof Gump is a good professor. He cares a lot about the content that he is teaching and tries to be as engaging as possible. The lectures can drag a bit, but attendance is not required (extra credit). Exams are 70% questions from previous quizzes and 30% new questions, which are more difficult. The course is manegable but does require some effort.

Definitely the best professor I have had so far. Exams can be kind of tough but if you actually go to lecture and listen to him you are going to learn a lot. He makes a ton of youtube videos to help explain concepts and genuinely wants his students to succeed. Also his exams aren't open notes anymore.

Prof. Gump has to be the one of the highest quality professors I have ever had. I am now in an accelerated nursing program and without a doubt, these two classes have carried me through school. His explanations of concepts will stick with you for years. Exams can be complex but focused on understanding concepts rather than straight memorization.

iClicker is extra credit, raised my overall grade by 3 points. Nice guy, too smart for his own good. If I paid attention maybe I'd understand, but don't. Rely on practical. Exams are confusing. Lots of things for grading, he wants his students to laugh, exam questions are 70% of old quiz questions. If memorize quiz questions guaranteed 70% on exams
DO NOT LISTEN TO THE GOD REVIEWS. If you do not need to take him DONT, his exams are impossible.

Kinda awkward but he's funny and caring. Regular textbook modules, lecture builds off material in a very specific manner, hw is meant to be a preface. Expectations are very clear, more abundant than difficult work. Lab is basically weekly pre labs and two relatively dense 'practicals' which are just 50q multiple choice quizzes on the lab material
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Clear grading criteria--Caring

reviews.comment: Don't listen to bad reviews! He is amazing. This class has a big workload but I have learned more than any other class. The test questions are difficult but scratch your brain in a good way. Lecture exams are 20% of your grade, so much EC is given just for showing up. If you put in the time, an A is basically guaranteed.

Jay Gump is obviously very passionate and knowledgeable about the material. His lectures are very helpful, you just have to pay attention to the words he says, not just read off the slides. There is a decent amount of work for the class, but it didn't feel like busy work and is a necessary foundation for the material you will expand upon in class.

Jay is such a nice guy but he is the worst professor I have ever had. It is insane that the exams are in person with no open notes allowed. Aside from the insane workload, it is even more insane to expect students to retain all this information and be able to apply it to difficult conceptual questions. Exam average is never over the 60s wonder why!

Exam is highly monitored. From the previous reviews from last year, exams were open book and some were taken at  home. It's unfair to give other students options to use notes in exams. Let everyone use open notes. Exams are difficult and in class. Last exam the average was 66, if it could be open notes the average could be higher.

HE'S HORRIBLE! It's so unfair because he literally made his exams open note and on zoom last semester and completely changed it this year. I feel like his class ruined my life. It's actually so defeating idk how anyone does relatively okay in his class. His exams are gibberish -- if everyone is getting a D average on the exam, professors; its you.

He rambles in every lecture and goes on about things not even closely mentioned in the hour long mcgraw hill readings. Prelabs take forever. Exams and quizzes were open note so they are easy to pass and he gave extra credit for iclickers but I just could not pay attention to his lectures for the life of me.

We could choose to take exams/final either in-person or on Zoom and all were open note. Two lab practicals: a lot of memorization but only 6% of your grade each. Would sometimes give extra credit for iClickers during lecture. HW 3x a week. Can be a lot of material but you're set up to succeed if you complete everything and with pretty easy grading.
reviews.rating_tags: Clear grading criteria--Graded by few things--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Homework was pretty light and simple, exams were pretty difficult although they were online.

Gump is a very kind and knowledgeable prof. There is a lot of material in this class and you do have to take the time to understand it well, however it is very possible to get an A in this class. There are five exams (final, 2 midterms, 2 practicals) but in total only about 38% of grade. If you have any questions he's more than happy to help you

Gump is overall a great professor. I personally did not attend the lecture but he offers extra credit if you answer the clicker questions. Exams are 70% of questions you have already seen before from the weekly quizzes. Lots of coursework but it helps even out your grade from practical and exams. The practicals are tedious, so study ahead of time.

Jay is super nice and cares about the topic and wants everyone to enjoy going to lecture. Some of the material is difficult but exams were open note and book. Attendance is not mandatory but he gives a LOT of extra credit for iclicker points. Overall the class was not super difficult and Jay tries his best to make lecture exciting

Great professor! Very funny and caring, hard material but makes it as easy as possible. Attendance is not mandatory but my one piece of advice is GO TO CLASS. Extra credit will boost your grade more than you think. I wish I had gone more!

absolute gem. very eccentric and you can tell he just LOVES teaching this stuff. often makes the whole class stand up and high five their neighbor or stuff of that nature. If you really dont care enough to try, I can see his antics as annoying/over the top, but if you come ready to learn, 10/10. Great guy, also SUPER easy grader.
Jay Gump is an amazing professor who has a genuine passion for Kinesiology. KIN 270 taught me a lot about the human body, overall it's a very good course to take if you're interested in this field.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Lots of homework--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Homework and exams were a breeze. Homework answers were mostly all in the online textbook (free). Exams were 70% online quiz answers so you were guaranteed a 70. Also could take the exams at home which was nice. Prof was a nice guy but lectures were incredibly long and slow. By the end of the semester, no one really showed up.

Jay is a nice guy but he can fall short as a lecturer at times. Lectures can be disorganized with him skipping thru slides, but lecture slides aren't rlly important as most information (70%) for exams and quizzes stems from textbook and learning objectives, with the rest being new questions requiring you to understand material to properly solve.

The homework I don't mind, its the fact that Jay really just reads from the slides, then will test you on information irrelevant to the slides but based in the textbook. Also, his exams are not bad, but he always has to omit questions because they were "worded funny" which I don't think makes a great professor. If you can, avoid his class.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: To be honest, he's an okay professor. I personally think his lecturing is unorganized and a lot of information in one sitting. He oftentimes skips slides and flies through material. The one good thing about the class is that 70% of past lecture quizzes are on lecture exams, which is helpful to study and review. The labs aren't bad at all.

He is a sweetheart! If you really apply yourself and do the HW/learning objectives this class can be a walk in the park. He is very caring and responds to emails within the hour at the latest. The content can be dense and new questions on exams can be difficult but go to office hours and he understands the wording is weird and you get points back

Exams are 70% stuff you have seen before, but the other 30% is a hail mary tbh. His lectures are ALL over the place and can't stay focused. It really is a self taught class. Practicals are easy if you just memorize. He is a really nice guy though and knows a lot so he is nice to talk to, just terrible at teaching. You can redo the quizzes till 100%
reviews.rating_tags: Clear grading criteria--Lots of homework--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: I like how he stimulated student participation in the course (extra credit), as well as how he made the textbook material accessible to us through his teaching. He also made his expectations very clear and had fun class demos. However, he was not very accommodating to disability services regarding lecture and lab quizzes.
Very hard class, wouldn't recommend if its for a prereq, take it somewhere else with someone else. Exams are so uncalled for
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Lots of homework

reviews.comment: This class is a lot of work and there are many components to it. If you stay on top of your work it is very manageable but lab practicals and lecture exams are difficult. He is difficult to follow in lecture and it is hard to fully grasp material so expect to do a ton of work outside of class.

Prof. Gump does a good job teaching this class! His teaching method is more about synthesizing/applying concepts than straight up memorization; this is much more applicable to the real world and makes you engage with the content! Lots of work/preparation/content but lots of extra credit as well. Pretty organized and clear in expectations.
reviews.rating_tags: EXTRA CREDIT--Clear grading criteria--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Open book exams that are 70% old lecture questions, weekly lecture & lab quiz that u can retake til u get a 100, extra credit for attending lectures. He's okay but lectures are kinda messy so I mainly self study from the textbook. Practicals aren't easy but doable if you study a lot

The class isn't awful in itself, but the way the exams, lecture quizzes, and lab quizzes are structured will make you wish you didn't take it. On the exam he claims that it will be mostly lecture material and questions similar to those in the lecture quizzes. They are not. I only recognized 5 of 50 questions from lecture quizzes.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Often says that students should ask questions and not worry too much about the class but then responds to questions and emails in a condescending way and makes students not want to ask questions. Lectures are extremely disorganized and very hard to follow. Exams are extremely specific and difficult even though they are online. Same for 272.

Jay is understanding. The material in this course is much harder than AP 1 but Jay gives you the necessary tools to do well in the course. Exams are open book and most of the questions he reuses from the weekly lecture quizzes. You get multiple attempts on the lecture and lab quizzes to get 100 on them. Provides extra credit in the course.

Jay is a good professor. Textbook is free. You have the option to attend class via Zoom. Theres also extra credit opportunities if you attend class. The tests are 70% repeated questions and 30% new questions. Tests are also open book. There is no homework but weekly quizzes that are pretty easy and you are able to take multiple times.

THIS GUY WAS TERRIBLE. He was dismissive, grumpy, miserable... I've had some great teachers, have loved almost all of my instructors.. But he was literally one of the worst. People told me to choose someone else for lecture, but I didn't listen - The guy is beyond inflexible, and treats students like annoyances & numbers. Stay far away.

A&P II is pretty tough (lots of memorization) but professor Gump is a super sweet guy and maintains a pretty strict and straightforward schedule for the entire semester. There is a lot of room for extra credit and just to raise your grade outside class.

In-person, Jay has real teaching skills which many professors lack. Anatomy is a hard subject - you need to pay attention and work. However, Jay is very fair with covering exactly what you need to know and integrating many knowledge checks into the lectures. This class is hard, but he gives you the tools to be able to rise to the challenge.
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Skip class? You won't pass.--Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: Jay is the best teacher so far that I have taken at Umass. He really cares about us and will go out of his way during lectures to answer questions. If you work hard and complete all the assignments you will do well in this class.

Dr. Gump is a great professor for both KIN 270 and KIN 272! He truly cares about all of his students and wants them to succeed. There are chances to earn extra credit every class. The exams and lab practicals are fine as long as you put some effort towards studying for them. For both online courses, he gave everyone a week off!

The class is pretty difficult, but extremely helpful if you are looking to go into the health field. There is a lot of work outside of class, I recommend keeping a good schedule around the course. He understands the stress of COVID, and works hard to make his lectures entertaining, fun, and informative. He's a really genuine and great person.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Hilarious--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: Jay is a great teacher who understands the impact of COVID. Unlike professors who upload old lectures and walk away, he sets up learning videos, holds lectures, and leaves tons of time for questions which are helpful for such a large class.

Gump does a really great job organizing all the material we are required to know. He is easily accessible and is not a difficult grader; as long as you stay on top of the material weekly it is an easy A

Gump did a nice job w/ this course during a pandemic, being online makes it easier to learn! Jay gives a schedule with everything you need to know. All lectures are recorded. He offers a lot of extra credit for in class questions. If you put in the work you will do amazing. Takes getting used to but jay is a nice guy who cares about your success

Professor Gump was a fantastic teacher. He understood the balance between teaching his students so they learn the material and not overdoing. As a non-STEM student I found A&P with Professor Gump not too difficult.

A&P isn't an easy class, but Jay does a good job of making the material accessible. All the exams are mostly homework questions and open notes, so if you know how you did on the homework it's an easy A. The lab practicals are more difficult. Jay's a great guy and actually had interesting remote learning lectures with bonuses for attending.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Accessible outside class--Participation matters

reviews.comment: Professor Gump teaches a pretty big subject in A&P, and manages it pretty handily within two semesters. KIN 272 was definitely harder then 270, but Gump explains well, makes resources available and doesn't hide behind weirdly worded questions. There really isn't much of an excuse for not doing well. He tells you what you need to know, that's it.

Professor Gump can be a little dry at times but you can tell he genuinely cares about his students and wants to give you the resources to succeed. Very fun in-class demos. Took A&P I and II from him, he did an excellent job adapting the class to Covid-19 restrictions. Seems like a goofy nerd but this dude runs triathalons regularly! Love him

Jay Gump is one of the best professors I have had at UMass. He takes a very complicated topic like KIN and breaks it down to be understood. This class is not hard if you study. He also holds weekly review sessions and genuinely wants his students to succeed. I just started KIN 272 with him

Jay is definitely one of the most brilliant professors I've ever had. He's also a really down to earth guy. KIN 270 was a breeze. Kin 272 was like World War II. Be prepared for the tests. Lab is easy for 272, the in class tests are like the Hunger Games.
reviews.rating_tags: Respected--Skip class? You won't pass.--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: Gump is GOAT

On day one, Professor Gump gives you a document with every single thing he expects you to know for the year. The TA review let you know exactly what will be on the test from that list. His lectures, surprisingly, are also about what will be on the test and when they aren't, he tells you. Do the work (completely manageable) Go to class Get an A <3
reviews.rating_tags: Accessible outside class--Clear grading criteria--EXTRA CREDIT

reviews.comment: Kin is a tough class but I can't imagine anyone teaching it better than Jay. Such a sweet and caring professor. You won't be copying notes off a powerpoint, so definitely listen to what he says during lectures. He explains everything very well. Can't wait to take his class for kin272 next semester.

He is extremely condescending through email when you ask questions about topics. Not helpful for those struggling during remote learning. He uses way too many sources to teach making studying for exams difficult as you actually have to read/watch all lectures, textbooks, mini videos, assignments, etc. Made exams even harder during remote.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Skip class? You won't pass.--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: Jay teaches differently, and can take some getting use to and adjustments. Get ready to do some work on your own so you can understand the material. He is fast pace, but very informative. I have learned so much from this class and it helped me in other classes and helped my with my EMT classes and exams. Highly recommend, but effort is needed.

Although he usually tries very hard, professor Gump is simply very hard to understand and learn from. In a typical semester I would say he is very approachable and tries to be helpful, but taking this course from home due to forced quarantine has appeared to make him much less approachable. UMass needs stronger anatomy professors!:(

Jay is hands down the best teacher I've ever had. He is extremely dedicated to his students and their success. He is always accessible outside of class and whenever you may need him. His effort does not go unnoticed and I wish other professors would walk in his foot steps. If you study and work hard, you will do very well.

Jay is one of the best teachers I have had. His dedication to his students and coworkers is admirable and he always leaves you feeling prepared and ready to take on whatever it is that he assigns. And, in the off chance you are uncertain of what is being asked of you, he is always accessible and always gets back in a timely manner. Jay is the best!

Anatomy can be a really tough class, but Jay makes it very easy to do well. He is extremely clear about what is expected for the exams and truly wants everyone to do well. Couldn't ask for a better anatomy professor!

I LOVE JAY! I don't know why anyone would give him a bad rating. Though it was a hard class, I feel that he was clear on topics and answered questions with ease. He has so many review sessions and even posts test keys afterwards and posts videos explaining why the answer is what it is. If you study the learning objectives you will be good!

Honestly loved him. You get out of this class what you put in to it. Lectures are not great he doesnt cover a ton of material but he offers tons of outside help which makes up for it. He wants his students to succeed and makes this apparent. Lab practicals have too much material in my opinion. If you study youll do great if youre lazy you wont

This class is the hardest class I have taken so far at UMass. Jay put in a lot of effort to help students in this class such as online review sessions on Tuesdays. However, it is super difficult to follow him during the lectures, and most of the time I ended having to learn it by myself. His handwriting is absolutely awful which makes it way harder.

Jay is passionate about the material, and he has good intentions (wants us to learn and succeed). However, his teaching comes up short. I left class more confused about material than I would have been if I just used the textbook/online resources. He is understanding and includes extra credit questions if you attend class, but overall he's just ok.

The other ratings on here say it well. Jay is a passionate professor that does a lot to help students understand important information. He goes out of his way to offer frequent student led reviews which he posts recordings of online, and is always looking for feedback on how to tailor the class to the needs of the students. Great guy + a solid prof
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Clear grading criteria--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: Professor Gump is very passionate and the way he goes about things is very efficient and innovative. His lectures are fun to attend. Very knowledgeable and good at explaining complicated subjects in a simple way. Usually puts several free extra credit questions on every exam. Teaches you how to actually understand instead of remember
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Accessible outside class--Get ready to read

reviews.comment: A & P I & II are classes you need to get the basics of if you want to make your pre- med track easier. This guy plus his supplemental instructor and TAs will get you to the spot you need to be. he is one of the nicest guys and puts out several things to help the class succeed on his exams

I've never had a professor care as much as Jay does. He constantly is holding review sessions for students open to questions about confusion points. He wants participation and question asking. His exams aren't very hard, highly recommend the TA exam reviews. Will be taking Jay for Kin 272. He's great.

Great Professor, and he works very hard to be. Always asking for feedback on how to improve the course and applying it. Lays out information pretty clearly, and makes tons of helpful extra resources available on moodle. Also, just a great guy. Looking forward to taking him again for KIN272. Nominated for a teaching award and he deserves it imo.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--ACCESSIBLE OUTSIDE CLASS--LECTURE HEAVY

reviews.comment: Great professor. He just expects his students to put in effort, but many expect to excel without trying very hard. He acknowledged the difficulties of doing well in A&P2, and helped to bring up exam grades through 17 possible bonus points, and has given multiple online review sessions. He posts all lectures and really cares about his students.
Gump is a really good professor and genuinely cares about his students. He tries his best to make his material interesting and he is very accessible. Great guy

Gump fails to successfully convey any course material in a logical fashion. He stumbles through his slides and can't even explain how the most basic physiological mechanisms work. It's not even worth going to class - you're better off attending the SI. The HW he assigns is pointless and the exam questions are overly complicated.

Jay is a really cool guy and I wish he was here when I took the first half of A&P. You really have to know the material through and through because his test questions have you apply your knowledge to unfamiliar situations. He's always willing to explain a concept again and really wants everyone to succeed.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--LOTS OF HOMEWORK--TEST HEAVY

reviews.comment: He wants us to succeed. The pre-class homework helps with lectures, and he has a decent amount of review questions. What you learn in class is what you need for the test, and he emphasizes it, too. He's got a Dad humor style, but it makes class better. However, lab is very intense, so be prepared for a LOT of memorization.

Jay is an amazing person and he's very kind. He is passionate about anatomy but is almost too smart. This class is EXTREMELY hard and he asks students to apply anatomy. You can't just know the information you have to be able to think about things that he hasn't even talked about. Expects too much for an intro class. Very nice, but class is too hard
reviews.rating_tags: Respected--Skip class? You won't pass.--TEST HEAVY

reviews.comment: Professor Gump is very passionate about what he teaches and I can respect that. However, his tests are impossible and make no sense. He expects you to perform at a level much higher than required for A&P2. A lot of the class is failing. I would 100% not recommend professor gump, especially at a school with a population like umass.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--TEST HEAVY

reviews.comment: Jay is very passionate about teaching. He wants all his students to succeed and tries to help us understand as much as possible. He offers a lot of extra credit when the class doesn't do well on exams. However, his exams are very difficult. You have to learn how to apply your knowledge in a lot of detail and relate many different concepts.

Professor Jay is the epitome of a great professor. He genuinely wants everyone to do well in the class and he goes out of his way to do so. He is an amazing teacher, explains things thoroughly and it is clear that he has a passion for what he teaches. I wish he was here last year when I took the first 1/2 of A&P. Truly a star! 11/10 would recommend

julie is very nice but so extremely disorganized to the point where class is frustrating. there is a lot of busy work and A LOT of reading but it seems like in class discussion never actually goes anywhere. im sure she is a very good professor but she never has a lesson plan and the half the homework is never on the syllabus
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Group projects--Lots of homework

reviews.comment: Anthro 394 is an insane amount of work. Felt like we were constantly preparing for the next assignment, which made it difficult to focus on actually learning. Professor Hemment is really cool and she assigns great reading material, but I did not enjoy this class.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Group projects--So many papers

reviews.comment: I personally enjoyed Junior Year Writing with Julie, but this might have to do with the fact that I'm concentrating in cultural anthro and was already familiar with a lot of the material. Bio and archaeology students might felt left out in this class. Her feedback on assignments was thorough and the multiple drafts really helped my writing improve.

Julie seemed to be a really great person. However, this course has nothing to do with anthropology, it is all about theory. This is what I found frustrating. She is a great professor, but the material and the class was awful.

Professor is nice and means well but the class itself is not all that interesting. If you go to class and do the readings you should do fine. It is not the best class for a gen ed or intro but it's not terrible.

She completely ignores 3 of the subfields of anthro. The only writing she taught was political and paper analysis. She was also rude and flat out rejected any conflicting opinions. My advice: if she's teaching, take it another semester.
Excellent Professor. Would recommend to anyone, not afraid of interesting topics.

This class is pretty easy. I was always confused on how to cite her definitions because she must have gotten them from somewhere. Tests were pretty easy but you do need to know the stuff. If you don't want to go to every class, team up with someone and exchange notes. This works just fine and she doesn't take roll.
Boring but pretty easy.  Don't sit in the aisle, I did once and she literally spit a chunk of food on my arm.

Professor Hemment does not deal well in a big class situation and has trouble contolling it.  She doesn't go in depth about anything and only skims the surface.  She also sees everything from a strictly feminist perspective and will refuse to even talk about other points of view.  It is easy with a lot of BS.
pretty easy class, confusing definitions but if you think things through logically, it all makes sense. good class, easy A if you go to lecture and take notes. easy grading!
Pretty easy class, just 4 non-cumulative tests. Boring sometimes but explains things very well. I would take again for this course. Has a fun accent,
could be a really interesting class, but she makes easy ideas and concepts seem harder than they are.

TA grading is easy. You don't have to go to lecture, but the definitions from there are important. Easy definitions or concepts are described with huge words, you just have to put it in your own words so you understand.
Very interesting material. Great professor!
her class turned me away from anthropology... she likes to talk a lot about random things and is not intriguing.
awesome teacher
Good intro, ludicrously easy if its your major (or if you can read and write at college level)
julie hemment is an amazing professor. any anthro majors should take her class, esp. if you're interested in cultural anth...she's phenomenal...

The discussion for the class is really interesting and almost fun.. but the lecture is confusing.  So many long, random definitions are thrown at us with very little explanation of how each term relates to one another.
No Comments
she brings up good ideas but she could do a better job at explaining. grading is easy by the TAs
talks too fast
take homes are bad, but easy.  and they arent hard grading
No Comments

Professor Hogue is by far one of my favorite professors in my college career. She cares and respects her students, and she shows that through every interaction, whether in person or by email. It is clear she loves her job and is passionate about the material she teaches. I also appreciate the jokes she slips in during hefty lecture material. 5/5!

EASY Gen ed. Class meets 3 times a week with 1 quiz. She doesn't tell you what day, but mostly Fridays. Class could sometimes get boring, but she tried to make it interesting. There a readings that are helpful to understand the material, but you don't HAVE to read. Exams are open note and online. Take it.
reviews.rating_tags: Clear grading criteria--Beware of pop quizzes--Caring

reviews.comment: Extremely easy class however TA's and professor are extremely difficult on grading and hard to get grade adjusted. Change syllabus in the middle of the year.
super easy history gen ed I took classics 100 exams online. once a week quiz in person almost always on Fridays. only 5 actual assignments. she's great.

literally one of the lightest classes I've taken in my life. All you need to do is show up most of the time. tests are open note. Hogue is dry and to the point but I love her for that. perfect for freshman year or Gen Ed.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Clear grading criteria--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: EXCELLENT Professor. Extremely knowledgeable & breaks down concepts in an understandable and interesting way. Attend class since there are weekly in-person quizzes (mostly on Fridays but not all the time). 3 exams, a few quote posts (short essays), and 10 MC class quizzes (lowest few dropped). Take notes based on what she says & put in some effort

Professor Hogue is clearly knowledgeable and passionate about greek archaeology which made the already interesting content extra engaging. She has a sense of humor and is respectful and accommodating to students. She's also a bit of a tough grader on exams, though if you study you'll do well. Would love to take another class with her!
She is a great professor. The short papers are mostly graded by the TAs but she sometimes gives extra credit opportunities which was very helpful!

Very nice and understanding and uses class time very well. lecture and slides are very easy to understand.6 quizzes and drops the lowest 2 grades and 2 exams that are two parts. There is a closed note in class section thats worth 20% of exam(very similar to study guide)and an at home multiple choice part worth 80% of the exam.Very managble workload

Best lecturer I've ever had, she explains things extremely clearly and in an interesting manner. There's a lot of readings but honestly you don't really have to do them. Exams are online, asynchronous, and open-note. Basically an automatic A and decently interesting.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--EXTRA CREDIT--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: Its clear that prof Hogue puts a lot of time and effort into her lectures. Homework is readings, but the material is covered in class. Weekly quiz given in class, so attendance is recommended. 3 of the quizzes are dropped so if you get sick you'll be ok. Course content is fascinating, I would highly recommend even if you're not a Classics major.

Lectures are genuinely interesting esp if ur into Greek history/mythology. She truly cares about her students academic success. There are 2 page papers to write biweekly but they're not hard. Weekly quizzes are like 3-5 questions and you do it together as a class. Exams are online + open note. You'll do great as long as you show up and take notes!!
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Amazing lectures --Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: Professor Hogue is so kind and helpful -- she has genuinely interesting lectures that help one reflect on what you are learning. This class had discussion time built into class as well with other students which helped reinforce/talk about the content. Very interesting lecturer! She is one of my favorite professors at UMASS.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Caring--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: She definitely cares about the material she's teaching. Grading is based on six quizzes and two exams only, lowest quiz dropped. The quizzes and exams are easy if you take notes and look at the possible questions/study guide. Lectures are recorded so you can just watch and take notes. She does talk kinda slow so I recommend 2x speed for lectures.

Professor Hogue clearly cares a lot about what she teaches. Her lectures are pre-recorded and mandatory to watch but theyre very interesting and well organized. Video quizzes for the lectures but theyre always multiple choice & 5 questions long + very easy. Easy A and shes always willing to explain something if you email her. Strongly recommend!
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Participation matters--Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: Professor Hogue taught a fully remote class with entirely prerecorded (but mandatory) lectures. They were well made, and she very clearly enjoys the material she teaches. Exams are straightforward, some are actually taken from the quizzes. Reminders sent by email. Pretty damn easy A, take the class.

Easy prof and class, make no mistake. But I'm disappointed in how uninvolved she is. Every single lecture is prerecorded and you get a generic email once a week. Other than that, I have no idea what this professor thinks. But hey, if you want the easiest A of your life and you don't care for human interaction, this is absolutely the prof for you.
She was awesome. The class was super interesting and easy. I would really recommend her and this greek civ class.

She's probably one of the sweetest, most enthusiastic professors you'll have. You can tell she really cares about the material and makes the lectures so much fun with her humor. She's very accommodating and it's really easy to pass her class as long as you watch/go to lectures. The lectures were short and easy to follow along.

If you need an HS gen-ed, I recommend this class. Same amount of work every week, never anything unexpected. Tests are easy if you just watch the lecture videos and do the associated assignments. Subject matter is clear and concise. Happy with how this class went, Professor Hogue is both kind and passionate.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Clear grading criteria--Caring

reviews.comment: She makes sociology so interesting. I'm majoring in it and this was the first sociology class I took. A great way to start my journey!

I really liked this class a lot. The content was fun to learn and the classes had nice discussion where people would just talk and waste time. It was really heavy on reading but the in class notes helped clear up everything covered in the readings. She made everything easy to understand and the TAs were pretty easy with grading.

Very welcoming and passionate. Opinionated, but encourages disagreement. Lectures are big but very discussion-based, although participation is mostly optional. No tech is only a bit of a pain. Grades are mostly tests, which I found pretty intuitive, and in class essays, which you plan entirely before class. Also easy weekly reflections.

She was a great professor, very smart. Super easy to get a 100 on her weekly reflections, but theres 2 papers and 2 exams that are a big part of ur grade. If u pay attention you will definitely get a good grade. Papers are in class written with a sheet of notes. Exams are in person, no notes but she posts a study guide.

Taking this course the lectures are honestly fun if your class is open to share their opinions the class will  go by fast, her topics are interesting, you do have to read and do weekly assignment but its honestly not bad at all I love this course so glad she's was my professor for this course

Very intelligent and passionate professor. She is very approachable and in general just very down-to-earth. She summarizes students' points in discussion to the class which is mind-blowing to me. Readings are heavy but interesting. Fills 2 gen-eds so very good in that sense. Overall, interesting class and a great professor!
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Inspirational--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Lectures are clear, engaging, & connect directly to the homework. She explains concepts in detail, takes time to make sure students have the chance to participate. There is a LOT OF READING & homework for this class so if that's not your vibe stay away, but she goes over the readings thoroughly. If you keep up, you'll do great. I'd take her again!
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Amazing lectures --Lots of homework

reviews.comment: The amount of work for a 100-level class was unreal. The workload, lectures, and the class in general were so unenjoyable. If you need one of those credits, don't take this class, or your semester is ruined.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--So many papers

reviews.comment: Prof Hikido was amazing. Her lectures were very interesting and the workload isn't bad at all. Weekly reflections on readings, but she always summarizes them in class. She takes attendance but honestly I loved going to class anyways, so it didn't matter. If you need to fill a gen ed, TAKE THIS CLASS. Super easy and interesting.

Awesome teacher had her for my field research class. Super transparent about the class and grades. Offered great and personalized feedback for every person and used her very her own experiences to help us with our research projects. One of my favorite teachers that I've had in my 4 years at umass.

Prof. Hikido is amazing!! She is a very engaging lecturer and gives time throughout class where you get to talk with those around you. The reading load can be a bit heavy, but she also summarizes the readings in lecture. Literally participate in this class once and she will remember your name for the rest of the semester. Highly recommend
Vincent is a VERY demanding teacher and his classes are tough. But he's genuine and well-intentioned and a good lecturer.
No. Just no.
hes trying his best but man...
He makes an effort, but is still a pretty clueless teacher. We got no feedback on anything and in general I did not get much out of this class.
We got no feedback on exams or homework. I have no idea what I've actually learned in this class.

Sarah is the goat tbh. The class doesn't actually meet on Fridays, unlike listed on Spire. Instead, you have to write a 3-sentence reflection about the city you learned abt that week. The exams are just like the study guides. One midterm and a final, both in person. Definitely the easiest GenEd I've taken

She is an angel and is so nice if you ask questions, her exams are pretty easy just have to memorize some details from the material. She is an amazing lecturer and the class never feels boring, I would highly recommend her if you have a chance to take any class with her! 10/10!
Loved this class. The professor was amazing, very kind and knowledgeable.

A very kind and knowledgable professor. There are weekly journals but they are super easy and meant to boost your grade, as well as a midterm and final. She doesn't try to make it extremely difficult and posts study guides. A very interesting gen ed, I would take it again!

So nice and caring of students, had their best interest in mind. Very knowledgeable of all cities presented. Class consisted of weekly learning responses graded on completion and also had a midterm and final. Attendance is required, but all information is given in class. Extra credit was also given. One of the best professors I've had thus farl

Pretty much I would say this professor should not teach this course. Continuously when I took this course the professor would go off tangent several times during lecture which halts the learning of the material. As I write this review he flat out insulted / accused someone of being dylsexic because they dont understand new material. Disrespectful .
reviews.rating_tags: Lecture heavy--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: I love this guy. He gives a great lecture and has a quirky sense of humor in the best way. Classes are interesting and you can participate as much as you want (but the more the merrier if you want to learn). I've taken Intro to Logic (Phil 110) and Logic and Language (Phil 400). Huge fan of both classes. He is also clear with grading. Great guy!

Other reviewers are right, his lectures can be a bit awkward. But they're not that bad, and he's a really cool guy. Super accessible through office hours and always willing to go in-depth. Very fun guy to talk to. Graded on 7 exams, 2 lowest dropped, so I didn't have to take the final. Lenient grader, 2 questions wrong on a 12 Q exam was a 90

While Gary has a very gifted mind for Logic. When it comes to teaching students with no background, he isn't the best teacher. He bases grades off your 4 highest test grades of 6 total tests. 2 optional tests being taken in a 2 hour period on finals week. Be prepared to do the HWs if you don't understand the material. Only take if you need credit.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: The grading is solely off four exams, of which the last two can be retaken. However, the problem with this is that if you do poorly on the first two exams, you are essentially screwed. His cut-offs for grading are also incredibly high to earn an A, you need a 95 average. The material is not difficult but he is not good at explaining it.
This man made up his own form of logic that has no application for the real world. It is the most stupid class ever. He wrote the textbook so that's useless too. I wish I didn't take this class.
Worse class in the world. Would give a zero if possible

Gary is a really nice guy, but this class was quite awful. Don't take this expecting an easy A, even if you show up and do the homework, you still might not do well. Learn from my mistake and listen to these reviews! If you're a Philosophy major and need this class, take it elsewhere, you won't regret it.
reviews.rating_tags: Graded by few things--Test heavy--Tough grader

reviews.comment: It's translating logic to English and back, nothing spectacular. Maybe because of the low level of difficulty, he will readily dock you points for not doing things the way he likes it. Maybe take a STEM logic course if you want some more exciting stuff.
reviews.rating_tags: Graded by few things--Test heavy--Tough grader

reviews.comment: Ive never had a professor make me so uncomfortable. He laughs at his own jokes constantly and he can be extremely rude and condescending. His grading is impossible and the final (rewriting 6 small essays) was the most annoying assignment Ive had in college. Would strongly recommending avoiding any of his classes.
reviews.rating_tags: Graded by few things--So many papers--Tough grader

reviews.comment: Lecture's were unnecessary to go to because they were all online and all he did in class was restate exactly what was on the slides. I didn't learn anything until I went to talk to a tutor. Would not take again

Professor Hardegree is THE BEST professor I've had at UMass - by far. He is super funny and makes his lectures engaging and entertaining, and his presentation slides - which he posts online!!!!! - are absolutely magnificent. My favorite class ever taken.

Hardest class I have ever taken, no idea what I got myself into and would not recommend for an R2 credit. Hardegree has an odd way of teaching, I wouldn't say bad but it absolutely did not work for me, his book that he uses for class is what the lectures is based off of. You can skip lectures bc they are all examples of problems that he post online

Phil110 was the worst class I took at Umass. As a senior with pretty bad math skills I just needed to fulfill my R2 requirement after failing calc and thought philosophy wouldn't be as bad. I was wrong. Prof Hardegree goes on random tangents, is rude and condescending, expects you to just naturally understand, and offers no test review. Boring,too

Professor Hardegree is definitely not for everyone. His humor is very dry, and he unapologetically laughs at his often-times bad jokes. Once you realize that he just doesn't care if we laugh, it becomes funny. Review the slides and the class is very easy. His grading is very straightforward. Understand the content and do as he asks and get an A.

Prof Hardegree is extremely bull headed and biased. He literally wrote the book on this class and acts like a pompous fool. His humor is dry, his lectures are boring, and you are only graded on your best four scores out of 6 exams. This class is a breeze if you review the slides he posts on-line. ONLY TAKE THIS CLASS IF YOU NEED THE CREDIT
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--TEST HEAVY--LECTURE HEAVY

reviews.comment: Incredibly boring and dry. His humor is awful and sometimes offensive. The class itself would be cool if the professor was better at presenting the information.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Clear grading criteria--LECTURE HEAVY

reviews.comment: Easy class! 4/6 exams count towards your grade. Free textbook online available on his website, which I recommend using to do practice problems before the exams. You don't need to do any homework (none due or collected ever) to understand the material if you go to every class. Don't skip and you'll never have to really study!

You either get the information in this class easily or you do not get it at all. If you are looking for an easy gen ed requirement (and you are not good at math) I am telling you right now you will struggle greatly. You can't learn this stuff overnight it takes time.

This class was stupidly easy. I stopped going to lecture because the professor would make unfunny jokes and would go so in depth into things that don't matter- you'd think he's trying to teach a kindergarten class based on how he would explain everything. I flipped through a few pages of the textbook before exams and got an A. Gpa Booster class.

Prof Hardegree was an awesome guy. You're only graded on 6 tests, and he drops the lowest 2. They're very easy if you know how to do it. He wrote the textbook so he provides it online for free! The website also includes his lecture slides and more. If you go to class, follow along and try a few practice problems a week you'll be golden!
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Clear grading criteria--Hilarious

reviews.comment: Dr. Hardegree was awesome! I had no experience whatsoever in logic prior to this class, and he did a great job of thoroughly explaining everything. Plus, he writes the textbook for the class and gives it to you free online! There are 4 exams in class, and an optional final that counts as 2 separate exams. The top 4 grades count towards your grade!
reviews.rating_tags: Clear grading criteria--TEST HEAVY--GRADED BY FEW THINGS

reviews.comment: Mr. Hardegree explains everything is several different ways so that eventually one will click for you. However, if you don't keep up with the readings and practice, you'll have no point of reference and may not be able to follow the discussion.

He post the slides online, but if you want to understand what is going on, you should go to class. He has a dry sense of humor and will make jokes. He is very good at exampling the material, if you practice you will do fine. The textbook is also online, but you don't need it if you go to class.

Attendance isn't mandatory for a good grade but there were 3 other people in my class, so it's obvious. Very cool, pretty funny, basically a lovable dork with sharp analytic skills. Material is difficult and explanations can be confusing but eventually he'll explain it in a way that makes sense. Math skills are neither required nor relevant.

Really easy class! There are six tests, but if you are happy with you scores from the first four you won't have to take the last two (which are the final exam).   However, there are some people who I think would feel more comfortable taking calculus or stats if trying to fulfill the R2 requirement. Logic is a really abstract type of math.

If you're trying to get out of the R2 requirement, and you don't think this class requires math, you're wrong. Go take stats or calc because at least you'll have the basics down. This class is not easy and you are learning lots of things new. But he does give six exams and only four are graded. The fifth and sixth exams are the same as 3rd and 4th.

This was a very interesting class; I didn't know quite what to expect when I signed up but I was pleasantly surprised.  The textbook is available free online. Personally, I never read the text because I found it to be more confusing than just attending lecture. I did use it to complete the the assigned (but not checked) hw.  Good class overall.
It's not all that easy a course, but the professor is great. Very thorough. I will probably take one of his courses again in the future.

If you don't understand logic, please get out of higher education. There's no need to bash on Hardegree when he so clearly goes through the material during lecture, offers his textbook for free online, and allows you to drop two out of six bad grades. Anyway, he has a dorky humor that's a bit cheesy, but he's a lovable guy. Pretty straightforward.

I am not a math person at all.Math is the devil for me.But if you do 3 practice problems out of the free text book a few times a week you will be fine.He is also a funny dude and I actually enjoyed the class

This class has a very specific type of person that should take it, and it's the kind of person that is good at math and can really wrap their head around some complicated concepts. I am horrible at math and this class is one of the hardest I've ever taken. He's a nice guy and all and really funny, the material is just not accessible to everyone.

Do not take this class. It's a waste of time. No one will ever need to know this stuff ever in their life. That said, it's an easy A. 6 exams, he takes the best 4. Especially if you are a Math guy. I suppose if you suck at Math this is not for you. Don't take this class expecting Philosophy, cus its Math under normal expectations. Dont buy the book

Semantics is a very difficult topic and in Hardegree's class our theoretical approaches varied.  This is a logic class, very different from the way a linguist would introduce semantic theory.  It' an awful lot to wrap your head around in 14 weeks, but Gary is often available for help and willing to devote extra time to make this subject clearer.

His textbook is online for FREE on his website. No need to buy the book. His lectures are sort of difficult and are verbatim to his textbook, still not clear. He seems to over analyze simple formulas. YouTube, drjasonjcampbell on symbolic logic he makes it easy and will help you pass

I thought this class was pretty hard. If you're good at math, you'll probably be good at this class. I'm not that great at math, so I thought some of the concepts were pretty hard to understand. He's a nice guy, though, and will put random video clips and pictures to make you laugh a little. Basically, if you suck at math, drop it.

Dude this guy silently laughs at his own jokes, and wastes class time for those who are desperately trying to pass with a D in his class. I took it because I thought it was going to be word problem deductive reasoning..or at least related to everyday logic. Instead it's basically calculus but with letters where numbers would be. DO NOT TAKE.
