Took his Bio 152 class and he taught it very well, materials in class were very important. He provided many resources before exams and has homework's on the weeks where there are no exams for that class. Overall a kind and accessible professor who is passionate about what he teaches.

Dr. Lonthair is such a sweet person, and I enjoyed his class. His lectures were informative and he used IClicker which helps a lot with recall. Although I enjoyed him and the material, his exams were extremely hard, even if I studied a lot (which I did). He is a great professor, but his exams were TOUGH. Office hours are very helpful, though!

I liked him up until the end. He's a great lecturer and very kind/helpful. BUT he made the last exam less than a week before the final and it was extremely unfair. So, many students who likely wouldn't have had to take the final had to sit for it. I should've received an A- but he screwed me/many other students at the end, so be aware of this.

Professor Lonthair is maybe one of the best teachers at UMass. All of his lectures are clear and easy to take notes on, he has a live Q&A service where he will answer questions submitted throughout class to clear things up, he helps people make sure they KNOW things through his iClickers, and he is just a super positive and fun teacher.
he was okay, lectures felt kinda passive aggressive but i passed so its aight

Professor Lonthair was amazing. Physiology is a bulky subject and his exams are relatively difficult for a 200 level class, but they are very reasonable considering the amount study resources he provides. I would definitely attend his exam review sessions and take his practice exams, but then there also TA sessions and practice worksheets as well.

Lonthair was an amazing professor. He describes material well and is always there for help. He holds review session before exams. I thought this class was hard because there is SO MUCH INFO. Have to put a lot of effort in, but it is manageable. The tests were hard!!! I would think I new everything and then mess up on the exam.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Lecture heavy--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: He is a nice professor, but he flies through slides. He is clearly passionate about the subject, and you get like 6 unexcused absences which is helpful. I recommend going to class though because he covers A LOT every week. The exams have so many parts. He tries to trick you with questions so be aware of that and you'll be fine. interesting subject.

Lectures are long and a bit boring at times. At least they're recorded. You are allowed to miss 6 or so lectures over the course of the semester. It was an overall easy class despite needing to memorize a lot of info before exams.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Gives good feedback--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: Everything is laid out at the beginning of the semester. Exams are not cumulative but still challenging. He goes extremely fast but just read the slides before class. He is a good prof and his exams are very fair. Do the practice exams! As long as you do the work and really pay attention, this class is totally doable.
reviews.rating_tags: Clear grading criteria--Gives good feedback--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: His class is hard but he is a great professor who will do everything he can to help you succeed. If you attend lectures and study you will be successful.

One of the most caring and passionate professors in the biology department! Class was very lecture heavy and exams were detailed but go to class, read the textbook, and take it seriously and you will do well. He is very accessible outside of class and wants you to succeed if you put in the work. Would highly recommend this class!

Professor Lonthair is really nice and seems to be genuinely interested in his students learning and progress. The class itself is lecture heavy and there's lot of content to cover, but he explains everything so well and will always clear up any point of confusion you may have. . If you have the right study habits and attend lecture, you'll pass

Dr. Lonthair is incredibly knowledgable, kind, and caring towards his students, and really makes an effort to make sure his students learn the material instead of just remote memorize facts. Physiology isn't an easy class by any means, but the way he sets up his class gives you a strong understanding of the content with manageable work.

The teacher is great. He is funny and so smart and knows the answer to absolutely every question. And he makes it clear that he is there to help up. The exams on the other hand…. My god. They are something else. Crazy amount of content

Joshua is very nice albeit sassy. However, his exams were so difficult and unlike practice exams or quizzes that the amount of content made it difficult to succeed unless you spent hours upon hours studying. He was very accessible for help outside of class and he wanted us to ask questions and tell him how to improve. Tons of content and very hard.

Taking this class is degrading and a form of punishment. Lonthair is a good lecturer and the content is definitely interesting but the exams are actually a set up. You can do so well on everything else and think you understand the material but the exams are so humbling because he does not give proper preparation materials. yall stay safe.

He is super lecture heavy and often says that his goal is for students to undeserving the material but will lie to your face about what we need to actually learn. His exams are completely the opposite of what is talked about in lecture and he answers your questions with questions which does not help, AT ALL. DO NOT TAKE IF TOU CARE ABOUT YOURSELF.

A very good professor who knows a lot about what he teaches. Assignments were very fair with decent extra credit opportunities. Only potential pitfall is that exams are very detailed and you need to go to lecture to have a good exam grade. Part of the exam grade is an open note multiple choice redo the day after the exam which is very nice.

If I could continue the rest of my biology education with this man I would, he simply is amazing. He makes a difficult class very interesting and easy to follow, asking for feedback, questions and reviewing often. Iclicker questions in class are often similar to exam questions, also his homework assignments and quizzes are great for exam review!

This class is extremely content and lecture heavy, be prepared to study an infinite amount of content for each exam. Even if you do feel well prepared for the exam, the 35+ multiple choice questions and 6+ open response questions will question if you even know what country you're in, let alone what the answer to the question is.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Lecture heavy--Test heavy

reviews.comment: Lonthair is my favorite professor during my time at UMass Amherst. His lectures are incredibly helpful, his assignments and exams are fair, and he truly cares about his students' success. If you have any interest in physiology, make sure you take either 288 or 564 with him!

Lonthair is a really nice guy but there is just way too much content discussed that it is very easy to get lost or fall behind. Exams are not too bad but prep is awful because you have to know so much. I would not take this class if you aren't passionate about the subject because you will get lost.

Dr. Lonthair is awesome, I had him 288 and I have him rn for 564 and he really tries to bring people along. He is open to criticism and he is willing to alter his course structure if needed. He is really nice and accessible outside class. His classes are fairly difficult due to the content so be prepared to study a lot.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--EXTRA CREDIT

reviews.comment: so much reading to do prior to class with the textbook or else you get lost in the middle of the lecture. Genuinely a kind teacher who will adjust things based on the class and is willing to improve his teaching. His exams and lectures are just so content heavy. Pay attention to the lectures and be ready to study a lot in this class

Lectures are VERY heavy and fast paced, so it is extremely important to spend extra time actually absorbing the material and making sure you understand it. That being said he is SO sweet and funny and accessible outside class. Exams are comprehensive, but if you study you will be fine! Offers a solid amount of extra credit!

Honestly, this class is super fast-paced, with about 40 slides in an hour. You'd need to be a speed reader to keep up. Plus, the iClicker questions are a real curveball. It feels like we learn basics in class, but exams take us to a whole different level. Do your own in-depth studying and don't solely rely on the lectures

lectures are fast-paced, which is fine, but the exams are tough. clickers are easy, not even worth studying cause the exams are just way harder. extra credit is nice, but it's needed. we touch surface-level concepts then the exams want in-depth answers. i wouldn't take him personally. its not worth, u will be scratching your head. find another prof

Lonthair is a very nice guy. His exams are hard though. He might say theres only 3 or 4 open response but in actuality theres multiple parts to each so its more like 10-12. Homeworks and quizzes werent bad. Just hard exams. Do the extra credit.

A professor that is truly good at teaching content. He puts in so much work to support his students- replacing class time with one-on-ones. He expects you to care about his class and turn in work on time. He is hilarious and provides tons of individualized feedback. Highly recommend taking writing with him if you can, you will learn a ton.
reviews.rating_tags: Clear grading criteria--Gives good feedback--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Very fair grader, not lenient with due dates. Lectures are very fast pace and packed with information and oddly specific details that you're expected to know on exams. He's a good professor and over the course of the smester he addapted the speed of his lectures and made the exams more fair. 1/4 exam grades was dropped.

Lonthair is very good at what he does but does it way too fast. He speed runs most of his classes making it very hard to understand what is happening. Participation in the class counts, he grades for correctness, so you can't just click randomly.

Prof Lonthair is a sweetheart. Has a lot of assignments, but they are easy and balance out exam scores. Lectures felt too concentrated, fast talker, but it was his first year teaching. Clear that he wants to improve as a teacher and will ask for feedback and this was commendable. Exams are fair and 1 got dropped, do not cram. DO THE EXTRA CREDIT.

Dr. Lonthair is probably one of the best professors I have ever had at UMass. The class is not easy and definitely requires a solid amount of your time, but it does pay off. He really wants his students to learn and succeed, and will do whatever he can to help. I probabaly could've done better in the class, but I got lazy towards the end.. my fault
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--EXTRA CREDIT--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Very chill class and Lonthair was cool. It's more busy work than anything, but it was more tolerable than expected.

I was not looking forward to writing in bio but Dr. Lonthair made the class tolerable and even entertaining at some points. His expectations for assignments are clear and as long as you listen to his feedback and put in the work then you will get a good grade in the course. He is down to earth, approachable, and obviously cares about his students.
This class was easy and understandable, Dr. Lonthair gives good feedback on the papers you write and gives great advice to improve your writing.

Joshua really wants you to learn, he just has a difficult time teaching in a way everyone can learn from. The lectures give you whiplash with the amount of information presented, information that is incredibly disorganized on 30 slide slideshows. It isn't difficult to get a good grade however. Utilize review sessions!

Dr. Lonthair is an absolute chad. He's easily reachable outside of class and will respond to emails super quickly. His lectures and case studies are so interesting and he pauses for questions if anyone needs any clarification. You can tell he really cares about physiology and his students, so please take this class! I highly recommend for pre-med!

Professor Lonthair is great. He wants his students to do well, he sets up his grading criteria so that even if you dont do the best on exams you can still get a decent grade. The exams are challenging but as long as you study you will be fine. He goes over slides then pauses to clear up confusion if there is any. TAKE THIS CLASS!!!

FIGHT to take his class! He is so caring, accessible, and passionate about physiology. The tests are easy if you study, take good notes and reach out if you have questions - he is fantastic at explaining. Lots of opportunities to do well, easy homework each week, and graded clickers but they are straightforward. Tip:Go to the extra credit seminars!

A very passionate, funny teacher about teachings. There's a lot of reading but not usually a lot of work outside of that. Overall he is very engaging and a caring professor. Additionally, he takes students needs and clarification into consideration when teaching the course. One thing to be wary about is there is a lot of content to know for exams!!

I couldn't speak more highly of Dr. Lonthair. He is so passionate and knowledgeable! Dense class, but if you put in the work it's easy to do well. He walks you through graded case studies - great for pre-meds/pre-PAs. EC available. 4 hard exams, but the lowest is dropped. Mandatory attendance with 3 freebies, but he makes you want to go to class!
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--EXTRA CREDIT--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: Dr. Lonthair is awesome! I'm pretty sure its his first year at UMass and he is the most approachable professor I have had during my time here. His lectures are not painful at all and I actually kinda look forward to going to class. You can tell he actually cares about his students.
Great professor. Funny, engaging, and very passionate about what he teaches. The class is not easy, but you learn a lot - which is what you're in college to do after all. Totally worth it.

Really passionate about what he teaches. The class is pretty technical, but he does a good job of making it interesting and relating it to the real world. One of, if not the best class I have taken in Isenberg.

Nikunj was one of my favorite professors at UMass, he definitely knows his stuff. This course was challenging, but the material (options) is really interesting. Tests were difficult but are offset by homeworks and a semester long project where you trade options in a paper account. Pay attention in class and understand the basics and you'll be fine.
reviews.rating_tags: Group projects--Clear grading criteria--Gives good feedback

reviews.comment: Class was extremely difficult. If you are not really into the topic of options, I would not recommend. You have to trade for a couple weeks for a project, which you learn a lot from. The tests were extremely difficult with the professor adding concepts that were not on the practice quizzes on there, so you have to study really hard.
reviews.rating_tags: Group projects--Graded by few things--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: The first review I have written at RMP and will probably be the last. He is the real GOAT!! Isenberg is lucky to have him. The best class I have ever taken and this man nothing but AWESOME. Take it

Great lecturer and very knowledgeable! Every class was interesting and the course concepts themselves are difficult. There are 3 exams (drops the lowest) and a group project. Overall learned a lot from this class!

Extremely smart and cares SO much about the subject. The topic is very difficult, not the professor. The structure of the class is perfect. For example, no busy work, you actually get to trade and manage a paper trading account which teaches you so much about Options. The class is not an easy A. You get feedback when you are wrong and learn from it

Nikunj is easily one of the best professors I have ever had at UMass. His knowledge and experience in the trading world is amazing, and he's always willing to share it inside and outside of class. His material isn't easy, so go to class and pay attention, but his approach and practicality will prepare you for the real world. All around great guy.

Class was absolutely terrible. Assumes students know concepts never taught before and teaches concepts already covered in other classes. Gives feedback/announcements with short notice. Unclear expectations. Rarely replies to emails or follows up. Not accessibly outside of class. Throws everyone in the pool expecting they can swim.

By far the best professor in Isenberg! All professors are experts in their subject matter and they teach you like you will be researcher one day. But Professor Kapadia stood out from the rest because he knows how to TEACH. Most important of all, he knows that we are learning to apply what we learn in real life.

Literally one of the smartest guys I have ever met in my life. I wish I could just download his brain into mine. His intelligence can be daunting at times, but if you see him in office hours he is a HUGE help. The class is challenging and you stay in the same groups the whole year so make sure you get a good one.
great!great!great professor~~smart, knowledgeable, and friendly....although his class is hard because of all the group projects, you will learn so much from him....

He is the best best best professor in SOM, very helpful,friendly,easygoing,nice......cant think of any bad side of him. You just feel comfortable asking him questions because he is going to answer your questions in detail...

Awesome prof. This guy just rocks. He goes over material a bit quick sometimes, but he's always willing to explain things after class or at his office hours.  He's worked in the real world, too and really knows his stuff.
tests are pretty hard, but what do you expect for a 400 level course? if you go to his office hours, he will explain to you any questions you may have.
the best
Pretty cool professor, if you go talk to him, he's very helpful, he clear out most of your questions.  Test is kind of hard, but it's all in the material he talked about.

Shes awesome.
Very generous grader. I really liked the different films and the discussions in section. Exams are easy to prep for since they're based on questions and quotes we go over in class. Great prof.

A LOT OF READING (!!), but it was refreshing to read outside my major and discuss war in contexts outside the United States I would otherwise not have known about. I feel like I learned a ton. The quizzes and exams were always fair since the prof. told us exactly what to study.  TAs were awesome - there is a mini field trip to the Mead Art Museum.

SO MUCH READING! My TA was incredibly helpful and the only reason I have this grade (thanks Ilse).

Lachman clearly cares about the material and students learning, but her teaching style is very boring and there's simply too much reading for proper comprehension of the course material.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--EXTRA CREDIT--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: I am a senior, and this is the most difficult class I have ever taken. The class was unorganized, and the assigned material changed in the middle of the semester (surprise! more books to read!). We watched 6 movies, 3 of them with no versions in English. This felt like a 400 level class. Be prepared to spend every waking moment reading a book.

Prof. Lachman is a nice/caring person, but I did not enjoy her as a teacher. She was very indecisive during class and would waste a lot of time, talking instead listening to the presentations. She made the class boring, even though it was a class graded heavily on discussion, she would usually speak the whole time and again interrupt presentations.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: I took African Lit, which is reading heavy, so be prepared. You have to lead discussion once in the semester. Prof. is very caring and always willing to spend time with you outside of class. The class field trip to the Mead Art Museum to work with African materials was definitely a highlight.

the TA's are harsher than the actual professor Prof is disorganized and the TAs will come after you over the most minor of mistakes, this is not an easy class at all imo she loves to trick you and find any reason she can to fail you likely cause she went to Yale and is bringing the ivy with her to umass so everybody has it hard in this class
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Beware of pop quizzes

reviews.comment: LOTS of reading and watching films which is very time consuming.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Beware of pop quizzes--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: I want to give up in this class so bad, I feel no matter what I do I can never achieve a good grade I feel as if its not possible as there will always be something very minor that will screw you on exams and if you dont gave perfect descriptions you receive no credit for the questions do not take my peers and I are exhausted and miserable
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Beware of pop quizzes

reviews.comment: War Stories class is one of the best classes I've taken at Umass! Prof. Lachman sets a high standard but this course has really changed the way I think about war.

I loved taking War Stories with Prof. Lachman. Her lectures are interesting and helpful, and she came into class each time with so much enthusiasm. She's also really understanding with extensions and extra credit. Only downside: a couple black & white movies.

Takes attendance because it's imperative we watch her alternate between struggling to use her computer and reading off slides in her high-pitched, lispy voice. Pay attention to the readings because you'll be quizzed on specific passages. Easy class as long as you read everything you're supposed to.
I feel like its unfair to make a generalized statement like "All professors want to fail you" in other classes but this professor has not helped the case of this statement, good luck
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Lots of homework--Beware of pop quizzes

reviews.comment: not enjoyable at all she doesnt have any regard for student's other classes and she expects the world from you nobody has the time for the amount of homework she assigns no matter what major you're in and the TAs can bet very harsh when grading anything I got 10 points knocked off my midterm because I didn't use capitals for book titles
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Lots of homework--Beware of pop quizzes

reviews.comment: she definitely was not the most personable professor ive ever had, but she was an excellent teacher and i really liked the assigned readings. a few short essays along with one longer final paper. the reading usually arent too long. amazing choice for a gen ed if you're interested in literature.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Gives good feedback

reviews.comment: Way too much reading, often reading 100s of pages per week. She's also disorganized, and ignorant for what the students may have for work in other classes. Not an "easy gen-ed" by any means. Avoid at all costs.

reviews.comment: good luck on the exams, there is no possible way to study for them and I mean that literally, you genuinely can't study for them, your preparation will not help you

reviews.comment: Im only a month into this class and I have never regretted anything more in my entire life.  There is such an absurd amount of reading to the point that realistically you do not have the time to do most of it, especially if you're in a major like engineering, physics or math, literally hundreds of pages a week and then shell pop quiz you

reviews.comment: By far the most boring class I have ever taken at umass, she assigns the absolute most reading I have ever seen in any class ive ever been in, half of it is useless, you need to buy like 6 books that she's gonna have you complete in like 3 days, on top of extra out of class reading she also doesn't put in the syllabus that there are pop quizzes
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--EXTRA CREDIT--Beware of pop quizzes

reviews.comment: She's nice but her class is very boring. You must participate or she would call you out. All of the readings are meant to be short but they could be 15 pages and sometimes she gives 2 readings. There will be a pop-up quiz that she never mentions before class start, mostly about the reading before class. If your a yapper, you will be fine
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Lots of homework

reviews.comment: Very pretentious, condescending, dismissive of her students. Used every chance to bring up her time at Yale, seemed like she's ashamed to teach here. Assigned very difficult readings every class & never helped students understand them. Very disorganized, would post instructions for essays the day before they were due. Wouldn't recommend to anyone.
wHEN I WENT TO YALE

Very generous grader I did not think I would get an A. She is very smart and knowledgable and if you enjoy short stories you will like this class. I found it difficult to keep up with the readings but I'd still try to participate even if I didn't know what I was talking about. She will call you out if you don't participate. Skipped 3 classes.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--EXTRA CREDIT

reviews.comment: Professor Lachman was very sweet and passionate about her class. The homework is super light: reading a short story in preparation for the next class, and occasionally writing an easy paper (typically 1-1.5 pages). If you're looking for an easy A or an easy Gen Ed, I would definitely recommend her class!

Kathryn is a very warm and kind prof. You have to print out a ton of readings but no textbook. You have to read a new story for each class but as long as you talk once or twice you'll be fine. Prof Lachman is understanding and will give you an extension even at the last minute. Her syllabus makes her out to be tougher than she is. Love her so much.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Great class - I didnt expect it to include so many movies - we discussed a lot of older films from early 20th century and more recent tv series. Readings were mostly short and theoretical. Gave me a good sense of what comedy is (not always funny). Prof is knowledgeable and caring.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Get ready to read--Participation matters

reviews.comment: I took this class as a get ed and because I thought it would be entertaining to learn about comedy. It was not entertaining, it was almost funny how much work went into a COMEDY class. I was hoping that we would get into making our own comedy by the end of the semester but instead we are evaluating more comedic works. Do not take this class for fun
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Get ready to read--Participation matters

reviews.comment: She is a great profesor. Actually facilitate discussions and she is very willing to teach you about film terminlogy.  Also lenient on due dates . Go to her office hours if anything because she will be great help.
great movies, lots of extra credit options, very informative and accessible
Other than everything being out of order, it was an interesting course. Learned a lot about culture, and that's what its about. She knows her stuff.

Class is completely run by TA's, except for 15 minute lectures before the film screenings. Professor Lachman seems nice enough, but you won't actually be taught by her. Communication between professors and TA's is rather terrible.  I'd still recommend this class to anyone actually interested in French film.

I did well for myself in Lachmans class, though she rubbed all of her students the wrong way, in class she seems harsh, but then I met with her outside of class and she was actually really nice and encouraging. The point is "dont judge a book by its cover", If you do the work and keep up with the work you will succeed.

Professor Lachman is intelligent, however I found her lecture presentations before films to be boring. I was not a fan of most of the movies we watched, but I also don't really find comparative literature particularly interesting.

I loved this class! Prof. Lachman is very smart and knowledgeable, interesting lectures (not too long), awesome selection of movies. I learned a ton about contemporary France and how to analyze film. Take this course!

Obviously this is a higher level course, so she does speak a lot of french. you really have to be interested in french to take it, you can't take it just to satisfy a gen ed. she's extremely helpful and gives great feedback too. she'll push you to speak french regularly, which is vital. she's also young and hot.
One of favorite professors. Makes French interesting and fun to learn, even if you have to work hard. She's smart, accessible, enthusiastic, fair, and very understanding.
Professor Lachman is awesome. Her class is inspiring, fun, and you learn a ton. She's always willing to help out, and she's beautiful. Great way to learn French.

If you take French 240, most of it is in French. She speaks English often but not a lot. She is hard to figure out. She picks apart your french speaking. She is 50/50 on nice or hard. I love French, but i almost hate this class.

boring class but she has a decent grading system. its a lot of homework, but no midterm/final, instead just 5 quizzes throughout the semester. overall just one of those classes you have to "rough out". attendance required via tophat, but can be done from home.

such a nice professor; her lectures can be boring because of her monotone voice, but she truly is a good teacher and explains concepts well. takes attendance via online poll questions during class, but you can do them from home too. good amount of homework for each chapter but no tests only chapter quizzes that are 10 questions and very easy.
Kerri was a great prof! All assignments are online and you have chapter quizzes throughout the semester. Accounting can be a lot though so always study materials. Discussion sections were light too.
She is the best. Course is very easy and graded very leniently, there are 5 in person quizzes and weekly labs but otherwise everything is online. I would 100% recommend taking this course with her.

Lectures weren't the most exciting, but I did learn a lot. The quizzes weren't bad, but you definitely need to study! She dropped the last quiz grade which was nice because they are weighted pretty heavily. Attendance is mandatory because she uses top hat, but you can miss 4 lectures. She is a caring professor and wants students to succeed!
reviews.rating_tags: Clear grading criteria--Test heavy--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Kerri is super sweet and wants her students to do well. Lectures are engaged and she loves participation.HW is tedious so def set aside plenty of time. 5 short multiple-choice quizzes no final and a lab each week with your TA. If you put in the effort, you should be able to do well.

Professor Bohonowicz was a great teacher; I learned a lot. There are usually 2 homework assignments per week. There is usually a quiz every couple of weeks (5 total in the semester), which consists of 10 multiple-choice questions. Overall, this class was difficult, but if you pay attention in lecture and study, you should be fine.
Incredibly nice and knowledgeable professor and my TA Shira was awesome as well. Lab sections with her were super helpful. Great stuff all around honestly.

Kerri is very sweet and does a good job in helping us learn material. In my opinion she made the material a bit hard to udnerstand in her lecture, the homework videos are definately way more helpful. She provides a ton of study resources for her quizzes. My TA kind of sucked since she went through the labs so quickly (Shira). Def take Kerri tho.
Kerri is so kind and knowledgeable about accounting. Easy A if you pay attention and know what you're doing. Lots of assignments which can take up a lot of time but it's easy & manageable.

Kerri is so great. Accounting is inherently a boring subject, but Kerri makes it about as interesting as possible. She truly cares about her students, as shown by her grading system that makes it very easy to get a good grade. My only criticism with her is that sometimes she speaks too quietly, but really not a big deal at all.
reviews.rating_tags: Clear grading criteria--Lots of homework--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment:
Kerri is extremely understanding! She goes over notes each lecture and you have discussion once a week. there are 5 quizzes throughout the whole semester, you get a cheat sheet but they are in person. 
100% recommend this class & Kerri as the professor.

Kerri's great! Cheat sheet for every quiz, no final, and she does a very good job at explaining material. Homework assignments can be lengthy but they really helped understand the topics better. Daily Top Hats ?s for attendance but obviously doable. TAs were great -- always accessible outside of labs for extra help. Would recommend overall!
love her and her lecture , its fun and easy classe to take , its very straight forward and its easy to score in her class

I absolutely love her and she is a gem, its easy to do well in this class and she is my most organized professor.

She makes me excited to go to class and she is so sweet.

She talks very clearly and confidently and knows her material. 

I wanna be like her when I grow up.

The course itself is hard to do good on based off of the weight of the test and then only being 25 multiple choice. She answers fast + cares about her students. Just put in effort

This is genuinely the worst calc teacher I have ever had. I received an A in AP BC Calc in high school and somehow this teacher made this calc one class seem harder than BC Calc as a whole.  Lectures were difficult to understand, notes were unorganized, information was rarely conveyed, and the class itself was a horrible experience. DON'T TAKE HER!

Somi really isn't that horrible. The lectures may not be the best but it's nothing that some outside studying doesn't solve. The exams were always fair and quite frankly very easy. As long as you study you do well.
I believe the negative sentiment of my classmates to be due to not being able to use ChatGPT on the final.

She explains stuff so bad I thought I was just stupid until I saw everyone else saying her lectures were awful. The practice test I studied hours each days leading up to the exam perfected it to take the final and realize it's nothing like the practice. If I pass the only reason is from the chem tutor on YouTube and my boy Mihir (shoutout).

reviews.comment: impossible to get above a C. She has no idea how to teach.

Awful. Just god awful. Exams are nothing like the study guide. I went into the midterm confident and left defeated.  Felt nauseous after the final. Unless you took AP Calc in high school, you're absolutely doomed. Somi can't teach, botched her own examples, and class is pointless. SAVE YOURSELF.

If you get stuck in Math 127 with Somi, you are genuinely cooked. Not only does she fail to explain anything she is writing on the board, but the exams are NOTHING like any of the practice problems provided to study. Unless you took calc in high school, good luck taking this course with Somi. ALSO, no curve on the midterm when the average was ~60%.

Without an AB Calc background from H.S., I would have been entirely screwed. Somi is super kind and understanding; however, she is absolutely horrible at teaching lectures. I recall multiple instances where she would work out a problem and make mistakes. Her language is very unclear, and hw quizzes and assignments are never similar.

Very awful class. Lecture is impossible to learn, her notes are horrible and makes learning calc feel like your own task. Exams are nothing like review and very hard questions. Terrible class and professor is horrible at teaching material. Would not ever take again do not recommend this professor.
Awful do not take, notes aren't help full, lectures aren't helpful. Your essentially learning calc online by yourself through youtube and.

She has an accent that isn't too bad, and I can still comprehend her. The class was difficult for me, and it was a bit hard to follow her explanations. With a lot of time spent outside of class learning the material, I'm sure you will do fine. She is a very nice professor, but I do not like her teaching style.

Do NOT take this class. You're better off learning the material yourself. Lectures are essentially her writing nonstop with little explanation, and she frequently messes up her own examples. She even kept teaching after a student passed out. Overall, a terrible experience. I used to be good at math, and this class ruined it.

I genuinely have no idea how she still teaches here. She made me hate math. There have been multiple instances where students in the class correct her answers because she got them wrong. I remember one class she started doing a problem and said "Am I doing this right? I hope." A student passed out in my class and she got mad at them.
How does she have a job?????? UMass needs to investigate here. I can't believe I'm paying really U.S currency to go here just to have terrible professors like her.

People who say this hard for this class mainly they are not actually study, they use whatever the reason to blame on her just to hide their laziness. There are several people who are racist to her, laughing to her accent, so if you take her, just finish every hw on canvas, wiley, you'll be good, and also attend her lecture, boring but helpful!

Lectures are horrible, i personally couldnt understand anything she goes through the material really fast and occasionally makes mistakes which will confuse you even more. Attendance is optional, youre better off learning the material by yourself.

reviews.comment: How did she get this job.
She is not good at teaching, and just overall kills your will to live!
DO NOT TAKE HER!!! : )

Take this professor if you hope to understand ABSOLUTELY NOTHING. She only teaches by writing notes on the board, and frequently makes mistakes that have to be corrected by students. One of her favorite phrases is "does this look right?" and she WILL teach through a fire alarm. Terrible, you are better off not going to lecture.

Her accent is hard to understand and she tends to say import words wrong making it confusing. Having the midterm and final be the only two grades means you're screwed if you have a bad day on one or the other. She also can't use the mic properly so you can't hear her clearly. Also no obviously available office hours.

Terrible, lost all love for math. She's nice but can't teach at all. Lectures are just her copying notes/problems from another laptop onto OneNote with 0 explanation, so its not worth your time going to lectures. And the notes themselves she posts confusing. Midterm avg was failing (57) and there was no curve. Avoid at at all costs 😭😭😭

This teacher was so bad that I could not understand anything she said. I literally missed all of her classes on purpose. I had to study on my own; going to lectures, honestly, is not helpful.  If you take this class, just go to the SI sessions; they teach better than her. If you ever have this woman as a professor, pick a religion and pray!
I can't understand half of the things she says. Her notes are messy and hard to read. Don't take this class if she is teaching it.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Lecture heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: DO NOT TAKE THIS CLASS WITH SOMI!!! She is sweet, but one of the worst professors I have ever encountered. I learned nothing this year because she doesn't teach; she tells you what she's writing, with no explanation. For the love of god, do not take her class. I will be surprised if she is not fired next semester. AVOID AT ALL COSTS.

My first time taking calc and honestly awful. Her lectures are terrible because I don't know what she's saying and her notes are so messy. I ended up not going to the lectures and teaching myself through her notes and youtube. Honestly so frustrating.

Class is challenging. The professor, though kind, teaches confusingly. She talks nonstop, making notes unclear, rushes through material, and provides only one example per problem type. Her messy notes skip key steps. With few assignments, you must excel in midterms and finals. Attend SI sessions. Her close-miked voice makes her hard to understand.
reviews.rating_tags: Test heavy--Graded by few things--Online Savvy

reviews.comment: Professor Kang's inexperience unfortunately is very visible with her lectures and style of teaching. She does not explain the topics clearly, nor in depth. I am glad that I took this course in high school, otherwise I would have really struggled. She means well and is a nice person but is a very incompetent teacher.

She seems like a nice person however, she is a terrible professor. I took calc in high school so about 75% of this course was review but I DEEPLY empathize with anyone whose first introduction to calc was with this professor. When dealing with this prof, please pick a religion and start praying today.

Thought you were good at Math? Think again, Somi is not only capable of delivering a good lecture but also makes you rethink what you knew how to do. One time the fire alarm and she just kept teaching for some reason until someone told her that you actually cant do that. 350 characters isnt enough to really talk about how you shouldnt take her.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Lots of homework--Beware of pop quizzes

reviews.comment: Terrible terrible terrible. DO NOT TAKE HER. She can't teach and the lecture don't help with anything. The class average for the midterm was a 57%. I took Calc in High School and this is my worst class. She constantly messes up and she can't write.
dont do it

Hard to understand in class, makes mistakes during her lectures, making math harder to follow. Assigns homework over breaks, randomly, and without warning, forcing you to constantly check WileyPlus for updates.
Hard to understand, makes mistakes during her lectures making the math harder to follow. Assigns homework unpredictably and over breaks, forcing you to constantly check her website for updates.

tests were pretty easy and averages were highish, like 80. HW was 2-3 webassigns a week. teaching is meh, makes a few mistakes sometimes but she writes everything on her ipad and puts it on the TV so it's easy to copy down and. mostly graded on tests (2 midterms 1 final, total 75% of grade). weekly quizzes but easy. gives practice tests to study.

I took AP Calc in High School, so this class has been mostly review for me. That being said, I got an 80 on the midterm - average was a 57%. Not horrible, but definitely goes to show that if you have no previous calculus experience, you should try to steer clear of this prof. She is really sweet, just not great at explaining things.

She's really nice but really hard to understand. Homework is easy too, usually 1-2 homework assignments and 3-question quiz per week. I took honors calc in high school and so far have an A in the class-if you have a background in calc, you'll be fine. Exams were also easier than expected. If you complete and understand the homework, you'll be fine.

She's very nice, but not well suited for teaching. If you haven't taken calc before, you'll likely be confused. Lectures move fast, and she solves the examples herself, leaving little time to process the information or practice. SI sessions help, but unless you're good at math or have taken calc before, expect to study 6+ hours weekly to keep up.

piece of advice, go to the SI sessions religiously in order to understand what's going on, she's kind but makes the class harder to understand than it should be. Honestly not bad material but she does not help at all, explanations are lowkey confusing.GO TO SI SESSIONS!

Math 127 with Somi is a very lecture heavy, face paced class. Homework and a 3 question "mini-quiz" after every class. The lecture usually ends ~15 minutes early and there is SI for the class but many students often have a difficult time understanding the content. Class average for the midterm was a 57 so be prepared to study, make sure to show up.

Her lectures are fast-paced; she usually ends 15 minutes early, and students would sometimes have to ask her to slow down because they could not understand her. In my opinion, she was a good professor! Go to classes, ask questions (she was always very open to answering), and if you are extra confused, go to SI sessions. Graded on 2 exams 55% and hw
I absolutely love this guy!! I wish he took other CS classes and I'll be sad to leave him. Amazing professor w zero cons
Incredibly energetic and fun lecturer. He cares a lot about his students, and explains concepts simply and clearly the first time.
Goated professor. You'll actually want to go to class.
Great professor with very well organized course materials and energetic lectures. Having him as your first CS teacher is awesome.

Prof. Liberatore is a genuine, knowledgable and enthusiastic professor, who tries his best to make mundane topics interesting and engaging. As he puts it this class can be like eating your veggies, but he does his best to make it stick. I will say this isn't the most difficult CS class, but make sure to review your coding assignments before final
Probably the greatest CICS professor in UMass history. If you've never taken a class with him, do yourself a favor and sign up as soon as possible.
He's the goat

CS majors absolutely love this guy. He is friendly, young, and is just as much computer science as he is teacher. He obviously cares a lot about the course. He is the perfect balance of effective & reasonable.
Awesome, funny, engaging lecturer - love him to death.
Great guy, great teaching, yadda yadda you get the deal

Marc is one of the best professors I've ever had. He's so caring and really cares about his students and their learning. The class is quite rigorous, there are a lot of assignments and quizzes but if you manage your time well, the work reinforces concepts and helps with overall learning. He is super enthusiastic and brings a lot of energy to class

Marc is a great professor and is extremely enthusiastic about the course. The one thing that was bad with this course (which is reflected by my grade) was the grading system. Exams and quizzes make up around 70% of your grade, so if you're not great at writing out code like me it's very hard to get a good grade.
Excellent. Wish I worked harder. Felt as though the grades were earned.

Marc is one of the nicest professors I've met in the CS department so far. I thought the difficulty of the class was perfectly in the middle with some very difficult bits and other extremely easy parts. His lectures were generally pretty good and the notes he posted afterwards were extremely useful. Overall a very funny and personable guy.

Marc is such a kind and caring man and an amazing professor. The course is manageable, and Marc is very good at breaking down high-level concepts into bite-sized chunks, and letting the student come to their own conclusions/form their own thoughts. Projects are not weighted very heavily, but that might be a department thing, not a Marc thing.

I was lowkey fighting for my life in this class, but he's a great lecturer. Really funny and answers Campuswire posts quickly. The exams are fair, and he posts lecture notes. The concepts are difficult, but that's expected from a 187 equivalent. I learned a lot from him. 10/10 recommend

Marc is without a doubt one of the greatest professors on campus. He seems to genuinely care about his students. Marc tries to make lectures engaging and has plenty of patience. The course is fairly hard, but Marc is well aware of this and tries to make it as easy as possible for you.

Amazing professor. One of the best I have ever had. He is patient with students and is willing to help students as much as he can. Always bring passion to the class. He also tries to make exams and quizes relatively easy.
Best Instructor ever

Marc was an absolutely fantastic professor. This is probably the hardest course I have ever taken and if any other professor was teaching it I probably would've failed. Marc was a great and entertaining lecturer and also provided very detailed guides for the quizzes and exams. There were also weekly homeworks, but they had autograders, so not bad.

reviews.comment: The classwork isn't too bad, and he is a very engaging professor. He has a great ability to take boring subject matter and make it interesting.
Marc is my Marius. He should always be teaching 230.
reviews.rating_tags: Amazing lectures --Clear grading criteria--Gives good feedback

reviews.comment: Great lecturer, very enthusiastic, assignments were well put together and pretty light.
Goated professor

Professor Liberatore was one of the best CICS professors I've had so far at UMass. His lectures were always entertaining to attend and expectations were made clear for a course as information dense as CS230. He always made sure to clear up any confusion with topics before moving on.

Energetic lecturer and a nice person, but terrible at course management. The class would have been all over the place if it hadn't been for the TAs. Exams do reflect course content but are graded harshly. We also could not see our final exam score and the overall course grade, so that was very frustrating.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Group projects--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: computer science classes are hard. computer science exams are also hard. people are being silly by rating him bad for that universal truth; marc is a good guy. exams fairly reflect course content, if sometimes tricky. great lecturer. course staff was awesome. slay.
Absolute Legend of a man. No complaints at all. Wish all professors were like him.

Marc did a great job in making a previously easy class hard to score well. The exams are hard, they have a MCQ and an open response section. The MCQ's for one midterm were 3 points each, which means getting a few questions wrong would lead to a lot of points deducted. The grading for open response was harsh and not too much partial credit was given

Professor Marc has done an amazing job at making a class with pretty mundane (for most people) material and making it interesting. He maintains a pretty high energy level in lecture not seen from many other CS professors here, and is also pretty funny. The work and quiz/exam difficulty is not difficult if you study, compared to CS220.

Prof Marc is a legend, super funny guy, always gives extensions. The content in 230 can be boring at times but Marc has some great jokes in lectures. 230 is a decently difficult class, weekly quizzes are hard af study for those

Worst teacher. Takes forever to answer on Campuswire or at all. Doesn't accept emails. Doesn't give answers to practice exams. Doesn't give u back the exam sheets after exams. Information on slides are very much limited. The quizzes are graded out of 5 or 10 so they will tank your grade. Lots of quizzes and were very tricky.
reviews.rating_tags: Beware of pop quizzes--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Very fun lecture even when the content was boring AF! made the projects easier by giving lots of help

Probably the best CS prof at UMA. Marc is kind, understanding, and amazing at teaching. He will excuse assignments if you get sick and is very flexible. He also has a great sense of humor which makes lectures entertaining, and as a result makes it easier to learn the concepts.

Probably the best CS professor at UMass. Marc genuinely cares about the wellbeing of his students and gives extensions when needed. His lectures are one-of-a-kind; he explains difficult topics very throughly and clearly, and is very willing to answer questions. He is also very accessible to answer questions outside of class. He is a must pick.

Marc is one of the BEST professors I have had. Genuinely cares about his students' learning experience and grades. He is easily accessible and is ready to answer questions - response times via email or Campuswire were generally within 24-48 hours. Definitely recommend taking as many classes of his as you can!!!
Great teacher. Really helped me understand java at a deeper level, and I feel a lot more prepared for CS187. Really recommend his class if you passed 121, but are still confused about things

Fantastic instructor and genuinely nice person. He'll respond to any question you have and wants to see you succeed as a student. CS186 was challenging at times but everything was clear and manageable given that he grades based on 4 different metrics. Definitely take his class if you're interested in Comp Sci.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Accessible outside class--Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: MARC IS THE MAN!!!! Really nice professor that cares for his students and you can tell how much effort he puts into every lecture by the energy he brings. Passionate and knowledgeable and sees students as people.
reviews.rating_tags: Accessible outside class--Get ready to read--Inspirational

reviews.comment: All around great guy, best professor I've had at UMass.

AMAZING GUY. Truly cares about each and everyone's success and wellbeing. If you have a valid reason for submitting homework late he'll give you enough time to do so. He is very understanding and caring, 10/10 would take again. Also, he looks sort of looks like discount Edward Snowden.

MARC IS AN AMAZING PROFESSOR! I have taken 3 classes with him and he is without a doubt the most competent professor I've come across within the CS department. He makes everything so easy to understand and really cares about your grade. He'll always give you extra time if you ask and he's such a great guy.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Amazing lectures--Caring

reviews.comment: I am so glad I took this class my first semester - although the coding projects (1 each week, 11 in total) could be difficult, they also felt like fun puzzles. Lectures can go kind of fast since there's a lot of material, but Marc made the material interesting and engaging. He was also super helpful when I went for help during office hours.

Marc was a very fun professor during class and lectures, but when I would see him during office hours and after class, he did not seem as happy as usual, which I was not expecting. Overall, a very fun, relatable, professor!
Best teacher of this semester. The greetings made me fresh every class and I began to strongly love computer science. And he even teach a little python at end of the class. Amazing!

So far Marc has been my favorite professor. His lectures were interesting and in-depth and he was always open to questions after class. The class is assignment heavy so it was a pretty easy A if you put in the work as you can submit the projects as many times as you want. Weekly homework and quizzes in discussion and only a final worth 15%.

Lots of projects for this class but he's really lenient on deadlines as long as it's reasonable. Make sure you don't take the tests too lightly even though they're not worth too much. START PROJECTS ON TIME! This is the bulk of the work and if you try hard on them you'll do really well in this class
I have complained about my workload for Digital Forensics to my girlfriend so much, that we now use the word "forensics" as our safeword, because it is an instant turn-off.

I signed up for 365 thinking that it would just be another schmuck course that I would have to get through to get all my 300 requirements done. But with Marc's teaching, I actually found that material interesting. His lectures are easy to understand and riddled with humor. His lecturing truly made dry topics like low-level parsing interesting.

Marc is probably one of the best professors that I've ever had. There was homework due every class, but it was all very doable. His lectures were amazing. He puts his notes up after class and uses those instead of a textbook. He is super helpful in office hours and very approachable. 10/10 would take it again.
reviews.rating_tags: LOTS OF HOMEWORK--ACCESSIBLE OUTSIDE CLASS--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: Marc is a great professor. He is really approachable, funny and takes effort to ensure that everyone understands what happens in class. He also had very low weight on tests and quizzes, and more on weekly homework projects.

Marc is an amazing computer science teacher and is very engaged in wanting to teach the material. He is very funny and made learning very enjoyable. He never asks for too much and will slow down if it is too confusing for the class. Take Marc if you can because he's amazing!
Fantastic teacher, mixes humor with learning makes the class engaging and fun. Lots of programming assignments but it's necessary for the class in order to learn.

There are way too many assignments and most of them test you on very similar things. There was a programing assignment every week. However Marc is super helpful if you go to his office hours and his lectures are interesting. The late policy was kind of messed up, but I don't think he'll continue it in future semesters.

The best teacher I have ever had for computer science in college. Clearly passionate about the subject, takes time for his students to understand every aspect of the material at hand, and is very accessible in person and online. I credit Marc for making me interested in CS again as well, phenomenal teacher and great person.
The best teacher I have had in my entire academic career.
BEST teacher. Made the COMPSCI experience for me
Hard class. Nice professor.
Marc is amazing! Best teacher I've had so far. 187 was great thanks to him. Very enthusiastic in lecture, and he's clearly passionate about what he's doing. He's young and stuff too, that helps

Marc is by far one of my favorite professors (or even) teachers I've ever had. He is always a breath of fresh air, and I look forward to the class regularly. His lectures are spot on, he even sometimes clearly writes out implementations of code you will be using in projects during class. He is always helping his students, and the tests are fair!
There is a LONG Coding Project Due every Week. So be Prepared to code, ALOT.

One of the best  courses I have taken here as a CS student. Not easy by any means, but you will be a significantly better programmer, and leave the class with a strong understanding of the material. Tests are not that hard; class is mostly assignment-based.
Young and full of energy, makes the morning lecture enjoyable

Professor La Raja is an intelligent, and charismatic lecturer. He's very funny. The workload may seem hefty, but it honestly consists of very little. If you participate, he will try to catch you off guard to make you think. I think you get 5 absences per semester before they count against your grade, only your highest quizzes are counted. Cool guy.

Professor La Raja was great, and despite the class being at 5:30 at night, it was my favorite class I took that semester. It was a flipped classroom, and I loved all the discussions held in the lecture. Quizzes and exams were not bad, and his study guides are very close to the material on the test. Highly recommend!

Professor La Raja is a very knowledgeable and engaging professor. He encourages students to speak up in class and creates an environment where everyone feels comfortable participating. The readings he assigns are interesting and are always discussed in class. I would definitely take another class with him.
Really cool guy who encourages everyone to speak up and is able to give wonderful feedback.

Raymond La Raja is simply an amazing professor. Although politics can be a heavy subject, he carries and explains it well. His lectures, both video and in-class, are concise. Overall a great introductory gen-ed course. The class is easy to understand and, as long as you pay attention to lectures and do your assignments, you should do just fine.

Some of the best lectures I have had at UMass; he really values everyone's opinions on current events. His readings are concise, and the study sessions are invaluable for understanding what is on the test. As long as you regularly attend and read the textbook, you will do well on his exams.

Funny profesor. Took for a gen-ed as a STEM major so not as interesting to me but those invested seemed to love course. There is a textbook and required readings-I did not do them and did fine. Not hard content don't need to watch all his videos to understand. Online pre-class questions and blogs each week where slightly annoying. Overall easy
Prof LaRaja is definition of a great professor, he's the kind of professor you would see in a movie that would drive the main character to being the best he can be, take his class he's amazing

Professor La Raja is an amazing professor who consistently demonstrates that he truly cares about his students. He's very knowledgable, approachable, and an excellent lecturer. Professor La Raja remains unbiased and objective, which is especially beneficial at a school such as UMass Amherst. Take his Classes!

La Raja is very smart & passionate about the class. He does well with challenging students' responses to discussion questions & plays devil's advocate to get us to think critically, unbiased and respectful. Class had 6 chapter quizzes (textbook needed, could take for highest grade), midterm & final exams, and 2 papers, everything spaced out well.

I took Professor La Raja for 208: Parties and Elections. Professor La Raja knows how to really keep a class engaged! There was 2 papers, some textbook quizzes, 1 midterm and a final. There is a textbook but you can find it online. You don't need to read everything to get an A in this class, listen to the lectures, keep up with the news and discuss.

Fantastic professor, stay on top of your work and you won't have a problem, the essays and exams can be slightly difficult but always study and check in with TA, he's funny, smart and accommodates, he usually always extends deadlines, he's extremely fair and always accessible, I hope I can take another class with him in the future

Great professor, super caring, well spoken and intelligent, the work load can sometimes be a bit overwhelming, the long essays are usually within walking distance of exams which can be a bit much and overwhelming, there are quizzes on chapters and its a good booster for your grade

Professor is accessible and can be easily contacted. Office hours are often empty and there is a surplus of resources for students to use to study. Open discussion format of class means that anyone is allowed to share their opinions. Midterm and Final Exam have several places to earn extra credit. If you come to him, he will help you.

This professor is great! I really liked his lecture style where it was more conversation based and less talking at the class. It was very interesting and I learned a lot. There is an in-person midterm and final, as well as two papers, so be prepared to put in a decent amount of effort.

This class is great and very informative for people interested in politics and how the American government works. The professor is kind and engages his students. However, I would not recommend if you are looking for an easy gen ed, as there is a short essay and 5-6 page strategy memo that are somewhat difficult and are graded harshly as well.

Professor La Raja is one of the rare PoliSci professors who doesn't show political bias, which I think is great (even as a left-leaning person). His lectures are held discussion style, which made the lectures super interesting and engaging. This is a great class to take as a gen ed, La Raja really cares about his students and what we have to share.

Took in Spring 2021. Very fascinating class with effective lectures and interesting readings. A good amount of discussion too though its positive effects were severely mitigated by covid. Teacher was very helpful outside of class and an incredibly thorough expert and lecturer on the subject. Highly Recommend!
reviews.rating_tags: Clear grading criteria--Lecture heavy--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: AMAZING professor! Had him for American politics fall 2021 and his lectures were great. He is really passionate about the subject and wants everyone to get involved. Provides lots of opportunities for grades and gives you a few chances to miss assignments. Approachable and loves talking about current events, which was the best part of lectures!

La Raja is the best professor I've ever had. Actually cares about the subject matters that he's teaching and cares not just about students succeeding in the class but also becoming politically active/aware. I now read the news everyday because of him. Blogs and papers were fun too, and coming to class for open class discussion was fun too.

I took Political Parties and Elections, LaRaja is an amazing prof and actually cares about what you think and doesn't discriminate based on personal views. Thr work is interesting and fun and the final research paper is very interesting. If you like politics and course description, take this class 100%, im taking another course with him in spring

I took this class because I'm an immigrant, so I wanted to learn about American politics. Prof La Raja knows his stuff and is happy to explain anything you need to know. He lets the debates that occur in lecture happen without inserting his opinion, which I appreciate. He is respectful of everyone's contribution, even if he obviously disagrees.

Very good at encouraging participation in class (in fact this ends up taking up most of the class often, and this may sound like a bad thing, but its actually really helpful for actually understanding the text book and will help later on in your essays). Always makes sure the discussions are politically balanced (which is a rare thing at UMass)

I could not recommend La Raja more! I have taken his class twice as a PoliSci major and both times he has exceeded my expectations. He is very neutral in class discussions and great at facilitating them. He goes out of his way to find great guest lecturers who have taught me very memorable lessons and information. He is very easy to talk to!
A great lecturer, with charisma intellect and the energy that transcends into the crowd to get dialogue going in large lecture groups.
LaRaja's Political Science 101 was good even in the pandemic.
Pretty passionate and driven

Professor La Raja does not grade his own assignments and his TA is a tough grader. Essays are graded fairly, but when it comes to exams TA looked for exact definitions if you even miss one word he would take away multiple points. All exams are definition based, but u r not given a study guide so you have to study every definition from the section

This is a blended course: you watch recorded lectures online and do supplemental readings before the class lecture (textbook reading is good for online quizzes). La Raja usually kicks off the class with some discussion about current affairs and then starts his discussion-style lecture. If you're interested in politics, you'll get an easy A.
Only take if you're actually passionate for politics.. workload is kind of annoying but not too bad

American Politics with Professor La Raja was fun and engaging. He does grade on attendance, but he gives you a solid allowance of absences. The class size can be huge, though, so work is graded by TA's. As such, it's hard to know how you'll score. Big exams and essays account for most of the grade.

actually the sweetest guy ever. hypes you up no matter what your opinions are. doesn't expect you to know much about politics coming in. people talk a lot in class if they know about politics, it gets heated sometimes which is kinda fun. he helps your grade sooooo much, legit drops lowest 4 everything.

Raymond La Raja, loml. I went into college as a psych major wanting to go to law school. After taking his 101 class first semester of college, I declared my double major in polisci-- it was the best decision. Going to class was always so exciting. I even took my bio major bf one day to watch and he left wanting to contact congress. changed my life.

I've had Professor La Raja for both PoliSci 101 and 208. He is a great teacher with a very clear understanding of the subject. I enjoyed both classes, but liked 101 better because of his discussion-oriented take on a huge lecture; he also handled presenting basic information objectively in today's political climate extremely professionally.

This is my second class that I've taken with Professor La Raja and he truly is fantastic! He is a funny guy, very smart, and very caring. The two papers for this class were very fun, and they helped me learn skills that will be useful in the field. Everybody should take a class with Professor La Raja before they graduate!

Ray is the best teacher in the Poli Sci department. His teaching is clear, he explains things well, answers questions thoroughly and clearly cares for his students. His exams are straightforward and papers or other assignments are fun and well explained. I took 101 with him as well and loved both classes. Talks about current events which is great.
Very smart professor, and loves to meet students. Pretty easy class if you do the readings

Smart guy, and really makes you invested in the subject he teachers. His lectures though, are online and watching them can be a bit of a chore. That being said it never exceeds 45 mins of video, and its pretty much all the homework that he assigns. Great class, brought in lots of guest speakers so that you could see the theory in application.

I had a really good time in this course. I loved hearing him talk about anything. He was incredibly easy to listen to and learn from. I actually enjoyed doing the assignments and studying the material in this course. This course is a perfect introduction to political science. I'm very grateful to have taken this course!
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--LOTS OF HOMEWORK--Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: Although Ray is a kind, well-spoken man with good intentions and hefty experience with the U.S. Government, it seems to me that he has become lazy throughout his years as a professor. His lectures are all online, which is inconvenient and time consuming, and we wasted three-quarters of class time discussing current events rather than class material
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--LOTS OF HOMEWORK--Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: The class has an odd blended setup where students do most of there learning outside of class. The classes consisted of a lot of current events and a lot of stuff that was not relevant to the course. If attendance was not taken with iClickers then there would be no reason to go to class.

La Raja is incredible. He is super knowledgable about American Politics (he has a masters in Public Policy from Harvard and his Ph.D. from UC Berkley) and he really cares about his students. His class is really straightforward and his expectations are clear. You watch lectures online, then come to class to talk/ review material. One of the best.
Cool professor! makes you learn a lot of things. Interactive  class, never boring. Go for it, even when you are not a political science major.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: Was my first Political Science class of college and sealed the deal for me that I wanted to continue with the subject as my major. La Raja is easy to understand and not boring to listen to during lecture at all. Prepares you very well for both the essays and in class tests. Go to class and you will get an A.

La Raja is the man! The class has busy work but nothing to be worried about. He posts his lectures before class so that was where I took the notes and in class he had great lectures with a lot of student involvement. He's funny ad actually wants to talk to his students. Ideas are driven into your brain without realizing it and the tests are easy.
Great Lectures, grading is more up to TA's. But overall great professor and great class. Highly recommend to PoliSci majors and non polisci majors

Prof. La Raja is a great guy, very informative, and smart. He posts his lectures online and that's where I got all my information. In lecture, he clarified some slides from his online lectures and then just talked about current events. I didn't really ever pay attention in lecture but there were clicker Qs almost every class that counted attendance

La Raja's American Politics course is fantastic! Although there is an unnecessary amount of busy work, you really get the contents of the course drilled into your head. He also has a really interesting strategy memo assignment which serves as your second (and last) paper which is not only fun to research but it also provides applicable experience.

Watched videos online, but I loved his lectures because he engaged the students and asked questions and made it interesting and relevant. A lot of assignments, but they are small and you don't have to do all of them. He is very approachable, and actually begs people to come chat with him. Very clear expectations. I would take another class with him

Great professor!!! He keeps the class interesting by bringing up a lot of current topics, and he promotes a lot of in-class discussion. I had him in the experimental class, so you learn the information before class. The tests and quizzes are straightforward, and he's really easy to talk to if you need further clarification. The TAs are awesome too.

The best professor I have had at UMass. I always looked forward to going to class and his lectures were very thorough and interesting and he reposts his powerpoints online for you to review later. Good attendance will only boost your grade not kill you. Readings were interesting. He´s very engaging in class. What you learn will stick with you.
La Raja is the man! I loved his American Politics class. The exams are all blue book open response and there are some outside papers, but the class isn't too hard and it's great information. Take it!
Taught everything well, reasonable clear. Not much work, mandatory lectures. Friday classes were only every two weeks. Def take a class with him

He is a good professor. His lectures are good. He does this group schedule thing to meet in smaller groups every 2 Fridays and it works pretty well. The exams are ok, the only bad part is the online blogs, and the strategy paper that should be for a 200 level course instead.

GREAT PROFESSOR!!!  He was the only professor I had this semester where I learned ANYTHING!!!  Such an awesome, approachable guy, and his class is fair.  He gives you study guides to review for the exams and his class is great!  Take this class!!!!!!

Incredibly interesting class. Ray was genuinely interested in the subject and often brought students opinions into the class for discussion. Not to difficult, not too easy. Lots of good info if you like politics at all. D

Very approachable guy. Always keeps lectures interesting, makes lots of jokes, especially about sports. There are lots of different kinds of grades so it's easy to earn points somewhere. Not a college-professor type, very down to Earth guy.

Awesome Professor. Lectures are interesting and he always starts class with current events and relates them to what we're studying. Attendance is by PRS and only worth 4% of final grade, so usually the people who show up want to be there. Generates interesting discussions. Tests are totally manageable if you study.

Funny guy who knows how to keep a big lecture entertained. Fairly simple concepts that he continues to apply throughout the course assignments to help reinforce. Tests aren't bad if you do the work an study..not something you can skate by on but nothing to stress about either. Cool guy.
Alright class. Exams are alright if you study the past exams he posts. The TA I had was a real dbag, but the professor was really funny and interesting.
Great professor and really keeps the class involved and entertained for a big lecture. Exams are fair. Funny guy and always starts the class off with current events.

LaRaja is amazing. I dont know what people are talking about, the tests are easy and he hands you the final exam essay topic (its in the syllabus if you read the description). I took it my first semester in the USA and I knew nothing of the political system here and got an A no problem. He is awesome, and tells you EXACTLY what to do for HW/tests

Great teacher but difficult subject. Exams were short answer and had a lot of definitions to know, so if memorizing something isnt your strong suit take notice. Papers were manageable but difficult and the different TAs grading schemes seemed very different from one to another. PRS Mandatory

La Raja is awesome! Attendance mandatory but class was fun.  Hes always cracking jokes and is great eye candy. legit. Tests are a bit hard because they are short answer go to class and take notes and you'll be fine. If he talks about something alot it will be on the test. Learned a lot would recommend to everyone.

Excellant teacher, lectures are fun and interesting. He's smart, involved and knows what he is talking about. Funny and good looking guy (babe). Always tries to get students involved during and outside of the class. PRS mandatory. Read the book and tests/quizzes aren't bad at all. Veryyyy liberal, don't let him brain wash you. And like I said, he's

good teacher. really funny and wants you to understand material. attendence is mandatory because of PRS. a few easy online quizzes and some reading. tests require some studying because its all short answers, but its fair. he really helped me understand politics. i recommend it.

Laraja is one of the most fun professors I have ever had. He makes a class of 400 feel like 40. He really engages the class and cracks alot of jokes. Seriously this guy could be a comedian if he wanted to. Tests are all written, but it is VERY clear what will be on them. The final exam essay topics are in the syllabus course description. Very nice.
He's a good guy, kinda funny. Bad teacher, TA's are horrible. Avoid if possible.
His lectures are fun and entertaining, but his tests are hard and he provides very little help with them.
fun classes, lots of interaction with students
Real down to earth guy, pro teacher, passionate smart knows his material everything i could ask for in a teacher. Highly recommended. I think you learn the most by your effort with this guy.
Really good teacher seems to really enjoy what he does. Attendance is mandatory because of PRS but going to class is helpful to do good on tests. Also helpful that he puts his noted on SPARK.
He's an all around good teacher. The class required attendance with the use of a PRS. Two tests that were multiple choice and short essay. A medium level of studying is required.
