This class is very easy, attendance is counted only because of the PRS clickers, LaRaja loves polling the class which is always interesting, good lectures.

Tough to say. Definitely a great teacher. Tries to bridge the studies to the real world often. I felt he didn't prepare us enough for the requirements of graded assignments. Class was a little loose but there was about 300 of us so what can ya  do. A+ for effort A- for achievement. Tries very hard to get feedback and improve.

I liked how he starts every class with a short discussion on current events. The tests aren't bad at all, and you only have to write two papers for the entire semester.  A great class to take if you want to learn the basics of American politics. PRS is required.

Excellent Teacher.  Lots of reading homework but not many people I know actually did the reading and still got an A or B.  La Raja is very enthusiastic about his teaching.  Funny guy, easy to listen to.  Tests are one essay and definitions.  One or two papers.  I highly reccomend this class to anyone.
He's a really great professor and he always starts discussions in class and lets people have different opinions no matter what they are.  If you love politics you'll love him as a teacher.
he's the man good class

My favorite class of the semester. Had to go because of the PRS but the lectures were interesting and based a lot on current events. A lot of student interaction and some random heated debates between students. Def reccommend this class
Loved this class, I actually looked foward to it. He is very good at getting people into poitics. He makes the political process fun!

This guy makes politics fun, his lectures are awesome, and his polls which he puts up on the big screen are hilarious. He makes you take a survey in the beginning of the year on WebCT and goes back to it nearly every lecture. He interacts with his students before class.. great profesor, great guy.
He's definitely a good guy. Took him spring semester. Class is easy, just go to lectures, they are at least somewhat interesting. Watches the sopranos so he must be a cool cat.
had him last semester, good guy, watches the sopranos so you know he's a cool cat
easy class. could've gotten a B+ if i showed up to discussion or wrote another paragraph, settled for a B though. just go to class and pay attention, prs required.

I LOVE Professor La Raja. Everything was interesting all semester and the PRS questions were eye-opening. Loves politics, does a great job interacting with students. Extremely intelligent and great Poli Sci professor for a GenEd! Strategy paper was close to impossible, but he had good intentions...it's all good
I love this guy! Just read your notes and going to class helps but you can def. teach yourself. His notes are awesome and tests are easy!
The class is intersting, he always gets excited about all sorts of things. Makes the class interactive with PRS and asks questions in class. Make sure you know who your US rep is in the house!
easy class, only need to go is becuase of PRS. all notes online, never homework. only need to read before tests.
Pretty Easy.  Mostly just discussions and you dont really take notes.  Do the readings and the paper and you'll do fine.
Not a bad entry class for the Polisci field.  Presents all of the information in notes online but fails to use class time wisely.  Not a bad class, could be a lot better, Mid term was unfair.
Really good class I recommend it for as a gen ed.

Pretty easy class.  He is always late for class and often unprepared.  He is nice and interesting but the class is very disorganized.  The assignments are hard to understand and since he doesn't follow the syllubus that is no help. Our campaign project was hard.  No one knew exactly what he expected or how to find the information we needed.

Attractive man.  Very organized and clear presentation of material.  Easy class all around.  Supplements regular facts with current events, making the class more interesting.  I liked getting to see other students' opinions from the PRS polls... unfortunately, the PRS also means attendance is taken.

Having had a good number of poli sci professors, I can say La Raja is the man.  He's funny and spawns thought while teaching you the basics.  I definitely recommend this class if you are into elections.
No Comments
Pretty easy class, if you go to lecture you don't really need to read much.  Grading can be pretty good depending on your TA.
Good class, pretty easy if you go and pay attention! La Raja is easily one of the best political science professors at UMass!
Fairly involved class, alot of reading and remembering tidbits of information for the exams.  Grading depends on the TA, and the discussion section is not very much fun.
No Comments
Great class
He always stimulates class participation and shows excitment about teaching. He is very helpful outside of class, and is also nice to look at in class!
Easy. Easy. Easy. On top of that its a fun class. Hes cool. If you study and make a lil cheat sheet to study..ur golden on the exams. Attendance isn't a must really.
Gets involved, tries to make subjects interesting.  Definately makes you want to know more about politics. No excuses kind of guy.  Great professor.
The subject matter was so boring to me that I couldn't return to class after the third week. I'm sure he's a good professor.
He made everything very clear, and tried to make the students interested in what was going on.  He was the best professor I have had so far.
Internship facult sponsor-I got so very much more out of my internship because of him.
He is a really nice person and he is well organized in the way he teaches class. I voted him for some teacher award thing.
Very nice guy.  unorganized.  didnt explain in great detail what would be on tests.  however, gave a generous scale. he was a d.i.l.f. u know what i mean.
good class, i would def take another with him. and hes a nice guy, got to sit next to him one class, and he was really interested to meet students and find out if they like the class or not.
Amazing course, gotta love the hair!
Very good class. Great professor. Very motivated.

Looks like Patrick Dempsey. Good class. Pretty easy if you read the book. Lecture notes are all online. He takes attendence through PRS but you can still miss 5 classes. Lectures go over the book and do PRS survays which all really fun. Good Class.
No Comments
He's so nice and really interesting and enthusiastic about politics
No Comments
Interesting class, he's into the class and explains it all pretty well. Not too hard if you study a little
very cute.
good guy
No Comments

Vey boring lectures, he has a mic in class but still somehow struggle to hear half of what he's saying since he's always facing the board writing some derivation. I will say though, his graph drawings are flawless and beautiful
Nice guy but extremely boring lectures. Better off using practice problems, textbook, and TAs to learn the content.

What should be an interesting class is made boring through PowerPoints of research papers. Uses some youtube videos to make it somewhat bearable.

Main project is open ended and unclear. Project feedback felt contradictory from session to session.

Dr. Lee is brilliant and cares about the material, but its just so difficult to stay engaged/focused

Unorganized Lectures, ignores questions asked in class, does not reply to emails and if he does his answers literally do not make sense. Only thing that somewhat helps is his online posted notes but it riddled with math errors as well as important equations just being cut off.

Do you enjoy getting your questions asked in class, getting prompt email responses, clear grading, clear notes and a general understanding of course material? cool me too and thats not what happened. He was extremely unclear in grading, speech, and in notes. I have no idea what we are doing beyond general equations.

Professor Lee puts effort into his class with a lot of nice slides and short videos to help students understand more complex questions. He also shares a lot of web links to good resources. He is very responsive to email and is understanding/usual generous if asked for more time on assignments.
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--ACCESSIBLE OUTSIDE CLASS--Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: Separations is one of my favorite subjects. However, Professor Lee made sure to make that into a class I somewhat enjoyed. Still get an A if you just do your work (Quite a lot of it at times).
reviews.rating_tags: Tough Grader--Get ready to read--TEST HEAVY

reviews.comment: He made math bearable, interesting, and not that hard for me! Very understanding, patient, and friendly.

One of the best Professors in the department. Asks the class questions during lectures, so keep up with the readings. He's very caring, so if you are stuck on something, be sure to go to his office hours.

Ousamma is a super caring teacher and he is always looking to make sure his students are understanding and keeping up. He does go fast and while lectures may seem tiring, he does a great job explaining his work and thought process in a coherent and understandable manner. Don't be afraid to ask questions and definitely go to lecture it helps!

I believe Professor Landoulsi works hard to ensure we understand the material. His lecture notes are a great resource, but please don't miss his lectures. They go a little fast, but they're good for tying down concepts.

Oussama is a good guy but his lectures can be very confusing. Calc 2 is a hard course and it has a lot of confusing topics. I found myself learning the most in discussions and doing the homework out. He is not a bad lecturer and is understanding, but he sometimes goes quite fast.

Professor Landoulsi is one of the most caring professors I knew who taught a lower-division math course at UMass. His lectures are helpful and organized, giving a smooth transition to the course (extra lecture notes!) I recommend taking the course with him if you like getting steady support on your course. Plus, he is an amazing person to talk to.
reviews.rating_tags: Amazing lectures --Gives good feedback--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Grading is pretty harsh and the class was difficult, but his lectures are great and he also posts helpful lecture notes which cover everything from lecture as well as anything he missed in lecture.

He is the best professor I have had at UMass. Extremely intelligent and funny. All the bad reviews are probably from people who do not care at all about giving one ounce of effort. If you actually want to expand your knowledge and grow as a human being, please take this class and make the most out of it, one of the best resources available.
Very quietly the funniest prof. i've ever had. If you show up you'll do fine, if he knows who you are and you make a concerted effort you'll do better.

Please avoid Marco. This guy is a joke. So many digressions in the class so nobody can really follow him. Nobody cares Fed stuff. He is definitely not qualified to be a good professor. The exam is also a joke. Just one essay question to explain the concept with tough grading. This is the WORST class experience in UMass. Please avoid if you can.

Avoid at all costs! This professor has zero teaching experience and often seems clueless about the material. He lacks clear explanations and appears to have no idea what he's talking about. Worse, he has a condescending attitude toward students and treats them with little respect. Easily the worst professor I've ever had.

This class was extremely disappointing. Marco was boasting his own career path all the time. Nothing useful was taught. He read everything directly from the textbook without using any slides. It made us very hard to prepare for exams. Additionally, the grading was very tough. This is the WORST class in UMass. Please avoid if you can.

Marco is clear on what he expects and if you come to class with some news headline from the week before and can talk about how it relates to finance for 1 minute (or less) you will get a good grade for participation. His exams are just one question but if you are not an idiot you will be fine. In the exam he just wants you to explain a concept.

He expects you to participate in class (30% of the grade) but does not create a welcoming environment. He also forgets to note down your participation and says it's your fault that he forgot you participated. He talks like he does not want to be teaching and cares more about speaking about his career than actually teaching the class.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Participation matters

reviews.comment: Marco is new to being a professor and I think he may not be cut out for it. This class was very expensive and I do not feel like I got my money's worth (i.e., learned much less than other courses). Marco rambles and looses the students because of it. This class is Real Asset Investing SCH-MGMT 686, required for the Master in Finance degree.

He's very knowledgeable about the topics. He's not an engaging lecturer and doesn't believe in standard testing. He inflates the grade distribution to make two tests worth 35% of the grade each. Its on one essay question and if you misunderstand the concept the question is on you will lose a lot amount of points so ensure you understand everything.
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Clear grading criteria--Graded by few things

reviews.comment:
New to teaching. He's well educated, but doesn't have the qualities of a good professor. He's more concerned about being logical. Lectures based on the book, never has any slide decks. Writes on board & asks students to participate. 

Grade consists of 2 exams (one essay question each), 4 HWs on Connect, & particip. You could easily ChatGPT exams
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Participation matters--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: For a hospitality professor she's not very good at practicing what she preaches. There's sooo many assignments, readings, and textbooks that no one reads. I've had both in person and online with her, don't recommend.

Really nice professor, she really cares about HTM. There are quizzes on each chapter along with four assignments. There are three exams (multiple choice) and no final. All slides are posted on canvas.

There are 3 exams with no final and they are very very easy if you study the material. Questions are very straightforward. She uses tophat to track attendance and you have 12 "freebies" which are questions you can miss without it affecting your score.

Very lenient on attendance, grade is mainly composed of three main exams. As long as you read or attend lectures, this will be very straightforward. The content is very hospitality themed and she is very energetic, and clearly a pro at this. No phones or electronic devices, but very participatory based lectures. very energetic person!
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Clear grading criteria--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: This class was a great introduction course for HTM. I had this class at 8:30am and it was a great start to my day.

is very laid back w/ attendance and making up exams but doesn't accept work late and no laptops in class. attendance is "mandatory" through tophat but worth a very low percentage of ur grade.  lecture HEAVY and hard not to fall asleep.  nice lady overall but class is boring and feels so long. don't buy texbook the slides are all you need.

She loves to talk and has a real passion for the industry. Make sure you take notes on her slides and study for exams because her exams are LONG and reference random material from lectures. If you go to class and take notes you'll get an A. Barely any homework and she assigns reading but you don't really have to do it.

Laurie is SO nice, i really enjoyed htm100 with her. attendance mandatory with tophat but only 5% of your grade. 3 in person multipole choice exma but so easy. take this class for a fun and interesting 3 credits
reviews.rating_tags: EXTRA CREDIT--Clear grading criteria--Gives good feedback

reviews.comment: Awful. Not a very nice professor, not willing to help students.
Lectures were LONG and boring. Exams had difficult wording but overall doable.

Laurie was a very good professor. The exams had some weird wording but were overall self explanatory and easy if you studied the textbook along with her notes that she provided on canvas so you didn't have to take notes during class.

Boring, tiring, long lectures. All common knowledge, she reads off slides, the only fun part were the TopHats (an app that does a poll for you to answer during class to track your attendance). Super easy exams, quizzes were mostly easy, doesn't show what you got wrong and she won't tell you either. Same for exams.

Laurie is wonderful. She cares a lot about the industry. Her lectures are super interesting. Attendance is counted through top hat but she gives you a lot of free absences. No computers/phones allowed in class. Assignments, quizzes, and exams are really easy. Super interesting course whether you're in HTM or not (I am not). Highly recommend Laurie!

Definitely take Lori for 100 if you have an interest in hospitality. She's super engaging and really cares about her students. HW consists of quick online quizzes and four straightforward assignments throughout the semester. Test questions are sometimes a little niche but it's multiple-choice so if you make an educated guess you should be fine
My favorite professor. She is so passionate about what she teaches, and I admire her deeply! Also very understanding and fair.

Professor Salame's HTM100 is a straightforward class. With engaging lectures, flexible assessment, and optional textbook, the course provides an easy A. Using unstuckstudy alongside the provided resources can further boost your success.
She's very understanding and truly loves the industry, also very helpful to explain concepts during tests or quizzes.

She is nice and very inspirational. Her exams are a bit tough though, you would have to study every single thing on the slides and you better study them well because she'll be stirring up the words and playing with your brain. She has an optional final exam if you aren't satisfied with your grade and you wanna bring it up. I got it from B+ to A-
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Lecture heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Every class is just her lecturing about things that are 99% common sense. You could probably pass the class without going to a single lecture but she's super cool and very talkative so they're pretty interesting.

Took this class for Management 260. Good teacher and some topics were more interesting, but the lectures weren't bad. Don't need to buy a textbook and can do good on exams as long as you show up to class. Good teacher overall.
reviews.rating_tags: Clear grading criteria--Gives good feedback--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: Professor Salame is extremely upbeat & positive and manages to make boring material pretty interesting. 3 exams that are easy to do well on if you study your notes, and one weekly assignment. She cares a lot about her students and just wants to see everyone do well and take something away from the class

She is very helpful and kind. Very knowledgeable, and you should go to classes if you can. She uses an old version of the textbook so it is relatively inexpensive. Definitely recommend her HTM100 class

The lecture dragged on for most of the time since it was an hour and 15 minutes. Textbook isn't really needed for the exams, just pay attention to the lectures. 4 major assignments throughout the semester that didn't take long to complete and there were quizzes after each chapter which also don't take long to complete. Fairly easy class overall.

Laurie is very sweet and represent what the hospitality industry is all about. I took this class at 8am and I would recommend taking it later in the day because it can get boring. Although boring at times, it is a super easy class and as long as you read, do the quizzes on time, and go to lectures you'll be fine.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: She embodies the hospitality industry, so if you don't like Laurie, change your major. The class is a bit basic and relatively boring, but an easy A as long as you pay attention and do your quizzes on time. Super flexible about exam schedule.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: I absolutely love this class. Her lectures are really informative and funny, and she posts the slides ahead of time. The quizzes are not very often, and they are open note. She gives you a clear study guide of what you need to know for the exams. The textbook was only $10.
Prof. Salame is an amazing professor. I enjoyed her class very much and wish she taught more HTM classes. I didn't buy the textbook for the class and didn't need it at all to pass.
The quizzes and tests have questions that are worded weirdly with no clear answer.
Lots of lectures to watch but she gives you a lot of time to get work done. Quizzes and test questions are worded weirdly a lot.

I really enjoyed this class and the prof. She was very positive, nice, and engaging. The class is pretty easy if you put in a little effort. Pre-recorded lectures posted every week, and the content was then reviewed with in-class activities. Exams and quizzes aren't bad and there are extra credit quizzes. 3 easy assignments. Great intro to HTM!

Laurie is a great professor and teachers a wonderful class. I would highly suggest her and this class. Lecture based following an online 5 question open book quiz with the opportunity for extra credit. Exams were very easy as long as you go to class and take the quizzes. iClicker is used for attendance points. Don't buy the textbook and an easy A.
worst HTM professor I wish I took the other htm320 Prof even though it was earlier in the morning would've been so much more worth it
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Skip class? You won't pass.--Test heavy

reviews.comment: This class is a fine class, however the length of the class is too long. The prof is a little wacky, and the subject is very boring so if you aren't interested in HTM don't take this class. Attendance is mandatory, didn't use the textbook. Easy A as long as you pay attention. Honestly don't bother if you can avoid taking this class.

Professor Salame makes her exams harder than they need to be. Additionally, she was completely non-accommodating about her extra credit. She requires you to leave Amherst to inspect a restaurant, and when I asked if I could stay in Amherst (because I don't have a car) she wouldn't even consider it. Her exams are tricky for no good reason.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Test heavy--Tough grader

reviews.comment: The class is super easy to pass. I took the class online and the set up got old fast. Each week you'd have to "read" the chapter, post a discussion, reply to two classmates and then take a quiz. I didn't feel like I was receiving my money's worth and on top of that there was no rubric for the discussions. She'd take points off with no explanation.

Very easy class. Three exams that are all multiple choice/ T or F, iclicker attendance and online quizzes. The lectures can get very boring but as long as you review the slides the quizzes and exams are easy. She also offers extra credit quizzes to raise your grade.

DON'T BUY THE TEXTBOOK!! The PPTs are literally just the textbook and she posts them online. I got a 50% on iClicker Attendance and still got a 98 in the class. Exams are super easy if you follow the PowerPoints. Weekly quizzes in Moodle based off the PPTs, 3 exams that are easy af. EASY A FOR ANY MAJOR

Professor Salame is by far the best teacher I've had thus far at UMass. You must go to class in order to receive participation credit through iclickers. As long as you show up and listen to the lecture (which is pretty easy to do since she keeps it engaging) you'll pass! Read the book if you need a review before the test. No need to study. Easy A.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Skip class? You won't pass.--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: Loved her!! I would definitely take her again. She gives positive feedback and is readily available.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Respected--Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: Laurie is an EXCELLENT professor! She makes her exams count for a huge chunk of the class (75%) so be sure to study those. More difficult than her 100 class but she makes class interesting and she is very knowledgeable on subject matter. Definitely take 320 with her if you want a class that doesnt put you to sleep.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Respected--GRADED BY FEW THINGS

reviews.comment: The first part of the class is very bland and boring. It is hard to pay attention. The class gets better as the semester goes on. The tests are tough but once you know the format it makes them easier.

Such an easy class. powerpoints are posted online and you will do well if you just make flash cards, no need to go to class except for iclicker which is 5% of grade. straightforward class definitely an easy A with little/no effort

Overall I thought it was an easy class. You have 3 exams, online quizzes, which most of the answers are online, and Iclicker questions ( based on participation) as your grade. If you read and take notes on the chapters and study, you will easily pass the exams. It does take a little work for this class, but it's an easy A if you put in effort.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--TEST HEAVY--EXTRA CREDIT

reviews.comment: Laurie is  a very clear professor. You get three exams, online quizzes, and attendance counts towards your grade. She tests you more on if you read the book than if you were paying attention in class, but overall the class isn't hard if you can focus long enough to get through the textbook. Her lectures can drone on, but she tries to make them fun.

Her class is easy to get you bored. And she never know to finish the class early if there's nothing valuable to say in class. The class is mandatory. No round-up grading. The tests are not easy. No electronic devices use in class.

Laurie is a great professor! She makes sure everybody is engaged in the material. Attendance is not mandatory but she uses the iClicker and those are easy extra credit points. Make sure you don't forget to do the timed online quizzes.

She is so nice and tries to keep lectures interesting.  You have to go to class because of iclicker attendance.  You should study hard for the exams because they really do have a lot of information on them.  Other then that it was really easy.  I didn't do much work for it and got an A. She gives out extra credit quizes too which is nice.

If you pay some attention in class, and READ THE BOOk you will do very well. She can be a little tricky on the tests and ask very specific (almost trivia-like) questions, which can be annoying. Her lectures last an eternity, and can be extremely boring. Just read the book, go to class, do the online quizzes, and click in the iclicker.
good lecturer kind of hard to get an A helps if you ask for help
She tends to give out quizzes almost weekly. All online, so it is still pretty easy. All logical stuff you should know.
Class requires an i-clicker so either show up to every class and answer the questions she has with the i-clicker or have your friend be a champ and do the clicks for you. Textbook is NOT needed.

You have to show up for class for iClicker points and there is no technology allowed, but I honestly didn't mind because she shares hilarious stories relating to the material. She's one of the reasons I'm an HTM major. You do have to read the book, but as long as you do that and follow along in class it's an easy A.
Not a hard class. Show up, read the book and complete all of the online quizzes. Grading is very clear and she does not allow any technology in the classroom.

One of my favorite professors in the department. Really cares about her students and helping them succeed. She is so funny and will tell a lot of stories. She is a tough grader and doesn't pretend to be easy. Will not round your grade even .01. Offers lots of opportunities to increase your grade, though.

She treats you as if you are not grown adults. She's absolutely annoying and like the way she approaches problems reminds me of a moody woman. If you can deal with that, read the book, and go to class you will most likely do well but she is almost unbearable.

Former lawyer who no longer practices, but now teaches.  Definitely a tough grader.  She asks you to apply what you've learned using the legal terms used thus far; however, it is no good enough.  I hated this class for that reason.  It was a required class for my major and i'm not going to be a lawyer.

The syllabus is so simple: 14 on-line quiz, 4 extra quizzes, three exam each is 25%, and 5% i-clicker attendance. But the points is the grading is so makes no sense. And the exam is so tricky, you have to read the textbook in every words and every sentences. If you get a 89.99, your grade is still  B+, she will never round the grade up.

Professor Salame is an exceptional professor. She was the one to inspire me to join the hospitality major. She gives online quizzes, three tests (lets you skip ones that you can make- up at the end of the year), iclickr questions (lets you miss 10 QUESTIONS, not lectures. About 2-3 questions per lecture), posts her powerpoints to moodle.
This class was an easy A. Just read and pay attention. She is very enthusiastic and fun!

Extremely hard class. She's wise and accepting of others opinions, but very specific with her work Eg. In an exam she will ask for the definition within the definition within that definition. Had to do alot of reading and meeting up with other classmates and the professor. Prepare yourself. Take the other class with a diff professor if u want an A

Buy the textbook, and pay attention to details. Class is boring most of the times i just went for iclicker grade. She tries to trick you on the exams. Very irrelevant questions on exams. She will not round up your grade even if you are .33 point below an A. Doesnt really care about the student.
Loved Laurie! She made this class so interesting! Ended up with an A, but it took extra work than just going to class. Absolutely recommend to people interested in business or HTM.
Loved Laurie, she has a awesome personality. Class is straightforward, do the reading and you'll get an A.

Laurie is an awesome professor. She is so full of knowledge and experience and she's passionate about what she teaches. She's easily my favorite professor here at UMASS. Her class is mandatory and there are 3 exams.  The exams are a very fair assessment given they are everything you will cover in class.  Study the notes and it's an easy A.

Amazing class. Laurie is informative and always very engaging with firsthand experience and stories about the industry. I do not understand the negative reviews at all. Class is easy as long as you review the powerpoints and skim over the chapters from the book before exams. You'll easily get an A if you put in the effort.

Annoying teacher. Do not take as an elective. If you go to class and take the notes you aren't even rewarded because she asks questions on one caption in the book. 90% of the material you review isn't even on the exams. Has personal interest in the subject, but her attitude towards students is demeaning. BUY THE BOOK.

Laurie was always very enthusiastic about HTM and has so much experience in the field. Her lectures were clear and she tried her best to keep class interesting. Exams were not too bad and were scaled if the class did poorly. I studied for 3-4 hours for each test, and I got an A.

Extremely difficult teacher! Exams contain material NEVER taught in class. Wont let you use laptops or electronic devices in class. She showed an interest in the subjects, but completely turned me off to joining the HTM major!

Hands down the best professor at UMass, and also one of the most entertaining people I have ever met. She's not the easiest professor but I have learned more from her classes than any other. I LOVE THIS WOMAN

I loved her. She rambles, but it's fun to listen to. She has so much info and experience in the field. Attendance def helps-iclicker question every class for credit. EASY online quizzes after each chapter and 3 tests that you have to study for. Her ppts are helpful but I suggest reading esp for tests. Participate!

Great teacher. Go to class, pay attention, and participate. Try to get to know her too..it helps. Use the iclicker and do the quizzes. And read the textbook! Its helpful for not only the class, but your career!

Professor Salame was by far the best professor I had this semester.  I loved the class and loved her! Knew a lot about HTM and cared about it too. Class was easy with online quizzes after each chapter. Exams are fair but you have to study. Iclicker counts as part of your grade. Overall a great, fun, and exciting class even if you're not in HTM.

Really knowledgeable professor in HTM. She's had a lot of field experience so knows exactly what she's teaching. Sometimes her classes would seem to drag since they're 75 minutes long, but she kept it interesting. Attendance is mandatory because of iClicker.   Quizzes online are SO easy but exams can be ALITTLE tricky if you don't read the book.

She is very interesting and often times comical. The class is very easy but pretty much mandatory based on the iclicker which counts for an attendance grade. The reading is not as important becaus she basically just tells you what you read in class. Only issue is you can NOT use technology in her class or she will call you out.

Laurie is my favorite professor at UMass and the original reason why I became a HTM second major.  She's really energetic and one of the most knowledgeable professors in the HTM department.  Homework in this class is key, make sure you do all the homework and study for the tests and you'll be fine. this is one of the best classes I have ever taken
She likes to scream into her microphone a lot but really easy class, if you actually study the powerpoints she puts online you'll do real well

Extremely SUBJECTIVE grading, which as you can imagine could be against you in a detrimental way if you don’t play the game correctly. Laurie is disrespectful to students(of all ages)& is unapologetic for it. Over-achieve & take this course by itself in Summer/Winter semester so you can devote your life to it. That’s what she’ll be expecting.
Very funny, entertaining, messes with students and keeps class entertaining! LOVE IT hope I can get another class with her later on!

Great professor!  Really knows her stuff and enjoys her field and has a sense of humor. Takes what could be a very dry subject and makes it interesting.  Text is hardly necessary, as she has detailed powerpoints that she posts online.

She is a a nice and fun teacher and really cares about her field, HTM. it's a pretty easy class, go to lecture, take notes, do the Iclicker questions. There are short little quizzes online which are pretty easy. The exams however aren't as easy you think, they're mostly from the notes but she always throws some tricky questions on there.

easy easy easy A! Laurie is very energetic and I found her quite entertaining. if you're an htm major, sit closer to the front. many people take the class as a joke and just talk through out the entire time. online 5 question quizzes after classes! prs used in class, easy point!

Easy A or B. All you have to do is attend class (she uses PRS), pay attention, and take the quizzes which are online. She posts the notes online. Everything on the exams are pretty much straight from the notes she gives.

Professor Salame is very knowledgeable in the field. She engages the class with questions as well as PRS. She uses trick questions on her quizzes and exams, so be careful with that. I always went to the T/A for help as I didn't feel comfortable approaching her. I honestly am reluctant to recommend her.
She's really nice. The material is interesting. She can get annoying sometimes cause she likes to hear herself talk... The exams appear easy but they're actually harder than you think.

She is very instightfull and has lots of experience in this field. I went to every class because it was fun learning. However don't think her tests will be easy. I got C's on both of them even though I reviewed all of my notes. I would recommend her.

As a teacher, she's okay. As a person, she is SO annoying. I hate the fact that she uses PRS because you have to go to class. I'm an HTM major, love the field, but sometimes she makes me want to switch out. She treats her kids like HS students, "no cell phones, no laptops..". Exams can get tricky which is annoying, but all the notes are online.

Don't talk in her class (or break any of her other many ridiculous rules) unless you're prepared to be humiliated in the middle of a large lecture hall. Her exams can be pretty tricky. It can also be very hard to pay attention in class, with everyone talking. Not really worth going though, because notes are online and PRS is only worth 5 or 6%
Don't take this class for an easy A because it's not worth it. she makes the exams tricky to make up for the fact no one pays attention in class and just talks over her.
Class is easy, all notes are accessible on SPARK.  She uses PRS but it only counts for 5% of your grade.  If you go to class you'll be guaranteed an A.
Enjoyable law class. Exams are somewhat tough, study the notes and some questions from the textbook. Go to class,questions on exam from lectures.
She's funny when she teaches and its a really easy class
Overall easy class but she is very annoying and rude.

Possibly one of the easiest classes if you actually try. I basically did nothing the entire semester and ended up with a B-. It would be an easy A if you actually went to class and studied from the book.

Go to class because you'll never know when she will give EC questions for the exams! No hws, easy quizzes and semi easy tests. READ and memorize the book and mostly notes if you want to do real good on her exams!

Really easy class, Laurie is really into what she is teaching and she can be rude at times but overall she's alright. Don't bring your cellphone to class she'll call you on it... incredibly annoying! Also just go to class when its rainy or sunny extra points for when there are under 100 people there!
If you go to class you can probably get an A easily enough, but the class can be incredibly boring, rumor has it she will be requiring prs next semester, so be ready to have to go to class.
this woman is a good teacher, however she is the biggest **** i have ever met in my life. she is extremely rude when correcting homework. her comments are so bad. she is mean, strong, and ****y 24/7.

She makes you earn your grade, but she cares about teaching you.  She may come off strong, but she means well.  She tries to gain respect by being strict, but if you know her outside of class, she's a real sweetheart.

Professor Salame is one of the best professors I have had here are UMass. I've had her for 2 classes and have done very well in both. She clearly presents information in well formatted and easy to understand power points, she is always available to help, and if you attend class, it's really easy to do well.
Laurie is a great professor. She is very experienced in the industry and uses those experiences as examples for explaining her powerpoints in a very clear and concise manner. Great professor!
Easy A. go to class, read the text chpt before the online quiz. thats it. no homework, do it if its your major (empty credits otherwise)

this was the only class I didn't get an A in last semester because this lady tests you on useless information such as "what is her favorite city?" and things you would need to know by attending class, which is difficult because it is hard to stand that woman talking about herself for an hour. unfortunately it is required for htm majors.
Easy 1st and 3rd exam. Hard 2nd exam. Does not all any sort of makeup.
If you're considering majoring in HTM, you should transfer out of UMass because your experience with this lady will ruin your future. I really mean it.
No Comments
class is not that bad, since it's a 100 level.  salame has problems though, thinks she's all that because she's a professor... likes embarassing you every chance she gets.

didnt go to the class once and got a b. I suggest to actually buy the book if you want an a, probably could have gotten at least an a- if I had that. just study powerpoints and online quizzes for exams.

If you pay attention in class, especially to her examples, and study for the test, you will do fine.  Just make sure you are actually paying attention-- she takes attendance and will randomly call on people.  You had better know what the question is if she asks you...

Very experienced in the Hospitality industry. While she does read right off the PowerPoints she has an interesting story to go with almost everything, good sense of humor... You need the book and to attend class if you want an A, otherwise you can easily get a B.

i took this as an elective.  she is boring, not funny at all, the only thing that was good about this class was the trip to Foxwoods, also she doesnt round up even 89.5 to a 90... very strict on grades. you'll definitely fall asleep because she just reads the powerpoint the whole class.

Laurie is full of herself. You don't really need to go to class, but prepare for tests with book. Material is pretty basic but gets boring after a while. The TA was helpful. Test questions sometimes include things only people that go to class would know.

I took this as one of my electives. I like her as a teacher but the material got boring. I hate how she refuses to round up grades. Doing the last exams bored me to tears. I'm so glad to be done with the class. She did take the class to foxwoods casino and did give us 3% extra credit. casino hold, drop, and win just gets unbearable after a while.
Interesting Class. Made me consider becoming an HTM major. Great teacher and is never boring.

Okay buy the book and skim it some of the stuff is on it and GO TO CLASS even tho all the lecutures are online she randomly gives u test ? for those who were only in class would know. its worth it unless you dont mind already being down 6 points. 3tests 80% of grade, 13 online quizzes (20%), 5 points extra credit. you can get an A with a lil effort

This was a great class. Very easy as well. I ended up with a B+ instead of an A though because I started bringing my laptop and bombed the 2nd exam. I ended up with an 88 and she wouldn't round it up but I don't necessarily blame her.

She is full of herself & likes to show off.Every class she gives examples of when she went to some place to show that she's been places.  She even puts dumb questions about herself on the exams.If you think that she will round your final grade up like any other teacher would then you're wrong.Even if you have an 89.99 she will still give you a B+.

I was expecting this class to be an easy A but it wasn't. I read on here that you only needed to study the powerpoints. Thats incorrect. If you want to get an A in this class you need to read the chapters and attending class helps. The online quizzes are really easy and help. The second exam was ridiculous and I got a 60 on it.So that hurt my grade

I hate this woman. She's the biggest snob and just tells stories the entire class about how she had bad service at a restaurant or hotel and how she embarrassed the person. First and third test is easy but 2nd one is all book. she's a **** with grading. I had an 89.96 and she refused to round it to an A. have fun.
easy teacher, nuts about cheating, so if you plan to cheat..not going to happen.. otherwise very good class
Salame is a great professor, and always makes things interesting... though if you get her talking about liquor or poor service, she'll never stop.

Easy A.  Went to class 4 times throughout the entire semester and still ended up with a 97 average.  No Final which is also awesome.  Class is entertaining, but you can more or less use WebCT to pass the class.
DON'T BUY THIS BOOK. NO REASON
She's goes on super funny rants, and she's lots of fun overall. Super easy, interesting class :-)

pretty easy class. the notes are all online and the quizzes and tests are pretty much based off of the notes. the class itself isnt that bad because she's a pretty entertaining lecturer and is very funny sometimes. also, she usually finishes pretty early so you almost always get out of class really early
She's one of the greatest hospitality teachers at Umass!

Laurie rants about the strangest things but shes funny about them. Shes wicked down to earth so u can easily follow what she talks about. This class is one of those courses u just fly through b/c u can seriously miss like 15 classes and still pass with a B since all her test/quiz questions are straight from the powerpoints.

This class was a real breeze, the powerpoints contain all of the important material for tests.  She sometimes tries to trip you up on tests with "tricky" questions; however, its nothing too hard to figure out
No Comments
She knows her stuff and teaches it well.

I thought this was a great class. She makes everything very clear and interesting. Its all powerpoint based but she breaks off from it a lot to involve the class. The online quizzes really help your grade, and the exams are easy for the most part. Usually the questions come from what was talked about in class and on the onlines quizzes.
Great teacher, great class... very dateable by the way guys! Snag her up!

Awesome class. She explains everything very well and gives great examples to make information more tangible.  By far my favorite class.  You have to go to and pay attention, but if you do you will probably really enjoy it and do very well.  Great class with really helpful information for life after graduation.

Great prof.  very very helpful to students... even while taking tests she'll come over to help/give you hints!  explains everything, and actually cares about you doing well!  much better than most other prof's
Salame makes class interesting. This was one of the few classes I actually wanted to go to this semester. Grading is fair, as long as you study and read the book. And, she's pretty hot, too.

Probably my favorite professor this semester. She has a sense of humor and makes everything interesting, even though law isnt that fun.  I didnt have her for 100, but if you didnt do well in the class, its probably your own fault.

I really liked this class, the lectures were really interesting, and this class is just overall an easy one. no attendance, the quizzes online are pretty simple, and the tests are all found from the notes and the readings. if you do the work, its an easy A
No Comments
Terrible class. Everythings online but her tests are tricky and she puts stupid random facts on the tests. Not a helpful teacher at all, and could care less about students.

supposedly an easy class but i think its gotten harder... she doesnt care about what you think at all. if someone leaves class early she'll yell things at you. dont need to go to class at all, everythings online. and make sure you dont sit in the last two rows, she'll have a fit!

This class is extremely easy! However, she puts a lot of material from the book on the exams... so make sure you buy it or have access to one! Prof. Salame is pretty rude, dont ask her questions because she will snap back some sarcastic rude answer! but at least the class is easy!
Easy, clear, actual work and assignments, but no tricks
Gives you all powerpoint presentations.  Hard grader and mandatory attendance policy.
easiest class ever! got an A. Not mandatory to go to class-it's all online. Straight-forward, common-sense knowledge. Take the class for an easy A. She's very nice and tells interesting stories.
Class was easy. All the slides are online so no need to go to class. Quizzes are online and are taken right from the slides. Class was not too boring though so showing up wasn't too bad.

Very easy class. Went to class maybe once every 2 weeks and got an AB. All of her notes are online, and the assignments are are submitted through WebCT, so are online quizzes. Very down to earth and it is evident that she enjoys what she is teaching.

she is very into her job, i love her class, a little boring at times but the work is easy and exams are pretty easy as well... i got a AB but i shoulda got A... messed up on an exam, because it was the first college exam ever!!
Easy A if you go to class..lecture notes online..quizes and exams are easy if u take the notes.
she sucks.  She doesnt help at all, especially for the ethics class.  Her grading is tough.  She doesnt try to understand students.  NO SYMPATHY AT ALL!!!! And worst of all, her class is boring
No Comments
Damn easy class, but boring and pointless. Helps out the GPA, but on the downside attendance is graded.
So easy. There are some assignments but all really easy. Also there is optional homework. Extremely easy A. Teacher really down to earth, but plan on going to class since she takes attendance.
This is the biggest waste of time ever- but so are most 100 level classes!
No Comments
No Comments

seems really nice, until you ask her for any kind of understanding, forget it unless you have extensive documentation. interesting lecturer but as for administrating grades, you better be on top of everything.

Definitely my favorite class i've taken at UMass. Lectures are the only source of material, but they are recorded. There is a lot of information to know for tests but he makes it so clear in lecture and on the study guide what will be on them.
reviews.rating_tags: Amazing lectures --Lecture heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: lectures are great and the exams are easy if you go to class

He's ok. I don't think his lectures are very helpful but you want to pay attention cuz he uses his own terms a lot in his exams (all MCQs btw). No textbook but there's packback every week. Gives back credits when many people got the same question wrong. Definitely recommend using his slides, study guides, and zoom session to prep for exams.

Honestly he is such a funny guy and makes it so easy to do well. You just do the Packbacks each weekend and he gives you a very clear study guide for exams. I recommend going to the exam reviews as he goes over almost every thing you need to know. Love Mitch!

Awesome professor and fun guy! His lectures were engaging, down to earth, and didn't throw too much information at you at once. Only work outside of class was weekly Packback and pre-exam quizzes that included word-for-word exam questions. Quizlets for exams are abundant. Very easy A if you listen during lectures!

He is the best. If you are someone that does not come to lectures, you will not do well on the exams. Everything he says in class is on the exam, and it is very easy to study and earn a good grade. He is also just a very understanding guy if you reach out to him about something.

Mitch is chill but he is a bad professor. The majority of what he says is not related to the material itself but related to the news and real-world examples of microbio- he does not teach. The exam answers are on Quizlet, making it easy but if answers weren't on quizlet the exams would be very difficult with questions on random things he says.

310 with Mitch Walkowicz is by far the worst class I've taken. This class is unnecessarily difficult. Completely true what others said about the exams being 2% of what the slides say, which is all there is to study. He actually gave half the class the wrong exam. There's a reason there's an influx of 1's coming in this semester.

HORRIBLE teaching style. lectures were ramblings, and he jumped from one point to the other with little connection. slides are just random pictures, so all you have are his ramblings to rely on. exams feel like they were generated by AI with how many strange questions there were. a thing he talked about for just 0.02 seconds would be in them.

Though I'm not a bio major, this was a bit difficult for a gen-ed. Mitch has a very particular teaching style. I tricked myself into finding biology interesting and then studied HARD for exams. Overall, he's nice, though. He drops the lowest quiz and exam grade, so easy to skip the final if you do well.

Mitch is an awesome person. I will say it took a couple classes to adjust to his lecturing style, but once I did I learned a ton. He was always super caring and available outside of class. If you put in the work, you will do well. This class reminded me how much I like bio and I would definitely take another elective with him.

I had to take a makeup exam and he made me take it on a bench under the stairs, right outside of N151. So beyond unorganized and goes on random tangents throughout class. He is nice but there was always a problem with his exams. He either didn't print enough or gives you the wrong one. Couldn't recommend any less.
reviews.rating_tags: Lecture heavy--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: This is the first time I have ever truly hated a professor's teaching style. I do not think I learned a single thing in this class. Mitch is very nice, but cannot teach material. He often goes off on tangents, most of his slides are just pictures, and he asks exam questions that are never covered in class. First time struggling to get an A.

Mitch is probably the worst professor I've ever had (in 7 semesters). He cannot teach but instead chooses to randomly speak in a way that comes across as riddles. Incomplete sentences, improper grammar, ramblings, it's not conducive to a students' learning. Exams make up 50% of grade but you may not even recieve A. an exam or B. the correct exam.

A good professor that teaches a difficult course. As long as you come to lecture and pay attention, you should receive a good grade. Gives quizzes/study guide in preparation for exams which are helpful.
Never went to class, easy to catch up. good guy, knows what hes talking about. im not a bio major, but just watch his recordings and you'll ace the class.

Everyone says its a hard class, thats not true. there are 5 exams, but one can be dropped. he makes it really easy to get an A as long as you watch his lectures. Just pay attention in class and take notes for an easy A. Really good professor, stimulates interest in the subject.

Feels like every week you are studying for a new test, as there are 5 throughout the semester. The slides are very disorganized and the material you are tested on is so random. He will mention something minuscule once and it will be an exam question, its ridiculous. He is a great person, however; the class is not run well.

One of those professors who is very unorganized. There are five exams including the final and the questions seem unrelated to what we talked about in class. He will randomly blurt out information that he puts on the exams but will never mention it again. If majority of the class gets a question wrong he does give points back. I wouldn't retake.
reviews.rating_tags: Lecture heavy--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Most reviews are too harsh. Just attend lectures and study the material before test.
reviews.rating_tags: Lecture heavy--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Great professor, it's not an easy class, you will have to study, but it's really not that bad. I'm awful at bio/science and consistently got 90s. Lectures are recorded so you don't have to show up, but you should so you can understand better. Mitch is very helpful, answers questions outside of class time and wants to help you learn.

Your best bet is to attend lectures so you understand the criteria. You have weekly packbacks but that's not difficult. 5 exams and drop the lowest score. You take quizzes online which is good padding for your grade. The test questions are sometimes not on the study guide so you have to attend lectures
Too many exams and way too disorganized
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--EXTRA CREDIT--Test heavy

reviews.comment: The lectures were all over the place. He would jump from one topic to another without really explaining how anything connects. Even when students asked questions, the answers didn't help much because he just repeated the same thing.  Also the exams are extremely hard, at least for me who is a non bio major

Prof Walkowicz was nice, but his lectures tended to be confusing. Attendance optional so I kinda lacked. 5 exams, 1 drop for your lowest grade. Packbacks weekly. Overall, easy course load, but just study well for the tests and don't leave till last min. He's easy to reach out to with questions and understanding. Better/easier Gen Eds though.

Lectures were optional but I usually tried to make it to everyone. Very interesting course and he teaches it very well. Exams were somewhat difficult, but it all came from the lecture, and he told us some of the questions that might be on it. Overall good course and if you have interest in cancer or aids, I would totally recommend taking this.

Just to start off, the mean for all FIVE exams, even though multiple choice, was in the 60s. The class was interesting, I did learn a lot, and Mitch is a nice guy, but don't take this to fulfill your bio requirement unless you love bio. Exams in person, weekly packback.

His negative energy is, imo, main reason for poor attendance/participation. Exams were HARD (i went to all classes & sat in front) He'll say not to study certain things but they end up on the exam, dont fall for it. Much of his statistics r from 20 yrs ago. Throw out your knowledge on current health stats, he tests u on how he teaches. Tyrant prof.
Very funny, speaks a little too quickly but uploads lectures to echo. Review sessions the weekend before exams were the most helpful, very passionate about the subject.
If you don't have background in biology, avoid this class or you will suffer. Prob the hardest class in my 4 years of college.

He says comments in lectures and makes them seem insignificant when they end up being exam questions. There's too many topics you have to remember for each test and I get that having background knowledge in cancer and whatever is useful but not really if your career has nothing to do with life sciences. Worst gen ed I was forced to take. Crazy.

This course is extremely straightforward. Five Exams, one of which is dropped. All exams are multiple choice and typically have generous curves (4-6 points!). Showing up is 80% of studying. Accessible Natural Science Gened requirement. Everyone should take this class to learn more about cancer and what it takes to treat it.

Lectures are super random & disorganized. He's interesting, and you can learn a lot, but it gets boring and has very odd slides (random dates & newspaper headlines). 5 Exams (drop 1), I never studied for them until the night before using his Exam Review, and I managed 85-92 for all of them. Not that great as a Gen Ed (an easy A if you work smart!).
reviews.rating_tags: Clear grading criteria--Test heavy--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: There's an online forum you buy (Packback, $40 total) to make a weekly question and respond to 2 others (super easy). 4 online quizzes and 5 exams but lowest grade was dropped for both. Rarely studied and got 75s on exams, but saved my paper exams and made a quizlet at the end of the sem and memorized it for the final (got a 96). Take this class!

Overall, I think he's a great prof. As long as you pay attention during lectures, you should be fine. He's a very fair grader, and gives points back if everyone missed the same questions on the exams.
Sometimes it's a bit hard to follow along with his way of teaching, but he gives out good study guides and does review sessions before every test.

The information he “teaches” is just random facts that you won't comprehend if you don't have outside biology knowledge. You won't have any idea how the things he says relates to each other. No words on the slides either so you really have no idea what you're supposed to study. Exams are so difficult too. DONT TAKE AS A GEN ED BELIEVE ME.

Mitch, you either love him or you hate him honestly. If you are the kind of person who is not a good exam taker (like me) this class is difficult. Exams are 50% of your grade and the homework doesn't really apply what we are learning in class. Speaks in a monotone voice and powerpoints seem scattered. This class would definitely benefit from an si.
reviews.rating_tags: Test heavy--Graded by few things--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: All 5 exams are all multiple choice but often feature random questions unrelated to the lecture slides, focusing instead on what he says in class. However, his lectures are disorganized and full of tangents, analogies, and unfinished thoughts, making it difficult to pinpoint key material.

I'm not a STEM major, but I definitely learned a lot of interesting stuff with this class. Useful things too. His lectures were mostly interesting, and homework/tests were not too bad. As long as you keep up with the slides and key points in his lectures, you will be fine.

Professor Walkowicz was a very engaging professor and it was clear that he wanted students to succeed. As a non-science major this course was a bit difficult but he drops one quiz and test grade. This way, it is easier to succeed in this class. He is a great professor.

the class was pretty unorganized, but I enjoyed it. You pick a relevant topic of choice with a group and do a presentation about it using research papers. Wasn't a lot of pressure and I learned a decent amount about interpreting data in papers.

Prof. Walkowicz is a great guy and clearly wants his students to learn. His slides are almost completely useless though so I would recommend taking notes on what he says rather than what is on the slide. There are weekly PackBacks, which really help out grade-wise. Exams are all multiple choice and true or false, which should be easy enough.

I love MICRO160! I was not very interested in the beginning, but I've learned so much that is actually relatable. The exams are on all of the content gone over in class, but in order to do good on them, you have to pay attention to what he is saying, rather than what is on the slides. Very knowledgable prof with easy PB assignments.
Mitchell is my man!!!!! He always delivers (he's not pregnant). A great professor with engaging lectures

Mitch is an engaging but disorganized lecturer. His classes are story-based and require attendance. While the slides can be confusing, the material is interesting if you engage with it. unstuck ai and Packback helped me stay on top of the content.

I hate biology and this class confused me but I always did better on the tests than I expected. He gives you the topics to study and I usually just spent a couple hours the night before and never got below an 85. Final exam is only previous exam questions and I aced it. If you don't like biology, Mitch will not change your mind. Very long winded.
Prof. Walkowicz is fantastic, he is funny and informative. His exams are pretty straightforward and should be an easy A, he curves the exams or takes off bad questions often if they're too hard.

Exams in this class are very straightforward as long as you watch/attend the lectures. Some of the exam questions could be some random thing he mentions in class once. The lecture slides aren't too detailed so you  have to listen to him explain certain concepts in order to get the full picture of concepts.
reviews.rating_tags: Clear grading criteria--Lecture heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Pretty simple Bio Science Gen Ed, Mitch is funny and makes lectures more interesting (if you go to them). Packback assignments that're mostly every week are kind of annoying but easy part of your grade.

Kind but terrible prof. Does not explain info, he just gives examples of stories. It is SO hard to follow along.
The slides he posts are missing key information he quickly says out loud, and yet full of unnecessary info at the same time.
Final mostly based off of old exam Q's. 
I got a C on every single exam and got an A on the final - memorize.
Take microbio of cancer and aids, you will learn A LOT!!!

Mitch was the worst professor I have ever had. He is extremely condescending and always talks in riddles. All exam Qs are based on things he mentions during class (very few things are written on the slides that help you answer the Qs). The material was intriguing but I hated listening to Mitch talk. Packbacks are easy participation at least.

Mitch is the man. He lectures very story-like, so attend the lectures or at least watch the recordings(you won't do as well if you just read the slides). He's a genuine guy who cares about what he teaches, and Packback is clutch for participation.I had an interview for a job during an exam day and he offered to let me retake the exam on Sunday.

Worst prof I've ever had. Only teaches in analogies & useless slides. Exams based on what he says so its nearly impossible to study, & refused to reexplain stuff. Rude to student & to the poor TA, often called the class lazy & spoke in annoyed tone. 5 exams but only counted 4, final recycled questions. Quizzes & packback cushion a lot. Do not take

The lectures are really disorganized and hard to follow. The slides are a mess with random bullet points and pictures. It's hard to predict what he's going to ask on the exams. Unless you have a strong bio background this class will be hard. Wouldn't recommend taking him unless you absolutely have to.

Mitch is really funny and entertaining, but he is not a good lecturer. He tends to ramble on, skip around, and go over ugly and hard-to-read slides very half-heartedly. If you're truly looking to learn a solid base about microbiology, either look to another class or another professor because Mitch won't do it. Decently easy to get a good grade tho.

Teaching style and class dynamic can be really confusing at first because it's really lecture-heavy but not too bad once you adapt. He has a dry sense of humor and makes a lot of memorable jokes. He doesn't want to see anyone fail so he's not a harsh grader at all. Also not a lot of work outside class.

I love mitch. Dry sense of humor and kind of out of pocket. Passionate about what he teaches but slightly disorganized/tends to go down rabbit holes; study what he says not what is on slide for exams. 50% of grade is quizzes and packback, 50% exams... 5 exams total including the final, one is dropped. You will learn a lot!

Mitch uses a non-traditional style of teaching which can be confusing at first, but the material is interesting so as long as you go to lecture and pay attention you'll do fine. Write down notes based on what he is saying and look at the slides later. Very easy class if you do the work.

Amazing professor! I was nervous about taking general microbio in the future so I decided to start with micro160. I have never learned more in any other class. Mitch is amazing at what he does and the way he explained everything helped all the material come so naturally to me. I plan on trying to get him again for general microbio

Mitch is overall a confusing lecturer with out of order slides and saying random things. He excepts you to know a lot of information before lectures. His lectures were not mandatory, honestly easier to skip class and watch later on echo 360. Overall not horrible class if you study, especially quizlets.

Prof Walkowicz is a chill dude, but his lecture style is very subjective and he goes fast, giving vague analogies often. The test questions can be pretty tricky as well, so after the first one I stopped attending lecture and taught myself. If you're willing to do that, then it's an extremely interesting class, albeit extremely content heavy.

Mitch is a nice guy but all his lectures are all pictures. You have to pay attention to everything he says even the smallest details because that's what will be on the exams. The exams are HARD almost everyone fails them and he doesn't curve them!!!! There are 5 exams and he drops the lowest one but I definitely would NOT recommend taking this.
Not a bad lecturer, packback was ok but became a chore. Exams are curved.

Has a weird rapper-esque obsession with the "haters". PackBack is fun at first but you inevitably run out of things to ask. Warning: will talk about your Grandma when referring to cancer patients a lot. Has good insights to questions as long as you have the courage to speak up. Lectures are overwhelming at first but the quizzes and tests are fair.

The way he talks/teaches is comedic and interesting, but sometimes I lose track of what we are talking about. Not easily accessible outside of class. He has made a lot of confusing typos and incorrect due dates on canvas. PackBack assignments are annoying, but workload is overall doable. Tests are 50% of ur grade!!!

mitch is so goddamn funny i can't leave him a bad review. but the way he explains things sometimes makes no sense. he is clearly very smart, but he assumes the information he is giving us is easier to digest than it is. once you can get his long analogies and riddle-like way of speaking, the content is interesting. tests require a lot of studying.
Bio 160 is the easy gen ed you are looking for.
Literally my bestfriend.

his teaching is all over the place, i mainly study off the textbook bc his lectures are so confusing. 5 MC exams (1 dropped), no attendance, quizzes are easy and def study them bc he reuses quiz questions on the exams. so far this semester no extra credit or exam curves yet. wish there was a better 310 prof tho

Prof. Mitchell Walkowicz taught this class for the haters, and I am definitely not one. Despite speaking in riddles and appearing perpetually fed up, he communicated some complicated topics in accessible ways. He also referred to God as "she" casually and honestly? His outfits kind of serve.

He is extremely unhelpful and no one has any idea what to do or how to study throughout the entire class. I went to every lecture, did every assignment, and typically do well in all of my classes, but this class is so unorganized and there is no structure. No idea what we are learning, and no help when asked.

Mitchell can have a dry sense of humor but it's evident he's very knowledgeable and wants his students to remember course information even beyond the final. His slides are sometimes out of order but the exams are based more on his lectures than the slides anyways. He drops one final, one quiz, and offers extra credit via Packback.

Walkowics is an amazing professor, he is very passionate. The material he discusses during lectures is very important for exams, definitely watch the recordings of the lectures if you don't go. I missed 2 of 5 exams and still ended well. You only have one homework assignment per week and there is usually 2 moodle quizzes before exams (with 2 tries)

Walkowicz is very intelligent, lectures are very interesting. Take notes on what he says rather than what's on the slides, then go back after lecture and jot down notes from the slides. His slides bounce back and forth between topics (can be a little confusing). Review basic microbiology terms and processes before this class and you will do great.

I enjoyed this class. 5 exams that are all multiple choice and you can drop the lowest grade. Weekly packback. Online quizzes every few weeks. Lectures are recorded so there is really no need to go to class besides exams. I recommend taking notes based off what he says rather than what is on the slide. He scales all the exams by like 5 points

Professor W is a very funny person, but falls short as a lecturer. He typically talks "around" a concept and neglects to give solid definitions. This gives you a weak foundation to build off of. I found that his exams, while all multiple choice, were not the most representative of the lectures. Hard to predict what he wants us to remember most.

I  hated bio in high school, but I enjoyed going to Mitch's class. He's funny and approachable. He is also easily accessible outside of class via email. Your grade is heavily dependent upon Packback (super easy, but tedious) and exams (~45 MC questions). Awesome and chill guy who doesn't ask for much from us. Just show up and pay attention fr.

Mitchell provided tons of important information that I am sure will be useful in the future. The problem was that he taught tons of it super quickly and expected us to know it. I found myself rewatching all of his lectures in order to get the grade I wanted on the exams. He ended up giving us points back on most of them and giving weird excuses.

not sure why he has such a high rating when he is not good at teaching lol. hes rude asf and his lectures are all over the place. hes late to almost every lecture and will imply/call students lazy/stupid. avoid taking him

Exams make up most of your grade. His lectures are all over the place. If you have good background in biology, chemistry, and microbiology then this class will be suitable for you, otherwise don't take it. He kept scaling our exams due to average being low and his final exam is recycling all the questions from previous exams.
reviews.rating_tags: EXTRA CREDIT--Lecture heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: TAKE THIS CLASS! This was my favorite class this semester and I genuinely looked forward to every lecture; very funny and engaging. Mitch is a fantastic professor and you can tell that he cares a lot for his students and he is very helpful if you have any questions. Graded on weekly forums, Moodle quizzes, and exams w/ lowest grade dropped

Walkowicz clearly knows what he's lecturing about. Material can be confusing at times but review sessions before exams are great for clearing that up. There are 5 exams but one can be dropped, Moodle quizzes and weekly packback discussion questions/responses. If you do all the assignments and study for the exams, you'll be totally fine.

Do not take this class. His lectures are all over the place. He doesn't put any information on the slides and then asks particular questions on the exams. So, if you missed something specific in his ramble during the lecture, you have to go back and rewatch the video to find it. He can seem charismatic when talking to the group but is rude 1 on 1.

Very kind and understanding. Course material was also very interesting & helped us engage with scientific literature. But, the lecture slides were never taught in order, & his train of thought was very hard to follow. His voice was also very monotone, which did not help his class being in the morning. Graded on weekly discussions, quizzes, & exams.

Mitchell is a great professor, and the class is not that hard. He does a lot of rambling and sometimes you'll have no idea what he's talking about, but when you pay attention and listen to what he says you'll do well in the class.  Only one homework assignment weekly for packback discussions and then 4 main exams with an optional final.

If you are like me and dreading doing your science gen ed requirement, TAKE MICROBIO160!! It was really easy and Mitch curves all of his exams which is always nice. I would say that I am taking more real life knowledge away from this class rather than actual core microbiology. Go to lectures+take notes+do the simple HW=easy pass.

Professor is routinely late to class. Lectures are ALL over the place and are often just pictures. He does not directly teach the topic, he will dance around it and make analogies that you are then expected to extrapolate the concepts from. He asks for feedback, does not take it, and regularly implies that you are stupid/lazy.

Frequently late to class, confusing lectures, doesn't provide a clear outline of the semester. I could go on and on. His lectures are just him going from topic to topic, skipping slides, he's not open to feedback about altering format of lectures. TA is also unhelpful. If it is possible to avoid having Mitch I would recommend that you do!

Didn't love this class because I signed up thinking it was going to be fun and easy. Walkowicz is a great professor if you're actually interested in the topics he teachers, for he's incredibly educated. Didn't love the slides though, it was mostly just blurry pictures with little to no words. Tests were straightforward and weekly homework was easy

Should have taken Biology in High School (would be easier to understand the phrases and information taught in class), however, this course didn't require you to understand very deeply of what you have learned. The professor is really engaging, learned a lot through all the lectures. There are only four quizzes and an exam (easy homework)

Walkowicz is a professor who knows what he lectures about and cares about his student's success. He'll be there to help you if you ask, his lectures are interesting and engaging. Lectures must be attended in person, watching them through ECHO-360 doesn't do them justice. 4/5 exams were graded, and everything else depends on the Packback questions.
reviews.rating_tags: Amazing lectures --Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: He is super funny and the lectures are fun to listen to. The lectures might be hard to follow if you don't have a background in cell bio, biochemistry, or microbio. Weekly packback discussions, some quizzes, and exams are your whole grade. But he drops one exam so the class is manageable.

Everyone loves Mitch! Attend lectures IN PERSON that's how you will learn, so don't rely on PowerPoint slides. Always gives 5-10 points back on exams and really does care about your learning. He also takes feedback good or bad to improve the course. Don't stress the class, as long as you attend lectures and know the review guide you will do fine.

Professor Walkowicz is a decent professor with well-thought-out lectures; they can be highly dull. The source material may feel like it is not worth sitting around for, but the workload is smalloverall, pretty fair class.

Took this over the winter and it wasn't bad at all. There's 5 exams & quizzes, lowest one gets dropped. Easy pack back that can be on anything from the course. Allows multiple tries on quizzes. His teaching is hard to follow because it can be all over the place. Exams are pretty fair when you refer back to the lectures. Overall, easy A.

Walkowicz is fine, took as a Gen Ed and got an A-. Grade based on best scores out of the 4/5 tests and participation on an online platform (don't remember name of it, but costs around $30). Watched a majority of lectures online, studied a moderate amount, and got mid 70s on the tests, but he always gave points back, giving me an 80 test average.

This man is incredibly down to earth, funny, and wants everyone to learn and succeed. He truly does care about his job and has immense passion for microbiology and what he teaches. His anecdotes and explanations are second to none, as they are very comprehensive and easy to digest. Guy is incredibly friendly and will work with you if you have issue

I really loved going to Prof. W's classes.
