You could tell that he really knew his stuff, and even though biology and science really go over my head, he made it easy enough to understand (most of the time). TAs were amazing, and he grades only Packback (just discussions) and exams (which he usually gives 5-10 points back on each). Don't buy textbook
all the lectures are available on echo360, daily homework could be make up if late, test in person is a bit hard but not unbearable
reviews.rating_tags: Graded by few things--Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: Professor Walkowicz is very knowledgeable in his field and does his best to make students interested/engaged. This class was all lecture based, with exams (40%), quizzes (30%) and online forums (30%) making up the grading. He always gave points back on exams. If you read through all of the lecture slides before an exam you will be good

It took me some time to get used to him, but after I did I learned a lot and did well. He can talk fast and assume that everyone knows what he's talking about, but he's also smart and funny. I really liked that he encouraged critical thinking about everything and taught about the social aspects of the subject, especially with HIV. Great guy!

Professor Walkowicz is hands down one of my most respected professors at Umass . I had him my freshman year and I still think back to his lectures all the time. He explains things intellectually well. I learned a ton from his class and he made it interesting which helped considering how complex the material is.

Really nice person, cares about his students and it shows. Will do his best to help you. Decent prof. If you like taking notes off of slides instead of writing down what the prof says then you're going to struggle a little to get down all of the info. Wish his slides were more text-based (they are very picture/infographic based.)

Mainly your grade is going to be discussion posts (you only have to do it, and it can be about anything), quizzes (multiple tries), and then 5 exams (1 dropped). The class was an extremely easy A, especially with quizzes and exams open book, however, I did not learn anything. He's a great guy, but his teaching is very informal and hard to follow.

I personally didn't like his style of lecture. He's very informal, kind of unstructured (skips around powerpoint slides) and sometimes hard to follow. Grading is set up so a majority of your grade is from quizzes with multiple attempts and forum participation. Tests are pretty fair, and easy when you can refer to notes online. Don't need textbook

Microbio was so boring for me, but I found Mitch absolutely hilarious. Every day it felt like Mitch wanted to be there just as little as we did, and his "I don't care" attitude definitely made me feel better about also not caring. Free 30% for participation and easy 30% for quizzes with multiple attempts - this class is an easy A
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: his classes are soooo easy, exams are open book if you're online, super chill dude everyone loves mitch!!

I really like Mitch, I look forward to his lectures he's funny and obviously cares a ton about the material. He relates everything to real life and makes complicated subjects interesting. It's nice to have a professor who cares about what they're teaching. The material isn't easy but if you study a little and keep up with lectures you'll be fine

He gets a bad rep because he can come off as intimidating but he really does care about his students success. This class was graded off forum posts (easy 100), some moodle quizzes (easy to do well on) and exams that he always gives EC on. Material isnt super easy, but with the time and effort you will do well. I suggest taking him! He is very fair.

Attend and pay attention. You're good. Can skip b/c of online videos of lectures. No textbook. Frugal. Very generous on grading. On avg we received 9 points back on tests. Drops lowest grade out of all tests. Only note take from slides? You're in for a bad time. His slides aren't good for note-taking. Try not to autopilot in class but you can

He is one of the best professors I have had at UMass. He is well prepared for class and understands the material very well. He makes a complicated topic so interesting and even though attendance wasn't marked, he made me always WANT to be in class to hear his lectures. He does a fantastic job presenting information, and puts all the notes on Moodle

Easily one of the best professors I've ever had. He puts notes on the slides but goes into more detail in the lecture. If you miss something he said or miss class he has all of his lectures online. He is a caring and incredibly knowledgeable professor and makes his lectures interesting by connecting them to the real world. Amazing professor!

Literally, just go to class, listen to him lecture and go on tangents, if you're confused, ask a question! It's one of the easiest 300 level classes I've ever taken; would recommend reviewing slides and notes for the exam for a couple days. don't stress it; he doesn't stress it much either.
reviews.rating_tags: Accessible outside class--Graded by few things--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: Honestly...I enjoyed the class. Copy down the slides (all posted on Moodle), look it over before quizzes/tests, and you'll do just fine. Quiz/test questions are usually the notes verbatim. Interesting stuff.

Classes aren't mandatory but most of the test info is from what he rambles on about in lectures or in random slides in his power points and they're very hard to study for. He's very unorganized. I would never take a class with him again. I was told that microbio160 was an easy gened and read good reviews about him but he's truly an awful teacher.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Lectures were horrible. But the slides online don't help either. Exams are difficult and the information is rather random that is on them. Miserable class. Do not take as a GenEd. Not easy, much more difficult than any of my other classes.
Disorganized, out of his mind. 80% of the words he is saying doesn't match the words on the power point slide. Interesting course, but bad professor

Really bad professor. Disorganized, quiz/test questions don't match up with class material, very difficult to take notes because his lectures are all over the place and go off on tangents. Slides aren't thorough enough to study off of. While the class is interesting, Walkowicz is a very unfair/unorganized professor and it's not an easy gen ed.

DO NOT take this thinking its an "easy gen ed" unless you're already good in science. The material is very in depth. He is hard to follow in class because he just talks around topics and never gets to the point. It's very difficult to stay with him in class-- hes the type of professor that teaches as if the material is common sense for everyone.

He did not always cover the material very well and a lot of times questions would appear on the exams that were either never discussed or are trick questions. He also messed up answer keys and grading so much in my class that we would always get bonus points back, and sometimes his study guides did not match up with the true answer key.

Mitch wastes SO MUCH class time, he goes off on random tangents that you don't need to know about and skips through important information on slides to make time for this. If I could have taken the class with just Yasu, I would have in a heartbeat.

Overall this class is very easy to pass, I showed up only to a few lectures throughout the semester. Class is lecture heavy but if you pay attention to important details its nearly impossible to fail.
reviews.rating_tags: ACCESSIBLE OUTSIDE CLASS--Clear grading criteria--LECTURE HEAVY

reviews.comment: The class is graded on 3 exams, 4 new forum posts and 10 replies through out the semester, and quizzes on Moodle. Although his lectures are posted online, It's very helpful to go to every class and learn the material in person. Make sure to go over slides before the class! Walkowicz is a great professor!!
reviews.rating_tags: Clear grading criteria--TEST HEAVY--GRADED BY FEW THINGS

reviews.comment: This guy is literally the worst professor Ive ever had. He talks around concepts so its impossible to follow his logic. He uses these obscure analogies that only make sense in his own head. He expects students to follow his circuitous, rambling lectures. Even worse, hes unavailable when attempts are made to schedule office hours.

Went into the class hating it but by the end of the semester, I really enjoyed the class. 4 exams and 4 forum posts. forum posts are essentially easy A's. exams are hard. go to class, study for it and you'll be fine. he gives extra credit.

A great class to take as a gen-ed. I would say the science is pretty comprehensive and the material is interesting, especially if you're at all into health sciences. Mitch's lectures are funny, and although attendance is not mandatory, it will help! He explains the material very clearly and you will only have to do some light studying for exams.
reviews.rating_tags: Clear grading criteria--GRADED BY FEW THINGS--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: Mitch knows what he is talking about but doesn't put much effort into his job because he does not think he is compensated enough. His exams are obscure yet still specific and unlike what he tells us to prepare for, usually twisting his words and making the exam more difficult. There are only three papers, three quizzes and three exams in the class.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough Grader--GRADED BY FEW THINGS--LECTURE HEAVY

reviews.comment: I hate science and decided to take this as a gen ed thinking it would be the easiest one. A lot of people don't go to lectures, he puts all powerpoints online, but i've found its v helpful to go to class. the papers/online quizzes are really easy. tests are not easy, but if you actually study throughly you can do well. he's pretty funny & easy goin

Lectures can drag because he's a bit monotone, but the material is interesting. If you get an 85 or up on the first test, you can stop going to class. He puts the slides online, anyway, and as long as you take detailed notes on them and study, you'll get a B+ or up. However, go to the review sessions he holds before a test. They're really helpful.

He makes the class interesting and is very reasonable with students. Exams are straightforward but difficult because the material is challenging. He doesn't assign homework but you have to read the textbook to do well. Doesn't remind you about due dates for syllabus assignments. Overall good guy and good professor. Cares about his students.

The class was very interesting and he is a pretty good teacher.  It's not too bad of a class to take for a GenEd but the tests are actually kind of hard.  I would study as much as I really thought I could and got 80s on all of the tests.

Overall, this class is an easy B+ and up. The material that we covered was interesting. Mitch covers material sort of fast in his lectures and is a little mono toned. If you miss anything you can just read over the info in the powerpoints. The powerpoints do contain a lot of seemingly useless info in the form of graphs. Would recommend 4 a gen-ed.
Walkowicz's lectures were interesting if you pay attention because he goes fast.  There's 4 exams, but he drops the lowest one. I didn't buy the textbook and thankfully never needed it.

Mitch is a great person and extremely knowledgable, however this integrative experience was extremely tedious. There are a lot of group projects and a lot of independent research of the topic you're discussing. Overall not a bad class, he is extremely lenient with deadlines which is a plus sometimes and he often goes on tangents which last awhile.

His powerpoints are terrible, they literally just consist of dumb graphs and pictures that never show up on the exams. He rarely ever teaches you useful information needed for the exam which absolutely screws you over for the exam.

This class was extremely interesting, and as long as you go to lecture the class isn't very difficult. The tests don't try to trick you although, you need to study. There is a textbook but I never read it. He has review session and is overall a really understanding man.
Honestly, Mitch is pretty chill guy and so long as you show up and barely pay attention, you'll pass. It's a very easy class. The reviews he posts on Moodle are nearly identical to the exam he gives.

Mitch is a really nice guy and knows his material well, but he is incredibly hard to reach. You have to email him 3 times before he will respond to you. If you have questions about graded material good luck getting answers. He is awful with Moodle and nothing is out of the correct point amount and there are lots of broken questions on the quizzes.
Ignores students Changes assignment dates regularly
He is super nice, and if you ask him to clarify something, he will do just that. Make sure to attend the exam review sessions held at night!

His class was FILLED with information, you had to pay attention in that class. The tests totally weren't hard, but you had to remember the easy-to-remember examples from class. He had a great voice to listen to, but he definitely went a little fast, and he doesn't put the words on the slideshow just the pictures so you do need to pay attention.

Mitch is not a very good lecturer but his class was decent for me. He tends to ramble on and get off topic and I was often unclear on whether what he was talking about would be on the exams. Some biology background would be very helpful for this class. Exams are 50 multiple choice, not very hard if you went to class and studied even just a little.

Does a good job at making the class amusing, however his lectures get confusing because he will start and stop a sentence multiple times. Lectures are difficult to take notes and online lectures don't have much information to go off on. Exams require a good amount of studying or you will fail. Only four writing assignments which are very easy.

Mitch doesn't require attendance and he posts all lecture slides online, so lots of people are tempted to perpetually skip. Then they complain the course was too hard.  Mitch is generally pretty great and he tries his best to make the material relatable. Just show up, give it a LITTLE effort, and you'll have a great semester.

Great guy. Jokes are on point during lectures. Class attendance does not matter. If you do the Writing Assignments on time and follow directions you'll get 100 on all of them. Really interesting stuff, tests are tough but if you study enough you'll do well. Cannot emphasize enough how cool Mitch is, really makes the class. Highly recommended.

Mitch is a great professor for general micro! He ties in real life anecdotes in order to help teach the potentially stressful material. The quizzes help prepare you very well for the exams, which are fair.
Best lecturer I've ever had.  Guy is super nice.

hes never prepared. hes a funny guy but the fact that your entire grade is based off three exams is not good at all. i do not recommend this class or the instructor, try to take a different class for this gen ed

Do not take this class as a gened because Mitchell does not know how to teach this material to people who don't know biology. Also, don't buy the books you'll never need them. And the exams are 75% of your grade. They're so much harder than they need to be so even if you study, you bomb them. This was too hard for a gened.

Extremely hard class! It doesn't matter how hard you study for his exams because they only test your analyzing skills. The questions are worded specifically to trip you up. The course material is interesting, but you won't get a good grade. CHOSE A DIFFERENT PROFESSOR.

I hated Mitch for the first few weeks of class, but once you learn his teaching style he isn't too bad. Just don't expect to be spoon-fed the material; he isn't very good at explaining things in a way that non-bio majors would understand, so expect to put in a little extra effort in order to do well on the exams.

Mitchell Walkowicz is by far the WORST lecturer I've ever had. It's impossible to follow him; his lecture slides have zero explanation, he jumps around from topic to topic, and his voice is inhumanely annoying. His exams are also unnecessarily confusing. And don't bother buying the books, he doesn't use them. This man is ridiculous. Awful teacher.

I didn't receive the best grade but I found this class to be very interesting and I'm glad I took it. I find it to be more on the difficult side, especially for a Gen Ed. I couldn't keep up with him, especially when he got into all the details. My advice is to make sure you do all the written assignments. Forget one and it'll ruin your grade!

I loved this class & Mitch. Great guy, down to earth, straight to the point. He'll intimidate you on the first day of class but he grows on you. Very passionate about the subject & sharing it in an understandable way. I left this class having learned A LOT. Exams aren't too bad either, and the optional final was a breeze - definitely take it.
Mitch is a down to earth guy who teaches very well. He is interested in the subject and cares about his students. Fairly easy Gen Ed and I recommend it. You will need to study a little to do well.
He is a super nice guy. Homework is extremely easy and light (roughly 3 a semester). The lectures are very fast paced. The exams are pretty straight forward. Attendence is optional.

Mitch is awesome. The tests are really easy as long as you study his previous tests. I went to class but I never really paid attention. He was good at what he taught I just wasn't really interested in the material. Overall it was a good Gen Ed
Nice guy, easy enough class, although exams can be a bit tricky. Not many people went to class; I'm guessing that has something to do with some of the complaints.

DO NOT TAKE THIS CLASS IF YOU ARE NOT A SCIENCE MAJOR. He is a really nice guy and always willing to work with you. However for non science majors this class is really difficult. I had hall A's prior to taking his class and ended up in the C+? B- range in this class which wrecked my GPA.

Always willing to help and answer questions. Really generous with extra credit points at the end. However, course material is tough, and exams cover small details. Sometimes wording on exam is confusing. Must go over lecture slides with the book for clarification. Do not cram for exams last minute.
questions on the tests that are only discussed in class. There are 2 projects that can up grade.

Great person but not so great professor. Goes over lectures VERY fast; gave up taking notes in class & would take them from the slides at home after. Recommend reading book to review the info covered in lectures bc there is so much. Tests were tough, but mainly only bc there's so much info.  Attendance not mandatory but there's always a few

Decent professor nice guy, attending lecture is optional and is probably not necessary overall. Just make sure to read the book. The exams are just one big vocab quiz (so make sure to use the book website) as long as you know the terms you'll have an A.

Awful professor. So disorganized and all over the place. He would rush review sessions and not show up to meetings or office hours. He is a nice guy and means well but he doesn't know how to post quizzes or grades on moodle and is unclear when explaining things. The class wasn't too hard and as long as you study you will be fine.

Mitchell is awesome. He knows his material and he teaches it very well. I feel like I learned a lot from his class, and I got a few laughs out of the occasional jokes that he made. Take this class. It's easy and you learn a lot of relevant information to two major problems facing today's society

No way that everything could be covered in microbio310. Walkowicz knows this and tries to make it as broad as possible so that in the end, students will walk out learning something. He needs help in organization, but is overall a great professor and is willing to help students succeed.

Great professor. He teaches a really heavy topic but keeps it very interesting and holds attention well, but moves very fast. He is very in touch with the students that he teaches. The class is a little difficult but there are only 3 tests with an optional final. The man is full of information and is really informative in class.

Just an overall wonderful person, approachable, humorous, interesting. He is very tolerant of kids who don't have any prior experience and he teaches the class to people who may not be interested in pursuing microbiology but are interested in having a firm, fundamental of its concepts. This class is a great way to make yourself more well rounded.
Not worth buying the book. He expects you to catch on. The class is very informative but is too much for a gen ed.

SO HOT! I LOVE HIM but he teaches way to fast and expects you to understand very quickly. Very interesting class and informative but not clear enough and slides are difficult to understand.. not considered an easy gen ed.
Love him as a person, but his teaching is a too fast for me.

Professor was extremely hard to follow and all over the place during lecture. Slides are confusing and no help! I attended every lecture, even though he was no help at all, and needed to read all the chapters prior to an exam. He covers material in a great amount of depth and then asks basic (but horribly worded) questions on the exams!

I took this class because people told me it was one of the easier gen ed requirements. Not totally the case, but not a bad class. Definitely have to study for the tests and it does help to go to class because he helps explain lecture slides in everyday terms.  I really like the class but wouldn't reccomend it for an easy A. Have to put in work.
One of the worst classes I've taken. He babbles and gets too off topic. Needs to explain his slides better
"Mitch is the epitome of the word BAUSS." Love his humor. He's Polish too, which explains it.

Probably one of the worst professors I've had.  Disorganized, terrible slides, and by his exams DO NOT correlate at all to the depth covered in lecture.  Took this class to gain insight in the field and complete my gen-ed requirement.  Ended up studying for this class more than my upper level chemistry courses.  TAKE WITH A DIFFERENT PROF.

I have no idea why people are saying this is an easy class.  I just checked the class distribution.  4 - 6 people out of the ~180 people in the class got an A (94 or above).  The median for the class was a C, which is the grade more than half the class received).  Save yourself the trouble, stay away.  Take an easier gen-ed that has a better scale.
Probably the most boring class I've ever taken in my entire life and I like science. Not a bad BS gen ed though the class is pretty easy.

The real problem with the class is if you don't go at best you can hope for is 85 (because he puts question on that aren't really covered in the lecture slides). On the other hand while you're in the class it's so boring that you can feel yourself decomposing.

Somewhat interesting class. Professor is prepared for class and seems to know material fairly well. That being said they tests are WAY too hard for a gen-ed class. An incredible amount of information is thrown at you every class and you are expected to know literally every single piece of it for the test. The homework is too personal and tedious.

microbe 160 was a terrible decision. DON'T TAKE IT! they changed the class and it is not easy like everyone was saying. the tests are ridiculous, he puts questions on there that should not be asked in a gen ed class. also the homework's he assigns are not useful and are tedious

Awesome teacher! Very helpful and got his point across clearly. Exams reflected the notes. Didn't need the book because he explained everything well enough in c lass. HIGHLY RECOMMEND THIS CLASS! Microbio 160 (Bio of cancer and aids)
DON'T BOTHER BUYING THE BOOKS! i never used them.  its a really interesting class but he just read off the slides and asked really hard test questions irrelevent to the information we learned.

VERY interesting class. I learned so much! I would definetly recomend it to everyone!There's not really a need to buy the book, b/c the slides have all the info you will need for the exams, which aren't too bad, but you need to study for them. Hope the review helps...

The tests are pretty easy, but you have to go to every class, otherwise you'll miss subtle points that he'll ask on tests. The slides he posts online are helpful, but only if you're going to class too. Don't bother buying the books, you should just find information online if you don't get something.

DO NOT BUY BOOKS. never opened them. going to class is POINTLESS. i went to every class it didn't help. he read straight off the slides.  HWs are easy. tests are tricky. basically you have to memorize every lecture cause you won't know whats gonna be asked. lectures online.
Mitch is the epitome of the word BAUSS.
The class is interesting, and Mitch is a good teacher, but it's a little hard for me to pay attention because it's at 9am and I am not a morning person.

Very hard to pay attention to/get anything out of the class at 9am.  Interesting topics, but must easier to learn if you just go over the powerpoints (he posts all the lectures online) by yourself. Don't waste your money on the book, you won't need it.  Fairly easy class
Cool class, it gets very boring at times especially at 9 A.M. Easy class though, and hes a good teacher, just a little dull.
I really like this class, interesting topics! He's a very good prof, always available to answer questions, fun class!
I love him!!

Such a nice guy. The class is very easy, I see it as a you get out of it what you put into it kind of class. You can tell he genuinely cares about students as individuals, and discussions get the whole class involved.

Nate is a fun professor and his class was always engaging! I enjoyed the readings and discussions. He's very easy-going and understanding. As long as you communicate with him, you will succeed in his class.

Nate is awesome! So nice and funny. I would say it's a very easy class, and anyone can pass. Comes late a lot, unfortunately :( i'm not a huge fan of arts classes because i'm a science major, however, the work was still enjoyable and i would recommend this class to anyone who needs a gen ed. going to miss being in his class!!

Cancelled class once a week. Very easy if you have to take this for a gen ed or major. You have to read/watch plays outside of class and while they can be lengthy they are really interesting and I enjoyed reading/watching them. As long as you participate a bit you will pass, there are weekly journals to submit.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: He's chill and you can lowkey get away with doing minimal work.

Very interesting + passionate. Take notes more on what she is saying in lec rather than the slides. What she explains is what she wants you to understand. She will be direct if she thinks you are wrong, so follow her guidelines/feedback. Google will not help you, only lec and textbook. Read + take notes for txtbook, seriously. Very kind TAs.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Gives good feedback

reviews.comment: The reading has built in questions making it take longer than it should. The lectures are pretty boring and the discussions are led by TAs, who do not engage well. Your entire grade relies on 3 worksheets that are graded pretty harshly. The exams are easy enough but do not take if looking for an easy A gen-ed.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Lectures are very interesting, discussions (led by TAs) are less so. Reading heavy, but there are few actual assignments. Don't take if you're looking for an easy A gen ed, but the course material is interesting and she knows what she's talking about. The midterm and final are easy, she basically gives you the questions ahead of time.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Amazing lectures --Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Topics are interesting and class is always the same format. It's more work than you'd like for a gen Ed, but it's not too bad. She talks about the textbook a lot, but I don't think it's necessary to read.

She's an awful grader with really bad TAs. Most take for a gened but they act like we should all be histo. The main portion of the grade are 3 worksheets that are graded so unfair. Awful feedback is given on assignments as well.
Professor Nash is wonderful! Loved her passion for indigenous people and equality. She taught me a lot and  enjoyed her classes very much. She wants everyone to succeed and it shows.

This class was amazing, I took it as a gen ed and learned more than in any of my other classes that semester. There's quite a bit of reading, and it's very lecture heavy, but I personally thought it was worth it. I loved Professor Nash, she very clearly cares about what she is doing, and is extremely passionate and knowledgeable about the material.

Professor Nash gives incredible lectures, and has a good class structure. The workload is manageable. The readings are usually covered in class but are a nice read. I had a great TA, which improved my class experience. Two exams -final and midterm- that she gave us study guides for and explained beforehand. Would take it again!

I think she is a great professor and I've learned a lot in this class. You'll learn a lot of things that make you angry, but it's necessary, because we need to know what our societal problems are if we want to address them. I felt like the course load wasn't too bad, it's mostly a lot of reading and participating in discussion sections.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: Professor Nash was amazing, it is very clear she has a passion and reverence for this subject! As a history major I loved this class though, a lot of people take this just for the double Gen Ed, hence the more negative reviews on here. This class is SO worth it and SUCH an important topic to learn about, especially as a resident of MA!
Take simple notes and understand the groove of the class and you'll do fine.
reviews.rating_tags: Clear grading criteria--Beware of pop quizzes

reviews.comment: Very lecture heavy, every class is her talking. Assigns weekly reading from textbook with no homework attached. Assigns a few reflections and worksheets throughout semester. Final and midterm both online essays, you get 1 week to write and she gave us the prompt beforehand to prepare it. Discussions have pop quizzes on content from lecture.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Beware of pop quizzes--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: Posts weekly textbook chapters but barely has any assignments attached to them. Only 5 short assignments the entire semester, with a midterm and final that are both essays. Gives plenty of time for both. Is very lecture heavy and might give extra credit to those who attend. Is very passionate about what she teaches, I would take her again.

Professor Nash is lovely, but takes this class way too seriously for a gen-ed. Harder than some 200's. I took this class out of interest and for the double gen-ed requirement. Content is genuinely interesting and easily my favorite aspect of this course. That being said, if you just want a quick gen-ed to breeze through, there are better options.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Beware of pop quizzes--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: Lecture material is interesting. Grading is rather unclear at times. Be prepared to read much of the textbook and analyze primary sources. The final was difficult but at least there were different options. Heavy reading/writing course. If you're interested in the topic, I recommend this class, but it is not an easy A. Lots of head-scratching.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--EXTRA CREDIT--Lots of homework

reviews.comment: Probably the worst class I've taken at umass ngl. If you put in the effort you can def get a good grade but it's a lot of reading and lectures of her just talking at you. The content is interesting sometimes but she takes the class WAYYY too seriously for a gen-ed... wouldn't recommend. The final exam was also sooo much work for no reason.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Lots of homework--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: Prof Nash is very sweet and passionate about teaching this course. The workload was doable but a lot of writing. However, the final was SUCH a force I wouldn't recommend this class solely because of the final. The biggest assignment imaginable with so many parts to it and only like 2 days to complete it all. The grading is also tough so good luck.

Prof Nash is so passionate about her class. Not too many assignments, discussion heavy, and 2 midterm essays that weren't too difficult. The lectures can get a bit boring, however, and the final exam is asking for WAY too much. I had no complaints before the amount of content they filled the final with- we have other classes to study for too..

Alice Nash is super sweet as well as her TA's, they all do care for you and really want you to pass with good grades. Just make sure you do the worksheets and go to discussions or do the asynchronous discussions. When she has exams they're just essays that she gives you an entire day to do it's really nice but don't wait last minute to do it.
The sweetest person ever and the work was ever too hard, easy gen ed and very interesting class. Also had great TAs.

Her lectures are very important to attend in person, although she did record the class. Most of what she covers in class reflects on the exam papers. Overall it was a very interesting class and being able to truly learn the history of the Indigenous people, discussions are mandatory but its helpful to go over topics plus the TAs were very helpful
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Participation matters--Get ready to read

reviews.comment: Her course was incredibly interesting, and I really did learn a lot about Indigenous North American history. None of her assignments were really that difficult. There is a good amount of reading, but it is a history class so that is normal. She was super accommodating and actually kind of funny as well. Great storyteller.

Wonderful professor, super caring and willing to work and go the extra mile with students. flexible deadlines helped a lot and she really knows her stuff one of the best professors on early America at UMass. Very funny as well. Graded on only 4 essays and readings and participation is crucial.

Dr. Nash teaches diversity history classes and is well aware that they are often taken for HSDU GenEd credits. Did not take attendance once, which is great because lectures can get repetitive and boring. All of the TA's were lovely, easy, clear graders who made the class. Dr. Nash is super nice& the class is an easy A (if you can listen). Take it!
reviews.rating_tags: Graded by few things--Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: If you think you're going to go into this class learning about ancient american civilizations, you're very wrong. This class is simply about white people screwing over the native americans. This class had an absurd amount of reading. As long as your TA is chill, you'll get an A in this class but trying to stay awake during lecture is brutal.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--LOTS OF HOMEWORK--BEWARE OF POP QUIZZES

reviews.comment: Super unclear grading criteria, class is so frustrating because I have no idea what she wants from me. It's not a hard class, but she makes it difficult to succeed. Don't recommend class with her unless you can read minds.

Nash is out there for sure - flossed during an exam review... Easy class though, and she definitely cares about the subject. Pop quizzes are a thing, so be careful about skipping class. You don't really need to buy the textbook, easy to get an A without it.

I felt this class and Professor Nash exemplified what GenEd classes should be. The class wasn't very difficult, but that wasn't the point. I learned a lot about an area I absolutely never would have otherwise. I often think about the topics and readings from class. Great class!
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--LECTURE HEAVY

reviews.comment: Alice defiantly knows her stuff. She unfortunately is very unprofessional. Instead of teaching the material she spends time every class talking about how important her class is, and even though its a gen ed she believes it should have the same if not more work than other classes. She also calls people out for headphones and laptops often.

Great Professor. Dedicated and Knows her stuff. Very understanding and willing to work with students. Gives pop quizzes! If you do well on them you don't take a final. Lots of reading from textbook and other provided sources. Extra Credit opportunities. Easy grader if you put in any effort. Discussion group counts heavily but easy if you read.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--BEWARE OF POP QUIZZES--LECTURE HEAVY

reviews.comment: Although I don't love history, Professor Nash's class was good. A few papers, lectures weren't bad, and if you did well enough during the semester you don't have to take the final!  Suggestion:Read textbook for first half of course, do well on the midterm. Stop reading text book because you don't have to take final.

Assigns very long readings every week, but you basically don't need them if you go to lecture. Lectures are not heavily based on the textbook and were fairly interesting . Wrote two papers, can opt out of final if you take enough of the in-class quizzes (which are easy, basically just for checking attendance).
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--BEWARE OF POP QUIZZES

reviews.comment: Nash's lectures were more interesting than not. Discussions mandatory. She gave some of the questions on the exams ahead of time which was helpful. When it comes down to it this is a Diversity U/History double gen ed and its pretty simple.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--BEWARE OF POP QUIZZES

reviews.comment: Alice is an awesome professor & person. She really cares about the material, and it shows in the way she teaches.  I've never been bored in her class before. Can honestly say I learned more in a 100-level history class than in most of my 300- to 400-level ones.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--ACCESSIBLE OUTSIDE CLASS--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: Interesting topic and nice prof but a TON of reading. She gives you midterm essay topics ahead of time so if you go to lecture and her review sessions it's manageable. If you don't like reading 50-70 pages from M to Wed not worth it as a gen ed. Discussion is mandatory as well as lecture (you can opt out of final if you do well on her pop quizzes)
reviews.rating_tags: Tough Grader--Get ready to read--LOTS OF HOMEWORK

reviews.comment: This class was super cool/interesting. Lots of extra credit opportunities BUT the tests are really tough, all essay. And the papers are just as difficult. I went to every single lecture and was still sort of lost. It's hard to pinpoint what exactly is important and it's hard to catch exactly what she is saying because her slides are mostly pictures

Your experience in this class depends entirely upon your TA. My TA was a very tough grader. There is also more reading for this class than for any class I've ever taken. The material is interesting, just be prepared to dedicate A LOT of time and stress to this class.

There is a lot of reading and prep for disc/lecture. There are 2 major essays, a midterm and a final. Participation and attendance in discussion are needed to get an A. My TA graded nicely for me and for the midterm you get two topics ahead of time (chosen at random for exam) and you can opt out of the final if you answer in-class quizzes correctly

She is a harsh grader as well as the TA that I had. For the 2 essays we had to write for the class, I received C's on after following the criteria and rubric that was set out and feeling confident about my papers. Really big on connecting every topic of the class together as a whole. You'll probably read more for this class than any other class.

Alice is really nice and really wants to help her students. There were no exams at all which was great. Grade was based on attendance, a big paper, and a couple little assignments. She was a pretty easy grader, I'm not a good writer and I suck at history but I still got an A.
Not very clear in class and feel we didn't touch on any real topics.
Excellent professor and incredible nice individual. I would meet with her after class as an adviser as well. Great for people interested in indigenous politics or how to make sense of life.

this was actually a pretty interesting topic, but the lectures were tedious at best. discussions were helpful. most of all i just want to say that she assigned a book about sexual assault and gave absolutely no warning which i have a huge problem with. if The Roundhouse is assigned and this is a problematic subject for you i would pass on the class

Professor Nash was very helpful and a fair graderno knocks on her as a person.  On the other hand, the course required more reading than my 400 level courses so be prepaired.  The class itself is not hard, just time very consuming.  I could see this class getting tough if you had more than a full load or if you're new to college.

I took the class online, and was interested before going in, but became frustrated by the amount of work and reading you have to do vs. how much you learn. Three hours of lectures, reading from two textbooks and additional content per week and I feel it is more important to read and listen to everything rather than form true opinions and learn.

Dont go to lecture, only go to discussion.. Thats what I did and i got a B+ all the "tests" are take home essays and there are 2 of them. the final and the midterm. Also there are only 3 other assignments that are take home as well.
She rants about absolutely nothing.  The midterm and final are take-home, aka easy.  The discussion sections are painful and unnecessary.  Way more work than necessary.

Her lectures are filled with meaningless pictures and quotes offering no history figures relavant to what she has us read and study for assignments, leaving you limited resources to study the course materials for the ill conceived assignments she grades you on. She posts readings that may or may not be helpful in turn offering little to the class.
shes awesome. super nice, super helpful, and pretty easy.

Very enthusiastic and knowledgeable.  Leads terrific discussions which shows she's not in this for herself.  Clearly she's really trying to teach people and that she allows other views that she's trying to teach people how to think.  Tons of reading, but that's because she's so enthusiastic and has faith you will be, too.

Ok class, too much reading! Going to class was almost useless because she just rambles on about stuff. Discussion was great. Everything is graded by the TA, but they aren't harsh graders. The exams were not bad because she gives you an outline what's going to be on the test, you just need to prepare for it. Definitely do the textbook readings!
Horrible class. I thought it would be an easy Gen-ed but it is a very time consuming and unreasonably hard class for a gen-ed. I recommend nottt taking this class.

Prof. Nash has very ambiguous lectures and still thinks she is in the 70s- nobody is an expansionist, hates indians or doesnt believe that indians were treated poorly- so get over it. Teach some actual history and stop assuming that all your students are ignorant wasps.

Never attended lecture, they were boring and instead of teaching, she rambled on and on about things, usually things we had already discussed thoroughly in previous classes.  Discussion was kind of helpful, TAs are rly nice. Do well on the essays and you'll be fine. She gives out detailed study guides for exams (exact questions).

Shes awful. Really boring lectures. One of those classes where the subject matter is so easy and limited that they grade them really hard, cuz otherwise everyone would get As. Not worth it for a gen ed. Spent half of every lecture trying to figure out how to use the PRS.

Easy A. Attendance isn't really mandatory even though she uses the PRS..she usually only gives 1 or 2 questions every once in a while. The exams are essays, but she gives you the question before the exam and allows you to bring an index card of notes.  Do the readings and you'll be fine.

Enthusiastic, but more of an interesting person to talk to than professor - she changed curriculum this year, so it's different. Gives test Qs ahead of time - understands point of history isn't memorization. Lectures aren't engaging or all that helpful, bad use of PRS clickers. Concerned about political correctness. Cares about manners. Should read

nash herself is very nice and loves her subject, but the class is horrible.  you have to read a chapter a week of the book, lectures put you to sleep, but you have to go to do well on the tests.  discussions are mandatory and like torture.  i just took this class for a gen ed and it was not worth the effort.
Great teacher, really cares about her students. Can be boring, but just go to class, do the papers, and you cant go wrongg

alice nash is awesome. you can re-do papers, get help from her at anytime, and pass in papers late as long as you give her notice. she's really down to earth and understands the hard undergrad life. i wouldnt recommend taking her classes unless your really interested in what she's teaching. class participation is a must
Boring lectures. Terrible discussions. For me, the material was boring. It's a gened course, and a boring one at best. She's nice, but I'd pass this one up.

Native American Women - A great class and recomended! No tests or quizzes, only 3 papers and a take home final. Lectures are more like discussions and great for serious students who have interest in subject matter. Nash is great and dynamic, always wanting to hear opinions. Completly refreshing.
boring lectures, useless discussions, regular 100 level course; student notes available online ... extremely helpful study guides for exams (make exams VERY easy)
boring lectures but awsum discussions

This class was ok. The teacher knows alot but gets off subject often. I didnt go to alot of lectures because it was pointless. You can still get a good grade if you just show up to discussion and read most of the stuff.

Professor Nash is extremely nice, and ridiculously helpful. She goes out of her way to make sure that her students can do well, and get a lot out of her class. She is amiable, funny, and cute. She teaches well, and knows a lot. One of her TA's needs to be replaced, though.
one of the nicest teachers I've every had

Will do anything to help. The night before an exam she gave a review session that went an hour over and she kept on answering questions. Has a real passion for her subject and is incredibly knowlegible.
Absolutely, one of the kindest and most thorough of teachers.  When she hands back a paper, there are more pages than you turned in.  Lots of helpful comments and examples.
No Comments
Marius is easily the goat.

Let us indulge in a social experiment. Invite your friends and family to take CS220 with Marius. If anyone complains, they should be removed from your life. Marius is a pleasure, and it is disheartening to see others blame their own shortcomings on him. Name a more iconic duo than Marius and Max. Their 2024-2025 run was one for the history books!

Very accessible outside of class, cares a lot about student success, but also blunt with high (but still reasonable) expectations. Reading slides BEFORE lecture helped immensely. Exams are hard but do lots of practice exams and recognize patterns in the questions and answers and you'll do fine. Curve is generous and extra credit is provided.

Marius is caring and easy to reach outside of class. He really tries to connect with his students. My issue lies with his lectures. His lectures contained significantly more material than the other class, and they were harder to understand. I had to read the other professor's slides and watch his recordings to understand the material.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Caring--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Marius clearly cares about making his students better programmers, and expects a high level of effort from us. His lectures are exhausting and confusing, slides are way too dense and inconsistent. I enjoyed the lectures from the TA (Max) more than his. However, homework is designed well and helped me learn. Tests are crazy difficult of course.

The only redeeming quality about him is that he responds to CampusWire quickly. He explains concepts in confusing ways. Quizzes and exams are unreasonably hard. Argues with students when they give him a suggestion for the class. I would avoid this professor at all costs.

I have had him for 220 and 311: Syllabus and course has been set up very well/clear. He is always available for questions on Campuswire. 220 exams were unreasonably difficult, but 311 was not bad at all. Makes students critically think about content by asking questions. Slides are too much. He genuinely cares about becoming a better teacher.
reviews.rating_tags: Clear grading criteria--Lecture heavy--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: I've had Marius for 220 and 311, and he genuinely wants you to be the best computer scientist you can be. His 220 exams are definitely unreasonably difficult and I don't even want to know what the 311 exams would have looked like without Sheldon, but it really seems like he wants to improve as a teacher, and he responds very quickly on campuswire.

Don't listen to anyone telling you to avoid Marius. You're at university to learn and be challenged right? Marius makes his class hard but he and his TA's do EVERYTHING to make sure students succeed. Amazing class.

I get it, the guy is caring. However, he is not a great teacher. There is more words on a single slide than the entire book of Genesis. Along with that, next to know live code. It is paying credits for a podcast. I just think he is someone who cares and tries, but his own intelligence holds him back from being a good professor.

Marius is quick to respond on Campuswire, which is great. Though his feedback can often be too verbose, as he wants to make the students think. There are many ways to LOSE points in this course (aside from the exams), whether that be from the quizzes, homeworks, or even class questions. You must work very hard for a decent grade, which is stressful
Marius is tough. Going to office hours is a little scary at first, but he actually gives really good feedback and will help you where you are at.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Gives good feedback--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Marius is the best CS professor in the department. His class is difficult to make you better, that simple. He'll respond to you on Campuswire the night of a deadline within minutes, or stay late after class to answer your questions. Everything is designed to make you learn. The exams are difficult, but you'll get out what you put in.
He's the goat but if you're a bit slow you might not like him too much. Difficult exams but very fair grading and very knowledgeable guy in lecture
Exams are very difficult.

Marius is a tough but rewarding professor. His class requires serious work, but he provides abundant resources and support. I found Unstuckstudy to be a helpful study tool alongside the practice exams.

CS 311 with Marius was easily the most involved course I've taken at UMass in terms of coursework, but I learned a lot. Marius is always accessible outside of class and has a great deal of respect for those who try their best to engage with the course material.

Marius is a pleasant man who seems to care about student learning, but let's not pretend he's always been charming and lovable. His exams not being anything like the practice exams wasn't really a 220 aspect many people thought were reasonable. Still, his CW response speed is impressive.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Test heavy--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: This is a professor who will force you to work, and you will benefit from it. Clearly puts a lot of thought into designing assignments. Happy to work with anyone who will show up and put in effort. Very active and accessible on the class forum. One of those professors people either really like, or really don't (because they don't want to work imo).

Great lecturer, very accessible for office hours, responds very fast on Piazza, tough grader but curves fairly, difficult exams and projects but UCAs/TAs/Marius himself are very helpful. Learned the most in this class out of all my classes at UMass.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Clear grading criteria--Lots of homework

reviews.comment: Honestly I think he's a great professor, but his classes are terribly hard and he makes them way more difficult than they need to be. But if you love learning hard concepts then you should totally take his classes.
It's a hard course but he's a good prof

Marius is a very challenging professor, but you will undoubtedly become a better programmer from CS220. He expects a lot out of his students which forces you to work harder, learn more, and find the most effective study strategies. My advice: Start projects early, practice old exams early (do mock exams all the way through), and go to SI sessions.
Start the projects early and you'll be fine.
reviews.rating_tags: Clear grading criteria--Gives good feedback--Lots of homework

reviews.comment: Watched him yell at some kid for 5 minutes straight during office hours for being not knowing what to do in the coding assignment. 5/5
Still better than 240 with Mark Wilson

He is an extremely caring when it comes to student doing well. Never had a professor so accessible outside of class and makes it a point to answer questions in the middle of a lecture. Offers an abundance of resources as practice for exams. The content is not as bad as it is made out to be, but some effort is required.

HW is very doable, just start early and go to office hours. He cares deeply about the success of his students and will answer forum posts at very early hours/weekends, but please reread HW specs, other posts, and think before asking. However, his exams are out for blood, the best way to prepare is to do as many practice exams as possible, good luck

Marius' CS220 class has been one of the most defining parts of my time at CICS. I personally chalk the negative parts of CS220 up to the class material; ex. the topics tended to be uninteresting and lectures were very dense and fast-paced. Still, Marius displayed a great deal of care for his students and genuinely seemed invested in our learning.

Clear your schedule for this class- 10hrs/week of outside work on average
A lot will be expected of you, but you will learn a ton.
Lectures are clear but packed with information. I re-watched more than half of the lectures.
Work through the solutions to the practice exams to prep for exams
Use office hours, Campuswire, and free CS tutoring.
GL!
best professor in all of UMass

Professor Marius is a great lecturer and a tough exam writer. He is very accessible in office hours and on CampusWire. The class goes through material at an incredible pace, so you need to be 120% focused in lectures and review. Exams are where this class is difficult: the questions are very challenging. Homework is not hard if you put in effort.

Marius often responds to questions with vague answers, but he puts in a great amount of effort to always be available, while acknowledging that a question a student asked was good. The class is structured extremely well. Exam questions are challenging and often poorly worded, but not as difficult as project questions, and become enjoyable leetcode

From a teaching standpoint professor Minea is a great professor with an unique teaching style which forces students to learn and improve. CS220 with him was an extremely difficult course with tough exams/quizzes and strict grading. The weekly projects were difficult but doable and took up a large amount of time.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Lots of homework

reviews.comment: Every class you take with him will be very difficult, and you will get mad at both him and the content. Some people justifiably do not like how he talks, but he is a very caring person who wants his students to succeed. He requires thorough effort from students, but once you've taken multiple classes with him, you'll realize how great he is.

Marius is a great person&truly cares about his students' learning; has high expectations of students! Always active on Campuswire. Grading & the class is generally well structured, but the exams/work load will make you want to drop. Exams are so difficult he himself has said he's worried about people not passing the 33% threshold.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Clear grading criteria--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment:
Nothing I can say that hasn't been said. If you take a Marius class, you will get out what you put in. Difficult exams, lots of homework, but you'll absolutely learn a lot of material. Isn't that why you're at college? 
He's a very nice guy, if not a little short in his Campuswire responses. But he genuinely wants students to succeed.

Have taken 2 classes with Marius (220, 311). Marius is a very caring and intelligent man. He teaches infamously difficult classes, hence so many ratings. His exams and homework are a survival mission. But he gives a solid and reliable teaching performance. He will never let you fail if you put in the effort. Pros and cons ofc, but 150% worth it.

Literally makes the class impossible for no reason. Makes the quizzes so dumb because half the stuff isn't even useful and isn't from the slides most of the time. You just have to know it which makes no sense because where am I supposed to learn it from when they are supposed to teach the material? Exams are even crazier and impossible.

Prof. Minea is one of the best teachers I've ever had. His lectures are engaging, with great examples and applications from real world to help us better understand the abstract concepts. Exams are not too hard, as long as we have prepared.
reviews.rating_tags: Amazing lectures --Clear grading criteria--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment:
For those reading, yes, Marius's rating is probably terrible with 1 star reviews.

But if you ever wanted to take a course and get something out of it, there's no prof who does it like Marius.  

Any of Marius' courses have difficult exams and homeworks and you will need to work extra. But also there's excellent communication and accommodation.
I've taken two classes with Marius. and I have to say that the classes I've taken with him are definitely the hardest I've taken, but I've also learned way more in them than any other class.

Marius comes across as rude sometimes, but he does seem to care. He's extremely responsive to Campuswire questions. The projects are well-designed and doable within a week. The quizzes and in-class questions, on the other hand, are ridiculously difficult, poorly written, and not a good indicator of whether you'll do well on the projects or exams.
easiest class of my life. we watched movies.

220 with Marius can definitely be considered a weed-out class. Although the contents covered are actually very interesting and useful in the field of computer science. However, some concepts are very abstract and you need to work your brain to understand it. Quizzes are difficult, exams are hard but mostly reasonable. Great officer hours however.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Lots of homework--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: The main downside to Prof. Marius is the extremely difficult quizzes and exams. The only good thing is he posts many past exams to review from but the exam averages will still be deadly. He does apply a curve on overall class grade. Lectures are boring and long

Marius's UCAs deserve to get berated for caring more about massaging their ego by defending his behavior and abstract teaching style instead of helping students thrive and listening to reasonable student concerns.

Pros: 
- Rsponds so quickly to CampusWire posts, very easy to reach for help
- Will host spontaneous office hours if needed
- Genuinely cares about the learning of his students.
- Notes have high detail

Cons:
- Exams are so hard
- Quizzes also hard, with the bonus of little to no feedback
- Can come across as mean. I don't think it's intentional
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Lots of homework--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: This man is accessible nearly 24/7 on campuswire. He may be a tough grader (the exams are deadly), but I really feel that I learned a lot more from this class than most others.
literally the best teacher ive ever had in my entire life

Always supportive when I came to talk about HW after class, praising good Qs and great response time on forum, advocating for my interests. Timed quizzes and lengthy exams took a yr off my life, but considering I'm not the only one who doesn't test well under pressure, all worked out with weighted grades. Liked his interactive lecs w/ code.

No exercises to bridge the gap between lectures and his expectations for exam/quiz problems. No resources could help you deduce what he would throw at you. Got frustrated with student questions during office hours. Answered genuine questions with new questions. Probably a good guy sometimes, but not all the time. Literally just relieved I passed.
Failed my first ever class thanks to him:) The concepts are easy when someone else teaches them to you but he makes it extremely hard. Exams are hard. HW's are hard. Lecture's are boring.
Challenging homeworks and exams, but if you try to learn, he is extremely helpful with answering questions. He is very knowledgeable so asking him any sorts of doubts will teach you something new.
Quizzes and exams are brutal, homework instructions are never clear.

TLDR: AMAZING TEACHER, TOUGH GRADER. I took him for CS 220 in fall 2022. The course was one of the best designed courses I've taken so far. However, the exams were almost designed to make you fail, so it did require a lot of reading. Even though it was a hard class, I can say I learned something real in this class.

Really difficult exams and quizzes. HWs are okay with lots of TAs and UCAs for extra help (+ campuswire). Lecture style is boring but the slides are good. Marius is a notoriously tough grader who will make sure you struggle but he's a really nice guy so don't be afraid to reach out for help. Also gives extensions for valid reasons.
Negative reviews=bad grade before the curve. He is the best professor in all of UMass by far
Marius is POG
He is amazing

Great professor who challenges his students. Most classes at umass are taught formulaically with the exams being close to the practice exams. Marius actually makes them different so the test is reflective of your knowledge instead of memorizing the practice exams.
Everyone who writes negative reviews just got a bad grade and they are mad. His curves are ridiculously generous. Trust me. Super nice and very approachable.
Horrible. Try no to take his class unless you are a CS nerd

Marius needs to learn to respect others like he was already respected. Jumping on to students is wrong, they could have had serious bad luck with their lives that semester, and the least they need is further childish behavior by a grown man. Students defending his behavior are probably UCAs attempting to uplift their privileged fragil ego again.
Marius is a good guy, but don't take too many credits while taking his classes because he is very impatient with people who have questions in his office hours (very different person).

Marius really, really cares about his students. He can be strict and is maybe not the best professor for everyone, but he is an EXCEPTIONAL person who will follow up with you and talk and listen. CS220 is a horrible horrible class that I hate with all my heart, but I don't think Marius really has much to do with it.

Marius knows the material, but he doesn't know how to explain it. While he puts in a lot of effort for students to succeed, he isn't helpful in his responses when you ask him or reach out to him. The TAs were friendly and helpful, but the UCAs are rude and incompetent. The whole structure and design of his classes needs some serious overhauling.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Clear grading criteria--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: I agree that you can't be spoonfed, but the reality is that Marius Minea is not a good professor. He may be a smart man but he does not know how to teach. Not every smart guy is a good teacher. His UCAs are very rude and care more about inflating their ego and ignoring valid constructive feedback than setting students up to succeed.
Good teacher. Only downside is he's way too hard on his students. His scales make up for it though.
really caring guy. works tirelessly to make sure that you learn. reach out to him and he will help

Great professor, anyone saying that "Marius sucks" are just soft people who expect hand-holding. Put in the effort, and you'll do fine. Marius wants to pass his students. Don't be soft, and don't expect hand-holding.

Ok this review is being left to address all of the 1-star reviews that convey the "waaah they didn't spoon-feed us" message. It's college, instructors aren't supposed to spoonfeed you their subject matters anymore. The nature of CS is that it's a difficult major. You have to work for your grade. His classes are tough, but a curve makes up for it.

He's a good professor who taught me the art of asking good questions. The people who say otherwise are the ones who expect to be spoonfed. Put in the effort, and you'll be ok. You cannot be spoonfed by your professor.

He's not the best, but I think he still deserves a 5 because he's a good person, he's learning how to be a better professor after acknowledging genuine student feedback seriously, and has at least a decent level of empathy towards students. The 1-star ratings have an ulterior motive because Marius isn't that bad anymore.
Genuinely the best teacher I've ever had. Go to his office hours and you will understand everything. I have never had a better teacher.

Overall, an ok dude. Marius may seem to care about student learning and answer questions fast, but unfortunately this gets overshadowed by his inability to construct meaningful assignments and exams for students. The course design of his classes needs a serious update.

Marius doesn't deserve this bad of a reputation. Yes, his classes are hard, but that's how it's supposed to be in college. He is not supposed to spoonfeed you his wealth of knowledge and subject matter. You have to put in the effort.

Marius is okay overall. He is very thorough in his lectures, as well as a knowledgeable person when it comes to questions, but at the same time it can be extremely intimidating to approach him. He expects a lot from his students (even for underclassmen), and asking somewhat basic questions are met with sharp replies.

I've taken 3 classes with him, worked with him as an assistant for one, and will take another next semester. Some might find him mean, but he really does care about his students. His homeworks and exams are harder than when other professors teach it, but I find it the most challenging and made me want to learn more.

Marius is a tough guy whose classes are demanding and getting an A is no easy task. BUT he does care and wants you to succeed. Marius is very accessible as he has at least two shadow clones constantly monitoring and answering questions on Piazza, Campuswire, etc 24/7. There is a person who keeps spamming him with bad reviews, don't listen to them.
Terrible! Designed the HW and Exam in unnecessary hard level, the hint of HW is to read the problem and textbook carefully.

Marius has made computer science, something I used to have a strong passion for, completely intolerable for me.
The class is too difficult and goes by without sufficient coverage of complex material. Marius also gets noticeably frustrated when asked basic questions.
I will never voluntarily take another class with Marius again.

311 is one of those classes that will drain your soul, and Marius will make it 10 times harder. Will he help you learn the content? For sure. Will he stress you out? Definitely.  Will it be worth it in the end? I hope so. Exams so far have been fair, but the HWs will make you want to cry to sleep every night. Textbook is a must-read along with lecs
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Lots of homework

reviews.comment: No offense to Marius as he seems like a good guy, but I could never learn from a professor who is way too unclear in lectures.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Beware of pop quizzes--Test heavy

reviews.comment: Marius isn't terrible at teaching, but to be honest he's too unclear, and I could never learn from a professor who just reads off slides directly without explaining the concepts in new ways.

The class is challenging but for the right reasons. Lectures are pretty interesting and lab exercises are good practice. The most useful CS class I have taken at UMass by far. The content is difficult and getting good at programming practices is difficult but the class is more than fair with dropped HWs, and quizzes. Great response time.
reviews.rating_tags: Clear grading criteria--Lots of homework--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Marius makes his classes harder than they need to be, but he really cares and is always fast with communication. His classes are extremely difficult, but in exchange you’ll boost your work ethic by being careful when asking questions. Plus, he scales everything to make up for the difficulty of the class.

Marius makes his classes harder than they need to be, but he really cares and is always fast with communication. His classes will kill you, but in exchange you’ll boost your work ethic by being careful when asking questions.

Marius doesn’t deserve the review bombs anymore. Yes, his exams are hard, but he’s very receptive to criticism, which is rare in many CICS professors. He began his redemption arc after the switch to in-person learning. The way he explains stuff could improve, but he’s doing his best.
220 has a lot of interesting material, but Marius singlehandedly took the fun out of that class through his dry and formal teaching style and condescending view towards helping students.

Severely underrated professor. His classes are hard, but final grades are scaled, lectures are interesting, and he cares a lot and puts in a lot of effort to help his students learn. Marius may seem stern, but he is also one of the most organized CS professors I've had, which is very rare in the CS department at UMass.

I was scared to take a class with Marius after hearing/reading the negative comments, but I was so pleasantly surprised. His classes are challenging, but lectures are engaging and he puts in a lot of effort to help his students thrive. He may seem severe, but Marius is the most compassionate prof I've had in the CS department at UMass.
I'm glad I didn't take 311 with Marius. Marius sucks at teaching, and his lectures are dry and a genuine waste of time. Don't expect any help from him. He's awful. Awful awful awful.

Marius isn't great at teaching but I don't think he's terrible either. Personally I found reliance on 220 peers to be more helpful than him, but I still went to his lectures to learn new knowledge. Marius's rendition of 220 taught me that the best tip to do well on the programming projects is to start them early and work with a peer for each one.

220 was lowkey a rewarding class for software engineering in terms of material learned, but Marius's lectures weren't very helpful for the difficult homeworks and exams as the lectures only brushed over the basics. If more online resources such as practice problems for each topic were posted, the workload for 220 would've been more bearable.

Marius expects a lot from his students because he thinks so highly of them. In our first class he was so happy for us to be in the classroom again eager to learn. I respect professors who make people work, it's kind of rewarding. He's always available through campuswire and though sometimes blunt, he will never not help you.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Skip class? You won't pass.--Test heavy

reviews.comment: Marius cares and his classes have the most generous curves, but that doesnt compensate for his poor teaching skills whatsoever

Marius Minea is a real joke of a professor. I went to his office hours, and Marius didn't help at all; he just wanted to lose patience with me and make me uncomfortable to ask questions in order to boost his ego. This attitude is not at all conducive to a welcoming work environment. I would never take classes with Marius ever again.

Good Prof. Knowledgeable, will take time to explain concepts again if people actually ask questions. Exams are really difficult, but the curve is always generous, and unlike popular wisdom, I don't think "more people fail" in his courses. Recalibrate your expectations for exams, you'll learn a lot and your grade will be fine.
reviews.rating_tags: Respected--Skip class? You won't pass.--Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: He is by far the best Professor Ive ever had. His exams are hard but his curves are overly generous frankly. Super accessible outside of class ( unmatched). Super easy to get a B but you have to work for an A.
Marius clearly knows his stuff, but has no teaching skills whatsoever

Stay away from him at all costs. He's condescending, his difficulty jumps from lectures to the homework is too much, and it's just stressful all around. Marius has a reputation for making hard classes harder. Maybe it's cause he cannot explain difficult topics. Maybe it's because he just cannot teach. Just a thought
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Accessible outside class--Test heavy

reviews.comment: The only reason I'm giving a Marius a 2 and not a 1 is because I feel he was very accessible on campuswire and he was very helpful in answering questions. However in lecture, he was just too confusing . Quizzes were impossible and stressful too, even though they're supposed to be a "learning opportunity". Final exam was way too long as well.

He makes the class difficult beyond practicality. Lectures were super simple, yet quizzes and tests were 100x more brutal than even practice tests so you never knew what to expect. The only way people get a decent grade is because he puts a massive curve. His facade of wanting to improve is fake since he resets his changes each semester.

Professor Minea changed in a solid way this semester. He is a strong lecturer that knows what he's talking about. He was very available always on CampusWire and office hours if you didn't understand the material. The tests for this class were VERY hard, but he scaled every one of them.

His classes go fast, in depth, and his tests/homeworks are hard. That's all true. But if you really want to learn, you will learn the most from his classes. The habits his courses hammered into my programming really had a positive impact at internships and interviews. The classes are insanely difficult for sure-- but you will learn so much.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Accessible outside class--Tough grader

reviews.comment: Marius really makes you learn the material to pass the class. Overall I really enjoyed his lectures even though he sometimes can struggle to explain hard-to-understand concepts in a simple way. He can also be very passive-aggressive which can rub people the wrong way, but I found it very entertaining. Always available on campuswide, would recommend

I think hes a . Yeah hes not perfect... it can be easy to space out at his lectures since he often explains things in a very roundabout, hard to understand way. Tests and quizzes can also be VERY hard. But its clear he cares about trying to teach us, esp with how much he answers questions online. Pretty ok dude

Marius seems to care about his students, answering questions quickly on campuswire and trying his best to improve himself with the feedback from previous semesters (though it seems hes got a lot to improve). However, while I did like his lectures, they were not helpful for assignments and tests because they were that hard.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Get ready to read

reviews.comment: Easily the best professor in CICS. His class is extremely difficult but you'll never find a professor like him that genuinely wants to see you succeed and actually cares that you learn the material
Easily the hardest class I've taken at UMass. Also, the most I've learnt. 311 is a must with Marius if you want to learn CS.

Marius' classes are brutal, there's no denying that. His homework, quizzes and exams are probably the hardest there are. In the moment his classes are extremely stressful, but looking back you will be glad you took the class with him. He will make you a better programmer. He's very knowledgeable, but can also be very brash. Expect to be challenged.
reviews.rating_tags: Accessible outside class--Skip class? You won't pass.--Test heavy

reviews.comment: Quiz: you would think the lecture is enough to go through the materials and prep you for the quiz; not true. His weekly quizzes are PAINFUL and worse because you only have 30 minutes to complete. Homework: His homeworks are lengthy and extremely hard because you have to think out of the box for every single one. Only 10% is lecture related.

He's like Anton Chigurrh: cold but calculated. Well he seems cold. Get to know him better and he's really sweet and supportive. He is a bit controversial, though. On one hand he's very responsive to your questions, but oftentimes the onus is on you to read the instructions, to which he will point you back to. You need to take him if you are in CS.

This has been the hardest class I've taken ever. However, if you really want to challenge yourself you will learn many things from Marius. The class will force you to learn time managment skills, become a better programmer, and be a better leaner. I only recommend if you truly want to push yourself. His tests are insane, but final grades are fair.

Marius is tough. His homework and exams are long and difficult. But if you understand the material cold, you will get an A. He is very very quick to respond to issues and provides all the materials you need to succeed. If you want to learn a lot, take this class. If you want an A, then don't.
Do NOT take his class! It's toooooo difficult, and generally it is hard to get help from him. The good aspect is that he replies questions very quickly, but those answers are too vague to understand.

One of the best classes ever. I'm way better at programming bc of this class. Many ppl just trynna collect a bunch of A's, but if you actually want to learn and grow, Prof Minea is the move.
