Alexei is knowledgable and cares about math but just not the content he taught. Unless he was sidetracking about some application, lectures were monotone and useless. The content is easy so you will still succeed and all the homework is posted ahead of time with online quizes + retakes. Exams are straightforward and he will help you if you ask.

I don't think Alexei is great at teaching but I don't think he's terrible either. Personally I found the textbook to be more helpful than him but I still went to lectures to add to my understanding for subjects I was more confused on. His office hours are pretty decent too.

Go to class. Professor writes some stuff on chalk board, difficult to follow along with what he's doing. Open moonami. There's basically nothing there. I felt there was very little structure and support in this class. Everything was self taught. Lectures weren't helpful. He's a very nice guy but teaching is not his forte.
reviews.rating_tags: Graded by few things--Test heavy--Tough grader

reviews.comment: I stopped going to the lectures after the first five or so because just doing the homework taught me enough for all of the tests/quizzes. For the lectures that I did go to, they were great. He explains things well and is always happy to go over something if someone doesn't understand it.

Hugely overrated. Maybe it's because we are online now but Alexei is the most iffy professor I have had so far. I totally respect that he does his very best to make lectures very engaging for night owls like me. The problem is, however, Alexei isn't helpful during office hours anymore and is sometimes condescending now that the course is online.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Participation matters--Skip class? You won't pass.

reviews.comment: If you're taking 235, do not take anyone other than him. He is the best professor for 235. Entire homework is 25% of the grade and there are no quizzes in his class. Overall the course is easy and if you're good at math it will be an easy A.

Alexei was a great professor who clearly has a passion for mathematics as a whole. He does a great job of explaining all of the concepts and is probably the best math professor that I have had at UMass

The way Alexei goes about teaching 235 is great. He goes over core concepts very in-depth, stopping frequently to clear any doubts, and tells you exactly what you need to know and how to do it. This class is frankly very easy the way he lays it out, and as long as you pay attention, should be a breeze. He is also freaking hilarious, 10/10.

235 is a standard math class: weekly hw, 2 midterms and a final. Alexei gives clear lectures, cares about his student's success and prepares us well for the exams (which are written by another prof). He's not the best professor I've ever had but he's definitely not a bad choice for this class.

Alexei is a good professor, but personally I would not take him again. There was a bit of a language barrier, but he tried very hard to make it so we could understand him, such as always taking questions to clear up confusion and bringing a speaker so he was louder. While it didn't help me that much, I still would say he's a good professor.

Professor Oblomkov is super good! He cares about his students and makes sure everyone is following along. His lectures are organized and he balances conceptual and procedural material by giving a lot of examples
Very smart and funny guy. 10 out of 10!
Perhaps not the best at explaining things right off the bat, but obviously cares about student comprehension. Great teacher with a fantastic balance of theory and practice.

His lecture is a bit unorganized, but he actually cares for his students. He never let any students fall behind. Ask him questions whenever you are stuck or confused. He is always willing to help you out.

Hands down the best teacher in the math department. Cares for his students, offers extra credit, and is very friendly during office hours. Encourages learning above and beyond course material. Can't wait until I can take another class with Alexei.

Alexi will make you work hard for a good grade, but he's a brilliant mathematician who clearly cares about helping his students to succeed. Ignore the negative reviews below; if you're willing to work hard and ask for help, you'll be very happy to learn from Alexi.

HORRIBLE TEACHER. One of the worst. He is hard to understand, as is his writing. Doesn't ever clear up points of confusion, which are plentiful. Going to his office hours is pointless as he is no more helpful than in class. I think Linear Algebra could actually be an easy and enjoyable class with a different professor...

He does not care if his students do well or not and fails to explain material clearly. He is also very difficult to understand. Very unwilling to help if you attend his office hours as he cares more about himself than his students.

He glosses over much of the material that he believes to be easy. While this gives a general understanding of the concepts, it does NOT prepare you for the exams that often have small tricks to them. Minimal partial credit is given. Avoid if you have the option.

Very knowledgeable and a good teacher, although soft-spoken and at times difficult to understand.  Willing to help if you seek him out, and does provide lots of study material.  Fair grader, will give points back where deserved but will ultimately give what he thinks is fair.

Super easy class to get an A in. From what I have heard her workload is slightly higher than some other profs (also slightly lower than others) but as long as you put in minimal effort you'll never have to stress about this class.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Gives good feedback

reviews.comment: Maxine Oland is nice and very considerate just talk to her if you miss anything or have questions for clarification. There was homework every night so be prepared for a lot of reading but if you skim it to put in annotations and read a summary of the text you'll be fine. Just put in effort and it's an easy A.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Lots of homework

reviews.comment: Ignore the older reviews as they certainly don't reflect the professor that I  know and completed my honors thesis with. I opted for a single-semester thesis and Professor Oland was incredibly kind and constantly engaging. Class was very student directed and she worked closely with us. I would not have completed my honors thesis if not for her help

Maxine Oland is one of the nicest professors I've had. She really cares about her students and their input. There were daily readings with 6 annotations needed per reading, but they weren't too bad. Her discussions were student led and really engaging and we did lots of other fun activities throughout the sem. I highly recommend this class!

I completed a single semester thesis class with Professor Oland and would highly recommend doing so if she is offering a thesis seminar again.

Caring and gives great feedback to help you grow and develop your thesis. Reading is manageable and usually interesting and can be influenced by the direction that the class naturally moves in.

Lots of reading but she does the harder ones at the beginning of the semester so the end is super super easy. You do 2 essays/projects 1 is an actually paper and one is a creative project like a podcast and you can chose when you do each one. Super kind and caring also super easy class.

Okay I get that she might have cooked herself a bit in her own department (it be that way sometimes) but her Honors 201H course is honestly fantastic and I have no notes whatsoever. She never inserted her opinion and used it as fact and allowed us to discuss as a group. Assignments were enjoyable and straightforward. I would take this course again.

I was shocked to see that Dr Oland has a 2.9?? I had her for 201H and she was the sweetest woman ever. She brought cookies in for us once and after Trump got elected we spent the whole class talking about our feelings regarding that. 10/10 would recommend for this class.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Clear grading criteria--Caring

reviews.comment: Prof Oland is super understanding, caring, and generous with extensions. You have to read a lot for this class, but class discussions were very helpful to understanding texts. Class has 3 projects/essays/presentations which were very doable and straight forward. Participation is appreciated. I would definitely take another class with her again.

Great class! There were readings to do before each class but they were not too difficult. There are discussions on them so come prepared. We only had 3 papers/projects that were very straightforward. She is very understanding with extensions. Overall, a very kind professor who makes an effort to build connections with her students!

She is very flexible with her grading-as long as you put in the effort into the assignments, it's almost guaranteed to get an A in the course. There's usually a reading that's required before each class, but it's easy to do. Be ready to talk in class because the class is more of a conversation between students rather than the professor lecturing.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Best professor at UMass Amherst. She is very accommodating, understanding, and flexible if you need anything. If you do bad on a project she emails you to fix any issues and then resubmit it. All students in my class passed their paper/project. She still requires some work to be done, but it is straight forward, failing is only if you are lazy asf.
Very caring and understanding. If you need an extension, let her know. Lots of reading but generally interesting stuff. Such a sweet person!

Absolutely find another gen ed to take. Lectures are incredibly long, boring, and contain poorly written slides. The information she expects you to learn is very specific, you won't remember any of it in 6 months. The reading is dense, not peer reviewed, and very outdated. Take another history class that you'll enjoy and learn something from.

The professor fails to understand this is a gen ed requirement and not a top priority for students. If the class is struggling she refuses to change anything about her methods. Does not attempt to make this class interesting but expects you to remember every detail of 80 slide lectures. I put more time into studying for this class than for orgo.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Lots of homework--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: Really long and boring lectures and readings (48-90 pages), as well as a weekly short essay. Expect to fall asleep during reading or class. Professor repeatedly uses words she doesn't know the meaning of in lectures, will ignore questions and respond with "I really *should* know". She often gets flustered and upset in class. Just a bad experience.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Lecture heavy--So many papers

reviews.comment: Professor Oland is a great overall professor. I took her Anthropology class as a Gen-ed, and had just the right amount of difficulty. She's very understanding and caring, very passionate about her career and students. She's pretty generous with grades and will almost always give you the benefit of the doubt. She really made me enjoy anthropology!
reviews.rating_tags: Accessible outside class--Group projects--Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: If you dont like archaeology you won't like an archaeology class Shes the reason Ive achieved anything I have, starting with the local conference I presented at as freshman (She convinced me) She puts pics on her slides which keep them interesting covers readings in class responsive to student feedback fond of writing assignments answers emails

Took this class as a gen-ed. I found it really interesting and information was presented efficiently. You need to go to class for i-clicker questions. The homework seems like a lot but it's not bad. Takes notes everyday in class. I loved the professor she was very knowledgable and organized. She knew what she was talking about.

Worst professor ever, and a every rude person. Lectures are slideshow with no keypoints on the slide and pictures all over. 300-500 words essay every week, tons of reading. The worst class I have through my whole four college years.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough Grader--Skip class? You won't pass.--LOTS OF HOMEWORK

reviews.comment: I took this class for a gen-ed and I enjoyed lecture. She does a great job at keeping students engaged in a 300+ person lecture and her slides are interesting. There's no book for the class so everything on the midterm and final are from lecture notes. There's one group project but it took almost no work. Highly recommended if you're a freshman.
reviews.rating_tags: Respected--Skip class? You won't pass.--Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: Great professor and class, interesting gen ed. There was a 300-500 word writing assignment every week that required around 50 pages of reading or less, which were not bad at all. It's a straight up lecture with minimal interaction except a few i-clicker questions. She posts recordings of all lectures on Moodle so you can miss class sometimes.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--ACCESSIBLE OUTSIDE CLASS--GROUP PROJECTS

reviews.comment: This is a rating of the class itself more than the professor, I took Ancient Civilizations because I thought learning about the peoples would be interesting. There is a lot of focus on the structures and excavation and its just not what I was excited to learn about. Obnoxiously long readings. Up to 40 pages per lecture but at least its on moodle

If you plan on skipping lectures, do not sign up for Prof Oland's class. Attendance weighs heavily in the grade book and skipping lecture will set you behind in terms of notes and content. There are a lot of negative reviews on this site, but there is nothing wrong with Prof Oland's class. You just have to be in class and pay attention to get the A
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--SO MANY PAPERS--LECTURE HEAVY

reviews.comment: Lectures are very boring, and you have to write an essay every week (which are based on 40+ pages of dense reading per week). These weekly essays are worth 20% of your grade, and participating in discussions are another 30%. You have to study for exams (memorize a large amount of boring information). The way she handled the final was poor as well.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--SO MANY PAPERS

reviews.comment: Lots of work. Do not take this if you don't like reading. She assigns 100 pages of reading and an essay each week. The exams are based on both lecture and reading, you can't skim it. She also sent an email to everyone saying we should "seek disability service" if we can't remember the answers to iclicker questions.

This class is not an easy A. Although she assigns one 300-400 page paper a week, the readings and articles that go along with them total about 200 pages a week. Her slides are useless and full of pictures making it hard to go back and review the material. The exams are multiple choice but the questions are specific. The study guides are crazy long.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--GRADED BY FEW THINGS--Tests are tough

reviews.comment: You'll be assigned reading every week, but skimming it through to write your weekly 300-400 word paper will be plenty of effort. Her lectures are passionate - and interesting, if this is your subject of interest. Show up to class because 5+ clicker questions is a guarantee. Only real assignment is the weekly paper, AKA take the class. Good for GEs

Every week you are assigned up to 3-4 30 pages assignments to read and then write a 300-400 word paper, which you have to site from all the articles. She takes attendance for every class, and her papers are due at the TA sessions so you cannot miss a class or else you will fall off. She is also incredibly boring and fails to capture my attention.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Skip class? You won't pass.

reviews.comment: The class is taught in an incredibly boring and unengaging way. Every lecture is just a slideshow of pictures while a professor who is clearly enthusiastic but fails to transfer that enthusiasm talks. Takes a very interesting topic and makes it boring. TA was fantastic though.

Professor Oland focuses on Mesopotamia, Ancient Egypt, the Maya, and the Aztec. As an Anthro major I find the course interesting and the work is not bad. There is 1 assignment due each week, a 300-400 word cited paper based on that week's readings. The only tests are the midterm/final. There is a discussion section on Fridays. I love the class.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: Don't take it. You will regret. The worst teacher ever. Slides are full of pictures, no key points and disorganized. Don't answer your question. 3-4 readings each week averaging 30 pages each. You need to submit a 300-400 words essay each week and must cited the sources from all your readings. Tons of work to do before midterm, and don't answer you
reviews.rating_tags: Tough Grader--Get ready to read--LOTS OF HOMEWORK

reviews.comment: If youre looking for an easy gen ed, steer clear of Maxine. 3/4 readings a week averaging 20 pages per reading for a 400 word essay every week. If you dont like talking, drop it now, or else your grade will be threatened. Also if you have trouble taking notes seek disability services - an exact quote in response to not writing down iclicker qs
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--SO MANY PAPERS

reviews.comment: Bad professor. Don't take this class.
Professor Jimi Oke makes his courses bearable.
Easy work, unorganized and obnoxious due dates on assignments, fair amount of time wasted in class, mandatory attendance through online in class activities.

Be prepared for links that don't work, code that doesn't run, autograders that give zeros, constant typos, unproductive lectures, and materials given for a final project two days before the presentation. Found it hard to pay attention because I sometimes couldn't stop laughing, as it seemed like everything that could go wrong did go wrong.

hes kinda unorginaized a lot of the time during lectures was sitting around and waiting. however hes a very sweet guy and the course was very easy. attendance is mandatory but sometimes he gives u treats in class. (like candy)

He's horribly unorganized and his un organization just falls back on the class. He forgot to explain the final project until halfway through finals week and then expected us to finish the final project in two days. He's a nice guy in the class is easy but he's all over the place and it makes it hard to get stuff done. Just expect to be blindsided.
Extremely nice and caring guy. He's a little disorganized but overall it was a good class. If I had the option to redo this class I would do it with the same professor
If I had to describe Jimi Oke with three words, I'd probably say hardworking, and amazing dancer. When he performed for us after the first midterm, I wept.
Fun class for the most part, assignments were a little tedious and the labs sometimes seemed unnecessary. By far one of the best dancers I've ever met.
He would be 5 stars if he switched to teaching dance
His lectures were very interesting and he gave us m&m's one time. My favorite part is when he did 'the dance'

Great person, not a great professor. Consistently unprepared for lecture, fixing code and slides mid class. Spends 20 minutes on difficult concepts and then wastes the rest of class doing unnecessary experiments. Positives: He usually owns up when he messes up and gives HW extensions, etc. You will just have to email a few times.

He is a good teacher but some lectures were confusing and had some problems. He clearly likes to teach and cares about his students a lot. Overall a good professor. If you go to office hours you should ask him to do the dance
Great class. You gotta ask him to do "the dance"
Ask him to "do the dance"

Prof. Oke is a good guy but not a good teacher. He is entirely unprepared to teach. He wastes upwards of 20min each class fixing the issues in his code that he writes during the lecture instead of preparing it ahead of time. He gives us homework that is riddled with mistakes and has to send us multiple corrections almost every week.

Genuinely a painful lecture to sit through but they are mandatory so you just have to survive. If you don't got to lectures just be on your phone at that time to make sure you can fill out attendance on time. So unorganized and would be making the codes he needed and making google forms during the actual lecture. Exams are online and no final.

Prof Oke always went out of his way to help students understand, and I got the sense that he really cared about students learning the material, whereas grading was a side concern. I really liked that approach because it took the edge off the work and yet we still learned everything we needed. Homeworks graded on completion, and open reference exams

Prof Oke is a very nice guy who cares about his students. Really tried to shape the course to the benefit of the students. Material was sometimes confusing and lectures were long but grading was lenient which was nice. Reference sheet really helped with tests and almost took the final for me. Very accessible and easy to talk to outside of class.
reviews.rating_tags: Accessible outside class--Clear grading criteria--EXTRA CREDIT

reviews.comment: This was one of my favorite classes this semester. I think there are learning-heavy classes and work-heavy classes and this was definitely learning-heavy, making it very easy for me. After the first exam there was a lot of material, but the little homework was not that important for grades. Very interesting class with a lovely professeur. :)
reviews.rating_tags: Beware of pop quizzes--Lecture heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: If you are someone who actually wants to learn about entomology, don't take this class. It focuses on unimportant things and you will never get a single question answered. Also the grading scale on the syllabus is not the same as the one she uses for final grade, super frustrating. A lot of it is not her direct fault, but still frustrating.

For a class on the biology of bugs, there was little to no connection between the things we learned about, making it very difficult to understand. Spent extended periods of time on things that didn't matter and skipped over things that were on the exam. Not clear who the class was for. Lots of material and graded on very few things.

Olga was a great professor, and this was a pretty hard class. She did a great job explaining the material, but it's a LOT of memorization and pretty much all grades are based on few exams. A great class to take if you are very interested in learning about insects.

Taking 109 was definitely an enjoyable experience. The labs were sometimes a bit unorganized but it is clear she knows a very good amount about this subject. I would say "participation matters" because going to this class is definitely the way to succeed and not get behind. She's also fair with grading and gives a good amount of extra credit

Olga is an amazing professor. Shes very intelligent and is really passionate about what she teaches. Theres a lot of information you end up learning in this class and it is by no means and easy A but she really cares about her students. Just work hard and attend the lectures and youll do amazing.
Pretty great prof. Had lots of fun with this course even though I'm a STEM major. interesting subject and lectures overall.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--EXTRA CREDIT

reviews.comment:
*ENG 131* 
I learned a lot in this class, and to be honest I am going to miss it! I enjoyed her engagement with our readings and her encouragement for critical thinking. No tests, but we read three books and write essays: rhetorical analysis, and reflection essays.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Group projects

reviews.comment: Jade is an awesome instructor. Her classes exposed me to English works from all over the world, covering interesting topics. Her interactions in class effectively guided students to think deeply about these topics. As a history major student, I think her courses have inspired me to think about my history studies from a new perspective.

Very genuine and caring teacher who puts effort into the structure of her class. Every lesson was thought out and meaningful, and some were even foreshadowing others that came later. Workload had a decent amount of reading but was very manageable, and there were a couple of short essays.
Overall, this professor was very good at teaching, I feel as though I genuinely learned a lot of real world concepts. I would a hundred precent taking this course with this professor.
She is clear with assignment criteria and what you need to do to do well in this class.
reviews.rating_tags: Clear grading criteria--Gives good feedback--Lots of homework

reviews.comment:
I had Jade for my summer college writing class, which almost everyone must take. 

She made the assignments and grading criteria very clear and easy to understand. Jade also gave great feedback on all my essays and first drafts and is easy to understand in lectures. Through her lectures and emails, I got all the help I needed to do good.
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Clear grading criteria--Gives good feedback

reviews.comment: Interesting lectures, nice guy. Not hard class, just try not to miss the pop quizzes and study a lot for the exams. The final is optional but worth taking. If you do better on average on the pop quizzes than the final, that replaces your grade for the final. So do both bc you got nothing to lose.

professor was relatively nice. Lectures “aren't mandatory”, but there is far too much reading and work for a 100 level class. What really irked me was the TA. Nice enough guy I guess, but a ridiculous grader and gave ZERO feedback, no matter how poorly or well you did, so If you're with TA nick, drop. Unless you want to be confused 24/7
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Beware of pop quizzes

reviews.comment: Just took History 141 and prof seems like a very sweet person outside of class but the lectures were LONG, plus no visuals or helpful slides so u just need to write down everything while he's talking. There are mandatory discussions, graded quizzes every week, and unhelpful assignments. Would forgo taking this class if you're thinking about it.

I'm taking about history 141, it's not an option to choose. I took this class only for my gen Ed req. it is beyond me to understand why this gen ed (if done right) would consume more time than all of my major's classes combined for this semester. Like 80 pages reading a week. Graded quiz every week. Irl exams. Unhelpful lectures. Unhelpful disc.

I had 3 classes with Professor Olsen. 2 were traditional classes where if you pay attention to the key terms you'll be all set for your 2 exams (midterm and final) the essays were graded by TA's so that will depend on your TA. I did an independent study with him which while intensive was also pretty relaxed and not stressful while also informative!
reviews.rating_tags: Lecture heavy--Graded by few things--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: The class i took with Jon Olsen is genuinely the worst class I've ever taken at Umass. He's so boring and his lectures are horrible to get through. The final is worth 30% of your grade, and neither the final or mid term were we given a study guide, which is RIDICULOUS for a 100 level class. As a history major, and you should not take his classes.

(History 141) Don't want to hate on Professor Olsen, but he can be pretty condescending and his lectures are him talking at you with a slideshow of images while you just take your own notes. Grade breakdown: 10% Friday Discussion Quizzes (5 minutes), 20% Avatar Assignments (Essays)(5% each), 15% Class Participation, 25% Midterm, 30% Final. TA nice.

For a class that is low credit as this one, the amount of homework is crazy. You basically have to read a WHOLE book every week and the quiz which is every week is on the smallest details of the book. The classes are optional and they don't even remind you when there is a midterm or final. 10/10 do NOT recommend
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Lots of homework--Beware of pop quizzes

reviews.comment: I did more work in this 1 entry level course then all 3 of my 300+ level history courses combined this semester. Your required to read about a book a week, an additional 3 readings a week, and then a quiz at the end of the week on all of these. Lectures don't even line up with quizzes so essentially tests are based solely on outside readings.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Lots of homework

reviews.comment: Bro literally makes his lectures optional, then didn't send an email or have his TAs warn any students for his midterm. It's 30% of your grade, and no notice of when it is. Even the wrong date on his syllabus. Tons of reading, discussions are mandatory and graded pretty heavily.

DO NOT TAKE THIS CLASS. I'm currently taking this class and it is EXTREMELY reading-heavy and you have a quiz EVERY week. His lectures don't help at all, it's just pictured while he talks. Only take this class if you love history. 10/10 do NOT recommend
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Lots of homework--Beware of pop quizzes

reviews.comment: You'll have a small quiz every Friday in the discussion. Everyone has done so poorly that they changed the grading to "if you get 3 of the questions right you pass." The slides are only pictures. no midterm study guide. 5-page essay due 2 days before midterm and the prompt is released 2 weeks before due date.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Lots of homework

reviews.comment: Prof. Olsen is clearly very passionate and knowledgeable and he's a nice guy, I just don't do well with his teaching style. During lectures, he just talked at you. There was an outline at the beginning of each class with guiding questions but I found it very difficult to figure out what was important. LOTS of reading.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Skip class? You won't pass.--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Professor Olsen is a very nice guy. I also liked how the class included a discussion section as that was integral for me to really understand a lot of the material. However, his slides are kind of worthless, with them more being pictures than content. Luckily he recorded lectures but I do not know if this was for disability services or not.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Skip class? You won't pass.

reviews.comment: Professor Olsen for History323 is probably one of the best gen ed classes you can take. German History has always fascinated me, and he does a great job at teaching it. There is not a lot of work, only two 1200-1500 word essays for the semester and quite a bit of reading, but it is only for discussion and the midterm/final. Highly recommended prof!

I had ZERO historical knowledge from the beginning and was really nervous. Just managed to get an A and switched from P/F to letter grading bc of the online setting and intense note-taking/reading every week, wouldn't recommend this if you have a tight schedule. The lectures were really informative nonetheless, suitable for history lovers.

Every week new texts were assigned, + textbook chapters, I was not willing to invest so many hours reading for a Hist101 course (some students just looked up the summary to save time).He never offered notes,& this wasn't very helpful for me in deciding what was important to remember for the exams. He was kind but teaching methods were not ideal.

His lectures were the basis of the 3 quizzes you had in the semester, so you have to take good notes. Luckily, he provides an outline at the beginning of class to help organize those. There are also 5 books you read throughout the class and of those 5 you write 3 1/2 page reports. There is also a big research paper you work on throughout the sem.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Skip class? You won't pass.--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: I've taken two classes so far with Professor Olsen, and I really like the organization of his course. It's pretty simple and you can really learn a lot if you pay attention in lecture. History isn't my primary major, but classes like Olsen's are really useful for more social studies-oriented degrees - having a knowledge of past events is helpful.

Class was SUPER relevant to random classes later. It flies, I'm not a history person and this class was totally digestable. Get ready to write. And make a buddy. Olsen gives good lectures but they have maybe max 5 slides for those visual learners out there. The class discussions are necessary and useful. Reading the text bfore exams/essays a must.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Skip class? You won't pass.--Hilarious

reviews.comment: Professor Olsen's class was probably the best way I could have been introduced to history courses at the college level. His lectures are incredibly detailed and informative, and he clearly loves what he does. He's also really fun o talk to outside of class and I'm actually sad I couldn't fit another course of his into my schedule next semester.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--ACCESSIBLE OUTSIDE CLASS--Caring

reviews.comment: Olsen is a great lecturer, he made history interesting, and more importantly clear. The papers he assigned were defiantly not a walk in the park, however you are given plenty of time and if you have written for a history class before it will not be a problem. Tests are easy, and there is extra credit.
clear lectures, makes note-taking easy, assigned readings are interesting and tie directly into the points made in class.  would take him again.
I took his class in a TBL class so it was mostly group work. He lectured for a small part of it the rest was group. He answered questions well, and the TAs are very helpful and give lots of feedback.

An intelligent and wonderfully spoken professor- I've learned so much from her. She knows what she's talking about, and I fully believe anyone claiming that she's “demeaning” is just intimidated by her extreme and confident display of knowledge in her field. Maybe a bit hard to reach over email, but so caring and kind if you go up to her in person!
Spends class monologuing and barely lets students get a word in. Few readings, so if you don't like a text you're probably still going to have to write a paper about it. Grades pretty nicely though.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Lecture heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: If you are not willing to be talked down to or demeened by this professor stay far away from her classes.  Every statement and action is taken as a challenge to her authority. Additionally, her comments like "in the real world..." and " when you get real jobs and have to listen to a boss..." is unnecessary, we are adults not highschoolers.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Lecture heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: she made someone in my class have a panic attack cause she yelled at them for going to the bathroom. my class only got one grade back the entire semester. was late multiple times and was condescending whenever people tried to participate
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Lecture heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Professor Patterson is very intelligent and caring. Her class is an easy one, as long as you don't expect a great grade for just showing up. You need to do the work she assigns, but she is not a hard grader. She has a way of speaking that is slightly grating and can come off a bit condescending sometimes. She is very excited by participation.

Materials for this class were unclear and inconsistent with what was provided in class. Many parts of the syllabus were not the same as the actual expectations of the class.

Arbitrary policy changes and confusing grading.

I just wanted to write one of these to urge anyone considering Prof Patterson's class to PICK SOMETHING ELSE. She is awful.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Participation matters

reviews.comment: She lecture about random historical context and sit on her laptop all class. Felt more like a history course rather than an English one. There were like 3 essays the final essay was worth 40%. She was very very rude to my class. She basically called us dumb, said we dont know how to write and should already know this stuff. I would NOT recommend.
She does not seem to respect her students and was rude and condescending on many occasions. Also seems to enjoy embarrassing students in front of their peers.

While the class itself provides interesting information, the professor gets off track and trails off of the primary discussion and will lecture for almsot the entire class. There are texts that she requires to be purchased, but can be found online. I do not suggest taking the class if you cannot focus for the entirety of the 1 hour and 15 minutes.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Lecture heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: One of the least helpful classes that I have taken at UMASS. Showed up late to nearly every class, took attendance randomly throughout the semester and lectures consisted of random callbacks to topics that had nothing to do with what we were reading. Moodle page was bare, and we didn't even receive grades in Moodle the entire semester. Avoid please

This woman is just plain bad at her job. She comes to class and tells us absolutely everything about nothing important, and then the actual information we need to have is either glossed over or just not mentioned. I was sitting in class and she said "miss mam, are you hiding?" in front of everyone like i was a child. don't take anything with her.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: I have her for African American literature and her knowledge and passion for the literature we read really makes this class and her teaching special. She grades for few things but her assignments are fairly clear she just doesn't update moodle a lot so ask questions if you're confused and she'll gladly answer. Gives v helpful feedback on writing.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Inspirational--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: I don't feel like I'm learning anything in this class. She makes us read books and then in class just talks about her notes and thoughts about them; there isn't any actual participation. There's 3 big papers that you aren't given any guidance or information about and the Moodle isn't helpful at all, and don't expect an understandable email back.

Professor Patterson is one of the worst professors I've had at UMass. She just talks the whole class, silently reads from some book and then summarizes what she reads out loud. She also only takes attendance at random, and will not respond to emails because she says they aren't as important as her other emails. Super painful class (Eng 378).
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Lecture heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: I love Dr. Patterson. Her own research and perspective on literature are so interesting. She never assigns more reading than we can accomplish and her expectations are reasonable (maybe 30 pages between each class). However, she isn't very accessible outside of class and people struggled to connect with her, so there was not a classroom community.
Great professor, had no complaints. If you have difficulties with subjects in the class she would help you.

Her syllabus just doesnt make sense. Theres no themed units and its also not in chronological order. She reads directly from her own essays for the entire class. Like bro you can just send me your essay I dont want to be here at 10 am.

Once she read and edited her own essay for entire class. She mutes students during class so we can't ask her questions. Don't expect any engagement, inside and outside of class. Does not respond to any emails, had to email her boss to get in touch and she didn't respond to him. On last day of class I still had no grades. boringest mf I've ever met.

Professor Patterson was extremely knowledgeable and passionate about her class. Most importantly was the degree of care she showed to us. Seldom have I taken classes with a Professor that really worries about their students. She was accommodating and I think she did a great job in light of the COVID19 epidemic to teach us all and keep us engaged.

I don't quite understand the negative feedback expressed by others on this website. In my experience Professor Patterson displayed a lot of caring for her students and frequently opened up class for discussion where she listened intently to the views and opinions of her students. Just an all around great professor.

Prof Patterson is very condescending in the way she talks to her students which results in less student participation in lectures. The majority of classes are spent listening to her lecture and occasionally a few students if they are brave enough to express their opinions. I would not recommend this course unless you enjoy being belittled.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: One of the most condescending and rude professors I've ever had. She would talk down to the entire class like we were toddlers and would demand respect yet not treat us like the adults we are - even taking away being allowed to leave to use the bathroom or give our own opinions. One of the worst professors I've ever had to deal with.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Skip class? You won't pass.--Tough grader

reviews.comment: My experience with Professor Patterson resulted in one of the worst academic experiences I've had as an enrolled student at UMass. She teaches the curriculum in a very strict and indoctrinating manner, expecting unrealistic discipline from the students, even deducting participation grades for using the bathroom! I do not recommend.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Lecture heavy--Tough grader

reviews.comment: Professor Patterson seems like a really nice person, but her American Fiction class was the worst english class I've ever taken at UMass in my three years here. She is incredibly strict, incredibly harsh, her reading quizzes are absolutely impossible even if you read (I failed every single one) and her lectures are boring. Do not recommend.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Graded by few things--Tough grader

reviews.comment: Very funny prof that taught you everything you needed to know about the course and gave tests that resembled the cw/hw/lectures. No complaints and shes the goat.
Professor Perry was an amazing lecturer. She does give pretty challenging homework; however, it prepares you well for the tests, and she will always give you extensions if you ask.
Professor. Perry is an awesome professor, in her class you will feel welcome and will learn a lot.

I thoroughly enjoyed this class. If you don't attend lectures, the homework will be difficult/impossible to complete, but there are recording posted. A very fair grader and always open to question both in and out of class. Lectures themselves are very informative and easy to follow.

Professor Perry keeps class fun and engaging while getting everybody to understand material. As this is an intro Chem E class, Professor really gets people to understand what Chemical engineering is. I would definitely recommend people who are interested in CHEME to take this class to have a taste of what it's like.
Lectures were not mandatory but a lot of people showed up to lectures. Very caring professor and classes were interesting. Should show up to lectures yet they are recorded if you cannot show up.

By far one of the most engaging professors in the ChemE department. She really wants you to learn, and understand the material. Her homeworks could get tricky, but she was super helpful during office hours. She even allowed more time during exams than just 2 hours, which was very generous. She hosted coffee hours in hopes of getting to know you! :)
Prof. perry seems really nice though deadlines were pretty strict. Learned a little bit of Matlab. Class is pretty easy though.

Professor Perry is caring about her student who show determination to learn. Wasnt the best student by any means, skipped class and slacked off. She reached out twice and we met to try and work things out even after the semester ended, she walked me through different homework problems during break and single handedly kept me from switching majors
good professor. class was a bit slow at times and I skipped a lot of class bc I just didn't feel the need to go. still did fine tho.
reviews.rating_tags: Group projects--Clear grading criteria--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Class gets easier after the process flow diagrams/matlab/exam 2. Go to office hours in the CRIB, the homeworks (from like 3-8) can be super hard and take a really long time. Make a group to do the homework with. The exams are hard but she grades giving partial credit so you probably won't do as bad as you think you did.

This class is definitely hard and you need to put the work in to do good. Prof was incredibly caring and sweet, always making sure that her students understood the content. Even though the material was challenging, she made the class go smoothly with her patience and resources she gives.
Prof Perry is the best prof you can possibly ask for a Chem Eng major. She actually cares for her students and welcoming for all of us. Her class is relatively easy but she makes it so amazing.

ENGIN 110 is only offered in the Fall by Sarah Perry. Nevertheless,  Perry is one of the best professors of ChE. You will learn the fundamentals and some MATLAB, and she will also try connecting you with UMASS alums and researchers. Just make sure to start the HW early and make use of TA's and Perry's office hours.

The class was difficult, but that is expected in any engineering class. Sarah managed to explain many challenging topics very well. She cares about her students, as she hosts weekly coffee hours to try to meet each one. Moreover, she brings in past graduates to better explain to the undergrads their future opportunities in the broad major.

Perry is super chill and understanding and her syllabus explains the whole class. She made an effort to learn every student's name even though there were around 50 of us. 9 weekly HWs (25%), 2 midterm exams (50%), a group presentation and paper (15%), and an individual research paper(10%). HW is due Fri at 10 pm so make sure to start it around Wed.
She's okay. Very relaxed and casual.

Literally the best! I have no idea why her ratings are like this, she's so helpful! The class is pretty hard, but she's very accessible out of class and really takes the time to make sure you understand everything. She responds really quickly to emails and knows the entire CHE curriculum really well so she's good with general help as well.
Prof. Perry is simply amazing! She goes over concepts in detail, and she cares so much about her students! Would definitely take this course again, if offered. Rock on, Prof. Perry!!
Sarah Perry is an absolute queen!!!! She explained concepts very clearly and understandably for those new to engineering. I love her so much and she is one of the best teachers Ive ever had
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Respected--Skip class? You won't pass.

reviews.comment: Homework is very time consuming. If you don't do it over multiple days, then you're most likely losing your Friday night. Tests are also very difficult as in little to no partial credit. The book is equally as confusing. Your only way to get through this class is if you really have a thing for it, or if you spend hours at tutoring.

Prof Perry is the real OG. Her class is fun, engaging, a little tough, and really well taught. She also provides a lot of opportunities outside the classroom. Whatever she teaches you should try to take it.

Professor Perry is a fantastic teacher who cares a lot about her students. I was extremely satisfied with this class and learned a lot about the chemical engineering basics and future in the major. Highly recommended.
She is great person and overall  very effective teacher. This course is very ambitious and exciting. I felt like I learned a lot compared to most other lab based courses.

When she does teach, she teaches the concept very well. However, there were a lot of things that we had to learn from the textbook ourselves. Homework is extremely time consuming so it's best to start ASAP. The tests and exams are really tough, it makes you reconsider choosing chemical engineering as your major but it will be fine.
reviews.rating_tags: Respected--Skip class? You won't pass.--GROUP PROJECTS

reviews.comment: She flies through material and you may have to learn a lot through the book on your own time. Homework can be very time consuming for this class. Study hard and be ready tut in a lot of time for this rough class. Possible A is you study and know the material that she tells you to know.

Perry is a nice person but horrible teacher. She goes over the material quickly... Her homework is quite difficult... My Friday night is gone because of it. If you have a mistake in your MatLab code,  good luck because it is difficult to find the problem.  I will not recommend her as a ChemE  teacher.
Perry is a terrible teacher who takes points of "in spite". Teachers really hard material very quickly and needs help from the TAs on MATLAB. Has many class pets who are all equally annoying.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough Grader--Skip class? You won't pass.--LOTS OF HOMEWORK

reviews.comment: She was nice and taught well I suppose. If you fall behind, you're pretty much screwed. Prepare for MATLAB.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--LOTS OF HOMEWORK

reviews.comment: Prof. Perry is an amazing woman/prof./and human being in general. Her class isn't easy but is 100% manageable (even an A) if you actually put the work in for it. There are more than enough resources for help though, just going to lectures alone, she's pretty good at getting her material across. One of my favorite professors. She's a real people per

Professor Perry is one of the nicest professors I've had so far and she is willing to help her students succeed. Her tests were tough but if you understand the homework and the lecture material, you should be fine. She explained the class material very thoroughly and kept her students engaged during lectures. I would definitely take her class!

Professor Perry is a really nice woman, gives clear lectures, and is very willing to help her students. I didn't find the class that hard as engineering classes go because of how carefully and clearly she taught the material.
Will NOT answer emails. Will not facilitate class discussion. Will not give time to read required readings. Will not give any feedback, grades, or outlines on essays. Will talk a lot.

Phan's lectures are about as interesting as reading the backs of shampoo bottles in the shower.He is dull, rambling, and never gets to the point. He never gives feedback on anything, despite saying he would, and his deadlines are way too close together for the volume of busy work he assigns.Avoid this "class" unless you like boredom and frustration

One of the worst professors I've ever had. He never grades your essays or gives them back to you, so you don't have feedback on how to improve. Lots of readings and not enough time to do them, and if you ask a question in class, he talks about something else and never answers it. His lectures are so boring and uninteresting, do not take his class.

Professor Hoang Phan is one of the worst professors I have ever had the misfortune to have. His lectures are atrociously long, boring, and without student input. His assignments are seemingly designed to confuse and exasperate, being as long as his lectures and somehow more lacking in useful or interesting information.
reviews.rating_tags: Beware of pop quizzes--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Really nice guy but not the best lecturer, classes are pretty uninteresting but for a required English major/minor class you just have to take it. Assignments aren't too bad for the most part he does take forever to grade papers beware.
Would not recommend taking a class with this professor at all.

Professor Phan genuinely seemed like he knew his stuff and interested in the subject, but lectures were dense and rather boring towards the end. The course was overall pretty easy though, so if you need to take it for a requirement I would recommend.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: As someone who doesn't like to talk in class, he lectured the whole class, leaving no time for students to talk, so it was less stressful. He's a fair grader and my little participation did not affect my grade. He is so kind and is passionate about what he teaches. Also offered easy extra credit! Take this class!

I had Dr. Phan for English 115H and he was very knowledgeable and passionate about the topic. Lots of reading for the semester but you are only graded on three papers and participation. His only downside is that he is a very slow grader. We did not have a single grade until the last week of the semester. His grading is very fair and he was helpful.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--EXTRA CREDIT
Get ready to read--Lecture heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Professor Phan definitely cares about his students and makes an effort to connect with them. No quizzes or tests but a couple papers. The lectures can be a bit bland but its definitely an interesting class. Would take again. Assignments are to read outside of class then discuss during lecture.

Very little time is allowed for students to speak during class even tho it's seminar style? Lectures are very long and hard to follow, nobody seems to be engaged in the class. Everyday is a lecture, and I don't really feel like I've learned anything from this class, and opinions about works are discouraged if they don't align with professors.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Lots of homework--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: Phan is one of my favorite professors, if not, my favorite. I took the class on a whim because I needed the credit and also it worked into my schedule well. I did not expect to love the class so much. He is encouraging, engaging, and just all around an amazing teacher. 10 out of 10 would take another class with him.

Ive had 3 English classes with him&he was by far my favorite English Professor at Umass. He is super intelligent and loves what he teaches. His lectures are long sometimes but full of great information that can inspire students that listen. He's very understanding and always willing to help. He is often flexible with deadlines & very down to earth

Gives lots of helpful feedback on papers. Seems strict at first but soft at heart - usually ends up bending on deadlinespaper length. As long as you back yourself up in the papers, it's okay if you present ideas other than discussed in class. Long-winded lectures, always forgets to do discussion, but he loves what he teaches. Interesting material.

Phan is very understanding of his students and is willing to accommodate his class's needs. I learned more in this class than almost every other course at UMass, and he was willing to sit 1-on-1 with me to improve my writing.

Professor Phan is kind, funny, and extremely understanding of his students needs. Although his classes arent easy, his grading is fair, his assignments will help you to develop your close reading skills, and his lectures are intellectually stimulating.  If you genuinely love discussing literature, I would highly recommend Professor Phan.

I would not recommend taking this class. He stutters alot, which means it takes him a very long time to get his point across, and when he finally does it's rarely coherent. His lectures are long, make no sense, and are rather boring. He never helps with writing essays, though he thinks he does.  Nice guy, but definitely not a good teacher.
Not an English Major and got a B. Nothing in this class made sense.

Obviously intelligent and learned, but could not present material in an efficient and clear manner. Lectures were paragraphs and paragraphs of words. Type of essay he expects was not one anyone in the class had ever been taught how to write. Final was nearly impossible to complete it was so long. Overall very difficult class- managed a B+ in it.

Seems very smart, but I have a hard time understanding what he's saying, both because it's very complicated and because he kind of stutters and chokes up. Maybe performance anxiety? Pretty funny, but a little sarcastic.

Professor Phan is by no means an idiot, but he either doesn't know how to make the material relatable or just doesn't care. In lectures, he read off a wordy prewritten lecture as if each word pained him. When speaking to the class, he was incredibly condescending and rarely gave clear instructions.

This class almost made me not want to be an English major. He doesn't speak clearly and goes on tangents. He wants you to write about the books exactly the way he thinks about them. Nice guy, but awful professor.

He knows the material very well, and he prepares very well for his lectures. He also has a sense of humor. It was an easy class as long as you do most of the reading and attend almost all of the lectures. However, my one major complaint is the final. Too much writing, too little time, and he got pleasure out of students' struggling.

He's obviously quite intelligent and well-read, but he's just not a good teacher. He is terrible at speaking in front of a class, yet he insists on lecturing on EVERYTHING instead of letting the students have an actual discussion. Good books, though.
The material is horrible, very boring and hard to understand. The classes itself are boring too.

He knows his stuff but he doesnt know how to teach it. Talks very fast and is uncompromising about slowing down or repeating what he's saying. I stopped going to lecture and just went to discussion and I did fine.

He is a brilliant man who has an amazing depth and range of knowledge in his subject, with a passion for this subject to match.  He is a terrible teacher. He is obtuse and confusing. He does not actually listen to the student?s questions and comments other than to pick up on key words and then answer the question he thought was asked, or respond

Challenging but rewarding. Take the time to do the readings and listen very carefully to what he says in lecture. Very intense, can be unsettling, but if you get him to warm up you see he's just VERY enthusiastic about his material. Only take him if you are ready to work, he expects a lot. If you do the work, though, it's worth it.

Kinda boring. He likes to teach though. When he asks questions there is almost always silence mostly because nobody knows that he just asked a question. A lot to read. If you do it right, you don't have to read all of the books. He is a little soft and he stutters and says um a lot. If you ask questions he will like you. Good at getting papers back
Bogdan is the goat. Great dude who wants to see his students do well.

actually in 462 - he's super sweet but I have a hard time actually learning. he tries to engage with the class and is super sweet and kind but doesnt employ an effective teaching style - its just not conducive to learning. tons of readings but you can get by with just skimming them. fair grader but exams are kind of hard. no final.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Group projects--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: Bogdan is the nicest and most understanding professor at UMass. His lectures are a little boring, there's two exams but overall very manageable. He's just a chill guy.

He's great! Class can get somewhat monotonous but Bogdan will definitely go out of the way to make his students feel comfortable. The group project is interesting and he is a very fair grader so I would say go for it!
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--EXTRA CREDIT--Group projects

reviews.comment: I mean, it was ok. I don't think I really learned that much even though I was interested in the topic. The exams were not too difficult and he scaled them a ton. He assigns a semester-long group project which is difficult and sucked because my teammates didn't do anything (not his fault). Material is easy enough if you read the assigned readings.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Graded by few things--Group projects

reviews.comment: Super thick accent, can't understand what he's saying ON TOP OF HIM WEARING A MASK. Lectures and slides are not helpful and I didn't learn much at all. Tests had things not even discussed in class and he didn't really make an effort to help. 2 exams and term long project that has no guidelines and is simply not appropriate for undergrads. AVOID.
reviews.rating_tags: Graded by few things--Test heavy--Group projects

reviews.comment: He is a great guy with a sense of humor. He definitely tends to get a bit distracted in class, and his slides arent great, but the concepts are easy, and he grades very fairly. If you do the readings and put in the work you will do just fine! He does have a thick accent, but youll get used to it and his English is very good.
reviews.rating_tags: Accessible outside class--Get ready to read--Participation matters

reviews.comment: Thick accent, tends to ramble during lectures and the second half of the class is all about this group project that is way too difficult for an undergrad course. Concepts from readings appear on exams and the case studies are boring. Take a different class to fulfill this requirement if you can.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Graded by few things--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: Really nice guy, concepts in the class aren't very difficult to understand. Attendance is mandatory so make sure to enroll in a time that you'll go to class most days. I recommend doing assigned homework readings, they're long and boring but give you a much clearer idea of what's going on in class and why you're doing it.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Skip class? You won't pass.--Group projects

reviews.comment: This class was a lot of fun. He regularly integrates interactive ways of learning, such as simulations and games. Class format and grading are very clear. Some exams, quizzes, a group project to create a sustainable company, and some discussion questions. Not too hard of a class, just need to put in some effort. Highly recommend.
Bogdan is an easy grader as long you participate in class. Classes are about 70% lecture and 30% group work, and most readings aren't necessary.
Overall a great teacher. Not a tough grader. Lectures a lot. Ukrainian. Has a deep accent. Has a sense of humor.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--GROUP PROJECTS--LECTURE HEAVY

reviews.comment: Material is pretty boring and Bogdan has a tendency to stand in front of the class and lecture for 75 minutes. While he can certainly be boring at times, he truly cares about students. The class isn't very demanding. 2 tests, a handful of quick HW assignments and a project. If you show up and are a good test taker class should be a breeze.

Boggs is the man. He and the material are certainly boring, but he is a great guy. Fair grader, cares about the students, and expects participation. Taking notes and doing EVERY assignment he gives should be enough to barely get an A. You never know what might show up on the exam, and group work is heavy. He is a gentle giant.

The class was boring and uninteresting. I found the lectures little help with assignments or tests. All homework questions and most test questions were straight from the textbook. I didn't like the question "What was the guest lecturers name". The test is curved; but he never tells what the curve is. Don't know how much till your report card comes.

Tests are worth 75% of your grade. Considering how poorly lectures prepare you and how little information there is about what will be on the exams, it's not a shocker that people do poorly. Never had a class that makes it this difficult to do well.

Other than the pointless iClickers, not worth going to class. Posts the powerpoints online but speeds through them in class it is 100% impossible take notes. Tests are 150 out of 200 pts which is ridiculous and are hard even if you study. The study plan and online homework is no help. Constantly complaining about people on phones.

The course is out of 200 points. 150 come from 3 exams (50 points ea). Exams  are multiple choice, 50 questions. He does not scale. This was an 8:30am course and iClickers/attendance were required (20pts); My Management Lab homework  30pts. His lectures were poor and unhelpful. He mumbles everything so you can't understand a word he's saying.

Nice guy but lectures are tough to sit through. Syllabus says up to 10 points of extra credit (class is out of 200 total points) but we haven't had many EC opportunities. Test are really hard and random and he does not scale.
150 of the 200 total points come from the exams, which make little to no sense. Awful class, awful professor.

This class was frustrating overall. About half the classes were cancelled, which led to us skipping an entire unit. Lectures were often unengaging. Slides were not posted, discussions were inconsistent, and the course felt disorganized. The textbook was a fictional novel that felt rushed. Overall, not a great learning experience.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Lecture heavy--Test heavy

reviews.comment: Get ready for a lot of notes! There are quizzes, a mid term, and a final. Additionally, our "textbook" is a historical fiction novel. Overall, the lectures are a bit dry and your hands, fingers, and eyes are tired afterward, but I enjoyed the class and would take it again if necessary.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Lecture heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: For Anthro 150 she never posted slides, no midterms, just online quizzes you can look answers to. A few essays and an easy final that make up your grade. Really not that bad...

I'm a senior STEM major taking this class for a gen ed and this is the first ever class I've had where a professor doesn't post the slides...I type fast and even I can't keep up with how fast she goes over the slides in class. The content is very easy. A high schooler could teach the class since she only just reads off the slides the whole time.

I loved her. My only complaint is use of class time. She would often have to continue lectures next class because she ran out of time. "Textbook" is a realistic fiction novel. There are many readings, but I got a 97 in the class without doing any. Extra credit on every test besides the final which isn't cumulative. Easy if you're a good note taker!

Extremely BORING lectures. Took this class with some friends for 2 Gen-Ed's, but recommend another class/taking the Gen-Ed's separately. Extra credit on every quiz but the essays, worth 40% of the grade, require multiple out of class readings + reading a 200 page book + immediately understanding how she grades.

I enjoyed the information I learned because it was interesting. She gives a lot of space for error. This class has a lot of work, you have to study for the final while also writing a paper for it. The quizzes don't come with study guides and the notes are only accessible during class or if you watch the Echo360, this isn't helpful. Didn't love it
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--EXTRA CREDIT

reviews.comment: Archaeobotany sounds interesting but she made it feel so boring. She's nice enough, but very quiet and unengaging. The amount of group projects and presentations in this class was ridiculous, like one presentation taking up the whole class every week. It felt like most of the class was us teaching each other and her sitting to the side.

The only professor I have had in my three years of being at UMass who doesn't upload slides onto Canvas before, or after the lecture. The final exam is the only exam there is, but don't get fooled by it, because it is cumulative. TOUGHEST gen-ed class ever.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Lecture heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Great lecturer but goes VERY fast, so its hard to take good notes. She doesn't upload the notes either, which doesn't help. For a gen-ed its a very interesting class and she does a great job evoking interest in it. There are two papers and a presentation, along with quizzes, attendance, and a final for your grade. Overall easy class, good lectures.

Professor Pacyga's class was really interesting and I enjoyed the content that was taught throughout the semester. Lots of information on North American natives that they dont usually teach in high school, that being said I really recommend taking this course in order to fill the Diversity U.S requirement.

ANTHRO 390M (making plants work): Prof. Pacyga is a pretty boring lecturer and relies on slides, but doesn't provide them to students. But, she's only ~1/2 of the class. Other than that, this class is AMAZING. I highly recommend taking it. Very high level of participation required, but material is sooo interesting and the readings are applicable!!!

This class was beyond boring. She spent the entire time lecturing reading entirely off her slides. She also seemed completely uninterested in her own course material. Quizzes required a huge amount of memorization. Two papers that were pretty easy. She responded to emails quick. Recorded lectures but didn't post slides. Boring and bad class.

I know a lot of people did not like the way she taught the class, but besides boring lectures she always reached out to emails fairly quick for help. Her quizzes require lots of memorization but the set up of them are nice, there is a bunch of extra credit throughout the quiz. Weekly discussion assignments were easy and attendance wasn't mandatory.

Class was easy, didn't even need to go to lectures because they were recorded. However, she refused to post slides so you would have to watch each 50 minute lecture. Her lectures she just completely read off the slides, extremely boring. Lots of memorization needed for quizzes.

Her slides weren't always the best, and there was quite a bit of OWL HW, but she gave tons of extra credit and had a great exam drop policy. Make sure you don't leave through the front door in the middle of class if you wanna step out, she WILL call you out.

You 100% get the grade you deserve in the class. Extra credit opportunities, and if you fail an exam the grade can be replaced by the final exam grade. Do not whisper to your friends, she will notice and call you out.
I love her she gives extra credit
reviews.rating_tags: EXTRA CREDIT--Clear grading criteria--Gives good feedback

reviews.comment: Great and clear lecturer, went over things at a good understandable pace. The exams were pretty straightforward you just really have to put in the time to study outside of class. I am not a chem person but would definitely take her again. If you took AP chem you'll def be fine.

Good professor but sometimes hard to hear. 
Doesn't like when people are talking while she's lecturing.
Always glad to talk to people
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Clear grading criteria--Lots of homework

reviews.comment: Sharon was great! She genuinely cares about everyone's success. The slides and lectures were very clear. OWLs can be time-consuming, but they're good review. The practice exams are pretty much identical to the real ones, and the extra credit is generous. Don't have side conversations during class tho since she will definitely call you out

Chem 111 is hard, but Sharon makes it a lot easier. Her lectures and slideshows are really easy to understand, which can't be said for the other teachers. The owl costs money, and there's a lot of homework, but every other Chem 111 teacher has to assign the owl homework too.

Lectures can be fast but concepts are solidified doing the HW. HW is long but good practice and straightforward.Exams are very important but are practically identical to practice exam. Was out sick for a month - she was v kind & understanding and responded to emails immediately. I think anyone can get an A in this class - I just got sick.
reviews.rating_tags: Clear grading criteria--Caring--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Prof Qin did an amazing job organizing her presentations and conveying the content clearly. She provided many additional resources and some opportunities for extra credit. You can tell she really cares about teaching and takes student feedback seriously.

Gen ed class so this grade is more a review of the class than the teacher. Doing all the homework and paying attention during lectures is crucial to your grade. I forgot there was lab homework until the last week of class and lost like 5 points of my grade. You're required to use an Iclicker and spent 100 dollars on OWL. >:(
reviews.rating_tags: Clear grading criteria--Lots of homework--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: Sweet professor. Lectures were really boring, but her slides are great to review after and very information-packed. Heads up, she uses iClicker, but she drops some of the points if you miss a few classes.

Thorough lectures but sometimes a bit hard to understand. LOTS of annoying OWL homework, but it is admittedly good practice for the test. Overall not a bad professor, but its genuinely hard to stay awake in her classes... they are so incredibly boring.
reviews.rating_tags: Clear grading criteria--Lots of homework--Test heavy

reviews.comment: The professor offers packed yet effective lectures and provides many resources. Some exams are graded out of 104 points rather than 100, which gives opportunities for extra credit. Practice exams are very similar to the actual exam. An A is more than obtainable if you're dedicated.

Sharon is such a sweet professor. Chem 111 was difficult for me but if you put in the work you will do fine. Homework through OWL for every chapter which can be very time consuming and not that helpful for exams. 3 total exams plus a final. She gives practice exams for the first 3 and they are basically identical to the actual exam.
She is a great professor and I liked her teaching style a lot. 111 is an easy class  but you have to go to lecture to fully understand everything.

She's great professor and explains concepts in an easy-to-understand way. Lectures can sometimes be a bit boring, but I personally found that she over-explained certain concepts. She taught at a good pace overall, and exams are all fair multiple choice. Definitely do the practice exams, and you'll be fine as long as you keep up with the workload!

Not a bad teacher, it's the content that's difficult. If you rewatch the lectures and do the OWL homeworks, this class is manageable. PLTL for extra credit, final replaces lowest scored test if it's higher than the averages of the other exams. Go to SI sessions if struggling, and practice exams are very similar to real exams, so really study those!
Exams worth 60% of your grade. Good luck if you're taking any other classes w this. Incredibly time consuming
So sweet and actually wants her students to participate. Highly recommend doing the practice exams before each test and reviewing the OWL homework. If you put in the effort, you'll do well!
She is a good teacher and explains concepts well. The hw is the same as the exams and there are 4 exams.

Professor Sharon is SO fantastic. If you need to take Chem 111, take it with her. Exams are super fair as long as you lock in a lot. Success is possible; in fact, you may even exceed your expectations.

Sharon was a great teacher for Chem 111. The homework helped me to learn what the material was, and the exams were multiple choice, with no surprises from what we learned in class. Homework and exams were basically the same thing. She was accessible during office hours, and there was a lot of support in SI sessions.
reviews.rating_tags: Amazing lectures --Clear grading criteria--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Great teacher

She also goes by Sharon. I thought Sharon was a great teacher who was funny and caring. If you show up to class, pay attention, take notes, do the Owl homework assignments this class should be pretty chill for you.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Lecture heavy--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Honestly one of the best professors at the entire school, she was kind and approachable and even at times a little funny. Her exams are directly related to the practice exams, her lectures are easy to follow and comprehensive.  at times she may go fast but she posts all her notes so there is no issue finding out parts your may have missed.
Worst professor ever
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Test heavy

reviews.comment: Her tests are so much easier than the other professors and only have multiple choice whereas the other professors have fill in the blank. Attendance is mandatory for iClicker. Her lectures are boring but you don't have to pay attention because she records her lectures and posts the notes. She doesn't like when ppl talk during lecture.
If you are a good test taker and have a good hold on chem, extremely easy class. outlines very clearly what is going to be on exams. homework is essential, really reinforces the content

sharon is great and really loves the subject. she moves a bit fast for me but explains topics well and you can tell she cares. practice exams are similar to real ones and she will do some fun experiments in front of the class sometimes. chem is a hard class regardless of your teacher, take her over hanz for sure. go to sis, youll be fine

Class is difficult but because of the amount of material, not the teacher. If you did AP Chem you will be fine. If not, definitely check out TA meetings and extra help opportunities (what saved me). Your worst test grade gets dropped if you do well on the final. Be ready for lots of homework.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Test heavy--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Lectures were clear and easy to follow. The class before exams was review and exactly like the test. If you took chemistry in high school you will easily do well. Use OWLs to study for exams. Lots of extra credit. Great class!

Sharon is a great professor! Most of the info covered in Chem 111 is material I already knew from basic high school chem, so the course was not hard. Prof can be a bit strict about students whispering in class, but besides that she is a good lecturer
Her teaching style is very good and helpful!

With all due respect to her, she made learning chemistry a lot harder than it should be. Practice tests are not like the real tests (at all), she gives very misleading information about the said tests, the final exam was very uneven with course material, and owl homework's very rarely reflect the test. Hard to contact as well.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Test heavy--Graded by few things
