reviews.comment: She is a very meh professor. I relied on redoing OWL homework, doing the practice exam twice, and going to SI sessions to get A's on exams. Her office hours and TA office hours aren't super helpful, and her lectures were boring. Go to the lectures tho b/c if you go to more than you get extra credit points at the end of the semester.

Goated. Lectures are great, slides helpful in and out of lecture time. iClicker questions for attendance. Reasonable homework load, late submissions allowed. Exams are similar to practice, she's very explicit with what wants us to know. Never really talked to her outside of class but she seems nice.

Chem is just hard in general.60%of your grades are from exams so be sure to do decent on them if you want a good grade.I don't think she's a bad professor I just don't think her lecture style is for me. She has very neat notes and is very accommodating when sick during exams. Join pltl it helps with your grades and studying. Practice owls questions

She goes through the material very fast and doesn't answer questions in class. She gives some extra credit points, but to do well in this class, GO TO THE SI SESSIONS AND TA SESSIONS!!! You have to put a lot of effort into the class to do well. Good luck if you have her I'm praying for you.
She was good I just hate chemistry. Still didn't understand it after finishing the class but I passed so yolo

Chem is objectively hard, the TAs she picks for the labs make it even worse. She talks very fast and it can be hard to follow the lectures. Good with accommodations, although the workload is pretty heavy. Tests are like practice quizzes and attendance is mandatory but not always enforced (through iClicker).

Sharon is a nice person but not a good teacher. Her explanations in lecture are not very helpful and half the time the homework is not even something we did in class. Her lectures are also very fast paced so definitely pay attention or at least try your best to. I would take another teacher if you have the option.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Lecture heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Her lectures are useful if you are very engaged, she will repeat this over the course of the semester. Make sure you do decently on the tests because only homework, attendance, and labs are the other grade categories.

Sharon is honestly so nice and very smart. She gave so much extra credit. Lectures are fast paced but if you just do the owl homework you'll be fine. Her exams are all multiple choice and 70 mins for 25 questions and her practice tests are just like exams.

not the most exciting, but she explains everything super well and efficiently, and if you go to class and work hard on the OWLs, you'll be fine. exams are exactly like practice exams so no surprises. lab is a bit annoying but often you can finish 1-1.5 hrs early if you're efficient, and it's not very hard
reviews.rating_tags: EXTRA CREDIT--Clear grading criteria--Lots of homework

reviews.comment: It's chem so it's difficult but she is by far the best professor for chem. She gives mad extra credit and gives extensions and reminders for all deadlines. You need Iclicker but you do for most classes so.
reviews.rating_tags: EXTRA CREDIT--Lots of homework--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: You'll do well if you study. She explains everything fairly well, but going over your notes after class is important. Lectures are fast-paced, so be prepared. Once you get your concepts down, you'll be fine. She doesn't like any noise during her lectures, though. TA review sessions are really helpful.

She expects students to put in work and be respectful and if you do this you'll do good in her class. She gets back to students in a good amount of time and encourages students to reach out if they need help. In class slides are hard to understand sometimes though and big ideas are sometimes brushed over.

Take her out of the Chem 111 teachers. All her exams were 25 multiple choice (3 midterms and 1 final) and the questions were just like the OWL questions. Be prepared to do lots of OWL questions, don't cram it. Attend the TA Exam reviews- the exam questions are exactly like them, sometimes the exact same and was really helpful before the exam.

The lectures can be boring if you took chemistry in high school, but overall she is a fairly interesting lecturer who cares about her students. She usually reads off her slides but explains concepts fairly well when needed. If you do all of the OWL homework (there is a lot of it) fully and on time, the class will be a breeze.

Lectures are decently well made, but sometimes brushes past complicated topics quickly
Sharon's biggest pet peeve is not talking while she lectures, which you kinda just roll your eyes about

HW (Owl assignments) are tedious and not very beneficial. SI + practice exams are all you need.
TA reviews often have questions taken straight from the exam

This professor was good, but lectures are boring if you have good chemistry knowledge. Owl homework does the majority of the teaching. She provided one extra credit for the whole semester. Emphasizes not giving more/additional extra credit. Exams have many repeat questions from practice exams. She was also very cute and did chemistry demonstrations
reviews.rating_tags: Clear grading criteria--Test heavy--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Great professor that I can understand and follow the problem she does on the board. Although the only downside is sometimes during lectures she gets easily distracted. Otherwise would take again.

Sharon is a very caring person, and she genuinely wants her students to succeed in her class. The only thing really difficult about this class is that you have spend hours doing the OWL assignments outside of class, but the OWL assignments are really helpful for understanding content. Her tests are exactly like the practice tests too!.
Professor Qin's CHEM111 class is challenging but manageable. Attend lectures, complete OWLs, and use unstuck AI - it's a great study tool! Expect a fair but rigorous course.

Detailed lectures with a lot of material given for homework to master topics. If you do the OWLS and attend help sessions when you're struggling, you will have no issue passing this class. Professor Qin is very caring and wants her students to understand the material, she also does a great job keeping grades updated. Overall a great professor.

She expects you to have a lot of prior knowledge about chemistry, for me this was hard as I had forgotten everything from HS chem. She doesn't give extra credit. She isn't a very understanding person. If you choose her try to study up on chem before the class starts, that's the only thing that will save you.

She is super nice and caring. Her SI and TAs are amazing. Her lectures are ok but her slides are fantastics and clear and you will understand. I highly recommend her class especially if you've already taken chemistry. Even without I think you'll do great. The practice exam is identical to the test so just do that.

I am kind of bad at chemistry but she is a good teacher TAKE HER ADVICE & you will do very well. You need to dedicate some time to review the lectures & do the OWL the practice exams are kind of accurate, anyone mad just didnt do their work and never studied. She does take iclicker attendance and its only there to boost your grade. She is my queen.

She teaches well and explains all concepts nicely. If u listen well in class and make notes u are definitely going to do good in exams. There are 4 exams total throughout the semester including the final exam. Exams are very similar to the practice exams with easy questions.

She's not awful but she definitely expects you to have lots of prior knowledge which can get annoying. She rarely goes over questions with the same difficulty as those on the exams, and even though the homework is harder than what she teaches it's slightly easier than the exam. You are going to end up teaching yourself most of the content.

Not too bad of a class but it's a ton of work especially for a gen-ed. She grades attendance so you have to go but if you just do the owl while she lectures and pay attention to when she gives an iclicker question you will be fine. Also spam the practice tests because they're almost identical to the real thing.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Lots of homework--Test heavy

reviews.comment: Sharon thoroughly explains every morsel of information. Her lectures can be dense, but she often uses other tools like in-class experiments or videos to demonstrate a concept. Missing lectures can be difficult especially when it comes to math-heavy chapters because she doesn't post completed notes so you won't have worked out solutions.
Great professor, just listen in lectures you will be fine!

This course is easy for those who like chemistry, but for those who don't I would advise against it with Qin. The slideshows really aren't bad but there is a ton of information and she expects it to be reviewed outside of class. However, the practice exams are exactly like the real exams, which made it very easy for me.

The class isn't bad, it's just the fact that tests are worth a lot of your grade. I have never been good at chemistry or a good test taker. When I asked her for help or tips on how to do better, in short words she just said to do better on the tests.

Lots of homework. Attendance is graded enforced by iClicker. Expects you to learn information before class on your own, but no one does. 4 exams, exactly like the study guide. Don't sit near the front because if you make a whisper she will pause the entire class to ask if you have a question.

CLASS: CHEMISTRY 111 | SEMESTER: SPRING 2024 -- Professor Qin is informative and caring. Her lectures are helpful, and she answers all questions but will stop the class for the slightest sound. Attendance is "mandatory" if you want the iClicker points. The OWL homework is exceptionally long. Also, there are four exams, and they are pretty fair.

There are homeworks on owl. There are three mid term exams and one final exam. All around 23-26 questions. You can join a PLTL for 1.5% extra credit on final grade. Iclickers are important for attendance and she only wants physical iclickers. IF YOU MISS ONE EXAM YOU AUTOMATICALLY FAIL!!!! It doesn't matter how well you do in the class.
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Lots of homework--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Just no. She is so cold and it's clear she doesn't care about her students in the slightest. That made it so hard to seek help and suceed. Im a STEM major and an A average student, but this class was something else. Trust me, avoid her if you can
As long as you do all the OWLs, attend review sessions, and actually try and study you will do well. I ended with an A doing these things and you can too.

Took her once and had to retake. She makes the course and its material a lot more difficult to comprehend and practice. It felt like the exams and OWLs were not representative of what she was lecturing, and if it was, she would hardly lecture enough on the important material.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Take her repeated advice about how to pass her class! Time consuming but because of the quantity of info, not the way she teaches it. She can tend to go fast. She was very kind in interactions. She will stare down groups of people talking while she's lecturing.
As long as you keep up in the class, put in the work, complete and use OWLs to study, you'll recieve an A. Plenty of extra credit, attend PLTL and go to review sessions, they really help.
she was good, just not my learning style
Farty teacher

She wasn't the most engaging professor, but she made her points clear. Her exams were exactly like the practice exams. Chem111 was overall a super easy class if you did the homework, and took notes in class. She did get upset when she heard people talking, and would pause the lecture, but overall it was a breeze.
Unnecessarily difficult. Assigns a ton of work that is not helpful and is insanely test heavy

Lecture slides are self-explanatory and extremely helpful in understanding the content; she does a good job of explaining each point, even if she does move at a faster pace. The owl homework reinforces the material and over-prepares you for the exam. GO TO TA EXAM REVIEWS! This is how I got an A. The exam reviews are basically the same as the exam.

Sharon is great I would recommend her if you need to take Chem 111 for any reason. She is very understanding when it comes to personal issues and gives occasional opportunities for extra credit. Exams are tightly timed and there is a substantial amount of homework, both of which are consistent with any other Chem 111 course.

Stay on task, don't fall behind and you will be fine in Sharons class. The exams are almost identical to the practice exams, so if you do well in those you'll be fine. Sharon gives alot of chances for extra credit so always take those and you'll get a guaranteed A.

Overall, she's an ok professor. Lots of OWL homework and lectures are very boring but class is easy, especially if you took AP chem. Does not tolerate any talking during class and will stop class if anyone is talking. Exams are short, all multiple choice, and fairly easy. Worth taking for an easy A but be prepared to fall asleep during lectures.

The content was difficult, and lectures could be hard to follow at times. She tended to skim through some of the more difficult concepts. OWL homeworks were tedious and took up a lot of time, but once completed, did help with hammering in the understanding of concepts. Chance to get lowest exam grade replaced with the final exam.

Couldn't stand this class. You had to buy an iClicker for attendance and OWL for HW. OWL taught better than her. Lectures are incredibly boring with her reading slides word for word. Passive aggressive and stops class for the slightest noise. If you've done AP or IB chem you'll be fine. If not, you're screwed if you don't go to TAs or SI sessions

Sharon is not the most helpful professor I have ever had, mostly because when a student asks questions in class she answers them with a passive aggressive response. 60% of the grade is exam based, an iclicker 2 is required for attendance.
Sharon's a great professor, chem is just a really difficult course.  She does assign a lot of OWL homework, but there's a ton of extra help outside of class that can help with it.
She's nice. I really liked her class. If you're attending the lectures and doing homework on your own, you're good.

Worst class i have ever taken, worst teacher I have ever had. Lectures are mind numbingly boring and sharon assigns a crippling amount of OWL homework. She also has a fairly strong accent so lectures are even harder to understand. Generally does not seem to care about student success.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--EXTRA CREDIT--Lots of homework

reviews.comment: I enjoyed Sharon's class. She explains things very clearly and concisely and it is obvious she cares about her students, indirectly. iClicker 2 is required for attendance though. Expectations are clear. Not that difficult but it obviously depends on your affinity for science, especially chemistry.
reviews.rating_tags: Clear grading criteria--Lots of homework--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: I dont know why people are giving her such bad ratings. By far one of the best professors ive had. I think the  other reviews just dont understand what it is like to take a real college class. The OWLs are annoying, but really do help for the exams. The practice exams were almost exactly the same as the real exam. Made chem 111 really easy for me.
Passive aggressive

Sharon was a very sweet professor. It is sometimes hard to understand her because of the thick accent, but you soon get used to it. She does take her job seriously and seems like she wants students to succeed. She does mention "class policy" multiple times, so reading the syllabus is VERY important to know what is due when.

Exams are worth 60% of your grade. You have to complete and understand the owls completely to do well on the exams. Practice exams were almost identical to the actual exams. Make sure to go to all the lectures and SI sessions, those really helped.

This class definitely had a lot of homework but I felt that this class was very fair. The practice exams were very very similar to the real exams so the exams always felt fair. She also gave helpful extra credit opportunities and clearly wanted you to succeed. However, lectures were not the most engaging and I learned best by reading on OWL.
reviews.rating_tags: EXTRA CREDIT--Clear grading criteria--Lots of homework

reviews.comment: Lectures are not super engaging always but I do like how she goes through practice problems with the class. She often stops lecture if she hears people whispering, claiming they are a disruption to the class when in reality it is a lot more distracting when she spends 10+ minutes every lecture pausing for people no one notices anyways. Otherwise ok

Very fast paced, runs over concepts rather quickly and the slides are a bit disorganized at best. Grading is alright, she provides plenty of opportunities to keep your grades up even with low exam scores. I just wish I learned more in this course. OWLs teach you everything you need to know -- typically better than the lectures.

Sharon is a great professor who clearly wants her students to succeed. Her explanations are easy to understand and she lectures at a comfortable pace to take notes. I enjoyed her class and would definitely recommend her for 111!

Prof. Qin dosnt give out individual extra credit because everything needs to be even for each student, but she did give out a couple extra points thoughout the semester. Chem isnt fun and it can be challenging but she does her best to explain the concept and material. Theres 3 exams and a final, and owl homeworks are a big part of your grade.
reviews.rating_tags: Clear grading criteria--Lots of homework--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Ngl this class is a complete and utter disaster class and the only one to blame is professor qin herself. Lectures are mandatory and you have to drop 60 bucks on an iclicker. I would rather tie stones to myself and jump in the pond than attend another one of these horrific and painstaking lectures. DO NOT TAKE QINS CLASS

Sharon is a good professor, she is very engaging and tries her best to explain the material. There are many resources for this class if you are struggling, and Sharon also has office hours. I wouls say she is the best professor to have Chem 111.

She starts with the basics. Lots of material. Not tolerant of talking during her lectures. Exams and multiple choice. Pretty good at explaining the material. OWLs are pretty helpful. Has SI reviews and PLTL - recommend both. Exams are NOT cumulative. Final will replace the lowest exam if the final is higher than the average of the first 3 exams.

I dont like chem very much but this class was fine. Exams were entirely multiple-choice. Owl hw was annoying but mid way thru the semester she got so many complaints about the hw that she significantly cut down the amount we had to do which was very nice of her. Definitely do the practice test before the actual exam.
reviews.rating_tags: Lecture heavy--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: I personally learned more from reading the book and answering the owls than from listening to her lectures. She is super caring though. She made our Quiz 3 relatively easy, which I think is because a lot of people got low in the 2nd one, and she gave 4 extra credits if we watched 2 online videos. Answer the owls and attend class for participation.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Lots of homework--Test heavy

reviews.comment: I took chem111 over the winter semester and loved it. The OWL homework are lovely in comparison to mastering physics. She allowed us to complete any missing homework for credit which was a absolute god send in getting an A. The online labs were very difficult, but that was not in her control. Exams are nothing like practice exams, study everything!
The professor only cares about rushing through the syllabus and discourages questions as a result. The course is awful and the OWL assignments take ages to complete.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Lots of homework

reviews.comment: It's hard to get a good rep as a chemistry professor, simply because the subject is tough. However, Professor Qin does an excellent job. She is organized, efficient, and funny, but she does move quick! Generally, if a student were to complete the assignments, shut up and attend lectures, and complete the practice exams, they should pass.
reviews.rating_tags: Clear grading criteria--Lots of homework--Test heavy

reviews.comment: Exams weigh for most of your grade. She doesn't care about the students who don't have a well versed background in chemistry. Has very low patience when you ask for help or express concerns. She seems annoyed most of the time will always refer you to the TA if you need help.

Lots of OWL homework but you have unlimited attempts. You won't pass if you skip lecture. 3 exams and a final that contribute heavily to the overall course. Qin takes time explaining examples in lectures and provides clear and detailed lectures along with lecture recordings. TAs were not helpful.

Sharon always requires attendance which is annoying. She will stop the lecture if 2 people are whispering in the back of the class. The grading though was fair with short exams. There is a lot of homework but you have unlimited attempts.

You learn more from the insane amount of homework than her. Also, the homework is nothing like the exams. Prepare to study the homework for hours and then receive a barely passing grade on the exams despite getting 80-100% correct on the practice tests. Go to every class because a 100% in the attendance section will boost your grade.

Some might find Chemistry difficult, but Xueying explains the material extremely well. You just have to pay attention in class. She is kind and funny, but she wants the class to be quiet, so everyone can hear her speak. I think she genuinely wants her students to do well, as there are many extra credit options. I would recommend taking her.

Lectures are very fast paced and you have to be naturally good with chemistry to do well on exams. The exams are way more difficult than the homework and many times the questions on the exams have never been seen before in a single homework assignment. She definitely treats intro chem like a weed-out class. Might be intentional but it's awful.

If you are not 100 percent confident with chem, never take this class. I learned so much better from Youtube, or just by reading textbooks. I rather not attend the lecture, however, participation grade counts. Concepts are pretty simple but her explanation makes them very confusing. It has been a stressful semester just because of one class.

This class is so hard and it doesn't help that her lectures are confusing. Everything that you learn comes from doing the owl homeworks but attendance is mandatory so you have to go to lecture anyways.
She goes very fast in lectures and there's a good amount of homework. The tests are hard to do good on if you're not naturally amazing at chemistry, but most exams are exactly like the practice exam.
Hates when distracted in class, she's not helpful in a group setting but is ok when in one on ones. She is a nice lady, just a very overwhelming amount of work.

The classes go so fast and the tests are unnecessarily hard. She continues teaching no matter whether the class is understanding or not. Attendance is very important - and there is a lot of homework that comes with it.

Im a bit shocked at some of the reviews. She was a bit fast paced, and she did get annoying at times. But if you are pretty good with science you should be pretty ok in her class. Lectures were recorded, full updated lecture notes were available. What was even better was all her tests were multiple choice! Attendance is mandatory.

Frequently stops due to 1 or 2 people talking (wouldn't notice if she didn't).  Laughed at us for not knowing the answers to brand new topics multiple times, saying things like "this is a really easy question". Overall negative energy about the lecture. Exams don't allow you to show your understanding of topics, no partial credit. No practice final

If you're cracked at chem you'll be fine, otherwise, do not take her. Her lectures are fast paced and she always says "you should know this by now" and "this is very simple." She doesn't understand that not everyone learns at the pace she goes at. She stops class if she sees someone whispering; very disruptive on her part. Did not like her at all.

If you're amazing at chemistry, I would say take her if you want. If not, stay away from her classes. I learned nothing in her lectures at all. I took a PLTL class on the side for extra credit and I learned everything from my teacher. she goes way too fast and doesn't stop for anyone. I swear she doesn't want you to pass her class. stay away

do not even think about taking her for chem 111 unless you're an absolute genius. she expects you to know absolutely everything on the first day of teaching the lesson. owls take like 80% of the day to complete. she's so awful at teaching and understanding the students. she might look nice but she's praying on your downfall. disgusting.

Professor Qin's class was very rigorous and fast paced. Owl homework are tedious and take up most of your time. Owl textbook and problem explanations are more helpful than her teaching. She is very contradicting when teaching and very condescending if you do not know a topic. If you do not have a prior knowledge of chemistry, good luck. F dat B
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Worst teacher I've ever had. Be prepared to learn absolutely nothing from lectures as she races through topics and leaves you behind. Owls teach you way more than her but will also take you hours and a lot of raging to complete. Tests are extremely hard. The SI Sophia is a 100x better teacher. If you get stuck with her... THAT'S TOUGH!!!
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: I am a good student+put in lots of effort. Exams are 60% of your grade. Lectures from this professor will NOT help you, you must rely on OWL to teach you and for you to do well on exams. The only way you will succeed is if ur High School teacher taught you before she did or you put in maximal effort. Sad that $100 OWL can teach better than her :/

Professor Qin is very organized and reasonable, the only thing that I would say that's negative is that she goes really fast, however Chem 111 has a lot of material to go through in a short period of time. She is helpful in office hours, and make sure you really focus on the practice exams for the actual exams, they are usually similar.

This isn't an intro to chem class at all. She will zoom by class and tell you to memorize the material with no help. Additionally she'll go 100 mph in class and it'll be hard to understand what she's even going over. The OWL assignments are tedious and super answer specific, but doing it will teach you better than she can.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Lecture heavy--Test heavy

reviews.comment: Goes through too much content in a single lecture in a droning monotone. Doesn't answer student's questions. OWLs are miserable because I learn the content as I do the HW instead of in class (this takes me forever to do). I highly recommend taking this class with another professor. Do not take this class if you don't have to.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Lecture heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: This is the worst class I have ever taken at this school. Lectures are unclear and she races through them and the owls teach me more than her. The owls are so tedious and take so long to get a 100, so manage your time. Exams are hard. If you have a lot of background info on chem you will be fine.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Lots of homework--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: OWLS and Lectures are consistent with other chem classes/professors. Was easy to reach out too. Class was pretty straightforward. Practice Exams mirrored eExams. Has a final exam (exams are like 65% of grade)
reviews.rating_tags: Accessible outside class--Clear grading criteria--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: She was ok. She flies through the slideshow so it's kind of hard to take notes but they're posted online so you can go back to them. She is very insistent you don't talk during class and will stop class if she hears people talking. The tests were basically just the homework assignments with different values, so if you're good at chem, you'll pass
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Skip class? You won't pass.--Test heavy

reviews.comment: Sharon was a good professor. Sometimes she went a little fast in lectures and it was hard to keep up. I didn't take AP Chem in hs so this was my first time learning chem since soph year of hs, but she did a good job teaching all. She was really nice and understanding. There is a *lot* of homework to keep up with, but do it, it helps a lot.

I'm so happy that the stars aligned and I signed up for Dr. Qin's course! Her lectures are clear; she does an amazing job at breaking down confusing topics. Her exams are straight-forward (no curveballs), so if you do well on the practice test, you'll do well on the real one. She's so caring, and it's obvious that she wants her students to succeed!

Sharon is really great. She really cares about teaching and wants you to do well. iClicker is important so just dont skip lectures and if you do the OWL assignments it will be an easy A. She is fun, flexible, and her exams are 25 questions multiple choice. Such a caring person and a great prof, wayy better than the other chem111 profs.

Qin was fine. The class overall was fine. The tests were 25 multiple choice each and there are labs every other week. You should try to do the homework early rather than save all of it to the end, they can often be quite tedious. She really values participation and will often ask you to participate in the lectures.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Accessible outside class--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Prof. Qin is overall a solid professor, although I will say her lectures are pretty fast paced but thankfully she uploads the ppts/lecture replay video on moodle. This class has a very heavy workload imo, lots of homework but the exams are just like the homework questions/practice exam. if you put in the work (which will be a lot) you can get an a
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Skip class? You won't pass.--Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: Sharon is very nice and has pretty straight-forward lectures, but she moves very fast and if this is your first time taking chemistry you'll have to work pretty hard. The exams are all online evening exams and are taken on OWL (25 Qs multiple choice)
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Skip class? You won't pass.

reviews.comment: Her lectures are clear, but her lecturing style really frustrates me. She will also stop lecturing over the tiniest thing until whatever it is stops bugging her. If you have any prior chem knowledge, you'll be just fine with her lectures, but the OWL's are more useful for learning. Shame you have to come to class for clicker points.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Clear grading criteria--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: I absolutely adore Professor Qin. Her lectures are easy to follow and she emphasizes what is important and what you will need to know for the exams, which are exactly like the OWLs. Theres a decent amount of OWLs to do per chapter but if you do it as the lectures go its easy to manage. Make sure to do the Lab + OWLs

She is excellent at explaining things during lecture. She has a fairly thick accent, but I had no trouble understanding her. The homework can be a bit tough though. As for the exams, they should be easy as long as you attend/watch lectures and do the practice exams.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Skip class? You won't pass.--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: the exams are very similar to her practice exams and the owl homework was pretty easy as well.
The class was asynchronous, so as long as you can follow the OWL assignments, youll be fine
reviews.rating_tags: Clear grading criteria--Gives good feedback--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: Qin recorded her lectures asynchronously, so it was very impersonal but lecture watching was mandated for points. She did make intro chemistry very easy to learn, so I would recommend her.

I took AP Chem in high school, so I don't know how much my experience will reflect others', but Prof Sharon was a really good teacher! Her lectures were very informative (even though they were asynchronous), and the exams matched the practice exams closely. She really wants you to succeed; do the OWLS and study for the exams and you will do great!
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Amazing lectures--Caring

reviews.comment: If you've taken AP chemistry in high school, chem 111 will be no problem. Lectures are pretty straightforward, and you learn most of the material through the OWL problems. Overall a solid professor, there aren't any curveballs on the exams and she discusses the more challenging problems prior to the exam.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Skip class? You won't pass.

reviews.comment: Prof Sharon's lectures were long and packed with info, but she never threw any curveballs on exams. She was extremely accessible outside of class and made sure you had several ways to ask questions whether to her, the TAs or in SI sessions. I highly recommend her for Chem111 or literally any other chem class she teaches, she's awesome.

Professor Qin is a brilliant explainer of topics. She really knows the material and wants to teach you, but remote learning ruined my experience. All her lectures are prerecorded from what seems like another semester. And we don't have any real synchronous classes. I barely know her or my classmates. But she's great through emails and office hours

Very easy A if you've taken AP Chem. The topics aren't hard to grasp and Sharon does a good job explaining things. Good amount of OWL homework, you won't pass if you don't do it but there's unlimited attempts. Lectures are absolutely mandatory online.
reviews.rating_tags: Accessible outside class--Skip class? You won't pass.--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: Attending class is very important because that is how you will learn all the information and the homework assigned help master the content you learned in lecture. I think lectures are well organized and very helpful to my learning.
reviews.rating_tags: Respected--Skip class? You won't pass.--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: The material in Chem 111 is easy for me, but I learned most of the materials through OWLs not the professor. She has an accent that can be hard to understand sometimes; however, she is a very nice person and is willing to help you if you need anything.

Xueying was a pretty good professor. I would recommend going to lectures because she does give participation credit through iclicker questions. Her lectures are a little boring but are very important to attend to understand the material. The only downside to this class was the amount of homework. She gives a lot of hard and tedious homework.

Your homework will be incredibly difficult and near impossible to complete. Your entire worth as a human being will be based on being able to solve purposely overly difficult chemistry question created on broken software. the OWL assignments are an insane amount of work, and often the software malfunctions, earning you a 0 when you've put in work.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Get ready to read--Participation matters

reviews.comment: The class is just iClicker, 4 tests, online HW, and lab. The lab portion of the grade is easy to get a 100% on and will help balance out the grade. She has a policy to replace a low test score if your final grade is higher than the average of all your tests. Overall, her lectures can be a bit boring and sometimes hard to stay focused on. Nice lady!
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Graded by few things--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: One of the heaviest lectures I've attended at UMass. Chemistry is obviously a lot of information however it is extremely hard to understand and follow in class. Doing your Owls is one of the best resources for learning and the TAs study sessions also teach you more than you'll learn in lecture. The one upside is her tests are all multiple choice.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Skip class? You won't pass.--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: Sharon is the best Chemistry professor hands down. She explains concepts extremely well and prepares you for the test so long as you put the work in. If you have taken AP Chemistry before, take this class again and you will get an easy A.

I basically relied on SI sessions and learning from homework to do well in this class. It gets pretty distracting and annoying when Sharon stops at least one time every class to address one student who is talking with a friend at a low volume that no one else in the class notices. She seems like a nice person.

Sharon tries, but isn't always the best at explaining things. However, her PPTs are all very clear and posted online. Theres a lot of online OWL HW buts its very helpful (often more than lectures). Tests are just like OWL assignments and only cover material from class. You have to put in some effort, but the class isn't conceptually difficult.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Skip class? You won't pass.--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: A good amount of HW, but if you do them, then tests are ridiculously easy. Does have an asian accent, but it ain't the worst. Does have online videos of lectures. Attend for iclicker points If you had high school chemistry then this class will be more of a review. If you hate chemistry, just pay attention and use HW to reinforce the material.
I have to say this prof is soooo great, and thanks for her explanation so clearly, I got a good grade.

Sharon is nice and does her best. She does care about her students, but it's hard to teach a huge lecture. Chem is hard for me, but I've found that as long as I read the textbook on OWL before doing the OWLs, it's easy to work through and understand. I only went to class to make sure I got the iClickers. She's fine for Chem 112 too.

Sharon is a great lady. I never really paid attention to class because CHEM111 is essentially all of HS chem, and her lectures were kind of boring but as long as you study properly from her lectures and do the practice exams, you will pass easily. She gives extra credit on homework, iclickers, and practice exams, which is a nice grade booster!

If you took high school chem this class should be easy, just do all the OWL's because they're helpful and count for a grade. She also gives good extra credit, but her lectures can get boring so be prepared for that.
Each thing led to the next subject must master to understand following chapters
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--LOTS OF HOMEWORK

reviews.comment: Easy A class. Maam puts lots of information on the slides and they are easy to follow. iClicker class attendance is annoying but necessary to prevent slackers. Just study the lectures and do the OWL Homework and you can score 100%.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--EXTRA CREDIT--Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: She tries to go through slides quickly, so try to do OWL homework beforehand if you son't want to get lost. Beware of iClicker questions. If you speak during class, she'll catch you out, and she's really picky about the noise level of the class. She does occasionally do cool demos and gives out candy for halloween, though.

The professor seems to be the person to get blamed, but the fact is that chem112 is harder than chem111. I had Sharon for both and she's not the best, but her explanations can help if you pre-take the notes (she posts them on Moodle). Not too many clicker questions, so you don't really need to pay attention in class.

I am so lucky to have taken Sharon for chem 111. she knows her stuff and makes class fun and interesting. GO TO CLASS and don't rely on extra credit (that she gave a lot of towards the end) to boost your grade. always do the OWL homework, take good notes, and do the clicker questions in class. I so wish I could get her for chem112!!
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--LOTS OF HOMEWORK--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: Just do all your homework and never skip a class. Get atleast 65+ on all your exams and take your upper pyramid exams. You will be guaranteed to pass! I got 60, 60, 74.4 and 64 and still managed to get a B- in the class with the help of h/w and attendance which counts for clicker questions so dont take that lightly since she still takes off 10%.
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Skip class? You won't pass.--LOTS OF HOMEWORK

reviews.comment: Sharon is a really nice woman and cares a lot about helping her students succeed. Her accent can sometimes be difficult to understand, but if you pay attention you will be fine. The tests are mostly based on the OWL assignments with conceptual stuff from the lectures. She gives a couple extra credit opportunities. You just have to put in the work.
reviews.rating_tags: LOTS OF HOMEWORK--GRADED BY FEW THINGS--EXTRA CREDIT

reviews.comment: Sharon is by far the worst professor I have ever had. Her exams are spaced poorly and stacked at the end of the semester right before the final. The questions include problems that were not taught in class or in the OWL assignments or pyramid exams. Even iclicker participation correctness would range from about 14% to 40% for the entire class.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--LOTS OF HOMEWORK--Hilarious

reviews.comment: I hated this class. She goes too quickly through slides and expects everyone to have understood the material in a matter of 3.2 seconds. Pays more attention to side conservations (about chem) than people raising their hands. Be prepared to put 150% in this class.

Shes probably a really nice lady, but shes wicked tough to understand and if someone makes a noise in class shell stop and stare at them. And then continue by complaining that students dont pay attention to her. The exams are super easy, but she assigns a ton of homework for each exam. Definitely space it out!
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--LOTS OF HOMEWORK

reviews.comment: Sharon's lectures are fairly boring, especially if you know basic chem concepts. She pre-posts the PowerPoints on Moodle, so you don't need to take notes in class and focus on the many clicker questions instead. She tends to go very slow and stop if she hears side conversations, but her tests are super easy.
reviews.rating_tags: LOTS OF HOMEWORK--LECTURE HEAVY--Would take again

reviews.comment: Qin mainly just read off of her slides which were pretty wordy. She couldn't stand people talking so would stop the class every 10 minutes or so to stare at people to stop. There is a ridiculous amount of homework that is due before each test so try to break that up. Other chem professors at Umass are better at explaining tough concepts.
reviews.rating_tags: LOTS OF HOMEWORK--TEST HEAVY--GRADED BY FEW THINGS

reviews.comment: Sharon has no tolerance for side conversations, even if they are chemistry related. If she hears someone speak she will stare at that person until they notice, then ask "do you have a question?" and then talks for 5 minutes about how rude we are. Lots of clicker questions.

Overall, she cares a lot about her students and gives extra credit, but not a very large amount compared to other Chem 112 professors. Her lectures are quite dry, and she uses iClicker occasionally.  Do OWLs and clickers because she drops a lot which can boost your grade. Focus on every test as well because they're worth 60% of your total grade.
reviews.rating_tags: LOTS OF HOMEWORK--TEST HEAVY--GRADED BY FEW THINGS

reviews.comment: Sharon is a pretty good professor. She wants a lot of people to do well and she cares about the class. She gives tons of extra credit. She drops i clickers and homework. If you do all of the homework and she drops some homework then that is more extra credit!!!
Honestly she is not that bad. People make her out to be worse than she is. She gives loads of extra credit and is specific on her grading criteria. She is way better than Mentzen!

Sharon is a great professor! She really cares about her students' success and even though the course is hard she gives extra credit and other opportunities to boost your grade. Overall, a great choice.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Skip class? You won't pass.--EXTRA CREDIT

reviews.comment: Sharon is a great teacher.  People often blame her for the difficulty in the content, but this is out of her control.  Obviously, Chem 112 is very different from Chem 111.  You must UNDERSTAND the concepts rather than just memorize.  If you want to do well in this class, go to SI sessions and PRACTICE!  She gives extra credit in exams and the final

She's new to UMass, but she's not a terrible professor. Her lectures are dull but she knows the material well. SIs really help. OWLs are shorter than chem111. She gives extra credit on exams, including the final. Unfortunately, labs trade OWLs for lab reports. Clicker questions every lecture.

Her lectures are incredibly boring. I went for the first month and failed the first test. The rest of the semester I didn't attend class and instead of zoning in lecture, I studied the book and did much better on tests. That being said, lots of the info in the tests is only from lecture, not the book, and she doesn't put full powerpoints on moodle.

She's new to UMass and a really good teacher who cares about her students. She takes our input seriously and wants to see you succeed. That being said, class is challenging and definitely not an easy A.

Prof. Qin is a solid professor and has very interesting and productive lectures and is good at answering questions. The iClicker questions are very helpful, although there should be more of the for practice. Also, there are not enough question on the e-exams. They are difficult and getting just a few wrong does hurt your grade.
Boring. She's a very smart lady, but my God the lectures are excruciating. I hardly ever went to class because of it.
This is the hardest professor in my entire life as an Africa-america studies major and world government minor. Beware. Beware. Beware. And if you do not, at least please do beware.
reviews.rating_tags: BEWARE OF POP QUIZZES--Clear grading criteria--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: This guy seriously the goat take this class. Mad funny, absolute chiller, don't have to go to class and if you do every class is no more than 30 mins, no hw except two which are about movies you watch in class. I didn't have to go to class but he was just such a beast I went and he gives out a lot of extra credit.
Feng is super nice, and as long as you show up to class and study for the exams, you will do well.

Feng is the sweetest, nicest man, like an unc u root for. Gives out tons of extra credit opportunities just by showing up. Empathizes with college bills so you dont need textbooks, just show up to class and learn even tho its not mandatory, he is funny & so pleasant you want to come anyways. I wish I had more of his classes! Genuinely amazing guy.

Attendance is not mandatory but definitely recommended for the extra credit. Had him for 314 and 330; would take another class with him again! The only thing that is "hard" is studying for exams but if you make a quizlet it's easy, just time consuming. Everything on the exams is through the powerpoint notes. One of my favorite professors at UMass!
I took 330 and 334. Very nice guy. Lots of lectures. No homework. Exams and case studies/presentations. Relates and cares for his students. Very accomodating. Great classes to take
Amazing guy, truly wants you to succeed. Class is set up and easy to follow so you won't get blindsided by random assignments. He is funny and does his best to make sure everyone is on the same page.
Mr. Qiu is an excellent professor with a great sense of humor. The class is enjoyable to learn and the assignments are moderate. I think every student can learn something in this class.

Feng is great. Gives lots of extra credit opportunities and makes lectures pretty entertaining. Grade is made up of three tests and a group project, so make sure to actually go to lecture and study the study guide, and hope that you get a good group. He made HR fun, I'd recommend him.
Feng is a really fun professor. Should plan early for the group project.

Feng is a nice professor. He gives out a ton of extra credit in some of the classes but attendance is not mandatory. 3 exams, one group project make up all the grades. Exams are based on the ppt and videos that he wants us to watch. Then you should be well prepared. I love him and wish he has another major class that I can take in the future.

Professor Qiu is easily one of the best professors that UMass has to offer. He is laid back and relates to students very well. Attendance wasn't mandatory, and he puts his slides on Blackboard for students who missed class. There were 3 exams which made up a majority of the final grade, but if you study the lecture slides you should do well
Professor's approach is quite different from other professors
reviews.rating_tags: EXTRA CREDIT--Amazing lectures --Graded by few things

reviews.comment: I'm pretty sure this is a good professor, he's considerate of all students, and he offers plenty of extra credit opportunities. You can choose not to attend every class, but then you'll miss out on great class interaction. and extracredit offered in class. He was friendly, enthusiastic and helpful to all students. Highly recommended.

Feng is great! Intro to HR is a great upper level elective to take. There are 3 exams and 1 group project throughout the course, no HW. There are multiple extra credit opportunities when you go to class as well. He is very passionate and wants his students to get the most out of this course!

Feng is amazing. Funny & entertaining lectures, and A LOT of extra & easy opportunities for extra credit. 3 exams & 1 group project is your grade, but exams are all multiple choice and somewhat easy (I'm not a good testtaker but just study the study guide). The extra credits are only if you go to class but they add usually 1 pt to your final grade!

Highly reccomend this class. Interesting topics on HR and business in general. Two exams (study guides provided) and one group project. Professor is very upbeat and keeps classes interesting and interactive. Attendance is not mandatory, but sometimes he does extra credit in class!

I've never rated anyone before, but Feng is so good that I had to! He's a super funny guy and clearly cares about his students. If you really use the study guide he supplies before exams, you'll be good. Group project at the end of the semester isn't bad either. I find the content really interesting as well, great choice for management majors!
Great class for the upper level, he is super nice and the lectures are always interesting! Exams are not too bad if you pay attention in class and take good notes!

Feng is great! He makes the lectures fun and gives great examples of different aspects of material we are learning. You are graded only on 4 things, 3 tests and 1 group project. I would recommend going over his study guides in depth.
reviews.rating_tags: EXTRA CREDIT--Graded by few things--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Feng is the best professor in the entire world. He is an overall great person, and is always willing to help his students. Each one of his lectures are engaging and interesting to learn about. Feng wants you to succeed and will do all he can to see that happen. No homework, only exams, group work, and extra credit.
He is the best!
reviews.rating_tags: EXTRA CREDIT--Group projects--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Cool dude! Easy class!

Professor Qiu is awesome!! Attendance is not mandatory and he posts the lecture slides. His exams are only 30 multiple-choice questions and there is a group project at the end of the semester. He is a great professor and makes his class fun and interesting. Definitely take a class with Professor Qiu!!

Professor Qui is great! 3 exams (multiple choice/true or false), 1 group project, and a ton of extra credit opportunities. If you need an easy Isenberg elective with a great professor, MGMT 314 is a solid choice.
great guy would take any of his classes again
reviews.rating_tags: EXTRA CREDIT--Group projects--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Professor Qiu is a kind, great man. UMass needs more professors like him.

Feng is the man. Super nice, down to earth dude that is knowledgeable about the things he teaches. Lowkey funny too. Always appreciate his personal stories he shares every class. If you get the opportunity to have a class with Feng, do it.
reviews.rating_tags: Caring--Graded by few things--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Feng is a great teacher. He describes material very well and relates it to the real world. Almost every class is a lecture but attendance isn't required. Only graded on 3 exams and a final paper. Make sure to do well on those or your grade will suffer.

Great professor! Dressed up for halloween, exams are based of lectures and slides, show up so you can get all the information and pass your exam. Let us vote and decide if we wanted a team based project. Great guy 10/10
reviews.rating_tags: Graded by few things--Clear grading criteria--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: Really good lecturer once you get past the accent which I got used to pretty quickly. Hes clearly very invested and excited to teach. This class was definitely my hardest class, but he made it enjoyable.

Professor Chen is one of the best professor in the department. His passion for the subject is evident, and his lecture notes are dense yet packed with valuable information. He derives the equation from scratch, allowing us to understand prob theory in a deeper level. However, be ready for the 6 quizzes spread out throughout the semester.

You can get away with learning nothing new in this class. The first midterm is Math 235 material, and while there is a final exam, you can do a project (very loose grading criteria) that replaces a test grade. If you want to learn, don't take this class. If you want to do a math minor or something and need an extra course, take this class.

No rubrics. Even for the final project, worth 30% of your grade, no rubric. Terrible communication. Bad accent + no sympathy for students. Simple concepts for him that are confusing for students get a mocking chuckle or "that is trivial". Overall, condescending and meaningless conversation with him. The math department fails because he is there

Prof Chen is very difficult to understand which makes his lectures impossible to comprehend. Instead of a midterm and final, he made the midterm into 6 quizzes spread out through the whole semester which was a constant stress. The first quiz was okay. The rest of the quizzes were made impossible.

Nice guy, not the best professor. He just reads off the slides (which don't go into complete detail) and doesn't do a lot of examples. HW doesn't usually line up with the things taught in class, either. He's straightforward about what will be on the exam, though. Also, optional presentation to replace final (definitely do the presentation!!)

Qian is very knowledgeable and passionate about the material. He's also good about being available outside of class to give extra help. He does have a bit of an accent and he teaches from slides that skip a lot of steps. If you aren't in class and paying attention the course can lose you, but his actual in person proofs are easier to follow.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--ACCESSIBLE OUTSIDE CLASS--Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: Your grade is based on HW, midterm, and final exam (40%, 30%, and 30%, respectively). The midterm is easy because it's a review of Math 235 (intro linear algebra). You have 2 choices for the final, a take home exam or a solo/group project. I suggest doing a project unless you're a whiz at proofs. HW is easy and graded generously.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Tests? Not many--Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: Diff. Eq's is a challenging course, but Chen makes it bearable. Go to class and don't bother with the book. The tests are challenging, but his reviews are solid. The final was almost identical to the practice exam. Speak up if you think he is going too fast in lecture or if you didn't understand something; he will stop and help you understand.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--BEWARE OF POP QUIZZES--GRADED BY FEW THINGS

reviews.comment: Chen does not speak much English, you will have a very hard time in this class if you are not able to teach yourself. There is not very much help available outside of class. He reuses another professor's presentations which contains a lot of errors and skips a lot of critical steps. Avoid at all costs.
Thick accent. Once you get past that, he's not that bad. The material of the course is tough, so naturally the class is tough. Just please, do the homework. All of it.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--BEWARE OF POP QUIZZES--LECTURE HEAVY

reviews.comment: Professor Chen loves to teach and knows what he's teaching. The problem is that he just isn't a good teacher. He struggles to explain the math topics properly. The way he teaches is by reading off the slides, which doesn't work for me. The only good things about the class is that the topic isn't really hard. Definitely practice the old exams.

I could not understand a word this man said. I'm sure he is very intelligent and I have no doubt he has the best interests of the students at heart, but his accent is thicker than any I have ever heard.

The class I am in with him right now is the only honors section. His tests are extremely difficult, and his lectures are difficult to understand (VERY strong accent). He doesn't hesitate to help if a student asks, but his lectures consist of him just writing material on the board (not good for my learning style). Do not take this class with him.
Amazing prof, amazing lectures. Such a funny guy, who made learning just as fun!

Not sure why his rating is on the lower side—he's actually a great professor. If you attend class regularly and pay attention, this course can definitely boost your GPA. Most of the assignments and discussions are designed to help you understand the material, and as long as you show a basic grasp of the content, you'll likely get full credit.

Course was very disorganized and hard to follow. Grade is based off of discussion attendance, weekly reflection papers based off readings, and a final paper or presentation. Overall class was meh do not recommend.

Renier is a really cool guy. He assigns a lot of reading but the workload is light aside from that. His teaching style is very loose and at points it can seem disorganized but it works fine. He has a fairly strong accent but if you get lost just let him know and he'll repeat it. Overall a chill class that's very student-directed, I'd recommend.

He's a nice man, so I feel bad writing this review but his class was just bad. His grading system makes no sense. I tried reaching out to figure out how the iclicker grade worked but all I got was more confusion. Iclicker is half participation half getting it right. Exams and quizzes don't reflect the material you are learning.

You would think that a proper professor would be able to make quizzes and exams that reward students for reading the lecture slides and studying past quizzes or at the very least practice exams. Not Daniel Wang,I kid you not he would say one thing but make the test purposefully on the material you didn't study (even though I specifically asked him)

Funny and energetic professor, but flies through slides and is way too complex for a gen ed credit. Basically physics but just adds formulas to slides and expects you to understand with no examples or explanations. Textbook is not required but free-access and often clears up a lot of confusion from the fast-paced lectures. iClicker needed.

There is way too much material covered through the semester in this class just for a gen ed credit. All quizzes and tests are in person on paper, 5 quizzes and 60 question midterm and final. He is a very nice guy, but his accent makes him very hard to understand and he flies through the lecture slides. Attendance is part of your grade.

brings great energy to class, all slides are posted after class, the midterm was posted as a pdf for "study material," gives many practice quizzes online, only a few homework assignments and quizzes. requires an iClicker. had an experiment / demonstration at least once a week, sometimes multiple a class. but also this class is basically physics.
Does not upload slides on time

I was a bit nervous about taking this class, but the professor was an unexpected delight. His lectures were on the more engaging side, and he brings a lot of energy and excitement to class. His exams take up a very large portion of the grade, but if you study they aren't all that difficult. He also offers a lot of extra credit opportunities.
reviews.rating_tags: Accessible outside class--Clear grading criteria--EXTRA CREDIT

reviews.comment: I can't really remember much from this class, can't say I learned much. Took it for a gen ed and got an A, may or may not have cheated on the final though. Teacher's thick accent makes it difficult to understand. Sometimes seemed like the TA was smarter than the teacher, but the teacher wouldnt listen much to him. Regular class to me.
Some of the best lectures of all-time. He is a truly pure human being. The class is hard, though, for us non-science folk.

My boy Daniel Wang's ASTRO100 class is amazing. The first half of the year was a bit  dull. After the midterm all we talked about was cool stuff about the universe and it was so fascinating. His exams and quizzes are easy if you pay any attention, and he gave 6 home works all semester. He also gave 20 points on ur final grade of xtra credit.

This is the hardest class I've ever taken. Im pretty sure the tests aren't even on the material we learned in class but i wouldn't know because i can't understand a word this guy says. Do not recommend. Was not an easy gen ed

I wish I never took this class. Great guy, just not an effective teacher. So hard to understand what he's saying, and he rushes through slides. Concepts are too hard to understand alone, with no guidance on exams. Reading through my notes before the final and realizing there's no hope. Worst grade I've received in my life, and I went to every class

Rating this professor now as I realize I am screwed for his final in two days. The man rushes through every slide, can barely speak english and cannot explain anything clearly. Do not take this class, look for something easier and with someone who speaks english to fill your PS gen ed.

If you are planning on taking astronomy and Professor Wang is your only option, DO NOT TAKE HIS CLASS. I took this course thinking itd be interesting as a gen ed but after the add/drop period ended, it turned into just physics and chem. You cant understand the man plus he cant explain anything well at all. Really regret taking this class.

I hate to give him a bad review because he's a great guy, but if you are taking Astronomy do not take it with him as the professor. He rushes through slides, and is not clear with what he is trying to explain. He also has a very thick accent and is difficult to understand most of the time.

He is adorable and hilarious, which helps get you past his accent and the difficulty of the class. The lectures and notes make it seem as though the quizzes and tests will be easy, but they always have unexpected things on them that make them extremely difficult. The class is hard, but he does offer lots of extra credit opportunities.
If you are motivated, there is plenty of extra credit for an easy A. Probably not the easiest PS gen ed, but manageable

DO NOT TAKE THIS CLASS! You cannot understand a word this man says. He speeds through the notes. You have to teach yourself the class but if you want to take the time to do that go right ahead. Attendance isn't mandatory you only need like 30 iclickers but with his 5 iclicker questions a class you don't have to go to that many.

The professor has a very thick accent, but he knows it. On the first day he says, if you don't understand me, please leave and take a different class. Listen to him. He says a lot of things that are directly on the test but they are not written on the slides. His course is SO EASY as a gen ed. He drops the lowest everything Optional final, Got an A

Class was pretty easy...teacher is hard to understand at times, have to attend most classes (can skip three). His exams and quizzes are pretty easy if you pay attention. Just hard to follow sometimes but an easy A, especially if you take a lab with the class where he weights your grade 3 parts class, 1 part lab.

Best prof out there...this guy is awesome..he gives you so much extra credit...counts the best 3 of 4 quizzes....best 2 of 3 exams and the final is optinal...(final is the 3rd exam)....he also gives you 3 free class skips....awesome guy..take him

I LOVE D-Wang! He is ridiculously funny and does a lot of experiments in class to try and teach complicated concepts. The class can get boring at time. There's so much extra credit that if you literally do anything at all you will get an A. 2 exams; optional final. 6 online quizzes. Take it for a PS requirement!
an easy class. 2 exams plus one optional. !!! RECOMMEND IT
A GREAT TEACHER

Ever seen "Chuck & Larry"? Prof. Wang is the Asian dude who marries them. "Its like a circle!" Anywho, funny guy, very nice, and very interesting subject. Weekly readings from textbook, 4 quizzes, 6 Owls, 2 exams, final exam, TONS of extra credit. I strongly recommend this class. Also no discussion and prof Wang will make you laugh.

An absolute hero. Prof. Wang is the man, astronomy is tough but Wang makes it so much easier. This guy is hilarious too, he's got a good sense of humor. I cannot stress enough how great this class is.

I couldn't understand a word he said, and a lot of his test questions are excessively hard and come out of nowhere. But he has a great scaling system and gives lots of extra credit opportunities. He's a really nice guy and he tries hard (and occasionally succeeds) in making lectures fun. But I hated the class...sorry Wang.

Incredibly hard to understand, but awesome scaling system makes up for it.  Attendance is far from necessary, all slides from lectures are uploaded onto the course website.  Very little homework, that of which is online, is almost a guranteed extra 240 points at the end of the semester.  Also offers several extra credit assignments.

Incredibly hard to understand, but awesome scaling system makes up for it.  Attendance is far from necessary, all slides from lectures are uploaded onto the course website.  Very little homework, that of which is online, is almost a guranteed extra 240 points at the end of the semester.  Also offers several extra credit assignments.
So much extra credit, thank god because I cannot understand a word he says.
OH MY GOD! This man is so funny and entertaining and this class is very easy and I LOVE WANG!!!!! take it, EASY A for gen eds. and take it with WANG, cuz he's the easiest astro teacher there is!

oh my god, i love this man! he will make you****your pants laughing without meaning to, drops the lowest grade on everything, has take-home tests, its impossible NOT to get an A, plus the material is pretty easy and he makes it fun. GREAT TEACHER

Daniel Wang rocks my world. He made class fun and enjoyed every second of it, such a nice guy, hates cell phones and loves the stars. Just wait until you see him fly across the room on a wagon and a fire extinguisher! three words: take home tests

Pretty good. The focus of the class is learning about satellites. Labs are helpful. Open note midterm. Open note chapter quizzes. Replies to emails fast and very good at making accommodations. Actually read the textbook - makes a huge difference. Can sometimes be hard to understand and scatterbrained. Easy to loose focus in lectures. Overall good

I took another class with Dr. Yu before this one so I knew that her classes are challenging but she is very helpful and supportive and all of her classes build skills very fast. All of the material in class was super useful and I had a real sense of accomplishment at the end.
reviews.rating_tags: Accessible outside class--Group projects--Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: Qian is super helpful if you give a good effort. She's also really sweet and highly competent. I highly recommend taking her GIS classes if you're serious about learning the material.
Professor Yu is very very nice,she is an expert of her study area,and give us lots of cutting edge knowledge ,it may be a little hard on the formulation ,but once you made it ,you will gain a lot.

Very nice and will always try to help and clear up points of confusion. Material she teaches is very dry though and you may struggle a bit in the labs when you learn more advance techniques. Her accent may be hard to understand as well at times.

Best class I have taken at UMass. The format of the class is great in its ability to teach R to students who had no experience like myself. While some aspects of the homework and group assignment were difficult, she helped as much as she could. She is passionate about the material she teaches and is always responding to emails outside of class.
reviews.rating_tags: Group projects--Gives good feedback--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Such a great and helpful professor. She made learning a new coding language simple and enjoyable. Great balance between theory and visualization with statistics. 10/10

For an intro Stats class it may seem like a lot of work towards the end especially since its a project based class. despite this, zhao is extremely considerate and caring when it comes to extensions and grading. lectures tend to get monotonous and repetitive in structure but zhao teaches R well and provides plenty of opportunities for improvement

Great professor, Randie is very passionate about biology and often connects our learning towards cancer research and the real-world situation. The exams are all (ALL) true and false, so always a 50/50 chance of getting it right. If you are going to take Bio 151 with Randie, I suggest reviewing slides religiously and going to his review sessions!

The lectures are not interesting at all, but he knows what he's talking about. He's very smart but it takes a while to understand. If you take him, be ready to put in the time and effort to rewatch the lectures and take more notes because he talks fast and you will miss information from lecture. His exams are very clear and he doesn't trytrick you.
reviews.rating_tags: Lecture heavy--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Very good professor, and the lectures were engaging. He focuses a lot of the content towards cancer, which is a bit different than other professors, but most people found it fascinating. He also shows cute animal pictures before the lecture starts.
The class itself is more difficult than I expected (don't slack like I did) but the professor is incredibly passionate and probably the kindest I've ever encountered. Highly recommend.

His class was pretty easy even as a student who did not take AP Bio beforehand. Studying is best done by attending SI sessions and reviewing the practice questions he provides. Attendance to lecture is by iClicker and is only 2% of the grade, but its vital to attend the Discussion sections. Overall, there's quizzes every Friday and 4 Exams total.
THE GOATTTTTTTTTTTTTTT
Randy is a great professor, always encourages participation and asking questions. GO TO SI SESSIONS!!! also do his practice tests they help A LOT!!!

Randy is an AMAZING PROF. Go to every lecture and you will be fine. Short quizzes every Friday which are insanely rushed but they're not too bad. Exams are very straightforward. Go to every quiz/exam review session and you will be perfectly fine. Can tell he genuinely wants his students to succeed. Definitely take 151 with him.

GREAT lecturer, you HAVE to go to classes it's literally the easiest way to get an A in this class. He gives quizzes every friday, but he always has a review session the night before, GO TO THOSE. He does exam review sessions which are also extremely helpful. HIs exams are all T/F and the wording is very tricky, so you have to get used to his style
He is very understanding of students.

Randy is such an incredible guy, you can tell he loves biology (especially cancer) and wants everyone to succeed. All his exams and quizzes are true false, and I took his class for that, thinking it would be easy.  It's not, true false makes everything harder. Take him if you want an in depth class, but if you just want an easy A, take anyone else.
I recommend!
Randy is very clear with what you need to know and his quizzes/tests are all multiple choice. I highly recommend taking notes on his lecture slides and filling in what you missed after class.

He's honestly the best professor I've had this semester! He's super funny, likable, and approachable. I made a mistake taking this class as a GenEd, but it was truly so interesting and manageable, even though I hadn't taken Bio since 10th grade.
Just go to class, discussions, review sessions, etc and you're likely to do well.
His exam can be a bit tough but weekly quizzes are extremely helpful! Randy is extremely nice and easy to approach. I learned a lot from him.
Do not take this class, he does only true or false and problem solving is not helpful for 152 at all.
reviews.rating_tags: Beware of pop quizzes--Lecture heavy--Test heavy

reviews.comment: Randy is clearly extremely passionate about the topic matter, However, I found the exams and in class questions to be much more intensive than expected. I have found that the return in effort you put into the  class is pretty on par, so just be mindful that if you slack in this class your grade will reflect it, there's not a super large cushion.

Really hard class, but a really cool professor. Lecture is pretty necessary to understand the material, reccommend review sessions or SI sessions to get a good grade. Really flexible and undestanding professor.

I looove Randall, he is so funny and such a great professor. He was one of my favorite teachers of all time, if you get the chance of being with him, 5/5 recommend! He is also super sweet cares a lot about his students.

Randy is the MOST INCREDIBLE professor I've ever had in my life. He has perfected the art of teaching; leads very compelling lectures, holds review sessions himself before every quiz & exam going over practice questions made by him. Exams & quizzes align with lecture slides and practice questions. He has amazing humor and cares. Absolute GOAT.

Randy is a great professor who really cares about his students. He provides a ton of resources for you to succeed in this class, and he holds his own review sessions every Thursday which were very helpful. It's lecture heavy but you can do good if you attend the lectures and put in effort. This is the first time I've enjoyed taking a bio class!!!
This was such a great class. It's lecture heavy but it doesn't feel that way. It's so clear he wants you to succeed and hosts weekly review sessions and has a ton of review material.

Randy uses purely AI, and you can tell in his slides. His lectures are not helpful as they are very disorganized, and he rushes through concepts. The most helpful thing to get through his class was the SI  sessions and the LRC. He gives no time for the weekly quizzes and rushes students and teaching model-based reasoning, and not actual concepts.

For an introductory Biology class, Randy's class was a little more difficult than it should have been, in my personal opinion. You are only graded by weekly quizzes which you are not given much time for, discussions, and exams. If you want an easier A, take Rounds or a different professor. However, he holds his own review sections, which helped
reviews.rating_tags: Lecture heavy--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: discussions in this class are really helpful, content is relatively easy compared to other bio classes. really nice and funny person, he goes over the content and explains really well but I found I needed the reinforcement of discussions

If you show up to lectures and go to his review sessions you should be good, he truly wants you to succeed and gives you tons of resources! For Bio 151 there's technically a textbook but he doesn't really use it. Would 100% take again

Professor Phillis is great! He does go through lectures quick, but reviewing the slides after class really helps. The exams and quizzes are much like the clicker questions. There is a quiz every Friday, but sometimes you can use your notes or speak to your neighbors. I recommend the review sessions the night before each quiz, they really help!
hes great, hes randy

Super nice professor. Most of lecture is him explaining pictures/diagrams. I personally do better when learning concepts then apply them as opposed to just applying them so I struggled. The class seemed challenging for a 100 level class...It was very similar to my cell and molec class the following year, except bio 151 was even harder

Amazing for Bio 151! Incorporates problem-solving into how he teaches the material, which really helps you remember it. Really cares about students and wants you to succeed. Frequent iClicker use in class, and all of the info is in the lecture slides. Tests are almost all true-false and Randy holds review sessions before each exam, go to them!

Awesome professor, awesome class. Prof Phillis loves what he teaches and encourages his students to love the material too. 484 does not have a normal lecture setup so be aware of that. Its entirely group based. You write 3 group papers that you need to do your own research for. Phillis is always there to help if your are lost or confused.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Group projects--Gives good feedback

reviews.comment: Randy is an amazing and wholesome individual. He clearly cares deeply about cancer research and seeing his students truly succeed and learn. The course format is quite interesting, working in groups of around 5 students to submit 3 large documents throughout the semester, treating your chosen cancer type. Randy's grading is not harsh he is so sweet
reviews.rating_tags: Group projects--So many papers--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: My initial impressions of Randall for BIO484 were good, great, even.
