However, after having completed this course I can say with confidence that if you have any qualms with AI usage in the workplace or are expecting a class that is doable without abusing AI that you should avoid this class. Randall crutches on it to get through the insane workload.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--So many papers--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Is kind, caring and a good lecturer, but has absolutely no idea how to manage and mediate groups despite teaching a group project course. Your concerns will be listened to but inevitably not acted on, and he will do nothing to actually enforce his groupwork guidelines when groupmates take advantage and do no work.

The class is a bit of a learning curve because he teaches it in such a way that requires a very specific type of problem solving, however professor Randy is funny, nice and it's overall not to bad as long as you show up to class
Easy tests and quizzes. Took AP Bio in HS and this was 1/10th the difficulty.
Funny guy and good teacher. Big yapper but goes in depth. Quizzes every week. Some lectures are boring but others are interesting.

Genuinely such a good professor. I took 151 and he is so good at explaining, and really shows that he cares about students passing through study sessions and practice problems he posts. He lectures with clarity and his questions are very direct and relate directly to what he teaches. Super super incredible professor I loved his class!

Randy is obviously passionate about biology, but he seems to forget that most people only have a basic understanding of biology and not decades of knowledge. He went through lecture slides at the speed of light and rambled on about irrelevant things. Classes are technically mandatory but no attendance is taken and lectures are recorded.

If you have taken AP Bio and done well on the exam this class will be a breeze. Doesn't go over a lot of basics and often flies through the material but the exam questions are true/false and very easy. Barely any homework and everyone gets extra time on tests. Quiz every Friday with review sessions the night before. Don't buy the textbook!!

Randy is extremely caring and an amazing lecturer. He is funny and his exams consist of material he has taught, no curveballs. I used alot of SI and past quizzes to study. Multiple true/false is the format of his exams and are confusing at first but if you do enough problems you will get the hang of it. Rewatch lectures and do practice probelms.

Biology 151 is a difficult class, However, Randall made it so much easier for us. he provided us with diagrams to use on all of the tests and quizzes. he also used a lot of examples problems in class, so there were never any surprises on the exams. He truly cared about students succeeding and gave us opportunities to boost our grades.

Randy is a sweet guy who clearly is passionate about biology. He starts off every class with pictures he took of different types of animals (usually birds) which is really cute. I really recommend to take full advantage of SI sessions and exam reviews, especially if you haven't taken AP Bio. QUIZ EVERY FRIDAY (study or these will tank your grade)

Although this class was challenging I have taken away so much information and I feel very prepared for future bio classes. Lectures are extremely content dense but if you review Echo 360 after class you should be good. Discussions are helpful/mandatory and there are weekly Friday quizzes. I would definitely take Randy's class again!

definitely important that you come to class as often as you can! the lectures are recorded and are really helpful to go over when studying, but they do go a little fast so its best to watch them on a slower speed. the lectures are very information dense but theres a lot of chances to go over questions and lots of review sessions & quizzes every fri
lots of scientific terminology without explaining what any of it means

I think that the subject is a pretty difficult one, so that reflects the class. You obviously have to put in the work, but he does so much to help you, he really wants you to succeed. Go to the reviews for quizzes, the SI sessions. Its challenging but its literally just about effort. He is a great professor to help you learn.

super nice guy and super caring- definitely has students best interests in mind, you can tell he is interested in the material himself. As someone new to biology, it was challenging trying to understand the material right away (study= +2hr a week). Discussion sections helped a lot. Final grade was unclear all semester. Super sweet prof.

Professor Phillis is very passionate about biology, and keeps his dense lectures very engaging. He teaches the material very well, but his tests can be tricky because its literally all just true and false questions, and there are quizzes every friday. However, once you get the hang of it, it becomes easier.

His exams are diagram based so as long as you get an understanding of the diagrams you will be on a good track. His exams may also contain a few questions that stump you but he makes sure to let you get points back if his wording was confusing. Coming from someone who only took bio in 9th grade the class is pretty easy to understand.

It's heavy on the lectures with lots of information but that's for every biology class. He explains everything well but goes fast. Attendance is mandatory and done by iclicker. There is an in-person quiz every Friday, but often is open notes or open mouths.

Go to the lectures and do the HWs and you have an A right there. He goes over every question type you will see and his exams are not ocnceptly hard. Some questions require logical reasoning and that's it.
reviews.rating_tags: Clear grading criteria--Lecture heavy--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: he is a king

This was the easiest class my freshmen year, all you have to do is study the models he talks about in his lectures and you will get an easy A. Make sure you go to his review sessions on Thursday they make the quizzes super easy.

He is such a nice guy but in my opinion the content is nearly impossible to keep up with. Everyday is a new complex lecture with tons of information. Also wish there was more opportunities for bonus points especially on exams, since I studied as much as possible and got a C. Just overall super frustrating if you're not into biology.

So Randall is a nice fun professor. However I do not love his form of teaching, if you don't have prior knowledge of biology you are in for a ride. Attend class and pay attention, cannot say this enough READ THE SLIDES (he explains the information better there), and review your hw and quizzes.
Teaches in the most unconventional, convoluted way ever. I've never hated the way a professor taught more before this class.

Randy is an engaging prof who makes dense material digestible. Attend class, do the practice problems, and use tools like unstuckstudy ai to ace the weekly quizzes. Challenging but rewarding if you put in the work.

If you are trying to pick your professor for Bio 151 you should 100% go with Prof Phillis. Very caring professor. Knows that students are stressed and takes the time to make sure material is understood. All quizzes and exams are true/false, which is really helpful. More wants students to understand the material rather than memorization.

Professor Phillis is one of the most caring teachers at UMass. He clearly wants his students to succeed and is always willing to stop to answer questions or clarify. Randy makes it very clear that he wants students to succeed. The content is fast + lectures contain dense material so attendance matters. Randy is a very smart, knowledgeable professor, although his lectures are long, packed with info, and overwhelming. If not bio major this class will be hard. one of the best professors I ever had. So kind and caring towards students. exams are extremely fair-- true or false. no homework but just attend class and you will be where you need to. clicker questions are similar to exams. always starts class with some pictures he's passionate about. you'll have a fun time with him teaching

Professor Phillis was great and very passionate for what he is teaching, which is always great to see in a professor. I still ended up with an A somehow, even though your grade is only 3 *really long* papers. Just gotta try!!

Prof is enthusiastic, understanding, knowledgeable. Little emphasis on grammar/writing, all content based.  Easy A for 400 lvl if you want to/are excited to learn

No homework, but make sure to look over the sample problems he posts. Everything is true or false questions, so practice understanding them in discussion. Go to his review sessions they're great!

Randy is an amazing professor! The class is pretty easy as long as you go to lectures and pay attention. I would suggest after class rewatching the lectures and taking notes (he records the lectures). There are weekly quizzes and 3 major tests. He holds review sessions every week and review sessions for major exams which you should attend!

Randy was great! Definitely would fail the class if I didn't go to the lectures. Everything he says in class isn't in the textbook and he shows his own test example Qs. He does go a bit fast, but he does record his lectures. You have a small quiz every Friday in class, which isn't bad if you go to class during the week. Only 3 big exams. Not bad!

Randy is a great bio prof. I would highly recommend him if you are taking Bio151 as a gen ed or a non bio or biochem major. Randy gives lots of practice problems that are identical to quiz and exam questions. There is a quiz every Friday. Go to his review session, he GIVES ANSWERS!

love him! i would def take him again. as long as you pay attention in class and go to his reviews you're set. the class is memorization heavy but he teaches in a way that makes it pretty easy to know everything.

As long as you show up to class, discussion, and the review sessions it will be an easy A. If you do not learn through listening DO NOT chose a discussion section right after class because you will not have time to review the lecture slides visually in time.

He was super clear about what he expected us to know, and if you paid attention in class and did the clicker questions, you knew what would be on the tests. I never missed a class but all his content and practice problems were only taught in the lectures so go to class or make sure you watch the recordings if you miss. Understand the discussions!

Best teacher I have ever had!! Randy gives amazing lectures and explains topics in a way that makes you feel like you really understand it. Professor Phillis is awesome. He explains things really clearly and efficiently and makes the class really engaging. Bio is already a hard subject, so it can be difficult at times, but Phillis gives people plenty of opportunities get help and succeed. Definitely take this class.

I would definitely take this class again, weekly easy Friday quizzes for credit, 80% of the time they were open notes and open to talking to people around you. No HW, 2 exams, and a final. His si's were amazing help. lectures are recorded. nothing bad about this professor 10/10 recommend it.

Randy is a great guy. No homework, you just have to understand and study the class material. Randall is a good professor just sometimes he explains things in a weird way and you have to do your own research to understand the topic. Youtube is a good resource for this class to understanding topics. Review sessions are helpful for this class and he is a funny and understanding guy. Professor Phillis is the BEST, you can't go wrong!!! Yes, you must put in effort to succeed in his class, but he makes it manageable by providing weekly review sessions. I love Randy! class is super easy if you read and keep up.

While his class is hard, I LOVE Professor Phillis. He is so passionate about the course material and really wants everyone to succeed. A hard class, but one of the best professors!!

Yes, his class was challenging, but I highly encourage you to take him IF you are up for that challenge (studying hard, attending most lectures, etc.) If you're looking for an easy gen-ed 'A', look elsewhere. If you're pre-med, Randy is a MUST!

I took Randys course 2 years ago and wanted to come here and inform people of how helpful his class was to me. He teaches you so that you LEARN not to memorize. I recount information he taught me in almost all of my classes, I think about the way he taught it and can understand it when my current professors fail me. HIGHLY suggest randy!!!!
He's a good guy
Randy really cares about his students. Loved his class but it is very important to put work in. SI and review sessions helped out a lot. Also, dont be afraid to ask questions.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--TEST HEAVY--Caring

reviews.comment: Randy does really care about his students, but all you do in this bio class is look at unlabeled diagrams, most the time your not even sure what the diagrams are about. He is obsessed with cancer and true false trick questions. Has review sessions before every Friday quiz which are extremely helpful, but this class is definitely not an easy grade
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Tests are tough--LECTURE HEAVY

reviews.comment: I really appreciated randy's class. He is very thorough in his teaching, which is annoying when going through the class but two years later I still remember what we've learned and its helped me in multiple classes. In this class you must be engaged, learning and participating. He wants students to succeed, to do well and to learn. Diagrams are key!
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Skip class? You won't pass.--LECTURE HEAVY

reviews.comment: He really wants his students to succeed, holds his own review sessions, and seems to genuinely enjoy his job. His lectures are very important, as are the handouts: the diagrams are everything.

Randall is a great man and is super passionate about Bio. Go to lectures, SI sessions and his reviews and you'll be good. Friday quizzes can work as a grade booster if you study for them. Know your diagrams inside and out.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Clear grading criteria--TEST HEAVY

reviews.comment: Randy's style of teaching is very lecture-based, and it is very important that you go to class and pick up the diagram handouts that he gives. They will be the exact diagrams and that will be on the quizzes and exams and they are very helpful. Also, he practices with clicker questions that are very similar to the quizzes (every week) and exams.

After watching all of my friends take Bio 151 with different professors, I'm so grateful for Randy. He really prepares you for the exams in class and holds review sessions before quizzes. There are clicker questions, quizzes every Friday, 3 exams, and a final. Definitely the best Bio 151 professor at UMass
reviews.rating_tags: Respected--Get ready to read--Skip class? You won't pass.

reviews.comment: He definitely cares about his students learning and holds his own weekly review sessions. He takes the time to answer people's questions and tries to get to know people's names, as well.

Randy is the best! He makes sure everyone understands the material before moving on to the next thing, and he has office hours right after class, as well as a weekly review session he leads himself. There are weekly quizzes so you should show up for class to learn the concepts, but he's very understanding if you have to miss class for a good reason
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Amazing lectures--Caring

reviews.comment: Professor Phillis really cares about his students understanding the course content and actually holds his own review sessions, where he has/takes the time to answer everyone's questions. It's a tough course, but if you're willing to put in the work, you will definitely learn from his class.

Professor Phillis is the nicest (and downright best) professor I've ever met. He genuinely cares about his students and wants them to succeed in his class. However, he expects you to put the work in. Practice clicker Qs, strive to learn the concepts well, and immediately clarify anything confusing. If you put the effort in, he will be on your side.

wasn't the easiest class. he really cares about students and what he is teaching. go to lecture, take good notes and you're all set, i never touched the textbook. Wish i had randy for bio II . he made the grading policy easier in the end of the semester for us to do better. lots of iclicker
Hes very kind and truly invested in the students learning. He activly changed the grading policy through the semester so it was easier to get a better grade.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Clear grading criteria--Caring

reviews.comment: I will admit he definitely does care for his students but the way his exams and quizzes were designed made it a difficult intro course. Multiple true false with limited multiple choice.  He also has material appearing on the exams which may not be reviewed in class. His powerpoints don't a lot of info either. Be ready to listen and take notes.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough Grader--Skip class? You won't pass.--LECTURE HEAVY

reviews.comment: Randy is a great professor who really cares about his students. He will do everything in his power to make sure you succeed. YOU MUST ATTEND LECTURE. Seriously if you just look at his slides and don't attend lecture all you'll find is a bunch of pictures  that make absolutely no sense. Study for Friday quizzes and exams a lot and you'll get the A.

All the tests & Friday quizzes are multiple true/false & the discussion assignments are T/F & free response so you have to be able to understand concepts and ideas to do well in his class - not just facts. He goes pretty fast so use a laptop or record it. If you pay attention and go to all SI sessions it's an easy B and a kind of difficult A.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Skip class? You won't pass.--Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: I had to really work in this class to get the grade I wanted. His exams are difficult with trick questions, so it is easy to get a few wrong. I had to study a ton in this class. I think Randy does care about his students, and even proposed a new grading system, but he definitely makes this intro class very difficult. You also don't need the book.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough Grader--Skip class? You won't pass.

reviews.comment: If you pay attention, you will love this class. You need to go to class to learn the material and iClicker, but he gives you 2 or 3 "freebies" if you miss class with clicker. Kind of funny, exams are multiple true/false. Quizzes every Friday.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--GRADED BY FEW THINGS--LECTURE HEAVY

reviews.comment: A professor that alters my view to biology completely. I appreciate his patience and caring for students who seek for help.

Literally no notes given within the powerpoints besides a few subtitles on diagrams. Tests are 70% true/false, 25% matching, and 5% questions that he makes mistakes on. Useful diagrams provided during exams, but won't help that much unless you know what you are doing. Attend SI sessions, definitely helpful and it will provide study guides.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--TEST HEAVY--LECTURE HEAVY

reviews.comment: Randy is a very nice guy, but man is he confusing and loves trick questions. He expects us all to have a biology background, which I did not. The review sessions do not help at all, as he loves trick questions. All True/False. I hated biology before this and now I hate it even more. But he is a good person, just needs to teach more clearly/direct.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Hilarious--LECTURE HEAVY

reviews.comment: Randy is without a doubt my favorite professor starting off my freshman year. He is passionate about biology and makes it his goal to instill the same appreciation in his students. His lectures are rarely boring and he can makes a lecture on signaling the funniest part of my day. Exams and Fri. quizzes aren't too difficult consisting of mostly T/F.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Clear grading criteria--Hilarious

reviews.comment: Randy is a great professor and wants you to do well in his class. He challenges you, which some People don't like, but he has taught me a lot and has an amazing personality.

Randy is absolutely hilarious and makes lectures bearable. He really tries to make the concepts as comprehensible as possible and genuinely wants students to preform well. The Friday quizzes are typically easy, but multiple true false exams can be confusing at times. Overall a great class and awesome professor!
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Hilarious--LECTURE HEAVY

reviews.comment: Randy is amazing, he's considerate, funny and kind. His class isn't for slackers; you'll need to attend every lecture and discussion to do well but he's worth it. He takes quizzes weekly but he changes his grading if he sees people aren't doing well. He once missed a quiz day so he automatically gave us all 100%. He's great, take him for bio 151.
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Skip class? You won't pass.--Hilarious

reviews.comment: Randy really is awesome. If you're taking Bio 151 just to fill a requirement and don't actually care about learning the material, maybe skip taking it with Randy. If you are really interested in the material, though, he's great. It's different from any bio class you'll take because its all application but it's so worth it and truly prepares you!
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Skip class? You won't pass.--LECTURE HEAVY

reviews.comment: Even with prior knowledge from AP Bio, his class is extremely difficult.

I love Randy! Randy is not rude/ not unhelpful whatsoever, his class is extremely difficult and requires a lot of outside work and reading, but he is always prepared to answer your question. He holds review sessions (be grateful, not all college professors do this) and his exams are True/ False and can be confusing but it sets you up for BIO152

Very condescending and rude if you ask for help outside of class. He expects you to have taken bio previously and fully understand the concepts. Only reason I passed was because I took AP Bio. Not very nice and not very helpful.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough Grader--Skip class? You won't pass.--BEWARE OF POP QUIZZES

reviews.comment: Jumps right into the material. Took AP Bio but still struggling because AP bio wasn't close to as in depth as he is right off the bat. He cares about having the students do well but lectures off of diagrams that you can't really take notes from.
Randy is an awesome person but no the best professor. Much too difficult...
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--TEST HEAVY--LECTURE HEAVY

reviews.comment: I struggled with this class at first, esp. being my first semester of freshman year, but definitely attend every lecture. His powerpoints are directly related to his exams, and you can only understand the material if you pay attention in class. If you tend to zone out or it still does not click in, GO SEE GARBIS at the LRC! He is the best tutor!!

Awesome class, great professor. As long as you focus on what he says during lectures, it's pretty clear cut. He's very conceptual and teaches you the concept, expecting you to be able to apply them. His exams are mostly true or false questions and can be tricky, but if you look over the lecture slides a few times, it's not hard.

Randy is the kindest man with great humor and he really does want everyone to succeed. He's obviously passionate about Biology and makes class real-world applicable. His teaching style is tough to follow, though. Take the best notes you can (struggle) and GO TO ALL THE SI SESSIONS if you want an A.

He's such a nice guy but his tests are difficult with a lot of true/false and he uses a RIDICULOUS amount of diagrams in class.  He uses the iClicker and has (pop?) quizzes on Friday but sometimes allows group quizzes (depending on how much you push him).

Every single test and quiz is true or false. There are quizzes every Friday, but sometimes they are open note/mouth. Randy is a funny guy, he makes the class tolerable. There is not any homework, but make sure to go to SI reviews so you can fully understand what you learn that week for the quiz on Friday.

I loved Randy's bio 151 class this  year. He's such a great guy and seems passionate about what he's teaching. Theres 3 exams plus the final which are tough but if you put in the time and utilize the SI sessions you should do ok. He gives quizzes every friday but they are pretty clear cut. Overall I really enjoyed his class and would recommend him.

Randy is a good man but can be a very challenging confusing professor. If you don't have AP Bio background, you have to put in work for this class. This class is not based on memorization, its all about applications. All his quizzes and tests are true/false. The wording can be very tricky, he likes to combine many things. Read carefully & work hard
loves trick questions

He gives unclear answers when going over questions so you are left wondering what the right answer is. The comments he makes in class and comments he puts on slides when they are uploaded can be contradictory.  Makes you think in depth about problems.

Randy is hilarious and a really nice guy. He expects you to know basic biology and builds on that in his Bio 151 class. I couldnt imagine taking this class if I hadnt taken AP Bio in high school. The class isnt easy but exams are only worth half of your grade and there are plenty of opportunities for extra help. Challenging but rewarding class.

Randy is a great guy, but he is not always very clear. The material he explains is good and easy to follow, but he loves clicker questions which he then fails to tell you the exact answer to. His tests are all T/F, but can be tricky. Randy loves cell signaling and cancer so be ready to have all examples revolve around those topics.

He's a funny and relatable guy, but as a general bio class, it is too difficult (and I took AP bio and got credit, and tend to think i know a lot about biology). He does not teach by the book, you won't even need it. He also focuses too much on cellular pathways and your ability to solve riddle-like questions, which doesn't actually test knowledge.

Prof. Phillis' class was challenging yet rewarding. He cares more about how biological systems work over straight-up vocabulary. This is reflected in weekly quizzes and the exams, but go to lecture because he doesn't teach out of the textbook and gives iClicker questions to help. If you go to his review sessions and tot SI, you will be successful.

Teaches concepts and application over specific facts.  Basically he wants you to be able to read a diagram and determine what would happen in a given hypothetical scenario.  No homework, no textbook but graded quizzes every Friday and iClicker attendance  every day.  He holds review sessions before quizzes and exams and will answer any questions.

He teaches you how things work when they are wrong, but doesn't explain how things work when it works correctly. Doesn't mesh well with my style, however the SI sessions were the only reason I passed the class!

Randy is my favorite professor this semester. I have never really understood or liked bio until his class. He is funny, his lectures are pretty interesting. The material and quizzes and tests can be hard but if you go to review and SI sessions you will be fine. Definitely recommend taking, he is a great guy.

Randy is an awesome guy, don't get me wrong, but there's no way an intro Bio class should be this difficult. He focuses to excess on cell biology and mutation without really teaching about the normal system first, so unless you have a strong background in biology, this class is gonna be an uphill battle. Weekly quizzes and 3 exams (no surprises)
He's good just go to the SI review sessions, they really help a lot. Hard to pay attention the whole lecture but it is a must if you don't want to get confused.
The man is the reason I can actually understand Biology. His lectures are engaging and his comfort in front of and control of the lecture hall is truly remarkable.

He is an amazing professor if you like to work with diagrams. He is all about application and less about memorization. Just a truly amazing class, he is basically the only good teacher for this course based on what I have heard from my friends. 10/10 would recommend.
DON'T TAKE THIS CLASS!!! exams are extremely hard, and if you skip a class you will forever be behind. Save yourself

Good professor if you like microbio and you have an interest in cancer cells as he likes to talk about them a lot. His tests are tricky at first but once you get to know the style it gets easier. Quiz every friday but he runs a review session himself every thursday night. Do your research before picking a bio151 prof as they all teach diff material

Awesome guy, but not a great professor. Never got anything out of his lectures. Doesn't email back, lucky for him he had some awesome TA's helping him out. Teaches a 300+ student class as if there were only 15 students there. Reason I changed majors. Need good notes and studying a lot from alternative sources than himself. Everything is TF.

I liked him a lot, he really seems to like his students and enjoy teaching. He encourages critical thinking instead of memorizing. I did wish we had a slightly clearer way of study besides just listening very carefully during lectures, but for the most part he was great and I enjoyed the class.
So. Damn. Confusing. He talks in circles and will say to you "I design exam questions to trick you. I want to trick you." No help.

Randall is a great, but different. He doesn't give very clear answers on what's right and wrong which CAN BE tricky. Tons of TF. There is a quiz every Friday: can vary from open notemouth to strictly test testing. Tries to make the class interesting and loves what he teaches. Holds weekly review for quizzes. Definitely have to work for the grade.

Very funny and inspirational guy. I recommend voice taping his lectures because there is no other way to review info that you need to know. Do not bother buying textbook. Tough truefalse exams. Quizzes every week (sometimes open note). Says "it could be A or B" in class and expects students to choose between the two on exams. Lots of grey areas...

Randy is a really nice guy out of lecture, however, he is not the best professor. He shows an obvious interest in the material and makes lectures interesting but the tests and quizzes are really hard. Most of his questions are vague but similar to the ones taught in lecture. If you write them down and use them to study you should be fine.

Interesting professor, I enjoyed his teaching style very much. You need to go to class for Randy though, most of them are built off of the last lecture. Gives quizzes every Friday, usually scantron at the end of class but will change it up once in a while to do it during class as clicker. Loved him, wouldn't mind having him again.

Randy is a great guy and is there for you. However, you may never know for sure what your grade is prior to the end of the semester being that he never gets papers back. BioTAP is very difficult, but also very rewarding. If you put the work in, you'll notice that you've learned more than you would have in a normal class. Completely project-based.

BioTAP is very different from other intro bio courses. The semester consists of 3 major projects, no tests. This would have been fantastic except we never got back the first project, which led to a lack of motivation for subsequent projects. Also, it's not super clear what he's looking for, but he grades generously (we think).

Randy is a great prof who loves what he teaches, however, he is very unclear in lectures and talks in circles. Exams and quizzes are all critical thinking tf problems that are confusing and hypothetical. The class was interesting but it is hard to do well on exams.

Randall Phillis is one of the best biology teachers I have ever had in my educational career. Taught the course better than my AP Biology teacher from high school. Allows you to ask questions and holds reviews every Thursday night for Friday quizzes. Also holds review sessions the night before every exam. Clicker questions in class are the key.

He holds review sessions every week which really helps clearing up small details that he just mentions in class. He really wants his students to understand and is willing to help out a lot. His tests are tough and his lectures can be confusing because he never really answers his own questions but its a great class. I would recommend.

Randy really is a great teacher. His classes run very smoothly and he tries to make biology as fun and approachable to the students as possible. While his unwillingness to give away answers for any clicker questions and his sometimes vague responses of "yeah, maybe" could be frustrating, his methods will grow on you and i very highly recommend him.

DO NOT TAKE RANDY'S CLASS. I should have listened to the rate my professor comments before this but I didn't, it was a huge mistake. You're expected to learn from sample questions that he doesn't explain. I have friends in 3 other bio classes who are all doing just fine and their exams are much more reasonable. DO not take this class

Randy is a funny professor! He really tries to make the material as interesting as possible. However, his class is pretty tough, making us apply the knowledge we learned in class on exams. Plus he never really gives you the answers to any of his iClicker questions in class, so going to class is pretty important.

I disliked him at first due to how he jumped straight into deep material on the first day of class, but afterwards I got used to his concept teaching style and was able to pull through. His exams are tough, no doubt, and you better be prepared for a quiz every Friday but most times he's pretty lenient with letting us use notes or discuss it
He refuses to help when I ask and i've asked multiple times

This is not a class you learn out of the textbook for. He creates his own questions and focuses on critical thinking. He lectures like it's a small class and there are plenty of opportunities to ask questions. The discussion section is unhelpful but required.

GO TO CLASS. I'm telling you now you will get behind after missing one class. He uses the iClicker for participation too. Every Friday he gives a quiz so you better not plan on going home on Thursday. He does drop your three lowest quiz grades though and averages the test grades out to be best for you. I really do like him as a professor.

I liked this professor. He knows a lot about genetics in which I am interested. He sometimes throws some random information at you. Cyclin D, Angiotensin etc. I love those random stuff. some don't. I highly recommend it. His exams are tricky tho.

Worst class ever, there's no structure in the class so you'll never know what you're going to learn next. Every question on the exam is true or false based on how well you can interpret and memorize a diagram. I hate this class!!!

Randall Phillis is a great guy, but his teaching style is very strange. He really likes to teach his own way without the book to get you to "think about biology not read and memorize" which I enjoy, but it also makes the class very hard. If you pay attention in class and go to the SI sessions you'll be fine, just don't skip!

Randall is clearly very passionate about biology and he is a great professor. I love how he uses his sense of humor to lighten up the lectures. He also makes time for review sessions where he brings candy! Don't get me wrong this class isn't easy but if you're going to take it, get this Randall.

Randall Phillis destroyed any love I had for biology. He is not only extremely disorganized but he also refuses to clearly answer anything and if he does not like you, will sass you in front of the entire lecture hall (did not happen to me, happened to a friend). Take any other professors class other than his. Do not recommend.

People who complain about the difficulty of the course just need to put in more work. He's an extremely helpful, friendly professor who is deeply passionate about the material, so of course he wants to go into detail. It doesn't hurt that he has a great sense of humor too, it really brightens up the class.

Phillis is a great professor despite being unpopular with some students. He would rather students learn to problem solve and think analytically than memorize facts. All exams include diagrams so you don't need to memorize. He is readily available to help students, runs weekly reviews. GO TO CLASS. He does NOT teach from the book. But read it anyway

Professor Phyllis was great! Although I didn't have any prior knowledge or interest in biology his lectures were understandable. The review sessions that he does is also really helpful. He answers questions for as long as you want. I think if you have an interest in bio he would be an awesome professor to have.

His class was definitely a challenge at first because he mainly only uses diagrams and true/false questions on his exams. But, by the second month, it turned into one of my favorite classes because his teaching style started to make sense and the class seemed easier. You should attend every class, and he gives weekly, easy Friday quizzes.

BioTAP 190H was a love-hate class. We had no book, and did 3 group projects. We learned to read/analyze scientific writing and think like researchers. Group dynamics were HARD! Lab was also hard. The course is hard, and Randy takes this into consideration for grading. Randy was nice and helped me with my group problems. Only take if you love Bio!

Extremely interesting class.  He is some what hard to follow at the beginning of the semester but once you get used to it then it isn't hard.  His office hours and reviews are extremely helpful and almost necessary.  He wants the you to learn and will help make sure they know what they need to know as long as they reach out for help. Real good guy.

Randy is a nice guy who really wants his students to do well. He does not spoon-feed you the notes or what he wants you to know - he expects that you are in college now and you will pay attention to lecture and write down what you think is important. If you take his class be prepared for his unconventional teaching style.

The content in his class resembles the content in upper level classes; however, his class isn't hard. Just go to the lectures, pay attention to what he says and you'll pass. He's a funny guy and wants you to succeed... it's just that his teaching style is unorthodox.

His me tires are almost impossible to follow never mind take notes on and he doesn't communicate well with TAs which makes discussions almost useless. The only savior is the SI of the class and then the exam reviews. If I have the choice I will never take his class again, makes things way more a stressful than they should be.

Great class. Awesome prof, he brought food for us! Three big papers (team papers), but the guidelines were loose so we could do whatever we wanted as long as we put a lot of effort in. Also took intro bio with this prof, unconventional teaching style but much more interesting than your typical 'read 40 pages and memorize the bolded words' bio class

Randall is a nice guy, but completely unclear in what he wants. He begins the class by teaching logic, not biology. He does not communicate with his TAs on what he wants them to teach, so the discussions are basically useless. His lectures are somewhat entertaining though.

WORST teacher ever. He didn't explain clearly and rushed. Tests and quiz's are T/F questions. I was left in the dark not knowing what was going on and I didn't know if what I was thinking was right. He never posted graded quiz's so you don't know what you have in that class until grades areposted at end of semester. Don't take this class with him!!

Took his BioTAP class and it was great! Really amazing stuff - we cured cancer, came up with gene therapies, etc. He knew he gave us difficult projects, but graded accordingly. He's very understanding and helpful, and I really liked him.

Randy is an awesome person if you get to know him. If you read the textbook BEFORE the lectures this class will be very easy. I hated being left in the dark about my grades though. Love Randy but I don't know if I'd take his class again.

I got an A in the class and can say it was the worst class I took last semester. I had no idea what my grade was going into the final and wouldn't have been surprised if I got an F. There is no homework but most people have to study every day because there is a quiz every discussion and every Friday. Good luck...

Prof Phillis is a good teacher if you already have a strong background in biology. His tests are very difficult and the discussion sections almost useless. There is no way to know how you are doing in the class until the very end. I hear SI sections are helpful. the only real plus side to this class is that there is no homework
The semesters been over for almost a week and I still don't know my grade...exams are hard, lectures don't make sense, overall, I wish I took this class with a different professor.

Randy is much more of a scientist than a professor. His lecture slides arent explained well and the exams are very difficult to do well in. He took forever getting our grades back- I found out all 4 of my exam grades during the last week of the semester. I wish I had enrolled with a different professor for Bio 100
Does not respond to emails.  EVER

Amazing professor.  His lectures consist of multiple iclicker questions.  The only prob is you have to listen carefully 2 what he is saying when he goes over the questio because he sometimes doesn't give u the answer He wants you 2 figure it out on your own. go to discussions. si sessions mos def people think its hard because they suck at studying.

Randall is a really good teacher! At first I hated him but I really like Bio so as long as you apply yourself you will do well. I strongly suggest going to the SI Review Sessions. You won't know your grade until the end of the semester. Overall great class.
Do not take this class with Randy. he is very confusing, his exams are ridiculously hard, and you will never find out your grades. the semesters almost over and I still don't know what I have...
Randall is awesome
Not a good professor, hard to understand, doesn't answer questions. Doesn't give grades back, and doesn't give clear answers to questions.

A great professor that gives interesting lectures and prepares you well for exams. You have to go to class due to clicker questions (although since his lectures are interesting this shouldn't be an issue) His tests are somewhat hard but go to SI sessions and you should be fine. Don't bother buying the textbook as its never used. Better than others.
Worst class I've ever taken, very confusing way of teaching. his exams are really hard and he's very unclear in class. you'll never know your grade and he will not reply to your emails.

This class is easy, but not what I wanted from a biology class. Randy genuinely wants his students to do well, but he has a strange teaching method - he tries to teach logic instead of biology. Test questions usually pretty clear, but rarely gives a straight answer during class.

He has a different style of teaching that takes a few weeks to get the hang of.  His lectures are pretty confusing, but reading the book helped me a ton in understanding the material and getting good grades on his exams. Just don't slack off and you should be fine.

Randy expects you to write down every word he says and provides no notes or readings. His teaching style is awful, review sessions are usually unhelpful, no grades are ever posted and he is just overall mean and uncaring about students grades. He also never responds to emails even if they are very important.
Pretty cool guy. Studies flies, doesn't afraid of anything.

You need to go to class because the clicker questions are on the exams, but as long as you question him you will learn a ton and he wants everyone to get the good grade but more importantly learn from it. An absolutely wonderful professor because he doesn't make you memorize, he makes you THINK!

Easy class to get an A in, but totally useless if you are looking to learn biology. WARNING if you are a Pre-med: you won't learn anything for the MCAT in this class, so prepare to learn it ALL on your own. (I'd also recommend taking 285 before you take the test, because that ended up being very helpful.) Phillis is the worst.

Genuinely wants to help people learn but not clear on answers and scatterbrained explaining things. Uses PRS to track attendance. Extremely late on grading, does not hand back tests. Almost no assigned homework.

Alright Biotappers, this is a logic class so learn to think the way he thinks and you will get an A. Refuse to go through what he says is right then its most likely going to be a B. You almost never use the book so just share with someone else. If you had a great bio teacher, get ready for the worst. He procrastinates and personally doesnt teach.

Randy's class is all about logic and interpreting diagrams. There is basically no memorizing. He rarely gives feedback on grades, especially on quizzes, but it makes you focus more on learning than on the grade. I learned how to think in this class instead of just being fed the material. Classes are very interactive. Overall, a good class.

Randy's class was based on logic. He assigned 4 chapters to read all semester- none of which were necessary for the exams. We didn't get any quiz grades back from the weekly quizzes because he wanted us to ponder the questions all semester. He put the exam answers up about a month after the exams. He used PRS every class. Overall didn't learn much.

He asks many questions in class on PRS and you will never know if your PRS worked or how much the PRS is worth for grading. He does weekly quizzes in a rush and never gives the grades back or posts on sparkbut they are worth a large portion of your grade.In addition he wastes class time and gives no outside reading material to help prepare for clas

Doctor Rich was a very "down to earth" and engaging lecturer. He structures the class with very reasonable expectations (one class per week in person, weekly homework/quiz), and is more than fair with grading. My favorite and most engaging science class I have taken by far.
reviews.rating_tags: Clear grading criteria--Respected--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: This class was awesome and I would recommend it to anybody at UMass, regardless of major. The information you learn is very interesting, and the only work required for an A is attendance once a week, a few PackBack entries per week, and a weekly quiz that allows multiple attempts.

Take this class for your bio gen ed. Class is half online and half in person and he is so understanding. You can miss like four assignments and still get an A. Lectures are actually interesting and you have weekly quizzes. The quizzes are not hard and you only have two assignments every week. The packback is very annoying but this class is awesome.

I took Plagues and Poxes for the BS requirement and it has become my favorite class yet. The structure of the class is half online half in person with two assignments a week. There is only one quick discussion homework and one quiz a week. Professor Rich clearly cares about his students and their workload. Professor Rich is an incredible professor.

Quizzes online, attendance at only one of the classes per week. Only grades are attendance (attend 10 out of 12 weeks), quizzes (do 10 of 12), and Packbacks (do 10 of 12). NO EXAMS, NO PAPERS. If you need a biological science gen-ed, 100% take this class. The material is interesting too. Attendance is on Menti (similar to TopHat).
Great professor. Tells you exactly what you need to do to get a good grade in the class. It is very clear what you need to do. 10/10 recommend

This was my favorite class. I took it for my BS Gen-Ed and I think everyone should. Stephen Rich is very caring and passionate. Lectures are engaging, there is one quiz every Friday (online), a weekly packback, and no exams or papers. Best Gen-Ed.
reviews.rating_tags: Clear grading criteria--Caring--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: He's a really great professor who clearly cares about the course material and wants to teach about it. The homework is really manageable if you stay on top of it, and there are no exams! I am not a science person but I really like this class.
The class was super easy. Attendance at one lecture a week is required, but all other work is online and there are no tests.
reviews.rating_tags: Clear grading criteria--Graded by few things--Online Savvy

reviews.comment: a legend.

Genuinely a fantastic professor. Knows why people take the class and doesn't make it any harder than it needs to be. One of my friends who I took the class with left for Sweden for two weeks and still managed to get an A. TAKE THIS CLASS

I absolutely loved this class so much. professor rich is super kind and makes his classes super interesting. attendance is mandatory because class is through an online site that you log on and go through the slides with him There is a weekly pack back discussion post and a weekly quiz do. There is no final exam and weekly quizzes are all online.

Yes, this class is easy but it's also kind of fun. I'm not a mircobio major but this was a very intriguing class and you learn a lot of basics. It gives you a taste of the major without any harsh commitments. Lectures are online and meetings one time a week which is great but the online lectures can get long and tedious. Either way good class

Best professor, super nice and funny. You have to attend class once a week and participate on a quiz game where he counts it towards your attendance each week is worth 20 points. Also every week you have to ask one question and answer two in packback, and take a really easy quiz. You can watch the lectures on your own time. TAKE THIS CLASS

I highly recommend taking Microbio 140 with Professor Rich. The format of the class is watching weekly lecture videos, going in person once a week, Moodle quizzes, and Packback posts. Prof. Rich inspired interest in the material, and I always looked forward to class. You can get an A without much effort, but if you try, you'll get a lot out of it.

Dr. Rich quickly became one of my favorite teachers and will become one of your favorites too. Extremely informative and interesting class that is not very difficult. Classes are interactive with menti quizzes. Science has never been a subject I have enjoyed but I learned a lot and would take any other classes taught by Dr. Rich in a heartbeat.

This class is the best and I highly recommend taking it There are weekly quizzes that you are allowed three attempts to complete. Homework is light. The class itself is very interesting and Prof Rich clearly knows a lot on the topic. while the class is easy the material reflects deep understanding of course content to further knowledge. no final!

Classes are split into online videos and one in-person class per week. Homework consists of a quick post to packback and 2 responses also weekly quizzes which can be taken anytime before the due date. Overall one of the easiest classes I have ever taken but also very interesting and informative. If you need your Bio Gen-ed then definitely take this
Literally the best

Amazing professor. Teaches Tue. & Thurs. and u only have to attend one or the other for attendance (u can go to both). Quizzes every Friday & u can use your notes. Engages w/ students. Packbacks due Sun. Extra credit opportunities @ end of semester.
Understands that most of us are taking it for a biology gen ed, super easy with minimal effort

Professor Rich was one of the best professors I've had yet. He really cared about his students, which made class enjoyable to go too. He understood most of us where taking it for a gen ed so the material was not too hard to understand. Would defiantly recommend if you need a relaxing class that fills the bio gen ed.
Low attendance requirements. Easy and interesting content. Extra credit available. Gives prizes to in-class quiz winners.
Professor Rich was very nice and he made the class very interesting without making it overly difficult for a gen ed.

We had to watch the lectures on our own and then go to class one day a week to do an interactive menti quiz but it was great! Great guy and he would give out gift cards if you won the menti. Weekly quizzes are easy if you watched the lectures

Professor Rich was one of the best professors I've had. I took this as a gen ed and found it very manageable. I really liked the structure of the class, only had to go to class once a week, weekly moodle quizzes and discussion posts. Super nice guy, gives plenty of opportunity to earn an A. Would definitely recommend taking this course if you can!
One of the best professors I have had this far at UMass. Stephen is so caring and nice, and genuinely wants his students to succeed. TAKE THIS CLASS for a BS gen ed, it is so worth it.
Best gen ed you will ever take. If you can take this class

He is so caring and kind to his students. His lectures are entertaining and he sparks excitement, even if you have no interest in the topic. He asks us how we're doing throughout the semester and seems to really care. We are only required to attend one lecture per week, but I love the class so much that I wish I had it more often.
This is a great class for gen ed. he is super nice and caring. work is so manageable and quizzes every week arent hard. you only have to go to 11 classes. highly recommend.
He is the man of the year every year. TAKE THIS CLASS. It is so easy and was not even an addition to my course load. He is the best and this class is cake.
Easiest class I have ever taken.

- Easy Gen-Ed

- Fair teacher 
- Two assignments per week
- Have to attend one out of two lectures a week for credit

reviews.comment: Stephen Rich is my favorite professor so far. He teaches so well and we only have to attend one synch class a week. We are only graded on weekly tests on moodle and weekly packbacks! Absolutely love him and would 100% take his classes again. We also usually leave class early too!
Stephen Rich is great. If youre looking for an easy bio gen Ed, take one of his classes. Absolutely effortless and amazing. Gonna miss this man.

This class was incredibly easy. Quizzes were all online, no midterm, no final. He only makes you go to 1 class a week and you do is answer questions on menti. His assignments are very easy and the weekly work for his class can be done in 30 minutes. Great professor, made his lectures interesting although the lectures had to be watched online.

Best professor I have had so far. Says class is twice a week but you only have to go once, no exams, he's super funny and nice and makes the material interesting, only assignments are weekly quizzes and packback which take 20 mins, best gen ed class for biological science!! take it

Professor Rich is definitely the best professor I've had at UMass. I was very anxious to take microbio as it was a required course for me and something I am not good at but professor Rich makes learning fun and easy to understand hard concepts. He cares a lot about his class and add humor to his lectures. p.s. i dont like lots of work. perfect! :)
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Graded by few things--Caring

reviews.comment: Professor Rich's class was the easiest I've ever taken. His lectures were out of class and we only had weekly quizzes and PackBack to do, and his classes were very easy with non-graded quizzes or discussions. A funny guy, who doesn't want to be overbearing for a gen-ed.

Professor Rich is one of the best professors I've ever had at UMass. I'm not even a microbio major, but he made the topic so clear and understandable. He clearly cares about his students and wants all of them to succeed, but knows when a student doesn't care. He is honest and respected and I would love to work with him again.
absolutely amazing teacher. He is so caring and genuinely likes to teach. Would take any class he teaches this is a true example of what a teacher should be.

Greatest teacher to have at UMass. He actually cares about his students, he even let us have a week off from work because he did not want us to be burned out from our other classes. The class is interesting with weekly quizzes that you can take up to three times, packbacks due every week as well as lecture blocks. Interesting material too!

Professor Rich is the best professor Ive had at UMass. This class is easy if you show up and are excited to learn. He truly cares about his students. There are no exams, just weekly multiple choice quizzes and Packbacks. The lectures are twice a week but you only have to attend one for credit. Overall, great class!! Definitely take it!!

Such a fun class. Stephen Rich is one of the best professors, he's super understanding and interesting. Great to fill the biological science GEN-Ed. One of my favorite classes at UMASS even though it's not related to my major at all. Quizzes weren't hard, lectures were interesting, homework was fun and quick, and he offers extra credit.
An engaging professor who is good at keeping it fun and interesting.
reviews.rating_tags: Accessible outside class--Graded by few things--EXTRA CREDIT

reviews.comment: The BEST professor I've taken at Umass by far. Classes are so enjoyable and I genuinely look forward to showing for his lectures. Super easy, interesting, and definitely would recommend taking for Gen-Eds if you are a non-science major. Weekly open note quizzes, no exams, and super understanding of student circumstance. Gave me faith in Profs again

I made a RMP account just to rate Professor Rich because that is how caring and awesome he is. He goes out of his way every. single. class to ask how we are doing, if we need help, and asks for feedback. He knows the content very well and is great at teaching, of course, but he goes above and beyond any other professor I've had.

Literally the best professor I've ever had. He always keeps the class fun and engaging, so while the class is very easy, it's not boring by any means. He genuinely cares about his students wellbeing and checks in with us frequently. Highly recommend this gen-ed.
He is the nicest guy and genuinely cares about all of his students and wants everyone to get As. Weekly Moodle quizzes but are easy. No exams.

I've literally never met another professor who genuinely cares about his students like this guy. He definitely commands respect, so he can be a bit intimidating at first. But stick with the class and you'll see that he's an incredible professor whose classes function like a well-oiled machine. Very straightforward.

Prof Rich is so nice and understanding. Always asks about students mental health and was very easygoing with work during online learning. Just one quiz per week and one little writing assignment type thing. No exams
reviews.rating_tags: Graded by few things--Clear grading criteria--Caring

reviews.comment: I took this class and it was essentially useless. It was nice to get 4 free credits, and barely do any work to get them. But aside from that...I don't even understand the point of it. I never even studied for a single test. We watched like national geographic documentaries and videos about vampires. I just don't see it ever being useful.

*This course was taken during the Spring 2020 Covid-19 pandemic* Prof Rich gave incredible lectures in class that unfortunately diminished in quality over Zoom. Very inspirational, and taught biology so that anyone from any field could understand.

LOVED this class. Wicked interesting, this class actually inspired me to change to a science major. Stephen gives awesome lectures, if you like learning about infectious diseases this class is a must. Allows cheat sheets on all exams. Gotta go to class though (or get notes) bc he doesn't post them, but I liked going to this class. Exams are easy
reviews.rating_tags: Respected--Skip class? You won't pass.--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: Professor Rich is such a nice guy, he is so passionate about what he teaches. I loved plague class it was super interesting and I learned a lot. It sucks that coronavirus made this stuff online but he has worked really hard to still teach us the material. Lectures aren't mandatory, exams and quizzes are super easy.

Great guy, passionate about what he teaches. Perfect gen ed. You don't need to go to class, but I always went. Exams are very similar to weekly quizzes so as long as you review those the class is easy. Definitely recommend!

Such an easy class, the first exam is the exact same as the practice exam. Just attend class and study the quizzes you'll be fine. He's such a sweetheart and wants people to do well. I would definitely take for a gen ed.

I love him and his class. He is funny and interesting and never biased. He is dynamic and wears great ties that match with the disease you're learning about that day. Everything is done online and the final is optional, and while his slides are sparse on info, he records and posts all the lectures on Echo360. I enjoy this class so much

Professor Rich is a fantastic professor. His class, Plagues: The Ecology of Disease, is easily one of the best classes I've ever taken. He's a funny guy, and he wears ties that coincide with the disease you're learning about on that day. His lectures are very interesting and he records them on Echo360 so if you miss class it's not a huge deal.
I love Dr. Rich, and so will you. He's amazing, the father I've never had, the brother I've always wanted. I would fail this class just to take it again with him. <3

Pretty easy gened, tests are straightforward and gives you opportunity to use index cards on tests sometimes. First test had an example test, use it. Then all the other assignments outside of the class are easy to complete, online quizzes as well.

Stephen Rich is an amazing teacher.  He doesn't "lecture" during his lectures, he tells stories of the content. This may sound odd but it makes the material really stick. The homework load is very light. He gives three midterms and a final each worth equal percents of your final grade, and the worst of the 4 grades you get, he drops.

Dr. Rich really loves what he is talking about. That is obvious in his lectures. He is so passionate about what he teaches, and that makes class so intriguing and interesting. He has pretty dry and intelligent humor, which I find hilarious! He is so knowledgable about what he is teaching!! Go to lecture, take notes, study, you'll pass!
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Hilarious--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: Fascinating topic! Great professor.

Professor does not provide ANY SORT of study guide for tests which makes it very difficult to study. Pretty much NO info can be found on his lecture slides, most of the info needed to pass the class is said in passing in lecture, you have to listen to him very very carefully. All other assignments are super easy but tests are what brought me down.
Just know you need to get a 96 in the class to get an A.

He is a very nice professor, it is just that you have to attend his class, no matter what. If you miss one class, you will fall behind and then you won't know what some of the answers are on the test. Other than that, I totally recommend this class, lectures are long, but it is an interesting class that will get you thinking.

Great option for a Gen Ed. His tests are very fair and almost entirely based off of lectures. Most notes are put online, but I found that attending and taking notes did help. Online quizzes/writing assignments were very easy, but lectures can be a little boring sometimes. He offers an honors seminar which was the easiest part of the course for me.

Professor Rich was a great guy. He's informative, intelligent, and can be funny too! I think he's just as smooth as Professor Cooley. The course is interesting, and the fact that they switched off mid-semester didn't bother me at all. The tests are super easy too. 10/10 would recommend.
Really liked the professor. Class was easy and very interesting. Honestly, all of the answers to the exams can be found on the slides. Probably one of my favorite classes here at UMass.

The person who wrote the other review really doesn't know what they're talking about. Rich is a clear professor and the class itself is easy. You don't need a study guide for this class if you aren't a moron.

Professor Rich knows his stuff but he does not help students at all. The class itself is somewhat interesting but he shows little to no interest on if we understand the material. If you are not good with science I recommend not taking this class. When Prof. Rich is lecturing as opposed to Dr. Cooley, he does not give study guides.

Rod is a great guy...knows a lot about club management. Class can be boring pretty much just lecture about clubs and a group project and a few guest speakers but everything is easy. Only complaint is the online exams are super long

I took him this past semester and I think he's an okay professor. Not one of the best but not one of the worst. Lectures are kinda boring and the few quizzes and three (online) exams he gives are a shot in the dark based on the notes you take. However, he does care about you doing well in his class and is very responsive with emails.

Rod does not deserve such a high rating! His class is terrible! He does not have clear directions for assignments and the class is graded based on 3 huge exams, 6 chapter quizzes, and one final group project. The exam questions made no sense so you have to guess and hope you get it right. Final presentation is graded very harshly! So Terrible!

Rod knows what he is talking about but his lectures are soooooo boring. There are 3 exams all of which are a shot in the dark. He makes the exams and the questions sometimes make no sense. His lecture slides are very messy and hard to follow. I do not know why he has such good ratings.

He has good intentions on helping you succeed but he isn't clear on his assignments; you need to clarify with him to see exactly what he is looking for. He shows passion for the subject but is a tough grader and is not clear on what he wants done on each assignment. Lectures are mandatory, but he allows opportunities to make up those days skipped.

This is an easy class if you put in some effort. There is little to no homework and if you do it, you'll get full credit. There are three exams which are all online so you can use notes. There is a big group project but it is relatively easy. Great class to take if you are interested in clubs or not.
lots of homework on blackboard work hard for an A big group project at end of the year online tests and online final

Rod is one of the best. He's passionate & he cares about his students & wants to get to know you. He's a major help when it comes to getting jobsinternships so take his class & get to know him.  The classes aren't hard, but there is some work.  Do the work & you'll be fine. Type your notes so you can search them during online exams.  NEED THE TEXT

Rod is very passionate about the industry and knows what he's talking about. He really cares about getting to know the students, and he also knows many industry professionals. Club management was a great class, there was a good amount of work but it was never hard and the exams were online!

This was my first online class through UMass and I highly recommend Rod.  The course was Convention Sales Mgt. and it was a great course.  Timed quizzes at the end of each chapter, discussions for each chapter, a couple of short projects (papers), and the final.  Course was very organized and professor was quick to respond to emails since online.

Rod is 100% there to help his students! He is an incredibly nice guy and has a crazy amount of knowledge about clubs, not to mention his seemingly endless connections. He is the man to know if you want to work in clubs. He keeps the class interesting. I never thought I would say this, but I would recommend this class
Great teacher, loves what he teaches and his class is fun to go to. His tests are fair and the group project is not bad.
Very good teacher, really enjoys what he teaches and all his tests are online. One group project that is not hard.
class is wonderful, very informative, tries to make it fun as possible... such a nice guy...
Totally agree with prior comments.
Great teacher!
I really enjoyed his class, it was informative and it was easy to do well if you paid attention. He took us on a great field trip of area country clubs.

Don't take this class, if you email her with an issue, she won't help you. A lab ran 45 min over and my TA said "it's your experiment" when I couldn't stay because I had class. I ended up missing my class to finish a procedure that was explained to us wrong. She doesn't do a good job at making sure her TAs know the lab the protocol is often wrong.

Emailing her is a nightmare since she treats everything as a waste of time. For example asking for clarification on extra directions is a "waste of time" (yes she will say that directly to you). The entire lab is doing work for her research as well you learn nothing actually useful or related to the actual bio class.

Class is honestly, very boring, not that useful, and pointless for some career paths. No excused absences. If you're 5 minutes less, you get 80% of attendance grade for the day. Very few classes when given time to work on assignments in class. Assignments due 4 days a week basically, and need a lot of understanding to do.
|Fall 2025| She was good. Her assignments were simple and straightforward.

This class is an interesting continuation of bio153 but there is SO much work and the professors don't understand that students have other work in other classes. There is very high expectations and you need AMPLE time set aside to work on 2-3 assignments per week. im so happy this class is over but on the bright side there's no exams.

Never saw the professor once. Was mostly taught by the assigned TA for the class (mine was ok but had an attitude/ego). The papers are tedious and absolutely stupid to do, just spewing out the same BS your already given. Lab was good though although its really 50/50 whether your lab mates are good or not
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Group projects

reviews.comment: She wasn't ever really there for lab as the lab was run by TA's but from my three times talking to her she was nice and helpful if we were confused or had mishaps in our procedure for our lab.

She doesn't teach it's TA's but lab is so easy and it rarely ever took the full 3 hours. It is dependent on getting a good group though so I would get to the first lab early esp if you know people in your lab
this class almost made me end up in the psych ward

Writing assignments are spread out through the semester, making it really manageable. Gives a lot of great feedback on writing and has clear grading criteria. I don't think Jess is teaching this class again but I would recommend any course she teaches. She gives clear directions and provides a lot of resources for extra learning.

reviews.comment: Fun class and a cool introduction into bioinformatics

reviews.comment: TA taught lab, meet one day a week for 3 hours. Pick a good group because you will be working with them for the rest of your semester. Literally the group you sit down with on day one is the group you work with. Highly recommend this class. There is a 3 day grace period for assignments. No exams just one lab practical, super easy.
Good teacher, hard exams
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: She has wrong/insufficient knowledge to teach this class. She only knows 2/5 religions in the syllabus. Not accessible outside class- No email replies and absent in office hours without prior notice. This was the only B in my 4 semesters in all straight As. Would not recommend her or the class for knowledge or even just credit.
Actually had her for Honors 201H. She is caring and a pretty easy grader. She made class interesting and asked good questions

Truly one of my favorite professors at UMass and one of the best classes I have taken! It's difficult-- the exams are tough and the material is dense-- but it is so rewarding, mind-opening, and interesting! Her passion for the topic is infectious, and her lectures are like watching really good TedTalks. Take as many classes with her as you can!

Sean is a cool guy and knowledgeable about taxes. He tends to speak fast. Around 4-5 homework assignments every week, which can be time-consuming depending on how well you take in the information he gives in lecture but is very manageable. 3 exams which are kind of identical to homeworks.Very responsive to emails and cares.

Wandrei is a fantastic professor and knows what he's doing. He provides endless resources from lecture notes to review videos to helpful pre-class quizzes/chapter homework. You're allowed to bring all notes to exams and have 3 hours (takes most students under 2.) As long as you put good effort into studying/tax return project, you will excel.

Good class and goes over homework. His lecture videos need to be re-recorded quality is not that good on half of them. Slow response time on questions and sometimes dose not. Can be confusing at times and not give straight answers. Even though i did good in the class it had its ups and downs. Test was majority of grade

Would not recommend taking this class for the business upper electives bc it's a lot of work & lots of assignments. The end of semester tax project is a bit difficult if you do it by yourself. The professor isn't bad tho and there's lots of office hours/help offered. The class does not meet Fridays tho, like SPIRE says.

Sean is a wonderful prof who is passionate abt tax. There are a lot of homework assignments but they help you understand the content. Attendance for class isn't mandatory. He makes videos for each topic along with textbook notes. Friday classes are replaced with an assignment which is awesome. Exams are hard but he lets you bring textbook & notes.
Sean is a great professor. Everything is fair and manageable. Great class!

SCHMGMT 651 had a terrible textbook, but Sean's video lecturing working through all possible examples step by step made it all accessible. Homework is required and "graded" but he changes those grades to a completion grade for the end. He's a fast grader and gives feedback on everything. The homework directly relates to the untimed exam questions.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Graded by few things--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Best professor ever. Talks fast, but not only does he post recordings of the lectures, he makes extra videos about each topic so you can watch what you are specifically confused on. Very willing to help in office hours. Makes amazing review videos for the OPEN NOTE exams. Drops questions everyone did bad on. 10/10 recommend
reviews.rating_tags: Clear grading criteria--Gives good feedback--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Class only meets M/W, even if Spire says M/W/F, he just gives some extra work instead. Exams are open notes/textbook, if you do the homework every week you shouldn't have to study too much for the exams. Both exams so far have been curved 10%, with another 10% extra credit for one. Great professor for tax, and is very helpful and understanding.

Graded based on three exams and few assignments a week. Exams were pretty easy since they're completely open notes and book, so I would just print out his slides and use those (I recommend vs using the book only during the exam) Attendance is optional because you can do the in class assignments outside of class however I found the lectures helpful

Sean is a great teacher especially for a subject that can be dry such as taxes. Grading criteria is straight forward and he tells you exactly what you need to study for his exams. Three exams, online quizzes, in-class assignments, homework's, and a big tax return project at the end of the semester. Keep up with the material and you will succeed.
reviews.rating_tags: Clear grading criteria--Lots of homework--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: super kind and approachable but the class is hard. the material is dry but he tries his best to spice it up. no class fridays ever which was a blessing, but 4 assignments are due every monday morning; can be time consuming so start before sunday night. big project due last day of class but its manageable. sean's great i recommend him for this class

Sean is a cool and flexible professor. The class itself isn't hard but there are a lot of homework's and in class assignments. 3 Exams all open book and one final tax return project for which you are allowed to check your answers with him as many times as possible. No reason to not get a good grade if you put in the effort.
reviews.rating_tags: Group projects--Gives good feedback--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: lots of work, 3 exams 15% each, all the out of class work is tedious and on Chegg. would take again and nice professor.

Prof. Wandrei is a great professor. Multiple opportunities for credit beyond the exams. There are 3 exams each worth 15% of your grade but they are open notes and open book and all multiple choice. There are a-lot of assignments throughout the week, but they take no more than a half hour each. Also the class meets in person only 2x a week!

Tests open-book and open-note, I'd recommend printing out the powerpoints before the lectures and taking notes on them to bring to the tests. Sean is a nice guy but the lectures can obviously be dry. Homework is usually an easy 100, but there's about 5 assignments per week so this class takes some organization and planning.
reviews.rating_tags: LOTS OF HOMEWORK--ACCESSIBLE OUTSIDE CLASS--LECTURE HEAVY

reviews.comment: Sean is a very good professor in the sense that he knows what he is teaching through and through, and he's a really nice guy. His lectures can be a little boring, and he spends half of the class letting you do in-class assignments, which I wasn't really a fan of. Overall a good class though with open note exams.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--LOTS OF HOMEWORK--GROUP PROJECTS

reviews.comment: Professor Wandrei is great! The class is pretty straight forward. It meets on Mondays & Wednesdays, Fridays are online (a "Friday homework" assignment). There are 3 exams and a final project all of which are open note. They are challenging but you can still manage to get an A if you do well on the online assignments (pre quiz, quiz, & homework)

He's a great professor who teaches the material very clearly. Also, he likes to send current events articles about the material we're learning which is interesting too. He's very helpful if you go to office hours. Exams are open notes and are fair based on the questions we do for homework and in class.
