Great professor.  He cares about his students.  He knows the material can be dry at times.  But he tries to make it doable and easy.  Start the tax project early and go to him for help.  Tax project was probably the toughest part of the class.  Tests are open note and open book, which is great.

goes over 1 ch a week and it's fast. you should print out the slides in advance, keep them in a separate folder, and take notes as he goes through them. gives you extra credit for coming to class on fridays. his exams are straight forward and completely open book/ notes. tax return project is work but just have him check it before you hand it in.

Not a bad class and Sean explains ALL the material but goes a bit fast so you really have to pay attention. Exams are open book open notes. Online quizzes suck but if you do them without somebody you should be okay. Adds 3 points to your final grade if you go to all the classes. Exams are MC and he gives you plenty of time but they're not that easy
Wandrei is the best. He takes the extra time to explain to students that are struggling with tax. I had him for 371 and knew I wanted to take his class. Great addition to Isenberg!
Prof Wandrei is the best.  Caring and very helpful. The class is not easy, however he is always available to answer any questions you may have.

Wandrei's the man, one of my favorite professors ever. He's really understanding and always available for extra help- and emails back faster then anyone I know. The exams can be a bit tricky but they're all open book and open notes. If you have the opportunity to take a class with him, take it. You wont regret it.

Hard class because taxes suck, but Sean is a great teacher. Super helpful if you ask any questions. There are weekly quizzes online with the lowest two dropped, and open book exams. Those are fairly hard but he is really reasonable and will tell you what slides are on the exam and what not to worry about. He's young and simply a cool guy. Love him.

Classes were sometimes redundant since everything he talked about was on the slides. But really use office hours! He is really interested in helping students learn and making sure they understand the material. By far the nicest and best teacher I have had yet. Not too bad to look at either ;)

He is a new professor and he is young, but he did a good job. His class is clear, he tells you what is important, and what is not important. The exams are mutiple choices, and open book test; however, it is not easy becasue there are so many rules involve. You will def do well if you do all the work, and ask him questions. He is a great teacher.
Just shows videos every class

Prof. Woodside honestly isn't that bad, you just have to go to class because of TopHat. There's a group project which can be annoying, but all the other HW is online. If you have previous marketing knowledge, this class should be a breeze.

This class is so dreadful to sit through. He uses TopHat, so you NEED to be in class the entire time to complete all polls and receive attendance code at very end of class. Everybody shows up to class because we have to, but NOBODY is paying attention. He's not engaging and doesn't deliver information well at all. 75 minutes twice a week is hell.

With all due respect, Professor Woodside is quite possibly one of the worst Professors I have ever had. His grading is arbitrary, his lack of understanding on how to utilize basic technology like TopHat is appalling. I really hope the University takes action in training this Professor, and maintaining a equal opportunity environment.

Professor Woodside is super knowledgeable and brings lots of real world experience. I enjoyed the guest lectures in this class. His own lectures can sometimes be boring and are pretty content heavy. There is a group project worth about 30% of your grade and you have to present in front of the entire class (150+ people).

Prof. Woodside is very knowledgeable about multi-channel marketing and often tells stories about his professional career. This class is almost completely based on group projects (you do not get to choose the groups). Attendance is also mandatory! Prof. Woodside provides many Extra Credit opportunities that you should definitely take advantage of!!
reviews.rating_tags: Group projects--Lecture heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment:
Professor Woodside is extremely caring and his coursework is designed to mimick an actual product launch with the group project in the end.
Students complaining either wanted an easy A or aren't really attentive or equipped for an immersive college level marketing class, it's laughable. I just wish we didn't have to buy 2 different text books.

I had this class with him in spring 2025, and the class was fantastic. He's a really kind guy who genuinely cares about his students. The TAs handle most of the grading, but they're super helpful and easy to get in touch with. The course is pretty focused on a group project and you'll wrap it up with a presentation at the end.

Big portion of grade based on a group project that you present infront of an entire lecture hall(200+ people). Grading is very unclear and an easy inperson exam. Would not reccomend. Nice guy and knowledgeable but if you get a bad group you are screwed. Wish the class had a better layout.

Nice guy but definitely technologically challenged, can't figure out how to get the computer connected to the screen and class always starts late. TA's grade mostly everything and aren't very helpful in all honesty, try and take this with other professors…

Woodside is very well-knowledged and has a a lot of experience to bring to the table and lecture.  His lectures may get boring and but it can be interesting.  TA's are responsible for the bulk of the class (technology and grading).  There is a group project that is broken up throughout the semester and a presentation.  Easy homework

I came in not knowing anything about business at all and expressed this to the professor and he helped me the entire way whenever I had doubts about my grade or the material. There's a large group project but as long as there is consistent communication, it's truly not that bad. Great guy, great class, interesting material!

I just started this class with this prof so take this as a warning. Completely clueless. Can't figure out anything in canvas, tophat, or zoom. Bad with technology. Don't how he even got a job as a professor here. do not take this class with him.

Don't know what his criteria was to be a TA for this class but the bar was low. While he was preaching to students about professionalism they'd just play games on their laptops. Couldn't believe the prof let a TA rudely interrupt a group presentation to write the attendance code on the board because time was so short for 30+ presentations. THIRTY.

I remember reading the reviews for his class last semester and telling myself "these people are just overreacting, this class will be fine". HAHA, I should've listened and chosen another professor. Woodside arguably has to be the worst professor I've had and I'm almost out of UMass. Although he's a nice guy, he just doesn't know how to run a class.

I've never written a review before, but I had to after taking Professor Woodside's class. It's group-based, and you're stuck with the same group all semester. He's unresponsive, TAs are unhelpful, lectures are disorganized, and assignments are a mess. Avoid his class and choose Professor Glennon instead. Outrageous money also spent on assignments.

Worst class I have taken so far. Professor Woodside preaches professionalism yet continuously shows a lack thereof himself. He rambles in lectures and provides no clear expectations of what students should know. He makes students buy homework software and a marketing simulation totaling ~$135. Introduced "talking sticks" for participation (???).

Wouldn't say he's bad but he's very vague with instructions and grading. Your project grade depends on your group members and his instructions weren't clear enough, especially for the PowerPoint and presenting. Go to all the extra credit to be safe. Content was easy enough, he just didn't offer a lot.

this class is awful he doesnt teach and it has the most boring lectures possible and al of the directions are always unclear, there is participation every class, it is not that hard to get a good grade but the lectures and work are all poorly crafted and he doesnt understadn technology it is a painful class

3 part group project with over 30 pages with little to no instruction. Coordinating groups in 400 people class is difficult. Not helpful with clearing up confusion. Lectures are boring basically talking off slides and shark tank videos. Attendance is TopHat questions that do not get graded so it is almost impossible to know if you got it right

Very unhelpful in terms of grading, gives zero feedback as to why you lost points and it almost feels random. Class is all group work but project instructions are very unclear. A different professor for this class would be recommended.

Gave us a 25-page assignment instruction doc and said "This is unclear... but I'm leaving it that way so you can figure it out." Primarily group work, so if your group isn't great, it's going to be difficult. Grading was a little unclear - I lost points and received no feedback other than "good work." He's nice but not super helpful.

Class not great, group project makes up large portion of grade, so if you get a not-so-great group, you're stuck writing a big project. Does offer a bit of extra credit, which is a nice grade booster. Attendance taken over Tophat, and HW on Connect (weekly assignments due at end of semester). Don't take if you don't have to
reviews.rating_tags: Group projects--Lecture heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: This professor is ok... I emailed the TAs for help once and they directed me to the professor. He directed me back to the TAs and seemed very frustrated about it. I have not spoken or emailed him since-- does not seem approachable or like he wants to help. And having us present in a 200 person class is just evil.

The lecture was enjoyable ,with the professor making jokes to keep us engaged.Towards the end, there was a focus on group activities.With no exams and only one presentation, this class was an easy A.I would highly recommend taking this class with him. He started teaching Fall 2023 thats why people don't know of him much yet but he's incredible.

This class is easy with no exams but boring. Attendance is mandatory but every class is just a snooze fest. It is this professor's first class so I understand if he just needs to adjust but other than that, super easy and team project at the end.

Professor Woodside is a great person and has a lot of knowledge about the marketing and advertising world. However, the class is just boring. All he does is show lecture slides with definitions all class and people just do other homework while he is talking. No exams which is nice, but just a boring class.
Professor Trust is a great professor! Her work is interesting but a little time-consuming. She is very understanding and easy to talk to! I would love to take a class with her again.

One of the best classes I've ever taken, it was so interesting and Dr. Trust was an amazing professor. Super quick turnaround with grading and while there were a lot of projects/assignments, they all felt very intentional and like they had meaning.

Dr. Trust is an amazing professor. She is super caring and teaches a super engaging class. I really enjoyed taking this class. On Tuesday it would be in person and then Thursday was asynchronous with weekly assignments. This class was super interesting and different from many of the other education classes I have taken!!
Very into technlogy so beware. Lots of projects and very time consuming

She was a great professor because she seemed like she actually cared about her students. It was an online class so it was super easy. Not required to read the stuff she gives and the homework is like tops an hour a week. Lots of in-class activities and group work though.

i love her. this is the only class i learned anything in this semester. if you actually want to be a great teacher and learn about technology- this is the class for you. if you want to slip by and not apply yourself, this class isnt for you. there are easier as that fulfill this requirement, but youll get the most learning and skill from torrey

Torrey Trust is an amazing professor. She cares about her students and their success. She is very knowledgable and has some of the best teaching strategies I have ever seen. There is a good amount of homework and group projects but everything assigned is beneficial to your learning. She taught me a lot more than just the courses's content too!

Dr. Trust was fine at explaining the material but left us puzzled by the emphasis on borrowing gear for our video projects while she catered her material to smartphone videographers. She definitely was interested in helping students succeed. All work except the final project was done in-class which made it easy workload.

Trust is my favorite professor at UMass. She is extremely knowledgeable and genuinely wants students to succeed. As long as you communicate and do the work you will likely get an A. Her classes are hands on, engaging, and even if you don't like technology very interesting. She is willing to work with you so you get the most from the course possible

Dr. Trust is everything a teacher should be: knowledgable, experiences, skilled and genuinely seems to care about her students. She certainly knows her stuff and is eager to share with all who are interested. I see her becoming very valuable to the UMass College of Ed in the not-so-distant future. A+!

Dr. Trust is a real bonus for the struggling TECS program at UMass. She brings hands on experience and an enthusiasm for helping others that has been sorely lacking. Take any class with her and learn something. A pleasure to be around...

She has a pleasant personality and kind character!!. She was an excellent example for us as prospective teachers. She appreciate what her students can offer. The course material (computer Mediated Communication) was extremely interesting.

130H - Professor Tory is great - she is super nice and clearly wants to get to know her students. The material is a little tricky but super informational! No short-cuts in the class, so you'll need to do all the work but overall its pretty easy for an Honors class.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Group projects

reviews.comment: My experience was a bit different from what the other reviews describe. No one dropped, the material isn't very challenging, and Dr. Troy walks you through the public policy paper. However, the seminar format paired with Dr. Troy's lack of enthusiasm definitely make the class feel dry/unengaging. Take this class if you're interested in FOOD POLICY.
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Gives good feedback--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Dr. Troy had unrealistic expectations from students and everyone hated the class by the end of the semester. She blatantly disrespected accommodations determined by disability services, and never gave clear instructions for any of the assignments. Don't apply to the CHC Sophomores Serve program, you'll regret it. Genuinely awful person & class
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Lots of homework

reviews.comment: Dr. Troy is not only inaccessible out of class, she is not accommodating to extenuating circumstances. The class had an unnecessary amount of work, and 4 of the 13 students ended up withdrawing throughout the course of the semester.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Graded by few things--So many papers

reviews.comment: Very dry personality. While her class isn't difficult, I wouldn't recommend getting to know her further.

Professor Troy is very nice and although her lectures sometimes dragged on, she is very nice and always willing to help. There are two take home midterms, about one worksheet a week, one final research paper (up to 15 pages), and a final poster to go along with the research paper. A great way to satisfy your biology gen ed requirement!

His lectures are boring but you need attendance through iclicker, most people didn't watch the videos before class because he reviews the content in class (I never watched them and I did fine on quizzes I just studied before). The lab was fun and helpful, most of them took all 3 hours. I would take this class if you want an easy A.

Honestly this class kinda sucked because he runs it in a weird way but once you adjust and realize you don't have to do half of the work, its not that bad. Everything is online except the midyear and finals but they are only on 5 chapters each and he uses questions from the lecture/quizzes. He offers extra credit which you should definitely do.

Everything was online but the exams. There were question sets and quizzes. There is a midterm and final. Both 25 questions and worth the same as a regular quiz. There are many chances for extra credit; take it. We also did nature journals, we had to go outside and write what we observed. 10 entries. He mostly teaches through iClicker questions.

I will say there are times when you can tell even he doesn't understand his slides or content. Lots of busy work, lots of reading. You better know the slides by heart because the graded iclickers for accuracy can make or break your grade. I did the math, and you can get ONE clicker wrong each class and still be able to maintain an A. Good luck
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--EXTRA CREDIT--Lots of homework

reviews.comment: He wants you to watch 2-3 hours worth of videos before the monday class. These videos, go over the same exact stuff, sometimes word for word, that is taught in the class next week. A total waste of time. His lectures are super dry and he is terrible at explaining. Iclickers are graded, yet on average 50% of people get them wrong, per question.

If you like a reversed class structure, this is the class for you. However, if it's not.... Then you're probably better off finding a different professor. There is so much busy work, it's not even funny. Be prepared.
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Lots of homework--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Very monotone voice so the lectures are boring. iclickers are scored for accuracy, but often even he will say "i dont even know the answer to this question". also rarely replies to emails

He cares a lot and is interested in the material, but his grading criteria leaves far too much of your grade to error. It is super easy to not do get an A if you aren't getting 100's on every assignment and doing well on the iClicker questions which are graded every class. Having friends in the class is a MUST.

iClickers are graded on correctness, which is bad 'cause the questions often have multiple correct answers. Material covered in class is just sped up and less detailed version of the videos, which are often several hours, and cover the same stuff as the textbook. Don't buy the textbook, you don't need it.
Yolo

Tristram has a very monotone voice that I believe is a barrier between his enthusiasm and his students. If you look past the tone, this is a person who is very passionate about botany and wants his students to see the world in better detail. This class was easy. You have to watch lecture videos for homework, but it's better for notes in this case.

Tristram is an incredibly boring lecturer who inspires no interest in the subject. His grading criteria is unclear, and he is not a fast grader. He requires you to attend AND watch daily online lectures, and grades you on accuracy for iclickers. It is incredibly difficult to keep on top of everything.

One of the most boring lecturers I have ever had. His grading criteria is very unclear, and he takes forever to grade exams. His clickers are based on accuracy, so you have to watch online lectures in addition to going to class, which is unreasonable for a three credit class taken during a full course load.

He is passionate about ecology and has interesting lectures. You have i clicker questions that match the exams. He's very caring and most students who don't like his lectures usually don't pay attention during class. He is soft spoken and most students take advantage of that and keep talking when he is teaching. GREAT PROF!

Tristram is definitely a good guy but BE PREPARED TO GO TO EVERY CLASS. The material is not difficult but over 20% of your grade is graded on clicker questions and they are graded on correctness. So you basically have a quiz every single lecture. His tests are definitely do-able and he wants to help his students

Great professor, teaches you all the basic ecology concepts, respectful, kind and cares about his students.
You can tell that he's passionate about teaching and making you LEARN.

If you can get past how monotone his voice is, you will find that Dr. Siedler is a great prof. He cares a lot about his work and structures the class well so it easy to understand/pass. He posts video lectures, slides, has a textbook so lots of resources for learning. Cares about feedback and is willing to correct things for students' benefits.

Rather than define his goals for the class as what you can memorize, he aims to help students open their eyes to the world around them. He has a bit of favoritism, but he is a really kind guy who structures the class hoping for it to be low-stress and low-pressure for students. No mandatory lectures but you need to go to 10/12 labs. EASY quizzes.

Seidler blows me away with how knowledgeable he is. 426 is a fun and low-key class. You will learn a TON and your eyes will be opened to the beautiful world of plants. Seidler cares about his students; he's not rude at all. He can be blunt, and his voice is monotone, but he's passionate about plants and will share that passion with you.

Professor Siedler's intelligence and his expertise in his field expansive but he is dry in his lectures and monotone which makes it difficult to follow. This would be fine if it wasn't for the fact that he can be very rude and almost refuses to answer questions saying "no" or "no not even close" then walking away. Awful. Do not take his classes.

Okay, I really liked Dr. Seidler and you could tell he is very passionate about his work, BUT he has the most droning, monotoned voice I've ever heard. I literally almost fell asleep in that class just because of how he talked. You had weekly mini essays/quizzes which were easy to get 100% on. Some questions will have exact answer in the textbook

Lecture is text heavy but he puts up slides online and you really just have to listen to what he says, and he clarifies what you need to know. Lowest grade of 4 exams is dropped (final optional). Short paper, 10 lab grades. Labs can be tedious but bearable, the trips are fun! Exams are reasonable - MC T/F, practical, fill in. I learned a lot!

DO NOT TAKE ECE 197DP. He seriously doesn't teach you anything and then expects you to write a final project (only thing he grades you on) in assembly language with no resources other than a 600-page manual on how the KIM-1 works. I learned nothing from this class.

The professor will make you work outside of class if you miss class. He is easily available outside his office hour or lecture times. He can be easily found in M5 and is a pretty hilarious prof. Rigorous classes but they are fun. You won't know how 2 hours pass.
reviews.rating_tags: Accessible outside class--Participation matters--Skip class? You won't pass.

reviews.comment: When a student struggles, he responds with "look at the data sheet". His lectures are extremely difficult to follow, only like 15/110 students showed up to his lectures. He grades very late. I still don't have grades for lab1&2,and it's a week after finals. He neglects answering students on Piazza to an extreme. Just awful, the worst I've ever had.

Horrible Teacher. Really did not explain much and relied on the TA's to teach the class. Taught us the bare minimum then expected us to create something by ourselves. Expected us to code even when we had no coding experience at all. Take another intro Engineering class!

Professor Soules does not do much as the teacher of this class.  In the Introduction to Computer Engineering 112 Lab, he merely stands at the front of the class, leads the name game (every class), gives a short lesson on a new piece of equipment we will be using in the lab, then sends us on our own to build a circuit.  The TAs are very helpful.

The lab course is relatively straightforward. There was little to no interaction with the professor, as was expected. You basically sit there with your "Make: Electronics" book and go through the various hands-on projects. As long as your final project at the end does what it's supposed to do, you will receive an A for the lab.

You guys are missing the point in taking his classes. IT'S ABOUT DIY. You are studying to be engineers not spoon feed helpless dumb wits. DIY learn to learn he can help you teach your self by guiding you in the right direction.
not helpful
Cool guy outside the classroom, but horrible teacher... really had to teach myself!
teacher does not explain clearly, needs to be more specific; is entertaining but lazy; students tend to teach themselves in this class
Very strange guy.  Awful teacher, couldn't explain he way out of a paper bag.  Half the time the students know more them him.
No Comments
Aweful class. Worst I have ever taken. He is a pretty cool guy, don't get me wrong, he just doesn't explain ANYTHING. Its the worst
I thought he was fun and interseting, haven't got my grade yet though
He is WEIRD!!!  He is NOT a predictable grader and is strange!

He's a really good professor despite the ratings. The test is like entirely stuff we've gone over in class, so as long as your paying attention in class you should be able to secure an A. You can also average a 70 test score and still get an A. It's a very forgiving and very interesting class!

This guy is an absolute G. Not sure how people complained. I like physics. I think that is a difference between me and others who only wanna get the gen ed over with and got mad he wants you to actually learn. He's literally changing the curriculum and grading of this HARD class just to see students win and actually learn without just chasing an A.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Caring--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: He is so enthusiastic about physics, I love him. Literally one of the most accessible professors, you can knock on his door anytime and he'll help you work through a problem. Once I actually listened to his advice and "stopped panicking, just start with the principle" I went from a 70 on the first exam to a 100 on the second exam. Great guy

P132 introduced me to CCPH. Prof has this pedagogy of being anti "puzzle physics" which basically means you can not figure your way out of a test question if you are shaky on the content by looking at the formulas. Overall I am grateful for the grading scale as my test average was ~30% and I still managed to get a C by doing well in other parts.

The grading is 45% for exams, there are 3. Each exam is 10-12 questions, so if you get one wrong, you're kinda screwed. The grading scale is generous (89 is an A). Attendance is required b/c he has quizzes you need a code for. He gives multiple +0.5 extra credit options over the semester. All physics courses suck but at least he is entertaining.

The best physics professor I have had so far. Physics is tough to understand, and he made sure his students understood the concepts by doing many conceptual problems. However his style of teaching is not for all. I appreciate his lectures and his passion in helping students in the class very much. If you are a serious learner, you will like this

there's like no overlap between what we learn in class and what's on the exams. literally every single person was cheating on the exams and he doesn't curve them at all. he's a really nice person just not a good professor. I would rather walk on shards of glass than take this course again.

you teach yourself then come to class to practice very confused. TAs are unconfident during exam reviews and contradictory. brokk is caring but cannot teach well. exams insanely conceptual, abstract, and 7-10 questions. he wrote the textbook and it isnt the same as course/exam material. Lab material also did not relate to class material.

did not enjoy this class. he makes basic concepts extremely to grasp using conceptual questions on exams that make it hard to even understand what he is asking. cares about students but the layout and setup and teaching yourself then coming in to practice is extremely unhelpful. genuinely shouldve been one of my easier classes but it tanked my GPA

genuinely makes simple physics concepts so hard to grasp by using conceptual and abstract questions/ scenarios. i would understand concepts but get completely lost on the wording and format of exam questions. textbook and homework isn't really what we learn. nice dude he cares but terrible class + setup + bad teaching style
Really caring professor who, if you come prepared to class, will teach you everything you need to know.

Honestly, one of my favorite professors at UMass. He tries to learn as many names as he can even in a big lecture! Tips to do well: go to every class, read/skim the txtbook for the HW, prepare for inclass quizzes by reviewing the HW Q its based on, and do as many practice problems as you can (esp from practice exam) and go to physics help room! GL!

Brokk is nice. His teaching style, however, is harrowing. Studying for his violating 7 question exams is hell because he tries to reinvent the wheel with the way he teaches you normally stupidly easy physics concepts. The cherry on top is that I can't even find external resources to supplement literally anything Brokk taught in class. What a joke.
Grading system is messed up. Will make students miss an A by very very little percentages.

Homework and practice problems are nothing like the exams. Textbook was useless for the last few units. Definitely recommend going to class, the in-class problems and practice exams are more like the exams. The exams were hard and the final was extremely difficult. Nice guy and wanted us to learn, but it's a hard class that requires tons of effort.

Nice guy but not relevant when you don't learn anything. This is a flipped classroom where you're expected to teach yourself. Then the exams are difficult on top of that and not similar to the practice exams or homework. The whole physics department is just .... the only reason students are able to pass is because of the crazy grading scale

Brokk is definitely a divisive lecturer. To be frank, the Intro Physics program at UMass s u c k s. Brokk however, is very passionate and engaging. I loved his in-class experiments/demonstrations. The tests are not easy and border on abstract. There is a lot he does to support those who struggle including generous grade scaling. (An 89 is an A)

This prof uses a textbook he wrote and teaches physics in a way that makes things way more complicated than they have to be. The tests are heavily based around the lectures and are only 12 questions and are semi-obscure. The class is scaled and the prof has a lot of energy, but the lectures were so confusing and the slides were unhelpful.

He is rated poorly because teaching yourself stuff is hard and physics is hard. Course designed so that each unit connects back to biology/chemistry. There is basically infinite help and resources, you just have to put in work. He is funny and a great teacher but his personality is not for everyone. Exams are kinda evil (8-10 q) but 89% is an A.
Smart guy but can't teach. Exams are difficult as I mostly taught myself the content using homework questions and the textbook. Good luck.

Prof. Toggerson is a great person who teaches with passion. Lots of help available outside of class. However... hw/exams are VERY hard and require a lot of studying. 1 or 2 quizzes a week, long HW due before unit is taught, and lab (which isn't super intense). need 89+ to get an A. Not impossible but LOTS of effort needs to be put in for an A.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Test heavy--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Brokk's class is no walk in the park - the exams are brutal and the flipped classroom model can be a struggle. But with the grade scale and Brokk's genuine desire to help, you can get through it. Definitely utilize Unstuck AI and other study resources to stay on top of this tricky course.

He is very supportive and understanding. There's a lot of TBL, but the group work can really boost your grade. You'll do well on the exams as long as you review the lecture notes, homework, and practice problems. He also offers plenty of office hours, which is great!

Brokk tries a little too hard to be an educator instead of a teacher. He focuses on his work learning how to teach rather than actually teaching. 181 Lab was straightforward, however, he expected no lab to be finished in class, nor did he explain (well) any of the code provided. He threw code at us, lectured for half of class, then said "hop to it"
great professor

The exams are insanely hard and are only max 10 questions. HOWEVER, the scale in this class means an A is only 85% which helps a ton. He is funny and very eager to help students. He really wants you to understand and knows this subject is difficult. Homework is easy and you only have 4 quizzes.
Professor Toggerson is a nice person so this is more of a critique on the class itself. this class is not well set up and its would be much better set up similar to the chemistry classes

He is the most obnoxious and insecure professor I've ever had. Every question would be met with "well, when you take quantum field theory..." or "when I took quantum field theory". We get it, you're smart. Now teach us the material please. Lectures were painfully slow and boring. Often he didn't know the answer questions. Fun class material, though
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Lots of homework--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: Physics 131 is one of the worst structured classes I have ever taken. Instead of a lecture session where you could learn topics and progress through the course, you have a TBL session where you spend 40+ minutes on two problems that you have no idea how to do. You also have a lab session with a different group so you better hope you get lucky twice

WORST CLASS, WORST PROFESSOR. THIS IS THE WORST CLASS I HAVE EVER TAKEN. BROKK DOES NOT CARE WHEN HIS STUDENTS ARE CLEARLY STRUGGLING. THE TEACHING ASSISTANTS ALL TELL YOU DIFFERENT THINGS AND CONTRADICT ONE ANOTHER. STUDENTS ARE CONSTANTLY LEFT CONFUSED AND DISCOURAGED. PROFESSOR REFUSES TO ADMIT THAT HES THE REASON STUDENTS ARE STRUGGLING.

This is the worst professor or teacher I have ever had in my life, and he is one of the better ones for the physics department. The HW and quizzes do not prepare you for the exam AT ALL. He expects you to fully understand the concepts before the unit has begun. He barely lectures and only does practice problems in class. WORST CLASS EVER.

I hate this class. Do yourself a favor and take an online physics class. This is a terrible joke! You read his book to prepare for quizzes but none of that prepares you for the actual exam. If you get a 70 in the exam you are a genius.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Group projects--Test heavy

reviews.comment: Worst grade I've ever received on an exam was in this class even though the topics were simple/introductory level. He says you learn more in a flipped classroom style but haven't learned much. Paying for a course to teach myself the material.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Lots of homework

reviews.comment: WHY DOES HE MAKE PHYSICS SEEM SO HARD? HOW CAN I GET As IN ORGO YET BE STRESSED OUT IN THIS CLASS. THE WHOLE FLIPPED CLASSROOM THING DOESN'T WORK IT'S HORRIBLE AND NOT EVERYONE CAN DO PROBLEMS INFRONT OF THE CLASS SOME OF US GET ANXIOUS WHEN WE ARE TOLD TO DO HARD PROBLEMS THAT WE HAVEN'T BEEN TAUGHT INFRONT OF THE CLASS. TAKE PHYSICS ONLINE

This class is bad. The course should be very easy, but its dumbed down too much. Toggerson also does a very poor job teaching, and students are at the mercy of the TAs. The TAs often dont understand how to do problems or tell they will tell you to do the wrong thing. The  worst part about this class was there were a TON of mistakes everywhere.

Very passionate about the subject, his explanations and examples made abstract topics easy to understand. Help is there if you need it. Little work outside class, exams and HW are super easy if you pay attention, read the textbook, and practice a little. l. Only problem was that the practice/homework often had errors he had to fix retroactively.

Honestly, this class was not as hard as everyone says; the material is not too difficult. Brokk is extremely enthusiastic about physics, however he is not a good teacher. He claims to value suggestions but will not implement any constructive criticism. I did not enjoy the TBL style learning but working in groups is the only way to learn.

TAKE THIS CLASS WITH BROKK!!! Brokk is an extremely funny, engaging, and caring professor with a unique approach to learning/teaching but it WORKS! You get to learn google sheets too which is very useful. Homework, exams, etc are all very reasonable. There are a lot of team-based activities in this course, but it can only work in your advantage.

Great person that cares about his students. Lab part of the class is useless and boring. I don't understand the way he teaches but exams are very easy. Homework and quizzes have nothing to do with the exams. For people that say nothing is like the exam, that is a straight out lie. If you can do practice questions he posts, you can easily get an A.

Prof. Toggerson knows his stuff but can't really teach others.use spreadsheets for all calculations and no calculator is allowed. the class also had a group grading system where each quiz was given as a group and individually which helped a little, but not much.NOTHING prepares you for the exams. Slides are difficult to understand.

Brokk is incredibly confusing (explanations make no sense, he goes off on random tangents instead of explaining anything). Impossible to know what to study and concepts that have never been mentioned in class show up on the exams. Impossible to learn in class and impossible to study on your own (because you have no idea what to study)

Toggerson is one of the best professors I've had, he cares, makes his own textbook so you don't have to pay, and he is hilarious. One thing I would say is that he has a different teaching method. It's very group based, so if you have a good group you're good. Exams are not similar to practice exams, if you understand the topics you should be fine.
Terribly organized. I felt like I learned nothing except laughing when he tells cheesy jokes.

Brokk is a nice guy but the exams are much harder than any material covered in class. Luckily he does occasionally remove questions that everyone got wrong or were overly confusing. If you do well in the lab it will save your grade.

Was SO nervous for this class but it is SO manageable. His office hours are the best and he really minimizes the material to what we need to know (really KIN focused). The class gets scaled so much that its possible to end with over a 100. Study slides and the "next time problems". If David is your SI, you are golden!! Don't cut corners you good.
reviews.rating_tags: Clear grading criteria--Beware of pop quizzes--Test heavy

reviews.comment: Can not teach at all. You will learn nothing except how to memorize the practice exams to pass the exam.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Lecture heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Very funny quirky guy. I hate physics but he made it make sense for me. I can see how his teaching style wouldn't work for others--some people told me they like the more mathematical approach to physics. Toggerson tries to separate physics from math and visualize it from the perspective of a life scientist. Tests were hard but possible. Go to SIs.

Exams were extremely difficult for the class level. Homework due before the unit is even started in class really makes it worse. His "textbook" that he wrote is pretty bad with no practice problems. You forget everything by the exam because there is no homework due throughout the unit which makes practice hard.

Toggerson was, by far, the most caring professor of a gen ed I have met. He genuinely wants to see you succeed and if you give him your best, he will give you his best. Don't be afraid to go talk with him privately for help and advice.

Very nice and understanding and has a grading scale so that a 89 is an A but his lecture slides are so disorganized and he does not explain things well. I failed every exam but still passed the class. Lab grades depend on TA. Does give extra credit though and I would do it. Quizzes were pretty easy though as long as you look at the homework.

You should always try to go to class! Ask questions and go to office hours if you don't understand something. He explains things pretty well. The practice exams are similar to the real exam, so you know what it will be like. Be expected to learn...it's not an easy topic! Dr. T wants you to succeed, so use the resources given and you will succeed.
reviews.rating_tags: Clear grading criteria--Beware of pop quizzes--Caring

reviews.comment: I am shocked by the bad reviews. Brokk is one of my favorite professors I've had at UMass so far. His grading scale is very generous where an A is an 89. 3 exams 15% each, homework & quizzes 10% , lab 20%, & team exams 15%. He is very passionate and makes physics fun and applicable to real life, I genuinely learned a lot.

His class is just a lot. He talks very fast which can be annoying plus I was in the 9:05 class so I was not a big fan of getting up that early. Exams are very conceptual. I would have preferred the TBL style were we as a group do practice problems rather than him leading it. The syllabus is 30 pages long so beware.
reviews.rating_tags: EXTRA CREDIT--Beware of pop quizzes--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: always keeps you late

The best way to put his teaching style is this, he throws you in into the deep end of a pool when you don't know how to swim, and once you've struggled and drowned, thats when he teaches. Don't get me wrong, he's a great guy. However, he needs to stick with being in a lab and not a professor.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Lots of homework

reviews.comment: Go to class, pay attention.  Great lectures.

He makes you read then entire unit and do homework on it. Then he does the unit again over the following weeks. I would rather a step by step lecture vs reading his own textbook (with many grammatical errors). I received a 98.5 final grade but am really having to buckle down in his class. it is doable but just mad annoying in my opinion.

I have no idea what the deal is with the bad reviews. Brokk has been wonderful so far! His lectures are interesting and engaging and he makes sure to cater to his students' learning needs, especially with the recent mask mandate lift. While this is a TBL class, I decided to not be part of a team and I don't feel behind or anything.

He’s not bad so far. The material is hard but he gives you enough practice to understand and a bunch of office hours to i attend. I just took his first exam and got an 87 which is an A- in his class. So far it’s not as bad as some of the comments make it out to be. Don’t use the homework to study is my best advice use the practice exam.

I'm here to address all the reviews that say his exams are unreasonable. His exams are perfectly reasonable. Do the practice test and the practice problems, and nothing on the exam will catch you off guard. Brokk gives great lectures and makes the material approachable. Don't be afraid of this class!
He wants his students to succeed. His lectures are actually pretty interesting and he always makes them fun and engaging.

I'm shocked at these reviews. Best professor I've had. HW is due before you learn it but all answers are in the FREE textbook. 3 points of extra credit to final grade & he's seriously passionate. Demos make concepts stick. Collab exams boost ur grade. He DOES answer Qs in class what?? & Test Qs are just not verbatim to classwork. Expect to LEARN.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Caring--EXTRA CREDIT

reviews.comment: One of the worst professors ever, all of the reviews below are true. He assumes you know chemistry and it is not a prerequisite. He skips steps when giving examples and refuses to answer questions in class. He has questions on the tests which he never taught. Your only hope is to get a good team in this TBL classroom. Good luck...
reviews.rating_tags: Test heavy--Beware of pop quizzes--Tough grader

reviews.comment: He's a nice guy, but is not a very good professor imo. He does not clearly teach the material, and asks a lot of trick questions. He uses team-based learning so be hopeful your team mates show up and know the material. Unit homework is due before the unit even begins in class so you have to do a lot of learning out of class. Would not recommend.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Skip class? You won't pass.--Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: Brokk and his condescending lectures will live on in my nightmares. He is rude, arrogant, and refuses to respond to student emails. He enjoys making it difficult to learn. He gives ridiculously hard exams and acts like grades don't matter which is not true if you plan on going to grad school. Avoid team-based learning like the plague!

I would not recommend this class. The in class problems and his way of teaching was extremely confusing. The class is group work heavy. However, if you and the members have no idea what is going on, you are screwed. The HW problems do not match test questions at all in terms of difficulty. You have to teach yourself the material. Do not take this
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Test heavy--Beware of pop quizzes

reviews.comment: Dr. Togg is one of the best profs I've ever had. Synthesizes physics with other fields (bio, orgo, etc) to show us why our concepts matter. Excellent examples, extremely engaging and caring. Time literally flies in this class because he makes it so interesting. I'm awful at physics but he explained the concepts so well I got an A on our first exam.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Caring--EXTRA CREDIT

reviews.comment: Worst professor I've ever had, and I'm a senior. Rambles for so long and is not helpful whatsoever. Has a 20+ page syllabus. Never responds to emails. Was late grading and missed deadline for final grades. He somehow took an intro class and made it so unbelievably confusing and complicated. Went on a 15min rant about cheating to guilt trip students

Pros: extra credit, passionate about the course Cons: HW and labs are unrelated / won't help study, minimal exam guidance (particularly the final) Tips: Exams are based off of lecture content but never questions from class, google topics as you go (the organic chem tutor, Bozeman Science)
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Lecture heavy--EXTRA CREDIT

reviews.comment: Most bizarre class, takes forever to reply to emails, missed the faculty deadline for final grades, don't know what this man is doing with his time.

NOT ABLE to finish grading more than one week after when the grade is due. The lecture does not teach you anything, you have to study by yourself. Put you into a small study group, but when the teammate is bad, or just rate you maliciously, you can not change anything, you just lost your grade. HW does not prepare for your exam.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Skip class? You won't pass.--Tough grader

reviews.comment: Even does not keep grading deadline. Makes students tired even After the end of semester.

Dr. T is a great professor and made this class enjoyable for me! I would recommend going to every lecture and lab to get the most out of this class! The exams are based on lectures and are not too bad if you put some effort into studying for them. He does give a lot of extra credit if you fill out the forms he asks you to!

Brokk is a great teacher and made physics enjoyable. It is okay if you don't do the best on tests, you can still do well in the class overall. There is a good amount of group work and I would definitely attend the lectures and stay on track if you want to succeed.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Clear grading criteria--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: Teacher ruined my entire three years here at the University of Massachusetts Amherst. Quite possibly the most horrendous class they offer, for a million dollars I would not take this course again. Lectures beyond difficult, hours of labs and homework with no correlation to the work on hand and little to no fun was had during the entire year. BAD!
Run!!!

When I didn't do great on the first exam I met with him and he told me my study habits were awful. He tries so hard to teach physics in a "unique" way that he ends up completely confusing us. HW doesn't have to do with the exams. Only redeeming quality is giving some extra credit.
Taking this class online was terrible. Boring lectures, labs that make no sense and take hours, very hard exams. Can't wait to just be done with this class
Too many things to do, study, exam and lab are not related to the class..
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Skip class? You won't pass.--Test heavy

reviews.comment: Worst class ever. Online labs are ridiculous and have nothing to do with the course material. Exams are hard, we have a quiz in class every day.
Very caring and gives extra credit. I do agree that although his tests are fair, they do require quite a bit of studying.
Least favorite class I have taken. Labs are so long and irrelevant to the course material and the exams have nothing to do with the homework + are extremely difficult. Teaching is confusing.

One of my favorite professors at UMass. He was very accommodating and gave extra credit and also dropped quiz grades, since you will have one every day. If you do not go to his lectures you will not do well in the class. His grading was very fair and he cared a lot about both the students and the subject.
reviews.rating_tags: Accessible outside class--Skip class? You won't pass.--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: Dr. Toggerson is a very caring guy. He definitely cares about his students + their wellbeing. With that being said this class was so hard, especially remote. The labs were so long and directions vague. His exams were extremely difficult. Make sure you attend every class and learn material as you go. The good thing is this class very scaled.
reviews.rating_tags: Respected--Skip class? You won't pass.--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: I have never seen a professor who was so passionate about teaching a subject and his energy at 9am was appreciated. On the other hand, his exams are difficult in general (especially the final) but the way the course is graded makes it possible to get an A in the class without acing the exams. Do well on the labs, homework, and in-class quizzes.

If you like bureaucracy, take him. He has a 24 page syllabus. I wish I were exaggerating. He took one of the easiest classes in the university, and made it somewhat challenging. Remarkable. He complicates simple topics, and rarely communicates what you need to know. The HW is untaught material, and his class is a confusing (mandatory) waste of time

Professor Toggerson is not the worst professor I have had, but given the difficulty of the material and exams, he did not do it justice in his lectures. He was unclear on what was important to know for exams (especially the final), so we went in blind. when people were caught using chegg on exam 2, he did not even consider that he didn't teach well
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Skip class? You won't pass.--Test heavy

reviews.comment: Brokk is a good guy. I simply cannot understand these other reviews claiming he is a bad professor. Im no physics major but this class seems much easier than other higher related physics classes. You have to do the work for a good grade but its kinda easy.

IM SO HAPPY I WILL NEVER EVER EVER SEE HIM EVER AGAIN. I HATEEEEEEEEEEEED HIS CLASS :) he tries to be 'on point' by giving us a 15-page syllabus which no other professor does. I think he is just trying to always do less work.
The only thing I wish is for the professor to actually try to lecture instead of making us learn the material on our own.....
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Test heavy--Tough grader

reviews.comment: I used to love physics UNTIL I had to take this class and now I never want to see physics ever again :)
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Beware of pop quizzes

reviews.comment: He made us read and take a quiz on a 50 - page syllabus... i think that's a little extreme and the class shouldn't have to be so "complicated". I wish the class had clearer grading criteria. I wouldn't recommend taking this class..

I've had Brokk for both Physics 131 & 132. To be honest, it took me over a semester to actually like him. However, he is super fair when it comes to student suggestions and you can tell that he actually cares about his students. The exams are heavily based on content from lectures, quizzes, and practice problems. Requires a lot of studying time.

Dr. Toggerson is an amazing person. He cares so much about his students and actually makes class fun. If you have a good group, do your homework and study you'll be fine. The TBL style class is so nice for physics and he is great at teaching. I really recommend taking physics with him he's the best.

Brokk is a pretty good teacher explains concepts well and wills people to participate during lecture. Tests are right about average and curve helps so an 89 or above is an A. Do the homework and don't skip class.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Skip class? You won't pass.--Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: Condescending and rude. Tried to make physics interesting and tries to teach it "his way", which you won't find anywhere else - ask him about other methods of doing things for clarification as seen all over the web and from other professors, he'll just shut you down and snap at you. Not funny, not a good professor, hope to never see him again.

Toggerson is a great professor. I absolutely hate physics but he makes you interested in the subject. If you follow his way of learning it will be easier. The exams are extremely difficult mostly because there are only a few questions to the exam. The class is scaled however and you will be pleasantly surprised about your grade.

While participation isn't mandatory, skipping the class will only hurt you. Make sure to actually try problems during class as it helps prepare you for the exams. There is a lot of homework, but TA's and Piazza can help a lot for ones you are stuck on. This semester he stopped doing in-class quizzes, but beware because it's easy to forget them.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--LOTS OF HOMEWORK--LECTURE HEAVY

reviews.comment: Great class and great teacher. Yes it's pretty difficult for most people, but Brokk presents it in a very interesting and engaging way. His class was the first time in my life I've actually enjoyed physics. However, the tests are very difficult. I would definitely recommend him over anyone else teaching physics 131/132.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--TEST HEAVY

reviews.comment: Grading is fuzzy. Nothing is clear cut, and doesn't clarify if you ask about it. He's rude when communicating. He's one of those professors that the subject makes so much sense to him that he can't understand why it doesn't make sense to you. Classwork is easy, but exams are difficult and near impossible.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough Grader--TEST HEAVY--GRADED BY FEW THINGS

reviews.comment: Dr. Toggerson is the best physics professor I've ever had. He acknowledges that the subject is hard to understand but is very clear in his lectures and is super accessible and helpful outside of class in office hours. The class is structured fairly and if you put a the work in, you might just not hate physics! :)
Quirky but truly cares about his students and their success. A great class to take especially for those who need it for a gen-ed but didn't like or didnt do well in high school physics.
reviews.rating_tags: ACCESSIBLE OUTSIDE CLASS--Clear grading criteria--EXTRA CREDIT

reviews.comment: I don't understand why he gets doubted a lot. Toggerson is the best physics professor. He wants you to learn and succeed. I hate Physics with a passion, but taking it with this professor is a must. I ended up receiving over 100 in the class. And to remind you, I hate Physics but if you put in the effort, you'll succeed. Recommend Toggerson 1000000%
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--ACCESSIBLE OUTSIDE CLASS--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: Toggerson is really amazing, he wants to get you learning and thinking differently than you have in high school and once you commit to his way, the class is 10x easier. There is a lot of homework, but there is 9 to 5, 4-day a week tutoring center of TA's that is ESSENTIAL to go to. Exams are tough, so do all the practice he gives.
reviews.rating_tags: LOTS OF HOMEWORK--GROUP PROJECTS--Tests are tough

reviews.comment: Brokk is such a good professor. He offers a lot of help and is very reasonable. The class has a large scale overall (still capable of getting a B if you do poorly on exams). Exams definitely require an understanding of material but he preps you fairly well with examples and LOTS of practice in class.

I took his Phys 131&132. He is an amazing professor! Humorous, patient and unprejudiced. No attendance(you won't miss the class as long as you like physics cuz his class is literally interesting), great amount of extra credits (he shows the mercy every time). Office hour and TA tutoring center are provided every week. Strongly suggesting!

Brokk loves to make something not meant to be group work into group work, like say just sitting in a lecture hall. His methods are a little weird and the tests are sometimes nothing like class work, but the amount of extra credit hidden in this course is insane. Do the assignments and watch as your test average of 75 turns into 100.

Toggerson really puts in the effort to help his students. I had him for both Physics 131 and 132 and it's clear that he really cares about teaching and inspiring his students. Physics is hard in general and Toggy always tries to work with the feedback of the class. Don't be scared by his rating, he is honestly the most caring professor I've met.

Don't listen to the other pathetic comments made on here by others. Brokk's a real gem. He's an amazing lecturer and is always there willing to help students learn at his office hours, except only about 20/700 students ever show to his office hours so the people that right negatively towards Brokk are from the other 680 people in physics 132.

A lot of people on here are being unfair to Toggerson. Yeah, the class is hard as all heck but he understands he's teaching to non-physics majors and factors that into his  grading and scaling. Plus every version of this class is hard, its hard subject material if youre not very math orientated. Again a lot of extra credit, plenty of time for hw.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Skip class? You won't pass.--EXTRA CREDIT

reviews.comment: homework makes me want to jump out of a very tall building
Either goes too fast... or waaaayyy to slow. There is no in-between and leaves students lost. I used to love physics.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--LOTS OF HOMEWORK--LECTURE HEAVY

reviews.comment: Brokk may be passionate about what he teaches, but he is not an effective professor. He tries to come off as a caring professor, but he is rude and disrespectful in & out of class. I do not recommend taking a class with Brokk; he does not care about his students, even if you put in the effort to do well. My least favorite professor at UMass by far.

Brokk is the best teacher i have ever had. He has made physics my favorite class by far which is crazy because i HATED it in high school. He is so enthusiastic and friendly and you can tell he is passionate about his job. Show that you are interested in the class and your grade will reflect that. 11/10 amazing guy.

Professor Toggerson's rating on this website is beyond me. He is dynamic and integrated TBL perfectly with lecture in addition to being  the most  dedicated prof Ive had at UMass. He seriously wants everybody to do well and makes you appreciate physics and not pure math! He is the mad scientist that the whole class respects.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--ACCESSIBLE OUTSIDE CLASS--Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: I understand a lot of people don't like him because of his TBL structure and difficult exams, but it is pretty easy to get an A in class if you put in the effort. He is scales and is super duper nice!!

If you put in the time and effort to do the 5 homework assignments you will do well on the quizzes and if you ask questions in class you will do well on the exams. Yes the exam average is very low but THE CLASS IS SCALED SO MUCH. Anything above an 86 is an A. You also get a team multiplier at the end of the semester up to 1.1 I think, so 70x1.177%

He's honestly a really smart man. Put in the time to figure out the Mastering Physics homework, and pay attention to his in class conceptual problems. They're huge on the tests. I'd definitely take him for 132 but i not think he's teaching until Spring '17. Good Luck and have faith in TBL

Professor Toggerson knows a lot. He's a very smart guy, and if you go to his office hours for help, he gives you excellent explanations. The material is hard and sometimes he isn't clear, but if you put in the work, you'll be fine. The Team-Based Learning aspect of this class though sucks, but it can help your grade if you're a good team member.

The class is really not bad. All the exams are 75:25 pyramid, even though he doesn't describe them that way.  Exam average is a C with his scale. The homework counts for a lot and is fairly easy. If your team likes you they can give you a 1.14 multiplier at the end for all team grades.  So an 80 become a 91.2 which is an A.  Team stuff counts half

Tests are horrific; class average is in the 50's and that's his goal. The TBL part is the most useless, counterproductive teaching method for a physics class. You have to teach yourself everything, no exaggeration, and even then, you can fail the quizzes and tests. Overall one of the worst classes I've taken. Lecture is horrible. AVOID THIS CLASS.

The worst class I have ever taken in my life. If you can avoid TBL classes, do so. You basically teach yourself the entire course. You will be teaching yourself one unit, while also "learning" a different unit in class, then he will test you on the unit you taught yourself. The work he expects you to do outside of class is phenomenalEXPECT HOMEWORK

I think this professor is pretty bad. I dropped the class early on because I hated his teaching style so much. I guess nothing against him, but he expects you to teach yourself everything and thats not cool, especially for a subject as confusing as physics.
Never teach in class. He wants us to learn from homework.

As someone that enjoyed Physics in high school, I am very disappointed in Toggerson's approach. By putting the workload entirely on us and hiding behind team-based learning as an excuse for incompetence, I am now going to do terribly on my first homework and RAT because the reading did not prepare me for the assessments whatsoever. 1/5.

Does not teach. Literally, you are expected to just read the book and there is no lecture whatsoever. Want to take physics with Toggerson? You're better off just buying a book and teaching yourself than paying $20k to have a professor tell you to read a book and teach yourself. Thanks UMass. I got to teach myself physics.
I hated this class and the structure of the course. Brokk was rude and unhelpful when asked questions and made the material worse than it had to be. I would not take another class with him.

The grading and homework in this class is more confusing than the material. The structure was a mess and hopefully they change it. However, Brokk was a really understanding and nice guy and made the class much easier. He really enjoys what he does and he was probably the only tolerable thing about this course.

I have always disliked physics. I was very confused the whole semester. This is the lowest level physics class offered (I believe) and was not that easy. It was a "teach yourself ahead of lecture" type class and team based learning. I hope they improve the class structure. Only did well because participation grade was contributed GREATLY.

Dr. Toggerson really knows what he's talking about, but physics is just generally tough for most people.  For some reason, attendance is worth about 35% of your grade, so yeah, make sure you go to class. As long as you put in the work, you'll come out just fine.

Showing up and filling in a scantron was 30% of the final grade. Literally just put down your name, SID, and a few bubbled answers and sneak out.  He tries really hard and believes in the power of TBL but it sucks ass. HW, lab, AND test material are not covered in class because he takes all class to explain 1 problem. Gotta learn on your own.

Only a few assignments, but they are kinda big. A presentation and an interview. Not the easiest first year seminar to take, but not that bad. Wouldn't recommend taking the class, but she's really nice.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Caring--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: I had Dr. U for equine management and loved it. She's an amazing professor and I highly recommend her for any course you can take with her! She really cares about her students.

Very fun and easy class. Accommodates for any skill level around horses and material is very important for future skills around horses. Leave at least 30 minutes between passing periods to get to and from this class as you need to drive to the Hadley Farm.

SHE IS AMAZING! Dr. U is definitely one of my favorite people at UMass. She's passionate about horses and makes me want to learn more about them even though I am very very very allergic. It was a first year seminar so there wasn't any work she gave a lot of advice on what to do with our future careers. She is also SO funny.
LOVE DR. U! Amazing person, very welcoming and caring. Was more than willing to answer my questions and provide me with any and all resources necessary for success! If you get her, you're lucky!

Equine mgmt was by far one of my favorite classes. The course was hands on and Dr U taught us many techniques used in this field. Her lessons were taught in the barn with a horse which provided students with a great visual representation. She customizes her class material with what the students want to learn. Weekly assignments quizzes and projects

Very informative and knowledgeable. Super sweet and looking forward to questions. Designed the course curriculum based on student responses to what we were interested in learning about. A little hard to reach outside of class but understandable. Not a difficult teacher at all. Super understanding with extensions and accommodations.

I took Women in Science. Great and interesting seminar to take. Rarely homework and no exams/quizzes. Dr. Urichio is a good prof! All projects for grades and some can be done in groups. Attendance is required because its a small course. Super easy A definitely recommend.
She's an amazing professor! Very thorough and very helpful if you're willing to ask. Understanding and will usually give you an extension if you really need one. 100% recommend.

Dr. Uricchio did a fantastic job teaching 236! The material was presented in an easy manner and the course was definitely paced well. I learned so much about equine science in a short period of time and it peaked my interest in equine medicine! Ill be taking the second part of the course and definitely recommend Dr. Uricchio.
She is amazing! Such an intelligent professor who wants the best for all of her students. Easy to learn from and easy to know what you are being graded on. Very fair professor
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Participation matters--ACCESSIBLE OUTSIDE CLASS

reviews.comment: Very knowledgeable about a myriad of equine topics. Could be quicker about returning assignments but if you have any questions she will answer them.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--SO MANY PAPERS--TEST HEAVY

reviews.comment: Dr. U has a I know everything and you know nothing attitude that makes her classes miserable. Difficult to ask questions in and out of class without being shut down. Not a good addition to the Animal Science department. Wish someone else would teach her courses. Poor communication skills.

Doesn't post very wordy powerpoints and tests on very specific info. Won't answer emails. Constantly hands out materials and assignments very late(like 3weeks/month). Rarely extends deadlines. Poor time management. Often late to classes. Boring classes. Teaches the same info repeatedly. Assigns a lot of busy work. Horrible lecturer. Worse adviser.
reviews.rating_tags: LOTS OF HOMEWORK--SO MANY PAPERS--TEST HEAVY

reviews.comment: Dr. Uricchio was both my professor and my advisor for my entire college career. She is an amazing professor who really cares about her students. She can be firm when she needs to be, but her ultimate goal is to see you succeed. Couldn't have done it without her.

Great guy, interesting lectures if you like geography, very passionate about what he does. Weekly quizzes but they're pretty easy, and a midterm and final project, but he forgot to give us the midterm project so we just didn't have to do it.
Each class, while going over the lecture, he has his eyes closed and mumbles to himself rather than the students. He loves to go on tangents and talk about the most random things.

Comes to every class late and spends five minutes trying to turn on his laptop and find the PPT. He talks with his eyes closed and mumbles to himself, with no interaction with students at all. Goes on to stories that are far from the course content, with slow progress. To compensate he simply jumps over sections and those are still being tested.
Nothing he talked about in class was on the quizzes. The lectures were mostly tangents.

This is a easy gen-ed, and I recommend it to everyone. Weekly open-note quizzes based on lecture/reading, final project is a simple slide-show that takes about 2 hours, attendance optional for lectures, and attendance mandatory for discussions. Only downside is that "homework" (quizzes) are on Pearson so you have to buy the book to access.

Professor Applegate was one of my favorite professors here. His lectures were very entertaining and he had lots of interesting stories to tell. His slides were easy to follow and take notes on. The workload was light--read a chapter of the textbook and do a quiz on it. Final was a easy 2 hour project, no exam.

prof applegate was nice and has a dry sense of humor. the class overall was so easy, i stopped going after the first month and have an A. discussion sections are required but helpful, and make up almost half of your grade in the class. the other half of your grade is weekly quizzes (open note) and one final slides project. no midterm or final.

Guy does not have his act together. Consistently comes in late and bad mouths the university that employs him. Talked mostly about when he traveled around Europe and non-sensical rants about his disappointment of a son. Super weird. Class is easy though, just if you value your time find another Gen Ed to fill your DG credit.
if you want an interesting and engaging class do not take one with applegate as the lecturer. rants on and on about nonsense
don't take him if you need extra stimulation. it drags on

I definitely recommend GEO220 if your thinking about taking it for an elective. Prof Applegate is super chill. Weekly online quizzes and mandatory discussions (discussions are super light). I missed two quizzes and he let me take them for full credit.

Great professor, really interesting to listen to. Only graded on out of class weekly quizzes. You might not agree with a lot of what he is saying, he has a lot of strong political opinions, but if you take that with a grain of salt and listen to the other stuff he is really good. You may not even need notes for this course.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Weekly online quizzes, 2 writing assignments, and a project instead of a final. He rambled a lot during his lecture about things not related to the class. This would be fine if he were clear about what he would test you on. There was clear criteria for writing assignments, but I was always going into the tests blind.
The professor is decent, but what's more important is that the class is incredibly easy. It's the perfect course to fulfill the SB and DG gened requirements and guarantees an easy A.
reviews.rating_tags: Clear grading criteria--Respected--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Applegate is a yapper to the highest degree. Very nice but lecture is a 50-minute, monotone soliloquy.  Doesn't matter much cause quizzes are all textbook info and open note. Show up, don't forget a quiz and you'll get an easy A+. Also, didn't post the slides ever but seemed like you could email him for them(?)
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: super awesome lectures, he's a really funny guy and made the topics super interesting. you don't have to read the textbook but i recommend having it open when you're taking the weekly quizzes.
reviews.rating_tags: Amazing lectures --Clear grading criteria--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Super nice, down-to-earth, knowledgeable guy. His lectures are just him spitting global knowledge and going off on entertaining tangents. Quizzes are once a week and online. Discussions are an hour a week, but these are super easy as well. Go to class and you pass with an easy A!

Lectures are very interesting and he makes an effort to make this class as easy as possible, noting that most people are taking this course as a GenEd. There's no final or midterm. Every week there is an online quiz which is approx 50 questions each and are all open-note and due the next week. There is one project which is a manageable slideshow.

Dr. Applegate is a great professor. He is funny and tells stories during the lecture. It was very entertaining. This class was very interesting and I learned a lot about the world. I took it randomly because I needed to take a Gen Ed and I am so happy I did. Super easy and interesting. I recommend 100%
Easy gen-ed class just do the work online you get a A+.

toby is a good professor, but sometimes tends to get a bit sidetracked. the lecture slides are not posted after lectures so it's very important that you go to class. there is attendance credit, and a weekly quiz which can catch up to you if you aren't careful. it's very easy to get behind if you're not planning ahead.
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Gives good feedback--Lots of homework

reviews.comment: Very good class if you need to complete a gen ed. Very easy and manageable workload.
Toby is the man, class is a breeze
Easyyyy class andhe is very fun to listen to

Professor Applegate is a fantastic lecturer. Class was always interesting, he does have a tendency to sidetrack the material with personal tangents but they are usually entertaining. Most important thing for this class is to keep track of the assignments and tests as its all online and his late work policy is very harsh. All material is very easy.
If you make sure you go to lectures and read the textbook chapters, you'll do well in the class. There is NO final exam which is a plus, and most of your grade is just based on homework assignments.

Couldn't recommend Prof. Applegate more, honestly awesome experience for a class. All the work was the occasional discussion post and quiz (online), and 1 500 word essay, no final. If you are looking for a great class to fill in a gen ed, take this class.

Prof. Applegate knows a lot about geography and just talks about a ton of stuff every lecture. The assignments are very repetitive and are manageable if you put in effort. I learned a lot about geography even without putting in a lot of effort and I actually wish I had paid attention in class more. Cool guy.
reviews.rating_tags: Graded by few things--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Super easy class and amazing prof. Everything is online, tests, quizzes, projects. Go to class because attendance is apart of your grade!! And the discussions are kinda annoying but just go and get the points, not point hurting ur grade when its so simple to do. They are easy anyway and usually end early.

He goes on about a lot of random things in lectures so it's pretty engaging and the quizzes are pretty easy. Although I dread Packbacks, they were only assigned once a week and were easy to get out of the way. Overall great class and a great professor

Professor Applegate is one of the best. His lectures are both entertaining and informative. There were no exams, just quizzes, 2 projects and discussions. Attendance in lecture was also mandatory and graded. Good class and professor to take for electives, the workload is not very demanding. Overall, great professor who is very funny and laid back.

I loved Prof. Applegate, very wordy slides but he breaks them up with little stories and bits of information. His tidbits of information can be random, but they always made me laugh and keep me interested in the content. The discussion section was good but there was a group project and weekly quizzes (for both class and disc). Overall 10/10 class.

He was a nice guy. This class had some homework, like weekly assignments, but never anything overwhelming. The two exams are LITERALLY the exact same questions as all the practice quizzes he has available, so it's easy to get a good grade if you just go through those enough and complete your homeworks every week. I didn't really attend lectures.
Overall good professor, very funny sense of humor. Lectures aren't mandatory, but go to discussion or grade will plummet. Textbook isn't very useful, study online quizzes and you'll be fine

Although attendance isn't mandatory, he says it's helpful to go as some of the things in class might be on the exam. Reading is excessive and about 60 pages a week. Midterm and final are 75 questions and practice quizzes are basically the same as both. 2 reaction papers that are short and easy. TAs are easy graders. Lectures are kind of boring.
Grading isnt made up by much other then exams and disscusion. He is a very fair profesor and wants everyone to succed
