Easy class... he says that you need to purchase the 100 something dollar textbook but if you study the practice quizzes, you will do just fine on the exams. To each their own but I could have succeed without the textbook. Also go to lectures because he mentions things that are not in the read/practice quizzes occasionally.

Good professor, pretty simple content but made lectures genuinely enjoyable. I would give a 5 but he isn't good with tech and it was frequently hard to find resources on the middle page cause he wouldn't post important stuff

Although attendance isn't mandatory, I recommend going as most of the test questions are based on what he goes over in class. He is nice, but don't be loud/talking during class or he gets upset. Don't bother buying the textbook; I didn't open it once. As long as you go to discussion sections and attend most lectures, you'll be fine.

Easy gen ed. Only midterm and final; the only way to study is to do the online practice quizzes. Two short essays. The discussions count for 1/3 of your grade and you don't even have to do anything. He'll round up grades if you need. Only downside is having to buy Packback. Save yourself money & don't even buy the textbook, didn't look at it once

A midterm and final exam that come from the practice quizzes on Moodle, it takes a lot of memorization to study. We had to buy packsack and post weekly responses. A few short essay questions. Discussions were pointless but they took attendance. Overall easy A.

He is prof who knows this class is being taken because it is easy. He doesn't care about it just as much as any student. Its really easy however some issues arise like constantly giving students the wrong grade. Overall its easy A and the lectures are not bad at all. Great for fulfilling the req but don't be surprised if grading issues arise.

Tests definitely felt like a guessing game at times, but reviewing the online quizzes multiple times was the best way to prepare. The discussion section was chill and was a big part of the grade so just go for the attendance. The online textbook felt unnecessary, but as for an easy A to fill a gen ed I reccomend.

Toby is really nice and understanding, rounded my grade up a ton when he really didn't have to! He rocks. His lectures are interesting and he actually wants you to succeed. Show up and at least skim the readings, you will learn a lot of cool stuff from this class.

Somewhat easy class but took forever to grade exams (which were scantron) and to grade essays. Talked a lot about things that didn't have to do with the material. Exams were impossible to study for unless you know every specific detail about the world.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Professor Applegate is a great guy who is very knowledgeable. Classes consist of just lectures. There is a required textbook which has long chapters. Assignments consist of weekly packback (discussion questions/responses), 2 reaction papers and a midterm and final. I recommend studying the practice reading quizzes and the exams will be easy.
Don't have to do much for this class and easy grader
reviews.rating_tags: Clear grading criteria--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: He is a great professor and so chill. This class is pretty easy and great if you are trying to get your gen-ed over with. He is so nice and friendly even though the lectures are kind of boring. Class has a mid term, final, project, and one paper. (Paper and project are both easy). Only issue is its 3 lectures and a discussion section which is alot.
Easy gened, funny guy, great lectures

He's an excellent professor and deserves every good rating he gets. Two important things: you need to attend the lectures as there are test questions that reference them, and prepare to read if you want to succeed. While the textbook may seem large and imposing it will seriously help you pass the exams and reading quizzes if you're struggling.

Professor Applegate is a nice, knowledgeable professor. His classes are all lectures, with homework being reading quizzes weekly that are easy. Interesting to hear his perspective on places worldwide and he is great at explaining world regions. A Midterm, Final and paper make up most of the grade. Discussions were also easy and interesting

Lectures have very little to do with material on exams. The entire course is searching things on google. The exams are actually impossible to study for, the whole course felt like a game of trivia. The most frustrating part of the whole thing is how poorly the class is structured. Syllabus is inaccurate and assignment/quizzes are posted at random.

Dr. Applegate is a great professor. He is very knowledgeable about what he teaches and it is clear that he cares about the subject matter. There were no exams in person, and all quizzes were online, open notes, and questions came straight from the textbook. He isn't the best about responding to emails, but he usually addresses FAQs during lectures.

One of my favorite professors and one of the easiest classes I have ever taken for a gen ed. Long quizzes every week but they were fairly easy same with the one only short writing assignment and project of the semester. Highly recommend if you are trying to fulfill the DG or SB requirement.
Not a bad class just super long quizzes every week. He said we had to buy an Iclicker and use it but never actually did. Discussions are a waste of time but mandatory.

No tests but longgggg quizzes every week. As someone who never ever buys textbooks, having the textbook would have made taking the quizzes a bit easier. This class is literally fine tho NBD. Cannot be set P/F as an elective. 2 easy projects. He claimed Iclicker was necessary but we ended up never using them. Lectures are recorded and posted

Class was easy as long as you attended lectures, although not mandatory he assigns quizzes where the answers are from his lecture directly. The lectures were from the textbook but he edits them a little, if you go to lectures you won't need to read the textbook, I only used it for the weekly quizzes.

Easiest gen ed there is. Toby knows most of the students taking this class are doing it for the gen ed so his assignments are pretty lax and simple. Most you have to do are two 2 page papers. Additionally all the quizzes are pretty easy since they're given on moodle ;) and attendance isn't checked. Overall easy class and great guy.

I took the class P/F so I did not really care about my grade which lead me to do every single assignment in the last two days of the semester (Yes I'm serious), got an A somehow, you don't need to watch the lectures I just ran them all in the background muted at 480P - which took 10 GB of RAM. The quiz questions were taken from the textbook.

Though his lectures could drag a little, his tangents were certainly interesting. The course itself was also pretty solidly organized and wasn't too bad. The quizzes were a little annoying, but there are so many of them that doing badly on one or two of them didn't kill your grade. The one paper and one project you have to do are also very easy.
World Regional Geography with Applegate was the easiest class I took freshman year. He is a little pompous but if you don't like him, you really don't have to attend lecture in the first place.

Toby Applegate is an amazing lecturer, keeping you entertained and interested in whatever region of the world we are visiting this week. Highly-Recommended for any student who loves to sit and listen to a good lecture.

This class was defiantly an easy A. The grading was clear and all the tests were multiple choice. I found the lectures to be very interesting but they are not necessary to do well. Toby is a kind and understanding person and if you cannot make it to class or discussion sections, he will work something out. I recommend taking this class.

Lectures were very boring. Has a lot of things to grade by and exams/tests are not worth that much. Exams were also scaled a lot. Discussion meets every other week and attendance is mandatory, but you don't do much but listen to TAs. Just do well on the online quizzes (answers on quizlet) and the response papers and you will get a decent grade.

His lectures were so incredibly boring. Less than half of the class came to class because there wasn't much of a point. The tests are ridiculously specific, but he scales the grades so much that it doesn't matter.

Professor was outgoing and had nice stories to tell, overall an easy class. Most classes were based on slide shows that he later posts before the exams. If you get the book he basically follows that so attendance isn't mandatory. Go to the weekly discussions for points, study the online quizzes because the exams are based on those

Great gen ed class. He's easy to listen to but the notes can be a little tedious. Weekly quizzes can be found on quizlet and biweekly discussions which don't add much to the class. If you actually read the book and study, you can pass the tests. should go to lectures since he doesn't post notes until before a test. worth the take, an easy B at most

I loved Toby and can't wait to take more classes with him. His class was an easy A and he's super understanding if you're overwhelmed or are having a tough week. He's also very knowledgable about what he teaches so if you have any questions he can clear it up super fast.
If you pretty much memorize all the quiz questions then you'll get an A, also show up to discussions but they're not difficult
attendence non mandatory but he didnt put lectures online until right before the test so u kinda have to go. he was really nice and the class was very straightforward i recomend him. very smart
reviews.rating_tags: Respected--Skip class? You won't pass.--Test heavy

reviews.comment: He apparently changes his exam criteria every semester. This semester the exams were 90-95% based on the online quizzes. Study them and you have an easy A. Almost all the answers found on quizlet .But be wary that he may change it up. BEWARE: Fall 2019 will have discussions every week (it was bi-weekly previously). Don't attend the lectures.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Graded by few things--Hilarious

reviews.comment: Confusing lecture notes, interesting topics but the material on the slides can be hard to follow. Overall an interesting professor with good stories and insight, but it can be hard to take down all of his material while trying to grasp the concepts that he explains because they often differ.

This is the easiest class you'll ever take. I never looked at the book and got an A-. Lectures aren't required and don't go over info on the tests, but are interesting. Take this if you want a GPA boost, with some intersting lectures.
Very easy A. Midterm and final questions were pulled all from online quizzes. Lectures often go off topic and talks about personal life, which is often funny and interesting.

My friend took this class last year and recommended it to me because it wasn't too difficult and it is very interesting. Though its interesting, he changed the way he made his exams because my friend said that when he took the class, all you had to do was the study the quizzes. His exam did not reflect any questions from the quizzes whatsoever.

Dr. Applegate is a decent geography professor, but his classes are unbelievably easy. You could walk into the exam without studying or attending class at all, and score at least an 80. He makes funny jokes sometimes, but I think he is generally pretty hard to listen to. Alas, not many people attend lecture.
didn't go to one class and got an A. take the online Moodle quizzes in groups and study them for the final and midterm.

Extremely easy class. tests were based on the quizzes. Have to show up to discussion even though its boring. Toby rants during the lecture and barely puts up any of the slides. No one ever showed up to the lecture.

He is very interesting and has a had a lot of experience in this field, and you can tell he really cares about it. The class was a gen-ed, so he wasn't too difficult, and the lectures were very interesting.
Geo 220 with Applegate is great. Show up to class and do the reading, pass with an A.
Applegate is the man and he knows a ton. He takes attendance in both lecture and discussion, but he makes the lecture interesting. Great sense of humor, would recommend Toby Applegate.

Took this class pass fail. Got an A. Toby might be the funniest professor I have ever had. He has a slideshow for each lecture, but kinda just rants about whatever side tangent that hits him first for the entire class. He's hilarious. Didn't buy the book, flipped through a friend's copy night before, got the highest grade for one of the exams. EZ A

Prof Applegate is a really nice guy. I enjoyed his class and his sense of humor a lot. Wasn't hard, fair grader, not too much work. Whoever said the south is pathetic for giving this guy a PhD, he literally said 20 times he went to Rutgers lol and he's clearly an intelligent person
While attendance wasn't 100% required, I'd still recommend going as the information he gives is pretty useful and he's also a really funny and enjoyable professor.
Who's this clown? Toby Applegate is a frickin' fool! How somebody gave this guy an undergrad degree, let alone a master's and then PhD... the south is a pathetic place.

Boring. Absolute snooze-fest. Waste of your time to go to lecture. Gives quizzes each week, but typically forgets to open them to you until the day or two before due. Rants about random countries nobody cares about. Is fairly humorous. Take as a gen-ed if everything else fills. It'll work, but you won't learn anything & you'll end up hating Tobes
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--LOTS OF HOMEWORK--Hilarious

reviews.comment: If you want to get an easy A, take his class. If you want to learn, don't take this class. There are plenty of other geneds out there that are easy, but where you also learn. I learned absolutely nothing in this class. I am an NRC major so I had to take this class for a requirement, would suggest asking Lena to take another Geo class.

Really nice guy, quizzes are easy, test are wicked hard. Changed his criteria from past years. Studying for the exams is impossible now, he makes powerpoints for test with over 100 slides each and random questions not from quizzes or anything. Everything else isn't bad, but like I said the test are really, really tough.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--EXTRA CREDIT--LECTURE HEAVY

reviews.comment: Hilarious guy. Goes off on tangents multiple times during class but at least they are entertaining. Lectures can be missed without much problem as long as you keep up with the reading. Even then if you know some basic history/geography you could probably pass this class without ever going.

Very easy to talk to outside of class. Not at all condescending. Down to earth and shares personal anecdotes from when he was a trucker to a philosophy undergrad. Genuinely interested in the work he does.

Tests dont reflect lecture material, were surprisingly hard 'cause he pulled direct quotes from the massive textbook, better hope you read the whole chapter! but tests only make up a little part of your grade, there are also easy online quizzes, projects, quick current event assignments, and extra credit offered. would recommend. entertaining class

Was recommended as an easy A and also an elective that fulfills two different requirements for enrichment or whatever. Weekly slash biweekly quizzes, but the lectures are not hard to focus in on, but you'll need the textbook! Labs were easy, three group projects but you get ample time.

Easiest class ever.  Basically did nothing all semester.  The tests are the online quizzes so you have every answer before pretty much. 2 papers that are graded the hardest but still so easy.  Never went to class.
This class was great.

The most hilarious professor at UMass. Lectures were enjoyable and informing.  Only 2 essays to write during the semester, the tests were multiple choice-only and VERY easy, some of the questions on exams were directly copied from the homework.  @ the person rating below me, why does every professor always have to teach to a test?

Applegate is, like many social science teachers, arrogant. He loves himself and it shows. Nice and funny I guess. He's an intelligent man, no doubt. But I have a strong feeling that his intellect went over almost all of his students' heads. Lectures are quality but too many of his own thoughts, and more importantly, irrelevant to test material!!!

Dr. Applegate gives funny, engaging lectures. His class is relevant, and the criteria needed to get a good grade is clear. He is by far one of my favorite professors on campus, and I will be taking the follow-up to this class next semester. That being said, his slides are largely photo-based and you have to be a good auditory learner to succeed.

Applegate is a great professor! He knows what he is talking about and can convey information fluidly. Although lectures aren't important for your grade they are entertaining and amusing. If you can take his class, take his class.
Easy GenEd, I didn't really do much of anything and still got a solid grade. The two tests were extremely easy. Nice and funny guy

Toby is the best. All he wants is for you to pass, that's it. One of the funniest professors on campus. The class is really easy. He gives a few quizzes that he ridiculously scales, and the final was online open book.

easy gen-ed .. he wants you to pass. online final thats open book. we took in class quizzes that I failed but he scaled them all to 100's. No homework except for a small essay we wrote on a movie we watched in class.

Applegate is an awesome guy. He's wicked funny and he tells some pretty hilarious stories. This class is pretty interesting, and all quizzes are online and open resources. One midterm and one final, also online. Would definitely recommend.
Very nice guy, but very boring and tough lectures to sit through. He isn't super knowledgeable about what he's speaking about, and often struggles to answer specific questions that students have.

Gazi is a really nice person and teacher. He does read a lot right off the slides, and there's always a chapter or so of reading for each class. 2 midterms, one test, and one take-home, but they're both easy. Also, some case studies here and there. The class is cool, just a lot of information to know- easy possible 4 credits to earn from this class

Gazi is one of the nicest people I have met. Although his lectures were sometimes boring, he gave enough work to make us understand why we were learning it. His slides had good amount of information and his tests were based off his slides.
Such a boring class. Gazi is nice but lectures were unbearable because all he did to teach was read off the slides.
reviews.rating_tags: Graded by few things--Group projects--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: Gazi was a character. As a teacher, his lectures would be a little boring as he would just read the slides, but as a person, he was a super nice guy. Always open-minded and willing to give you extra time on a paper. For a four-credit class, this is a no-brainer considering the amount and difficulty of the work: take the class.

I hate to be THAT person but her accent is simply too thick to learn anything (she's from Bulgaria). Especially because she moves at a very fast pace through topics. Very sweet lady though. But if you're not good with accents, do not take her class.

She has a thick accent, so be sure to pay attention during lectures as well. MyOpenMath for weekly homeworks about 10-12 questions. 3 tests thru out the semester and a cumulative final. But she knows her statistics so ask for help and she will always do her best to make sure you understand. Go to class and take notes.
She is nice and very accessible outside the class. I learned a lot from her and looking forward to having her again.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Respected--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: She is nice and gives clear examples for an easy A. I didn't gain a lot of intuition from the class though. I would like to spend some time and go through some other learning resources on these topics so I feel like I fully understand. But just to re-iterate, the class is efficiently taught, lots of examples and an easy A.

Prof. Utic is by far the most helpful and easy to understand Professor . She gives real world examples and makes the material really easy to understand. She doesnt take attendance and Im not sure who does in this pandemic times. She comes always prepared and knows her stuff very well. I would recommend.

Worst math course I've ever taken at UMass. She wasted class time by taking attendance, showed repetitive examples and step-by-step instruction on how to plug in the numbers instead of providing intuition/motivation or proof. I got an A and still learned nothing from her. If you want an easy A and be treated like middle schooler, take her class.

To be honest, I was really disappointed with the instruction of many teachers during remote learning. For fall 2020, I took her class Statistics II, and man it was relieving to see a teacher so dedicated to teaching so that we UNDERSTAND. She gave a lot of homework tbh, but you KNEW you were getting great exam practice when you were doing them.
Such an easy gen ed, highly recommend, put in minimal effort and she is very lenient with grading, take this with Una for an easy A to fill in Gen ed requirements ALDG.

In my opinion she was very engaging in class which made getting participation points easier. There is a decent amount of reading that you need to do before some classes but apart from that the assignments are easy.

She was always open to discussion and never hesitated to speak her mind. The assignments were were not hard but required some effort. No matter what prof was available to talk about anything and that definetly helped through the entire semester. Would absolutely take her again!
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Gives good feedback--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Una is not only an amazing intructor but also an amazing individual. She gives such feedback on your work that your wiriting will improve without you knowing it. Definetly take her class if you want to improve your way thinking. Classes are discussion heavy and with clear grading criteria
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Clear grading criteria--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: Una is a great professor. She makes excellent lessons plans and I learned a lot throughout her class. If you get the chance to take her class, please do! I'm referring to her for English Writing 112H.
Una is the best teacher I've had! She's so inspirational and caring. I took her 112H writing class at UMass, and I wish I could take it again!

I took jr year writing with her and it was my fav class of the semester. She isn't a prof yet, she is a grad student, but trust me, her classes are amazing and if you have the chance you should take a class with her!
Una is a wonderful instructor and seems to have a genuine interest in her class. I would recommend this class to my friends and would even like to take a class with Una again.

I like her policy about being able to rewrite essays for a better grade but you have to make conferences to meet with her. I made 2 conferences on serparate occasions and she missed both. I got As on the essays and I particpated everyday but got a B in participation I got an 89.35 and she refused to round up the .65 for an A-, ridiculous! bad class
Una loves what she does and it shows every day in class. She really loves to teach and help you out. She is always looking to get better as a teacher too, great class for a gen ed.
UNA is the greatest instructor at UMass!

Una is a wonderful teacher. She isn't a professor yet but is one of the best teachers I have ever had the pleasure of being in class with. She is so nice, so knowledgable, and always willing to help you. Her lectures are interesting and fun and she is really impressive at stimulating discussion. She  justseems like the sweetest, nicest person ever

Una's not a prof yet, but if you get a chance-TAKE ANY CLASS WITH HER. I like to read/write, & I felt like she always stimulated amazing discussion (well prepared, makes things fun), but at the end, even ppl who had no prior interest in the class said it was 1 of their best. She's young, European, polite, funny, understanding, super chill, & smart.

At the end of the course, I was even more confused by the overall objective of her teachings. I admire how she encourages class discussion but it seems misleading and unrelated to the actual articles.

DO NOT TAKE THIS CLASS IF YOU AREN'T A FILM MAJOR. I took this class as part of my global education requirement, and hated every second of it. There is no leniency on those who aren't versed in film critiquing and no explanation of what kind of critiquing she wants you to do. she chastises people for not participating and doesn't help you.

took this class to fill my schedule;taken anthro before and am pursuing a film certificate so, why not?- please, do not take this class. Prof. Urla is so incorrigible and lazy. And what's worst of all, she expects the world of you,and nothing less:perfect attendance,papers every week, two and a half hour screening labs.holy moly.avoid at all costs.

Many assignments and a couple papers. The course, though really specific, gave me tools and knowledge to apply in a broader sense. Overall, Urla is a decent professor and is passionate about teaching.

I actually just created this rate my professor account to warn people to not take the class.  She assumes you have hours of free time to look at everything she wants to show you and is one of the least understanding people I have met. By far, the worst professor I have had at UMass. I actually loved anthro before this class DONT TAKE IT

not accessible; students teach, student learn from one another, tenured prof instructed first class, students required to instruct the rest.  no graded feedback until close to end of semester. so, uncertain of expectations and direction. write a paper a week additionally.  entered excited by potential; exited dissatisfied.

Assigns a ton of work and doesn't have the time or courtesy to even grade it or pass it back. Assignments are created for a cookie cutter answer. Doesn't want you to think, just wants you to spit back what she told you. Turns your brain to mush.
Jackie is EXTREMELY intelligent and very nice. Take her class only if you are interested--you need to be very invested in the subject matter. She takes class seriously. It's great and engaging.
a brilliant scholar.
Lots and Lots of writing, but if you don't want to write so much maybe you should get out of upper division anthropology classes. Also very interesting choice of reading and viewing materials

the WORST professor I have ever had.  Everyday is a fight to keep my eyes open.  Pretentious, but at the same time ignorant. She invents many words that sound impressive, but actually do not exist. Demands excessive writings - so far over 60 pages total.
smiles at your ignorance.  less discussion and more explanation of theory would be good.  she also pronounces Tagalog words with a French accent.
Excellent teacher!
unclear of expectations, unfair grading
I had ulrike in WPI. She is great

Horrible, she did not cover what she was supposed to and then when I went to ger230 I had to do extra work with my new teacher to catch up! Focuses too much on "culture" and not enough on vocab and grammar. You can't really learn german with her but you can certainly slack off! I'm so happy that she is gone!

Ulrike was a good teacher, and likes to get the class involved.  Too bad she was so busy with watching other classes (fair amount of subs).  She is good with giving students extra help if they need it.
No Comments
Very nice, very good teacher

Professor Ubaka is one of the best professors I've had. She genuinely cares is passionate, and always helps when you ask. The class is not hard if you put in effort. Most bad reviews come from students expecting an easy A with no work. If you attend class, try, you'll do great in the course. Seriously don't let the bad comments not take this class!

Professor Ubaka is fantastic! She creates an environment where you actually want to participate. The lectures aren't just one-sided; they are filled with great discussions and insights. If you show up and engage with the material, you'll get a lot out of this course. Highly recommend for anyone who likes a dynamic classroom!

Bad.I wish I was being dramatic. I have never seen a professor or any type of faculty speak to students the way she did. She singled students out in an effort to promote diversity but really just promoted the idea of needing a savior. It was so odd and ended in a hostile environment. She clearly favored people and their grades reflected that.

She is very passionate about her character, which can be overwhelming for most, but she is a good professor class really was not to hard the quizzes are open book and there's no final just a group film project that has to be 5 minutes but this class is not hard and I do think the other reviews are a little much.

Professor Ubaka is AMAZING. While there is a reasonable amount of readings for the bi-weekly quizzes, the overall course is not bad at all. No final for the course; there is a group project. However, she sets it up in a way to ensure that everyone pulls their weight. IDK why she has such a poor rating - she's an amazing person and prof.

Definitely avoid this class, it's just not worth it. Professor gives off a weirdly hostile energy that just makes every lecture uncomfortable and tense. Also she's been emailing some students to post positive reviews for her, which feels super sketchy, especially from someone teaching HR...
Most passive aggressive professor I've ever had in college consistently 15 minutes late to class she will call out students in class who aren't doing well I hate this lady

Avoid this professor. She showed my class unprofessionalism when she expected everyone to follow her criteria to a T. She often came 15+ min late to our class and emailed 1 student to tell everyone. She even contacted students to write her a positive rating on here. Do not take this class with her

Worst professor I've ever had. I don't even have words to describe how she treated my class last semester, it was disgusting and extremely unprofessional. Don't listen to the good reviews, she's been contacting students asking them to write them.

Professor Ubaka was a delight to learn from. She kept her lectures engaging and easy to follow, and the topics were easy to understand. She also helped me in coming out of my shell and feeling confident when participating in the classroom. I hope that others can take this course as it is one of my favorites I have taken at UMass.

The work is manageable and not difficult. I learned a lot from her, especially about HR, and the concepts were easy to understand. It's not an “easy A” where you just show up and get a good grade—you actually learn and apply the material. She sometimes posts exams (openbook online) a bit late, but overall, the class is not bad.

Work load was very inconsistent some weeks almost nothing other weeks more than 3 assignments. Her grading made no sense. She would copy and paste feedback. Class would get canceled randomly. Passive aggressive towards some students. Overall not a good time. A good thing is that there's a lot of group work and people bond over the frustration.

These rates are insane. Prof. Ubaka was amazing and I learned so much. The class material was not hard at all to me.. idk I would recommend her 100x over. Learned so much and was inspired by her. Give this class a chance, she's truly great.

This was the worst professor I've ever had in college she is a very tough grader for no reason I took her intro to HR class and everyone in our class hated her she is very passive aggressive towards students and she even would post students individual assignments on canvas and tell the class why the individual student did poorly this lady blows

My experience with Prof. Ubaka has been very negative. She made a poor first impression by stating that she “never makes mistakes,” which led to the uncomfortable implication that we should not contact her. Her attitude towards students seems to reflect a desire for control. She is more interested in asserting her authority than helping.

whoever rated Ubaka a 5, don't give false hope to other students. Genuinely the worst professor ever for all of the reasons everyone else said. Made a terrible impression during her first semester teaching at UMass, and made a disgrace out of Isenberg.

Assignment expectations were unclear, quizzes were posted late without due date adjustments, and late submissions weren't accepted. Feedback and gradings were harsh, and she was unwilling to consider student input, instead placing blame on the class. She frequently arrived up to 25 minutes late but required attendance.
This class was tougher than it needed to be. The professor's demeanor made the whole vibe pretty stressful, which made it hard to focus on the material. Would not recommend.

Tests were posted at strange times and late. There were obvious needs for feedback from the class, but she invited none. Had alot of trouble with her email format because of her extreme standards for email professionalism and double standards. She tends to need students to take complete responsibility before admitting any fault on her own.BAD class
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Group projects

reviews.comment: Professor Ubaka has higher standards than most professors to prepare students for a professional career. She cares about her students and will do anything to help them. She presents concepts in new and exciting ways both in lectures and in exercises. Don't take this class for an easy A, but you will learn WAY more than others. Awesome energy.

She cares, you know she cares but she a bit too much at times. She has insane mood swings in class and WILL lash out at you for no reason, other than "she's hungry." This was supposed to be one of the easier classes this semester but she made it hard by being a tough grader. She's the complete opposite of what she preaches she is.

MANAGMNT-314 -- Take 314 with a different professor if you can. Professor Ubaka is demeaning in her feedback, extremely unclear with her expectations, shows up to class 20 minutes late, doesn't most quizzes on time, sometimes even days late without extending the due date, and clearly cares more about her personal life than her student's success.
Horrible teacher. Doesn't understand the material enough to help others. Thick accent also.

He was not a very helpful professor.  When i went to his office to ask for help he made it seem like my questions were dumb and it was a waste of his time trying to help me.  He doesnt seem to care if his students pass or not
Fine teacher, doesn't deserve rating this low. Hard to understand at first, you should ask questions and participate in class.

Oh come on, this guy is a great teacher.  For the first few days it was hard understanding his accent, but once you get used to it he's very clear.  The quizzes are simple if you study, and the homework is easy.  Throughout the class he inserts random comments that keep his lecture interesting.  And he really wants to help you learn. Recommended.
He is probably the worst professor at Umass. He doesn't know to teach and is very awkward. Avoid class with this guy.

Worst teacher ever.  Can't undertsand his writing and does not spel English well at all.  He just can't teach and is always making mistakes. The material wasn't that hard in my class, but he made it impossible.  Also gives extremely difficult quizes.

Nice guy, just not a good professor. Teaches by working out a lot of examples, but doesn't really explain anything. Gives the definitions for proofs the way he talks, i.e., he uses the word "maybe". More people went to discussion every week than class.

This guy speaks "spanglish" throughout class.He should definitely not be a calculus teacher, he is extremely hard to understand, and hardly explains anything. I would avoid taking a class with this guy.
Can not understand a word being said throughout the entire class.  Struggled through the class
On the whole, a nice teacher with a warped sense of humor. Gives in-class demonstration and kept my attention, which is quite a feat at 8AM.

She wasn't very helpful for teaching the material. All she did was read directly off her slides. For this class you want to READ THE TEXT, DO THE EXTRA CREDIT, STUDY FOR THE QUIZZES because it's 84% of your grade. If you study, you will do fine.

She isn't awful but I DID detect an attitude from her. I won't go as far as to say she was pretentious but there were times where she would act inappropriately towards a response. I recall answering a question in class and her making a face as if I was wrong and I was not. That stood out to me. The TA's (other than Fred) were utterly incompetent.

She's pretty confusing so read the book before the lecture to actually understand what she's talking about. Go to class because there are in-class assignments. She is vague and sometimes it seems like she is either nervous or doesn't know what she's talking about. Overall an easy course as long as you read the book and go to class.

STAY AWAY.. class average on the first two tests was a 53 and a 57...... you sit through the whole class worrying about your grade until in the end she finally decides to scale. For tests you are expected to know every single minute detail from her numerous slides and from over 100 pages of text.  she often cant answer questions.

Her class is challenging and you won't get anywhere without reading the text and coming to class everyday. She strives to help students any way she can but in the end its your effort that gets the grade. Take this class if you are willing to put the time in to learn the material otherwise don't complain!

Worst Dean's Book class ever. Work is not that hard but its made impossible by her inability to give clear directions. Refuses to clarify anything, condescending, and pretentious.  Avoid her like the plague.

Pretentious is an excellent word to describe her.  Condescending would be another.  Expects you to know all the material when she comes to class and sometimes can't answer your question fully.She treats men and women differently.  Does now about the subject but doesn't clearly explain things to the point of confusion. I do NOT recommend her at ALL.

Unja is rather pretentious. She doesn't actually know the answer to any questions or what the questions are about, reads directly off of her slides, and expects a ridiculous level of detail from the 200 pages assigned for each exam. I love neuro and I just can't stand the way she teaches.
Unja's a really dedicated professor.

Very knowledge, but didn't do a good job of relaying the info to us. Expectations were too high and her pace was usually too fast to catch much. The work was do-able, but overwhelming. We had debates (w/much research), quizzes (more like exams!), a topic paper, and reading material. Take this class if you're really interested and have the time!

Good explanations+lec slides. I had this class at 8am, and since lecs aren't recorded, I really struggled when I missed class. This is a tough class. Much worse when you miss lec. Midterm 2 (mostly ch.11: series) cooked me, but you can make a comeback in the final since its easier/less series. Office hours+heavy final exam studying saved me

Professor Srivastava knows the material, is very kind, and cares about his students. He explains everything clearly, and I'm confident that I would've aced his class had I not slacked off and skipped out on a couple lectures. Calculus II isn't a joke, so make sure to stay on top of everything and complete your homework authentically.

He's actually amazing. He genuinely spends time explaining.  Very interactive in class, gives a lot of practice problems in class that are usually harder than the exams.  So, the exams seem super easy. 
Made Calc 2 one of the easiest classes I took.
Explains super well. Very kind.

He explains the material in a clear and easy-to-understand way. Homework problems tend to be harder than actual exams and are more similar to in-class problems. Definitely do practice exams because they prepare you well. Overall, it was a chill class.
reviews.rating_tags: Clear grading criteria--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: This guy is the absolute goat of Calc 2. Although lectures can happen at a fast pace, he will stop at any time to answer a question or explain concepts to you. Homework problems will be harder than the exams; exams are always identical to the previous semester's exam questions. The grading is generous on exams and quizzes.
He's very organized for class, and he answers questions pretty fairly. Sometimes if there's a question, he'll put it off to the end of class though, so make sure you remember what you want to ask.
I liked him. It was what a class should be.
He was always quick to answer questions and clarify confusion, made the content very digestible despite the sheer amount of topics.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Lecture heavy--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Calc 2 in general isn't easy, but he made the content easy to understand. He's willing to stop to answer questions and is very understanding and considerate. Also his office hours are great if you have any questions, he is always eager to help.
Very good at stopping to ask questions, and calc 2 is a hard class but he was able to break it down well.
reviews.rating_tags: Caring--Graded by few things--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: There is something different about this prof. He wants you to understand the real world as we experience it. I have never seen this in an econ course before this. I was blown away by his knowledge and willingness to engage. My class had many curious students who always wanted to ask questions. He was attentive always. Would recommend.
The lectures were very clear. Learnt a lot about the ideas of macroeconomics.
do not take this class if u have a life. essay every week with final exam at the end
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--So many papers--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: Vamsi's class is probably my favorite class I've taken at UMass, I learned so much from him and he's able to break down super dense reading which was really helpful. He's very passionate and knowledgeable, take a class with him, you will learn so much!!!

this prof is one of the smartest people i've ever met. you can tell he understands the material very deeply, and he is great at conveying complex ideas in a more digestible way. the reading is DENSE (capital vol 1) and there are 1000 word papers due weekly, so this class is definitely a challenge, but it is worth it imo. great dude great class
First time I could relate economics to the real world - I felt excited about going to every class. Only two tests and three home works - the only drawback!!!
reviews.rating_tags: Clear grading criteria--Inspirational--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Awesome professor and great class.

One of the best professors I've had. He is exceptionally knowledgable about the content he teaches and the course itself bring light to a different point of view of economics. You will have weekly response papers (40% of your final grade), a final term paper (40% of your final grade), and participation (20%). Overall, an amazing course to take!

I really enjoyed the course. There is a lot of reading and sometimes it was tough to write a response every week but by the end of the course, Vamsi showed us how we could see the world around us in a new light. Great Teaching!!!!
My best course in college - learnt a new language to think about the world. RARE treat!!!!!

Professor Vamsi makes his class very engaging. Attending classes will be your best help, he does not lecture with slides and all of the notes he makes are written on the board. Coming to class will ensure you at least get a B, otherwise writing the final paper is going to be very difficult given the course material is hard to understand at times
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Amazing lectures --Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: Econ 204 was easily my favorite class last semester. Vamsi is a great teacher and makes the class very interesting. Final exam was tough but Vamsi is a generous grader.

Good guy, but his teaching format wasn't good. Only 2 exams (midterm and final) + 3 problem sets, overall grade curved w no clear grading criteria. Can be hard to reach out of class bc he commutes from NYC. No TA. Passionate about research + makes class interesting, but no slides or notes so don't miss class or you'll fall behind.
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Lecture heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: First of all great guy. Generally will be happy to explain things if you ask for explanations on certain problems. Only thing is there are only 3 hw assignments and 2 exams, meaning one bad exam one you might have to drop. All in all professor is great, class structure could be better.
This class blew my mind and changed my life. It gave me a new perspective to think about the world. The best class I have ever taken in my life so far!
Very interesting class,, each will learn as much as they want to! have seen very few classes like these.. not much work involved - 10 weekly discussion papers and one long term paper.

It's not an overly interesting class and is somewhat dry, but he's always open to meet outside class and genuinely seems to care about his students. Very chill and funny, not too hard to get a decent grade (B) as long as you do the weekly easy homework responses, and actually put in some effort towards the end of term presentation and term paper.

It is a relief to see a class without too many powerpoint slides. This class uses an active learning technique of teaching and writing using a document camera rather than hitting students with fully pre-prepared slides. Learnt a lot!!! Vamsi explains difficult concepts clearly. Great semester of learning!!!

Just finished my final exam. Learnt lots about different ideas in macroeconomics. Very important course, and fair but slightly hard exams. Overall, super-useful course to understand the real world macro policies and underlying ideas!!!
reviews.rating_tags: Respected--Skip class? You won't pass.--Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: I compared France and US for my term paper for this class. Learnt so much from the theories that we learnt and from the extra readings for my paper. Professor was very helpful suggesting the literature, and his lectures were stimulating. Would highly recommend!!!

I learnt about many countries.. ECONOMIC SYSTEMS, Lots of READINGS BUT LOTS of Learning.. the instructor is too good.. very knowledgeable!! Work burden is not heavy.. one term paper, and weekly discussion papers!!

Econ 204 was my favorite course this semester.. We were sent the syllabus on Moodle (UMass) and homework assignments were specified clearly, and TAs were helpful in solving the materials. The instructor was very friendly, and took students' opinion into account in determining exam dates and assignment deadlines.
reviews.rating_tags: Respected--Participation matters--Skip class? You won't pass.

reviews.comment: Very nice class.. Economic Development may not happen in this world for the poorest countries.. but we should all learn and try to do something about it.
reviews.rating_tags: Respected--Skip class? You won't pass.--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: Great class. Vamsi's lectures created a lot of interest in the subject. The exams and assignments were fair. Would recommend
Such a good class. Had no idea about developing economies.. incredibly new and exciting.

This class had many country case studies that it was like a learning tour of the world and its different economic systems. Vamsi made this class very exciting by giving stimulating lectures. Student presentations also helped class participation. Although Vamsi does not take attendance, I did not miss a single class!!!
Great lectures, and lots of learning
It was a great class! Vamsi is one of the best economics teachers I have ever had!

Vamsi makes the subject pretty interesting. This was a pretty tough course at times because he never did example problems in lecture and they were only occasionally done in discussion. Tests are calculation problems and sometimes there were problems that I had never seen before. Tests are also very long, leaving you no time to check your work.
reviews.rating_tags: Respected--BEWARE OF POP QUIZZES--GRADED BY FEW THINGS

reviews.comment: Learnt so much!
Excellent class. Final exam was lengthy and a bit difficult but very reasonable, based on what was taught in class. Highly recommend.
reviews.rating_tags: Respected--Skip class? You won't pass.--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: I am reviewing this class before my final exam. It is a class that is a requirement but I have found meaning in it! The professor is a really smart and caring person, and looks out for students. It is tough material, but he presents it with super clarity, and he is attentive to the differences in ideas and perspectives. Enjoyable despite math heavy

I am truly enjoying this class.. I did not know that macroeconomics can be so fascinating! I am also really glad that there are no powerpoint presentations (they put me to sleep)! We are learning about different ideas (Keynes, Milton Friedman) and ways to think about the macro economy. I hope the class continues to excite..
Just finished my final exam. Very fair exam, based on assignment questions and classroom instruction. Learnt a lot overall.. good and clear lectures.

Econ 204 is a mandatory class for my major.. Vamsi made it as interesting as he could. The course is light, and the lectures and the discussion sections are more than tolerable. I would recommend this class.
reviews.rating_tags: Respected--Skip class? You won't pass.--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: Vamsi is very smart and knows econ very well, but his lack of use of Moodle is a detriment. He does not post any lecture notes or even your grades, which is extremely frustrating. There's very few assignments, so it can be kind of tough to actually learn the material. Lectures are sometimes confusing.

This class requires a TON of writing (a 2 page paper every week and a 20-30 page term paper) making it relatively time consuming but he's a pretty relaxed grader so if you do the work you can get an A.  Also, the topics are relatively interesting and you can easily skip class because he doesn't take attendance and there are no tests.

The Macro (204) class is very lucid. Vamsi makes his best efforts to teach in an interesting way.. he is very smart.. and the class is relatively easy. Two exams and three assignments. Would highly recommend!

In the class you will have two exams and three assignments. Vamsi uses no technology in his class and his notes are confusing. The exams are hard because we never practice the type of problems we would see on exams.  My TA was incredibly unfriendly and did not  clear up any confusion with the material.

Very smart, very interesting story.  Class was two 6-page papers and 10% participation.  Not hard, you just have to be willing to put effort into the papers.  Also, if you participate in class and he knows who you are, it will definitely have a positive impact on your grade.  You don't necessarily need to go to class, but it makes doing well easy.
What is amazing is that he can teach without any notes for a whole lecture! He made Marx interesting by bringing many contemporary examples.. Definitely worth taking.

Vamsi is a great guy. Feels like he's too smart to be teaching. I learned so much from his class and he was a forgiving grader. A 3145 b+? That just shows that he has high expectations but won't bomb you. One of the few classes I actually looked forward going to.

Excellent Class! He did not allow calculators for mid-term (not sure why?) but then he did so for the final exam. He said in class that students seem to need the calculators and he will always allow from now on.. very clear lectures, and if you attend  lectures, and pay attention, you will do very well. Very nice man.

The way he had grading work for the 371 class was 10% participationattendance and the other 90% was split between 2 papers (6-8 pages each) which came around mid semester and finals time. There were no exams! Doesn't use or post any powerpoints, its all chalkboard teaching. Lecture is definitely worth going to, you will learn a lot. Very Nice Guy!

Vamsi is a very helpful professor believe it or not, compared to what other people have said below. The midterm we took was very difficult because he did not allow calculators on the exam, but when he graded the exams he didn't count for mathematical errors. He explains content very clearly and makes it easy to understand. Very fair and kind
Unnecessarily difficult. Almost went through the entire book, 3 homeworks that are HARD, 1 extra credit assignment that we begged for and a midterm+final that were next to impossible.

Best economics teacher I've had so far.  He's organized and he breaks down the otherwise hard material so that it's easier to understand.  If you go to all the lectures and take notes than it's an easy class.  He's pretty strict about using technology though and he'll call you out if you're using a laptop or are on your phone.

On our midterm I'm pretty sure most of the class did poorly. He didn't allow calculators even though complex math had to be done, he didn't give us any study guide, most of what we learned in classdid for HW wasn't on the test. We are all worried about our grades and he doesn't seem to want to do much about it. Worst professor I've ever had.
good class
reviews.rating_tags: Clear grading criteria--Lecture heavy--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: usually a long lecture before lab starts. a couple quizzes that are pretty specfic but you just read the slides and lab manual and you'll be fine. The worksheets were not bad clear questions easy to answer. Overall I really enjoyed the content of the lab and it was actually fun.

Professor Carvalho is a strict grader, but if you literally sit down with her for 10 minutes to talk about a project or exam she will give tell you what to do and explain what you need to know 
All assignments she gives are well described and rubrics are detailed to all you need to complete each assignment 
Especially lab presentations and notes

I really enjoyed this lab, the worksheets were done during her lectures, which weren't too frequent. The lab content was super interesting and a great introduction into microbio labs. Presentations and lab notes were grader w a super clear rubric, easy to get 100% and her and prof siegrist who taught w her were very happy to help explain anything
The class was not too bad I didn't go to most lectures and the exams were based off of the slides and little quizzes after class a lot of memorizing but not too bad and she gives lots of extra credit

Lots of assignments/tests but having ur lowest dropped is worth. The exams can focus on random details too much but overall its not bad. Prof is interesting and clearly passionate about material. Frequent TA reviews are helpful too to lock in what random stuff is important to memorize. Main complaint is how often you need to memorize random things.

Professor is passionate and knows how to teach the content well. The lecture slides are well made and they are everything you need for the exams. Exams are well written and really do test the content covered well. 5 exams and 1 gets dropped. take home quizzes and weekly packbacks. Loved the content and style of teaching.
reviews.rating_tags: Amazing lectures --Lecture heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: I really liked this class and her as a professor, Ive heard from other people that more of her bad reviews are from her lab classes but her lectures were good. lots of homework with a short "quiz" after every class and a discussion post due every week and lots of exams but they are pretty easy and she drops the lowest score

Spring 2025 was run by grad TA not Verena. The labs were fun! Not very intense. No lab reports- only pre and post lab worksheets (put in effort bc grading is pretty strict) A couple quizzes which arent too bad if you review the material. Material goes hand in hand with micro310 lecture which is helpful.
reviews.rating_tags: Test heavy--Graded by few things--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Slides are dense but the class itself is super organized. Review in class after each chapter by the grad TA which is VERY helpful. PLENTY of extra credit available. Exams are pretty light as long as you put in some effort into studying and memorize the facts the TA points out. 4 in class exams and a final optional.

The professor is the worst I've had at UMass. I've never left a comment about a professor before. The exam is too detailed, with questions on topics barely covered in class, like which microbiome is used to make bread. The TA said a general understanding would be enough, but it's not. The exam goes beyond the outline and causes constant stress.
The lectures were everything off the slides. But the slides were so dense. The exams are based on minor detail.

The worksheets are not clear on directions. The questions do not say exactly what you need to write. You are graded on minor details that aren't in the question. They won't give points back because they are always right.

She lectures for half of lab time which is  unnecessary since there's pre lab. There is no correct grading scale because the TAs give out different grades. She doesn't help during lab instead she talks down to students.

When I asked why I got points taken off when the TA said I should get them back she didn't have an answer. Instead she said based off my one question that I clearly had no idea what I was doing. The girls at my table had the same answer as me and got full credit. She refused to give back points after because I left out one specific minor detail.

This class was so easy. There are daily quizzes and unit review quizzes that are all online. Exams seemed to be the same as questions on the review slides from the TA. Drops lowest quiz, drops 1 review quiz and 6 day quizzes. There's also weekly discussions, which could be time-consuming, but not too hard. extra credit opportunities!

Microbio 310 was a super well organized course and lots of points are packed into the day quizzes + review quizzes + packback. All these are easy to do if you're organized and chatgpt definitely helps a lot in this case. Tests are probably on the harder side but as long as you pay attention and take notes during lecture you'' be fine.
reviews.rating_tags: EXTRA CREDIT--Clear grading criteria--Lots of homework

reviews.comment: Dr. Carvalho was a great teacher and very knowledgeable about the material. The class has a lot of material and the exams are worth 50% of your grade, but they are very similar to the quizzes and the lecture slides. There are weekly Packback assignments and daily attendance quizzes. There is lots of extra credit and overall a very manageable class.

Very short pre-labs and the lab worksheets are not hard - take your time to fill them out. If you answered fully you can get an A on every lab worksheet (make sure it's detailed).
The instructions are clear and often we finished the lab early.
Quizzes are based on both the lecture and the lab handbook, you NEED to review.
Professor is very kind.

Weekly prelabs are easy, but weekly postlab sheets are graded kinda tough for no reason. Unfair grading in different lab sections. Prof was snarky a few times for no reason. Quizzes are lowkey hard, but I also didn't study. Don't skip a lab or you are doomed.

Professor Carvalho is a sweet professor. The class was interesting. Most of the grading is based on assessments and Packback. Only downside was exams were worth 50% of overall grade (which isn't ideal for me). Some exam questions were confusing, but not too bad. Really focus on the lecture slides. There were many extra credit opportunities.

IGNORE ratings. Prof is so nice, wants to engage/encourage learning. Lots of "busy work," but helps you to learn, 3 hrs max a week. Attend lecture (little disorganized/dense) or rewatch recordings. Everything you need to know for exams is in her slides. No surprises, some trivial Qs e.g %s. 4/5 exams count, dropped final. Lots of easy extra credit.

There was 3 weekly packback posts to do, quizzes and 5 exams (final optional). Lectures were dense! But I didn't go at all and just studied the slides, and watched the lecture if I needed to. She is nice but not the greatest teacher for such a dense subject. The class was very interesting however and I liked it! Q's are not online she writes them!
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Lots of homework--Test heavy

reviews.comment: This lab while not super easy was the best lab I've taken at Umass. Each worksheet/pre-lab takes about an hour to finish each week and is not terribly hard. Professor Carvalho is very knowledgeable and helpful when answering questions.  The TAs were great and super helpful and understanding. Quizzes are easy if you study for just an hour.

I hate labs but LOVED this one. It taught us actual, useful knowledge and skills, and was /very/ achievable. Weekly easy prelabs/worksheets that'll take you an hour max and so easy to get an A. Lots of extra credit. Everyone at my lab bench and I agreed that this lab is the best and most useful one we've taken at umass. Take it if you can!

I took this as an on-line course and found Dr. Carvalho to be clear, well organized, respectful and one of the nicest profs. Her lectures were clear and it was nice to be able to re-watch them in preparation for quizzes and exams.There are a lot of quizzes, but they keep you on target and prepare you well for taking the exams. Lots of   EC.

I don't get her low rating. You can earn up to ~8% extra credit on your final grade. For the online class, everything is open note. She gives opportunities to go over what you did wrong on exams for extra credit. I met with her and she is so caring and kind, and very intelligent. The material is fascinating. One of the best classes imo

The lectures were comprehensive about what we'd be learning for and using in the lab and she always knew the answers to questions I asked. She was not very available outside of class, but if you get to the lab around 30 minutes before it starts and have questions, you can ask her or the TAs! Sometimes the lab ends an hour early, but it depends.

Carvalho is not easily accessible outside of class. Everytime I asked for help, she never helped me to understand but told me to just "look at the textbook". She does not assist in class and is always expecting the students to just know the answers. TAs not helpful either as they didn't even know what was going on, be sure to take with a friend.
Lectures are excessively too long. Too many quizzes. AVOID!

She is super nice and obviously cares about the topic, but this is just an example of a really smart person not being a great teacher. She reads off of her slides which are posted online anyway. Got better scores when I started skipping class and just going over the material on my own. Her exams are straight memorization but very similar to quizes.

She reads directly off the slides and crams an entire chapter into one lecture. She often goes over the 50 minutes or speeds through the last couple of slides to finish in time. Theres so much info it's hard to know what info is important for the exam. Weekly Packback discussion posts of 1 question and 2 responses are busywork.
Was dreading this lab, but it was super fun and super easy. Never took 310 with Carvalho, but am pre-PA and highly recommend this lab!

I honestly really enjoyed Verena's class and I don't understand why she has gotten such harsh reviews. She was one of my fave prof this semester and it was very easy to do well in her class. Lectures are recorded, weekly discussion posts, 4 exams (that are based on the quizzes), short Moodle quizzes, and lots of EC! 100% taking this class w/ her!!
reviews.rating_tags: Accessible outside class--Clear grading criteria--EXTRA CREDIT

reviews.comment: Like others said, she reads off of the slides and crams an entire chapter into every class, which ends up being an unreasonable amount of info to remember for each exam. That said, there's lots of ways to get points outside of exams and some extra credit chances. Still would recommend taking it with someone else if you can.

Professor Carvalho has been one of my favorite professors at Umass. I don't think her rating is fair. The exams aren't terribly difficult but it's incredibly easy to get an A in the class with the bare minimum effort. The class material is interesting so I found it easy to pay attention. All the other ratings giving her 1 star seem a little harsh.

Wish I dropped this class when I had the chance. If you need this as a pre-req take it with someone else or at another school. She just reads off the slides, exams are nothing like review sessions or class material and class averages are extremely low (she still won't curve, basically blames it on students and saying the unit is hard). Steer clear.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Test heavy--Tough grader

reviews.comment: She's a really nice person and does her best to make sure students are successful. I hear she's a new teacher, and even if she's not amazing, she's open to feedback. In terms of material, study as you go. Don't cram. It's hard to predict what will be on exams. It can range from really easy or really specific questions, but she really does care.

If you want the A she makes you work for it. Only thing that makes it hard is the quizzes, the last half were tough. Other than that the lab course is fun but the professor gets a bad wrap because people dislike her as a person. However I think she's good as long as you don't skip. Extra credit for pure pet culture and unknown lab at the end!

One of the more easier lab courses at umass. Grade is mostly based on worksheets. Quizzes at times were tricky but she does add extra credit questions. She is very nice but stern when your absent. Lab was wicked fun and worksheets are easy to do. No lab reports! Extra credit at the end of the semester. Don't skip lab! TAs are sweet; no lab reports!

I only had her for the lab section but it went quite smoothly. Quick short lectures at the start and then an overall fun lab experience. Quizzes weren't too difficult and the lab reports were worksheets that weren't so bad either. Overall I loved the lab section.

She reads directly off the slides, flies through material and there's SO MUCH INFO. Does not explain points of confusion. She went over class time almost every lecture. Basically take this class with her and you'll be teaching yourself Microbiology. I'd have to rewatch lectures and slow down the video because she talks SO FAST.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Test heavy--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: Do not take this class with this professor. Although Prof Carvalho seems really nice, her class is awful. She throws so much information at you and expects you to memorize the smallest details for her exams. She reads directly off the slides. I would not go to class if it wasn't mandatory (iClickers). The worst class I've taken at Umass.

She is nice and says she is limiting the amount she is throwing at us but literally nothing has changed since then. She speeds through an average of 30 lecture slides in 50 minutes and has up to 50 at times, it's ridiculous. I put so much work into this class and I feel like my grade does not reflect that. Avoid this teacher if you can!
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Test heavy--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: She's just an awful teacher. She lectures super quickly and the lectures are so dense. She hasn't been understanding at all since our review of her. Very few things have changed. Her tests are hard. She seems like a nice person just awful at teaching. I hope she reads this and changes.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Test heavy--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: Terrible professor. Seemed like she didn't know what she was talking about half of the time. Says "um" a lot, very distracting. Goes through her lecture extremely fast, if you're a slow writer try to type notes to keep up. Goes through a whole chapter per class. TA wasn't too helpful either. If you're taking for prereq, take it @ community college
She reads DIRECTLY OFF HER SLIDES AND DOES NOT TEACH ANYTHING.

I hate to say this because she is so sweet, but this is probably the worst class I've ever taken in my entire academic career. Verena legitimately does not TEACH. She regurgitates information already written on her slides. Do not take this class.

Her powerpoints have SO MUCH INFO & she does not slow down to clarify whatsoever. She talks so fast you cannot keep up with her & you eventually end up zoning out in lecture. She's clearly very intelligent, but teaching is not her strong suit. Even after studying an absurd amount for the exam, I was completely blindsided by my grade!!!!!!!

Verena seems to be a very nice woman, but her teaching abilities are subpar. She reads directly from her slides, goes SO FAST, and does not explain ANYTHING. I felt well prepared for the 1st exam and ended up doing so poorly that I thought there was a mistake in the grading. There wasn't. I am at a loss for words.

MARKETNG 410 Consumer Behavior is one of the greatest classes ever took it in the FALL 2025. Dr. Martin Ruiz is prepared, very knowledgeable, and professional teaching the course. I highly recommended this course to anyone who is interested in how consumer act to buy products or services.

Very negative and angry professor. She has a clear grudge against the business students that she teaches and talks about all the opportunities we have that she doesnt. She also makes us do activites relating to the "looks" of the average isenberg student including racial and socioeconomic which is uncomfortable and wrong.

Don't listen to the 301 reviews. Professor Martin Ruiz is such an intelligent, caring, and dedicated professor. Yes, she is strict about grades and expects you to be responsible and timely, but she does it for her students own benefit. She will always listen to you and give great feedback. She loves what she does.
I really enjoyed this professor. Yes, she was tough at times but I learned so much from her teaching and feedback. Would recommend taking Marketing 410 with her!
Would not recommend to anyone.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Lots of homework--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Great professor, her 410 class is good as well
super invested in her students and livens up the classroom with all her lectures and inspires student interaction and interest with the subjects LOVE HER

Laughably easy course, mostly a small amount of busywork each week, open book exams, and easy in-class work. Clearly passionate about what she's teaching, and tries to get students engaged, but the material and assessment is kind of a joke. Everything felt kind of made-up, even though it came straight from the textbook.

Cares about what she teaches, but lectures are fast. Often went only to get the attendance / in class assignment grades, which are barebones text-box filling sessions that you never really got proper feedback on. (The questions were conceptual). Read & notate from the textbook and you'll do fine, but GO TO CLASS or the attendance grade will tank u.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Lots of homework

reviews.comment: She cancels class before/on exam day, and there's 4 mini open-note exams. There are NOT that many classes, so I don't get the whining here about attendance. She moves through material fast bc there's SO MUCH material. Not really her fault. Sucks to have to self-study sometimes, but she's nice enough A's are easy with basic effort bc the xtra credit

Don't listen to all the salty students who left bad reviews. It's a college class- duh, you have to put in some work! Prof. Martin-Ruiz has a great personality in her lectures. The material is dense and can get tedious at times, but it's an easy class! All exams are open-note and there's lots of extra credit. She is also very accessible.

These awful reviews are by people who don't go to class. Yes lecture is mandatory. Just show up she cancels class the day before and after exams too. Easiest class ever just show up take notes and the homeworks are a guaranteed 100. Exams are online and easy. She offers over 15% extra credit to your final grade so if you do bad its your own fault.
Worst professor I've ever had at Umass.

How did i get a 48/50 on all four exams and a 100 on almost every homework besides one and manage to get an 81% in the class? Because she forces you to come to lecture and makes attendance EXTREMELY mandatory by doing in class writing assignments. Actually insane.

Run. Has a hard time inspiring the class to listen and learn. She is very firm on her rules which are scattered throughout a long and complex syllabus. It is difficult to understand what you have to make up for class when you have excused absences. Lectures are mandatory and rather dull.

This class is absolutely awful. A mandatory attendance lecture is absolutely ridiculous. Going to the class is completely useless as the in-class activities are the dumbest things to ever exist. They are completely unhelpful and the only useful thing about this class is the online smartbooks. This professor is one of the worst I've ever taken.

The most important quality a professor can have is one who wants their students to succeed. Professor Veronica Martin-Ruiz lacks this quality. She does not offer accommodations due to illness, even COVID. She is the world's worst boss, and we are her employees. For someone representing the Isenberg, she lacks almost every management skill.

Class is a cake walk but this professor tries to scare everyone into thinking it's the most important class they will ever take. Long syllabus with arbitrary rules. Beware if you try to go around her and use campus resources for problem solving, you will be successful, but she will try and intimidate you out of pursuing the matters further.

Awful professor, worst class I have ever taken, although I am yet to take MGMT301(pray for me). Why Isenberg mandates MKT+MGMT301 is beyond me, absolute scam. However, this class is incredibly easy, if you have a bad group, just do all the work, she is a tough grader w zero feedback. Final was online + ez; might make her the better choice for the A

She is blunt. Aside from her personally as it does not matter how your teacher is if you get a good grade, the class is not super difficult. HWs are always a 100% and the attendance code is easily shared if you have friends in class. Final exam easy A. Only difficult part is the big group project but a good group can secure an easy A.

A true feeling of embarrassment throughout this class. I hope Professor Ruiz is just new and doesnt have a good grasp of how classes work at UMass. Her attempt to properly teach this class and administrate proper grading processes is simply horrendous. I would not advise taking this class as my expectations as a student felt consistently unclear.
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Skip class? You won't pass.--Tough grader

reviews.comment: Absolutely laughable professor, by far and large the worst ive ever had at this school. Professor Martin-Ruiz is demeaning, rude and just overall the most confusing professor ive ever met. Every question is met with ambiguity so dont expect anything to be clarified. Assigned arbitrary participation grades and teaches nothing during lectures.
Every quiz and test is on Quizlet. Boring dry lectures that are mandatory. The project is easy. I mean just take this class and google everything and you get an A. 8% of extra credit is offered.

Very tough grader I can not stress that enough. during the lectures she tends to run through very fast, to the point you might as well not take notes. I think her strictness comes from her just being very passionate about what she's teaching. she did give extra credit so that was nice, not sure if this is something that'll continue though.

Sometimes she seems nice, sometimes she's very harsh and rude, Idk what to think of her. Her guidelines are unclear, and a mandatory attendance lecture is enough to make me wanna drop out. The project is annoying but it's easy. Mandatory attendance lectures should not be a thing, it's not learning, school is a scam, drop out

Her guidelines for everything is completely unclear, she gives no feedback, she is generally mean to students but expects you to show up to a non engaging lecture because she mandates attendance. I thought she was just a bad professor and an alright person but now I am just sick of her because she is rude and not helpful. She is wildly unorganized
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Group projects--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: She literally sucks she's so mean and unorganized and yells at you if you get an answer wrong yet she begs for class participation. Wonder why u don't get it???? Try being nicer to your students. She doesn't explain anything clearly and gets mad when people don't understand. There are many other teachers for Marketing 301 so choose any of them!!!!
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Group projects--Tough grader

reviews.comment: Incredibly boring and mandatory lectures. Her grading and projects make zero sense. She is unorganized but expects everyone else to know when everything is due. There's no need to read the book, just do the Connect HW without reading. The activity hw makes me feel like I'm in elementary school. I dread going to this class.

She is my least favorite professor Ive ever had. Attending the class is pointless except she makes attendance mandatory. The syllabus is 10+ pages of every project description ever because she doesnt separate anything. Her class epitomizes why college is a scam. The hw is ridiculously tedious and not relevant.

The class is graded pretty much on 2 things only (the midterm and final). The exams are open notes (handwritten only) and they are open ended. If you can show that you did the readings, you'll do good. He is a very intelligent and kind person. He takes attendance and forbids any electronics. Overall, would take again.

All of these reviews are honestly misleading. If you are an econ major I think this class is completely worthwhile. Van Den Berg is so knowledgable and has a very unique and educated perspective. Everyone saying "too much reading" is genuinely lazy. Put in a few hours a week and you'll be more than fine.

Compiles extremely fascinating content pertaining to the course. Knowledgeable about history, politics, and of course, econ and creation of economic models.
