Assignments are short and just check you pay attention in lecture and do some of the readings. Accessible outside of class and not hard to talk to. Could listen to his lectures for hours.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Amazing lectures --Gives good feedback

reviews.comment:
Here's how you get an A in this class: 

1. Don't waste time going to the lectures, they're completely useless. All you need to do is take very thorough notes on the readings (everything is open note). 
2. Do well on the weekly quizzes, as they're your only grade other than the final. 
3. Study extensively for the final. It's 100 MCQ's in 2 hours.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Avoid this class at all costs.
The final exam is worth most of your grade and the reading amount is insane, the tests are all reading comprehension and do not help to better understand the material.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Lecture heavy--Test heavy

reviews.comment: 40% of the grade is the final exam. 50% of the grade are quizzes. 10% is attendance in discussions. Enough said. Horrible.

This was the worst class I have ever taken. What he talks about in lectures has nothing to do with what the weekly quizzes are on. I went to tutors in the library to get extra help, and not one of them knew how to help me and literally said to me that his textbook made no sense. The exam is extremely difficult and in-person and has 100 questions,
Easy class, one online quiz a week and a couple papers. He definitely is knowledgeable and gives a great course. If you put in decent effort you will do just fine.
You have to read 30-40 pages every week then take a timed online quiz on the chapter. Lectures were irrelevant  so no point in going.

v easy 2 see the bad rates on here +not want to take his class. i did 2. however, if you know what ur doing + actually like econ its basically a walk in the park. just read + quiz + write. granted, i am only a month into class but its so easy 2 c that he's passionate + 2 me that is a really big deal. if u value prof and not j easy class ull b fine

You ARE going to have to put effort into this course. I would recommend breaking up the reading into smaller chunks over the weeks to make it manageable. If you read and pay attention, you can do really well. Don't get behind, though, because it can be hard to get back on track.

Would not recommend this class. Lectures are pointless, only bother going to discussion sessions. Weekly quizzes that are only open from Friday-Saturday afternoons are nearly impossible to get an A on. The only things I learned in this class were from my TA. Only good thing is he provides the PDF version of his own textbook.

reviews.comment: He's alright I guess, lectures aren't very helpful but as long as you read the textbook you'll be fine.

reviews.comment: lectures are boring but he is passionate about the subject. very approachable. quizzes every week on the readings and 4 essays. TA grades essay fairly easy. take home final. if you read the text book you will be fine. van den berg is very approachable and available to his students. i would take him again despite the rep he gets.

reviews.comment: This class is so hard, I do not recommend taking. The lectures and the textbook (written by the professor) are extremely confusing, and the discussions are not helpful in the slightest. I have read everything I am supposed to and feel like I know nothing.

Lectures aren't needed. You'll be quizzed on what is in the textbook. Take decent/thorough notes. There are a lot of pages. He wrote his own book but it is provided for free. 

My TA was a godsend, funny and energetic. The discussions act as a review, not detailed enough to replace readings tho. Lots of writing papers but the TA feedback was clear.

reviews.comment: DONT TAKE HIM!! The evaluation of your effort in the class is completely unfair and innaccurate. reviews.comment: Stopped attending lectures. Weekly quizzes based on the textbook he wrote (he gives them to u.) Quizzes are 15min long online. 4 essays due in the semester. Kind of boring to listen to. Grades depend on your TA (I got lucky). Final was 120 questions. Assigns 30-50 pgs. of reading each week.

reviews.comment: This class was fine. You do need to read the textbook (that he wrote) in order to pass the class. Going to lectures is not enough. 1 quiz per week and 4 papers throughout the semester (graded by TA) and 1 final worth 30 % of your grade. honestly though it is not bad, but lectures are very dry. I skipped most of them and still did fine in the class
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Professor Van den Berg is very tough. He knows a lot about economics but is pretty monotone and dry in his lectures. He uses his own textbook and assigns 40 pages of dense content weekly which the quizzes are on. Weekly quizzes (30%) are 15 questions in 15 minutes. Pretty extreme but not impossible. 4 papers (40%) and a Final (30%) make up the rest

reviews.comment: I thought professor Van Den Berg to be a good professor. It is clear he is super-passionate about what he teaches and that makes the course enjoyable. reviews.comment: Eh... pretty bad. Really tough grader.  Doesn't know how to teach, just talks for hours about political stuff that he can't control. Nice guy just a really terrible professor. Assigns so many readings as if I have nothing better to do with my life and taking 4 other classes. Wouldn't recommend taking this class at all. Immigration 335 is awful.

reviews.comment: the only way I passed this class was from my TA and discussion class. His class is based off of his own textbook that he wrote and he expects you to read and understand it as much as he does, when he is literally the one who wrote the book. thank god my TA basically gave us the answers to the weekly quizzes.

This class was terrible. The lectures were extremely boring and confusing, and same with the discussion section. He assigns so much reading from his own text book every week. There were weekly timed quizzes, 15 questions in 15 minutes. There were a few written assignments and the final was multiple choice. I highly do not reccomend taking.

This class is taught from the perspective of a Marxist professor. Yes, the class offers a differing viewpoint, but his self-made textbook is infused with an incredible amount of opinionated material. Reading 40 pages a week of this material gave me nothing to take away from the class. The one positive is the quizzes are easy.
I took 105 and 335 with him he is a great professor don't believe the reviews they are crazy, one of the best in the econ department

Had this back in Spring 2020 but I wanted to say, he is the worst. Quizzes were horrible and had an unreasonable time limit. It would be 15 questions in 15 minutes and you couldn't even go back to check/change your work despite having 2 minutes left. Our TA's had to practically BEG him to give us more time, and even then he didn't want to do it.
He's not horrible but I didn't like this class. He makes you read the textbook he's writing and there is a quiz every week and I had to do 4 essays this semester.

BEWARE - DO NOT TAKE THIS CLASS!!! Unless you want to have to read 40 pages of his self-made textbook EVERY week, have quizzes every week (which count for 30% of your overall grade), and go to meaningless lectures. The quizzes are oriented around the readings, and although the guy has a passion for econ, his lectures don't correlate with quizzes.

This professor is really bad at explaining important information in lectures. The textbook is very hard to understand and uses lots of complex languages. If this class is required for you take it with your friends for help or choose a different professor. There are weekly quizzes that are timed and impossible to get a 100 on
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Van den Berg is very knowledgeable about macroeconomics and wrote the textbook and offers it free to his students. If you dont read you will not pass the class. If you read and can understand it you will do great. The only grades are 1 weekly quiz (15 questions, 15 minutes, online) and 4 writing assignment and the final. Overall he is a great prof.

Super well-educated in economics wrote his own textbook (used in class) and YEARS of background in it. HIs lectures are great for understanding big concepts in economics and most of it is pretty interesting. Unfortunately, weekly quizzes (15 questions in 15 min) are rlly hard and are worth 30% of grade. Writing assignments (40% grade) are easy tho
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Get ready to read--Caring

reviews.comment: I simply do not understand all these terrible comments about this professor. His lectures are a tad monotone, but always very interesting. You'll have a mini-quiz each week that you can literally take at home, with no midterm. Do you want to actually learn Econ or just cruise by? If you actually want to get somethin for your 30k, then take Econ 104

He either doesn't know how to teach an intro class or just wants to use the students to proofread 40 pages of his own book every week. The book is extremely vague and doesn't to a good job in explaining concepts. The lectures are decent but the quizzes are based on the book. The quizzes are a train wreck and you get a minute per question. AVOID HIM

reviews.comment: To be fair and realistic, professor Van Den Berg is a very knowledgable and caring professor. However, he isn't a very great teacher, at least for an intro course. The main issue I have with this course is that the lectures are practically useless to watch as they do not actually prepare the students for the quiz which is a big part of the grades.
reviews.rating_tags: Accessible outside class--Get ready to read--Test heavy

reviews.comment: Shouldn't be teaching an intro class. Cares about economics and says he wants you to learn but makes his quizzes and tests harder than any other class I've taken - no checking answers and insane time limit. 30-80 pages of reading per week and a final that was 30%. TAs were the true saving grace of the class and knew he was crazy. Take anyone else.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Graded by few things--Test heavy

reviews.comment: Ok, he is not a prof for an intro course. There is no definitions of terms or background info, so figure that out on your own. Reading is like 95% of the class, and he writes the textbook as the class is happening which means its kind of giberish. Good luck besties. The assignments (which are essays) are like 40% of the grade are pretty easy

I loved this class! It's a lot of material to cover in one semester, but she does a great job answering any questions (either in class or over email), and providing study guides. Plus, she's really kind and genuinely wants everyone to do well.
Very good and patient professor

I loved this class an having Jing as a professor! It really showed how much she cared about her students and is very understanding that students have other lives outside of school. I would take a class again with her in a heartbeat!

She was super kind! She usually did games or discussion questions even in a huge class to get students more involved. Tests and final grades were curved pretty generously, not a tough class if you take notes + use the very clear and extensive study guides she provides.
Really passionate and caring professor. Lecture content was generally interesting although sometimes hard to follow. Overall a good experience.
Jing is so so amazing! She is very kind, cares deeply about the success of her students, and is very passionate about what she is teaching.

Her lectures changed a ton from the beginning to the end of the year from student feedback. The labs were super easy and usually ended early.  Professor Jing is extremely kind and caring. The one drawback from this class was that it was a little tough to understand the professor in the lecture hall. Tests were hard but not impossible if you study.

Her slideshows are very informative but she goes very fast. It is hard to keep up and you need to re teach yourself many parts of the lectures. Many people just look at the slideshows on their laptop to do notes and go at their own speed(at home or in class.) She is very understanding and kind though, answers questions, and the labs are easy.

Professor who gets problems wrong during class and is unsure of how to solve their own problems. Disorganized and let problems go unsolved and had difficulty explaining them. Tests make up majority of your grade. AVOID.

Professor Xu's lectures were not very helpful. You should watch the videos that are posted through Wiley plus. Watching the videos helped when understanding concepts. However, if possible take this class with another professor.

Not accessible outside of class by any means. Don't go to lectures because the online videos will teach you more than he will. Luckily for anyone having him as a professor, this is the one of the easiest classes in the math department, and the content isn't hard to understand. Class weight: 30% online HW, 10% written HW, 60% two exams.

Ok at lecturing. MATH 331 is one of the easiest courses in the math department, so not too hard to follow along, but easier if you've taken  MATH 235 (lin alg). Idk if he ever had office hours. Pick another prof if you can. Online vids are posted by the other prof, so watch those. 2 exams 60% and 40% HW. Wouldn't take him for a harder class.
reviews.rating_tags: Clear grading criteria--Lots of homework--Test heavy

reviews.comment: Incredibly boring and hard to understand lectures. Basically had to self-teach myself the entire course, waste of time, take the course with a different prof. if you can.

Course itself was very disorganized. Concepts and problems were not properly explained by the professor and left a lot of questions hanging. Prof Xu was sometimes helpful when asked clarifying questions but it still didn't make me learn as a whole. He also disappeared for a week without letting us know until the last minute. Overall disappointing.

Most disorganized professor I have had at UMass. Lectures are confusing with little explanation of concepts introduced or problems done in class. This class was so poorly organized (not solely Professor Xu's fault) that after subpar final exam averages, the grading scale had to be lowered by five points. Do not take his classes if you can.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Man just wants to hoop

Nice guy, but doesn't know how to teach. He just copies from the textbook during lecture with little to no explanation. He also skips calculations in example problems. Tests make up most of the grade. You basically have to teach yourself. HWs are easy but were due AFTER the weekly quizzes which didn't make much sense.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Prof. Xu is a nice guy but he has been the worst math teacher I've had. He's very smart but he doesn't explain his work all that much when he lectures, and is very confusing to follow. I go to extra help every time because of this which is NECESSARY (for me at least). I hope he figures it out eventually, he's got a lot of potential.

Spends little time on each topic and does not explain things very well. The entire class is integration but he will not do the integral at the end assuming you know how to do it each time when he went over integral rules and how to solve them for one class. Has at least 2 technical difficulties each class.
Just completely copy pastes the whole textbook, barely explains what's going on.

Math 132 is understandably a difficult course. However, this professor makes it insufferable. Doesn't respond to emails. Unorganized course moodle and lectures. Messy notes. Microphone dies frequently and then scrambles for his batteries. Literally just reads the textbook outloud during class. Be ready to teach yourself. I wish he listened to us.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Lots of homework

reviews.comment: Dude talks so softly, can barely hear him. Doesn't really teach that well, he would be annotating on his ipad and would present that no the TV, which wasn't very easy to understand. Writing on a white board would have been better.

I didn't learn anything in this class to be honest. He is passionate about his work but the course itself wasted my time. He never responds to emails, even when a deadline is imminent. The final brought my grade down a full letter grade after maintaining an A the entire semester. I watched almost half the class drop out over the semester.

Save yourself and do not take this course. The professor talks about nothing related to assignments the whole class and then gets annoyed when every student has questions. If you email him he will NEVER respond unless you sent 10 emails. Grades so tough and gives awful instruction. Doesn't update grades unless you ask him to do it in front of you.

Professor clearly cares about the students and works with them to ensure they succeed. Works hard to make the class content flexible so that students have multiple options. Excused me of some assignments that I missed due to being sick. Class was easy if you keep up with it all semester.
Lectures are pretty boring but they aren't mandatory. Pretty easy course especially because of the extra credit opportunities.

He is a nice guy but is a tough grader. Doesn't give chances on any assignment which really affected my GPA as it was a stressful year but nothing would be classified as 'excusable' for the school standards. Wish the study guides for the in-person exams were more clear or straight forward.

This professor has a lot of heart. Responds thoughtfully. Energized about the topics. He's as curious about learning and interested in the topics as he expects his students to be. This class was awesome. The material wasn't easy on its own - his instruction made it easy to learn.

I loved class with Wayne! Lectures and guest speakers were super engaging and interesting. Assignments were also thoughtful; follow the directions and youll get an A. Wayne loves to incorporate podcast, videos, and popular media to supplement academic readings. Accessible outside of class and really sincere and caring. Would take another class!

I really enjoyed Prof Waynes class. I was interesting and utilized videos and podcasts to make the material more digestible. If you take good notes during class and listen to the podcasts you will get an A.

Wayne is a fine prof, lots of extra credit and tests are all multiple choice. No HW really. Don't really need the textbook, just listen to the podcast episodes he does before exams. Class content is pretty easy, which lead me to stop showing up to lectures when it was cold or I was tired, but he does randomly take attendance via pop quizzes. Easy A
reviews.rating_tags: EXTRA CREDIT--Beware of pop quizzes--Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: Tests are all multiple choice. Very monotone lectures but he is a nice guy and offers a ton of extra credit, which is not hard nor time consuming. Grade is solely based off 3 exams. Overall nice guy and cares about your grade but shows it in a very bad way. Not a terrible class just wouldnt do it again.
reviews.rating_tags: Graded by few things--Lecture heavy--EXTRA CREDIT

reviews.comment: Wayne is a great professor that just wants you to learn. This class is so great you mostly do all the work in class.

Most dry, dull lectures i've ever had to sit through but he offers up to 10% of extra credit in pop quizzes and tests a super easy. He occasionally does random participation activities in class for points so you have to attend, but all of the info for his tests is straight from the slides and reading
as long as you do all the homework and understand the math youll do well

I didn't go to a single class after the first month. I didn't study and she allowed reference sheets for the exams and was able to get 90s. it was 45 percent for 3 exams, then the rest was weekly HW and discussion participation.

Lectures can be boring, but there's no attendance, I went to most of them because there very helpful. Discussions attendance is mandatory, 3 exams with one-sided notes, not too bad if you can cram a lot in. Before an exam I would go to the study sections that were insanely helpful. Not a bad professor, but can get off topic a lot.

Val is charming and I like her, but as a teacher she isn't the best. her slideshows are a bit of a mess, with most important facts being straight copied from the textbook. The TA I had didn't teach us essential math until the second midterm. but the Supp Instructor Matthew was a great teacher and helped a lot on math.

Prof. Val made ECON 104 feel very manageable. She was consistently supportive and took time to make sure students understood the material. Her office hours were especially helpful and productive. Overall, she created a learning environment that made the course much easier to navigate.

Lectures are not super helpful. TAs grade assignments and take forever to do so. She's very funny and passionate about Econ, and she allows for a 1-sided cheat sheet for midterms and 2 for the final. There is a bit of work outside of class, but manageable. Textbook readings track your reading time. Discussion attendance is mandatory for most TAs.

You need a 95% to get an A. Lectures aren't mandatory but discussions every Friday are. Val is a kind person but not a great professor and she's bad with technology/grades. Decent amount of HW every week (long worksheet and reading assignment) and 3 exams (not too hard) throughout the semester.
Nice teacher but not helpful lectures. Having to get a 95+ for an A is annoying. I showed up to class but you really don't have to at all. Fine to take, but probably are better options for macro

Professor Voorheis is a great professor, and the class wasn't bad at all, although I skipped most of the lectures. You're allowed a cheat sheet on the exams (1 sided for the first and second, and double sided for the final). Homework consisted of readings, worksheets, and quizzes, but they're doable. Overall pretty great class and would take again.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Lots of homework--Caring

reviews.comment: He knows a lot and is really funny. She clearly cares about the class. I did not find her to be the best lecturer as she would consistently misunderstand questions to explain concepts in a not-so-straightforward way. Her slides are pretty messy so be ready for that. Other than that I learned a lot. Go to SI sessions they are great.

val is super funny and kind. she's really enthusiastic about what she's teaching. exams are super straightforward; you also get to bring notes in with you. discussion sections are mandatory but helpful. there's a lot of reading but just skim it and you'll be okay, the hardest things were the homework worksheets, imo harder content than the tests.
Great professor, take this class.

Lectures were not helpful and kinda all over the place. TA labs were very helpful and thats where you will learn everything. Online perusall readings that you dont have to do, but are annoying. Class was very mid.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Lots of homework--Respected

reviews.comment: Val is entertaining, but I did not think she was the best lecturer. Her slides are often confusing and look jumbled, and some of her explanations of the material are confusing. I sat up front with ChatGPT open and just asked it clarifying questions whenever I was confused, and I found that that worked well. Lots of reading but you can skip it.

Valerie is chill as a professor. Personally, I struggled a lot with this subject. Nothing really helped. My TA sucked and she was incredibly unhelpful and never graded assignments but that was besides the point. Midterms are pretty straight forward but I had no idea what was going on. SOOOO much reading and it was still unhelpful.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Lots of homework

reviews.comment: Val is very engaging and very nice and she clearly cares about what she teaches. There's a lot of homework but its not that hard and honestly there is a lot of reading but as long as you look at it you'll get an 100 on the reading grade. Midterm had reference sheets.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Clear grading criteria--Caring

reviews.comment: Valerie is a very passionate professor who truly loves what she teaches and cares about her students. She is always there to help when students need it. She is also hilarious and keeps lectures entertaining. For exams, you get a cheat sheet, and assignments are reasonable. If you study and do your homework, this class is a breeze.

Didn't process anything from class, so much rambling. Lotssss of reading assigned for hw, the online textbook tracks how much you read as a grade. Taught myself everything/the discussions were tremendously helpful. Homework also kept you up to speed. She's really funny, relatable, and sweet though. Love her as a person just not a professor.

Didn't go to class or watch the recordings. She allows cheat sheets for exams so I just spent the day before writing every single concept on the paper to use for the exam. ChatGPT'd all the homework. I put minimal effort into this class but it would've been a lot less stressful if I actually went to class. Easy either way. Her slides are incoherent

There are two bad things about this class: the syllabus was only on canvas and can't be downloaded, and that you need a 95+ to get an A. Simple content, exams (2 midterm, final) are high school level, worksheets and quizzes (each once weekly) can be solved by looking at the posted powerpoints, and readings (once weekly) are simple

If you can take 104 with Val I would recommend doing so. Super caring and really wants her students to do well. Lots of reading each week, but as long as you skim it you should be fine. Straightforward worksheet and multiple choice quiz each weelk, and two  straightforward midterms and a final

Very easy going class. Get cheat sheets for all the exams. Homework is very easy if you just look at the slides. Study guides for tests were also very straight forward and exactly what was on it for the most part. Nothing to complain about.
She made us show up an hour early to our final exam and didnt print enough copies. Been 20 mins and still only 150/300 kids have exams. Lectures never make sense.

Slides are confusing to read through and readings can be a bit of a word mash. It is also hard to sometimes find supplemental readings, but the course itself is fairly easy. Open note exams, 5-6 homework assignments, & attendance is extra credit. She is friendly and entertaining, but material isnt straightforward and you will have to read extra
I thought she was great. Open note exams, bonus points for attending lecture, not much to complain about, though her lectures often go over the time allotted and she can go off topic. Easy A
reviews.rating_tags: Lecture heavy--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Only recitation has taken attendance, I felt like the lectures were not that helpful, homework and recitation was the most helpful

Prof Voorheis is a genuinely entertaining lecturer. She can go off on unrelated tangents, but she is really good at explaining difficult concepts in easy terms. Her slideshows kinda suck so I would recommend going to class and listening to her lecture instead. I have taken two classes with her and she is a very funny, nice, and intelligent person.

Professor is a slow lecturer not worth going to class when you can watch them all online. Grades can vary a lot between TA's if you get a bad TA you are screwed. Sophia Normak is a bad TA if you get her drop the class. Study guides for exams are misleading not telling you everything you need to know and the exams try to trick you.

You get a one sided cheat sheet for each midterm and a 2 sided cheat sheet on the final. You must pay for the text books which are online. Attendance to lectures is optional and discussions are mandatory. I liked Voorhies, she had some good one liners and jokes through the semester. Slides are wordy and she moves through them fast.

Professor's lectures can be hit-or-miss, but discussions and study tools like unstuck ai make this class manageable. Reasonable workload, good TAs, and tests aren't too tricky if you stay on top of things.

All she does is ramble. There is way to much reading. A weekly assignment which she never goes over anything on it. The TAs grade everything and ofc mine is a hard grader. Tests are alright. Overall tho you have to teach yourself everything and no one does the readings. About 100 pages per week. oh and a mini quiz weekly but you can use chatgpt.
take her class for 104 and not anyone else
didn't find the lectures to be helpful for the tests. discussions were more for that, and tests were a little chaotic/thrown together but overall pretty okay!

Professor Voorheis is very experienced in economics. Grade breakdown: 15% HW, 15% Reading, 15% Mini Quizzes (Online, open all week), 10% Discussion (Participation), then 15% for the Midterm 1, Midterm 2, and Final.

Easy to get A, I was able to skim reading and Google when necessary for HW. Tests easy as long as you review information night before.

She was super helpful during office hours. Although there were heavy readings and worksheets to complete each week, they were manageable. If you do the worksheets and study for the exams, they should be pretty easy. Midterm and final we were allowed a cheat sheet. I would recommend this class, as long as you put in effort you should be good.

This class was interesting and overall easy if you do the readings. There are 6 assignments throughout the semester all based on readings and class lectures. The exams are open notes, make sure your notes are typed out/written out on exam day because you can't use your laptop. If you take good notes, the exams should be a breeze.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: if you want a professor who goes off on unrelated tangents in a 50min lecture, she's your virtuoso. lectures do not match content in the textbooks, which cost a fortune. heavy readings every week and unclear ab test material. overall a bad teacher but is accessible outside the class.TAs are super helpful so go to discussions!
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Lots of homework--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: her lecture structure was not very organized as she'd go on meaningless tangents and had super wordy slides. always left lectures feeling like I'd learned nothing. my ta was understanding and helped me out in discussion and office hours. tests were a disaster too (being way too long, grading scale being off etc). she does respond to emails tho

This class is easy to teach yourself, but Valerie's lectures are pretty useless. Her slides are filled with random, niche information. I would recommend going to discussions and review sessions to learn the content. Easy class with reasonable expectations, but she rambles rather than focusing on actual important course content. Nice prof though.
Good Professor

Professor Voorheis is a very amazing person. Her class consists of 3 exams, and readings with a worksheet and a mini quiz every week. Not too bad, just a little bit of reading. Lectures are not mandatory. Overall pretty good class, would take again.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Gives good feedback--Caring

reviews.comment: Good professor, readings, worksheets, and quizzes each week but do able. She pretty much summarizes the readings in her lectures every week, and lectures are recorded.

reviews.comment: worst power point slides ever seen

reviews.comment: Valerie was an amazing professor. I initially took this class just to fill a gen-ed, but she was an amazing instructor who made this my favorite class of the semester - I am going for an engineering major so it's irrelated.

This class was just ok, Val's lectures weren't super helpful and there is a lot of reading in the textbook. Reading, quiz, and worksheet due each week. The discussions are the most helpful thing so try not to miss those.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: Kind and caring professor, but way too much reading. Weekly Moodle worksheets/quizzes, 3 straightforward take home exams, and discussion attendance. There was a lot of content to learn, but everything was open notes. Your grading depends on your TA so beware. Her lectures had lots of examples and she sometimes went on irrelevant rants.

Personally found the class easy. Lectures aren't mandatory and I haven't attended them. Read textbooks and go to the discussion section to learn the concepts for hw worksheets. Tests are home taken and not hard. The professor is understanding and caring about her students
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: Overall easy class should end up with an A. As long as you are okay with reading lengthy chapters in textbooks the course is very easy. Exams are all online and in a short answer / essay format. You are given 3-4 days to complete the exam so it's not very difficult.

She is very caring and accessible. Weekly readings, worksheets and quizzes are all fairly easy. Same thing with open note exams. Stay on top of your work, go to discussion and try on these assignments to get an A in the course. I found in person lectures unhelpful, but attendance does not count (just make sure to do the readings)
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: 104H is a super tough class, but Voorheis is a great teacher. The material is super dense, but she explains things well, is helpful in office hours, and is really funny. She is super approachable and reasonable if you're struggling. There is a ton of reading assignments and the weekly worksheets are very time-consuming. You'll learn a lot tho
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Lots of homework--Caring

reviews.comment: Care about students!! enjoyed her lectures
reviews.rating_tags: Accessible outside class--Clear grading criteria--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: If you took an Econ class in high school, it should be a breeze. She is very accessible outside of class and cares about students.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Get ready to read--Caring

reviews.comment: For ECON104 everything was posted online and accessible with the option of in person lectures. Some of the lectures are boring, but you can tell she cares about the topic. The worksheets and quizzes are straight-forward especially if you attend the discussions. Very reading heavy, but Val gave out a bunch of free book codes which I thought was nice
reviews.rating_tags: Accessible outside class--Get ready to read--Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: Love Val. is one of the only professors who respond to emails and she even does it in a timely fashion! When I had questions she was ready to zoom with me one on one to answer questions about the course and offer me advice in general. Tests were very fair, homework could be difficult but she is always down to help. one of the best online classes

Valerie is so sweet. She's clearly very passionate about economics but her lectures lack literally everything. you can easily skip every class and still pass. Everything in the quizzes and tests is in the readings. LOTS of reading, in addition to a quiz and lengthy worksheet every week. Just make sure you set aside a lot of time for reading and hw.

Honestly, Professor Voorheis is all over the place during lectures. I've noticed all her slides are just copied from the textbook and she reads off of them the whole class. She seems super nice and is passionate about the class but she really isn't a great professor. This said, she defineitly structures the class based on what is best for students

posted lecture recording, slides, assignments and chapter readings in moodle every week. weekly quizzes and worksheets (quizzes were max 5 or 6 questions, some worksheets were long some short and easy). lengthy readings - graded for annotating. 2 midterms (2 parts: MC/SA) and a final exam. not a crazy good class, nothing bad either.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Get ready to read--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: I went to almost no lectures and still got an A. The 3 exams have a lot of material, but she posts study guides that cover most topics. There are weekly worksheets that are graded P/F and are lengthy but not hard to do if you use the lecture slides and textbook. I basically just reviewed her posted slides and the worksheets to prep for midterms.

Valerie isn't a terrible teacher whatsoever, but I found her classes to be pointless. Stopped going halfway through the semester because I learned more in the discussions and didn't have to sit through her rambling about politics. Slides are online, never bought any of the textbooks, and got an A. Gotta put in some effort but easy if you do

An incompetent, vague and quite frankly, terrible professor who spends the lectures purely reading off her slides, which is the exact same thing in the textbook, while not teaching any of the math needed to be successful on the test. Try to switch out of her class if you can, she's not great.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Skip class? You won't pass.--Test heavy

reviews.comment: Val is easily the best economics professor I've had by far. If you have to take macro, TAKE HER CLASS. She is really good at breaking things down to make them easier to understand. Worksheets graded on a P/F scale, two midterms and a final. As long as you show up to class and do the work, it's not hard to pass. She really wants you to do well.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Skip class? You won't pass.--Caring

reviews.comment: This class really isn't that bad. Econ is super boring but I feel like I actually learn in the lectures and Valerie Voorheis is good at her job and u can tell. If u can, get Everest as ur TA bc their discussions help so much. overall not bad
Best Economics professor at umass! Never boring and easy. Skimmed through the books to make cheat sheets that are allowed during quizzes. Fun class
Val is depth with Econ! I learned a lot in her class. Just go to lectures, read her slide and make notes!

Lots of reading, but you can get away with not doing most of it.  One individual class presentation. Instead of a final exam, there is a group project. Participation is a grade booster. Quizzes are open notes. Overall she is a nice teacher who grades pretty easy.

She isn't a bad professor, just not the best. She reads all the information straight off the power point and goes on many tangents. If Economic policy and theory is tricky for you don't take it with her. There are two exams, a final and a few homework assignments so tests are basically your grade. Her lectures become confusing fast.

This class is the easiest econ course.  Didn't buy the books and barely went to class and am still doing well in the class. Val is the coolest and she lets you use cheat sheets for tests and the assignments are pretty much test questions.   Attendance is extra credit.  Don't get the books. Not boring lectures.

Really great lecturer and could actually keep my attention  She lays out everything in the slides and it's pretty straightforward.  No need to read the books just learn her slides.  Exam questions are taken right from the assignments so if you study those you'll ace the exams.  Only hard thing is a 95 is an A.  Attendance is extra credit (sort of).

Val is the bomb! I learned a lot in her class. Tons of reading but if you show up and understand a few core concepts you dont really have to do all of it. 3 quizzes, 2 short papers(1-2 pages), one solo presentation and one group presentation.

Her lectures and discussion are all extra credit. She is loud, super opinionated and all over the place. Her lectures were only 50 min but they dragged on. Her tests aren't too hard but the material isn't that interesting. Also, you need a 95 to get an A which I think is unnecessary

Valerie might annoy some people as she is very opinionated, but if you agree with her or if you just pay attention to the material itself you will learn pretty quickly. Got an A in this class without studying very much. She puts all the slides up online so you don't really need to go to class unless you want to hear it explained in person.
She's super friendly and posts all the lecture slides on moodle so you never actually have to show up

Val is super nice and the perfect professor for ECON 105. The class is basic (as it should it be) for a gen ed. I went to about 50% of lectures and did minimal to no studying and got an A-. If you need the gen ed or just want an easy class about economics then this is it.

Val is a good teacher who is knowledgable about the subject, but she sometimes gets carried away with other things during lecture & doesn't go over the important stuff as in depth. You don't really have to go to lecture b/c the slides are online. The exams are based on all of the homework and slides mostly, so if you follow along you should be set.

Val is a pretty good teacher, she's kind and laid back.  Lectures were ok, boring at times.  Very easy class imo, many ppl skipped class almost everyday and still got an A(NOT recommended). No need to buy textbook, answers to problem sets were deducible via google, although the book probably would have helped.  Exams are fair, on the easy side.

Valerie is an excellent teacher, and I highly recommend her classes to anyone. There's a reason she won an award for being a distinguished professor. She covers the topics exhaustively and handles questions very well while keeping the course moving at a good pace. Easy but extremely helpful writing exercises, and no surprises on her tests. A+.
This class wasn't that bad. There are 3 exams, 2 through the semester and 1 cumulative final. The second exam was hard, but the TAs were helpful if you don't understand something

Val isn't a bad professor, just not my favorite. She makes class interesting, but most of the information she says in class is right off of the powerpoint slides or she goes on a random tangent about something. The first exam is ridiculously easy, but the second exam was impossible. TAs grade so they scale them. Mandatory discussions.

Val is so cool! I love her lecture teaching style and she's really chill. Goes on rants sometimes but it's not a problem. Mid-terms are very similar to the study guides she publishes. Didn't read the textbook that much since she puts the powerpoint slides online.
I never went to class so I can't really comment on Valerie's teaching, but the tests were pretty easy and graded leniently. Doesn't explain the math too well, but I still got an A with little effort.
Test was ridicously easy.

Some students swear by her, I personally thought she was pretty unhelpful. She puts the powerpoints online which is somewhat useful but the tests involve you knowing the math. She's not available for office hours and the lectures are a waste of time. Go to the extra help before the final.

Val is a fantastic and witty lecturer. Her powerpoint slides basically summarize everything that is in the book-in class she goes over them and provides helpful commentary. Attendance is not mandatory but it is helpful to go to class. Val is very approachable. Homework is graded easily. Exams aren't tough if you study the night before. I got an A.

I don't know how you can take these classes and not get an A. The powerpoints are online and attendance is extra credit. Tests are graded leniently. She's super nice and lectures aren't boring. I never did any reading, just went to class half the time and read the notes. Still got an A.

The class is easy. Valerie is an interesting character. Although she makes some strange comments and goes off track sometimes because she loves to talk and make jokes, she usually presents the information for exams pretty well
A very easy class, but I would say that Val teaches the technical aspects, ie the math of economics in the worst and least intuitive way possible. Probably should not get tenure.

Val is an awesome lady who is very knowledgable but her classes are a bit confusing and hard to take notes in. Got an A in the class by taking her study guides and teaching myself everything basically. Her review sessions are very helpful. Tests are a lot of writing but if you prepare yourself you should do fine.

Had Val for 330, 104, and now 105. She is a great professor! Her exams were straightforward as long as you did the assignments and went through her powerpoints. If you were confused with something, she is really nice and clears up any confusion. I am glad I ended my college career with Val's class!

Had Val twice now, for 330 and 105. Her lectures are typically boring and Powerpoint based but she doesn't make attendance mandatory which is nice because doing the readings and assignments will usually adequately prepare you. Tests are always a lot of writing instead of multiple choice or T&F but grading is usually lenient.

Lectures were very, very boring. Not mandatory and you definitely don't need to go. Do the weekly worksheets, read over the online notes, and study for the midterm and final. Exams were a lot easier than I expected.

Val is definitely passionate about what she teaches and I enjoyed listening to her lectures (which she posted recordings of online, if the technology worked). Weekly homeworks and discussions which you should attend, and the tests were very long but doable. Her office hours are helpful and she is able to better explain the more difficult concepts

I loved Val. She likes to rant in class and can sometimes be confusing at first. But if you read the book and go to discussions/lectures you will honestly be fine. Material not that hard, just the way she presents it makes it seem that way at times. She loves to help you out, so go to office hours/review sessions, she will tell you what is on exam.
Don't buy the book or go to class, lecture is useless. Print out the notes posted on moodle and go to every discussion and you'll be fine.

Overall a good class. Attendance is not required. Would not recommend taking as a gen ed since it requires a lot of work and reading. Yet if ready to study, she gives all the opportunities to get a good grade. 2 tests, weekly worksheets.

Attendance is optional but you get EC if you go. It really helps if you are borderline with your grade. Tests are straightforward because all you need to do beforehand is memorize all the notes. No need to get the textbooks! I will take another class with her next year.

Attendance optional. Lectures were boring b/c she just read off the notes. Don't need to read the books or go to lecture. Just memorize all the notes she posts online and regurgitate everything on the tests.

Class was boring, she just read the notes on the overhead, and the notes were online.  Study the notes before the test, and memorize as much as you can.  Spit everything you remembered out on the test. I never did the readings, never listened to her lectures, got an A-.

Still uses overhead projector so notes can sometimes be disorganized. BUT she posts all notes online and you can probably get a decent grade in the class without going to class. I wouldn't recommend to any business school students because she hates you. That being said its a kinda easy gen ed if you're desperate.
She is funny at times.  I would only go to class to laugh.  The class is basiclly useless.  Just go to duscussion- and you can still get a good grade.  Tests are hard but get scaled.
AVOID THIS CLASS

She is really nice and tries to be funny but the class is just awful.  The notes are online which is nice but the exams are difficult. There is a lot of theory involved. She really cares about econ and assumes everyone else does too. You will definitely need to devote a good amount of time to this class if you want to get an A.

Val is really nice and very willing to help you out if you need it. She is not a good lecturer at all though. The lectures seriously lack continuity, they are just her stream of consciousness about the material. The notes make no sense until you do the readings, but once you have an understanding of everything it is a pretty cool class, worth it.

This professor is among the most frustrating ever. Her notes are completely disjointed, her review sheets are horribly disorganized,and studying for her tests is extremely bothersome. Her class is easy, but she makes you run around a LOT to find any information. I recommend avoiding her.

This class is really easy by itself.  You don't even have to go to class, just read the slides she posts online.  Don't bother with the extra credit since she just ends up forgetting about applying it to your grade.

Despite what other people have said this class is not that hard.As long as you are semi intelligent and can grasp concepts and even if you arent interested in econ she does a good job of explaining whats going to be on the test. Since there are only 2 tests heavy memorization/studying is required but thats not out of the ordinary for gen eds
Terrible class.  She acts like everyone in the class cares.  Some people take this class for a Gen. Ed., not a major. awful.

Never had to show up to a class because the lectures include no helpful material and the most drawn out rants about nothing I've heard in awhile. The TAs are pretty helpful. Definitely a good class... until you have to take the final and then you realize how awful the class actually is... all I can say is find another teacher.

Makes her notes accessible on SPARK, but pretty much reads off of them in class peppered with rants on the current economy which makes attendance not very useful. If you get a helpful TA, go to them with questions. There are 10 worksheets with info from her slides. Exams were tough and counted too much midterm 30%, final 45%, discussion 25%.

She's nice and can be funny and laid back.  I attend probably half of the lectures.  They are usually real boring and the concepts are really simple so I just read the slides online since she just reads off of them.  She talks a lot about the current economy which gets old fast though.

Class isn't bad- 3 exams, 1 easy paper and 5 hws answering questions right out of the notes- If your good at cramming before the tests, all questions come right from the study guides so its easy to get an A-Had the best TA who helped A LOT.

One of the most useless classes I have ever taken. Books are completely unnecessary, has mandatory attendance for an 8 AM class, terrible TA, gives no reason to care about the material. overall, just plain useless as a professor.

I've taken 104 and 330 with her and have done extremely well in her classes.  Everything she expects you to know from the textbook she'll go over in her slides so no need to actually read the books.  Exams are not hard at all as long as you do her study guides which she'll provide a week in advance before the test.  Easy A even if you cram.

Pointless going to the lectures, she reads off from the slides directly. Just read over the notes (the book is too confusing, she summed up main pts in her notes), do the worksheets, and keep yourself up to date with the economy. Understand the material and you'll be fine! The TAs are great, just turn to them if you need to clarify anything!!

Boring class not the easiest. She doesn't always teach the material on her syllabus. Rants on the current state of the economy, gives you one side of the story but not the other when she gets into politics (TOO POLITICAL! ITS AN ECON CLASS). I found problems in her lectures about Social Security and the Bush Tax Cuts. Some of her data was wrong.
I've taken econ103, econ104, and econ330 with Val. She is a really good, down to earth professor. It is a lecture, just like stated, and she knows her stuff. She is very helpful in office hours too.

This class sucks. She spends half of the class talking about current news- stuff that won't be on the test. She goes too fast- thank god she puts notes online! Her tests are wicked hard. Only buy the book if you're planning on skipping a lot.

I GREATLY DISLIKE THIS WOMAN. Needs to learn compassion for students. Never follows the syllabus and talks about everything BUT macroecon during lecture. Again, avoid this woman, and avoid any class she teaches. So self-absorbed and her attraction to herself takes away from the material. Lecture is pointless.
Read the textbook, do the homework, and go to discussions. You'll be fine.

This is the greatest class in the history of possible classes. Valerie deserves not only an award for outstanding excellence in the field of economics but a Nobel Prize as well. Thinking about taking this class? I am taking it again, even though I received an A just because I enjoyed it that much. I would recommend this class to anyone
Very intersting in lecture, and you can actually listen because she posts the notes online. Go to discussions and do worksheets and you will get an A.

Ok, so the nature of lectures is that they suck. You and the other 150 people can prob aggree on that. I went every 3 or 4x and did fine. Val posts notes online with corresponding textbook pages, book on reserve, don't need Real World. Turn on the radio and listen to NPR- economists on all the time- may lend some clarity. And talk to your TA!

boring, played bloons all the time. real world macro not needed. TAs did all the work. not a good professor at all. she wrote the exam a day before the exam, very poorly written even the TAs hated her.

8am lecture, went to 5 only. went to discussion. got a B. who seriously goes to 8 am lectures? OH my classmates...half the auditiorium. CRAZY. she's entertaining to go to...I learned something at one of the lectures, but 2  out of 5 were VIDEOS ! omg.

The exams weren't hard but she scares you a lot. Lectures are important but staying up in them is the hardest thing which consumed all of my energy this semester. The most important thing is your TA. If you have a good TA than an A is guaranteed otherwise all I can do is wish you luck.

For those complaining, on the midterm if you knew the material you'd do well - those complaining about "her trying to trick us" obviously never took any APs in high school; tests are supposed to be hard. All around a sold, nice, helpful professor; great to talk to during office hours, don't need to go to class and only need the book as a reference.
She is not clear and trys to trick you on the test. If you do not have a good TA you are in trouble.
Easy class, pointless lectures. Get notes online and go to discussion. Don't need real world book.
class is easy, prof. is lazy and doesnt care just rambles on about the current economy all during class. midterm 30 per, final 45 per, wksts/ atd for disc 25 per.

All around terrible class. Going to class is pointless because she goes on fifteen minute rants about current events that do not pertain to actually learning macro. Notes are usually limited. She cancelled two or three classes. The textbook is all around inacessible and bland. Just avoid the class because you won't develop an understanding.

Hated this class.  All she does is go on rants about whatever she feels about and says wicked corny things.  She takes the overheads off way too quickly.  Her tests suck, she always screws them up.  If you take econ, don't take it with her!

She doesn't really do much. She just reads the notes that she posts up on the course website, which make going to class stupid. She goes on rants about current events. She is very disorganized especially with exams. Just read the lecture notes and the text and it'll be fine.

It's obvious that she has no interest in teaching considering the fact that she cancels classes a lot and spends more time talking about current events than she does teaching the actual curiculum. She made our midterm at 2am the night before and told us about it and screwed up the answer key; I don't even wanna know what the final's gonna be like.

Pointless to go to lectures... she just spends the entire class talking about current events that have nothing to do with the topic we're supposed to be covering. Goes through overheads too fast. All notes are online... so just read the book and go to discussions. Otherwise you're wasting your time sitting through lectures and learning nothing.
She talks about current events in class which is not on the test. If you want to pass the test you have to read the book and do the worksheets. Useless to  go to class.
AWFUL TEACHER. She makes up tests the night ebfore and they're full of mistakes. Her elctures are boring, useless, and erratic. I'm teraching msyelf the course. Avoid taking her course.
Val is friendly and usually enthusiastic about class.  You might find the lectures boring.  If so, just don't go to class.  You can still get a B if you read.

I found the lectures pointless toward the class. She talks about current event which is interesting but useless when its comes to trying to learn the material. Read the book and learn the material on your own and there's no reason to go to class unless the discussions interest you.
The lectures are boring, and the readings are intense (if you choose to do them).  The tests can be hard if you don't understand the material well.

Great professor with a really warm heart. Only 2 Exams, notes posted online. Material is as dry as any economics class but she works really hard to make it interesting. I would recommend the professor, not the class.

Decent lecturer. Excited about the subject. (You may not be; micro isn't known as the accessible, thrilling portion of economics.) Notes posted online and extensive review sheets make passing easy. To excel you will have to do some legwork (extensive reading, etc) but generally not a bad class.

Easy Easy.  No need to go to class. she emails out the notes.  go to the review before the test.  midterm and final.  shes really boring.  Just teach yourself from the notes and use the review sheet and study before the tests.
I wrote the review below this and I meant to put econ 105, not 103.

Easily my favorite class of the semester. She truly loves what she does and loves the subject matter. Extremely helpful and always welcomes after class discussions. She wrote me an excellent recommendation letter as well. Many people did not like her in the course because...well they were either lazy or uninterested. Great class, great professor.
BORING BORING BORING. You basically teach yourself. Read the book.
pretty mediocre teacher, dont have to go to class, all notes are sent to you. tests are not bad if you study

Its a really easy course...i got an A without much effort...although i love econ...the 3 for clarity is because the test and worksheets dont make sence some times...but that wont conflic with your grade because the TA's love pointin her nonsence to her :-)...take the class....its easy
Fantastic course. She's a great professor, and the material is fantastic, useful, and applicable to life.  this course, and her teaching of it, has the ability to motivate you to make a difference.

horrible horrible teacher. didn't learn anything. went through overheads way to fast. wouldn't put them back when students asked. only half of the class showed up for lecture, and of those that showed nearly half left out of frustration before the end of the class. avoid taking an intro class with this woman.

Voorheis was a pretty good teacher.  She has an interest in what she is teaching and she is very approachable.  She lectures during class, which does get boring, but how else is she supposed to teach labor economics? Grade: B
Far too preoccupied with being a mother to be an effective teacher. Poor lecturer. Reads straight from the overheads. Do not take this class if you have a desire to learn, only if you want an easy A.
bad, bad, bad.  i couldn't physically sit through an entire class when i went.  it is extremely easy, but not interesting at all.

easy class. don't have to do all the readings. for the exams, just memorize the outline on ereserves. homeworks come straight from the notes as well. she gives plenty of extra credit in case you screw up.
No Comments
awesome
She's a very nice woman, loud though, but overall she's a good teacher with good insights.

her class is left wing bs and I love it.  I don't get pissed off in many classes becasue of the content, but her's is one in which I do.  Take this class, if for no other reason than to learn how to exploit workers when you are a wealthy capitalist owner.
she likes beans. she will talk about beans. she will make you dream of beans. but its all good. tests are ridicoulously easy if you go to a few classes and do some studying
Easy material, common sense to most.  Although, tests are long and very in-depth.  Opinionated. Notes posted online.  Not the best Econ class.
Anyway I learned a lot
Great Class! Valarie really cares about the students. She is very easy to understand and all course notes are online, lots of opportunity for extra credit. She is a great professor!
Not to bad, some homework, but it usually helps your grade and the tests are right from the review questions...not really hard at all!!!
way too many assigments.  Last 2 weeks of semester we had a paper due every class.  None-the-less we had to do 11 out of 12 possible papers, which took forever to get back.
fun class. real easy. takes a long time to get papers back.

If you're grown-up and/or take a grown-up attitude, Val is a fine teacher.  Knows her stuff, is easy-going - worst point is she's too easy going.  The subject sucks, and no professor could make it interesting, so a lot of the flak should be aimed at Econ.
Not a full professor, not even done with her grad work.. but i think she'd put more effort into making the class harder if she got that together.  For now as long as she's employed she's ok with it.
I cannot get over how bad this woman is. I've learned nothing. I can't believe UMass would employ this kind of instructor.

If you're a socialist, and you believe white males are ruining the economy and you enjoy reading  books  titled  How Capitalism Underdeveloped Black America  then this is the teacher for you.  Otherwise, run.  The manure she spouts is unbearable.
The course material isn't that difficult to grasp, but her teaching is an atrocity. The worst professor I've run into in the economics department.
easy class, interesting but takes forever to give back assignments
sucks-not fair with grades-takes forever to pass back assignments
flip this guy

He makes class very boring, nobody shows up. Waste of time. Light homework and exam was pretty much the study guide, but the study guide was hard to follow and did require work before the exam/lots of memorization. Don't recommend, but definitely a chill guy.

attendance is not mandatory, half of the class is almost always absent. you don't need to take notes. seems confused at times but he does know a lot about what he is teaching. lots of project work and analyzing sources outside of class. almost every test question is straight from the study guide.

Doesn't know the material well, uses chat gpt i swear. Not engaging, i have never payed attention. But does give good study guides and theres not much HW. the class in all is so boring, dont take it. Use the rap to get into southwest then drop!!!!

This was an interesting class because there was ZERO student participation at times and the professor would do nothing. You can tell he cares about this topic and if you do the easy assignments you'll get a good grade (he grades most things off credit or no credit) but if you're looking to actually learn it's not here.

Just came on here to combat the bad reviews! I actually took this class in the fall, but as one of the first class I took in college, it was easy enough, and interesting. Idek why everyone is up in arms about the class participation; nobody except for a few people talked in class, and it made things way more awkward.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Gives good feedback

reviews.comment: Okay, so a lot of these reviews are valid. However, half the blame is on the absolutely dead students who expect to take this class for an easy gened. Like, y'all, what other than class participation do you expect? Xu Li def has his quirks. However, he's one of the only professors who focuses in Asian lit here, and the readings are cool.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Do not take this class unless you want to waste an hour and fifteen minutes of your day. I don't know whats worse, the complete lack of engagement in his class or his determination to make students participate. there are reading reflections every class and he expects you to be familiar with each one and be ready to discuss in class.  Never again.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Lots of homework

reviews.comment: This is a dreadfully boring class. Li is a chill guy, friendly enough, accessible when needed. But every class is the exact same format, and there's no big takeaway or point to the course: Li never gives actual analysis or applicable commentary. Makes it frustrating and uninteresting, even when the course should be cool.
Xu Li is a good teacher when you do your work, he doesn't assign a lot of work he just gives readings that are 20 pages. It's a good class for an art requirement

The course mostly focuses on international 20th century short stories. The overall workload is quite heavy, 2-4 short stories per week and discussion forum before each class. Because there is a large amount of reading covered, it is hard to get a deeper analysis from him or in class. Exams are very easy though.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Participation matters--So many papers

reviews.comment: Xu Li is an ok professor at times. He's very pushy to get students to participate, even when they genuinely don't know the answers to his questions. The "short stories" are comprised of works that'll actually take a while to read. While the exams aren't actually hard, the two papers are what take up the most time. I only had an okay time in class.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--So many papers

reviews.comment: Professor Liang doth move with the elegance of a willow in a gentle breeze. His every lecture, so refined and graceful, could make the heavens themselves blush with envy. Truly, his lecture is as captivating as a dancer's most delicate pirouette, drawing the eyes of all who chance to behold him.

Lo, the bearing of Liang is as that of the nimble antelope which doth roam the canyons of Africa – a vision to quicken the soul. When I sit at his feet and hear his wisdom, my heart is made light, and I am filled with a most peaceful joy.

Professor Liang's form, so lithe and vigorous, is as the antelope of the Grand Canyon – a sight to inspire the heart. Each time I attend his discourse, my spirit is lifted, and I find myself in a state of serene contentment.

Prof Liang is a man yclept with mickle pride, and holdeth scant account of his fellows' wit. He doth dispense his lore with a scornful mien, as though all others were but dolts and nincompoops. Verily, his self-regard doth wax so great, 'tis a marvel he doth not cleave the welkin with his head.

Professor Liang has a marvel of egregious indifference to the most fundamental tenets of social grace. He seems to have forsaken the most rudimentary vestiges of empathy and decorum, as if they were but forgotten relics, lost in the labyrinth of his own self-absorption.
The 5 star comments are fake.

His words, like streams of crystal water, refresh the minds of all who gather to hear them. With a mastery of his art and a kindness of spirit, he illuminates even the darkest corners of ignorance, imparting not only knowledge but wisdom. In his presence, the flame of curiosity is kindled, and the noble pursuit of learning flourishes

He evinces an apparent disinclination towards the benevolent dispensation of aid and must often endure an inordinate delay before securing his audience. his comportment betrays an air of apathy towards the scholastic endeavors of his charges.
Deciphering their sentence feels like solving a riddle wrapped in an accent, enveloped in mystery
I would say mediocre. Nothing to write home about.
I would not recommend him because his office hour is boring.
GREAT PROF!
Hilarious, extremely hilarious. He is very hilarious.

Very nice professor and good intro course. Listen to what he says in class, that's where you'll learn the most. Exams are not horrible and there's many chances to get an A in the class. Not going to kill your gpa and not a stressful class.

He is a good teacher. The lectures are long but have a lot of good information and extra credit quizzes are given if you attend class. The exams are mostly memorization and can have a few difficult questions so you have to study. Overall a good professor who is nice and wants to help you succeed.
reviews.rating_tags: EXTRA CREDIT--Lecture heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Class was not hard but was very boring. He pretty much just reads from the ppt he made. He could have made the class a bit more fun and engaging. There are 2 midterms and a final exam and he also offers chance for extra-credit in the form of in-class quizzes.
Great teacher! Three tests that cover only lecture material, so although attendance isn't required it's best to go. He also offered extra credit in the form of in class pop-quizzes.

The class is 85% exams, so you have to go to class and study to do well on the exams. The lectures were boring because he goes so slow. No homework. He's super nice, but he chooses weird specific things to for the exam content. He does random participation quizzes sometimes.

While lectures aren't mandatory in Professor Xiao's class, you should still attend them because there's always opportunities for extra credit and they're the only way to learn material. There's really no homework or supplemental practice, which sounds nice but means you have to make your own study materials if you want to remember anything.
reviews.rating_tags: EXTRA CREDIT--Lecture heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Professor Xiao is a solid lecturer. The slides are online as well as the lecture videos so coming to class is not required. However, he explains more in class than is what is on the slides. He has an accent but it is easy to understand. Your grade is made up of 3 midterms which are not cumulative and extra credit with practice exams. No curve.

Has a lot of practice problems during class and posts his slides. He does move a bit quickly through some slides so I found it helpful to have them open during class or watch the echo 360 lectures at my own pace. Good guy but sometimes doesn't tell you when weirdly specific stuff is important to know. Only grades on 3 exams and practice completion.
reviews.rating_tags: Graded by few things--Test heavy--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: Glad I took his class. I did better in 265 than I did in 150 (took 265 first) and they covered essentially the same material. There are 3 exams and they are curved heavily, and while his lectures aren't exactly captivating, he is quite funny and definitely cares about students. I hope I will be able to take another class with him!
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Hilarious--LECTURE HEAVY

reviews.comment: Don't be hesitated. Take his course! He is definitely the best one. I've taken his 265 266 and 391A course. You can get A as long as you take the notes when he says "you guys gonna pay attention..." A lots of extra credits, no homework and you have practice exam to get an idea for your exam every time. Very fun classes while I've learned a lot.

I don't think he was as bad as people are saying. I am a freshman take Food Science 265, and I added the class late(r) in the semester. He curves every exam heavily which is nice (I have received a 79 on both exams so far, which equates to a B+ in his class). The material is interesting but he doesn't explain it in a particularly captivating way.

Accent can make it hard to understand at times, DO NOT get up to leave class early or he WILL call you out in front of the class... iClicker questions are key, and he plays favorites with the students in class.

Pretty easy, all you have to do is show up even though he's kind of boring during lectures. Said the final wouldn't be cumulative but it was and he didn't show up to the final to explain anything. Slightly hard to understand but not too bad. No textbook yet very detailed notes and tests were detailed as well.
He isnt as bad as people think. He does have a strong accent which makes him a little hard to understand, but the material is interesting and the workload is pretty small.

Yeah, do yourself a favor and stay away from this class at all costs... tests are ridiculously detailed, and class is just powerpoints. super boring. He def doesnt care about the students, he knows most have failed the past 3 years, bust just curves everything instead of changing his approach to teaching. BAD.

Do not take this class unless you absolutely have to. The professor isn't helpful; .he didnt show up for my final exam and he also didnt show up to a class review. There's 3 exams in the class and that's your grade. Exams are extremely detailed..memorize the power points the best you can. Attendance is mandatory. Also no textbook.

He has a thick but mostly understandable accent. Must attend lectures for iClicker points. Exams and clickers are the only things he bases grades on. Exams are easy if you don't sleep through class, take the practice exams online, and read the powerpoints posted online. There is no book.
He posts very detailed slides and expects you to know every detail, though he will say he doesn't.

Professor Xiao knows what he's talking about and is relatively easy. His accent isn't hard to understand. The class is overall quite easy and as long as you go and go over the lecture slides before each exam (2 midterms and a final) then you'll be fine.

A lot of notes to memorize for the test! I suggest to study beforehand so you won't be overwhelmed! Not the easiest class even though it's a lvl 100 class. Don't take this class if you don't need to, there are so much other better classes!
Very hard to understand, test questions can be very tricky. Exams are relatively hard for a 100 level class. Attendance is a most as PRS counts a lot for your grade.

He just read the notes directly from the slides. Must attend class because of PRS. The tests are based from a ton of his notes. If you really want to do well on his tests, study (and memorize!) his notes ahead of time because he asks specific questions! Test averages are in the 60's. FS101 is a little bit tough for a lvl 100 class.

worst class. do not take. food science majors are failing. 3 exams which are impossible and such minor details of what we learned. class averages have been low 60's and hes happy with that? TERRIBLE teacher, notes are terrible also. prs quizzes so you have to go to class. worst class ive taken

I would say the primary reason why this professor has a low rating is because of his rather thick Chinese accent. However on top of this, his lack of experience in teaching clearly shows. Class itself wasn't too hard. If you went and studied the notes the tests were actually okay. Overall definitely not a good class, but not too bad.
Rude, will manipulate a question so that student appears wrong then will smirk/laugh at them when he answers the question. Also extremely difficult to understand
I thought a foodsci level 100 course would be easy but it's the hardest of all my classes and I'm a senior as well. Worse class and teacher I've had, don't bother with this course

This is a level 100 class, should be pretty easy for a senior who goes to class?? The first exam gram avg was a 60 and he blamed us. Tests are extremely difficult even if you go to class. Theres no way a level 100 class should be so difficult. I wouldn't recommend this class to any one unless he changes his teaching style. (he is a first year prof)

I love this man!!!!!! He cares about you and his office hours are amazing. His projects at times were unreasonably difficult but you will ultimately get a good grade if you try your best and explain your thought process.

Really nice guy, just a very time-consuming class. Projects 1 and 3 were not bad at all, project 2 was very difficult. Grading is super lenient and the TAs were great. I didn't learn too much in this class, but I guess that should be expected with a design class. Brush up on system and regular dynamics for projects 2 and 3 and you should be fine.

He seems like a nice guy who means well. But it's simply unacceptable that it's more than halfway through the semester and zero assignments have been graded. It's not cool that he retroactively made an assignment worth 20% that the syllabus said would be worth 15%. And now he's giving us 1 week to do another difficult assignment worth 20%.

Confusing lectures with terrible exam reviews.  Difficult to ask questions because he will start to answer what he thinks you're gonna ask before you finish.  Be prepared to do a lot of self study (the textbook is helpful).  His teaching isn't effective so I relied heavily on the TAs.  They pretty much taught everything to me. Grading was clear.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: His exam review is trash, also he sometimes does not even give 2 hours for an exam. It's extremely easy to get lost in his lectures. He was ok, and the material is challenging.
basically no exam review material, confusing explanations for concepts
He's very enthusiastic and nice. His lectures mostly make sense and so do his exams. However his review/exam practice is extremely lacking.

Shane is a very funny guy who for sure cares about his students. Sometimes his lectures can become complicated, however he is very helpful at explaining outside of class. His exams are somewhat tough (although the first one was pretty easy). Definitely a tough class for material, but Shane is there to make sure that you understand it all.

Du is one of the best in the program. Super kind and cares about his students' success. Gives homework with clear grading criteria that is similar to the exams. Lectures legit prepare you for the tests with highlighted information that you put on the cheat sheet he lets you bring to the exam. Super fair, awesome guy, all-around good class.

Amazing human being, but kind of an average professor. The redeeming factor was how accessible he was outside of class. His lectures tended to be confusing, but he was great in his office hours. The textbook is also very helpful. The material is pretty boring, but it's not too bad once you get the hang of it
reviews.rating_tags: Accessible outside class--Skip class? You won't pass.--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: I loved Shane. He was extremely kind and explained things so thoroughly. He applied the content to real life and made the lectures something I wouldn't dread going to.
