Prof Du always is happy to be in class and this passes on to the students. When the course got more difficult Du sometimes struggled to slow down and explain difficult ideas. Cheat sheets are a huge help on exams, but he does not scale regardless of average. Class is not mandatory but, he does give quizzes and even extra credit, it's worth going.
reviews.rating_tags: Accessible outside class--Clear grading criteria--Beware of pop quizzes

reviews.comment: Du is a very solid professor. He cares about your learning, and does everything he can to make sure the grading is decent. Tells you exactly what is on the exams, there are no surprises. You get a cheat sheet, and he is accessible for questions. He struggles with pace, he goes fast when going through proofs. His examples help a lot though.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Caring--EXTRA CREDIT

reviews.comment: Xian was new to teaching this semester, but really cared so much about each student passing. The language barrier was difficult to get through at first, but by the end you get used to it. He gave pop quizzes and a lot of extra opportunities to do well. Tests were very difficult for me, but I also did nothing in class and googled the homework.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--BEWARE OF POP QUIZZES--Caring

reviews.comment: Does not treat students fairly.

Professor Chait is very nice, however, the class is total disaster. The lectures are unhelpful. You cannot see a thing he writes. The shadows and his hand writing make it impossible to understand anything he writes.

This class is a disaster. Impossible to hear him, impossible to see what he's writing on the projector, and when you can hear and see what he's writing it is completely unintelligible. HW is challenging. Do not take this class with Professor Chait.

Messy handwriting and drags on some topics and hard to pay attention, but it isn't his fault just MIE402 is not a well structured class. Lots of the assignments did not clearly state what you needs for the reports and ended up just having to email the TA every week to get as much information as possible. Very good curve though. Great guy though.

Really nice guy but often gives un clear explanations during lecture. I would highly recommend reading the text book instead of relying purely off lecture notes. Also be prepared for exams that are more difficult than the homework.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Beware of pop quizzes--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Yossi is a really nice guy but you will have to teach yourself

The lectures can be boring at times but everything you need to get a good grade is in the lectures. He gives you the matlab code and helps you with the math, answers all questions in class or over email. Extremely open and positive about class wide extensions, he understands you have exams in other classes and will give generous extensions.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--So many papers--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: His lectures can be a little boring sometimes because he over explains some things, but other than that he was awesome. He's approachable and understanding, and this class really improves your technical writing. Would take again.
get ready to teach yourself hours of understanding his under-commented Matlab code as well as not telling you what you're actually supposed to be looking for in the lab/memos

He doesn't give ANY sort of direction with writing lab memos. If you have a lab early on in the week, forget about knowing what to do on the pre-lab assignments. He uploads multiple versions of the assignment last minute and expects you to have the most updated version completed and submitted before lab too. Lectures are useless, he just mumbles.

Yossi is a great guy, probably one of the most helpful professors out there. The way the online class is structured, however, makes it very difficult to follow along in my opinion. Especially when using Simulink, most students are very lost and while he makes himself readily available outside class it's still rough. Not a fan of asynch lectures
Yossi may not always be the best in class professor, however he is always willing to help outside of class time. Defiantly a teacher I would love to sit down and have a beer with

I didn't get statics at all (dbk was no help), but everything made sense in strengths with Yossi. The solution manual REALLY helps, and the material is largely self taught, but sitting in lecture listening to his explanations helped me too. He's a good guy and genuinely cares about students. Definitely a passable class.

Yossi Chait is a cool dude but sometimes he can be all over the place when teaching. Between him and the book, the class is passable, but not without a challenge. If you have the paper and ink to print out his pre lecture notes then class can be a lot more bearable and easier to understand. He gets off to FBD too so make sure you have them on tests

Yossi is a bit confusing. He does tend to mess up a lot pf the in class problems and it's usually up to the advanced students to save him. He sometimes will even discourage you for being wrong, then say that you need to think. Don't take this class if you don't want to feel down on yourself for making mistakes!

anyone who passes this class is as qualified to teach it as yossi.  doesnt teach, just screws up problems in class. class is self taught out of the book. the guy is arrogant and thinks his time is more important than anyone elses. waste of taxpayer money
Yossi? Just do the hw. Call him yoshi if you want, just don't tell anyone. His exams are decent and he forgets gravity sometimes. Otherwise, you can get the grade you want.
The material was complicated and Yossi is all over the place.  He's the man though, he keeps it real.

Boring. Went to clas only to hand in Homework. He did offer multiple times to help students outside of the class. Class, however, was too god aweful boring to go to. He teaches right out of the book, examples and all. You have to teach yourself...

You have to learn it yourself- luckily it isn't to hard. Gave homework with 2-3 days notice and it was usually due on days we didn't have class! He is the absent minded professor- He forgot when the final was! Class is painful, he is annoying.
Yossi messed up a lot.  He knew what he was talking about, but he was very scatterbrained.  He posted incorrect hw solutions, he did problems wrong in class and his tests were very tricky.

Yossi could have been better. He posted hw solutions which were often incorrect and he consistently made mistakes when doing problems and then butchers us on exams when we do the same. He also managed to forget when our final was and didn't show.

A horrible man.  Little notice was given with homework and he made too many mistakes during class to count.  On top of this you are expected to learn everything on your own.  Very harsh when grading exams.
No Comments

His lecture style is completely incompatible with my way of learning. Very dry and hard to follow. Exams are very tough. Homework is hard. There was an extra credit opportunity that was very clutch. I skipped a lot of classes because you're better off reading from a textbook and watching Jeff Hanson.

Nice guy, not the best teacher. Lectures were dry and confusing. Exams were also difficult- the 3 exam averages were a 66, 80, and 64 (and there's no scaling). Luckily the HW and projects are heavily weighted, so do well on those and you should be fine. Also- watch Jeff Hanson videos. They're way better than lecture and makes the HW easy.

Professor Sun is a fairly lenient grader, just drawing a free body diagram can get you so much partial credit. However, his lectures can sometimes be a little confusing and feel disorganized. Very fair guy though and gives extra credit.
reviews.rating_tags: EXTRA CREDIT--Clear grading criteria--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Yubing Sun is my goat. His grading is so good. You could think you bombed a test but in reality, my goat and his TAs are ready to rescue you with an 80. One of his projects has the easiest extra credit option ever which gave you an entire 4% extra to your grade. For every Yubing Sun hater there is, there is always me, his top supporter and defender
He will make you fall asleep within the first 15 minutes of class.

Lectures were unhelpful and the work is incredibly difficult. He also schedules projects during midterms just to make your life more difficult it seems. Worst class I have taken at UMass which says a lot.
Bad teacher. Notes, solving processes for example problems, etc., are indiscernible. I have taught myself Statics by watching Jeff Hanson on YouTube.

He's nice but his teaching is so meh. Lectures are so disorganized and just plain boring. You're better off just learning from youtube. Exams don't seem that difficult when you're taking them, and then they take off as many points as possible.

Reading all these reviews made me super excited to have Professor Sun, but I was very disappointed. His class notes are very disorganized and not good at explaining. The exams weren't too hard, but they took off points where ever they could. The average on the first exam was a 51 with no curve at all. He does give a lot of extra resources though.

One of the better professors at UMass. Lectures could be boring. Exams were always fair with topics discussed in class. Homeworks weren't bad if you attended help sessions. A solid choice for statistics

Doesn't always do a great job explaining things in lecture. But has plenty of lecture videos to look back at. Always go to office hours for special problems. Test questions are easier than then connect problems so if you can do those you should pass just fine. I would recommend watching Jeff Hanson on YouTube to explain the concepts.

Professor Sun's class was very easy to understand conceptually he provided a clear cut diagram of the content that was going to be covered over the year. The homework's can sometimes prove difficult make use of offices hours they are super helpful in this class.

The class is pretty tough, the material is complicated and the projects are harshly graded. Professor Sun is a good professor, he has extra help sessions where he will help you and he communicates with the TA's so they can help you as well. Tough grader and the exams are difficult.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Test heavy--Tough grader

reviews.comment: Sun is the absolute GOAT. He is very smart and good at explaining. The homework is not terrible, the regular problems are essentially graded by completion and the special problems are never too difficult. He made a group homework session to work on it whilst he is there to ask questions. He is very forgiving about deadlines and granted extensions.

He is an amazing Professor. he hosts homework sessions for 2 hours and sometimes for 2 days week where you will have full access to him. He is very sweet and kind. Cares a lot out his students. If you put in the work you will do very well in his class. If you don't understand something he will keep helping you until you understand.

Great professor, really accommodating during the pandemic. Cares about students and wants you to do well. Tests aren't too hard. The projects are a pain and you can lose a ton of points for small mistakes, so be sure to triple check everything. His lectures are really well done, overall just a solid professor.
reviews.rating_tags: Accessible outside class--Skip class? You won't pass.--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: Pretty nice professor was really understanding during online classes. He expects lower grades on exams so don't be too discouraged when you don't get an A. I wouldn't mind having another class with him, but might not be a first choice. Homework could be quite difficult but the test questions were simpler most of the time.

Sun is a very smart man, not a great communicator though. Lots of blank faces in lectures and usually he only did examples of a concept, he never actually explained the concept. Online lectures from other professors helped but he was tough on grading. Lots of failures given out.
reviews.rating_tags: Accessible outside class--Skip class? You won't pass.--Group projects

reviews.comment: Sun is a good overall professor, he may be hard to understand in lecture but 1 on 1 he explains material well. Homework is very important in this class, exams are similar to hw, hw is hard and takes hours but you must understand it, additionally lots of extra credit is available which really boosted my grade, projects are also meant to get 100s.

Does not explain things well in lecture and then gives the most ridiculous homework. Invest in a chegg account or the homework is impossible. Very difficult class but there is plenty of partial credit on exams and extra credit opportunities so definitely make sure to take advantage of that. The only reason I did well was because of my TAs.
reviews.rating_tags: Test heavy--Beware of pop quizzes--EXTRA CREDIT

reviews.comment: Sun really wants to make sure that students are learning the material. I learn more from visiting his office hours than I do lecture. Dr Sun cares a lot; but the way he presents material is not the best. Pro tip: use chegg when stuck on hw and stop by his office hours when confused. He always helps and is patient while explaining examples
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Beware of pop quizzes--EXTRA CREDIT

reviews.comment: Lectures usually consist of a lesson on one or two new concepts and a few practice problems. They are kind of dull and confusing but he answers questions well. Homeworks are very difficult but helpful for tests because he will usually pull a question from the homework to put on the exam. He is a fair grader and will give as many points as he can.
He's a solid teacher who puts a lot of effort into making sure that students do well and understand the material. Exams are fair, and he is reasonable when it comes to grading.

A competent professor who, although not incredible at student communication, gives understandable and digitally accessible lectures along with homework that properly prepares you for the exams. Show up to class, do the homework (make sure you understand it), and you will have no problems.
reviews.rating_tags: Test heavy--Beware of pop quizzes--EXTRA CREDIT

reviews.comment: The instruction style often made concepts more confusing than necessary. Lectures felt abstract and key distinctions weren't clearly structured. Grading depended heavily on specific phrasing and alignment with the professor's framing. Feedback often stated answers were wrong without explaining why, making it difficult to improve.

Took Phil164, not Phil105. Poor guy is a phD student not a professor, and most bums in this class just wanted to get into Southwest through the RAP. I don't think he's a naturally great instructor by any means, but his class was easy to follow and an easy A. People have to cut him some slack, he's not THAT bad.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Lecture heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: A lot of people hate him because this class was a RAP, and they were more interested in building this class takes place in. He's not the best teacher, and I do agree that he isn't super clear, but he is understanding, and as long as you communicate with him. The assignments and class are passable as long as you write an essay with ok grammar.

Lectures are really unclear and hard to follow. He often makes topics more complicated than they need to be. Overall the class wasn't super hard it just wasn't enjoyable and I feel like I learned absolutely nothing.

Takes attendance 10x over the course of the semester, unclear lectures, hard to understand, very indirect with his takes on every question, very few assignments with mostly unclear feedback on papers.

Honestly so hard to follow along with and no one really knows what's going on in the class. I find myself not engaged quite frequently and when I do try to pay attention I just don't understand what is going on. And when you ask questions he doesn't do a very good job answering but then gets upset when we don't get in rather than trying to explain.

Worst and most unclear class I have taken at UMass. Nobody has a clue what is going on, and neither does the professor. The online textbook does not match the content we are learning in class, and the professor doesn't provide any explanation of what we are learning. He does not answer questions, and no one has a clue what grade they have so far.

This guy sucks, I don't think there's any other way to describe him. He is very unclear during his lectures, and even more so when you ask him to clarify. He makes simple topics overly complicated for no apparent reason, and his slideshows are impossible to review because they are so long, repetitive, and just make no sense overall.

Easily the worst professor I've ever had the displeasure of taking a class with. NOBODY knows what is going on in his class, and if an admin were to walk in I have no idea if they would be able to justify his position as a professor. The man looks lost standing up there, and I have no clue how he got the job in the first place. Take anyone else!

Mobile phones, laptops, and any other electronic devices is prohibited in the classroom. Also, be prepared for a solid amount of reading. 
The professor is a nice person though.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Lots of homework--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Such a wonderful and caring professor! Dr. Yang was able to mindfully address contemporary and historical issues while inspiring interest. She also frequently brought in guest speakers (like Ocean Vuong) and clearly valued class opinion. Graded by a few things (reading quizzes, one short paper, and final project). Books were also fun to read!

Only one mini paper on whichever reading you want, one group presentation, and one classroom participation question, and a final paper with creative option. This class was so interesting and fun, and very flexible. Professor Yang is informative, kind, and clearly cares about her students and teaching Asian American stories.

Mrs. Yang is an amazing professor at UMASS. If you ever decide to take a class that she teaches, you will see how passionate she gets with the topics she presents. She also truly cares for the students in her classes and want them to learn the material, not just memorize and forgot the information the next day/week/month.

Prof Yang is fantastic at what she does! She commands respect, but also makes sure you feel comfortable speaking up in class and creates a really welcoming class environment. There is a lot of reading and essay-writing involved but as long as you keep up with the work the class is a real joy to be a part of.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Get ready to read--Caring

reviews.comment: Prof. Yang is super sweet and wants everyone to pass this class. All the readings are on moodle so you aren't buying any books. Just do the readings because she does give the occasional pop quiz (Easy A on all of them tho). She has one rolling paper & one final paper, topics are very open so you can write about anything you want.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Skip class? You won't pass.--Beware of pop quizzes

reviews.comment: Professor Yang is incredibly intelligent and passionate about the subjects she teaches - she also can be very funny (in a dry type of way lol) and cares a lot about her students. If you go to class, participate and read - you'll be FINE. but seriously, read the books or you're going to fail - she gives random pop reading quizzes that can be tough
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Respected--Get ready to read

reviews.comment: She's a really cool person who is super passionate. However, she seems to be operating under the illusion that hers is the only class that her students are taking. Expect about 150-200 pages of reading on top of moodle posts or reading comprehension questions per class meeting. The papers are not bad for this class but the daily work is too much.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough Grader--Get ready to read--LOTS OF HOMEWORK

reviews.comment: This class was easy enough. Fair bit of reading and film watching as homework, but only 2 essays and 2 exams + the final. If you're good at literary analysis, this class will be fine for you. Totally not what I was expecting from the course description but ended up being okay and an easy A. Good choice for a gen-ed because it covers 2 requirements.
If you do the readings and watch the videos, you'll do great. It's interesting and an easy class.  Discussions have pop quizzes on readings so you have to go.

Workload is intense, class attendance is helpful, and having a passion for the subject helps out greatly. I do no recommend this class if you do not have an interest in the subject because the workload is intense and the lectures aren't very helpful. She's a very sweet woman but I did not learn much from her.

Caroline is sweet but lectures can be a little boring. She reads straight off the slides which she uploads to moodle. I would do the readings and watch the documentaries, but she does go over everything in detail in class and TA's go over everything in discussion as well. This class is easy, and not too much work
Interesting lectures. Especially enlightening class. Very straightforward.

She assigns readings and students are expected to attend class and discuss the material. Discussion matters, so reading is essential... the readings are also interesting and enjoyable. She'll lead discussions, and ask thought-provoking questions, it isn't too stressful because it's a small group. The assignments are straightforward.
one of the best gen eds
reviews.rating_tags: Caring--Graded by few things--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: I would say that he is an amazing professor. And sure, the content could be difficult at times. But other than that, his classes are easy to pass and very interesting. I recommend this class if anyone is looking to complete a gen ed or a major requirement.

Very boring class, but the professor was really caring and answered emails pretty quick. Music 100 is the best option if your trying to fulfill your Art requirement. Attendance was mandatory because we had in lecture writing we had to turn in at the end of every class. 3 easy essays that make up 45% of grade and in lecture quizzes.

Class was very easy but boring. Little homework, boring lectures, prof is a really nice guy, seems like he's putting effort into making the class more interesting. I just wish we did more modern music stuff instead of going over stuff from like the 1500s.
Not willing to help either gave not helpful lecture

No attendance , no hw , no exam. easy A, but graders can be difficult sometimes and the excersises are not very clear. she doenst really teach-- reads off slides (not useful). but good class if u want less work.

Super theoretical slides which didn't really apply to the group projects or class assignments and felt unrelated to the main course work yet held mandatory attendance. Also, wish we had spent more time and dived into group projects earlier instead of halfway through the semester which forced our group to scramble towards the end.
She's nice. TAs are awful.

She seems uninterested and reads off the slides. Lectures are typically very theoretical software engineering knowledge that won't be useful for us in a job. One of our homeworks was graded so unfairly that students are escalating it to the dean.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Group projects--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Very uninterested in teaching and clearly show she is forced to do it. Doesn't care if anyone listens or engages, just talks through slides to finish. Homework instructions are unclear, and she ignores past feedback. No homework solutions are provided. No concern for student success. If attendance weren't mandatory, no one would show up.

If Tim Richards is Michael Jordan, Juan Zhai is a middle school level junior varsity bench warmer.
There is a desperate need for a course restructuring, as the lessons are often found to be meaningless, with often clarity issues on a couple of assignments. Avoid taking the course unless you are entering with a group of people, or are feeling lucky.

Professor Juan can't teach, I did not learn anything from her lectures. Also, we spent weeks just on presentations instead of learning something valuable. The course is poorly organized and seriously need a lot more work.

Absolutely horrendous professor. Yells at student post lecture, horrible grading criteria, no medical exemptions given -- ever. Class had no directive, professor is confusing, unmotivated and driven by a clear disdain for students. Do not take.
Exams matched up with the HW assignments and Discussion sections. Allowed a cheat sheet too. Solid guy.
He taught us all we needed to know without going off topic. Solid professor.

Class was overall interesting. He is a great lecturer; however, the lectures sometimes have a lot of information. He does derivations in class and sometimes skips some steps; however, it is all to save time and steps that he has already done before in previous derivations or problems. It is a good idea to go through the textbook after class.

Prof. Zhao was great! Thermo at first felt intimidating, but he was very accessible, which was very helpful for understanding the material. He made use of class time very efficiently, and taught all that was needed. Exams were straightforward; he told us what to expect. Practice problems and homeworks were greatly helpful for exam preparation.

Lectures very quickly, leaves important info on the board briefly, skips important steps in example problems, and a few times, glossed over important things saying "Go watch a Youtube video if you don't understand." Regrades a lot of assignments to remove points. Project had vague guidelines and rubric wasn't posted until AFTER it was graded.

It's his first time teaching thermo but I think he did a great job getting us ready for exams.  He taught us everything we needed to know and he actually writes out important information on the board instead of blatantly telling us which I thought was helpful.
For exams regrades make sure to ask Professor Chao because he is generous in giving points back. Lectures were sometimes hard to follow but the example problems he put in the slides helped a lot.
The pace if this class felt fast at times but the professor taught us the material and got us ready for exams well.

Professor Chao is one of the nicest and most professional professors you will meet. In lecture he explains how to solve problems that could be directly on exams. He is also very approachable outside of class and will give you guidance. His exams are also very predictable as he tells us exactly what kind of questions will be on the exam.
He teaches from the textbook and is very friendly overall. However, his rubric is a little unclear but is quick to reply to messages and questions to clarify any issues.

Clark is a really nice and friendly guy but his exams are not. He gives a cheat sheet, which is nice, but make sure to get started on it way in advance. Include EVERYTHING. Be prepared for lots of calculus.
nice enough guy. terrible handwriting tho.

Professor Chen, although not the most engaging professor, covered the material in a decent manner. My main complaint is that he doesn't tend to respond to emails at times (granted he is busy), and is very sassy during office hours. He graded exams and the project leniently. What you know about that Purple Monkey Dishwasher beer?
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Lecture heavy--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Amazing professors. The class covers a lot of materials, but his lecture slides are very clear and comprehensible. The exams are nearly the same as practice exams (you still need to understand to do well). He is easygoing and wants everyone to do well. Professor Chen is giving Wei Fan vibe :)

Professor Chen is a super nice and approachable guy that really wants all his students to succeed. While not the best lecturer right now, I believe with time he will be a gem.

Very helpful 1 on 1, If I went to more office hours I would have Aced this course. Go to office hours!!!

Dope slides.

My favorite professor this semester.

He's a slow talker, and lectures were boring. Quizzes weren't too hard, but I found that I wasn't fully prepared for essays, and he graded them pretty hard. The class was fine, but I wouldn't take it again.
Very manageable workload. Take this class if you need to fulfill a gen ed and have a hard semester schedule.

Professor Young is great. Very knowledgeable and understanding. The class content is super interesting and you will learn a lot. There is quite a bit of reading but nothing unmanageable. Highly recommend this course.
Very manageable workload, plenty of reading but not all that much for a college course. Took his class on Capitalism and Latin America as well which I'd heavily recommend.

Prof. Young is legit. Super interesting lectures/readings, a wonderful intro to political economy grounded in LatAm history. If you are interested in social movements, a chill history class that's not alienated from reality, or just want to re-consider your relationship to capitalism/history/the world, this is the place.

He wants you to walk away from the class genuinely having historical knowledge that applies to our current lives. Great lectures and will meet with you during office hours to break down complex topics. Wants to see students succeed.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Amazing lectures --Gives good feedback

reviews.comment: Took US in Latin America (Hist 392E) in Spring '24. Knowledgeable but boring. Quizzes are reasonably easy but keeps you on your toes. Tough grader, especially with papers. Wouldn't recommend, there are plenty of other easier 300 level courses in UMass.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: Good lectures, very structured, knowledgeable and overall organized. Lecture heavy. Very specific standards in terms of writing style and format. Expects one correct answer on papers, quizzes etc. Leaves lots of feedback. Not super personable, but a kind person, lots of respect for him.

Professor Young treats his students well. Overall as I person I really enjoyed him. However the class itself you must do weekly readings, pay attention, tough grader on the essays and make sure you are prepared for the quizzes even though they are online. If your taking as gened there are probs easier ones but this one was interesting in itself.

Professor Young is a decent lecturer and most of the work in the class is pretty manageable if you get your work done and do the readings. There is tons of readings and Kevin is a harsh grader so this class will largely depend on your TA being good. Only take this if you love hearing about Cuba, communism, polisci, econ, and love to read.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Participation matters

reviews.comment: Took 220 and 390STA on Utopias and Dystopias, one of the best history professors here, especially on Latin America.
Cool guy. His lectures were interesting, a little biased towards one side. TA graded a lil hard but just show up to class.

Overall, not a bad class, just kind of "eh." The course content was interesting, but readings were incredibly long, and the often dry lectures kind of made them worse. Nonetheless, he was a good professor, but I don't think his style was really for me.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Gives good feedback--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: Based prof, solid course. Kevin keeps things pretty interesting and grades forgivingly. Econ and Latin American history knowledge helps but isn't necessary. Your grade is two short essays (20% and 25%), participation (20%), and a choice between four short open-book quizzes (35%) or a final exam (if you fail more than one quiz). Recommend!
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Do not take for gen-ed if you are not into history that much. 5 quizzes that have 6 questions each week take up 35 percent of your grade. Lectures were mandatory and so were discussions, participation matters in discussions or you don't get marked present. Really wish there was tutoring for this class.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment:
Would absolutely recommend. Prof. Young is an interesting and refreshing professor who really invests in his students and works with them towards their success.

Disclosure: Kevin was my Honors Thesis advisor and recommender for Grad Programs
very enthusiastic and obviously knowledgeable. Not many essays or projects but weekly heavy readings and about 5 quizzes throughout the semester
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Amazing lectures--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: I really love how well Professor Young knows his audience. He understands the dynamic of the classroom, and knows when to bring in guest lecturers when he believes having an alternative voice will help students digest material better. This was an incredibly interesting course - definitely recommend History 200.

Loved this class! Lectures are clear and interesting. He encourages students to participate and ask questions. Readings are long but interesting and easy to read. There is a midterm and a final exam, both are easy and he gives an extremely useful study guide. And two fairly easy essays. He gives a lot of feedback and is very approachable .

I have taken 3 classes in total with Professor Young and I can attest to his professionally and commitment. He expects you to come to class having read the assigned material, and to participate in discussions. However, if you choose to read the material, you will do well in this class.

Professor Young is relatively new to teaching and sometimes feels like he is reading a script when doing lectures. He also emphasizes class participation but is usually looking for specific replies, which make many students unwilling to answer. However, he is also very kind, clear, and open with his students and loves teaching the material.

Prof. Zhang is the GOAT. She took such good care of all the students. Her office hours were also helpful. The lectures are Heavy on content, but she tries to make it as fun as possible. Exams are closed book, so you have to study hard. But all the help she provides makes the class a breeze. Best Prof for me in Isenberg. Highly Recommend!!

Very sweet professor who genuinely wants you to succeed. Presents topics very clearly and keeps slides interesting and the class engaging. Exams are in person on paper but very fair, and group projects aren't too bad.

Professor Wei is genuinely the sweetest professor. She wants everyone to do well. Audit is a tough topic so lectures can be boring but she tries really hard to get us interested. 2 exams (MC&short answer). HW  (MC & can redo). Final group project but very low stakes & final project but also not too bad. Need to participate in class though!
Amazinnnnnnng

I didn't mind the actual content of this course, for the most part, it was more of how the class was taught and the assignments that made it hard. She doesn't take attendance, if you miss one class you will be completely lost and the end of the semester is PACKED with assignments that pile up on each other near finals, making it really stressful.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Skip class? You won't pass.--So many papers

reviews.comment: this class was a ton of work (especially the last few weeks) with lots of reading. I didn't read everything but it would definitely have helped for the take-home tests. Lectures are also super helpful because the readings are really dense but she does a really good job of breaking it all down. Also, you can find most of the readings online for free
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--So many papers

reviews.comment: I've tried to take theory twice before and dropped it both times because I hated it. Fareen keeps it interesting and the class isn't too difficult. There are 2 take home exams and a few smaller papers but none of them are too difficult. Discussion attendance is mandatory, lecture isn't, but if you don't do the readings, lecture really helps.

I thought theory was gonna be awful, but Professor Parvez actually makes the tough language very accessible and interesting (and actually somewhat easy?). I really enjoy this class and she's a great lecturer. 2 giant take-home exams, 2 smaller papers, and discussion section.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--SO MANY PAPERS--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: Professor Suetta's class was honestly really good. He always came prepared and explained things clearly, plus his feedback was actually helpful. There were also a lot of extra credit opportunities, which was nice. I learned a lot from this class and would definitely recommend it.
Extremely difficult grader. Grades assignments as if we're graduate level course. Rubric standard was unfair with the amount of work he wants wouldn't recommend.

Professor Suetta is an amazing professor! His class is super easy to follow, the assignments are very reasonable, and if you actually put in the effort, getting a good grade is totally doable. He also offers a lot of extra credit, which really helps. I 100% recommend taking his class!

Dr. Suetta has been the best professor I've taken here at UMass so far. You will need to put some effort in, but he spends a lot of class time making sure you are well prepared for the three major assignments. He makes an effort to know everyone's name and he loves to banter. 10/10 would recommend

This class was a complete waste of time, showed up like everyone else expecting a laidback gened class, was the complete opposite. In class writing graded on correctness not participation, some kid in my class who knew music said that he was grading him wrong on answers he knew were right. Not a 100 level grading system or class.

Great teacher, way too overqualified for a 100-level class. He knew what he was doing, but if you are not interested in the subject, the class is insufferable. He did not add any grades the whole year till the end, leaving me with a C- out of nowhere. Way too hard for a base-level class and a very tough grader, do not recommend him at all.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Participation matters--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: This class was a gen-ed class. Very easy and I do recommend taking it. However, Prof Setwart has the assumption that everyone in that class is fascinated by music and art, the same way he is. It made it very hard to enjoy the course. The TAs were great and they carried the entire class.
This is a pretty cool class, but the lectures can be boring. It is the easiest gen-ed of them all and only a few short assignments over the semester. Dr. Steward is chill and nice.
reviews.rating_tags: Clear grading criteria--Caring--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Talks at a pace in which almost anyone would catch on to. Tells you exactly whats gonna be on the exam. Only complaint was that exam question wording was almost a puzzle sometimes.

Made the second part far more interesting than the first. Although, repetitive, his style is definitely more effective to remember things. However, he can be very anecdotal at times.  He is very reasonable and tries to help you. I think he understands memorization is not easy, so he tries to make it less of that.
Cute guy who recorded his lectures.  Easy stuff...just basically memorization.  Very easy A

He is clear on the material and what the exam will require you to know. He emphasizes important points and where he sees a lot of students make mistakes in order for you to not make them. He breaks down the material better than Rotondi. Rotondi is really nice but he goes too fast. I do well with Heuck, but when Rotondi comes, its another story
He was fair, and clear. You really couldn't ask for a better prof. I like Rotondi, but he was not as clear as Heuck. I definitely did better when Alejandro took over.

He is soo much better than the other teacher who teaches the first half of the class. He has an accent, but he still is clear and would spend all the time necessary to make sure his students understand the topics. Offers extra credit OWLs, and 24-hour late grace periods on all OWLs too. Very Fair, tests are identical to practice exams. Awesome guy
awesome teacher really easy

Prof Yates is an amazing professor! You need to take him. He's so caring and understanding and so chill. It's the best class I've ever taken at umass, and he really get your thinking. Put in the work, and you will get so much back.

SOC course mandatory for Umass and this professor is clearly biased towards the far left. Generally felt disrespected for being too smart in this class and was marked down on essays for extremely frivolous reasons (like restating the prompt in the beginning of a long answer).  Consider a different professor for this mandatory course.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: This class was had a lot of reading with it but most of the time you just have to have the idea of what they mean. Not too heavy on homework besides the weekly writing assignment. Attendance is part of the grade and its good to participate. Overall nice teacher and interesting class.
He is very passionate about his work and the workload is very light.
Hes a very good professor, light work load

Yates is a great professor but is very passionate about the readings he gives for homework. Very discussion and reading heavy but the class is an easy A. The class itself was pretty boring but it was an easy class.

A lot of reading in this class that was lengthy and the majority of the time boring. Class was pretty boring but Prof is laid back and caring. He also always answered emails as soon as he could. He really cares about his profession. Very dedicated to learning everyone's names and helping whenever you needed it.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Skip class? You won't pass.--Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: awesome guy

Aadam is a great professor. He always stays behind after lectures to answer questions and wants to make sure everyone understands the content. He makes the class engaging and fun. Exams are a bit tough, and projects require time dedication. He explains really well and has frequent office hours for anyone who needs help. He's a great teacher!

Aadam is a great professor who truly cares about his students, always offers to explain more in depth, and makes lectures more fun by handing out candy, rubber ducks which all comes out of his own pocket which is very kind. I personally found the class a lot of work, but that was not his fault as he has to follow the universal CICS guidelines.

He is really nice and very engaging. He puts in the effort to teach and make the class fun. Attendance is mandatory for both lecture and lab. Class is very doable, just do all the projects, readings, quizzes and put in a little more effort on the exams and you will have a good grade.

Aadam is a great professor, and he is very helpful. No matter the issue he is willing to help and he genuinely cares about his students. He is also hilarious and makes learning fun and I looked forward to every class. 10/10 would recommend!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!

Really cares about his students and is always willing to stay and help people who are behind. The homework is very manageable, with weekly short textbook reading and ~biweekly projects that take a few hours to complete. He's also really kind and makes an effort to learn students' names, and also loves throwing candy to those who participate!

He's new but passionate. His slides are easy to understand and he is always happy to explain any concepts again. The class is fun and engaging. There are also some small rewards for participating in class activities.
Really makes sure a concept is learned in lecture and does an amazing job explaining subject matter. Also is very hilarious and makes class fun.

Really fantastic teacher, great mix of slides and vocal presentation. Concepts are clear and he's very good at answering questions and diminishing confusion. Always willing to go back over material that builds into the units at hand. Lectures aren't boring, he keeps things amusing and engaging.
reviews.rating_tags: Clear grading criteria--Gives good feedback--Online Savvy

reviews.comment: He is a very understanding and engaging instructor. He will always stay after the lecture to answer your questions.
hes teaching really easy
Very Engaging and good professor.

One of my favorite professors. Very knowledgeable and engaging and easy to talk to when I was confused. Seriously one of the best professors I have had here, and I am not an English major. Made me want to go to class. Work was sometimes a lot, but always doable and worth it. Never any pointless work.

Overall, a great professor. Truly cares about sparking meaningful conversations, engaging us with compelling literary concepts, and giving good feedback. The class was easy enough that you don't need to worry much about failure and come to appreciate writing from a new perspective-- especially since I went from a place of hating it to the start.

Professor Tillman is honestly one of my favorites, his class is easy to digest and understand. He feels like he truly cares for his students and does his best to create a vibrant and engaging environment. The course work was fairly easy and I was never stressed about an assignment, 10/10.

Professor Tillman's class was very enjoyable. Classes were laid back, and there wasn't an overload of work, as homework rarely took more than an hour. Despite this, he was still able to give good feedback on assignments and help students improve their writing. If you do the work, you should get a good grade an enjoy the class.

Everything about this prof is great. He structured the course well and gives plenty of feedback on essays and assignments. There's homework but it can be done in 15 mins or less - unless it's an essay. I never had to cram for this class, the workload is split up well. No stress class, easy A, seriously no complaints.

Professor Tillman is easily my favorite professor I've had so far. He makes assignments actually interesting and usually gives you some choices to pick from. Most of your grade is if you turned the assignment in on time so you should be fine as long as you are trying your best. Wish I could have him again for another class. Highly recommend!

Great teacher that truly cares about teaching students to become better writers and not just fulfilling the university’s English requirements. Conversations in class are always engaging and fun. Definitely recommend taking his class!!

Dr. Tillman is the best. I really enjoy his class, and it sucks that the semester's over soon. He really emphasized the revision process, which opened my eyes to a whole different world of writing. He is very reachable and happy to schedule office hours to help you through your essay writing process. His classes have a very positive energy too!
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Lots of homework--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Class is long and filled with basic boring slideshows but professor understands that and does his best to make it go smoothly. He just wants you to succeed and this section seems better than the ones taught by other professors as I have heard from friends.
Take him if you can!! Such a reasonable and interesting teacher. Tests were a bit unpredictable but he can be easily convinced to curve grades and give extensions etc.

Aaron is a great guy and I really enjoyed his class. Assignments vary from group projects to quizzes to papers, but you have a lot of time to complete assignments and grading requirements are very clear. There's an online midterm and final, and a final paper which is about 7-10 pages, which you have a lot of time to work on and get feedback on.

A three hour lecture is gonna be painful no matter what, but Aaron is a great prof if you have to take one. He cares about students and is great with extensions. There are a few quizzes/exams (all online) but nothing too bad. Final paper is 7-10 pages but it's doable because you do so many prep assignments and he gives good feedback. Aaron rocks!
Professor Aaron is such a nice guy. all the exams and papers were fair. Very generous with extensions. Take him for MGMT-260!

Aaron is such a great professor and despite being in a 3-hour long class, he made it worth it. Attendance is mandatory but you have two unexcused absences in case of emergencies. We have a couple of online quizzes/exams and one final paper that is about 7 pgs but he is SO generous when it comes to extensions. He is awesome & I would def recommend!

Class attendance is mandatory, so try not to take 3 hr class. He's a warm-hearted and kind professor that has pretty easy grading. He will spend time with you outside of class for help and understands students' situations well. I barely worked for this class outside of classroom, and exams were all open-notes and online.

Aaron is great. He is very knowledgeable in his field and puts together solid lectures. Quizzes every few weeks and a 7-10 page law paper due at the end, but it really isnt that bad. He has you do multiple drafts and gives good feedback early on. Try not to take the 3 hour class its really painful to sit through even tho Aaron is cool

This is Aaron's first sem teaching and he was great! Online quizzes based on reading every other week that were basically the only homework. Tests were also held online and open note. Lectures could be pretty dry but that's inevitable for three hour night classes. There's a big paper due at the end of the sem but it's doable and he preps you for it
reviews.rating_tags: Accessible outside class--Clear grading criteria--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: Very kind old man who's genuinely interested in what he assigns us to read. The books aren't the most interesting and the lectures can sometimes get boring, but you're really free regarding work, and I believe my writing skills have improved.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Clear grading criteria--Caring

reviews.comment: Ron is literally the worst. No doubt, the most boring teacher I've ever had, and on top of that he lost several of my papers and almost didn't give me credit for them when I pointed out his mistake. Nice guy, but literally the worst teacher. Avoid at all costs.

He was a very nice individual, however the way he lectured put many members of the class, myself included, asleep. Although he was extremely knowledgeable, his tone was very monotonous. The papers were relatively short and easy, but follow the instructions he gives down to the last detail. Don't miss more than three classes.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Skip class? You won't pass.

reviews.comment: Prof. Welburn is extremely kind and knowledgeable, he cares for his students immensely. However, the classes are extremely boring and he gives barely any guidelines for essays (250 words on average, so short). That said, he is an easy grader if you put in minimal work. He doesn't inspire the class and assigns novels that are barely discussed.

One of the most intelligent and caring professors I've ever had. He has background knowledge of everything, and if you find the subject (or literature) interesting, you will not get bored.  Anyone who is struggling can go into his office hours and he is more than glad to talk with you and help. Essays are to be expected for English classes.

The most boring class I have ever taken. There were student in the class who I'm sure enjoyed it because they were interested in the subject. If you aren't particularly interested, DO NOT take this class. Professor Welburn is a nice guy and very smart but he is just so so so boring. I read two of the required books and didn't even buy the others
Welburn knows EVERYTHING about EVERYTHING and he expects you too as well. He is the nicest professor I have had and a fairly easy grader. The class, however, is extremely boring.

I have taken multiple courses with Professor Welburn. He is a very kind man who genuinely cares about his students and how successful they are in his class. Sometimes he is a little unclear when describing assignments, but it usually isn't too difficult to figure out what he is looking for.

Welburn is such a nice guy, but he is unbearably boring. He is a very smart, very kind old man. He loves history and literature and can talk about them endlessly. His class is boring but the upside is that he's an easy grader and rarely assigns any work other than some light reading. I wish he was more exciting because he's so cute and nice.

I had Welburn for English Writing 112 during the first semester of my freshmen year. He did not explain the assignments at all. He told us about homework assignments the day of class it was due through email. He graded the essays harshly as the semester went on so put lots of time into them. Compared to other eng writ classes he was RIDICULOUS!!!!

DO NOT TAKE ENG 116!!!!If you are not an English major, you are doomed.  He tried to get us to write 3, 5 page papers for a 100-level final.  That's insane.. we complained but still made us write 10 pages.  The books are awful, the lectures are also awful.  Attendance is mandatory, if you miss 3 classes you fail.  DO NOT TAKE THIS COURSE!!!!

Professor Welburn is well versed in American Studies and is clearly passionate about that subject matter but the way the class is conducted leaves much to be desired. It's painfully dull, there's little class participation,  and for papers you develop your own thesis which is tough if you don't get the course material. (in terms of what he wants)

Good teacher - lectures can be boring as he goes off on stories, reciting unknown names and places... Papers assignments left a lot to the imagination - good for those who want to be creative. He's also very approachable
Ron is very educated and he shares his experiences with his students. There's like seven essays and a a dumb panel but its fun.

Ron is a good natured guy. Very insightful, has alot of experience, and will share it with you. Sometimes he can digress a bit in his discussions, but as long as you show an interest through your work and write well, you should be fine. Panels can be a bit of a pain, but I would recommend this Professor

ron does tend to go on, but he means well and wants to be helpful...it's a pain to do all sorts of essays, but that's what english classes are about. if you don't want to put any effort into this cass, then don't take it

Class is boreing boreing boreing. No class particepation required - which is partly why is is so dull. Essay questions are vague and you can get by without reading material. Prof goes off on tangents and hard to fallow. CLASS IS PAINFUL.
Great Professor, full of knowledge, and very helpful if you ask.
Good guy.**** load of work. I've had much worse classes than this one.

One of the worst teachers I have ever had. He was an **** with no vision. He graded papers on who he liked, not how well written they were. He offered little to no help at all and was one of the most boring people I know. His class made me want to hurt myself.
Incredibly nice and helpful

Classes are informative but more lecture- than discussion-based, which makes class rather dry sometimes.  However, he's a fair and generous grader.  Only three (eight page) papers throughout the course, and it's a 400-level Junior Year Writing req...a better professor for English majors than others.
Way too much needless writing. 7 Papers. That's a lot for a two-hundred level. He's nice, but i would seriously reccomended not taking a class with him
Class is pretty easy, he knows a lot of stuff, but prepare to sleep with your eyes open...

Did about 7 papers before the end of the course. The fact that I'm not the only one dissatisfied should make things evident. I learned more playing Gameboy in his class than I did in the course. Hey, if he could tell, at least he was nice enough to let me
Kinda dry, but what are you gonna do?  Really smart, knows more than any person ever needs too.

One of the worst/most boring professors I've had in all 4 years here.  If you're taking 116 for the Diversity requ., think twice.  I did more work for this 100 level english course than most of my other courses (and I'm a bio major).
Grades really easily (from what I've seen), but soooo boring.
nice guy, but boring as hell.
No Comments
B-O-R-I-N-G and grades harshly.

Aaron Gerding may be a little difficult to understand - however, he has always been helpful in emphasizing that he is there to help students and he will always go through examples to clarify even the smallest confusion.
Probably the most underrated professor on here. His lecture isn't the best, but not as bad as other people described. He wants his students to succeed, so come to his office hour, it's super helpful.
Aaron Gerding did not do his job well. He rarely prepared for class, and didn't get through the material we needed.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--TEST HEAVY--GRADED BY FEW THINGS

reviews.comment: Aaron Gerding is such a kind and caring professor. It's definitely a bit tough to hear him sometimes but he puts a lot of effort into the lectures and slides he presents. He definitely is a gem of a teacher if you come to his lectures and listen more closely. The grading scale is easy and he's very accessible.
reviews.rating_tags: ACCESSIBLE OUTSIDE CLASS--Tests? Not many--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: I would not recommend taking any class with Aaron Gerding. He is a very nice guy and seems to be extremely approachable but I haven't learned anything from him. For starters, he is very tough to understand. He also does not do any in class examples and only teaches from a power point presentation. He doesn't know how to teach the information.

Aaron doesn't have homework outside of WebAssign which can make learning difficult. He is a little hard to understand verbally, but his lectures are great with everything explained by 3D diagrams. He cares about students, and you should ask him for help. Calc 3 is an otherwise easy course if you have passed M132.
reviews.rating_tags: ACCESSIBLE OUTSIDE CLASS--GRADED BY FEW THINGS--Caring

reviews.comment: In class he reads off of slides and he assigns homework through webassign. The combination of webassign and his teaching gets the job done of teaching you the material. Very nice man, definitely shows interest in his students learning the material.

He is a very caring guy, but his message at the end of every class is desperately unclear. He really just reads off slides to a powerpoint and tries to explain equations with confusing diagrams, but hadn't done a single example until halfway through the semester and even still did very few in a class that NEEDS examples.
Great guy. Really willing to help you and is good at explaining and giving examples. Try sitting in the first two rows, because he's kinda quiet.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Get ready to read--Caring

reviews.comment: Prof Gerding is good at giving examples and explaining concepts. I'm a big fan of his Python notebooks. He's a bit hard to understand, but if you sit close to the front you'll hear him well, no problem. Linear Algebra isn't a hard class if you do all the homeworks. Exams are exactly like the homework problems. If you do all your work you'll be set.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--LOTS OF HOMEWORK--Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: Had him for Calc 3. Was genuinely a nice guy, but... dude can't teach for his life. I honestly did better in the course by not attending lectures, as it's nearly impossible to understand him. However he does post online notes that are far less confusing than his in-class teaching.
Speech impediment and shyness makes him hard to understand, be ready to sit in the first 2 rows.  Every class feels like you've missed the past month of classes.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--GRADED BY FEW THINGS

reviews.comment: Professor Gerding is a really nice guy. Sometimes, he can be a bit confusing when explaining material but he is always there for you whenever you need help. He cares a lot about his students and he is very considerate.

Professor Gerding has a speech impediment (among other things).  If you aren't a strong math student, avoid his section...His is by far in a way the least structured.  For the rest of us, this man is a dream.  He's interesting, brilliant, and enthusiastic.  I found myself going to office hours just for a chat =).  Nice guy.

i really didn't enjoy his class. I failed his class and i'm realizing that i really didn't learn anything in his class  even though i went to almost every class. i reccomend not taking a class with this guy, in my opinion he really sucks!

Yes, I would second that remark. The course can seem disorganized at times but that is just typical UMass, and relates to the fact that the course coordinators for almost all the sciences here are terrible and should be shot. Aaron does a very good job with what he has got, knows the material, can teach it, and does his best to do so.
Explains calculus so we can understand it. Really nice and honest guy. Always available to talk to.

He teaches slowly and goes over every concept thoroughly.  Students understanding the material may feel frustrated by this pace, but anyone having difficulty with the course will appreciate it.  He encourages students to ask questions and is available for extra help anytime.  Really nice guy.

Good. Little bit of disconect between course chair's section and our own at times, but this was true for all sections. Keep up! And since there are a zillion different sections, keep eye on chairperson as they often dictate the tone of the exams.
Makes the material very clear and simple, but goes through it very slowly. Expect to be behind other 233 classes.
No Comments
Slow as molasses. Spends most of the time rambling and doing review from Calc 1 and 2 which is all good until the department exams show up, then look-out! Definitely not a good instructor.
Aaron is an excellent teacher, who really devotes himself to his teaching. He is an extremely nice guy and very helpful. Great class, and with him it's as easy as Math can get...
Horrible, Horrible, Horrible, Horrible.  Sooooo slow. Easier to learn out of class than by going to his classes.  I've seriously considered going to another teacher and sitting in on his/her lecture
He is a graduate student. A little nervous at times, but he knows his stuff. Math 131 is just a tough course, but he prepares students well.

Professor Hellem is an awesome teacher and is incredibly passionate about his work.  He will do whatever necessary to make sure you understand his assignments and get any help you may need.  He starts really interesting discussions and truly believes there are no wrong answers.  Definitely take his class!
Aaron truly makes you want to push yourself as an existing writer or simply "give it a try" as a newbie! Such a great mentor!
great professor! only need to write four essay's the whole term and you can pick what you right about. he usually ends class early and is an easy grader!

Aaron is the man! He's a very interesting professor and makes you like to write.  I personally hate writing but I loved writing in his class.  Just have an open mind when writing because there are no more thesis papers.  Instead you write of experiences that illustrate a thought or idea you have. He's a real down to earth guy.

Aaron is the best! I personally hate writing essays but I love writing in his class.  No more thesis papers but personal papers that illustrate your point through a described experience.  I loved this class and he loves to talk about butternut squash and cooking.  He's a down to earth professor.
good guy class isnt boring like most english classes
Makes banjos out of butternut squash. Enough said.
Such a great teacher! He seems a little crazy at first but he totally grows on you. Very talkative and friendly. The work load isn't bad either. Take his class!
aaron is the man! best dude. crazy as a hoot but that might grow on you.
This guy is a great teacher! He is extremely helpful and funny. He is a little bit strange at first but it'll grow on you.
Makes a mean reduction sauce.

Aaron Hellem is the best writing professor there is. He writes fiction in his free time, plays the banjo, and smokes cigars. Four essays and daily reflective writings coupled with funny, interesting class conversations make for an awesome course. You will love this course from the first day to the last. Hellem is the best. You can't get better.
best writing class ever.  tells good stories.  and he actually cares about his students.  quirky guy who loves miles davis.  i wish the rest of my classes were like this.

At first he seems like an uptight guy, but he's very laidback and entertaining. The kinda guy you wanna get to know out of class. He tends to focus more about our individual progress in expressing ourselves rather than grammatical/rhetorical standpoints.

Probably one of the most fun classes I've ever had. You read, you show up, you discuss and that's every class. The stories are interesting and the discussions are almost always entertaining. Not exactly an easy grader, but he gives you enough freedom that you ought to get an A if you paid attention.
SO DREAMY.

Hellem ROCKS...you can write your essays about anything, we even wrote ours about drugs, and i hate writing and i suck at it and I got an A- in the class...hes very interesting, and yeah he smokes a pipe, hes pretty much the best teacher ever.

Hellem is the man, he comes to class everyday smoking a pipe and wearing his straw hat. He's young and is jsut a pretty kool guy in general. There are no tests, just take home essays and they are easy and you can do them on anything you want. He's an easy grader and a funny guy, you got him and you got yourself and easy A-

He will lie to you and say the class is easy. Don't believe him. He will lie and say attendance isn't mandatory. Don't believe him. He will take one class to explain to you how to use MATLAB, despite all of the homework being dependent on MATLAB. The final project he will go over once and basically tell you to figure it out. Save yourself the grief

At the start of the year, he said this class would be easy and attendance would not be mandatory. This is not the case. Bro made the homework dependent on the lectures he gave during class, which half the time you couldn't understand what he was saying during those lectures. For a 1 credit class, the amount of work is way more than it should be.

At the beginning of the semester he said that attendance was not mandatory, but than made in class assignments as the semester went on. There are 3 assignments one of them being a presentation on 6 research papers with little to no guide lines for all assignments. He than asked for criticism about the semester and refuted what everyone had to say.

Instructions were always so unclear. A homework that was supposedly very easy to do required an hour of time in outside research because most of the questions did not have answers on the slides. One class he "showed us" how to use MATLAB when all he did was write a bunch of stuff down and make us copy. He does not actually care about your learning.

Unclear instructions on every assignment. Lots of work for a one credit class (three mini projects, a full research paper, and a presentation). He wasn't a bad person, but I think he just wanted to get his grad credit over with, and made the class harder for no reason. My other classmates were also confused. You couldn't pay me to do this again

Took his biomedical signal processing class. Very unclear from the first class what we were learning. Never figured out what we were learning. We didn't learn anything. He would just stand and talk for 50 minutes. Homework had nothing to do with what we "learned". Instructions were never, ever clear. You also apparently need background with MATLAB.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Group projects--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Genuinely the nicest teacher I have had at umass. You can tell that she is very passionate about what she teaches and cares a lot about her students. Only thing you are graded on is participation and a few essays. She never came to class without a smile on her face which made the learning environment very nice.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Caring--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: I would 10/10 recommend taking a class with Chamini. Class was very easy and we only got 4 assignments throughout the semester (which you can ask for extensions on just by emailing her). She is very understanding and not a harsh grader at all. Participation is strongly encouraged.
Knows what she's talking about! Class participation matters.
One of the classes I looked forward to. Hands down the best class I've taken at UMass.
Great teacher!
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Amazing lectures --Gives good feedback

reviews.comment: Her class was a mix of western and eastern spirituality, but we spent more weeks learning about Hinduism and Buddhism. But she informed us of her intentions on the first week. I LOVED her classes. Gave the best lectures. She's the whole package. Participation matters. If you want to work on your own thing during the lectures, this is not for you.

Chamini's passion in spiritual literature was infectious. Her knowledge in the material was remarkable and she gave the best lectures. The class felt like a safe community where we had open conversations about life and how the content in the literature we read shed light into our own lives. One of the best professors I've come across at UMass.

Chamini is an incredibly caring and supportive instructor. Her feedback on my essays was very specific and helpful, and she is very easy to talk to. I enjoyed my discussion sessions with her, and I hope to take another class with her someday.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Gives good feedback--Caring

reviews.comment: She brought a lot of energy and enthusiasm into the discussions. Made me feel safe to share my thoughts. Respected everyone's ideas and didn't shut down any interpretations of the films. She encouraged us to dig into the historical background of the films which was interesting. Had great conversations in her class.

I liked how she started the discussions and how she entered into every topic. She gave wonderful introductions, made us feel safe to share ideas, and was respectful toward our comments, ideas on the text. The discussions were very smooth and spontaneous, I felt confident after every session. She is smart and caring, a rare combo. She's a treat!

She was very engaging in regards to the course material and class discussions. She provided thorough feedback for my essay assignments which helped me a lot to improve my writing skills. She spoke clearly and her explanations were very clear. I liked how she tried to keep everyone on track with her course. She was a wonderful teacher & good mentor.

She was extremely good at making students feel at ease with the work load. She also was extremely patient and made sure to try and include everybody in discussion. She had a really good knowledge of material which helped the class understand things they wouldn't otherwise understand.

I put forth an obscene amount of effort in this class, and I have years of experience, this class should have been a breeze. She gives a lot of work, and projects that are hard for people to do if you don't have access to children. Her grading was the worst. No matter how much effort, I was given mediocre grades, and told to check the syllabus.

reviews.comment: When asked questions says to refer to the syllabus like I havent already looked. Gave me a zero on extra credit because she didnt believe what I did counted. I met all requirements on projects and I still got a low grade. 28/50 could of been more detailed
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Skip class? You won't pass.--Test heavy

reviews.comment: This teacher was racist and unfair in a discussion where I shared my beliefs. She is unkind and uninspiring, hard pass.

In the future, another #metoo movement will come out. Except this time, it will be about how poorly Professor Abbott handles and grades assignments. Oh, you gave everything and met all the criteria? 75. Oh, you have a question about an assignment? Look at the syllabus you swine. Hopefully UMASS evaluates her the same way she grades us.

Terrible. Everything is refer to the syllabus, and grades given are not fair. She expects us to know everything and fails to remember that were learning still. Very rude while responding to emails, and directions are extremely unclear while posting assignments. If I could give 0/5 I would, just like her grading.

She expects you to already be a pro at what she is teaching you. When grading she doesn't understand that you are still learning as a educator. When asking question she will say look at syllabus and not help you and then when you do the project grade you so low.

Zehnder was always very clear on the expectations of this course, and they were easy to accomplish. She was a great lecturer and very fun to talk to as well. I hugely recommend her for anyone even slightly interested in the field of biology.
Professor is awesome. She is very organized and explains difficult topics in an easy to understand manner. Take her class!

She is organized and explains topics in a clear way. It is a bit easy if you took AP Bio, but you still learn some new stuff. Overall, very enjoyable course and she does not throw any curve balls on exams. If you stay on top of your work, you should be good!

Dr. Zehnder is great. BIO151 can be challenging if you haven't taken bio in a while, but she gives many chances to improve your grade, including a final that can replaces your lowest exam score. Her slides and lectures are clear, and many iClicker questions are very similar to exam questions. Overall, she's a great professor.

Dr. Zehnder is an amazing professor. She wants her students to succeed, and gives many resources to help you study for the exams. Make sure you use the readings, practice test, and iClicker questions to your advantage because getting the grade you want is very feasible.

so many opportunities to get your grade up, exams are mostly multiple choice questions from lecture, and open response questions from discussion hws. cares so much about her students. loved her so much taking a 9 am next sem just to have her again!

Very personable and good at explaining things, but this class might be too easy if you had a good AP Bio teacher in high school. Exams are pretty straightforward and in-class questions are very helpful for identifying gaps in knowledge.
Very nice, class was simple and informative, and at times she would let us out early.

reviews.comment: This class was amazing and very fun.
Good teacher but make sure to do the reading and homework. Nice person but it can be tough to talk to her because its a lecture hall.
