reviews.comment: Super intelligent, sweet, will take the time to explain difficult concepts to you. I'm a research assistant under her direction and I am so glad that I signed up. She is easy to talk to and I enjoyed my relationship with her, since it's more project oriented and personal. This lady is brilliant and if you take the time to talk, you'll be rewarded

Papers are most of your work, but they're only 800 words each which isn't bad at all. Two take home papers were both 3 800 word essays and then there's an inc lass final. The readings are all right but if you're not a reader you might find it difficult over all I'd give it a solid B

I thought she was great. The lectures can be tough to sit through because she doesn't use a lot of visual aid, but she is clear and helpful when discussing the readings. She's also clear about what she is looking for and what she expects on exams.

People are complaining about the readings. I actually didn't read a single thing really. Just skimmed before discussions and before papersexams. One of the best lecturers I have ever had when she is going. Sometimes though she goes off on tangents that want me to put a drill through my eyes though. Take home exams, I had an easy grader.

Toughest readings I have ever had, certainly not meant for a intro level course. Take home exams are as vague as possible and are extremely difficult. Has no idea that students have lives and that the last thing they want to do is get an essay assigned on Friday at 5 and have it due on Sunday.
She is a great professor, and her lecture slides are really helpful for her take home tests and for quizzes.  Its an easy class if you put some effort. I would  greatly recommend taking her class!!

Worst class I've ever taken.  The midterm was absurd and she assigns essays Friday night at 5 and there due sunday night at midnight.  If I could withdraw from this class I would in a heart beat but then I wouldn't be a full time student so I cant.  Whatever you do don't take PoliSci 111.

Class was interesting and not very difficult. Professor on the other hand sucks and has terrible communication skills with students. Doesn't believe in answering emails and phone calls are nonexistent. Hard to believe but the TAs were even worse. Discussion section did nothing to help the class.

Great Professor. Engaging, passionate, competent. Historical/thematic framework. Fantastic foundational course. Lots of reading/analysis. 3 short papers, 2 take home exams & 1 page cheat sheet permitted for final. Medium workload. Lecture slides won't be posted.

The lectures themselves are She doesn't engage the students (which is understandable in a large class), but the lectures can be painfully dull.  The readings are long and incredibly dense, and definitely not suitable for an intro level class. The class might be interesting if you already love the subject, but I would not recommend it as a gen ed.

I would definitely recommend this class for a gen ed. Her notes are really clear and all the tests are take home, except the final. There are some papers but they're short and really easy. Good class and reasonable amount of work for a gen ed. Definitely take this class.

I definitely would recommend this class. The reading was a bit challenging but she does her best to make sure you really understand the topics unlike most professors. The exams are take home and she gives you a lot of time to do it except for the final even but you get to have a page of notes. She made me interested in poli sci.
Huge amount of work for a gened. If you're really interested shes a great professor, if you're just looking to fulfill a requirement, go elsewhere

Easy class as long as you pay attention in class and take down the notes she shows on her slides. Her slides are not on moodle so you should show up to every lecture. She's always very clear. I didn't even buy the textbook.
Professor Ahmed loves what she teaches and she usually is very helpful in explaining the concepts of comparative politics. Overall I'd recommend her for any class.
Loved her! one of the greatest professors ive had so far! class was very interesting- i learned a lot!
Nice lady, ok class. There for help if you need it. Trys to forces her views on you esp. middle eastern b/c thats were shes from. Too focused on that region.
Amel's a very nice person, and it's clear that she wants her students to learn. However, her class wasn't something I looked forward to. She can be strict, and not entirely clear.
She's cool. Her lectures were clear, the readings were tough but sometimes really interesting, and they're not always necessary. If you enjoy this kind of stuff, it's awesome.

All around a good class. The readings can be difficult but are not critical to your learning. Take notes and go to discussion and you will be fine. Professor Ahmed is very helpful and friendly, as well as very knowledgeable.

This class is awful. The material is dogmatic and incredibly boring. The teacher makes you take an oath on the first day of class. I have not learned anything from this class, except for a few word "definitions". This class does not "compare" much. Fairly easy class, but incredibly boring and a waste of time for everyone involved.

She's a very good professor and very helpful. The readings are hard but you don't need to read all of them. There are 2 take home exams and one in class final. You get to use a cheat sheet so it's really easy to get an A. Go to the discussions and you'll do good.
I used to sleep in this class or just go to discussion and still passed it. Exams are easy.
Very good teacher knows a lot about the subjects 2 take home exams and a final not too hard go to discussions and class and you'll be fine.

Go to class and you'll do fine. She doesn't post her lectures on SPARK. Good at explaining concepts, is usually interesting to listen to, cares about her students and is open to anything anyone has to say during class. Two take home exams and a final.

This professor is extremely intelligent and really knows what she is talking about; that is evident in class. Her lectures are critical to understanding the material, and if you pay attention, you get a LOT out of the class. Very TA-orientated; readings are difficult but attempt them and you should be fine.

grading system is fair; 2 essays and a final. you dont really need to read until your starting to write your paper- and by then you can tell what your looking for b/c everyone posts the answers on SPARK. DONT TAKE IF YOUR A POLISCI MAJOR- you wont do well

She wants to help you.  Her lectures (which she does not post online) make the reading and material easy to understand.  However, the grading is hard because 60% comes from 3 exams (two take home and a final).  These are all graded by the TA and 70% of each exam is essay-based; the grading seems arbitrary.  A cheat sheet can be used on final

Hard material but worth it. Approached in a very theoretical way. She is a hard ass but sweet and cares about her students. Very knowledgeable and and eager and willing to pass this knowledge along to her students.
a lot of work, but worth the gen ed. 2 papers and a final- t.a.'s grade the papers and overall will change your grade a half letter grade if you show up

GREAT CLASS! I was not very interested in it, but have gotten the most from this class. Prof. extremely clear on content and talks in a manner that all can understand. Recommend going to class because it makes the readings 12 times easier. Keep the material for future classes!!

The only professor I've had in the Department that I didn't like. She was naive, seemingly unaware of anything that happened outside of the limited bounds of her class, and talked down to her students, all while making little to no sense with anything that came out of her mouth. Your time would be better spent watching paint dry.

Great teacher, great class. You have to work hard on the take home exams, but you will be very well prepared for further polisci classes. Go to class and take notes and you'll be fine, the readings are hard but she fully explains them in the lectures. These people saying its a hard class probably aren't attending..
The readings are VERY long and brutal. I think you'll learn a lot, but it's very abstract and the assignments are not easy.

EXCELLENT professor! Take ANY class she offers. Genuinely explains the topic without dragging on forever. Essays are directly related to course material & allows a 'cheatsheet' at the final exam. GREAT experience!!!
it's mandatory unless you know someone you can get the notes from. but she's goes slow enough that it is easy to write it all down
Very Interesting Topic, but approached in the hardest way possible. Not very clear. Extremely advanced readings for an intro level course.
Nice person; easy to get  along with

Professor Amhed provides a concrete introductive approach to comparative politics by throwing her students right into the hardest aspects of the subject. I found the course fascinating but I am also a political science major. The readings can be tedious and very time consuming but the lectures help digest the material.

Assigns long, graduate-level readings for a 100-level polisci class.  Essay prompts are extremely vague and frustrating - be prepared to be penalized if you approach an essay in a way she or the TA doesn't like.  Take American Politics instead.

Amel is a very knowledgable professor and knows her stuff, she also has a sense of humor. That being said, her grading system for 111 is a little out of whack, since there are only two essays, a final, and class attendance. Fairly complicated reading also. Worth taking.

Horrible class. Readings were long and very hard to understand. Very broad essay topic that were incomprehensible. Definitely not worth it for a Gen Ed, and speaking as a Pol-Sci Major, not worth it for an introductory level course either... take American Politics and World Politics instead.
Clear lectures; good discussion.

NOT WORTH TAKING FOR A GEN ED! Her class material is not meant for a 100 level course. The readings are ridiculous and extremely hard to understand. The TAs help a little but not enough. She gave little to no guidance for the essay. She needs to re-evaluate her teaching methods and shouldn't be teaching this course.

Taught a big, introductory level course with grad school level readings. That wouldn't have been bad, but she assigned these incredibly vague and frustrating essay topics based on the reading, which a majority of the class didn't completely understand anyway. Avoid this class as a gen ed, it's not worth it.
Loved the topic, relevant. Prof Ahern is an expert, a must take.  Students from different majors take, so great for different perceptions.
Wonderful professor Jack.  Learned so much in Green Urbanism.  The class was so great that I wanted to take it twice.  The course has really sunk in and influened my words and actions.
interesting, thought provoking

jack is the best professor in the department. he knows literally everything. the whole class was discussion based, so you have to do your reading, but he'll answer any questions and wander off topic to let the students control the discussion. only 2 papers, you can write about basically anything.
Good guy.  Knows his stuff.  Straightforward, won't pull a fast one on you in a test.
smart guy, very clear, helpful and interesting.

Jack is very passionate about the topics he teaches, and is quite knowledgable about them, but over complicates the topics and doesn't give anyone a clue as to how to do the final paper. His tests suck too.

he's helpful and a beautiful spirit. he is one among the trees, and the leaves, the land, and the earth. he recognizes spirit in all God's creatures and shares his love and passion for what Mother Earth kindly shares with us everyday. God Bless Jack Ahern
No Comments

Participation is 5% and Chris wants you to participate and actively engage a lot. Great professor, made hard and dry concept easy to understand and engaging. No study guides though, so make sure you pay attention in class and watch the posted videos.
Hard class, great professor. Explains things well and tries to keep material interesting.

The class is kind of boring but its not because he's boring its just that the material is really boring. Exams are kind of hard. Now that this class is an elective option I think 371 is a much better choice all around, and will probably be more useful if you're planning on being a CPA anyway.
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Clear grading criteria--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Best professor I have had at UMass. Makes the class fun, really teaches the material well, and is always coming up with applicable real-world scenarios. Exams are not easy but if you pay attention and practice the class problems you will do well. HW is optional but do it. Attendance is not taken but class is valuable.

LOVE this prof, so passionate about accounting & loves his students. grade based on 3 exams & 1 quiz + ~5% participation, no graded hw just problems that you should do (do them FR) not a boring lecturer, tells stories and makes fun examples that help you remember the material. he knows everyone's names and remembers things about you, very personal
Basically an advanced accounting222. Professor is decent. Would rather of taken a different account elective because material is dry

He knows what his talking about but lectures are very long reads directly from slides and doesn't explain much. The syllabus keeps changing doesn't follow it and the syllabus are very confusing the readings don't match the assignments. His TA also isn't very much help either

Great person, full of wisdom, and love when he's passionate; reminds me of Yoda a little bit. However Very, very confusing lecturer. School needs to provide him with a TA. Vague on assignment instructions, DOES NOT USE CANVAS, weird grader; and just is very disorganized. No criticisms against his character but not good class experience.

He has been very disorganized (hasn't posted grading criteria or guidelines with a paper due in 3 days) and I personally have a lot of trouble following his lectures. Unsure about how he is for grading because nothing has been graded yet. 10 page midterm paper and a final paper are each 30% of your grade, barely discussed them in class.

Agustin is one of my favorite professors I've ever had. I could see disorganization being an issue, but I found this class to be consistently eye-opening and engaging. If you are ever unclear, talk to him and he will be very helpful. This was a reading-heavy course, but honestly manageable, particularly if you engage and participate.

SOCIOL-335 Radical Movements. Unorganized; readings/due dates sometimes changed 1-2 days before class; unclear, confusing midterm & final prompts; class is lecture ONLY/group presentations for last few weeks; does not use canvas/moodle. It's a shame bc he's clearly an expert in his field. I wasn't able to pay attention bc of how the class was run.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Lecture heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Worst professor I have ever. had. Avoid at ALL COSTS. He is completely disorganized, and gave no structure for the course other than the very dense books he assigns. He has taken an interesting subject and destroyed it -- his lectures are long, rambling, and make absolutely no sense. If you want to waste your money and time, take this course.
He is not clear on expectations and you will have no idea what your grade is until after finals
Agustin is a nice guy, but the class is unorganized (he doesn't use Moodle).  Also, there are a bunch of required textbooks that you'll need to have read to write the Midterm paper and Final paper.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--SO MANY PAPERS--LECTURE HEAVY

reviews.comment: Agustin literally lectures the entire time. If you don't bring your laptop to class, you will be bored to tears.
reviews.rating_tags: GRADED BY FEW THINGS--GROUP PROJECTS--LECTURE HEAVY

reviews.comment: Love him, hes like the greatest ever.. just dont expect to get your grades any time soon.

The class consists of reading 5 books and writing 4 book reviews and a group presentation on the fifth book along with a take home midterm and take home final. He is unclear about deadlines and gives poor feedback on assignments.  DO NOT recommend!
reviews.rating_tags: Tough Grader--Get ready to read--SO MANY PAPERS

reviews.comment: Professor Agustin is just the greatest! He always come to class in great spirits and awesome outfits. He is very passionate about his work, which I appreciate. While I did well in the class, I did struggle at some points with the readings. Some of the books he assigns are a little dense and dry. There are book reviews and 2 take home exams!

I could see where some people who are not interested in this type of class would give it a bad rating. I found this course to be extremely interesting and challenging not in the coursework but about how I thought about past and current day issues. I recommend this class if you have an open mind and willing to learn something new.

Worst professor I have had in three years of attending UMASS. It'll feel like hes been talking for at least an hour after 10 minutes. He doesn't utilize moodle or any online program. Doesn't respond to emails, the syllabus might as well not exist because he changes the due dates on everything and you have no where to see the new dates. Awful.

I took this class to fulfill the last class for my sociology minor. A friend previously recommended the class to me (different professor), and man do I wish I had taken it with them. This guy is unorganized, and doesn't offer really many grade opportunities, so you never know how you're doing. He doesn't put assignment dates on the syllabus. Nope.

After taking this class, I lost all interest in getting my so minor. I am very interested in race relations and racism, but this professor would always give a long drawn out and highly repetitive explanation of the same things every class. During the last month of school, he decided to suddenly assign presentations & give a midterm and final paper.
worst class ever he is terribly  disorganized

He was really disorganized. He didn't follow the "syllabus" and went on and on in lecture. He would jump from social issue to another without a good transition or connection. It was just an awful class to sit in. He wasn't clear about what he wanted for assignments. Just avoid at all cost!!!
He is an AMAZING professor, i really enjoyed his class. He is very insightful and knows a great deal about what he is teaching! TAKE HIM!!

prof is insanely smart but doesn't realize not everyone in the class is a phd in sociology.  unclear.  DOES NOT COMMUNICATE WITH TA.  ask the ta a question, he tells you to ask the prof - ask the prof a question, he tells you to ask the ta.  doesn't care about the class at ALL!

Prof. lao-Montes is the kind of prof. that will atke  you to another level, your insight and understanding of  very difficult concepts will be  forever altered, in a good way.   He is not lazy, he just does notknow when to say "no, I can't"  so  he is somewhat overstretched.  He is working  with a lot  of people, profs, activists, grad and undegrad

He would come to class 15 late and leave 15 minutes early. Felt like to talked to the minority members of the class (it was race relations) and avoided the broader scope of the class. He talked about the same stuff over and over again.

Seems like a really interesting guy, very involved in local and campus activities. knows his subject, but doesn't really get into it. not a very exciting class. very repetitive but not a bad class overall.
One of the few UMass profs I felt was worth listening to. Would be great in a smaller classroom
I don't think I have ever encountered such a lazy professor in my 4 years of college.
SOOOOOOO BORING .... REALLY REALLY REALLY REALLY BORING

What I like about his is that he's not the traditional, boring academic we see in academia. He works with community and wants to know more about it. He is interested in people, not just paper and publications
No Comments

Makes everything way harder than it needs to be. Exam 1 is the 2nd hardest, 2 is the easiest, and 3 is literally impossible. Do good on the first 2 so you can fail the last one. Not a lot of empathy from him, and he can be very condescending.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Agha is amazing and doesn't deserve the negative comments he gets. He sets you up for success and tries to explain the material several different ways if people have trouble. I never had a complaint about him. As long as you study, you will do well on the exams, which are almost identical to the practice exams. Cannot recommend him more!

The first two exams were understandable, but the last one is awful. Do good on the first two so you can fail the last one. He was kinda mean to me and lacks empathy, but he is kinda funny. Do all the extra credit!!

I was scared to take Ali for OIM 301 after hearing Burch is way better but that was nonsense and I ended up liking the class more than my friends that took Burch. Everything you need to know for the exams and quizzes is on the lecture video clips. Halfway through I stopped going to lecture and the clips on 2x speed were perfect. Great explainer.

I personally did not like this class. The professor was very belittling when asking questions about the slides and homework. The packets given in class are helpful but I mostly depended on teaching myself and learning from taking quizzes and self assessments. Would recommend taking this class with a different professor if it's required.

Ali is a really caring professor with an interesting background. If you actually go to class, then you will be fine. The material really isn't that hard, but it can be a little time consuming to get it down. Practice exams are identical to tests & worth 60% of ur grade, HW is worth 40% and u get a few attempts. He sets you up for an A pretty well.
reviews.rating_tags: Clear grading criteria--Caring--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Agha comes off as intimidating at first, but after a few classes you realize he's a super genuine and caring guy. His character isn't the issue, it's the content of this class. The material is quite difficult, and the last 3 units of the course are incredibly hard. There are no answers online. If there's another professor for OIM 301, take them.

Prof Ali is a super nice guy. I definitely think that he explains things in a more complicated way than necessary, so you are going to have to do some work outside of class to understand everything. That being said, the class isn't difficult, you get a "cheat sheet" on exams, and exams are just like the practice exams that he gives you.

MGMT 670 (UWW) sucked my very soul out of my body, sent it to never-never land, from where it can never be recovered. 1) Beyond dry canned lectures 2) uses the longest, oldest ways of doing things in Excel 3) He could save his students so much grief by working/teaching how to work with Solver or Analyze, yet he chooses not to.

Ali is one of the best professors I've had, unfortunately they dont offer this class anymore due to low volume. The amount of knowledge and experience he has and shares with his students is far greater than any textbook could provide. I would recommend him to anyone. He will challenge you, but learning environment has ever benefitted me more.

Anyone who says this course is bad is a brick. I never paid attention in lecture, but it was helpful to go. It's relatively simple to teach yourself the material and if you put the work in you should do well. Tests are nearly identical to the practice exam PLUS you get a double-sided cheat sheet. Ali is also lowkey funny, he had some good stories.
reviews.rating_tags: EXTRA CREDIT--Lecture heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: His lectures are boring, but the paper handouts are necessary to do the quizzes. All the quizzes are on owl and there is no helpful feedback on the problems. You get 2 attempts on the quizzes. Exams are almost identical to the practice exams. There is extra credit in this class. I recommend taking this professor as a last resort.

Professor Ali is a great guy but man does he make this class hard. The material is not hard once you figure it out, but he makes it seem confusing. You will teach yourself everything in this class. Exams are 75% so you have to do good. You will spend HOURS on the quiz homeworks. Thank god its almost over. TA office hours were very helpful.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Very difficult class but great teacher. VERY intimidating at first but after the second class I started LOVING him and learning alot. Go to class, it's sad when fewer people start showing up and he gets disappointed. He will remember you if you sit in the front and he shares his brother's poetry in class. His stories are great & I'm gonna miss him

This is unquestionably the most difficult, least enjoyable class I have taken during my MBA program at UMass Amherst. Horrible grading structure where grade relies on quizzes. Huge range of material to read and study. I had a 3.9 GPA until this class, but can't see myself passing it because it is so difficult. Do not take it with this professor.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Lots of homework--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: He's nice and understanding but made the class/content more difficult and confusing than it had to be. It started off pretty easy but got really difficult towards the end. The final exam was really tough and dropped my grade a lot. Homework quizzes were only graded on a couple of questions, so getting one wrong significantly lowered your grade.

Lectures really are not worth going to until the end of the year. Class was relatively easy until the end, but the final was damn near impossible (Dropped my grade quite a bit). Homework quizzes every week, usually out of 5 questions so getting one wrong consistently will ruin your grade. Extra credit is available, but don't rely on it.

Professor Ali is great. He is extremely reasonable with exams (they are similar to practice exams), his slides have pretty much everything you need to know, and he offers good extra credit. Although some content can be dry, lectures are worth going to, and he often tells fun stories to make them more interesting.

I hate this class. I teach myself everything for hours to just get a fraction of a question wrong on a weekly quiz that impacts the final grade HEAVILY. Lectures are NONSENSE and professor does a confusing job of introducing topics. Nothing he says makes sense or seems relevant, only after hours and hours of teaching yourself will you get it!!
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Graded by few things--Tough grader

reviews.comment: Ali is a great teacher. He definitely knows what he is talking about. Lectures can be very boring however, and I struggle to stay awake. Everything is posted on blackboard. Weekly quizzes can be time consuming and practice exams are just like the real ones

Makes the criteria seem simple in the lectures but the questions are always far more complex on weekly quizzes that impact your grade heavily. Quizzes consists of few questions so getting one wrong drops your grade significantly. Very difficult class that you have to teach yourself pretty much the entire time. Slides don't even relate to homework.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Graded by few things--Test heavy

reviews.comment: Ridiculously difficult to come back from a couple bad grades considering 3 exams account for 75% of the final grade. Weekly quizzes are usually under 10 questions and pretty difficult, you get one wrong your score drops significantly. Don't bother going to lectures cause they take forever and he goes way too fast. Really just not a great teacher.

Lectures go on forever and what he is saying never seems to be relevant to the topic. Introduces new topics/formulas as if we already know them. Weekly quizzes are extremely difficult and always under 7 questions so your quiz grade goes down significantly if you get one wrong (still yet to get 100% on one). Exams are worth 75% of the final grade...

Attendance is not mandatory and lectures are dry and not worth going to. Weekly quizzes are difficult and take a few hours to complete while the slides provide minimal help. Exams are straight-forward and very similar to the quizzes.
reviews.rating_tags: Graded by few things--Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: Where to start? The fact there were only 8 of us in the class should have been a big enough clue to run. The lectures often end late and if you're lucky enough he will pick on you non-stop to answer questions in class. Weekly homeworks take HOURS. Have a question? Good luck! His help is minimal and your on your own. Avoid this class at all costs.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Skip class? You won't pass.--Tough grader

reviews.comment: One of the best professors I've ever had. Incredibly smart, with great stories, examples, and experiences. 410 is has some very complex material to grasp, but he does a great job of explaining things out and is very available for help.

Lecture is dry even though Ali does try to make it interesting. Most of the concepts are easy but it gets harder towards the end of the semester so it is a good idea to go to class. Two in class exams and a final. He gives a practice test that is almost identical. Weekly homework quizzes that aren't bad and a few extra credit opportunities.

The real MAN. As has been said, kind of like a James Bond-esque personality... cool, smooth, and smart as heck. You do need to pay attention in class because he does move quick and expect you to stay focused, but that's not such a bad deal. Really entertaining, and he's the department head for OIM, so a great connection to make.

This guy is the man. The indian James Bond. Suave, manly, and super hot. Love this guy SO much. I've had the opportunity and pleasure of having him twice.Highly recommended.. Funnier than any other professor I've ever had. Absolutely Brillitan

Dude is the man...First 2/3 of class are really easy..the last third is a little tricky. Do the practice exams before tests and youll do fine on the first 2, the third one you should do a bit more studying, i.e watch his videos and what not but guy is the man, attendance not required yet everyone goes because he is so entertaining. book not needed

Once in every 2 years he returns from the dark corners of the world to teach. One of the best professors in SOM , but its very very very rare to have him as your professor. Hes sports expensive suits , was a famous dj in India, and have a great sense of humor SOM needs more professors like him!!!

Prof. Agha's winsome personality and stylish aesthetic/teaching technique guarantees a full class eventhough attendance is not mandatory. Material requires a bit of dedication and may be dry at times, but Prof. Agha does his best to keep you entertained and thinking Socratically! Worth it...you'll laugh when he says "boohoo Billy Boy Gates"

Agha is the man! Attendance is not required, but the class was almost always full because he's entertaining.  If he feels you don't understand he will stop the class so you do.  Awesome class and professor
No Comments
He is hot.. funny...sexy.. stylish.. teaches with zeal and passion... so cool... LOVE his class
She always listened to the details of my ideas and gave excellent and enthusiastic feedback.
Just terrible..
Just awful
Very nice woman.  She gives clear instructions and positive, constructive feedback on written assignments.  These assignments are generally pretty simple, but she very rarely gives out As.
Great teacher! Very clear and concise about everything. She's a tough grader though so I wouldn't call this an easy A. But go to office hours and ask for help and you'll be fine!

Prof. Agrawal is the best professor I've had in the Math Dept. Made Math331 seem so interesting and relatively easy for the content it involves. The written HWs are the most stressful thing, but he helped with any problems or confusion I had with them. If you're looking for Math331, you can't go wrong with any of the profs, but this guy is the best

He made differential equations really fun and easy to learn. Lectures were asynchronous but he would always go through them, explain them thoroughly and clarify any confusion. Would highly recommend taking a class with him, hes a great math teacher.
One of the best in the Math department! MATH523H is a tough course but with people like him teaching, it becomes so enjoyable.

Analysis is a tough class, but he is a very good professor. Goes in detail in lecture and answers any questions and lets students participate so you get to actually think about what you are writing. For the sake of the future math students, I hope the department offers him a tenure-track position.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Accessible outside class--Skip class? You won't pass.

reviews.comment: Goat

Professor Agogo is awesome.  He is very funny and considerate.  You get what you put into the class.  If you show up to class and do all the homework thoroughly, you will learn a lot.  He also uses real life examples of how the material we learn is being applied in the real world.  Highly recommend

A very typical professor, not bad, not great. The lectures are kind of boring and not interactive, he goes really fast. He is very knowledgeable though and a real nice guy. Allows you to turn in things late if you need to which is great.

Prof. Agogo is pretty knowledgeable about the subject matter but he basically lectures at the class , instead of to the class. The material is extremely dense it might be helpful if students problem solved together-this way he could cover more material. Granted it would take more effort on his part but students would learn a lot more.

Prof Agogo's very knowledgeable & passionate about the course content. He consistently addresses students' questions w/ thorough & clear responses, but w/o students participating, some may find lects a bit dry. The assignments make it 1 of the most valuable classes I've ever taken at UMass. Definitely take 453 (Agogo & Hess are both great)

The content is hard, I'll give you that. He does a good job of sparking interest in the subject matter and I feel like I am learning stuff that will help me in my job. He is also nice and easy going with deadlines, which is great.

His lectures are basically optional. They aren't captivating or particularly helpful. Slides+textbook needed to pass. Tests aren't on quizlet, long open ended answers and grading pretty tough. No extra credit. I wouldn't have taken this if I had known how it'd be. He's nice but not very great an instructor. Good luck

David is not only a wonderful professor, but he is both understanding and kind of students needs. With some professors, it can feel like concerns are never heard or cared about. David truly wants students to understand the material and asks for feedback too, like how prepared we feel etc. He is a great professor and a kind, respectful person. :)
Supported cruelty towards animals.

she is dead behind the eyes and anyone who takes her class should beware of the fact she drills holes into her test subject monkies skulls on campus, and now is getting away with her tourture once again at university of wisconsin. make it known

Agnès seems incoherent at times. Boring lecturer. I do not recommend her class. I also discovered that she allows cruel experimenting on animals which is really not necessary for the world of psychology.

Very clear about what will be tested on exams, and lectures are easy to follow. Lots of opportunities for extra credit.

This professor is completely inaccessible outside of class and constantly changes around the syllabus including exam dates without warning. Exams are SUPER easy as long as you go over the notes and pay attention in class (multiple choice with a few short answers). Very accessible, wants students to succeed. Up to 8 SONA credits accepted.

Agnes is a great professor and offers so much extra credit! Also there are 5 exams and a final but one of the 5 exams can be dropped. She does clicker questions for attendance. If you have any concerns or questions she is enthusiastic to help!
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--GRADED BY FEW THINGS--EXTRA CREDIT

reviews.comment: Awesome lecturer! Clearly explained the material and was very nice!
She is great! Very knowledgeable and really wants to see her students learn. She is reasonable and the class is fair.
Great teacher. Challenging material but she has very fair exams, lots of extra credit opportunities, and is very patient with questions and being asked to repeat something.

Easy class if you study notes. Must attend lecture to get notes tho so come to class! Pay attention during class, she basically emphasizes what will be on the exam. Exams are pretty easy but there are A LOT of exams and 2 lowest scores are dropped. Also, heavy accent you'll have to get use to

I've had this professor for a couple of different classes... 320 is tough and is a requirement for a lot of students. She is super nice, and does her best to get you through it. She is AWESOME for the Animal Behavior/Cognition elective courses. This is what she researchers, and you can tell she knows her stuff. Makes a big effort to get to know you

Easy class and a really, really fair grader. You can tell the tests get progressively easier when people aren't doing well. Attendance is mandatory and the class is quite interesting. People in my class are doing either really well or really bad. I suspect the latter aren't putting in the effort. Recommended!
Easy grader. Super nice. Very Fair.

The material is definitely hard; the book was really dense.  She tried her best to teach, but attendance wasn't really mandatory.  Memorize the 10 or so pages of slides before each test and you're set for an A.  She wanted everyone to succeed and curved the grades.  Not the best professor, but Prof Mennella was 100x worse on all aspects!
Made changes to the tests and was receptive to student feedback when she realized most of the class was doing poorly. Also offered some extra credit. The subject is hard!
She seemed nice but she is hard to understand (accent) and the material is hard.  buy the book it really helped clarify things.
Nice woman, wants us to do well.  Tests are difficult and demand a lot of critical thinking, but they're doable. GO TO CLASS THOUGH!
No Comments

Prof. Dahl is more concerned with the advancement of his career than the teaching of his students. To his credit, he is evidently knowledgeable, but is a mediocre lecturer and grants his TAs too much flexibility/variation in their grading. My TA, as opposed to others, refused to help me with my essays beyond giving generic, unhelpful advice.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Participation matters--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: This class was supposed to be an easy gen ed credit, if you are not a poli sci major do not take this class I couldn't tell you one thing we learned. The essays are easy though and I lucked out my TA isn't to harsh of a grader. Attendance isn't mandatory but you have random in class discussions that count for a grade so you kind of have to go.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Lecture heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: The professor is very approachable and does a good job of engaging the students even though the class size is large. He's very knowledgable and seems to be genuinely passionate about what he teaches. Attendance is not technically mandatory, but he does give random graded discussion assignments that can't be made up so you should probably go.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: Professor Dahl cares about his students and is really knowledgeable. Lectures are boring. There are in class discussion assignments given at random times which is kinda like attendance but they are easy and you can kinda predict when he's gonna give them. A few essays but grading is really tough and they are most of your grade.

I never rate my professors here, but Adam Dahl is one of the best professors in the political science department and he should be given the credit he deserves. I absolutely loved this class. While it is reading-heavy, all of the readings are discussed at length in class in ways that are easy to understand. Assignments were easy and TA was great!

Professor Dahl presents the content of the course in a really interesting way, he seems genuinely passionate about the material, is unbiased about the content throughout the semester, and openly encourages discussion.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Adam was a good professor who was very knowledgable about politics. Lectures, while boring at times, were very informational and I learned a lot. He was always available to help and was glad to do it. He can give between 20-50 pages of reading a night, but all main ideas are touched upon in lecture. They were, however, very very tough graders.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: Prof Dahl is a great lecturer & is clearly passionate about politics. His lectures & discussions about black history & US systems were eye-opening. However, the material tends to get boring. The readings are lengthy & dry much of the time & his over-use of academic jargon can be hard to follow in lecture. Also is a tough grader w high expectations
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Participation matters

reviews.comment: Professor Dahl is one of the few professors who made me WANT to go to class. He's kind and genuine, and always available to answers questions or give feedback. The reading is manageable, and the lectures were solely based on readings (so do them!). My TA gave extensions when needed. This class was such an amazing experience, definitely recommend.

This class only has 5 grades: discussion participation, two papers, a midterm exam, and a final essay. All of these are graded by TA's, so if you get a bad TA you will have a tough time getting a good grade. His lectures are really interesting and help you to learn the material. Lots of reading though.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Amazing lectures --Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Professor Dahl is genuinely the best professor I have ever had. I am bummed his classes for next semester filled up. He made me love Poli Sci again, if you need faith in the PSCI department at UMass take prof Dahl.

He is so smart but also chill. My TA was down to earth and she helped me basically every week in office hours. I think he forgets we aren't smart as him, but I could tell he was just so passionate about the material. I learned so much about underrepresented people in political thought which was the opposite of my other white washed classes.
reviews.rating_tags: Amazing lectures --Gives good feedback--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: HE IS AWESOME!

He is the best prof in the department. His lectures were really engaging even when reading old or boring stuff he made it interesting. I think my TA was an undergrad and underprepared but he was also very nice. Cool guy.

He is really passionate and caring about what he teaches and the lectures aren't too bad. A few papers and 1 midterm exam but the grading is on the tougher side. If you go to the lectures and take good notes you will be fine
His recorded lectures were really engaging. Honestly Im actually pretty sad I didnt get to meet him in person!
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Amazing lectures--So many papers

reviews.comment: It was a remote class with prerecorded lectures so I didnt get to know him that well. Hes an amazing lecturer though and gives a lot of interesting historical context. reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Amazing lectures--So many papers

reviews.comment: Guy deeply cares about his classroom. He made an almost seamless transition to online learning last spring! Would recommend his class to anyone!
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Accessible outside class--Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: Adam really cares about his students and the subject that he teaches. You can just see how excited he is to teach! A lot of reading, but he explains it really well and clarifies points of confusion.

He's a great professor who cares about his students. Don't be afraid to reach out to him if you need any help or have any questions at all! The TA's are great and helpful as well. Homework is easy and doable. Weekly writing exercises are easy too. Honestly one of the best professors I've had at Umass so far.

Really amazing teacher. You can tell he cares about his students, and is passionate about what he teaches. Lectures can get boring especially at the end, but that has more to do with the material being teach
reviews.rating_tags: Respected--Accessible outside class--Get ready to read

reviews.comment: Lectures were a bit dry at times, but the class made me think. Always got a lot of feedback on my papers which was helpful. reviews.comment: Professor Dahl is the best theory professor I've had at UMass! I came into class as a student who hated any form of political theory but Professor Dahl changed that. Art230 is meant to be an intro photo class, but projects are too conceptual to teach anything meaningful about technique. The only assignments that relate to learning basics receive no feedback. Do not take for gen ed if you have another option. Not the hardest class but you could find an easier gen ed. Lectures are hard to follow and tests will basically make or break your grade. Also he doesn't allow you to see your grade until the very end when it's final.

This is a decent professor, probably average, but he offers a lot of extra purchases when teaching, and I can make reasonable inference that he is making profit from our purchases to the websites he appointed to.

I took this as a gen ed; my advisor told me that this would be a relatively easy class to get my gen ed out of the way. This was a lie. DON'T TAKE FOR GEN

Honestly he's not a bad option but if you could pick someone else do it. I spent all semester going to class and no one would pay attention, no one even bothers pretending to take notes anymore atp. reviews.comment: Professor is passionate but tests can be tricky. Attendance is mandatory and clickers are used. unstuckstudy helped with study prep, saving time. Overall, a manageable class if you engage with the material.

The first class I was in, I thought he was a great professor, and I was excited for the rest of the semester. That ended quickly. His lectures are long and boring, but takes attendance at the end so you have to attend. He's the type of professor that cannot break down complex concepts to help students understand. Every MC is a trick question.
the exams are very tricky with weird wording. The homework is strange as we had to do forums on topics that relate nothing to class topics. would not recommend taking him for bio280

He's a decent professor and is very passionate about this course, which makes lectures more engaging. Test questions are written weirdly but I didn't find them super confusing. Stay away from this class for evolution. Adam is a nice guy but his exams are very difficult because of the way he words questions. Very confusing. His slides are also all over the place and the homework questions are very unrelated to what we learn in class. I thought evolution would be an easier bio class but I struggled a lot in his class.

Adam is a nice guy who is passionate about what he teaches but has a very hard time being clear in his lectures which leads to confusion every lecture.

His exam questions can be described as riddles and extremely tricky and based on interpretation of words, to the point where even people with the right answer are confused.

Take a different class!

The iClicker questions and forum posts were very easy and free points. The tests, however, which made up 70% of the points, were poorly worded, very confusing, and contained many false dichotomies. Even the true/false weren't just simple yes or no questions! 
tl;dr If you want an easy gen ed and stress-free midterms/finals, skip this class.

His tests are awfully written with many trick questions. Some questions are not reviewed, just something he mentioned that one time in his lectures. his tests were hard due to trick questions, he's boring and i hated going to his class. he seems nice tho, really into bio. pay attention to slides (recording and slides are up on moodle)
He is so sweet seriously father figure. the grading criteria is easy as well, the exams not as much though

He is very kind and down-to-earth. His lectures are as clear as they can possibly be, and he gives you all the resources you need to be successful.

Lecture heavy, but he is passionate about the subject and answers clarifying questions. Attendance is graded. Good guy. 3 exams (2 midterms, 1 final). Exams are not too difficult. He posts the exams from the previous semester, and TA's hold review sessions to go over the answers. Relatively easy class if you attend lectures.

Amazing very passionate professor, loves to talk to you after class about different subjects of interest. Genuinely cares about his students and makes sure you understand the subject before moving on. Very lecture heavy so be prepared to take detailed notes which you need to do well on the exams. Made the subject of evolution extremely interesting.

Do not take evolution with Adam Porter he made such easy topics into one of the most complex things possible. The absolute worst class at UMass. He seemed nice at first but is very passive aggressive. Will ruin your GPA

He is not the best teacher as his lectures are disorganized but the material is easy and can be learned quickly. This class is very lecture heavy with many concepts being on the exams. Work is split into attendance, exams, and discussion posts. reviews.comment: His slides are so confusing. I regret taking this class already. He is making easy concepts so complex for no reason.

Homework is quick and simple is 30% of grade

and the rest is tests

Genuinely do not understand all the negative feedback on this professor! Professor Porter's lectures were interesting. I took his Evolutionary Biology gen ed last fall, which was interesting especially in the midst of the development of covid variants. Half of it is genuinely interesting and the other is a snooze fest. Porter is fun but that's hard to appreciate in a huge gen-ed. Not too much work and the tests are fair. Solid choice of a gen-ed coming from someone who hates science.

If you are looking for a bio class pick a different one. Porter's slides are all over the place and very confusing. He likes to go on tangents during lectures leaving the class confused. Make quizlets and pay attention in lecture, because there are no outside assignments besides the forums, and that material isn't on the exams.

Show up to class, participation graded based on iClickers. Tests are relatively hard... if you go to every lecture and do thorough review you should at least get a B on an exam. reviews.comment: DO NOT TAKE THIS CLASS! Just for insight, I got an A in Orgo 2 but couldn't even get a B+ in this class. He is a very caring man don't get me wrong, but his exams are a joke. Adam is a funny guy, but his exams are always rough. There are many questions he ends up dropping because he decides that they made no sense himself after the class takes the exam. I am an A, 3.9 student btw

Prof. Porter is a good guy, really funny and really passionate. I enjoyed going to class. Just pay attention and you'll do fine.

My favorite class so far. He is really enthusiastic about what he teaches. He takes time in class to answer everyone's questions and give everyone's view a fair shot. The tests can be a bit tricky with wording, but he lets you challenge that. He makes his office hours up to you to be as accessible as possible.
reviews.rating_tags: Accessible outside class--Skip class? You won't pass.--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: Personally, I was not a fine of his style of teaching. The lectures are monotone and have no organization to the "slides." His exams are filled with "trick questions" and confusing wording, which is proved by the fact that he accepts challenges to every exam for questions you disagree with (it doesn't always work). Wouldn't take him. Little grading

He throws examples, diagrams, and figures at you with little explanation of how it connects to or exemplifies what you're learning. His equivalent of powerpoint slides are incredibly confusing because the color of the text is changes without rhyme or reason. However, he is an incredibly kind instructor who is excited to answer all your questions.
He's a nice guy and the class is not bad at all. The tests are very straight-forward and the homework isn't ridiculous. Just do the online work and show up to class if you want a decent grade.
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Skip class? You won't pass.--Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: Porter definitely loves what he teaches. Class was relatively easy, tests were a bit more difficult but doable. Best part was there was no physical discussion/lab but an online discussion. Porter was pretty clear about the info teaching. Good gen ed class.
Adam porter is a a very sweet professor. Only issue is that he doesn't round up grades even if you're at a breaking point between letters and it really affects you. Good prof otherwise
Professor Porter is a nice guy, but this  was a really hard class because he makes the tests impossible. Would not recommend.

Awesome guy and a passionate teacher who really loves teaching his class. That one lecture you don't mind sitting through. If you ask him questions he will go through every step with you and you can tell he really wants to help. He gets so happy when people ask him questions.

Professor Porter is a great guy and a good professor. He's very passionate about what he's teaching and he makes the material really interesting. For a bio gen ed this class was so easy and interesting. Also there's no lab component, only online discussions every week and you're allowed to skip 2 of them. I would recommend this class.

Porter's a good guy, and clearly passionate about what he teaches. He's pretty engaging, and the lectures weren't that bad. He seems very accessible and willing to help. Bio 109 was a relatively easy course, though the tests tended to be harder than expected.

Dr. Porter is a decent teacher.  His class (Evolution Explained) was fairly easy.  He explains evolution more or less well, and tries to make class interesting through discussion. Many of his assignments seemed pointless and irrelevant, but easy nonetheless.I would recommend his class as a BS gen ed for non science majors.  BIO majors please avoid.

Porter was a nice guy. The class was okay, his section was more interesting than Normark's. We used iClickers and the book is slightly helpful. I suggest going to SI sessions they are extremely helpful. Over decent class.

I liked him a lot more than Normark. He really loves his material and always seemed to enjoy teaching it. His clicker questions are hard but you have to enter any answer on any question to get full credit for a class. The biggest downside is he isn't always clear when he's explaining things. He says um a LOT. I kept a tally and his record was 225.

He's just alright. Didn't like him as much as Normark. Difficult professor. Need to read the textbook before lecture of that week. GO TO SI. She will save your grade. Take this class with Holihan instead.

Teaches with Normark because of incompetence. How many idiots does it take to teach a bio 101 class? More than two apparently. Anyway, he's better than Normak so just be grateful while he's still around.

Porter's alright. I thought he did a pretty good job of actually explaining the material, but his PRS questions are often tricky and confusing. If you had Zane for 100, you'll be used to the logic-based (rather than fact-based) exam style.

He's super excited about what he teaches, but that isn't always helpful. He's superbly better than the prof I had for bio 100, but that also isn't saying much. His PRS questions are somewhat confusing and his tests are worded the same way. Lecture is mostly just some notes with a ton of PRS, that accounts for attendance. There's a quiz every friday

Lectures are extremely boring. At times, he seems almost too excited about what he is talking about given the material. Discussions are far more interesting. He gives out possible essay questions before each exam so if you study those it should help a lot.

This is defiantly the worst teacher I've ever had. I got a 4 on the ap bio test and aced bio 100. I had a 4.0 before i took this class. The test are unfair and there is no way to study for them because he pulls his questions out of no where.

not at all an affective teacher. speeaks around topics that he never explains well. prs questions are usually a waste of time. No teaching skills at all. I took AP in high school and even topics that I knew did not make sense after he explained them.

Ridiculous final. Normark actually tries very hard to explain to the best of his abilities through email and lecture. Even though people find him incomprehensible at times, he is much much better than Porter. When I asked Porter a question, the only thing he said was, "Follow the molecules and see what happens..."
Extremely poor lectures, and notes are very unorganized. Likes to catch students on wording instead of actual content. Avoid.

Really takes advantage of tenure. He doesn't care if you don't understand the material. The tests are worded in a really awful way and if he was just more clear about things, then maybe people would learn something. He says "um" too much when he lectures so it's hard to follow his entire point because it's so broken up. avoid the class if you can.

Makes simple material much more difficult to comprehend. Many mistakes in grading. Tests were extremely difficult and had questions and diagrams that were very different than the concepts done in class. Stay away and try Houlihan instead. The extra book in that class could not be as bad as this nightmare.
Great, helpful guy!

enjoy the time he is teaching, because his material is much easier than normark's (second half of the semester). exams are only difficult if you don't memorize pathways (he will give you multiple diagrams-LEARN THEM.) he gives a lot of PRS questions, doesn't aim to be tricky. overall, not a bad teacher.

He's a nice guy but the material is kind of confusing.  Sometimes he presents step-by-step processes backwards, which makes it even worse.  His tests are based on changing things in the pathways from class and how the affect specific responses.  I found Normark easier, but I know many people who preferred Porter.

Despite what other students might tell you, Porter is a great professor. He might stumble over what he's trying to say and it can take him a little while to get the point across, but he's very eager to help. The slides are beautiful! He gives little animations and everything which are extremely helpful. Just go to class and pay attention.

Nice guy, but not the most clear.  Definitely could have done a better job at explaining concepts.  Slides were not that clear.  I've had better, I've had worse.  If you have a bad grade, hold out for Normark, he does a better job explaining things during the second half of the semester.

Nice guy, but when he uses PRS in order to ask students some question about evolution, there is no clear cut answer to his questions. There were times that I felt that the right answers to some evolution questions were the answers answered by the majority of the class. He is bot a bad teacher, but i mos def seen better than him.

He is one of the easiest teachers ive had but he is also boring.  never uses the book and pretty much teaches you nothing unless you didn't take evo bio in highschool.  just have attend friday classes and have someone PRS click for you.

Prof. Porter is great. He is very organized, presents materially cleary and makes sure you are keeping up with him so you're never lost.  He really makes the material interesting.  He was great at putting up review materials and grades online right away, unlike other disorganized bio lecturers (Barlow Coleman is a notorious one.)

He'll test you on some difficult material (which might give you a headache during the exam), but was very helpful when it came to visualizing how biological systems work. I had him for half the semester and then Normark took over.
This professor excels at tormenting his students. He is the most mean and awful teacher ever. He doesn't help at all and he certainly tries to weed peaople out. Try to avoid taking class with him!

This prof. is wicked nice, very intelligent and helpful.  He isnt arrongant, and wants students to learn.  He gives ample opportunity during classes for students to participate, and enjoys their feedback.  Def. take his class if ur a bio. major, he is interested in teaching u if ur interested in learned. (what a combo!)

Don't listen to the other ratings.  Porter is incredibly intelligent and easy going.  He is not arrogant, he just knows his stuff.  You can challenge his exam questions, but u have to do it WELL (obviously).  You will enjoy this class if ur a determined bio. major. It is easy if u pay attention...also readings in classes are never really optional!!

AWFUL! the class was easy but it is obvious that he has no interest in teaching and he hates students.  lectures were hell and when i was there, i was never awake.  read the textbook and u should get a A
DO NOT TAKE BIO 101 WITH PORTER!!

He's SO ARROGANT! He only takes answers from people that are only EXACTLY what he wants. He's kind of confusing most of the time, and the tests are nothing like the practice exams! the practice exams are way easier. more than half of the exam material is from the book, too. and that usually covers like 5 chapters!!! try to take bio w/ someone else
very awful teacher, boring.. often either skipped questions or got confused and taught the lesson wrong. Normark is a little easier, but even more boring. Not many people go.

DONT TAKE THIS CLASS unless you take it with someone else. This prof is horrible, he is not helpful what-so-ever and when you go to his office hours he tells you that you shoudl memorize every word of the notes till you can take plain paper and write them out yourself. If  his goal is to torment his students and make them miserable, his succeeds!

Adam Porter is the worst bio professor at umass. He repeats "can i roll" 100 times a class, the attendence to his class dwindles to about 50-75 people out off 300 after 2 days.  His quizes are hard and they give you no breaks on grading them and he has the most annoying voice. DO NOT TAKE THIS CLASS

He seems like he hates teaching more than anything in life and he has no interest in making sure you understand things clearly. Also, he spends tons of time on the stupidest things, and no time on the hard things.
He is an ok prof. he likes catching people on subtle things. very unapproachable. he is definatley too hard for a 100 level course. the other guy Normark is very monotone but definatley easier.
No Comments
Not a bad teacher, but impossible to approach for help.  His tests are hard and he likes to catch you on little things.  Definitely trying to weed people out...

not a good teacher has a way of not seeing raised hands thinks he's clever when he does advertising tricks reguarding percentages this confused many people NOT CONCISE often interchanged terms which were for seperate bio structures seemed snotty too
Taught well, made exams much too hard for a 100 level course.
He's great...does a great job of explaining tough concepts...though he relies to heavily on his computer and gets very flustered when it isn't working right

Class was prety hard because i suck at BIO. Tests were not that difficult but i managed to screw up anyways. Guy is very concise, tries his best to explain difficult concepts with animations(which are really helpful).The other guy,Normark sucks
No Comments

I'm not an English major so balancing 8 plays with my other courses was a lot. Lectures were good. He does not use Canvas so you won't know your official grade unless you calculate it yourself.

The TA's are awesome. Overall fine class

He is an amazing guy with so much knowledge on Shakespeare and the connections. In class, he is hilarious and makes the time so entertaining by blending the text and language he uses excellently. As long as you read the plays and ask questions in lecture, you'll get an A. Honestly, top five teachers I've had in my career.

Prof Zucker is hilarious and makes lectures fun. 3 papers, 2 exams and participation in discussion section with your TA make up your grade. Heavy amounts of reading and test questions can be a little obscure at times but papers are generally easy to pass on. Good class to take P/F.

I truly did get so much out of Professor Zuckers Shakespeare class, he's amazing! However, this was one of the most demanding classes I have ever taken. The amount of reading each week is almost impossible, and the exams are also pretty hard. I did very well in this class but I also studied for 8 hours a day for each exam. Be aware of this!
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Inspirational--Lots of homework

reviews.comment: Prof Zucker is so funny and extremely passionate. I loved going to his lectures; the papers and exams were pretty straightforward. There is a lot of reading, but he picks very interesting plays, so that was fun.  The TA's were kind and understanding. There are two exams and two papers, one smaller paper, and reading reflections.
His lectures are very engaging, despite it being difficult to make the topic of Shakespeare fun and interesting. He somehow makes Shakespeare funny.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Hilarious--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Lectures were fun, he's a good professor. Clearly extremely passionate about Shakespeare, makes it interesting for people who normally wouldn't be fans of him. I never really read the books and I still did pretty well. Just go to class/discussion. Do extra credit to boost your grade, probably would've taken me from A- to an A.

Adam Zucker is an incredible professor. He is extremely passionate about his material and loves nothing more than to engage in conversation. He is hilarious and I honestly loved his class. It was a lot of reading but nothing unmanageable. He made grading very straight forward and he wanted everyone to succeed. 100% would take another class of his.

Prof. Zucker was amazing! He is an incredibly engaging lecturer. The reading load might seem like a lot for new students, but you get used to it after the first month. He always wants to help students succeed and is wonderful to talk to!

Zucker's lectures were always very engaging and informative and I always enjoyed them. He prefers no electronics  in class unless you talk to him about needing one, so if you have a strong preference for taking notes on computer you might want to consider that. Don't let that dissuade you though, I absolutely loved taking the class
Funny, accessible, passionate, easy to listen to.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Hilarious--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Adam Zucker is hilarious and the only professor I'd want to take Eng221 with again. His TAs are great and he's easily-reached outside of them. You can tell he genuinely, wholeheartedly cares about what he's teaching. You're mostly graded on a few papers, so be aware you have to do well on those to pass.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Hilarious--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Funny, knowledgable, interesting. Difficult if you struggle with fast-paced readings but I found the analysis incredibly insightful and genuinely I use the information I learned in this class often. My TA (Cam Cocking) was also incredibly insightful, understanding and helpful. If you are an English major take this class!!!

The professor is great and really challenges the mind to understand the work that is being read. However the workload is INSANE. I took English 221 and we had to read 8 Shakespeare plays, weekly reading responses, three 5-page essays along with a midterm and final. The midterm and final are also impossible to study.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Amazing lectures --Lots of homework

reviews.comment: Professor Zucker is great. Clearly very passionate about his work, lectures are energetic and engaging, essays are manageable and - dare I say - fun. Read/ watch the plays (because they're masterpieces) and attend lectures (because they're awesome), and you'll get a lot out of this class.
A good dude

reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Participation matters

reviews.comment: Hilarious, thoughtful, and understanding. You'll be interacting with your discussion leaders/TAs more than him, but his lectures are clear and interesting. Communicates everything that you'll be graded on, cares more about content than the smaller details. Doesn't like computers or phones in class.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Amazing lectures --Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: He was one of the best professors I have ever had. As someone who is not an English major, he made me love the subject. I was always excited about his lectures. If you need a Lit gen ed, TAKE HIM.

Read the assigned texts and attend or watch all lectures and this class will be a breeze and a blast. Prof. Zucker's lectures are a delight to be in, he's clearly excited about what he's teaching and is working with students, not against them. Couldn't recommend this class more!
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Amazing lectures --Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Professor Zucker is a wonderful lecturer who encourages in-depth thinking about the writing of Shakespeare. Discussions never feel tired or dull the way one may expect a Shakespeare course to be. He is hilarious and engaging. one piece of advice ATTENDANCE MATTERS. If you don't take notes, all hope will be lost.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Hilarious--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Very cool and engaging professor, he knows so much about Shakespeare and makes it so interesting (coming from someone who used to hate Shakespeare). TAs do most of the grading in the class so depends on who you have for grading. Assignments are nicely spread out & clearly explained, good to read, but only tests you on what is gone over in class.

I'm currently in Professor Zucker's Eng 201 class, Early British Literature. One of my favorite classes I've ever taken, he's very knowledgeable on his material and runs an incredibly engrossing classroom. The only real problem I have with the course is the sparsity of graded assignments, as I prefer to have more than a few graded assignments.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Hilarious--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Professor Zucker is great. He is passionate about what he is teaching. Attendance not mandatory but he encourages you to come. Physical books and notebooks are recommended as he does not like computers in class. He has a wonderful humor and chooses really interesting Shakespeare works across different genres. A lot of reading but an amazing course.

I took Professor Zucker's Intro to Shakespeare and I absolutely loved it. He's so passionate and you can really see that he cares. We read 8 plays and as long as you read, you'll do great. Attendance was only recorded for the discussion sections once a week. I had Dina as my TA and she was amazing. Def go to lectures even though its not mandatory.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Clear grading criteria--Hilarious

reviews.comment: SO SWEET. So interesting. Not allowed to use technology in class but makes lectures interesting. It is an english class so the textbooks are books and you have to read to keep up. Tests are all based on stuff from lecture so you have to go to do well. Tests are straight forward and Ta's are really nice about grading.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Skip class? You won't pass.--Inspirational

reviews.comment: Professor Zucker is AWESOME. He is so passionate about what he teaches, so it makes the class even more enjoyable than it already is. Zucker is very educated in his field, and makes reading / learning Shakespeare so intriguing and easy(ish). This class helped me decide to declare my major as English!

Professor Zucker is a GEM. He is hilarious, extremely passionate and an overall wonderful teacher. I already loved Shakespeare, but after taking his class I love his works 100% more. Zucker is also VERY fair and gives great feedback. You will also never regret going to his office hours - he's very helpful and very caring.

Professor Zucker made this English class one of the best I've ever had. He's incredibly funny, approachable, and knowledgeable of his material. I would highly recommend taking ANY course taught by him. There's a decent amount of reading, but if there's one man who can make The Faerie Queene and Paradise Lost fun, it's this guy.

Professor Zucker is very knowledgeable about the content of the course and gives great lectures that supplement the reading very well. The tests are entirely based on the lecture, and outside reading. Two papers, two exams, and participation in the discussion make up your grade. A great choice if you're interested in Shakespeare.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Skip class? You won't pass.--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: Adam Zucker is very insightful and stimulates levels of complex thought that make students more interested with the texts! He is also a super cool guy! I took his Shakespeare class, and we covered a lot of plays, but he did a very good job at simplifying the class enough, but also covering a lot of material and themes. Just go to class & read!

He's incredibly intelligent and does his best to engage students with the subject material. His lectures are interesting, well thought out, and always help you understand the material better. No one ever has anything bad to say about Professor Zucker. He's caring, friendly, and hilarious. Take his classes. Lots of reading but doable.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Clear grading criteria--Hilarious

reviews.comment: I absolutely loved English 201 with Adam Zucker. He made reading old english fun and knows so much about his material. He loves what he does and engages the class to appreciate it too. I am definitely taking another class with him again and would highly recommend his class to anybody seriously interested in English as their major.

One of my favorite professors at UMass! Sincerely wants every student to succeed. Willing to meet with you to help with anything, class related or otherwise. Helped me to understand British Lit and poetry. Awesome professor! Take any class with him.

This man changed my life and the way I read and write. The voice inside my head that babbles on as I scribble away lines of poetry is now and forever will be his. Tis' a silly thing but I do find myself asking WWAZD every time I sit down to write a paper or a read a bit of Shakespearian verse.

Professor Zucker is amazing. He is INSANELY intelligent and passionate. His lectures are really fun because he loves interacting with his students, he's incredibly funny, and you will learn A LOT. Take any class he teaches.

Great professor, great guy. Funny, interesting, knows how to keep your attention and make the lectures worthwhile. Very smart and creative, knows a lot about Shakespeare. Graduating as a UMass English major without taking a class with him would be a tragedy.

Zucker is HILARIOUS and has pretty awesome hair. He's by far one of the best professors on campus. He almost makes Shakespeare enjoyable, and that's pretty difficult. Your grade really depends on the TA you get, but I've gotten an A on everything so far and have not read a single play. You just need to pay attention and take good notes.

Hands down the best professor on campus. While Shakespeare is a think and often times dull subject, Professor Zucker makes class more than interesting. He clearly loves what he does and it is represented in how well he teaches. Funny, witty, and an overall joy to have as a teacher.

All time favorite professor, not just within the english department.  Class goes by so fast and I never wanted it to end.  Zucker is hilarious without trying and brilliant in his subject matter. Even if you dread Shakespeare, you will enjoy this class.

Amazing professor. Makes class fly by with his wit, and self deprecating humor. He isn't an easy teacher, but he is very fair, and has extremely flexible office hours. He wants students to learn and he will grade higher if he sees improvement in work regardless of overall quality. His hair is also amazing, and he openly makes fun of it for laughs. Highly recommend him!

Class flies by because this guy is hilarious. You cover a lot of material though, so don't be fooled by how funny he is- it's not exactly an easy class. Since it's required for the major, he makes the class wonderful. As for a gen ed, I wouldn't really recommend it

Zucker is just plain wonderful! He's funny, straightforward, respects everyone's opinions, and is obviously very intelligent. He's definitely my favorite professor in the English department and actually got me interested in poetry. And as an added bonus...he's gorgeous. Take his class!
Sort of reminds me of Pierre LaRouche, the way he can deftly evade sticky points while roofing his delivery to make every one understand his goal.
Zucker's a really smart and interesting guy.  He's definitely a true wit.
FANTASTIC prof.!  Keeps the interest in the subject going no matter how much it might drag by itself --- Definitely, the hippest teacher at UMass, by far!
Great professor...could seriously do standup if he ever decided to give up teaching.  Very smart, very cool, and yes, a  hottie!  More Zucker, please.
This man made me appreciate Shakespeare.  His lectures are fun,loose and usually interesting.  Plus he looks a bit like Willy Wonka.

Zucker is so cute! Really nice, fun, quirky teacher. Thanks to Zucker I have a new appreciation of geese. I must admit though the classes did drag at times, but I dislike Brit. Lit. I recommend this class if you are taking it as a requirement, but if you really want to be challenged, you might be a little frustrated.

Zucker!!  What a hottie, I loved his class...he makes it so entertaining because he is so funny.  Real cool guy, dresses well and is a fair grader.  His classes were boring at first but then I realized how awesome he is.  TAKE THIS CLASS...

Zucker is too cool for school.  He is tough to please, but I learned a TON in his class.  He loves his subject and seems like he loves to teach.
