People may complain about him, but unlike so many professors here he actually cares whether or not people LEARN.  UMass would be a better place if there were more profs like him.  Oh, and he's a hottie!
No Comments
Anticipates that students won't enjoy the material or say anything meaningful about it- a self-fulfilling prophesy.

Not as good as I had hoped after reading such glorious recommendations. Boring class, annoyingly arrogant teaching style, not much help outside the class, tough grader. Disappointing. On the bright side, he has great hair.
great teacher who loves the material.  enjoyable class!

Adam was awesome and he got me to respect and engage with another time period.  A time period in which I knew existed but never had any interest in studying it.  Adam is awesome and highly recommend taking any class that he teaches.

Prof. Zucker is a great guy who makes the difficult material clear and tries to create interest in a sometimes dry subject. He is very helpful, providing extensive feedback on papers and tests, etc. His sense of humor is sweet and he truly wants to help students learn.
good sense of humor!

adam is funny, clever, gives great lectures, kind, gives excellent feedback on papers, and has the largest collection of shoes for any male i've ever met.  i sat in the front row, so that's all i look at.  his shoes.

This is for her 317 class not 335. Overall a nice and understanding professor, however, she never gave clear instructions or rubrics for assignments. When she did give instructions it was always extremely vague. Syllabus was also pretty much useless because the course didn't even follow it. She also cold calls a lot.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: I love PH441. Class is super informative and Sasha genuinely cares about their students (offers make up class every week, is helping NINE honors students with independent studies this semester) and takes feedback---they made multiple changes to the course per our requests. If you're confused about grading, assignments, requirements just ask them!

PH441 is one of the best classes I have taken. Sasha is so well spoken + knowledgeable. This class is simply inherently political. Environmental justice is not a red winged ideology. Not our prof's fault that the president doesn't believe in the topic (ie. planned EPA budget cuts). Why are you taking the class if you don't agree with these views.

This class felt extremely biased and politically driven. The professor often pushed her own beliefs and dismissed credible sources that didn't align with her views. It was hard to participate or share opinions without feeling judged. The environment felt tense, unwelcoming, and academically unreliable. Super easy class though.

Sasha is great, and I love taking classes with them. If you're interested in the environment, social, and political public health, I would suggest taking any of their courses.  A lot of the class is repetitive, taking notes is very helpful, no exams, and there is an online makeup session if you miss class. The class is extremely political tho :(
Doesn't seem to really understand much of the material for someone with a PHD.....

Easy A class, the grading is purely attendance based, she teaches in an entirely subjective topics, no syllabus, no structure, no notes. Immunocompromised so wearing a mask is necessary in the classroom, very repetitive. I may agree with subject matter taught in this class and in 378, but her teaching methods make me want to dissagree

PROBLEMS WITH PLASTICS CLASS- NOT PUBHLTH335
class was said to be in in-person class; half the classes were online? graded on attendance and material was repetitive. felt there was no structure/rubric to the class. lots of guest speakers- one instance where the speaker was there but the professor wasn't (?). Easy class but didn't learn much

Sasha clearly cares about their students. I appreciated how they tried to create a space where everyone in the class felt comfortable. Their lectures can get a bit boring but I still learned a lot from the class.

I learned a lot in this class, but it was quite repetitive. You aren't graded by many things so attendance and participation do matter. The class is formatted in a unique way. Sasha cares a lot about the subject, but if you disagree with them, good luck!

Can't understand the professor or the TA. Takes attendance randomly and will subtract points from your final grade if you're not there. Exams are 70% of the grade and in each exam, there's multiple choice worth 30% and 3 open response question worth the rest. So your entire grade is based off a couple open response questions. Worst class avoid.
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Class is hard, and it was even harder to understand her. Mandatory attendance but she'd only check periodically and take -1pt to ur grade if ur not there. Hard to focus in lecture and many people struggled at the beginning. Take Econ 203 instead if she's the prof for this class. TA was hard to understand too but discussion he never took attendance

Dan Ai is the worst teacher I have ever had. It is already a difficult class, however Dan is impossible to understand. Attendance is mandatory, however, she only takes it randomly throughout the semester. If you aren't in class when she takes attendance it is one point off of your final grade. If possible, avoid at all costs.
reviews.rating_tags: Lecture heavy--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: She is a very nice woman and very understanding for extensions needed. However her lectures were very boring and honestly not helpful for any of the assignments. I dreaded going to class as it was just so boring. Stata is very confusing to use and the TAs were not very helpful considering it was our first time using it.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Lots of homework--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: the class was definitely difficult, but professor villanueva was really nice! she doesn't always explain everything super well in class, but she has a lot of office hours and will readily explain everything you ask if you do go. you can tell that she really wants to see all of her students succeed! not the easiest class by any means, but i did it!
reviews.rating_tags: Clear grading criteria--Lecture heavy--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: This class didn't have any tests and the professor was so sweet. But get ready to teach yourself how to code and show up to her office hours because the material is pretty complex. Don't fall behind too much or it'll be difficult to catch up! Be prepared to spend hours outside of class working on assignments.

Professor Villaneuva is so sweet and made what would have been a boring required class interesting! Her lectures are engaging and she provides plenty of office hours. The assignments are easy and she basically gives you the answers to the lines of code. She obviously cares and wants you to succeed!
reviews.rating_tags: Amazing lectures --Clear grading criteria--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: This class isn't what I expected it's basically a coding class. But the TA I had was very helpful and always was having office hours. This professor was always willing to help and meet with students but in class it moved very fast and the coding aspect wasn't really talked about at all in lectures. So be ready to do most of the work on your own.

Professor Villanueva is one of the best professors I've ever had at UMass. She is easily accessible outside of class and genuinely wants all of her students to succeed. Attendance and participation are required, but lectures are engaging. Definitely take this class with her, if you can!
This is a really interesting class of you put the effort in. Lord of readings and attendance is mandatory as you do a few grades in-class activities.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Caring--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Passionate about her subject. Her slides have a lot of information, and the charts she provides are important for her exams. Grading is pretty relaxed, just put in a bit of effort, and you'll be fine.
So smart and funny. Definitely do the readings and come to class. Some of the material/concepts are difficult but a very important class

Lecture slides are packed with information, and her tests can be hard. She's a very knowledgeable person and she's very passionate about her subject. She is sweet though! She does post a study guide a week before each exam, which helps a lot. Overall, a solid class but it can be a lot of work.

Love her!! She has been my favorite professor so far. Her lectures are content heavy but she still explains each topic well. Discussion groups are also very helpful. For exams she always does review and what I found helpful was putting the exam review into quizlet and then practicing flashcards and practice exams.
reviews.rating_tags: Amazing lectures --Clear grading criteria--Gives good feedback

reviews.comment: A lot of notes in one lecture, which she expects you to know all. Very nice and sweet person. Lectures get very confusing. Books assigned don't really seem to help with the class. Overall, too many topics that really don't tie together in the end.
A lot of memorization. Lectures can be difficult to get through because a lot of info is thrown at you. Amazing TAs!

Discussions in groups were nice. My TA was very helpful and open to help when needed. Professor truly wants students to succeed. Lectures were helpful but her voice is grating. Glad the class is almost over with.

lots of readings from textbook, 3 exams but 1 gets dropped, a few essays in between the semester, almost weekly discussion/participation on packback. she's really nice but it's a lot of info to memorize for exams imo. a lot of ppl ik didn't do as well on exams. literally did better on my orgo & kin270 exams lol

Prof Martinez is super sweet and TAs were really helpful. There was a good amount of reading that got boring sometimes. Tests and assignments were kind of unclear at the beginning of the semester, but that could've been because of the change to online. Nothing crazy tough, but also not super easy, if thats what you're looking for.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: Zoom Class once a week, async lectures with slides to watch. Make sure you post on Moodle forum and talk in the breakout room for participation credit. 3 exams and one is dropped, 2 essays and 1 short project. The essays were a lot of effort for only being 10 points. The TAs were very helpful. I liked the class, but it was difficult at times.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: Kaikman takes the cake for the best prof in Isenberg imho.
Prof. Aikman really cares about the people. Defying all odds, he is a man of solid character and questionable jokes.
Very passionate about financial modeling. A real cutie.

Nico is a really great professor. He is young and has that drive that newer teachers sometimes have. He goes out of his way to help you learn and is always available either online or in person. The class wasn't the most interesting, but Nico made it the best that it could be!

One of the best math professors you will ever come across. Genuinely interested in the material, funny and willing to accomodate to meet everyone's need. Going to class and office hours was actually fun and it's sad that the class has to end! Would highly recommend taking his class!

Amazing teacher! 2nd Best Math teacher I've ever had. His quizzes are hard if you don't look for his tricks. Take home quizzes are also challenging. Go to his office hours! He gives hints and will work through them with you! He can explain the most complex math problems like they're elementary school arithmetic. Very passionate, great guy!

Great professor! Makes mundane mathematics interesting. Easy to understand and goes out of his way to help you. I can say I look forward to attending this class. He is funny and keeps the class interested. Best math class I've taken here. I look forward to going every lecture.
Great Teacher, clear. Always willing to meet and help with any topics. Quick on email and provides tons of review material and review sheets.
easily the best math teacher on campus: student from other classes would come to review sessions

Agreed! Nico is a God send! He explains the material better than the other instructors and is always willing to help you. He led his own review sessions that students from other classes would attend to help clarify things.
HONESTLY A GOD SEND

Great teacher. Young, funny, and easy-going. He holds his own review sessions (apart from the huge, course-wide sessions), compiles excellent review packets with practice problems, and is happy to help any student understand the material. Calc II sucks, but he explains it better than anyone. Go to class...that "Transcendental" text is useless.

Nico is definitely the greatest teacher for 131. He will do anything he can to help the student learn. He is very passionate about math and brings humor into it. 131 is a very hard course in itself so I highly recommend Nico because he is very helpful and does whatever is necessary for the students to do well.

Nico was an excellent instructor. He really did a good job explaining everything in detail. The best is that even though he has set office hours, you can stay way past when they are over and he'll help you until you are done.

Nico is the man. Great teacher. Young. Cool. Funny. Class is not a simple one, but if you must take it, I highly recommend getting Nico. Nobody is as helpful as he is, and his willingness to help is remarkable. <3 PRETTY BLUE EYES!!

Nico was a great instructor. Gave a lot of care to make sure the class moved at the right pace needed for each section. Flexed office hours to work around students. All in all a great teacher just a hard class, doesn't matter who you have. Attendance is not mandatory but deffinitely helps to show up.
Math relays are such fun! I love Nico!!

Nico is an excellent TA and teacher.  He is willing to give extra help you if you ask and does a great job of clarifying what we do in class.  He's very nice and tries to make class interesting.  Just try not to get lost in his eyes.
Nico is so great! Even though I basically failed the first test, I can't blame him! Maybe I was just too busy staring into his beautiful eyes to pay attention...
'easiest class ever must take. Class is wild. he can't control anyone. If you need a GPA booster or just an easy class this is it.

Take this class if you can. Stormin' Norman is one of the craziest men I have ever met. His class is chaos. The man has seriously lost it and cannot control the students. He does not explain or teach anything, but ends up giving all A's. I only needed to get something like 12 questions right on the final to get an a. Take for pure entertainment.

The bottom line, this class is a waste of time. Here's a tip: take it with a friend and give him your PRS so you both don't have to sit through this mess. If you hate meaningless waste of money and time classes, don't bother. If you are looking for an A you will get it after much frustration. Copy down the prs questions because some are on the test and study from the book. Do the quizzes that are in it and offered online from the book. Some questions are exactly the same. Good luck!

This guy doesn't do anything. he can't teach. But the class is easy. You only have to go for prs points. theres 2 essays and in my class he just gave everyone full credit for both because he lost the essays. i got a B+ and i hardly ever went to class, and did poorly on all three tests. theres 2 exams in class and the final. easy class, i love norm.
Everyone in the class went into the final failing, then magically left with A's for the semester.

This is probably the worst teacher I've throughout my 4 years in this school. Extremely unorganized and expects you to know things even if he didnt go over it just because it is in one of the readings or something. If you can avoid him I would STRONGLY RECOMMEND IT!!!
VERYYYYY UNORGANIZED!!! don't follow the syllabus because he doen't follow it either. Know your macro otherwise you'll be lost.

Very little experience with powerpoint. Often gets confused and has wrong information on slides. Expects you to learn using the textbook without any help. Uses class time to give example questions that he doesn't go over. Worst class I've taken in my four years at the university.
This guy has no clue what he is doing but the good thing is you don't have to know what your doing either to get a good grade...he gives away so many free points i dont think its possible to do bad

Amazing professor, couldn't have asked for a better professor. She's very easy and tries to make the class fun, as it may be a gen-ed for some people. Slides are very easy to understand, and the talking pace is slow so that we can take notes during the class. The exams aren't hard at all if you put in the work and study!

DO not take BIO 151 with her. Study guides for exams are absolutely heinous, and take hours to get through. Her voice is like nails on a chalkboard.  You have to buy an Clicker for the class, and you get points off if you miss lectures.  Her weekly quiz/exam questions are extremely wordy and confusing.

Took this class for a gen ed thinking it would be easy, but no. No textbook so you need to go to the lectures. Hard to focus in lectures, she speaks w lots of pauses and SO slowly. Work is manageable if you try, dont cram for exams trust me, theyre weirdly specific. Dont take this for a gen ed
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Lots of homework--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: The lectures are so engaging and fun. Cass makes the material super simple and easy to understand. I barely had to study for this class but I can understand how some of the concepts can be difficult to grasp as there are many small parts to certain mechanisms. If you can do all homework/quiz questions and review slides you will be great on exams.

Lectures are very material heavy, but that is expected in a biology course. Everything on the exams are given to you in the slides. As long as you attend class and review the slides you will fly by with an A. Attendance is mandatory through an iClicker you need to purchase. All in all, probably the best science teacher I've ever had!!

Great professor. I didn't have to study for any tests because all the lectures had easily digestible information that stacked on top of each other. No complaints except for the TAs, they were all snobs who never could accept being wrong

Dr. Cass is great professor period. Her lectures are fairly easy to understand, and she's very enthusiastic about the content. There is iClicker attendance and questions, and weekly assignments and quizzes, but they are manageable and help balance out exam grades. The content isn't terrible either.

Amanda is a great teacher. In my opinion the best bio 151 teacher. Class is very easy, lectures are very clear and teach you well. I highly recommend Amanda. Tests are also very easy, the hardest assignments are weekly quizzes but are still not even bad.
She was a good professor, but material is hard and she adds unnecessary information to her lectures that just confuse you further. Work is manageable, but time was definitely put into it.

Amanda was a great professor for Bio151, she is clearly extremly passionate about biology and definitely inspires many student. Weekly assignments are easy and there is not a large amount of homework by any means. You never need to pack up early as she always ends lectures with perfect timing.
There's weekly problem sets and quizzes but they are helpful to study for the mid terms. As long as you study, you will get a good grade and she is super helpful and there's a lot of resources.

Lecture heavy and some topics cane quite confusing, I found it helpful to use the TA's notes instead of the slides. Weekly quizzes and assignments all online but they can be pretty confusing as well (worded really strangely sometimes?) Overall, I wouldn't mind having her as an instructor again
Grades way too hard, get points off for anything

For this course, I mostly self taught myself everything by going back to her slides. I never payed attention in her lecture since she does many pauses and speaks slow. However I still managed to do well. She gives out a lot of extra credit. One thing I wish was that she posted the grade averages but she doesn't.

Just a very nice person who did not make the class too hard. There is no text book so you def need to go to the lectures but besides that and the 1-2 hours of homework you have per week this class does not take up too much time.  The tests arent bad if you study. solid chances to get extra help if needed.

You will be expected to stay the whole lab. Also, you are expected to be picture perfect- she will breathe down ur neck at all times. And you will always lose points on lab notebooks...I'm not sure why the grading is so picky lol. Not necessarily hard or not doable just irritating. Most assignments I've had for a lab.

Took Bio 151 and it was her first sem teaching at UMass. Was amazingly engaging and comprehensive, while also being incredibly open to criticism and comments. Weekly problem sets and quizzes did tend to get a little annoying but had loads of extra credit and overall helped me learn the course content very well. Overall a super nice professor.

This course was definitely one of the more difficult classes I have taken but was honestly super rewarding. Cass takes time to teach you super useful things that you will not learn in college unless you take Bio 284. I honestly hated this course at first but once I got the hang of it, I really liked it. Having a good group is extremely useful.
reviews.rating_tags: Group projects--Gives good feedback--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: She's a really great professor! She's very passionate about what she teaches, and is super accessible and is always willing to help students out. To do well, make sure to attend class as attendance is mandatory, and put effort into studying the material; you'll do just fine.
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Gives good feedback--Lots of homework

reviews.comment: Difficult but wonderful prof. Leaves good feedback, very little homework, tons of extra credit opportunities, lecture recordings posted, and helpful TAs. Her class requires lots of studying, as exam questions are very applied and require thorough knowledge. If you put in the time, you can succeed well in this class. TAKE HER OVER LAURA FRANCIS!

She's a very engaging professor who is super enthusiastic about what she teaches. The multiple choice section on her exams are worded in a confusing way. Definitely requires studying for the exams but the workload is very manageable.

Dr. Cass was a good professor, but somehow the quizzes were extra harder than the homeworks and that frustrated me a lot. Definitely need to study or do some kind of extra work, like the SI sessions (amazing!!) or office hours (which I didn't do so thats probably why I got a B). Attendance was mandatory and you need an iClicker. fast talker too
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Lots of homework--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: We did two projects; one about yeast and the other about dogs. You write a paper for the yeast project and do a project for the dog project. There is a final exam-multiple choice and open response. I didn't like the yeast one it was too complex but the dog one was fun. She's a good professor for this lab.
She is very slow in lectures. She has good quiz reviews and offers extra credit. You will have to put effort into the class to do well but she is willing to help you and wants you to do well.

This was the worst 2 credit course I've ever taken in 4 years. Basically, every single assignments along with projects are graded as a group. If you get a group who doesn't participate enough, you will also get a bad grade even if the syllabus indicates “individual grading”. Spent so much time, done 80% of project, deducted for 20% that group did.

She's a very enthusiastic professor who wants all her students to succeed. This class did require a lot of studying, but if you're willing to put in the work, you will definitely get an A. Her tests are very fair and not too difficult.

Really nice and caring and gives lots of opportunities for extra credit on exams. Weekly problem sets and quizzes but all open note and can redo problem sets until you get a 100 and drops lowest quiz. There is just a lot of content and you have to understand how things work rather than just memorize vocab and facts. Exams have drawing.

She is such a nice and caring person. She explains everything in simpler terms but I did study quite a lot outside of class because it is a 9am class so it's hard to stay focus. The grad TA sucks and discussions were hard. Participation is through iClickers. She only has one day for office hour and it's in the morning so not very accessible.
She give no extra credit, so you have to really put in the extra effort.

Difficult class that is very dense in terms of content. Her exams are the worst exams I have ever had to take in my academic career and you have to understand and memorize content EXTREMELY DEEPLY and apply it. Lectures are technically mandatory but I just take notes on the slides out of class. She is nice, passionate, and extremely energetic.

Pretty solid professor. The lab was straightforward and I was personally blessed with a good lab partner, making it a nice lab in general. It's a smaller class so she is easily accessible, not to mention the other professors who are lab assistants and the TAs who can help you throughout the lab. Cool project in the end where you DNA swab your dog.

Cass was a good professor for Biology 151! Her lectures have a lot of information, and some was hard to understand, but she was very accessible to meet with and always would answer questions. Exams were a little tough, but nothing too grueling.

Cass is an amazing professor. Provided slides before class and rarely made changes to them, stuck to the syllabus to a tee. Slides were full and explained everything on them thoroughly. Homework (unlimited attempts) and quizzes weekly, but all open-note. Very responsive outside of class. Exams are exactly the material taught in class.

She loads a lot into her lectures, so as long as you attend class and pay attention you are good. She can move a little fast so be prepared to take notes. Very passionate about what she teaches and wants everyone to get a good grade. If your final exam is higher than a midterm grade wise it will replace it. Perfect for first year students.

She is such a sweet and caring person but her class is so hard. The tests are way harder than the other Bio teachers, includes drawings, labeling, fill ins etc… Other profs i heard of are just T/F. She is really sweet though and gives extra credit

Super sweet and enthusiastic, but lectures are very fast and cover a lot of content. 1 homework assignment and 1 quiz every week, but they go into more detail than what is covered in class. In-class iClicker questions help, and she walks around offering help to anyone who needs it!

I love Dr. Cass, I understand how others found her pace of class difficult at times but other than that she's an amazing professor who provides tons of materials and is easily accessible. She's very passionate and loves to answer any questions.

Dr. Cass is undoubtedly the best professor I've had at Umass thus far. She's very passionate about Biology and her lectures are very engaging and entertaining. The workload is not bad as you only need to complete one weekly problem set and quiz which are both open notes. Her tests are fair and she does give extra credit questions. TAKE HER CLASS!

I love Dr. Cass and she genuinely cares about her students and their success. I will say the lectures are paced very quickly and the problem sets and quizzes were often more difficult than what was taught in class. She does however have tons of materials to help you out and is easily available to help you.

Dr. Cass is amazing! She is so passionate about what she does and is energetic during lectures. Lectures can be fast paced at times but she posts slides and recordings so you can fill in any gaps. She is always willing to answer questions or "talk your ear off" about all things science. Love her and wish I could take every science course from her!
Such a passion for what she teaches which helps keep students interested

Prof Cass is a great teacher and is very enthusiastic. The weekly problem sets and quizzes were much more in depth than the material taught during class. Her questions are not very straight forward which made doing well on the weekly assignments difficult. She takes attendance using iClicker, and drops 20% of the points at the end of the semester.

Professor Cass was a great lecturer, gave time for questions, and built iClicker questions into the lecture. She covered a lot of content and spoke very quickly, but she gave many resources for extra help. The class did have difficult content, but she was also available for office hours. As long as you take  good notes and study you will do well.

This professor is extremely vague with her homework and lectures, and expects her students to know everything. She gets mad when students ask what material will be on the exam. She talks about stress load and how teens should be less stressed, when she is the one causing my stress. One of the worst professors I have had.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Lots of homework

reviews.comment: Dr. Rubin is an amazing professor who really cares about her students. If you put in the effort, you will be fine. She does give a ton of homework, but all of it helps prepare you for weekly quizzes and exams. Tests were easy if you did the homework and studied the material. If you are willing to put in the effort, I highly recommend this class.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Lots of homework--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: The year honestly started out exciting and I was so ready to learn but Dr Rubin is so inconsistent and idk but mean/angry sometimes, sometimes she seems like she cares, sometimes she can almost be funny.  Feels like students are an after throught. She talks down to us but we are trying to learn.

Dr. Rubin can be particular but she is always accessible in and out of class. Very caring for her students and 110% wants to see them succeed and do well in vetmed. If you want to actually gain something from class I reccommend her as a professor.

Inconsistent teaching and irrelevant in-class activities. Exam topics never explicitly mentioned and you are not allowed to study past quizzes or exams for other exams or the final. Lots of memorization, avoid this class if possible.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Lots of homework

reviews.comment: The good ratings are from herself.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Lots of homework

reviews.comment: The other bad rating are true.

Dr. Rubin treats her students in a very condescending manner. The veterinary field can already be draining on your mental health and she claims to advocate for it. Many students dread going to class because of her attitude and how she likes to humiliate you in front of your classmates for not knowing something.
Dr. Rubin is demeaning and unorganized.  Rude overall and not into trying to educate us or help us learn.

Dr. Rubin is passionate about what she teaches and wants everyone in the class to succeed. There can be a lot of course work and tough material, but it is all to prepare us for a difficult field and a difficult national exam.

Going into the field of Animal Science in my freshman year, I was excited, and looking forward to exploring what I was truly interested in. Much to my chagrin, this professor lacks respect for her students and is quite stubborn. I will say she understands the topic, but she does not understand kindness. If you can avoid this class, do it.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Lots of homework

reviews.comment: Lots of homework but it is all to help learn what we need to know for the VTNE! Very helpful, awesome professor
reviews.rating_tags: Clear grading criteria--Gives good feedback--Lots of homework

reviews.comment: I really like this class but Dr. Rubin makes me dread going. Dr. Rubin for some reason thinks that she has the right to her student's respect and that she can treat them as she pleases. She needs to learn that respect from her students is earned and that just because she is in a powerful position doesn't mean she can be terrible to her students.

Not a nice person. Very unapproachable and I dread coming to class. It's a great class because you are doing hands on things and it relates to our future but this is one course where I can say that the instructor ruins the class.

Dr. Rubin can be an intimidating professor when you first meet her but don't let that fool you. She is THE BEST professor and adviser I have ever had, but don't get me wrong I definitely struggled in her class at some points. I don't think I would feel at home at college without her being such a supportive and caring mentor to me and my peers.

Dr. Rubin is definitely a tough professor but she care a lot about her students. She takes time out of weekends + after work to make sure we get extra opportunities to practice our skills and participate with the community. She may seem intimidating at first but once you get to know her she is an awesome professor. My favorite part about UMass.

Yes Dr. Rubin has high standards for her students, but it is only because she is proud of this program she runs, she wants to produce outstanding veterinary technicians, and she wants us to succeed. She cares about her students inside and outside the classroom. Additionally, she is probably one of the most helpful advisors you could find on campus.
Dr. Rubin is an amazing professor and advisor who takes the time to get to know her students and does a lot despite her busy schedule to help them succeed. My friends and I love her!

Dr Rubin is an amazing professor and advisor, she is caring and respectful to all of her students. Her class was tough and she can be strict but she was always willing to help with anything we needed. She is so funny and sweet, and I am so happy I have her as my advisor and as my professor.

As the other reviews mention, she can be hard on her students sometimes but keep in mind that you will be working with live animals and her priority is keeping everyone safe. Her tests are somewhat difficult and require a lot of memorization. However, the information will be useful for the future. She's strict because she wants us to do our best.

Dr. Rubin is the sweetest person. Her class was straightforward and fair with all exams. She also took the time to help me plan my classes for the next year even though she isn't my advisor. Definitely take her class.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Lecture heavy--Caring

reviews.comment: Have to agreed with the other rating. Shes just terrible and students are scared of her. I wish she showed respect to her students in the same way she demands it from them.

Unprofessional and just plain mean. Really unapproachable. Students dread when she comes into the barn because there is a good chance she will yell at you. Not a great representation of the department.
Lectures were easy to follow and homework was closely aligned to them. Exams were worth 80% of the grade, although he always tells you exactly what to expect on them.

Nice lectures, lots of colored chalk. 1st half of course was taught incredibly. Once he gets to E&M it's hard to follow and I just relied on old exams and homework to learn from. Exams are graded generously and you lots of partial credit if you can reason out your work. Lots of homework but it matches pretty well to lectures/exams. Good guy overall
reviews.rating_tags: EXTRA CREDIT--Gives good feedback--Lots of homework

reviews.comment: This is for ECE573. AVOID THIS CLASS. This is easily the worst taught class in the whole ECE department. The lectures just leave you completely confused and the homework is borderline impossible. Going to office hours is just a waste of time because he doesn't help. Nobody in the class has learned anything, it's just a terrible experience overall.
reviews.rating_tags: Beware of pop quizzes--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: The course material is uninteresting but Professor Arbabi makes the class worth taking. Plenty of homework assignments, lots of examples and great review material to firm up concepts for the exams. Has 3-4 colors of chalk going at any given time and boy does it help. Take any class he teaches.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Lots of homework--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: Among the great professors in the department. The material is difficult (fields and waves) but he works relentlessly to frame the material in understandable terms. ALWAYS prepared for class, listens carefully to student feedback and adjusts accordingly. Exams are remarkably fair, consistent 75% average. Provides plenty of practice material. 10/10

Wow, this guy is SERIOUSLY underappreciated. His lectures are *amazing* and he works very hard to put together a wealth of resources to help with the difficult but necessary coursework (eg. whenever he uploads a new homework assignment he also includes a unique set of sample problems w/ very thorough solutions to help you get through it). Top tier.

Hes able to teach incredibly hard material very very well. He is the hidden gem of this department. You wont have him for underclassmen classes which is sad but when you have him. Just know. Youre good.

This course has a strict final-exam minimum required to pass, regardless of overall performance. In the compressed winter format, this makes the final extremely high-stakes. Students should be very aware of this policy and consider whether the pace and grading structure fit their learning style.

The professor isn't too bad, the course is just a lot of writing, esp. considering it is for math majors. You won't learn any new math except for research for the final. Attendance is mandatory, but you can miss a few classes. Participation is important, kind of (you grade yourself at the end). If you hate writing, wait for a different professor.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Clear grading criteria--So many papers

reviews.comment: Although attendance wasn't mandatory, there's no ECHO360, and she doesn't post her annotated notes, so it's advised that you just go to her class. She's an okay teacher, color codes, and I like the worksheets, but don't take it as an 8 am, you'll want to skip and fall asleep.

Math is hard for me but Adena is a saint. 10/10 lovely person. I have ADHD and dyscalculia, go to her office hours if you struggle. She walked me through the entire semester and I passed with a little wiggle room to get the credit. She is phenomenal, it's so refreshing to have a professor that cares about her students. Shes perfect.

She is really nice but is strict with deadlines and doesn't offer extra credit. There are 2 exams the whole semester but they impact your grade a lot so do well. She does, however, usually take out the lowest grade of an assignment, etc.

I was nervous to take calculus in college since I hadn't taken it in high school, but Adena explained difficult concepts clearly and simply. Although lecture was at 8:30 a.m., she posted them. The midterm and final are weighted heavily, but homework and mini quizzes help balance your grade.

I was not good at math in high school but Adena explained everything so simply. Mini quizzes were easy, homework was tough. The average on her exam was consistently around a 60%, and there were only two (midterm worth 25% and final worth 30%), so be sure to study for those. This is overall very basic calculus and not a hard class.

Dr. Calden makes the Calc 127 lectures so engaging and accessible. While attendance is not mandatory, I found that going to the lecture in person (even though it was at 8:30 AM) was so much more helpful than watching the videos. Many mini quizzes and wileyplus ($50 purchase), but not too bad if you keep up with it.

I don't know why her rating is so high. Yes she's very nice but her teaching is very confusing, she posts little to no practice problems, then makes the exams nothing like those practice problems. The only people close to passing her exams are those who've already taking calc. Lots of homework that is a waste of time.
Adena is nice but the way she teaches made learning Calc way harder than it should have been. I'm always left confused after every lecture. I'd say she is the best option for 127 though

Adena herself is very nice and does try to make you understand her material but moves way too fast during her lectures and does not give enough time to take notes. The average on the midterm was a 60% and the workload can be very overwhelming with homework questions being way harder than anything we did in class.

This professor makes an entry-level Calc127 course way harder than it needs to be. Midterm average was about 60% with no curve, even though the exam is the same as other sections. Lectures are unclear and rushed. The high RMP rating does not match the actual classroom experience. Higlyh doubt all those good reviews are FAKE

Great professor! Makes difficult concepts more comprehendible as someone who as scared of calculus. She uses different colored pens during lectures which is SUPERRRR helpful. Based on what i've heard from friends, she is by far the best MATH127 professor to have. Wish the exams and HW weren't the only thing you are graded on.

Adena is a great professor, for a calc class she teaches very well. Her lectures are well taught and she always informs us in class of any changes or material on exams/quizzes. It is not an easy class but if you have to take this class definitely GO TO CLASS!! Lectures are recorded but it is way better to just be present in case you have questions.

Took this as a freshman in my first semester. I don't recommend it. The material is tough to follow and overly complex for a 3-credit class. Adena is passionate and cares about students, but the workload is overwhelming, with too much homework and constant quizzes after every lecture.
reviews.rating_tags: Amazing lectures --Lots of homework--So many papers

reviews.comment: Adena was great at teaching math127. Very organized and taught the material very well. Homework consisted of wiley plus which was very annoying, and quizzes that were on canvas (One after every lecture)... Take Adena if you aretaking 127. The only annoying thing was the extremely difficult final worth 25% of your grade.

I took Math127 with her online over the summer, she is AMAZING! It wasn't as much course load as I thought and her lectures were so easy to follow. I am not the strongest in math but I managed great. 100% recommend her!

She is nice but the median score on the midterm was around 60, with no curve. Why is she 4.4? Is this the first year having both midterm and final?????? Practice problems and exams only share same topics and concepts but completely different difficulties.

Kind and cares about students, had no discussion section and attendance isn't required for lectures, but go. Provides handout/guided notes w/ problems for the lecture that she goes through, explains things well. Frequently gives practice problems in class and then explains. Short online quiz and homework, ~30 minutes, after every class. Take her!

Shes awful, i dont know how she has a 4.4 it should be a 1.4. Average for the midterm was a 59, and no she didnt scale it. The homework and quizzes are all online but she decided to give us homework over Thanksgiving break??? Yea alright

Very sweet teacher and super easy to reach via email/office hours. Homework and mini quizzes are weekly but not super time consuming. Just go/watch the lectures and stay on top of homework and you'll be ok.

DO NOT TAKE HER FOR SUMMER! Tons of quizzes. Lectures are long and useless youtube videos; ALL of the content in them do not show up in the homework, quizzes, and final--thus forcing you to self-learn the ENTIRE course. If you don't get more than 50% on the final you get an F on the entire course no matter how good you did on everything else.

Professor was nice but just went through the lecture without stopping most of the time. 
Homework was online and you had multiple tries which was good. Only 1 exam too!
reviews.rating_tags: Clear grading criteria--Lots of homework--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: TOO MANY TESTS

Whatever you do don't take during summer. She made the final worth 50% so even if you did good in the class you fail the final you fail the class. Lectures unclear barely had what would be on the homework. Practice exam didn't have anything near what was on the finals overall just an upsetting class.

Do not take her during the summer! The class seems almost haphazardly thrown together from pre-existing recorded lectures and it shows. While the lectures themselves do a great job teaching what they cover, the rarely cover the breadth of problem types you are required to know for the homework and quizzes, and the TAs rarely were prepared to help.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Beware of pop quizzes--Graded by few things

reviews.comment:
-graded on discussion post responses :|
-you have to get at least 50% on the final to pass
-you are required to pay for the homework website
-multiple quizzes every week
-long boring recorded lectures. AVOID AT ALL COSTS!
Don't take during the summer!!! Professor is nice but summer class is a ripoff everything is YouTube videos and Wiley. you also have to get more then 50% on the final to pass.
Do not take this class with this professor. It is not worth it when there are so many other options in the calculus department. Very unresponsive and unprofessional emailer.

Class was alright. HW's are on Wileyplus and she had mini quizzes on canvas, which was annoying to manage what I had to do. All HW and quizzes are online, only in person thing is the final exam. Don't recommend skipping class as one missed class can set you back far. Final only worth 20% of final grade so take that as you will

Do the homework, weekly quizzes, and chapter tests (all online). Watch/go to lectures and the SI session and you'll be chilling. So many resources to get help if your struggling. I guessed on the final (in person) and I still ended with an A-
Super nice professor and great lecturer. Do the homeworks and go to the lectures or watch them online and you'll be good.

I was very nervous about taking this class, coming from a non-traditional college student perspective. Last time I took calculus was junior year of high school. Then went on to do my military service. I ended up finishing the class with a 96! Do the homework, go to lecture, SI for exam reviews and you will do great. Final was easy and was curved.
60% of the grade is from online quizzes, do the work and it'll be a easy class

Love Adena! She's very accessible outside of class and is always down to chat. She understands that some people think they're not good at math and teaches things step-by-step to reduce confusion. I am not the best at math, and I was never confused in this class. Easy to do well on quizzes and homework which are all online. 10/10 class
reviews.rating_tags: Amazing lectures --Gives good feedback--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Adena is great and as far as math classes go, it's generally easy. All work is online except for the final exam. Don't miss your online mini/chapter quizzes as you can't retake them or do them late, and they're worth a combined 60% of your grade.
Good professor. Weekly quizzes and homework. Can watch video lectures instead of going to class. All exams online besides final
Super sweet and caring, made math fun and easy suprisingly , i hate math. Gives extra credit and take home exams

Teacher could care less about seeing her students succed, after many times of trying to schedule times for extra help.. I recieved none. One of the worst professors I have ever had and would not wish this kind of support on anyone. DONT RECCOMEND.

Lectures are uploaded so you don't really have to go to class; online textbook for homework, good practice; chapter quizzes and mini-quizzes are online and take-home. Do your homework, it will help your grade a lot. Easy to do well if you put in some effort and do all the assignments

Such a good teacher. The reason I did not get an A was simply because I didn't go to class so I did not do too great on the final. As long as you keep up with the material, you will be fine. Only issue was having to buy a textbook no one used.

so was so sweet. All assignment were online including chapter quizzes. The only thing taken in person was the final which was easy. Everything was multiple choice and I got an A without attending lecture this class is an easy A.

the tests,quizzes, and HW were online & the final was in person. We were given a study guide, that she claimed was similar difficulty to the final. I spent  two weeks  studying the material alot & paid over $100 for a tutor. I felt extremely confident going into the test, but I was shocked when I only knew 7/30 questions. I got a 53% on the final.

She seems nice but you literally cannot miss a class and still pass the homework. Doesn't post any of the lectures or completed notes. The mini quizzes also contain concepts we learned weeks after. One bad mini quiz grade tanks your grade. I went to every class and reviewed constantly and I still feel I might fail the (in person) final.
2 mini quizzes each week + homework. Final is no longer optional but it was not too bad as long as you paid attention in class. Adena is a great professor who really cares about her students

Do not listen to the reviews for this class, the final exam is mandatory and in-person. There are assignments due every Wednesday and Sunday, which are not that hard but she still requires homework over breaks. Very unprofessional with emails swell, writes them like they are texts and doesn't answer simple questions.
I am not a math person but Professor Calden made math manageable. 2 take home exams, only 1 in person with some group projects as well. Super caring, funny, and effective in her teaching.

Prof Calden is certainly the best professor I've had at UMass, and one of the best teachers I've had throughout my education. Her class can be tough but she is always there to help if you have the initiative to stay after class or go to office hours. She once got me Advil from her office when she noticed I wasn't feeling good. She is truly a saint.

I would say I really enjoyed this class but beware the other reviews…they completely switched the curriculum this year. The classes were attendance optional but she doesn't even post the lectures so you can't really miss a class if you want to do ur homework. The final is NOT optional and the formula sheet looks like it's gonna be no help.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: She's a nice teacher, but her class does not reflect on her reviews. Class is mostly online with 2 mini quizzes a week (3 q) and 2 HW a week, so one quiz and HW per lecture. There's 5 chap. quizzes (10 q each) that are online. Mini quizzes have material that she hasn't covered in class yet. Final exam is now in person and not optional.
Good teacher in general. All the quizzes are online. No midterm. Homework is reasonable. Adena is the best person to take Calc with

Very broad in teaching, expects all students to know formulas that are not shown in class, and expects you to answer just like her on the board even if you get the same answer. Doesn't re-teach any material that people get and the test averages are low, especially for a take-home exam. She expects you to be a genius already, it's her job!

She teaches really well and makes all the concepts easy to understand. Weekly mini-quizzes and homework. There is a chapter quiz after each chapter finishes and they account for 40% of the grade so doing them good helps u get a good grade for the course. Best teacher for MATH 127
reviews.rating_tags: Amazing lectures --Clear grading criteria--Lots of homework

reviews.comment: Nice teacher. Lot's of the other review's on her admire her simply because the whole class was online up until this semester. In-person final this time around. Doesn't post recordings now, ridiculous. Homework scheduling makes it feel like we're backed up in the class when we're not. Homework and quiz due on the first day of finals. Extra stress...

Professor Calden's MATH127 is well-structured with weekly mini-quizzes and homework on Wileyplus. While attendance is mandatory, everything is available online, so you can still succeed even if you miss some classes. Unstuckstudy AI and ChatGPT were super helpful for study prep.

Enrolled in her class based off of her reviews and wasn't impressed in the slightest. No echo 360, assessments don't reflect lecture material, one attempt on graded canvas quizzes, only 5 attempts on hw problems. Paying $2000 for a class and not being able to rewatch lectures is absolutely crazy. Also the final is NOT optional anymore (fall 2024)

Can choose between a(synchronous) and lectures are extremely well organized w/ guided notes. There's a mini quiz and homework assignment corresponding to each lecture, as well as 5 chapter tests throughout the sem. Final is an optional chapter quiz. Need to purchase access to hw on Wileyplus. Do NOT skip a class cause math is cumulative.
reviews.rating_tags: Clear grading criteria--Accessible outside class--Online Savvy

reviews.comment: The class was graded on mini quizzes, two per week (25% of your final grade), weekly homework assignments (25% of your final grade), and five chapter tests (50% of your final grade). Overall, she explained every concept very well and would have examples that demonstrated the concepts in use. Great professor who knows how to teach the material.

There are at least two 3 question mini quizzes (2 tries) every week based on material covered in class. There are 5 chapter quizzes (1 try) that are 10 questions long and an optional final (10 questions). EVERYTHING is online- lecture videos, quizzes, and tests. There is also homework to be done on WileyPlus. I think its $50 using code.

I have noticed that she only teaches 70% of the actual material in the mini quizzes and exams. There were a times in the semester when I did a mini quiz, and at least one question was on a topic we would learn the next week, so I got points off that since we never learned it. She also gives 3 minutes per practice problem, which is not enough time.

I didn't attend lectures the entire semester since everything is online. She posts all her lectures and the homework, quizzes, and exams are online so I used Chegg for everything. If you don't have Chegg though she explains things super clearly in the videos. If you actually did all the homework it would probably take a lot of time though.

I followed this class online asynchronously. She had videos made specifically for this which were way more concise and this was better for me since the contents for a review for me from high school. She was very nice and caring. She communicated really well over email about reminders about tests. The grades were based on hw, quizzes and topic tests
reviews.rating_tags: Clear grading criteria--Graded by few things--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Love her, great professor
reviews.rating_tags: Clear grading criteria--Gives good feedback--Lots of homework

reviews.comment: The setup for this class is non-required lectures, then homework assignments and weekly quizzes graded on correctness. If you are taking Calc127 this class is VERY easy. I had an 8:30 for this class, I went twice all year and then watched the online version and ended with an A.
reviews.rating_tags: Clear grading criteria--Lots of homework--Test heavy

reviews.comment:
Lots of mini-quizzes throughout the week (3 questions). Don't forget a few as your grade drops due to it (ex. mine).
Exams, quizzes, and hw are all online! An optional online final was given which replaced the lowest exam score!
Easy to get a good grade as long as everything is done!

Extensions won't be granted if you forget a date.

Sweetest professor ever! You do not have to go to every class, but the textbook is MANDATORY. It is an online textbook where you do all of your assignments on. Adena actually cares about her students and is very approachable. TA hours are 100% worth the time, as they are all super sweet and patient.
reviews.rating_tags: Amazing lectures --Clear grading criteria--Gives good feedback

reviews.comment: I loved Adena as a professor. All the lectures were available online broken in segments (made it easier to get through). Everything was explained in detail and had plenty of examples. Tests were online (with an optional final) and we were allowed our notes.
HIGHLY RECOMMEND ADENA!
Highly recommend this class for people who have struggled with math in the past. Her lectures are very clear and she also posts them online.
HIGHLY RCM
Adena is the best, she is very caring and lenient. You'll definitely have to do a lot of writing the grading is very generous and should be an easy A
She's a good professor and really nice. You can basically complete this class completely virtually.

Excellent instructor for this writing course.  Normally I do not enjoy writing, but in her class you are given freedom to write about things you are passionate about.  There was a solid amount of work, however, that can be expected for any advanced writing course.  I also got to work with a diverse set of really good people which I enjoyed.

Adena is great. Started class with calm scenarios or thoughts that honestly made my day.
Class can be taken in person or asynchronously. Both options are really useful.
Grade is a true representation of your understanding of the material.
No textbook but you need to purchase WileyPLUS for this class to do homework (there's a discount code).

I cannot recommend her enough.  Math, and especially calculus, are my weakest classes, but she breaks down difficult concepts & makes the material very approachable.  What puts her above and beyond, is how much she cares for her students.  I had a very difficult semester, and she couldn't have been more understanding, working with me 1-on-1.

Overall great class, but we have assignments due every time we see her, which typically amounts to 2 hours homework from one day to the next. It just becomes a hassle especially when in class we just talk about random math topics, and then the students are expected to do all the work outside of class. Unclear grading criteria too
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Lots of homework--So many papers

reviews.comment: I loved Calden. I took this class online and it was one of the easiest classes I've ever taken. I did take AP calc which contributed to how easy it was, but she just really knew how to teach an online class. She gave a lot of lecture material and the discussions were great to help understand material. Overall, super easy but learned a lot.
I had her lectures for MATH127. Her lectures are easy to follow. She doesn't rush from one topic to another, and she really takes time to make everything clear.

This was a class I struggled in at the beginning of the semester, but eventually got better at it as the semester went on. Which how many things that were graded I got my D+ all the way up to a B at the end of the semester and the final was optional to make your grade even higher than it was before. She really cares about her students.
I took this class over the summer. Was a bit difficult but was worth it. I already took her 127 class and had to take 128 with her.  I totally recommend her!!
Adena is very helpful, i recommend taking any class she gives. Her TAs are always awesome.
reviews.rating_tags: Clear grading criteria--Lecture heavy--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment:
Lectures posted as short videos (summer course). Exams+final are multiple choice. Homework is important. Participation is easy (a few forum posts). Adena & TAs are really accessible outside of class for extra help. Extra credit at the end.

As someone who struggles w math I found this class doable - but not easy. 
Put in the work & you'll be okay.
reviews.rating_tags: Clear grading criteria--Lecture heavy--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Taking this class online really saved me. I only attended the first class in person. Watching the lectures and filling in the notes is helpful if you actually pay attention. Otherwise the homework and quizzes will be a bit difficult. If you complete the homework which is pretty generous with attempts before doing the quizzes you should be fine.

Love her! She teaches very well, shows lots of examples, and connects to real-life situations. Sometimes her quizzes can be a little hard but usually they are pretty easy. She has lots of resources to help explain the units more. Lot of homework and weekly quizzes but are not bad, just don't do them last minute! Overall good class.

I had Adena for 127 and 128. Both courses showed how well Adena has adapted to online learning. She gives out notes for you to fill in while she lectures, provides several videos she's made to go over the topics in more depth, and provides optional extra worksheets for every unit that were entirely optional but so helpful. A saint.

The class was okay. At times, the mini quizzes contained material that was definitely not covered in the lectures. Some questions were so hard and random and since there were only three questions there was a lot of pressure to get them all right. The chapter quizzes weren't that bad and the review packets were helpful

expected us to learn a whole section in one day and take a quiz the next. quizzes were only 3 questions so if you got one wrong, you already have a 67% overall. quizzes, tests and homework on wileyplus were nothing like the questions in lectures. only extra credit was the final but other than that she gives you no chance to boost your grade.

very nice, explained concepts very well, i have always struggled with Math and i really understood this class. lectures were posted to BlackBoard to watch it was ten over the Winter Session. Final was easy but no final during Fall/Spring semesters. Mini Quizzes and Chapter Quizzes are easy. WileyPlus for hw is straightforward
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Clear grading criteria--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: Professor Calden is great. Her lectures are very detailed, and her TAs have drop-in hours for extra help basically all day. Her quizzes and tests directly reflect the material covered in lecture, and are very straightforward. She also offers one extra credit assignment at the end of the course. If you took calc in high school it's a breeze!

I was very scared to take this class because I did not do well in Math 127. I found it easier than 127 because she did a great job explaining the material and gave us a doable amount of work. Questions were always answered well and quickly through the discussion board. I would definitely recommend taking this class with her!
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Accessible outside class--Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: She was remote this semester, but she posted all lectures on Moodle. There are mini quizzes and homework assignments every week. You'll pass if you put in effort, the chapter tests were pretty hard but they are open note.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Test heavy--Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: Very kind and offers so many resources to help you succeed
reviews.rating_tags: Accessible outside class--Clear grading criteria--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: Grade is based on homework and unit tests, all online and class attendance is optional. If you took AP calc in high school, this class is easy.

Sweetest teacher ever. I took Calc in highschool so this was the easiest class I took this semester. She teaches things so well and there are usually 2 homework assignments per week but none of it is hard. There is also two mini quizzes per week which you eventually are able to take twice. Not a hard class and a great teacher.
I never went to class because their were lecture videos. She would send out the kindest emails and always made herself available to students.

A lot of homework, although a good lecturer and professor in general, her tests and quizzes sometimes don't match what we learned in class and were sometimes harder than the homework she gives us. The average amount of homework is 3 pages with 10 questions each (online textbook) with 2 quizzes a week. It would help to go over the fundamentals.

Great professor, super sweet. Lectures are straightforward and easy to understand. Lots of weekly homework assignments, weekly quizzes, and chapter quizzes, but they only take like 30 minutes maximum to finish. Easy A as long as you do the work.

Adena was excellent at explaining concepts but her lecture examples were insanely basic and easy. The mini quizzes and chapter quizzes were very hard and often looked completely different than any of the classwork/hw. While I know this is a critical thinking class, a timed test doesn't seem like the best place to introduce a new type of problem.

I would say that Adena is alright, but its not an amazing class. I think I went to 2 in person lectures and then have been doing the rest asynchronously on my own time since. There's about 2 HW assignments a week, a 3 question quiz twice a week, exams are 10 questions and online. I took Calc in high school and have been doing fine, easy a

One of the best math teachers Ive had. Amazing guided notes for every lecture and will answer questions without making you feel dumb. Not too much homework and two mini quizzes per week with 2 attempts each. Overall amazing and kind
Do everything, I don't understand how she grades, even if you do well in homework you gonna end in B . I would prefer other professor for calculus if I take it again

Mini quiz (3q) & homework (20q) every wk, 5 ch. exams & required participation throughout semester by joining study group/SI Session/or posting commentary on Moodle. Relatively easy going course which has been prerecorded w/ helpful notes/ex. to help better understand concepts. Only stressing factor is the amount of videos we must watch at times.

Adena is definitely one of the kindest professors at UMass. The mini-quizzes can be difficult but other than that she gives a lot of opportunities to do well in the class and is always open to extensions and meeting with you one on one. The only thing is she won't round up your grade but that is the math department policy I guess!
reviews.rating_tags: Accessible outside class--Clear grading criteria--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: Adena definitely cares about her students and their success. It is very lecture heavy, I would often be overwhelmed by the amount of videos posted, but they are not mandatory. Participation does matter in this class but there are many ways to get these points. I usually thought mini quizzes were difficult but it didn't affect my grade too much.

Adena has been a great professor. The only downside is the Wileyplus interface, which isnt the best for homework imo. She's very understanding and gives plenty of time throughout the week to get help. Miniquizzes due everyweek and weekly 10 question exams. Only watched a few lectures because knew the material already.

Adena has recorded lectures that you have to watch to understand the material, especially if you do not love math. She does explain everything in really good detail and although it was asynchronous there were office hours with TAs everyday with flexible hours.

Adena is amazing, take her class! Her lectures are awesome and so easy to follow. She really wants her students to do well and is very lenient with giving extensions and helping in any way she can. This class is an easy A and was way easier than pre calc!

Professor Caden is one of the best professors I have ever have. Her class was the only class I did not mind putting in the work for. You have no cumulative tests which itself is a blessing. I got super sick and was in the hospital and she gave me extensions on everything and let me pick when to make up work. She explains everything so throughly.

Whoever is saying Adena isn't a good teacher or the class is hard probably just did not do their homework or watch the videos. The lectures are very well put together and you will easily get an A- (or better) if you simply do the work she asks you to do. If you get a 77% she will give you a B. If that doesn't sum it up then I don't know what will.
reviews.rating_tags: Respected--Accessible outside class--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: I failed calc in high school. Adena speaks like she's explaining to kindergartners, explains every topic in depth and the material is straightforward. Extremely easy to understand and get a good grade, just listen to the lectures and attend office hours if you're confused
I took this class online so it may be a little different than in person. She does a great job of explanations but I had to watch a bunch of youtube videos and did not completely love this.

This class has been a breath of fresh air since all my classes are online. The lectures are really easy to comprehend and, the mini quizzes help boost your grade. No final, so there is less stress at the end of the semester!

I took this class last summer. Calden is the best math Professor I have ever had. She is very methodological at teaching and knows how to make things memorable for her students. Take it and you will love it.

Adena's class is great! Her recorded lectures are really interesting and they make the concepts so much easier to understand. You are quizzed on every chapter and the questions are pretty hard. The final was a breeze, only covered basics. Participation counts like no other. I strongly recommend doing the practice problems in Wiley, very helpful.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Test heavy

reviews.comment: Calden is a great teacher. She provides a lot of examples in class and presents topics clearly. The tests can be tricky, but if you go to class and do the reviews it gives you an idea what to expect. Wiley is the worst, so definitely go to the tutoring center if you have trouble with the wileys.
reviews.rating_tags: Accessible outside class--Graded by few things--Hilarious

reviews.comment: Grade was based off homework and 3 exams. About 2-3 online homework assignments a week. Curriculum was relatively easy. Really easy if you've taken AP Calculus in high school. Went to 2 classes the whole semester and passed with an A.
reviews.rating_tags: Graded by few things--Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: If you have little to no background in calculus, please hold off on math 127. This course is made for those who have a decent background, even if she doesn't say it is. The lectures are very simple, but the tests are difficult for kids weak in math. She is great at getting concepts across, but she does not cover what is needed for tests and HW.

If you didn't take AP calc in high school, good luck. You take three tests worth 80% of your grade, and the homework very rarely translates to the tests. I put more effort into this class than any other and still did poorly. Calden is a nice person, but, in my opinion, does a poor job of explaining the concepts.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: I don't get the point of a class where the homework is nothing like the classwork and the classwork is nothing like the tests and the tests are nothing like the homework. It just comes around in full circle where nothing in this class correlates with each other. But Adena is a very nice and knew what she was doing but seriously fix this mess
reviews.rating_tags: Graded by few things--Test heavy--Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: Great teacher who is kind, sharp and caring. Show up to class and you'll do great.

Adena was one of the best teachers I had at UMass. She taught the material well, and also made sure that your grade reflects your effort. Most importantly, she cared about her students as people, instead of just grades.

adena is so sweet and funny and makes sure everyone understands the material before moving on. Wiley the homework platform sucks but she's trying to get rid of it. a hard class if you've never taken calculus but a lot of help available

She really enjoys giving group work assignments. This course only had 6 projects, but covered more than what is expected of a normal calc 128 class. She is very fair about everything happening in class. Extra credit if you all ask really nicely

A great lecturer. Learned more from her lectures than most math lectures. However, I found that self-studying with the texture was significantly more effective than the lectures, though this is no criticism of Adena. She is more than accessible when you need additional help, but assuming you self-study with the book and do the hw, you will be fine.

Adena is incredibly nice, and truly just wishes the best for her students, both in the classroom and beyond, and she really makes this known. She is always accessible whether after class or in office hours, and does an incredible job of positioning the material in a manner that is easily digestible,& will take the time to make sure you understand

Adena was the best math teacher that I've had to date. Her honors class seems like a huge challenge and it really is. The exams are take-home which sounds great, but they are pretty challenging. She gives numerous opportunities though to get extra credit. I got a 47/100 on the first exam and it eventually was upped to a 99.5 after extra credit.

Graded on online homework and a couple exams. She is a GREAT teacher but if you need extra help you have to see the TAs outside of class, which has proven difficult for me because my classes are in the afternoon during their extra help. Tests are pretty hard, but Calden will stop lectures to make sure everyone understands the material. Good class.

I once said Math teachers have no personality, but Adena proves otherwise. She doesn't have that boring math teacher voice that puts you to sleep. It's a tough course but she makes it easy to glide through. Kind of a lot of homework, but it's math so what else do you get graded on?
reviews.rating_tags: Respected--Skip class? You won't pass.--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: Adena is a great professor and a great person. She really cares about all of her students and makes it clear that she is there to help you succeed. While calc itself is hard it would have been far worse if I had a different instructor. If you have to take calc, take it with her.

Adena is a great professor who covers the material clearly. Exams are take home (for the honors section) and are some of the hardest exams I have taken to this point. However she is a super fair grader and wants everyone to do well, she grades easily and finds extra credit. There are also 3 group projects but she grades you based off contribution
reviews.rating_tags: ACCESSIBLE OUTSIDE CLASS--Clear grading criteria--GROUP PROJECTS

reviews.comment: Adena is honestly the best math professor I've ever had. Learned more in her class than I ever did in AP Calc. Her exams are straightforward and she assigns homework through Wiley. Her teaching style is very easy to understand and she's always up to answer students' questions.

She's brilliant at explaining the material. I've taken calculus before (which is why I found the class to be easy), but I used to struggle conceptually. This class really helped me understand what I didn't before. In my opinion, the homework wasn't too much. Do all the practise exams to study, and an A should be very doable.
Her final exam study guides have no answer keys. You're left guessing on a majority of them unless you sell your soul to the devil for the answers.
reviews.rating_tags: Respected--Skip class? You won't pass.--LOTS OF HOMEWORK

reviews.comment: Adena was a decent lecturer but the class was terrible. The homework were nothing like the classwork or the tests, the classwork was nothing like the tests or the homework, and the tests were way harder than what they should be. I took Calc BC in highchool so I had a huge advantage. If the tests were as easy as the practice ones, it would be good.
Really nice and loves to help students.
She conveyed the information well and gave multiple examples of each type of problem, making tests easy and very predictable. Lots of homework on WileyPlus but she is very flexible about late work.
reviews.rating_tags: LOTS OF HOMEWORK--TEST HEAVY--Would take again

reviews.comment: She posts her outlines to what she goes over in class online which is helpful but not everything on tests and hw is gone over in lectures. Every other class you spend the class working on problems which isn't always helpful.
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Tests? Not many--Tests are tough

reviews.comment: As a teacher, she's very good at explaining different concepts and does plenty of examples so you can make sure you understand the problem. As a person, she's extremely kind and doesn't get annoyed if you don't get something. When it comes to homework, keep track of the due dates. She gives you 8 attempts for every problem so it's hard to fail hw.
Good class, somewhat challenging. Only two exams so do well on them
reviews.rating_tags: Clear grading criteria--GRADED BY FEW THINGS

reviews.comment: Adena knows her stuff, and is one of the most well informed professors I've seen. She cares about everyone, and makes the material seem easy, and right when it's all going well, BAM, the exam happens. There is lots of homework, but it is not nearly enough to master the material. The exams are incredibly hard, but the HW grades can keep you alive.

She is super friendly and pretty clear in class. If you took calc in high school its a cake walk, if you only took through pre calc (like myself) its still pretty easy. Didn't show up to class at all after the first two weeks and still found the hw material and tests pretty easy.
reviews.rating_tags: Clear grading criteria--GRADED BY FEW THINGS--Caring

reviews.comment: Adena was always a joy to see. She is great at clearly explaining concepts and does examples with the class. I had taken calculus in high school and she helped me get a deeper understanding of it. Make sure you do all the practice tests she posts, it will help you for the tests! First test is fairly easy, second is hard, final isn't too bad.

As someone who struggled in high school and college calculus, Adena made it much easier. She is truly a great teacher and ensures that her students understand the material.
