reviews.comment: She is one of the best history professors in UMass. Her lecture is both interesting and straight forward. She will clear the confusing historical issues with her excellent grasp of key points. I enjoyed her lecture so much that the mandatory participation was never a problem.(The 50min lecture was too short for me).

She's really amazing, she's an absolute gem and really enjoys her topic. Great lectures, very informative and genuinely a great class. Takes attendance every day, we have in-class reading assignments but she warns you ahead of time and it's on the reading so it's easy. good speed on slides, exams aren't hard hard, but aren't too difficult.
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Skip class? You won't pass.--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: Never miss an opportunity to take a class with her. Absolutely phenomenal professor.

Professor Broadridge is a great professor. She specializes in the history of the Mongolian Empire and Genghis Khan. Beware though she is a tough grader and expects a lot out of her students. Her Middle East Gen Ed class is lecture based and she encourages student participation in class. If youre interested in Islamic history I highly recommend her

I was really impressed by professor Broadbridge's ability to make me actually enjoy a gen ed that I was dreading the thought of taking. Three exams make up most of your grade however she goes over the material before hand and provides various example answers of varying quality. She enjoys the material and knows it very well. Also no papers
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Clear grading criteria--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: I took this class to fulfill my History gen ed as a senior and it was ridiculously hard for a gen ed. The only significant grades in the class are the three exams and they cover monumental amounts of information which you will forget immediately after. If you are interested in this then she is great and is very knowledgeable but be prepared.

If you require Power Points, you won't get it with Prof. Broadbridge. She moves quickly with her lectures but is always willing to go back and clarify. She's incredibly kind and is very attentive in office hours. She will let you do rewrites- even if you do well. She's clear with what she wants. This is one of the best classes I've taken at UMass.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Get ready to read--Skip class? You won't pass.

reviews.comment: This class moves very fast, especially because the professor believes that most people are marginally interested in the class. When I took this class, exams were a WHOPPING 85% of the entire grade. THERE IS NO CURVE. Be wary of TA grading too. It doesn't hurt to double check your grades with her.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough Grader--Skip class? You won't pass.--GRADED BY FEW THINGS

reviews.comment: Amazing class, very interesting material covered in a clear manner. Professor Broadbridge makes an effort to ensure that everyone is on the same page, usually with "is this topic perfectly clear to everyone?" Beware, don't underestimate the value of the exams, as they are really the only significant grades, and graded in a tough manner.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough Grader--TEST HEAVY--GRADED BY FEW THINGS

reviews.comment: Her readings are all free from the library website, but she expects you to read them and be able to answer questions about them in class. But you literally only have to speak once during the semester and she'll give you credit for participation. The tests can be hard and it is a lot of memorizing but if you go to class you'll be fine.

I was apprehensive about taking this class, as I wasn't too enthused about the subject matter, but this professor is an excellent lecturer and inspires interest in the topic. If you are willing to do the readings and go to class, it's not too difficult, but you do have to work a bit for a good grade.

Expert on her subject and a great teacher.  Over 2 years after her class I still remember a lot of it.  I heartily recommend her classes with the caveat that shes a tough grader. I normally come out of upper level history classes somewhere between an A- and a B. I did not get those in her classes.

One of the best history teachers at UMass hands down. She has a great sense of humor and I (a terrible morning person) often found myself woken up and excited for her class. The tests are difficult (only a midterm and a final) and you will need to study. The readings are frequent but fairly short. An average workload. Great class, great professor.

I took this class to fulfill my history requirements, and found it difficult to understand some of the material. It was nothing I was interested in or had studied before, so the tests were difficult as well. She seems like a nice enough lady, but you can tell she finds the lower-level history boring also.

Excellent prof but a very tough grader. The workload was what I would expect for a four credit or honors course. However, I learned a ton, and she was very engaging. Plus, anyone who can successfully pull off a lecture while managing their two-year old because they couldn't get a sitter that day is impressive in my book.

This class is fascinating and Broadbridge is a great lecturer. She is, however, the hardest grader I have ever encountered. She flat-out told me she doesn't give As in her upper-levels. You will work incredibly hard.

Great professor. Class structure is clear and work is manageable. No overwhelming research assignments. If you do the readings, you'll do well. Readings are short and have questions to go along with them. Overall, pretty easy in comparison to other history classes but you still learn a lot. DEFINITELY would recommend.

She explains everything fully and has no problem going over things either in class or at office hours. It's test-based and there are occasionally short responses in class. Keep on top of the reading and study really hard for the exams.

Kind of appalled that this is classified as a gen ed. It takes a lot of effort. Attendance is mandatory, and exams are very detailed. She's very approachable though, and with the effort its possible to get an A.

Middle Eastern history is not an easy subject, but Broadbridge does a great job explaining the subject.  There is a lot of material that is covered for a 130 class, but if you take notes and do the readings you'l be alright.  If history aint your thing, avoid.  If you like history and the Middle East, I cant think of a better introductory class.

This class is awful. Long readings online, mandatory participation in class, tests are really hard, and you have to attend an outside event. During class you have to take notes from her lecturing - she speaks so fast and thinks that everyone loves Islamic history..worst HS gen-ed. Don't do it to yourself DEF NOT WORTH IT

Who ever says take this class is out of their mind. This is class was dreadful. If you have no prior knowledge on Islamic studies or are uninterested in this topic, DO NOT TAKE THIS CLASS. Very confusing woman, fast passed, oral notes. EW.

She does take attendance but you get two free misses. I would not recommend missing though as she gives notes all class and you'll miss a lot. The tests are somewhat difficult, but if you have good notes then you'll be fine. Great professor overall and very helpful. She gives weekly readings that can be tedious, but you can often skip those.

Attendance is not mandatory but I recommend that you don't miss a class because she gives lots of info in one class. But  class is very interesting. She is helpful and very clear. Lets you know when something should be written. Tells you exactly what she wants on the exam. 1 thing is that notes are in black board and test are not multiple choice

Broadbridge is one of the best teachers I've ever had. Homework is not huge, just do the reading. Prepare to have intense classes with tons of notes. 95% of test studying will be off class notes. I'd go to class totally lost on the subject, after an hour I felt like I had mastered it. Extraordinary communicator. She's no ****. Dont piss her off

She is so interested in Middle Eastern Hist and knows everything. Her lectures are always to the point, and you can always tell if she says something that you should be writing down. We always have a review day before exams which are extremely helpful. Just come to class, and don't sleep and you'll do fine.

Love her. A very intelligent woman who knows her subject. Incredibly CLEAR and HELPFUL. Wants to help her students more than anything. Manages to maintain people's attention but is not pompous at all. Readings not as useful - class sessions more important. I have tremendous respect for Anne, a really genuine and levelheaded teacher

Energetic, efficient, and lectures are "entertaining" to say the least. Her position regarding the history of the Middle East, however, is completely biased. Tries hard to "sound" objective, but anyone who knows the true history of the Middle East knows she is not. Many facts are twisted, downplayed, or left out altogether. BE CAREFUL.

Anne Broadbridge is the best professor I've had anywhere, ever.  Her lectures are clear and the information is challenging but straightforward.  You will work hard and learn a lot in any of her classes.
Anne is a great professor. Class is very interesting, lots of material for a 100 level course but she is clear and very fair. Highly reccomend it!!!

Prof. Broadbridge really knows her stuff, and is really clear on what she wants you to know and get out of her class. It's an interesting subject; I recommend this class for non-majors because she makes everything so crystal clear. She forces you to do readings and attendance is mandatory, and be forewarned: it's tough, but you learn a lot.

She's awesome! I hate hate hate history, but she got me to love the class. She's clear about what she expects, and is very knowledgeable. For all those non-history majors: I definitely recommend Broadbridge.
Firstly Broadbridge is a god! And the Crusades are ill. Take any class with this woman she is awesome!  Very witty abrupt lectures.

This class was great. The professor is very clear, even blunt at times, and teaches very well, especially in an intro class where some students have no background in the material. Study guides for tests are very thorough, and as long as you put in the effort, tests are easy. Great course for understanding history of modern issues.
She clearly doesn't have anyunderstanding of Zoroasterianism or other civilizations in middle east. Google can do a better job in these cases. Nice professor overall.

Amazing professor! She really knows and loves her subject. The class is a lot of work, but she is very clear about what she expects and her lectures are fun & interesting. definetly not an "easy A" class, but its great for those who are interested in middle eastern history and are prepared to do the work.
Open my mind?  Maybe if I could have opened my eyes. ZZZZZZZ

Stupid previous comment. Broadbridge is a great professor and is there when you need her to be. Clear lectures and she keeps the class very interesting. Yes, the class is exceptionally hard for a level 100, but like any other class figure out what you need to do and youll get a good grade. You will learn ALOT! in this class. It will open your mind!
worst teacher ever

Broadbridge is a great teacher. She is VERY clear and helpful. Her tests are challenging but they are not impossible. I learned a lot that helped me understand the current situation in the Middle East. 3 exams, 4 easy in-class papers, and an easy map quiz.
NOOOOOOOOOOOOOOOOOOOOOOOOOO
fantastic professor. she's interesting, so attending class is easy. she's just great all around. one thing that really stuck out, she learned everyones name. the class easily had 100+ students.
Do yourself a favor, take a class with Professor Broadbridge while you can.  Even if you aren't a history major, she's the best.  I love this woman

One of the best classes and best Professors I have ever had. Very hard, but at the end of the day you have really learned something! She loves her topic and now so do I! Always willing to help and answer questions. Very respectful of opinions that varied from hers IF you could back it up.
Very good teacher I never missed a class, class was pretty enjoyable, but there was TONS of information.. class is decently hard though

A hard class, but very interesting. She makes class fun, and always adds some unusual details to make certain events/people stick out in your mind. Three tests, no papers. Alot of reading, little written homework. Lectures are pact with info, so attendance is a must. Come to the review sessions!
She is one of the best professors on campus. She makes class fun and always interesting. Take as many classes with her as you can.
She is by far one of the best teachers I've ever had and shes WAY hot
Good professor
She knows her stuff more than any other prof. I have ever had!! She has a great sense of humor and always answers questions clearly.  I would definately take another class with her.  She is great!!

Master of her subject - she really knows her stuff. Has high expectations but is very fair and is a good teacher. Very helpful, very good advisor as well. Learned and was challenged a lot in the class and found it interesting.
Her lectures are highly informative and help in summing up the material at hand. She also has a great sense of humor that is founded on profound intelligence. I will miss going to this class!
I learned a lot of things in this class, which is uncommon now a days.  SHe is extremely intelligent, and has a great personality.  HIGHLY RECOMMENDED!!!

Broadbridge is wonderful - I'd take a class with her no matter what it was about.  She's very smart, and she makes it fun, because she's so passionate about what she's doing.  She's really helpful, and really nice
Great Prof.  She knows here stuff, and likes to teach.  I take her classes just because she teaches them.
Absolutely the best teacher I've ever had

I've had Prof. Broadbridge for 3 classes now.  She is an amazing teacher.  TAKE HER CLASSES.  You have to go to lecture and pay attention and study for tests but you LEARN THINGS.  It's what college education *should* be.
No Comments
She knows her stuff.
Fun professor; great personality, makes lectures interesting, is passionate about her area of study and is a wealth of knowledge about the middle east. fair grader, friendly and nice.
Knows her field extremely well and always willing to help students.
She's awesome :-)
always discusses interesting material, great prof

Lots of resources to read up on (often like 10+ pages).
Lectures are a little on the boring side but it's feasible to just be on your phone and look at the slides later.
Great professor :)
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Lecture heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: I had her for NRC 309. She did a great job at making our lectures not feel like lectures by making us get into discussions with small groups at our tables, sometimes doing mini projects. Homework was mainly just annotating and commenting on Perusall readings; tedious but pretty easy.  The course was somewhat difficult but expected for a 300 level.

this was a good class to take if you are interested in the workings of how policies are made! i loved that we got the option to actually experience "making laws" and used games to help our learning along. easy class; only two exams and most hw were reading assignments
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Clear grading criteria--Gives good feedback

reviews.comment: This class is a very fun setup because you get to sit at different tables throughout the semester and get to know different students. The only grades that come from this class are the 3 exams and the three review sheets that are connected. The exams are kinda hard but very doable if you go to class.

Professor Milman is absolutely wonderful. For the envisci major, this class is required. Her lectures are far from dull and there are a lot of opportunities for student engagement. She takes feedback from students and applies them incredibly well, and is easily approachable if you need help. Overall an easy class.

Professor Milman did a really good job teaching remotely. It was nice because she really tried to make the class as normal as possible and made an effort to connect us with other students in the class. The topics are mostly interesting, but could be a bit dry sometimes.

Probably my favorite class taken this semester. Prof Milman is so understanding and instead of forcing three exams in a shortened semester, she made 5 45 min mini exams. Her lectures are actually interesting and interactive. Instead of staring at a screen she has her students participate in group activities such as debates. Highly recommend!
reviews.rating_tags: Graded by few things--Group projects--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: This is a TBL class so there's group work. Her lectures are detailed but she's a good lecturer. There are random iClicker questions for attendance so you have to go to class. There are two tests that require a fair amount of studying since there is so much content in the class, but its easy to get a good grade if you study and DO WELL ON THE HW

Professor Milman made this class interesting and fun. I looked forward to it. Group work, class, activities, and reading quizzes are the important chunk of your grade. I took the class as honors and the projects she had us do made us very passionate about the subject of environmental policy. This was a class every major should be required to take.

Very enthusiastic and passionate about policy. 10 HW quizzes straight from textbook 3 exams (sorta hard especially the multiple choice parts) and class assignments done in table groups. Attendance is mandatory but never actually taken. Overall a pretty easy intro to environmental policy class-PS 1st month is just intro to policy.
hundreds of pages a week and diabolical grader
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Lots of homework

reviews.comment: This professor is a very nice guy; however, this class consisted of way too much work. This was a small class, of about 20 people, and at least 5 people withdrew from the class due to the workload.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Lots of homework

reviews.comment: People in my section complained about how much reading we had to do, though it was manageable, especially compared to similar gen-eds. Great guy, fair, arguably lenient, grader, overall a quality professor. Beware: the first half of the course was pretty slow, but it picks up, and even so, he's interesting to listen to.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Amazing lectures --Gives good feedback

reviews.comment: Professor Donson is a really nice guy interested in his studies, however he does not really care about his students. In my class there was lots of homework, lots of reading, and he was a TOUGH grader on papers. The most common grades he gave people in my class were 0-70%. He also went against the umass policies several times.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Lots of homework

reviews.comment: Terrible Teacher.

If you are reading this please do not take this class. Professor Donson does not provide you with adequate feedback on your papers. The class itself I imagined to be relatively easier based on the assignments but this is not the case. Please do not take this class it will ruin your semester.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Participation matters

reviews.comment: Great Professor with wealth of knowledge. A bit inconsistent  with expectations and at times it was frustrating to keep up with the reading and homework. I would defiantly would recommend Prof Donson for World War 1 /German history related interest's. Very Laid back demeanor which is great.

This is the worst class I've taken. Sample sentences consist of body shaming and domestic abuse in a way that is very triggering. Does not attend meetings with students that he sets. Grading is outrageously strict, and if you submit edits for additional credit, he'll forget to grade them. This is genuinely the worst classroom I've been in.

Professor Donson is particularly arrogant, unhelpful, and generally annoying. This course was structured in a way that made it so that actually working on the biography was nearly unfeasible. He bombards everyone with peer reviews, three entire novels (all 200+ pages and due a week after being assigned), and countless other worthless assignments.
Great guy who lets you rewrite assignments as much as you need. Has a clear passion about Germany and it really shows.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Gives good feedback

reviews.comment: Prof. Donson is a really nice guys and wants his students to succeed. That being said, he is a very difficult grader. He does give multiple chances to improve on essays, and homework is relatively easy and counts for a good portion of the grade. In-class participation is very important to him as well.

He's a good guy. There's a good amount of reading, and I felt like one of the textbooks was overpriced, but enjoyed the content of the class overall quite a lot. Any and all tests were pretty easy, and the guides for them were clear.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Get ready to read--Skip class? You won't pass.

reviews.comment: As a science major, I had to take a history to fulfill my DG and history gen Eds. Its a 300 level class but extremely easy. You dont really have to do the readings for discussion because the questions are graded on completion. The class itself is very interesting if you like history, but he is a little monotone. He does not allow cell phones.

Very good history prof, but can be monotone. If you don't have a real interest in whatever subject he teaches he's not for you. He is however a chill guy that wants to help you do well and will respect you if you respect him by handing in all assignments on time(aka give you a good grade). Just don't think he is "easy" or "hard" - he is fair.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Skip class? You won't pass.--LOTS OF HOMEWORK

reviews.comment: Professor Donson is not only a horrible teacher but a really mean person. He genuinely does not want you to do well in his class. He will go out of his way to get you in trouble and grade your work so that you do poorly. If you dont want to ruin your life than dont take this class.

The subject can be very interesting for those that are interested in the topic. Otherwise, you'll find the class to drag on. Definitely attend every lecture, and do all the homework. Also, rewrite your essays; it's an easy boost for your grade.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Get ready to read--LECTURE HEAVY

reviews.comment: Lots of reading and he gives us questions to fill out. Need to get a lot of books. When we did have to read books, he would also assign textbook readings. 2 short and 2 long papers. 2 exams. Tries to crack jokes in class. You do have to attend class, because his lectures will be on the exam. There are no recordings to watch later.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Skip class? You won't pass.--LECTURE HEAVY

reviews.comment: This class is pretty easy, but there is homework due every week. There are 5 one page papers and a midterm and final. As long as you do the work, you can easily get and A in this class

Prof. Donson is a mono-toned lecturer. I don't find his lectures interesting at all. There are 15-20 questions due every Friday that require reading from a book, your textbook, or outside reading he has provided. Not hard to pass, but pretty boring and time consuming even if you just do the bare minimum. Don't take if you have a big course load.

This is the class your high school teachers warn you about. The lectures are fast paced and the homework is intensive. A lot of material is covered and from many different perspectives. It is an interesting class in some aspects. The tests are very hard and the final essay is also a challenge. If you're taking this fora gen ed, pick something else
Donson is wonderful. He loves his topic, he's very learned, he's open to discussions with students, and was always around to discuss topics relating to Germany and beyond. Definitely recommend.

Donson is a really great professor. Overalls I enjoyed his class. There is a lot of reading, but assignments correspond to reading and they count a lot for your grade so that's a huge incentive to do it. He gives great feedback on essays you have to write, which are only 1 paragraph. Tests aren't hard as long as you study the guide. Overall the class is interesting, not an easy A. You have to do the work.

Warning: NOT A CLASS FOR THOSE WHO WANT AN EASY A.  Now that that's been said, this class should definitely be taken by anyone who wants to learn as much as possible about German history.  Professor Donson is super knowledgeable and helpful but he assigns a lot of reading and writing which makes up most of your grade.

DO NOT take this class if you're looking for an easy history gen-ed. He is very knowledgeable but assigns a lot of reading/questions every week. Sometimes readings don't match up with lectures and discussion sections are not helpful at all. The topic is very interesting but definitely not an easy class.

The best teacher I have had so far. He is so accessible and really wants to see you succeed. Sure, there is a llot of course work but it is always really interesting. There are so many opportunities to get a good grade in the class, you just have to try. I feel like im actually learning.

Lots of busy work such as reading assignments and short essays. Comprehensive professor that is fair and intuitive. Doesn't inject biases on subject matter. Overall a good course with a very viable instructor.

Very hard professor. He holds students responsible for knowing and understanding the material. This is one of the only classes at UMass that I felt was a true university experience. Don't take any of his classes if you expect to skate by.

The person who commented on GER 376 is dead wrong. He is an excellent professor, gives you EVERY opportunity to pass his class. Sure, attendance is mandatory - boo hoo, it's a 300 level college class - get a grip! Reading is intensive, but discussion is extremely helpful - and one of the MOST accessible profs I have had! Do readings, get an A

The lecture isn't bad, he talks fast, but its interesting.  The discussions are boring, and you have a reading assignment every week.  There are a couple essays a midterm and final.  the tests arent hard, but papers are graded hard.  You have to keep up with the reading every week or you will be lost, and there are a lot of books

This class is SO hard. Attendance is mandatory.  You have to do weekly assignments where the reading is over 100 pages. Tests are hard.  He gives you a 66 question study guide and only 5 of those questions are on the test.  It is a ton of work for a ged ed. don't take it.

Fantastic professor and really funny.  He truly makes the material he's teaching come alive and explains its relevance to today.  The readings are fascinating so discussion was really interesting, yet the class is still super easy.  Pay attention and do the readings, and there's absolutely no reason you won't get an A.

He goes in spurts; sometimes it's interesting, sometimes it's drudge-work. He assigns a LOT of homework which ends up being the only work I'm constantly doing. But the work is graded very easily; basically, do the work, don't worry about the grade. In lecture, be prepared to listen, because the slides aren't very useful.

If you keep up with the reading you'll do great.Bonus Quizzes on spark for each chapter of textbook There are reading assignments due every disc which you get 100 points for if you hand an attempt in, its not graded on the actual answers. You have to do 80% of them to get a 100. He has a sign in sheet for attendance, can miss 5 classes w/o penalty.
The man opened up my mind, like a birdcage, and let me free.  Now I soar in the heavens of thought and understanding.  Easily my favorite professor, I owe him everything.

DO NOT TAKE THIS CLASS FOR A GEN ED. I devote most my time to the homework and the study guide is nearly impossible unless you understand and write down everything he says in lecture. Lectures are terrible, puts up about 3 slides during class and seems like he is reading an essay to us. Fact after fact. Mumbles and can not even hear him well.

Amazing teacher! I took  holocaust class with him i learned more then i ever could have expected. He keeps discussions interesting and keeps you active in them. Lectures for 9 am are very interesting. if your not willing to do hw or get up for the class you will fail. Attendance mandatory and alot of reading and hw  but best class ive ever taken!

Donson never ceased to amaze me. I never got bored sitting in his class. It was a lot of work, no doubt, but if you put in the time, you got a good grade. He graded effort much more than knowledge, which is weird for a history or German professor, honestly... I highly recommend him. I'm taking another class with him in the spring.

Donson was incredible.  I will be taking modern german history with him in the fall.  He makes things interesting, and really brings the old stuff to life.  The work?!  The grading scheme was set up in such a way that it was impossible not to do well.  You also learn a ton.  Take a class with him!
Very boring class. Unbelievable amounts of work for a 101 level class. TA's grading is very strict and hard to please them.  Regret taking the class, but pulled off an ok grade.

Professor Donson is not only a nice guy, but he is also a great instructor.  The work load was not overwhelming at all, and his grading policy was extremely fair.  It also helps that he has a great sense of humor that made the sometimes boring material interesting to learn.  I would definitely take another class with Professor Donson.

nice guy..geeky but funny..he really tries to make the stuff interesting even tho its not the most exciting information to be learning. if you do the reading assignments, the essays, and go to discussions then u are garenteed an A regardless of the midterm and final..alot of reading and work but easy grades

This class is a rediculous amount of work for a level 100 class. The TA's have a strict grading policy and the teacher does not really teach, the TA's do all the work. I regret taking this class... I HAVE NO MORE WEEKENDS due to this class.
Way too much work for a gen ed 101 class. TA's grading is harsh and lectures are quite boring...overall I regret taking this class.

Awesome teacher. The material was tough but Donson was more than willing to help you in any way possible. You can tell he is sincerely interested in the job he does and also in the success of his students. Couldn't ask for much more from a teacher.

Extremely know ledged and passionate about the subject. Has a cute accent when he does authentic foreign pronunciations of words. Your effort usually works like a perfect machine; what you put in is what you get out of it. Helpful and extremely friendly to talk to. Maintains very generous office hours. Donson's da bawmb.

Donson's the man. As long as you try on most of the assignments, you'll get 100. Personally, I am terrible at history and I'm getting an A in the class. You can ask him and the TA's for help on essays which brings your grade up and theres even bonus quizzes you can do to raise your grade. He also throws some comical things into his lectures.niceguy

Holocaust.  I thought the class would be about the suffering of Jews, but it was more about the History of the Holocaust. No interesting movies. This guy is pretty tough, if you like to read...alot...the work is very time consuming as in 8 hours a week...but you learn alot and he is a really nice, and interesting guy!

This guy is the man.  The lectures are easy to understand and he has a lot of cool visuals.  Ungraded reading assignments count for like 40% of yr grade so do them and you'll do fine, esp since most of the midterm/final ?s come from them.
A lot of work if it's your gen ed, but Donson genuinely cares and you end up learning a lot.  fair, good teacher, good guy.

He is a really good guy who wants to make sure that students understand the material and do well.  He is always willing to explain things if you ask and makes time to meet with you.  The material is pretty tough, but if you commit to studying it really isn't that bad.

The exam was simple if you bothered to do the reading assignments, and he is more than willing to review your progress on the course papers.  He seems to really care about the progress of students in the course, but you *are* expected to do the work.
Very interesting, thourough and prepeared lecturer.  Enthusiastic, energetic, and funny.  A bit tough to keep up with , but worth it.  A great class for students who want to learn.

Donson is one of the few professors who has challenged me in my classwork.  He is one of the best teachers I have had in college. Both for his passion of the subject and excitement for teaching. In lectures I was entertained, educated and exorcised, of all those inner demons  (in a good way).
No Comments

There's a difference between a professor making us work hard to truly learn the material and one who just assigns a ton of irrevelant incoherent material, makes us memorize it ALL and then regurgitate it word for word on the exams.  His lectures are absolutely horrendous and he doesn't care.

As a professor he requires that you actually DO the work assigned, obviously not for everyone particularly those accustomed to the ease of skirting by.  Does have a tendancy to drone on, lectures may be a bore, but you will find you have learned something, that or failed miserably.

He sucks.  All he does is bombards you with trivial facts.  There's no point or direction in his lectures at all.  His exams are ridiculous and ask things that were neither in the reading nor covered in class.  He's goofy looking too.
No Comments

The man is nice enough but assigns way too much homework. Our midterm consisted of 15 questions for which he gave us a study guide of 85 possible questions. The class is way too hard to be a requirement for german minors. I would not recommend it.

He is the worst professor i have encountered in my college career. terrible lecturer who does not create any clear picture for the student.  he assigns tons of reading from which the student must teach themself. really snotty
No Comments

No SI, no resources, no study guides, no help outside class besides only one help session from the TA right before every exam. She flys through hundreds of slides and expects you to know it all. Luckily, the content of this class isn't very hard, but her inability to convey information effectively to students is what made people hate this class.

Professor Caicedo was amazing! She is very passionate about the topic and does a great job expressing that. The lectures are very dense with content and exams contain info from everything (lectures, homework, etc.), but you are allowed a cheat sheet which is very helpful. There are at least 3 extra credit points available which are super helpful.
HAD TO COME BACK!!! DO NOT TAKE THIS CLASS

This is the first time in my four years that I actually feel compelled to write a review for a class. DO NOT TAKE THIS CLASS UNLESS YOU ARE IN LOVE WITH PLANTS!!!!!!! Exams have no study guide and you are supposed to know basically all the content from about  200+ slides. She allows a notecard that cannot be typed out because ...who knows. painful

She is a very lovely professor. Exams were made in class for the first time in her teaching this class. She allowed a half-sheet cheat sheet. Exams were pretty easy and she gave back points. You are allowed to miss 4 classes without losing points. Overall, pretty average to easy class.

This class was easy, we were given a cheat sheet on exams and only had homework every other week-ish. No textbook, attendance is required because she uses echopoll for attendance. Cheat sheets are half a page double sided, I would recommend taking this if you need credit for upper level bio courses.

Dont take this class unless the only thing you have ever cared about is plants and plant history. This is quite possibly the most boring class of my life and she now has in person exams w a notecard and is conviced we do worse because we typed our notecards instead of the last 6 years when they were online open note. Extraordinarily boring.
reviews.rating_tags: Lecture heavy--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Exams were switched to inperson after add and drop. Did not curve the exams and spoke abt how students did better previously when it was clearly online. Speaks even after class time ends and people leave which doesn't even get recorded on echo 360. She's sweet but j cannot explain well imo even though she tries.

Prof. Caicedo is very caring and passionate about the subject she teaches. Her lectures move quickly, but you always have the slideshow and lecture recordings available if you miss anything. Her exams solely include information discussed in lectures and presented on the slides. Exams make up most of the course grade, but she offers extra credit.

the WORST class ive taken. would rather retake orgo than this. she waited until after add drop to tell us she's changing exams from online open note to on paper closed book exams. and then decided later that she's not letting us type cheat sheets anymore. doesn't realize that genuinely nobody cares about plants and just wants the bio requirement.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Lecture heavy--Test heavy

reviews.comment: Exams moved from online to in-person after add/drop, then the cheat-sheet rules changed after Exam 1 to handwritten only. No study guide; only 50+ fast slides per lecture. As a prereq student, it was hard to know what to study. Expected a chill class ended up my most painful one. Found the class unfair with all changes after add/drop she made.

She changed her exams from online to in person after add drop so no one could drop the class before she announced this, then said the average was lower so shes not letting us type up our cheat sheets anymore. She expects you to watch a mini lecture before each week of classes to add more content to the exams, yet our grades are going to get worse.

She is very passionate about plants and the class is quite interesting with the plant challenges and bringing plants into class. Attendance is mandatory, but the exams were online and open notes. There is a pre-lecture video and quiz every week, but the class is manageable and if you go into class prepared you will do great!

Clearly passionate about the topic, but that makes it painful for someone just taking it for bio reqs. The lectures are lengthy and detailed but attendance is absolutely mandatory (iclicker location services are on, so you literally have to be there). She tries really hard to keep engagement- I think she may move away from online exams.

Prof Caicedo is a great lecturer. You do have to come to class prepared, having done the outside videos and readings. She is all about making topics easy to understand she sometimes does fun in-class activities that get students involved. STUDY for the tests, they are not going to be easy just because they're open note and multiple choice.

Caicedo taught the first half of 335 and the class was very manageable. There were 4 online exams which make up 70% of your grade but there were no surprises on them. If you want an A I'd suggest at least lightly reviewing the material as if it were closed book bc looking for answers during the exams are a good way to run out of time.
reviews.rating_tags: EXTRA CREDIT--Clear grading criteria--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: AMAZING PROFESSOR! SHE MADE ME LOVE PLANTS

Prof. Caicedo is so sweet! She teaches at a great pace and it was actually more interesting to learn about plants than I expected; her passion is clear by the way she teaches. Grading is very exam heavy but they are online and open note. Do the plant challenges! They are easy and boost your grade. Definitely learned more from her than Prof. Hazen.

I love Dr. Caicedo! She taught the first half of this course. Open note exams that are easy to get a good grade on even if you miss class. 70% of your grade is based on exams, 30% based on quizzes (lowest dropped). I would absolutely recommend this course and professor.

The entirety of your grade is determined by your quiz and exam scores. Luckily, she drops the lowest quiz grade out of 5 and both the exams and quizzes are open note. You'll do fine in this class as long as you can take good notes, and since her lectures are recorded you can always go back and watch them to get anything you missed.

Although we are graded on very few things (quizzes and exams), she teaches the information very clearly and is more than happy to answer our questions. Very sweet overall and it was a pleasure having her for the first half of the semester :)

Dr. Caicedo is one of my favorite professors I've ever had. I think a LOT can be noted from how much professors try to adjust their classes with COVID/onlin, and she really tried! She was always ready and happy to answer any questions I had, and she was very understanding when mishaps arose online. Course is very difficult, but she made it doable!

Ana taught 1/3 of Bio 335. This course was taken remotely but Ana was awesome. She definitely had the most material but exams were super easy. She offered extra credit which could add up to 8 points on your exam. No HW and her quizzes were very easy. Just watch pre-lecture material. Kind and considerate, really interested in her students wellbeing.
reviews.rating_tags: Graded by few things--Test heavy--EXTRA CREDIT

reviews.comment: Ana is so sweet. You can see she cares about the students by the way she teaches. She always stops after each concept to see if anyone has a question and is very approachable. She was one of the profs for this class and the only one to offer extra credit (8 points). I'd be careful since her exam is a bit difficult and is worth 80% of your grade.

Dr. Caicedo tries very hard to make the class fun, but it's very hard. The tests aren't reflective AT ALL of the material in lectures/ slides and they are worth 50% of your grade. She wants very specific answers, but will give you broad general knowledge to work with. I would definitely not recommend taking this class unless you love genetics.
reviews.rating_tags: Graded by few things--Lecture heavy--Tough grader

reviews.comment: Do not take this class unless this is your last option! She goes over material in variables instead of actually numbers so it can be hard to follow. She is very nitpicky on the exams and homework with your answers! Homeworks are done in groups that she made. Some portion of the homework is based off online portion that isn't even relevant.
reviews.rating_tags: Graded by few things--Group projects--Tough grader

reviews.comment: Dr. Caicedo is a great professor, but 2 other profs teach it too. Don't take this class because it's not an easy A, it's more trouble than it's worth, and it's pretty boring. There are other plant classes that can fulfill your major requirement and are much more interesting. Avoid the stress and copious amounts of work. 0/10 would not recommend.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough Grader--Skip class? You won't pass.--LECTURE HEAVY

reviews.comment: She's fair in terms of giving students an opportunity to do well in her class. Attendance is mandatory via sign in sheet. All you need to know is the material on her slides. The textbook is supplementary to the lectures but not necessary. Overall great teacher and is very approachable for extra help or questions.

Great class. Everything you need to know for her exams are on the slides. Slides can be a little unclear but she will clarify anything. She is extremely nice and approachable. Top 3 biology professors I've had. Learned a lot and was far more interesting than I thought it would be. Would take her again
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Clear grading criteria--Caring

reviews.comment: I loved her. Both her slides and lectures are clear which is great for a class with dry material. She's kind and enthusiastic. Just pay attention in class and go over notes and clicker questions. iClicker for attendance, slides posted online. Teaches 1/3 of class so there's 1 quiz and 1 exam for her portion.

Great class.  Exams are straight forward, attendance mandatory (factored into your grade).  Homework is probably the most difficult part, but if you are careful and follow the math as outlined by the lecture slides you should be fine.  She is very picky about wording, but it's a 500 level class so it is what it is. MUCH better than other 500 levels

She's a nice woman, but this class is incredibly dull. She enunciates clearly but her actual explanations of material don't make any sense. She doesn't hold any review sessions or supply students with any type of review at all before exams. I wouldn't recommend this class unless you're really passionate about genetics.

Population Genetics.  Attendance is mandatory, but class is actually pretty interesting.  Half of thursday class devoted to current news story related to pop gen.  Easy enough if you pay attention and ask questions in class.  Worth taking!

Attendance is mandatory, has you sign a paper to make sure you were there. Weekly SPARK quizzes are easy grade boost & Thursday in class discussion is extra credit if you talk & contribute, HW is hard but she helps you with it. Tests are easy if you go to class and pay attention to concepts - all open ended and very generous with partial credit.

I wish I was as passionate about anything as this lady is about plants. She's funny and makes the material semi-interesting. This class is very dry. She teaches 1/3 of the course and her quiz and test are both fairly easy as long as you read/listened to the lectures. She posts lectures/audio recordings of her lectures online so don't go to class.
No Comments
no quizzes/tests/exams, attendance is required, the professor is nice and so are the ta, and you get assigned group tables

This class is super easy. As long as you do the homework and discussion posts, I don't see how you could not get an A. Attendance is very important, so try not to miss class. Prof. A doesn't really do much honestly. As far as I know, the TAs grade everything. Fun class.
No exams or quizzes. Only grades are 6 wellness Journals and 6 discussions, along with a project that is easy. Hard to not do well.
okay okay okay okay okay okay okay okay okay okay okay okay

such a good gen-ed to take. group based learning so if you get a good table you will be set. just a few assignments a week but none of them take a long time. attendance mandatory but really is not hard to sit through since so many breaks to talk and stuff

Would definitely recommend taking this class. Andrea is an amazing professor and really cares about what she teaches. I found the content to be super interesting and there are no exams or quizzes. There is a good amount of work outside of class but it is mostly busy work and isn't difficult just tedious. 10/10 recommend
Extremely time consuming class with tedious yet mindless homework assignments.

Easiest class I've ever taken. Professor and TA's all care about the course and want to genuinely make connections. Just show up to class and talk to your table and you'll be all set. HW is pretty much all busy work but easy to do. No exams.

Class was easy, although the wellness journals (hw assignments) felt like busy work and could take a long time to complete. You end up with the same table for the semester, and you need to participate and have conversations with them every class. She is a nice professor who cares about the course material. It's a good and easy Gen Ed

No quizzes no tests but homework assignments can take up to two hours. You don't do anything in class so it can be very boring but it is an easy A for 4 credits. Recomend taking if you need the credits but don't wanna put in lots of work.
The easiest class I've ever taken. The class itself is boring but so easy. Definitely take it if you need the gen ed requirement.

This is a good gen ed or class to take for credit, very easy and straightforward. Attend class and do the few assignments plus an individual project assigned throughout the semester and you'll be in good shape. Team-based learning and a lot of discussion but if you can take this class.
reviews.rating_tags: Clear grading criteria--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: For my body my health you WILL get an A if you show up to class. NO EXAMS OR ESSAYS. graded on showing up to class and turning things in on time. small amount of hw, its all busy work. you can bs most of it. class is very boring but worth it for the diversity credit. pray for a good table group tho.
Easy Easy Easy gen ed. You have like 6 assignments 1x week, and 1 big assignment. It is rlly boring but mad easy so I would take it as an easy gen ed.

very easy, no exams, 6 "wellness journals" (homework assignments) and one semester long project. homework was super easy but very time consuming. grades depend on your TA, for some reason mine thought i had a learning disability. i would have this professor again but not the TA.

(I think) easiest class in UMass. You come to the class and do some activities with your table of 8 people. Assignments are easy and based on completion. It was fun. I'd warn that attendance is strict (long make-up assignment for absences) so don't take this class at a time you might not make it to the class often.

Fun and easy for a gen ed. we sit at tables in the classroom and are with the same group all semester. our table also had our own TA who grades everything and most of them are so nice and chill. We learned a lot of interesting things and did fun activities like a Tik Tok and scavenger hunt. no exams, one weekly journal and discussion post

This class is a super easy gen ed. No exams, one journal a week and one discussion. Attendance is mandatory but if you have a good group it isn't that bad. Easy A, highly recommend this class. Andrea is super nice as well.

This class is less about her and more about youre table, so if your group is social, you'll have a good time. There is quite a bit to do outside of class but its relatively managable and nothing takes more than 30 mins. There are some assignments that require doing somthing beforehand so I wouldnt reccomend waiting till the last minute.

This is a good Gened if you need one. Group based discussions which can make it hard since no one really wants to participate. Assignments are straightforward. You won't learn very much - it felt to me like a high school health class at some points. A little boring, and they are strict about technology. She is friendly.

SO. MUCH. HOMEWORK. insane amounts. but ig it's fine considering there aren't any exams in the class. the class is fine, but she makes us do a lot of group activities which is kind of annoying when everyone in the group collectively doesn't wanna work in a group y'know? she's nice, the TA's are nice. lectures are kinda boring, but you do learn alot

Super easy DU gen ed class. Had some journal homeworks and a health behavior change project which were all easy. Classes can sometimes feel like a drag and attendance is required but worth it for the easy A. Lots of group work but never any difficult work. Would recommend!

The class material itself isn't boring, which is awesome. The lectures are usually composed of the professor lecturing, then leaving you to discuss in groups, and there are some group activities, so it can be pretty fun if you get a chill group. There's like two assignments a week that'll take 1-2 hours max, and a journaling project. Chill A.
Easy A, nothing more nothing less. I will say while the class was kinda boring, it was lowkey better than just some lecture where the professor drones on and one about stuff.

The easiest class you'll ever take. 6 discussions, 6 journals, and 1 easy paper at the end of the semester, plus attendance. The material is a little redundant and some of the group activities were just cringe-worthy, but overall the best option for 4 credits at UMass. If you actually value learning stuff this isn't the class for you though

The professor is amazing and caring. This class is an easy A and actually interesting. Even though my class was an 8:30am class, I actually did not mind it because I enjoyed the class. There are no tests or quizzes and only 6 wellness journals, 6 discussion posts, and 1 project in total and all easy. Really recommend this class I would take again.
6 written assignments, 6 discussion posts, and 1 project, all fairly straightforward. Attendance is mandatory. Nice class to knockout a gen-ed requirement.

While the class is easy, it is so incredibly BORING. Attendance is taken and a huge part of your grade. Electronics are supposed to be put away and if you're caught with them out, a TA will mark it down and your grade will suffer. The assignments were fairly easy if a little bit tedious. She's a nice prof, but just so so so boring.

This class was easy and good for a GenEd credit, but BORING. Not allowed to use technology during class so it can be hard to make it thru a 1.5 hour class. But, very easy and interesting and she makes it fun to learn. Only a few easy assignments, one paper, and no tests or quizzes.
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Clear grading criteria--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Prof Ayvazian is great! Her lectures are awesome and I learned so much. The class is very easy; 6 journal entries and 6 discussions, as well as 1 project with a short paper. She makes the class interesting and engaging, and she really cares about her students. No exams in this class, and as long as you put in the effort you will get a good grade.

MBMH is a good class to learn about simple and important aspects of health.  In this class, you have assigned seats and discuss with peers throughout the class. If you have 6 absences you fail the course. The homework is easy with a health project, wellness journals, and discussion posts. There was barely any work in the class. Easy but beneficial

This class if great if you need a GPA booster or a DU gen-ed requirement. The projects and discussions are super easy while having no exams. Not going to lie, the lectures can be kind of dry and boring. Some of the things she says can be political and she makes some of the stuff she says sound "groundbreaking". Overall, it is a good and fun class.

This was a good introductory course as a freshman at UMass. If you show up and do the work, you'll get an A. You have assigned seats and talk about topics every class with the 8 other people at your table. Low pressure class, just participate with the people at your table. Most of the homework is wellness journals, discussion forums, and projects.

grade depends on TA, however, the work is SUPER easy. it feels like im in middle school during class because of what she makes us do (draw our thanksgiving break, etc). This class is the easiest class ive ever taken in my life and im not even lying. Extremely easy A even if you dont get a good TA. the hw is easy and there are no quizzes or tests

very enthusiastic and wants students to succeed. Class is very discussion based and set up in tables that you reflect on basic health and wellness. No exams, no quizzes, only reflective journals and occasional projects. If you keep up with assignments, its an easy A. Would recommend this class!

Lots of reflection on just basic habits and the everyday stuff you do and you kinda do a project where you try and cut one small bad habit or build one small good habit and try and make little improvements on your life. Solid in terms of a pure nutrition class and also teaches just your basic be-a-decent-human stuff to the kids in the class.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--So many papers

reviews.comment: Ayvazian is an extremely caring professor who shows her students she cares for them in many different ways. She is constantly there to give advice or to help any student in need. Her MBMH class is easy as long as you show up and turn in your work. No tests, the only homeworks are opinion based journals and discussions& the final is an easy project.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Graded by few things--Caring

reviews.comment: This class is extremely easy but very helpful. Highly recommend this class if you need to fulfill DU requirement but don't have plenty of time.

reviews.comment: This class is an easy A. Journal entries and group discussions are easy. Just show up to class for participation, attendance and do your assignments. Very straightforward to get an A

Very easy class. If you can't pass this class then I don't know what to say. Easy grader. Show up for participation, discuss in your groups, and do the writing journals and discussion posts (EASY). Easy projects. Respect your assigned TA, they grade your work most of the time. I took this course online, it may be different in-person.
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Skip class? You won't pass.--Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: TAKE PUBLIC HEALTH 160 YOU WILL GET AN A AS LONG AS YOU GO TO CLASS. Such an easy class like if you need a DU or a random class for credit TAKE IT!
Extremely easy A- just show and you will pass. Homework once a week and 2 "projects" (so easy). Really suggest Andrea and this class. Don't use your phone during class or skip- major overall grades.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Skip class? You won't pass.--EXTRA CREDIT

reviews.comment: Easy A! Lectures can be boring and you have a lot of discussion with your tables but its not bad. Easy grading done by TAs. Attendance is mandatory and counts towards your grade so as long as you show up and hand in your homework you will get an A. Two short papers but I got a 100 on both because they are easy.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Graded by few things--EXTRA CREDIT

reviews.comment: Extremely easy class, great GPA booster, literally do the bare minimum and get an A. The only downside is the pure and utter boredom you have to deal with each class. Attendance is mandatory and the policy is extremely annoying. You will lose points if the absence is not excused. And don't look too bored in class, because the prof notices!
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Skip class? You won't pass.

reviews.comment: Public health 160 is the ultimate easy A class. You legit have no tests or quizzes. You have to write a journal entry every week, but if you make the word count, you get an 100. I didn't learn anything in a whole semester. She lectures as if she's super profound, but if anything she sounds out of touch with reality.

Literally just show up and pass. This health class didn't teach me a single thing, I just kind of faked everything and got an easy A. The professor acts like everything she says is profound and monumental, and sometimes it seems too dramatic. There's no tests, so it really is an easy class as long as you can stand the boredom.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Participation matters--Skip class? You won't pass.

reviews.comment: She's so sweet! This class is an easy A!! All group work and reflection journals. Only two big paper but they were only 2 pages each. Life changing class!! I recommend it to everyone it's so easy and you learn so much

reviews.comment: She is very nice and knowledgeable. It is easy to do well in this class as long as you do the work and show up. It really is like a middle school health class, but you should see what you can get out of the class and take the time to self-reflect.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--SO MANY PAPERS--Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: I really liked this class! A lot of people go in with a bad attitude so they don't gain anything from it but it really is full of valuable information. It is fun, goes by quickly, and makes you evaluate your habits. Although there are a lot of journals, they are never hard and are good for reflection. Overall I really like the class.
She is a very nice lady, but the class is absolutely useless. It is an easy A as long as you show up and do the journal entries. Feels like a middle school class

The most useless and meaningless course I took. You will learn nothing in her PUBHLTH 160. And course, it is very easy for you to get an A if you can finish all the meaningless and awful journals. By the way, she put many journals due on days during final exam days, which means your review plan for final will be disrupted by this useless course.

Lecture is kind of boring but very easy stuff, lots of group discussions to keep you awake for an 8:30am class. Points are easy to get if you take  the reflection journals and discussion forums seriously.

Very sweet lady and very passionate about the subject. Class is easy, however it's frustrating that attendance counts for most of your grade. You don't even get 1 or 2 "free" classes to miss. Team based learning class.
no test, essays or homework really other than the occasional journal and discussion. Heavy on group work and projects
Easiest class I have ever taken. However if you value your money and time don't take this class because you learn nothing. No tests, instead you have in class group activities and reflection papers.
Neal is the best, great guy, I wish he would teach ECE244 instead of raj :(

HIS section of the course is amazing (lectures + exams). His notes are so detailed and make the content digestible, I just wish he had some example problems in lecture because he and raj were not on the same page. This is one of the only classes were I can confidently say I learned and retained the information in, he's incredible at teaching.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Amazing lectures --Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: One of the best ECE profs. Lectures can be a bit boring, but he genuinely wants students to succeed. Super approachable, and his office hours helped me clear doubts and go beyond the syllabus. Always greets with a “Hey, how's it going?”—makes him really easy to talk to.

My favorite professor in UMass ECE. Not my favorite lecture style because he focuses so much on the concepts and I could use more examples, but he's great for advice, remembers students/names, and is the warmest, friendliest engineering prof I've had anywhere. It makes my day better anytime I see him in the hall and he says, "Hey, how's it going?"

Anderson is a great professor. His discussions are better than lecture for 221. He's an expert at clearing up confusion and he does great examples that are relevant to the exams. I found many times that if I was confused by Ciesielski in lecture, Anderson had a way of explaining it in simple terms that made it all click.
Once I went to office hours with a lot of doubts but not specific questions. He was like, "Let's change this, you will understand this" He is always willing to help students.

One of the best. Dedicated to getting the majority of the students to understand the material (computer guts...awesome but complicated stuff), and he really knows how. Great pair with Tessier. Go to him with any question. Also Honors advisor.
The amount of info this guy stores in his head is scary.  He is a wizard.

Anderson is by far the best professor I had in all four years of engineering.  He knows more than most human beings ever hope to achieve.  He is a nice guy, very fair, and very approachable.  He could make any class seem easy.
AWESOME teacher.
Really great discussion teacher. Go to discussion, you will learn more than from the boring lecture
Only had him for discussion. Easily the best professor I've ever had. Go to every discussion with him and you'll do good in the class

Neal Anderson is a great teacher. Very clear in his course. He is so popular in engineering dpt. I very want to tell him something which is that he very looks like Simpson, but I am just affaid to tell him. Anyway, he is one of best teacher in umass. If you hate him, you will like nobody in umass. Great teacher!
Professor Anderson was an incredible professor. His office hours were extremely helpful as well as his non-academic advice.

He clears everything up. period.

Superb professor!
Excellent guy, I wish he taught Electronics, or Fields and Waves. Great notes, very straight-forward tests, one of the best ECE profs around
Excellent professor, notes are enough to study..never needed to open the book...his daughters good luck is always with u before any test..
great teacher can explain topics very well.
Great Guy
very clear and helpful
very descriptive, clear, and concise

This guy is great! Very helpful and can explain things easily, plus he's a lot of fun in discussion. A++++

always helpful in discussion and office hours
Great professor-- always prepared and easy to understand.  Helpful too-

He was not a bad prof for sure. But the way he organized CS 311 class was pretty awful. Exam was around 65% of the grade, which is pretty high compare to others. Homeworks are very long and doesn't count that much. I wish the homeworks and quizzes were counted more. Also hw was graded super slow and criteria was very vague.

Tests are about 75 percent of the class grade so the homeworks that take many hours don't really count for anything. In the lectures he never solves or understands his own examples well enough to be able to teach algorithms and offered no late days which is brutal because if the homework is one minute late its a zero. Wait for a different professor

He definitely knows his stuff. Ask him a question and he'll give you a clear answer. However, for Algorithms, the material he was teaching was really intense and difficult. Sometimes, he'd go too fast and I'd get lost. Some concepts are tricky to explain, and that's where he stumbled, but he's a good professor otherwise.

reviews.comment: Akshay is an ok professor, but I found the Algorithm Design textbook to be more helpful for this class. I struggled with the first third of the material, but by the final I ended up feeling confident with the stuff. Can't recommend taking this class with this professor, but the textbook is good enough to make sure you do alright.

Course was a mess for the most part. Lecture wise, he is no good and often trips up over himself and his lecture slides. Luckily the book and MIT OpenCourseWare exist and make learning on your own very manageable. However, going to office hours, he is clear and concise. Difficult homework and doable exams. Skip the class and learn on your own.

While the long and somewhat difficult homeworks (it's not too bad since he gives out answers in office hours) should be weighted a little higher, and the exams could be a bit more consistent in difficulty, I think Akshay does a good job of teaching difficult material. Lectures are difficult to follow without preparation, but this should be expected

The homework is hard, but he responds really quickly on Piazza. (like within 30 minutes most of the time) It's manageable unless you don't start until the last minute. Midterms are inconsistent in difficulty.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough Grader--Skip class? You won't pass.--LOTS OF HOMEWORK

reviews.comment: Akshay's explanations and examples are pretty clear, and he does a good job of answering questions. His sense of humor keeps lecture from being too dry. That being said, the midterms have had some iffy questions, which is unfortunate considering they weigh so heavily. The homeworks take a good deal of time to complete and can be challenging.

Homeworks count for nothing and take many hours, lectures go over extremely basic concepts and then we are expected to calculate and prove exponentially harder problems. Exams range from unbelievably easy questions to extremely complex proofs that might as well have been homework questions. He's not ready to be a full-time professor.

Akshay is one of the best CS/math professors I've had. He's always willing to clarify concepts and repeat himself/explain something differently if he sees the class doesn't understand it the first time. Algorithms is a pretty tough class, but Akshay manages to make it manageable. Also a pretty funny dude.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Hilarious--GRADED BY FEW THINGS

reviews.comment: It's hard to be mad at this guy cause I think he's actually trying but man is he incompetent. The only reason he could give for taking this class was that it might be useful for interview questions. The homework is very hard and you will not learn much from it. I learned more from the TAs in discussion than in his lectures.

One of the best ECE professors. Charismatic, intelligent. Midterm average was low, 40-50 region. This was expected and intentional for some reason. No clear explanation of how test would be scaled. Dropped the class because of anxiety about grading. Many students get homework answers from Chegg. This class needs a change but nice prof. Don't cheat.

Read the textbook and do practice problems. His lectures are very dry and powerpoint-based when they should be more rooted in examples and problem solving. Midterm was a nightmare then the final was based off the practice exam.

Very nice and funny guy but also a very boring professor. His style of teaching is showing the derivation of stuff through slides with occasional blackboard drawings.  Wished his class was more example problem based. Also doesn't help that the material can easily get confusing. Be prepared to read the book to follow along.
He actually teaches like a normal person idk how to explain it but he swears so much and is so real in the best way possible. Hard class but the way he teaches it is great
Same guy here. Also took a picture with him and his fish tanks. 10/10 experience.
Met this guy once. Seems like a chill guy. 10/10

Honestly disagree with his ratings. He is a nice guy, content is hard but it's a 582 level class what do u expect. He provided study guides that were nearly identical to exam so it's 100% manageable despite being open response if you just study that. I find the reading quizzes to be harder than exams. Lab fairly easy. Great lecturer imo
Just don't take any of his classes, does not know how to communicate and his exams and grading are just ridiculous, wouldn't recommend
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Test heavy

reviews.comment: This class was a lot more challenging this expected. There was so much information to memorize and just the overall content was not what I was looking forward to. Exams were hard overall and required a lot of studying. Some cool topics and really nice professor maybe just was not for me.
Lots of memorization so review and study a head of time. Study guides are provided that outline everything that could be on the exam. Exams are fair and multiple choice.
reviews.rating_tags: Clear grading criteria--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Lots of material, tests are worth a majority of the grade, no corrections or real extra credit (only when test averages were low) as well as a recorded group poster project.

Craig is a cool chill dude, funny at times. There aren't a lot of grades so you need to do good on exams. Exams are very difficult and detailed (all MC). Use the study guide and ask ?s before exam. Not an interesting class unless you're actually interested in evolution.

Craig is hilarious and this makes his lectures very entertaining. Only downside to this class is that there is only exams, weekly quizzes, and a poster project for points. Basically no homework besides for the quizzes (they take like 20 mins) and attendance is not mandatory. Seems like a really cool dude, I bet he's a secret stoner.

Craig's exams were hard, all short answer or essay questions, and he's a tough grader. Exam scores brought my grade down even though I did great on the reading quizzes and labs. The class material was interesting and the lab section was fairly easy, just be prepared to study hard for exams. You'll have to memorize quite a bit.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Albertson is the GOAT; He is entertaining person and lecturer; passionate about what he does; cares about student success! Class has lab, good exams and creative paper; basically Bio 280 taught in a fun way! For upper level/IE I highly recommend! hard work required to get an A but it is possible!! Takes time to host review sessions! TAs helpful!

Professor Albertson is a nice guy, really smart, and is obviously passionate about what he does. However, this class is really about 10 steps up from any other biology class I've taken at UMass. If you love biology and really want to dive into its depths take this class cause it was cool, but be ready to read professional, confusing research paper
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Skip class? You won't pass.--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: Worst bio professor I've ever taken. Lectures are super long, boring and I've fallen asleep in a few of them. Every class there was a quiz on a bunch of difficult papers that had to be read more than once to understand. I got burnt out pretty fast in his class. He's a nice guy and really tries his best but it just didn't make the class interesting.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Lecture heavy--Tough grader

reviews.comment: Prof Albertson is the best! Of all the bio professor I have had none have been more engaging and cared about me. He makes study guides for the exams and hosts review sessions. As long as you do the study guide, your fine. Also pretty nice guy and makes things interesting in lecture. Engaging, funny, most people end up w/ B+-A

Craig Albertson is the best professor that I've ever had. His style of teaching is not just about memorization, he teaches concepts and ideas. He is very approachable and truly cares about his students. I was genuinely excited to go to his class and I learned a ton. If you are a biology major at UMass, his class is a must.

I had him for 280 as well and got lucky there because the material for 582 was 90 percent identical to 280. There is a lot of material, so take good lecture notes. Some of his slides just have pictures, though he provides some text but I really recommend listening well and jotting down as much as you can. 2 exams, and 1 paper to get creative!

I had Professor Albertson for Bio 280 and Bio 582 and he is easily one of the best biology professors at UMass. Albertson's lectures are engaging and so easy to listen to I actually looked forward to attending his class. Neither course was easy, but if you put in the time and go to class you'll have every opportunity to succeed!
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--ACCESSIBLE OUTSIDE CLASS--Hilarious

reviews.comment: Prof. Albertson really wants all his students to succeed. As long as you do all your online quizzes and assignment, it's relatively easy to get a good grade in this class. This class does require a bit of memorization but he tries to make the class as clear cut as possible. As long as you review lecture slides and go to class, you will pass.

There is a lot of memorization involved, but if you put in the time and study, it's not too hard to get a good grade in this class. Prof. Albertson makes the material interesting and is a very funny person; I definitely recommend taking this class with him

Professor Albertson has been my favorite professor thus far. He is a funny and likeable person, and he gives you exactly what you need to get a good grade in the class. Study and you will do fine. He does NOT try to trick you on quizzes or exams, very straightforward questions all coming from the lectures. All lecture slides are posted online.

the second exam had a lot of memorization but he's really nice and understanding about it and there's lots of grade boosters. he's really passionate and a great lecturer. if you put in the effort its a great class.

Evolution is one of those requirements you try and avoid, but Dr. Albertson tries to make it fun. The course is somewhat intense and requires a lot of memorization of lineages and organismal developmental. The moodle quizzes and virtual labs really boost your grade, though the tests were a bit more difficult. Study and attend lectures to get an A!

I loved loved loved this class. Dr. Albertson is HILARIOUS and so great at making the material interesting and valuable. He goes fast in lectures, so make sure you take notes on what he's saying, but other than that he was amazing. One of the best professors I've ever had. He also doesn't require a textbook cause he thinks its a waste of money!

This class was great! Attendance was not required, but it will definitely get you a great grade. Albertson was good on clarification on any confusion. The class is a LOT of material, but most of it was understandable. He's a funny guy, and quite handsome. I definitely recommend 280 with him than the other professor. Overall, I enjoyed it a lot.
he's a smart and is knowledgable. Try to clear your concepts during the office hours. If you do so you're good to go.

Professor Linot did an incredible job in his first semester.  For the first half of the semester the class was taught by another professor and Dr. Linot was there for each and every class. He was very knowledgeable and even though exams could be tough he had a very generous curve for the class.
P.S.: very responsive outside of class time.
He is nice but the final he wrote was diabolical. Very smart man but forgets that we are not experts like him.
First time teaching, great understanding of fundamentals, lectures were kinda hard to follow, and difficult topics were not made easier through lectures

One big group project, but you can't work solo given to you the whole semester that isn't due to the very end and two exams with an optional final she's mad chill and want you to succeed take this class if you need bio requirements

Akiko is overall an awesome professor. She goes through lectures relatively quickly and ends some 30-45 mins early. Only 1 problem set per week with 12-14 multiple choice questions. Only 2 exams, and one final project. Each week, one lecture is content, the other lecture is problem set time. Walks around and checks in with students.

One of the best professors I've had at UMass. She cares about students, and is very accessible in and out of class. Usually, part of a lecture is spent on completing the weekly homework, where you could ask questions. Tests were very fair with an optional final, all of which allowed for a cheat sheet.

Prof. Okusu is genuinely one of the best professors I've ever had. Her lectures are interesting and easy to follow, and she prioritizes group work and collaboration in class. She is also very supportive in the laboratory section, as the second half of this course involves an independent research project. She truly wants her students to succeed.

Wonderful professor and super sweet.
