Relatable and definitely wants to see you succeed as long as you put in effort, especally in the lab portion of the class (akiko if you are reading this thank you for a wonderful semester) :) Made ecology really fun (I typically don't prefer that portion of biology much).
GOAT Professor super nice. Maybe have to learn a lil by yourself but deal with it cuz she's goat

Any negative comments on her are cap, she is by far the best teacher I've had at umass so far. Super interesting professor and an amazing human being. She was insanely supportive of me when I opened up about some of my personal struggles and regularly checked up on me throughout the semester.
Really nice person and will do her best to help you get a good grade, 3 midterms but you get to retake them with help to boost your grade

This was a good class and Prof cared about her students doing well. If you put in effort, you will be fine. Her lectures can be confusing, but if you watch them back on echo360, they make more sense when you break them up. Would recommend!
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Lots of homework--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Akiko is the sweetest person ever, and she has your best interests in mind. Her tests are fair, and the homework she gives isn't crazy. This semester, there was a final project and an optional final exam to improve your exam average. There are extra credit opportunities every week. I could not recommend a professor more.

Akiko is the best and most caring professor I have had while at Umass. This class is super interesting and she really cares about her students. The sweetest lady and wants you to do well. The material is relatively light, weekly quizzes and discussion papers and you must attend all classes and labs!

Very caring teacher that clearly loves the subject. Downside is that it's pretty hard to prepare for the exams as there isn't much practice and they can ask some tough questions. While she's accessible in person, she isn't really accessible through email. Make sure to ask to see your exam as she won't hand them out until you see them.

Akiko is awesome. She is seriously so kind and wants her students to succeed. Marine bio lab is also super interesting and its in groups. In class assignments are exactly what we went over on the slides and the lab reports are easy enough. Shes easily accessible outside class as well. 10/10.
She's a queen need I say more?

Akiko is a great professor! Lots of collaborative work and exams get a double-sided cheat sheet which is great. I have MW class, M is lecture and W is a lecture wrap-up then free time to work on the problem-set due Sundays with the people around you. Not a super challenging course, would definitely recommend!!
reviews.rating_tags: Group projects--Amazing lectures --Graded by few things

reviews.comment: This class comprises of weekly quizzes and three exams, including the final. The silver lining is that they are all online. Attendance is recorded. Akiko runs through her lectures quickly, but you only really need to know main idea anyways, as assessments are usually applications of the concepts. I would reccomend reviewing the TAs lecture notes!

There are online weekly quizzes every Friday (which are not too bad since they are open note and on the lecture material from that past week), optional extra credit almost every week, and then a total of 3 online exams. This is honestly a really good course to take, all of the material is online, so every test is open notes. Would reccomend

She is very bad at explaining the material and just reads off the slides. She also goes very fast, the class itself is all online exams. If you take this class, make sure you have friends to work with on the take home tests.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Lecture heavy--Test heavy

reviews.comment: She is the single sweetest professor I have ever seen in a classroom. She is so nice and accommodating and very flexible. She is such a good communicator as well. the exams are however always so hard and the stuff was not mentioned in the lectures at all.

I think Professor Akiko is the best Professor for an Introduction to BIO class at Umass, such as 152. She tries her best at her lectures using examples and uses case studies. She highlights the main point on what you have to focus on the most. HOWEVER, her exams are tricky and can be somehow heavy, so you have to be able to understand the material.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Beware of pop quizzes--Test heavy

reviews.comment: She is such a sweet women and her lectures are easy to understanding and follow along. she also does TA problem set days which are great. the only thing that was super frustrating with her class is the exams were so hard because most of the material she put on the exam was not in lecture.

Akiko gave me the easiest bio class I'll ever take. Evolutionary biology is easier conceptually but Akiko is more forgiving than any other professor you'll meet. The two things you're graded on are problem set sessions every Friday (attendance is optional) and exams which are mostly very straightforward. She's also very sweet and accommodating!

Prof. Okusu is a great choice. She's very nice and accommodating, and it's always a pleasure to go to her classes. As long as you attend classes, take good notes, and ask for clarification whenever needed, you should be able to do well in the class.
reviews.rating_tags: Respected--Accessible outside class--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Very passionate about the subject. Very kind and understanding.

I went into this class excited and hopeful after reading all the positive reviews, yet Akiko has been my worse professor yet. Im ending the year with A's in all my classes (including organic chemistry and cell/molec bio), yet barely scraping by in this class. Her exams are 10 times harder than what she teaches. The only people with A's cheated.

Professor Akiko has been wonderful this past semester, given the past year and a half has been online. Her class is exam heavy, but as long as you go to the lectures and understand the material you'll be fine, the SI sessions before exams have also been super helpful.

Akiko makes it clear at the start of the semester that her lectures are not meant to be learned from and that they serve more as review for the weekly textbook readings in the course schedule. That being said, as long as you do the reading(s) before class that week, lecture is always a breeze and you are never tested on content from lecture slides.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Graded by few things--Caring

reviews.comment: Such a caring professor. I would not say it's the most rigorous course bc I'd say she was a bit too nice with the grading. That's a good and bad thing because it's very easy to do well, but it also makes it harder to learn stuff if you're not interested in a topic. However, her being "too nice" is bc she's a genuinely kind and empathetic person.
You will never regret taking a class with Akiko ever. Kindest prof, accessible, and very kind.

Super nice professor, very kind. The downside was that lectures were confusing and kind of all over the place. Very passionate but class is mostly case studies instead of clear definitions/notes. Open book exams, can take with other people- heavily based on lectures. Not an insane amount of work. Does exam retakes for extra points too.
Such a sweetheart and is dropping the lowest midterm score this semester. So understanding during a covid semester, definitely want to take another class with her.

I've taken 3 classes now with this professor, and all I can say is she is just outstanding. Extremely caring of her students, and very understanding of covid times. This class (Marine Biology) was so much fun, and she made it interactive and enjoyable! I actually really looked forward to her class every day! It was never a chore to go.
She's AWESOME! Super accommodating :) She genuinely cares and wants her students to succeed.

Akiko is a great lecturer and addresses any students questions in class. If you have any questions she makes herself available to explain whatever you are having issues with. Her exams were exactly on the course material, and most of them weren't too hard.

Probably the best professor we have at UMass. She is a gem when it comes to the stem side of professors. She cares immensely about her students and also makes the final optional to boost your grade. Also makes material easy to learn and identify by highlighting everything needed for the exam. DO take her

Professor Okusu is probably one of the best professors I've had. She truly wants you to learn and understand the material; she is always available through email, office hours, or after class if you don't. She is also super sweet, funny, and she cares about her students and understands that this semester has been tough for many.

Akiko is a literal angel! She lets us COLLABORATE on exams and has amazing lectures. All of her attention and effort is on her students. She had Zoom background contests with Amazon gift cards as rewards. And she will read and leave a detailed response to all 200 of her students' answers to the Q "What did you learn this week?" ICONIC!!

The BEST professor I had at UMass! She truly cares about her student well being. There are three midterms and a final in the semester, the exams are open book and similar to problem sets. On Fridays, you work with your peers on problem sets. Her lectures are recorded so you can go back and watch them when studying. Take this course with her!

Shes an amazing professor, cares so much about her student doing well. Lots of chances to make your grade good. My class was online, but she did an amazing job at it. Weekly problems sets that you can either work with a group on or just do by yourself, three midterms and one final where you can also work with a group on. Lectures are very helpful.

Akiko is GREAT! She breaks up her lectures into very comprehensible amounts of information. Her exams are very similar to the weekly problem sets, and she adds a ton of practice problems throughout her lectures to prep you for exams. She is the first professor I've had at UMass that I can tell really enjoys teaching and cares about students.

I cannot say enough good about this professor! I had her for Bio152 and 312, and got an A in both! Bio312 is graded on writing (it's Writing in Biology) and she really grades you on how you improve in the class. Effort will give you an A. She's helpful, caring, and understanding. Very approachable and friendly.

So, so sweet and super clear when presenting! She cares about her students and their quality of learning. She is flexible with grading policies when she sees her students are struggling, but it's easy to succeed if you keep up with readings, homework, and lectures.
reviews.rating_tags: Accessible outside class--Clear grading criteria--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: Akiko is my favorite professor so far at UMASS. She is super approachable and cares so much about her students. She is clear about everything she wants you to know and explains topics so well. Study, go to class, and do practice problems and you will do well!

Akiko is probably my favorite professor so far at UMASS. She is so approachable and cares so much about her students. She is clear about everything she wants you to know and explains topics so well. Study, go to class, and do practice problems and you will do well!

Professor Akiko is one of the best professors I have had during my time here at Umass. She is always positive and creates lectures that are suitable for all different types of learning styles. She is approachable and always available after class. Her exams are not too easy, I would say average, so you do have to study for them.
Good teacher. As long as you go over study guides you should get around a B. She does require iclicker though which makes attendance mandatory.

Although Akiko cares about her students doing well, her way of teaching can be confusing and disorganized. If there were not iclicker questions and weekly in-class quizes, i'd say that you could easily do well in the class without showing up to lecture because she posts all the material online.
reviews.rating_tags: Accessible outside class--Participation matters--Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: The best professor I've had. Her lectures are really good and expectations are clear. She was also able to help me with an issue I was having because of disability services that was not her responsibility.

Professor Okusu is one of the best bio professors at UMass. She cares so much about all of her students succeeding. Her tests are extremely straightforward and 90% comes straight from the study guides she provides. Attendance is mandatory, as she typically asks iclicker questions during every lecture. She allows opportunities for extra credit.

Marine bio with Dr. Okusu was easily one of my favorite bio classes I've taken at UMass. She really cares about her students and wants to see them succeed. She does do clicker, so even though attendance is not mandatory, you should go to lecture. A lot of people that take the class are seniors, and she knows this - so is very understanding.

Akiko is a great professor. She makes the class really interesting and easy to understand. There are three exams + a final, and you definitely need to study to do well on them, but she provides plenty of resources to help you do well. She grades on participation, weekly online quizzes, and exams. Put in work and you'll have a good time and do well!

Akiko single handedly made Bio152 one of my favorite classes. After struggling through Bio151 due to a disagreeable professor and class structure, I was hesitant to complete this course. However, Akiko is attentive, caring, knowledgeable, and compassionate. She is a fair grader and allows some extra credit opportunities. One of the best at UMass.

Professor Okusu really cares about her students and is looking for everyone to be successful. There is a healthy amount of material, but professor Okusu's lectures are very easy to follow along with and she is great at clearing up point of confusion. Collaborative in class quizzes which are open note, definitely put in time to study for exams.
Akiko is so kind and wants to see all of her students succeed, would take any class with her in a second!
Great professor, would definelty recommend her. She really spends a lot of time on each student and seems to really care how each individual does.

She cares so much about her students and her subject matter. Lots of little quizzes in which you can use your notes etc., lots of opportunity for extra credit. Exams are fair but read the questions very carefully before you answer them. Studying is important in this class.

I loved Akiko! It is apparent that she wants her students to get good grades but also understand the material. Extra credit is given and a few quiz scores are dropped. Though it is obvious how intelligent she is, with knowledge spanning far beyond this intro level class, she never seemed condescending, but instead presented the material simply.

If you study you'll do great. She definitely sometimes makes you think critically and carefully during tests, but if you study you'll get to the answer. There's a quiz every Friday but open note. Her lectures are great and they are recorded. The best thing is that she super great at explaining concepts and easy to follow along. Youll learn a lot!
Akiko is such a sweetheart! She wants her students not to fail. She drops your two lowest quiz grades and forgives 3 Iclicker absences. It is an easy A- Class but you have to work for the A

Akiko really wants to see her students succeed. Her lectures are easy to follow and she attempts to make the class enjoyable for all 220 students, which is a really admirable endeavor! Homework, course load, and exams are reasonable. On top of all of this she's an incredibly kind person if you ever go to office hours or talk to her individually.

Seriously the best professor I've had at UMASS. Akiko is passionate about what she teaches, putting together easy to follow presentations that spark interest in students across the board. Truly look forward to this class and grateful to have a professor that cares so deeply for her students success.

An inspirational teacher because it is obvious she wants her students to do well. Intelligent and passionate about marine biology. This is her first year teaching this course so beware to students who get easily frustrated.

The class seems a lot more intimidating than it actually is. The problems he covers in class are much more complicated than those on the exams, I used the practice exams and OWL problems to guide my studying and never had issues. His lectures are not helpful for learning the material but if you can do basic math you'll be fine.

I was very scared at the beginning due to the negative reviews, but it the class turned out to be great. He gives a lot of practice exams, which prepare very well for the actual exams. Sometimes the grading in some questions can be a little bit harsh, but not too significant. Average exam scores (70-75ish), will result in an A in the class.

Exams start brutally, but the course as a whole is manageable, and if you can spend a few hours a week to learn to recognise what the questions are asking of you, you'll be fine. Other course activities are very manageable, despite some people's complaints about "tons of work". It's a level 4 class if it matters, but it's not bad!

4 exams, owls, and prelecture quizzes. The lecture doesn't really prepare you for the exams. The exams are difficult.  3 questions exams and you need to complete 2/3. If. you're good at math/physics you'll be okay but if not get ready to struggle.

This guy has the most awful boring and slow paced lectures. Even if you go to class it doesn't help at all as he just touches upon the basic ideas and expects you to go home and learn everything yourself. I basically taught myself the whole class and only go for exams. Wouldn't recommend Alejandro if another professor is teaching this class.

This guy is a terrible professor. He barely teaches and even when he does he's impossible to understand. I would avoid him at ALL costs if you can, 471 is hard enough with a good professor, let alone with someone who can't teach

Professor Heuck is extremely caring and deliberately goes out of his way to help his students attain a fair grade in his class. I found 471 to be very difficult because I've always struggled in terms of physics problem-solving, but he provided grading criteria, aside from exams, which I found to be helpful in terms of understanding the material.

This class was awful. His lectures are very hard to understand and he gets frustrated when students ask questions. There are only three questions per exam so if you don't know one your already at a 66.
Exams are so difficult.

Easily the worst professor I've ever had. Doesn't teach well, doesn't give example problems, reads off a note sheet, randomly stops talking in class, doesn't prepare you well for exams, and his handwriting is illegible.
reviews.rating_tags: Graded by few things--Test heavy--Tough grader

reviews.comment: He covers the basics in lectures and gives a lot of extra practice on the side to make sure you are prepared for the exam. The owls helped in this class to study off of similar to orgo courses. Overall okay, not too hard given it is a Physical chemistry class.
easy but boring (took him for 494LI)

This class has 2 parts, the 1st taught by Gerson. Lectures were dry but if you study the slides & show up it's ok. Everyone didn't bad on his exam so he curved it. He graded summaries easily and if you show up you get 100 in participation. He wants everyone to do good. Ended his section with an A however I didn't like the class bc of the 2nd half.

Every professor in the UMass Biology department should study the ways of Professor Dr. Gerson. This a 288 class so it will have its challenges but Dr. Gerson accommodates and makes this class enjoyable instead of a nightmare. Exams and quizzes are very straightforward and he won't try to play with your head as other STEM professors do.
reviews.rating_tags: Accessible outside class--Clear grading criteria--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: This semester was a hard one. Our professor ended up dropping out after the first half and Gerson stepped in. He understood the situation that all of us were put in and gave us as much help as he could. He tried his best to clarify and gave us points back when he realized the lectures weren't clear enough on the quiz. Overall a solid, caring guy.

Each week we had to read primary literature and write a summary of it. It wasn't hard, but he didn't give us clear guidelines on what to write. He was also a hard grader and vague with the feedback. Lectures were posted late and always 1 hour long. Careful with his exams. It's a lot of work for the time (75 min for 10 in-depth short answers).
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Graded by few things--EXTRA CREDIT

reviews.comment: This class is challenging, but if you put in a lot of work you can definitely do well. As long as you do the study guides before exams, you will do well. As long as you are familiar with the material, his quizzes are straightforward. He is a great teacher.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Lecture heavy--Tough grader

reviews.comment: If you're planning on taking the MCAT, TAKE THIS CLASS. SO helpful if you put in the work. He's a tough test grader but just do the study guides he sends out and you'll be okay.

My biggest complaint about him is that he let us out early almost every class.  This was mostly because he would breeze through his lecture slides, without explaining anything.  However he still tested us on the material in depth.  If you prefer to teach yourself the material outside of class, you'll do well.  If you want to be taught, avoid.
Lectures are a bit dry, but the material is pretty interesting. Tests are pretty difficult just because of how much stuff you cover. As long as you pace yourself and don't try to cram you'll be fine.
Great teacher. She really cares about her students. She is willing to help if you need it. Readings are pretty boring in 213, but 214 is great. Great class overall. One of my faves.

One of my favorite classes at UMass. April relates material to our lives. She is always available to answer questions, gives extra credit, and the material is not boring at all. Great Class and its a lot of fun.

April is really nice. She is concerned when there is anything that u do not get/ do not like. She is young and related a lot with her students. Her TA Steph is THE BOMB!! take the class... 213 AND 214 with her.. its an easy A and interesting stuff

teaches PubHealth 213/214...so nice! Always interested in her students.  Classes generally small so she really gets to know you.  Show up and do the very few assignments and you'll have yourself an A...it's fun too!

***FOR PUBHLTH 203***
Great guy to talk to, genuinely interested in hearing him lecture every time.
Lots of notes to be written.

**this is for pubhlth203** he didn't stay on topic most of the time, would just kind of ramble through while reading directly off of the slides. very rarely did i learn more from going than just reading the slides, but oh well. he's nice so it's hard to dislike him. he's a great researcher who's skills just don't translate to teaching.

Prof Arku is very nice and the 360 lectures are very clear/interesting/informational. Most of the work is group work so its not that difficult. The class itself is kind of boring and he does sometimes cold call but honestly its not that bad.

Lectures are clear, he wants students to be able to explain what you learn in "plain language". HWs are simple news reviews on the topic of Air Pollution, a con is tons of group work, however, the midterm is a relatively easy short response form. Paying attention to lectures is crucial for this. would definitely take this course again.

HORRIBLE. A lot of small one page papers, a group project, a longer paper and an exam. None of which are explained very well. He just seems to wing it and the class was all over the place. There is only one exam and it is cumulative, and his lectures don't inspire you to come to class so definitely don't take this class with him unless you have to.

This class was so confusing. There's no clear grading criteria, and he seems to just come up with stuff for us to do as he goes. Assignments are just busy work, and he assigned a group project with no rubric. Lectures are dull and while he's a nice enough guy, don't waste your time with this class unless you absolutely have to. Textbook used once.
Please do NOT take him for your Math132. I don't understand a thing he teaches tbh. The videos in the textbook are way better than what he teaches. I'm suffering in his class right now.

Professor Stern definitely understood calculus. Unfortunately, he did not teach it. His homework often had stuff that wasn't talked about in class. Class was very non-interactive, which is unusual for an honors class. Please do not take this class.

He gets his own math wrong in class/homework/answer keys, which obviously makes it hard when you're trying to learn/study. I've gone to tutoring multiple times and even they get confused with his assignments.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Course was very difficult. Written hw is a lot. Explanations in class are confounding, you may as well learn from the textbook. Final test was written incorrectly. Offers test corrections but don't rely on them. Too much work for calc 1 for life/soc sciences, please run the other way NOW.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Lots of homework--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: If you ever have to take this professor, I would recommend dropping out or hiring a therapist because either way, you are likely going to lose your will to live. The lectures feel like riddles that leave you more confused than before, and he teaches as if everyone has an engineering degree. No calculators or reference sheets, save yourself.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Lots of homework--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: He cannot teach, do NOT take this class.  Nice guy but horrible prof.

Arie does not know how to teach properly. He doesn't have a personality or try to get to know his students at all. Every time he teaches, he explains the material in a very unclear and confusing way. When a student asks a question, he seems mad and disturbed. Does not have a friendly personality and doesn't seem approachable to ask questions.
dont take him

Arie definitely doesn't hesitate to make his students feel dumb... also, don't fall for the extra credit for exams... He'll have you in his office for hours explaining all your mistakes and all you will get is 2 additional points. and be prepared to write 500 words per question on the exams and homework.

Wanna take a class that makes you rethink your entire major?! Take a class with Arie Stern!!! While yes, he is kinda funny, he has no idea how to teach. His explanations are horrible and he makes simple topics impossible to understand. Things as easy as long division or simplifying fractions seems like brain surgery if you follow his instructions.

There isn't any leniency due to the strict rules that come from the math department. No rounding of grades are allowed either. Exams are worth the most. Don't miss math discussions as most of them are the quizzes (missing more than 2 ruins your grade). Exam 1 and Final are easier, and Exam 2 is "harder". Make sure to practice more before Exam 2!
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Lecture heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Genuinely the worst professor I have ever had. He once told the class "It is funny to see you all struggle because these problems are so easy." He doesn't care if his students pass or fail and gives you points off on HW and tests if it doesn't explicitly say what he wants.

Given a study guide with material from over the past few units, expected to know every concept but only ten problems get put on the exam. if you do not write as much information as he wants you lose credit. Hard course. Online homework is easy but the TA weekly homeworks are impossible. The class average on every exam was around a 60%.
Great guy, you have to participate in the class and will definitely learn if you give the effort. Wouldn't call the class easy but studying for the class at least for me was enjoyable.
Professor Figliola is great! He's kind, funny and has an engaging teaching style. I learned so much from this course and genuinely enjoyed going.

Absolutely amazing!!! He says hi outside of class, responds to my emails, is very easy to reach and dedicated to helping all of his students. He's genuinely so kind and funny, he makes Italian fun. He teaches by barely speaking English in class, but won't hesitate to clarify. Can't wait to spend the next few years getting my BA with Italian.

Arturo is an absolute king, if you have the opportunity to take Italian 126 or 246 with him, do it. I literally speak Italian today because 5 years ago he had stellar rate my professor comments, and I'm so glad I signed up.
ARTURO IS AMAZING!!! This is the second time I've taken one of his classes and I cannot say enough good things about him. He truly is amazing and I hope to have him as a prof again.

I was really nervous going into this class, and at first it was very intimidating. But now that the class is almost over, I've realized what a good professor he is. He loves it when you ask questions, and will make sure you understand. Make sure you read the book and take good notes. The quizzes deal with a lot of grammar as well as vocab.

Arturo e' un bravo maestro.  He was direct with expectations and spoke clear, straightforward Italian during class - my comprehension of Italian increased in all facets.  If you're concerned about the lack of English in class, he does speak it if necessary in order to communicate a key point, but he quickly resorts back to Italian, which is good.

Arturo is an amazing professor and very passionate. I really enjoyed going to his class. Subject material was very interesting and he is extremely helpful and approachable. You should definitely take his class if you're interested in Italian!
Arturo was an amazing professor! He made things fun and explained everything in a way that made it easy to retain. He used props and stories and skits, which made the class fun and easy.

Arturo is the best teacher in the Italian department.  It's a shame, though, that he doesn't teach any upper-level courses but 303.  He was amazing.  He explains things in Italian until you understand.  I wish I could have taken him more than once.  He's also nice and hilarious.  Yay Arturo!!!

Loved him, best Italian teacher I've had, such a good character and hilarious. Really gets kids involved in learning the language and rarely lets you speak english.. but its for your own good! take his course!
he's awesome. though he did accidentally squish a caterpillar in class haha
Two Words:  WICKED AWESOME

Arturo is an amiable, comical professor but firm. His dislike of English in the classroom makes it a class you really have to be paying attention in (as I have often been caught out not doing) but that means you pick up more and are more immersed. I am a fan and am taking another class with him next semester.

This was probably the most fun class I've taken at UMass.  Arturo is always energetic and funny.  I learned an incredible amount in one semester.  He makes me want to speak Italian all the time.  e una clase molto bene!
Kind of tough but a great teacher, I've learned a lot from him and I would like to continue taking Italian with him.

He is one of the best Italian teachers i have had since high school.I recomment this class for anyone dedicated to really learning the language.True he only speaks in italian during class but i found that helpful for learning how to speak the language. His review was also very helpful though some people here are bitter about his teaching methods.
good

Here is the truth about this guy: He is charming and funny but he does not have a good teaching method. Very few students can learn from his "emersion method"(no english in the class). It seems like he writes the tests last minute (his reviews are a joke). Dont take this class unless you already have a good understanding of the italian lang.
he's cool, good teacher...TRUST ME, forget all other entries, he's good peoples

Non credit summer course. He did very well with a diverse group of older and younger learners. There was a method, and I wish that I hadn't missed the last class and "il pranzo con gli altri allievi."

Took his class at Mount Holyoke.  Obviously does not put in the time and effort here that he does at UMass.  Overall, I found him to be a very dry character with little creativity.  My interest in the language has vanished and I wonder "...why didn't I take French???".  Not Mount Holyoke material.
Nice guy, but his teaching style was just awful. I don't think I learned anything this semester, and I've seen enough worksheets to last me a lifetime.

he is adorable. one of the best language professors ive encountered while at umass. He's interactive and ridiculously funny...he could have his own show but at the same time you really come out with a greater understanding of italian
Someone that the UMass faculty should be proud to have representing them. His style and enthusiasm is enough to make everyone want to study La Bell Lingua.
Ratings based on Non-credit classes, but I would not hesitate to take his credit courses. Classes are a lot of fun -- and there is method to his madness!
I LOVE THIS GUY!!
Arturo is a really dynamic and amusing teacher.
the best one in the department

He is a wonderful professor. cares about his work (a lot of the readings are his own work -- but good). Very, very interesting topic. I did not know much about the Vietnam War, and now I want to continue learning more. He is also very interested in the lecture; would take it again. GO TO CLASS, PAY ATTENTION!!! Do this, and u will do great.

One of my absolute favorite professors! He is the kindest professor and his personality itself made you want to attend the class. The lectures aren't mandatory but he makes you want to show up regardless.  He also cancelled the final but you have two papers to do and 2 or 3 exams that weren't bad if you studied. Great TA's.
Amazing lecturer, likely the best of my entire undergrad. His lectures were so interesting.

Topics were interesting and he got straight to the point for each of them. Only a hand full of assignments so lock in. Discussion relies on having a good TA. Overall, pretty simple and straightforward class. Doing bad on one assignment can tank your grade but there are a few extra credit opportunities.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Clear grading criteria--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Professor Appy is a really amazing lecturer. The lectures are super engaging and he's really passionate and knowledgable about the topic of the class. Attendance is mandatory but you get a lot of skips to use. There is a decent amount of reading to do, but none of it is hard, and there isn't much other work to do in the class.

Appy is one of a kind, a truly GOATED teacher. This class overall isn't too difficult and you will learn so much. I mean even on the last day when he canceled the final and there was no reason to go to his lecture but 3/4 of the class went, that's how great of a lecturer he is. Put in the work you will get an A and much more

Professor Appy is definitely one of my favorite professors that I have had. He is knowledgable, fair, and understanding. His lectures are engaging and go by quite fast. I truly enjoyed this course and although my major has nothing to do with the topic, I would take another one of his classes in a heartbeat.
Appy was one of my favorite profs. class was very easy just dont miss lectures
Love his lectures, very engaging.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Amazing lectures --Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Appy is an awesome lecturer, obviously knowledgeable and engaging to listen to. Class is fairly graded, if you pay attention and do readings papers are easy and fair. Chill dude to talk to, great prof overall
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Amazing lectures --Graded by few things

reviews.comment: One of the best and most knowledgable professors I have ever had. Truly passionate about teaching history to his students. For a 9am lecture, I never dreaded going. Course work was not too heavy either, and very manageable. Also offered many extra credit opportunities. Would love to take another course with Prof Appy.  Highly recommend.

Prof Appy is the best professor in all my years of study! His lectures & guest speakers were well prepared, engaged,& interesting. Prof Appy enjoyed teaching the students and stayed after many times to answer  questions,. There's a lot of reading but the books he chooses are perfect and easy to read including his own brilliant American Reckoning

Never has history come so alive in the classroom. This is a highly intelligent and critical scholar; leaving Umass without taking a class of his would be a loss. His book, American Reckoning, is one I now recommend to my friends.

I enjoyed the class. Very lecture-heavy, but Appy is a great lecturer. Clearly a very knowledgeable and well-respected voice on the topic, so he's really interesting to listen to. Two in-class quizzes, two essays, + the final. A lot of non-mandatory work for the weekly discussions, although discussion participation is a chunk of your grade.

Appy is a very good lecturer and is definitely very knowledgeable. I am not a huge history person myself but ended up enjoying his lecturers because he made them interesting. His exams were difficult but he let you know about some topics that would appear on them beforehand. His papers were fair and he also canceled our final, which was nice.

I hardly ever say this, but Professor Appy's lectures truly were a delight to attend, even if they were at 9:05 in the morning! He was engaging, always willing to take questions and very well-versed with the content of the course. I thoroughly enjoyed Professor Appy's teaching of HIST201, and would recommend it to anyone interested in History.

Took history of the Vietnam War with Professor Appy. He is truly an expert on the subject and extremely passionate about it. His lectures are fascinating. Average amount of assignments and grading. Fairly easy to get an A as long as you get your work done. If you like history, professor Appy is a professor you must take a class with.

Professor Appy is an incredible lecturer. I was never bored in his class and he always made sure to keep things interesting. There are a lot of outside readings, but they all really do help expand your knowledge on the subject you are learning about. Overall, if you put in the effort and take your time, you're going to do absolutely fine.
Avoid Chris Appy. He's a nice guy who's clearly an expert in his field, but his grading policy is extremely punishing.

YOU CAN NOT MISS A SINGLE CLASS IF YOU WANT TO GET AN A. IF YOU WANT A B DO NOT MISS 3 CLASSES. this class is solely graded on 2 quizzes, 2 essays, and a final exam, as well as attendance, if u miss anything or do not half decent on any of these things you are screwed!
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Participation matters--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Good professor but not a good gen ed class. Attendance policy is the strictest I've seen, if u miss more then 4 classes you can't get higher then a B, 5 for a C ect. These numbers are halved for discussion. Professor Abby interacts little with class making lectures dull and dry. If 9 ams don't scare you then 154 is an very easy DU HS, if not, Run.

Very nice person and extremely knowledgable. He made the lectures interesting and straightforward. TA's graded papers differently though so if you got stuck with a hard grader you might suffer a little more. Overall wicked cool class.

Professor Appy was one of the best professors I everhad during my four years as a history major at UMass Amherst. Hes a well respected academic scholar on the Vietnam War and American imperialism. His class lectures are clear and straight forward. In discussion he encouraged student participation. I would highly recommend him for history majors.

Professor Appy was very interested and knowledgeable about the material that he was teaching, so he was able to make his lectures exciting. Has clear powerpoints that are posted on moodle, but TAs take attendance so must attend. Grade determined by two 5 page papers, 2 quizzes, and a final. Pretty easy gen ed
reviews.rating_tags: Respected--Skip class? You won't pass.--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: This Professor is by far one of the best history professors located at UMASS. His lectures are well formatted and documented. Even if you were able to skip class (you can't), the presentation this professor displays well worth sitting through. Not only that, but outside the lecture hall he is willing to help with any problems with the course.
reviews.rating_tags: Respected--Skip class? You won't pass.--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: Everyone I know who's taken his class on the Vietnam War loved it, and I have no clue why. He hardly said a thing about the war itself, just the politics and protests with some social justice propaganda. Not bad overall but I can't stand professors who take attendance in large lectures, and he makes you buy his own book, which makes me seethe.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--ACCESSIBLE OUTSIDE CLASS--LECTURE HEAVY

reviews.comment: Prof. Appy's, "The American War in Vietnam" class is amazing and I highly recommend it to all students interested in taking their History Gen. Ed. The class has three books to read (one written by the Prof. himself), two ID term quizzes, and two essays, and a Final Exam. If you want a very knowledgeable History Prof. then this class is for you!

If you're a history / english major or you're looking for an interesting course to take to check off a Gen. Ed. requirement, I highly recommend Professor Appy. Lecture heavy class, but there's always good powerpoints to accompany them. Also knows how to actually teach and doesnt just drone on all lecture long.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Inspirational--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: If you have any interest in the Vietnam War, take this course. Appy wrote one of the books so he can provide a different type of insight than the typical professor. Tests are easy if you pay attention in class; couple essays aren't bad if you have a good TA (mine was awesome). Definitely recommend!

Such a smart guy- Harvard Ph.D. and it clearly shows. His lectures are really informative (though they can be slightly dry and my class was at 9am). Mandatory attendance to the lectures/ discussions, but it is helpful to go anyways. He assigns a lot of readings that are mandatory for tests/ essays, but the content is always really fascinating
reviews.rating_tags: Respected--Get ready to read--Skip class? You won't pass.

reviews.comment: Appy is an amazing guy who is truly passionate about everything he discusses. I really can't complain. There are three exams, including the final, and two papers throughout the semester. The TA's do all of the grading. He assigns four books and there is reading every week. At least skim through the readings because they are discussed in discussions
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Skip class? You won't pass.--LECTURE HEAVY

reviews.comment: Professor Appy is one of my favorite professors I've had at UMass.  Super interesting class, and easy if you do the readings and pay attention to the lectures.  There are 2 identification quizzes, 2 five page essays, and a final.  Highly recommended.

Amazing lectures, interesting and informative with all notes put up on moodle. He loves what he is doing and knows what he is talking about.  Recommend to anyone . Does not use official textbooks but three novels/memoirs and his own book on the topic, all are extremely useful. Books are interesting and actually worth the read.

Really interesting and not hard at all if you want an easy history gen ed. He wrote the main textbook, so he's really knowledgable about it and it's all interviews, so it's easy reading. About 100 pages a week, but you can get away with not always doing them. Quizzes are easy if you read the powerpoints which are posted online. Very straightforward

Not sure why everyone thinks this class is so great. His lectures are incredibly boring. The quizzes are solely ID's & he doesn't even tell you what you need to know for them. There's 2, 5 pages papers which admittedly aren't so bad. But if you're not into history then do yourself a favor and don't take this class.

I have taken almost all of Appy's classes, and this one did not disappoint. It was eye-opening, interesting, and not too difficult. Two papers, easy reading, and three "tests," including a final. Take his classes!

Appy is a great story teller and keeps you interested throughout his whole class. difficulty wise this class is simple; if you attend class you will get a good grade. overall its an interesting class and an easy grade

I took contemporary US with Appy, and I'm taking another because he's an awesome professor! He is very knowledgeable and really knows how to engage people with the material. The quizzes and papers are easy, and he posts the PowerPoints online.

Professor Appy is the best I've had at UMass. 2 5 page papers, 2 quizzes, and a final.. all are so easy. Slides are online. He is so interested in the subject and is actually worth listening to. I'm taking another class with him in the fall- he really is the best.
Appy was amazing, intelligent, and very kind. He really knows his stuff, and he loves engaging with students. I am taking more of his classes!
First time ever rating a professor just to say Appy is a great one. Take a class with him if you get the chance. Best one I've ever had at UMass.
Christian Appy is a great professor, by far my favorite at UMass. History of Vietnam War is the bees knees. I highly recommend it for a history gen-ed

Appy is so awesome. He's wicked smart and knowledgable, presents material clearly, the class is fascinating, books are actually hard to put down. Slides are online, but don't miss class. Study for the quizzes, do all the reading, and participate in discussion and you'll be fine. TAKE THE AMERICAN WAR IN VIETNAM!!!

Easily best history professor at UMass. Learned more in this class than any other at UMass. Class is extremely interesting and useful. Appy has a sense of humor. Quizzes aren't hard if you study. Papers aren't hard if you do the readings. The books Appy chooses are extremely interesting and pop culture-esq. A must take class

This is my 3rd class with him, and sad to see Ive taken all of his courses. Great lecturer, all powerpoints online, gives essay for final out before hand, quizzes can be challenging if not prepared for properly. Highly recommend to those who need Gen Ed or for Hist. Majors, or even for fun.

Extremely organized and articulate - a fantastic lecturer. Uses film clips sometimes. Is acutely aware of social justice issues. Regularly relates lessons to the present and touches on the larger themes and significance of history. Great text choices. Tests/quizzes can be tough. Essays intriguing. Encourages participation. Definitely recommended!
Professor Appy is a great Professor, fair quizzes and paper lengths as well as ease of access to powerpoints online. Highly recommend taking his classes.
One of the best professors in the department!  Great lectures and assigns interesting reading.

Professor Appy is the man. I adore him. He writes really well, gives interesting criticisms, and expects a lot from students. But I really enjoyed his commentary and lectures. I recommend any of his classes, he's a great professor who will instill you with curiosity.

I took Vietnam with Appy and am currently taking his Pearl Harbor class and his Jr. Year writing class.  This is by far one of the most amazing professors I have ever ever EVER had!  Some nice, soo helpful.  Great class, great material- you will learn so much!  Patriots is am amazing book too.

Appy is the best lecturer I've ever had.  Class was fun and interesting, readings were on topic and manageable, paper topics were thought provoking, and tests were fair.  Honestly, one of the best classes I have EVER taken.  For sure would have received an A if I hadn't missed 3 lectures(any more then 3 absences drops your grade 10 points).

Prof Appy is AWESOME! He is one of the best lectures I have had at UMASS, his class is very interesting, as are his readings. You aren't going to want to miss out on one of his classes. One downside, he normally teaches t/th with a f discussion w/ TA

He's really awesome and a really nice guy in general. He taught at Harvard and MIT so needless to say, he is a smart dude. Lecture notes are all posted online, but he takes attendance every class. His book is really interesting as well. A really great class and a good teacher.
good teacher
Awesome teacher, learned so much in this class. It was a lot of work but definitely worth it.
Lectures could have been a lot more interesting considering the subject matter, but he seemed to drone on endlessly.  Test grading was rough.  In class film clips were good though.
Often unclear in lectures. Balanced out by him being chill with homework extensions, which there's a lot of long homework, and in class. didn't need to do much in class except show up for quizzes
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Pretty good professor, if you're given the option, I would recommend him over the other calc 1 professors. He played the biggest part in getting me through the course.

I enjoyed attending his lectures, he does a great job at including real world applications to concepts. He is very understanding about homework extensions, I would take more classes with him if he were teaching.
reviews.rating_tags: Amazing lectures --Clear grading criteria--Gives good feedback

reviews.comment: He was a good professor, the subject is just hard. If you attend lecture and ask questions, you'll be fine because he explains things so well. But you need to put in effort.
He was an understanding professor. I missed a few lectures and attendance group quizzes but he met with me outside of office hours to explain the material. He even let me make up some of the quizzes.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Beware of pop quizzes--Caring

reviews.comment: Best professor I had this year. His lectures were enjoyable and made me want to attend. I had to work hard for the good grade, but he made it seem like an achievable goal! Wish he were teaching calc two next semester. Highly recommend if he is still teaching.
reviews.rating_tags: Amazing lectures --Clear grading criteria--Lots of homework

reviews.comment: Haven't gotten my final grade, but I expect an A. He was a good professor, gave group quizzes for attendance credit, and held office hours in case you had any additional last minute questions before exams. Was pretty funny, made some memorable math jokes I may use in the future. Be prepared to do homework though, but he gives extensions if asked.

Showed up to class prepared and was easily accessible via email and office hours. Very understanding about granting homework extensions. Gave group participation quizzes, but nothing too difficult. Just go to class, and you will do fine. Would take calc 2 with him if he was teaching it next semester.
reviews.rating_tags: Group projects--Gives good feedback--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Great TA, understanding and allowed group Quizzes. Single-handedly saved my exam grades.
reviews.rating_tags: Amazing lectures --Gives good feedback--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Santiago is a wonderful professor and great lecturer, he seems to really care about his students. His grading scheme allows any decently motivated student to get a B- or B without too much trouble due to how tests and homework are graded, but the last bit of percentage you need for an A will be heavily fought for.
best professor in the math department

Santiago was a great professor, especially given the fact that this was his first semester teaching. However, this course is incredibly hard. His teaching is good, but do not miss lectures, and even if you don't you will definitely need to supplement your learning with a good amount of studying.

I cannot understand him because he is from Turkey and is not fluent in English. He is nice and gives good feedback. Attendance is mandatory, but students often skip class or show up halfway through. His lectures are so boring, but usually we have guest lecturers. There is a lot of homework (podcasts and quizzes) and group projects—harsh grader.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Gives good feedback--Lots of homework

reviews.comment: Not bad class for freshmen year
reviews.rating_tags: EXTRA CREDIT--Clear grading criteria--Gives good feedback

reviews.comment: Good for an introductory course

This review is for ANIMLSCI 386 Veterinary Oncology Lab. Professor Arcaro is a very good professor and will help you learn an incredible amount of essential lab skills in this class. She is extremely kind, helpful, and smart. Labs are long and packed with wet lab work but very engaging.

Prof. Arcaro covers a huge amount of material, adds lots of new case studies not in the text.  Great intro to ecology field, beyond high school level because you have to think, read scientific papers, understand problems. You won't do well if you're not interested and expect an easy A and can't handle the fast pace.
I found her lectures interesting.  But the lectures compliment the text, not replaces it.  It is best to read the material before class and use the lecture to reinforce what you read.

READ THE BOOK! if you end up in one of her classes make sure you read the book thoroughly, she moves through the lecture notes way too fast to be able to get anything from them. she doesnt do a good job of answering questions during class. her tests are not too hard if you read the book and get all of the key points.
She's nice at least but her tests do hit pretty hard. She does give A LOT of easy extra credit though. If you just study the book it's not too hard to get a solid A

You need to attend all classes. Arcaro comes off as a sweetheart but she is not very reasonable or down to earth. Notes aren't easy to take in her class because she moves through slides ridiculously fast. I would have probably failed this class if I didnt read the book thoroughly because I learned more from the book than class lectures.

she was very sweet and funny, but also could be quite rude/dismissive of the undergraduate students in the class. her grading was extremely unclear. the topics and projects were really interested. she's very much more of an artist then a practical landscape architect.

I took 592 M with her and was faced with unclear grading expectations among other things. The class had nothing to do with landscape architecture and she was incredibly rude to several students. I would like to say she offered constructive criticism but it was just pure criticism she did not help to improve project ideas, just laughed at them.
Carolina is the best!! She is super helpful and understanding especially during covid. taking another class with her next semester.
Professor Aragon is super sweet and helpful! This class was a lot of work, but I learned so much, and she always gave great feedback. I would definitely recommend taking her classes.

Great class, but showed visible annoyance when students would be quiet. TA's lead discussion sections, so this is a three day a week class. My discussion section was a bit boring, and the assignments assigned and due in discussion were very rushed and under explained.

Dr. Arnold is by far the most outright supportive of students with accommodations that I've ever seen, and that is the first takeaway I had from her class. Her grading system is incredibly forgiving and makes it difficult for anyone who does the work to come away with a bad grade, and the way she discusses topics is highly engaging.

Not the easiest gen-ed you could take, but the material is really interesting. The iClicker questions in class are often open-response, which is a bit different. The course is split up so that the first half of the semester you are learning concepts, and the second half you mostly apply those concepts. The TAs are amazing in discussion sections

At the end of the semester professor drops my grade from an A- to a C- instantly. There was an essay that was due at the end of the semester and I got around an 85 on the rough draft. I sent a final draft that was nearly identical and apparently "looked to me as if it was written for another class". Makes zero sense and she refused to change grade.

Prof. Arnold can be very kind and is very invested in what she teaches, but if you are someone who learns through critique or wants to ask questions beyond the material, I don't suggest taking this class. Criticism was in and of itself criticized, and she also at times seemed to get annoyed with students for asking questions.

This class only have 1 midterm and our final is writing a reflective essay. The workload is not a lot, attendance is mandatory since she used IClicker to check your participation grade. Her TAs are very helpful and friendly as well. Homework is fairly easy and she always has a rubric for you to follow through.

Both of the major assignments in this class are overindexed. For the final paper, she has essentially decided what you will talk about, in what way you'll talk about it, and how it will be structured. In the group project, she forces you to assign to your group members specific roles that turned out to be unhelpful and unnecessary.

This class was really easy. There were three online exams and a final paper that was done in lab. Labs were easy to understand and had light work. There was no homework outside of class besides some readings, which I rarely did and still got a good grade.

Dr. Arnold was very knowledgeable about her material. She relies on outside of class reading a lot. Quizzes in section which are not too difficult if you review a bit. TA's make or break this course in specific. Due dates for assignments are at odd hours, so be prepared for that and make sure you put a reminder for yourself to get them done.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--EXTRA CREDIT

reviews.comment: This class isn't super challenging and there aren't a ton of assignments, there's no final and if you are into linguistics you'll probably enjoy the course. Only thing to really worry about is remembering the vocab words as they are used for the whole semester. Also you need an Iclicker. Easy gen ed

this class was fine- prof arnold's lectures are not super memorable, but the content is fairly interesting and the class requires minimal work to get a good grade. attendance is mandatory, she uses the iclicker app every class. overall, a perfectly fine class if you need a requirement out of the way.

professor arnold is teaching a good class poorly and gives off awful vibes when doing it. she fails to properly give students access to the information and leans way too heavily on readings which are mandatory because they are the only things you will be quizzed or tested on. pray you get a good TA in this class

This was a great class to fill out the anthro ARM requirement, the whole class is basically one big research project on something you're already involved in. Super doable workload and a small enough class that we frequently workshopped together. She's a great professor and I'd love to take another class with her!

There is Iclicker App attendance every day and quizzes every in weekly discussions that cover the topics you learned in class, but if you study for just a little bit it should be fairly easy. Exams were fairly easy if you studied a bit, not too tough of a class for gen ed as long as you show up to class. Although, lectures can be a bit boring.
Easy A great for a gen ed requirement

The class overall was very easy but you are required to participate using an iclicker which also manages attendance. Her class is fairly boring and she tends to speed through lecture slides, so I would suggest typing the notes and not handwriting them. There is a weekly assignment every Sunday and a quiz in every discussion section.

This class was just okay. For being a Gen Ed, there was a lot of homework and reading assignments. There are weekly examples, a quiz in discussion every week, a midterm, and 2 papers. For me, the material was a bit difficult to understand, and it wasn't really explained in the best way during lecture.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Gives good feedback

reviews.comment: Professor Arnold is truly one of the most caring and enthusiastic professors. She is very open and accessible when you need help. There are reading journals and quizzes every week but if you keep up with the hw the class is relatively easy to pass.
reviews.rating_tags: Accessible outside class--Get ready to read--Caring

reviews.comment: The class was really interesting and the work was pretty easy. She gives out the work weekly so you know what you have to get done by Sunday which is nice. We only had one paper and it was pretty interesting to write because your supposed to take what you've learned and talk about yourself. Overall, she's a great professor!

A very enjoyable course taught by a very passionate instructor. I took this class in an online format and the instructor handled it very well. Assignments range from quizzes to posting weekly examples on moodle, accompanied by a midterm and a final. Workload is not demanding and as long as you watch the lectures and take notes youll be fine.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Clear grading criteria--Gives good feedback

reviews.comment: Professor Arnold is one of the most amazing teachers I have ever had the pleasure of taking. I wont lie, the papers she assigns in class are meticulous and heavy. BUT her dedication and connection with her students allow her to understand student lives and difficulties. I appreciate her class and her as a teacher. Try to build a relationship!
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Inspirational--SO MANY PAPERS

reviews.comment: Lectures are not engaging. Professor Arnold does not see the major papers or midterms/finals which takes away from her understanding of the students needs. the workload is average, but i suggest if another professor is available you take the course you want with them.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--GRADED BY FEW THINGS--LECTURE HEAVY

reviews.comment: The class has a lot of interesting material and topics, however Arnold is a poor lecturer, leaving no time to take notes. She shows interest in her students, but not in passing you. Tests are DANGEROUSLY short, choosing only 12 or so of the 100+  concepts from class. Also a lot of reading, though the lectures cover most of it, NOT ALL OF IT IS!!!
reviews.rating_tags: Tough Grader--Get ready to read--Skip class? You won't pass.

reviews.comment: Don't take this class. It sounds interesting but it's not- it's all concepts people already know and Lynette requires an absurd amount of busy work. There's constant writing and heavy readings and it's a just a huge force. Also, several group projects that she throws at you and assumes everyone can work on her schedule. She's very opinionated
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Skip class? You won't pass.--SO MANY PAPERS

reviews.comment: Prof. Kulkarni is an engaging instructor who explains complex concepts in a way that's easy to understand. Group project provides an opportunity to learn how to apply these concepts to real world problems. The course is well-structured, fair in grading, and you can tell he genuinely cares about student learning and success.

Grading was vague on the exams and the homework did not reflect the toughness of the exams. Lectures included a lot of information and he went through slides fast. Exams were open note which made them harder.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: Lectures are engaging and interesting. Professor is also very chill and is always ready to clarify any question you might have.

Professor Kulkarni is very chill and cares about his students. His lectures are really great and I would recommend not to miss these as the concepts covered are a bit difficult to understand on your own. He has a clear grading criteria and the homework aren't that hard. Make sure to organize your notes for your open-book exam as you won't have time
The best and most interesting class I had taken at UMass. The professor covers a lot of cutting edge research in the class and discusses real life examples. I learned a lot in this class.

The class was sometimes lecture heavy but Prof. Kulkarni makes every effort to keep the students engaged in the class material. He is very responsive to your questions and grades homeworks and exams fairly. One of my favorite class.

This is an amazing class and Prof. Kulkarni is very passionate  and knowledgeable about the content. I thought the material was really interesting! It was the first time I have been exposed to a lot of the material. Prof.Kulkarni really cares about his students and listens to feedback and responds.

I wasn't very fond of his class. The lectures were long and boring, and he was just a power point reader. His exams were okay, but very bio heavy after the first one. The exams were open note, which was nice, and he assigned a big group project. He curved very nicely at the end of the semester though, and his homeworks were easy.

Prof Kulkarni is by all means a great professor. He cares about the subject and gives decent lectures. This class is basically AP bio with math, but the lectures are mostly biology-focused. Be prepared to ask questions, because the problems on HW/exams constantly either had mistakes (such as needed info not given) or were not covered beforehand.

Prof Kulkarni is one of the best professors in the whole ChemE department. Immuno is a wonderful class that I recommend anyone looking to fulfils a tech elective. The curriculum is very well structured, the first half of the class is a bit content heavy. Exams are easy. Second half of is much more chill and involves a lot of group work

Immuno was a fantastic class, and Prof. Kulkarni did shine in this class. The first part of the class was a crash course on the immune system, and the rest was reading and discussing different RP about methods and tools in immunoeg. No HW, one exam, and just some group work that made the class more engaging.

 A class that everyone should consider!
Great Professor, Easy class. Can be a bit Lecture Heavy sometimes.

Savage, absolute unit of a Professor. Basically teaches you AP bio and math at the same time. Exams are hard but if you take well-organized notes, you too can understand Okazaki fragments. Very approachable, kind-hearted Professor that wants you to be the best chemical engineer you can be. I N S P I R A T I O N A L

Prof. Kulkarni is great. His class is difficult but he makes every effort to help you learn the material. He really cares about his students and wants them to learn. He is always willing to answer our questions. His exams are harder but if you understand the homework and attend discussion sessions, you can do well.

Professor Kulkarni really cares about his students and wants them to learn. This is an engineering course, so it is difficult and moves relatively fast, but if you pay attention in lectures and do the homework you will do fine in the class. Readings are helpful too, especially if you don't have a strong bio background prior to the class.

Overall a difficult professor, Has no mercy for late homework yet takes 2 months to grade homework and exams. Talks very fast so if you want to understand what's going on you will have to interrupt repeatedly and ask. Made attendance mandatory halfway through the semester, 3 or more unexcused absences  points off final grade, including beforehand

LOVE Ashley! She's a fun and meaningful professor, and she does a great job at providing a well rounded introduction to the topic. The class is basically only made up of readings and discussions each week, with 3 exams and 1 group project. There are readings every week, but they're all really engaging and enjoyable.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Group projects--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: Ashley was an outstanding instructor and created a safe and inspiring learning environment. Each reading and assignment seemed carefully chosen and contributed to my learning. Ashley was very accessible outside of class and demonstrated deep care and concern for students. She also offered assignments in multiple formats to ensure accessibility.

The class is basically four papers and some discussion posts. If you show up to class, participate, and make an effort to follow the structure for the assignments, you will get an A. Dr. Woodman doesn't care about grades so much as that you learn the content.
reviews.rating_tags: Caring--Graded by few things--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: While I think what Professor Woodman is doing with DDHS program is great, she should NOT be running it. She is EXTREMELY disorganized. She never gets backs to emails and is always behind in grading. During the last week of the semester, we only had 2 out of the 6 papers graded. Having her as a professor is extremely frustrating and stressful.

No, it's not the most organized class and attendence is mandatory (which it should be because your choices impact the kids), but Dr. Woodman is a sweet, fun, and lenient professor and this is such a fun class and she had really great horses. 11/10 would reccomend.

Ashley is so wonderful! This class is a seminar so expect to do the readings for discussion - they are interesting so you won't mind it. Complete 6/10 case study reflections and post discussion questions; 2 perusal readings - the same thing every week. I find her passionate, easy to follow along, and organized. DEFINITELY take this class.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Graded by few things--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: She's great! lots of readings but not a lot of work besides posting discussions for every reading. One thing I think that is annoying is when it comes to missing classes we have to do extra work when she cancels, which is unfair because it's not our fault, and yet she makes us do extra work. Other than that this is a good class!
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Gives good feedback--Lots of homework

reviews.comment: Psych481 was a very interesting class and Ashley did a great job teaching it. The class is mainly just group discussion about different topics and readings. There is no real work outside of class besides a few readings and a final project/paper. I loved learning about the impact of disabilities on families and she brought in many speakers.

She is a very sweet and nice person but classes are so disorganized and all the students are always confused and then she gets confused. Nothing is clear and her plans constantly change and nothing is updated. Again, very nice person but any of her classes are kind of a headache and a pain just because of the chaotic disorganization.

She is a mess. She is so unorganized, and responds to emails very late. Often times she, you won't even get a response. She schedules things last minute and doesn't post assignments on Moodle. She's a nice person, but a horrible professor.

Ashley is one of the best professors I have ever had. She is so sweet and treats you like a peer rather than her asserting her dominance over you. She really tries to make the class based on participation rather than lecture style. 4 long papers, but she drops the lowest grade. One of the best classes!

Great professor. Very quick response and always willing to help with assignments and course materials. Materials were very informative, engaging, and diverse. All exams open notes and quizzes are based on student generated questions. No text book and novels that were required were very short, easy and enjoyable also. Highly recommend this professor

Professor Nadeau should not be teaching English. I enrolled expecting to learn about theory and important information for my degree, but her curriculum was disappointing. Her course focused heavily on specific political perspectives and less on what her class description described, which was not helpful for me. Consider exploring other options.

Dr. Nadeau is an exceptional professor! Her classes are not only engaging but also showcase her superb choice of content, reflecting her evident love and passion for the subjects. Additionally, she is kind and provides valuable feedback.

I had Professor Nadeau for my ENGL 2010 class at Utah Valley University. I really enjoyed this class. You have to work for your grade, but she is very helpful and gives great feedback on every assignment. There is homework almost every day, but most of it is short and really enriches your understanding of the class. Overall, I highly recommend her!
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Skip class? You won't pass.--Caring

reviews.comment: I had Dr. Nadeau for ENGL 2010 at Utah Valley University and I liked her. I did find some of her homework assignments unnecessary and without purpose but I appreciated that she took an interest in the academic wellbeing of her students. She presents herself well and is a well spoken individual. I would take a class from her again.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Participation matters--ACCESSIBLE OUTSIDE CLASS

reviews.comment: Professor Nadeau is an absolute gem. I took her Victorian Novel seminar because it fulfilled my 1700-1900 requirement and her enthusiasm, encouragement, and overflowing knowledge of the subject matter got me through the texts. She structures the class to focus on discussion of the readings and gives prompt and thorough feedback.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Clear grading criteria--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: Such a great professor who made the content of the class very easy to understand and connected back to the main objectives. Lots of reading and writing. Was super interesting course. Main assignments were a few essays and 2 exams. Not mandatory attendance, but easier to understand if you went. I really enjoyed this class.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--So many papers--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: It was such a difficult class for a GenEd. The professor was nice, helpful, and passionate. But his slides don't have much, so you have to attend the lectures to know what he's talking about. So many papers and readings that rely on the lectures.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--So many papers

reviews.comment: The final exam is super difficult (he picks 6 terms out of 36 to put on the exam, so good luck studying it all, and then the second section is an essay). A lot of reading and writing. The TA is helpful, but the class itself is super difficult to balance with other classes. Do not take this class if you are taking other demanding courses.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Participation matters

reviews.comment: The paper is ok, many readings, take-home midterm, assignments: 1analysis assignment, 1essay thesis, 1essay draft (5-6 pages), and a final essay. The class is boring, and discussion is mandatory, TA is quite good and give useful comments to improve your essay. The final exam is extremely hard, 2 part, in class, on paper, essay and terms definition.

The material is interesting but the readings required each week feel pointless because no one's really checking if you read them. Participation is key in the discussion sections but the instructions for each assignment are kind of unclear and there are few assignments you are graded on.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Lecture heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: I think most people who critique Professor Siddique's lectures as boring were probably uninterested in the class to begin with. I found lectures very fascinating, relevant, and easy to understand. Papers are graded based on readings that aren't necessary to understand lectures, but pretty easy. If you don't like history, you won't like this class
reviews.rating_tags: Amazing lectures --So many papers--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: The entire grade consists of several five page essays, and one final exam. These assignments are solely graded by one of two TAs; never the professor. Rubrics do not encapsulate what is expected from you in your writing. Expect deductions of over 25% on the essays with zero coherent reason on why. DO NOT take this as a gen ed; your GPA WILL suffer!

Attendance is not taken at lectures and only at discussion sections but no way you can pass this class without going to most lectures. There are a lot of difficult and long readings assigned. Although there are very few assignments for the class overall, assignments are very hard and require lots of work to get above average grades from the TAs.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Lecture heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: A lot of boring lectures and very few assignments that are papers. The TAs grade them relatively difficult, most people that attend lectures and do readings receive B to A- range on them. Definitely possible to do well but it's very boring and requires some solid effort to succeed.

Prof. Siddique is obviously knowledgeable but can be a snooze during lectures. Regular weekly readings, grading is fair and based on a few papers. Despite being interested in the content I started skipping lectures because I would fall asleep, still did fine by doing reading and reviewing slides

Professor Siddique is incredibly well-rounded and intelligent. He took the time to acknowledge his students and their contributions thoroughly. Super reasonable and thoughtful, creating a comfortably productive learning environment!

His lectures are really boring and hard to follow, but the class itself was extremely easy. Very light history GenEd. The only assignments were 4 papers. You don't need to know anything from the lectures to do them. There are also weekly discussion meetings but you don't need to know much for them (they got cancelled half the time).
reviews.rating_tags: So many papers--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: very nice person but his lectures are really boring and he assigns a TON of readings. i skipped all of them, only read them for the papers and did really well. boring class but pretty easy
He's very passionate about the subject and obviously cares a lot about the students, however the lectures are not very engaging.
