Ok choice for a history class. The only homework is papers. I seldom paid attention in lectures and did okay for the year. If you aren't interested in the topics, you will find the class boring

He is a really nice person, but very lecture heavy and if you zone out for even a minute you become lost. Only 2 papers, a midterm that was a paper, and a final. There are readings weekly and some are what the papers are based on.

Part 3: This class was hard for me because I dont enjoy history and it was hard gened. I took it because it satisfies HS and DG requirements. If youre interested in history I recommend but if not it will be painful. Professor is so nice and is always looking for people to stop in during his office hours. Theres lots of opportunities to ask for help

Part 2: The readings are dense and often time primary sources from the time period so they can be challenging to read. The papers are graded easily but you have to try because this material is very hard to make up in an essay because it is based on the readings.

Part 1: This class is lecture heavy and dense. Professor talks the whole time so if you zone out you'll miss something. He does record the lectures so you can always go back to them. Lecture attendance is optional but discussion attendance is mandatory with one free pass. Homework is readings and papers.

This class is really great. The only homework is reading and a few papers. The readings are used in the discussions which are really helpful and well planned out. The lectures are very heavy, however, so you have to listen carefully. But he does record them so you can always go back and watch. I highly recommend this class.
reviews.rating_tags: Clear grading criteria--Lecture heavy--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Although this was a weird experience in that the pandemic meant it was remote, asynchronous, and hybrid, it was a pretty pain free class. Good as a Gen Ed.

She frequently returned grades to the wrong students so other people could see your grade on a paper. Her generic feedback always states, "You need to develop x, y, and z," but she never explains how when asked. Overall, the class was easy. There was little to no homework besides the three papers, and we barely read the textbook.

She cancelled class like once a week so sometimes it got confusing what we were doing. Leads the class and allows us to participate as much or little as we want to the group. Kind of a hard grader on papers but gives good feedback if you go to conferences. She also ended class early every time so that was nice. I would prob recommend.

Very reasonable professor. Only homework is reading or writing that you do not finish in class. Classes depend on participation and keeping up with work. She will give extensions if you need them, and she does care about her students. I would definitely take a course with her again.

Professor Canter is a very nice woman, she really values participation in class. If you don't do the readings, the papers will be difficult and in-class discussions will be confusing. This class is easy to follow, and she is not a tough grader. Three major papers, one final project, and discussion posts on the reading for HW. Fairly easy class
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Did not follow the syllabus and did not receive grades until after the semester ended. Assignments were confusing and he was unable to clear up many of students' questions. Over-explained simple topics and spent the class ranting or repeating information. Not much content was covered.

We did not follow the syllabus, were consistently behind schedule, frantic and borderline incomprehensible lectures, wrote notes that were illegible on the blackboard instead of posting notes, frequently goes on tangents that are unrelated. Over explains simple economic concepts to the point of confusion.  Difficult to reach, but very nice guy.

Professor Ash is highly knowledgeable in economics, and his lectures are always engaging and informative. He explains concepts clearly in layman's terms, and provides helpful examples. The workload for the course is relatively light, with weekly readings and a couple of problem sets and short response essays throughout the semester.

Concepts were explained well but this class felt boring. As an SPP course, this class was heavy on the Econ with not so much connection to policy. The syllabus changed halfway through the semester, we were graded off four in-person paper quizzes (w/ revisions) and an oral final. I usually get As but I'm not feeling confident about this class.

Ash is kind, engaging, and cares about your learning. However, we read a difficult (yet intriguing) text, "Raising Keynes", and class was remote, so all 7 students sort of disengaged and fell behind. Your grade is a couple problem sets and an oral final, after which he just decides your final grade. Take if learning is your priority, not grades.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: The only reason I didn't completely fail is because my TA practically carried me through the course. Ash is a knowledgeable guy, but I don't think he realizes that this is an intro course. His lectures are impossible to follow and he even confuses himself sometimes.
reviews.rating_tags: Graded by few things--Test heavy--Tough grader

reviews.comment: A lot of Homework, A lot of.......

He is a very smart professor and knows what he is talking about. He is also really nice and responds to emails very quickly. But there is too much reading and is hard to prepare for exams because there are so many materials to study for. He is an excellent professor if you want to REALLY learn about macroeconomics, but not an easy A class at ALL.
reviews.rating_tags: Respected--Accessible outside class--Get ready to read

reviews.comment: Tests with little/no incorporation of course material? Ill have 3 please! Textbook readings from the 1940's? Time machines are soooo cool. Did you get 3/3s on the last 10 readings? Don't worry those grades are subject to change! A robot professor? Sweet! I'm a comp sci major! Problem sets that question your entire existence? Call me socrates bro!
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Group projects--Tough grader

reviews.comment: He does not explain a single thing and assumes we know everything about macroeconomics and so do the TA's. Unless if you want to withdraw a class, I do not recommend.

A brilliant master of the macroeconomic science. He is able to simplify even the most advanced topics into terms that the common man can understand. He is the reason I decided to continue studying economics. Regardless of your assigned TA and their grading policies, you will still learn more than you'd imagine from Ash's lectures.
Not actually a very hard class if you take notes and pay attention in lecture.
reviews.rating_tags: Respected--Get ready to read--Skip class? You won't pass.

reviews.comment: I wish i spent my last semester at the bottom of campus pond instead of in Michael Ash's class. He changed his grading a few times and screwed the students
reviews.rating_tags: Graded by few things--Test heavy--Tough grader

reviews.comment: If you want to take a class with Ash then let me tell ya, you might as well go sit on a flagpole now. His class was the toughest college class I have taken so far. For the tests, they rely on the problem sets (which is based on stuff that ISNT taught) and his lectures are confusing. The test reviews are 5 pages and nothing is on the test.
reviews.rating_tags: Graded by few things--Test heavy--Tough grader

reviews.comment: Ash is a great economist but lacks any sense of how to teach, more so in a human way. This guy is robotic and speaks economics (that's his language) opposed to slowing down to simplify and translate what he's spitting out at rapid fire. He's oblivious no one understands his lectures and he relates nothing from lectures to the textbook and exams.
Just choose another professor. Hardest tests I've ever taken.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Graded by few things--Tough grader

reviews.comment: Ash is the only one who knows what is going on in class. His exams have little to no correlation with his lectures. I thought I bought the wrong textbook because lectures are so random and all over the place. He is smart but not able to teach if you are someone with no prior knowledge for this 100 level class

Tests rely on the problem sets even though his reviews are 5 slides long. The problem sets are very hard and you aren't taught how to do them and every TA has their office hours on Friday's so you can't go to get help bc that is when they are usually due. Discussions don't help at all and neither do the lectures. I dont know ECON
reviews.rating_tags: Graded by few things--Test heavy--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: Do not take class with Ash. He has long lectures in which he speed through and you can barely understand him and the material on the lectures are not even touched on the test. He assigns 5 problem sets throughout the year but you don't know how to solve any of the problems because you never learn how to. This class is terrible with Ash, don't take
reviews.rating_tags: Graded by few things--Test heavy--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: Ash is a nice, nice guy who has no idea what he's doing. Began the course assigning 100s of pages of reading from two books, continued to assign (lessened) reading. Focuses on one model for the entire class. Boring lectures. No clarification on grading; changed grading mid-semester! Avoid this prof if you aren't a big econ fan!!
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--LOTS OF HOMEWORK--LECTURE HEAVY

reviews.comment: Mikey Ash is a legend amongst men. The workload is pretty manageable; competency quizzes don't count for a grade, short homework assignments, no midterm, there is a final. His grading is pretty easy if you do the work. This class is just enough challenge without the high stakes. Ash is incredibly smart and he has great insight into economics.
Horrible lectures that cover nothing on exams.

Unfair professor. Promised the class on the second midterm that the exam would be graded out 100 with 145 possible points and then decides to actually grade it out of 145, and not tell anyone. His methods of grading are completely unfair and end up screwing you over in the end. Avoid Ash if you can do so.

I just discovered that exam grades were adjusted so that the letter grades were evenly distributed among sections, dropping my final grade a whole 5 points than what I earned. The syllabus said grades were not dependent on other students and this is exactly what happened. This was never mentioned in class. DO NOT TAKE WITH THIS PROFESSOR.

Michael was probably one of the worst Econ professors I have had. He would spend the entire lecture drawing 1 graph or going over 1 PowerPoint slide that had no info on it. He would make study guides for exams and put virtually nothing that was on the study guide on the exams. He had to scale the second exam because people got 40s on the first one.

Econ 204 is a hard class and Prof Ash monologues on a ton of information for the entirety of the lecture. He's a nice guy but his lectures are pretty much useless and the discussion section is the only place you'll actually learn what you need for the exams.
he sucs. worst teacher ever. dont take him. he never emails you back and when you try to schedule a meeting with him he doesnt get back to you. intresting class. terrible teacher!

It is basically an online class because that iss where all the assignments are and you don't need to go to class. The problem is the dates are really confusing online so it is really easy to miss assignments. If you are the type of person that needs a class type setting it's probably not for you.
No debating take the class, he's not going to blow you away but he's easy and extrodinarily knowledgeable

Very enthusiastic and excited about the class, but slightly absent-minded. He gives weekly online quizzes (which are straight from the reading and slightly difficult, but he ended up scaling them), 2 take home exams (which were fairly easy), and various short assignments. Not great with email..but very interesting class! Ended up with a 102 average

im giving Professor Ben-Ur a 4, but I did not enjoy the class. She is just a good lecturer if you are interested in paying attention in your gen-ed. Class is in a small classroom with mandatory attendance and randomly calls on people. This class would be better if it was in a big lecture hall. Some topics were very interesting though

Despite heavy lectures, Ben-Ur sets you up for success for assignments. if u listen to lectures and look over class review quizzes, the online exams will be easy. She assigns tons of readings but u will b fine w/out them. Attendance is important, only allowing 2 non-excused. 2 writing assignments which aren't awful. Ez class if you just try.

Professor Ben-Ur is very knowledgable of the subject. Jewish history is a very dense subject with thousands of years worth of material to examine, but she does so in a way that makes most in her class engaged and interested in the material. Very kind person and easily accessible outside of class.

she really cares about the subject, but super boring lectures attendance is mandatory she assigns hundreds of pages of reading a week but honestly I did none of it except for skimming the test question ones do her RAQs and you'll be fine start the end of semester project early and get feedback and it'll be easy a lot of work for a gened
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Get ready to read--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: This was an insanely dry class. I took it for a GenEd and I wish someone had stopped me. The class itself is 4 quizzes, two vocab quizzes and a paper. However, the lectures are painful to sit through and the quizzes require reading and preparation. Attendance is important or you will fail. Don't take this for a GenEd.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Lecture heavy--Tough grader

reviews.comment: go to class. study the RAQ before the exams and you will get an A. easy prof and very nice

I think a lot of the reviews are old... She now has optional practice quizzes online that don't count and most of the questions on her actual quizzes are from those practice ones. She makes you read but I never have and am not doing bad.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough Grader--Get ready to read--Skip class? You won't pass.

reviews.comment: Prof. Ben-Ur is a very smart lady. She knows exactly what she's talking about, but unfortunately she expects you to know exactly what she's talking about as well. Quizzes are very specific, and no partial credit is given. She also has a debilitating inability to use technology.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Skip class? You won't pass.--Tests are tough

reviews.comment: I heard it was an easy class- completely wrong. Maybe the other teacher was easy, but she is extremely hard. For a 100 level intro course, this was definitely one of the harder classes I've ever taken. Would not recommend at all unless you know a lot about religion. I'm an A/B student and I completely failed the first quiz & exam, lets hope I pass.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough Grader--Get ready to read--Skip class? You won't pass.

reviews.comment: This professor literally does nothing to help you, and her tests are way too specific. She does not take students seriously, she is pretentious and condescending, and there is way too much reading for her class. Attendance is mandatory and if you're absent, you need a documented University excuse. You can work hard and still fail hard.

Great Teacher and class if you are willing to put in the time and effort. She is very helpful, and cares about the students. The readings are dry and long, and you have to do them. The class are interesting though, and she's very passionate about what she teaches.

At first, this course was unbearable and I was planning on withdrawing, but I didn't and I'm glad I stayed with it. Although expectations are not always clear, if you go to her for help, she WILL help you. She also gives you credit for improvement, but you have to do the readings and participate in class. Overall, she's a fair and respectable prof.

First off, she is a strict teacher. Attendance is mandatory and graded. No extra credit opportunities and lots of reading. She treats her students as I would expect a professor to treat students in a 300 level course. She is very fair though. She gave loads of feedback on our writing assignments, and was always very kind and friendly.

She is too detailed about the most non important things. She makes students feel inadequate if they don't understand the readings she assigns. She needs to be more clear about her information and her power points. The power points she has have way too little words than what she teaches in class.

Honestly, worst professor I have EVER had. She is completely unclear, makes you feel as if you are stupid, and her quizzes are on the most minor details in one of her 50 page readings. I cannot emphasize enough how awful she is. I am doing ok in this class because I dedicate HOURS a night to it. DO NOT TAKE THIS CLASS WITH THIS PROFESSOR

This prof is terrible! She's very unclear and speaks so quietly it's impossible to hear what she is saying. The readings are at least 15-50pgs per night. She isn't helpful at all. The quizzes are 70% of your grade and are extremely hard to pass. She gave 2 extra credit opportunities but doesn't help much in boosting your grade.
Super anal about everything, quizzes are extremely hard to do good on. Not an easy A anymore, she is a bad professor.

this class used to be unbelievably easy but the curriculum has changed, probably because Aviva realized a third grader could have passed the class but now apparently a prequisite is you have to be Jewish. so don't take this class expecting to pass!! shalom to all and to all a goodnight

Her grading system is easy, but her quizzes are extremely difficult. Quizzes are worth 70%, but you only need to score 15/30 each quiz, but it's almost impossible. You need to be very detailed w/ every question you answer otherwise you won't receive any credit. I really wouldn't recommend this class unless you're religious.

Horrible professor; calls her TA "Mr Cumfort", makes him fetch water, and calls out random students awkwardly. Quizzes are specific to an anal level, if your answer isn't beyond perfect, WRONG!!!!! Extra help is useless; she is condescending and unhelpful. Readings are tedious but you need every little detail for quizzes. Good luck with her BS.

Seriously this is the worst class ive ever taken. her lecture has no relation to the ridiculous amounts of reading assigned. The quizzes are extremely hard and 70% of grade.no partial credit. TA is no help whatsoever. random graded activities so you have to go to class. She whispers so you can barely hear. Expects everyone in the class is jewish.
"Ms SMith??? Mr Winn??" Aviva Ben-ur is so confusing I fail every quiz it is so boring help she just shows pictures to the class and speaks hebrew half the time.

The grading system is ridiculously easy. The quizzes are hard but if you get a 15/30 on each of the 6 quizzes you'll still get an A- in the class. I can't stand this class but it's probably the best history gen ed for someone who doesn't like history.
Good teacher. There's a lot of reading that she expects you to do. You have to go to class.

If you attend lectures and pay attention, you will get an A in this class. The class consists of 6 quizzes (based on lecture, reading) and 6 "engagement exercises" which are surprise in class attendance (and questions about the assigned readings). Aviva herself is in her own bubble, but she is passionate and extremely helpful.

You will not learn anything in this class. Lectures are all over the place and have nothing to do with the subject. You can barely hear her voice, she lives in her own world and has no sense of the class. Quizzes are about readings and not about lectures. Not an enjoyable class. I dont recommend it, or any class with her.

class is pretty easy and if you really read the quizzes some questions can be kind of obvious you only really need to go until you get 90 points total on the engagements and quizzes which may seem harder than it appears but i got there by the 4th quiz. readings arent necessary for the reason stated above but could be interesting. Easy HSG gened

this class is easy-there's only 5 quizzes and a few attendance grades that count toward your final grade.but she's odd, and her teaching methods are odd. the text is required, but only assigns 2 readings from it all semester. the rest are on Ereserves. she also seems pretty biased toward judaism/against christianity, which is pretty uncomfortable.

Honestly this was a class about nothing. We read random texts of her choosing, each one more arbitrary then next. From this class I learned...nothing. Her teaching style can be characterized as: very very awful. I suggest you take this class if you're looking to make yourself miserable over the course of a semester.

awful class  so boring with ridiculous quizes that have questions that you never went over in class!!! Like where is yemen!!! Take this class with one of the other teachers i hear stern is good it would have been an interesting topic i feel if i wasn't asleep through every lecture. By the way don't let her know your name she will call you out!!!
I think Professor Ben-Ur is a great teacher. She keeps the class entertained, and the material is very interesting. I definitly recommend this class for anyone!

I found this class very interesting. She does random attendence sheets so going to class is a must. I barely did the readings for this class and just went to class and took notes and my average for the class was a 98%. Quizzes are straight from the classnotes. if you are a good note taker then you should be fine.

I thought this class was very interesting and extremely easy. I didn't study for the quizzes just looked them over real quick before the class started and always got at least a 90 on them.  Take the class if you are interseted in jewish history or else class may be boring.

Professor Ben-Ur is certainly knowledgable in her field, Jewish history. I want to put this in the nicest way possible: it would be beneficial for her to explore the histories of other people. I think this would vastly improve her teaching and give her perspective.

not bad cause you dont have to take a final and there are no tests only 6 quizzes. all quizzes are announced but they have such specific answers that they are hard. if you go to her office hours she helps you out a ton and gives you extra points. very nice person but class can get boring.

She goes over many many years of Jewish history, seemed like a good class but was horrible. She uses a projector and just constantly talks the entire time covering years. I took 5 pages of notes every single class. It was so bad I switched out. I will never take a class with her again!
easy and interesting

I hated her. She just keeps talking and everyone gets behind. She just talks and expects you to take notes. She has the hardest teaching methods. Everyone switched out. Don't take her unless you are planning to work extremely hard and forget all your other classes.
stays impartial on political matters-- extensive jewish history that really extends onto the rest of the globe for this 2,000 yr. span-- definitely taught me a lot.

guaranteed easy A, just attend the lectures and take notes. can get very boring though...she has a tendency to make 75 minutes feel like eternity. but if you manage to stay awake, you'll have no problem.

Guarenteed easy A... Very boring lectures, but as long as you go and stay awake, you are gaurented an A. No papers, no exams, only 6 quizzes (lowest one dropped, and 6th quiz counted in place of 2nd lowest quiz.)
Go to the classes and you're guarenteed a good grade. We have a ton of readings, i've done none of them, and the lowest grade i've gotten is a 93 & you dont need to be jewish to do well!
Awsome teacher! made Jewish history VERY interesting

Easiest class I've ever taken.  Attendance is a must though, almost all quiz material comes from lecture.  She's really into the material and it shows. Strict on politeness and respect, but I'm glad she is cause some students act like jerks.

She knows a lot about what she teaches & seems to be well educated, but her lectures can be very long. She only gives 6 quizzes & will drop your lowest grade;no final or papers.  Missing a class sucks tho because her "notes" online are just outl
incredibly boring, doesn't know how to budget class time, skipped over the creation of israel so she could lecture about the hannukah song.  avoid at all costs.
Very boring and time consuming
the class seems like it lasts forever, but she tries to make it interesting. the quizzes aren't too hard if u study
worst class i've ever taken.  VERY boring professor, just stands at podium and speaks for 75 minutes, not animated at all.
No Comments

She gives clear notes that are also on the web.  No attendence kept, no final, and your grade is based on 6 quizzes, the lowest of which is dropped, and the last can count as 2 quizzes if it helps your grade.  Only one cheap textbook needed.  Great class.
She is extremely strict.  There are only 6 quizzes (no papers or tests) but do not take this class if you don't like to take notes!
VERY boring
No Comments
No Comments

Lectures were ramblings never related to topic of the week. Unreachable; emails would go unanswered. Attendance mandatory, yet they themself were almost never present. TAs are very harsh at grading, while prof slacked on grading--gave everyone a rushed A a week before close. Extremely disorganized; due dates constantly changing. Very long readings.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--So many papers

reviews.comment: The professor never responded to any of my emails, despite telling us they were always reachable.

B skipped about half of the lectures. Mostly forgot to email us when class was cancelled, and we had to find out from the TA in person. I don't think they graded a single assignment and just gave me an A. Attendance was mandatory even when B didn't show up to class. Overall, this class was such a waste of time. Terrible professor, who meant well.
Don't take this class.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Absolutely horrible class. Rambles on during lectures about the readings which are very long, doesn't teach actual information and talks in gibberish. Takes forever to grade one thing, journal entries are very specific, I got points taken off because I didn't relate to a subject in my daily life. Extremely unorganized, avoid this class if you can.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--So many papers--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: I don't recommend taking this class, I found the material exaggerated and long. There are no due dates and things are constantly getting changed. Cancels a lot of classes and tends to trauma dump in class. I do not recommend taking this class with this professor.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Lecture heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: dont take this class. i read the reviews and i thought it would be nice to have class cancelled if they never show. no! theres no structure, no communication and no help. the topics of this class is really interesting and B is very nice. but they just ramble about whatever they have to say. no due dates on canvas. lots of reading.

So before taking their class i wss aware they'd take long to grade but it is now jan 5 and I have one singular assignment graded. I have no idea what my grade is. B cancels class a lot is is really mia. that's all i gotta say (i also took both of their classes, same situation for both).

This professor was the bain of my existence for four months. DO NOT TAKE THEIR CLASS. They never showed up for class and never answered a single email. No one in that class ever had any idea of what B was talking about and the readings were just lengthy gibberish. I could not tell you a single thing I learned and they still don't have grades in.

B frequently missed class without telling anyone, TAs then had to create a lesson on the spot. The lectures were unstructured and were essentially rambling about nothing. B was unreachable outside of class and placed all work onto the TAs: grading, teaching. Only time I learned was in discussion with the TA. Syllabus lacked any info on the work

I wasn't a fan. The professor barely showed up for class (the TAs were the ones teaching it). Also, they never spoke loud enough or wrote big enough on the board so no one ever paid attention during lectures. There wasn't any structure to the lessons either (no slideshow, no notes), just talking for the entire lecture. The TAs were fantastic though
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: This professor is horrid, I had difficulty this semester with my health issues. The professor did not answer ONE email the ENTIRE semester. Completely impossible to get a hold of them, and class is terribly redundant. You literally just hear the professor lecture what you read and talk in circles for an hour.

I love B as a person, but not a professor. They never showed up to class and left all the work up to the poor TAs. B never left any guidance/instructions for them, so often they had to come up with the work themselves. For attendance, a piece of paper is passed around, and the entire class complained about their attendance grade being incorrect.

This is my second time taking a class taught by B! I really enjoy their lectures and passion for subjects in WGSS. I suggest for homework assignments to focus on the reading for that week. I have heard from other students that some lectures can get confusing but if you show up to class and use the readings in your assignments you are set for an A.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Caring--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: literally never shows up and makes the TA's do all of the work. the class was just rambling and no real teaching, i cannot tell you a single thing i learned this year. easy A so if you need credits!
I didn't learn a thing and he didn't give good feedback. I seriously considered dropping the program so I wouldn't have to sit through that class.

He is without a doubt the best professor at UMass Amherst, period. He is willing to help so many students succeed with their careers. If it wasn't for him, I would not have been able to do my research project correctly, and from his teachings and advices, I was able to succeed a lot and made me prepared for my career. I've been blessed to have him.
He's hot and FINEEEEE my king great prof

Scott was great- you can tell he loves what he does and he's good at teaching it. Chem 112 is a tough class, but Scott is so helpful and cares a lot about his students. Exams are fair, def put in a lot of work but it paid off. He is willing to work with you too. Great guy, funny, would take again

Scott is a great dude. The man is very smart and passionate about the topic, and he urges you to reach out if you are confused. He is understanding and very clear when there is confusion. One of the best professors I've had at UMass.
Scott A is a man who has transcended mortal limits only to return to the corporeal plane to instruct students in the big ideas of chemistry

Genuine good caring professor. Attention drawer in the beginning of class but hard to stay focused til the end. Learn mostly from owls. Occasionally go to SI. Then I believe you will do well. Just try to do homework owls before he teacher the topic.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Skip class? You won't pass.--Hilarious

reviews.comment: Super cool dude, very passionate about chemistry and really knows what hes talking about. Makes analogies to try to help you understand. Chemistry is hard in general, and nothing about the class is easy, but at least with scott you have a prof that tries his hardest to teach you and help you understand. Funny and caring.

He is such a nice guy. I think he wastes a lot of class time doing stupid stuff and making us feel like we are some talk show. It is wicked weird. But overall, he is such a nice guy, well educated, and teaches well.

An instructor like Professor Auerbach is the sort of person you want guiding you through college. He is a great chemistry professor, but more importantly a great person. He's extremely helpful and is always willing to meet with students. One time when he was snowed in, he cross-country skied over to campus for a review session. Yeah. Take him.

Professor Auerbach is one of the best teachers I've had in school.  He genuinely wants all his students to learn the material and do well.  He is passionate about what he does, and is a very nice guy with a charming corny sense of humor.  His tests are challenging but he is always available for help and teaches class outside when its nice enough.

Great teacher, has a dry, but good sense of humor. Loves his grateful dead and chemistry. Takes difficult concepts and makes them intuitive and easy to understand. Also takes all of general chemistry and wraps it all together
Auerbach really wants you to learn, and will explain the leaves off a tree to make it clear.   Good in class, out of class, wherever.  This was my favorite class, totally!
Professor Auerbach is the best prof you could have for such a daunting subject.  And he's an all around nice guy.
One of the best teachers Ive Had
Not just a great professor, but, more importantly, a great human being.
Does everything he can to help students understand material and pass the class.  Knows his stuff!
OUTSTANDING teacher, very clear and interesting with difficult material.
He needs to work on his joke material

I liked Prof. Aulino, and the class is pretty easy, but I dreaded coming to class every day. I'm not sure that was her fault so much as the topic and the other students. If you are thinking about taking the class, make sure you are okay with a lot of discussion about death and not a lot of connection with classmates.
This class changed my whole outlook on life. I'd strongly recommend this class!

Professor Aulino wants 2 things: for you to participate in the course and its contents and for you to succeed. Grading in this course borders on angelic. The course structure is crunchy, Hampshire College vibes. However, it's important for you to be passionate and engaged in the material. If you like intense discussion, this is the class for you!

Genuinely one of the most interesting and engaging professors I've had, like, ever. She can kinda go off on crazy tangents, but her stories only help to make the course way more interesting. Lots of freedom in assignments and the final allowed to me research topics that I personally wanted to write about.

I absolutely love her as a professor and as a human being. Grades in a reasonable way and gives room for creativity and thinking for oneself. She is super smart, but in class, her focus is on students. Classes can be a bit tangential, and since she tries to give many people the chance to speak, but it's worth it. Go to office hours.

The material in this class is dense and tough but with professor Aulino's expertise and thorough lectures, combined with open class discussions, one can learn to ask really interesting questions and learn from there. There are several assignments throughout the semester and one final project at the end.

Great class! Prof. Aulino is always enthusiastic and very knowledgeable about different cultures and their approach to death. You talk about different topics. No text book, all readings online and every week is reflection paper.  Discussion heavy class but has great videos and outside sources. one of my fav classes!

I took Approaching Death with Felicity. She assigns a ton of readings, but you don't necessarily have to read the whole thing. She's very passionate about what she does and is also just a really nice person. She has weird antics, but she makes it work. The class is an easy A, but you can get way more out of it than just the grade if you particiapte
Rude and uncoordinated. Will never take a class with him ever again if I can help it.

Technically this is for M217 but I also had him for 215. He is an amazing professor and really wants you to succeed. Not the best at music theory but I do well in class because he always takes time to explain things until you get the concept down. Homework always prepares you for exams. 100% would take another theory class with him again.

This was the first time I had Dr. Auerbach for a music theory course and I was very happy with my experience. He's so knowledgeable and very interested in the subject and his lectures are interesting as a result. HW feedback is thorough but office hours help too. He makes music theory lots of fun and he wants you to succeed. You'll be just fine.

Only good if you already have a foundation in aural skills; doesn't coordinate with other aural skills teachers, which creates issues when moving on to future classes (his classes are often way ahead of other aural skills classes because he teaches too fast and its a pain when you go on to future classes).
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Lots of homework

reviews.comment: He was not a great teacher for an introductory class for aural skills and is not very understanding. He is very hard with his attendance policy and goes way too fast. If you have past experience with aural skills then you will do well but if you are new with the subject, you will most likely struggle. Terrible with dictation quizzes

So it's actually Music 114 for Aural Skills I but anyway, this class was pretty challenging but it gives you a strong foundation for future levels of aural skills and theory. You'll have weekly singing assignments and the TAs will give you PLENTY of good feedback. The professor is a tough grader on singing, but it teaches you to be detail oriented.

Had him for MUS114 (Aural Skills 1) but the option wasn't there. It was his first time teaching it this year and the class was very enjoyable. The workload wasn't bad but the content is difficult if you haven't done any ear training previously. He's really fun and kept the class awake at 9 in the morning, not an easy feat.
Terrible teaching ability. Terrible attitude. One of the worst on staff at the university.

Professor Auerbach is a very thorough instructor, and quite willing to discuss material in a deapth beyond what is required for the class outside of lecture time. The projects, assignments (including keyboard audits used to help the students understand the theoretical practices taught), and tests are stimulating, reasonable, and designed to benefit
reviews.rating_tags: ACCESSIBLE OUTSIDE CLASS--Amazing lectures--Would take again

reviews.comment: Fantastic theory professor. very challenging but the knowledge one gains makes the challenge worth it.
Very clear and effective teaching. Tests sometimes have a curveball, but he's a fairly easy grader. Also he scales the class at the end of the semester
adequate teaching. tests and exams are not easy, he always throws a curveball. it keeps you on your toes.

Tends to get frustrated very eaisly and takes frustrations out on the students. Is usually burned out at the end of every semester making him difficult to work with. Watch out for aural skills singing finals. He's usually in a bad mood and will take it out on you DURING your final.
Be still my heart.
Tough class, but knowledgeable in subject areas. You work for your grade.
No Comments

Not a bad instructor, but seems to have not adjusted to the American education system. Requires mandatory attendance and encourages participation. He's nice if he sees you put effort in class, but the opposite may also be true.

Professor Nzokem is by far the worst professor that I have ever had in my life.  He sits in front of the board all class and copies the textbook word for word with no further explanation.  He provides no example problems in class, and is not helpful if you have any questions.  The lectures are utterly useless.  Take Diff EQ with Cahill if you can.

TERRIBLE PROFESSOR. Differential Equations is a relatively easy class, you can find the lectures posted online. This guy's English is terrible, he speedruns through the material reading and copying straight from textbook to chalkboard, never explains what's going on. Find Garreth Cahill's lectures and learn from there

Although he seems like a chill guy, teaching wise he struggles in making a lesson comprehensible. He would spend a bit too much time writing transcripts from the textbook, as well as barely being understandable when explaining what the proof and theorem then means.

So I actually had 131 with him not 331 but it wouldn't let me select it for some reason

He was horrible. Passive-aggressive and obviously didn't care about the success, learning, or the mental health of students.
Absolutely TERRIBLE!!! Cannot recommend against him more! Bottom line is that if you can avoid him AVOID HIM.

If you have Aubain Nzokem as your instructor, you might as well be prepared to self-teach the material on your own and learn nothing because he is either MIA on email or belittles people who ask the simplest of questions via email such as updates to grades or any clarification of course material.

With all due respect this man falls well short of the practical requirements of being a college professor. He fulfills every negative stereotype and is the reason why people hate professors.

reviews.comment: Dropped the class. First week was horrific. Can't understand him and he essentially copies the textbook onto the board with no examples. Please don't take this guy for anything and drop him asap if you're already enrolled.

Nzokem was ok for Math 233. Lectures were fairly clear and he cared about student learning, but when asked questions he often struggled to rephrase content in different ways. reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Clear grading criteria--Lots of homework

Never take a class with Aubain Nzokem when you can take it with Garrett Cahill.
I'd rather get hit by a bus than take a calc class with a woefully incompetent instructor like Aubain Nzokem ever again.

HE IS IN THE WALLS. HE. IS. IN. THE. WALLS.

He will actively hinder your learning, and many other professors are excellent at teaching 233.

Above all, this man is very disrespectful. He gives back rude responses to genuine questions and avoids giving coherent answers at all costs. I stopped going to class and have had better success teaching myself via youtube. If this man still has a job come future semesters, avoid him at all costs or you will have to teach yourself vector calculus.

Worst professor I have ever had at UMass. Writes paragraphs of theorems on the board that could be explained in one to two sentences, yells at students for asking questions, never explains things more than the text book does, and most importantly never does examples in class. Avoid him at all costs. You will learn more from YouTube than lecture.

Easy and covers multiple gen eds, if you go to class you're fine.
Not helpful.

Professor Barnes is the least of your worries in this class -- most of your grade comes from discussion section. Go to every class that you can, but don't feel bad about doing other work. The lectures are not at all engaging, and she speaks with a monotone on the occasions she decides to show up instead of just showing a movie.

Maybe one of the easiest classes I've ever taken. Lectures are mandatory but completely pointless and unnecessary seeing as the only work is two papers and weekly reflections. She is the worst teacher ever. So bad with technology and simply reads off the slides. Class focuses way too much on race and not enough on other forms of diversity. Easy A.

Attendance is mandatory and does a good deal for your grade. 1 midterm paper and 1 final paper, which are very manageable. TA discussions are what make the class. Recommend if you're looking to do the Educ. Minor. Very manageable and able to pull out and A.

The lectures are boring and useless. Barnes isn't a good lecturer, but most people sleep through that class. You have to attend because they take attendance and do clickers however. Discussion is where you get your grade from, so it all depends on your TA. 1 midterm, 1 final essay, and weekly simple homework assignments. It's still an easy A

Easiest A I have ever received, however the fact that this woman is a tenured professor at Umass really makes me wonder about the hiring process here.  Professor Barnes relies heavily on videos, and when she choses to lecture, she stutters and stammers while repeating what is written on the slides.  Truly embarrassing to watch sometimes.

I really like the material in this class and the discussion sections. However, this professor just doesn't know how to teach the students in her lecture.  She copies and pastes information from wikipedia onto her slides. Doesn't really explain things well. 1 midterm paper and 1 final paper. NO TESTS/QUIZZES! :D Good class, bad professor
Class was mad easy once you get the hang of excel

Requires attendance and will call you out for being on your phone / laptop. Lectures have almost nothing to do with climate engineering and are structured like primary school class. Class is entirely a waste of time, this professor should not be teaching engineering at UMass. Guest speaker accomplished more in one lecture than she has in weeks.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Group projects

reviews.comment: In class she mostly does practice problems that you are put into groups for, as long as you vaguely understood the reading they are not super hard. There is Iclicker attendance so attendance is mandatory. Homework is light apart from the readings that are occasionally extremely long. Exams are not a lot of questions but are open note and open book.

She's a terrible professor. Unless you are very proactive in trying to understand the material and ask her questions directly, she gives unreasonable examples during lectures that are nothing like the exam or quizzes. The lectures confuse you even more and statistics isn't the toughest subject out there.
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Skip class? You won't pass.

reviews.comment: She is a great person, very approachable, but was not a fan of her teaching approach for my engin prob and stats class. Had to pretty much learn everything on my own. she didnt teach anything useful that will be on the exam in class. classes are fun and interactive, not gonna lie. be ready to teach yourself everything from the book. uses iclickers
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--LECTURE HEAVY

reviews.comment: She may be the most unhelpful teacher i have ever had the displeasure of having to learn from. Class is uninformative and mandatory. The homework is completely unrelated to what we do in class. The textbook is not helpful. Maybe some people like flipped classroom but i haven't met any. It's en engineering class; teach equations and give homework.

A pleasant person but gave A LOT of reading for an intro STEM class. The quizzes asked about small things on the dense pdfs. Often I got 60% on the quizzes even though I read it all and tried to memorize it. Loves iclicker questions and the class is team-based so you can't skip. Kind of a boring intro class, but I think she tried her best.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Skip class? You won't pass.

reviews.comment: She was an awesome professor with a heavy background in environmental issues in third world countries. I would definitely take her classes again.

Erin Baker is a nice woman. She is not a good teacher. She will have groups do "engineering" activities in class that are just pointless. The group never has enough time to get anything done. She also doesn't prepare you for the "IRAT" tests (online test done individually). She grades easily because she had to, everyone would fail otherwise.

The only hard thing about this class was the creo tech drawing lab aspect and even that you get the hang of. The class is a joke and i feel as though i wasted a semester going and "learning" the "material" from that class. Very easy to get a good grade though

Professor Baker was a very nice lady... but her teaching was god awful. She gave bland lectures and many times would just not show up and have guest speakers. The class was useless and I don't feel like I've learned anything about engineering other than a CAD program in the lab.

ENGIN 113? More like HIPPIE 101. Learned more about sustainability than I did engineering.  No need to even take notes or pay attention in class.  The lab is what I looked forward to the most, even though you teach yourself how to use desigining software.  Creo 2.0 is a must have for this class, since you'll be learning straight from the book
not a teacher just a speaker

The only useful part of this course was the lab which was very useful. Other than that the class was pretty pointless. Half the grade is a project that is graded easily but boring. The material seems pointless to engineering. Baker is the only professor teaching this course so you're stuck with her.

Whole class was focused around her own research on energy technology. Labs were interesting, until the final one (in which they, after not teaching us a thing about actual engineering all year, expected us to be able to design and build an engine in CAD with particular specifications). Would not have taken course if I'd known it would be like this.
I hated this class with a burning passion even if it is ridiculously easy.
Her class was super easy.  It didn't really relate to engineering at all though.
Interesting class. Powerpoint driven. Giant project at the end. All MechE and Industrial Engineering majors take it. CAD is the hardest part.

Extremely boring class. Has nothing to do with learning mechanical engineering. Learn more about economics than anything. Pretty much learn what you could easily learn in one day over the entire semester. Lots of guest speakers. No midterm or final and the quizzes are open note.  Project required that's worked on all semester.

I know its an intro class but I don't feel like I learned any mechanical engineering. It was basic economics other than the lab section which seemed useful although it teaches an inferior program. If you have to take it, its fairly easy and mildly interesting though I often feel I am smarter than her.

I know it's an intro course, but she assumes that everyone is dull as dirt.  I know absolutely nothing more about my major than I did when I started the class.  The class is easy but is absolutely terrible to sit through.

Great class if youre a industrial engineering and wanna go towards the finance end.  Work hard on the practice exams, your homeworks, and go to class.  You do thoose three things youll get a good grade.  She wont try to be all tricky on the exams she just wants you to know the material.
very easy class, sometimes boring. Exams are open book open notes, just do your homework and you'll get a good grade
No Comments
No Comments
No Comments

Incredibly slow lecturer, can't get through 30 slides in a class. Not great at explaining; I taught myself everything from the textbook. Students deal with the consequences of his inefficiency, often having multiple assignments due right before an exam because he pushes due dates to align with lectures instead of altering the content of the exam.
Taking Klaus for a lab was a wonderful experience. He was clearly knowledgeable and wants his students to succeed.

Contrary to what I read professor Becker was fantastic. His experience and enthusiasm for cell and molec bio on top of his caring personality made it easy for me to learn the material from class. His tests required an actual understanding of the material, and not just memorization which I really appreciated. I would absolutely take his class again.

I think Klaus is retiring and it def showed this sem. As much as he wants everyone to learn, his voice puts ppl to sleep, the course is graded on very little things, and exams could have been spaced out better, but the course itself is tolerable. Tests are almost identical to the quizzes he has us do, si is helpful, and attendance isn't mandatory.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Lecture heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: His lecture slides are only pictures and he expects us to be geniuses and know what it means. His exams are mostly the practice quizzes and sometimes off quiz questions. The weighted grade started at 85% exams and 15% homework and quizzes combined so it will barely raise your grade. Everyone in class had horrible grades and they changed the weight.
reviews.rating_tags: Lecture heavy--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Unclear, unfair, unprofessional and unpredictable in his exams.

This professor is very nice but difficult to learn from. There were only pictures on the board from the textbook and he is all over the place in explaining the diagrams from the class. It is very difficult to follow his thought process because he will go off on a diatribe of something not related to what we are supposed to be learning in class.

I had Professor Becker for Animal Science 385 Lab. He is so kind, understanding, and knowledgeable. This was his first time teaching this course so it was a little disorganized. We didn't always know what was being asked of us but he was always very accommodating. All he wanted was for us to learn and didn't harp on useless busy work. He's the best

I had Dr. Becker for AnSci385, but that's not listed for some reason. He has a thick German accent that can be hard to understand, but he's extremely helpful and happy to explain and clarify if needed. He's also very understanding of students' circumstances, so if you need help or extra time for assignments, he'll usually give it to you.
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Gives good feedback--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Not sure how he is when teaching lectures, but as a lab professor I really enjoyed his class! Although he's older, he enjoys helping kids learn and will never reject a student's question or need for more instruction. Material is a little complicated at times but for homework, he provides basically all the answers in his PowerPoint. Grades easy too!
reviews.rating_tags: Clear grading criteria--Gives good feedback--Lots of homework

reviews.comment: There's a lot of homework/discussion posts and you probably won't learn much, but it's an easy A if you do all the assignments. Required final exam was ridiculous and most likely scaled. He's a very nice and chill guy, so take him if you actually want to pass AnSci 200.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Get ready to read

reviews.comment: Klaus is a great guy --very intelligent too-- but I never understood what was going on in his class. The exams had questions removed/added in the middle of the exam.

Says his quizzes they are meant to be easy and people who go to class should do great on them but the quizzes have things he never mentioned. Exams are hard and his answers are sometimes wrong but won't fix them. First exam had things on it from the next chapter and he pretended he talked about them and didn't give back points.

Klaus is such a nice guy, but his lectures are pretty confusing and made me very sleepy, which is hard to do. He wasn't always clear about what he wanted us to get out of lectures (minus 5' to 3') and his test questions were difficult and sometimes hard to understand. His videos were more helpful. But, he's super willing to help you if you need it.

Nice guy but I couldn't understand a word he was talking about. His lectures and videos he made would put you to sleep so get those videos open if you had a sleepless night. Tests were tough because he asked about details that no one seemed to have noticed. Also the wordings on tests were bad. But again, he is a nice guy and cares about students.

Really nice guy. Very down to earth and easy to talk to. He sometimes wanders off into tangents during lectures. Sometimes he relays misinformation and confuses himself and others; he once told us that ddNTP's still have a 3' OH and nobody had the guts to tell him he was wrong. Overall, still a great professor and I highly recommend him.

Biochemistry itself can be real hard to learn. But Prof Mearls was a great professor and lecturer. Really explains concepts well and gives you everything you need to know to succeed in her class. If you study and review lecture notes, you will do a good job on the exams. She's also super chill and down to earth.

Prof Mearls is a nice person, but she makes the material much harder than it should be. I had to use Chat for the last half of the semester to re-explain the notes because she just goes around in circles instead of getting straight to the point. Just expect to put lots of effort in this class. You need to really study and read and practice

Mearls is a nice lady. She genuinely wants students to succeed and puts more effort into teaching than other professors. The exams are usually easier than the practice problems. She can sometimes be longwinded to explain simple stuff but overall was an easy A.

Mearls is a great teacher. While there is a quiz and a group activity assigned on Fridays and due on Sundays, they relate to the tests, and the quizzes have two tries. She gives lots of outside help and extra optional practice sheets.

People are being very dramatic about the difficulty of this class. Mearls explains things very well and posts echo360 so you can go back and watch if confused. Exams are challenging but you will be fine if you study a lot. I learned a lot in this class.

The class was difficult but she was a decent professor for the content. She can be intimidating but is actually very kind and is willing to work with you and help you. Dont skip classes if you want to know whats happening, theres a lot she mentions thats not on the slides, and the exams are pretty difficult but at least she allows a notecard.

She's very smart, but the setup of this class is not the best. Lectures are densely packed with tons of information, and she does allow a notecard on exams, but it's rarefuly helpful. You NEED to know the content inside and out to perform well on exams. Gives extra credit, which is what saved my grade. Final was ridiculously hard, she had to curve.

She's a really good professor. I am a Biology student who opted to take the biochem version of 285. I had an easier time than a lot of my classmates in the ansci version and the bio version. There are 3 exams that are worth 60% of your grade. She offers 2 points of extra credit on each one and has a really good grade replacement policy. Good class.

Mearls is very knowledgeable and gives clear grading guidelines. The class is very structured, and extra credit opportunities are available. The class is very densely packed with material however, and it's easy to get overwhelmed.

Mearls is an incredibly smart professor, but she has clearly made it a goal for students to suffer in this class. I spend a lot of time on this class, probably more than all my other classes combined (this course is very challenging). This class truly tests your academic ability, and you need to be willing to put in the work. Exams are ridiculous.

She's amazing!! Super kind and you can tell she puts a lot of effort into designing her lectures. It's by no means an easy course but she does everything she can to make it easier. Double sided index card for exams, +2 pt ec reflection after exam, and ability to get even more ec by attending different seminars. I recommend this prof for 285.

wasn't the worst professor, but she wasn't great. Lots of exam questions were about topics we discussed once then never again. You don't know your grade during the semester, which is hard for bmb majors because you need a B- to get into any upperlevels. I ended with a 79.8 asked her to round and told me I didnt work hard enough. Girl what??

I took her class and did NOT enjoy it at all PERIOD. She gave lots of practice problems but they rarely were helpful for exams, additionally her study guides did not help. When reaching out to her in emails, my friends and I found she was passive aggressive and not approachable. Would not recommend, fine class but bad professor.
reviews.rating_tags: Lecture heavy--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: This is coming from someone who failed the first exam and got a 100 on the 2nd one. Do all her practice problems and look over the class activities. Know the concepts and teach the material on a whiteboard or something, I promise you'll see your grade improve. Get a good group to do the class activities with. Wonderful professor.

All homeworks/quizs can be worked on together and while the exams can seem like a lot of material, she summarizes it all pretty well within the study guides. This class is only hard if memorization is difficult as the material is just bio 151 expanded out. Recommended to make friends as this class is a ton easier with friends (find a bio major)

Prof Mearls is an understanding professor who always wants her students to succeed. Her lectures are clear and she always answers questions in a helpful way. Exams are a large portion of the class, but are often easier than the homework questions and practice problems, which are intended to make you APPLY the concepts covered in class.

Mearls is such a kind and caring professor but her lectures are extremely dense and exams go into depth. You will need to study a lot and really know your stuff to do well on exams but it is not impossible. Gives 2% extra credit on all exams if you do the reflection and give you the opportunity to add to your total course grade by going to seminars

despite what the reviews may say, it is not impossible to do well in this class. the quizzes have two attempts and all of the information can be found in the slides. when you get a question wrong, it will tell you before your next attempt and provide a brief description that hints towards the correct answer. study slides and use review material!

Biochem is difficult no matter what, I'd recommend Mearls over Miller. She goes very in-depth and at a slow pace in order to help students understand. Attendance is required but either in person or asynchronously. Multiple extra credit chances were given w/ exam reflections and an optional paper at the end of the semester. HW was useless though.
The TAs suck at grading. Giving low grades to so,e ppl but not others even if they worked together

Unless you completely understand the questions right off the bat, you're screwed. Doesn't use layman's terms at all and throws a million things at you per lecture. An extremely average teacher for the level of material she's supposed to be teaching. If your major is outside of BIOCHEM you're going to need luck to pass this class.
This class is making me consider how it feels to have a scruffy 1/2 inch diameter rope around my neck

Dr. Mearls is caring and her class is very organized. The slides, videos, etc. are always posted which is helpful. No formal lab reports apart from lab notebook checks and answering simple questions. There are four bigger assignments throughout the semester but overall, if you just put effort in you will be just fine!!

Nice person but average professor. She is really kind and ready to help you if you reach out. Although Professor Mearls' lectures look straightforward, her class activities and exams are super confusing. She gives a lot of extra credit tho. I barely got an A thanks to that.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Lecture heavy--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Biochem is a difficult subject but I think Dr. Mearls is a wonderful professor. She goes at a slower pace and simplifies concepts w organized slides. The material gets much harder as the semester goes on so dont procrastinate studying, all the concepts build on each other. Exams worth 60% but you get a note card. SI exam reviews helped a lot.

Very challenging course for sure, lectures weren't required but counted for 6% of the grade and if you didn't attend that 6% would switch to your exam grad (so exams counted for more). Lectures were way too fast and exams exceptionally difficult. TA's and SI's were helpful.

This is one of the most difficult classes I've taken at UMass yet, but it is possible to do well if you put in the work and start studying more than a week before exams. Be prepared to learn a LOT of information. Mearls is a good professor but she will only go over things once, and the questions on activities and exams are very specific.

285 was my most interesting class this semester! Mearls does a great job teaching and is happy to answer questions/clear up doubts.

Lectures are dense and can go by quickly. Exams/class activity questions can def be pretty ambiguous or specific. Difficult but NOT impossible to get an A. Attend SI & TA review sessions, you'll only thank yourself.
Mearls finds joy in our suffering.

I took this class with Mearls to avoid taking it with Laura Francis, a professor I also hate. After finishing this class with Mearls I wish I went through the horror of taking it with Francis. Every day you go to class, get material thrown at you and leave questioning your major and life. Mearls prays on her student's downfall. Do not do it.

Elizabeth Mearls appears to almost have a desire for her students to struggle, the tests are genuinely unlike anything I have ever seen. You're allowed a notecard of notes (Front & Back), but it rarely mattered because her tests are pretty hard. Unless you fully comprehend all of the content and have it well memorized, be prepared to struggle.

Wow, what a doozy. When taking this class you will look in the mirror at least 50 times this semester and think: "is school really for me?" and the correct answer to that after this class is no. My god does nothing make sense. Each day we blitz through new pathways at ranging amounts of detail, yet come exams you are expected to know everything. No

Good professor, the slides are pretty useful. The weekly quizzes and worksheet are pretty tedious, but the slides can get you through it. The content is mostly memorization so there is not much that she can do to help you. The content is basically just bio151 but a bit more in depth.

I would not recommend this instructor. The slides she uses for teaching are poorly made and she fails at conveying relevant information in a meaningful and organized way, where concepts could have been explained easily. The exam questions are difficult and often center around aspects of concepts not taught in the course or present in the textbook.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Participation matters

reviews.comment: I did enjoy the class and her teaching, but the main issue was the exams and the quizzes. I found some questions vague and so confusing to determine the right answer (e.g. select the "best" answer). I think the structure worked against the students leading to losing so many points even when the concepts were clear. The lectures were great though!

Great professor teaching a challenging course. Lots of resources exist to help students understand. Lectures can be quick and cover lots of information, re-watching them is critical. Class quizzes and activities can be tricky, review before completing them. Extra credit options help a lot, make sure to take them.

very nice professor however, she will only cover materials in lecture once and it will be on the exams. exams are difficult with both a combination of multiple choice and open response. exams are 60%. there are class activities (15%) and quizzes(20%) both graded on accuracy as well. it feels as if she doesn't want us to succeed.

She is an awesome professor and cares a lot about her student's learnings. yes, it is definitely a hard class, but she makes the material very understandable and has lots of resources to help students. If you're willing to put in the work, and go through the material thoroughly, this class is doable!

Elizabeth Mearls was a kind person and really wants the best for you. This semester she tweaked her grading system that allowed me to get a better grade than I probably deserved. I personally thought this class required a good amount of studying. There were 4 exams all weighted 15%. The other 40% was pretty much free points so don't miss out.

Offers extra credit, quizzes aren't timed and class activties are graded based on effort. Her lectures are good but she will only explain things once and topics that she barely goes over is fair game for the exam which count for majority of your grade. My advice is attend SI sessions and her office hours. Decent class but wouldn't take it again.

Exams and quizzes do not match up with lectures and are extremely difficult yet make up majority of your grade. She only explains things once but does not explain it well and you end up teaching yourself through the book if you want even a chance at succeeding. I switched majors because of this class. i can tell she wants to do well but fails at it
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Lecture heavy--Test heavy

reviews.comment: she is the best!! teaches biochem so well given how hard of a class it is. takes the time to actually learn people's names and she truly cares about her students. pay attention in lecture; exams are hard but you will do well if you study and she also lets you use a notecard on the exam.
reviews.rating_tags: Clear grading criteria--Lecture heavy--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Her lectures are spoken clearly and explained relatively well, but she will only say anything once. Exams are frequent and difficult, and everything covered in lecture up to the DAY OF an exam is fair game. Questions require critical thinking, and for the first exam, Bio 151 was better preparation than Mearls' own class. Go to the SI exam reviews.

Took summer sesh Biochem 320, she is one of the most organized, straightforward professors I have ever had. A difficult class but she gives you the opportunity to learn w/ minimal stress over grades. Lots of xtra cred and forum posts based on participation. Her notes/slides are very organized. Never thought I'd actually like learning biochem!

She is one of my absolute favorite professors on campus. She is a very caring professor who wants to see her students succeed and learn the information. Her exams are based on understanding no just memorizing so you have to make sure you know the material well. Go to her office hours and talk with her, she is a very nice person.

Great professor who really cares about her students. Her lectures can be dense but going to SI sessions and TA office hours really made the difference in my learning of the material. She gives easy extra credit and her exams are tough, but not nearly as bad as people warned me about, you'll do fine if you understand (not memorize) the concepts :)
reviews.rating_tags: Lecture heavy--Skip class? You won't pass.--EXTRA CREDIT

reviews.comment: Professor Mearls is a great professor. I did terrible on the first exam but was still able to get an A in the class. You need to figure out which study methods work for biochem and make sure you don't fall behind. Review material and make sure you really understand it for free response questions. There are many extra credit opportunities.

Prof Mearls is very caring, approachable, and has tons of extra credit. She even makes an active effort to memorize every students name. She very much cares about her students succeeding. If you put in the work (which you WILL have to do, it is biochemistry after all), there is no excuse not to do well! Seriously though, she is great.
Be prepared to work very hard for your grade. Theres opportunities for extra credit throughout the semester. Tests are difficult, critical thinking and hypothetical questions.

Prof. Mearls is a caring lady. Best way to study for this class is to thoroughly make sure you know everything on the slides and do the practice problems. She offers a lot of extra credit throughout the semester & opportunities to provide feedback on the course. Sometimes wording on exams can be confusing, but for the most part is fine.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Lecture heavy--EXTRA CREDIT

reviews.comment: Her exams include a lot of stuff that was hardly discussed in class and are not often what we would expect. However, she gives a ton of extra credit opportunities! Plus I find her lectures easy to follow. Overall this class isn't bad.

The exams were 20 mc and 2 open response but the open response was worth 40% of the grade. The topics she chose were always ones she barely talked about and/or talked about the lecture before the exam. I studied all week for an exam and still failed it. The lectures won't help you learn anything.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Skip class? You won't pass.--Test heavy

reviews.comment: I really loved having Mearls as a professor. She was my favorite professor last semester! Mearls is very passionate and understanding. I reccomend her.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Skip class? You won't pass.--Group projects

reviews.comment: Do not take biochemistry with Mearls. Dropped the major after taking a class with her. Her exams are non-related to the lectures and it seems like you need a big brain for biochemistry other than the things she teaches you in lectures. Absolute horror. Would not recommend.

Professor Mearls lectures make it seem like shes confused about what shes teaching about. The exams are hard and the wording of the short answer questions is terrible. She offers extra credit essays at the end of the semester. I wouldn't recommend taking this class if you want to actually learn something :/
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Lecture heavy--EXTRA CREDIT

reviews.comment: She is a kind, good person but not a good professor. Unclear and exam is very hard.

Professor Mearls is unclear or confusing during lecture. Her poll questions often have more than one right answer and she asks for the "best" answer then will contradict herself on the equal level of accuracy of other answers. Her exams are equally confusing so with the already dense topics doing well requires much more work in this course.
The exams don't really reflect the lectures and weekly quizzes. Not many opportunities to come in and ask questions.

Professor Mearls is a great person and clearly has a lot of passion for her field. Lots of extra credit opportunities and plenty of free points in the form of problem sets, which aren't graded on correctness. Her exams are what bring her rating down, as they often don't reflect lecture material and got quite frustrating.

Professor Mearls is fine. There is no homework, so some students fall behind due to lack of actual time spent on the material as none is technically required. That being said, an hour or two a week outside of lecture spent on the quizzes and a couple hours per test makes for a pretty easy test. Lecture material and exams are often different.

Professor Mearls is fine. Seriously, no more and no less, just fine. There isn't a crazy amount of homework, which leads some students into thinking there isn't any work to do, but just studying every week and putting effort into the weekly quizzes makes most tests a no-brainer. Point to note, lectures are wonky and tests often don't reflect them.

In all honesty, shes a kind person and a good professor. I wouldve definitely done better in the class had I not given up on my work and began studying a week before exams. Dont be like me!! This class is really dependent on YOU understanding the lectures and making connections to the activities we do in class. Shes there to help!

i found that they werent a good teacher to take online, the work load could be overwhelming and their lectures and notes were hard to follow along with especially if you struggle with any type of learning disabilities.

Mearls is just a really nice person who really cares about her students, which makes the class worth the effort. It's a tough class with a lot of information, but she does a great job of making it accessible and giving plenty of resources. Lots of opportunity for boosting your grades as well!
reviews.rating_tags: Respected--Skip class? You won't pass.--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: Mearls exams are hard but it is applied knowledge meaning you have to understand the material and have great critical thinking instead of memorizing facts which is what I like. She gives you a lot of opportunity for extra credit because she knows her exams are hard. There are a lot of stuff to learn in her class but the lecture are not too long.

I loved mearls!! We had 2 lectures, 2 lecture wrap up questions, a worksheet (done with 3 other people), and a quiz every week. 3 midterms (non cum.) and a final (mostly new stuff but cum.). She gave the individual option of having asynchronous or synchronous group work for the worksheets every week and there are so many extra credit opportunities!

Mearls is AMAZING. She's the best instructor I have this semester. You'd have to try NOT to get an A in this class. 3 midterms only worth 10% of your grade and a final worth 20%. Tests on conceptual knowledge so it's not just memorization/regurgitating little details. She's also extremely accessible outside of class. Definitely take 285 with her!!
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Amazing lectures--Caring

reviews.comment: Take 420 with Miller instead. Mearls' exams are hypothetical, application questions which make it 10x harder (35 mc, 2 short essay on OWL). Talks fast during lecture, speeds through everything, provides vague answers to student questions. She cares but doesn't know how to communicate material effectively. Study hard. Get 100s on hw and exercises.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Test heavy--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: She cares students, but not good at lecture. She wants to help students and gives a lot of extra points tho.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Skip class? You won't pass.

reviews.comment: Professor Mearls and Miller worked together during the transition to remote learning which wasn't taken well by students and made the class 10x more difficult. I loved attending lectures and there is little work to do outside of class. Watch the lectures, take notes, and do the class activities and you'll pass. Her HW's are on masteringchem.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Clear grading criteria--EXTRA CREDIT

reviews.comment: Professor Mearls really cares about her students and wants them to succeed. The class is not easy, and she did not make it easier due to covid-19, however she wants us to work hard. Given these things, she is very effective at teaching the material, and explains things well. Tests are difficult but if you study a lot you will succeed.
