reviews.comment: Course designed to help you succeed like each exam only being worth 10% for 3 exams(1 drop). Lectures were largely information heavy and simply reading slides, slides which weren't released until days before the exam. Also answered key questions like what to focus on for exams with "I don't know." You'll do well if you keep up with the busy work.
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Clear grading criteria--Lots of homework

reviews.comment: Simple weekly assignments were a big part of the grade for this class, which helped to offset the difficult exams. Lots of the exam questions were so niche that no amount of studying could prepare me for them. Labs can be confusing but the TA's were usually able to help. Bill answered almost every question with “I don't know.”

I have tremendous amounts of respect for this guy. He's kind, and well dressed, and keeps the class engaged. He's very smart and fair. The labs are a bit confusing sometimes but I think he's the best professor in the geology department. His classes always start with good music and he's a no BS professor which I think is funny to watch.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Lots of homework--Hilarious

reviews.comment: Busy work, waste of time

Do not take this class if you want an easy A. The lectures are very laid back and casual, and they don't cover a good amount of what's on the exam, and the questions get very specific. It's easy to miss assignments since they are due at 9 AM, and points get taken off for dumb reasons like writing more than 1 sentence.
reviews.rating_tags: EXTRA CREDIT--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: just go to class and do the readings and you'll be fine. There was a lot of busy work, but the subject is interesting and Prof Clement tried to engage students. He's very direct though, which can take some getting used to. Labs were fun.

This class is very simple to grasp and doesn't take a lot of time outside of the classroom. If you go to lecture and pay attention this class will be an easy A. The labs are easy yet a little time consuming, and the TA's are very helpful. The professor is great and everything is well organized.

Professor is personally a great guy. Loves what he does. But not the best teacher. Slides are confusing and not straightforward. Labs are tedious and harshly graded, not to mention irrelevant to what will be on the exams. Labs need to be helpful for exam prep, not irrelevant material. Lectures need to be more clear and organized.

The lectures were full of random facts that would pop up in the 25-multiple-choice-question exams so paying attention is important. The lab is totally unrelated to the lecture and is honestly more important to do well in. Go to TA office hours they will give you the answers to the labs. If you miss lectures, just go to the exam review session.

there is a textbook but doing the readings is time consuming and unessecary. all the information you need is from the slides. exams can be dificult but he drops the lowest one plus curves them well. theres a lot of little homework assignments that would take me ten minutes total and really are clutch. great choice for a gen ed requirement.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--EXTRA CREDIT--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: Has a lot of boring assignments that are due each week but are easy and can be completed in less than 15 minutes a week. The lectures are boring so make sure to study the slides if you don't go to class. There are 4 tests but 1 drops and there is group portion. Lab is easy when you go to office hours so they can help you.

Lecture slides chaotic and almost 100 slides long, most of your grades are from your labs, and good luck if you get a bad TA, does not explain concepts well, offers no study guides or practice tests, exams are unpredictable, harsh grader
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Lecture heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: I do not think Professor Clement is boring, you can tell he loves what he is teaching and he wants you to do well in the class. Also because of the lab, the homework, and the exams there's a lot of places for you to improve your grade. He also puts silly videos in the lectures to make you laugh :)

He is a nice guy, but his lectures can be boring, and he sometimes veers into off-topic subjects. I found the labs to be fairly harshly graded, especially with how vague questions can often be. Only way to study for exams is through the slideshows which are often filled with unnecessary slides, sometimes making it unclear what to focus on.
:clown:

His lectures are extremely chaotic, he talks about random stuff that won't even be on the exams. He doesn't give study guides or practice exams (which means you have to know the slides extremely well to do well on exams) and the TA review sessions aren't structured (they expect you to bring in questions). The lab is also terrible.

Bill is very passionate about his students and his class, though he seems to have some trouble incorporating this energy into his lectures.  Lecture slides were very dry, but I definitely took some good things away from this class.  Exams were unnecessarily difficult and require you to know specifics about the slides.
Great class if you need the PS GenEd. Chill proffessor, easy homework assignments,  and lots of available office hours if needed. Lectures slightly chaotic but they are always posted on Moodle.

Even though moodle has a discussion board program, he makes students pay for a $30 program because it has an AI grading system.
The semester consists of busy work for easy grade points, 4 in class exams with one getting dropped, and labs that take up too much time.
It's an easy class, I just can't respect it from a CS perspective.
this guy loves rocks!

Bill is okay. He clearly knows what he's talking about and does a very good job conveying the information in lecture, but his personality is a bit bland. Doesn't really make lectures exciting. He's a nice guy, though. His homework assignments were kind of useless. Three (small) weekly assignments that teach you precisely nothing about geology.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: early attendance classes filled with slides that one could just read on their own. unaccommodating professor during exams. neglects emails for weeks which is annoying and shows effort
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Test heavy

reviews.comment: Attendance wasn't required and lectures were always posted online. Weekly homework takes up a significant portion of the overall grade so definitely do the homeworks.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: Clement was awesome, difficult exams because of tricky questions so I would say you really should attend lectures to get a full grasp on things.

Bill is a great character. He is very passionate about geology, almost comically. He can be pretty monotone, especially at 9 in the morning, but at least he really cares about the subject and doesn't care if you show up. He gave 3 weekly assignments, which seems like a lot but was very easy, just tedious. Easy class, definitely recommended.
If you attend class you will get an A. Easy class for grades but if you dont show up you will be lost. Really is passionate about what he teaches.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Get ready to read--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: He's a good professors and he cares about the class a lot. He tries to be understanding and joke around. The homework isn't difficult it's just a decent amount of it just like any other class (it is time sensitive though). If you go to the class and study for the tests then you'll do great.

He can be somewhat confusing at times, but he has genuine passion for both geology and teaching. He is patient and kind with his students, and during covid has listened to student's needs. He has even gone so far as to reach out to students who have not done well and offer encouragment. His tests are hard and somewhat confusing to prepare for.
Bill Clement is the most mundane man you'll ever meet. The class was very boring (for a 9am) and many students nodded off each class. He did teach the course well, so credit to him for that.

To me, the class wasn't that difficult. The homework (weekly packback responses and reading a news article) wasn't difficult, just a little time-consuming. The lab does not correlate or matter at all to lecture. Don't bother buying the books, they aren't on the test if you do want them just rent from the library. Tests are on content from lecture

He is a kind-hearted, funny and adorable old professor who will seem to be a good professor at first, but towards the middle of the semester, you'll come to realize he's an incompetent, boring, and nagging professor who assigns way too much homework for a gen ed. It's not a hard class per se, and I do like him, but if you're looking to learn.. well

I didn't know I loved Geology until I took this class. Bill is a nice guy and really understands the student lifestyle. Therefore, the class isn't too much work but you still learn a lot. The tests aren't as easy as you think they will be, but all of the grading is fair and you can make up lost points with homework and easy labs.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Clear grading criteria--Caring

reviews.comment: Pro: Pyramid lets you use anything during test Cons: Tedious irrelevant lab (to class/tests) Echos has no sound Goes through slide too fast to take notes Slideshows unclear, picture-heavy, no context/information Inaccurate class schedule condescending Writes small on the board with light markers Asks for feedback, doesn't listen to it.

Bill is super helpful and kind. It helps if you get to know him, as in any big lecture classe. I found it wasn't hard to stand out after introducing myself and showing up to all the classes. Hardly any homework (2 small assignments throughout the semester plus a book that most people didn't read). Dry lectures, but you learn a lot if you want to...

Very hard for a 100 level class. Exams are very info-heavy, no guidelines for studying you are expected to know everything. Lectures are boring and attendance is taken. Mandatory field trip all day Saturday before Easter. Labs sometimes interesting, comparatively but long. Lab every other week and take home labs. Nice guy but would never take again

Please just spend your time elsewhere. For a gen it's boring and a waste of time. Mandatory attendance is annoying. As you've collected from other reviews: wack grader and he WILL bore you. Get ready to sleep and want to skip. Sure AI the essays but they are tedious prompts for vague grading. Never accessible outside class. Take an easier gen!!

I definitely enjoyed his class, but he was a tough grader and didn't provide a detailed grading criteria. Even if you participate in class and do all the work it was fairly difficult to get an A. I think the highest grade on every assignment wasn't more than a 95. Really cool class though and you can tell he cares a lot about the content.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Gives good feedback

reviews.comment: It's a shame because I like the topic, but he has a big ego which tends to put down some enthusiastic people in the class. He grades tough, doesn't prepare lectures pretty clearly, doesn't even try to engage the class in a meaningful way. Always coming in talkin bout I'm tired, It's been a long week. Not a ton of work but tough to get an A
Voice puts you to sleep and overall boring lectures but not hard to get in A if you show up to class and do the few papers

Amazing class! Some people complained that he was a “tough grader” but he's just trying to make you a better writer, and if you listen to his notes, and pay attention in class, you can pass easily. 
Has dry humor that I think can be mistaken for sarcasm/being rude, but it definitely isn't.
Very chill guy, super understanding and funny. I feel like his essay grading was pretty harsh, and the discussions were a lot of reading and dragged.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: I thought he was a fairly enthusiastic teacher, and I enjoyed the subject matter and class discussions. However, I genuinely have no idea how anyone is supposed to get an A in this class. I got nothing lower than a 90 on the essays and had one unexcused absence and got an A-, as you need a 95 to get an A but the highest essay grade given is a 93???
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Participation matters--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Clearly has a big ego and he doesn't let anyone forget it.
Do not take this class!
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--So many papers

reviews.comment: Was not helpful in the slightest, talked down to his students.
Can be extremely rude and does not truly care for his students. Completely unavailable by email or canvas outside of class time. Not understanding about family emergencies or difficulties.

Professor Torres is a nice guy with a good sense of humor. His classes were long and lecture heavy, sometimes difficult to pay attention the whole time. He asks questions that are difficult to answer, so there wasn't a lot of opportunity for participation. He assigns a lot of reading that you can get away with not completing.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Don't take this class if you do not have to. Professor Torres does not respond to his emails which makes it impossible to ask questions outside of class. His lectures are typically lazy and he always talks about how tired he is which is extremely unprofessional. He is a very tough grader and takes weeks to grade your papers.

He's super chill but I found his lectures to be so boring. He speaks in a very monotone voice and I was just so bored in all the classes. As for work there's readings for every class that you can get away with not reading. There's also like 4 mini essays which is whatever. I didn't really like him or the class tbh.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: A chill guy, but the grading for the essays was harsh. Hard to get an A bc it's 95%+. Grade dependent on TA. Hard to pay attention during lecture. Speaks very slowly and monotonously and the room is dimly lit, like a guided meditation. Do not sit in back or you will fall asleep! Not an easy Gen-Ed! Only 4 grades: attendance, 2 papers, and mid term.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: He's very chill/laid back, very lenient, and really cares about your opinion on the topics he teaches. Assigned readings for each class and we spend class time discussing and connecting it to society. Only 4 major grades: attendance, two papers, and one group presentation. Only critique is canceling class last second. Would recommend!
Knows about his material but understands that people just take this as a GenEd. Easy class, cool guy

He is a cool guy. He knows a lot about the subject. He likes to interact with the students in the class and even takes the time to memorize our names. The class is only graded by attendant and 3 papers so there not that many places to get points however he is a light grader is submitted an essay with no sources and he gave me an 80%.

barely any work and super flexible about all deadlines. i turned both the papers we had in late. he gave me a 96 and a 95 (I'm an awful writer truly). he would just sit on his desk and ask about our day and discuss the(very optional) readings he assigned. I think he just gives everyone 90+ because he is too lazy to put effort into grading. good guy
reviews.rating_tags: Group projects--Lecture heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: took afroam101 with him this sem. he seemed to not be prepared at all for the courses and often the lectures seemed kind of random. the material was interesting and there was only a few assignments but we would hear about them very late and not have much time to work on them, for example we just did our midterm pres during the last week of class.
the best!

Such a nice and chill guy. The moodle/ course in general is just really disorganized. He's really fair and there's not a lot of work, just a lot of readings that you have to do if you want to participate in discussions. 2 essays, attendance and scattered discussions on moodle make up your grade.

DON'T TAKE THIS OVER BREAK. Either way be ready to give up a lot of time. Makes ECE 124 look easy. Not all Bill's fault, it's the way the class is. Start work ASAP; better yet start during the lecture. You'll have to resubmit everything 3+ times if you want a good grade. His feedback is good, do everything he says. Don't fall behind no matter what.

I had him for ECE 213 and it was his first time teacher the class so I don't think he had everything fully figured out yet. he is very willing to put down whatever he is doing and help you when you come into office hours. I had numerous occasions where I took a while to understand a concept and he never got frustrated or impatient with me

I took ECE202 and it;s absolutely the worst ever. Bill assigns a homework about every 3 days and the only way to get good grades is to attempt at least 3 times per homework, meaning that you have at least one hw each day. The workload is way more than any other classes and it's just a 3 credit course. He simply wants you to have no personal life.

His grading system and harsh feedback on assignments was just an example of how inconsiderate he is. I should have been wise enough to take this class in the fall with Prof Parente like all my other friends. This guy literally drove me into a ccph counselling session.

You can literally write a perfect code and still be far from a perfect score just because half the things in the feedback are not given in the instructions. He knows what people think of him but is still unwilling to change. Man just doesn't have a life...and expects the same from his students as well( to be immersed in matlab all their lives)

Gives good examples in discussion and offers alternate approaches to problems than in lecture which is very helpful and gives you a better grasp of the concepts. May come off a little cold but willing to help and youll do well if you put in effort

Absolutely terrible feedback for assignments. Your work can be completely functional yet if you're missing a certain word in a comment, half of your points are deducted. He also wants you to start the next assignment before you can even get feedback for the first, so you don't know if you're doing things wrong. An ADHD's student's nightmare.

grades incredibly harshly. expects students to submit assignments multiple times long before theyre due so he can correct them but doesn't give feedback until the day before theyre due. youll submit a project that works perfectly and he'll give you 5/100 because you didn't name variables how he likes them. very unforgiving and inconsiderate system

Bartu was an incredible professor and his passion made his lectures so much more engaging than some of the other profs I have had so far. He was always wiling to answer students' questions and I could tell genuinely wanted to see his students succeed. Both Bartu and his TA, Jacob Lee, increased my confidence in my ability to do math.

Bartu was an incredible professor and his passion made his lectures so much more engaging than some of the other profs I have had so far. He was always wiling to answer students' questions and I could tell genuinely wanted to see his students succeed. Both Bartu and his TA, Jacob Lee, increased my confidence in my ability to do math.

I came into this class dreading Calc 2, and am coming out with a good experience all thanks to Bartu. He cares a lot about everyone and their progress. He takes time during class to answer everyone's questions and is really clear with his answers. And he makes sure the lectures address what the class is struggling on. He's the best, please take him

Bartu is so clearly passionate about what he does and will answer any question you have. He explains the topics very clearly. Very understanding about extensions. Great teacher and great person overall.

Bartu is the absolute best. He made Calc 2 my most enjoyable course and I looked forward to his classes. He was always very passionate about math and you could tell he genuinely cared about how you did in class. On top of that he always explained everything extremely well. Take him if you can.
Amazing dude. Have never been to a lacture where someone is clearly so passionate about their work as him. I would take this guy for every class if i could.
Bartu did a wonderful job explaining complex topics and you can tell he's very passionate about math. Assignments were reasonable and it was very easy to get help if needed. Great guy!

No rubric or guidelines for assignments and grading seemed extremely subjective. When asked about grading, professor would not provide a response. Was bad with answering emails and exams were difficult to prep for given the amount of content and specificity of questions. Avoid this class if you care for your gpa.

He has a hard time replying to emails in an appropriate amount of time and addressing all contents of said emails. Exams are half MC, half similar to HW problems. MC is extremely specific and cannot be prepared for in advance as he expects you to listen and remember every word he says in lectures. 
Ex: Q on Final- something about Galápagos Islands.
reviews.rating_tags: Group projects--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Bing is an excellent, highly-qualified upper-level finance professor. His long track record in the industry provides students with great insight on the evolution of hedge funds and financial institutions over the years. Make sure to form a good group to do projects and homework with, as you work with them for the entirety of the semester.

I can tell Bing is a smart guy, but being smart doesn't always make you the best teacher. Most of the homework questions looked nothing like the exams. The only prep he gave for exams is taking a few practice questions from the textbook. Most of my studying was simply reading the textbook, because what we learned in class did not prepare us.

Tough Grader, tough exam, tough projects. However, those are what it takes for you to get into the top Quant positions in Wall Street. It's really your option to have a easier life or a challenging & well-rewarded life.

Although Mr Liang is knowledgeable, he is a rly bad teacher. Homework assignments on chapters we havent started yet. Very unclear what to expect on the exams and the homeworks are nearly irrelevant to the exams. Projects are extremely unclear and difficult. You practically learn everything from the book and not him. BAD at helping you understand
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Get ready to read--Group projects

reviews.comment: He is very knowledgeful and always has a passion for his lecture, but the tests are very difficult you don't always know what to expect or study for it.

Bing is extremely knowledgeable. He also is a decorated professor and very well respected in the industry. His class however is very difficult. His texts are difficult. The first project was one the most difficult projects I have ever completed. Second project is a 12 page paper. This class is hard but if you put in the time you will learn a lot.

Clearly extremely knowledgeable and his enthusiasm shows in class, but he's not the greatest teacher in my opinion.  He goes very fast through lectures and can be confusing at times.  Projects and exams are difficult and he can be vague about what to focus on studying.

Bing is super smart, and a great professor. However, this class is really difficult. The tests are tricky and require a lot of studying. The projects are nearly impossible (a confusing excel assignment, and a 12 page paper). Take the class with him because you will learn a lot, but it will not be easy.

Professor Bing has an impressive resume of studies and research work done on finance, specifically on alternative investments and hedgefunds. His class is hard, but interesting. His lectures are a little brief for the topics covered, so make sure to study the text. 2 Midterms,  2 Projects, 1 Final & Attendance for final grade. Pick your group well!

Awful. Did my first ever bachelor lab internship at his lab. Yet I had no mentor and he is not an approachable man at all. Waste of time. Yet he had extremely unrealistic expectations. In the end he did a cowardly thing by writing a negative LOR instead of giving direct feedback and had me rejected from Unis. He does not intend to help students.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--So many papers

reviews.comment: It has been years since I have taken a class with this man. I don't even know if he still "teaches". He was absolutely the worst professor, teacher, educator that I have ever had. I thought I could learn so much from him because he is so known in his field but he is not someone who should be teaching. He doesn't know how to. Brilliant but terrible

Don't take this class unless you have a lot of time and also love being stressed and unhappy.  The material is ridiculously dense and exams are awful.  Lectures are monotone and not enlightening, and talking with him is unpleasant at best.  You learn a lot, but honestly it isn't worth it.  Take A&P instead if you value your love of the subject.

Be forewarned: His exams are all open response and graded quite subjectively. It doesn't matter if your answer is correct, if you do not hit the exact bullet points he writes down on his answer key, you will not receive full credit. Refuses to scale exams or course even when average grades are in the 40-50 range.

You will need to know every detail in order to answer questions on the exam as Bittman teaches from a mechanistic perspective. There are no tricks on the exam if you know the material cold. You will have to read and reread chapters several times and consult alternative sources. Expect to work very hard but the results are rewarding. Good luck!

Avoid this class. The material is super complicated and Bittman expects you to know everything about everything. The amount of material covered is absurd, and tests are near impossible, with most people not finishing and regularly failing them. He uses the book a lot and its critical. Do NOT take this class, I wish I hadnt. GPA destroyer.

I took Human Physiology because I was really interested in the course material. I had read reviews about him before but ignored them thinking it couldn't possibly be that terrible. DO NOT take this class with him if you value YOUR GPA AND YOUR FUTURE!!! He cannot teach and his exams are crazy long and difficult, no matter how much you study.

Inspiring and helpful professor IF YOU ARE SERIOUS ABOUT PERSUING A CAREER IN SCIENCE OR RESEARCH. He expects you to be self-motivated. If you care enough to read into things and develop your own questions, you can learn a TON from this man. Do not take his classes if you are looking for an easy A or can't handle criticism.

If you really want to be a scientist; take his class. "Wahh it's hard, and he doesn't coddle me!". If you want to have a significant advantage over other biology majors, take one of his classes. Ask him for help with anything, but don't expect to go to his office looking for a handout when you haven't put the work in to try and learn yourself.

You are probably thinking of taking this class because Bio Rhythms are interesting.DO NOT TAKE THIS CLASS with Bittman, he is a terrible teacher.You only have 2 exams.They are on 17+ papers and you are expected to know all the  pathways.I was really interested in this subject.Take this pass/fail if you must but don't expect to learn anything.
He is honestly the worst professor I have ever had at UMASS. I do not recommend taking ANY classes with him. I'm serious!

I took Bio Ethics with Mr Bittman for my freshmen seminar, a one credit course. He is insane. I found myself dedicating more time to the class than my Bio 100 class due the extensive presentations and papers he assigns. DO NOT TAKE THIS CLASS, DROP IT IMMEDIATELY.

Good guy but an awful professor.   There was a lot of memorization in the course because there is no textbook and his slides were just bad. Don't take this course or any course with this professor unless you enjoy being unhappy and wasting three months of your life.

The hardest class I've taken at UMass. You don't need to MEMORIZE 35 scientific  papers as other reviewers write, but you're expected to understand them. The work is difficult,  but once you finish, your critical thinking/reading/scientific skills are greatly enhanced. Prof. Bittman is helpful if you meet with him after class. Very knowledgeable!

Terrible terrible professor!He provided no background on the material he taught. He also expected us to memorize 35+ scientific papers including the molecular pathways for the final and half of that for the midterm. Did his own SRTI not the schools because I think he knows he was bad! Interesting material but terrible class structure and professor.

DO NOT TAKE THIS CLASS (unless you enjoy getting F's and reading papers that are graduate level without any background or lessons from the professor). He expects you to know procedures and exact biochemical pathways before taking course. He is not helpful in clarification. NO textbook for help!

Don't take this course, unless you have a genuine interest and I mean unless you love this stuff, DO Not Take this class. Incredibly elitist professor, worst one I've ever seen, Looking down on your students isn't the right way to teach fyi! Avoid the class or you will regret it.
This professor has no interest int inspiring or even teaching college students. He has a temper and is very damaging to students during class and outside of class.

Don't take it unless you can dedicate alot of time to this class. I spent over 20 hours studying for each exam and i still got low 60's on both...which is in his B range. Nice guy though, very personable if you approach him after class or in his office. He loves what he does, and I'd say one of the most competent professors i've ever had at umass
All I can think about is why why why didn't I heed the warnings of you RMPers? Please do not make the same mistake I did. DO NOT TAKE THIS CLASS!! It will have you bashing your head against the wall.

Terrible professor. Came in loving physiology and now I don't care much for it. He's very egotistical (compares himself to God) and it is ALWAYS the students' fault when they get a question wrong, it is never his quality of teaching. Terrible, terrible professor. As a senior, he has been the worst professor I have had the past four years.

People who have commented seem to think 'difficulty' and 'how much you learn' in a class are automatically related. This is not true, especially with this class. He puts enormous effort into trying to nitpick students on quizzes/tests. You DON'T learn much because you have to focus on how he'll try to trick you. AVOID THIS CLASS!
Horrible class and teacher. DO NOT TAKE IT!
I truly learned nothing and it was such a waste of time. He was really the worst teacher I have ever had and he talks to just hear the sound of his own voice

He seems knowledgeable about the topic but cannot relate it to students who do not share his passion. He doesn't answer questions and gets overtly annoyed when we do not understand something. Lectures are boring and I loved biology before I took his class. Good thing he was only for a 1/3 of the semester. Johnson is WAY BETTER for the 2nd part!
read right off slides that you could find online.

Horrible class! Very difficult to understand and he has a hard time connecting with the students and teaching in a way that actually benefits non-bio majors. Pick a different class if you are looking to fulfill a gen-ed.

Do not listen to the course description on this class, Bittman just talked about corn the whole time.  He speaks on a level far above the students, and his tests were so ridiculous a 23/35 (about 66%) was scaled to a B+.  Avoid him.
needs to understand that all students are not at the phd level...huge temper problem
One of the worst! Avoid him, he has a temper problem and expects way to much from his student. his classes are as harder or maybe harder then med school classes.
He goes fast, but if you can stay on top of things you will learn a LOT of physiology.  You have to take this class very seriously, but it is worth the effort.  Material helped a TON on the MCAT.
Expects you to do the reading and understand it. Only take this class if you're serious about biology. Knows his stuff, but be prepared, because it will be hard- but you'll learn so much.
Extremly fast, you are expected to comprehend  subjects far to quickly. I do not recommend this professor.

Expects everyone in the class to be at PhD level and is very unforgiving- accused our entire section of cheating on DUCK quizzes by using the guest login before our own login, threw temper tantrum and lowered everyone's grades...real mature...

Goes extremely quickly through the information and expects that students are able to comprehend it as quickly as he rattles it off.  Exams are hard but scaled, and he tries hard to help students through office hours and reviews.
If you want to learn, I mean, LEARN endocrinology, take it with this professor. He knows his stuff. Clear lectures and difficult tests, but you come away with alot.
No Comments

If you have the opportunity to take one of her classes, DO IT. Decent amount of reading per week but never an insane amount. Many attainable assignments will result in a good grade and a legitimate understanding of the material. Kindest and most personable teacher I have ever had who gives fantastic lectures that are engaging. Go to office hours!

Professor Billings is the best professor I've ever had at UMass. She is extremely caring and kind toward her students and offers many support outlets. Class lectures were extremely engaging, and they felt like Ted Talks! All of the work in this class is meaningful and has left a strong impact on me. Take a class with her if you get the chance!
Professor Billings is a phenomenal. She really cares about students and her lectures are so interesting. This is honestly my favorite class and she's my favorite professor at umass. Highly recommend.

Her lectures feel like a TedTalk- she genuinely cares about the content as well as her students. The pop quizzes are extremely easy if you just skim the reading for the day. Only two long papers but you were able to decide the topic for both. Highly recommend Katie!
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Amazing lectures --Gives good feedback

reviews.comment: Katie was overall a good lecturer. My biggest issue was the lack of extra credit given, as well as unclear syllabus. She said that participation and attendance was one grade, but only graded us on attendance based on pop quizzes given out randomly. I intentionally participated for nothing. Pretty unfair way of grading.
reviews.rating_tags: EXTRA CREDIT--Gives good feedback--Beware of pop quizzes

reviews.comment: Katie is super kind, helpful, and engaging. She truly cares about all of her students and offers ample opportunities to meet outside of class. She offers a good mix of readings, films, short news articles, and other forms of HW. There are flexible deadlines for two short reading reflections, and then two longer papers later in the semester.

Katie puts so much thought into every aspect of teaching, from the content to course policies to having an engaging mix of lecture and discussion. Attendance is important- there are quizzes every few classes (1 question, easy if you skimmed the reading), but 10% are dropped so you can miss a few classes. 2 500-word response papers and 2 long papers

She cares about getting to know students and makes sure that she is accessible and approachable outside of class. Her lectures are engaging and interesting and the readings are well selected and of a reasonable length.  Overall a fantastic professor and a wonderful class that I would recommend to anyone in Sociology.

she is so caring and really cares about getting to know you as a student/person. she wants you to succeed and makes talking in class a very comfortable space even for all the heavy topics. her lectures are straight forward, interesting, and fun. there are only 4 essays over the course of the semester and pop quizzes, low stake and 10 are dropped.

The content Prof. Billings teaches is super relevant and engaging. The class is a mix of slides/lecturing & small group discussions. She is funny, interesting, entertaining, kind, & really inspires us to think deeply about social topics & to reevaluate things that we think we already know about. This class challenges social norms and our mindsets.
Awesome professor and great person would love to take her class again!
Professor Billings is awesome! She does a great mix of lecture and discussion which always keeps class fun and interesting. I'd recommend taking anything she teaches. You'll learn a lot!

Swati is misrepresented online. At SUNY New Paltz the majority of Sociology students that take her classes truly respect and enjoy her lecturing. There have been a few that have given terrible reviews - these are people I recognize and recall being discriminatory towards her due to her demographic. I have and will continue to recommend her classes.

I had Prof. Swati for Sociological Theory for Fall 2023 at SUNY New Paltz. She is an easy grader when it comes to her weekly reading summaries, however, the amount of work she requires for your midterm & final "papers" are ridiculous. Also, don't email her if you have a question bc she doesn't answer. I never want to take another Theory class.

For New Paltz students. I would avoid taking a class with her at all costs. She's an unfair grader towards assignments that made no sense. She has no sympathy if you miss a class and will penalize your grade even if you're able to submit the homework on time and be up to date with what you missed when you return to class. Save yourself the trouble.
Worst teacher, avoid at all costs. Calls you out in class extremely disorganized and has no idea what she is doing.

she taught me nothing except that my biggest regret is coming within a ten foot radius of her. her assignments are ridiculous and unhelpful and you will not get credit if you submit one second after midnight. the "discussion facilitation" is just an excuse not to teach by making students get up and do it. stay as far away from this class as you can

WORST professor I've ever had. She currently teaches at SUNY New Paltz and has stated she's never taught a sociology class previously. Based off class assignments that has proven to be true. She is extremely unclear in what she wants form students and then gives you a terrible grade when you don't understand what she wanted. She should be fired.

Worst teacher here on campus. Lectures are EXTREMELY unorganized (when she actually does a lecture --> students present every Monday.) She speaks way to quickly and not clear enough, so it is impossible to take notes. None of her slides make sense either, and then we have in class writing assignments every Friday when students are still confused.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Skip class? You won't pass.

reviews.comment: She is a nice person and you can tell she wants her students to learn. The issue is that her lectures are unorganized. She speaks quickly to the point where it is difficult to take notes, and she speeds through the slides. Each week is a new topic and we meet twice a week, but one of those days are spent with students presenting, not her teaching.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--GROUP PROJECTS--LECTURE HEAVY

reviews.comment: Ridiculously vague and unclear in lectures about work we have to do. She is too often all over the place when it comes to grading and assigning work. She needs to get things straight instead of constantly messing up and confusing students. No tests, just in class quiz questions weekly on ridiculously long and redundant readings.

DO NOT TAKE A CLASS WITH SWATI BIRLA. She is unclear in her expectations on class assignments & explanations of class material. We basically watch movies every class and are expected to read way too many pages of material she doesn't explain then write essays on them. She has not once lectured a class, relies on student discussion and movies. DUMB.

i cannot praise professor black enough. he is SO knowledgeable, intelligent, and passionate. seriously, deserves all the hype--he clearly knows what he is talking about, and is so open to your ideas and feedback about various topics which makes the class so much more engaging.

had him for junior year writing history of the book. the material might not be the most engaging, but he is so fun to talk to and will invite any sort of conversation. its obvious that he cares about his students, going as far as remembering certain authors and texts students like and bringing rare/old copies into class for them to see. so sweet
Absolute goat
Fantastic professor, interesting lessons great teacher

Prof. Black is a solid lecturer. However, the most notable aspect of his class was his clear kindness and caring. I debating dropping his class due to health issues that resulted in poor discussion grade and instead he helped me boost my grade and stay in the class. He clearly cares for his students and will do anything in his power to help them.
Great Professor, very passionate about the material.

This lecture is one of the most engaging ones I've had. Professor Black is passionate about the subject matter and provides thoughtful, informed readings of Shakespeare's various plays. His class is extremely entertaining and the subject matter covered in lectures is thought-provoking and crucial to success on the final.

Joe Black, great guy and loves Shakespeare. He definitely knows what hes talking about, its hard to pay attention in his lectures cause they are long and boring especially if youre not into Shakespeare like me. the 3 essays required and the discussion section will make or break your grade. read the plays, talk in discussion youll do fine

His classes definitely require that you do the readings. He explains things in great detail and always clears up anything confusing. He's really interested in what he's teaching and it makes the class much more interesting/bearable

Great variety in plays, great professor. There are 8 plays and you have to write 3 papers but will let you write as many as you want with the top 3 grade kept. There's a final. Read the play as fast as you can if you want to avoid "spoilers". Only complaint is the papers are due before hearing the last full lecture on the play you wrote on.

One of my favorite English professors... Was extremely understanding, insightful, interested in what he was teaching, enthusiastic...Not the easiest grader, but pushed me to work to my full potential...Witty, engaged the material with pertinent material from journals/magazines/etc....I heard he is teaching a course on the "novel" in '11/'12 - TAKE!
I wish I could have taken Shakespeare with another professor. Black was horrible.

He makes the class pretty easy, but it is also very easy to fall asleep in lecture.  I really wish he would encourage more class participation through powerpoint, PRS, video clips of plays etc.  Very nice guy, but drink some caffeine before you go to class.  There are 3 papers, weekly quizzes, and a lengthy final exam.
EXCELLENT professor!  One of the best in UMass!

makes shakespeare very accessible and makes great links between themes of the plays and real life. quirky sense of humor. pretty easy class because you have the chance to write on every play and only have your 3 best papers accepted
Extremely nice and very knowledgeable.  Obviously loves his subject very much and it shows in his teaching.  Highly recommended professor!
extemely helpful
Excellent Professor, Excellent Lecturer, Excellent Class
Professor Black was always well-prepared and interesting.  I thoroughly enjoyed his lectures and his sense of humor.

I was intently listening in every class because he made you want to read deeper into the writing. He seemed to show so much enthusiasm in the subject he instilled the urge to want to find your own interpretations of classic plays.
Phenomenal teacher.  He honestly knows what he's talking about...it's amazing how much he tells you about shakespeare's plays. Great guy, funny, interesting, smiles, and willing to help.
great professor and lecturer! very passionate about what he teaches. i just wish the class could have been smaller instead of a large lecture.
Nice guy. My TA sucked though.
Very passionate about his subject, but also very boring. I never went to class and am getting a good grade. Basically, just do the reading, and you'll be all set.

His lectures can be a little droning, but he's obviously passionate about what he teaches. Shows great/helpful video clips and has good guest speakers in lecture. Very helpful with questions if you e-mail him. And he responds promptly.

He knows the subject very well and you can tell that he's interested.  It's just that the subject matter is so boring that it makes me want to rip my eyes out and throw them at him.  There's really no point in going to lecture if you do the readings.
Joe Black knows his subject very well and conveyed the information well. The only problem that I have with him is that he seems ill at ease in the classroom.
Professor Black is great for getting help; although he claims he's a tough grader, if you get a bad grade and then meet with him, next time around you'll be pleased with the result.

Professor Black is one of the nicest teachers I've ever had. He is totally interested in the material & even brings in artifacts & texts straight from the era you're studying. He is very genuine and makes everything easy on you. If you need help, he's more than happy to help you out! Great teacher!

Good guy, if you show up and do your work you'll be fine. Professor Bloomfield goes on long monologues about random topics or AI and will sometimes just change up assignments on a whim. The assignments aren't very demanding and just require some effort

Professor Bloomfield taught through personal loss and a sick child and still showed up to class. Many instructors would have taken extended leave; he didn't. Syllabus changes weren't incompetence but circumstance. His feedback was honest and thought-provoking, which is expected in upper-level courses. I'd take his class again without a doubt.

Luke doesn't express feedback well. He chooses the most harsh way to say things and proceeds to leave judgmental feedback on all essays. The class is extremely boring and attendance is required. He ran out of time to complete the assignments in the syllabus so decided to make our last project worth double at the last second. If possible stay away.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Group projects--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: caring and passionate about what he teaches. lectures are extremely boring but go to them for participation credit. make sure to stay on track with the readings bc the quizzes will have you do a deep dive on the chapter you read that week. offers a helpful feedback on assignments and helpful in office hours. pretty average but nothing glaringly bad
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Group projects

reviews.comment: He's a nice fella. Caring. Big group project at the end of class. Lots of readings but it's an interesting book.

might as well be a self-taught beginner R coding class. labs were sometimes helpful, but oftentimes were confusing and unclear in both expectations and instructions. blanchard was friendly and helpful when asked directly about the code, but the class itself was frustrating. take if you are willing to be independent or work with tablemates, no exams

I took BIOLOGY 476 - Evolutionary Genomics and Bioinformatics. I have never used R and this is a class for beginners. Class is just working on the assigned code and he will answer any questions. Definitely more of self-learning style but you can work with your group. He's a fair grader, very nice and cares a lot about his students.

Took his Social Life of DNA seminar, there were only about 4 or 5 assignments the whole semester which were graded easily but the class itself was disorganized and not useful. Most of the time was spent discussing the professor's life or self-learning R Studio. Maybe he is a better professor for other classes but I did not enjoy this seminar.

Dr. Blanchard is great! He really deserves a better rating than what's on here. He's extremely understanding and really wants his students to do well. The classes I've taken with him have been very student-led where we do projects with minimal guidance. That can work for some and not for others, but if you ask for help, he's more than willing to!
reviews.rating_tags: Accessible outside class--Participation matters--Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: This was a 1 credit topics course on the gut microbiome. The entire course was spent coding on R. We didn't even talk about bacteria in the gut until the 9th week. You are graded on are R labs that he doesn't give clear directions to. He gave feedback to fix the labs and even after the corrections, said more was wrong but it was too late to fix it

AdvGen is an easy class as long as you do all the work on time. Some of the R labs can take a while, but as long as you get them done you should be fine. Class is centered around reading primary literature, although the environment isn't always so great for productive discussions. Getting your genome sequenced is a fun extra to this easy A course.
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Skip class? You won't pass.--Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: This class was a joke.  Blanchard flew through slides during lecture, covering a lot of material but never explaining things well.  The exam questions came directly from the online quizzes, so there was no reason not to ace them.  There were a few projects throughout the semester, nothing too difficult.  Hard not to get an A.

This class was one of the best I've taken thus far.  Yes, he goes through notes quickly, but they're all in the book.  This is one of the classes I've learned the most from.  Tests are essay format, but if you read the book and prepare, (which he gives you

This professor flies through powerpoint slides too quickly to take notes, ending class early most days.  The potential 6 essay questions were available 2 weeks before you write 2 for the exams, so reading those topics in the textbook was essential.  Trying to be a good student here can lead to carpal tunnel syndrome.
Goes to fast to take notes, exams are essay with zero feed back, no one goes to class and he doesnt take attendance

I'm on the fence about Blomfield. On one hand, he gives good feedback and is pretty accessible outside of class, but I think he's also a bit of a harsh grader. Capsim takes over the second portion of this class, so beware of that. Make sure you know what you're doing on the simulation or you won't do good on the final. No exams other than the final

This review is for Management 494BI Capism's capstone course. I disagree with the ratings, yes his lectures are boring to listen to for sure. But he's smart, he gives good feedback, he's a fair grader, he embraces students who require help, overall take him for sure.

This prof will bore you to death, but the class is interesting. On the first day you will probably like his British accent, but by the end of the semester you will want to cry. The exams make up a lot of your final grade, but he provides an in-depth study guide. There are 2 group projects that you do not get to pick your partners (graded easily)!
reviews.rating_tags: Group projects--Lecture heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment:
this mans voice will make you want to die. you wont think so at first, but wait for it. going to his OVER AN HOUR LONG LECTURE feels like there is broken glass in my ear drums and my face is melting. 
other than that, super easy class. you will probs get an a if you study for exams. (he is bad with technology and goes over class time)

Lectures can be boring because he's not the best at making things interesting, but his slides are well made and you can learn a lot from reading off them. Quizzes are sometimes difficult, but they prepare you well for the exams which are not hard IMO. Group project was relatively easy too. The class was great!
reviews.rating_tags: Group projects--Lecture heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment:
Blomfield does not spark interest in the course material in any way whatsoever. The material is dry in his defense, however he puts no effort to enunciate or use his voice to aid in his teaching. 

Class often feels like listening to someone talk to themself in the shower.

I don't have anything really negative to say, but not much positive either to be honest. Lectures were boring but he tried to make them interesting with real-world examples, but I don't think there was any way to make this material worthwhile. The class was pretty easy overall, but I didn't learn anything useful.

He was not a bad professor this semester. He tends to read from the slides sometimes which can make it uninteresting, but knows a lot about the industry. The chapter quizzes are a little tricky in their wording, but they are easy to think through. He does exam reviews for all 3 exams that are really helpful because he lists potential questions.

Blomfield is one of the nicest and most accessible professors; he always goes out of his way to help his students. The class is lecture heavy, and the exams and quizzes are primarily based on lectures. He covers lots of materials and the class can sometimes get boring. But he gave his best and it seems it is his first time teaching at Umass.

Much worse professors than him but I would probably still avoid. Lectures are very dry, group projects are tough, quizzes and exams are pretty difficult. He seems knowledgeable and nice but just very inexperienced. He uses a lot of British sayings in lectures and even on exams which make them complicated to understand.

One of the worst professors I've had so far. Relies on his lectures for everything, while also just reading exactly off the slides the entire time. Quizzes are supposed to be based off slides, but are hardly ever in there. He gives no help or exam prep for his couple exams, forcing you to remember all his lectures. Highly don't recommend him.
reviews.rating_tags: Graded by few things--Test heavy--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: Scott is a nice guy, but he was easily the most unorganized professor I've had at UMass. Most grades were in the last 2 weeks of the semester, and they were graded incredibly harshly. Very unclear, gave me a grade that did not represent the rubric, with unclear feedback. We did not know what to do most of the time, and neither did he. Bad class.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Group projects--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Blinder is a nice guy but he was all over the place this semester. His grading criteria is very unclear and gives little grace while grading. His use of lecture time was often times misused to talk about news for the entirety of class and to top it off he made us watch recorded lectures on our own time. Sorry to say this was one of the worst classe
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Group projects--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Professor Blinder is a gem. There was an exam at the beginning of the semester which was easy if you studied. There is one group project but he does ensure there aren't any free riders on the project by having students give feedback on the students' work in the group. He also welcomes participation and is genuinely extremely caring about students.

Blinder is a decent professor who gives you the information very clearly with very little fluff around it. He's basically the type of guy you'd think of when you imagine a college professor. This course is EXTREMELY back-heavy, 65% of your grade is decided within the last 3 weeks of the course! He also posts his powerpoints on moodle!

This class was my favorite one I have taken. While the reading load may be substantial, every book is captivating, and his feedback is active/supportive. The lectures are informative and interesting, making learning enjoyable. Don't hesitate to take this class with Professor Blackstone!!

Assigned many discussions but not to the point where it was unmanageable. The only thing I didnt like was that they were due on fridays and that we had to respond to a classmate on EVERY post which can be difficult if you are the first one responding because you have to go back.
Professor Blackstone is amazing! He would interact with his students frequently and answer all your questions. Amazing class with well-selected materials. I've learned a lot in his class!
Outdated material. Hast been changed in years as all texts and videos over 20 years old. Lots of information not even accurate as times have changed. Very little Inter action with students online.

Took his class online. Lectures were informative and the expectations were clear. Grade was determined by weekly discussions, a midterm, and a final exam. 100% would take the class again if given the option. The content really gets you to think.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Get ready to read--Participation matters

reviews.comment: I absolutely loved SOC 242 with professor Blackstone. The class a lot of reading and will keep you busy! The lectures are interesting though and the topics really make you think and teach you something new! He gives excellent feedback and generally wants everyone to succeed. Its not a class you can slack through but definitely worth taking.!
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--LOTS OF HOMEWORK--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: Prof. Blackstone gives great personalized feedback to your posts, he shares many interesting videos, articles, and books. I learned so much and he will make you question everything. I hope to take another online class with him in the future.

Professor Blackstone was the absolute best professor that I have ever had!!!!! He genuinely cares about his students and actively participates in the class. Readings were fascinating!! Whatever your major is you will learn things in this class that you will never forget. You will also learn a lot about yourself! He is genuinely a very nice person!!

One of the best professors I have at UMass. You can tell that he is genuinely interested in helping students learn the material. There's a decent amount of work, but read the lectures and you'll sail through the class. Would definitely take again.

One of the best professors I've ever had.  Extremely knowledgeable, keeps the class interesting.  Discussions were great, he participated.  Exams were tough, but fair.  If you read the lectures, you'd do fine.  Highly recommend taking a class with Professor Blackstone.
Wonderful professor! Grades very fairly & is extremely understanding and helpful. I learned a lot in this class, it was really interesting. I recommend this prof!  :)

AWESOME PROFESSOR!!! He was the best professor I have ever had.  He is interesting and makes learning fun.  I think I learned more in his class which was an elective than in any other class I have ever taken.
GOOD GUY.  Approachable and easy to talk to.  Interesting subject, interesting lectures.
AWESOME PROFESSOR, KEEP THINGS INTERESTING, ENJOYED GOING TO THIS CLASS ALOT
No Comments
Really cool guy. He made the class interesting with his videos and stories. Awesome personality.

You'll def. relate to this class, being a college student and all ;) He's got some great stories which gets you through classes. He says not to by the Mad-Dashers cause they aren't good, but he lies, he just wants you to go to classes. Get the dashers.

I think the class itself is overrated. However, Lee is a cool guy and tells tons of stories, which gets him off track and he cracks himself up, but it's funny. Didn't get to all the material on the syllabus,exams okay,grade is based on midterm and final
hilarious prof who teaches subject matter closely related to college life and experience...the tests aren't too bad

One of the best professors I've had while at at UMass.  He is informative and animated.  His classes are alwasy enjoyable, and he really knows what he's talking about.  It would be a shame to graduate without taking one of his courses. :)
Awesome guy! Told really funny stories and kept the class interesting.
No Comments
I never missed a class, and that is a big deal for me.
No Comments

I took this class online and thought he was a great teacher. Although I am conservative and he is a liberal, he respected my opinions and was not biased to his own like some teachers would be. I highly reccomend this class.

Lee is the absolute BEST teacher I have ever come across during my time here at UMass. His classes are so interesting (esp. 242), but his jokes and stories are what make him the friendliest, most real, most interesting and best professor around. THE BEST!
Lots of information, but this class is the most fun you can have for thousands of dollars.  Blackstone rocks!

HE MAKES ME LAUGH EVERY SINGLE CLASS, THE MATERIAL IS GREAT AND HIS PERSONAL STORIES ROCK!
im a senior and he is the best teacher ive had since ive been here...and that laugh is hysterical :)
Most interesting class I've ever taken.
No Comments
The best class ever!  Interesting and fun!
interesting class
an ode to napolean brandy, dunkin donuts and a cornfield
Great stories to go with interesting material!
Best class ever
THIS IS THE COOLEST PROFESSOR I HAVE EVER HAD
wicked hot- spiked hair and leather pants...
so cute, leather pants and all
This class is no easy feat, but Unstuck AI can help make it more manageable. The homework is tough, but the professor rounds up grades. Attend TA sessions to boost your performance.

Definitely a challenging class, the homeworks are really heavy against your grade but he rounds up by 10%. Go to the TA help sessions they boost your grade. A lot of work for a gen ed wouldn't recommend if you're not interested in weather.

The class is very interesting, and i enjoyed it. Homework is so much more stressful than it should be and graded quite harshly, but for a physical science gened i much prefer it over regular physics or chem. The lectures are very important for both the homework and exams, and going to the ta help sessions are very helpful.

Very difficult grader, and with all the homeworks, quizzes, and graded readings it can be a lot, however he rounds the homework grades up by 10% at the end which is helpful and the worst exam grade is worth less than the other 2. Very hard class, but probably more manageable than any other physical science gen ed

Don't take this class unless your interested in Astronomy!! Very difficult impossible to get good grades unless you care about the topic. For the homework they dock points for every little thing so read carefully and answer all parts of the question.

I took this class as a physical science gen ed and trust me it was no worth taking. Spent more time working on homework and studying in this class then I do on classes for my major. Impossible to get 100s on quizzes and home works. As well as a $60 textbook...

His test questions were extremely specific, often statistic-based questions that make it almost impossible to do well on the tests unless you have a photographic memory. Tests were a large percentage of your final grade.

Funny dude but the class was so hard. I took this as a gen ed, might pass. Weekly quiz online, weekly reading with mandatory comments online, and weekly homework. He puts the slides online and lectures which is great but that alone won't be helpful. No extra credit really. For exams, there's 3, he allows a piece of paper but that doesn't even help.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Lots of homework--Test heavy

reviews.comment: Find a different class to fulfill your gen-ed. And if you need it for your major, consider switching majors. That's all.
Don't take this class

Every great review you see for Astro 105 ignore, do not by any means take this class. Guy is a hilarious dude don't get me wrong, his lectures are quite funny, but the class itself is awful. Far too much work for a gen-ed, very confusing work he gives very little support for, and possibly the worst TAs I've ever experienced. Avoid.

Teaches as if its not a gen ed, and expects that you have background knowledge on astronomy. Too much work for a gen ed, and be prepared to teach yourself math you have never seen. TA's grade harshly. Avoid this class.

I swear on my life this is by far the worst class I've ever taken. The TAs are useless, I went to many sessions and my grades were still tanked. The professor although quite funny, he just expects you to know A LOT about math for an entry level course. The tests feel almost impossible, and the homework is such a joke, they grade it so horribly.

This is by far the hardest class I have taken at umass. He requires you to just know all the math needed without teaching it.  None of the homeworks make any sense and tests and impossible to study for. Do not take this class.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Lots of homework--Test heavy

reviews.comment: Homework was outrageously hard and counted for a large percentage of the grade. $100 textbook for a gen-ed. Very math-heavy. The lectures were boring. Tests were impossible to study for and contained mostly random questions. Material that I honestly don't need to know for life.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Test heavy

reviews.comment: If I could give Guy a zero I would. Lectures were mediocre at best and cringy at worst. Homeworks are worth 45% of the grade and are long, difficult and graded harshly. Two exams make up 50% of the overall grade and are trivial MC questions that are difficult to study for. The exams do not relate to the class material at all and prof isnt helpful.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Lots of homework--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Guy is the goat. Pedagogy is super respectable and fair. Course material and lectures are engaging with genuinely useful real-world applications. If you do the work, take lecture notes, and think critically, then you'll do fine. Just make sure you're interested in the subject and good at MCQs: two 25-question MCQ exams are 50% of your grade . . .

Guy is a great professor. Lectures are interesting, full of demonstrations that keep you engaged along with his sense of humor. However, the exams are 20 multiple choice questions, so if you mess up a few questions, you grade suffers greatly. Would not recommend for a gen ed as it can be a struggle.

Guy is so funny and the lectures were very interesting. HOWEVER probably the hardest class I've ever taken. The homework is once a week and 45% of your grade but the TA's grade it extremely unfair and makes it almost impossible to get a 100. The exams are 50% of your grade and they are so difficult and you never know what's it gonna be on.
DO NOT TAKE. Signed up for Physics 100 as a gen-ed and had the most miserable semester of school because of this class.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: do not take this class if you're looking for an easy PS gen ed. It doesn't matter if there is no lab attached to this class, do nottttt take it. exams are worth over 50% of your final grade. so it doesn't matter how well u do on the thousands of hw assignments, u do badly on the exams, u FAIL. And the cherry on top is the exams are short and HARD.

He is a funny lecturer, and he rounds up HW, which is 40% of your grade, by 10%, which is very lovely. Tests are complex and worded weirdly but definitely do able. I also missed a bunch of lectures, but it is an excellent class and should be impossible to fail if you do the work as a gen ed.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--EXTRA CREDIT--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: I actually took physics 281 with Guy and it went great. He was funny and honest. The more you are wiling to participate the better the class will be. Grading is extremely fair. Would definitely take another one of his courses.

Astron 105: good + clear prof, lectures are engaging and he's really funny, 3 exams w 25 mc, lowest grade counts for 1/2, weekly reading and hw, not too bad tho. Pretty tough exams imo, biggest tip I can give is to pay attention to what he says rather than take notes. He posts all his slides. You'll prob understand the material more by listening

I took AST105: Weather and Our Atmosphere with Guy. For material that is difficult by nature, he does a pretty darn good job teaching it. He is caring, passionate, and clearly excited to educate his students. His lectures are quite funny, and for someone who is not super interested in astronomy, I almost always enjoyed his lectures.

Professor Blaylock is an amazing and funny human being, but with that being said, his class was the opposite of amazing. Professor's sense of humour was the only thing making the lectures bearable at all. The homework assignments while weekly, were insanely difficult and didn't have to do with material covered in class at all.

This has to be the most mundane class the physics department at UMass has to offer. By far does not meet the standards necessary for it to be a 500 level class. Instead of furthering your understanding of quantum mech, this class has you read a paper a week and have pseudo-philosophical discussion at the end. Sometimes it does physics.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Group projects

reviews.comment: He is very passionate about what he teaches, but his class is extremely hard. The homeworks are long and graded on accuracy, and the exams are by far the hardest ones I have ever taken. The TA's hold office hours that I highly recommend going too.

Guy gives great lectures, and you can tell he really cares about this subject. Pretty group project heavy, but he gives you the chance to tell him who isn't doing their work. Homework is also pretty difficult and lengthy, but the TAs are great and offer help sessions weekly. One of the harder classes for a PS req, but I enjoyed it!

Amazing teacher, lots of passion for what he teaches. Weekly homework assignments and frequent group projects, but no tests. Grade heavily inflated through 10% homework boost and lots of points relying on group-mate participation rubrics. Often people slack on group projects so you have a way to punish them for it by giving them a bad grade.

Professor Blaylock is an amazing individual who really got me to get super interested in Physics. It is clear that he does not teach this course for the sake of it but because he actually cares about this field. He definitely changed my views on how to be sustainable and he was an excellent professor with some good humor.

Blaylock is a super inspiring and smart individual. Im not a scientist but he made me want to be one in this course. The course itself is super difficult but Guy does a great job at making sure you understand the concepts. Definitely attend TA office hours cause they will give feedback on your papers

Prof. Blaylock is a great teacher, and his Energy and Society is amazing. The homework sessions were very helpful in explaining the math questions. Readings were on Moodle, so no need for textbook purchase. Don't be intimidated by the title of the course, it's actually mind boardening, and the math was easy. International student friendly!

Guy is my favorite professor I've ever had. He has a good sense of humor andclearly loves his field and it shows. That being said his class does require some effort, participation isn't required but it really helps your own understanding. In his class there truly are no stupid questions and he relishes the chance to go more in depth to help clarify

Has fair methods of working in class. Go to class, doing the problems with your team and TA will genuinely help you. He doesn't teach though. Also, if you do well, and if your team does well, you get 10 extra points. Never turn in an assignment if you weren't at lab, he will find out from TA's. Academic Dishonesty will screw you over a bit. 8/10!
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Skip class? You won't pass.--Group projects

reviews.comment: Prof. Blaylock is by far the best teacher I have every had in my life. His lectures were truly inspiring and I actually enjoyed going to class for the first time in my life. I am not at all science inclined, but this class felt completely different to me. There is a lot of homework but it was definitely manageable and he offers homework sessions.
reviews.rating_tags: LOTS OF HOMEWORK--ACCESSIBLE OUTSIDE CLASS--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: Really boring lecturer, is unable to convey material clearly & assigns a ton of HW. There are mandatory weekly essays (1000 words) recapping what was discussed in lecture + midterm + final paper (2500 words each). I had to teach myself the material bc lectures and readings did not correspond/make sense to me . This class shouldn't be a Gen Ed.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--LOTS OF HOMEWORK--ACCESSIBLE OUTSIDE CLASS

reviews.comment: DO NOT TAKE THIS CLASS unless its required. Im currently taking this as a GenEd and I could not have picked a worse class. Blaylock really does care about his lectures, but not your grades. the homework has no relation to is lectures or the book, and you have to google everything (which I a lot harder than it seems in this class) 0/10 recommend
reviews.rating_tags: Tough Grader--LOTS OF HOMEWORK--Tests are tough

reviews.comment: Blaylock's got a good way of teaching the course and explaining such difficult concepts (his lectures and demonstrations are great). He's helpful outside of class (pro tip: go to the homework sections) and it's clear that he wants you to pass. I'm not a science person, and while this course was a lot of work, I really enjoyed it.

I am not a science-inclined person so admittedly a lot of what Prof. Blaylock was talking about went right over my head, but he was simply a nice, funny, enthusiastic guy which made his class a surprising delight. There was a fair amount of writing in this class, which didn't bother me much, but might be alarming for some.

Failed this class the first time around and had to retake it a year later. My favorite course both times. Blaylock has the driest sense of humor and never laughs at his own  jokes. Worked with leaders in his field yet doesn't take himself too seriously. Just go to the homework helps and office hours, submit hrw on time and you'll get an A

WORST CLASS EVER. Took this to fulfill a PS gen ed and it is the biggest regret of my life. Nothing in the "textbook" has anything to do with the homework. This class relies on you Googling everything. He even asks you to Google things instead of teaching it himself. Your homework is graded by TAs that are never in class. It is literally hell.

Energy and Society is a gen ed class for nonscience majors. The material itself is not difficult (basic high school level physics with simple algebra). Despite the easiness of the material, the class is unnecessarily difficult. Unorganized lecture slides, unclear grading material for very long weekly hw and unfair test questions. Dont take with him

Physics 118 Energy & Society is extremely difficult for non-science majors. There is a somewhat lengthy homework assignment due every Thursday and it consistently has nothing to do with what it taught in class, or what is in the textbook - you'll end up Googling EVERYTHING. Blaylock is unaccessible and unhelpful. I regret taking this class.

Undergrad TAs grade your papers without any rubric or grading criteria (do you trust?). Half the TAs look more at your grammar while the other half look at the actual physics. You have to write the term papers with no drafts, just an outline due in one week then a 2000-3000 paper due the next. If you honestly love physics, then go for it.

Great guy, lectures are very average.  Tests in this class are half about reading the question correctly and making a good cheat sheet.  This makes the class a little frustrating when you know the material but the test is full of trick questions.

Guy is really good at getting physics under your skin and making you think beyond the academic study - test - move on mentality. He gives demonstrations that are inspirational and fun, and makes you think about the concepts.   That being said, the tests were without a doubt the hardest tests I've ever done in my life.

Blaylock is one of the best teachers at UMass. However, this class has some pretty tough tests and if you don't stay on top of learning the material, you will not have a good time. He really shines when students ask questions. His demos are also super cool. Physics is hard but Blaylock is fantastic. Also, MasteringPhysics for HW sucks.

Prof. Blaylock is an entertaining and inspiring guy. He has great demonstrations and makes you interested in physics. The tests are challenging, but that is not his fault, you need to have an understanding of physics rather than know how to do certain types of problems. You get a cheat sheet on the exams which is useful for formulas, but that's it.

AMAZING guy. He inspired interest in physics for me which was amazing. His lectures are awesome but you need to read the book. Tests are tough but doable, excellent professor he just has a hard class to teach! Also they allow sheet sheets but study and don't simply  rely on them. Physics requires lots of in depth understanding not memorizing.

He is a funny dude.. but his teaching is more conceptual rather than teaching HOW to do the problems. the tests are pretty tough but if you do enough practice problems and make sure to study you will be fine. (I tested out of this class but decided to take it because it directly applied to my major)

Blaylock is a def a genius, but cannot explain enough for most non-physics majors looking 2 take Physics 121 to fulfill their PS requirement. I was not overly confused at lectures, I was; however, puzzled by the poor  online homework and lecture highlight grading on the part of the TA's. BTW, not paying for 3 textbooks as a non-physics major...

Guy seems like a chill dude and everything but he is an awful teacher. My high school physics teacher explained things better than he did, and even after putting countless hours into studying, his tests were impossible. I am an engineering major so I'd like to say I know my stuff. His class was the only below A class I had.

Guy is a smart funny guy. He shows you a lot of fun experiments and knows his stuff. His exams are extremely hard, harder than practice problems in the textbook.  If you never took physics before, don't take this class if he's teaching it.
