Guy explains physics concepts really well, but he doesn't really show you how to solve actual problems. The tests are really hard! You will not pass by doing just homework alone. Be ready to read the book and do end of chapter questions for no credit in order to study, because this class is going to be a major pain!

As a ps gen-ed, I took this class only having some knowledge in physics. I assumed since it was a 100 level it would be more basic than 131 or 151-not so. The professor picks and chooses slides from 151 and 131 and present them without much explanation, expects you to know what he's talking about without introducing background on topic.

Professor Blaylock is hilarious and is very clear when he teaches.  He gives demonstrations on the subjects that we are learning, and uses himself as the test dummy, often slamming himself into walls and such.  Attendance is not mandatory, but it is recommended to understand the difficult curriculum.  Tests are very hard, do not cram hours before!
Classes are very interesting but the homework is very inconsistent to the classes. he often does not teach what is on the homework.

This guy is awesome an awesome lecturer. He won't explain step-by-step each problem though because you're really expected to do the reading. If you haven't taken AP, definitely take notes on the textbook. I didn't take AP, but I'm doing way better than I expected just by keeping up with the readings and doing the assign. and pract. exams.
That class was so hard!  He made it interesting and had extra help available.  If you work hard, it's not impossible to do well.

Difficult. I took AP Physics in hs and enjoy the subject. I only managed to receive a C+ .. and that's only because the class has a big curve. Blaylock, although he is VERY entertaining, he doesnt use class time well; he spends lots of time on clicker questionsand asking the class "what we think". The labs may save you. Still, Blaylock is magical..

He's a good professor in general, he can really inspire interest in the subject, but if you want to do well be prepared to do a lot of learning outside of class because the lectures are pretty vague sometimes. I didn't take physics in high-school so this class was a challenge, but if you do all the homework's and go to class always you'll be fine.

He is a very interesting guy but his slides are very late compared to when the homework is due and when he asks to read the chapter. But once he gets to the powerpoint he makes sure people understand the problems that will be on the test. Overall great guy and best Physics 151 teacher. Better than Boris.

Blaylock is awesome. He interacts with the class and performs experiments to help students understand the material. He's very funny and helpful. It is a lecture so the class is big, but he does a good job handling it.

I had high expectations for this class. I had a great first impression because he was funny and knew how to keep me attentive. He is very likable. As the semester is going along, I have grown to dread the class. He digresses far too much instead of using up all valuable time for learning. The tests are much different from what he focuses on most.
Really funny guy, great teaching style. Makes everything clear in his explanations. Best Professor ever!
Guy is the man, I just slacked off in his class and once you're behind in physics you're bankrupt! xP

Blaylock is a smart guy and definitely knows his stuff. He leads class discussions well and lets students participate often. He will help if you have a question and does cool demos so class is definitely worth your time.

He treats class like a performance. As long as PRS questions are answered, they count for full credit (5% of grade). His grading scale is favorable. He scaled down my lab grades though.  If you've taken physics in high school, this class should be a breeze for you.

I had almost no physics background going into this class. As a result I thought it was extremely difficult. He goes off on a lot of irrelevant tangents that will confuse you even more if you don't know the material. If you a PS gen-ed, take 131 instead.
He treats class like a performance. He will occasionally do fun demonstrations. You must go to lecture because of PRS. This class is very easy.

He is very smart, friendly, and overall a great prof.  He makes mechanics interesting with fun demo. Mastering physics is hard but going to his office hours help a lot. Make sure to read the book if you don't know mechanics otherwise you will get lost.

Funny guy, good demos.  But I just didn't really get a lot from the lectures.  A lot of people seemed to like him more than I did.  And get ready to buy a new laptop when you throw yours out of the window out of frustration from Mastering Physics.  But at least you get a cheat sheet for each exam.

Coolest teacher I've ever had. Does all kinds of crazy experiments during class. He is very good with his subject matter and is never without an answer to student questions. Makes a hard subject interesting.
Very good professor. Was always prepared and very funny. An interesting class to go to.
Great teacher
enthusiastic professor, teaches very well.  has a good sense of humor and an interesting personality.  i love this guy!

Great teacher, tries his best to teach a tough subject. Has homework online that is worth 20% so read the book and do all the homeworks and you should do well on the midterms and final. Blaylock will warn you at the beginning of the semester if you slack off on the readings and you'll fall behind, and hes very right.
the man. hes real sarcastic, if you enjoy that kind of humor you'll love the class cuz he spends most of the time ripping on people who give stupid answers

OMG such a good teacher. I actually PAID ATTENTION and actually WAS INTERESTED. Complete opposite of Professor Corrada. I FAILED this last semester with Corrada as my teacher, and now I'm getting A's on exams that are challenging, but fair. I can't say how much this guy rocks. TAKE HIS CLASS IF YOU CAN!
Guy Blaylock is alright.  For 151 he is pretty fair. Just do all the homeworks and readings on time and you should be fine.

Really enthusiastic and valuable professor, and he definitely knows what hes talking about. Agreed, the tests were a little challenging, but not impossible, and grading was always very fair. I approve, and would recommend him as a professor to anyone.

A skilled professor who really knows the subject he teachers, Blaylock is one of the most fun professors i've ever had. His demos. are really great! The important thing about the class is its fairness for homework and tests. They were not hard, but challenging.
guys mad funny lol

The scale on the class is VERY fair.  Midterms not too hard, final was tough though.  I ***ked myself, after the first test I stopped going to class.  Just go to class and do the homework, it's the easiest 25% of your grade you can earn.
Great class, very interesting
Class was very interesting and wasnt bad to attend, but his lectures dont really help at all vs. homework.
Awesome demonstrations.  Probably my favorite teacher so far.

Everyone I know likes him, and he is clear, helpful and entertaining.  But I can't help feeling like the class was more of a show than a session for learning.  He isn't serious a lot, and you may like this, but if you're into something other than analogies to monkes falling from trees, you might want to try elsewhere.  He's just really out there.

He is brilliant! His lectures are clear, engaging, entertaining, and thought provoking!  The work load is relatively easy, and completely worth it. Notes are easy, since every lecture's powerpoint presentation is also online! Do yourself a favor and take at least one class with him! Just brilliant!!
Very nice guy and very willing to help accomodate students with problems or difficulties.
He's the man. His demonstrations are funny as hell.

This guy is probably one of the nicest, funniest professors you'll have. However, his teaching style doesn't really get to everyone. If you are extremely smart and already understand Physics, you will know what he is talking about. Otherwise, good luck on the exams. You'll probably fail all of them.
Doesnt do a good job of teaching, mostly just presents PRS questions to try and fool you.  Exams are insanly hard and questions seem to come out of the blue.  He has great demos though

He was a nice guy and tried to keep the lectures fun, but he always ends up explaining to the geeks in class.....its more like a disscussion section than a class. If he explained things as new material, rather than revision like , then he would be a great teacher.
No Comments

Nice guy but doesn't do a well enough job teaching the material in class. There's so much stuff left unexplained, and the test are extremely hard. I just wish he knew how to explain things without rushing through the material.
Blaylock is the man!

Super boring lectures no one would go to class and just take the tophat in their dorm. Exams have companies from lectures and the questions are worded very strange. He is so unbelievably boring to listen to and waking up to hear him yap for over an hour at 8 am is brutal. The group projects aren't hard if you have a good group, just time consuming

Super long lectures with huge slides. Attendance is required, but you can do an assignment online to get the participation points. Have to do 2 group projects that are 6ish page reports. The exams aren't too bad, but the wording can be a bit strange. Have to make sure you know the examples he provides in class, as they'll appear on the exam.

Lectures can get a bit boring but you can skip them if you wanted and do a small assignment on tophat instead. Exam 1 was hard, but everything else wasn't bad at all. The group projects will be easy if you have a solid group.
He's British

Lectures were boring but he would take attendance. Exam 1 was harder than 2 and 3, make sure to study everything and also the companies that he talks about during lecture. Although the material was easy, the exams were worded to be confusing. There are 2 reports and you must work in groups.

Overall good class, but 1st exam is toughest and there are 2 group projects (I worked with mine on zoom). Downside is that the class is lecture heavy with 40+ slides per lecture for a 50 minute class. Not too bad, it seems better than the other prof from my experience in this class.

Pretty easy class but 3 tests make up for around 50%+ of your grade. Tests are simple as long as you study the study guide and watch the videos for recap. Professor gives you time to make up attendance every week incase you do miss class. No extra credit so every point matters for this class.

Yes the lectures can be boring, but it's an easy class and I learned a lot and found the material to be interesting. 3 exams and 2 group projects, both are easy. He cares about the class and students and is willing to help. Slides are posted before class, look through them and take notes so you can pay attention in class - the slides are lengthy.

Professor Bloomfield is super nice caring guy. Although his lectures are a bit dry and long, he makes up for it by giving ample amounts of times for due dates, grades easy, and is very accommodating. Theres six quizzes total all online and lowest one gets dropped. Two group reports easy w good group. lastly there r 3 in person exams scales heavy
He is a really nice and understanding guy. The class is easy and its not that much work. However, his lectures are extremely boring. He just reads off the slides and they are very long and boring.

Only 1 homework assignment, 2 group projects that aren't that difficult, 3 exams that are not cumulative but are taken in class but they are not too difficult as long as you put a little effort into studying, 6 quizzes. Take him over the other management professors.
reviews.rating_tags: Clear grading criteria--Lecture heavy--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: professor is nice but lecture are terrible. They are not super engaging and slides are super long. exams are in person and on paper so kinda hard
The grading was based on completion, and i never missed any points for assignments. Good teacher and good prompts, i definitely improved my writing over the course of the class
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Clear grading criteria--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Danielle Blackman is an awesome teacher. She is very understanding and knows how to teach English well. English is not my first language and I still got a 4.0 in her class. Attend class daily, put time into your papers , and you will get your 4.0!
Great teacher. Helpful and a joy in the classroom

Dani is hands down one of the best english teachers i have ever had!  She brings a whole new view to writing that i have never gotten before and really helps you to develop your own unique writing style.  Even if you dont like to write, you will like this class!
Amazing professor.  She really knows how to catch your attention at 9 am.  I actually look forward to class!
shes excited about teaching and i think im actually going to like and english class for once..
No Comments
No Comments
danielle is one in a million,,,after 13 yrs of school im finally looking foward to class,,shes wonderful...this woman should never leave Umass
No Comments

Danielle is an awesome professor.  She actually got me interested in writing where as before I basically hated it.  The way she teachers her writing class is unique in that students can truly express themselves through their writing.  Highly recomdended.
Words can't describe this class.  We have an awesome time together, and I wish we could keep taking this class into the future.  Awesome, Awesome time.

John is kind and funny, and he doesn't make things overly difficult or complicated. 4 exams, and you get two chances to do a makeup exam if you aren't happy with your grade. He does surprise reaction papers during class but there are 9 total and I think only 4 or 5 are necessary, so if you miss class one day you should be okay.
best professor ever. he's super engaging with the class and funny. the tests are open note and exactly like the notes and textbook readings.
His last name is Bickford so i think there was a typo but he is overall a great professor. I have taken two of his classes and his grading criteria is clear and feedback is always given.
reviews.rating_tags: EXTRA CREDIT--Clear grading criteria--Gives good feedback

reviews.comment: Bickford was great! Sometimes his class was a little dull but I could always follow what he was saying. If you have a chance to take one of his classes, take it. His tests are open note and the grades aren't just based on tests which is always good for getting a better grade.
Boring professor. Open note tests, you can even bring in printed slides. Read the book. A really easy A, but an annoyingly awful professor.
Bickford's class is fun, interesting, and has open note tests!
Great man, loves his subject. Took his personality psych,TAed for him, and going to take his senior seminar. Great teacher!

Bickford is engaging, funny, and makes class enjoyable. You do something interactive every class, including PRS and Reaction Worksheets you need to pass in, which count towards your grade. It's a fun psych class, & he allows cheat sheets on all exams.

So monotone, lectures put me to sleep. But all exams are open notes. He was nice, caring, and understanding but I didn't retain any information from class. The homework on Pearson is hard to keep up with the deadlines because it's not really mentioned in the syllabus. I like to make an academic calendar before each semester but couldn't with those.

He's a great guy that cares about his students. Very flexible and if you reach out to him he is always ready to help. Attendance is not mandatory but he gives pop quizzes like once a week. However, he moves very quickly and is not the best at teaching. Does not slow down for students, kind of goes at his own pace.
reviews.rating_tags: Beware of pop quizzes--Caring--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Semih is a great guy. Took the class in the spring of 2024; not sure what has changed but he was always easy to reach outside of class and genuinely cared about the students who made a connection with him. He does have pop quizzes and the tests are annoying but overall if you prep for them and ask questions you should be fine.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Beware of pop quizzes--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Great person who is very understanding and cares about his students. Understands that the material is difficult and tries to make it as understandable as possible. Very flexible on homework assignments and tests understands you may need extra help.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Beware of pop quizzes--Caring

reviews.comment: It is apparent that he has an extremely solid foundational understanding of the material being taught. Sometimes he speaks quite fast. However, he acknowledges this. Everything is uploaded to Echo. Boone is funny and cares about his students' success.  This is one of the harder sections of ECON 103, but if you are passionate, I'd recommend Boone.

If you want to learn a lot, you should take Boone. However, he's harder than other Econ 103 profs. Lots of homework, "study plans," which are due every week, along with mostly weekly problem sets. Boone talks very fast and also goes on tangents. You learn more from discussions. The 1st & 2nd exams were easy, the final was hard and cumulative

I'm not an econ major but still had a great time in this class. Prof Boone is clearly passionate about the subject; it shows in his lectures. Classes were entertaining and the content was fun. There were lots of opportunities to do well/make up for lost points on exams.

Chris talks at a very fast pace, making it hard to follow his ideas, especially if you have no background in Econ. It's hard to reach him during office hours as he is usually booked out months in advance. If you don't get a good SI leader, you'll have to teach yourself the topic. Difficult class, but you can get through it if you are driven.

Professor Boone is not a bad professor but the class is really hard. Exams make up more than half your grade and they are really hard, but there is extra credit offered after the first exam. The weekly problem sets are pretty annoying, but they aren't too bad. Great professor though.

Great guy and professor but pretty difficult class. Exams are most of the grade, and tend to be harder than practice exams. Attendance for lectures is not mandatory, but you have to go to a TA section weekly.

While professor Boone was not a bad professor, the class is pretty hard. 2 midterms, and a final make up more than half your grade, and he assigns a good amount of Homework. Practice exams are not identical to real exams, and exams are not easy at all. There is extra credit offered after the first exam though. Good guy, but show effort to succeed.
Packed a lot of information into his lectures, was very clear with the material. Your grade does depend a bit on your TA.

This class is not as easy as the other ratings say. He did now allow us cheat sheets despite allowing his previous classes to. The exams are cumulative, so midterm 2 involved topics on midterm 1 and the final involves all topics thru the semester. I did not like this class. Luckily I've been fine on the exams but they're HARD. Find an easier prof
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Lots of homework

reviews.comment: Boone taught the class very well and the discussion sections were even better. If you have Ananya she is the best... He does give out a ton of homework but it is all helpful for learning the material for the exams. There are 3 exams that are not that difficult, usually identical to the practice tests... Take Boone, you will learn a lot.

Class is easy and lectures are good but he talks really fast and doesn't allow laptops. Discussions are the most helpful and what will help you really learn. A good bit of homework but it's not hard a lot is for completion and easy grading. Tests aren't bad but definitely need to study don't go in blind. Do the homework and you will be fine.

Super nice guy, talks soooo fast. That man is not on speed, he is speed. But the lectures are posted. Lots of hw but it's not hard, good to raise your grade. Put in the effort and you'll do fine. Prof Boone rlly loves what he teaches lol.

Boone gives a lot of outside work to do but it's all related to what will be on exams and to help you understand the material or help get you ready for lecture. The weekly problem sets are annoying, but if you do all of them and do all the other homework you will do fine. He curves exams by a lot too.

Very fast lecturer. Almost to smart to be teaching an intro class. Didn't explain difficult topics well. Had to put in so much time and effort outside class time. So much homework and really difficult exams.

Prof. Boone talks VERY fast (which he makes note of) but I found it very hard to keep up with him throughout lectures. He's nice and accommodating. Attend TA office hours & discussion for help on the Problem Sets; they help you with exams. Lectures tended to be boring and more example-based as opposed to note-taking.

High caliber professor– he knows what he's talking about and what he's doing. Very good at giving lectures. He assigns a good amount of work on Canvas but it does help you learn the material. The exams are in person and they're basically the same thing as the problem sets. Boone seems like a very genuine guy, I wish him well.

Professor Boone is great at teaching. He relays the information in a way that's easier to understand. He's very knowledgable on the topic. Work consisted of study plan every week w/ quiz, problem sets, & video. TA Pedro is funny, good teacher, and fair grader.

Hes average. Talks fast, average amount of work. You do have to buy something but I think it was cheap. 3 exams, he gives a cheat sheet on the last two exams. First exam was easy the second is a lil hard. Lectures are recorded but discussions are mandatory. Dicussions don't really help. Hes not the best prof but I do fine in the class. very average

Boone was a very good professor. He is very organized and is very prepared for lectures. Lectures were very helpful to me, but discussions sometimes seemed pointless. Canvas is always updated and offers a ton of things to help you learn. Tests were a little difficult, but not horrible. Would recommend

Took Econ 103 as my first ever Economics/Business Related course. Thought that the lectures were very helpful and gave me a notebook filled with good notes. I am a terrible test taker but the tests weren't terrible, if you study and understand whats going on, than youll be fine. Discussions were the worst part because they were boring
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Test heavy--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Very solid professor, his lectures are actually useful and the grading is very fair. He's also very helpful in office hours and is definitely the best professor available for teaching 103. This guy can teach!

Although the lectures were fast paced and heavy, Professor Boone took the time to develop study guides (that were integrated with the textbook in Canvas) and send out recordings for each chapter quiz, midterms, and final. I also loved that he connected concepts and ideas to the real world, which made me appreciate the class even more.
reviews.rating_tags: Clear grading criteria--Lecture heavy--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: LOVED this professor and class. I learned so much! He speaks super fast but he is so passionate, engaging, and explains the topics so well. Highly recommended! Attendance isn't taken, however, if you don't go to class you will be lost. I missed one class and had to watch the recording; it wasn't as valuable as being there in person.

Great professor. Speaks fast during lectures but they're always recorded. There is a lot of homework but it helps you keep up with the lectures. Allows a cheat sheet for the second midterm and the final. Also gives an extra credit assignment for the end of the semester.

Lectures are boring but all the quizzes are online. 2 midterms and a final. A cheat sheet is allowed on the second midterm and the final. Boone is the best option for Econ103. Great choice to fulfill SB gen ed. All lectures are recorded and posted online

Boone is a really caring guy that obviously knows a lot about microeconomics. He does his best to simplify the somewhat difficult to understand topics he teaches about and it works out really well for him. He gives out tons of homework that is more graded upon completion rather than actual performance so it's a great way to practice for exams.
reviews.rating_tags: Clear grading criteria--Gives good feedback--Lots of homework

reviews.comment: He is a good professor and I would recommend taking his course because he seems to be the best professor for Econ103 compared to the other professors. There is a homework assignment or two a week that can take long. The 2 midterms and final take up a lot of your grade. Just apply yourself if you want a good grade.

Pretty alright overall. I did end up getting majorly bored during lectures and therefore stopped going to them, but the material was easy enough and Boone did an alright job conveying it. Would recommend as a prof for ECON 103 cause yeah hes chill ig.

Caring professor who is really knowledgeable on the subject. Decent amount of homework but you just have to stay on top of it. Exams are a little difficult, just have to study, and he scales up grades a good amount. Even though attendance non-mandatory, I recommend going to lectures.

He is very understanding prof and will scale up exams, does not grade hw based on accuracy, and gives full credit for late submissions. For this course, the most important thing is to pay attention to the lectures. Material is very easy to understand, but focuses more on memorization rather than large concepts.

Professor Boone is amazing. He is a nice and entertaining guy, and his lectures are always clear and straightforward. There is weekly homework, but it doesn't take long and helps a lot with solidifying class concepts. Two midterms and one final, grades were generously scaled on both midterms.

This class was my hardest class so far but that's simply because I have absolutely no background in economics, and took stats instead of calc in high school. Lectures are packed with info and go pretty fast. DO NOT SKIP a lecture if you value your sanity. Discussion classes mandatory, exams scaled, extra credit, lecture heavy, and good teacher.

Great professor, if you're taking ECON103 he is going to lecture VERY fast but it is still possible to keep up with all of the information. Workload was relatively low for the class in terms of the week to week. There are two major exams throughout the year but neither of them are especially difficult.

Professor Boone was a great professor who knew what he discussed during his lectures well. There are two midterms and a final, but they aren't worth a considerable percentage of your grade. On the first exam, he was very forgiving, scaled the test by about ten points, and offered extra credit. He gives the past exams as study tools which is helpful

Professor Boone showed us that he clearly knows the material like it's the back of his hand. I recommend going to lecture and before any midterm+final to do all of the practice exams- they helped me study a lot! the problem sets are graded generously, and he drops and scales a fair amount of the work. i struggle with math, but i figured it out here

Boone is a very passionate teacher. His lectures are hard to follow and uninformative. Make sure to use the videos and additional resources. I struggled in the class, however he is very caring and office hours are a great resource. Would take a class with him again.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Caring--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Amazing lecturer. Explained a lot of tough concepts really clearly. 2 midterms, 1 final, weekly quizzes, biweekly problem sets, 2 video per week. Problem Sets and exams were graded generously. Grading is dependent on TA. Lots of work but it isn't hard, just gotta do it. Extra credit is offered a lot. Releases practice exams before actual exam.
reviews.rating_tags: Amazing lectures --Clear grading criteria--Lots of homework

reviews.comment: Amazing professor! His lectures were really clear and helped explain a lot of the tough concepts. Problem Sets were graded very generously. There is a lot of work associated with the class but it isn't tough. Grading is entirely depended on TA. 2 midterms, 1 final, weekly quizzes, biweekly problem sets, 2 videos to watch per week. Highly recommend!
reviews.rating_tags: Amazing lectures --Clear grading criteria--Lots of homework

reviews.comment: Prof Boone is an awesome professor. You can tell he knows his stuff very well. There is a decent amount of math in this course. We had weekly quizzes, problem sets and videos (few mins). Try to do good on these though, because his tests are hard if you don't study a lot. He preps you for them very well by giving you last semesters test and answers.

Overall, great professor. Lectures aren't mandatory, but great since he distills essential information and content relevant to the exams/quizzes-- usually more valuable than online study guides. He seems open-minded and presents multiple sides to economic theory in ways that help you make your own conclusions. I loved the class and would retake it.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Clear grading criteria--Inspirational

reviews.comment: If you struggle with math, then this class won't be easy. There is a lot of homework and quizzes, and the 3 exams make up 55% of your grade. You can utilize the tutors, but you might have to wait an hour or so each time you want to see one. Sometimes they are all booked up.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Clear grading criteria--Lots of homework

reviews.comment: Prof Boone requires paper notes and lectures can be a little hard to follow. Content made sense if you did the online interactive reading/lesson. The class consisted of weekly readings and quizzes, several problem set assignments throughout the semester, and three exams. Content wasn't difficult if you did the homework.

Going to lectures is super helpful, he explains everything well without reading off of the slides. Found it hard for an intro level class but I am also not an econ major. Would recommend and he scales the exams so you get a better score.
If you have a good TA and are a goof test taker you will Ace this class.

Personally, I loved Professor Boone, he is great! Although attendance is not mandatory, you should still go in person cause his lecture is very helpful. He talks fast but is always there if you have any questions. You should really study for the tests, they are not the easiest.

I found lectures to be very dull and Boone to be not the most organized with notes. As well, the homework was pretty tedious:each week there was a quiz, a video to watch before class, and a problem set due on Friday. Exam could be tough and you had to prepare. Overall, it was fine, but I would try to get someone else if you can.

Great guy and energetic! The material wasn't sticking for me personally. I had to use outside materials and extra hours to understand it. 

Most of the information will be within lectures. Be prepared to do math and some real-world problems. 

Lots of office hours were offered, though I didn't go. If I did I would've spent less time studying.
Beautiful lecture with realistic examples, and fair tests. I shook hands with him after finishing the final and asked him what classes he will be teaching next term(s)!
He gave my class a tough midterm. The class average was a 67 and he said the final would be just as hard. That is the definition of setting students up for failure. Enough said.

I found it really hard to learn with the way he teaches, but he is very knowledgable and seems like he cares about his students learning. Attendance isn't mandatory, but not going definitely affected my understanding of the concepts. Some assignments and exams were hard, but a lot of it was graded very generously.

Boone is a great lecturer, but it can be hard to get a chance to talk to him due to the sheer class size. 
You generally don't need to attend lectures, but he usually explains content better than the study guide's do. 
Your grade is in large part based around your score on exams and a small number of problem sets.

Lectures are fast and he expects you to be competent but I really enjoyed that. It was a challenge but he teaches so well it makes you want to learn. Super easy to reach outside of class and will help break down concepts with you if needed. Would definitely take a class with him again.

Lectures are very fast-paced, so effort must regularly be put in outside class to understand the material. There are weekly quizzes, ungraded study plans, and videos and readings every week. There are problem sets every couple of weeks. Overall, the subject is really difficult but Prof Boone is genuine and cares about his students' learning.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Accessible outside class--Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: Although Mr. Boone has only recently joined the University's Economic Department as faculty he has shown both passion for Economics and willingness to do what it takes to provide the best possible experience to his students. What Boone lacks in experience teaching Econ203, he makes it up in his expertise on the subject.

Professor Boone is an amazing lecturer and is really passionate about what he teaches. He tries to make economic models as applicable as possible and always gives real-world examples of the application of economic concepts. He assigns weekly homework, quizzes, and a few problem sets; and some of them are a bit difficult but manageable.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Lecture heavy--Caring

reviews.comment: He just likes to hear himself talk. The classes themselves are a waste of time except for the fact that he will randomly take attendance throughout the semester. I didn't need to take notes and mainly used the class as extra time to take a nap or daydream. Overall, an easy class, and I probably would take it again.

I honestly didn't enjoy this class very much. Its possible that Anthro just isn't for me, but I found most of the material to be very pedantic and boring, and generally the class felt kind of pointless. Boone is kind and the coursework wasn't too difficult despite this. Weekly journal/response activities, manageable readings, easy final and midterm

The class is easy, but the lectures are pointless. He doesn't allow the use of technology, and keeps falling into politician rants every 30 minutes. Definitely recommend for the free A, but don't expect a class you will enjoy.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Lots of homework--So many papers

reviews.comment: Classes consisted of 2 lectures per week as well as a discussion section once a week. There are 5 random attendance "quizzes" (not real quizzes), that are taken throughout the semester. There is a short paper due every week, about 500 words. Overall, this class was good, and I did learn a lot. I would recommend taking it.
Love this class. His lectures are very interesting and not just talking at students. He doesn't allow technology while in lecture and honestly that has helped me a lot.

The class isn't hard, and assignments are easy, but lectures feel pointless. He won't upload slides or allow technology, stopping class if anyone uses a device. It feels childish, like we're in high school. He also goes on random political rants, which makes the class uncomfortable(I say this as a very liberal guy btw)

Lectures are repetitive and not very topic based. The hard to follow lectures are unnecessarily political and negative towards views opposite from his own, which is awkward to watch. Work was easy and not a bad class for an easy A, wouldn't recommend this class to people who like to or have to use technology for learning.

Boone is incredibly kind and gives really helpful feedback. He understands that we all have lives of our own and are trying to navigate a really difficult world, he is extremely compassionate and an overall wonderful person!

I learned so much from this class, and it was very formative to the way I will interact with the world now. So much reading. He's pretty understanding about things and recognizes that everyone has other stuff going on. I wish I could've only taken this class and no others so I could put more time into it.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Lots of homework--Caring

reviews.comment: He made anthro an interesting topic while having the grading not be so harsh with online exams and homework assignments anybody from all majors are capable of doing. This is how every Gen Ed class should be, but overall I enjoyed it and he's pretty decent
Interesting lectures and interesting course materials. A lot of reading but weekly writing assignments were easy and helpful.

Class was really easy,  minimal hw just a weekly reading and a writing response, one small paper, and "exams" were t/f take homes. No recorded lectures or slides are posted, so I don't recommend skipping too often. That said, lectures were super repetitive and I'm not sure I really learned anything. TAs do the majority of the grading.

This class was not fun or easy, he expects you to read so many pages each week with a pretty long discussion post every week. Lectures are not recorded, no slides posted so if you do not write fast enough in class you will miss stuff. He is so anti- technology and says no phones or laptops so many times throughout class it became obnoxious.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Lots of homework--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: I suffered in this class so much as a non-native speaker. No lecture slides posted, no laptop allowed, no recordings, and I had no clue what was happening in the lectures. He only has one resource for people to study which is a note that he updated with what HE THINKS necessary. TONS OF READING. SHORT 500 WORDS PAPER EVERY WEEK.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: Be prepared to read 30+ pages every week, followed by a 2+ paper assignment. Lecture not mandatory, but no lecture slides or recordings posted. 2 big papers at end, I put more effort in this class than my core classes. He says no to technology multiple times every class, I did learn a lot, but it's a heavily biased class
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Lots of homework--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: While this is meant to be a general ed, the cou
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Lecture heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: This brotha Boone is the GOAT! (Grandest of All Time.....)
Lectures are not very interesting. There are online quizzes and two big papers; one paper and a final project. There are also weekly two page papers.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Lots of homework--So many papers

reviews.comment: Professor is very outgoing and charismatic but the overall class is boring if you dont like anthro. You are graded on weekly questions that are pretty easy and the grading is lenient. 2 "big" papers; one paper and then an interesting final project. Quizzes are online and not hard. Easy class but don't expect it to be super interesting.

Class was easy enough, just very boring material if you aren't interested in anthropology. If you need it for a gen ed you'll be fine just dont expect it to be an amazing class. Attendance to lectures is not mandatory, but discussion is. Readings are boring.
He doesn't allow laptops, phones, ipads, or even the use of Grammarly for writing assignments. Attendance is pretty strict, with no recorded lectures. Other than that he is chill.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--So many papers--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: Lectures are amazing and cover really interesting and important topics. Boone is really chill and clearly passionate about what he is teaching. Weekly discussion papers, two "exams" and a mid-semester larger paper. Also a weird final project. Lectures are essential, nothing is posted online so you might get lost if you don't attend.

Boone is a pretty cool person but sometimes the lectures got a little repetitive and boring, but you kinda have to go or you will be lost in the class. Weekly discussion papers due but you will get an 100 just for doing it. You could probably get away with not doing all the reading but I would recommend doing them. Super easy online midterm/final
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Lots of homework

reviews.comment: Loved this class. Must go to lectures or you will miss important information that isn't reviewed in discussion sections. Weekly readings/discussion responses were super easy and overall the workload was very manageable and clear-cut. Boone is passionate about what he does and his lectures are usually very interesting.

This was easiest I've ever taken. Weekly work that does not take long, automatic 100 if you put in any effort. Papers are graded a little more difficult but still very easy. Boone is a super nice guy and understands that a 104 level class should not be rocket science. Attendance is not really mandatory but recommended.
lectures weren't mandatory only discussions and final was 21 true or false questions.

Disappointing. His lectures were repetitive, narrow-minded, and political. *Weekly* readings/responses. My TA didn't read my work, just gave me 100's for handing in (annoying since I put work in). No one in my discussion did the readings so it was awkward/waste of time. Student once openly verbally attacked me in class and prof didn't do anything.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Lots of homework--So many papers

reviews.comment: Lectures could get really circular and confusing, but the material was interesting and Boone is really nice. Incredibly easy grading but directions on assignments were occasionally confusing.

He is a good teacher and cares a lot about his students. He drags the lectures to the point were it gets boring. The discussion sections are mandatory but I lucked out. I didn't go to any discussions but emailed him that I was struggling and next thing I know, I got 100% on participation. I didn't read a thing, but I also don't know what we learned
Boone is a great professor. He is very reasonable. One discussion forum is due every week about the reading and then 2 (easy) exams. If you pay attention you will get an A.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Get ready to read--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Lectures can sometimes be boring and hard to follow but occassionally there are good pointers to help with your weekly reflections. He is overall a really nice guy and understanding. Class was easy and had a lot of built in extra credit. Do your work and you will pass. Would definitely recommend this class to anyone who needs it as a gen ed.
Great professor who graded easily and fairly

He's clearly a nice guy and cares about his students' success, but the class was a little lame. Great to take if you're not an anthro major and need the gen ed. A lot of reading, but I barely skimmed most of it and did fine. I'd love to take a more in depth class with him!

He is so sweet but the class has a lot of prerecorded lectures that can be boring. The TA you get will determine how the semester goes because you don't have any live lectures other than the discussions. My TA was really good.

Boone is a wonderful professor, one of the best I've had at Umass! He's very understanding and easy to communicate with. Class content was always interesting and engaging. There are 500 word papers due weekly but they are totally doable, and honestly help your grade so much if you just do them. Its an easy A so long as you do your work.

I took careers and beyond. Boone is great. The class was small, discussions were good, and over all I feel more comfortable about graduating now. Professor is funny and caring, will accommodate you if you need it, especially now.

Though he seems like a nice guy, as a lecturer I was often bored and found it hard to pay attention  also the class is basically just definining culture in a bunch of different ways. Put in the work and it's an easy A (summarized readings. Very vague about material on exams (since he makes it a few days prior), and TAs weren't that helpful either.

a great guy with a great passion, however if you zone out once in lecture youll be lost for the rest of the class. He does a good job at sounding interesting but often it can be hard to really understand what hes getting at. Tbh your grade is going to depend on your TA. Didnt read the books besides for summaries, 1-2 page papers due every Mondays.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Lecture heavy--So many papers

reviews.comment: Prof. Shear's super chill as a person. I didn't like him as a lecturer because I thought he was repetitive and boring. However, I really loved the assignments because Prof. Shear really tried to include interesting relevant topics and modern day issues/trends. That made the class so much better and all those papers worth it.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Inspirational--So many papers

reviews.comment: So I took this as a freshman, and it was a lot of work. For a GenEd, it feels like a lot to have tests, papers, and multiple page essays due at the beginning at every week. However, I did those all last minuet, did not study or read, and went to only about half of the lectures and got an A. Going to seem hard but if you do the work you're good.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--SO MANY PAPERS

reviews.comment: This was my favorite class taken so far at Umass! This professor was amazing. He is so kind and makes the class actually enjoyable. Attendance isn't mandatory however, attend lecture because the tests are all about what he talks about. The Ta's graded papers and gave no feedback. Papers due every Monday but they are easy. Love this class!!!!
reviews.rating_tags: Respected--Get ready to read--SO MANY PAPERS

reviews.comment: He is a great professor, very engaging and hilarious. I was in the honors section so the best part were discussions. Wonderful discussions and interesting reading, easy grader on essays and tests. Reading material fascinating. Will challenge you if you're not into anthro but worth it.

Lots of work for a gen ed. writing 3 page response papers ever week is a bit much for a gen ed. Doesn't seem that knowledgable about the class. just regurgitates information from the Huffpost articles he reads. whenever a student asks him to expand on a topic he seems to struggle. There are easier gen eds out there, don't waste your time
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--LOTS OF HOMEWORK--SO MANY PAPERS

reviews.comment: Good amount of work for a Gen Ed but if you do it all you will get an easy A. Interesting class, gives a new perspectives.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--EXTRA CREDIT

reviews.comment: Took this class to fulfill a GenEd requirement. Lots of writing and reading but the class makes you look at things in new ways that I think helped me a lot through my first semester of college.  Very easy grader, if you do the writing you'll get an A guaranteed. Would Recommend!
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--SO MANY PAPERS--EXTRA CREDIT

reviews.comment: Boone is a great guy, however his class is tough. On average, he gives about 3 five page essaysarticles to read every week. Also this is a writing intensive course so expect to write papers every week. If you are a slow reader, or a bad writer, please listen to me and do not take this class, save your GPA.

Boone is a great teacher. He is very informative and helpful. Very passionate about teachings. There are weekly questions that are turned in every Tuesday but they are not graded harshly at all. He seems very genuine.
Honestly the best teacher on this planet. He understands the students he teaches and tailors his grading and curriculum to them. He will become your friend after one class and is no doubt amazing.

very liberal and open about his politics. helpful as long as you are working hard and engaging with the materials. long readings, and weekly writing assignments that range from half a page to 3 pages. only one in class test, and one take home exam. overall interesting and smart guy. if you keep up with the readings and participate you'll get an A.
Great Prof!

Prof Shear was always interesting - I looked forward to go to his class. The exams and written assignments are pretty intense, but that's all in terms of work. Friendly and helpful, he leads a discussion that clears up most if not all questions and delves into all the material. Awesome class and awesome professor.

He's a nice guy with a well-structured class. Our assignments are GIS labs where we have multiple TAs to help us. You can turn in things late with no grade-related penalty (not turning in an assignment will block you from accessing the next module, however). Fun final project which is a poster you present at a symposium. Has a snack box in lab.

This class was great - pretty much all of the work for it and most of the learning gets done in lab time which is really well structured and you always have the TAs and Forrest there to help. He's a super fun and caring guy who I'd definitely recommend taking a class with.
Really nice guy, and fun to listen to. Low stress class with easy grading.

forrest was a great professor! it was easy to contact him outside of class and labs were graded fairly with opportunities to correct them for some points back. he was a funny professor and cared about his students. 100% recommend taking him for gis!!!
amzing

Love Forrest, he's really understanding and helpful. I really did not understand GIS but he helps you through it. Lectures are not really important, just have to go to labs and complete the labs (since that's all you're graded on)
reviews.rating_tags: Clear grading criteria--Gives good feedback--Online Savvy

reviews.comment: Dr. Bowlick really pays attention to all parts of putting a class together -- he selects useful skills to build and he thinks hard about the best way to learn them. You emerge from this class feeling confident that you built a lot of solid, relevant skills, and you'll also have a portfolio to share with employers! He makes scary topics fun.

I loved Forrest! Lots of work in the WebGIS class but he is super understanding and cares about his students. Online the lectures were not mandatory but I think they are when in person. If you're ever stuck on a project he is super helpful you just need to reach out. Super nice guy.
Forrest is one of the most genuine caring profs at UMass. The course is a lot of work, but he is extremely accessible and wants the best for you.

Forrest is a really nice guy, and a good teacher. His lectures didn't always seem to relate to the labs, but that's ok. The labs were a lot of work, but the help of the TA's and Forrest made them do-able. Super helpful, and gives plenty of opportunity to earn back any points lost if needed. I went from a 60 to a 90 on an exam with the extra credit!

Forrest is a dope professor and made GIS fun and interesting! GIS is a real life skill and I learned so much in this course. I wish I took it sooner to take more classes with Forrest - highly recommend!

Forrest is a good professor for intro to GIS. He is a really nice guy and although he's a little awkward, he is passionate about you wanting to learn and is clear about the basics of GIS. The grading can be a little tough but there are plenty of opportunities to earn back points. Make sure to work hard in the lab and the class won't be too hard.
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--ACCESSIBLE OUTSIDE CLASS--Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: I would not recommend this class. Quizzes are frequent and full of trick questions. The biggest issue is the group project worth 50% of our grade, assigned halfway through with very vague instructions. asking for help only made it more confusing and made us feel more alone. Overall, it's stressful, unclear, and lacks guidance. Avoid if you can.
reviews.rating_tags: Group projects--Lecture heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Professor Sargent is an excellent, organized teacher. His lectures are super engaging. His course builds practical historical research skills through a semester-long project. Brian is a fair grader who gives personalized feedback, even in a large class, and shows genuine care for students. Highly recommended.

I enjoyed Brian's Social Inequality Policy course. He's an amazing lecturer who intentionally chose his words and engaged well with students' questions. The readings and lectures were dense, but all of them were very helpful for my understanding of the subject. I find myself referencing back to this class very often. I recommend him to any friends.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Group projects--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: The lectures were very engaging and easy to follow, so even though the exams were writing heavy and a bit long, they really weren't as bad as you would think. Prof Sargent is also extremely understanding and makes sure to grade fairly and tends to make changes to the curriculum that helps bring your grades up.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Group projects--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: Brian is one of the most passionate professors I've ever had. The group project's challenges are intentional—he knows the confusion it causes. The goal is to navigate bureaucracy while fostering creative social change. He is a delight, please do not be discouraged by his other reviews.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Group projects

reviews.comment: This is in reference to Policy & Social Inequality. I would highly not recommend taking this class even if you are driven and care about the subject. If you have anxiety and don't like group work and vague guidelines, this is not the class for you. Exams and group work required a lot of mental jumping through hoops and made the class stressful.
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Group projects--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Although Brian grades on very little, his exams are open note and open book. His lectures are incredibly interesting. If you're lazy about attendance DO NOT TAKE THIS CLASS. Things he teaches in the lectures are on the exams. Good class for good note takers!
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Honestly a really nice guy. He does online exams so if you have friends in the class, take the exam together. I can't stress this enough GO TO CLASS, he lays out whats on the exam in class and its a better use of your time than studying the slides.
reviews.rating_tags: Lecture heavy--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: During his lectures, he reads off his notes using a complex vocabulary that makes it hard to understand teaching concepts. He makes the slides he uses for the class accessible to everyone, but he tells us that the slides give misleading info. He wants us to take notes on what he says in class. your final grade is based on three tests.

While Prof. Sargent grades based on very few assessments, which can be stressful, his tests are open-note and his lecture slides include almost all the information you need to know. As long as you look over the lecture slides and/or take notes, it's manageable. Prof. Sargent divides the syllabus in really nice ways and explains things very well.
reviews.rating_tags: Lecture heavy--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Do NOT take Sargent's class. He's awful and rude. No extra credit opportunities or group projects to get to know classmates. There are only 3 exams and your grade is dependent only on these 3 exams which are hard and the questions are stupid and not on the lecture slides. I took way harder Econ and Stats classes, and soc110 was my worst grade!!

very smart and knows how to teach the subject pretty well. the whole class is graded on 3 exams. def have to attend lectures - you can't get access to recordings easily. he talks really fast and it's hard to get everything down. i liked the subject and it was easy to do well on the exams if you pay attention in class.

WORST GEN ED. If you don't go to lecture good luck getting anything above a D. Every exam question is designed to trick you in the hardest way possible, not test your knowledge of the subject. Tests are based on exact words from him in lecture, not the slides and the textbook you pay for.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Lecture heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: He was the worst professor I have ever had. There are only 3 exams that count towards your grade, and there are not many questions on it. He rambles on on tangents about absolutely nothing and wastes time every class. Wording on the tests is difficult to decipher, and he clearly does not proof read because there many are spelling/grammar errors.

Brian is a fast-paced professor, he will just talk and talk for 75 minutes without stop unless someone has a question. All the slides are posted so I recommend that the notes that you take are of what he says, not what's on the board. The grading is based on 3 open note exams (each 33% of your grade).
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Lecture heavy--Test heavy

reviews.comment: The teacher only has 3 exams throughout the whole semester and if you get one semi bad score then you are screwed. No work or extra credit and not scaling the tests. Goes way to fast in lectures. test questions designed to mess you up or trick you.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Only 3 exams for the entire semester and they are so hard and make no sense! Multiple choice but confusing wording and not related to the lecture material. Even if you work hard, you won't necessarily do well.

SUCH A HARDO. Literally wants to see his students fail for an ego boost or something. Lectures are abs mandatory and a lot of his test questions are answered in class so write everything he says. Honestly if ur in STEM taking this as a pre req you'll prob be fine. Find a friend to "study" with bc tests are online !!
lose points in one exam and you will never get an A. some questions designed for you to get wrong. stupid class and I regret taking it.

He only grades based on 3 exams. The wording sucks and it is often unclear what is the right answer. He also goes through lectures with no time to type and too many words. He doesn't even cover material in the exams in class.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: DO. NOT. TAKE. I had to switch from hand-written notes to typing on my computer after Exam 1 because his lectures move so fast. The slides are wordy and he tests on things he doesn't include in the lecture slides. There are 3 exams throughout the semester each worth 33% of the final and there are no other assignments. Sargent is just the worst.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Lecture heavy--Tough grader

reviews.comment: This class is graded entirely on three exams. I attended almost every class and did well, but because he refused to make lecture recordings available to those who missed class it would be very difficult to pass without attending class. There is absolutely nothing special about Brian and found myself annoyed with him frequently.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: literally the worst class i took this semester. he talks at lightning speed and expects you to write down his words, not the slides. graded entirely on 3 exams which were all confusingly worded. he genuinely does not care about his students succeeding. i would never take a class with him again even if my life depended on it.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Graded by few things--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: Worst professor I have had so far. Entire grade is spread across 3 MCQ exams where answer choices are always ambiguous. Get ready to memorize word for word what he says in lecture. Took this class because I was passionate about socio but he makes me hate it. Does not give extra credit, does not care about students doing well. I could go on.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Test heavy

reviews.comment: If I see Sargent in hell, I won't even say hi. His class grade is only based on 3 exams with 25-30 questions that are poorly worded and more than one right answer. He does not reply to emails, or care about his students at all. I took this class as a pre med and its harder to score than my toughest science classes.
reviews.rating_tags: Graded by few things--Test heavy--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: Grade is based on 3 tests. The questions on the test can be worded terribly and there can be multiple correct answers but he wants HIS answer. He doesn't care about his students individually, only cares about the class "average". He goes way too fast during lecture and tells you to write what he says, not what the slides say.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Graded by few things--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: Do the readings, especially the chapter work. It'll make or break your grade, you can't get by on going to lecture alone. That being said, he's a fast talker who gets really impassioned about subjects, so learn to write down only the important stuff and not just copy straight from the slides. A good professor who will teach you a lot!
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Clear grading criteria--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: Just a very horrible class. Avoid if you can because the grade is based on 3 exams. And his exams are soooooo tricky that its impossible to get it correct. Very inflexible and not understanding.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Graded by few things--Test heavy

reviews.comment: The entire class is graded by three exams and nothing else. The the exams are hard and have "trick" and/or poorly worded questions. He lectures too fast to take good notes, refuses to post the lectures. He snippy towards questions. You have to provide "valid proof" in order to obtain lectures outside of class, even for studying. Awful experience.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Graded by few things--Test heavy

reviews.comment: Not the best gen ed to take if you're looking for an easy A. Grade is based on 3 exams and no extra credit. Exams are only around 30 questions long and some of the questions aren't even based on his lectures! You can't even watch the lectures until you email him and have an excuse. Not a flexible class and doesn't explain lecture materials well.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Graded by few things--Test heavy

reviews.comment: goes way too fast in lectures, makes lecture notes extensively long (my hand is cramping as we speak), refuses to posts lecture videos online unless you emailed him you were absent ahead of time (can't rewatch lectures to study for exam), gives no study guide or any help when preparing for exam. 2/10 do not recommend.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: While the lectures are interesting, the only way you can apply your knowledge from the lectures is through one small-paragraph weekly discussion post. There are exam questions not relating to anything in the lectures and the exam grades are harsh, each exam being only out of 25 multiple choice questions.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Graded by few things--Test heavy

reviews.comment: I took his class completely remote during the covid era so take my rating with a grain of salt. He is a very nice teacher but his classes are very lecture heavy and important for the tests. The tests also weigh so much and there are only 25 questions so if you are a bad test taker like me its not that fun.
reviews.rating_tags: Graded by few things--Test heavy--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: Asynchronous online lectures were a bit slow, but nothing too bad. You are graded on your posts in a discussion board following every lecture , and 3 exams. His exams are incredibly easy, gives four hours and open note privileges to answer 25 multiple choice. Not very interesting class, but only a fool couldn't get an A.

Decent professor, he's kind of hard to understand sometimes but I did fine on exams. The whole grade for the course is just 3 exams (noncumulative) and a discussion board. The exams are difficult (even with open notes and 4 hours), some of the things on the exam aren't mentioned in class. Prof Sargent does want us to succeed though and gave EC!
reviews.rating_tags: Graded by few things--Test heavy--EXTRA CREDIT

reviews.comment: Why is every single reading (several depending on the unit) twenty pages long fine print? Some of the lectures are almost word for word taken from the book but he also spends a lot of time talking about how plagiarism is a cardinal sin. Doesn't define due dates but expects you to turn things in on time. Other than that, pretty standard class.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: He is a very good teacher. understanding. generous. sympathy.

Dr.Brunner is a great person and they made the topic fun and engaging. There is quite a bit homework in the course including three essays and reading quizzes but they aren't to bad. The midterm and final aren't bad if you study as well. You also get notes on the exams too.

I don't know why people are writing that shes rude and her lectures are boring. It is a very easy class, you don't need the textbook and quizzes are open note. She explains concepts well and has many turn and talks during the lecture so you get to chat and get help from the students around you. This class was easier than AP psych. Great prof!!
TERRIBLE. This class was honestly so not enjoyable. She was extremely annoying and did not do a good job of making her lectures engaging. It was a waste of time.

She can be mean sometimes but she's not that bad, and the class is not difficult, you don't need the book. Attendence is mandatory, but you have around 4 free absences. The only thing is that her quizes and test are very confusing and 3 out of 4 anwers can easily be correct but only 1 gives you points.

Professor Brunner's lectures were long and boring. A lot of people got away with not coming to class. Her quizzes were easy & all online, as well as the final. We had 3 finals: a project, paper, & exam. She was rude to students and was unclear about a lot of assignments. Would not take a class with her again.

She will not answer your emails even when she offers to set up a meeting, leaving one without a meeting or a chance to revise their grade.She was very rude and simply just unclear about all directions. Final paper, final project and final exam.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Lecture heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: So rude, and showed no respect towards her students. It was difficult to reach her outside of class, because she rarely responded to emails. The class itself wasn't particularly difficult, but because of her attitude HUMDEV270 quickly became one of my least favorite classes. Sitting through her lectures felt like watching paint dry.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--EXTRA CREDIT--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: Brunner was not that bad. She was never in a bad mood and always seemed very interested in what was being taught. Quizzes were all online, there was a paper, group project and a final that was online. Lectures are mandatory but honestly I sat on my phone during the whole thing.
She gets a lot of hate, but to me she was so much fun! She tried to make learning fun with the projects, and always was in a good mood!
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Group projects--Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: Attendance was mandatory with three allowed absences before it started affecting grades, but excused absences didn't matter (I missed 2 classes because I was sick and still only had one absence left). Otherwise pretty chill, with very few tests (replaced by group projects). She lets you have a cheat sheet on the tests.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Group projects--Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: Prof Brunner is fine. Her class is easy and manageable. Don't bother buying a textbook because all the chapter quizzes can be found online and the midterm and final are online too. She forgets to post stuff a lot but overall the class is easy. Get ready for a lot of group projects.
great class, but a lot of reading every week. Lectures are very interesting and the group projects are a lot of fun.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Group projects--Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: You do A LOT of reading, and group projects. If you have to take this as a requirement for education- don't worry, its not terrible. You can find most information online and it's really not hard if you can learn from slideshows. Prof. Brunner is very straight to the point, and a good person.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Group projects--Test heavy

reviews.comment: you do not need to do the readings and all the answers to the quizzes are online. the power points are easy to take notes on, but all she does is read off of them. she does not really know what she's talking about. BUT the final and midterm were both online. so as much as i kinda dislike the prof, the class is easy and worth it.

I love Dr.Brunner's class a lot! There is a lot of reading in the class, but totally manageable. I always find her lectures super fascinating, and you can tell she really cares about what she is teaching and works hard. I would highly recommend her class! Don't let the other reviews scare you at all.

I thought that Dr. Brunner was very accommodating. She will give you extra time to complete tasks as long as your request are reasonable and you let her know ahead of the due date and explain how you are struggling and how extra time would benefit you. She is a fair grader and fair teacher.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Group projects--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Dr. Brunner is rude and insensitive. She barely responds to emails, and when she does, it is with attitude. Attendance is mandatory for students, but she will take as much time off as she pleases. If you're not feeling well or cannot come to class for a legitimate reason, she will not even pretend to care. She is incredibly apathetic.

If you have to take the class: don't buy the book, quizzes are online, and don't expect to know what your grade is until finals
If you don't: don't. I learned nothing in this class - used it like study hall and just did the hw.

Don't buy the book. Mandatory attendance in lecture (25min walk) even though she just reads off the slides which already lack content and are posted online. Last class is in a week and only one or two grades are in. Almost weekly quizzes (online, quizlet) and a few papers (reflections) plus the final (online) and final project (group or paper)

The class itself is easy and has little workload, but Prof Brunner is terrible. Takes attendance in a 200 person lecture and is incredibly strict on it. If you skip a class without an excused absence, your grade gets knocked. However, if you have an excused absence, she won't see it because she does not respond to emails. She can be very rude too.

Mandatory attendance (30 min walk from SW) , she reads right off the slides so you get nothing out of being in class, takes MONTHS to grade things, does not respond to any emails, however easy class because exams were all online and she takes every question from quizlet for exams and weekly quizzes. Not the worst but not the best.
Very easy class but did not enjoy the professor. Took forever to grade stuff, doesn't respond to emails, and a little rude sometimes.

The class itself is interesting, however, Brunner takes so long to grade papers and assigns new assignments without providing feedback. Brunner also ignores emails-I'm not the only one who waited over 2 weeks for a response. She reads directly off her slides, and even though the take-home exams are open-note, she takes all questions from quizlet.

She grades so slowly and you really have no idea the weight of each assignment. She also does not reply to emails and is nearly impossible to communicate with. I had to send her 4 follow up emails just for her to tell me she was "sick" and thats why she didn't respond, even though we had class that week. Awful professor, but easy class
Really interesting course, but it is a lot of her just reading off the slides. Also very disorganized. Lots of busywork. Do not need to buy the textbook.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--So many papers--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: Prof. Brunner is not as bad as the reviews make her seem. I enjoy human development and I think she teaches it well. She does attendance at lectures and once a week the class breaks into discussion sections within the lecture which is kind of odd but it's not that bad. She only gives a midterm and a final project.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Group projects--Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: The course itself is really interesting but Dr. Brunners lectures are just her reading off the screen. Which doesnt makes mandatory attendance a weird requirement because she posts the slides on Moodle. The final was in a two hour period rather than a full day so I missed it. Shes a sweet person though.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Group projects--Tough grader

reviews.comment: Bad online class. Prof always posts things late and inconsistently. The moodle page is horribly disorganized and is reflected in her lectures and work. The two T.A.s are these two 50 y/o women, be prepared to get some harsh and unfair grading from one of them and non-sensical but overly merciful grading from the other. Easy A, but annoying class.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Get ready to read--EXTRA CREDIT

reviews.comment: This class is alright. There are quizzes on the reading due every class and all of the answers are online. There is an easy project, research paper, online quizzes, and two exams with an optional final. Attendance is required which is annoying because she reads right off the slides which she posts on Moodle.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Skip class? You won't pass.--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: Professor Brunner is welcoming and thoughtful. There is a lot of reading but she always goes over it in class. She gives extra credit opportunities and makes her lectures interesting with videos and real life examples. She is very open to adjusting the way she teaches in order for the students to understand the material and she is always cheerful!

Prof Brunner is a really nice person, knew all of our names in a 75 person class. Fun group project. There was an excessive amount of reading, however you could get by just skimming. The quizzes for each chapter were 5 questions each and not hard if you at least skimmed. Attendance is taken at every class meeting and is 5% of your grade.

Worst online class. Course materials are always posted late, no feedback  throughout the semester. Final project consists of submitting a final lesson plan with revisions based on feedback we never received. Never even received a grade for the final project. Half the assignments still weren't graded so no idea what she based final grade on.
Don't take this professor unless you hate yourself and love pain and anguish and unclear guidelines and poor instruction

Dr. Brewer destroyed my confidence. He was very rude when giving feedback. He never highlighted something someone did well. His comments were just plain mean. I was never scared of writing before, but now I am. Ironic since the aim of the class is to make you a better, more confident writer.
this class was a waste of time and his assignments made no sense at all. do not take!

He made us go out in the field and do random studies for the numerous pointless projects in the class. Why was I made to go count the number of lichen on certain trees across campus on several different occasions? In all honesty, this class just gave us inconvenient projects that were more annoying then difficult. He was obsessed with lichen.

Brewer did a lot right in this class-- he was accessible, gave feedback, and structured the class well-- but I dreaded the class every week. The assignments were pretty confusing most of the time and he likes to drone on about stuff that makes class uninteresting and even frustrating. I felt like I learned very little in this class.
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Clear grading criteria--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Very harsh grader and doesn't have clear grading criteria. He makes all the projects very hard to understand and won't explain what to do leaving you very confused with no idea of where to start
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--So many papers--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Professor Brewer is a nice guy, but at times it seems like the class has no idea what's going on. This is most of the time. He is very quiet and has trouble directing the class's attention toward what he is talking about. He is incredibly lenient and responsive, so WHEN (not if) you have question about a particular project, he'll help out.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Accessible outside class--Online Savvy

reviews.comment: Professor Brewer is one of the nicest Professors I have ever had. As others have mentioned, some of his assignments are confusing but if you just shoot him a message he will usually respond to you within minutes to help and explain. He is just a super easy going and nice professor all around! Highly recommend!

Dr. Brewer is a nice person and seems like one of the more lenient writing in bio profs. Directions and rubrics were confusing for almost every project; there is weekly homework (at least no research papers!), and his grading can be harsher than anticipated. But you can end with an A if you just complete the assignments and put in a little effort.
omg where do I start, yes he is a nice professor and all but this class is so much work. the worst class in biology

Brewer is such a nice guy. His assigned work was confusing to comprehend a lot of the time, but he's patient with explaining it over again. He is thoughtful in how he evaluates work, and a lot of work is to be put in for the few big assignments in the class. There was a required textbook, but I survived without it.

Dr. Brewer is a great guy. This class is a lot of work but if you show effort and are actively engaged with the class, Brewer will notice this and your grade will reflect. There was 4 projects throughout the course with the middle 2 taking up a substantial part of the course. Don't save stuff for last minute in this class, it won't be fun.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough Grader--Skip class? You won't pass.--GROUP PROJECTS
