Provides a lot of examples for each of the questions and gives students many opportunities to receive help. Tests are graded very fairly, and the instructor explains how to do certain homework problems during class.

She communicated the information clearly and allowed cheat sheets for every exam. The content wasn't extremely difficult but it did require a bit of studying, but she offered a lot of resources. Every lecture is recorded but attendance via TopHat is required. Great teacher, funny, and enthusiastic. Would recommend.

Prof Burch is a good professor, but you just need to pay attention. Definitely go to office hours they can be really helpful in understanding the content because it is challenging. Exams are nothing like the practice exams, so work on your cheat sheet thoroughly. As long as you understand the content, you will be fine.
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Gives good feedback--Lots of homework

reviews.comment: Super nice professor, the class is on the more difficult side especially for an intro class / requirement for all majors. She is forgiving with the grading on exams, lots of partial credit. Fair class, just requires lots of effort.

I loved her class! She cares that you learn the material, and is great at teaching it. Pay attention in class, keep up with the work, and make a good cheat sheet to study and you should do great in the class. It's pretty easy material overall, just need to focus.
Tests are the same as the practice exams, course is relatively easy if you pay attention. Homework is 35% of your grade and it's all busy work that takes forever. Offers no extra credit.

Definitely yaps and gets sidetracked, but she's trying to keep you engaged for an hour 15 minutes. 3 exams are straight forward and you get a cheat sheet. Homework is usually very different from how you are taught in class for no reason- but not too difficult.

Michele Burch thinks she is charming... she is not. Even though this class is mandatory, it is the worlds most useless content if you are not an OIM major. The tests are just like the practice exams and she rewards having good cheat sheets. Also, buckle up for the homework! It is nothing like the examples from classes. Good luck!

Professor Burch is one of the highest-rated professors at Isenberg, and for good reason. You can miss two classes but beyond that, you will lose participation points for the top hat so show up to class. Exams are fairly easy and allow an 8.5 x 11 double-sided cheat sheet which must be handwritten and turned in with the exam. Homework can be tough.

Big yapper and gets sidetracked, but the class is set up for you to succeed. Exams are similar to practice exams, and you get a whole double-sided cheat sheet. As long as you do the homework and have a good cheat sheet, you'll do fine on the exams. Tophat is mandatory and you have to get it right for credit, but she gives out the answers in class.
literally doesnt teach just yaps the whole lecture i dropped this class

Professor Burch is a great professor who wants you to do well. 3 exams (60%) and homework (35%) make up your grade along with Top Hat. Exams can be challenging, but cheat sheet helps. Practice exam is similar to real exam. She tries to make it as interactive/entertaining as she can early in morning. Overall, she is funny and makes it a good class.

Professor Burch is very kind and passionate about the subject. The homework is very beneficial, I learned mostly from doing those problems. Exams were challenging, but having a cheat sheet was super helpful (the exams are a lot like the practice exams, so I would recommend putting those problems on your cheat sheet)!

Burch is a great teacher that wants to help the whole class succeed. Homeworks were very quick each week and then the 3 tests didn't take much prep plus you get a cheat sheet. She goes over a practice test that is basically the same as the real test. She's a fun lecturer but the content is dragged on, so you could just do the homework in class.

I really enjoyed this class. The homework did take a while to do every week, however it was worth a large percentage of the grade which helped raise my grade. The exams were moderately challenging, but you got a cheat sheet and she really helped you prepare for them. Overall, I would definitely recommend taking this class with professor Burch!

Prof Burch was a great professor who teaches very well. It can feel like the lectures are dragging on sometimes. The HW is very helpful for the exams. She goes over the practice exams in class, which is really helpful. She also allows you to have cheat sheets for the exams.

This was one of the most useful courses I've taken in Isenberg to date. The team project in collaboration with Dell Technologies is so helpful in terms of gaining tangible experience providing recommendations for a company to enhance efficiency in processes! Really interesting material, makes the work fun, and is an overall joy to have as a prof.

I took OIM this past semester and I loved prof. Burch, she sometimes tries too hard to be funny and it can be awkward sometimes but overall she's a great teacher and the TA office hours are really helpful and she wants her students to do well. The homework assignments are great practice and she lets you have a cheat sheet on the exams.

Professor Burch is the absolute best! She explains all the material clearly, and she is always willing to help. The class has three exams and as long as you pay attention, you'll do well. Plus homework and participation is worth 40% so you have a ton of opportunities to do well if you don't do good on the exams.

Michele Burch is THAT girl. Taking this class with anyone else would be a waste to be honest. HW is worth 35% of your final grade and you get unlimited attempts, plus a bonus homework where you can get over an 100 for your hw average. Moderate challenge but she is so sweet and accommodating. Go to class for tophat, worth 5% of final grade! Love her

She made it interesting and fun to learn. She kept class entertaining while also managing to keep it on topic. She is the reason I switched my major; she inspires interest in the major and career. This course is built for you to succeed.

Professor Burch is an enthusiastic, quirky lecturer who clearly cares about the subject matter she teaches. Never brings dull energy. If you pay attention to the slides, and more importantly can apply them to the homeworks / organize the important formulas, you'll pass with flying colors easily.

Isenberg is filled with very easy classes with teachers that give less effort to their students. Michele Burch goes the extra mile, conducting in-person exams that are moderately challenging and forcing you to really master the content. BBL is very clear, highly organized, and clearly cares about students. Moderate challenge but manageable
reviews.rating_tags: Clear grading criteria--Respected--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: She makes class so interesting and she is so funny. Decently easy class and homework is manageable and really helpful. Exams have cheat sheets and are like the practice exam. Definitely recommend!
Prof. Burch gave so many opportunities to do well and get the grade you want while still learning. She made the class way more interesting than I thought it would be.
I thought she was a great professor

One of my favorite classes in the MBA program, mainly because of the subject matter. No textbooks used, but 5 books that can be listened to or added to a Kindle. Interesting (and short) lectures with accompanying videos. Grades are based on discussion participation, two small "projects" or summaries, and one final project. Definitely recommend!
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Clear grading criteria--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment:
Burch is great

OIM301 will be a shock because it's the hardest of the 301s. Theres a lot of complex topics that take some effort to understand. Attendance isn't required BUT you don't want to fall behind

Burch makes a possibly challenging topic enjoyable and easier. She's very approachable. I changed my major to OIM from MGMT after this class.
Solid professor with great knowledge. Do the work and you will be ok.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Group projects--Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: Disregard anyone saying the class is hard, only downside is mandatory attendance for a lecture. I skipped every class after exam1 + did not complete every hw, then used the extra credit hw +did well on the last 2 exams & comfortably got an A. Barely knew her but she seemed nice. The study guides are almost exactly the same as the exam, dont be dumb
reviews.rating_tags: Graded by few things--Lecture heavy--EXTRA CREDIT

reviews.comment: Attendance is mandatory but she tries to make it as enjoyable as she can, really fun prof. Homework is doable but if you need help there's office hours. Exams were straightforward as long as you study and understand the concepts. She lets you use cheat sheets, front and back. If you do the work you will get an A, its college, just do the work.
reviews.rating_tags: Accessible outside class--Participation matters--Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: Michele is a super kind teacher but her grading is kinda rough. There are 4 exams and no extra credit. If you screw up on one exam, you won't be passing. The class in mandatory so you much go to class. Homework takes up to 2 to 3 hours but you can go to office hours for help. Cheat sheets are allowed on exams. Overall you gotta work for your grade.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Skip class? You won't pass.--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: Taking this class online is near impossible because she posts old lecture videos, when the exam format was different due to in person classes. Exam reviews and lecture content don't correlate with the exams online which makes learning difficult. Although she is nice, she flies through examples in class. Only saving grace are exam cheat sheets.

I really like her teaching style and how she does participation. Literally one of the only classes thats not a joke and I actually learn stuff thats beneficial. Also exams are easy because we get a cheat sheet which is very helpful. Honestly no complaints for this class.

Professor Burch is the best professor I've had in college so far. She does such a great job of explaining material to her students and does a great job spacing out work outside of class so you don't feel too overwhelmed. She is funny and relatable and really wants to see her students succeed. The cheat sheet on exams is a bonus too!!
reviews.rating_tags: Accessible outside class--Skip class? You won't pass.--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: Michele isnt a regular mom, shes a cool mom. She explains the problems in ways that make sense logically, which was helpful since Im not a math person. She lets you bring a cheat sheet to the exams and the exam questions are really similar to whats on our homework - she doesnt try to trick you. Highly recommend taking this class with her!
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Clear grading criteria--Hilarious

reviews.comment: Professor Burch is a nice teacher who is also funny. The only thing is that her lectures can get kind of boring and you have to really pay attention and stay engaged to understand the material. She also does lecture questions so you have to view every lecture in its entirety.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: As someone who doesn't like OIM, this class wasn't awful. I hated the material but she did a good job of explaining it. Cheatsheet for every exam and there are no surprises. Go to lecture, do the homework, and write your notes from lecture on the sheet and you'll pass. Tophats are annoying but they're your participation grade. Super accommodating.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Skip class? You won't pass.--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: I love her she is my favorite professor at Isenberg. You have one presentation, no exams, quizzes every week on the readings and they aren't bad at all and a group project

Professor Burch is the only one who teaches OIM301 so ur stuck with her. There are 3 exams total with 5 questions on each one and you're allowed a double sided cheat sheet for these. Exams are graded by TAs who will give you as many points possible if you show ur work and formulas. We went online so there was no partial credit and it tanked my grad
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Skip class? You won't pass.--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: I really liked Michele. She was funny and does remind me of Leslie Knope haha. The lectures are mandatory but not a struggle to sit through. The homework is kinda hard but if you have a chegg you will be golden. The exams are difficult but study the practice exam and slides to do well. This class is easy if you are good at math, if not oops gluck!
Not gonna lie this OIM class was tough, but she is a great teacher and cares about learning.

The class was only easy because you get a cheat sheet on all tests and unlimited hw tries. If it wasn't for that this class would be impossible. She really wants you to do well in this class. I wish she did not take attendance because lectures are pointless and boring, she post slides online so I used class as time for other homework. Chegg for hw.

SLOW SLOW SLOW grading.  3/4 through the class and received only one of seven grades, despite six being submitted.  You dont know if hitting the mark on responses since no grade.  Reached out twice via email, no response
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Clear grading criteria--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Pointless equations that could be done in an excel spreadsheet but she makes you do them out yourself. There are 3 tests worth 75%, cheat sheet, but every exam has 1 problem that isn't on the practice exam that's worth 20% of the test. Unless you are able to have microscopic handwriting you won't fit every equation and will be shafted.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Test heavy--Tough grader

reviews.comment: Cheat sheets on exams! She just wants everyone to do well.

Michele is one of the best Profs I've had. Her lectures are very similar to what's on the exams. Cheat sheet is allowed for exams and it's very helpful. Exams are pretty easy, but definitely pay attention in class and go to her if you're confused. She is very helpful and is very sweet and caring. Great professor.

Michele is a very nice woman who tries to make her lectures as exciting as possible. Class participation is required via tophat, but not bad at all. Grade consists of weekly homework, three exams, and participation. You are allowed a double sided cheat sheet for the exam, which is very helpful. Tests are just like practice exams.
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--ACCESSIBLE OUTSIDE CLASS--Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: Great class, not too much work. She does a good job in keeping us interested during long lectures and is very understanding. Exams are easy as they are similar to home works and examples in class. Just put the effort in and you will get a good grade.

Michele may be a great professor in a live classroom setting, but her online class etiquette is lacking. She takes weeks to grade discussion threads and we're still waiting on the final project to be graded, with final grades due in a few days. This impacts tuition assistance for folks that are company sponsored.

Michele is a super nice teacher- kinda like a cool mom. 3 exams, each 25% of the grade, but you can bring a double sided cheat sheet with all the formulas (the exams consist of 5 math problems). Homework is tedious, but you get unlimited tries to get 100% (worth 20% of final grade) and is very close to the problems on exams. Not too hard!

Class is very easy if you go to class and actually pay attention. Problems on exams are identical to class and HW problems so pay attention. Class takes a little bit of work, but if you do it you will easily get an A
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--LOTS OF HOMEWORK--GRADED BY FEW THINGS

reviews.comment: One of the best professors in Isenberg and at UMass Amherst!!! If you can't get OIM 301 with Michele Burch, wait to take it. Her lectures are pretty straight forward and she always goes over what will be on exams. Regardless, she lets you have a cheat sheet on the exam so that also helps. She is funny and understands her students.

Makes a pretty dry subject interesting! Unlimited tries on homework and class is mandatory because of TopHat, but she makes them lively enough. Tests are pretty easy due to a cheat sheet. Very nice and helpful in office hours. Didn't end up needing textbook material but the hw is online so i bought it anyway. Most learning self-taught thru HW

Michelle is the best professor I've ever had at UMass. Would highly recommend taking her courses because they are interesting and fun to learn about. You have to read the assigned books to do well but it isn't bad since you're learning useful information.

Michele has to be the most energetic and positive professor at Isenberg. She wants everyone to succeed! She lets you use a cheat sheet for exams and the homework has an unlimited number of tries. The exams are practically the practice exams, but look over the power points right before an exam just incase! Never studied except for the night before

Like OIM210, OIM 301 is very easy. Burch makes the class much more energetic than it should be, which makes it easier to show up. TopHat will cost you a good amount and there's questions every lecture, so you have to show up. Cheat sheet on the test is big, with the test being just like the practice exams. Hard not to get an A.

To sum up this class, if we didn't get to have a cheat sheet it would be impossible to pass. The hardest part about this class is making the cheat sheets. I will say that for the first two exams, she barely gives you enough time. Most people finish after the class time has ended which can be very stressful. For homework, the MyOM labs are simple.
reviews.rating_tags: Clear grading criteria--GRADED BY FEW THINGS

reviews.comment: Michelle is awesome! I didn't really pay attention to her class but she is really funny and heartwarming like a cool mom

She is amazing! Very clear, helpful, and really wants you to learn. She grades all of her exams by hand so that she can give partial credit, and really tries to make the class as interesting as she can. By far my favorite professor I've had in Isenberg
BRO

I wish I could actually give professors a grade because PROFESSOR BURCH DESERVES AN A+++++++++++++ ALL THE WAY! She is so awesome, as long as you do the hw and make a good cheatsheet (including hw questions you don't know and the practice exam, then you will be fineeeeee! :)
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Clear grading criteria--Hilarious

reviews.comment: Attendance via top hat (phone app) and all lectures videorecorded online with all powerpoints. infinite tries on pearson hw. full page cheat sheet for tests. literally can scheme an A without showingup to class if you put in 2 hours a week tops. she's really chill, great at explaining, and low key funny. easiest class, as long as you understand it

Very very easy class. Burch is an awesome prof who clearly wants to see her students succeed. Lectures can be boring and are mandatory, but she puts the ECHOs online to rewatch. Practice exam is just like the exam & she allows a cheat sheet. Homework once a week, always accessible for help. Overall very easy A

One of the best professors I have had in Isenberg. Professor Burch is an extremely fair grader and gives partial credit on exams as well as allowing a cheat sheet. Everything you need to know is on the slides and she is always willing to help you out. Material can be tricky but everything is very straightforward and explained well. Would recommend.

Easy class and very nice lady. Grade is made up of homework, which can be taken until you get a 100%, participation (show up and do Tophat), and 3 exams. The exams don't have trick questions, and are similar to the practice exams. Put time into making your cheat sheet for each exam and it's an easy A.

Burch is amazing! So caring and tries to keep students engaged. I would buy her powerpoints at the campus design store since she goes off of the powerpoints completely! Really recommend her class, you get to make a cheat sheet and her entire exam is partial credit.

Professor Burch is the best professor I've had at UMass by far. Funny, gets students, and extremely transparent when it comes to what she expects for the test. For OIM you literally have the same questions on the test that you did in lectures. So with a cheat sheet its hard not to get an A.

Professor Burch is one of the best professors I've had at UMass. She really cares about the students learning and offers extra help for those who need it. There's 3 exams in total which are easy if you pay attention in class, review the powerpoints, and do the practice exams. It's not hard to get an A in this class.

Professor Burch really cares about the success of her students. She's funny, engaging, and very reasonable. Class can be boring, but just go through powerpoints before the exam and right down a ton of examples from the homework and notes on the cheat sheet and the tests will be no surprise. She's awesome!

Very clear and concise lecturer. Part of your grade is participating online in class via phone or computer which requires you to pay attention in class but it helps you learn the material. You get a cheat sheet for all exams, none are cumulative. If you make a good cheat sheet -- she has examples in her office -- it's very easy to ace this course.

Professor Burch is a very clear and succinct teacher who does a great job conveying the material. I feel I have gotten a lot out of her class. She makes good time with the lectures and keeps everyone engaged. Definitely would recommend taking her class.
A very fair and honest teacher.  Thought she did a nice job teaching the class.  The class itself had a ton of reading and writing.  Participation was a key part of the class.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Get ready to read--SO MANY PAPERS

reviews.comment: tests are difficult. lectures are pointless. have to work a decent amount for an A but there is cheat sheet allowed for every test. Very nice woman

One of the best professors I've had a UMass. Extremely funny and friendly. Teaches the class in an organized fashion and is clear about everything. Communicates with students well. This class is all math based with a little bit of critical thinking.

She honestly cares about the students and tries her best to reach out even though this is a huge lecture. She also loves the discipline itself, so it's interesting to hear out. Highly recommended to me, and I have too. Have changed my major to this field after Burch! So helpful, good energy, positive. Get the course workbook, textbook unnecessary

Prof. Burch reminds me of Leslie Knope from Parks and Rec. She's just like Amy Poehler. Very dedicated, quirky, and you either love or hate her, right away. She knows her stuff and will work with you to help you succeed. Definitely the best professor I've had in any OIM class so far. Would recommend.

I recommend you print out all powerpoints before lecture, it will save you so much time later on. The homework can be tricky(ish), but the exams are easy because you get a cheat-sheet and tests are non-cumulative. Many people don't, but if you pay attention in class then it will make your life so much easier. She is great help in office hours, too.

Simple class if you attend lecture & think about the powerpoint slides. You don't really need to take notes. Double-sided cheat sheet for all exams. 1 homework assignment per week with unlimited attempts. Most of the material is easy math, but if you struggle, she is willing to help. Never read the book, just used her ppt slides. Also, she's funny.

Overall a good professor. Her lectures are fairly easy to follow and the subject matter is interesting. The tests aren't too difficult but you will have to keep up with material to do really well. Reading is not necessary to do well. There is homework but generally one assignment per week at most.
Shes dope

Michelle is one of the best professors I have had in Isenberg so far. Going to class is important because it's her explanation of the concepts and how to understand performing the models that get you to learn the material. It's not enough to only copy formulas on your cheat sheet for exams. Homework can be tedious, but indicative of the exams.

Michelle is so much fun! For an 8AM she knows how to make class interesting by cracking jokes left and right. Her exams are a cakewalk and she always lets you bring a cheat sheet. As long as you write the formula she gives you at least half the points. Anytime you're confused her office hours are great! Super funny and always willing to help!

She ask to read 5 books the semester I was in, and we had quiz every week. But later on I  found the readings very useful and they lead you to some certification. She is very funny, and is very willing to help.
Worst class I have ever taken. Her module (1st of 3)was the easiest though. Very boring material and a ridiculous amount of things to know/remember for exams, like acronyms & years of random laws.

Loved her and this class! Great professor, she's very knowledgeable and always clear. Lots of information but slides/class captures/book are online. She will also respond to emails in less than 24 hrs! She's funny and makes class engaging and entertaining. One of my favorite professors at UMass for sure.

Michelle is a wonderful teacher. The hw posted online was actually helpful although sometimes tedious. The powerpoint slides were a great tool, and all the lectures are online so I can always review them before the exam. Best part about the exams you can bring a cheat sheet, so no reason not to get an A in this class. Like her style shes funny.

her HR module was the most straight forward but theres SO much stuff you have to memorize. know everything on the slides because she can ask about random laws and acts. try to get something in the high 70s, low 80s and the extra credit should get you to an A. also will have to read the textbook. not easy but if you can memorize, not horrible either

The HR portion of the class is all I've taken so far and it wasn't hard but this is hands down the most boring class that I've taken so far at school and that's saying a lot, especially coming from an accounting major. Make sure you bring your phone or something fun to entertain yourself.

Very straight forward and gives all information in her power points so no need to get the book for her section of the class at least. Study power points and you're good to go for the exam. She's nice and super quirky. Overall good professor!

Love Michelle!! shes a really great teacher and goes over things very well to make sure everyone understands.  great examples too. shes also very nice and cares alot about students!! her test was the best in the class and made the most sense

Dr. Burch is the best of the SOM. She is humble and the most approachable, I wish she taught more classes, She also seems more in touch than other profs. When ever I needed help, she was there. I also think she's hot! Her videos are interesting. The only bad thing is, she doesn't teach more classes. Seriously, awesome!
Dr. Burch really knows her stuff. She is my favorite teacher at UMass, without a doubt! She really cares and wants you to learn. I wish they all were like her.

Don't stress over the Critical Path method! It is so much easier once you step back from it. Professor Burch was the only professor who I thought was very clear with expectations regarding the exams and class material out of the 3 teaching. Definitely recommend going to class when she is teaching.

She was the best out of the three professors. She's the only one who cares about how each student does and is the only one who held a review session before the exam. She's nice and shows lots of videos during class. Definitely a great professor who really knows what she's talking about.

Burch was my favorite of the three. Probably because her section was the most straight forward and not completely opinionated like Marx's section. Is she as good as Alan Robinson? No. But she is a fairly good stand in all things considered.

Fairly obnoxious, and disorganized. On the module exam, know the Critical Path Method, MPS, and productivity, and read "Ideas are Free." Seems to have trouble keeping her thoughts/lessons organized. Most things are pretty straightforward. RFC assignments are easy exam points. Also - dresses like it's 1990... it's weird.
Shes not that bad.  Lectures can be kind of boring.  Her test isn't that hard.  Just read "Ideas Are Free" and know the critical path method.
I'm just trying to post a comment
reviews.rating_tags: Beware of pop quizzes--Test heavy--Online Savvy

reviews.comment: A very capable and engaging lecturer, challenges you to engage with material deeply. No exams, few HWs (deadlines are very flexible) + a few small quizzes + a final proj. Very accessible outside of class. You'll have a strong foundation in many things math-computing if you take 552 with him. The Math Dept is lucky to have Andreas, truly brilliant.
Very interesting / engaging lecturer and very good at explaining things. Always available to questions and willing to help.

551 is hard as its the first time you're solving problems numerically but Dr Buttenschoen is a gem of an instructor, and puts all of his efforts into helping you learn. Very knowledgable. He'll make sure you get your tuition's worth. Always, always accessible outside of class. Even when not 'office hours', he will happily spend hours helping you.

If you are a very theoretical math student, I highly encourage taking the course with Andreas. Personally though, I'm a hands-on and examples kind of learner and Andreas didn't give much room for either, so I left most classes feeling exhausted. This felt more like a pure math course than an applied math course. Go to lectures or you will struggle.

Admittedly I am not the biggest philosophy enjoyer. I want to give Moises credit because he clearly cares a lot about his students and is very passionate about philosophy. He does give decent feedback as well. But the assignments felt like busywork and the lectures were pretty dull. If you like philosophy a lot you may enjoy this class more.

Bruh I had no clue what was going. He canceled class multiple times with less than a day's notice and would come to class late multiple times. It's such an easy class though. On the syllabus it says there are 6 assignments throughout the semester with a final paper, we had 4 with no final paper. Can barely understand him but he cares a lot.

He's nice but he does not teach well. All assignments were pass/fail. He was often late to class or cancelled it abruptly. His lectures were unstructured and unengaging, and it felt like he often lost track of the topic at hand. It is an easy course, and he's always willing to discuss class material outside of class one-on-one.

Very nice person, but his teaching style is very convoluted. I have no idea what my grade is in the class because we have not gotten a single graded assignment back (this is the last week of classes). He was frequently late to lectures or cancelled class. Not a hard class, though. If you have questions, he is very enthusiastic to answer them.
this guy is so passive aggressive, makes a lot of bad grading decisions but does offer extra credit. would not recommend only took the class so I could live in kennedy

I had Professor Bustos my first semester. Although this is a lecture heavy course, so are most other college courses, so I found that this course prepared me for others. He is a great, caring guy along with very forgiving and willing to give extensions. Professor Bustos wants his students to succeed and found a way to make philosophy interesting.

Kind and knowledgeable, but not always completely understanding. We wrote around 5 pages during the whole semester, but then had to write about 10 pages for the final exam/paper. Very accessible outside of class. If you want to get an A, say something (vaguely coherent) in every class and complete every assignment. Attendance mostly mandatory.

Moises is a good guy outside of class, but his lectures are long and confusing. He'll take all class just to make his point. However on assignments he will offer you a lot of help and is easily accessible. He writes guides of all the lessons so if sometimes it's hard to pay attention, which it may be, then you can look to his guides to understand.
reviews.rating_tags: Lecture heavy--Graded by few things--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: I tried liking him and as a person he's a great guy as a professor, very inconsiderate. His assignments take extra time he makes you read extra articles and listen to podcasts and videos. He thinks hes just making us better writers but no one else burns me out like his class. I hate philosophy maybe because of this class idk
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--So many papers--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: He drinks 6 cups of coffee before class on top of having ADHD he constantly pases around the room. I don't know when he is covering important material in class. The information is easy to understand but he overcomplicates it. Heavy on participation. You will be teaching yourself and you don't know what is important to learn
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: I wasnt aware of what Philosophy was so make sure you know what it actually is before you join. As much as I hate philosophy, he gives very long extensions if you need them If you reach out to him he will give you a lot of grace and negotiate on the final if need be. He's a very caring teacher that just wants to push us. His guides are great.

Don't recommend this class. Tons of work that piles up and everything is confusing and makes no sense. He seems nice outside of the classroom and seems as though he cares about students mental health. Recommend taking any other rap possible.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--So many papers

reviews.comment:
DO NOT TAKE THIS CLASS!!!! DO NOT. Worst Kennedy RAP you can take. 

His lectures are hard to follow and you have to teach the content to yourself most of the time. He calls out people mid-class to say that they need to participate more and put more work into assignments. Going to that class or thinking about it puts me in a bad mood.

He is a great person outside of the classroom, but his teaching style is very hard to learn by. You most likely will be very confused by everything he says, but it's okay because it won't be just you- the entire class will be confused too. Few things are graded but classes are short.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Lecture heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: He expects you to do one writing assignment per week but sometimes forgets to post them leading to a lot of weekly assignments to pile up at the end when a final paper and exam is due. He also takes a very long time to grade stuff. Its one week before the final and I have gotten back one grade. Overall nice guy and def cares about what he teaches
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Lecture heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Small class, super interesting stuff. Bustos was an amazing lecturer, you could really tell he cared about what he was teaching. Just two longer papers (not more than 6 or so pages), and eight shorter responses. Super lenient with turning in work late. Chill guy, allowed me to be interested in the subject and not just treat it like busywork.

As far as you attend lectures, pay attention and take notes you will get a good grade. For the midterm and final papers he says he will grade them tough, but you will most likely get an A on the papers if he sees you putting in effort into the class such as attending lectures and participating. Beware that he handwrites notes and doesn't post them.
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Graded by few things--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: Never take a rap class with him it will ruin your life, i have to write a 10 page paper for my final and a 5 page paper is due two days before my final is due, i hate my life

Nikki has been my professor for three years now and I am extremely impressed by her abilities and knowledge. Her classes are an amazing break from traditional lectures, and I felt productive learning so many useful topics within agriculture. She is very caring and understanding, and really wants you to understand the material.
Material is boring but she does a good job at engaging in the class. Lots of presenting but not too bad. Stay on top of work and you'll be okay.

Nikki is my favorite professor! I learn the most in her classes because they are so experiential. She is so sweet and fun to be around! If you try to form a relationship with her she becomes such a mentor. Homework is easy if you're interested in the topic and there aren't any tests.

I would highly recommend this teacher to anyone interested in agriculture. Her knowledge, teaching style, and kindness make her an exceptional instructor, and I feel grateful to have had the opportunity to learn from her. I am confident that any student who takes her class will come away with a deeper understanding for small farms and agriculture.

(For Comm376:Sidewalks and Screens). One of the best professors in the communication department. You will get a lot out of the class if you pay attention. Short weekly responses is the only HW, and three reading checks that are easy if you listen. She helps you with the final research paper. I highly encourage taking any class with her you can.

I have taken a few classes with Burcu and have enjoyed her as a professor. There are weekly readings that you reflect on through a weekly slack memo, 3 readings checks that are easy, and a final research project. She cares a lot about the content she teaches and for her students. She is easily accessible via email and in person
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Amazing lectures --Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: There's a good amount of reading. She's enthusiastic and knowledgeable about the material and adapts the class to the summer format with brief video lectures and articles. She's a fair grader, but some of the quizzes are only a few questions, making it easy to tank your grade if you aren't careful.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Graded by few things

reviews.comment:
burcu is so slay. funny, personable, and wants to have real discussions. participating makes it so much more fun, and I was lucky to have a fun class of people.

graded on a few exams and the midterm and final. the exams were easy if you just did the study guide. shes great, would recommend!!
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Gives good feedback--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: The topic itself was so inspiring and relevant to our everyday lives, and she did an excellent job of bringing the complexity of the subject to the table and sturred our minds to conduct a more critical/in-depth analysis of stories around us. Reasonable with grading and coursework, and the assignments are always engaging. One of the best courses!

This was a great class we had to post weekly posts that she was super fair with grading. One final paper that she gives a lot of creative freedom for. She is so nice and understanding on of the best professors who truly cares.

She is so nice and truly wants to see her students do well. She is a very fair grader and the material was actually interesting. Very understanding and only a few papers and some attendance credit. I suggest participating as much as possible
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Graded by few things--Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: She cares about her students, is always available and willing to help, and is extremely intelligent and passionate about her studies. HIGHLY recommend taking her.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Accessible outside class--Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: Perfect way to run a course, keeps students engaged and essentially have all semester to work on your stuff. perfect
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Accessible outside class--Get ready to read

reviews.comment: This professor is a top-tier mensch. The material for Stats 315 is very difficult and intimidating, especially for people who are taking the course for the first time, but this professor really takes the time to make sure that students understand the material. He encourages students to ask questions during lecture and is fair towards each student.
Nicest guy ever, very thick accent but very smart and super easy grader. Finished the material easy and let us work on practice problems in pairs for three weeks.
Very informative and helpful, always makes sure everyone understands. Very nice guy. Very strong Chinese accent, though, makes it a little tricky to understand sometimes.

Bahn brings the passion when teaching in the classroom. He always ensures confusions on topics are answered and sometimes throws a joke or two during the lecture to bring life into the lectures. Has an accent but after a week it'll grow on you and will be able to understand him.
The professor is amazing and is very passionate. His style of teaching should be an example to the whole math department. His lecture slides are very detailed yet easy to understand.

Great guy. Really cares about his students and wanted us to do well. Arguably the best professor I've had in the math department through 2 years at umass. Also very responsive and easy to reach out to. Final was surprisingly easy compared to quizzes.

MATH 233 is a challenging course, but the professor made it manageable and rewarding. I especially appreciated the group quizzes, which were great preparation for the exams. He's also very helpful outside of class. I would gladly take another course with him!

Great Professor, highly recommended. Takes interest in teaching the material and also cares about his students. It is a pleasure taking a class with him. I would definitely love to take another class with him if given the opportunity.  Encourages participation within the class and ensures everyone learns everything properly.

(difeq) Clearly passionate for the material, enjoys teaching, very happy to answer dumb questions, or inference questions and stuff. His upbeat personality brings an engaging and fun vibe to the material, giving it more life.

The dudes goated. Lectures are clear as long as you listen, and he's extremely kind and wants you to succeed. Every Friday, there is a quiz in class, but it's a group quiz, and he often helps you with it. I prefer doing the group quiz as it's just questions from midterms and finals from years past, and I felt a lot more confident on exams bc of it.

Clearly passionate, Byeong-Ho is a new lecturer who has a lot of room for growth. However, he really cares about his students and was kind and helpful during office hours. I think my class would have been better if more students participated and asked questions. This is a very tough class though. Go to the SIs for sure!
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Test heavy--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Very passionate teacher! Although there was a lot of homework, it was often more difficult than the exams. He is very fair with grading, gives opportunities for extra credit, and he drops the lowest scores. He's a super nice guy, and he loves when people ask questions and participate in lectures.
reviews.rating_tags: Clear grading criteria--Lots of homework--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: This is a really hard class regardless of who teaches it. He's very caring and wants his students to succeed. The final exam is 30% of your grade. I genuinely have no idea how i passed this class. Attendance was not mandatory

Kind and super enthusiastic guy! Ask questions and GO TO OFFICE HOURS. He can be fast paced so getting 1 on 1 helps. SI + Peer tutoring helps a ton for this class. Quizzes every week (more difficult on purpose to help prepare you) but note submission will get you out of it.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Test heavy--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment:
The AI policy in this class is predatory. They fail any assignment "suspected" to be AI-generated, including work completed *in discussion* under their supervision.

This "guilty until proven innocent" attitude goes against everything an institution of higher education should stand for and calls into question Bunk's priorities (and ability to see).
Easiest gen ed at Umass. Very little work, but make sure to do whatever is assigned because that is your grade. No essays or papers and lectures aren't mandatory.
I really loved the class. Easiest gened.The concepts are really interesting, and Prof.Bunk is an amazing lecturer.
I took History and Video Games with Prof. Bunk (HIS290), and he was awesome. Kind, genuine, and  wants to hear and engage with your thoughts, no matter how half-baked.

One of the best/easiest gen eds to take, no exams, class is graded based off of weekly discussion assignments (that are pass/fail), perusall assignments (reading/annotating homework), 4 lecture quizzes, and 10+ weekly reading quizzes. Quizzes are due at the end of the semester and are open note. Great guy and learned a lot, lectures easy to follow.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: I would highly recommend taking this class as a Historical Studies Requirement (HS). Lectures were always recorded, and attendance was optional. The textbook is affordable and lots of the homework questions were straight out of the textbook. This class was an easy A, great teacher and great class!

A great easy history gened. Never went to class, followed it as a flexi class. There are a few components like quizzes, perusall and discussion. It is almost impossible to not get an A if you just put in the time. Discussion is a group project which is just pass/fail so basically you pass if you submit something. Learned a few interesting things.

Super easy class, and the material is interesting! Lecture Quizzes are important so don't forget to attend class or watch the online lecture (like I did). There are a lot of assignments, but they are all super simple.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Clear grading criteria--Caring

reviews.comment: Did not hold one single lecture throughout this entire pandemic semester. I essentially had to read the textbook and do weekly quizzes/assignments based on that reading. No guidance, however did allow extra time on assignments. Seems like a good guy , my big issue is that we had no class and it's like what am i paying for? to teach myself?
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Get ready to read--Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: Sweet guy who knows a lot about subject material, encourages in-class discussion. 3 books required for a series of papers you'll need to write but all other texts provided online for free. 5 papers, weekly discussion posts for online annotated texts, and participation make up final grade. Overall solid course and professor.

Hist110 is a team based learning class, so how it goes for you depends on who you get put with, and you don't get to pick. The readings were difficult, so if you're the only one who does it in your group, you'll be carrying the team on all the on class work. Bunk's a good dude and he just kinda facilitated, the grad students did all the grading.

The class seems like it will be fine, especially if you have a good group because this class is based exclusivley on group work. There are no lectures, quizzes, or tests all you do is in class work with your groups and a final group project. The TAs are the ones who grade your work and mine are ridiculously nit picky and do not easily hand out A's.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--GROUP PROJECTS

reviews.comment: The only things that are graded for this class are the exams. Participation in discussions matters a LOT, it counts for 30% of the final grade (more than any of the exams do), so make sure to do the readings. Definitely makes it easy to not show up to class though, I only went to three non-exam lectures in total.
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--TEST HEAVY--GRADED BY FEW THINGS

reviews.comment: The class is super easy(unless you get put in a terrible group). What is expected from the groups is very obvious and the grading for the reading notes and team reports are pretty lenient. Definitely put scavenger hunt, life experiments, and peer assessments for the highest % of your grade because they're super easy.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Clear grading criteria--GROUP PROJECTS

reviews.comment: Its a team-based learning class, so hopefully you get a good team because basically all of your assignments are with them. You get to pick your own grading scheme. Definitely put peer assignment, scavenger hunt, and life experiments as high percentages! Class is really easy you don't have to buy the books they're online.
Extremely easy for a gen ed. Would recommend for anyone who is looking for an easy A. Only thing that sucks is this is a team based learning class and some groups are better than others.
Uninspiring and painfully monotonous. The 1 - 2 combo of bland lecture with a sub- blah professor killed my spirit, I'll never get all those hours back.

This class was very interesting if you like history. You MUST go to discussion, if you miss more than 3 discussion sections you fail the entire class. You get assigned weekly reading with questions and that what you do in discussion. Theres 3 tests and thats it. You need to actually talk in discussion or your grade is bad. Seems bad, but good GenEd

Professor Bunk is a very knowledgeable and passionate professor, but can occasionally be confusing on what he is looking for with assignments. Also, this has nothing to do with Bunk, but the class was a "TBL- Team based learning" class, which is absolutely awful. If you are put with lazy classmates (or those who do not speak English) then good luck

The class structure is very straight forward. There is a short paper due every discussion that is based on the readings/ class notes. There are 2 primary source in-class essays based on class notes. For the tests he would give you 3 essay prompts a few classes before and then 1 of those prompts was the test so it was very easy to prepare for.

Good professor. No tests, just papers in this class. He sometimes takes too long to illustrate his point and becomes redundant at times. He is usually clear though. He is very wise and interesting to listen to. Many books to read in short spans of time, but you can get through lectures without reading them entirely.

Lecture slides are posted online they are only pictures and not helpful if you do not attend class.. The hardest part of this class was the discussion which is worth 40% of your grade overall. Every week there are assignments for discussion that are tedious and long, you have to do the readings as the assignments require citations.

I really felt the class was disorganized. He goes on these long ramblings for lectures, and then during the exams, you can basically get a decent grade just by remembering things from the reading he assigns! Hope you learn by hearing, too, because his power points don't have any real notes on them.

As a non-english speaker, this class was the most difficult class for me, especially the readings. Readings are long, and literally I spent huge amount of time before every class in order to finish online quizzes in the limited time. The quizzes are hard too. Some of them are based on the details of readings. So you have to read first.

Professor Bunk is a nice guy and his lectures are okay to listen to.  His class is so disorganized.  The readings are so long some weeks with hard, specific quizzes.  Discussion sections are pointless.  A hard 100-level gen-ed class.

The primary source assignment was way to large a percentage of the grade. The readings were rather long. The online quizzes were horrible, much too specific w/ time limits that made them irritating. The Final exam prompts also encompassed too much material. He takes this class too seriously for a 100 level. Say goodbye to Thursday nights.

Prof Bunk is a nice guy, and he keeps the class interesting enough. There are 500 word papers every week, and a large annotated bibliography at the end of the class but it isn't too bad. I liked the class well enough.

Seems like a nice enough guy, yet I do not recommend this class if it is in the Team Based Learning format. It is the first time he taught this class in this way, yet it was a disaster. I doubt it will be a TBL class in the future, but if it is be prepared for confusion.

Honestly one of the easiest classes I've ever taken.  I barely went to lecture and skimmed the readings/books but still got an A-.  He gives you the essay questions ahead of time, so if you do badly it's your own fault.

Bunk is a great guy, he tries to relate to his students so he references sex a lot in his lectures.  His lectures are powerpoints which he reads off of and gives us his input and the exams are essays.  Pretty easy but the necessary discussion is a bit a pain in the butt.  Used textbooks a lot but I never even bought them.  Highly recommended class.

Really nice guy. He gives you the questions to the exams before hand so there are no surprises. There's a lot of reading but its simple and you don't really have to do it. Textbooks are affordable. I strongly dislike history, but I would recommend this class.

Bunk is an egotistical jerk who assumes all his students (in a gen ed class) are majors and LOVE history.  Thinks you already know everything that happened in world history and that he just needs to go over the details. Way too "multicultural" of a class, basically ignores Europe and USA. Tough grader, hard essay exams and too much reading and work
Lots of work and reading for a general education class. I am a history major and I still dread coming to the class. I am so bored.

Hardest class I've taken so far. It's a Gen Ed, but Dr. Bunk caters towards majors.  So much reading, and very hard grades on all written assignments. His "cultural" history knowledge seems limited (e.g. misinformation about Beethoven). A nice guy, and a little funny, but material is dry and class is difficult. Take something else.

Now the class is a 4-credit class, and I feel like he's taking it too seriously. It's history 111 and they are a little too critical on the grades for the exams and primary source analysis. Make sure you go to your discussions, since there are assignments due in discussion every time. Lots of readings due from SPARK all the time.

He is easily one of my favorite teachers. I'm taking this class now and it's one of the couple that I don't dread. His class is really easy going but you have to go to discussion, if you miss more than a couple I think you fail. No textbooks but you read a few short books which aren't painful and his exams are essays that he gives you in advance.
Brian Bunk is an amazing professor. He always looks fresh and makes great history jokes. You will honestly love every second that Brian Bunk is teaching. He's a great guy. Take a class with him!!

Bunk isn't bad. He's entertaining enough and at least tries to be funny. He doesn't use textbooks, but rather stories and novels so the books are cheaper than most and the quizzes are mostly easy. The discussion sections are a necessary evil and missing more than 2 fails you. Two tests, both essay format, but overall a good intro class.

Brian Bunk is easily the best professor I've ever had, I've taken 5 courses with him, almost all just for fun. He loves what he teaches, and he is always happy to help students. He often makes somewhat awkward comments which get a good laugh from students, If you can take any of his courses you won't be disappointed!

He talks to his students as if they were children and don't know anything, but he knows what he is talking about.  His slides are easy to follow and so is he. His exams are slightly difficult but overall he's a great teacher

He is one of the best history teacher's I've ever had. He knows so much about WWII. Although the class mentions the battles, it's mainly the ideologies faced in the war. If you like WWII, I recommend taking this class.

He is a really good teacher. Your grade is based on 2 exams and weekly quizzes. The exams are essay format; he gives you 3 possible question before hand, and he then picks one. I recommend taking him. Knows a lot about the subject
No Comments

I really enjoyed this class because I'm interested in History.  Our class picked quizzes every week which were tough.  Reading was mandatory for the quizzes. Papers weren't too bad.  You can skim through the horribly boring books to do them.  Tests I really studied for, which are on the lectures and are short answer and an essay.

Lets students pick the grading system of the class, i.e. no finals, percentages that assignments count. A little slow with readings, assignments but a good teacher, easy grader. Cooler than he seems at first.
good in-class notes, go to every class and easily get an A

TA'ed for him...While he does, overall, make a very good effort, his presentation is a bit biased--in a materialistic way--and he makes it difficult to aid students, as he doesn't communicate policy or plans either timely enough or clearly enough.  Also, he should allow the students more assistance, and TAs, leeway, in test preparation.

Alright professor. lectures are really boring. as long as you get the notes, you don't even need to go. reading is pretty much optional as long as you can bs your way through a 1 page paper. doesnt actually grade anything himself, so your grade depends on the ta.

Lectures were interesting enough. I was able to connect a lot current events to his lectures. However, he relied on the TA too much. I would have rather had his feedback sometimes than his grad students.

Very good at what he does. Although once I asked for an assignment for the class and he sent me the wrong assignment, but he quickly sent me the right one before the due date. Good guy overall. History isn't boring to me so I liked the class. If you don't like history then try the retard history, you're not going to learn anything anyways.

possibly the WORST class possible! Bunk the borer. I feel asleep in his class everyday. The TA was worse than he was and a real harda$$ about grading the lame-O papers. Not worth your time or effort. UMass should be ashamed to offer such a class.

He does a good job of making a very boring class at least slightly interesting. The reading assignments are horribly boring, but as long as you go to lecture and sort of pay attention, the tests are easy. The 10 writing assignments were just busywork. But he changes his style every semester.
This guy is a class act all the way!  Bright, funny and a very good prof all the way around. Bop Bah!
Is a nice guy and always helpful, but expectations aren't always clear for assignments.  Class is a little dry, readings are VERY dry, doesn't always connect ideas.
Pretty Easy. Bunk is a rad dude. involves his students
Proff. Bunk is way cool. Awesome class and super interesting. Knows about his subject and involves the class. This was one of my favorite classes.
For a survey course, it's not too bad.  Bunk makes things relatively clear, and hits the high points of thousands of years of history.  A bit on the dry side, but not bad.
he seems to be pretty excited about what he teaches - always a plus, but doesn't always connect things.  class doesn't have alot of structure.
Prof. Kim is very unorganized and not helpful at all in the lab. He likes to take out his class list and call on random people during class too.

All I can say is that he's the worst professor I've ever come across. He takes his slides from Carnegie Mellon University, and I cant even follow what he's saying in class. It's clear he doesn't prepare for class. If you take a class with him, your best bet is to not go to class and instead use that time to learn on YouTube.

Byung is an engima. He seems like a great guy... but when it comes to teaching hes pretty subpar. I've taken 3 classes with me now and for the life of my I can't figure out what goes through his head. He does care about his students, but his grading is just bizarre and as others have mentioned, his research comes first, which leads to some isssues

Yes just as the guy below my said, he will curve. But he lied you can't learn something from him. I asked question and he didn't help at all, he just wanted to get rid of me. I got an A in this class but still, he is a horrible person. Don't enroll in his class if you want to learn something other than how to BS.

Happy to give majority of the class low Fs on quizzes and ruin their grades because he claims he doesn't have time to actually grade them by hand. He says "his research is his first priority, his students come second." Tries to leverage the bad grades to have students personally request administration to give him less work. Just a horrible person.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough Grader--TEST HEAVY--GRADED BY FEW THINGS

reviews.comment: Terrible lecture, All he did was just pulling equations from his ass and made awkward jokes. There were 3 quizzes, has an average of 20 ish out of 100 and it worth 10% of the total grade. NO PARTIAL CREDIT. Try your best to avoid his class if you don't want to get a D+ after all the hustle.
He doesn't care about his students. His stories are awful. Just generally a mean person.

Definitely knows the subject matter but struggles to explain it in a way that can be understood and retained to new learners of Assembly programming. My advice is to try your best, get a study group with your friends going and hope the curve at the end is enough to save you.

Well, Prof Kim is a really nice guy but he can't teach to save his life. He's the only option though so get someone's work that already took the class to try and teach yourself what is going on. Sometimes he would hand out quizzes on stuff he taught literally just minutes before even though no one understands the material.

Never have taken such a terrible professor in my life. He will not help. Went to office hours and he just wants you to memorize the materials. It is not the proper way to learn. Is extremely sexist to women as well. He is a total disappointment. I took the class for fun and he is making my life miserable.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough Grader--TEST HEAVY--GRADED BY FEW THINGS

reviews.comment: This teacher is a bully. If you answer a question in class that's not correct, he will make fun of you. On top of being incredible condescending his grading rubrik is brutal (no partial credit) and as someone else mentioned- quizzes worth 10%-20% of your grade (WITH ONE QUESTION!!). Pretty brutal professor, avoid if possible
reviews.rating_tags: Tough Grader--Skip class? You won't pass.--TEST HEAVY

reviews.comment: NO  midyears and finals. Sounds nice? Yeah no it isn't because his weekly quizzes are wroth everything. You do bad on one quiz and your grade will drop 10%. Some quizzes are worth 20%. HW is assigned but doesn't count for anything. So basically the quiz grades are everything. Oh and his teaching is terrible but is one of the few options so yeah.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough Grader--Skip class? You won't pass.--GRADED BY FEW THINGS

reviews.comment: Hard to understand him and the content. not a good teacher, would not recommend
reviews.rating_tags: Tough Grader--Get ready to read--Skip class? You won't pass.

reviews.comment: The single worst Professor you will ever have.  Cannot speak English, has no idea what is going on, he is unbelievably rude to students.  Grades unfairly and tests on material that was never even remotely touched upon. Did not learn a single thing.  He messed up final exams and everyone ended up getting a 'P' as a course grade.

Worst MIE professor at UMass. His exams are extremely hard and it's all from lectures and usually the things he mentions only once. Reading won't help your grade at all. He's out there to fail students. I wish I could give him all 0's.

Will do everything in power to never take a class with him again. Gives online assignments that don't work out the way he thinks (he is too lazy to grade it himself). Humorously unclear lecture notes. Often gives  unwarranted sarcastic responses to questions students ask. Shows no sympathy to students. He is smart, that's the only respect he'll get

Awful lecturer and his tests are based off of his lectures.  Belittles students for asking questions or answering questions wrong.  Intentionally takes points away from students. Impossible grader, the last average for my test was a 50.  He scales the test at the end but doesn't scale the tests.  1 midterm worth 30%, final worth 55%.  Ridiculous.
Unreasonable grading policies.  Avoid taking his classes if possible.

My least favorite Professor I've had at UMass. Does not prepare you for the test in class and is useless in getting information across in class. He does joke around sometimes though, so that is okay I guess.

In the 3 classes I've taken with him, he hasn't taught me a thing. I took 211 with Sergio Brena and got a very easy A. His lectures are pointless, but you'll lose points on I clicker if you don't go. He's so full of himself that he wouldn't let me take a class, that I needed to graduate on time, that overlapped with his for 10 minutes per week

After the first few lectures you won't want to go to class,  only incentive being in class exercises. Hard to understand during lecture, writes examples too small on board to read. Getting the textbook is a must as you will learn more from it than lecture. Exams not representative of homework, with hardest problems from lecture appearing on tests.

No partial credits given on exams When he teaches new chapters on the book, he gives all the formulas you need (which are all there on textbook) and tell you to remember them, then he demos sample problems the next day, the same problem in different format the next day, until new material.  Text book is a lot more helpful than lectures
Hardly explained material. Didn't help. didn't tell us what he wanted for reports. Mostly busy work. I know the class would be useful if taught by someone else

313 - spent time talking about birds, Samsung, and his family. Getting wrecked by 313 because he couldn't teach.  375 - spent time talking about things not in the book but in his 302 lab that half of us don't take. Rubs in our faces that he owns a 4k from Samsung cuz Korea.
Byung would just go off rants in class about things that have nothing to do with the class. He intentionally tries to bring your grade down.

Homework is worth 0% and doesn't reflect test questions, there are no TAs, and the lectures tend to be rambling and disjointed. The only hope of learning the material is to memorize the textbook, which is unreasonable. The class shouldn't be difficult, but the exams consist of random, sometimes insignificant details. We did not have a good time.

He is a nice guy, and has a lot to offer in terms of real world experience.  He is incredibly smart and also jokes in class which makes the class better.  He gives out exam hints and cares about the students

Good: Clearly wanted students to learn, 2 easy exams, nice guy, easy to understand. Bad: Not clear at all in terms of what he wants for assignments, sometimes stood in front of board as he was writing, expects students to have all of strengths memorized and available off the top of their heads the first day of class.

He was a little hard to understand, but the grading was fair. Beware if he has his TA's try to teach matlab on their own again...they don't really know what theyre doing, and they usually don't know how to teach. Overall? Not so bad.

The most useless professor I've ever had. Didn't show up to more than 60% of the classes, and didn't respond to any emails. Inconsistent grader and makes the TAs do all of the work. Thank god he scales.
If I didn't know my statics before I took this class, I wouldn't now. (helpful)^-1
When I had him he did not teach me much but that might have been his first semester teaching that class.
Never take a class with him

Spring 25 was Bruce's last semester teaching!! He was my favorite lecturer in all four years at UMass. This class was great, I hope they can replace him with someone even half as passionate.

Will miss Prof Byrers 💔
Byers is a nice guy who really cares about the material. He's really into ornithology, so a lot of the examples used are about birds. Take good notes because the online exams are open note.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Clear grading criteria--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: You have to do the readings for the weekly reading assignments. There are also weekly review questions. There are two midterms and a cumulative final, all open note and online. His exams are based on lectures mostly. His lectures are mostly slides with pictures. He is a decent professor.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Lots of homework--Respected

reviews.comment: Bruce is definitely the best professor to take this course with. Online exams and open note. Readings are super heavy but never on exams, only weekly homework and assignments can be done without reading. Super genuine guy and I enjoyed this class.
no attendance, homework and exams online. so easy and bruce is a nice guy. the weekly homework assignments are online but kinda suck sometimes and are long. definitely take evolution with bruce!!!

Bruce was extremely engaging during class time and was very straight forward about what was on the homework assignments. The review questions were all very easily answered if you took notes on what he says during class. The slides are all pretty much only pictures which allowed me to actually learn more as I took better notes.

To do well in this class you must go to lectures, or at least watch the video recordings (no attendance). Weekly problem sets rely on the lectures. Lectures can drag at times, but you can tell he is super passionate about the subject! Exams are online and there are weekly reading quizzes too. The class is a lot of work, but it is manageable.

Very passionate about the subject. Lectures were engaging; he encouraged the class to discuss and ask questions. The weekly reading assignments were lengthy and the weekly review questions took a while to answer thoroughly. It was often unclear what topics would be covered on exams, and exam questions referenced very specific details from lectures.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Amazing lectures --Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: Easy to understand lectures, a reading quiz and review questions weekly, but nothing too difficult at all. Exams are online and not too hard. He's a super nice and funny guy and super passionate about the subject!

Super chill and interesting guy. His lectures are actually something that I would listen to. His exams are all online this semester along with quizzes and review questions every week. Definitely lots of homework and reading to do, but once you get the hand of his schedule it's do able. So far I enjoy this class!
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Lots of homework--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: Amazing lectures, very detail oriented and I really think I learned a lot. A great teacher and the class is manageable. Personally I didn't really like the way the class was set up-- throughout the entire course I never really was sure of what was detrimental to know and what wasn't (made preparing for tests difficult). Great guy though!
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Inspirational--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: Bruce is a great professor with a sense of humor, and his lectures are interesting but make sure to go to class because his exams are very specific and tailored to what he says in class. He is super nice and willing to help out if you want to chat about grades or evolution. Super interesting topics in evo!
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Skip class? You won't pass.--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: Bruce was a good enough guy and teacher, but between the lab and the lecture this class was way more work than my other three 500 level courses combined, ton of textbook reading and homework in addition to lectures and an intensive lab component w/ out of class lectures and a massive research project makes class take at least 9-10 hours a week.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Get ready to read--Skip class? You won't pass.

reviews.comment: Byers uses a lot of real world experimental data to demonstrate topics, which I found helpful. This classes requires a lot of reading, and there are weekly reading quizzes with very specific questions. Exams only have material covered in class though. He has a subtle sense of humor and is clear in his explanations and direction in each lecture.

Prof Byers is awesome! He is clearly very interested in the course material and provides lots of interesting anecdotes and facts. The majority of the assignments are weekly review questions that are easily answered if lectures are attended, but difficult otherwise are questions are tailored specifically to lecture material not found anywhere else.

Very sweet man, but class can be tedious. There are quizzes based on the reading each week, but I never bought the books and did fine. There are also review questions each week and only 2 exams and a final. Lectures were interesting because he always tied in a real world example or study of what we were discussing.

The sweetest man to walk the face of the Earth. The class is just very very tedious. Lots and lots of reading with pretty difficult reading quizzes every week. A lot of homework and exams are pretty difficult if you don't study really hard. AMAZING lectures, makes evolution so interesting
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Get ready to read--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: Bruce is a decent lecturer, but this class has an insane amount of work and you get almost no feedback on it unless you go to his office hours. You will have one 30 question reading quiz every week (and the readings are massive), plus a set of review questions that don't help you at all. None of this relates to the exams which are heavily weighted.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Get ready to read--Test heavy

reviews.comment: Made me fall in love with evolution. If you do the readings (or skim them as you are taking the online quizzes) and take notes on the lectures, you will have everything you need to pass. His exams cover every topic discussed in class - so pay attention! But Bruce makes it easy to do so: He is enthusiastic and uses accessible examples for concepts.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Graded by few things--Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: Grade based off two exams, a final, and one quiz a week. Exam questions are on obscure topics lightly covered in class with the expectation of knowing more than we were taught. Lectures are extremely boring, the weekly reading quizzes are pointless and are on readings never discussed in class or on exams. Interesting material but awful professor.

This class can end up being a fair amount of work between the lab and lecture. Exams are tough! However I really enjoyed the class! Bruce is a great prof and there's no way he won't make you fall in love with birds. If you take this class be prepared for lots of readings and studying. It may not be an easy course but I recommend this class for sure

This class and professor was really hard because a majority of the questions on quizzes and exams were about obscure and irrelevant things that most people skip over in the reading, and it's information that's not easily findable. Lectures are interesting, grading methods are really unfair.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough Grader--Get ready to read--GRADED BY FEW THINGS

reviews.comment: Bruce really shows a passion for this class and he makes you want to learn! Have to read assigned chapters and hand in notes for grades. All his tests are short answer but if you fill out the study guide and just study that you'll do fine! The lab portion run by Aaron is packed with work but he does a great job explaining everything & is lenient.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Skip class? You won't pass.--GRADED BY FEW THINGS

reviews.comment: His exams were very hard at first and the class was curved, not interesting at all but genuinely cared about the material. A lot of memorization so get ready to make flashcards.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--LOTS OF HOMEWORK--LECTURE HEAVY

reviews.comment: Weekly reading quizzes. If you don't read you will fail. If you don't attend lecture/ take notes, you will fail. Exams are exactly what are said in class! Lectures are dry and hard to follow. Avoid at all costs, unless you have a passion/previous knowledge of evolutionary biology.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--GRADED BY FEW THINGS--LECTURE HEAVY

reviews.comment: Powerpoint slides are awful, comprised of mostly photographs with no caption, making it difficult to review them. Poor organization of the class /chapters. Tests mostly on things he says in class and less off the textbook, take a lot of notes because the slides are not helpful. Material is quite easy, but class was a semester long headache.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Skip class? You won't pass.--LECTURE HEAVY

reviews.comment: Good professor and listens to his students' needs. Course is alright if you read the textbook and attend the lectures.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough Grader--Get ready to read--Skip class? You won't pass.

reviews.comment: Took Bruce's BioTAP seminar for my RAP. He's really sweet and gives you 2 absences per semester. The only homework was a review of one of the speaker's lectures at the end (you get to pick which one) and the rest of your grade was participation. Everyone did fine.

Finds a way to make a law class fun. Good lectures that really make sense of all the legal terms. His MBA and law degree are pretty helpful as the class is "Business Law." I would recommend coming to class because it will make the class a lot easier (Also pop quizzes).  He also gives you 5 points extra credit on the tests making them a breeze.

I really enjoyed this class! Professor Byers is very helpful and sweet. However, his lecture slides are mostly pictures, so I would not recommend taking this class if you aren't going to show up, as the slides are the only way to get the information. The reading quizzes are a bit tough, but the tests are relatively straightforward. Would recommend!
