Not a horrible class but it's tough in the sense that the exams are not all trick questions like  Houlihan's were but there are at least 6-7 questions on each exam that make you question whether or not he clarified that in class, or he might have said it a single time in lecture . Or the way it's explained in class confuses you when put in q format

This class was amazing! Bruce makes you love evolutionary biology and actually learn it as well. The tests are EXACTLY like the weekly review questions. The weekly readings are super long and the quizzes are very specific but you learn how to manage your time. YOU HAVE TO GO TO LECTURES. Every word he says is usually on the exams so take good notes

Weekly quizzes helped with the understanding of the chapters.  Tests were focused on weekly lecture materialexamples of experiments presented in class.  SimU text assignments not explained clearlytough grader.  Would not take this professor again.

There's a weekly reading quiz, and you can't skim. You have to really read it and understand to pass. There's only 3 exams and the questions are very specific. Honestly if you go to class and take notes on what he says you'll do fine. It's not hard if you put in the effort. This is the easiest class I've had this semester.

Personally I found this class a normal Bio class. He expects you to come to class, and if you actually do come to class and listen its an easy A. Yes you have to put in the work and do the readings etc, but its not a hard class. Just don't skip lectures because his powerpoint don't contain any information. Just come to class and you'll be fine!

I've been struggling real bad in this class!! Weekly reading quizzes (40+ pages to read) questions are super specific so better read the readings more than once. oh yeah, and they are timed so you can't skim through while taking the quiz, impossible. Tests are hard!! I wish I never took this class . tip- write down everything he says in lecture

Probably one of the hardest classes I am currently taking. There are weekly quizzes where you absolutely need to read the chapters that are assigned. Questions on the quizzes and tests are incredibly specific. Lectures are extremely boring and he rambles on for the entire class about the topic. There are two simulation assignments which are a pain.

Weekly reading quizzes. It is essential to have the two mandatory textbooks. Have to actually read the chapters before you take the quiz, can't just skim the section to answer the questions. Have to go to class because his slides are mainly pictures that he discusses. The problem is that the class can be pretty boring and hard to sit through.
In small classes, Bruce is an awesome professor. There arent any exams, just reading notes and computer simulation experiments for hw. Great class, easy enough for an upper bio class.
He is a good professor, can be very complicated at times and does ramble on and on but is such a sweet and nice little guy.

If you take this class you will learn lots of fascinating things about birds and the natural world, from fossil history to modern conservation issues. However, it is not an easy class. There is weekly work for lab, reading notes for class, and the exams are detail-oriented. If you put the work in you'll get a lot out of the class, if not, you won't

LOVE Bruce! He sounds just like Joel Osteen which makes the class interesting. His class is wicked easy but you do have to attend lectures all the time to get notes because theyre all pictures. Write down everything he says and you should be fine for the exams. They're not that bad. He made me love evolutionary biology even more!

He's a sweet little man and a pretty good lecturer. However, you have to write down every little thing he says because his slides are all pictures and his exams are impossible. I know so much about evolution from this class but got all 75's on the exams. Don't take this class if you value your GPA and you're a normal test-taker.

It's his first year teaching 280. Textbook reading every week and reading quiz. Quizzes are kind of specific but you get the hang of them and you do them at home with the book. he scales tests. he encouraes questions in class and ive emailed him before with questions and he always replies promptly. overall fair class but you need to get the book
Good teacher but makes exams way harder than they should be. Expects very detailed responses to weekly readings and very, very specific answers on exams

This class is a ton of work. Very detailed chapter notes due each class on which it is impossible to get a check plus unless you just copy the whole book out. Also, although I studied my ass off for the exams and knew all the material, he managed to find ways to take off points. Did I mention lab is also a ton of work? Only take if you love birds!
Super Hard Class. Super picky on exams. Lab demands a lot of work or it's impossible...Lots of reading and work.

Bruce is a great professor, clears up confusion really well.  He does have a sarcastic undertone at times but he's trying to get people to think along the right path.  Lab sucks, quize material is broad and every quiz is partially cumulative.  Class is well worth it, you'll learn more about birds from Bruce than you'd ever imagine.

Class is SO hard. Have to keep up on the readings. He assigns a new chapter for every class and gives you quizzes on the reading that are extremelyyyy detail oriented. Lab is ridiculous and there's a quiz about ever class. This class is incredibly boring unless you like birds. Don't take it unless you're ready to do a LOT of work!!
Bruce is a difficult person to get along with at times.
This class was challenging, but very interesting. Bruce made it understandable all the way.

Great class. Bruce does a good job teaching a huge topic. Lab is great, but does have alot of work. Must read the book and articles assigned because you're quized on it every week. its a high level class and feels like it. But its my favorite class this semester
Class was hard, but Bruce makes it pretty interesting.  Anyone interested in evolution should take this class for background.
He knows his stuff and is very willing to help, but the teaching style is a bit dry.

I feel like Bruce is the daddy of the Bio Dept. He's really interested in his students, and if you do well you can tell he is proud of you. It's definatly worth while to get to know him, he's and interesting  guy and onr of my favorite proffesors
Bruce gave very straightforward lectures at a reasonable pace. He made evolution quite interesting! His multiple-choice tests could be tricky at times, however!

BEWARE HIS TESTS! Loved his teaching, notes were online, but his multiple choice tests were pure hell. LEARN HOW TO TAKE HIS TESTS. That's as invaluable a tip I can offer for this prof. Other than that, he's a cool bird-watchin' prof.
Sorry to break it to you but Octopuses IS a word since it is Greek, not latin. Octopi...is not. Common mistake, but he was right, not you. Too bad you stopped listening.

Make no misake: Bio 528 is a HARD class.  We had group papers (using just primary research publications) due every 2 weeks. On the other hand, he really makes you think critically about science, and it's been a long time since I improved that much.
great professor
No Comments
Pretty easy guy, goes nice and slow, but we cover a good amount of information.  Tests aren't too bad, but they can sometimes be tricky.

Easy enough part of the class. He goes slow and we spent like his entire half of the semester defining natural selection.  Mediocre teacher...but somehow there is an inherently evil nature about him (and I'm not joking!!)
He's a great guy and is always willing to help.  Bruce is the man.
Evolution could have been so much more interesting but he made it very dull. Tests were sometimes tricky but not too bad.
He's the man. Straight up. Best Bio teacher on campus.
i hated his section of the class...he was a good professor though.  his exams were really tough, and some of the answers contradicted things he said in lecture.
great guy.  always helpful.
Really cool teacher. Loves birds!
unique teaching approach, great thought provoking discussions that affected the way i look at the world (i'm not trying to be cheesy, it's true!).. lots of work but worth it!
Great instructor. Uses slides in class instead of the board. Very clear. He's a little nervous at times but it doesn't affect his performance much.
great professor. makes lecture interesting and fun. always helpful.
It was a lot of work, but interesting work... and no exams. A great discussion class!
No Comments
No Comments

Class is graded on 10 hw and 3 exams. The hw is graded on correctness, though the syllabus mentioned it would be effort-based. Exams are another story with questions that weren't explained thoroughly in lecture. Not every student can attend discussion/office hours sections where the prof explain things much better than in lecture. Prof is nice.
Amazing professor.

The reviewer below this one is just a bad student. Kearney is a great professor. He's very knowledgable on the material and can even explain concepts not covered in the course when asked. The exams are tough, but he lets you get back points. In discussion sessions, he covers grading distributions for exams and also solves homework problems for you.

He acts nice in class but that's just a facade for his harsh grading and unsavory attitude when it comes to trying to get help over email. For the exams, he doesn't provide a rubric or explain where you got points taken off so you will have no idea why you got a bad grade if you did. He also refuses to elaborate when asked about what you did wrong.

Kearney is my favorite professor in the BME department. You can tell he genuinely cares about his students and gives ample help. The class is not easy by any means but he made me extremely interested in the content and is makes class fun. Weekly homework assignments and 3 exams, office hours help a TON.

Dr. Kearney is a kind, inspiring, and encouraging professor.  I could not give a higher recommendation.  You'll have to work hard for an A, but he is approachable and wants to see his students succeed.  Definitely my favorite prof in the department.

Dr. Kearney is well spoken, BME 330 was the most interesting BME class this semester. Content is cool, homework is tough, exams are on the moderate-hard side so definitely study. Definitely need to go to lectures because some content is quite difficult. 
Office hours are essential for doing well on the homework.
Oh, and uses kahoot.
Dr. Kearney is one of the best professors in the BME department. You can tell he really cares about teaching and helping his students succeed, but he will make you work for it.

Really passionate about his subject and a good teacher. Will make sure to clarify any points quickly if asked. Can be a difficult grader, but if you email him he will make sure to explain it to you and give you a few more points. Really nice guy and cares a lot abt his students. Exams are insane tho.

She's very understanding and kind. You can tell she actually really does care about her students' success and has a strong passion for teaching. If you finish early, she lets you go and doesn't make you stay to do busywork. There is a textbook for the class, but I've never opened it and have a 100, so you probably don't need it.
She truly cares about students' success. She explains everything very simply. Homeworks related to the class material and was relatively easy. The exams were also very easy.

I thought the class was pretty easy besides some concepts toward the end. Showed up to like a quarter of my lectures, and still did fine on tests. Just do the homework and the study guides! Have to pay for the homework software though, which is annoying.
Very rude and just disrespectful in emails

reviews.comment: Very unfair with grading
Don't take
Doesnt allow calculators like every other math class ever, teaches way too fast, uses weird methods of teaching and weird formulas.
extremely kind and chill teacher

Class was enjoyable. I like the way she delivers her lectures and the ability to get sheets to follow along with her during office hours. Homework expectations were realistic. Tests were easy and multiple-choice. I appreciated her showing up to exams and being enthusiastic no matter where she was. I would definitely take another class with her.
Good professor, but easy class to fall asleep in.

SHE IS AMAZING. Caitlin is an amazing professor and her class isn't very difficult. She explains everything so well and honestly is just an amazing professor. She makes me love math or at least like it lol.

Without a doubt one of my favorite professors at umass. She's very caring, and explains material clearly. As this was a class I had struggled with in high school, she did an excellent job and I accredit her to my doing so well. Highly recommend!

Caitlin is such a sweetheart, she really cares about her students and puts in a lot of effort to make sure they succeed. She goes over material thoroughly and encourages people to ask questions. She does lots of review before exams, and her office hours can be very helpful. Highly recommend.
She has great resources to get you prepared for the exams

She is super kind and grades pretty fairly on the exams, and she teaches the content in depth and very digestibly. She writes out all her notes in class and posts the pdf's ahead of time of the notes and writes them on there. Her thought process is clear and she is always willing to answer questions.

This professor was amazing. She was always available for office hours, gave extra help when it was needed, went over exams in office hours if you wanted to know where you went wrong, and her lectures were clear and easy to understand. She really makes the class worth your time.
reviews.rating_tags: Clear grading criteria--Gives good feedback--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Professor Worth was a great teacher. Although the class size was big she always made sure everyone understood and was great at answering questions. From what I've heard Professor Worth was by far the best teacher for 131. Her lectures were very clear and to the point. She always made sure that we knew what would be on the test and how to solve it.

Breaks down everything. A good teacher though the pacing of the class can be annoying at times. I feel like homework and exams were more aligned than classwork and the exams which caught me off guard for the first exam but if you just practice then should be fine.
She explains most material pretty well in lectures and wants students to succeed. Homework is much harder than exam material.
she makes at least 3 common math mistakes per lecture and has no control over the room
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: She grades very disrespectfully, she acts like she still in high school, Very immature and does not know how to teach. She ends up confusing me more than anything and half the time takes a detour. Please leave.

Great instructor! Easy to understand her teaching of integrals and derivatives. She normally goes over some material twice without anyone asking just because she feels that it may be a bit complicated. Definitely recommend!

This lady is really nice, and she is a super fair , as long as you try and go to class do your homework,she'll give you the benefit of the doubt, but she is no pushover. She is really easy to understand as well. I highly suggest taking a class with her, shes a great teacher.

I didn't even have him as a professor, and I still went to his lectures because he really is *that good*. Super accessible outside of class and clearly cares about student success. Super enthusiastic and easy to follow, and really good about clearing up points of confusion. Don't take MATH 331 with anyone else but Garrett.

Took over the summer. Very clear criteria listed in the syllabus. It's easy to pick yourself back up after falling behind, but you should still stay on track. Please don't cheat, just pay attention so you can learn the material normally. Trust me, your experience will be much smoother that way. Effort is required.
reviews.rating_tags: Clear grading criteria--Lots of homework--Test heavy

reviews.comment: Super caring and accessible outside of class. Took the time to get to know everyone's names. This class wasn't super challenging, but he explained concepts very clearly. Simply the GOAT.
truthfully the goat

Took asynchronously. Great prerecorded lectures, as well as TA and prof office hours. Written homework and practice exams reflect exams perfectly, no surprises in this class. Concepts can be tricky to grasp, but there is a lot of good info provided in textbooks and lectures. My only complaint is how long it took for written homework to be graded.

Garret is one of the best professors I've had. Calc 3 is a really fast paced and difficult class but Garret explained it well. He had many office hours and was available outside of class. He took time to get to know students and answer questions clearly and in detail.

Garrett makes complicated material straightforward and takes care to get to know his students. He made calc 3 approachable and broke the content down so it was easy to follow. I really enjoyed his class and got a lot out of it. Would recommend as I believe he is one of the best math professors I have had.
Easily one of the best professors I have had, his lectures are great and his supplementary material is even better. Literally gold standard of professors

Great class and well explained along with well made videos of course material if you need skip a lecture. Easily reachable outside of class and has great pacing (unless you took linear cuz last few lectures require know determinants, eigen values, and eigen vectors)

Took this class over winter break. Lectures were prerecorded but they were really helpful. To be honest, I found this class kind of difficult if your goal is to understand all the course content, but still definitely doable with the materials provided. I really liked how many graphs and ways to visualize equations were provided in the lectures.
I didn't even have him but I thought he was chill, especially during office hours. Great professor!

His lectures were clear and easy to follow, better than most UMass math professors. He really cared about his students and wanted us to succeed. I wish he did more example problems in class, but he was willing to help on the hws in office hours. Just be careful with the due dates, hws are due at the end of the sem, so it's easy to forget.
reviews.rating_tags: Amazing lectures --Clear grading criteria--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Professor Cahill is one of the best math teachers you'll find. His lectures are extremely detailed and yet easy to follow. He's very lenient on deadlines and his exams are exactly like the course material and practice exams, no surprises. Diff eqs is definitely one of the easiest upper level math courses, mostly just plugging into formulas.

Nothing that hasn't been said elsewhere, Cahill is awesome, and his diff eqs class is (as far as math classes go) extremely doable. Just a nice guy, and the homeworks/exams aren't too bad at all. The WileyPLUS quizzes get a little annoying though

Garrett is a very kind professor and teaches at a pace where anyone can understand. In addition, you can learn remotely if lecture times are not convenient since he has videos of all topics available through canvas.

Garett is the best math lecturer I have had, bar none. He's extremely charismatic in a field where lecturers are often dry, and his class is structured in a way where you are just overall prepared well for the exams, which were not too hard. He is also very understanding, allowing you to submit many assignments late for full credit if you ask.
Professor Cahill was amazing, easily the best math professor I've had at UMass (coming from a Math Major)! Take his class if you can!

Garrett is seriously one of the best professors I've ever had at this school. He loves math and teaches in a way that just made things click. Uploads lectures on every topic so if you miss class/don't feel like going, you still have a way to learn without falling behind.
Such a nice guy. Very easy class. Very pedagogically sound lectures. Good in practice and theory.

Garrett is a great lecturer and takes the time to make sure everyone understands. Homework is pretty easy with lenient deadlines, and exams are totally reasonable if you practice (they're pretty similar year-to-year). All his lecturers are pre-recorded, and attendance is optional, so you can learn online if you want.
The reviews don't lie. I truly believe he could make even the most advanced of courses feel easy. Wish I could take every math course with him.
Love this man, and everything about him. He made differential equations, a daunting topic, look easy and made the class fun.

Best Instructor I've had at UMass yet. Got me to visualise graphs although I always hated them. Actually cares about how the students do in class even if they don't attend lectures. Leaves resources on online platforms for students and tries to keep the course simple. Loose deadlines.
reviews.rating_tags: Amazing lectures --Gives good feedback--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Cahill is the GOAT. He is just an extremely solid professor who knows how to teach the material very well. If you miss classes there are online videos that he has, however I would not rely on them since he is much better in his in person classes. He is extremely caring and answers all questions and is very helpful during office hours.

Professor Cahill made me love math again. It was extremely productive to come to class and learn from his recaps, examples, and explanations. The pacing he uses is spot on. The number of exams is great. I loved coming to a class where the professor knew me. You can't come by those very often at UMass.
reviews.rating_tags: Amazing lectures --Clear grading criteria--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Calc II was hard in general but professor Cahill took the time to actually help me and get through the class. Best professor I have ever had UMass.

Took Diff eq online with Professor. Cahill and it was an amazing class. Surprisingly active for an online class, by far the most active I have ever been involved in. Exams were extremely similar to the practice exams, very fair grader as well. Written homework is difficult, but manageable. Best math experience here at UMass, Amazing prof !

Best math prof at UMass, the only one who actually knows how to teach. Knows how to cut out all the unnecessary junk and clearly and succinctly deliver the most important, foundational information. Doesn't give confusing, intricate examples. Because of this, has time to deliver lectures slowly so you can actually understand the material. Nice man.
reviews.rating_tags: Amazing lectures --Clear grading criteria--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: I really liked this professor, he is very smart and takes time to ensure all students have a deep understanding of the topic being taught. Also very flexible and understanding, and will take time to work with you. Not many professors like him left.

Garret is awesome! Differential equations is certainly a hard course, but garret provides great lectures for the material, and gives all students access to virtual lectures from covid-times for exam reviews. Exams are not easy, but not of Calc III difficulty either, and they are only 60% of the grade, meaning that homework (40%) can boost you a bit

I hate math with a burning passion, but Professor Cahill was always willing to give extra help and go the extra mile. Wicked nice guy in and out of class, and I would definitely take another class with him.
Garrett is lovely and wants to see you succeed. And you will succeed, because the tests are wicked easy! Great guy :)
I love him.

Professor Cahill's lectures are clear and concise and never spent too much time delving into topics that you don't need to worry about. He's also very caring and easy to reach if you're struggling. The homework assignments can be tricky but you can find lots of resources online to help. The exams are extremely fair.

Great professor caring, understanding, and accessible outside of class. Does a great job conveying the material and ensuring everybody understands it. All coursework was online on Moodle or the textbook website including the final exam.

Garret is a great professor but has to teach and grade using materials provided by the math department that aren't that helpful. Overall though he explains things very well and answers questions in and out of lectures. There are multiple mini quizzes weekly and 5 quizzes throughout the semester. All of the work is online and the quizzes are timed.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Test heavy--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Probably one of the better, if not the best, maths instructors/profs I've ever met. He's pretty accessible, and he gives very useful feedback and explanations too. His content in class matches the homework and the quizzes, so as long as you follow the lectures, do ur hw, and go over review questions, it shouldn't be too difficult to score.

I don't have a history of having solid maths teachers, but he's legit the best maths profs/instructors I've ever met.  No cap. Cares about his students. Very accessible outside of class through the discussion board and his office hours. The stuff he talks about is very aligned with his homework/quizzes. Easy to follow.
He's a good teacher and is pretty lenient about test if you ask him.

Such a great professor. He is funny and easy to access outside of class. Always gives us resources to better understand the material. He teaches everything well and is very easy to follow. You do have to buy Wileyplus which was like $70 I believe. Quizzes/homework twice a week manageable.

very sweet professor that is easy to follow. if you are confused about something, he will go over the problem for you. he and the TAs are very accessible and the TAs will hold review sessions. tests and quizzes are online and are open note. overall, great class and great professor.

Garrett leads very concise, understandable lectures. Although he is fast paced, he explains the fairly basic calculus concepts very clearly. Math 127 requires a pretty good understanding of algebraic skills, and you will do fine if you either attend his lectures or watch the online ones that he posts. Take advantage of the TA review sessions!

Great Professor who is exceptionally kind and flexible, not to mention a great person too. He is very good at dissecting difficult concepts and presenting them in digestible chunks. Highly recommend him.

This class gets pretty difficult quickly but Garrett was awesome. The written homework gets pretty terrible by the end, but if you had a question you could always look through the textbook, his 2020 lectures on Moodle, or just ask him the next day to figure it out.

Would give a 6/5 if I could. He's great at teaching, not to mention he's a great guy: super kind and caring. His lectures are so clear and engaging; I felt like I didn't need to do any textbook reading because the lectures made so much sense. He's also super willing to clear up points of confusion. Best professor I've had.
Great math professor. Probably the best in the department since Pat Dragon left. He's very reasonable and kind, and his lectures are clear and make sense.
just take Math 331 with him. nothing else needs to be said just DO IT! he is SO amazing.

From my experience, the course was the most difficult at the beginning. Garrett did such a great job teaching. Very helpful with answering students questions. Also, if you ever miss class, detailed explanations for each unit are also available on the Moodle page! I strongly recommend taking M331 with Garrett. You wont regret it!

Professor Cahill was a very solid professor. The class for a good portion of the semester isn't too difficult, but it does ramp up a little. His lectures are mainly spent deriving and then at the end you apply it to problems. He is a very smart man and is excellent at answering questions. There is quite a bit of homework, but I still recommend him.
Excellent professor, willing to help. Easy class.

Took math 331 as a summer class. The lectures were very good and the homework assignments were fair. This might only apply to a summer course but the program used for the online assignments was very bad, a lot of issues and marked correct problems as wrong. Tests were fair and what was covered in class.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Clear grading criteria--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: He was alright, the lectures were solid at the beginning, but for the last 2 chapters they weren't very helpful. He cut out a bit of the overly complicated math explanations with proofs, which was nice. Lot of WileyPlus homework, but flexible due dates. I would take this prof again

Garret Cahill, Who's he? There was no face-to-face interaction with him at all. Videos and online hw were provided by the book. No zoom lecture. Deadlines were extremely loose which was nice as we could do things at our own pace, but dangerous as it can pile up if you put things off. If you don't understand things you have to figure it out.

Very good professor in the online structure, khan-academy esque online lectures which were well formatted and accessible. Very well structured classes given the circumstances and professor Garrett is a great guy! Couldn't recommend enough.

Regret that I wasn't able to take this class with him in person but he really did everything he could to make the most of it for us online this semester and I think he did a great job. Homework was easy to keep up with and he was always looking to help us out in Zoom lectures. Even the instructional videos were concise and effective.

He's fantastic! Even online, he's caring and understanding, posts lecture vids and goes over content in class. Def a class I really wish was in person so I could get to know him better. I've heard he's the best 331 prof.

Best professor for mathematics I have ever had. He is a real gem and cares about the students. Very flexible about the deadlines and handled this course really well during the pandemic. Do not take M331 with anyone else other than him. Coursework is really easy if you pay attention to the lectures and self study!

Really great teacher who gives really clear instruction and is always open to feedback. He had to teach right through the pandemic and handled it really well. I'd say you can probably get through the class on his posted notes, but with little outside study, his classes were enough for me. Highly recommend his class if you want to pass diffy q's
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Accessible outside class--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: I had Garret for diff eq, great professor. His lectures are engaging and he cares a lot about students. The tests are heavily weighted, but pretty easy. He handled the pandemic compassionately, he was generous with extensions. I got a C+ due to external factors surrounding the pandemic that prevented me from giving the course enough attention.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Accessible outside class--Test heavy

reviews.comment: I mean its calc and its hard but hes a really good teacher so if you just show up to class he explains everything very well and you will understand it. The exams r not too bad its just he weekly homework that sucks but everyone in calc has it so just make a friend whos smart so they can send u answers.

Math127 in general can be difficult, but Garrett was a good prof, was clear in explaining things, and made calculus slightly less painful. Lots of homework, be sure to start it ahead of time. Class is in a big lecture hall, not really necessary to go to class.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Skip class? You won't pass.--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: Garrett Cahill is the best math teacher I've ever had, hands down. After years of boring calculus professors, Garrett made me love math again in this course on Ordinary Differential Equations. If you don't like math or think you are bad at it, take one of his courses and you'll change your mind.

Professor Cahill is a great professor! Differential equations are fun to learn, and this class was quite easy. Professor Cahill definitely does a good job explaining concepts and answering questions, and he really cares about his students.

One of the best math professors I've had. He explains the material in a very logical and easy to understand manner. Prepares you well for the exams via homeworks and takehome quizes. He posts two versions of notes online, is leniant with deadlines. Most surprising is that he cares for his students, and despite large class knows them by name.
Definitely wants to help the students learn, cares about your grade and your understanding of the concepts. He's flexible and will always go out of his way to help.
A real human being A real professor 10/10
He is always willing to help you understand the material outside of class. He is very kind and understanding. Take his class if you can

I did not enjoy him at all. His teaching style was confusing, and he was borderline rude to me when I asked if I could make up an exam I told him I would miss due to a family vacation. I considered dropping the class because of this. I do not suggest any HCC student take his class.
Absolutely wonderful! One of the best professors at Umass hands down. He has since moved and I envy the lucky students that will call him professor.

An awesome professor/graduate student. He goes over the material at a good pace and makes sure that everyone understands. He doesn't skip steps in examples. He knows how to look around if anyone has a question. He's real nice and approachable. One of the best.
Garrett is a thorough and fair teacher. He explains things clearly and is one of the best I have had at Umass.

Cedric is one of the best teachers I've ever had. The class is incredibly engaging, focusing very heavily on the effects AI has on the workforce. He is very transparent with how he grades things, and the TA's were pretty generous. The only critique I have is there is an insane amount of reading, but I only did about the first half and was fine.
Cedric is really passionate about what he teaches which makes his class really engaging. He is also really down to earth and very funny, super easy, chill grader, I would take another class with him!

One of the best professors I've had. Just go to class and you'll do fine. Very engaging class and allows for open discussion. creates an open environment and members all of his students' names by the first day of class. who you sit with you will become friends with and that's just the nature of the class

I had him Spring 2023 and he was the best professor I've had so far. Incredibly smart, funny, and able to break down theory so even a child could understand it. Group discussions were always interesting as he was the type of professor that made everyone want to engage. I can't recommend him strongly enough.
Cannan is really caring and enthusiastic!!At first she seems intimidating but she really wants her students to do better
Queen!!!!!
She is very smart, explained the material so well!
She was super helpful and cleared up any confusions I had. She genuinely cared about us and even met me outside of her office hours
I am really surprised by some of these comments, my experience was quite different. The class was very difficult and without her help I would have failed. She was very helpful and fair.

No discussions or class interaction, prof sent a total of 2 emails the entire semester: 1 welcoming you to the class and 2 telling you to prepare for the midterm. No lectures or anything explained, she just gives you the book and a powerpoint and good luck to ya. Other 2 rates here are spot on, this class is like having a ghost professor.

Having this professor, is just like not having a professor. Doesn't respond to emails, and many quizzes are dropped because the class does so poorly. Avoid this instructor unless you like learning everything on your own without support.

Class may seem daunting at first but it is extremely easy. Ceren is a great prof and the exams are a piece of cake. quizzes tend to get hard at times but she goes over similar problems in class. nearly impossible to not get an A.

Ceren is a kind and highly competent professor who wants you to learn. We covered 400+ pages (~10min./page) of kinda conceptual material, but that's not so unreasonable for an honors course. If you actually do the readings as Ceren suggests, you'll do just fine. Grading is fair if not lenient; plus, regular 203 seemed a lot more disorganized . . .

Dont take if you dont have to. Intro to econ is already hard enough the honors makes it worse. All she does is lecture and has thicker accent so is hard to understand. She does help alot in office hours but prepare to feel belittled as she giggles/snickers at your confusion. Test have quiz questions on it. She is a good person, but bad teacher.

Don't be fooled by the first unit, it gets much more complicated after that and she does not do a good job connecting or explaining topics. Class can be very boring and it is easy to get lost. Nice woman, but not a good teacher.

Her lectures can get a little boring sometimes but she is a very attentive professor and easy grader if you show passion for the class. She grades generously and gives a curve if the class average is lower than expected.
She is a very understanding teacher and likes to engage the class! The problem sets can be long but she is pretty lenient with the grading, so if you're in the ball park she gives you credit.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Group projects--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: Ceren honestly does not deserve such a low rating. She teaches courses that are very math based, which can be hard for students that struggle with math, but she's a generous grader and is definitely willing to work with you if you go to her office hours. While sometimes her lectures are boring, she's a kind professor that cares for her students.

The worst lecturer. over complicates, inaccessible. TA's seem like they are learning the material with the students. Laughed at questions I asked. Takes 2.5 hrs to get through one video. Be prepared to read the textbook, watch the lectures and still feel lost. the quizzes help with comprehension but you don't want to do bad on too many.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: This professor shows very little care for her students. Not responsive to emails, does not put much effort to make lectures interesting, and is overall a horrible communicator. It's almost the end of the semester and she has not graded a single problem set. I only needed to take this class for an honors gened, but I would not recommend.

I don't know what it is with her, but her lectures are just incomprehensible. She has an extremely monotone voice and goes through slides like a robot. There's no clear explanation of how to do problems or how we would answer questions, or even understand graphs. I've learned everything myself, do not take anything with this professor.
The teacher simply sucks. She has a monotone voice and has a bunch of 'errs' when speaking. Very boring.
Do not take this class unless you want to spend your time teaching yourself the material.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Skip class? You won't pass.

reviews.comment: She is a very bad lecturer. She is very boring to listen to, and drones on for an hour about the subject. She also has a very thick accent which makes it difficult to understand her, and she does not make the class interesting.

Lectures are dry and the quality of the audio is poor, making them hard to understand. TAs and Soylu are not responsive to emails. Material itself is not that difficult but remote learning seems to have made this class much more difficult than it needs to be.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Skip class? You won't pass.--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: she seems to think that because her lectures are asynchronous, she can make them over an hour long when the class itself is 50 minutes. she gives way too much material to be able to understand it fully and her problem sets are unreasonably hard. doesn't care about her students and never answers emails ever. avoid her and this class all together
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Lecture heavy--Tough grader

reviews.comment: Problem sets and exams were relatively easy if you put in some effort and pay attention. Plenty of opportunities for points through revisions and extra cred. She's caring and sweet but not the clearest lecturer. Her mumbling and monotone make lectures boring despite very interesting material, so don't expect to be inspired. Overall not bad though.

Game theory was graded by 4 problem sets, 1 midterm and 1 final so there's not much room for error. You must work but it's not hard to get an A. Go to office hours b/c she can help with HW problems. Exams are easier than HW. She allows a cheat sheet for the exams and provides lots of extra credit. I was lucky that grades were scaled at the end.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--ACCESSIBLE OUTSIDE CLASS--GRADED BY FEW THINGS

reviews.comment: Game theory was honestly one of the most enjoyable subjects I've taken, and she does a fantastic job of explaining the material. She'll even work through problems in office hours if you need help. The problem sets can be hard but she is very reasonable with grading.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Respected--Skip class? You won't pass.

reviews.comment: Soylu is a good professor, though her problem sets are very  tricky. As long as you do the work you'll get an A.
great professor, just be aware of pop quizzes on assigned readings

reviews.comment: Great class, nice lady, interesting topics and fun to talk to.  Makes you become a better writer and all you have to do is show up!

good teacher-is very approachable and nice. She gives a decent amount of work but it's probably the average amount for any college writing class. Not much reading-do the writings and you'll be fine.
No Comments

I hated missing class for two reasons. 1. If you miss a lecture, you'll fall behind and 2. She is an incredible professor. Her lectures are fast but so interesting/helpful/engaging. She is a fair grader and you know exactly what to expect on tests. Go to class and pay attention closely (which is fun) and you'll get an A. Grading for papers is clear

Feldman did not respond to emails, skipped a couple classes and our exams, and moved too quickly in lectures. I take notes on a laptop and even then it was hard to keep up. If more than 2 questions are asked in class we're already running late. Towards the end I skipped more than half the lectures and still got an A on the final.
Long lectures, really interesting stuff. No exams, the entire grade is based on a research paper on a topic of your choosing. Lots of readings

Professor Feldman was an amazing lecturer. She explained things from the reading very well. Her tests were super easy as she let us use cheat sheets for them. Would recommend this class to anyone who wants an easy good grade.

Feldman gives the most amazing lectures ever but she moves very quickly. No quizzes - just two fairly large papers, a midterm, and a final. Readings are long and heavy. Expect one breeze of a homework assignment per week. Friday discussions are an absolute joke.
shes ight, the class is pretty easy, you have to write 7 analytical reflections which are three pages but pretty easy. Ive never done the hw
Loves when you participate it class. A lot of papers but nothing is too hard.
Makes you do a lot of drafts and revising.

Cecilia Weiss is a spectacular lecturer. She manages to spark up dull information and make it not as tedious to learn. She has a passion for Classics and so much outside experience as an archaeologist. Fantastic young prof.
Awful Gen-ed. Got a B on all four quizzes that make up 40% of grade because they are only 10 questions and quite tricky. Now, I will most likely get a B in the class. GPA killer.

Her powerpoint slides have almost no information on them and they arent put up until two weeks before the quiz. You have to go to class and really listen to what she says to make sure you have good study notes. There are 4 quizes that add up to 40% of the grade, and 2 VERY easy writing assignments. The quizes are usually easy to fake your way thru

Super nice and helpful. Tries to make the class interesting. She is understanding and tries to make the class easier. A lot of work just because of how the class is set up, but you do learn a lot. If your gunna take 240, definitely take it with her! (i think y'all spelled her name wrong)
Very friendly, open, and helpful. Tries really hard to make the class interesting, sometimes disorganized
useless and dumb. watch a movie in portuguese and you'll learn more than her class. did I mention useless and stupid??

Professor Wilinsky is an excellent lecturer! The slides and Echo360 recordings are posted in Canvas, and attendance is taken through TopHat. She's very lenient with deadlines, you get 4 late passes and 4 absences, plus your 2 lowest grades are dropped. She is also willing to point you to more resources if you are interested in the subject!

Just attend class for tophat credit, homework was lab and multiple choice questions that are easy to complete, test were online and open book, final exam was online and open book as well. There were about 5 written assignments/discussion posts to complete. Complete SONA points early to get them out of the way. Total of 7 extra credit points.

Psych391MA (child maltreatment) is one of the best classes I've taken. Professor Wilinsky is amazing and is an expert on these topics. Heavy topics but Professor Wilinsky does a great job of keeping the class interesting and engaging. One discussion and one quiz weekly, which can feel like a lot but I have learned more in this class than any other!

Professor had engaging lectures which got the class to take interest. She always supports students and will be there to answer any questions. Overall Professor. Wilinsky is a great professor that has a teaching style that you will like.

Good teacher, I liked her lectures as she was engaged with the slide.
If you did every assignment but SONA, you would pass with a B.
Some extra credit was given.
ONLINE TEST (FINAL ONLINE).
good amount of work given each week (3-4 assignments), not too hard.
Attendance is through Top Hat questions, which can be done anywhere.
recorded lectures.

this is the worst class ever mandatory attendance and you have to do these research studies in person where they make you do some dumb study that is a complete waste of time. I highly advise against this class and would recommend you do something better than this.

Very kind professor, it was clear she knew what she was doing. Homework was sometimes annoying but it was always due on Sundays so you had all week to do it. Exams are super easy and open note so they are easy A's. I'd definitely recommend!

The content is very interesting, Prof Wilinsky is passionate about the material, and questions are encouraged in class. There are readings and quizzes or discussion posts due every week but they are not hard. Overall a great course, it is a bit challenging but I think that is a good thing and that the professor is accommodating to struggles.

She was great! I loved going to lectures, and she always kept me engaged in the topic as a non-psych major student. Took this class as a gen-ed requirement and would do it again. The exams are usually open notes and take-home. Just make sure you do the readings because they help tremendously with assignments and exams.

Really dumb class for a gen-ed, first attendance is mandatory, you have to spend hours of your time doing these research studies, and homework catches up to you. Every week I dread doing these assignments and this class is more work than upper-level 300 CS/Math classes. Literally take anything other than this class.
10/10 my queen love her to the moon and back

One of the best profs I've had. She is incredibly nice and genuinely wants you to succeed and become more invested in psych. Easy exams that are through connect, but homework assignments can catch up to you if you get a few wrong each time so beware. Lots of extra credit and mandatory SONA, which is interesting. Overall AMAZING
Easy A class with no exams. She's very kind and you can tell she's very passionate about what she teaches! Attendance is mandatory with top hat, but besides that you'll be fine.

Easy A class with exams being open note and online. She's very kind and you can tell she's very passionate about what she teaches! Attendance is mandatory with top hat, but besides that you'll be fine.

Professor Wilinsky is probably one of the best in the department. Very organized and clear grading criteria, gives detailed lectures, and a reasonable workload with take home exams. While attendance is mandatory, the lectures are definitely worth it and encourages participation and questions in class. Take a class with her if you can!

She is an ok professor, but you get points off if you miss a class. I would not recommend this class if you get bored easily. The class feels longer than it is. If you miss an assignment, she lets you make it up, but if you miss a few, even if it is for medical reasons, then you won't be able to, which is rude. She is very sweet and kind, but idk.

I took Psych 100 so read this review with that in mind. Exams were take-home open book, note, and slide. All lectures were recorded and the final was a take-home as well.

This is an easy course with a solid professor. Not the best of the best, but still very good and worthy of a 5/5

She is actually the sweetest woman ever and she is so passionate about what she teaches. There were weekly assignments, which were not too difficult. All the exams were online and open note as well. Just come to class as tophat attendance is taken, but one of my favorite classes ever!

attendance is so annoying. you only get two missed and she will wait to launch the tophat until the END of class. it's an easy class in general, exams are online, and homework is easy but it's just annoying that we need to physically be present because everything could be asynchronous.

Dr. Wilinsky is so nice. I disagree with some of the reviews, in my section she really engaged by asking a lot of questions to the class and made sure everyone understood the concepts. The material itself was very easy to understand and covers/reviews the fundamentals. Coupled with online exams, I think any non-psych major could get an A with her.

Charlotte is very caring, and she gives many opportunities for extra credit. I took the psych 100 course, and it was really easy. All the exams were open-book, and she gives us a study guide a week in advance to prepare the tests. Her slides are very detailed and she explains the material well.

She was cool, a little uptight. Her grad TAs are nice, but some of the UTA's were not as great. I noticed the UTAs were harsher graders and would give me 4/5 on discussions multiple times even though there was no clear rubric on what constitutes what is needed in discussion posts. Overall, good class and does not require too much effort.
Love her teaching style. Really easy class to take and makes you feel comfortable. Exams and tests are open material. Do recommend taking one of her classes whether it be for a major or gen ed.

Professor Wilinsky is one of the better professors I have had. This course is good to take as an elective because of a manageable workload and open note exams. Attendance is mandatory and taken through Top Hat questions during each lecture. Overall, this is a great elective to take and would recommend.

This is a mandatory course for all psych majors and is held in a large auditorium. She could not for the life of her make people want to go to class. Her mistake was making attendance optional. I am not sure if this was her first time running 494PI, but it sure did seem like it. While very easy, be ready to figure things out on your own.
great professor, very kind and open minded when people share opinions in class, puts together clear, engaging, and facisinating slideshows for lectures.

attendance mandatory this semester, but pretty easy class and she's nice - engaging / asks questions, exams are open book and super easy, weekly quizzes or discussions based on the textbook or readings & easy to get As on. extra credit too

Very caring professor and answers everyone's questions in class. Her class is relatively easy and her lectures are not required but I went to a good amount of them to take notes. Her lectures can be a bit boring but they're useful for exams. I did not get the textbook and do not recommend getting it.

I love taking psych 355 with her and I am also taking 391 with her as well as my small psych seminar. I would 100% recommend taking a class with Professor Wilinsky. Her lectures are interesting, there is homework but it is not unreasonable and does not feel like busy work.
Lays out expectations well and gives plenty of forewarning about assignments.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: such a good class and its very engaging. very open about asking questions during class and she will answer your question! the exams (including final exam) are online and open note. make sure to do your homework and this class will be super easy. totally recommend
There 3 exams that are open note and weekly quizzes. Also, she offers extra credit. Overall she is a great professor!

there are a few assignments, weekly quizzes, and 3 exams in this class (all of which are open note)! attendance is optional, but she offers extra credit questions on top hat during her lectures which helps boost your grade if you do show up. she is good about answering questions in class but sometimes spends too much time on it. overall she's good!
reviews.rating_tags: EXTRA CREDIT--Lecture heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Can seem a little rude sometimes but I don't think he is trying to be. One of the best professors I've had and I took him for both 151 and 152. Pretty easy class if you pay attention, the Iclickers are very very helpful for studying

Bio152 content is NOT difficult but many of his questions (including those on tests and quizzes) have grammatical errors and confusing wording. His slideshows are terribly organized, making studying for this class with them basically impossible. If you ask a question he gives you a purposefully vague, snarky answer.Also he is painfully unfunny. RUN
Mandatory lectures, 1 quiz+1 test every week (multiple attempts, forgiving late assignment policy, easy points), hard exams (rewatch lectures, redo quizzes), not a lot of extra credit opportunities
Super passive aggressive to students. He was as rude as possible when answering questions during lectures. The material itself was not difficult but the lectures were painfully boring

Very passive aggressive, especially when asking a question. Must buy an iclicker $50+, lectures were boring and there was a lot of complications with the iclicker program. The one good thing is that he drops the lower exam and makes the final count for that lower test grade if the final is higher, final becomes 33% of grade rather than 18%.

He explains topics decently well and uses iClicker during lecture (this is ''graded'' for attendance) to see if he needs to clarify further if there's confusion. Multiple resources are offered for people struggling with homework/material. Questions are rather straightforward, but he'll remove them from the exam if too many people struggle.

He explains topics decently well and uses iClicker to see if he needs to clarify further if there's confusion. Multiple resources are offered for people struggling with homework/material. Questions are rather straightforward, but he'll remove them from the exam if too many people struggle.

I had Caleb for both Bio 151 and 152 and for both semesters, I absolutely dreaded going to his lectures. This doesn't seem like it would be a problem, but he is PLAGUED by spelling errors and other mistakes, for every single problem set and even for the final, he has to send out a correction. He is a relatively nice grader, at least.

Caleb is a great professor! He's kind and cares about his students success! There is a lot of weekly homework but it is manageable, and there are extra credit help sessions weekly, which are super helpful! The TAs were kind and cleared up any confusion I had. Lectures can be very content-heavy, so I recommend going to SI sessions.

Caleb is overall a good lecturer who cares about his students and likes interacting with them, though some topics weren't explained as well as others. Just make sure you pay attention in lectures and participate for clicker questions.

Caleb is generally a good lecturer, but sometimes he can move a little fast. Sometimes his explanations for certain topics were a bit confusing, but still manageable. It didn't help that 151 contains most of the parts of bio I don't really find interesting, but Caleb still did a good job of teaching it.

Lectures are important, but they can make you sleepy at times. The class is easy if you're good at studying and attend lectures regularly. I found the discussions to be very helpful, and TAs were very nice.

You have to pay attention in class to understand the material. He does go over things kind of fast, but if you go over it a bit after class and know how to do the lecture quizzes + iclicker questions, you should be okay. Funny guy he makes class enjoyable and he cares about his students.

He is a diva. He kinda has an attitude and it can be a little scary going up to him to ask for help after class becasue of his RBF but he is really sweet and wants every student to do well. His study guides are from past exams but every semester he goes over different material so sometimes they don't help.

Has IClicker attendance in lectures lots of questions easy to miss even if your sitting in class. Slides are pretty bare. Explains concepts well but talks very fast. Assigns heavy readings almost every week with a quiz after, and a post lecture quiz. Is clear about what will be on exams and has good practice tests. Overall good guy and funny tho.

Lecture and homework quizzes were pretty straightforward and so were in-class clicker questions, but as a non-bio major I have to agree with a lot of these responses that his exams were pretty cryptic and hard to do well on. I used all of his provided resources, studied for weeks, and still didn't do well. I wouldn't take w/ him if a non-bio major.
I really enjoyed his lectures and he explained everything well. A lot of hw but it doesn't take too long and def helps with exams.

His rating should be much higher than it is. He makes everything very clear from the start and gives many opportunities to prepare for the exams( problem set sessions, quiz sessions, etc..). He utilizes the Iclickers a lot within lecture, but he does allow the clicker app version. His tests were mostly easy even when I didn't really study for them
reviews.rating_tags: Amazing lectures --Clear grading criteria--Gives good feedback

reviews.comment: The HW is hard but the are TA hours for extra credit where they help u.

He has a bit of an attitude and rbf. He cares about student success, but it can be scary going up to him to ask a question. The exams are similar to questions he asks in class, but his study guides are exams from previous semesters. Some semesters, he covers things he doesn't in others, so the study guides are not the most helpful.

I really liked his lecture style, super iClicker heavy but it helps you understand the material well, similar style to Laura Francis. Hated the quiz/exam questions, super cryptic for no reason. Best way to study is spam the iclicker, quiz, and p set questions.

I actually liked his teaching style a lot. Tons of iclicker questions which are used on prob sets and exams. Can be kind of sassy but it's kinda funny sometimes. However the grading of prob sets/reflections differs so much between TAs it is super inconsistent. I will have almost the same answers as a friend and our grades will differ a ton.

Honestly, Caleb was one of the best professors I have had. His assignments were very straightforward and based very much on the lectures. His quizzes reused many of the iClicker and problem set questions. He didn't throw anything he didn't teach on the exams. He is also a good lecturer.
Overcomplicates simple questions...not that bad but not the best.

I really like the way Caleb teaches and he explains things very well in lecture, but his exams are ridiculous considering that this is a majority freshman Intro to Biology class. Unless you took AP Bio in high school and have some idea of the different systems you'll learn about, it is very difficult to do well on tests from my experience.

A lot of iclicker activity, but they're honestly very helpful and he walks us through every answer to make sure we understand. He loves to make jokes and lectures go by pretty fast. Weekly homework that is weighed pretty heavily BUT you can go to SI/UTA sessions and they will help you!
good teacher, weekly homework but you're supposed to use notes. tests are literally just homework and in class clicker questions so if those are easy you're good.
he answers questions in class which is helpful and uses a lot of visuals and pictures. definitely attend SI sessions and review sessions which he gives extra credit for some of them.

Caleb is funny and explain things very well in lecture. He does go fast and into extreme detail so I kind of struggled with that because science isn't my best subject, but he offers so many resources for help outside of class. I really liked his style of teaching and would take Bio again if I had him as a prof.

Calebs lectures are very heavy in material and he does like 30 iclickers per class. His exams are part open response which was graded harshly and then multiple choice was fine. Review the iclickers from class and make flashcards with definitions, memerization will not help you in this class it's all conceptual.

Caleb is a great professor and just an awesome person. His tests are very reasonable and gives you ample resources to be prepared. I'd highly recommend if you want to take this class take it with him!

caleb is nice but he is very condescending. he expects you to know everything before even having a chance to take the class. there were 4 problem sets and 2 tests and a final. he had weekly lecture quizzes that were hard but the reading quizzes were biweekly and easier than the lecture ones.
The exams are meant to trick you so be careful, read all the wording and don't just skim through and go quick you will mess up. The true false is meant to be deceptive and trick you!!!!

Would definitely suggest going to lectures when you can. Sometimes he forgets to remove material from lecture quizzes that he did not cover in class. Overall, not too bad. I felt like his exams were easier than a lot of the homework, quizzes, and problem sets. Not very accommodating when it comes to extensions, when it comes to being sick.

He had 4 problem set packets, 2 mid term exams and one final. All exams consist of open response and multiple choice, post-lecture quizzes and homework each week. He does extra credit but its useless and hard to get it since you have to go to multiple help sessions for 1 point. He was alright, I wish he gave straight answers when you asked for help

The WORST professor I have had at UMass. He is rude, annoying, and doesn't care about his students. I have always been a great student, but he makes it SO difficult to do well in his class. This is my worst grade of college. No extra credit (except attending like 7 review sessions gets you 1 point out of like 700 - this does nothing.) HE SUCKS.

prof. Rounds was very difficult to understand at some points in time, but other times the lectures were very easy to understand, it's like a 50/50 shot of getting him on a good day vs. a bad day for the lectures

Funny prof. Had him for 151, but for 152 it was a complete turnaround. Honestly depends on your taste, but in this class the grading is more specific and non-molecular bio is harder to understand through his iClicker questions when comparent to cellular bio in 151. Very accessible on discord and gives lots of EC opps.
just ugh. disliked his teaching style and tests. would've picked 2.5 instead of 2 for overall rate.

passive aggressive, but funny when it's not directed towards you. weekly hw quiz (3 tries), lecture quiz (2 tries), and short reflection helped boost my grade. exams are similar to in-class iclicker. one page free response and a little less than 50 mcq. good, but not outstanding. learned more than other classmates with diff profs though

He is so passive aggressive for NO REASON. The way he structures his lectures is just a lot of iclicker questions so if you think that's your learning style then you'll be fine, but I found it really difficult to learn that way. Exams have a short answer and multiple choice section.

I was kind of nervous before I had Caleb, just because I am not a biology person at all.. But Caleb made this class really enjoyable for me, and actually made me interested in the topic. Definitely go to every lecture you can, take good notes, and use practice exams to study. Overall, he makes the class super engaging! Really enjoyed his teaching

As some who despises biology, I found his lectures to be extremely helpful, informative, and interesting. He was very helpful when it came to my disability. His exams were very fair, and didn't throw any curve balls. TAs were good and they seemed to like and know what they were doing. Study and you can pass the class no problem. Overall, fun guy!
A passive aggressive man that teaches like dirt. Run.

Unique sense of humor with some passive aggression, but overall a caring nice guy. Attend his office hours and the TA session and you will do just fine. He is an understanding guy and knows what he is talking about.
reviews.rating_tags: Clear grading criteria--Lecture heavy--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Super passive aggressive. Even when asked simple questions in class or during an exam, he acts like it was a slap in the face. Super smart guy, however he is a terrible professor. Exams are tough even if you know everything, since the questions are written horribly and will be confusing. TAs and SI will carry you in this class.
I can't help but sit to myself and wonder the things I could have done if I had a better professor.
Condescending when students ask questions. Not understanding of extenuating circumstances. Strongly recommend taking with another professor if you can.

Really great lecturer. Class is super engaging and interactive. Lots of iclicker questions (which make a great study tool!). Attendance is 1% but if you go consistently you should get a good grade. SI sessions and practice exams are really helpful too.

Good teacher and helpful in and outside of class. Be ready for a lot of iClicker questions, they're used for participation and a lot of the questions end up showing up on exams. The weekly quizzes are not too hard but do the reading beforehand since a lot of the content comes from that

this class has extensive material, especially considering it's a class most freshman bio majors would take but he makes it a little simpler for you and his exams are a lot like his lecture slides and homework quizzes. has several extra credit opportunities as well, and make the most of the discussions for this class
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--EXTRA CREDIT--Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: Prof. Rounds is an amazing professor! He loves whatever he teaches and his exams are very similar to the lecture slides and homework quizzes. If you go over them, you're all set for his exams. He has several extra credit opportunities too.
The positive reviews are from his TAs, this guy teaches concrete. His tests have nothing to do with the actual class material. By all means take another professor

He's just annoying. I wish someone from the Biology Department would sit in and watch one of the lectures. Snarky towards students and extremely useless outside of class. He doesn't give direct answers to questions, as his intent is clearly to just confuse students more. I dreaded this class because of his personality.

Rounds is an amazing lecturer. He explains things in a way that you will 100% and he is engaging and you can tell that he is passionate about what he teaches. Exams are similar to practice exams, fair grading system. If you put in the work and learn the material properly, you will recieve an A.
His lecturing can be convoluted and confusing and his slides were not fantastic. He was kind of funny but I found myself hating every lecture.

He's incredibly knowledgable and covers a lot of material quickly. He's very receptive to questions and fosters engagement during his lectures. The questions he asks on quizzes, homeworks, and exams are lengthy and often require a lot of critical thinking about what was taught. The SI sessions and exam prep/review were vital.

Very straightforward and fair course set up. Very snarky/sassy prof. Great lectures, just pay attention and you'll be fine. Also a bunch of boosts for your grade at the end. Bottom line, if you didnt do well you probably just didnt pay attention (or show up). If you get confused, go to sessions, do practice, REWATCH LECTURES!

Professor Rounds is nice, but the class was pretty difficult for me. I found myself not understanding anything during the lectures, and did pretty bad on the lecture quizzes. Maybe it's just because I struggle with biology in general, but the questions were very confusing. The SI sessions helped a ton, but I needed to teach myself the material.
worst professor for biology someone get him replaced

Bio is just hard rounds is not a bad teacher. The concepts he is teacher are so boring it's so hard to pay attention, but nothing too bad. If you go to class and actually force yourself to pay attention you'll do good other than that good luck. It's way easier than 151 but just harder to listen to but rounds has a lot of options to boost grade.

exams questions appear tough but in reality are basic definitions, Definitely no trick, just have to understand the material. He doesn't give straight forward answers in discord instead asks questions to let you get to the answer bc that's how learning works.  his class was pretty easy if you just listened. Those complaining didn't go or listen

Caleb held great lectures that covered the material well enough that I rarely needed to review it outside of class. IClicker questions were great too because they were very similar to what was on quizzes and homework. Not sure what these other reviews are saying, but practice exams were similar to real ones, and lectures were enough preparation.

Caleb is not a great lecturer.The class is very heavy and complicated course material and he does not do a good job at explaining things very well. This is one of those "learn yourself" classes which can be very overwhelming at times. His tests are mostly trick questions and hard to prepare for. Its hard to stay engaged in his lectures.
Worst professor in the department
all his questions practice and on exams feel like trick questions. learned nothing from class si sessions were the only thing that helped. don't take him unless you absolutely have to

I'd only recommend taking his class if you took AP Bio or have no better option. He's a nice guy but he's almost too smart and doesn't thoroughly explain concepts. He's VERY accessible outside of class through discord. TAs & SI leaders were very helpful and much needed. TONS of iClicker questions which are reused for exams so they're familiar.

caleb ruined my love biology. if i didn't take ap bio as a senior in highschool i would have done much worse in this class. the lectures and iclicker questions are meant to confuse you. his class is more biochemistry than actual bio. The amount of times he has been snarky or rude when someone has tried to ask question is countless.avoid if you can!

prof knows his stuff but if you have not taken a biology course since beginning of high school like me, DO NOT TAKE HIS CLASS. he acts like everybody in his class is a bio major and doesn't review any basic material. passive aggressive through discord and gets annoyed when students ask certain questions. lectures were so confusing so glad its over

If I could give this class and professor a -100 out of 5 I would. He destroyed my passion for anything biology related for the foreseeable future. Do not believe the good reviews they're delusional, and just think he's funny when he's not at all. Every lecture made me feel like I knew less than I had before I entered class. DO NOT TAKE.

I don't recommend unless you wanna rip your hair out, someone said he used to be an English professor and it makes sense. He asks questions in paragraph form when they could be so simplified. He's rude to students and passive aggressive in the Discord messages that are supposed to help support you. The worst class I've ever experienced

His lectures are not very useful for preparing for the exams. In class he just does practice questions so when you go back to look at the slides to review for the exams they are pretty useless because we've already done all the questions before. I sent him an email asking why I got a question wrong and he basically told me to search it up myself.

The consensus of him is pretty accurate. He's a very snarky professor, and doesn't show any respect for students whatsoever. Lectures and his "practice exams" are completely useless. I genuinely believe he wants students to struggle. It's a 100 level class, it shouldn't be this challenging. The questions that shows up on actual exams are crazy.

Has a discord to ‘facilitate' questions but when you ask something he gives you a snarky comment which leaves you more confused. Overall bad teacher. All the good reviews must be from people who thinks his jokes are funny, which they're not. If you don't understand a concept you better look online because he won't clear it up for you.

I felt like the lectures were there to confuse you, rather than help you. All of the questions on the exams are trick questions that aren't really covered in SI sessions. He gives you SI/TA sessions to help you pass and study for exams, but all though I went to so many of those, I never felt prepared once I took the test. Also, he is lowkey rude.
great lectures, provides good resources to help pass exams. practice exams are just like the real exams.

Caleb is easily the worst professor I had in college thus far. I am a senior who is taking this course for grad school, and this class is so aggravating and annoying to the point where I rethought if it was even worth it. Each question that should be a straight answer is the longest, explanation he can possibly come up with that leaves you confused

Lectures are not there to help you learn, it is only there to confuse you more in my opinion. I have shown up to every lecture and walked out thinking "what is my life" every single time. And not in a good way too. iClicker questions are hopeless and every single one of them is like a trick answer that you cannot figure out. Skips over questions 2

very cool guy. you can't see your grade in canvas though which makes me super nervous. I think I'm gonna end up getting a B. I'm taking his 152bio class next semester. If you don't have a long attention span good luck, Clicker is required for this class.

Although he's a funny guy i hate the questions he asks. Iclicker, quiz's, and exams feel like they're all trick questions and I hate it. I don't feel like I'm understanding the material more so memorizing practice questions and scenarios. It really depends on the student but personally I don't like his teaching style.
Choose a different professor

Professor Rounds sets clear expectations, though his lectures can be dense. Use resources like unstuckstudy ai alongside the textbook to ace the exams. Overall, a worthwhile class if you engage with the content.

Caleb has clear guidelines for how to succeed in his class. The readings he gave were more complex than you need to know but are useful. He sometimes does not explain topics as clearly as he should, but gives you the tools you need to understand them. Questions from practices come up on the exams and your exam questions are 50% of the final.

Caleb does a wonderful job of challenging his students and making sure they gain a lot out of his class, so its super worth it in the long run. That said, his lectures are very heavy and it's easy to miss something important. Some of his exam questions also tended to have crappy wording so you're forced to play roulette between answer choices.

His lectures have a lot of information. There is a post-lecture quiz and a homework quiz every week. There are two mid-term exams and one final exam. He uses discord for the class which is very helpful. There are extra credit opportunities (1 extra credit) but you have to do extra work to get them like example go to five help sessions for 1 credit.
reviews.rating_tags: Amazing lectures --Clear grading criteria--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Caleb is nice and all but he expects a lot from you in this class; there are no practice exams and if you ask him about it he'll get upset so getting an idea of what content will be on exams is difficult. The final is cumulative and it's hard to know what to study and how thorough. Definitely take advantage of TA help sessions for extra credit.
Why was the final cumulative? So much material. I went crazy.
Don't believe the positive reviews, these are just from people who found him funny. His exams have nothing to do with the course material and his lectures are pretty much useless.

I was told he was good for 151 but he was awful for 152. The worst teacher I have ever had teaches concrete, exams don't make sense, practice exams are useless since they have nothing to do with the actual exam. I had an A in Bio last sem while putting in far less work than I did this semester.
Prof Rounds is my favorite lecturer i've had so far at UMass!

Overall pretty good class especially for STEM, I could get everything done on time and I feel like I have a deep understanding of the topics. He's a nice guy and throws in some funny quips. Also the textbook is just readings that he provides. The only small complaint I have is that he was oddly kind of sassy, especially on the discord that he has.
Prof. Rounds is the best! I am so glad I got him for bio 151 last sem and that I stuck with him! Just go over the iclicker questions before exams and you should be fine!

So I really liked Caleb. He was a chill guy when I talked to him and seemed pretty accessible outside of class. The only 'bad' thing I noticed was sometimes, when he would write a question, it wouldn't make sense.
