It is as if the question was originally written, translated into 7 different languages, and then translated back to English.

He does a TON of iClickers, but overall the iClickers get at simple key concepts, that help you understand the material better. He does weekly quizzes which require reading, but he provides the links to articles/videos that are needed to complete the quizzes. Overall a really good prof though.

Rounds is an effective lecturer. I can't really speak to the difficulty of the class because it basically AP bio all over again, but if you use the lecture and quiz questions to study you will be fine. Sometimes the quizzes had incorrect grading or questions on things we didn't cover but he usually fixed it. Very accessible through discord.

Exams are strictly based on the scenarios in his lecture slides. Couldn't tell you anything I learned from the course despite doing well grade wise. No teaching was done. Grateful I didn't have him for 151 & will be steering clear in the future. If you're looking to learn the 152 material as a foundation and not just get the grade, don't take him.

Funny and informative lectures. Exams can be a tiny bit confusing, but all the info on them is given on the slides/clicker questions, and both Prof and SIs are easily accessible. Minimal homework overall. Attendance graded, though I personally enjoyed his lectures and found it easy to get up for them. Prof nice and interested in what he's teaching.

Caleb is a really great person overall, seems really sweet and is quite funny. The lectures did not help me, but the SI sessions did wonders. My grade actually increased with the less class I went to and the more SI sessions I substituted in. Bio discussions were really helpful, and lots of homework to give leeway for bad exam scores.
reviews.rating_tags: Group projects--Lots of homework--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Prof Rounds was funny, engaging, seemed to enjoy teaching and was good at it too. This was probably the most I've ever learned in a class, at times I struggled with the content but the TAs were super cool and helpful!

Biotap is extremely difficult and he made it somewhat digestible. Very nice, really was foundational for 285. Anyone who had him for intro classes are much more well off than others I have noticed. I can only imagine how good he is for other classes as well

Spectacular professor! He is a bit of a tough grader, but class really is not hard if you're willing to put a good amount of effort into it. The course is incredibly comprehensive and what you learn from his class is invaluable. Incredibly engaging guy who actually teaches you for understanding and makes you critically engage with course content.

Prof. Rounds is amazing once you get to know how to study for his courses. Hi lectures are hilarious and his slides are VERY easy to understand. His courses have discord channels too so that helps a lot. He often replies very promptly to ANY question you might have.
Great professor. His lectures are not too boring as he gives a lot of practice questions. Exams are not too hard and there isn't too much homework.

Despite the rumors, he's good. A lot of people say that his lectures are difficult to understand, but I think he breaks them down in a funny way that makes things easy to visualize. Always has a funny joke or snarky response, which is better than 99% of the dry lectures in other classes.

Love or hate the class, at least it's taught by someone fun.
He's a good professor but he is not as funny as he thinks he is

Rounds was an amazing professor, I loved his lectures. SI sessions are extremely helpful for exams and general material review. Use the clicker questions to study, they show up on the exams. The homework is basically just an easy grade boost. Really an easy class if you care at all.

Caleb is one of the best Professors I have ever had. If you are genuinely interested in the subject you should definitely go with him. The quizzes are pretty fair but, the exams might be a little hard. He's always there to help and makes sure his students understand everything. He replaces the lowest midterm if you do well in the final.

Great class and teacher, but can be pretty rude if you try to talk to him tbh.  As long as you show up to class, take notes off the slides and what he's saying, and do the hw/quizzes, the class really isnt too hard.  Gives extra credit, quizzes/hw have grace periods, and resurrection points from the final.  I'd say take gen bio 1 and 2 with him.

Rounds is a really good professor. He cares for his students and gives them plenty of resources to learn about cellular and molecular biology. Lectures can be long, and the exams can be tricky, but if you use the information he gives you and go to SI's, you'll be fine. He truly tries his best to make the class fair and values your feedback.

I loved Caleb Rounds! He is a great professor. He teaches concepts very well and takes time to pause during lectures to let people ask questions. he also includes a lot of iclicker questions in his slides that helps you understand the concepts he's teaching. His exams definitely aren't easy but if you study and utilize his resources, you'll do well
Professor Rounds is an outstanding professor. His lectures are super engaging and he goes over all of his points multiple times make sure the concepts are well understood. He is also hilarious.

Very manageable pace, and he doesn't try to cram material into each lecture. 2 online quizzes a week, 1 based on lecture, and another on readings/videos, untimed, open book. Exams cover material taken right out of quizzes and iclickers. He is very willing to help and re-explain material. He has stopping points throughout the class for people to ask
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Graded by few things--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Professor Rounds spends more time cracking jokes and appealing to student's sense of humor rather than their learning. Doesn't do well in explaining concepts for this reason. Nice guy and cares about student academic success, but lacks the ability to teach the content he is testing students on, exams are difficult.

Caleb's slideshows contained little information, and the information that was provided was not explained well in class, so be prepared to teach yourself. He has an attitude problem and gets annoyed when people raise their hands in class, although he encourages students to ask questions. If you have the choice, pick literally any other professor!!

Caleb is really great like a real life Hank green. He does have a lot of work and quizzes but also a lot of recourses. Quiz sessions help and si sessions. Lots of clicker questions but they help keep you engaged.

I love Caleb. His lectures and quizzes and test questions are funny!! He makes them humorous!! For someone who struggles with paying attention in class, he is very engaging and the dad jokes make life more bearable. Lots of quizzes and homework, but no more than I had w/ Moscarella in 151. His iClicker questions will come up on tests and quizzes.

Genuinely cares about students, very easy to reach, everything was graded reasonably in both courses I took with him. Not sure why people had such an issue with his class being centered around iClicker questions as they helped a ton with exam prep. Not sure if it necessarily made my learning better though.

Caleb's a funny guy and you can tell he's enthusiastic about bio. However, lectures are difficult to follow and there are so many iClicker questions. I've heard of other professors easier than Caleb, but his class isn't outrageous, you just have to put in a lot of work. Quiz review sessions are extremely helpful, especially if you find a good TA!

I really enjoyed this class. The problem sets were helpful to learn from, but sometimes lengthy and confusing. The TAs in this class really are the ones that got us through. The lectures in this class are engaging but can be confusing. The only complaint I had for this class was a lack of communication. Would recommend for people who love bio.

Great guy with a good sense of humor. He tends to lecture a bit quickly and his slides don't contain much information. Wouldn't survive this course without the TAs and their review sessions. Accessible outside of class and provides clear explanations during his office hours. The course has weekly quizzes, weekly problem sets, 2 exams, and a final.
reviews.rating_tags: Group projects--Lots of homework--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Overall a good lecture, I was able to understand the material and the tests were pretty easy. My only true complaints would be a lack of communication with the TAs (mostly for grading), and unprofessional behavior when communicating with the class. Caleb is a friendly professor but had some times where he would be disrespectful towards students.

Caleb is great! His lecture slides are interesting and he's a very engaging speaker. The iClicker questions are interactive and are a great way to stay focused and review content. No homework and just one quiz a week. Exams are easy and are just like longer quizzes. My only criticism is that there are a lot of typos in his slides and quizzes.

I loved caleb! I came into this class after taking AP Bio in high school, but definitely still felt like I was learning.  Focuses on understanding rather than memorization, and his use of clicker questions during lecture was super helpful.  Almost everything I learned was through lecture, but they are recorded. Go to TA weekly quiz help sessions!
reviews.rating_tags: Clear grading criteria--Lecture heavy--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: I love Caleb! Very nice, funny, and approachable guy. He really wants you to succeed. You get to miss 4 lectures unexcused with no penalty. Don't miss discussions & review the iclicker questions- they will help you pass. His exams tend to be tough, but if you do better on the final than one of your exams he'll replace it & drop the low grade

Caleb is a very knowledgable teacher who presents extremely engaging topics through mostly powerpoint slides followed with interactive clicker questions. I find myself being able to easily attain the information through simply attending the lectures and not even taking notes.

Mixed feelings about this Caleb Rounds. I have to rewatch lectures and put a lot of extra work in just to understand what is going on in class. He's a funny person who makes an effort to connect with students, even through discord, but can seem annoyed when you ask questions. His questions & phrasing are confusing.
Great professor. Very objective and clear, lectures are very enjoyable.

I started the semester by failing the first exam. Then came back and got a 98 on the second one. Caleb is an amazing professor and his lectures are exactly like the exams with the clicker questions. He gives lots of study material and you can do really well with him.

He went way too fast. He did not cover the basics of Biology and skipped straight to gene expression. As someone who hadn't taken biology since my freshman year of high school, I would not recommend Professor Rounds. He does not care about answering his students questions and he gets frustrated when people would raise their hands.

I took Bio 285 over the summer and online. The lectures were very informative and Professor Rounds want you to learn. However, the tests and quizzes are difficult as the questions can throw you off immensely.  If you want a good grade in the class, you have to study every slide and every lecture video very carefully.

Professor Rounds is probably one of the best professors in the sense that he wants his students to learn and his lectures of very informative. That being said, this is not an easy class as his tests are very difficult. Moreover, the extra credit barely makes a dent in your grade. If you want a good grade, study everything thoroughly and carefully.
I love Rounds! He was so funny wxcept that his test literally set us up to fail and can be unecessarily difficult. Though he does truly want you to do good and learn the material.

Caleb is very knowledgable about the topics and makes himself available outside of class for questions/concerns. He can be a bit condescending and the class is EXTREMELY test heavy. The material is pretty straightforward and he provides practice exams but expect to study this is not a cake walk.
reviews.rating_tags: Lecture heavy--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: his classes are entirely made of clicker questions so it is very difficult to understand the material. the 3 exams and final make up 75% of your grade so if you aren't a good test taker good luck. tests are composed of multiple choice and open questions.

Caleb is so enthusiastic about bio and it shows. Each lecture starts with a recap of the last weeks material and a little science meme that he likes. He is super accessible and a super fast responder, and always is willing to stop class to explain a topic that confuses people. My class had weekly quizzes and monthly short answer quizzes- BEST PROF!

Caleb slays the day. This class is definitely do-able, but I would not consider it an easy A. But if you attend the lectures, take good notes, and do the SI sheets, you will most likely pass with an A. He's also very helpful during office hours

Not my favorite professor. Caleb was a solidly okay lecturer although his presentations were often difficult to follow. The course content was also rather difficult but if you're in this class you are probably in BIOTAP so you should expect that I suppose. Overall not the best class but not the worst.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: He's a amazing professor to get as a first year, and although his exams are a little tough, they're properly fair in difficulty (tough to a point where you can't go in blind), and proper studying can result in a easy A. Only issue is he might talk too fast during lecture, but he's always happy to answer fun & curious questions and repeat himself.

lectures are messy but write down whatever he says and review them. a few short answer assignments, weekly quiz, 3 exams, final. TAs can make or break the class especially for quiz help sessions, go to them. have a buddy because short answer assignments + quizzes are open note/collaborative. he has a discord server for the course as well
Nice guy, but tests are ridiculous
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Get ready to read--Tough grader

reviews.comment: His lectures can be messy and a bit boring. however, he does lots of iClicker questions during lecture which are very relevant to exams and help u gauge ur understanding of the material. weekly hw quizzes are super easy and I recommend attending the TA quiz review sessions on zoom for the weekly lecture quizzes so you can get 100% on all of them

Love Prof Rounds! Super funny and can tell he wants to connect with his students. Lectures are a little messy and confusing, but all the important info is there. The TAs definitely can make or break the class, though. Will be taking 152 with him. Great guy.

He is nice, funny, and cares about his students. His class is challenging and heavy, though: 1 Discussion, 1 quiz, 1 homework. Also, have to use iclicker and is GPS tracked. If you want to get high scores, make sure to understand all of the iclicker questions. He prefers to teach with graphs and images rather than theoretical questions.
reviews.rating_tags: Accessible outside class--Skip class? You won't pass.--Hilarious

reviews.comment: Classes like Caleb's are what college is all about. His lectures are so engaging--lots of iClicker questions. This class requires outside work to get an A: study daily and rewrite your notes. His tests are tough. The secret? Practice exams! Go to every SI session, too. I truly loved this course and look forward to Bio152 with him next semester! :)
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Hilarious--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: Caleb is a pretty okay guy overall, professor wise? Mediocre. He is funny and tries to make it interesting, I'll give him that. But, he expects you to know absolutely everything in order to pass the class. He doesn't go over any definitions. He doesn't explain concepts well either. Super fast paced. iClicker required. Would not take again.
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Skip class? You won't pass.--Test heavy

reviews.comment: Caleb is a great guy. He's funny, is awesome about giving extensions, and really cares about the subject matter. Lectures can be fast-paced and hard to follow but manageable. The content can be difficult but as far as professors go he's one of the best I've had.

I took this class for a major requirement first semester of freshman year and it was worst thing ever. Caleb is the least understanding professor and gives no sympathy. The exams are impossible even though I get the questions right in class and prelecture videos have little to do with class. Attendance is mandatory and there is no exceptions.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Test heavy--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: Make sure you go to the TA review sessions and office hours because Caleb lectures quickly in class and it's hard to keep up. Also make sure you study for exams because the questions are not very straightforward and there are often trick questions, so make sure you pay attention to the questions and have solid knowledge to back up your answers.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Clear grading criteria--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: I would take any opportunity to take Bio151 with a different professor if possible. He's personable enough, but expects you to come into class knowing everything already from illegible readings and Crash Course videos. He goes WAY too fast and makes every quiz/exam question unnecessarily wordy and confusing. Don't take it with him... just don't.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Skip class? You won't pass.--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: He is a fairly good lecturer- not amazing, but he gets the job done. The main issue I have is his phrasing of questions. Questions have multiple interpretations, making the answer very ambiguous. If you ask him to clarify, he tries to lead you in the right direction without telling you the answer- which usually increases confusion. Solid overall.

Caleb is a nice guy, but he makes this class difficult for no reason. He often doesnt explain things correctly and for exams he expects you to recall things he said in passing. Exams are very conceptually based and tricky, but if you go to UTA review sessions and put in the work youll be good. Its hard though, so try to take it with someone else.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Skip class? You won't pass.--Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: I didn't expect an introductory biology class to be this difficult. Caleb was a fine teacher but he went a little fast and the lectures are often very long. You will struggle in class if you do not show up! He goes over 50-70 slides per each class. He allows you to take the weekly quizzes online and provides UTA review sessions to help you.
reviews.rating_tags: Accessible outside class--Skip class? You won't pass.--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: I and all of my classmates that I've talked to think that Caleb is pretty bad at explaining concepts. It makes it very hard for people like myself who have a hard time with biology. I had to spend so much time trying to learn the material on my own because his teaching was not effective.

Caleb is aggressive and refuses to clarify his extremely ambiguous questions on quizzes and tests. Be prepared to be extremely stressed. I'm pretty sure he gets off on that. By far my least favorite class ever. The TAs were great though. Praying I never have to deal with this man again. I advise that you stay far far away if you care about learning

Caleb is good at teaching but it's hard to keep up in lectures. It's easy to wander off and he tends to go through slides very quickly. The lecture quizzes and discussions impact your grade the most outside of the 3 exams. DO go to the uta quiz sessions. They pretty much guarantee a 100 for all your lecture quizzes. Exams are hard to get an A on.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Skip class? You won't pass.--Tough grader

reviews.comment: If you are not good at science or biology do not take this course. 0/10 its terrible. This class is so stressful and Caleb isnt a bad dude but I feel like he gets very easily annoyed if you dont understand something as if he hasnt studied many years of it and expects you to know it. He puts too many trick questions on exams. This course is hard

I love this class, but I wouldn't say it's easy. I did very well in AP Bio and would consider this class moderate, but I can see a lot of others struggling. There are weekly readings that kind of act as a textbook. Some of the quiz and test questions are tricks, so read carefully. Discussions give a good idea of what the questions are like. Study!
reviews.rating_tags: Respected--Accessible outside class--Skip class? You won't pass.

reviews.comment: This is the worse professor Ive ever had in my ENTIRE life. I hate this course with a passion thanks to rounds. I even read his reviews before I took his class and thought Id be okay. Please run away now do NOT take this course. You will be saving yourself. He goes way too fast, his exams are horrible u can study 8 hours n still fail. Ugh.

He sucks. If you took AP Bio in high school you should be fine but not anyone else. He goes way too fast through his slides and theres more iClicker questions than actual notes. Theres no textbook which seems nice in the beginning but leaves you no resources to help. His tests are hard and he teaches material up to the day before the exam.
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Skip class? You won't pass.--Test heavy

reviews.comment: Rounds is a solid choice if taking Bio 151 or 152. I had him for both and if you do the clicker questions and put in the work you will do fine in the class. His grading criteria is very straight forward and you either have prepared and know the information or you didn't. Caleb is a good guy and will help you if you have any questions at all.

Caleb is a pretty good professor. Takes a lot of time in lecture to answer questions. Exams are difficult, best way to study is to re-do lecture clicker questions and UNDERSTAND WHY an answer is correct (not just memorizing the answers). Lots of TA sessions and office hours. He let us collaborate on exams which was nice but sometimes stressful.

Rounds is a good guy. But 152 is one of the lesser classes I have taken. Three tests and a cumulative final are worth 65% of your grade - all are convoluted and have trick questions. There's a lot of weekly work: three quizzes, supplemental readings and videos. Lectures are hard to follow with important foundational details left out.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Get ready to read--Tough grader

reviews.comment: Would not recommend this class. Professor Rounds is condescending, though he's well liked because he plays it off as a personality trait. As someone who got an A in this class, it sucked - lots of trick questions, and he ONLY teaches through examples without prior info, if you're someone that needs actual material to learn from you're out of luck
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Test heavy--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: I had him last year for Bio 151 and 152, and after taking some classes with some other Bio professors, he is my favorite. He did a great job of helping his students understand material even if it can be a little overwhelming at times. Compared to my professor right now, his lecture slides are much more clear on what we need to focus on for exams.

Caleb is a really caring and great guy, my favorite prof I've had. He truly wants his students to succeed and is always willing to take time to slow down and answer questions. This semester lecture attendance was extra credit but definitely very valuable. Exams are the hardest part of this class but if you study and pay attention you'll do fine.

I absolutely adore Caleb Round. He is such a great professor and human being overall. I will definitely admit that you do have to work for the grade in this class, however, there are so many resources for help- take advantage of his office hours! I truly recommend taking any course with Dr. Rounds, he's the best.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Hilarious--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: I took this class because it was a prerequisite and I honestly wish I hadn't. I don't know whether it's the lack of motivation or interest but this class is super difficult. I feel like his lectures were difficult to understand and I was so lost that nothing I did made this class better for me. I'm honestly hoping for at least a B at this point.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: Professor Rounds spends more time trying to be funny than he does trying to make the information digestible. He uses convoluted language on already complex topics which causes further confusion in trying to understand the material. He can be condescending when students ask questions which deters them from asking future questions.

i took AP bio in high school and did well so this class was pretty much a repeat of that. rounds does his best to make sure everyone knows the fundamentals and will spend a ton of time answering everyone's questions. also offers tons of extra credit opportunities.

Great professor but can go too fast during lectures. Attending lectures is optional, but I would've failed if I didn't attend and there's lots of extra credit just for attending. There are also so many quizzes and HWs that can easily outweigh bad test grades. I didn't do great on the tests but got 100s on almost all the quizzes/HWs so I was fine.

Dr. Rounds was a great 151 Professor. Lecture participation matters 100%. You cannot simply remember facts for this class and you need to understand the concepts as test questions are not just spewing facts. There are so so many resources that Caleb provides to help all of his students succeed. Ill be taking 152 with Caleb as well. 100% recommend

Caleb is a very chill guy. His sense of humor can be a little snarky for some but honestly he means well and he seems to care about his students. His expectations are reasonable and even though the coursework can be a little tough sometimes, it's not that bad if you're willing to work for it.

Caleb was amazing. While optional to attend, every lecture was enjoyable. He is friendly and funny. He allowed students to work together on assessments since everything was online. The work would have been hard if solo but with a group it was doable. He made bio enjoyable to learn, everything you want in a science teacher. His pets are cute too.

Don't take this class if you want an easy A. Despite being remote, Caleb has given students a lot of resources. Go to UTA Review sessions to do weekly quizzes & you're guaranteed a 100 on quizzes. Plenty of extra credit opportunities. A lot of what's on the exams are specific to what Caleb speaks about in class, so go to lecture to understand.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Lecture heavy--Caring

reviews.comment: Test questions dont make much sense. Everything in the class was fine and engaging, liked the lecture and clicker questions. Unfortunately it would almost be impossible to get above a B on exams or prepare for them, so its very hard to get an A.

Caleb is a funny guy, his course is well planned out and can be accessible (sometimes). I understood the material well But he covers too much material in a single lecture and goes too fast. His exams are very tricky and his questions are worded really badly. Even though I knew my material but didnt do well on exam questions.
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Skip class? You won't pass.--Test heavy

reviews.comment: No. just no. this class is the reason I switched out of my biochem major.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Get ready to read--Skip class? You won't pass.

reviews.comment: His bio 151 class was very difficult for me as I had never taken AP bio before. Pay attention to the clicker questions and make sure you try on the weekly quizzes.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: Professor Rounds is great. He knows his stuff, and helps his students know it. He answers all questions and helps you understand the material no matter how long it takes. Participation is mandatory, but he tries to keep things interesting. Weekly homework that is super easy, and weekly quizzes about the lecture material.

De. Rounds is a good guy. Lectures are great and material is clear enough for an intro bio course. Only gripe is that some questions will leave you in the "Need to think how he wants me to think, not logically". If you are not normally solid in bio (like myself) make sure you study hard for exam one to get used to his questions. Take him. He's good

Prof Rounds was a great lecturer! I would absolutely recommend taking Biology with him. He is very passionate and intelligent in the subject. Lectures are recorded and posted (which is SO helpful because the exams are directly drawn from his lectures- no textbook). ADVICE: Learn how to interpret the diagrams and you'll be good to go on exams

Caleb is the least considerate professor I've had. There is a pandemic & he assumes his class over rules everyone's personal lives. He adds & takes away points on his own terms without updating you. He made the material much more difficult after corona. He's difficult to communicate with & gets mad when you email him asking to clarify. DON'T TAKE!!

Caleb's class has always been my favorite class to sit through, including BIO152. He is very passionate about the topics which come out in the lectures. How to pass the exams: write down EVERY iclicker. like seriously. I would take screenshots of the questions on reef then put them in my notes, writing down everything he says about the questions.

He was hilarious and incredibly nice. He really likes his job and wants kids to pass. However, if you suck at Bio like me, you will be screwed in his class. I almost passed but didn't understand anything that was going on and missed the mark by 2 points and now I'm retaking the class. If bio is your thing you will have no problem in his class.

Records all his lectures with live note taking so missing a class is okay, but there is an attendance/participation grade so you can't just skip. has all quizzes and homework on Moodle so you get your grades as soon as you submit the assignment. you are even given a grade calculating spreadsheet to see how well you need to do before finals.

If you've never taken Bio before, you'll probably find yourself often lost in his class. 'Introductory Bio' is truly a misnomer if he is your prof. Tests are difficult, you have to study hard to pass. Rewatching the lectures on echo is helpful, and redoing clicker qs can help too. Hes funny enough but if you are looking for a good grade, dont take.

Clicker questions help turn what would be a boring lecture into what is a chance to study every class. The homework quizzes also help learn content. There are plenty of SI sessions if you are struggling. There are 4 tests in the semester but they are manageable. Caleb is funny and he knows the content well. TA discussions aren't helpful though.

Pay attention in class and do the work and you will understand the material, not too much memorization. The clicker questions also help a lot. He actually makes an effort to help you learn and improve the class.

If you manage to develop your ability to leave your phone face down and take your headphones off when applicable, then you will do well and you might even have a little fun while doing it. Unfortunately I discovered this around the third quarter of the semester. It's a tight fit class, he runs it until the absolute last minute, but I like it.
reviews.rating_tags: Accessible outside class--Skip class? You won't pass.--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: Weekly assignments that are only available for 36 hours in the middle of the week. Clciker questions are mandatory for attendance (part of grade). Tests are crazy difficult at time. Always 6-8 open responses that are mostly based on memorization of clicker question graphs. No extra credit.
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Skip class? You won't pass.--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: Had Caleb for 151, 152, 153. Clicker based classes with grade boosters in weekly quizzes and homework. You will get an 80+ on every exam if you understand the clickers. First day of class, just start a Google slides and put all the clicker q's in there. His finals are hard though, not going to lie. Take him if you want to truly learn.

I've never felt like I've learned more from a class, but the way the bio program is set up at UMass, you can take another professor and very likely make an A. I got an A from BIO151 with less work, but for Caleb I had near perfect averages and perfect attendance in every category, but his exams are awful and I couldn't get an A. TAKE A DIFF PROF.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Graded by few things--Tough grader

reviews.comment: Caleb does a great job running the bio153 lab class but he is not the best option for 152. He is really confusing and makes very difficult exams. He gives students unclear explanations to their questions. He doesnt answer emails often either. I would not take his class again. However, hes cool. 8/10 would hang out with outside of class.

Caleb's a solid and chill professor. Some people really don't like him but it depends on your learning style and how much work you're willing to put into the class. Exams are difficult and require actual effort but what STEM class doesn't require that?
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: Clicker based slides which is VERY helpful for exam & have cute funny jokes in them, very little notes on slide, if you like clear notes maybe not the prof for you. Quizzes & HW weekly online, easy & grade booster. Very funny friendly guy who is helpful. Exams are sometimes tough & questions can be vague/confusing. use clicker & quiz for studying!
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Hilarious--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: Caleb's lectures are 80% clickers, which is helpful to an extent until you're trying to study for exams and there are barely any notes to look at. It may work for some people, but definitely not so much for others. Tests are rough but grades are also made up of quizzes, homework, and clicker, so do well on those which should pad your grade.
reviews.rating_tags: Respected--Skip class? You won't pass.--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: Cool guy, pretty funny. Most importantly he is very fair. Nothing is on his exams that arent in the lectures. Do all your homework and go to all the lectures and youll be fine. Homework doesn't take too long. Not a hard class but not super easy either. Makes lecture interesting, great at explaining concepts.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Skip class? You won't pass.--Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: The leader of this class is a gamble; I got a random TA named Han Ling who honestly sucks as a person and a TA, and other people got Caleb himself. I've heard good things about him, but I personally didn't have the best lab experience. Han Ling graded strictly and was not flexible. I had to work hard for a good grade. Just hope you get a good TA.

I have been both a student and a college level biology teacher. I have taught the same material he has to student as well as having been a Druid Rounds. Having said that, it is clear he completely lacks any teaching ability. His exams are nonsense. This material was over complicated and there was an over use of trick questions AVOID THIS CLASS.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough Grader--Participation matters--Skip class? You won't pass.

reviews.comment: My hardest class by far. No textbooks to follow up on. The powerpoints are very vague and there are more iclicker questions than the actual material. Lectures are disorganized and difficult to take notes. Since the tests are hard, make sure to do well on the take-home quizzes, discussions, and iclickers because they bring your grade up greatly.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough Grader--Skip class? You won't pass.--EXTRA CREDIT

reviews.comment: Never had Caleb, as Bio lab was instructed by a TA. Your TA in a huge way can make or break your grade. The Lab itself is ok as long as you do your work and work efficiently with your group. Many lab reports weren' too bad but some took me 3-4 hours at least to complete, I did them in one sitting. Put in work, attend lab, and you will do well.

Calebs exams are ridiculously hard. I genuinely tried in his class to learn the material but the exams are simply insane. I cant say that I learned anything coming out of that class. Dont recommend...
He has a meh sense of humor, but gives interesting facts. I must say that over the course of the semester, Caleb became a better teacher in my eyes. There appears to be a method to his madness.

Caleb is not only one of the best professors/teachers that I have ever had the pleasure of learning from, but he goes above and beyond with his students. His frequent use of iClicker questions, as well as his genuine sense of humor keep me and my friends completely engaged and makes learning Biology (which I admit can be boring sometimes) enjoyable
reviews.rating_tags: Tough Grader--Skip class? You won't pass.--Hilarious

reviews.comment: Avoid this professor. Caleb likes to think he's a good teacher, and relies on clicker questions to gauge how well students are understanding material. This is inaccurate because he purposely leaves pieces of information out until he sees everyone getting it wrong. He sets the students up for constant failure and calls it part of learning.

His lectures are really good and educational. In a group setting he is very kind, funny, and informative. Tests and quizzes are hard but fair. However, when he is in a one-on-one student/teacher setting he tends to be short/rude causing the student to feel stupid and disrespected. If you're someone who wants help outside of class, avoid his classes

Caleb has good intentions when he teaches, as in he wants people to demonstrate their knowledge through application, but he expects you to learn from weekly readings without going over it in class, then jumps to applying it. The way he explains things is with the assumption that everyone has a strong background in biology, so he skips lots of steps
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--LECTURE HEAVY

reviews.comment: Caleb definitely knows his stuff. No textbook, but there are weekly readings that you have to comment on for homework. His classes are interesting for the most part, and he's pretty funny. Definitely go to office hours, he's very good at explaining things one-on-one, and is a good professor to get to know. He has lots of connections.

Caleb really knows his material. He is passionate about teaching his subject and it reflects in this course. Unfortunately, his tests are very difficult. Questions are confusing, and diagrams misleading. It is possible to get a good grade in this course, but you WILL have to work.

Caleb is- for the most part- a really solid professor. Although his explanations are sometimes confusing, he uses a ton of clicker questions, which help to learn/ remember concepts. Also, he uses Echo360, so you can always rewatch lectures. Lots of Dad jokes, whether that is considered positive or negative. Not necessarily an easy A, but achievable
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Skip class? You won't pass.--Hilarious

reviews.comment: Most of his exams are based off the questions he would typically ask in lecture. Pay attention in lecture and thoroughly review the questions he asks in class and you should be fine. He usually makes his PowerPoints accessible for his students online. Bio 153 on the other hand is dependent on your TA and the lab reports are not graded easily.

Really good at teaching and pretty funny and kind of of attractive as well. The only issue I had with him is that his exams were very tricky. Be prepared for a lot of clicker questions but they're very helpful for studying! He also posts lecture recordings which are helpful as well.

Really funny and caring. The tests are exactly like the clicker questions in class. The at home quizzes are guaranteed grade boasters. He is very good at explaining all concepts and there are practice tests for every exam.

This course is a Intro Bio lab so I never saw Caleb, just the TA's, but he did all of the rubrics and protocols. They have funny jokes in them and are pretty clear. You have to try to get a good grade, but it's easy as long as you make sure to read what he tells you and triple-check your lab reports to make sure you do everything it says to.

Professor Rounds is awesome and he tries hard to making his lectures and slides interesting. The tests can definitely be a challenge but sometimes he drops questions on the tests if a lot of people get them wrong for a reason unrelated to comprehension. He is approachable and will help out a lot in office hours and make sure you get the concept.

Caleb Rounds is a great professor and really knows what he's talking about. Clicker questions can be a source of extra credit depending on whether you get them right or not, and he's available to help if you ever need it. Exams can be hard, but if you study for them you'll do fine. Lectures are recorded and PowerPoints are posted online as well.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--EXTRA CREDIT

reviews.comment: His lectures can be really interesting and funny. Study hard for the tests but he is very accessible outside of class but just make sure to study the iClicker questions, go to office hours, and do the practice exam until you know it super well. Also doing well with the online stuff can really cushion your bad test grades- my mistake in the class.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough Grader--Skip class? You won't pass.--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: Overall he is a very good professor! He really does make you work for the grade! The exams are a bit tough mostly of the wording. Sometimes is lectures dont make sense but if you go to SI sessions it helps a lot. Hes a huge iclicker Person which is a good way to study for the exams along with the practice exams! He does post everything on moodle.
Caleb is very passionate about biology and is a terrific professor! He makes his students work for a good grade, but it is very rewarding in the end.
reviews.rating_tags: Respected--Skip class? You won't pass.--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: Caleb is a really smart guy and you can really tell how much he loves bio!! I had to work hard to get an A, but I really enjoyed his class. I would recommend taking bio151 with Caleb, but don't expect an easy A. Go to all the SI sessions and you should be fine. His tests may be difficult but with all the help you are offered you will do well!

Caleb definitely makes you work for your grade. His lectures are very clicker-based and does not have much information on them. Instead, he makes you think a lot about the material you just learned. one thing I do not like about him is that i feel like when he teaches, he purposely teaches in a more confusing way that he needs to. Not bad overall!

Caleb is a really smart guy and a really good guy. But, his tests are very very difficult. It's not that the material is hard its just the way he words them, its like he is trying to trick you even if you know the material. You will learn a lot but don't take if you want an easy A.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough Grader--Skip class? You won't pass.--Tests are tough

reviews.comment: I am so happy I took Bio 152 with Prof. Rounds. He loves the material and has a great sense of humor, making lectures engaging and fun. He's great at explaining topics in different ways and really wants his students to learn. Definitely take advantage of office hours, it really helps clear up confusing topics in class!
You need to study the lecture materials.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough Grader--Skip class? You won't pass.--TEST HEAVY

reviews.comment: If you're going to take Caleb's bio class, you have to have a sense of humor. He spices up his slideshows with memes and just funny stuff to keep you interested, which is great for all the non-science majors. He's also really approachable, and loves visitors in his office hours, even if you don't discuss lecture.

Dr. Rounds is very good at keeping you engaged in lectures through i-clicker questions (grade booster) and a good sense of humor. He makes it easy to get a good grade in the class through collaborative weekly quizzes and east homework. If you pay attention in lecture, really try to engage with the material and ask questions, you'll be great.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--ACCESSIBLE OUTSIDE CLASS--Hilarious

reviews.comment: Professor Rounds is a good professor he seems very passionate about the subject. Clicker questions and quizzes provide a nice cushion to your grade and clicker questions will show up on the exam. My only complaint is that he only releases practice exams 2 days before the exams so if you want to study, you should start at least a week in advance.

His exams are poorly made. He's a good explainer, but he knows that his questions are often unclear and does nothing to fix it. He does allow you to argue exam answers, but this does not address the root of the issue. Students should not be penalized for understanding a question in a valid, but different way than their professor intended they did.

Caleb's one of the best professors/teachers I've ever had. He's super passionate about biology, and it shows even in a lecture hall of 300 students. His tests are difficult, but fair, and if you pay attention in class and study for tests it's not too difficult to get an A. Clicker questions count towards your grade so attend class.

He has really difficult exams and is has unprofessional lecture slides. He knows what he is talking about but honestly it doesn't compare to the exam. I hate him. Don't take his class if you can avoid it.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough Grader--Skip class? You won't pass.--GRADED BY FEW THINGS

reviews.comment: Caleb is a great prof who loves the material. The tests are mostly on the lecture. If you go and pay attention and study from the clicker questions and practice tests then you'll do fine on the tests.
Most of the questions you see on the test are directly from the questions he asks in class. If you go to class everyday and understand every question you get wrong you should get an easy A.
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Skip class? You won't pass.--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: This is an introductory bio class. Caleb is a great teacher, uses great examples and although his clicker as well as exam questions are tricky sometimes, he does his best to be fair to everyone. Very approachable outside of class. His exams are mainly true or false patterned. He's kinda funny sometimes too!

Fantastic biology teacher. He is engaging and genuinely cares about what he is teaching which is rare to find at college level with large leactures. He also actively tries to improve his class and how he is teaching which is VERY UNUSUAL for teachers who have tenure. Great teacher, highly recommend.
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Skip class? You won't pass.--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: Caleb is a super nice guy and his lectures are pretty good, because he is pretty funny and is always willing to answers questions. His test questions are pretty similar to clicker questions you do in class and also the practice exams. His tests are definitely not easy, but getting good grades on them is achievable. Also you don't buy the book
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--TEST HEAVY--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: Caleb is fantastic and really cares about his classes. He always tells you if he cant answer a student question and will research it and tell what he has found at the next lecture. Tough exams but very kind and funny teacher. Would definitely take again

By far the best professor I have had so far. He's funny, his lectures are fantastic and very interactive, the homework is minimal and his tests are fair. He does a great job at explaining concepts and all in all is a very well 'rounded' professor (get it? because his name is Dr. Rounds?) 11/10 would take a class with him again.

This professor clearly knows what he is talking about. There are so many clicker questions in each class, so attendance is pretty much mandatory. However, those questions helped me study for tests. The tests were pretty hard. Overall, a great professor.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--TEST HEAVY--GRADED BY FEW THINGS

reviews.comment: Caleb is an excellent professor. If you are not here to actually learn biology then this will be a hard class for you. If you go to lecture and review his clicker questions you will be golden. His exams are difficult and make you think. He is a tough teacher but by the end of the semester you will actually understand biology.

Caleb rounds is amazing. If you go to class, pay attention, and try you will do well in the course! Take advantage of the help he offers during office hours. It helps to rewatch his lectures, do the clicker questions and quizzes again before an exam. You have to try for your grade but he will help you understand anything if you just ask!

Tests are ridiculous and poorly made. Mostly true/false or could be true/could be false. If you ask a question he will probably be rude or condescending when answering. If you need help as a TA not him. Do well on quizzes and homework because tests are out of left field.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough Grader--Skip class? You won't pass.--LECTURE HEAVY

reviews.comment: My favorite science teacher of all time! Such a great lecturer that I sometimes wish he taught all my classes. I wouldn't listen too much to people who were frustrated with him, his tests have tricky questions, but I reckon most of their frustration is because he makes the intro courses harder than most kids would like. GREAT GUY.

He gives you a ton of opportunities to boost your grade through the homework and quizzes. He has clicker but it makes you go to class and learn the material a lot more than reading the book and looking at the slides alone. He's also really passionate about biology and is funny and enthusiastic! I'd strongly recommend him for bio 151.

I DO NOT recommend taking a class with him. He expects you to learn from the book and then apply what you learn in his class. He should be more focused on teaching the material. His exams are meant to trick and confuse you. I went to his office hours and he essentially told me to "figure it out myself". Extra help session are helpful (Excel, SI)
reviews.rating_tags: Tough Grader--Skip class? You won't pass.--LECTURE HEAVY

reviews.comment: Tests hard, study a lot of the slides read all the textbook sections and do all the online quizzes, go to the room he reserves for them because groups do it together much easier. Exams suck and final is cumulative and annoying good luck

The key to the tests in this class is to go to the lectures, read the textbook, and memorize the slides. Don't even need to ace tests because the points given for lab and hw quizzes is an easy way to bring your average up. Rounds is tough but a great professor.

Professor Rounds has a very unique teaching style compared to other professors. He includes a lot of clicker questions in each lecture and bases his exams on the lecture material. In order to do well on the exams, make sure you study and understand the diagrams and graphs that he uses in class.
Caleb is a great professor - cracks cute Dad jokes all the time. 4 tests in the semester including the final - studying his slides will give you an A or B+. Would recommend
Great class! Would take again, and the grading criteria is clear. Do your share of the work and you'll get a good grade.

Professor Rounds is easily one of my favorite professors I've ever had. He is SO intelligent and knows everything about everything. I took 151 with him and HAD to take 152 with him again. His exams are extremely hard but bearable! Funny guy (sometimes) and extremely kind!

Lecture Powerpoint and iClciker questions are very helpful. He has pre-class quiz that asks about the materials from the readings and post-class quiz that asks about materials of the week. He's super helpful during office hours and genuinely wants to help students succeed in class. He gives extra credits for correctly answered iClicker questions
I loved this class!Caleb is a great teacher and wants you to do well and understand the material. I thought the information was clear, and the PowerPoints were helpful.

Caleb is intelligent beyond belief, and that will become apparent after your first class with him. Although, with his amount of knowledge, he can be a little hard to understand at times, or even explain things in ways that are still too complicated to grasp. With that being said, he's unbelievably devoted to his students. If you can take him, do it

Caleb is a really nice guy, but he's a little more ambiguous than I would like in a professor, especially because some of the ambiguous material he attempts to clear up (sometimes unsuccessfully) and then you're tested on it.  But he's a really nice guy and he gives you the opportunity to "fight" him on exam questions :)

Professor Rounds is a great professor.  He really wants you to pass the class.  He gives so many opportunities to boost your grade with weekly quizzes and IClicker questions. He really cares about his students.

I'm glad that AP Bio credits aren't accepted because of this man. His tests are based more on case studies, data interpretation, and some memorization as opposed to hardcore textbook information. Look over iClickers, quizzes, and practice tests, and make sure that you understand the material, and you'll be set

If you put the time and effort in you really learn a lot and after completing the course you have that good feeling about knowing you accomplished something hard. Caleb is great and even though the material is tough there are many opportunities to get help.

Caleb was a very good professor. You need to attend lecture to pass, but this isn't an issue as they were interesting and he keeps students engaged with helpful clicker questions. He gives homework and weekly online quizzes, but they are relatively easy. The only issue is that his test questions can be wordy and occasionally confusing.

Took 151 with Caleb and thought at the time he was a good teacher. However, after taking 152 with another professor I truly wish I had Caleb again. He is one of the few biology teachers who seems to have a genuine interest in teaching. His tests are harder they aren't trick questions but he wants you to actually think. In hindsight, great teacher.

I thoroughly enjoyed taking Bio 152 with Caleb.  He always kept me interested and was cracking constant jokes that were actually funny.  His tests are difficult and I often got a B no matter how much I studied, but still enjoyed the course.  Highly recommended.
If you are more of a solving person, you will struggle. He is very conceptual based.

Very interesting lectures, I was not bored once. However, tests are quite tricky; he likes true and false questions which is very unfortunate. Taking his Biology 152 class because despite the test difficulty, I liked this class.

If you're going to take a Bio 151 or 152 course, take it with Dr. Rounds. HE is by far the best out of all of the bio teachers. His class isn't easy, but his tests never have surprises, and he also leaves a lot of room for a high grade as long as you participate. He does a very good job at clarifying difficult things, especially one on one.

Caleb encourages students to ask questions, and answers clearly until students understand. Lectures are really helpful and usually cover the reading that was assigned, but you should still read. iClicker is required and answering the polls is what counts as the participation. Sometimes humorous. Tough wording on exams. Weekly quizzes and homework.

LOVE love love 151 with Caleb. His exams are difficult to study for, but if you commit to going to class and asking questions to slow him down in lectures you will be great. He uses lots of iclicker questions that mimic the questions on the exams so ask questions if you don't understand them in class. Very funny, made a challenging class enjoyable

Professor Rounds, in my opinion, was fantastic at presenting the information in bio 151 and making sure all students understood the information.  He uses many iclicker questions, and makes sure all students understands each question and/or slide before moving on.  Show up to class and ask questions and you're all set.

Caleb was a really good professor in my opinion. If you want help learning the material or have a question all you have to do is email him and he will either email you back or address the question in lecture the next day. Tests are kind of hard but all you need is a general conceptual understanding of stuff to pass. There are a lot of Iclickers

I had Caleb for 151 and loved his class despite its difficulty. I found 152 to be easier because I was used to his testing style and because of the content. He makes you work for your grade and expects you to think critically and to participate in class lectures, and uses those skills heavily on his exams. He's also funny and a genuinely nice guy.

Caleb is seriously the best intro bio professor. His tests are hard, but he gives points back for unclear questions and really wants you to do well in class. He is always willing to explain things, but you need to put in effort for the class. I didn't take his section of 152 because it was MWF instead of TR, and it seriously was my biggest regret.

Caleb is very passionate about Bio 151. He is hilarious, a little dorky (which is awesome!!) and he does his best to explain things in depth until everyone understands. The exams are difficult, but if you attend lecture you will be prepared. Super fun course!!

Caleb Rounds is a great professor who brings humor and wit into his lectures. You will learn a lot from him and this class by the end. BUT his exams are ridiculously tough, he purposely puts tricky answers on it like "false" and "cannot be determined" when it could be either. I liked him a LOT better for BIO151. Get ready to work if you want him.

Professor Rounds is great. The only complaint I have is that his exams are tough. However his lectures are awesome, everything he presents is always neat and clear. He also likes to add some humor to his lectures. Had him for BIO151 and chose to take him again for 152 despite the challenge. You take so much out of his class it's definitely worth it
His exams are extremely hard however his lectures are very clear. He has many double negatives in exam questions to fool students.

He is honestly a really good professor. The clicker questions can be tricky but once you get it, you will get it on the exam. He is really cares about helping and teaching you. You learn a lot and if you work hard and go to class you will pass. Taking AP Bio also helps.  Currently taking his 152 class and it has been great also.

Caleb Rounds is a great professor. He tries his hardest to explain the material as clear as possible only sometimes getting a little confusing. His tests are pretty tough but as long as you study the quizzes (on-line, on your own time) and clicker questions as well as the lectures, you'll do fine.

I also had rounds for 151 and he is a really great teacher once you get used to his style of teachingtesting. The material itself was pretty easy for me (taking AP Bio definitely helps), but sometimes it is still hard to do well on the exams because of their annoying wording. He is willing to help students and always enthusiastic. Go to class!
He's willing to change answers on exams so as long as you can back up your thinking, there's a good chance that you'll get points back. Exams are similar to clicker and quiz questions.

His classes really make you think about the concepts behind the material, and he makes it clear that he wants his students to get more out of his class than just route memorization (that won't help you do well anyway). If you are confused ASK QUESTIONS either outside class (he's very helpful at office hours) or in class if you feel comfortable.
A lot of clicker questions, but answering them and critically thinking about them really really does help

If you can avoid him, do so at all costs. He expects you to know what he's talking about in class before the lecture and the notes are no help either. The only way to pass is to do really well on the weekly quizzes and weekly homework he gives.

I cried so many times last semester because i failed almost all the midterms. do hw and other things to bring your grade up if your not a good test taker like me. Avoid him as a professor because he dent word his questions on exams well. But you do get extra credit for the questions most of the class dsnt get right.
This class was terrible. His iclickers are all tricky and so are his exams. Try to take this class with someone else or youll ruin your gpa

Caleb is an awesome professor - his lectures are interesting and funny, plus, his clicker questions really make you think. However, his tests are heavily critical thinking & class based, so you have to attend lectures in order to do well on them. This class is not an easy A, but despite it being my hardest class this semester, it was my favorite.

Caleb's class is definitely challenging - especially if you haven't taken AP biology in high school. Although I did take AP bio during my junior year, I still had to dedicate a lot of my time to studying for his class because the exams are mostly critical thinking rather than knowledge based. Just be sure to review his lectures before exams!!!

Caleb is not a good professor at all. He doesn't know how to explain and his exams and iclickers are tricky on purpose. In the discussion everyone had good grades and he made us have a "quiz" from the middle of the semester and after that we had to solve by ourselves and not in a group so tht our grade became worse and his average stayed as a BB-.

He's terrible! He never teaches you anything and if I didn't have any bio background I wouldve failed this class. All he does is iclickers and he goes through them super fast and doesn't explain them clearly at all. He tries to explain them only if most of the class got it wrong. His exams are super hard too. He's obsessed with having an 80% avg.

Dr Rounds makes attendance and attention a requirement(iclicker). His exams are vigorous and he expects you to read the textbook and lecture visuals inside out. Weekly online quiz and homework assignments are an easy A, giving you a nice grade booster for Cs on your exams; you could end up with a B+A- if done right. Funny guy, but demands studying

He's defo the best among all the other professors for BIO 151. A kinda challenging class but if you put lots of efforts and study hard, A is still possible. Participation matters as everything you learn in class is important for the tests. I especially like how he teaches by asking you questions and solving it. Btw he is super nice and very SMART!

caleb is awesome, i definitely think he's the best of the bio 151 profs at umass. if you go to lectures and do the readings, which are light and don't take too long, you shouldn't have too much trouble. his lectures are engaging, he explains things clearly, and his practice tests match his exams. (they're still pretty tricky tho. study up.)

My favorite teacher at UMass.  Engages the class with questions at every turn and makes sure everyone understands the material.  Very nice and has great TA's.  If you need to take bio151, its this professor rather than the others, as you will do much better with Caleb

Although attendance isn't mandatory, I highly recommend you attend - you get credit just for answering iClicker questions, whether you're right or wrong.  All of his quizzes and exams are multiple choice and truefalse, and you get a week to do the weekly homework. He's a great professor, and his class and exams rely heavily on critical thinking.

He is a great professor and I really enjoyed it. He expects you to actually think. Read the section in the book before class to understand, but dont study from the text. The exams are difficult and all, but they are very similar to clicker questions and quizzes. Class avrg. is a 82!! Each exam is only 10% of grade. Discussion counts for a lot.

While his classes are genuinely hard, he does what he can to make sure most of the class understands- he gives difficult iclicker questions for the class to answer, and if there is a split, he explains further. He makes himself and TAs available as much as possible. Almost all of notes are on the slides, which he shares with class.

He's actually a really good professor. I actually learn in that class lol. There's a lot of information to memorizecover. I do fairly well on the midterms (86%, 74%, 93%) considering how i havent taken bio since 1st semester freshmen yr of high school and i can keep up. his clicker qs are very similar to exam qs. theyre challenging but helpful.

Not a bad prof, he is just often SUPER confusing . Questions (iClicker and on the test) are very wordy and confusing. He could ask the same questions in a much clearer manner. He even trips himself up with his own questions! If you have a solid background in bio, I would recommend him. Tests only count for 10%. Flexible prof, will listen to you.

Caleb is a good teacher once you're used to the way his questions are worded. I would assume it would be way more difficult if you have not taken bio in a few years, however if you have taken AP or a previous course the material is not that hard, mostly review. Study clicker questions for tests and go to SI sessions they are very helpful

Rounds is knowledgable about the subject, and his passion for biology clearly shows through his lectures. He is extremely willing to help his students, and wants them all to succeed. His tests are tough though, he will word things in a confusing manner. Expect lots of true or false questions, and some possible "might be true".

Look, he's a good guy, but his style of teaching is erratic and no one ever knows what to expect on his test. He once said, "Don't study. Ask questions." So that gives you a view on his teaching style. The whole class is i-Clicker questions and more critical thinking.

He's a nice person and he means well but he deviates from the book and makes all of his own questions which prove to be very difficult. His tests are hard. Skipping class is not a good idea or else you will be very confused. If there is an easier teacher I would consider taking them over Caleb. His class is definitely a challenge. Uses iClicker.
Ive never taken Bio before and this class is super hard. Go to class and the  SI sessions. show up for class for clicker questions which can save your butt
Please do yourself a favor and avoid him at all costs.

He simplifies many things. He doesn't teach some important stuff. His questions are sometimes challenging. He teaches Bio in a different way. He always stays after class and answers my questions. He knows a lot about plant physiology. His exams are more straightforward than other professors.

I have never taken an biology class and his materials are so confusing. But I know Caleb is the guy who will help me improve my biological science skills. He challenges me, and I like that the most about professors.

Literally killed my love for biology. Tests were unreasonable. What kind of professor puts a 3rd option for  true and false questions unless you want to screw over your students on the exam? A) True B) False C) could be true. The lectures were interactive but he doesn't explain concepts very well.
He is a funny guy and very likable but his tests are difficult if you have not previously taken Bio. Also he doesn't explain concepts that well which makes the class ten times more difficult.

Caleb is really helpful and always willing to go the extra mile to explain concepts (he even made a twitter dedicated to asking questions in class). The lectures are genuinely challenging to understand but he does a good job teaching it. All in all, as long as you read the book and attend the lectures, and study HARD for the tests, its doable.
STAY AWAY ! His tests are not only really hard, but he doesn't teach concepts, and you start falling behind because he doesn't explain things.

Caleb is a great professor, but be prepared: his tests are really challenging. The lecture slides are all you need and everything is based off the diagrams from class. I love his class because he tells you everything you need to know and everything that will be on the exams- there's not a lot of book reading as well. Great class, will take again!

He will never explain something to you, but instead will ask you questions which he says makes you come up with the answer - not much help if you're lost. Tests were quite hard. I remembered things long enough to take the test and after that lost them. He skips around a lot and doesn't teach the material in a logical order.
He expects you to know everything he knows

I really recommend staying away from this teacher, unless you've had previous experience with biology. He doesn't explain basic concepts, and basically assumes that you know them. He is a really nice teacher, but his class IS HARD if you haven't taken AP Bio or some sort of advanced biology class.
Lecture is REALLY important. Especially for tests, but he makes them interactive which is nice.

He is a great professor. The stuff you need to learn is hard, but he tries really REALLY hard to make everyone learn.  You will need to buy a clicker. I enjoy using them, and in class, the questions he makes us answer really help us learn.  Go to SI sections because it will clarify anything. There is always someone to help.

I took this class because I had to, and I regret it. You will read something and then he will start talking about it weeks later. Readings DO NOT correspond to class whatsoever. Basically he talks about whatever the hell he wants in class and no matter how well you keep up with the reading you are going to be confused in class. Good luck.

I am taking his bio class as a freshman and am about to change my major becuase if he is the best professor in the field then there is no way I am getting into med school. He is all over the place and the homework does not go along with the class. He does not explain things clearly and I have been ready to cry in the middle of class with confusion.

I love Caleb! He's so funny and makes things memorable. He's always willing to answer questions and help when needed. Don't listen to reviews and just take him because I can guarantee the other professors aren't nearly as good.
his teaching is very back and forth and scattered. He's passionate but it's very hard to follow

He is an incredible lecturer and super super funny, but the content of the class is really difficult to understand a few weeks in, and it only gets more difficult. There's barely any homework you actually have to do, the grades come from weekly discussion sections where there's one graded question on anything from the lectures, so you gotta lock in

Made lectures very entertaining and explained everything thoroughly. Make sure you attend the lectures because the video recordings make it very hard to read the board. The readings are not that helpful, and all the content you will need to know is from the lectures.

Funny guy who I think makes the content interesting. Attendance not mandatory for lectures but I recommend going because he writes a lot on board which is hard to see on Echo360. Good amount of reading assigned but I didn't find them too important for getting work done. Only assignments were weekly question in discussion, 4 freebies.

This is the best class I've taken in my life, I was heavily engaged in every lecture, which is all that really matters for this class. ALL THE WEEKLY QUESTIONS AND TESTS ARE ANSWERABLE FROM THE LECTURES. Doing the readings actually make this class harder and makes the material more complicated than it needs to be.
Pay attention and the class is easy. Very entertaining lectures.

I dont even know how to explain this, lectures are boring and confusing, readings are boring, useless and confusing, and very overwhelming. Most of the readings are in old English so get ready to be confused. Chill professor, just a terrible course to take if you're not a philosophy  major. This class is curved so you're graded against your class.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: You will be graded in comparison to your classmates and have to compete for an A! This worked out for me although I resent this grading style. I will say the lectures were very structured and the tests were straightforward, so as long as you study the questions on the study guide, you will know what to say on the tests.Heavy reading (not important)
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: The class sucked, but the professor was good. The topics weren't what I thought they would be. I tanked the first midterm, so I chose to pass/fail. Exams are pure memorization. Even though attendance isn't mandatory, I'd highly recommend it because you can't read his writing when watching the recordings (Grainy).
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Based off the other reviews here I consider myself lucky. I enjoyed my time in Phil164 and I think that comes to my TA, I had a great TA who was fun to talk about the topics and easy to reach. For a philosophy class there is not much discussion mainly retention of reading so don't come into class expecting anything super profound.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Horrible. As a senior in college with a double major and pre-med this was the only class i have ever gotten an A- in. Got over a 95 and still didnt get an A. SO happy for my fellow students that got 100s all semester but being graded on a curve is insane and harmful to students. might as well all give up together. TA missed pages on my exam grading
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: I should've listened to the other warnings. The TAs grade everything and they're so strict and unclear with the grading if u get unlucky with urs. Little to no feedback when u receive a bad grade. The curve is also confusing but they say it's supposed to help us in the end?? Idek. I seriously wouldn't take this class unless you absolutely HAD to.

The grades on assignments and tests are quiz based, and graded unfairly harsh for a Gen Ed. It was very frusterating, slides were never used, the writing on the chalkboard was illegible and audio was missing in online lectures.The sound of the chalk scratching the chalkboard and the amount of chalk flying around is also quite annoying.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Don't take this class

I really wanted this class, even ignoring all previous ratings, to get exactly what we were warned:

- Midterms with little critical thinking (just super specific memorization)
- Only covering a few topics of actual ethical concerns in medicine (right to life, abortion, disability)
-grade-deflating curves
- 'talk-at-you-and-not-with-you' lectures

All this course does is force you to memorize a bunch of random nonsense, and tests on pure memory, instead of critical thinking. The curve is bogus, as sometimes a 48/50 isn't even an A on a test, and its infuriating and makes no sense to be pit up against our peers. DO NOT take this self deprivation tank of a course if you value your time/energy!

I dropped this class after the first day-best decision ever. Not worth it for an AT Gen-Ed considering how test-heavy the class is. You are also graded on a curve in comparison to how the rest of the class does
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Meacham is a cold, impersonable professor. In 164, you would expect discussions to be about sharing our perspectives on ethical problems, but no, just recapping lecture material. No interaction with peers or challenging others' ideas, no creativity; just memorizing notes/readings so you can replicate it on an exam. This class is WASTED POTENTIAL.

Good class but NOT a good choice for genEd! 3 tests & weekly discussion assignments r the whole grade. discussion helps... if u get a good TA. Grades depend on how everyone else does. 56 on the 1st exam was a B+ w/scale. U won't know where u stand until final grades come out. Use study questions to prep 4 exams! Material is interesting but bizarre.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: he writes on the chalkboard so if you miss a lecture you don't get the notes. 3 exams all with a lot to memorize but if you know what you're talking about it's easy. weekly assignments were a bit harder since the TA grades it but those weren't bad either
HE IS A GREAT TEACHER, MADE ME WANT TO MAJOR IN PHILOSOPHY, I DON'T KNOW HOW I GOT A B+ LOL WAS EXPECTING AN A OR STH

Medical ethics is a great philosophy course. It focuses a lot on the philosophy side of learning, which works really well if you have a logic / math oriented mind. 
Chris gives great lectures, interesting material, and its not a hard course. It is graded on a curve though. 

GREAT medium difficulty gen ed.
Interesting course.
Do NOT take Professor Meacham for medical ethics. He doesn't use slides, the Echo videos are very very poor quality, and he's not even an ethics professor.

Unclear study guides, expects you to memorize word for word specifics about topics. TA's are unhelpful and offer no feedback on assignments but are quick to give you a bad grade. The weekly assignments you are expected to master the reading content before Monday lectures. You have to do that when the professor lectures the readings. Waste of time.
reviews.rating_tags: So many papers--Graded by few things

reviews.comment:
i strongly dislike this class man. prepare to be stressed to the next level because you will not understand a single thing in your readings and lectures. go to discussions because that's the only way you'll learn anything. 

also a side note his voice is very annoying.

I worked so hard to do well in this class, much harder than my actual major classes. Everything is open response on homework and exams, no opportunity for extra credit. You must memorize word for word everything or else your answer is wrong. Homework questions are knit picky. So much to read. Spent hours upon hours studying or else I woulda failed.
