reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: AVOID taking this class!! You have a weekly assignment every week and are given no feedback on how to improve! Lectures are recorded but he does not have any slides! Tests are not too bad, all based from the lecture! Discussion sections are not mandatory! Everything is graded on a curve and you do not know your grade until the end of the semester!
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: I took this class because I needed to fill a gen ed, and this class seemed interesting. However, it was probably the worst decision I have ever made. He grades on a curve compared to how well the class does. So if I do bad and others do good, I do even worse. Never take this. Avoid at all costs
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Test heavy

reviews.comment: Chris is an excellent professor, and you should take his class if you want to learn and have a good time doing so. However, there's a catch. He chooses to grade on a curve, which means that the grade you receive is not entirely dependent on you. It's very demotivating and frankly, archaic. What would otherwise be a top shelf class is dragged down.
Aced every assignment and exam, didn't receive an A from the curve downwards.

The grading scale sucks. He doesn't care about students during a WHOLE pandemic! One week before finals he changed the final to 3 separate long essays and DON'T get me started on the questions. Take it with another professor or take it online. AVOID at all costs! Lectures and discussions are boring and useless.
The grading curve is terrible. The assignments were annoying and he is not clear on what he expects from the assignments. DO NOT TAKE THIS CLASS.

The grading scale in this class is ridiculous. As quoted by a TA they do not grade you on material learned but rather how you perform against your classmates. He also changed the final into 3 separate full length essays a couple weeks prior to final week. Even acing exams means nothing from the curve, do not take as a gen ed!

Anyone planning to take this class needs a big red flag before doing so. While Chris is an excellent and hilarious lecturer, the grading scale is extremely harsh. For our first two exams, the cutoff for an A was a 97%. It was extremely demotivating to study and do well, receive a 96% on exams and still not get an A.

He's very funny and a great professor. Class is never boring but tests are based on lectures, so you should try to come to every class. Grades are on a curve, so study more than everyone else. He doesn't give much work except you have a one page assignment due every week, which are also graded on a curve. Really easy arts gen-ed!
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Hilarious--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: Great guy, super funny. Very easy A, one of the easiest classes ive ever taken. >30 min of hw/week. Studied >2 hours for each exam. Class is scaled which helps. Highly recommend. interesting lectures too.

as long as you go to class and take notes you will do well. there are 13 easy one-page papers but you can skip four of them. he gives a study sheet before each of the three tests and as long as you can understand everything on the sheet you will do well on the test. your grades are based on how well you do compared to the other students
reviews.rating_tags: Accessible outside class--Skip class? You won't pass.--Hilarious

reviews.comment: Chris is an awesome, funny, nice guy. Class is v little work. One page assignment due once a week w/ a Q from the reading but I think I've read a total of 5 pages for this class. You can usually afford to skip a lecture in the week bc discussion section is just review mainly. All grades are curved so getting a good TA doesn't matter so much

Easy A. You have to do 9 one-page papers based on the readings, but the readings are easy, I only did the ones I had to. You can't skip class because he doesn't post slides online, but as long as you go and take notes the tests are easy. The grading is very confusing because the TAs are in charge of it, which would be my only complaint.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: A really interesting class but not a super easy gen-ed. Readings are somewhat difficult but you really only need to do the readings for the weekly papers, which can be hard but there is good tutoring. The grading is pretty fair and the tests are very straightforward if you attend lecture and take good notes
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Respected--Skip class? You won't pass.

reviews.comment: Chris was great in the first section however once we started talking about abortion and affirmative action policies, he lost me. He was offensive (comparing mentally challenged people to dogs), inaccurate (making extremist claims for the sake of proving his point), and he thought he could make a few sex jokes and everyone would love him regardless.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Clear grading criteria--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: I took this as a gened and is one of the best classes I took at UMass. Chris is hilarious in a weird way and his delivery of material made what could have been a mundane class into an interesting one. All necessary material is in lecture, so go. TAs run discussions &offer support. Short written assignments and 3 written exams. Definitely recommend.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Hilarious--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: Chris is incredibly smart and inspires interest in the subject. Lectures are necessary. You will NOT pass without them. But they're super interesting; you just need to follow along! He seems non-approachable but when I email him he's super helpful and timely. Great course. Learned so much. Not to mention he's hilarious, hilarious, hilarious!
Good professor overall, made classes interesting. Used a lot of unique examples. Tests were very to-the-point. Had a bad temper though that made him seem way less accessible.

EASY EASY EASY. People complaining about this being hard probably didn't attend lecture. Chris writes everything on the board that you need to know for exams. Class is ridiculously easy as long as you attend lecture. Lectures are entertaining due to Chris' humor, excessive swearing, and squeaky voice. Best class I've taken at Umass.

SUPER DIFFICULT FOR A GEN ED. You can memorize all of the notes taken in class and receive C's on all exams. TA's do not grade clearly and discussions do not help your grade. Overall, you will stay completely lost in this class with no opportunity for help or explanations.  Do not take!!!!

HARD. HARD. HARD. This was the hardest GenEd class I've ever taken. Grade is only based off weekly assignments and 3 exams. No extra credit and no opportunity to raise your grade. If you get stuck with a bad TA, you're SOL.

Lectures can be long but Chris does a good job at adding comical moments. The class isn't difficult if you go to lecturesdiscussions. Grading depends on your TA, not many assignments but they can be confusing. Exams require studying but lecture notes are very straightforward to the exam.

Such a funny guy and very clear. The tests are not very hard and the work load is light. Attendance isn't mandatory but it helps so much for the tests and if you go to the lecture you don't really have to do the assigned readings. Very interesting and pretty easy class, I definitely recommend taking it as a gened.

Even though the material was not very interesting since I only took it to fulfill a GenEd, Chris lightened the mood of the class with funny examples. There is a discussion section too. Not too bad, definitely should go to class because the tests are questions based on lecture notes. Definitely need to study but overall not a bad class.

Prof. Meacham explains the material very clearly from the philosophical readings you're supposed to do outside of class. Though attendance isn't mandatory, go to class. It'll make all tests so much easier. The examples he gives are pretty funny.

Chris is very intelligent and does a great job explaining the philosophical theories in the area of ethics. No textbook, just readings from some very prominent philosophers. Go to class, it's only 50 minutes and there's less than 2 pages of handwritten notes each time, and you still learn everything you need to know. My favorite class this semester

Terrific professor! Very captivating and absolutely hilarious. No text book, just online reading selections. Attendance is not necessary, but the test questions, open response,  are directly related to the notes he writes on the board. The only down side of this class is that it has a discussion section :(
In order to do well in this class you have to go to class, no questions. Everything on the exams you learn in class, sometimes the topics are unclear, and the TAs aren't helpful at all.

Meacham has no concept of ethical philosophy at all. He does not distinguish between morals and ethics, presents no analysis of natural law and human nature, and the whole class is just him presenting farfetched, irrational examples of noname want-to-be philosophers. This class taints ethical philosophy to be something it is not. Do not take it.

He really makes class interesting. If you go to lecture you'll do well in the class. He doesn't drag on and teaches in a way that will keep your interest. He's a little out there but he's a fun guy to take a class with. I'd recommend this class/teacher.

There are weekly 1 page assignments. They can be as long as you want within the page limit as long as you answer the assignment questions. Exams (which are written) are lecture based so memorization is key. Chris makes funny, memorable examples. TAs grade the assignments and exams, but it's based on a curve. Good class to take.

Chris is a very charismatic guy and can easily draw your attention on the course subject. If you need this class for a gen ed its an easy way to get a good grade if you attend the lectures and take notes. He's also really funny.

This class is interesting. Attendance is optional but you need to go to lecture in order to understand the notes. He is slightly crazy but funny. There are 3 tests based on the lecture notes and a one page response paper due every week, but you can skip 4. Pretty good class I recommend it.

Go to class to understand the notes. Tests are directly from the lectures.  Papers can be annoying but if you choose the option to write your opinion then they're easy to get a good grade. Great class.
Gives interesting examples, rights on the chalk board. Weekly 1 page paper, and 3 exams.

for philosophy of ethics - amazing amazing amazing. awesome guy, awesome teacher, awesome class. inspired me to switch my major to philosophy. more thought provoking than any other class i've ever taken.
Awesome professor!! Would take the class again in a heartbeat. He keeps it interesting and entertaining. His analogies are crazy. Very easy class.

He is great! He can clear anything up with a hilarious analogy - so the material is easy to remember because he's so funny. There's no pressure even though it was a small class because there's no participation grade. The class really made me think and I would recommend it to anyone.

This was a great class, and Chris Meacham is a great teacher.  He is funny and you can tell that he is really interested in the stuff he is teaching.  He is very good at clearing up points of confusion, and makes everything really easy to understand with (often ridiculous and hilarious) analogies.  Definitely take this class if you can!
He was the most incredible teacher i think I've ever had. He explain things very well and is hilarious. He absolutely caters to his audience and knows how to connect the material to relatable topics.

Good lecturer. He keeps the class fats paced and interesting. He encourages participation (even in 250 people lectures) but has no problem putting people in their place, which is kind of funny. He swears a lot, which is weird at first, and then is cool, and then gets kind of old. But whatever.  His notes are clear, but you have to study to do well.

Even though the class was small he refused to learn people's names which was cool bc you could skip wo consequences. Midterm was easy and his lectures are hilarious because his examples are ridiculous and full of swears. interesting class over all. I reccomend it.

The class was funny.  Meacham definitely kept lectures interesting because he was all over the place.  His notes are clear and he provides relevant examples, but he doesn't answer questions very well.  The TAs sucks; they all think you're a philosophy major.  It's graded on a curve, so it is easy to do well.  Not a bad Gen Ed.
I didn't go a lot to this class.  It was an easy B though.  Make sure you go to discussion the week before the final and midterm.

Chris is cool and keeps class interesting with funny examples and lots of swearing. If you do the readings and go to class you'll do well, discussion doesnt matter, doesnt take attendance in lecture or discussion, all readings on spark...weekly 1pg responses a midterm and a final...ok for a gened

Professor Meacham is a nice guy. Class does little to explain ethical theory in application, and while the history is appreciable, most of the stuff he talks about is not relevant to real practice. He treats the students like children, and he makes many extremely crude jokes, but is thoughtful if you talk in person. Picks worst TA's, awful graders.
DO NOT TAKE IT. nobody even knows what hes talking about. ever.

Class says no previous music knowledge required, which is completely untrue. He talks to fast and half of the things he says have no correlation to what is on the quizzes, which we have like twice a week. The class is extremely boring and super hard for no reason. Don't take for gen ed!
He talks too fast and nothing he explains in the class shows up on the absurdly hard exams that happen twice a week.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Beware of pop quizzes--Test heavy

reviews.comment: Loved Chris, he's clearly very aware that most of the kids in this class are non music majors so don't worry if you don't have any type of music experience. The material is difficult enough that you have to study but easy enough to keep up, he's always glad to answer questions and review and clearly enjoys what he does. Also clearly loves bow-ties.

I have heard a lot of things about Ciesielski before I took ECE124 but he is better than previous years have stated. Grading style is similar to Engin112 with lowest 2 hw grades be dropped so that is nice. His lectures are at time hard to follow but the textbook helps a lot too. Biggest advice is ask question after class or officer hours.
reviews.rating_tags: Clear grading criteria--Lots of homework--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: I would just suggest not to take this class online, that's it.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Lots of homework

reviews.comment: Took this class as an alternative to the other VLSI class. Prof. Ciesielski is incredibly invested in teaching his students, going to his office hours will truly help you understand concepts better. Trying to decipher the notes & textbook alone is impossible so make sure to collaborate with other students and ask questions during class.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Gives good feedback--Caring

reviews.comment: This class was great! During lecture he sometimes talks about stuff we hadn't learned yet but he's happy to answer any questions and explain, which he does well. His office hours are great, he's a really nice guy. There is an auxiliary textbook but you don't really need it as long as you dedicate time to understanding the homeworks

unless this class is required for your major, DON'T take it. professors worse than him are hard to come by. midterm avg was a 58 and he wouldn't curve and was just impolite, additionally there have been several cases of him crashing out on his students. i'm giving him a 2 because hes passionate and could be better if he tried

Ciesielski is incredibly smart and kind, his hate is undeserved. He isn't perfect, but he can explain difficult topics pretty well. Homework is usually pretty long and tough, but if you can grasp the homework, you're golden for the exams. Show up, pay attention and study! Just don't expect it to be a walk in the park, it is engineering after all.

to address the no empathy, being impolite, rude etc. I would just say respect goes both ways. It's clear people don't care, (back of the lecture sounds like a gym locker room, maybe 8 people outta 200 go to office hours, etc). It's a two way street, respect him and he'll do the same

Go to office hours, he'll basically guarantee you get 100s on the hw and will also drop hints and tell you whats on the test or not. Make an effort, show that you care, and he'll reciprocate and help since most of the class doesn't do that, shown by the low test scores even thou they're the exact same as the practice. Just my personal experience.

cont. You have to reciprocate in your effort thou. Honestly the crashouts are justified. Every lecture the entire back quarter of the class is always talking extremely loudly and he has to stop class multiple times to get people to be quiet. It's clear most of the class doesn't care. I studied for the tests ~8 hours each and did completely fine.

Ifl I should post this to defend him, just personal experience thou.
Lectures can be confusing, HW can be hard, highly reconmmend going to office hours, he'll basically walk you through all the problems and will stay there wayyy past to make sure all questions are answered. It's clear in office hours he wants you to do well and does care.

Very tough course. Last year, almost everyone got A's due to a generous curve. This professor made the tests harder and barely curved like changing the C cutoff from 78.99 to 78.8. Half the class's GPA took a hit. No empathy or support. Would not recommend taking this course with him.

Withdraw immediately. He is super bad with his lectures and super rude. The homework's are near impossible, and take up to 5 hours for the hard ones. The tests are super difficult as well, so buckle up. Overall a terrible professor and should not be allowed to teach this class especially because it is difficult enough as it is.
terrible, impossible to understand anything in lecture

Overall not that bad. He's fair enough. His homework is indeed hard. You are supposed to spend hours (at least 5+) on the hard ones to get a 90+ score. You will struggle for sure. But struggling is the very nature of engineering lol. Since this is an intro lvl class it might give you a shock. Get used to the HWs your grade will be fine
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Gives good feedback

reviews.comment: Smart guy but expects you to know everything. He really cares for your understanding of concepts and will help you succeed if you show some effort. Make sure to revise concepts after class.

I don't know what happened last year, but while he doesn't have the best lectures and isn't the best at answering questions, as long as you read the textbook and take notes from the book you'll do fine in the class. He is VERY lenient with extensions, giving multiple day extensions for every homework we had. Don't be lazy and you'll be fine.
reviews.rating_tags: Caring--Graded by few things--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: One of the worst in Umass, please widthdraw from his class
really rude guy
Never taking this professors class
Really impolite to class.

Ciesielski's lectures are terribly boring, but the material he talks about is almost all relevant to the exams. I found just watching Ciesielski lecture and taking notes from his slides after class to be the best way for me to learn. The practice exams are similar to the exams, but look at the slides as well. You don't need to read the book at all.
Knows what he is talking about, but very very very boring in lecture.

Not very clear.  Supplement the lectures with the slides he posts online.  The subject isn't too hard, but don't make the mistake I did of skipping discussion, Prof. Vouvakis isn't a nice guy but he does a far better job explaining the material and basically tells you how to do the homework.

Ciesielski was not very good in the lecture. He was especially bad at answering questions. That said the course is easy enough to get by just reading the lecture slides, the textbook, and going to discussion.

The lecture wasn't very enlightening, and was often quite boring. If you start skipping the lectures, MAKE SURE you read the textbook. Attending the discussion sections is very important if you want to know how to solve the problems.
Hes  good if you go to his Extra help sessions, otherwise hes really not. Hard subject but with discussion and extra help its not bad.

Half the class slept through every single lecture. I stopped attending halfway through the semester when I realized that I would learn twice as much just reading the slides on my own time (and I was far from the only one). Without discussion sections (prof. anderson!) this class would have been an utter mystery to the vast majority of students.
He is a really good professor. To get the most benefit you should go and see him during his office hours.

If you want to see VLSI from the top-view this course is brilliant. Very well executed, a good balance of theory, practicality and use of tools. Its offered every other year, make sure you don't miss it.

reviews.comment: Lots of writing but I have taken several of her classes and have always got an A. She expects a lot of effort compared to other courses but marks very fairly. I like her classes because its always the same structure and expectations. If you are literate you can get a good mark in any of her classes.

I wish I'd have read the reviews for R.C. before taking her class. She posts ~30+ website links for us per week, having us sort through hours of readings from the internet.  Then we write around 1,000 words every week in homework and discussion posts and responses.  Her "lectures" are 5 min long descriptions of the readings.  Very disappointing.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Lots of homework

reviews.comment: Ciulla doesn't have a teaching style. You have a teaching style. The only teaching done is by yourself. You read and you read then you write and you write. She has the most work to complete and spends the least amount of time teaching.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Lots of homework

reviews.comment: Shes so smart and has a lot of experience in Ag which would be so helpful if her homework wasn't so mind-numbingly boring. It is just link upon links of monotonous articles which you then have to regurgitate in at least 300 words minimum. I hate her classes, spare yourself the headache.

Renee is a nice person who knows a lot about agriculture, so it's a shame that she rarely lectures. There are two homeworks due on Thursday and Sunday at 7pm, that are 1.5-2 pages long. All the material in the class is just links to random websites and articles, most of which are arduous to read, and boring. She also doesn't allow any late work

Ultimately had to withdraw from this class midway through the semester. I wanted to like Renee, she's a nice person and easy to talk to but assigns so much work with hard deadlines to make (7pm on both Thursdays and Sundays every week). Also has a minimum word count on weekly homework (usually at least 450 words). Overall pretty inaccessible class.

Took Sustainable Ag. Renee is super kind, but this may as well have been an online class (boo). All educational components are online blackboard posts and readings. Assignments are long and boring. We visit farms once a week as our only face-to-face time, tours are cool but we end up spend hours doing free labor for the farm more than learning.

reviews.comment: Organic vegetable production is a great class and Renee is a wonderful and inspiring teacher. We took lots of field trips and were able to gain hands-on experience and understanding of the course material.

No lectures for entire class, had us read from websites as main source of information for class, did not moderate online forum until after weekly discussions, where lots of incorrect information was stated. Very disappointed in how little information I got from this class.

If you don't consider Dr. Civjan to be an excellent professor, you are in the wrong major. He is more than fair in his grading and is truly passionate about what he does. He wants you to learn and cares about the success of his students.

Dr. Civjan was an amazing professor, he really cared about his students even offering to meet up and set up office hours to help with homework. Pretty flexible with homework deadlines as long as you provided an acceptable reason. Homeworks were pretty lengthy but could easily be done with the manual and lecture notes.

It is because of professors like Dr. Civjan that I love civil engineering! 5. He's hard but so worth it, his lectures are of amazing quality and he is extremely accessible outside of class, and has moderate sense of humor.

terrible grading system, way too much homework and readings, grades exams and homework unfairly, this class alone took up as much time as all my other classes combined (took 5 including strengths), unclear/trick exam questions, spend hours in the library studying, good luck for real ill be praying for you, the only thing is the lectures are good

Let me specify that this was a hard class. Understanding Statics is 100% a prereq. for doing well in this class. Civjan gave lots of HW but was very clear on what exams would cover. His lecturing in class was helpful for understanding the chapter material and the examples would help with the copious amount of HW. Go to class & find a study buddy!

A nice professor who cares about teaching the content and the class. However, he makes the class much harder than it needs to be. Long homework assignments, extra written assignments, and these assignments do not fully match what we prepare for on exams. Definitely a class set up to not fail, but not get an A. Would not take again.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Lots of homework--So many papers

reviews.comment: There is a lot of homework for this class, which takes up a lot of time. Examples in class don't really help that much with the homework to be honest. Overall, doesn't teach the best for me. Makes you turn in homework in person.

If your structural interested take this class. It will be a lot of work but it is very much worth it. HW's are involved but doing them really helps prepare for the exams. He grades everything himself for this class so grades come out quickly. With adapt class to feel and flow of semester and students. Has great intuition of students understanding.

Civjan cares about his students doing well. The course is not easy but he teaches it in a way that made it bearable. Homework's do take a lot of time but they help a lot when trying to comprehend the topics taught. Would take a class with him again.

Dr. Civjan is the ideal professor. He is very caring and checked in on how we were often and changed workload depending on how we were. He gave prerecorded lecture videos that were not super draining or time-consuming. He had zoom lectures to review and answer questions. Weekly HW sometimes difficult and long but were the only assignments + exams.

The material professor Civjan teaches is far from easy, but I think if anyone else was teaching it I wouldnt do nearly as well. He is really good at explaining the tough material in his lectures. Homeworks are really tough but they are important for understanding the topics.
Tough class but if you put the work in it's great. Prof Civjan is a great guy, one of my favorite classes I've taken.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Lots of homework--Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: He gives sooo much homework but it's very helpful for learning material. Very strict about using online sources though.

reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Lots of homework--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: Prof Civjan is probably the most thorough professor I have had in CEE. reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Get ready to read--Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: Prof. Civjan, along with prof. Brena, are by far the best professors in the Umass CEE dept. It is obvious he is both brilliant at what he does and enjoys it as well. Take his classes, I promise you will not regret it. Homework can take time but they are fair assignments. Take notes, pay attention in class, do the homework and you will succeed

I'm a senior and Civjan is the best teacher in the dept. He's straight forward, his hw is challenging but reasonable. I wish he taught all of my other classes. He actually wants to be here, and wants you to succeed, it's very refreshing. He's the first prof that has made me consider getting my Phd.

Best CEE professor! I took class with mixed feelings, and although it was not easy, I loved it! None other class was anywhere near the real-life problems encountered here. He does not let you repeat generic problems, but teaches you creative thinking while doing design/consulting type problems.

Had this teacher for Steel.  I learned a lot, but did not think this teacher was fair.  Went to every class and still had a hard time of what the teacher was talking about.  He did not help, even when I asked during class.  He will either like you or not.  My least favorite teacher at Umass Amherst
Explains material very well, helpful example problems and relevant homework. Fair grader and one of the most helpful professors I have had at UMass.

World Cinema and Fashion (different course) were amazing. Extremely knowledgeable, enthusiastic, and encouraging Prof. Lectures and screenings were well thought out. Discussions and activities were also fire. Readings and assignments can be challenging but are helpful to explore the topics.

well worth it, material is interesting and teacher is very knowlegeable and enthusiastic about world cinema, grading is also fair and you'll learn alot if you go to class and do the work

Good meaningful class. The professor cares deeply for art and community and really helped students to learn and get involved. There were lots of opportunities to develop skills and apply concepts individually and in group projects which were fun too.

Prof C is a little disorganized, but she was mostly OK. She definitely has a tendency to interrupt student led discussions, sometimes in an uncomfortable way. She's great! It's unfortunate that SBS students can't get major credit from any WGSS classes, because what I'm learning from her is VERY relevant to what I'm doing in Soc. Professor C is the best professor I've had at UMass. She's great at facilitating discussions and explaining difficult material. She assigns of lot of reading, but it's all interesting and you will LEARN in her class. She's also super nice and approachable; the material can be dense but she makes to easy to understand. Take a class with her.

reviews.comment: Professor C. is one of the most passionate and inspirational professors you will ever have. Do not take for a gen ed requirement and you have to be interested in WGSS otherwise you will not make it through.

Professor C is probably one of the best professors at UMass, but definitely don't take her class if you're just looking to fulfill some diversity/global Ed requirement - she will make you work for that grade. That being said, if you are at all considering Women's Studies please take 201 with Professor C. She really cares and will teach you so much.

Professor Ciolkowski is seriously one of the kindest and most intelligent professors. I loved every second of her class. Do not take this class if you are not genuinely interested in feminism and social justice. There is an insane (but usually interesting) amount of reading. There's tons of extra credit and it is an easy A if you care

Carson is on a mission to turn me into a lit scenester!  I would recommend him though; he gave me freedom to write fun and creative papers I normally wouldn't in a writing class.  He uses great sources and tries to expose students to good stuff like Brahms, Machiavelli, and Vonnegut (who would frown on my use of a semicolon).  Go for it!
Excellent sense of both tangibles and intangibles, his mind is like an irrepressible dirigible.
Erudite
English 112 is not the most exciting subject but Carson always made the class fun!  He gives useful feedback on papers and this class was probably the most entertaining class i've had at Umass.
unfit for teaching

carson cistulli. where do i start? if you have him as a teacher then consider yourself blessed by the schedule gods. his clothes alone are reason to come to class. never mind the fact that he's an awesome teacher. just wait until he wears "the bear" you'll know it when you see it.

By far one of my favorite professors so far. He really made the class fun by giving us extra points for using cool words in our essays (fantabulous, mega fly, the bomb diggity) and by always being able to relate ANYTHING to sports. Such a great guy, personality kind of reminds me of Mo Rocca.
A passion for poetry and an excellent grasp of the English language combined with a sense of humour make this prof a winner.
guy is brilliant

If you have a chance to take a class with C-Money then do it! He is very funny and entertaining. He loves sports and The OC, so talk about those in class and you'll get an A. This is actually the first class at UMass I think I just might miss.

Semi easy but lots of work. Only taken because to be a programmer I have to learn about rocks for some reason. I hate the system

Bill is one of my favorite professors at UMass. Clearly cares about what he is talking about and brings that passion for the subject to the lecture. As long as you follow the instructions for the homework assignments, you'll be fine.

Cares about the class and material being taught. Exams are not very difficult. There are very easy small assignments for homework that if you skip will really hurt your grade. Great teacher, Great class!

Not the best class out there. I think the professor is trying but there are a lot of things that are wrong with this class. For one, the sound does not work on the recording and the lectures really are not too cade. However I do think that the professor cares.

Hardest Gen-Ed I ever took! There is a lot of material, and the tests are concept-heavy; also, the review sessions are TA's answering questions. Weekly labs are fun but exhausting. The teacher is inspirational and tries to give helpful life advice. He's definitely a bit of a nerd. The lectures are recorded, but have no sound.

Probably one of the worst courses I have taken at Umass. The labs are very tedious and often have you doing mindless calculations for the sake of nothing. It's not particularly difficult but it is the worst class I have taken at Umass. It's no wonder the geology department recruits so hard with this intro class, it's easy to see its not any good.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--LOTS OF HOMEWORK--TEST HEAVY

reviews.comment: I would really avoid taking any class with this professor at all cost. The lectures slide make absolutely no sense outside of the context of the lecture, this would be fine if he did not fly through the material and you could take notes at a reasonable pace (I write fast). The echo 360's have no sound which makes them useless. The test are ok.

He is a great teacher and incredibly straightforward. If you do all of the readings and take good notes, you will be fine. The amount of effort you put in will correlate fairly with the grade you get. He is a genuine person who really cares about students and the things he teaches.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--ACCESSIBLE OUTSIDE CLASS--Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: He drills in the most important information, speaks to relevant issues. Tests had trick questions and double negatives, which I struggled with, but it only took an extra hour or two of studying to get at least a B. The people that showed up did well. Bill cares. I absolutely adore him. Wish he taught more classes, he's got a lot to offer.

Took Dynamic Earth as a gen ed as an alternative to other sciences, the material was generally easy and he posts all of his lecture slides online (attendance isn't mandatory) but attendance is helpful b/c he emphasizes what is important for exams. 4 exams and drops lowest, barely any homework at all. Very kind and has a funny/sarcastic attitude
reviews.rating_tags: Clear grading criteria--GRADED BY FEW THINGS

reviews.comment: The exams were 90% and homework 10%. There are 4 exams and he drops the lowest grade, which is nice. The homework is a joke and takes 2 seconds. HOWEVER, each exam was only 25 multiple choice. He puts overly specific questions on there and I noticed questions about stuff we didn't even go over until after! No extra credit. Very frustrating.

Professor Clement is a great guy and a solid teacher. If you go for extra help he is really accommodating and sweet. Class was my easiest by far, kind of common sense and a no-brainer. Absolutely would recommend as an easy Physical Science gen ed.

I did not enjoy this class at all! Only took Dynamic Earth for a Gen. Ed. but it was super boring. He only has 4 Exams drops the lowest grade which is 90% of your grade, and a few assignments that require you to write two sentences worth 10% of your grade. The "textbook" was a Geology novel that I did not read but 1 or 2 Q's are on the exams fromit

I greatly enjoyed having professor Clement as a teacher. He is passionate and cares what students think of his class. I would definitely take a class with him again. For GEO101 the best way to do well is to show up for lecture. There are no study guides for tests but if you go to class you'll know what to study.

he loves going beyond what you actually need to know to further educate his students.  attendance is mandatory.  he gives some pop up questions that only count as two points to check up on who is in class.  he is nice but this is a very boring class i was not interested in it as all and its way to hard to be a gen ed or a 1 class.

One of those professors that does not realize 95% of his students are taking the class as a general education requirement. Tries to teach english and writing skills more than geology and 2 of his 3 tests were ridiculously specific in their questioning. There are easier physical science gen. eds. out there, avoid Bill and his arrogance at all costs.

The first test was super rough. I still did okay but a lot of people did not. The next test was A LOT better. I think he realized. The final is all multiple choice this year i think.  I didn't buy the text book but I have done just fine. I think if you go to class everyday and take good notes you wont need it but overall id recommend getting it

He's pretty clear with teaching the slides but he's very old fashioned. You haaaave to read the chapters before the lectures or else you won't understand the exam. He's also gives no study guide and your grade is 25% attendance basically and then exams. I'm not a fan.

Professor Clarke is passionate about what he teaches and fully explains everything. The material was difficult for me to grasp as it was an introductory course about AI; however, it was just a first-year seminar, so the course's assignments simply consisted of easy weekly readings. He was happy to answer questions and gave feedback to each student.

A great TA who's quite helpful in office hours, although it does take time for him to post stuff on Moodle. 348 is pretty laid-back and if you simply do the work and go to his office hours, you will do well.

Justin Clarke was the TA for CS348 and is the best one I have had thus far. He is genuinely helpful on Piazza and easy to talk to. When the professor was busy, Justin was usually fast to respond on Piazza and took time to clarify any misconceptions people have during his office hours.

Chris McDaniel is very knowledgeable about chemistry but frankly, he does not care about his students. Make-Up labs are extremely difficult to get and the grading strongly depends on what TA you have. He accused me of lying about why I needed a make up lab and insulted my character. Almost filed a complaint with disability services over him.

I do like how his class is structured, meaning due dates are consistent and I know what to expect when I go to lab. However, it is confirmed by another chem prof that he does BAIT STUDENTS INTO USING AI. So don't use it cus he will know. Kinda unethical if you ask me, he wants students to get caught and he plans on a few every semester.

I'm sure you're reading the rest of the reviews here and wondering how bad he could possibly be... But he really is as bad as everyone is saying. The lab procedures were all written by him, and they don't work as written. He's incredibly unhelpful in emails, condescending, and overall just seems to think that students aren't worth his time.

Took it 4 years ago. Ok as long as you put in the work outside of class. organized lecturer, makes sure you get through all the material. content is not necessarily above 261, just different pacing. His course fails to introduce complexity early on and does not draw on the modern literature at all. Too by the book and lacking for chem majors.
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Clear grading criteria--Lots of homework

reviews.comment: Organic chemistry lab is something I really enjoyed. However, the method of teaching and the grading is making the class an unbearable hurdle to jump. I think it is very telling as a educator if students come in expressing love for the subject and leave hating the class not because of the content, but because of the pedagogy.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Graded by few things--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: It was hard to communicate just because he was never there. Grading criteria was unclear and there wasn't feedback. Your TA definetly makes or breaks tho

The lab reports were graded by an unforgiving rubric. It's not necessarily conceptually difficult, but it is really easy to lose points for small errors like capitalizing a compound in your report. The labs themselves are pretty fun though.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Lots of homework

reviews.comment: Simply awful. Was so stressed that I had to enter the hypobaric chamber after every class. Do not take.
Genuinely just a bad person who thinks his lab class is more important than individuals.
This instructor was artificially rude to us whenever we questioned him, wish I could give him 0 stars.

McDaniel knows orgo really well, but his treatment of students is seriously concerning. I think we all are mature enough to know professors can't coddle students, but many reports of him denying legally mandated accommodations are troubling. If these allegations are true, it's unacceptable that he is getting away with it whenever he runs orgo lab.

Never take a class with McDaniel when you can take it with Surampudi. Orgo is naturally challenging, yet McDaniel exacerbates the difficulty with inconsistent expectations and dismissive responses. Students lose points despite following directions perfectly. The real struggle is surviving his unreasonable grading and patterns of rude behavior.

Hard work and effort should matter, but under McDaniel, it never does. Students lose points for minor errors, TAs grade inconsistently, and accommodations are always denied. Let's be honest: the course feels impossible not because organic chemistry is hard, but because Chris McDaniel turns a rigorous subject into an unfair ordeal of abuse.

The “hard class” excuse doesn't cut it at all. Chris McDaniel's lack of consistency, poor communication, and refusal to provide grounded guidance are what make McDaniel orgo brutal. Students fail or lose points for reasons unrelated to chemistry, proving that the struggle is his fault, not the subject's.

Orgo lab doesn't need to be cruel, but McDaniel makes it one of the worst experiences. TAs have different grading standards, he rejects ALL accommodation requests, and interactions can be hostile. Hard work isn't good enough, students are intentionally set up to fail by his arbitrary methods.

Blaming difficulty is a smokescreen. McDaniel's impatience, sarcasm, and rigidity are what make students dread class. Even competent, hardworking students face hostility and unpredictable penalties, proving the challenge comes from him, not just orgo itself. Hard work alone does not equate to fair evaluation here.

Orgo's difficulty DOES NOT excuse being on a high horse. It's easy to claim “it's just orgo,” but McDaniel actively worsens the experience. He's dismissive, controlling, and unapproachable. Hard chemistry does not require hostility or condescension, yet his behavior makes this a toxic, unnecessarily stressful endeavor.

McDaniel treats students like burdens rather than freshers. He rarely acknowledges effort, and constructive questions are met with unhelpful, demeaning responses. The course feels like navigating a minefield where understanding the material does not protect you from losing points or facing hostility.

McDaniel's behavior toward female students is deeply concerning. Misogyny is evident in his condescending tone and dismissive treatment, which discourages participation and undermines confidence. Combined with harsh grading, this creates an unfair and hostile learning environment.

McDaniel's behavior shows clear misogyny. Female students often feel demeaned, dismissed, and undervalued in both labs and lectures. Combined with harsh grading and lack of accommodations, this creates a hostile and inequitable environment that discourages learning and participation.

This class is more about surviving an unlikable version of Hopper from Stranger Things than learning chemistry. McDaniel's inaccessibility, strict enforcement of minor rules, and lack of meaningful feedback create an environment where students are stressed, anxious, and often feel powerless.

This class feels like being at a Korean reform school from the start. McDaniel sets a tone of condescension and makes even simple interactions unpleasant. It's difficult to respect a professor who belittles students rather than supporting them. For a demanding class like orgo, students deserve far more patience and respect in communication.

McDaniel seems to take pride in being inflexible. Extensions, accommodations, or even basic empathy are off the table. This rigid approach isn't about high standards, it's about micromanagement, control and the classic power trip. By prioritizing harsh rules over actual teaching, he strips away any enthusiasm students might have for chemistry.

Students need professors who encourage them, but McDaniel clearly does the opposite. His dismissive and short-tempered responses discourage participation. It's not just about difficulty, it's also about a total lack of respect for students' time and effort. The lack of compassion and consistency in grading makes the entire experience unbearable.

McDaniel runs orgo lab like a punishment rather than a learning opportunity. Minor errors are treated as major failures, and students are never given the benefit of the doubt. Instead of guidance, you're met with coldness and rigidity that crush motivation. He then gets defensive and would clap back at anyone who questions how he ran lab.

The course could be manageable if not for his hostility. Students already know orgo is tough, but McDaniel adds unwanted stress by being curt, unhelpful, and dismissive. It feels less like teaching and more like policing. The negativity overshadows the content. Rather than feeling like you're working with a mentor, you feel like a burden to him.

Chris McDaniel doesn't hide his disdain for students, and female students especially report being talked down to or dismissed. This kind of treatment fosters a toxic atmosphere where people feel singled out or devalued based on gender, which is honestly unacceptable in any classroom.

Deadlines are absolute, with zero tolerance for flexibility, even in legitimate emergencies. The powerhouses like Sravan Surampudi and Nathan Schnarr show empathy, but Chris McDaniel refuses to adapt. It gives the impression he values rules and appearances more than the actual well-being and learning of his students.

McDaniel's teaching is overshadowed by arrogance. Instead of creating an open learning environment, he exudes superiority, which discourages students from asking questions. Paired with rigid grading, the course feels more like a demoralizing and demotivating test of endurance than an academic experience.

Even though the subject matter is important, McDaniel's handling of the course drains motivation. Artificially strict deadlines, unyielding policies, and inconsistent grading overshadow any learning. Students leave feeling undervalued, and the sleep deprivation caused by his style far outweighs any lessons learned.

Instead of serving as a mentor, McDaniel acts like a gatekeeper. Expect no flexibility in this class. Even with valid reasons, late work is not accepted, and accommodations are often disregarded. The rigid approach makes the course inaccessible to students who need support, and his dismissive attitude only adds to the frustration.

Chris McDaniel runs the course with little regard for fairness. Communication is curt, grading feels arbitrary, and policies are inflexible. Students often feel like they're walking on eggshells rather than learning. The lab itself isn't unmanageable, but his leadership makes it unnecessarily harsh.

Professionalism is severely lacking. Chris McDaniel's communication is often curt or unhelpful, leaving students without clarity. When problems arise, he tends to deflect responsibility rather than working toward solutions, which reflects poorly on his pedagogical commitment. Students leave orgo lab with McDaniel demoralized instead of inspired.

There is no sense of fairness in this course. Grades often reflect arbitrary judgment rather than the actual quality of work and effort students put in. Female students in particular are penalized harshly for minor formatting mistakes, while larger academic efforts are overlooked. The lack of consistency is disappointing.

Mistakes are harshly punished, and deviation from his preferred methods can result in significant point loss. Questions are often met with sarcastic comments or condescension. The focus is on catching errors rather than teaching, which discourages learning, undermines student confidence, and fails to prepare them for the organic chemistry industry.

Lab management is inconsistent. Some TAs are strict, others lenient, and McDaniel exerts control in unpredictable ways. Students can't rely on clear standards, and even correct work can receive arbitrary penalties, making the grading process feel unfair and stressful.

Chris McDaniel never shows concern for student well-being or learning. Extensions and accommodations are almost always rejected, even with legitimate, thorough documentation. Personal emergencies and health issues are treated with inflexibility, adding stress and demonstrating a lack of professional responsibility.

If you're a female student hoping for a job reference or letter of recommendation based on your hard work in Orgo Lab, expect McDaniel to pass on your request as it's clear he doesn't care about students at all. This is a guy whose misogyny and indifference toward student effort/learning all overshadow how knowledgeable he is.

McDaniel seems more focused on catching students making mistakes than helping them learn from mistakes. Points are deducted for trivial errors, and TAs are instructed to enforce strict, nit-picky rules. The environment feels punitive, discouraging learning and creative experimentation.

Female students report feeling particularly targeted and demoralized. McDaniel's comments and grading often weaken their confidence, creating a hostile environment. This behavior crosses professional boundaries and makes orgo lab feel unsafe, and it's unacceptable how a chem prof with a reputation for misogyny is allowed to run this class.

McDaniel prioritizes control over teaching. He micromanages TAs to enforce strict, arbitrary rules and rarely explains the grading policy for orgo lab. Students, particularly the ladies, are often penalized for minor deviations, and more importantly there is no transparency or fairness. The class feels more like punishment than learning.

His attitude has already been discussed so let's change the topic. McDaniel's approach to exams and assignments is inconsistent. He introduces material not taught in class and applies arbitrary grading. Students can follow all instructions perfectly and still lose points. This lack of transparency undermines trust and makes orgo with him brutal.

Expect minimal to no support in this course. Chris is largely MIA outside of lectures and labs, leaving students to rely entirely on TAs. He rarely addresses questions adequately and is quick to penalize mistakes, making consistent success dependent more on luck than dedicated effort.

The class environment under McDaniel is stressful and unsupportive. He dismisses student inquiries, enforces rigid policies, and seems more interested in abusing power than helping students learn. If you have him, expect artificially hard workload (not actually content based hard) and a generally hostile atmosphere even with careful preparation.

Communication with McDaniel is nearly impossible. He rarely responds to questions and is rude to students for no reason. Lab management is not consistent among TAs, and grading can feel random. His attitude prioritizes control over learning, and students often feel ignored, unfairly evaluated, and unsupported.

Hard work doesn't guarantee success in Orgo Lab with Chris McDaniel. Lab and exam grades often depend on TA discretion or his personal preferences. Small errors are penalized harshly, and content not covered in lecture appears on exams. He shows little regard for student learning, support, or fairness.

Just like the reviews say, the guy is cold and shows no care for student success. Even if he is your only option, consider putting the class on hold until the next semester or be prepared to fight for your GPA.

Taking a class with Chris is like playing squid game. Chris will lie and tell you that there clear grading criteria, but rubrics randomly change from week to week. Even my grad TA thought this man was crazy. The class is not hard, but Chris goes above and beyond to make students lose points wherever possible. I did not enjoy playing his mind games.

Very badly run class. Your grade is almost entirely dependent on your TA's grading skills. If they grade poorly, you will not get a good grade. The actual professor never shows up and I have heard that if you have issues he is not very lenient.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Lots of homework--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: This guy runs the orgo labs like the third reich. He is the single least caring person I've come across at umass and it's a terrible misfortune that he is the only orgo lab leader. Your TA can make the labs tolerable if you are lucky but pray you don't ever have to so much as email Mcdaniel becuase he will go out of his way to ruin your day.

Far and away the worst and least caring professor I've ever had to the misfortune of meeting. This guy could not care less about his students. His labs are unreasonably hard with an impossible final and without a good TA you will fail. He is rude in person and worse over email, I would give him a zero if I could.

He's one of the worst and least caring people on this campus.I had the displeasure of taking this lab, and unfortunately,got to experience why he gets these bad reviews. The TAs that teach you are lovely-I loved mine, but Chris, that's a different story.20q+30 min final with math and ChemDraw is absurd. Grading rubric's worse. Don't take the class.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Read the rest of the reviews, they are accurate! You better hope your sweet cheeks gets a good TA, or the class is hell. The grading criteria is posted for reports, but they'll get you for not including nuances that they have never described to you. Actual lab is enjoyable to be in, NEVER forget to do your OWLs, or youll pay his wrath.Condescending

The grading criteria is unclear. For lab reports, you are told what to put on them but no matter how closely I followed and triple checked the grading reqs, I could not seem to do better than a 90ish on each. Believe me, I tried. Might be up to TA's, mostly. Though I will say everything is doable if you show up and put the time in.

I genuinely enjoyed this class, one of my favorites in college so far. I never liked chemistry, but this class was easy as long as I showed up to the lectures and took notes. He explains it well and links the teachings to real life scenarios. Can't believe all the hate because he was an amazing professor. Him being strict makes you learn better.

The class itself is fine, like all labs just hope you get a good TA (there are thankfully many for this course). Pray you never have to interact with this man. Thinks he can get out of giving people their due accommodations by putting *no exceptions even for people with accommodations.* Even the TAs don't really like him. Lab is kinda fun tho
STOP MAKING FAKE ACCOUNTS MCDANIEL! I KNOW THERES NO STUDENTS WHO ACTUALLY ARE GIVING U ANYTHING OTHER THAN A 1/5
Hope u read this cause ur my most hated professor karma will get u

actually really liked this class! 3 exams but he allows students to bring a cheat sheet and work in groups. as long as you come to lecture and do ur homework you'll be fine. also really nice and knowledgeable, but does not give extensions or change grades.
reviews.rating_tags: Group projects--Lots of homework--Graded by few things

reviews.comment:
Genuinely not a good person. I do not think he should be teaching and working with students because he does not care about their wellbeing. He goes above and beyond to put students down and even to tell me personally I did not put my academics first because I missed a lab due to a competition.

I have a 4.0 btw and I am doing GREAT. not a fan.

He really does not care about a single student. It is very clear that he is not compassionate or even kind. Very unfortunate that he is the only orgo lab instructor at UMass. They need to hire a new one asap!
You will hate him until you take lab with Paradise at which point you will feel eternally grateful for my glorious king.
Super unlikable and unwilling to help. Accused me of plagiarizing when I didn't and refused to meet to talk about it or help at all.

In the 2 month winter course, I had to complete over 130 homework problems for it to only be worth a minuscule part of my grade. Most of it came down to how you did on the three exams and five quizzes he also assigned. 10% of your grade was based on watching the lectures, but you weren't allowed to skip a single second of it, or you would get a 0.

orgo lab is fine. owls suck as always. grading really depends on your TA. he was super understanding of my accommodations tho which i appreciated. he runs orgo lab like a well oiled machine which can feel a bit alienating.

Grading criteria can be vague. A general rubric available, but it isn't always helpful. I had a great TA who was helpful during lab and lenient with grading. Reports are the worst, but you can ask for help in LUH (basically office hours). Sometimes LUH is mandatory to do the lab, but it's not time-consuming. The final sucked, take it with friends

McDaniel was probably the most inconsiderate person when it came to grading and did not care about understanding his students. He was not there during lab and was absent during instruction periods. I would avoid him at all costs.

Honestly not as bad as everyone said it was. It's one of those classes where you just gotta follow the guidelines exactly to get an A. Follow the rubric closely for the lab reports, always show up to lab on time, and be prepared for a 30 minute final with 18 questions on it(study all the previous owls, glassware, etc).
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Gives good feedback--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: The brutalness of the grading is highly dependent on your TA as they grade your papers so take all ratings here about difficultly with a grain of salt. It not a hard class for everything but the papers, just show up and do the simple experiments. The final is brutally quick with a 1.33 minutes per question to look up MW and such

This course is an utter failure. The very illogical grading criteria is what is worst. If you capitalize a chemical name by mistake, forget to put a space before the unit, and similar meaningless details, they'll deduct so many points. I don't know why UMass won't hire another professor to teach it and just restructure the whole thing.

Every bad thing you heard about him is completely true. You have to do a full lab report every week with the most bare bones rubric you've ever seen in your academic career. But, even if it's not on the rubric, they will still take points off because you're just suppose to read his mind and know what he wants. Mistakes are heavily punished.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Participation matters

reviews.comment: Everything you've heard is true. Avoid at all costs. Does not respect disability accommodations. Try not to have any problems because if you do communicating with him will be your worst nightmare.
he's just mean, the TA's teach the labs but just avoid McDaniel at all costs and don't be late he will make you feel bad. Lab reports are graded very harshly.

The course is very unforgiving. Small mistakes in even the spacing of your lab report will get you points off. Your lab report grades depend on your TA's generosity. There are no plausible excuses for lab reports being late so be aware of due dates. The moment you call him out for being unfair in his grading or decisions, you're getting ghosted.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Participation matters--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Truly a bully. Dealt with a difficult TA who was a bit inexperienced. I spoke to McDaniels about the situation he dismissed my concerns saying that the TA and I had a "cultural difference". Accused several students of cheating and when they were able to prove they weren't he changed the lab handout to support his side.

The labs are TA-led, so the professor is mostly absent. While McDaniel can seem unapproachable, engage with the subject and you'll find he's passionate. Use unstuckstudy ai and the free textbook to excel in this course.

He is incredibly pessimistic about this age of students post-Covid (don't care about their education and will cheat in any way possible) - assuming the worst about us. Help yourself out and show interest in the subject, talk to him outside of asking for favors. You'll find he's funny and passionate about helping those who want to be helped.

He is horrible. I have no words. The best way to describe him is if you added up all the bad reviews of his and combined them into a list. Its terrible that he doesn't even try to change his teaching style/methods, despite almost everybody having a negative experience in his class. The homework assigned is way too much for it to only be worth 15%.

Really hates his students. Created a 30 minute final with 20 questions because it was too difficult for him to schedule a make-up final exam. Making a 30 minute final be 15% of our final grade is crazy.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: He does not deserve to run such an important lab course at a university like UMass. He thinks all the criticism he receives is the fault of others. Such a person must be avoided at all costs in college and life.

I'm not sure who's writing all these bad reviews. Chris is one of the nicest people in the chem department and truly cares about orgo. He's very enthusiastic in class and explains everything clearly. Maybe he's not the most present in lab but he cares about his students and sticks to his grading rules no matter what. Bad handwriting unfortunately

This isn't even about the difficulty of orgo lab, moreso that you never see McDaniel and when you need to communicate with him, he replies to you with in a rude and egotistical way. He is not kind or caring. Make sure to do your work before deadlines; he will never give you an extension or make-up.

Chris gets a bad rep, for good reason. He is stuck up and rude. However, the lab itself is not bad, as it is fully run by TAs. A 4 hr lab was not my favorite thing in the world, but definitely survivable.

Surampudi cares about student learning, puts in effort to make sure his expectations are clear, and is approachable. McDaniel, on the other hand, can't do any of these things. Orgo with McDaniel is a chaotic mess of unclear, fuzzy instructions with befuddling grading criteria. Assignments are bad and you don't learn much. Worst class I've taken.

Well, well, well...it would appear Chris McDaniel's cocky and disrespectful behavior towards students led karma to bite back at him by making him the most reviled chem faculty member. I'd love to see Sravan Surampudi and Nathan Schnarr get promoted to Professor positions and hopefully for McDaniel to get laid off from the chemistry department.

I've never seen someone with a bigger superiority complex than Chris McDaniel. It's obvious his blatant textbook narcissism resulted in him being the most reviled chem instructor on the planet. Rachid Skouta, on the other hand, is a fantastic stand-up guy. Down to earth, humble, kind, and charismatic. All attributes McDaniel sadly does not possess.

Honestly he gets a lot of hate but I don't think he's out to get you. You almost never see Chris in the labs and when you do, he's there to check on the TAs (who do all the work and grading). It is entirely TA based, and from my experience, mine was very kind and a nice grader. It is annoying to sit in a 4 hour lab but it builds resume skills.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Clear grading criteria--Lots of homework

reviews.comment: Worst professor I have ever had at Umass.He is very stingy with extra credit and my lecture grade was graded incorrectly due to glitching and he wouldn't change the grade. Had to go to the head of the department
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment:
I had a heart attack and asked for an extension as I was in the emergency room. 


Chris McDaniel was unwilling to grant an extension. 

Take surampudi, take Schnarr, take anyone else.
Surampudi is pretty much everything McDaniel couldn't be
all the other reviews already cover how terrible he is

Orgo Lab is a big leap from the typical GenChem labs. The writing criteria is not clear, but the grading is very tough. The only easy way to do OWLs is if you understand the 6+ page handout sheet. I spent 4+ hours on the non-formal reports. No deadline extension. Have not finish the course, but overall knows it is a big stress on my GPA.

He is not present at all. This course depends fully on your TA. It is a 2 credit course that should take a total of 6 hours per week, but it ends up taking much more. 4 hours for the lab itself, minimum 2-3 hours for post-lab, minimum 1 hour for pre-lab, 1 hour for owls, and 1 hour for LUH hours adding up to 9 hours, which is a big understatement.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--So many papers

reviews.comment: Be prepared to be set up for failure. You would expect that once you hit rock bottom, there is no way to go down even further, but trust me, McDaniel will find a way to make that happen. Not an example of what reasonable professors are supposed to do. Poor sportsmanship in so many aspects.

A straight up bully, never admits he's wrong, looks down on everyone, and thinks he's superior to everyone else. Will never give an extension even if you're on your deathbed. Doesn't explain anything and expects you to "know it". He would rather stomp on a malnourished child than admit that he's wrong. He needs to be fired.
Rudest professor I've had at Umass so far

The TAs do all the grading of the lab reports. Attendance is mandatory at every lab. The lab practical isn't as bad as it seems as long as you actually show up to lab. This class is a lot of outside of lab work, but it's like any other lab, people just aren't used to outside of lab work b/c they have never been in a lab before.
Stingy with how he grades his students and will not admit that he is wrong. You might get a grade lower than you deserve in this class.

He gave a final exam where the average was a 35. With how bad everyone did he turns around and says "that's on you(the students) and not curving the exam". You didn't teach us anything and give us a final exam with no preparation and a loose "what you did in lab will be on it" and expect us to pass! BS get off your fn high horse and quit teaching.

A review for his winter class: McDaniel sometimes straight up glosses over content that shows up later in tests. He also doesn't address underlying concepts, the understanding of which is crucial to your success. Resorting to memorization will never work. Do NOT take this class unless you have experience self-studying and a good grip on gen. chem.

Chem lab was the biggest waste of my time. The experiments themselves were fine, however the lab reports along with prelab work, OWLs, post lab OWLs, and LUH hours is too much for a 2 credit course, oh and the unnecessary final. Extremely strict attendance rules, you cannot be late or submit any late work past 3 days. My TA made the lab bearable.

The amount of work given is disproportionate for a 2-credit class, and is graded quite harshly. The lab would run better if someone else were running it. Quite literally anyone else. The lab in and of itself isn't bad, depending on the TA you get. You mainly interact with your TA, and Chris McDaniel doesn't really show up.

The lab itself is easy and could be fun if Mr McDaniel didn't make it so stressful. The TAs are awesome and do all the work. Lab directions are unclear, ask the TA for help and you'll be fine. Biggest gripe is the LUH times: not told what time they are during course reg, I could only make .5 hrs of them, made the course way more stressful.

I don't think I ever had a professor who I have never. once. seen. He has never participated in my lab section, which is completely run by the TAs who do the professor's work and are the only reason the experiments don't fall apart.

This is a lab with a assigned time yet you are expected to show up outside your session for "LUH" whether the available times fit your schedule or not. Our attendance is mandatory, I have not seen this man once, yet he has the audacity to give a 30 minute, cumulative practicum with 20 questions. 2 credits. Need a makeup lab? Too bad.

Good TAs tho.

Chris McDaniel is completely inaccessible outside of class. In fact, despite taking this class with him I have never even seen him. He's just not there, at all. He talks through all of the lab TA's like a omnipotent God of the lab. Your grandma died? Too bad. No extensions. No humanity. If you are late, you're basically dead to him.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Lots of homework--So many papers

reviews.comment: It was something.

Worst professor in the chem department. He does not care about his students at all. Doesn't give any extensions even if ur grandma is dying, he doesn't care. All labs were graded at the same time even though he said we would receive them back every week to fix what we did wrong on the next report so you lose the same points on all of them.

This professor has no respect for his students and provides no support. It is truly despicable how he treats his students and is unwilling to provide make-ups or extensions for legitimate reasons. I have always loved chemistry, but now he has made me never want to take another chemistry class, truly disappointing.

Yeah just don't take his lab. This guy has no tolerance for missing lab due to illness. I missed out on the lab and filled out the make-up lab form but was denied because I didn't read his email. For god's sake, how am I supposed to read the email while I'm lying on the bed suffering from illness?
Pretentious chemistry instructor who is sarcastic (not in a good way), rude, and short-fused and doesn't really care about students.

Previous review clearly comes from an orgo lab TA with a big ego. This class destroyed my mental health and social life and is the most unorganized class I've taken because simply put, Chris doesn't seem to care about the success and learning of students, and he is lazy, making it impossible to schedule 1-on-1 appointments with outside class.

I have previously TA'd for Chris for CHEM269. Many of these reviews are blown completely out of proportion. This course expects you to put on your adult boots and take responsibility for your work and attendance. You don't get to miss labs or reports without valid excuse because a lab with 500+ enrollment does not bend over backward on your whim.

The orgo lab requires far more work than a 2 credit course. Be ready for about 9 hours of work per week (4-hour labs, required LUH times, pre-labs that can take about 2 hours, and lab reports that take about 2 hours as well). The grading outlines are not clear and little formatting mistakes significantly impact your grade.

The class is like any chemistry class in terms of work/difficulty, however, Chris makes it a nightmare. I genuinely have not ever come across someone, nonetheless a teacher, who acts the way he does. Kindness or compassion are two words I don't think Chris understands. Arrogance and megalomaniac match better. If I could rate him lower, I would.

You can have a functional relationship with Chris McDaniel. However, he lacks empathy, social skills, and common sense. So, that relationship is not very healthy. And to top it off, he reminds me of Walter White from the final season of Breaking Bad.

Orgo lab managed by Chris McDaniel is an awful class to exist. It's full of conflicts of interest, hazing rituals, harsh grading, toxic sweat-shop culture for female students, and lack of departmental oversight. He probably has some serious personality disorders and seems to transmit negativity and guilt to whichever student he 'mentors'.

Chris is a dangerous and creepy character who is avoided by everyone if they can. Even students who publicly "claim" to have not been treated badly by Chris do concede privately that the kind of hostile environment Chris has created in orgo lab hinders completion of the academic objectives of their degree programs.

This guy made me have too many all nighters while I would cry myself to sleep on the weekends studying for this course. For just an organic chemistry lab he treats it like it's a PhD course. I lost 15 pounds because of this professor and I'm still recovering. If you can take this lab with another professor please do for your own sake.

Dr. McDaniel genuinely cared and always helped. I literally would email him all the time when he was not in office hours and he would still respond. He is a great professor and the only thing I'm upset about is that he wasn't teaching orgo 2 this summer. Orgo is not meant to be a walk in the park, so don't let any of the comments discourage you.

reviews.comment: Dr. McDaniel is awesome! Obviously organic chem is a difficult subject, but he really explains things very well and really wants students to succeed. He really cares about his students. The lectures are awesome, and he is really funny. Definitely take organic with him!

A lot of the comments here don't do him justice at all, he's overall not that mean or rude. Well to the Chem majors at least. He's always willing to explain topics and help you pass Orgo as much as possible. Unlike some professors, he gives you the material and its up to you to figure out how to use it rather than him telling you how to get to it.

There's 11 lab reports, a few owls for pre and post lab, and a final that is basically 17 questions pulled from the owl hw questions. Chris is easy to reach and usually responds fast, the moodle is dense to navigate but the information you'll need will be there. Grade is contingent on the TA who grades your lab reports, criteria isn't super clear.

reviews.comment:
Chris was very forgiving - even opening up past homework deadlines when he had said he would not do that. You don't ever interact much with him.

Your experience in this class depends highly on your TA. I dislike chem but looking back this class wasn't the worst. Don't be afraid of asking your TA many questions - that's how I did well on labs!

The great Christopher McDaniel. Where do I begin? Firstly, he is a sincerely kind man. I came into this class full of dread and left with a warm heart from the countless generosities extended to students. I had read a review on this very forum that described an instance of child consumption. Do not fear. Your children are safe.
