reviews.comment: Despite the negative stigma around Chris, I thought that he was a great professor. He was always fair in grading and providing helpful feedback on homework/exams. Majority of the negative comments come from students who just don't want to put in the work. Chemistry is hard, but Chris gives you all of the materials you need to succeed.

Honestly the guy is very clearly a research professor and I frankly don't blame hime for making this class a pain. However good lord this is simple chemistry but you would think it's some kind of a divinchi code. He completely lacks any understanding whatsoever and just has absolutely no real social skills.
Chris McDaniel is probably the biggest sore loser when it comes to professors in the orgo field of the chemistry department.
He is always out there to fail students. You have to actively try to pass.
Rude and hateful.

He is like Joffrey from Game of Thrones. He doesn't accept anyone else's opinion but his own, the lectures are completely one sided and he won't guide you to say what he wants to hear. Boring and he can be very belittling when it comes to questions. His grading process is old-fashioned and unclear. Your effort is never good enough for him.

Very unforgiving professor who has no problem holding grudges against those who make the simplest of mistakes. Wants everyone to follow his methods and doesn't leave much room for creativity. If you don't get on his good side by adhering to common sense in orgo lab, your grade WILL SUFFER. Oh, and good luck asking him for an explanation or help.

His orgo lab TAs deserved to get berated harshly for caring more about massaging their ego by treating orgo lab  as a common sense course and talking down on students who ask reasonable questions than helping students succeed and thrive.

Orgo 1 is easy! You learn about drawing structures, resonance, chirality, and these are all very simple concepts. You'll see how easy this class is, when you take orgo 2. But even orgo 2 isn't that difficult, so that gives you an idea of how easy orgo 1 is. Many people got a perfect score, so this class with Chris McDaniel is great!

Chris's lectures were very clear and he explains everything in full detail. He is able to break them down into the very fundamentals of chemistry, so it's easy to understand. Just make sure to do homework and don't cram it, unless you know you'll do well. There's many chances to get your grade back up, so if you put effort you'll get an easy A!

He is a great professor, he knows the material inside out. Students blame the professor for their poor work, here's the statistic from Chris. "155 students (67%) didn't even attempt the practice exam", "52% of the class did not attempt ANY OWLv2 homework or quizzes until 3 days before the exam... 30% of the class still have zeros in all quizzes".

I do not know how some people rate the teaching element for a practical lab such as Orgo lab. McDaniel may have had a hard time last Spring due to some family issues, but he is an OK lecturer. I took Orgo 1 with him, and I did not have any issues. The only thing I disliked was Owl V.2, its grading and functionality.
No extensions. No understanding for emergencies or difficult situations. Went to the dean did not help. Need a doctors note if you want to even make up a lab but still you get no extension.

I'm not really sure what all of these reviews are about. If you're taking ochem lab with him listed as the instructor, there is a very low chance of ever interacting with him. You really only interact with your lab TA. The labs are well designed, the moodle page has all the info you need to do well, and he accepts work up to 3 days late.

He gets a bad rep but as a chem major I think that's just because chem is hard and he teaches orgo. From my experience he gave very effective and informative lectures, with a smaller workload than one may expect from orgo. While he can come across as standoffish sometimes, I think he does care about the wellbeing of his students.

Surampudi > McDaniel

McDaniel is the embodiment of a no-good, selfish, horrible professor who deserves to get review bombed as he is an absolute villain and bully who cannot manage orgo labs properly, is very disrespectful to women, and shows no signs of kindness, empathy, or warmth for students during tough times like COVID. McDaniel is an absolute villain of a professor, the most disrespectful chemistry professor you'll ever meet. While Sravan Surampudi and Nathan Schnarr are total fam when it comes to orgo professors, Chris McDaniel is a completely reprehensible brainless bag of skin and bones who has a big ego and clearly thinks he's better than his students.

McDaniel is a real bully. Anytime you question anything about his classes, he will cold call and gaslight you. Pretty brutal professor. Avoid if you can.

Never had such a disrespectful professor in my life. McDaniel will not help you. I went to his office hours, and he just wants you to memorize the materials. This is not the right way to learn. Please avoid.
Chris is super disorganized and not helpful at all in his office hours. He likes call out random people during lectures to make class uncomfortable.
Will do everything in power to make chem majors avoid him. Tries to leverage poor exam grades to force students to voice complaints against the chem department. Just a horrible person.

Unreasonable grading policies. Belittles students for asking questions or answering questions wrong. Intentionally takes points away from students unfairly. Extremely rude. No sympathy. He is knowledgeable and qualified, that's the only respect McDaniel will get.
He doesn't care about his students. His management of required orgo classes is awful. Just generally a mean person.
McDaniel is such a mean and condescending professor. His exams allow no partial credit, and he will do everything he can to set students up for failure.

McDaniel sucks. Sure he's knowledgeable and qualified as a chemist, but he's arrogant and rude and makes orgo labs seem like a real sweat shop.

RMP for McDaniel deserved to get lambasted with a sea of formal complaints because simply put, Chris is incapable of writing a reasonable exam and answering student questions with respect.

Also the dif TA's have dif grading difficulties and are incredibly inconsistent. He can't run lab.

He said in the beginning to take 2-3 hours a day for orgo and he was right. He goes fast in lectures you will need to review, and exams are 50% of your grade. Tough professor and not very accommodating given certain circumstances.

He is not empathetic and grades harshly, with too high expectations. There is little room to make up a failed exam besides the hours of Mastering Chem hw.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Test heavy--Tough grader

reviews.comment: The man is absolutely merciless. Don't, and I can't stress this enough, expect empathy. He does not care at all, and it feels like he wants people to flunk out. Hope to whatever you believe in that your TA is decent. You'd best make sure that you read EVERYTHING this man puts on the course page, because if you don't you will be absolutely screwed.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Skip class? You won't pass.--Tough grader

reviews.comment: Chris is one of the worst professors I've ever had. He doesn't care about students whatsoever. His handwriting matches the quality of a ten-year-old, so his Inked Lectures are useless. His lab reports and exams are impossible, the grading is so particular and nit-picky that full credit is unreachable. To top it all off, he reminds me of Ben Shapiro

He genuinely does not care if his students succeed or not. He is absolutely insane about the syllabus and does not like to make any exceptions or accommodations. I came to leave this review after an email exchange with him. I have never had a professor at UMass that cares less about his students than this man.

You don't deal with Chris much in lab, but grading is inconsistent and based your TA. (Good luck if you have Ben Adams). Even if you read and followed all the directions, some will choose to take off points for crazy nit-picky things. Hard work doesn't pay off here. It's all luck. Read everything through and maybe you'll get a B. If they like you.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Skip class? You won't pass.--Tough grader

reviews.comment: This class solely depends on your TA. Reach out to your TA and find out EXACTLY how they expect the lab reports to be!! Grading is extremely picky, its easy to lose points over things that you didnt even know you had to include/have. If you reach out to Professor McDaniel dont expect any help, just an unreasonable and unhelpful response!

Don't bother reaching out to this man regarding basically anything, his response will most likely be something snarky, rude, and entirely unhelpful, followed by "sent from iPhone" (not accommodating whatsoever)
Never care his students. Worst professor. Run away!!!

Underprepares all his students, the exam averages were in order, C-, C-, F+. Completely unreasonable, nitpicky and just in general mean. He doesn't care at all for his students, help sessions are essentially mandatory as the TA's carry the class by doing his damn job for him. Avoid at all costs.

This professor is by far the worst ever I had. He is extremely rude & not understanding. If I could rate him -1, I would do that without a doubt. All the other professors that I have came across care about the actual knowledge and not just making the class hard. I feel like he gets a satisfaction by seeing student suffer. Worst is an understatement

Had him as lab prof. What makes/breaks lab is ur TA. Chris's lab procedures & grading criteria are clear, what he expects in lab reports can be confusing @ first but reach out to your TA, do exactly what they say & you'll be fine. By the end of the class you'll be a wiz @ lab reports. Labs don't go w/ lect so if you struggled in lect don't worry.

Massive jerk. Didn't even make an attempt to make accommodations for students nervous about Covid. He actually said that if you got covid and missed two labs that you would not pass. This man is an awful professor and a mean person.

McDaniel's actual criteria for grading is incomprehensible. He seems to grade more on whether or not your method is similar to his and wants you to follow his every move, simultaneously expecting you to already know the material and punishing you for doing it differently. If you diverge, expect a C- on a test you got every Q right for. Awful.
Some of the positive reviews, especially the recent review, are false. Mcdaniel is by far the worst professor in UMass! He does not care for his students and not a very good professor.

Professor McDaniel oversees the labs for organic chemistry. He was accessible outside of the lab, and was very accommodating, especially during the COVID-19 pandemic. The grading in this course was always fair, and shouldn't be challenging if you put in the necessary work!

Chris McDaniel was the overseer of the labs. We were scheduled to have lectures before lab to go over what we would be doing before lab. We ended up only having two of these - we were on our own from then on out. Our labs included material and reactions that we had not done in orgo chem class yet, which made comprehension more difficult than needed
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Skip class? You won't pass.

reviews.comment: Honestly, he is not a bad professor compared to what has been said. Yes, his lectures are boring but if you rewatch the lectures you actually understand the reactions he mentioned. Make sure you go to all the classes for participation. He let us take an exam with open books which basically was a guaranteed 100. People complain too much its orgo.
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Skip class? You won't pass.--Test heavy

reviews.comment: By far the worst professor I have had at UMass. His lectures are not helpful, he grades iClicker on correctness, and his tests are impossible (averages in the 50s). If you send him an email, he will not respond to it and he is not willing to work with students. If you have to take Orgo 2, DO NOT TAKE IT WITH HIM. Wait for a better professor. Awful.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Test heavy--Tough grader

reviews.comment: I got an A in Orgo I and this class was nearly impossible. The practice exams and many OWLs do not prepare you for his ridiculous exams (averages were in the 50s!). Lectures are far from intuitive. His only saving grace was the partner exam & final extra credit. Eli, the SI, should've taught this class because he's the only reason anyone passed.

This class is quite possibly the hardest thing I've ever done. Clicker questions are based on correctness for full points, exams are ridiculously hard and include structure drawing and typed questions. Exams do not correspond to the homework. Condescending, REFUSES to curve, says its grade inflation. Meanwhile, the exam average is always an F.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Graded by few things--Test heavy

reviews.comment: I took this class online and the quizzes were extremely hard and heavily based on owl. His lecture recordings were helpful somewhat but the examples that he goes over are reasonable and then quiz problems are entirely different. The tests are actually easier than quizzes, so that is nice. Do all owl problems and watch khanacademy for the hard units

i've noticed that at UMass chem professors are either a hit or a miss. Dr. McDaniel is definitely a miss. His lectures are very unclear and hard to follow. He has a good understanding of the subject but he does not know how to properly convey that to the students. Only upside was that you could work with others on exams. Terrible professor.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough Grader--Skip class? You won't pass.--LECTURE HEAVY

reviews.comment: Dr. McDaniel is clear with his lectures, offers plenty of resources for you to get ahead, posts his lectures for future reference and is a very kind man. His Organic Chemistry 2 course is one of my favorites that I have taken. Yes, it is a hard class but its organic chemistry.
I did not understand anything in his class. I had to teach myself everything. The exams were very hard.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough Grader--Skip class? You won't pass.--LECTURE HEAVY

reviews.comment: He clearly has a strong understanding of the material and a passion for it. That said he is an ATROCIOUS professor, largely due to the fact that he expects you to come to class already knowing the material. Answers are condescending, slides are illegible, and tests are disproportionately more difficult than OWLs/lectures/iClickers. RUN AWAY!!!!!!!!
reviews.rating_tags: Tough Grader--Skip class? You won't pass.--TEST HEAVY

reviews.comment: He was terrible at teaching, the class was incredibly boring and repetitive. The exams were crazy hard and he refused to scale when the class average was 67 just because 10 people (out of 200!) got over a 90. He didn't offer any extra credit and exams made up 65% of the final grade and there were only 2 + the final

Got an A in Orgo I no problem but his class was just way too hard, avoid if possible. He's a really great guy, a good lecturer, and cares a lot about the subject. He just doesn't seem to be interested in student success, lectures were impossible to follow and the material was much more difficult than what other classes covered.

Worst professor ever. Got an A in orgo 1 but was struggling in this class. First exam average was around a 50. Second exam 60s. His problem sets are a waste of time. He doesnt favor practice exams, ignores emails and seems to not care about his students. Worst of all: no partial credit on E-exam open response even if you made the slightest mistake
reviews.rating_tags: Tough Grader--Skip class? You won't pass.--TEST HEAVY

reviews.comment: Honestly he gets a bad reputation he is pretty nice to talk to in office hours and gives helpful feedback when asking simple questions. Don't no why people don't like him. I got an A easy and he gives us open exams.

If you see Professor Mcdaniel's name, run the other direction and never look back. This has been the most impossible thing I've ever done in college. He posts lecture slides that are ILLEGIBLE and he goes off on tangents and attempts to humor the class so listening to his recordings are also USELESS. You'll be better off learning the text w osmosis
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--LOTS OF HOMEWORK--ACCESSIBLE OUTSIDE CLASS

reviews.comment: Professor McDaniel definetly  loves the subject ; however, he is not affective at teaching it. The lectures are dry, and there are too many tangents. I never knew what the main goal of each lecture was. Also, exam expectations were very unclear and the exams were very difficult. If you ask a simple question, some answers are condescending.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough Grader--Skip class? You won't pass.--LECTURE HEAVY

reviews.comment: Explains the material very well and provides many examples for each topic. Orgo itself is a tough subject but he makes it easier to understand. Also provided a number of extra credit quizzes to make up any lost points in the quiz portion (15% of overall grade). Responds quick to emails and the TA, Kat, is great!
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Skip class? You won't pass.--LECTURE HEAVY

reviews.comment: You never really see him but the grading rubric the TAs use is very specific, and he doesn't round grades even if you're less than 0.1 point away from the next letter grade. Like all labs, attendance is very mandatory and there aren't many acceptable excuses for missing.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough Grader--Skip class? You won't pass.

reviews.comment: He's a great professor and solid guy. Take him.

McDaniel is by far my favorite professor here at UMass. I took orgo for majors with him. Organic chemistry is already a difficult subject but he definitely tries his best to clear up any confusion. He is almost always available for office hours and he really does care about how well we do.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough Grader--Respected--Skip class? You won't pass.

reviews.comment: Completely dependent on who your TA is. Some grade WAY harder than others. McDaniel was always nice when he walked around the lab checking up on the experiments. Lab reports were time consuming but mostly easy if you make an effort to understand the lab. Final was all OWL questions from pre/post lab super easy.

He has no standardization across his TA's so that's a mess. More importantly though he is one of the most condescending person I've ever met. He makes it abundantly clear that he doesn't care about his students because he's a research professor and this is just a requirement he wants to get out of the way.

This class truly depends on your TA. Pray for someone who is an easy marker. The final for this class is truly disgusting and dates back to even chem 112. Try and get as much points from labs and owls. The lab write-ups were the longest part of the lab

This Lab class was such a joke of a class, but your grade is mostly determined by your TA. The Owls are easy, the experiments are stupidly long and tedious. The final was only 20 questions and a handful were on the stupidest topics that were barely discussed. It's clearly a requirement class or you wouldn't be taking it. Stupidly time consuming.

Dr. McDaniel was one of the best professors I've had, if not the best. His lectures were extremely clear and he explains things fully down to the basics. The supplemental problem sets he provided were very helpful, since he writes them and he also writes the exams. He really wants the students to understand the material, which is a great quality.
So very unclear and not helpful.  Tricky quizzes for no reason and unnecessary stressfulness

Ontop of weekly OWLs which usually consists of a ton, he assigns problem sets due every week. The first exam wasn't tough and a majority of the class got a good grade but he didn't like it so decided to make exam 2 and 3 hard. It is a lot of material to learn so be prepared. He tries to crack a few jokes and he is a bit rude.

Very rude person. Doesn't help you if you are in trouble. He will make you feel you are damn stupid, and he doesn't care what you feel. Don't reply the e-mail which he thinks this problem he doesn't care. You'd better to deal with your TA more than him. If take this course, try not deal with him in person. I will piss you off.

McDaniel recently started teaching the Organic Chemistry lab as well. The grad TAs are the ones that you'll spend the most time with, not so much Professor McDaniel. He's fantastic though and so is the lab class! OWLs are easy, the experiments don't take too long and the final is 19 MC questions. Super easy!

Very difficult.  Tests are absurdly difficult and cover material not presented or briefly alluded to in class.  Extremely helpful in office hours.  Does NOT scale, NO extra credit.  Plan to put at least double the work into this class than any other (in college).  Friendly as a person, extremely rigid as a Grader and Teacher.  You will learn much.

McDaniel is decent enough at teaching, however he's a ridiculous grader and assigns an overwhelming amount of homework. His goal is for the class to have a C+ average at the end of the semester, and will only scale unless the average is lower than that. DOES NOT scale exams, with the last exam and final having averages in the D range. Avoid him.
Very unforgiving professor. I never had a professor that made me feel so stupid after asking him a simple question. He is a good professor but can be very condescending. Exams are tricky.

Very rude sometimes when you ask a question. Makes you look stupid. Exams are not impossible, but most of the class will fail even with all the extra credit given. Studied for 20 or more hours a week and still ended up failing the exams, which make up the majority of your grade.  Take another professor if you can.

Great guy who really cares about the course. He makes sure the only way you'll succeed is if you put in the work yourself. Gives a lot of opportunities for success. If you like being motivated, take orgo with McD

I've taken several courses with McD; this guy knows his stuff, especially organic chem.  He really cares about his students and want them to learn, even if it means being a jerk at times. His lectures make you pay attention with iclicker questions, which are often tricky/sneaky. Exams are hard but fair. I would recommend taking his class for orgo

One of my favorite teachers at UMass! Had him for both 261 and 262. Although the class size is large, he is so helpful in office hours. Seriously go see him if you're confused and don't leave until it's all cleared up. He wants to see his students succeed. Lots of extra credit thrown in. Also, master the problem sets and you'll be fine on exams.

Worst professor ever. So rude and talks down to you like you're stupid. Assigns so much homework and its barely even worth any point. Exams are everything but they're extremely hard. On the first day he even told us our exams would be very hard.. DO NOT TAKE CLASS WITH HIM
Great professor, very smart. If you go to office hours, be prepared; you should understand material and have specific questions. Exams are impossible.

If you want to pass the course, do ALL the practice exams and problem sets McDaniel posts on Moodle. They provide a way to gauge how much you understand the material, and are great study tools. Don't leave studying to the day before the exam! Give yourself at least a week to study, cramming does NOT work in this course.

VERY challenging course, not sure how I ended up passing. I thought he was fair - very scaled. His exams are extremely difficult. Review your lecture notes (he records all lectures, quite useful). Do NOT wait until last minute to study for an exam, you will do terribly. SI sessions were of great help. McDaniel is a nice guy, funny at times.

He really knows his stuff and throws a lot of material at you. The exams are near impossible and there are a ton of OWLs. The material for the class itself is intense. He never reviews for exams in class.

This class is difficult. He throws a ton of material at you for exams. He forces you to study. If you do so and work hard you will get a good grade. scale for this class is crazy. I took 261 with him as well, he scaled the class 8 points. Low exams averages, around 65%, but do the problem sets. I'd study 20+ hours the week b4 each exam and got an A

This is not any easy course by any means and McDaniel tries not to baby you with his exams. However, he is a very good instructor. He is a great lecturer and all of his slides and lecture videos are posted online. Exams are tough, but he usually ends up scaling them. I liked him very much.

I took 262 with Hixson and got a flat out F. Taking 262 with McDaniel was completely different. He was clear, available for extra help, and gave out problem sets for every chapter. He cares about his students and understands that orgo is hard and makes the occasional breaking bad reference. Great Professor.

Curt in office hours, vague in lecture (he often transposes IMPORTANT terms), deceptive in test-writing.  "I didn't prepare you for anything like this, but I think you should be able to infer the correct answer."  If you really want too teach concepts, how about assigning some of these trick questions during the semester, eh pal?
very informative
Avoid him at all costs. Every exam the average would be around a 60%. He's not very clear, and exams are impossible. Definetly take any other professor.

This guy ? I just don't know . First , the way he replies to your questions are just annoying and like he's not even interested . He knows the course but seems to rush through things with most 'inexperienced' kids in class . Honestly , to take this class you must be extremely smart in chem . And his exams ? OMG ?class 55% average and low medians :(

I took summer session chemistry with him, so it was EXTREMELY fast-paced. SO many OWL assignments with seemingly little time to do them. However, I learned a LOT from this course. McDaniel is great at explaining the material, but make sure you go to class and do your iClickers! And homework! You'll do poorly if you don't.

He is a straight-forward teacher. His teaching-style either suits you or it does not. The course material itself is not too difficult as long as you apply yourself to it. However, his teacher to student interaction was very unprofessional. Frankly, he can be quite rude.

McDaniel is a wonderful professor but he really makes you work for your grade. This class is anything but easy, but you'll leave feeling ready to jump right into a research lab. I would highly recommend him for Chem 112!

I think McDaniel is a great professor. Class is relatively easy if you study and do all the OWL assignments. He doesn't try to trick you on exams, they're very straight forward. I was very pleased with my learning experience with him.

Very good teacher for those who have a good understanding chemistry.  The lecture may move a little fast, but he gives you lots of practice problems to attempt and makes himself very available for help in office hours. The exams force you to think about what he's talked about in lecture rather than just asking for parroted info. Very good professor

One of the worst professors I have ever had in Chemistry.  He is unclear and goes over information that is not in line with the exam.  The exams are way more difficult than the lecture.  I wish I had known before taking the class.  I had Botch my freshman year for Chem 111 and I thought she was amazing compared to him.

McDaniel was one of the best professors Ive had at UMass. His lectures are clear, and he is greatly helpful in office hours and consistently available to his students. The problem sets he provides are extremely helpful and I found the course to be very rewarding, as the amount of effort you put in is def. proportional to the grade you receive.

Organic chemistry is the most challenging, but rewarding courses you will ever take. That being said, McDaniel is hard but fair, and always there to help and he scales a lot if need be. He is probably the best orgo professor in the chem department though. Just study HARD and go to class, and remember its orgo.

Organic Chemistry is not easy. However McDaniel is a great professor and explains material in great depth. He is always available to help you if you need it. Do the supplemental problems and seek help if you need it, go to lecture, and DO NOT take this class lightly. Exams can be tough but do your best. OWLS are pretty easy and there arent many.

Professor McDaniel is an engaging teacher who makes himself accessible to students. His tests are not easy, but if you do all of the OWLS, go to lecture, and study then an above average grade can be achieved. I have had 3 other chemistry professors before him, and he is the best.

Amazing professor! He doesn't just give you a bunch of definitions and equations... he actually makes you think so you really absorb the material and understand the concepts. Exams are challenging but if you do all required OWLS & optional OWLS you will get at least an 80 on the exams. Daily iClicker questions are easy way to raise your overall avg

Orgo is hard, but McDaniel is super helpful. He is always available for office hours, and his lectures are very clear and concise. Do all the practice problems and take advantage of his office hours and review sessions. Most helpful professor I've ever had.

This class requires A LOT of work. OWLs are great practice, but you must must must put in a lot of effort and make sure you understand each lecture as he teaches them. DO NOT wait until the last minute to ask questions or you will feel so screwed...

I'm accustomed to working hard for a grade, but this class was ridiculous.  Hundreds of OWLs, and up to 60 due a week! And I studied harder than I've ever studied in my life for each exam and didn't get above and 87 on any of them. The averages for two mid terms were in the low 60's with no scale. Ended up with a B+ after all that stress. Avoid

Great Guy. Organic Chemistry is nto an easy subject but he does an extraordinary job teaching it. He is very helpful and he is always available for help. Go to class, take notes, if you dont understand something just ask, chances are that your not the only one. He clears up points of confusion. Does clicker credits on random days so go to class.

Fantastic professor. Orgo is in no way easy, but he makes it interesting and helps you at every step. Definitely the best chem professor at UMass by far. Study hard and go to office hours and you'll pass the course.
McDaniel is an amazing teacher. Honestly for the people who do bad in Chemistry 111 or 112, just re-do the OWL homework problems. That's all the studying you'll have to do for the class.

Mcdaniel's an awesome guy, really laid back and clear in his lectures. But his lectures in class don't reflect the difficulty level of his tests. Go to office hours and SI sessions as much as possible. But even with that its difficult to get a good grade in his class.

This class is so hard, chris is definitely helpful and goes through lectures slowly but the tests are ridiculously hard compared to all of the practice exams and questions he gives. The average grades on the tests are in the 60's and he never scales. I got an A in Chem 111 and didn't study half as much as this class and as of now I have a 69.

I love McDaniel for Chem 112!!! he is an amazing teacher. his tests are fair and there are NO trick questions if you study the lecture notes, do the OWLs, and go to some SI session an A is no problem. i definately recommed taking him for chem 112

McDaniel was an excellent professor.  He explained everything well and moved at a decent pace.  He was very helpful and was willing to spend time in office hours helping students understanding the material.  His tests were very hard, but fair.  They really tested your knowledge of the material, as they were mostly short answer.  Take orgo with him.

BEST organic professor you will ever meet! Organic is a very hard subject however, he will give you everything you need to succeed. His lectures are so easy to follow, exams are straight forward (if you take advantage of his help). Could not have asked for a better prof. for such a rough subject.

The class itself was very clear and I THOUGHT I understood everything, until the exams. The exams are very difficult. He does not scale them up very often, even with a 46% average. It was his first semester teaching orgo with us, so he may change his test style with so many low averages...In the end I believed he did scale up overall.

favorite professor i've ever had. exams are difficult, however once you go to office hours you realize they are very fair. does everything to make sure you understand the material IN OFFICE HOURS. go to office hours. owls are wicked easy and there are like 5 per week. best orgo prof out there wish i had him for second semester

McDaniel is awesome! He posts lectures online but attendance is mandatory due to the iclicker questions every class. He is super helpful if you go to office hours but you can get by without it if you study diligently. Orgo is hard but if you put the time into it, you will be fine with McDaniel as your professor. An A is pretty hard to achieve

cool guy, good teacher, but Organic chemistry is a hard subject, so be prepared to put in 200% effort to get an A, a lot of memorization but McDaniel helps alot, if you take Orgo take it with him, probably the best teacher here for the job

very clear organic chemistry teacher.  He is available for help, he may be a bit rude at points, but he is to the point in that sense.  If you like nerdy jokes he is full of them as well.  Tests are hard, but he provides tons of review materials and answer keys.  I recommend taking the class with him, you will learn your stuff, not just memorize it

Keep up with the information and go to his office if you don't understand the material. He goes through the material pretty slowly and gives good notes during class. iclickers every class and some OWLs, not many. Does many examples during class and tries to make sure everyone is understanding the material. Good teacher. I recommend taking his class

Dr. McDaniel is NOT an easy professor. However, organic chem isn't an easy class. He's very helpful and stays in his office as long as you need him to. 4 Exams and a final, iClicker every class, not too much homework. Exams are very difficult but no trick questions. If you study hard and keep up with material, this class isn't terrible.

He comes off as a pretty nice guy, but if Chemistry isn't your thing, he's not one to make you feel comfortable. He openly makes fun of people who ask stupid questions. His exams are mainly open response...which are NOT fun when it comes to Chemistry.

Nice guy, mediocre teacher. doesnt prepare you for tests well, cant explain material effectively, but the class is graded on a scale. Says "the point is" at least 50 times per class (we tallied). Not recommended.

He explains things well, but I found that the examples he gives were very specific, and made it somewhat difficult when attempting homework problems or to study for tests.  Tests are straightforward, but make sure you know everything.  His mannerisms and personality make the class really fun.

Teaches well, gives good examples and clearly shows hot to solve the problems. Has very funny mannerisms and speech patterns, and his jokes are hilarious, i.e. was talking about functions we should now know how to integrate, and when he was talking about radicals he said "root functions, not to be confused with the 80's."

Chris has potential to be a good Professor, but he is very unclear, particularly about grading policies.  For our class, no set grading was established, and it left a lot of us uncertain how we were doing in the class. He is very willing to help outside of class, I just don't think you should *have* to come see him out of class because of lectures.

He was very helpful and understanding of my meager math understanding and always went out of his way to make time to meet with me. I think the reason some of you might feel badly about his class is you were too busy reading the news paper or interrupting the lecture talking with each other. we are in college, maybe you should act like it
I don't think this guy could possibly be any worse. He's never clear and he never has anything intelligent to say. He can't teach even the simplest thing. Avoid him.

worst teacher ever. he stutters and if you ask him a question he'll act like he's been attacked. he'll never answer you clearly either. his jokes aren't funny and his class average will show just how terrible he is at explaining the simplest of concepts. avoid at all costs.

FYS How Gay Culture is Made. Very passionate, kind, caring, funny, etc. Just a great guy. No big assignments or HW in this class. Great environment. Just a PSA this course is more abt gay pop culture history (think drag and camp) rather than gay history vibes. Would def take his class again.
RECOMMEND TAKING THIS CLASS. Tyler is a really nice professor, the materials are really interesting to learn
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Clear grading criteria--Caring

reviews.comment: Had him for the Gay Culture first year seminar. He was passionate about everything he taught. Radiates the most positive energy.
I loved this class and really enjoyed Tyler's teaching! Super interesting course readings and discussions, worth noting he uses Google Classroom rather than Canva.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Gives good feedback--Hilarious

reviews.comment: I took him for his English 131, outgoing and loud professor who is passionate about what he teaches. Class was fairly easy, but also he keeps it involved and its not dead in the classroom. 3 books, 3 essays. You can also skip class he takes attendance randomly.

Very very very nice profesor. Take his first year seminar, way easier than everyone else's that I know. Very chill dude, you legit just have to show up. I think there was 2 assignments which were each 30 second presentations where you could stay in your seat.
Such an amazing person who really cares about his students. I had a lot of fun. Class was always a safe space!

College Writing 

Prof very passionate about what he does, uses a good combo of his own material and given curriculum to make the class actually useful in becoming a better writer, 3 papers for the semester, all other work is completion and not difficult, also clearly very knowledgeable
Worst professor I've ever had. Grading made no sense, didn't have a lesson plan, etc. Disorganized and I learned nothing. Didn't respond to emails or verbal attempts to discuss issues or questions.

Carey is one of the best options for a professor choice for the honors 1-credit discovery seminar. Fair, respectful, understanding, and cares about her students. She asks for participation but won't force it if you don't want to talk. Put in some effort and engage with the readings, and this 391AH section will probably hand you an A no problem.
Carey was such an amazing prof. She was super caring and considerate of what we could do after a year of virtual learning. I learned so much from her and my classmates from this class!

Awesome professor, and I had a fantastic experience. Best 391A at Umass.  Discussion based seminar, great readings and only a interesting presentation is what you are responsible for. HIGHLY recommend.

This class was awesome! It had weekly readings which were short, 1 20 min presentation, and a 2 page paper. She's been all over the world, so she has really cool input on a lot of things. She also brought tea to every class! I would definitely recommend this class

This professor cared about my growth as a writer. I enjoyed the readings because it was a diverse group of writers. I also felt like some students didn't take this course seriously because a lot of them skipped. It wasn't like my life was changed, but I could see a marked difference before and after the course. I would take this class again.
I took their creative writing course and enjoyed the peer feedback and how they were willing to adjust the course in the middle when we didn't get enough time to put or poems out for feedback.

This Professor really cared about my writing. I read a lot, but can tell a marked difference in my writing before entering this course and after. It didn't change my life, but I could see the difference. Some students complained about the reading, but they were great because they also gave extra credit for falling behind.
This teacher was mostly okay, but I just needed the credit.

I esp liked folks reviewing my paper and the different things I would see. I think this professor could work on some things, but overall was decent, and I would take them again. I also took their poetry class and I appreciate the variety of diverse readers we read together in class!

I enjoyed this class because the assignments seemed fair and even though I wasn't a writing major. I learned a lot from the readings. I would take this course if it was more reading based than writing. This professor made me laugh and helped me ease into writing papers.
Claudia was supportive of my writing and helped me to think about my own writing process. I'm surprised she has so many nevative reviews. I thought I's add this one since that's the case.
Wasn't prepared for class sometimes…cancelled class often….didn't seem to take the workshops very seriously. Not sure if teaching is for them

Avoid if you can. Easy A, but nothing of value is gained from taking English 356 with them. Cancelled at least 6 classes over the semester (almost always cancelled classes just before they were supposed to start) and late to the rest of classes (usually 10 minutes). No constructive feedback from professor during workshops either. Waste of time.

Review for English 356! Claudia Wilson is clearly very passionate about poetry. However, I seriously doubt their ability to teach a college-level poetry course, as the analysis was often surface-level and uninspired. They also have a strict attendance policy but were late or canceled class on multiple occasions with little to no warning.

Truly one of the worst teachers I've ever had. Like the other reviews said, she was disorganized all year. She was incredibly lazy, giving very lackluster feedback weeks after assignments are due. I had no idea what my grade would be until the final grades were posted on Spire because she never grades any assignments. Overall complete waste of time

EXTREMELY DISORGANIZED. Cancels classes all the time yet throws an extreme fit if a student misses class. Mind you this was an online class... Rambles on about so many different things and has no classroom management or control whatsoever. Criticizes your essays without clearly showcasing how to improve your writing. Not like other 112 professors.
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Lots of homework--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Class is constantly canceled without warning. Nothing you turn in will be graded in time to help you fix it for your final paper. The directions you receive are never clear and you are often left to figure out how to do things on your own. One of the most disorganized classes I have ever been in.

I was hopeful going into this class seeing 2 really good reviews, but I have never been more stressed out in a class. the grading criteria, prompts, deadlines are insanely disorganized and its causing me and many others to fail. they also often cancel class 5 minutes b4 but expect us to be on top of everything when they're not. so frustrating:(!!

Do not take this class with her. She assigns significantly more work than other college writing teachers and has no idea how to run a classroom. She misses class frequently not telling anyone until 10 minutes before and as of writing this, it's 2 weeks before the semester ends and I have still not received a single grade back.
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Lots of homework--So many papers

reviews.comment: class was entirely online and run through google classroom for some reason? she takes forever to grade and is the most disorganized professor i've ever seen. it's a miracle if we even have class once a week, let alone twice.  gives feedback weeks after papers are due and will suddenly change the due date and say your essay doesn't fit requirements.

Mx. Wilson was really great.. As long as you put in effort you will do great in this class, even if your writing skills aren't amazing. She/they don't give meaningless/busy work hw and doesn't try to force class time. She often lets us leave. I highly recommend this teacher

Mx. Wilson was really awesome to have this semester. They are super down to earth and are really understanding as a person. I will miss seeing them and getting to write about things that interest me as a student. They incorporated themes of intersectionality in a basic college writing class which was super important to me as a student.

She was a very good teacher in class, very fun and lively. HOWEVER, She never responds to emails, none whatsoever. She also never grades anything, all assignments were graded the day grades were due. There is a lot of work without any directions, its a guessing game. Overall, she seems like a nice person just all over the place.

She's a really good professor, and the class is not difficult at all, it's one of those classes where you feel like the professor actually wants you to learn. No "final exam", just a final project that had multiple options. Very sweet lady, and I would recommend the course. She is very passionate about what she teaches.
This class is very heavy on class discussions and 'turning and talking.' Has been a very informative class.

This was my favorite class last semester. CJ got us thinking about how to be happy in and out of his class; his class was engaging, fun and made me think about why we make the choices we make in our writings and lives. He's an open book and always made us laugh with his stories and helped me get a summer internship. Best professor at this school.
CJ helped me realize my true writing ability by allowing me the right amount of freedom and guidance. I owe him my continuing passion for the written word.

I loved taking his class. There are a lot of essays but he broke is down in to smaller assignments and was helpful in conferences. He told funny stories to make the class more comfortable and connected them to my essays. Thank you for everything!
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Accessible outside class--Participation matters

reviews.comment: Great overall, he makes a hated first year class amazing and fun every lecture. There are only a few major essays which you really need to worry about and he exteneds if need be. Also his conferences tell you exactly what you need to do to get an A on the paper. The best thing about CJ is that he is more a peer than a prof.

Great guy with lots of knowledge/connections in the industry. He is a great resource to go to for guidance. In Business In Society, the class typically consists of one group presentation per week, and he leaves his projects up to interpretation.

Professor Clark is dedicated to helping students learn and trying to give them skills that will actually benefit them in their future careers. Class was lectures on Mondays and group presentations on Wednesday. Large portion of the grade was made up of large case studies.
Great teacher, made going to an 8:30 class somewhat easy. Class is pretty test heavy but the material is not insanely difficult if you pay attention in class.
reviews.rating_tags: Amazing lectures --Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Professor Clark is very understanding and respectful, so never be afraid to ask him for guidance or support! He took the time to get to know everyone in class. He is an easy grader who mainly assigns group projects and some self reflections in between classes. Very easy class and easygoing professor.
Took a seminar class with him and got 100% in this class by just showing up and submitting work. Very respectful and caring about his students!
Took a seminar with him. I literally got 100% in the class with zero effort. Great guy overall

Professor Clark is among the best professors at Isenberg. If you have an opportunity to take his classes, you should. You will have no issues if you do the work. I learned a lot in his classes and he does a good job. He will grade you very fairly. I have taken all three courses in the series and it was one of the best decisions I could have made.
He is one of the greatest professors at Isenberg. Take his classes.

I have taken all three courses in the series. Professor Clark is among the best professors at Isenberg. If you have an opportunity to take his classes, do so. If you show up and do the work, you will have no issues. The series builds, but it is not that hard. I learned a lot in his classes. He grades very fairly and you will have no issues.

Jeff Clark is one of the best professors in Isenberg. He really wants to see his students succeed. I took all three of the real estate courses and enjoyed them all. Not only is he a great professor, but he helps his students get jobs/internships. He is the reason I have my job post graduation.

Attendance taken and you will only have like 7 grades total. Your grade is the 3 exams. The exams are hard and he doesn't give a study guide or anything. If you did better on the 3rd exam than the 2nd then he would take the 3rd exam grade instead. BUT, he wouldn't take it vise-versa which was completely unfair. Only take if you are interested in it
I wish the class has more interactions not just lectures
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Lecture heavy--Test heavy

reviews.comment: Grades based on 3 exams, he didn't teach much, you basically learn all of the materials from the textbook not him
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Group projects--Test heavy

reviews.comment: Easy A, your grade will be based solely on the exams. Not engaging
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Lecture heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Low ratings seem harsh. Jeff is an extremely nice guy and wants everyone in the class to do well. Lectures can be boring and most of your grade is dependant on the exams, but if you have a real interest in real estate I would definetly recommend this class.

I took all 3 real estate classes with Professor Clark. Easily one of the best professors at UMass. If you have an interest in real estate, he'll teach you everything you need to know. The classes gradually get harder but he is not a tough grader. When I think of my time at Isenberg, Professor Clark's classes will be the first to come to mind.

Any of the classes with Professor Clark will be the best class you will take at Isenberg. This is not a class you can BS your way through for an easy A. The knowledge you learn from the RE certificate will make you feel like college was worth the investment. If you picture yourself in a career in real estate, take this class with no hesitation.

Prof. Clark is a very knowledgable man with great experiences in the real estate industry. He genuinely cares about teaching students in and outside of the classroom. I definitely recommend this class if you are interested in real estate.

Professor Clark is an outstanding professor. He truly values the education of his students and has great industry experience. He also makes time outside the classroom to help students when needed. I definitely recommend taking any of his classes if you get the chance.

Professor Clark is one of the best professors I have had so far at UMass. He is an industry professional who is teaching because he loves what he does and believes in teaching the next generations. I definitely recommend taking any of his classes.
Fantastic lecturer with great experience and understanding of the industry. Always present to help students when necessary especially with Argus Training

Prof. Clark is a very knowledgeable and successful professional in the industry who offers valuable insight. Amazing guy and very motivated to help his students succeed. If you read the assigned textbook pages and pay attention in class, you'll get an easy A. Overall highly recommend taking his courses if you're looking to break into real estate.

Professor Clark is an outstanding educator who is committed to helping his students succeed. His ability to connect with students, convey complex material in a clear and understandable way, and create an engaging learning environment makes him a valuable asset to the UMass community.

Professor Clark is a great person who is very approachable. The 333 course can be difficult, however, Professor Clark does a create job breaking down content and gives students many opportunities to succeed.
reviews.rating_tags: Group projects--Clear grading criteria--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Professor Clark was an amazing professor and a genuinely good guy. His lectures in class were very relevant to the course and he went above and beyond to make it interesting and keep everyone engaged. The course work was very manageable and he is very accommodating to help students succeed in the class. I would highly recommend all of his courses.

Professor Clark is one of the best professors at Isenberg, hands down. Not only does he make the course content interesting, but he often speaks about his background in real estate investing and consulting which makes the class very engaging. I would absolutely recommend taking a class with Prof. Clark to anyone interested in real estate.
I felt let down by his lackluster teaching approach
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Lecture heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: He reads off slides very quickly and then goes on random tangents. He expects you to know things that were never brought up in class and tests you on them. If attendance weren't mandatory, it would be easier to go through the slides on my own in peace. Hes a nice guy with an interesting backstory, just an awful professor.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Lecture heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: if you are looking for an easy A take him, but if you are looking to learn something, he is not a good option
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: There are 3 homework assignments (not including reading) each semester and 3 exams. He made an agreement twice to have a higher grade on a later exam to double and replace the one for a previous one. Funny in class. Professor Clark is great.

Class has 3 exams and that is your grade. Exams are no walk in the park so if your a bad test taker I wouldn't reccomend unless you are going into real estate. He is very knowledgeable about real estate but this class is not easy by any means, so only take it if you have an interest in real estate.

Favorite class I took last semester. He has lots of knowledge about the industry and has guest speakers. The grading criteria is clear and well made. He is lenient and understanding. There will be one or two group assignments and one group will present something every week. The class requires attendance and was at 8:30 AM, but it was enjoyable.
Jeff knows about the industry and gives a clear explanation in classes.  An interesting intro course for students to learn more about real estate. Straight A if you put some efforts.

Professor Clark is one of the best professors I have had in Isenberg. He offers such great advice and is a smart guy. Since this class was only a seminar, I got to learn more about his career as a professor and working in real estate. This is a special class and if you can take it, DO IT.
After 4 years at Isenberg classes, Jeff is hands down the best Isenberg Professor I've had! Great lecturer, better guy.

Prof. Clark is one of the best at Isenberg and teaches his intro to real estate class in an easy-to-understand way. Attendance mandatory and your grade is based on 3 exams, 3 group projects, and a group presentation done in front of the class. If you put in the work, have an interest in real estate, and show up to class, you'll get an A.

Came into this class with little to no interest in real estate and left considering a career in it. Jeff is the best teacher I've had at UMass hands down. He's an easy grader, gives no busy work, and is an enjoyable lecturer. The grade for the class is based on a few assignments that are pretty easy and enjoyable and a few exams. 8:30 but worth it

Professor Clark is one of the best professors I've had at UMass. He is super passionate and knowledgeable about what he is teaching and you can tell he cares. Lectures are interesting and tests are easy if you pay attention. Highly recommend to any interested in real estate
Professor Clark is amazing! He's so kind, so inspiring and really fun to chat with too. I am taking the second level class now, it's a hard course but I still enjoyed it.

Great Professor! Tremendous lectures, great guest speakers and very easy grader. Jeff does not try to make this class difficult and it is far from it - show up, do some of the reading and you will get an A, and learn a tremendous amount!

Jeff is a fantastic Professor, the best I've had at UMass, he is always available to meet for office hours, and has some great connections in the real estate world as he used to work for CBRE. I would recommend 333 or 433 to anyone. 333 is much easier than 433, but they are both great classes. 433 is very excel-based.

Jeff is awesome. He's a really funny guy and does a good job of keeping the class interesting. There is no homework; 3 projects, 1 presentation and 3 tests. Exams are pretty easy as long as you pay attention and read the book. Jeff is pretty helpful if you ask him questions. If you're even mildly interested in real estate take this class.
He was ok to listen to the first couple lectures but after that it became a senseless repetition of droning on and on. After the first exam I didn't bother to show up and I did just fine

Not an amazing professor but knowledgeable. Lectures are pretty boring. You get a double-sided cheat sheet that is super helpful. He is pretty shy but I felt like I got to know him & I like him much better now. People are saying they didn't learn anything but honestly I learned a lot & the material is soo important to know in the current world.

Overall, the class wasn't the hardest I've taken, but it could be frustrating at times. Lectures were a bit slow early on but got better after the first midterm. Be aware there are two midterms and one final that are hard and make up a large portion of the grade. He was a good guy just was hard to get a good grade because of the weight of the tests
Class was super interesting, and he's obviously very knowledgeable in Clim Sci. He's a nice guy, and he's passionate about what he teaches. :)

just pick another class for the gen ed. you won't want to go to the lectures and the exams aren't hard but a lot to memorize. i personally found them somewhat difficult. he's a nice guy and i genuinely appreciate how much he cares for his students, i just wouldn't recommend the class to anyone.

What is going on? I have a good grade in this class, but it is only by the grace of God. I've heard other people are struggling. Tim is a cool guy, but his lectures are so so so slow. If you're gonna take this class, add all the homework questions to your cheat sheet. #timcookisnotreal
reviews.rating_tags: Lecture heavy--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: I tried so hard to care for this class, but I just do not care one bit. Going to class made me tired, so I realized I can learn so much more from watching the recorded lectures and reading the online textbook than attending the lecture in person. If you want a super easy A, take the class. If you want to learn, stray far from Tim Cook.

good professor, from reading other reviews that say he is passionate about climate science but lectures are boring i can say the same. i am showing up less and less to class. there's this one annoying guy in class who speaks and makes conversation with the professor but classes can be boring as he reads off the slides and u can barely hear him.

He seems like a very nice person, but sometimes the lectures can get really boring, even though the topic was interesting. I barely went to class, but it's an easy A, however you might not learn as much as you want. There's weekly quizzes and then 3 tests for the grade, but it's super easy. Really good class for a physical science gen-ed to get by.

Nice guy but not a good professor. There were 178 people enrolled in my class and barely 10 would show up. Very passionate about climate science, but not good at conveying it to his students. Simply reads off slides that are difficult to take notes on because of his tangents. Class is a VERY easy A if that's what your aiming for though.
Interesting topics but class can be very boring. There is a weekly canvas quiz that you get two tries on

Lectures were super boring but Professor Cook seems like a nice guy who is interested in what he is teaching. Very straight-forward and easy gen ed. Every assignment, even the tests were online and open note.
Went one time. One online assignment a week. No idea why this dude has a bad rating freest PS ever

I took Cook's class as a gen-ed. He is very kind, but lectures are boring at times. Later half of class gets into social/political perspective of climate change and I enjoyed that more. He is very passionate about what he teaches. Easy online take-home quiz every week with 2 attempts. All tests + final are take-home. Take this as an easy gen-ed!

He is so genuinely interested in what he is teaching and you can tell he wants to be there. It is truly inspiring and makes me want to come to class and learn- material is really fascinating. He is SO kind and one of the most considerate and kind professors I've ever had. He genuinely cares about his students, their grades, and their well-being.
He is a nice guy and genuinely cares about what he is teaching and his students. Class itself is pretty easy to follow and exams are online and pretty easy.

I took this class with four friends. I never skip classes, but by late March, none of us were going to class. The lectures are so slow, even though some of the material is quite interesting. Weekly online homeworks (multiple choice, 2 attempts). Three online exams, many answers from homeworks. Incredibly easy, I almost forgot I was enrolled.
Tim is an overall nice guy who cares about the students and the course, but he is so boring. 1 homework assignment every week and 3 tests, so not too much work, but definitely boring. Easy gen ed.
boring class but nice professor, took for my science gen ed and it wasn't that bad

I am not a STEM lover- I chose this class because I thought it would be a more applicable physical science credit but I was wrong. He has no passion and the class is really boring. Like I can't imagine a chemistry class being much better, so I'm not sure what better options non-STEM majors have, but at least all of the answers are online!

Class is straight forward and the lecture slides can be very long. A lot of people take this class as a physical science gen-ed. The class didn't have clear communication since class would be canceled without notice and the grading rubric changing at the end of the semester. Overall, an okay class.

Definitely don't take his class. It was his first time teaching which I am sure played some part, but he decided to change the way the class was graded (lowering everyone's grade) two weeks before the semester ends. When asked about the grade change, he basically said "I don't care, figure it out." Take any other class with any other professor.
reviews.rating_tags: Lecture heavy--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: I hate this guy. He changed the grading scale week 11, which negatively affected so many students' grades. I dropped TWO LETTER GRADES in the span of hours after this. He was not willing to change the scale back, only open up old HW's for 20% penalty. HWs and exams were NOT like the lectures at all. Changed syllabus and reading schedule frequently.

This is not an easy Gen Ed Physical Science credit for non-science people. If you are not a science oriented person, you will struggle. I do the work, go to class, and do not understand his lectures. Very stream of conscious lectures with incomprehensible graphs to follow. He randomly changed the grading percentages Week 11 of the course.
the professor is nice, quite lecture heavy but interesting topics - feels like sphhs150 but with some challenge

I love Beth!!! She's the best. If you're struggling, go to her. She cares so so much and really wants everyone to be heard, and supported in their learning. I credit so much of my love for epi to her because she makes it so interesting and fun. My fav UMass prof.
Worst class I've ever taken. Expectations are not clear at all and she randomly crashes out on the class. Do not take her class ever.

This is the second course I have taken with Dr. Cook; she is an amazing professor. Lectures are clear and she is very kind about any sort of questions, both she and the TAs are very accessible out of class. Attendance is mandatory but I missed half and still got an A. SUPER EASY CLASS!

(SPHHS 150) Ridiculously easy content. Little reason to go to lecture. Exams were sometimes difficult but luckily only count for 30% of the entire grade, the rest is made up of discussion attendance and written assignments

Disliked this class. Attendance in discussion is mandatory and there is a new long assignment almost every week. The exams were difficult and had questions from the textbook and videos. I was able to pass without reading the textbook. Definitely needed to study
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--So many papers--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: THIS IS FOR SPHHS 150: This class is extremely boring. Assignments were harshly graded (even though the material was easy) because the grading criteria provided is so specific and made to find as many mistakes as possible. This class could easily be self-taught and it effectively was.

I actually took SPHHS 150 with Beth (wasn't an option). But Beth teaches a damn good class! I could see how people might find this required class a bit boring and it's pretty packed with info, but she does a fantastic job of making all of it super applicable and pretty interesting for the content it is. Straightforward content, clearly passionate!!

10/10 recommend Beth for this class!! I learned so much and she was a great lecturer. You could use a cheat sheet for exams, which is helpful because the lectures had A LOT of content. Lectures were recorded and you could submit in class activities through canvas for credit if you couldn't make it in person.

Beth is a very caring professor and wants to get to know each and everyone of her students in a 100+ person class. The class is at times difficult due to the nature of the subject, but she explains things very well and is very easy to reach outside of class. Definitely would recommend her as an epi professor

The lectures are so long for no reason and basically describe the same thing. It is such a boring class that I literally can never stayed focused. Yes you get a cheat sheet but every test question is basically the same so it ends up pretty much being useless. It is not the hardest class I have ever taken by any means but it is so brutally boring.

it's not too bad as long as u put in the work. u get 1-2 cheat sheet notes for the exams and 20 of the 100 pts are from easy post-exam reflection questions. there are in-class activities with your group but if you skip class just do the class activities on canvas and you still get attendance credit. beth is rly nice too!

Love her as a prof! Such a slay. Very fair and caring! (always asking and implementing feedback). Graded based on participation (to get a perfect score u had to come to 20 classes), 3 exams, weekly moodle quizzes, and homework. There is extra credit and u can make cheat sheets for exams. Not an "easy" A but veryyy attainable + worthwhile if you try

Best Epi professor out there. Her work is fair and if you put in some effort into studying and doing the homework you will pass with an A. Homework isnt much and are always very helpful for the tests. She is always offering office hours and additional help plus extra credit all the time. she gives slides so you dont rlly need txtbook.
reviews.rating_tags: EXTRA CREDIT--Clear grading criteria--Gives good feedback

reviews.comment: Professor Cook is a great professor in the sense that she teaches the content in a way that makes it easy to understand. She offers students a lot of support and resources and always does unit reviews before each exam. I hated math before I took this class but she made me fall in love with epidemiology.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Clear grading criteria--EXTRA CREDIT

reviews.comment: Pretty decent class! 3 exams, homework assignments, and readings (plus extra credit if you choose). I-Clicker questions/activities in class are helpful. Always accessible outside of class and easy to get help on things. She does lots of course evals so she can make positive changes to help everyone out, so be honest and get help if you need it.
Very good Introductory Epidemiology Class!  Dr. Cook is super nice and teaches very well.  Uses a mixture of lecture, discussion, and group assignments.
Great professor, may not be the easiest marker at times but very clear what she wants so it's not too bad. Interesting, engaging. Easy on the eyes (great bonus when you have to sit for 2.5 hours)!
Explains things well. Follows book and syllabus closely. Discussion period, classwork, all worthwhile. Recommended. Be prepared to do some work and learn.

Good and interesting class. A lot of reading to keep up with definitions of various measures. Very reasonable workload for a grad course (only meets once a week.) She's a cute hottie too which makes it more motivating to go to class.

Interesting lecturer, very hands off. Only 3 grades all semester. I thought he was quite funny. Your grade is really TA roulette. Prof would give all As if he could, but my TA was a mess. Clearly very little guidance or structure given to TAs. Sometimes he takes attendance but usually forgets. Exams (essays) are handwritten but open note.
Soft spoken professor who kept coursework very light. Created the open response exam questions in class, allowing students to prepare their answers in advance.

If you like reading comics/graphic novels you'll enjoy this class. He is knowledgeable and funny. Lectures are mandatory, sit at the front tho because he speaks quietly. Honestly, I never bought a single book and just found PDFs online. Midterm/final questions were given to us in advance and the exams were open-note.
Super chill, very funny, and genuinely passionate about what he teaches. The only assignments are the midterm and final tests, as well as a final paper.

This class can be very interesting at times but the guy is painfully boring. He obviously cares a lot about the subject but considering this is a class based a lot on superheroes...I would appreciate a little more enthusiasm from him. Overall chill dude though.
Hes awesome

Honestly, he's passionate about his subject, and he's also hilarious yet relatable. It's honestly sad how no one ever laughs. Homework is just reading the graphic novels, and the first assignment that happens in class is a midterm that is done in class. The structure of the class is clear and predictable as well.
This dude is lit.

His passion for the subject makes lectures very interesting. you are graded by attendance, exams, and a final paper but you write the exam questions and can write the paper about any graphic novel you want. He's a really good prof, just expects you to show up to lectures and follow along with material, having a background in art hist or lit helps
reviews.rating_tags: Clear grading criteria--Caring--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Best gen-ed I've ever taken. I had no background or interest in graphic novels prior to this class but the lectures are engaging and digestible for any student. Show up and pay attention and you will do great. He is caring and personable, clearly passionate about publishing, art, and comics and that shows through in his lectures. This guy is great.
reviews.rating_tags: Clear grading criteria--Caring--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Course consists of a midterm paper, a final paper, and a 10 page essay project, each containing a couple of essay questions. Questions are made in class and are "open note," meaning you can write your essay in advance and copy it down. There's a discussion section every Friday, which is easy, and half of mine got cancelled. Great gen ed for STEM
reviews.rating_tags: Clear grading criteria--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: This guy is the man. Very passionate and lectures vary in how interesting they are, sometimes they're better than others. Only complaint is that you're only graded on like 4 papers and then attendance. But paper grading is very forgiving.

Chris's classes are always a blast. His lectures are engaging and his handouts are super helpful. There's not much work in the class, just a final and midterm (both two short essays on questions we come up with in class) and a final paper, where you can write about a topic of your choice. Great class, and you'll learn a lot!

Grading: 30% Midterm, 30% Final, 30% 10-page paper, 10% attendance. You don't need to do the readings even though they're "required". Midterm+final is open note and you're given the questions before. Lectures are very boring. Easy class but very boring.
reviews.rating_tags: EXTRA CREDIT--Lecture heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: I really liked this professor and thought he was very educated and funny (it actually made me sad when he would make a joke in class and no one would laugh). Don't let the midterm and final scare you because the students come up with the questions, you know them well in advance, and they're open note. Not a hard class and I would recommend!

Loved him all semester although he was a little all over the place, and the films we watched were fantastic. Workload was 2 short essays for midterm, and a final film analysis that was 10 pages...my guy did not grade my final paper and when I emailed him multiple times he didn't reply...hence the bad rating. Lots of hard work for nothing but okayy.

Prof Couch is a decent professor. The grade for the class itself was determined by a midterm, final, final paper, and attendance. The two exams were very fair as the class came up with the questions and we were given cheat sheets that we could bring in. Lectures can be quite boring but overall good gen-ed class

Prof Couch's lectures are interesting (they are pictures of comic books on slides), and the class is very little work: two in class essays and a final 10 page paper. Sounds like a lot, but I spent 2 days TOTAL doing any sort of work for this class, so great for STEM majors. Rec getting in his discussion, it was the only one NOT on Fridays.

this is such an awesome class to take as a gen-ed! i entered this class knowing absolutely nothing about comics or anything like it and that did not hurt my experience or grade at all. the professor is very interesting in my opinion and can be really funny. he speaks quietly, so sit up front, but this is a very easy and entertaining course.

Let's just say I learned my lesson to never enroll in a class without checking Rate My Professor first. This guy is the absolute worst. Studying comics should be fun and easy but the lectures are unbearable boring. Lectures frequently are off topic and have nothing to do with the midterm or final. His voice is also horrid. Do not take this class.

Prof. Couch is very kind, nice, and smart. He is a quiet talker and sometimes it is hard to hear what he is saying. His lectures are easy and you learn something new every day. Only 2 papers for the whole semester. This is a good gen ed class that fulfills AT and DU. I would recommend if you like comics, easy discussions, and classes.

Prof. Couch is a really nice guy. He is always happy to have a conversation after class and it really helped me connect with the course. He is very quiet, and there is a lot of reading, but there is very little participation, and the readings are not really necessary. Skimming them is fine. You basically can write your own midterm and final.

Prof Couch is a silly little guy. Very monotone but that makes his deadpan jokes that much funnier. This film class was only once a week and very low stakes (he literally talks for 15 mins then you watch a full length movie). I think I would struggle if I had him in a regular lecture - he's very quiet. Not even a film major but this class was fun

Professor Couch is very passionate about comics but his style of teaching does not fit me. He speaks very quietly and his lectures are very unorganized. The course is graded on a midterm, final, and final paper (which have very unclear guidelines) so it could be easy to get a poor grade. He speaks all class and doesn't attempt to engage you.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Lecture heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: I think Dr. Couch would be better in a non gen-ed class. He's nice and very knowledgeable, but his lack of engagement with the class is frustrating, he instructed us not to email him and made us write our own midterm questions. I also wish he would talk less about his own industry credentials, that's not what I'm in the class to learn about.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Lecture heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Prof. Couch's class was a delight to take. The films we watched were varied and his lectures on all of them were really interesting and helped to develop a genuine understanding of course material and a larger social context. If you watch all the assigned films (which are all enjoyable and worth watching, anyway), you'll do great and have a blast.
reviews.rating_tags: Amazing lectures --Clear grading criteria--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Took to cover my DG and AL GenEds. This class wasn't too hard, and got easier once I realized that the readings were not really necessary. The class was graded on 3 assignments: an open-note midterm and final that consisted of two essay questions, and a final 10-page paper. Attendance is mandatory so show up and you should do fine on your papers.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--So many papers--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: AMAZING PROFESSOR! Took this class as my gen ed and I loved it. Lectures were a bit boring and the slides were just pictures, but that's not too important because the midterm and final were basically open notes. The only downside was that there were only 3 assignments (midterm, final, and 10-page final paper). Good class.

COMPLIT135 is the intro to graphic novel class and I would say that its a pretty easy and enjoyable one. Prof. Couch talks a lot but he clearly loves comics and has some nice jokes.
