Grading is on midterm, final, and paper. the midterm and final are open-note short essay, and the final is a 10-page paper. If you're looking for a gen-ed take this

Prof. Couch is very knowledgeable AND enthusiastic about what hes talking about. The class was graded on a midterm and a final (both essays you are allowed to outline them outside of class), along with a 10-page paper on a topic of your choice. I also had my discussion section with Prof. Couch, where he was very engaging and open to conversation.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Skip class? You won't pass.--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Interesting class for anyone who enjoys comics or history. Attendance taken at lectures is a bit annoying as they can be boring but discussions are much more engaging and no homework ever. Be prepared to write a ten page paper but you are given plenty of time to do so.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Graded by few things--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: This is an interesting class. Couch's lectures can be boring and he's often hard to hear, and his slides are vague with little to no words, but not too bad if you pay attention most of the time. Graded on a midterm, final, and paper. Discussion sections are really interesting. Overall it isn't hard to do well if you put in some effort.
reviews.rating_tags: Graded by few things--Lecture heavy--So many papers

reviews.comment: He absolutely loves the content that he teaches and is willing to talk about it at length and in detail while simultaneously including you in the conversation if you care to speak up. Discussion sections are actual conversations about interesting topics including comics, scifi, and pop culture. An amazing dry sense of humor if you pay attention.

This class is honestly a fine class. Professor talks for the whole time and honestly lectures aren't even necessary. Exams are all open book and they give you the questions ahead of time. Final paper at the end kinda sucks cause its 10 pages, but other than that this course isn't difficult and a great gened.
Really nice and funny prof. Easy class (1 credit), but couch is always a blast.

I took this class as a Gen-Ed requirement and it was by far the best decision. Just one midterm and one final report. The midterm is open book, open notes, open laptop test and it's really easy if you prepare the notes beforehand. I would highly suggest this class to fulfill the DU/AT requirements. Easy A.

International Graphic Novels is the second class I took with Couch and unsurprisingly and thrillingly good! He is incredibly well-read and so knowledgeable about graphic novels as a genre across cultures (Japanese Manga, American comics, European art). This man's commentary is amazing and I highly recommend this class to anyone in Five College!

Absolutely loved this man! His Comic Art in North America is undoubtedly the best non-major course I have ever taken. If you are a comic fan like me, you will definitely enjoy this class. Couch is incredibly knowledgeable and insightful about pop culture and a respected scholar. He gives you so much freedom in choosing a topic for the final paper.
reviews.rating_tags: Graded by few things--Amazing lectures--EXTRA CREDIT

reviews.comment: awful awful awful!!! did not show up for midterm, had us write 2 essays with no direction and gives 0 explanation of movies. He also leaves during screening and has no open dialogue with students or TA.

Only three assessments: one midterm, one final, one paper. Lots of interesting readings assigned, but you'll decide if you need to read them all by the midterm. Attendance is "mandatory" but the professor and TAs never figured out a way to actually record it. They also do not know how to use Moodle, haven't published grades in spire a week later.

I took this class Fall 2015. One of the best classes I've ever been in. Try to get into is discussion. He's an extremely genuine guy who really wants you to learn. If you don't mind researching a few comics and writing a paper on them then you should be golden. Would take again.

I took this class as a gen ed thinking it would be an easy A. I attended every class to take notes on everything he said (b/c there are no words on the PowerPoints-- just pictures of comics). Grading for the class consists of 2 exams, a 10 page paper, and class attendance. Avoid this class if you have no interest in comics and only need a gen ed.

This class was the biggest disappointment of the semester. I was very hopeful about Prof. Couch because I had heard  really nice things, but he simply doesn't give a damn. He either canceled classes or invited guests instead giving lectures.  I haven't learned anything from this class and don't recommend Prof. Couch to anyone at all.

I took his International Graphic Novel class and loved it! Chris Couch is extremely passionate about his field and he makes it known in lectures. There's very little work involved, just reading the graphic novels, the exams and a final paper. It was a good choice for a gen-ed, I highly recommend it.

He teaches this class directed towards avid comics fans, so for those taking it as a gen-ed it is an absolute drag. With that said, if you suffer through the lectures you should be rewarded with an easy A. However it's entirely dependent on if you get an easy TA, as they are who grade everything. 2 exams and one 10 page paper are all the class is.

Too much reading for a gen-ed, and had a to page paper due at the end of the semester, which is not clearly explained, discussed in class, and no paperwork is given out about it. No help on the paper, I asked, just had to figure it out myself. TA does most of the grading for the class. Couch is uninterested in his students.

If you can suffer through the dull lectures, you'll be rewarded with an easy A. Open note midterm and final, basically write your essay ahead of time and copy it into the test booklet. Two essays all year. Great choice in GenEd. Couch's speech impediment might drive you nuts though. Consider watching Breaking Bad during class to pass the time.

Class is easy, if you put forth an iota of effort you should do fine.  Professor does mumble and go off on tangents, but those are usually entertaining.  One drawback is that this professor is notably bad at responding to email, even though they are pertinent and important.  I understand profs are bad at returning emails, but this is noteworthy.

Ehhh.  This class wasn't that great.  Lectures were painfully boring.  Professor is caring and fair but often mumbles and goes off on tangents.  TAs entirely responsible  for your grade and are very reasonable/friendly if you get to know them. If you don't have an interest in comics and want this as a gen ed, I suggest looking elsewhere.

Easy class, but he mumbles, oral lecture, you watch cartoons or a documentary on cartoons for 2 hours, 1 10 page essay for the semester on your topic on animation of choice. Midterm and final are easy, they are in class essays where the class creates the questions to the exam, open notes and textbook. Attendance is mandatory.

He is the greatest.  Extremely passionate, always interested to hear what students have to say, gets very into his lectures.  Genuine guy and great TA's - both he and the TA's are incredibly understand, knowledgable, and helpful.  TAKE THIS CLASS - ONE OF MY FAVORITES - I knew nothing about comics and thoroughly enjoyed my time and every lecture

Chris Couch is a very good professor. Unfortunately, he does mumble, so it's good to sit close to the front in lecture, but he clearly knows a TON about comics and wants to help all his students do well. I learned more about history and culture in his class than in a lot of history courses I've had. It's definitely worth taking a class with Chris.

Chris Couch does take a bit of time to acclimate to. If you can get past the slight awkwardness that he initially presents, you will find that he is one of the most wonderful professors you'll ever have. He is SO dedicated to his students. Couldn't ask for a better professor.
Exactly what I expected the course to be. If you can't pull off an A in this class, you're probably going to have trouble in your others...

Chris Couch is my favorite professor ever. He DOES take some getting used to. He mumbles a bit and stumbles over he words sometimes but if you get to know him a bit, he's incredibly receptive and lovely. Most classes of his require a 10 page final paper. Start early - it's not as easy as you think it will be. Trust me.
This is such an easy class. If you want an easy A without doing any work, take this class.

Prof. Couch talks very fast and it's sometimes hard to take in his key points. However, he is VERY knowledgeable on all the topics he covers. Only 3 grades in the class, 2 in class essays for the midterm/final and a 10 page paper. You can use the textbooks on the midterm and final so I recommend picking them up, they do help.

Intro to SciFi is not his forte - mumbling, terrible lectures that are pointless. Just read the books on your own time, show up to class to sign your name, then leave. But I can only speak for this class - apparently, his other classes (comic books) are phenomenal. I got nothing out of his SciFi class, only good for filling like, three geneds.

holy cow, there are no words to describe how much i love this man. he's super-helpful, knows so much about his subject matter, and never hesitates to make the students his priority. sure, he mumbles, but is that really anything to complain about? he is the best professor i've ever had.

He tends to mumble and say um quite a bit initialy.  Once he's gotten comfortable with the class this lessens quite a bit.  He's a really smart and cool Professer.  He worked for DC for quite a while and knows plenty of movers and shakers in the comics industry.

He mumbles a lot and says "um" so much you will grow to hate the word. We took a tally. He said um more than 200 times in 10 minutes. His lectures are BORING, he just reads from a piece of paper the whole time. But the class is easy, the midterms are essays which he gives you the questions for beforehand.

speaks really softly during lecture, which makes it hard to pay attention sometimes - but he is helpful in discussion sections or if you talk to him one or one or something.  the class is relatively easy

Just to be clear, I think Couch is great. However, a lot of the people who take his class are WEIRDOS! If you aren't immersed in art history or punk-rock then I guarantee that you won't understand when people call out weird facts and then everyone laughs. A quote from my class: "It's kind of like EC, but its not" (everyone laughs) Couch: "Exactly!"

He spends a lot of classtime name-dropping semi-famous people he once met, but can be forgiven because he's so knowledgable and succinct. Treats his subject seriously and knows how to get people interested.

An absolutely fabulous professor! His understanding and insight into science fiction and pop. culture makes him the perfect teacher. He is a person of good character, good humored nature and a good listener. A wonderful teacher overall and any of his classes are worth taking!
Chris is amazing and funny and he really knows his**** even if sometimes he slurs his words and mutters.  good man.
A god amongst little geek boys and maybe one or two giggling old ladies.

The perfect teacher for Comic Art in North America.  Couch fits the profile of comic book geek, but defies the stereotype and his complex rendering of the artform does it justice for those of us (like me) who came into the class with limited knowledge of the subject matter.
Never look at comics in the same way after this class.

Chris really listens to his students and learns from them as well as teaches them.  Wants students to do well and will help make sure they do.  Fabulous teacher, nice guy, interesting class.  I recommend him.
A GREAT professor who is both knowledgeable and passionate about his class subject: Comic Books!

I had Prof. Correia for Math 545 - Advanced linear algebra, and also some lectures of Calc 2(Math 132). She is one of my most awesome lecturers at UMass, though she has a very thick accent, you get used to it in 2-3 lectures, and it never hampers your understanding. She is very excited to teach, and you can literally see that in her lectures.
A lot of lectures, homeworks are nothing like exams. Likes to make accusations for students over cheating

Her lectures are incredibly helpful. Missing a class is missing a concept because the lectures aren't recorded, but as long as you pay attention and follow along, it is incredibly helpful. It is clear that she cares about her students and will go out of her way to make sure that those who ask for help get the resources they need.

Professor Correia provides solid engaging lectures. The lectures are not recorded, however, notes are provided for each lecture which are very useful as they cover everything you need to know for the exams. She does have a slight accent, however she writes everything on the board. I enjoyed this course and would highly recommend!

She does not care about students' extenuating circumstances, is a harsh grader, and her accent makes lectures impossible to understand. I would take the course with another professor, or better yet, not at UMass.

Maria was an amazing professor (she's the course chair!). Her lecture slides are incredibly helpful, and the lectures are paced quite well. As long as you attend them and pay attention, you should do well. She was also more than happy to answer students' questions. The course also had a discussion section, which I didn't find too helpful.
Enthusiastic and explains well. Lectures are optional and slides/solutions are posted to Canvas. Make sure to do practice exams, they are almost identical to midterms/final (except MC).
reviews.rating_tags: Clear grading criteria--Lots of homework--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: Even though attendance isn't mandatory, you should definitely go to class, it really helps. There's usually a quiz during discussion, and if the discussion class is cancelled you'll take it in class instead. For homework keep track of deadlines. Pay attention to notifications, and if you struggle, use the available resources, they're super helpful.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Beware of pop quizzes--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: Maria was a wonderful professor and was very enthusiastic! She often simplified seemingly tricky concepts very well. Be sure to look over her notes for at least a few minutes after lectures.

Prof Correia was a very enthusiastic lecturer, she made learning calculus genuinely interesting. She did a great job at engaging with the class and would always answer anybody's questions. Highly recommend her. The material is difficult, but exams are very similar to past exams.

Solid lectures, enthusiastic about teaching and getting students to participate in class. Homework is reasonably challenging most of the time, and I recommend doing most of them manually. No recorded lectures may seem like a big deal, but organic chemistry tutor exists. I recommend a small class size, though most students didnt show up to them.
Lectures aren't recorded, and the notes she uploads don't even match what she writes in class. Completely disorganized and unhelpful.
Absolutely terrible lecturer. She constantly makes mistakes and students end up correcting her. It's like we're teaching the class ourselves.

She's a horrible lecturer, they are not recorded, but she does post notes but it's not the ones she took in class. She often makes mistakes during lectures and students have to correct her. I depended on the weekly discussion because the grad TA was so much of a better teacher. She does have an accent so it can be hard to understand.
reviews.rating_tags: Clear grading criteria--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Honestly take math 132 anywhere other than UMass
0/5 quality professor

Tests make up 80% of the grade, never responses to emails, reads straight off textbook in class and is not engaging, I would retake this class with any other professor or not even at UMass. Ruined my love for math.

Whoever is giving her a good rating has to be suck-ups and/or people who took BC in highschool. I work 2 jobs and at one point had chemical burn and she was not understanding of my situation when it came to extensions. Her office hours aren't helpful but I will say she is a good lecturer although they are rather boring.

I really liked her class. She does examples throughout the lecture. However, since it was an honors class, there was extra homework with written problem sets that were sometimes a pain to do. Her tests are fairly similar in format to the practice ones, but honors exams are more difficult if you have her.
Not particularly hard material, but lectures are awful. They are dull and she is often hard to understand. Also accused me of cheating on the midterm.
never ever would recommend this teacher to anyone. she is rude and not understanding of any circumstances whatsoever.

Maria is very kind and really knows her stuff. She tries to make sure we understand the content instead of memorizing it. Her accent is a little tough to understand. Personally, I feel like her office hours are not helpful; I had to use YouTube to help me understand the content. The exams are mostly examples we went over during class.

Maria Correia was nice and the most energetic professor I had this semester; she definitely cares about her students. The structure of her class made it very passable IMO like there weren't really any surprises as far as questions on the exams ever except the grading criteria. She did have a bit of an accent and the lectures were hard to follow.

Calc II is such a hard class but Maria does an excellent job teaching it. She is sassy funny and always answers questions clearly!! Go to class, do the hw yourself and you will pass fs. I will miss having her as my math prof

Terrible unclear lectures, only goes over practice problems without explaining the concepts, made only all the more worse by her thick accent. Was not responsive to emails. Assigned subjective bad problems sometimes. Still an easy class though.

Not understanding to student's circumstances. Rigid in policies with no extensions. Took in a summer session. One midterm and one final. 5 quizzes (MC through Webassig/Cengage and Open Response through Gradescope). Used honorlock extension for midterm and final. Final has multiple choice and open response questions. First time got this horrid grade

She knows what she talks about and makes the lectures very engaging. The pace is perfect and she makes everything very clear. Will answer questions and reiterate on the more complicated stuff. Calculus made easy.

Maria was a great professor, and she performed a lot of in-class examples. She made calculus 2 easy to understand, and she was very passionate about the course. She clearly knows what she was doing, and she was always willing to answer questions. The only thing was that she had a thick accent, so understanding her was sometimes a challenge.

Professor is not accessible outside of classroom. Does not reply to emails for the longest time, if at all. Thick accent and everything she "lectures" are slides from the book. Tough grader, no tolerance!

She very clearly passionate about math and is always really excited to help students. Her accent takes some getting used to, but as a lecturer she explains concepts very well and connects the ideas to real-world examples. It is also super important to pay attention in lectures to actually understand the material and do well in the class.

Winter class. Lectures are recorded on canvas and uploads annotated slides. Each section has homeworks and a quiz with around a week to get it done but theyre really tough at times.The midterm and final make up 70% of your grade but practice exams she gives are amazing. Calc 2 is tough but she was pretty good at teaching it online.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Graded by few things--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: This professor lacks a sense of communication. If you have an issue with her grading, get ready for her to never respond to your emails. The mini quizzes are horrible and your notes don't even help you with it. Better off going with a different professor and save yourself the stress.

I literally dreaded this class because I never understood what she said. Her accent is a bit difficult to understand so I just learned everything myself. She does not communicate well and writes everything from the little stack of notes she carries. The quizzes we have are way more difficult than the other professor for the same coursde. hated it
Avoid this class. So much homework and quizzes each week. Her lectures are not helpful and you have to teach yourself the course.

She copies off of the textbook so you can get all of her lecture notes online. The quizzes and homework are heavily weighted. She also has a thick accent which makes it extremely hard to follow along and understand her lectures. Would only recommend taking her course if you have experience with the content and are willing to teach yourself.

Her notes in class are all copied off of the textbook, even the examples she uses are step for step copied from the textbook. All of the information from the lecture can be found online. Quizzes and homework are heavily weighted, even though the quizzes are only 3 questions each (meaning a 2 out of 3 is a 66%).
She is a hard grader, and she has a lotttttttt of homework. Be careful to choose her class

I will not take this professor class again!! She teaching is ok, but is really hard grader, Can you believe I got a 0 with the correct answer, with the correct test way but not the step that she want? It is unfair. She has a lot of homework. Be careful to choose this class

Exam problems are much harder than anything you do in class and she has the habit of taking off points for ridiculous things. Also really rude when you ask why something was graded in a contradictory manner from what was taught in class. As a math major, this class is useless for understanding concepts.

I chose her as a professor as the reviews were good. But y'all cappeddddddd. The in class lecture is her rewriting notes that will be posted after anyways. Hardly anyone goes to lecture for that reason. You could really get by this class cause everything is online--including the optional final and every quiz/hw. GPA booster fs.

literally can't understand her. she gives you practice quizzes/ past quizzes that help alittle, but then gives you harder questions on exams. I go into exams feeling confident then immediately want to cry after the exam because they just are 10x harder. if you have her, sit in the front and get a tutor. has made me hate math.

do not take math127 with her. she is not good at explaining the lessons to the point where it is not worth going to lectures. at least 2 homework assignments and 2 quizzes due every week. really hard to understand what she is saying. avoid her if possible.

Prof. Correia is good at teaching. While calc 2 has a few difficult concepts, her lectures were simple enough and helpful in exams. She uses the slides for the class and goes over the examples in class which is helpful when you follow the way she solves a problem, Overall, she is a good professor who gives great lectures and cares about students.

Maria is an amazing teacher. She tries her best to explain some difficult problems so that we know how to answer them for the tests. If you go to her moodle course page for math, she has pervious years tests available for you to use for upcoming tests. As long as you do those and the homeworks, you should be fine.
reviews.rating_tags: Test heavy--Graded by few things--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: She's an ok professor and the course is difficult. She has a thick accent which you kind of get used to after a while. Her lectures are very hard to follow because she introduces topics very quickly and does very difficult practice problems right after but I can't blame her because she has to cover so much material.
Don't take this course online. So much material is squeezed into 2 months and for some reason she dosen't scale tests that obviously many people did terrible on.

I am taking the class online during winter and to be honest, some of the lecture videos are not helpful. The concepts she illustrates in the video do not match the homework we are doing. Some of the concepts are explained poorly and expect us to understand everything. Seems like a nice professor, but would not recommend taking her class over winter

Correia's lectures are thorough and incorporate theorem to justify concepts. Most of lecture is dedicated to covering examples from the textbook to help students apply what they just learned. Know there is a language barrier which can cause misunderstandings, and use past exams to review for tests b/c the general format and content are the same.
reviews.rating_tags: Clear grading criteria--Lecture heavy--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: I found Prof. Correia's 132 class to be very good an effective. In lecture, she'll introduce a concept and then do several examples for virtually every type of problem with that concept. She's very willing to expand on concepts, and she'll extend her office hours the days before exams to help students out. The homework reinforces concepts well.
I found it really hard to understand her

I took this course online over the summer and Professor Correia is one of the nicest professors I've ever had. She is extremely caring, passionate about the subject, and super accessible outside of class. She even made allowed me to take a make-up final exam because I was traveling out of state that day.

Prof. Correia is great at clearly explaining tricky math concepts and her examples are always helpful for homework and exams. She offers several office hours each week over Zoom or in person and they have always been useful. She is extremely kind and caring and she wants her students to do well. If you have to take math 233, take it with Correia!
reviews.rating_tags: Caring--Graded by few things--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Good professor. thick accent but you'll get used to it. Lectures were clear, good examples. Exams were straightforward.

Very hardworking & caring. Her accent is heavy though her notes and materials are amazing! Solves questions in class. She doesn't give extensions for homework and no make-up for quizzes unless a legit reason. She gives solutions to all the sample & past exam papers & also provides with formula sheets making it easy to study for exams.

Very kind and helpful professor. She puts her all into teaching (would walk out of class with pants covered in chalk from writing on the board). If you don't understand things she is very helpful with explaining.

Prof. Correia genuinely wants her students to do well and this is evident in her lectures. She answers every student's questions with respect and patience. Her in-class examples are very similar to the material on the exams and her lectures are very in-depth. Highly recommend taking her for Math 132.

Prof. Correia is kind and knowledgeable on the subject. Lectures are very thorough but can be fast-paced. However, her accent takes some getting used to. Her examples in lectures mimic the exam questions very closely, I suspect she plays a heavy role in deciding which questions are on the exams. For this reason, I would recommend Prof. Correia.

Prof. Correia was one of the most helpful and caring professors I've ever had. Math132 is in no way an easy class, and Prof. Correia made it clear when her office hours were and ensured that if students couldn't make those times that she would still make time for them. So clear and so helpful. GO TO OFFICE HOURS and she'll love you.
Prof. Correia is a solid professor, only complaint is that she does have an accent that will take time getting used to. Otherwise great prof ��

Prof. Correia was great, but be careful if you take math 132 without taking 131. Class can be VERY tough in that case. Be ready to study for ages before tests. Prof. Correia understands how hard it is though, and does her best to help at all times. If you think your test was graded incorrectly, shes willing to fix it, too.

I'm really good at math so I liked her class. There's not much homework but the tests makeup a huge portion of grade. To pass you have to do the work. She won't take attendance but you really should show up to class. I liked her a lot, but a lot of people in my class didn't end up doing well on the two exams we had. Also she has a thick accent.

If you can deal with a strong accent, she's a fantastic professor. Even if you don't get it all in lecture (which you usually can if you pay attention), she's extremely accessible outside of class. Her examples and practice exams mimic the exams very well, with enough variation that you are still in fact being tested on whether you understand it.
reviews.rating_tags: Accessible outside class--Graded by few things--Caring

reviews.comment: Correia is a nice teacher, and cares about math and her students, but I learned more from the lecture videos than from her zooms, and she's not even the one teaching in the videos. I mainly learned from the lecture videos and homework assignments. As long as you watch the videos and do your homework well, you'll pass the class with a good grade.

She was awesome. Frequently extended deadlines, was understanding, and I think she just overall understood that taking Calculus II online during a pandemic is not easy. You could also tell she enjoys math and wanted her students to understand deeper and be excited about it. The grading was also pretty lenient for quizzes, tests, class participation

She is a great professor, and is very understanding of students. The class is test heavy, which works well for me. She is also a very fast grader, and will often put in grades at 3 in the morning. Her moodle is very organized, and concise. Would recommend her for 132.

This professor is is a very clear and concise teacher. I've taken Math 132 over the Winter, and her lectures really helped me understand the material. She held office hours every Friday, and the lectures were prerecorded, which was good for me, but might not be helpful for others. She does problems step-by-step in the videos, which are a big help.

I took MATH 132 over the winter semester. It was pretty intense. Thankfully, Professor Correia explained the lectures very well. She is also very nice to students when answering questions and resolving issues.
reviews.rating_tags: Graded by few things--Clear grading criteria--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: Very bad class design with online learning. Attendance is required for full participation credit. The pre-recorded lectures aren't even her lectures. Just a bad experience overall.

Accent is a bit tough to understand at times, but you quickly get used to it and her lectures are always very good. Shes very accessible outside of class and is always willing to help meet with you if you dont understand or missed something
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Graded by few things--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: Maria was such a good professor. She cares for her students a lot and is very helpful. 132 is definitely a harder class but she is great at explaining and the help is always there. Class is majority tests and the grading criteria is a little bit harsh, but if you try you will be fine!

Built the same way as Math131, with 3 exams carrying almost all of your grade, but that is course-wide. Maria is a great professor who really cares about how you are doing and is always available for help outside of class and before class starts. Lecture heavy, but she goes over any confusion and questions in class, which breaks it up. Great 132.
Tough class, but amazing teacher. Highly recommend her for any math courses, she does a great job with her lectures.

Though she has an accent that may be hard to understand, you get used to it throughout the semester  she's a great person but can be hard to learn from as she can rush/forget things and make us confused. Helpful class slides and is always willing to help during office hours the best she can. Homework took forever but if work is put in, you're set.

Maria has a thick accent, but you'll find her lectures easy to follow once you get used to it. She's always willing to help you during office hours if you have homework questions. She's really passionate about teaching the material and I actually enjoyed taking 132 with her.

She's an amazing teacher and really cares for her students. Initially, her accent was a bit hard to understand but I got used to it in a couple of classes. 10/10 would recommend her for Math 132 over anyone.
Although she has a French accent, her lecture is always nice and easy to follow once you are familiar with the accent. A lovely professor, would take a class with her again.
Has an accent, but great professor, always willing to help you in office hours if you put in the work, recommend her for 132.
Very helpful. Treats students with love and compassion.
Will end the class with an A

Professor Ryan was very friendly and easy to get along with. His class is very easy to do well in. However, I often wished for more chances to talk and debate with my peers, as he often remained front and center in our group discussions.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Gives good feedback--Caring

reviews.comment: GOAT & nicest guy ever- 3 books and 3 essays is the workload for the semester; every class is pretty much a socratic seminar but he yaps the whole time so honestly u don't even have to know whats going on to do fine but it gets boring sometimes. he gives feedback on essays & lets you resubmit for a better grade and is overall a really awesome guy
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Gives good feedback

reviews.comment: Chill and easy A, but I won't lie 201H with Professor Ryan is hugely overrated. You'll get plenty of feedback on papers, which helps grades if you put in effort. However, his Moodle page is basically empty and discussions often turn into long, dry monologues with not enough room for students to talk.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Gives good feedback

reviews.comment: Overall, he is fine but draws on for a long time when he speaks and loses most people's attention. He trying to answer most questions in an elaborate philosophical way that just leaves you more confused than before.

Prof Ryan was one of my favorite professors. He's super passionate about what he teaches and jokes all the time. Every class is an open discussion consisting of 15% student participation and 85% monologue. Participation isn't mandatory but attendance is. We read three short books and were supposed to write three essays, but ended up writing two.

He's so funny, creative,& entertaining! His class is a conversational, discussion-based class where you can be part of the conversations but aren't pressured to if you don't want to. There is hw after each class but it isn't hard (usually just reading). We only had to write a few essays (which he gives great feedback on) & the class is pretty easy!
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Gives good feedback--Hilarious

reviews.comment: Great guy. Doesn't put any pressure on students. You can easily show up to class without any preparation but he chose interesting material and discussions that made me want to read on my own. He puts a lot of detail and great feedback when grading essays. You won't have to try in this class at all but it will be nice intellectual stimulation.

He is all over the place, completely disorganized. He gives out 2 maybe 3 essays for the semester and those are basically the only grades besides participation. He does not have a canvas and sends emails with work but never responds?! But I wasn't able to come to all the classes and he was super nice and let me make up the participation.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Participation matters

reviews.comment: Professor Ryan is entertaining and enthusiastic. There is a lot of reading, but not much asked of you during class. You'll write three papers where you can write about anything related to the topic. He gives detailed feedback and grades extremely fairly.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Gives good feedback--Inspirational

reviews.comment: This dude is literally amazing and cannot recommend him more. I wish I could take his class again. Be prepared to read a good amount, but it's nothing too crazy and it's all discussed in class. The essays aren't hard to complete and he gives you examples of essays he's liked. The GOAT.

This class has a lot of reading and attendance is mandatory. He asks us to come in ready to say something about the reading and ends up just talking all through class. It's pretty boring and I have slept in class multiple times. There are 3 essays and he says you get an A if you have good effort but gives out many grade pending. Most will get an A.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Gives good feedback--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Great, animated prof who made an earlier class easy to want to come to. Very reading-based class & you have to participate but he always elaborates & encourages your points. A few essays on the readings but he gives immense feedback, an entire page of praising. Gives you an A, A- or grade pending & allows you to fix mistakes to get up to an A.

Incredible professor. The class is discussion-heavy but does not pressure you to speak, although you'll want to contribute because the topics are fascinating. He is hilarious! He either gives you an A or A- on essays, or a grade pending which means he just wants you to revise something for an A. He is extremely caring and gives great feedback.
gives very good feedback on essays. doesn't pressure you to speak in class which was very nice. talks a lot but keeps it engaging.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Gives good feedback

reviews.comment: His lectures are very entertaining and he gives great feedback on your essays. The first class he told everyone he hates to give honors students anything less than an A. As long as you do the work and revisions if needed, you should do well in the class. You need books for the class but I just got them cheap on Amazon. He doesn't like technology.
He's the best professor for Honors201H. Period.
Great guy, classes are engaging, books were easy to read, essays were easy to write. Take him for 201h, you won't regret it.

Best lecturer I've had. He reads everyone's essays intently, leaving a full page of compliments. Really lenient grader, never gives anyone below an A-. Super interesting classes, and if you're late to one, he's chill with you attending the next lecture. Plus, he allows revised essay submissions for better grades! 10/10 cannot recommend enough.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Amazing lectures --Gives good feedback

reviews.comment: I would kiss him on the mouth. Great class, would recommend, talks about otherwise unapproachable topics.

TAKE HIM FOR 201H - made my experience with that class engaging, and not stressful. Must buy 3 book. No moodle, just emails. 3 big essays, but not a tough grader and you can revise one. Lots of readings, but I was abskim and they are interesting. DISCUSSION -BASED on the readings - must participate but can say anything. He is SO SO FUNNY.

There was a decent amount of reading but that was to be expected of. Prof Ryan does not use Moodle and only emails assignments and all papers must be turned in hard copy. There was never a syllabus sent out nor a grading rubric for essays. With essays, you either get an A or a grade pending which means you must revise. Overall okay and talkative.

Very interesting professor. Super funny and borderline inappropriate. Tends to ramble while simultaneously using every word in the dictionary. There was not a lot of work, and I did enjoy his class. Definitely would recommend taking his class. I was going to quote him, but it was censored for being innaproporiate by ratemyprofessor.

Professor Ryan may have a nice personality, but the way he constructs his class overshadows any laughs he may give you. He had no idea how to use Moodle and only posted long podcasts as lecture material. He is in dire need of a TA, but even with one, I'm not sure how much better this class would be. Take his class if you like to be left guessing.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Graded by few things--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: This is one of my favorite classes that I have taken at UMass, and Professor Ryan is one of my favorite professors that I have had. There is a lot of reading, but it is interesting reads and his lectures are engaging and inspiring. He is very passionate about the books that we read as well. If you have to take ideas, take Professor Ryan!

Prof. Ryan is amazing! His lectures were long, but his interesting and quirky nature makes up for it. Our lectures were asynchronous audio recordings, but I would have preferred to at least have video. There is sort of a lot of reading and writing, but that is the case with any prof for this course. We only had one paper all semester.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Get ready to read--Hilarious

reviews.comment: Can't recommend him enough. His classes are interesting and entertaining. He is extremely understanding i.e. letting students turn assignments in late, never assigning too much homework. Honestly, an easy A that you'll actually enjoy attending.

201H Professor Ryan is an ok teacher. The amount of homework and readings that he requires you to do outside of class is wayy to much for basically a gen ed. Expect anywhere from 40-60 pages of reading a night or a lengthy documentary. Due to the virus, he is also making us write 2 page essay responses and/or 4 page responses on top of the reading
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Get ready to read

reviews.comment: Super fun guy that makes the class as interesting as possible. Took this with my RAP so the class got along well and his countless quotes helped the group gel even better.

Prof Ryans class was a really good experience. Really quirky and interesting guy. Class can get boring sometimes, but he does a pretty good job at keeping it interesting. There is a lot of reading and a few essays but it is manageable. Overall good guy and interesting class! I enjoyed hearing his opinions and teachings. I recommend
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Get ready to read--Caring

reviews.comment: One of the most amazing professors out there. Kind, understanding, brilliant, and hilarious. He has high expectations for the quality of your essays and you need to read a decent amount every week. The work was worth it and I learned a lot from this class. If you need to take Ideas take it with Prof Ryan.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Skip class? You won't pass.--Hilarious

reviews.comment: You need to read four books and write a paper for each. He lets you rewrite the first paper if you don't get an A, and he never gives below a B+. He gives extremely thorough feedback on papers, and he keeps class interesting with his quirky and explosive personality. Expect at least an hour of homework every night.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Get ready to read--Hilarious

reviews.comment: Loved this class! Just 3 papers along with weekly book reading. Had one pop quiz with various threats throughout the semester but none came to fruition. Overall an extremely easy class. Prof Connolly is zany and borderline morbid at times but he took a soul-sucking class and made it fun and engaging. 11/10 would recommend.
Best teacher ever. Barely any work compared to everyone else's professors. Wicked funny. Take him!!!
Professor Ryan gave all of us A! Even some of them never participated in the discussions in class. But you can still learn a lot of things from him. A great professor!

Just show up! You don't even have to talk and you could miss a couple of classes too. He let us out early sometimes. You really will learn a lot about BDIC too. If you an incoming freshman choose this as your seminar it's the easiest A ever!

I am not big into writing or literature in general, but Connolly made this class one of the best I'll ever take. You'll love his humor and the classroom environment that it creates. His feedback on essays is like none other, and if you do your work he will reward you with the good grades. If you can get him, GET HIM.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Get ready to read--Hilarious

reviews.comment: He makes lectures very interesting, but you definitely have to work for your grade. The feedback on essays are extremely helpful and you can tell he really puts the time in for grading the essays. Overall, the class could be a lot worse and he definitely makes Ideas better.

Connolly is absolutely hilarious. By far one of the best teachers you will ever have at UMass. I was totally dreading taking this class, but it was actually very interesting and VERY entertaining with him. Do not take this class with another teacher.

Aside from the fact that his humor is stuck in high school and he tries too hard to be "relatable," his ideas on life are pretty complex and deep. I think his lectures get MAD boring by the end because the books you read in his class are all pretty much tied to the same idea. Not much room for discussion. Don't get him started on Hampshire College.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Skip class? You won't pass.--GRADED BY FEW THINGS

reviews.comment: DO NOT TAKE IDEAS WITH ANYONE ELSE! Connolly is the funniest, friendliest, zaniest professor I've ever had and likely will have. I look forward to this class all week. There's a lot of reading but not more than what the other profs give and as long as you show you care, you will get an A (he's told us this). 4 graded papers are the grade. Great guy

If there is one class that I would take again, this is it. Connolly is everything you could imagine and more. He's a quirky lad with an undeniable affinity for literature. He doesn't care what you think, so long as you have an opinion. Yeah, there's lots of reading, but it is oh so worth it. Don't take 291a with any other professor.

Connolly is by far the best professor for Ideas that Changed the World. There is a lot of reading, but he makes it interesting. He is a really hilarious guy who sings and uses voices. The only graded assignments are 4 papers, but he gives really good feedback and is a fairly easy grader. If you are honestly trying, you won't get lower than an A-.

Incredibly interesting and funny guy, tells amazing stories.  His class is great, you get a lot out of it by the end of the semester.  Assigns a lot of reading. Definitely the best 291A teacher to choose from, and is one of the best liberal arts teachers here.

When this class ended, I wanted to cry. What a great guy. He's very passionate about the art of literature. He's cool with the times so he tries to make the discussions informal in a way where everyone feels free to speak up. He gave detailed feedback on essays that showed he actually cared. This guy pretty much changed my life.
He's the most awesome professor at Umass! You have to take his class, he really makes you think and cares about giving you feedback. Not to mention he's hilarious.
Connolly is an amazing professor, brilliant and hilarious fellow. You must take his class. It is pretty easy, you just need to read the material and write a few papers. TAKE HIS CLASS.
This course is absolutely horrible but Connolly makes it bearable - he's hilarious and rewards effort and participation. Probably one of the best professors for this class.

can't recommend connolly enough. TAKE 291A WITH HIM. he's hilarious. discussion based class and he does most of the talking which is fine since he's smart. i just skim over the text, no need to read thoroughly. he's also very kind and never puts down a students comment. grades 4 essays very easily and can redo them if you dont get an A the 1st time
Great prof. Best for 291A. Easy grader. Likes to rant in class, but is very enjoyable. It's kind of a lot of reading, but definitely manageable. You really have to try NOT to get an A in his class...
Connolly is the man. His class was interesting and I enjoyed the material. He likes to ramble but great teacher and a really good guy. Not a stressful class. Reading and four essays.

Definitely an interesting guy and class.  Class is discussion based and anything goes during discussion.  There is a lot of reading in the class but for the most part it is enjoyable and engaging when it is brought up in class.  You will get an A in this class as long as you make an honest effort on the writing assignments.

Take 297A with you, no matter what. Its an easy A based on 4 essays that if you didnt get an A the first time, you can rewrite. He is very informal, lax and extremely funny! makes this class extremely fun. Great book choice tho.

Loved this guy. He is the man. Funny and imformal. Very upto date on popular culture. Encourages discussion in class. His choice of books were very funny/interesting. Worth reading and I'm not a reader. 4 essays are your grade and they were unique engaging prompts.

Cool guy, nice to have as professor. Little unprofessional, but in a good way, as class is very informal and discussion is encouraged. His choices of texts were engaging and he was quite witty. The class was always entertaining, and quickly became my favorite of the semester. Land this teacher if you can, he makes freshmen year enjoyable.

Great teacher! Funny and engaging but smart and has great things to say. To get the most out of the class, get involved with discussions. Assignments are interesting and always are accompanied by a learning experience!
Great teacher and an even better guy. The class is funny, but we get a lot accomplished. I look forward to this class everyday. I am in his Honors Seminar and I advise you to take any of his classes.

He has true passion for this class and his excitement and enthusiasm rubs off on the rest of the class. I honestly look forward to this class whenever it meets. There are a lot of laughs, but we get a lot accomplished as well. I truly encourage you to take any of his classes. I am in his Honors Seminar.

I can't think of anything bad to say about, Connolly Ryan. He's one hilarious dude. He always keeps the class involved and laughing. He find great things about your writing and never just shows the bad. He's my friend inside and outside the classroom. English class has never been so awesome. Keep doing what u do! compliments of ur brown bear friend
This class was so fun! We didn't need to take many notes (just on reading) because it was based mostly on discussion. Always making jokes and kept class interesting! NO TOPIC WAS OFF LIMITS!!

This guy is funny and makes the ideas of different historical phylosophers very understandable.  His assignments are never boring or tedious and he makes the classroom setting very friendly.  I'm not just saying this, you will actually look forward to having this class.
Easy class but I like to read anyways. He would find good things about everyone's writing that no one has mentioned before. Wish I could take another class with him.

this guy is the MAN! Intelligently funny and has a way to make you pay attention the entire class...makes you think about the material without it feeling like work and is enthusiastic about teaching!!!!

Amazing. I had him 8 years ago and I still regard him as the best teacher at UMass. I took two writing classes with him and both were great. He knows how to get you writing without it feeling like work. The class only seems easy because you actually enjoy going to it. The fact is, you're writing more than you ever have. Readings were great too.
this guy is awesome! he is having write a paper on people watching. Probably the best topic for a paper I've ever been assigned.
A good discussion leader, easy and very nice. An easygoing guy who is very sarcastic in a good natured way. Enjoyable.

this guy is great, good class discussions and he brings up great topics, really fun class too, he'll always find a way to keep you interested, he's a good guy too, he always wants his students to do well in his class
He's the man.. lets you talk about whatever you want, doesn't assign too many papers, but the ones you DO have to do are interesting and not bad to write. DEFINATELY try to get him
haha, connolly made me laugh the entire class...i'm looking forward for his course this semester
He's a great guy and instructor.  He is witty and throughly engaging. A stickler for grammar, but overall an easy class.

One of the best professor's I have had at Umass-make sure you get him for Dean's Book! Really funny and laid back guy, really interested in what his students have to say and always brings up really interesting discussion points. Lots of fun!
Excellent, fun professor. Doesn't give a grade below a "B" basically, easy to get an A. Not too much work, very fun class. Makes you want to go to his class.
No Comments

Absolutely hilarious!!! Makes class interesting and exciting. It was a very nice intro to college writing from high school. There was only one reading for the entire semester, everything else was jusy your own life experiences. Topics are very open, so theres room to make it fun and unique.
Make sure you get him for Dean's Book.
Made Dean's Book Enjoyable somehow! Funny guy, real chill.
By far my FAVORITE prof. , I looked forward going to his class and I learned alot. He keeps it interesting and is a riot.
had him for dean's book..awesome guy! wicked funny and helpful
the class is a lot of fun and very interesting. Great teaching styles!!

Did not follow the syllabus, got rid of assignments and added others, HAVE TO ATTEND lecture or else you will get a bad grade, not helpful when you go to office hours and lowk creepy. Try to avoid this class unless you want uneccessary stress and anxiety every time you attend lecture. Changes grades up/down 5% as he sees fit!!!!
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: He doesn't have slides for the class and doesn't post anything on canvas besides readings so you have to be in class. He does not follow his own syllabus and says he can change your grade by any percentage he feels based off your effort and participation. It doesn't feel like he knows what hes talking about half of the time. I would NEVER suggest!

Very disorganized professor, frequently arrived late to class, very aggressive, and not understanding. Class was not related to business at all. He encourages asking for help, my experience doing so was extremely awful: his email response was rude, passive-aggressive, and unprofessional. He also plays favorites. I DO NOT recommend this professor.

Genuinely the worst instructor I've ever had in my whole life. The most immature and disorganized person ever. His mandatory office hours are a waste of time, never answers questions, and he expects you to know everything. Expect a more workload than your important classes. DO NOT take this class! Not worth the graduation credits!
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Group projects

reviews.comment: The professor is always late to class by at least 10 minutes and has no structure to the course. His assignments are vague, none of us know what we are supposed to do. He talks about helping you with assignments during office hours but gives close to no feedback and expects you to just do better. Would never recommend this prof
Don't do it
This man was actually the most disorganized professor I've ever had at Umass-if you can take this class with anyone else, do it

He changed the entire curriculum from medical ethics to philosophy of medicine because he was too embarrassed to talk about abortion and pregnancy. He gives heavy lectures and grades each student very differently. He also changed student's grades on assignments at the very last minute before grades were due. DO NOT take his class, RUN.

Not a professor but a PhD student. Grades different student's same assignments very differently. The class is about medical ethics, but all he teaches us is philosophy in health. never answer emails and expect too much from students when the material and lectures are confusing and useless. Run, if u want to take the actual medical ethics.
horrible.

The worst professor I've had. He's unwilling to help, and his rubric is always unclear. Doesn't teach AT ALL and expects you to figure out the material yourself. Lectures are confusing and the class is not what's in the course description. He's late to class every time plus tries to extend class because he's not finished. Run if you can lol.

he doesn't answer emails ever, he tells us to work together in class but lectures the entire class and is surprised we didn't collaborate. he changes the assignments from whats on the syllabus, tells us to remind him of our assignments. his lectures are unclear. i asked him a question and he rolled his eyes. his bare dogs are out in office hours :/
Never answers emails, unprofessional, would not take it again
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--So many papers--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: This class gave difficult papers that took longer to understand the language than understand the piece. Prof didn't like questions and had a hard time helping when confused which was often. He required office hours and had a lot of group projects which were difficult when a solid amount of people in the class didn't understand. Decent lecturer tho.
reviews.rating_tags: Group projects--So many papers--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: No exam or quizzes. We had weekly readings and group presentations. The readings are a bit wordy and confusing. Your grade mainly depend presentations so if you are someone who doesn't enjoy public speak or reading, this class might not be the best for you.
reviews.rating_tags: Group projects--Lecture heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Easy class and interesting, the professor is nice too
reviews.rating_tags: Group projects--So many papers--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Showed up late almost every day. He sent emails with required work at 3 in the morning, due in a day, then didn't understand why people were confused with his unclear instructions. Never made it clear what we were supposed to be doing in or out of class; majority of class was confused all of the time. Rude to students and makes inappropriate jokes.

By far the worst professor I have had at umass. Showed up late half the time and couldn't teach. Spent half the semester talking about venn diagrams for probability and more then half the class still didn't understand it. Assigns group projects but then gets mad when you work on it with your group. Doesn't like when you ask questions and is rude.
reviews.rating_tags: Graded by few things--Lecture heavy--Tough grader

reviews.comment: The entire semester, he did not reply to any email I ever sent him. Gets very frustrated when you don't understand the content and often refuses to further explain because we "should just know this by now". Is always 10+ minutes late to class. Understandable to think this will be an "Easy A" gen ed. IT. WILL. NOT.

Still questioning if this class was one big joke. This was one of the most frustrating experiences ever. The assignments, or serious lack there of, didn't follow the syllabus at all. He doesn't respond to emails. Nothing is on Canvas. Don't know how he's still allowed to teach. Please DON'T take this class or any with Craig, for your own sanity.

Didn't upload half the assignments on the syllabus and never responded to my email. I got a B+ and have no idea why bc only 3 grades got uploaded so now I have to send him another email so I can know why I got the grade I did. Incredibly unorganized, the class meets only once a week and has TAs so idk what he was doing instead of grading.

I don't even know what this class was about. We did a few group projects which were never graded and then one really long group project which was also never graded. Had us read a book to write a review and then never assigned it. Doesn't respond to emails. Nice guy but was completely disorganized. Easy A if you show up to class.

Never prepared for class + always sweaty- by far the worst class I've taken at UMass. Didnt follow the syllabus or put a single grade in Moodle. I didnt know it was graded attendance till halfway through the semester, p sure he was scrambling to make up grades since he barely assigned anything for us to do. Waste of my time,but at least I got an A

Craig is a really nice guy, but the class was completely disorganized. His lectures were dull and i learned very little. Pretty easy A if you show up for most lectures and participate. Had a few VERY drawn out group assignments. He did not make any criteria for grading clear the whole semester. easy 4 credits (2hr lectures on W/F) but no lab

I took her Envi Ed class (NRC 520) and was SHOCKED at how rudimentary the class was. I loathed coming to class bc of how surface level the material was (I study this stuff 4 my major). I got a C+ bc I didn't do the BS weekly nature journals. Not engaging or challenging whatsoever; ridiculous for a 500 lvl class. The final was so bad - Hot Mess

Class was very discussion-based. Read a couple of articles and papers each week and talked about them in class. I usually am not a fan of this teaching style, but hearing perspectives and thoughts from classmates and from Britt always helped me to piece together different themes and ideas from readings. Learned a lot, highly recommend!
Really good class. Prof was really passionate about our topics. She'll notice if you skip class though.
Class was pretty interesting and easy. Not a lot of prep/effort from professor. Very discussion based. Grades are not posted throughout the semester and expectations are unclear.

Pretty good class and prof. Curriculum is relevant, thought-provoking, and well-structured, but not unreasonably difficult for the most part. Grading is attendance and participation (30%), material response posts (30%), current events post (10%), and final research project (30%). My only frustration is that Britt has literally graded nothing yet...
If Dinner for Schmucks was a class this would be it. NEXT!

Prof Vlas is great! This class has a bad reputation in Isenberg but Cristina made it really fun and low stress. She makes sure you're well prepared for exams and gives great feedback for the capsim simulation. She will not let anyone fail!! Class was overall very easy and she is so nice and really cares about her students.
Avoid!! Heavy accent, hard grader and knows little about business outside of the text book stuff. She does know a lot about farming from back home. Those stories were interesting.

This class is a pain. However, Professor Vlas makes it a whole lot more manageable. We weren't graded on the CAPSIM which is a god send because that software hates fun. My class got moved to online midway through the semester because the Isenberg basement flooded lol. Overall, pretty easy course, workload kinda a pain at times. Make a good group.

This is a hard class, but mandatory. Ask her to zoom outside of class! She is so helpful and caring one on one. Do the extra credit and try your best to get high scores on at least 3 of the Simulation rounds. I can't stress enough - meet with her one on one!!!! I twill make all the difference in the virtual world. She is very sweet and caring.

You have class 15 minutes once a week. She expects you to have already read the slides. Talks about nothing during those 15 minutes. Lecture quizzes every week for the first half of semester. 10 minutes, 8 questions, never had enough time and they're hard questions. Similar with exams. Simulation makes absolutely no sense. No help outside of class.

Not a bad choice for an instructor for this course. The lecture portion of the class is pretty easy and very passable. The simulation section will make you lose your mind, but it is not her doing. She tried her best to help us along and with extra credit at the end, it was very easy to get an A.

I loved this class. She was a very easy grader, as long as you participate you will get a good grade. The discussions are interesting as long as you do the readings for them. Honestly great class overall, I do not know why she has such terrible reviews. Would definitely take a class with her again.
Professor Paul is very sweet and understanding. She is kind and accepting of all her students and wants all of her students to succeed. Would definitely take a class with her again.

An absolute nightmare. You never know what grade you could possibly be getting because she is an insanely tough grader. I am convinced nothing will satisfy her and she finds enjoyment in marking down papers. Do not take this class if you value your mental health.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Get ready to read--Tough grader

reviews.comment: She is a VERY tough grader and often goes over class time. She makes you pay for books in the middle of the semester and says that it's "not that expensive." She teaches it as a grad class as there are a lot of papers/assignments, on top of that, she wants you to finish the semester off with a 50 minute presentation - which is harder than you think
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Get ready to read--So many papers

reviews.comment: She is a very nice person over zoom (I took this class during COVID so online only) however there is a LOT of work. She is a TOUGH grader on the discussion notes also. The readings for the notes are VERY long and often hard to read. At least 2 assignments due per week both of which are somewhat long and difficult.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Get ready to read--Tough grader

reviews.comment: Crystal Paul is a nice woman. However, a very tough grader and is really picky when it comes to discussion notes. She is very strict on due dates and hates to reopen assignments. You mainly learn from the readings, not in class. Overall, she lacks a bit of empathy and doesn't really care what your situation is, she really only cares about the work.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Get ready to read--Tough grader

reviews.comment: Prof. paul is honestly a nice person so I feel bad saying anything negative about her, but this class is just horrible it was structured so poorly, you literally are not directly taught a single thing, you just watch videos and hope your classmates will teach you the rest. Definitely wish I had not taken this course

Worst professor ever. Teaches you absolutely nothing and assigns so many assignments. I had to get on Prozac because of the anixety this GEN-ED R2 course has caused me. This prof is clueless and this course will ruin your GPA. Worst prof at UMASS hands down.

This class was online during quarantine, so yea - it was going to be hard. She did not teach us anything. She simply gave us assignments to teach our fellow classmates, which doesn't actually teach us anything. She assigns weekly quizzes about things we haven't learned yet. She seems very inexperienced, and I strongly do not recommend this class.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Graded by few things--Group projects

reviews.comment: I guess Ill add my positive opinions like everyone else. Professor Cruise cares about her students. She wants to get to know everyone and is willing to help everyone. She deserves to get an award for supporting students.

Gail is such a sweetheart. She respects all of her students and always provides great feedback. She also gives very good grades in my opinion. I am not the best writer and I still managed to do well. Best prof for junior year writing.

From day one, I could tell that Gail actually cared about her job. She wanted to know everyone personally and spend individual time with each student to give personalized feedback. Definitely a great resource to have. The projects seem to be pretty tough, but she grades mostly on effort and improvement. Take Gail for 310 for sure.
Gail is awesome! Very useful feedback to students on business writing and makes applicable assignments to the future. Loved her class!
reviews.rating_tags: Respected--Skip class? You won't pass.--ACCESSIBLE OUTSIDE CLASS

reviews.comment: Loved e tech and learned new ones
Great professor!

Never really understood her grading system, but she did make it clear how she wanted you to improve and how she'd look for that. Pretty lenient grader otherwise - she just wants everyone to enjoy the class, participate, and become a good speaker. Not much work outside of class necessary.
This class was great. She gives you a lot of feedback and helps you through the assignments. Very helpful with resumes and cover letters. Prepares you for the real business world. No textbook.

She is a fabulous professor. Her passion about her work shows. The teaching style makes it apparent that she wants your success in the world just as much as you do and even though she is a strict grader, it is so beneficial. From what I experienced, as long as you do your work, it's impossible to get anything lower than a B in this class.
She's a character, but really help and down to earth. Loved her and actually learned quite a bit. Very helpful in the writing center as well.
I had her for the Diversity & International Fellows Seminar. She is really nice and cares for her students.
loved her! loves to teach, very helpful and easy to talk to. One of the nicest in SOM. I highly reccommend taking any class with her.

Consistent work and effort are important throughout semester especially to get an A, but if you do the work, attend class, and participate you will do well. Will extend deadlines on assignments when students have a lot due and considers students' busy schedules. Great edits on assignments--if you follow her feedback you will do well.

Down to earth and really makes sure that everyone understands the material.  She expects you to work for your grade but she shows she cares about the students and gives all kinds of feedback.  Great notes and good explanations.  I would definitely recommend her class!
strict but fair, good teacher
she is the worst teacher ever. Requires so many unnecessary stuffs. Even you try it so hard, it it impossible to get A in that class.
it's just so hard...so many writting assignments...basically every class.

She is definitely one of the best lecturers. She understand other cultures and I really enjoy being in the class. She is very caring and friendly. Also, she is very good at dressing too!! I love her class so much and this is the only class I make so many friends from various background.

I came in looking to get a solid basis on animal physiology/anat. Professor Cousin gave inaccurate information, and degraded students. Labs were disorganized, and she put individuals down to gain superiority. Above all, I left this class learning how to deal with the real world's difficult individuals.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Lecture heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: A lot of content and diagrams on the exam would be pulled from recorded lectures she posted, because she would run out of time during class. Must memorize basically everything for the exams because there are so many potential questions you may see. Her handwriting is difficult to read and she often misspells or forgets parts of a diagram

Her exams were mostly material from the practice quizzes. However, when she would label diagrams in class, she would ask you for things on the exam, that were never gone over in class. You have to go above and beyond to teach yourself the full systems outside of class. The labs also felt unorganized, the TA's never seemed to know what was going on

BIG time commitment, you have show practice every week which schedule builder doesn't state so be prepared to spend 3 hours a week at the farm. We do way too much for a 2 credit class and the exams are packets. Spending time with chickens is fun but only take this class if you have time to dedicate to it outside of class.

I would say don't take this class but unfortunately you probably have to. Dr. Cousin is a nice woman but she cannot teach. Her lectures and labs are very unorganized and you will have to watch additional videos outside of class, as well as get the answers to everything yourself b/c she does not provide her TA's and SIs with the material to help us.

A lot of lecture material but that's anatomy for you! She made the class super enjoyable for me, varying up lecture material with drawing content. Exams were questions taken from the hw quizzes, so an A is achievable! Only downside is it was hard to get in contact with her outside of class, she doesn't look at her email often. Extra credit too!
Dr. Cousin is one of the best and most talented faculty members on this campus.

Best class by far. doctor cousin is interested in what she is teaching and is super knowledgeable on the topic.Her lecture notes can be difficult to read but they are interactive so as long as you are writing while she is speaking it won't affect your performance. A ton of material but exams are the exact same questions as the homework quizzes

Dr. Cousin is very kind however is not a good professor. The lectures are unorganized and she often did not complete the material on time. The labs are poorly structured and the correct answers are not given. It is difficult to read her hand writing during lecture. Make sure you do the reading she provides and study a lot for the exams.

Terrible class. Grade boundaries are rather daft, the grading is not all mentioned in the syllabus, hard grading (making getting an A which is above 95% even harder), as well as a lack of support and hard to reach outside of class. Some of the TAs were good, some. Sticking to any other management class.

Dr. Cousin has difficulty keeping lectures organized. Often goes over time and needs to make up lecture time by recording videos. So you spend a lot of time on lectures. Quizzes and exams are not difficult if you study and pay attention.

This class is 2 credits but with the amount of work,it should be a 3 or 4 credit class. Class is great & very hands on though. Cousin is vague about class instructions but well respected in ansci. Lots of busy work and outside of class work including weekly poultry journals,weight entries,quizzes,5 morning chick checks,homework,and a group project.

Professor Cousin cares about her students but overall is a poor professor. She fails to go through her lecture material and posts additional hour long videos to finish the material. Her notes are messy and incredibly hard to read. Additionally, during labs the correct answers are not given and it is the students job to google them. Good luck AnSci.

Overall, she is a great professor and really cares about her students. I emailed her a few times with questions, and she got back to me quickly to explain it thoroughly. However, studying every source is a must (quizizz, SI, coloring books) as it was all on the tests.

Overall, she is very kind and knowledgeable. Practice the quizziz-es before each class to prepare for pop quizzes. Grades are very dependent on exams. Study ALL diagrams - use coloring book, quizziz-es and go to SI sessions. Labs can be hard. The lab practical is tricky, have good notes. I liked the textbook. Email her questions if you're confused!
reviews.rating_tags: Beware of pop quizzes--Lecture heavy--Test heavy

reviews.comment: Dr. Cousin refused to share the answers of the labs before the test so we could figure out what we did wrong. She is very unacommodating and frankly rude. She always goes on a tangent in class that has nothing to do with the material. She wastes class time and blames the students for not moving fast enough.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Beware of pop quizzes--Test heavy

reviews.comment: Dr. Cousin cares about the students and was willing to make practice tests about any topic on the exam if asked. The lab practicum (final) format was unexpected but the tests are pretty predictable and easy if you study the material she provides. Flow charts she makes and activities are fair game! The SIs were extremely helpful!!

Overall I think Helene took a course that is very hard to teach simply because of how broad of a topic it is and made it very graspable. The one thing that did kinda bother me was how to some degree attending SI sessions are essential to grasping all topics taught in the class. It was helpful to have a partner to work through everything with.

Dr. Cousin is a very caring teacher. She's very good at explaining concepts. Her lecture slides can be overwhelming sometimes and it's stressful that she gives A's for 95 and above, but overall a great prof that only wants her students to succeed.

An A is above a 95 which is already tough and it feels like every single assignment determines the final grade. There are at least two quizzes a week plus in-class quizzes. Lectures are slide-heavy. I wouldn't be exaggerating if we went over 1,000 slides all semester. Content is hard, exams are memory-based, labs are usually hard. Go to SI sessions
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Clear grading criteria--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: You can tell that Dr. Cousin is passionate about what she teaches. There is a lot of material covered in this course, but Helene does her best to make it bearable. She gave up to 5 extra credit points this semester and also dropped the lowest exam. GO TO SI SESSIONS. SI PACKET QUESTIONS SHOW UP ON EXAMS.
reviews.rating_tags: Accessible outside class--Skip class? You won't pass.--EXTRA CREDIT

reviews.comment: You can easily tell that Cousin cares about her students and wants them to succeed. The material can be a lot at times, but the TA review sessions will save you a ton!!!
One of the best animal science professors at umass. She makes lectures very engaging and exams are very fair. Extra credit is available, but you probably won't need it.

Super caring professor! Attendance is mandatory (can't skip any) and she counts clickers for correctness. There are no exams, only 3 big homework assignments. Then she gives an option of a final exam or a presentation with a group. Always available to meet and enthusiastic to help! Grades fairly and really passionate about developmental biology
reviews.rating_tags: Accessible outside class--Participation matters--Skip class? You won't pass.

reviews.comment: She's not mean, but she's set up the class to be as difficult as possible. It's basically a 5-credit course as she created her own discussion section which "isn't mandatory" but where attendance is taken and all the info for the exams is taught. The lectures themselves were basically useless, and she's really vague about what will be on the exams.

It was very clear what she expected you to know and gave that information to you through extra discussion periods. To earn an A in this course you need an exact 95, which is incredibly unfortunate when you earn a 94.87. She is very knowledgeable and kind. It's unfortunate that the TA's were not more knowledgeable, often giving incorrect information
