Attendance was "mandatory" only because of iclickers ( only used like 4 times). The best advice given for this class is GO TO DISCUSSION, all her tests are best on the discussion packets so just study the packets. Honestly, half the notes I took in lecture are useless and I never used the textbook. Also, you don't have to download the $10 apps

Dr Cousin is a very caring and sweet professor who clearly enjoys teaching and this subject as a whole. Love the non-cumulative exams, labs were fun and easy. TA review sessions are not required but mandatory to pass the exams. Unhelpful TAs who dont know what theyre doing. This is a hard class, you will need to work for your grade.

super hard to understand her and almost impossible to please her in this class. she had a lab and then in addition to her lecture she created her own discussion section without us enrolling in it and declared it mandatory. IT GETS WORSE because her TAs don't know what's going on and are useless. DO NOT TAKE A CLASS WITH THIS PROFESSOR
reviews.rating_tags: Tough Grader--Skip class? You won't pass.--LECTURE HEAVY

reviews.comment: Gives papers and clickers for grade, very good professor need to be in class for iclickers. No tests! Just 3 homework assignments that you can complete in a group and the final is a group project or test option (do the project) Grades fairly and is always accessible to talk to outside class. Knows her stuff you will learn a lot!
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Respected--BEWARE OF POP QUIZZES

reviews.comment: The lectures were very in-depth and well done, but only blank slides were posted online so attendance is key. Iclicker points counted for a lot, and correctness mattered but only a bit. Dr. Cosuin was very into the topic, very helpful in office hours and in class, and pretty understanding. There are NO exams in the class, only three HW assignments!

I took BIO58O (Development Biology) with Dr Cousin. She is an engaging instructor and is clearly passionate about the subject matter. She often referred to real world examples of the concepts discussed in class. I wish there had been a rubric for the homework problem sets, because I wasn't sure how to answer.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough Grader--ACCESSIBLE OUTSIDE CLASS--GRADED BY FEW THINGS

reviews.comment: Long and difficult open response test. My year was the first she tried doing a lab practical, and i got unlucky and had to do it alone, while every other student got to work with a partner. When i sent her an email to complain she never responded, had to get my adviser involved for a response. I sent her an email back, and got nothing again.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough Grader--Skip class? You won't pass.--LECTURE HEAVY

reviews.comment: Awesome professor for an awesome class. Material can sometimes be dense, but she'll always clear up points of confusion. No exams, just 3 major homework assignments, which can be difficult but find some friends to do them with. Didn't use the book at all until the final project, so make sure to go to class, and she uses iClickers for attendance.
She's a very fair grader and will give you all the opportunities to do well. Attend lecture and focus on taking down her notes that are supplementary to slides.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Clear grading criteria--Caring

reviews.comment: Dr. Cousin is a very nice woman, but this class sucks. There is almost no such thing as taking notes in this class. This is essentially a 5 credit course that needs a discussion and laboratory section. Her 5 exams are often heavily involved in one subject that if you get wrong will leave you with an automatic C. All diagrams and memorization.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough Grader--Skip class? You won't pass.--TEST HEAVY

reviews.comment: Labs are fun and easy, lectures are interesting! Professor Cousin tries her best to make her lectures entertaining and she's very funny! Go to discussions, her tests are based a lot on those packets and be ready to study! Exams are open ended, you have to know your stuff, but she's very friendly and willing to go the extra mile for her students!

I came into the class when Professor Cousin changed her teaching style completely, she made 5 / 7 tests count and that helps with the amount of material there is on the exams! She's really helpful when you ask questions! You MUST go to the TA review sessions because she tests you on stuff you go over in those packets!!! :)

Awesome Professor especially in lab!  There is a lot of material to know and it is hard to know exactly what she is going to put on the exams. If you have trouble with fill in the blank then the exams will be hard and I suggest you go to office hours right away if you do poorly on an exam. She wants her students to succeed and is happy to help!

Her lectures can be very confusing and boring, being non-specific about what we need to know for exams and what's just "cool to know" but she gives so many chances to do good in the class. The exams are fairly hard and open-answer, but she drops 2 of them if you take the 2 cumulative exams. Lab was pointless. I-clickers occasionally.

A&P is a very difficult subject and I'm glad to have had Professor Cousin. She is very passionate about what she teaches and the class is the right amount of challenging. There is a LOT of information to learn for the tests and you have to study to do well. But Professor Cousin is very kind and I really enjoyed her class.

Wonderful professor! Her exams are a little rough: fill in the blank, annotating diagrams, filling in charts. It's a lot of information. Her lectures are very helpful, so don't bother buying the book. I enjoyed her French accent, it made boring material interesting.

This is a tough class because there is a ton of material. The exams are mostly diagrams and fill-ins. Cousin is very nice and will help if you ask, but she is very unclear in what is going to be on the exam, and really only gives specifics the day of. May just be my TAs but exams were graded VERY inconsistently. Frustrating class.

This class is so hard, so much material, and she's very confusing. She gives study material that is factually incorrect, tests are graded with MANY mistakes. Grades do not reflect effort because how well you do on exams depends on whether or not you studied the right material: too much to study everything. Hated this class.

This is a hard class, there is no way around that, and I am very glad Helene was my professor. She is very knowledgeable and seems to enjoy teaching anatomy. However prepare to do LOTS of studying, because its never quite clear what will be on the exams, and there is a lot of material to cover. But I learned a lot from this class.

She can be hard to understand at times and the material can get tough. However, the grading system is student friendly and if you do the take home exams with friends and know what she is talking about, the in class exams are literally the exact same thing. She offers extra credit to people who attend seminars. She is a great prof. very helpful too

The material is hard to comprehend with no background. The class is a bit disorganized. BUT she is an extremely helpful professor.  Any trouble, you can go to her and she'll go through it all. She is very nice and SUPER smart.Easily in the top 3 of all around (personable, knowledgeable, grading) professors in the UMASS Bio. Dept.

One of the nicest teachers I have had at UMASS.  Sometimes a little hard to understand, especially with the pretty dense material. But she gives you all the opportunities (extra credit, corrections, and very helpful practice exams) needed to get an A.

Prof. Moritz is an expert in the field of computer architecture and his classes provide good intuition for the design challenges in the field. As a processor design engineer, I can unambiguously state that the topics discussed in the class are closely relevant to the industry and provide solid foundation to excel in the field. Very useful course.

One of the best teachers at UMass. He provides intuition for each concept that makes it very easy to understand fundamentally why and how it works, which not many teachers do. Very easy to talk to, patient and approachable. His lectures are always interesting and include lessons from his research and professional experiences.

He is an amazing teacher, and a great mentor. My PhD journey in his group started with his 668 course. The lecture contents include components from traditional computer architecture literature and advanced research topics. I learnt a lot, and I could publish a conference paper out of the course project.

This guy is terrible. He is my advisor and my teacher. He is awful at both. He is interested in seeing students learn, but if you have not perfected your knowledge he doesn't give you any credit. He doesn't grade fairly at all. He basically grades with an "A or F" approach. The other teacher for the class is fair so I will get an A in the course.

Great professor! Very very knowledgeable. His lectures are the best and his interviews during the lab demos are very professional. The class is very time-consuming and hard, but Prof. Moritz is one of the few professors in Engineering who is concern about students learning. I'm glad I was in his class, and look forward for future classes with him.
uninterested in teaching, preparing question papers, grading projects and answer sheets..

He's a good guy but the class itself is pretty slow moving and pretty much just read off the slides/videos are played of other people giving lectures. The grading is easy as the tests are all take home but there are very few assignments so you have to do well on those to get a good grade.

As person Curt is great, however after taking two classes with him I can confirm that the questions on his exams (all online) are never one's that I'd expect, so even looking at my notes wasn't helpful. NRC565 has a lot of labs and projects that require you to go out and collect data outside of classtime, so I don't reccomend during a busy semester
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Group projects--Beware of pop quizzes

reviews.comment: Good professor who cares about his students. Quizzes and exams are online and some questions can be very specific, but because the exams are not timed you are able to look back at your notes. Interesting guy with good stories to tell. Clear passion for the subject.
Great class, better person! He gives multiple exams so that you always have a chance to improve.
NRC 565 Wildlife Population Dynamics brilliant professor. genuinely wants to see you learn and do well

Great advisor and mentor.  Solid feild experience prior to taking it to the classroom.  Very willing to help clarify issues.  Took population dynamics and modeling with him.  Very interesting guy, hope he stays there a long time.  Still in contact with him.

There should be an "Accent" circle to check - Curt's Texas accent is half of the reason why I love him so much.  The material for Pop Dy wasn't the easiest but Curt presented it well and was sympathetic to our stupidity.  He's a great guy and presents an interesting class.  Get him started on elephants and he'll talk forever!
Good class, great guy
Well traveled, great knowledge in Conservation Biology. Will even drink a beer with you on occasion. Great personality.

took family&state w prof Curtis sp24. Great class, got a lot out of it. Heavy on participation tho so that was a hurdle to overcome. Spent most of the sem working on final research paper. Presentation on research at end of sem. Grades everything based on completion, so if you put the effort in and do all the assignments you'll get an A

I took legal reasoning my senior year knowing that I was planning to attend law school. At the time, the reading and assignments seemed like a lot of work but it is nothing compared to law school. If you have any interest in law school take this class! Entering law school knowing how to brief and analyze cases is an invaluable skill.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Get ready to read--EXTRA CREDIT

reviews.comment: I just finished taking her class Legal Reasoning, and it was the best experience so far at UMass. If you have any interest in becoming a lawyer, or have an interest in the law, I would recommend that you take this class as soon as you can. She is intelligent, charming, hilarious, and is always willing to help you any way she can. Take her class!

Very kind and charming person. The class is organized, timing is compact, and the reading materials are precisely adhered to her goal of teaching. Very lenient grader, giving 90 points of extra credit in addition to the original 600 (60 percent of grade).

Professor Curtis is second to none, I wish I could stay at umass just to take more of her classes. She does require a lot of reading, but if you're interested in the subject it is manageable. Professor Curtis is always available and eager to help students. She's open to viewpoints and encourages debate. 100% would recommend taking a class with her.

By far one of the best professors at umass! I had the option of taking her class or an easy a to fulfill a requirement and I'm so glad I chose hers. Beware it isn't easy and its a lot of work but I learned more in this class than any I've ever taken and she is so inspiring. If you put in the work you'll genuinely enjoy this class

Professor Curtis is hands down the best professor I have ever had at UMass. She is extremely helpful and clarifies any questions that you have. I have learned more in this class than any other class I have taken. I highly recommend taking a class with Professor Curtis.
Diane is a great professor. She teaches you how to think like a lawyer. This class will help you decide whether or not to attend law school.

I have taken 5 classes with her, literally exhausting her roster of classes. She is the best professor I have ever had at UMass and among the best teachers I have ever had in my life. She inspires interest in the topic and she challenges you to think outside the box, sometimes to defend ideals you do not believe. I'm her biggest fan!

I love this woman! She is brilliant, very interesting, and extremely helpful. Do not take her class if you want to breeze through, though. You will need to put significant effort in to get a good grade, but that is why we're in college.
Great class, great teacher I wish I had more professors like her.
Diane was one of the best professors I've ever had. Her class made us think in ways we weren't used to thinking, it was challenging but also one of the best classes I've taken thus far.
Diane is great, shes interesting, engaging, and personable. I found her class challenging but in the best way. She always kept us interested and always wanted our feedback. She is a great professor

Diane is awesome. She explains the course material well, inspires interest, and gives plenty of time to finish the assignments.  She posts discussion questions on SPARK for you to fill out- make sure you do this, it's the entire final exam!  She's great!

Pretty tyrannical when it comes to the syllabus. Makes homework due 24 hours before the start of class. Unwilling to listen to students and their criticism of her syllabus. Instantly fails your writing assignment if it is late, doesn’t read it, no way to get that grade back. Laughs when students talk about their mental breakdowns.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Participation matters

reviews.comment: She is not lenient with anything, for this class she adopted the syllabus from a different professor and wasn't willing to change anything to adapt to the learning of anybody. When the issues were brought up she seemed defensive.

Prof. Curcio was a very chill teacher who fostered an open community in her class. She isnt clear on her grading criteria, but if you put in decent effort and follow whatever instructions she DOES give, youll get an A or B on pretty much everything. Her lack of concrete instructions does give chances for creative liberty, which she loves to see.

Prof. Curcio can be pretty difficult to work with. She doesn't have a rubric that I know of. She says she looks at everyone's piece at the same time to compare instead of looking at the individuals' success in the skill. She doesn't give any specific feedback and doesn't set any expectations. Easily swayed and doesn't seem to have a plan nor care.

by far the worst professor I've ever had in Fordham. She is very rude and does not value any student's opinion except for hers. Also, she likes other students than others and gives them preferential treatment. Please by all means, avoid her when registering for classes. There are other professors who are better than her.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Graded by few things--Tough grader

reviews.comment: In class , she simply goes over the exact content we were instructed to read in the textbook. Papers often are given low grades simply for formatting. She has good intentions though.

Very mediocre. The class was interesting, but it's more accurate to chalk that up to source material than whatever was brought to class by Prof. Cuevas-Molina. Most lectures consisted of slide shows and general conversation about what was going on in current politics. Somewhat disrespectful to students, not recommended unless you enjoy polisci.
Martha is quite frankly the best. She gives such helpful feedback. She knows how to take your acting to the next level and she will. She truly cares about every student succeeding.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Respected--Skip class? You won't pass.

reviews.comment: She is super sweet and understanding. This was my first theater class at the university and she just has so much experience and knowledge, and shes WOKE. Mostly did group projects, wrote responses, and watched and reviewed plays on campus. If you need an extension or something, do not be afraid to ask. A lot of her projects made me grow as an actor

Martha is very caring and super sweet. The toughest part of the class was the auto-drama. You make a 10 minute drama about your life. These are very emotional and deep. They are personal and special and very tough but rewarding to do. The rest of the year is scene work and short papers on plays and is pretty much just memorization of lines and fun.

She does not introduce any new information and her paper grading is more or less her inserting synonyms that she prefers to what you used.  She provided almost no helpful feedback and I did not learn much outside the readings. She pretty much just summarized everything I already knew from the assignments.

She is a difficult grader but gives you opportunities to improve your grade. It is impossible to do poorly in her class if you go in wanting to actually do the work and learn. My writing became so much better because of her. Best legal research and writing professor I could have asked for.

she should stick within the sociology dept.she gives little law perspective and her lectures seem as if she just googled whatever reading assigned and repeated that.when you challenge her copied ideas she will get offended and grade ur papers really hard. Stick to professors who can teach the material and aren't arrogant trying to prove themselves
No Comments
Anna is the greatest thing to happen to academia since the document camera.  She is a great teacher and is smoking hot!  Woo hoo!

Anna is just a TA..she's friendly but hopefully this is as far as she'll go in the UMASS teaching field.Lord help the child who gets her as a Professor as she seems unorganized and is A VERY DIFFICULT GRADER!My compensation did not fairly reflect my work!

I took my writing intensive with him at Smith College. He is amazing. Not only did we have a great in class relationship but after the course was over I still very much keep in contact with him. He is one of those professors who truly cares about his students and what they have to say. Take any of his classes!

Great guy, he helped me so much when I was on probation. If it wasn't for his help I would've gotten kicked of college. He's Pretty laidback and all you have to do is go to class and do the assignments and you will be fine.

He is very interested in what he teaches, and was able to make most of the students interested in the topics as well. He was pretty laid back and overall a great professor!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!

She changed the curriculum to embrace what we were dealing with and I really enjoyed the semester, even lockedown.

She is clearly passionate about the subject. But her Moodle page is a disaster - super confusing, so many sections, all over the place. It's really unclear what homework is due, what the expectations are, even with her calendar. We don't get a grade back for most things. She is not very receptive to feedback about Moodle or grading. Ugh exhausting

reviews.comment: It was good

This class is BORING. Probably my least favorite class Ive ever taken. She rushes through assignments and the moodle page is a mess to find stuff on. She gives lots of assignments and most are aggravating and meaningless. 10/10 avoid taking this class with her!
The best part of this class was working with students in other majors and getting a different perspective on issues. Also the Emperor's Pot!
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Skip class? You won't pass.--GROUP PROJECTS

reviews.comment: Lots of cool ideas. Not sure my writing improved but it was good practice. First time I got into group work - ever. Got a lot from the Career Development part. I'll use the quick writes. Good feedback and food for thought?
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Skip class? You won't pass.--GROUP PROJECTS

reviews.comment: Same as NatSci397A. Really care we understand assignments, which is good because a lot of what she teaches you need for jobs. She understands there is life outside her class, as long as you try hard she will help.  She is somewhat disorganized, especially her moodle.  THE MORE THE WHOLE CLASS CARES, THE EASIER THE CLASS (because of group projects).
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--ACCESSIBLE OUTSIDE CLASS--GROUP PROJECTS

reviews.comment: Better like group projects!
Way more interesting than I thought it would be. I wasn't interested in writing but got to write things I'll use to get jobs.
Way better class than expected.
Didn't realize I'd need this until I left. Teacher cared, required course.

Deb is annoying.  The class is extremely aggravating but her deadlines are very flexible.  She really wants everyone to participate online but as long as you participate in class you'll have no problem passing.  Grading sucks, you could work all night on a paper and still get a C

A very boring class.  The professor isn't terrible, but she never sticks to her deadlines.  You'll stay up all night finishing an assignment, to not have to turn it in the next morning when it was supposed to be due.  Everything ended up getting pushed to the end of the semester and we were rushed for time on everthing.  You get only 2 absences.

Easiest class ever. No writing. Read only 5 books. Every lecture is a summary of the most popular books in history, no analytical thinking required. Everyone had very lukewarm takes that made me mad. Take if you don't have a high school education.

I am not the biggest Shakespeare fan and still found something valuable in this course, mainly because of Professor Degenhardt's passionate and informative lectures. I highly recommend taking this class, you will learn valuable skills even if you don't particularly love Shakespeare. Prof. is great.

The negative reviews on here about Professor Degenhardt are severely outdated. This class is overall pretty easy and is a great gen-ed level class. Your grade is made up of attendance in discussion, three essays, and a midterm. Her lectures aren't mandatory, but are really interesting. Overall, a really great class and professor.
reviews.rating_tags: Clear grading criteria--Caring--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Professor Degenhardt is very enthusiastic about the material and gives interesting lectures. Even if you don't like Shakespeare, you will get something useful out of this course.
Exciting lectures. Class is fun and easy if you keep up with the reading and engage with the text.
I hate English and Shakespeare and got an A in her course. It's not heavy on testing or grading but more on how much you participate and read the plays.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--EXTRA CREDIT

reviews.comment: Most of your interactions will probably be with your TA, but the professor isn't bad. Some of the lectures get boring, especially if you didn't like the text, but you can miss them and be fine, since attendance is only taken for discussion. Your grade is based entirely off 3 papers, a midterm, and participation (~20% each), which kinda sucks.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Clear grading criteria--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: She was an amazing professor and her lectures were pretty good. Make sure that you buy the folger versions of the book, use thriftbooks or ebay to get them cheap. You will read, The Merchant of Venice, Measure for Measure, A Midsummers Night Dream, Henry V, Tempest, Othello, Hamlet. 3 essays, a midterm and discussion participation make your grade.

She's really nice but sometimes her lectures were boring. Also I don't think that the midterm and final are designed fairly as it relies less on actual literary analysis and more on general knowledge.

There should have not been a midterm or final exam for this class. She wants you to memorize passages and speakers along with other small details. Harsh grader. TA's were awesome though and you could tell they did not agree with her pedagogy. Wants you to buy 8 books for the class and shames you for using PDFs. Cool class, though.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Lecture heavy--Test heavy

reviews.comment: She is a kind, calming woman. She helped facilitate respectful discussions that no one felt uneasy participating in. She always has something nice to say and is incredibly encouraging. She helped us with our creative writing by giving feedback via constructive criticism that was never irrationally harsh. Shes a bit scattered and never in her office
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--SO MANY PAPERS--Caring

reviews.comment: The lectures with Professor Degenhardt were great, but the access to her outside of class was abysmal.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Clear grading criteria--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: Not inspirational.  Okay.

This class was surprisingly hard. It might've been cause I had a tough TA, but they expected way too much from us. She's a nice professor, but her lectures were incredibly boring and didn't prepare me for the exams or essays. Don't take this class if you want an easy A

Jane was the worst professor for a large classroom setting like this Shakespeare class. She talked about what she wanted to talk about and it was usually irrelevant to the plays, then would ask questions about random things she mentioned in the quizzes. Also, for the final she gave us 1 1/2 hrs instead of the two, which was all writing.

Jane Degenhardt is a sweetheart. She is kind and compassionate, and she has a good sense of humor in her lectures. The only problem I found with the class is that Shakespeare is very hard to teach in a lecture format. I'm sure she is great in a small class setting, but I feel like the class was not the greatest quality because of the size.

A great teacher who really takes student input and discussion into consideration.  I could tell that she really tried to keep student's attention by showing various movie clips during class.  Going to lecture is mandatory if you want to do well, but it is very enjoyable.

I really enjoyed Shakespeare with Prof. Degenhardt. The lectures were always filled with useful and interesting information, and I feel that the course was designed very well. With a large lecture format class, a lot depends on the TA, but I am looking forward to possibly taking another class with her in the future.

Classes are devoted to 3 theses she has about whatever acts we're covering at the moment- you can tell she has done years of research on Shakespeare, and put a lot of thought into each class.  She is clear, and holds my interest.  She also keeps class entertaining with clips of movie portrayals.  I am now a full-blown shakespeare fan.
Such a nice person, and very helpful.  She teaches interesting material and is flexible and understanding without being a pushover.  I liked her class a lot.
He's very intelligent, but can easily make assumptions about what you know because of it. Made me cry twice.

This class is extremely difficult and requires a lot of time outside of class from the student to succeed. I think Rafael is far from perfect but I think he does the most he can to prepare you in class, and the lectures are pretty interesting. The grading of the class is unfair, but I think that's just how it is for 400+ level physics classes.

He is a good lecturer, and easily accessible as he has many office hours. However, it is near impossible to get an A in this class (2/70 students, if I had to guess), because the final exam (worth 40%) had an average of 30%, and the curve was not very generous. You needed a 90 for an A, but a 76 for an A-.

The class is hard, but it's quantum. He knows his stuff & likes teaching it. Not a bad lecturer, but goes fast. Tests are hard, final was impossible (and 40% of the grade). HWs are very dense but due every 2 weeks. Anything you don't learn in class can absolutely be learned from Griffith's. I personally did not like the TA, but others did.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Test heavy

reviews.comment: I took the class in F23, and many in this class thought him to be a bad professor. Rafael is a fine lecturer. I will say, few who criticized his teaching style took the time to do practice problems from the textbook. Quantum mechanics is meant to be hard, but doing many practice problems will make it easy.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Lots of homework

reviews.comment: Really tough class. But he will teach you what you need to learn.

I have only taken his first midterm so far this semester but I can already say that his exam grading is extremely unfair. It's either you get the problem right or you don't. I did a whole test worth of work and I got 0's because I either didn't get the right answer or I used the wrong method. How is that the same as someone who turned in nothing..?

Raphael is by far the most difficult professor I have ever encountered. He did not explain the topics well, and expected us to know a lot of things we have been never taught before. His exams are unlike anything he will ever teach in the class or in the homeworks. His grading system is a complete mystery. 
Not recommended
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Lots of homework

reviews.comment: Rafael is one of the best professors I have ever had. He's funny, charismatic, and is obviously passionate about what he teaches. I have never learned more in any class I have ever taken.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Inspirational--Lots of homework

reviews.comment: Ralph is the worst physics professor in the department (even worse than Ben). Insane amounts of homework, no extensions unless your mother dies, difficult exams, can't teach, and doesn't care about teaching, forced to take exams in pen. When most people had missing assignments due to the heavy workload he emailed the class offering an INC...

Ralph is a cool guy but he cannot teach to save his life and its clear that he doesnt care to do better. He makes you take exams in pen only for whatever reason and hes very strict about no late homework. Awful experience taking this class and the semester isnt even over yet
Rafael taught Quantum Mechanics, which is the most difficult topic anyone can ever learn. Rafael made it manageable, and I loved going to his class every week.
Great Professor that explains the topic very well. Made the class very easy to understand for the MCAT. Prof. Danai does talk fast, but articulates things very well.

I think Professor Danai has a bad reputation because it is the first hard class in the BMB curriculum where you need to understand the content and not cram. She's very helpful outside of class and will definitely go over concepts again in office hours if you need it. She also cares about the students. You WILL have to put in effort outside class.

She said we did a good job when the average on the exams were a C- across the class... Her exam questions are insane and borderline sadistic. Problem sets are graded so harshly, and it's extremely frustrating when I'd spend about 4-5 hours on them. Quizzes were really hard and heavily time constrained. This is coming from a straight A student.

Hardest BMB class ever taken. The material is a lot & you do need to put in work, but I feel that Danai makes this so much more difficult. Her exams RARELY match any practice that is done, and her wording on exams always seemed deliberate to trip students up. Interesting material, but exams, and her way of explaining material make it unbearable.

It's a shame that my experience wasn't the best with Danai; exams were 'fair' but awful, considering we had a notecard and there was still content not present in slides/HW. The class itself was engaging, and Danai is even a good lecturer, though the major assignments, even if you have been doing stellar in college thus far, will hurt...

Wow, this class has been a doozy. I wake up every morning and ask myself "is college really for me?" and the answer is "hell no" after almost completing this class. I do not typically bash professors, but Danai makes an effort to ensure students struggle and the difficulty of her exams 100% reflect that.

This woman is useless. USELESS I tell you. I learned better when I stopped going to her lectures and just taught myself the material. She's also not a nice person, very condescending and passive aggressive. The material in this class isn't that hard but she makes every effort to burn you out from it.

Danai is a great professor, she is very good at explaining challenging concepts. Her exams are challenging but not unfair. This class is A LOT of work though, if you put the effort in you will do well but you have to put in a lot of effort. Really not as scary as people say though, enjoyable material and Danai clearly enjoys teaching it.

Her class is a LOT of work, but informative. But I will say this: deadlines are very, very strict. On group work, turn in the work yourself and do not trust anyone to turn in the assignment but you. She *most likely* won't have sympathy for your partner failing to turn it in like they said they would. Take this class *very* seriously from day 1.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Group projects--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: You're gonna see a lot of bad things about Danai on here, and that's due to people who have managed to get straight A's throughout college without really working for it thus far. Go to every lecture, actively participate, read the textbook before class, do PLTL, don't look up masteringchem questions, and redo all in-class activites for review.

Danai holds her students to a high standard which gives her a bad reputation. But she cares and she is a great professor. Tests are really hard so ask questions in and outside of class. 

Go to class, work hard, and attend office hours and TA/SI sessions. You'll do well.

Prof Danai is nice as a person, and is helpful if you ask questions. However, the exams are hard due to unclear statements, which can make you do things wrong even if you know them. The exams also weigh about 50 percent of the class grade. Going to the TA review sessions, and asking TA's questions is good for practice.

Clear on expectations, really wants students to learn and understand the material fully. Provides plenty of resources to practice. Doing well on the exams is important, and absolutely possible if you study hard.

Material is not that difficult, but the exam questions are sometimes sloppy- example the first exam had a skeletal structure of a peptide which just looked like a 3-year-old drew it last minute. Other than the exams being annoying Prof Danai was cordial and very approachable.

Biochem 423 is challenging but it is possible to do well if you put in the effort. Exams are weighed heavy and are not easy, but if you read the textbook, attend SI/TA reviews, and practice with in-class, pset, dsm, and pltl problems, you will be okay. Danai DOES care about her students and even makes an effort to remember names during lecture.

Danai is quite the engima. She 100% pushes her students to learn, but I think a few things could change. The questions on the p sets often felt too ambiguous, which is good for really thinking, but at the same time, it feels a bit out of place when it's for a grade. Exams were not too bad. Also this class does NOT have to consume your entire life.

I started the semester holding out hope that she would turn things around and help us out after the 1st exam, this was not the case. I think she got worse as the semester went on, maybe due to the content but more so with how she conducted the class. Really nice person, can tell she cares but there's a reason why its a graduate level class.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Laura Danai's exams are difficult which is why she gets a bad reputation, but this is due to the sheer nature of content and not because of her teaching. She is a great lecturer and pushes students to think critically and apply knowledge to complex problems. She also provides many resources that students can use to succeed in the class.

Inaccessible, uncompromising, and a terrible communicator. This is a professor that does NOT want you to succeed, and the class is treated like a freshman year weed-out class. Test questions are borderline sadistic, and your grade is your grade. Despite her imprecise language on exam questions, she accepts no disputes, and offers no extra credit.

The class, 423, is a very difficult class, where it is very detail heavy and the exams are very difficult as well. Professor Danai is a very good teacher and your success in the course depends on paying attention in class, reading the textbook, and putting in time in order to do well on the exams.

Danai was a kind person but a tough professor. She advocated for students and was always accessible through Teams and office hours. Her TAs were great and very helpful as she works closely with them. The class is extremely tough!! SI sessions helped me most. The practice exam was easier than the exam always. I enjoyed her class but it's difficult.
reviews.rating_tags: Group projects--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: The class is difficult but not excruciating. You have to be a master of the material to receive an A. Do readings before class, stay on pace, expose yourself to as much material as possible, and study normally before exams and you will be just fine. If you try hard for an A you will get one. Danai has reasonable expectations and is a great teacher.

The class is certainly difficult, however that is part of being a biochemistry major. The reviews make it seem like she is a terrible teacher/person but that is not the case. She is a fantastic teacher considering how difficult the concepts are to explain and does her best to make the materials accessible for all learning styles. She is respectful.
reviews.rating_tags: Clear grading criteria--Lecture heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Biochem 423 is not an easy course and it requires a solid foundation in chem, ochem, and biology.  The course combines this knowledge into a cohesive image relating to organ systems and metabolic response pathways. Dr. Danai tries to convey the material as best she can but that is not an easy task. Overall, Dr. Danai is supportive and available.

I have nothing but nice things to say about Professor Danai. She is one of the best lecturers I have had at UMass and she is very kind and down to earth. Do not get me wrong, her class is hard but every exam is fair, you have the information to answer every question. I am certain that people who rate her poorly are just upset with the difficulty.
if you care about your GPA, do NOT take this class. Very few people get As. Most get low Bs and Cs even the super smart ones.

BIOCHEM 423 is a tough course and requires effort, no doubt. But Prof. Danai does everything in her power to make the material accessible. She is a great lecturer and encourages you to stop her to ask questions. She genuinely wants students to learn and succeed. Poor reviews are definitely coming from those who did not do well in the class.

Class feels like a mass of confused people, except for the 10 people who somehow know everything because they are all friends with the TA's, who tell them what is on the tests, and share their notes/cheat sheets from prior semesters.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Lecture heavy--Test heavy

reviews.comment: This class crushed my mental health and social life and is the lowest grade I've ever received. The amount of information you have to memorize for exams is insane and I was always crunched for time. I went to every class, reached out for help, and was still beyond confused. Overall she is a nicer than she seems but I recommend avoiding this class!
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: For a 400 level class, tough grading and exam heavy weighting is to be expected. Although this was a difficult class, Professor Danai is very understanding and accessible for help in and out of the classroom. As long as you go to class, do the readings, and ask questions when confused, the class is passable.

She's a decent lecturer and she seems to genuinely care about teaching. Participation is important for her. There are 4 exams and the majority of your grade is based on exams. Its not super difficult to pass the class, but it takes effort to get an A. Only bad thing is that some exam problems are worded weird, but its only 1-2 out of 20 per exam.

I have to be honest. The people who are giving low ratings of Professor Danai most likely did not get a good grade in her class. Professor Danai is one of the best lecturers I have ever had. The class  by no means an easy class, but you can get so much out of this class, as long as you are willing to put in the time and effort. and ASK QUESTIONS!!!

Yes, this is a challenging class but it is completely manageable. From my experience, the students who struggled in the course are the ones leaving these scathing reviews because they did not come to class/do the readings she assigned as homework. You can't expect a 400-level class to be easy but it is certainly doable if you put in the effort.

If you need to take BC423 and you are scared because of the low rating:
This is a lvl 400 class, it's not going to be easy. But you can make it easier for yourself. Read the txtbk before class, attend class, & ASK QUESTIONS. Prof. Danai is not this mean professor that students are making her out to be. She will support you, just put in the work.

My first C letter grade ever in uni. Her exam question writing is atrocious with only 18 questions per exam. Otherwise a great lecturer but sets incredibly high expectations for her students. Incredibly frustrated, don't take this class unless you absolute need this class
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Lecture heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Definitely not as bad as people here made her out to be. Exam questions were very wordy and definitely had a time crunch, so more time + practice questions would have helped. Still, she is a good lecturer, the TAs were very helpful and the problem sets weren't graded too harshly.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Group projects--Test heavy

reviews.comment: She has changed a lot from last year and actively made this class easier for students. Exams quite fair, and at times, quite easy. The class isn't a death sentence anymore.

reviews.comment: This isn't a weed-out class, it's a drop-out class. This was the hardest required class of the major. reviews.comment: Absolutely avoid this professor at all cost if you value your mental health

reviews.comment: Probably the most unfair and evil professor at UMass. Leverages poor grades as an excuse to gaslight students. If you take a class with Laura Danai, don't expect to learn anything but rather expect to file reasonable complaints on her lack of empathy, hostile communication, and dangerous handling of a mandatory course for biochemistry majors.

Do NOT take any class with Laura Danai! She was incredibly lazy, disorganized and mean, and she clearly hated most of her students. Her  inflexibility and lack of respect towards students with ruined sleep patterns also created an environment unsuitable for learning.

I want to preface this by saying that I got an A but with an immense amount of work. NOT WORTH IT. All the good reviews are other professors or TAs that were forced to write good things about her. There was no SI, few office hours, very difficult and poorly worded exams, and lack of overall communication. Upper lvl class, we r all smart, bad class!

The fact that Laura Danai claps back at students who voice constructive feedback on how she can fix her classes and destroys the sanity of students through her inability to write a reasonable exam serves as evidence that Laura Danai is the worst biochemistry professor of all time.

This lady is NOT a human being. Laura Danai has a reputation for her nasty communication with students, inability to accept constructive feedback, and preventing students from learning by lambasting those who ask valid questions. Apart from that, she's unreasonable, close-minded, and mean, and it was a disappointment to take her biochem class.
The worst professor I have had at this school. If possible avoid at all costs.

reviews.comment:
Definitely one of the harder courses in the Biochemistry majors track. BUT, so worth it and necessary to fully understand the content. Don't procrastinate, be on top of your readings, and you'll pass. 
The textbook is a little confusing at first, but the lectures did help clear up any problems I had.

This class was so hard compared to prerequisite biochem courses, but Danai works with you to develop the necessary skills and routines to be able to succeed. She is accessible if you reach out to her and TA/SI sessions are helpful. If I planned ahead and procrastinated less - I would have done better in the class.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Lecture heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Danai is the embodiment of a no-good, selfish, horrible professor who deserves to get review bombed as she is an aggressive monster and bully who has a huge ego, clearly thinks she’s better than her students, and is notorious for her inability to take criticism. Get this poor excuse of a person terminated from UMass.
Worst teacher I ever had. The professor who teaches it this semester is absolutely more caring and better at teaching.

Although the class was quite challenging, I did find that a learned a lot; but this required about 40 hours/week of studying outside of class. I found the lectures to be super helpful, but the book was overly wordy and time consuming to read. I found the problem sets to be especially challenging, and I thought the exams were generally fair.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Test heavy--Tough grader

reviews.comment: Hardest class I've taken yet, but Professor Danai does a good job of teaching it. Although her tests were quite unforgiving, she went through a lot of effort to make sure we learned the material effectively. She drops one of each type of homework assignment and gives full credit for completing participation assignments. Quite understanding overall

This class dominated my entire semester. The structure of this class is so unforgiving. You have to diligently do the readings. I'm all for feeling challenged in a course, but if you design the exams to trick students, don't make them also worth 60% of our grade. I never saw her bad side, but that's because I only spoke to her like 4-5 times. Skip!
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Graded by few things--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: It's honestly so sad that Danai is getting so much hate. Her standards seem impossible, but they prepared me in ways I didn't realize being in the class. Looking back, this class was exactly what I needed to have a solid base in biochemistry. She's an amazing professor and set me up for success in my other classes. She is 100% not out to fail you.
The lectures are good, I think she's nice as she gave me extensions due to personal problems. Her exams were just way too hard

Danai is a great lecturer, her lecture are easy to follow and understand. She is very informative and organized when it comes to teaching. Best class in term of teaching and always love to come to class. Why a 1? I come to exam knowing all the material, but she test on some material that she never go over in class. She is rude and inaccessible.

Professor Danai is not caring nor supportive of her students. Many students were doing poorly in the class and she was not accommodating at all to help them improve their grades. She does not feel like a real person and is not readily available or will try to interact with her students. Her exams were all over the place in terms of difficulty.

Pick a God and pray to it because there's really no other way to pass. She says things that are just straight-up wrong during lectures, is unavailable after class, refuses to use Moodle, and writes the most far-fetched exam questions. My overall GPA is 3.906 and I'm getting a C/C- in this class. I genuinely dont understand how she is still employed
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Lecture heavy--Tough grader

reviews.comment: She is completely disconnected from students. Writes exam questions that are impossible to understand, relies heavily on the textbook, and doesn't scale anything. A huge part of the grade is quizzes, which you are NOT given enough time for, and challenge problem sets that are intentionally difficult but graded for correctness. Avoid if possible!
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Test heavy--Tough grader

reviews.comment: This class honestly made me regret majoring in Biochemistry. It was way harder than it needed to be and Professor Danai was so unaccommodating .
Mean, bad, worst professor ever. Exams are so difficult, tough grader for assignments, no extra credit at all.

Professor Danai makes an easier class impossible. She insists on using Microsoft Teams instead of the standard Moodle, making assignments, etc. harder to find. She consistently makes errors talking about the course material in lecture, leading to many, many corrections. It is my opinion that she is not qualified to teach high level biology. Avoid.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Graded by few things--Tough grader

reviews.comment: This is literally the worse class Ive ever taken. She rushes through lectures, hides behind teams instead of actually being available and prides herself on giving evil exams. Will teach new material the day before an exam and expect you to know it. I hope after this semester the school does something about this because this is not okay

reviews.comment: oh my god she truly is the worst professor at umass. her class is incredibly difficult. it's nearly impossible in every aspect. she makes mistakes in lecturing, and confuses mostly everyone. you could fully understand the lecture material before an exam and then fail the test. I got entirely straight A's before this class, not anymore. 0/10

Worst class ever! She prides herself in making that class hard but has no clue. She's still figuring things out it seems. She's inaccessible, only half an hour of virtual-recorded office hours(heard there was none before). Everyone I meet hates this class. Do yourself a favor and don't take this class! It's not good for your mental health! AVOIDDD!

Hardest class I ever taken at umass. Cried everyday, it's like this class spawned from hell. Just get ready to pray. The exams are almost impossible, she's never available. The quizzes and problem sets are extremely challenging. This course is required for biochem majors, and she is the only professor that teaches it.. So good luck, you'll need it.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Test heavy--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: Where to start. First and foremost, I got an A-... However, this was due to 20+ hours a week dedicated to solely this class. I got an A- in spite of this professor, not because of this professor. I'm fairly certain that she doesn't understand the material herself. Please give this class to a deserving grad student who would actually try.
