I have taken and sat in on a number of courses in chemistry and the department does its students a disservice by not having DV teach more of them. Very few professors are able to challenge students while lowering the focus on grades and outcomes. DV's course environment emphasizes learning above all else.
This is a life changing role model. Honestly, I would recommend taking this class regardless of what you want to major in. If you do not, you miss out in the meaning of life!

DV is the MAN. Best professor I've ever had at UMass. The class is insanely hard and will work you like never before, but DV helps you every step of the way. He inspires greatness in his students, and teaches you to do things you never thought possible. If you ever want to do anything even minutely related to organic chemistry, you NEED to hear DV.
Easily the best professor I've had. This man is brilliant, helpful, understanding, and most of all a fantastic teacher. He *really* taught me organic chemistry.

Best guy ever.  His teaching is awesome and you will learn organic chemistry very well.  His tests are impossible!  Expect to fail at least one of them.  Its OK though because he curves the class so you will be happy with your grade as long as you try your best.

DV is a good teacher and he tries his hardest to help us understand Organic Chem, which is a hard subject no matter what. His exams were difficult; some class averages were down in the 40s and 50s, but it shows he expects a lot out of us. Plus there's a huge curve.

Organic chemistry is hard no matter who the teacher is, but DV made it a bit more interesting--he once compared reactions to Facebook relationships. Also the scale at the end of the semester is pretty amazing.
Great teacher. Focuses on making sure everyone understands. Doesn't rush. Good teaching skills. Very fair. 10/10

DV is a cool guy. He tries to explain everthing very well. This was his first semester teaching orgo, so I think he cut us some slack. The material was hard, but if you spend some time studying and going to class, the exams aren't too bad. He gave some practice questions too and used OWLs which helped.
He is a great guy.
No Comments

always willing to help you very promt with feed back and will explain until you understand everything.. awesome professor and gives lots of scope for getting a good grade.. definately recommend him for this class
Really nice guy.  Sometimes he talks a little fast but he's clear in his concepts.  Gives extra credit oppertunities which help a lot. I deffinatly recommend him
Great guy, and good professor too. A little unclear at times but always willing to help you understand

Great teacher. Has an accent but you catch on fast. Do the readings, participate, and you'll do well. Some of the topics are a bit awkward in this class...I think the gender and sexuality section crossed the line a bit, but she didn't force us to use that in our papers.

This professor creates an interesting class room environment that intrigues its students. Discussion is necessary if you want to do well in this class. If you are serious about doing well, she can provide you with the best support. Very helpful and personally helped one to one on my final thesis paper. The literature used opened a new world for me.
Kanchuka is a really nice teacher. The texts are not so bad once you get into them. Her quizzes are pieces of cake as long as you do the readings. She loves discussions so participate a lot!
slides have no words, making it hard to follow along. wears super tight shirts

I love Todd!! He is funny, knowledgeable, and respected in his field. This class is very interesting and I would take it again; however, the reading is SO HEAVY. He doesn't test you on it, but it is helpful to understand the material.  The papers are a bit long, but any science/anthro student shouldn't struggle. would love to take this again!!

Todd is a really knowledgeable guy! He clearly loves his work and sharing his life with students! He is extremely honest and understanding. His general policy is that you need to turn one assignment in before the next one is due, he does not individually grant extensions and begs you not to email him. He gives everyone a 3 day grace period.
i had an a on canvas until it was bumped down to a b because of the curve, which the ta only found out two days prior to the semester ending.

Chill guy, chill class. Actually the guy is a bit nuts but in a way I fw. -2 points for not a single word being on any slide all year. Just random pictures. Might as well not post them then. Would've attended more if the class wasn't so early but that is a registrar problem. Please just give the pics one line captions at least man.

Ridiculously easy class, so much so that he grades on a curve. I have an A+ but might end with a lower grade due to that. Never went to lectures because he gets off topic quick, just followed along with the textbook as he assigned it. Labs are very easy, and TAs are very willing to help clear up all questions. "Final" is a 600-700 word essay.
Love this guy
Good gen ed class, its easy enough but beware that it is graded on a curve, I earned an A points wise but it was bumped down to an A-

Disotell is a good professor, he's a bit of a yapper during lectures but it's not hard to keep up. The readings are insane, he gives a LOT of papers to read before class. You have to do weekly writing assignments, they're super easy, 1/2-1 page. There are 4 essays throughout the semester. Show up for class and do the assignments. Not tough at all.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Lecture heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Although, Lectures on not attendance mandatory I still recommend attending because they are very interesting and things said in lectures may appear on quizzes. The labs are very simple and usually take less than an hour and are graded pretty nicely. I recommend this class for an easy Gen-ed.
reviews.rating_tags: Clear grading criteria--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Papers were relatively straightforward, don't have to do the reading he assigns as long as you can do your own research for them. Lectures were interesting and he clearly knows a lot about the topic. Always gives extensions if you ask for them and is very friendly.
Literally the easiest class. Lectures are useless and he says go to them but never takes attendance. The labs are also just group work so you're out in like 30 minutes most times.

Fantastic professor and interesting lectures, papers, while accounting for much of your grade, are very easy and he gives automatic extensions on every assignment. Very funny and clearly has a deep passion for what he teaches.

Had anthro290STA (emerging diseases) with him. Attendance isnt technically required but he doesnt post lecture recordings. The class grade comes from four papers (5pages average)+some short weekly responses. He is VERY fair with grading and due dates are basically a suggestion. He's a super kind and interesting guy, a bit monotone though sometimes.

Professor Disotell was awesome. He covered a great variety of intriguing topics, and really made you think about and appreciate the human body. He's made incredible contributions to his field, and his passion is manifest. Quizzes are open note and labs are decently engaging. The only negative I can think of is that he takes some jabs at religion

I've taken two classes with Todd and he has been engaging, funny, and gives fantastic lectures without the work being too difficult. He has written a lot of papers and been on TV but is very personable and easy to talk to. If I had more space to talk about him, I could easily fill this review but overall he is my favorite professor from UMass
If you need a gen ed, this isn't a bad choice. The lectures were boring but the grading was fair and done exclusively through papers. If you show up every day and write the papers, you will get an A.

Went to most lectures even though he also offered them through echo360. Graded by either quick weekly responses or 4-6 pg papers. Gave short readings to read for each class but never really discussed them. Tells many stories about his experience and the crazy tales he has. One of the smartest people you'll ever meet!
Super fun guy, the quizzes weren't hard if you go to class

Pretty awkward and unfunny, and the lectures are extremely boring -- they are not worth attending. That said, all the quizzes were online and were extremely easy, there was no final exam (just a one page paper), and the labs were very easy. Easy, but boring GenEd.
Very sweet and funny professor. The lectures are quite complicated and long. The quizzes that pop up here and then are really hard and you learn a lot through the labs which are fun

Prof Disotell is great, his class was very engaging, he's very understanding and the workload is not heavy at all. Had 1 half page responses due each week on your own topic and a few papers. He's not heavy on grading.
He's a really cool person who is very passionate about his field. The class has no tests, just the average amount of papers.

Prof. Disotell is a wonderfully passionate and hilarious professor! He really tries to keep his lectures engaging and relevant which is extremely rare for profs that teach gen-eds. Also, was one of the few profs that genuinely cared about the safety of his students during another semester of Covid. Would highly recommend!

The only good thing about this class is that attendance was not mandatory (at least online). Super material heavy, quizzes (60%) were very intricate free response (not multiple choice). Grading is based on class average, so I ended up with a B+ with a 93. Did well only because collaborated with a couple of friends and roommate. Not recommended.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Test heavy--Beware of pop quizzes

reviews.comment: The class was actually pretty easy overall. While some of the content could be a little boring, he worked to make sure that it was both engaging and understandable. He also used a green screen and dressed up with a specific theme for every lecture, which helped to keep my attention. Good amount of reading, but assignments were very easy.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Clear grading criteria--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: This class was a Gen Ed but was so unnecessarily hard. Unless you really care about biological anthropology and memorizing useless facts about primates do not take this course. The lectures were boring and the exams were difficult as well.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Test heavy--Tough grader

reviews.comment: Extremely unclear with some of the material. Some of the TAs weren't even on the same page as him and didn't scale any of the tests. Easily the hardest class I've taken at UMass and it was only a Gen Ed. Unless you have a serious passion for anthro and can keep up, would not recommend it.

Profa is by far the best professor I've ever had at UMass. Her lectures are lifechanging. She's a brilliant speaker, theorist, historian, and educator. I would argue that her classes are appropriately rigorous for the history she's trying to teach - the least you could do as a student is engage with them. Everyone should take a class with her!

Diana is one of my favorite professors, she is incredibly passionate about what she teaches. She is really attentive to your work and gives extensive feedback. There is a lot of reading but it was all very informative and interesting, I've learned so much from her class!
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Amazing lectures --Gives good feedback

reviews.comment: I took HIST 301 but it won't let me rate it. She clearly cares about the material but wayyyy too much reading. More effort than its worth for a class that doesn't even fulfill the gen ed.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: She's very knowledgeable and clearly knows what she is talking about. However, she lacks basic empathy and compassion for her students. She is cold, indifferent, and should not have been a professor! I always got the impression she hated me even though I participated and attended lectures. She also ALWAYS had something negative to say.

Had her for Hist356. She's awesome. So dedicated and knowledgeable and truly cares about the subject. Decent workload but generous grader. Cares about her students and wants everyone to succeed. Can't explain how much this class meant to me, so sad that it's over

After my second class with Profa, I can say without a doubt that she is one of the most committed and caring professors at UMass. She genuinely wants her students to do well and she acts like a real human being. Additionally, she is incredibly knowledgeable and flexible in her approach to learning.

She was great, when we had questions outside of class, she hardly checks her email to get back to us. There were complaints of her loading on last-minute assignments at one point which threw us off towards the end of the semester.  Her passion is there for the course and was very enjoyable overall.

Profa is truly one of the best in the history department. She is incredibly caring about her students and passionate about her work. Readings can be somewhat dense at times but it's worth it. Only a few papers throughout the course and you have to facilitate discussion once (like a presentation). Highly recommend.

Profa Sierra Becerra is an engaging educator who teaches revolutionary histories from a trauma-informed pedagogical style. She created a classroom environment where I felt very connected to my peers and was allowed the space to really learn and reflect.

Genuinely the best professor I've had thus far. Incredibly knowledgeable about the topics covered in class, super approachable, and overall very kind and caring. The course was structured very well and she was able to communicate really complex and difficult concepts in a way that actually made sense. Really down-to-earth.

This guy speaks English with a heavy Spanish accent which is weird considering he's never been to a Spanish-speaking country before? His last name had me fooled into thinking he was a native speaker but in reality he's really just a Filipino dude from eastern Mass. He should really stick to CS instead of teaching in the language department.
took this Spring 2024, he's alright

It's my first semester here at UMass as an anthropology major and I have to take a language as part of my graduation requirement. When I added this class to my schedule there wasn't an instructor listed so I wasn't sure how the class was going to be, but luckily I got Profe Diaz. He's not a native speaker of Spanish but he's good, highly recommend.
He is so fun! I'm an engineering major and even though I have to walk all the way to Herter to go to class, it's worth it.

Professor Diaz is incredibly passionate and caring towards the subject he teaches. He reignited my love for the Spanish language. Nevertheless, this class is a type of class where you get what you put in, and should not be taken lightly.
this man is goated fr
Chill guy, interesting enough to the point where he doesn't have to ask us to participate because we do it voluntarily
He's the goat, I learned Spanish in high school for 4 years but I learned more from him in one semester. Take his class if you can
Took it last year with him. Cool guy, easy class

Profe Díaz is a phenomenal professor for Spanish 110 and Spanish 120. He is willing to help each of his students out as much as possible as long as you put in the effort to learn the language. Theres a lot of work assigned, but every single one of it helped me in my Spanish learning. Take his class if you absolutely want to learn Spanish.

She's a very kind woman. Exams were easy, in class assignments were extremely difficult, and lectures were very confusing. If you make time to attend her office hours and talk to her, she is wonderful. I don't think she enjoys teaching very much, which is understandable. She puts in maximum effort and cares for her students, but not an easy class

she teaches as though she made the slides the night before the lecture and is as confused as the students, overall doesn't seem confident in the material. slides were picture and diagram heavy, making them confusing to review as it wasn't clear what was being shown, lectures aren't recorded. in class activities were confusing. exams were reasonable

she just seemed unprepared and confused. her exams were very easy though because you get a notecard for them. did not attend like 90% of lectures because I didn't find them helpful and the in-class assignments were ridiculously confusing. she's really kind though.
Three weeks into class and I'm overwhelmed + struggling to keep up.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Group projects--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: 3h zoom lecture 5x per week. Hardly any breaks. Dense and confusing lectures. Hefty work requirements and not really willing to work with students.

One of the worst classes I've ever taken. There are only 5 Moodle calculation exercises, 6 Moodle quizzes, and 6 group case studies to base your grade off of. She doesn't seem to know what she's talking about and constantly contradicts her own words. Quizzes are unnecessarily hard and case studies have very vague directions and grading criteria.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough Grader--GRADED BY FEW THINGS--GROUP PROJECTS

reviews.comment: Is not a clear lecturer at all and makes her quizzes way too hard. She doesn't upload her powerpoints either so you can only go off of your notes and the book for her quizzes. Only quizzes and case studies for the class but they are so difficult.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough Grader--Get ready to read--LECTURE HEAVY

reviews.comment: Not a good lecturer, reads off of her notes, contradicts her own words, has difficulty expressing what she wants us to learn. Quizzes are difficult with a lot of information that you need to know. If you are taking this class because you're interested in the subject and want to learn, not recommended.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough Grader--Get ready to read--GROUP PROJECTS

reviews.comment: Prof Felton is sooo nice and enthusiastic. She even brought us donuts a couple times. She tends to make things due at 5:00 pm tho, and grades a bit meticulously. Readings aren't too bad. I think she said no tech at one point, but she never enforced it. Interesting class, but felt like a little too much work for a one credit seminar.

DO NOT TAKE HER FIRST YEAR SEM. It will only add extra stress to your first semester unless you are VERY interested in the subject matter. Basically just felt like almost anything was overcomplicated (long readings, reflections graded for word choice, etc.) Just be ready to have to put in more effort than is maybe deserved for a one-credit class.

Generally a very unforgiving professor. This class consisted of work that was either laughably juvenile or much too difficult. Insanely harsh grader. Attendance AND participation are heavily factored into your grade. Would not recommend her classes unless you have prior knowledge or possess a very strong interest in the subject.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Participation matters

reviews.comment: Professor Felton loves what she teaches but I don't recommend her class. The readings are interesting but sometimes egregiously long. Be weary of her papers, she doesn't grade on what you say but how well you fit within her standards of how you should write. Her grading is never consistent and the quizzes were incredibly hard, beware.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Participation matters

reviews.comment: If you are not a classics major do not take this class, you need knowledge of classics. Felton has many issues in the way she teaches, grades and helps students. It is clear she has favorites in her classes. It is also clear she loves classics but forgets not everyone is, DO NOT TAKE FOR GEN ED YOU WILL MOST LIKELY STRUGGLE (I am a classics major)

Prof Felton is wonderful! She's enthusiastic and very knowledgable. I highly recommend to anyone going into healthcare; it provides fun mythological and historical context. She doesn't try to trick you and really wants you to do well. Do the readings, attend lectures, and know forms/pre/suffixes, easy A. Optional final exam, 2 short 1-page papers.
[too long to type out]

You want some background on Ancient Greece or Rome before going into Classics 330, but if you have that, this course is a wonderful GenEd for Classics enthusiasts. Professor Felton was very enthusiastic about the topic and totally accessible outside of class. Her grading was clear and lenient, although the exams were quite a bit of open-response.

I took this as a GenEd. There are quite a few readings that need to be completed before each class. Each reading assignment would take me at most an hour. Attendance is part of your grade. Exams are open response. I'll admit, I did quite a bit of studying for the exams. Maybe too much for a GenEd. Debbie is super sweet though.

I want to preface this review saying that Professor Felton is one of the kindest professors I have come across during my time at Umass, very kind and wants to see everyone succeed. But If you do not HAVE to take classics 330 I do NOT advise doing so. It is way too difficult for a gen ed. The tests are crazy difficult and very specific. Lot of hw.
DO NOT TAKE THIS CLASS IF YOU DON'T HAVE TO. I took this class as a HS requirement and the Exams are extremely hard, not worth it.

I have taken several classes with Professor Felton. She is very sweet and genuinely caring. She is a bit of a hard grader and does genuinely require that you pay attention in the class. But with effort, it is easy to get an A while in her course. I would highly recommend this professor. Her lectures are also very interesting!
Easy A

Class was okay, seemed too difficult for a gen ed. Prof is nice and all but the classroom was horrible. Too many kids for one room, hot and desks are all squished together. Too much work for a gen ed class but kinda interesting I guess. Don't take this class if you don't like classics. It's less medical and more classics unfortunately.
reviews.rating_tags: Accessible outside class--Get ready to read--Group projects

reviews.comment: Professor Felton was wonderful in nearly every way. She is understanding, compassionate, and more than willing to work individually with students. Also, her various studies were fascinating! My only complaint is that the class was too large for discussions, but that was no fault of hers.

Professor Felton  is a very balanced instructor. I took several courses with her, and in each she supplies numerous examples of the  information she wants you to learn  via readings, lectures and group projects. All of her exams draw directly from this material; very few surprises. She also responded promptly to emails and held regular office hours
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Get ready to read--Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: I've had professor Felton many times throughout my college career. I've always found her way of teaching and grading great for my personal learning style. Her exams are very straight forward, everything she puts on the exam was in your readings and mentioned in class. She points out the important things in class so take good notes and read!
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--GROUP PROJECTS

reviews.comment: 5 in class group assignments that were graded pretty easily. Two tests during the semester and a final; her tests were not an appropriate measure of material comprehension. She sometimes words things as a trick; other times the "most correct" answer is debatable. Her scale also seems funky as an 87% is a B, not a B+. Funny and interesting; take P/F

I took origins of western medicine and medical terminology with professor Felton. I highly recommend it but only if it interests you. I tried so hard in this class and enjoyed every minute of it. There are quizzes in most classes that are easy if you pay attention. It just takes a little getting used to her and then the class is great!

Prof Felton is kind of rude when responding to questions on her syllabus but overall a great teacher. Tests are incredibly easy. Basically if you can remember a story you will be fine. Going to class is a must but the info is at least interesting enough that you wont want to stick a pencil in your ear.

I feel bad for the person below me cause the course is very straightforward and easy. It may at first seem like a lot of readings, but you only need to skim them and attend lecture for the real stuff. Only 4 HWs that you work in groups so they aren't that bad. Exams are super easy scantron questions. She does laugh a ton but is super nice!

Most annoying teacher ever, all she does is laugh after every word she says. Everything about this class is awful. Took it as a GenEd and immediately regretted it. The homework assignments should be easy but they're not. If you don't have to take it then don't
Debbie Felton is awesome and I loved this class. Would take it again in a heartbeat. You don't really need the book, so I recommend renting it if you get it.

She is a great professor. Really knows her subject, and is really nice. She talks a little fast but you won't even notice it after the 2nd class. Her tests are pretty well made. Just take notes on her lectures since she doesn't upload 'em online.

Professor Felton is a fun teacher, sometimes she can be a little wierd. I'm pretty sure she wears the same clothing to class every day idk. But overall good professor the class is pretty easy but the final isnt what you expect.

Professor Felton is really giggly and funny.  She gets embarrassed about some of the things she talks about, but she gets through it and makes it fun. There are extra credit opportunities, but she's easy to understand, it's hard to fail.
she's wicked easy. all you gotta do is attend class and take a few notes. you dunt even have to read the book and you'll do good. i got over a 100 on all my exams and passed the class with an A.

Love her, she's extremely fun and charming. Her 224 class is very easy, but also very interesting. I didn't even buy the book for the class, and I got 100 on the last exam. The only issue I have is how the essays are graded (oh yeah, there are essays).

She is SO enthusiastic and LOVES what she does!  I find the random giggling to be charming. There is a good amount of HW but it's so easy and it reeeally helps you learn the material. GREAT professor!
Great prof! Love her enthusiasm. Really knows her stuff. Fun class.

It's very unfortunate to have such low quality class in UMass.  Rushing through material is normal when an instructor misses lectures 4,5 times for random reasons. She is very boring, but I felt bad for her, and how students treated her sometimes.

I really liked this class. Granted, at the beginning of the year her random giggling was kind of annoying, but after a few lectures you don't even notice it anymore. She's very nice, class notes do go into slightly more depth than the book, but attending class isn't essential. Tests are really easy. Great class, as long as you're interested.

Lots of reading, exams are relatively easy. No study guides or review sessions for exams which is really retarded.  Gets very annoying when she keeps laughing at the stuff she says even when it isn't funny. Too many references to Lord of the Rings, Star Trek, and Harry Potter. She insulted the class twice in 2 lectures; really unprofessional
cheerful, tries to make class fun, but has trouble getting class to settle down--needs more authority
SUCH A BAD TEACHER AND THE CLASS NOTES ARE USELESS FOR STUDYING FOR THE TEST
After the first test you'll realize what she wants. Her notes are terrible no need to go to class at all! Just do the readings and you'll be fine.
Interesting material, and fun presentation.

horrible teacher...don't go to class - all the tests are verbatum from the ten thousand readings that you have to do... class notes are not helpful - we spent 1 whole week going over the gods and goddesses and not a single q on the exam was on them. baaad classs...
Her tests are so easy if you look at the online study guides...she pulls the questions off of them.

She is a fun teacher and always has a cheerful attitude even when she is sick. She is a fair person. Her exams are relatively easy if you do the readings. If you have questions, she is more than willing to answer them. :)
No Comments
No Comments

A bit quirky, but very enthusiastic about teaching. She is also very approachable and easy to talk to. There may be a lot of work, but as long as you go to class and keep up w/ the reading you should do well. I highly enjoyed this class and would recommend her to anyone intestest in taking greek myth (or other classics courses).

Hi folks, I took her for two classes (Greek I and Drama) and was pleased. If you prepare before class, you will not only understand what she is saying, but you will grow to like her and her "giggling." She is a good person and a very good teacher in that she is always prepared for class. Don't judge her based on your own intelligence! Peace, xoxo

Some of those comments sound like some sour grapes from students expecting an easy class. My roommate and I liked this class so much we are taking  her class next semester. She's quirky but not your usual stuffy prof.
A lot of work for a gen ed but prof is very enthusiastic and always answered my emails

the woman was a complete lunatic. she spoke too fast and all over the place, brought her personal issues into play, would ask if anyone had any questions and then told them that they should already know the answer to the question they asked. she threatened students. it was absurd. she pleaded that no one bring a gun to class. PS i got a 93 on exam1

She is a frekin nutjob who giggles at every little thing and asks u every 2 seconds if you can see the overhead slides, greek myth is interesting but she blasted it with a rifle and dragged it through hell, don't take any of her classes

This class sucked. Not clear on what you are being tested on. She does not give a study guide for her tests. I was very unhappy with the overall class. I enjoy learning greek myth and she just destroyed it.

This is not an easy class, lots of reading and she is out of her mind. Thinks every comment is funny and doesn't explain things as well as she could. Keep up with the readings and owls, study a lot, should be ok

I went into the class thinking that it would be an easy A.  Man was i wrong.  The lectures are ridiculously boring and she is the goofiest person ever.  The tests are short answer and absolutely impossible to finish on time.  The book is 500 pages and she assigns 200 on every test.  Her notes are completely pointless.  bottom line - horrible class

i think the person writing the previous good reviews is either a ta or the prof herself because they are too preachy and advice giving - anyone who takes this class knows that it sucks - she doesn't use powerpoint nor does she give review sessions for her impossible tests - she is also extr. rude - she should really go teach a kindergarten class
No Comments

This class is fairly easy if you take really good notes and actually try to pay attention instead of blowing off the lectures as stupid.  Do the OWL assignments from your lecture notes and supplement it with the readings. Use the OWL assignments as study guides for the exams because they ARE the study guides for the exams. Not hard if you try.

DON'T TAKE THIS CLASS FOR A GENED, WHATEVER YOU DO. Tons of information to study for exams and only a small portion of it is actually on the exam itself. I spent a week straight studying for my last exam and got a 70. Please please dont take this class, you'll cry yourself to sleep EVERY SINGLE NIGHT

I'm willing to bet that those who left negative to horrible comments did so because they didn't like the grade on their first exam.  Here's a tip, just as the Prof. said: 75% of the class expected to get A to A- in the beginning of the class. I think it's student's expectations that needs adjustment, not the Professors teaching methods. Work hard~

I was really interested in the subject beforehand. i attended every class, took notes on everything possible, did the owls, did the readings, and got a C on the first test. she doesnt give study guides, she doesnt give review sessions. even in emails she's very unclear and vague in response to questions. interesting, but dont expect grade u deserve
this class is easy if you read the book RELIGIOUSLY!!!!! the tests for this class were graded so unfairly, maybe it's just the TA's but, i would steer clear.

worst professor ever, goto class if ur tired and want ot take a nap and listen to someone rabble on and on. Worst grading system ever, dosnt prepare you for tests no review, she should be teaching a preschooolers class.

She's more difficult than you think, but I believe if you work hard enough, you will do well. My recommendation: take REALLY good+detailed notes. This goes especially for those complaining about the first exam, which I got a 92 on, thanks to my LONG but VERY HELPFUL notes. In short she's not as easy as one thinks, but hard work will get you an A.

I thought this class was going to be fairly easy, but after the first exam, I wish I hadn't taken it. I got a 55 on the first exam (an extremely unfair test given that I put hard work into studying), which is a lot lower than any score I have gotten before. She is not a very good speaker in class, and her newborn son is going to be very ashamed.
She's pretty good, but a bit giggley
No Comments
Interesting stuff, and she was so sweet :) Quite helpful and very knowledgable
No Comments

Greek Drama. She didn't talk down to the class at all. There were no prerequisites, so she started everyone off at the same point. She was very thorough, and if that bores, take an independent study. She considers all students needs and doesn't rush students. Not everyone is a Classics major.
She seems to know her information, but talks down to the class as if they won't understand.  Seems nervous and giggly in lectures.  She is the low point of the UMASS Classics department.

She teaches with a lot of enthusiasm. The way she teaches make you pay attention and not drive you to sleep. It was a pretty interesting course. There were lots of reading assigned, but as long as you take good notes, you'll be fine.

Dr.Difulvio is the BEST. She is super engaging and does the best lectures. If you sit in the front she will check in with you and loves to talk with students and ask how they are. My class had over 200 people and she made a point to remember my name, such a sweetheart.

Gloria is an amazing woman and never fails to succeed while teaching. She makes you want to keep learning in her lectures. Although, her assistant for the class, Meghan, is terrible. Meghan is new and was a teacher before she moved and also helps with the lectures. I would not take this class only because of her assistant because she is terrible.

Took this class online also taught with Laura Vandenberg, they work well together. 2 exams and a final(open note), need to watch and focus on the lectures and take notes. reviews.comment: Took on Zoom with 2 profs. Class was entertaining and breakout rooms always got us involved. TAs were very accessible outside of class, and they held review sessions before exams. Watch the async lectures before class- they are easy listening and a good length. 3 exams, open note but "thinking" tests, so know the material- study guides provided.

reviews.comment: Very nice and fair professor. Interesting class.
Her lectures are very clear and prepare you to get As on the exams
Pubhlth 200 with Gloria is such a great class. Class is very straight forward. Some short writing assignments and easy exams. You also learn a lot!

She caught a bad rep due to past PH 200 classes being a lot harder, but it was remodeled this past semester and now it is great. Work is super manageable, grading is fair, and theres even extra credit on exams. Exams are fair. Discussion helps to solidify material taught in class. Gloria is super sweet and approachable.

This class was super easy for me. Not gonna lie I sat on my phone for every single class and I have gotten A's on every single exam, project, and paper. As long as you study and read over the study guides you'll do great. The papers are also super straightforward. don't buy the textbook it is not at all necessary for the classes, papers, lectures

There are 5 mini-assignments throughout the semester, they're pretty easy. DON'T buy the textbook. The exams are pretty easy if you studied. It is team-based, so you discuss concepts and material with your table mates which is pretty helpful. Overall, an easy A class.

Now that the class is team-based learning it is very easy. Graded on 5 short writing assignments, 3 exams, attendance, and a final project. All of the powerpoints are posted and the exams are easy multiple choice with extra credit. Overall pretty easy A as long as you do all of the assignments.

The class was completely restructured. Very easy class. Shes sweet and approachable. Her rate my professor isnt indicative of her PH 200 class as its totally different now. Some easy assignments through out the semester, 3 easy and fair exams. Attendance is counted.

Pretty easy class if you attend lectures. The exams have extra credit questions on them, so you have a cushion in case you get a couple wrong. The discussions are pretty helpful when it comes to exam reviews, but otherwise it's just a repetition of what happened in class (which I'm sure is helpful for some people).
So unbelievably tough. The exams have nothing to do with class work.
reviews.rating_tags: Graded by few things--Test heavy--Tough grader

reviews.comment: Gloria is great/very informative. The course is disorganized(though it will be team-based next sem - big improvement). Guest speakers come in often, with varying effectiveness. Great class. I learned a lot and info was helpful in other classes in public health. Guest lectures made the class interesting.

From the start i wasnt really a fan because she tried to push her LGBTQ agenda way too hard, but oh well I can move past that. However she herself barely taught the class, there was a guest lecturer almost every time the class met. I really can't judge her teaching because she hardly taught at all. She seems kind though, and the class wasn't bad.

reviews.comment: Gloria is the worst professor I have had so far at UMass. The exams are unreasonably hard and the TAs are uptight too. You should avoid this class.

Most of the classes are taught by guest speakers and they all have different teaching styles so it is difficult to get accustomed to the class. Also, the questions on the exams relate to info the guest speakers taught and Gloria is unable questions about that information. She is also pretty disorganized with powerpoints and iclicker.

Very knowledgable about public health, very bad professor. She got so frustrated with whispers in a lecture hall of over 300 students that she gave up and made guest lecturers do her job. I learned nothing because the guest lecturers read right off the slides about concepts we had not been introduced to yet. The worst class I have taken at UMASS.

She is clearly a knowledgeable person but has a difficult time trying to teach it to her students. The class is mainly comprised of guest speakers who read off of slides for the entire lecture period. The exam did not reflect what was gone over in class. Lecture heavy and uninspiring class. Classes felt unorganized and a waste of time.
Great professor super knowledgable. Exams are very aligned with practice exams. Make sure to put a lot on your cheat sheet.
christos is my favorite! do not use the textbook to solve homeworks. read the slides. the exams are just like the slides. know the slides.

Physical Chemistry is tough in the sense that it's dense with content. Professor Dimitrakopoulos is so nice and really is passionate about the class. He encourages student participation and discussion. Although he mostly reads off the slides, his exam questions are based off of them. Study hard by making a good cheat sheet and reviewing his slides.

Lectures are mostly just him reading off slides, the material is pretty interesting but there's a boat load of content. You need to fit literally every law, equation, graph etc. on your cheat sheet for the exams or else you are just gonna get a question wrong, because the practice exams/questions he gives really don't transfer.
fun class, really interesting 'material'.

The class is very interesting for how dull the material is, most of the people who complain about this class just go on their phones the entire time and don't pay attention. That being said, the exams grade you based on copying down the slides, not understanding the material.

Nice professor. He is welcome to help students after lectures and during office hours. His lecture slides are overwhelming yet easy to understand, and as long as you manage to put all of them in the cheat sheet you will do fine in the exam. Very little and fair homework and crazy curve final grades (I got 80 on exams and still got an A).

This entire class was so bland. A lot of the content had the potential to be covered in an interesting way, but the professor never even tried. Instead, he used oversaturated lecture slides which he expects students to flat out memorize for the tests. His term paper has no rubric so you have no idea what his expectation is. Also it's on zoom :(

Truly the most nit-picky grader. Exams are essentially just a regurgitation of the lecture slides. Someone in my class lost 20 points on a question for the first exam simply because they forgot to label the axis on their graph. Additionally Christos assigned us a paper with no rubric and then gave out rather poor grades with no explanation.

There is such a lack of care on this class. Lectures are him reading off slides, Hw does not reflect Exams at all, and his exams are graded so harshly worst chem eng class I have taken so far at the school

Great professor. He really only cares that students learn something from the course so he barely assigns any HW, makes the tests easy, and doesn't take attendance. The class can get boring but its the material, not his fault. He's a smart guy and is always willing to help.

Christos is a great guy. He is not a harsh grader. This class is truly hard to grasp and boring, it is not his fault. Usually, he reads a lot from his slides and although it can get boring he has no problem answering questions and clearing points of confusion in or outside class.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--ACCESSIBLE OUTSIDE CLASS--Caring

reviews.comment: She is a very sweet and caring professor! 2 and half hour long class but never felt boring. Has a great selection of guest speakers and gives great feedback on assignments.

As long as you attended it was very difficult either, the readings were long but she covered everything in class so you don't need to grasp the all of it. reviews.comment: Great teacher who tries to make things engaging and interesting as possible through videos and current events. If you're looking for a chill lecture class (3 hrs) this is it.

She's very nice, but I didn't learn much. She's the most outwardly liberal teacher I've ever had, which is unfortunate because the material should be objective. Her class is 3 hours long. assignments were free marks. Exams weren't too hard, but not enough time was accorded. He won't answer 'easy' questions if you're behind. Class avg was very low. Pick another prof.

He clearly knows his stuff, but is unable to teach it to others. Going to office hours was useless because he was impatient and couldn't understand why I was struggling. He should not be teaching at all and needs to stick to research only.

I disagree with most of you.  I had him a few years ago, and he is the reason I became a math major.  I was not very interested in math before this course, but it was require for my major.  I thought he explained the material in a very clear way that made it interesting.
He is such a nice, smart, and wonderful teacher! It's really sad to see him go. What a great guy!
He does go a bit fast, but his sense of humor is nice.  Also, he was very helpful during his office hours at explaining material

He's really smart and definitely knows a lot. I found him very helpful, approachable, and even with a sense of humor. He DOES scale the tests as he grades them. Since he does this, he doesn't scale them afterwards. Also, he gives bonuses which is a plus. Great Calc teacher. I'd recommend him.

Absolutely brilliant man, but he cares nothing for his students, is VERY impatient with students at his office hours & writes the hardest exams you could imagine. He moves at lightning speed in lectures & outright failed 9 of 15 people in my class.
Lenient grader but the lectures are kind of not needed. Still, she is a nice person and gives you good feedback on assignments. Easy class.

Very smart man, incredibly high stakes assignments with limited room for improvement. Does not grade until end. Avoid for GPA. No one I know gets an A, harder than orgo 1 and 2 and cell molec to get an A.

reviews.comment: I took bio 572 in fall of 2023 and I enjoyed it. Yes it was difficult but certainly not unreasonably difficult. If you actually do the readings, you're good. The journal articles incorporated are interesting and really help you grow as a student. As a neurobiology class, be prepared to discuss molecular bio concepts in the context of neuroscience.

I understand it's a 500+ class, but this was brutal. Gerry is a pretty nice guy, I have no issues with him, but the way he runs this class could not have been worse. reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Beware of pop quizzes--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: Best professor I have had at UMass I would definitely recommend anyone take his class. Does cool experiments to show class concepts and can tell he cares about the well-being's of his students.
Professor Downes was an incredible professor! I enjoyed his class immensely. I highly recommend!
The first in the bio 105 trilogy. He's nothing special and not a bad professor. The worst out of the 3 for sure. His section was kinda boring but he never gave up on the class.

reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Beware of pop quizzes--Tough grader

reviews.comment: Lectures were nothing special, but he talked slowly enough for us to get everything down. His exam was the easiest out of the three. Nice and funny guy.

Teaches you material that you need to know. Random in class writing assignments. reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--BEWARE OF POP QUIZZES--LECTURE HEAVY

reviews.comment: The atmosphere in his class was amazing. His lectures were great because he was funny and laid back but he was passionate about what he was teaching while giving great notes. He truly made me interested in what he was teaching. I got a 99 on his exam by showing up, doing the readings and doing the online quizzes.
reviews.rating_tags: Respected--Skip class? You won't pass.--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: My favorite professor of the 3-professor course. The material isn't anything special, but Downes' teaching of it stood out to me. Kept things interesting and makes me wish I was a bio major so I could take him again

I could have done better in this class if I studied harder and did all the readings. I expected an easy A and that is not what this class is. I got 100s on all the quizzes and in class writing assignments and even on the essays, but the exams killed me They are so specific and even studying wont help much because there is so much random material.
reviews.rating_tags: Respected--Get ready to read--Skip class? You won't pass.

reviews.comment: He gives a lot of notes comparing to the other two profs, so get ready for that and study well. The advantage of having these notes is that you know exactly what you need to study for
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Skip class? You won't pass.

Extremely tough grader, he looks for very specific answers. 25 multiple choice, 15 T/F and generally 8 open response q's on exams. You really have work hard.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough Grader--Skip class? You won't pass.--SO MANY PAPERS

reviews.comment: Downes doesn't really care about each student's learning. He reads off his slides and speaks precociously. His tests are focused on memorizing the smallest details and don't reflect well on the important concepts of the class. He is also very disconnected from the students. Scheduling office hours with him is difficult.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--BEWARE OF POP QUIZZES--LECTURE HEAVY

reviews.comment: Professor 1 in a 3 professor class. He had a lot of interesting things to say I thought. Easy class too, probably the easiest I've taken at Umass.

Beware Psych/Neuroscience students thinking they'll have an advantange in a neuro class: this class is extremely challenging. He's tries to cover SO MUCH material so lectures are long and he moves through it so rapidly; it's challenging to keep up so if you fall behind, get help early.
This class in insanely hard and he puts SO MUCH material into each exam. you have to read the book because exam questions are straight from the book. extremely fast-paced hard ass class. good luck
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--BEWARE OF POP QUIZZES--LECTURE HEAVY

reviews.comment: A great teacher, interesting material in class. He makes sure that you know what is covered on the test. 3 essays and 3 tests for the class. 3 different parts with 3 different professors that swap. This class requires you to take notes and be attentive. There are also online readings since there is no textbook. Take it for your bio Gen. Ed.

Bio 105 is the easiest class I have taken at Umass. If you take notes, study for the exams, and write the papers, you will do well. Gerald Downes' is a nice, friendly guy who doesn't expect much from the class. The three essays you write for the course are really easy if you just follow the format. This class is an easy A if you try.

He's not bad but there was something I can't pinpoint that I don't like about his teaching style. Aside from this, a bit disorganized and fastpaced. For some reason he doesn't come off as clear about material as you'd like. Take additional notes bc slides alone aren't enough. Attendance matters. You have to really try hard, exams can be tricky.

He is smart & an expert in neuro. Lectures are long and too fast paced. 2 tests+attendance+forum posts +final +2 in depth article reviews. Tests are detailed, memorize all his slides. Tough that theres a lot of material & so much to know. Have to attend class for the ?'s of the day which are on tests. Lots of primary lit reading. Dont buy text book

I had him as a professor for Biology of Social Issues. He tends to explain broad concepts and not expect too in-depth of a knowledge. He still explains things really clearly and also is willing to clear up any confusion on the spot. He is extremely knowledgeable and can be funny. Tests are easy and short. Readings posted online, no textbook.

Easy class. Good Professor. His slides are sometimes too long and full of unnecessary information. His tests are really easy. Go to class and you should get the easiest A ever. If you don't go it is still an easy course. The class is really interesting too, and he makes it engaging.

Had him for BIO 105. Easy class and straight forward professor. Very wise and knowledgable. Explains very clearly, but sometimes rushes through his lecture and it's hard to write everything he says down. Overall great guy, great professor for an easy class.

Had Gerald for Neurobio, the class is challenging just because of the material but he is really knowledgable, reasonable, and available for help. You do have to read the book and put in effort to get an A! Those who say he is a bad teacher are probably just lazy. Know the study guide material, seek out help, and you will pass.
Had this guy for Neurobio- one of the hardest classes I've ever taken. He does surprise attendance checks, has ridiculous "quizzes" which are actually exams.

He's a nice guy and can to teach the lecture materials well but BEWARE: His exams ("quizzes") are VERY hard. The questions are very specific and have information that only the book has. The upshot is that his lectures closely follow the book, so if you get the book and read the chapters, you should be good on exams.
Wont post the study guide until the day before the exam But exam material is only partially related to it. Completely killed my interest in this subject.

Great teacher. Very clear and knowledgeable about the material. Unfortunately the tests are poorly written, and I believe by another teacher, because Gerald Downes does a fantastic job with example questions and the text book material. I would highly recommend taking this class with him.

Really nice guy. Approachable. His lectures are straight from the book. You definitely have to read the book before coming to class or else you won't really understand what is going on. Exams are a little hard. THE BOOK IS YOUR LIFE!

Pretty bad teacher.  Tests aren't that difficult but you have to teach yourself everything.  All he does it copy paste pictures from the book onto power points and reads the captions.  Tests are worded as to trick you and many questions are on fairly irrelevant things.  I'd avoid this teacher if your not good at teaching things to yourself.
Amazing professor. SO helpful!

Gennifer is very kind and and enthusiastic about what she teaches. She gives a lot of readings that are very long but honestly they are not necessary to the class. We wrote an essay about some of them eventually but you can get away with the class by not reading them. Her essays were easy and always did well.

read two extremely long "short" stories weekly w homework on both, essays take up 60 PERCENT of ur grade, she doesn't give out 100s, nearly impossible to end w an A. she is nice tho. but so much group work and attendance taken. way too much work just to fulfill literature requirement.

Nice woman but nothing is ever good enough for her. I am a very very good writer yet she always finds one minor thing to critique and almost never gives 100s. SO much reading with little time to do it. Lots of group work which I hate bc I hate talking to people
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Participation matters

reviews.comment: she was a really bad teacher. and attendence matters!!
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Participation matters

reviews.comment: She was a great teacher and very caring towards her students. The essays make up 60% of your grade, but she was easy to reach outside of class and always gave helpful feedback on them. Class time is almost always spent discussing the reading as a class, which helps you with the essays when you're analyzing the text. Overall a fun/interesting class.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: She was a really caring teacher and her class lectures never felt too awkward which can be hard for english gen eds. The three essays were moderately difficult but she provided lots of feedback on them and gave lots of opportunities to meet with her. Overall a great class with interesting readings and discussions.
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Clear grading criteria--Lots of homework

reviews.comment: While a really nice person, this class is graded weirdly. She never gives higher than a 95 so if you get one bad grade it's almost impossible to get an A. She always made us sit in a circle and sometimes gets mad when you are on your computer.

This class is dense despite Lan's dry and slow lectures. I had to put in an enormous effort into this course, and I had previously taken STAT315. Lan doesn't seem to care about the material and was the opposite of inspiring. The midterm was ridiculously hard and the homework grading is unforgiving. Not enough resources available to prepare.

Lectures were a bit dense, but discussions, homework, and quizzes helped reinforce material. The midterm was quite difficult, but the final was very reasonable. In addition, there was a very generous curve and extra credit provided. Almost 70% of the class received a B+ or better. Overall, I would say that he is the best of the CS 240 professors.

I think a math heavy course like CS 240 would be a lot better in small sections compared to large lectures. Still, I found Professor Lan to be quite solid. Although lectures can get quite dense somewhat monotonous, he's actually a pretty funny guy. He curves by standing(quite generously) and is still by far the better professor to take 240 with.
reviews.rating_tags: Lecture heavy--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Terrible decision to make the midterm THAT much harder. The class average on it being abysmal speaks volumes. Course has been well taught and managed in the previous years, but the midterm's difficulty this time around was completely unfair and a horrible mismatch to any past exams we were given to help prepare.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: His lecture is boring and harder than it needs to be.

Lan revamped the class to make everything way harder than it needs to be. Midterm median was a 60. Although there is a curve, don't count on it. Everything in this course is quite hard and there are not adequate resources to prepare. Take this class with Parvini.

Andrew Lan's section covers strictly more material than Parvini's. The midterm was also significantly harder than past semesters, making practice materials useless. Lectures are dry, and assignments are just PDFs/Canvas quizzes, leaving no room for error and forcing you to compare answers. The only highlights are his humor and a generous curve.

One of the most boring and monotonous lecturer I have ever encountered at this school. It seems like he is not even interested or passionate about teaching the class. How can someone make such an interesting topic like probability so boring to its core.

This guy is a savior for CS students who want to avoid Wilson for CS240. If you can take 240 with Lan, go for it! Exams were reasonable as they were very similar to the practice exams, and lectures were clear and relatively simple for what otherwise might be difficult concepts.

Lectures were very theory-heavy and sometimes he went on tangents that were not relevant to what we needed to know. Homeworks were fine, medium difficulty, quizzes were definitely the most annoying part of the class, but its doable. Midterm was easy, Final was hard but he curves your final grade a lot. Hard to fail the class.
reviews.rating_tags: Clear grading criteria--Gives good feedback--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Great professor. Kind of easy exam where he wants his students to perform the best. Curve and lenient grading

Professor Lan was pretty good. Lectures are a bit dry and in depth but he covers everything well enough. The first half of the class is basic stats then the second half is more CS-oriented stats. Midterm was fine, final was a bit tough but the final grade thresholds were curved. Homeworks were also medium difficulty.
Love this guy and his name.

Decent professor. Rather dry lectures but made the exam super easy, so there is not much to complain about. I wouldn't take him as a professor again since he seems so unpassionate and unrelatable as a professor-- especially for a higher-level class. Ultimately, not a terrible professor if you have to take him but pick someone else if you can.
Andrew was a decent lecturer, the material was rather dry for CS 240. Felt like I was trying to game the syllabus rather than actually learn the material in this class.

Uncompromising and stubborn. Course policies are super contrived and unintuitive. Most difficult part of class is trying to not get scammed by syllabus. He was an okay lecturer. He complained about having to teach the class once because he co-taught and had to teach the 'boring/easy half'. A bit unenthusiastic
Unrelatable, does not care about students or take feedback. Maybe it would be different if it were a higher level class.

Most challenging and interesting class I've ever taken. Topics were hard but applied and useful, really had to work hard to succeed. Complaints about Professor Lan in other review are somewhat inaccurate. He expects you to try, learn, and find resources on your own before reaching for help, and his office hours are super helpful

Assignments were very challenging but graded fairly, he was very helpful in office hours, had to re watch lectures to understand assignments most of the time, lectures were usually pretty good though, very theory focused whereas the assignments are very applied. If you put in a good amount of effort you'd more than likely end with a good grade.

Based professor. I think a lot of the negative reviews mention perceived rudeness, but that's just the way he talks. All of his piazza responses have been short, concise, and exactly answer what the student is asking. The course topic is about applied methods, which is mostly what you get graded on (projects), but lectures are heavy math/theory.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Gives good feedback--Respected

reviews.comment: The only valid complaint on RMP that there are only 1hr of office hours a week. During the first lecture Andrew made it clear that you need to be motivated to learn. Lectures are usually very interesting with a lot of intuition given for any new topic, proof heavy but that is not tested. 590OP has def motivated me to take more higher level classes.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Amazing lectures --Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: Class was too easy so might want to take it, however Andrew is quite possibly the rudest prof. I have come across in higher ed. Beware not to say the wrong thing and piss him off lol.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Lecture heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Course is difficult and you are told that at the start. Expect very minimal support to succeed in the class from Andrew and the TA's. How well you do in this class pretty much depends on your self-study skills, which is against the point of taking a class in general. Expect to feel unwelcome at office hours (which are 1 hour a week).
There's not much to say besides that he gave great lectures that made things clear and assignments and tests were fair.
Hes a good guy and his exams/hws arent very hard. Wants everyone to do well.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Graded by few things--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: This review is really late, but I took 590 with professor Lan last year and it was probably the most interesting class I have ever taken. Expect to work hard on the projects and watch (and then rewatch) lectures to understand what is going on. Prof gave really hard exams, but was a very fair grader. This class inspired me to go to grad school

Great professor. Great lecures. Cares about both excellence and well-being of students. Extremely accomodative but definitely no pushover. Lan is our man. Frequent polling, publicly asking for feedback is rare in most CS courses at UMass but Lan is OUR man.

Lan has been the best CS professor out of all the courses (6) I've taken so far. The exams were easy (he was very understandable about quarantine and going online) and the homework wasn't terrible. I'd recommend him.

Andrew is an absolute legend, made the class very easy and his snarky meta emails/piazza pinned posts were so funny. Outside of lecture, he tries to make himself as much as possible, which I appreciate. Some of the explanations in his slides were a little unnecessary, especially since I took STATISTC 515 before. Overall, take 240 with him.
great semester, very responsive

One of the better professors, especially consider it is his first semester teaching. Although the exams could be better, the final exam was good and hopefully a reflection of what's to come. One of the friendliest and most accessible professors I have had, with good lectures relevant to the course material. Overall, good professor.

Professor Lan is a great professor and a great guy in general. He cares a lot about helping students learn. He is very approachable if you have questions, and tries to deliver the content in a digestable way for everyone. The content is hard but everything ends up making sense through practice. I'm glad I had Professor Lan for this class.

Professor Lan is very knowledgeable about the content in this course. Hes very receptive to criticism and adjusted his course to fit multiple learning styles. The tests are tough but fair assessments of the content. He does struggle with explanations in class but its nothing that cant be solved with a drop in at office hours. Highly recommend!

He's a very smart guy who cares a great deal about his students. The tests are a bit hard, but he'll give you everything you need to do well. He isn't as intuitive as he could be, but at the end of the day, you'll have a great understanding of everything.
Lan is a great professor, the class is one of the more difficult classes Ive taken but his lectures are incredibly helpful. Your grade is heavily weighted towards your exams.

Lan is great, very witty and receptive to student feedback. Tests were fair and completely doable if one studied well, but since so many people complained on Piazza, he created an insane curve. Take his class while he's still a fresh and sweet guy who listens to entitled students.

Lan is a great professor who illustrates concepts such as joint pdfs and cdfs very well for people who have no background in multivariable calculus by prompting us to visualize the vague problem statements in terms of the familiar material (dartboard accuracy probability problems etc). He makes sure that everyone learns. Exam time limits suck tho.
Amazing teacher. It's his first semester and already his lectures have been the best out of every CS professor i've had.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Test heavy--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: A lot of people complain about the exams being too difficult, and I agree. However, after receiving this feedback Professor Lan made steps to create a reasonable scale based on the classes performance and added an extra credit problem to the homework which he gave the answer to in class. Overall, the class is hard but Lan makes it more enjoyable.

Andrew is a new professor, the last two comments seem to be really trying to take a crack at him for making exams difficult, as this is supposed to be a difficult major. Andrew has a distinct teaching style, and though he could work on making the class more interactive, he does care for his students and is trying to learn how to be a better prof.
reviews.rating_tags: Respected--Skip class? You won't pass.--Tough grader

reviews.comment: Amazing professor and makes complex problems seem easy by explaining it in a detailed manner. The lectures are great and very easy to understand.

Only had four quizzes over the entire semester, they were very consistent and pretty easy if you actually pay attention to the lecture handouts. Lecture handouts were incredibly helpful, but otherwise there's nothing much to care about. The class was pretty boring, but a requirement for my major.

He is a very knowledgeable professor, but his lectures really don't help that much and sometimes make you more confused. His exams are super straightforward, and as long as you keep up with the readings, you will be fine. I had an amazing TA, so my experience was good. Definitely not a hard class at all
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Clear grading criteria--Graded by few things

reviews.comment:
He does not care about teaching, he does not want to engage with you and he lets the TA's do whatever they want. Entire course grade was based on four exams!

Should have taken this course with the original prof who is apparently amazing. He also screams so loud he broke the AV equipment multiple times.
He gives very interesting lectures! The grades depend on only a few assignments, but he is a fair grader and gives extra credit.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Gives good feedback--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Andrew does the bare minimum with his effort to the class. He knows what he is speaking about however he doesn't know how to be an actual professor. He changed the final exam date so late that the TAs had to change their schedule. When I asked about it he just brushed it off like it didn't matter and decided to act like it was the student fault.

As of November 24th, he sent out an email, somehow forgetting that the FINAL exam was to be taken place on December 3rd instead of the eighth. Andrew does show his knowledge about the topics are good, but besides that, he does not know or care to be a professor. Doesn't even care enough to make lecture notes for in class. I took this for fun too.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Lecture heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Prof does not think its important to make lecture notes or slides at all. The most you will get from him is a brief summary of the philosophers covered in class, the only things that are graded are 4 in class exams and the discussion section. you will lose 10% every time you miss class. TAs could not care less to help out. TA or Prof doesnt care
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Good professor, cares alot about the subject. TAs will be your best friends and are the ones in charge of grading your tests. Lectures not mandatory but super helpful
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Amazing lectures --Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Expect nightly reading, usually between 25–100 pages per week. Lectures are delivered without slides and consist of him speaking continuously. Has no problem calling you out for using your phone in a 200 person lecture. The grade is based only on 4 quizzes. He has a tick where he coughs or clears his throat during lectures which gets annoying.

He's definitely condescending and pretentious, but understandable bcs he is a very smart guy. Lectures can get hilarious with the examples he gives. Lectures with no slides, and will call you out in a 200 ppl lecture if he sees you using your phone. The readings every week were like 40-80 pgs depending on week. Only grades are 4 quizzes 20pts each
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Lecture heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: I failed a Quiz and when I was trying to reach out for help it was ignored and when I did get a response he criticized me for not looking at my notes when he did not send them to us at all. He also does 4 quizzes and that is your lifeline to passing the class. Lot of reading he made it hard to understand as well.
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: I did like 2 readings all semester icl but very interesting class
Very interesting prof, lots of readings but most aren't necessary if you understand the concepts. Super engaging classes and discussions on topics you wouldn't experience otherwise.

He's pretentious, kinda arrogant and makes you feel stupid, but at the same time he has every right to be that way. Brilliant mind however, if he wants to succeed as a professor he needs to develop a little more of a soul.

Overall a great prof who is knowledgeable and your grade is determined by five short essays. His lectures are insightful but its always unclear what answer he wants from his questions. He also has a no technology policy, but the discussions were great and very helpful in answering questions on the readings. If you put the work in you will do well
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Lecture heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: The class had A LOT of reading due each time the class met (sometimes like over 30 pages) and it was super dry and old material. However, the lectures that Professor March delivered were really engaging and informative and made this class so enjoyable for me. Grade is made up entirely of five short writing assignments.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Lecture heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Class consisted of him lecturing the whole time. No slideshow, just talking. I'd zone out and act like it was a podcast tbh. There's a no-computer policy which sucked, but the whole grade was 5 500-750 word essays+attendance. Super manageable/easy. March clearly knows what he's talking about but he's kinda insufferable. Still an interesting class.

Lecture-heavy class with required attendance. He's a good lecturer though (he can be very loud), and provides lecture outlines. A lot of reading, but he explains it in class. Very strict about using technology in class. Graded on five papers throughout the semester, which are pretty easy to write if you do the reading and pay attention in class.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Lecture heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Pretty much all he does is lecture, but it's not so bad. Assignments are just 5 short 500-750 word papers throughout the semester which are pretty easy A's if you draw from the readings. He can be pretty loud but if you ask him to turn it down he would.
Professor March is very passionate and lively, the lectures are informative and interesting if you follow along with the readings

As a warning, pretty much all that he does is give lectures in class, but those lectures can be very interesting if you've done the readings and understand what's going on. Pretty chill professor and if you just do the readings and pay attention, it's hard to get a bad grade.

There is SO MUCH READING. But I used online summaries to get through most of it, and the handouts + lectures + discussions that he has are very helpful to understanding what he wants us to grasp from each reading assignment. I copied all the handouts in a notebook instead of printing and it's how I passed the three essay assignments.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Clear grading criteria--Inspirational

reviews.comment: Professor March is very knowledgeable about political Islam and has actual experience writing about it and meeting with major thinkers. His teaching style is not the greatest, but the class is nonetheless intellectually rigorous. Has a tendency to shout when lecturing, which can be a little much. Still, I did learn a ton from him.
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Lecture heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Amazing class! March did a great job of explaining political theory with fun and interesting lectures. Grade was based on 3 writing assignments and discussion participation.

March is one of the best professors I have had here at UMass, but his classes definitely aren't for everyone. He is insanely knowledgable on political science and has a way of explaining things that makes it all click. However, your grade is based on 3 assignments so if you don't go to class, you won't pass. But if you enjoy poli sci, I recommend.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Amazing lectures --Graded by few things

reviews.comment: You honestly don't have to do the readings since he goes over them so in depth in lecture. Attend lecture and take good notes and you'll be fine. I didn't read anything assigned the whole semester and got an A just from doing good on the 3 assignments using only lecture notes. Assignments are 3 parts: identification, short answer, and short essay.
reviews.rating_tags: Amazing lectures --Lecture heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Not going to lie, funniest man I've ever had the pleasure of learning under. Really great and engaging lectures to be honest. Just make sure that you're actually putting effort into the class, because he likes to cold call on people (especially those who aren't paying attention.) As long as you don't slack off, this class is a riot.

The class itself isn't too bad: your grade is mostly based on three assignments (which are basically take-home tests with an essay at the end). However, there is a lot of reading that needs to be done for every class. Professor March is also a bit intimidating, though extremely knowledgeable and very good at explaining political theory in lecture.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Lecture heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: March is an intelligent professor, and very well spoken. However, as an introductory class I found this to be difficult. The readings were difficult to understand and without the lectures would have been impossible to dissect. I also did not find my discussion to be remotely helpful, as my section was unorganized and felt unplanned.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Skip class? You won't pass.--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: The class is basically just him lecturing all the time, and your grade is based on three papers. March is super smart and interesting to listen to, although sometimes it feels like you are just listening to his brain ramble on.

Prof March attempts to engage students in lecture, but if you aren't all that into political theory or philosophy it will be difficult to get through lectures and complete the assignments. Grading is 3 writing assignments, 33% each. He sometimes speaks in confusing monologues and metaphors, but explains readings well so you don't have to do them.

You don't *have* to attend class, but you really should just because of how information-packed each lecture is. It's definitely a difficult class but it's super interesting and I liked the way he presented the different philosophers that we read.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Amazing lectures--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: I stopped showing up to class halfway through the semester because he posted the notes the day of anyway. There were only three assignments the whole semester including the final, which all had the same format. This makes it important to do well because if you get bad grades on two of them you're kind of screwed. Overall it wasn't too bad though.

Lectures can be long and boring if you aren't in the right mindset, but he tackles really interesting subjects and I find the lectures very thought-provoking. I did all the readings through the first paper but after that, could not bear to read any more theory, its very dense. If you pay attention and put effort into the papers, you'll succeed.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Amazing lectures--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: Very text heavy class, it was political theory. Could be confusing if first political theory course/dont have prior knowledge of the canon. Lectures were good, Prof. March was able to explain concepts from the readings well. Grade based on three papers. Papers are basically explaining what the reading says. So, do the reading.
