Reading heavy, material long, and difficult to understand, way too many complex topics discussed at the same time, has difficulty explaining those topics in a clear manner, entire grade based off 3 ten question exams, participation required even when you don't understand nor have an answer. More of a history class than polisci. Not worth the effort
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Skip class? You won't pass.--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Definitely a text-heavy class. Requires high level of attention but Prof March is able to explain high level political theory to practically anyone. Can sometimes appear a bit intimidating as he is not afraid to put you on the spot, but don't be afraid to say you don't understand something - he is surprisingly approachable.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Amazing lectures--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: Professor March definitely knows his stuff but that does not make his class worth taking. I've never felt so confused about every single part of a class--the lectures will make your brain explode and the assignments have zero structure, no rubric no nothing. Entire class based off of three assignments. I would not recommend
reviews.rating_tags: Graded by few things--Lecture heavy--Tough grader

reviews.comment: The course was fine. The class structure was a bit weird and definitely encouraged procrastination. The lectures were interesting and Prof. March (dude is seriously knowledgeable & clever, Oxford grad and isn't in your face about it) was able to bring high-level political theory to be understandable. Papers just asked you to rephrase texts. Easy A.

Dr. Spracklen is a very kind person. He teaches in a very clear way and simply wants you to improve your writing skills. He requires you to meet with his twice throughout the semester to check in on two of your papers, which honestly helped a lot. He gives tons of feedback on your writing, which is daunting at first, but again very helpful.

This class has multiple projects which run throughout the semester. Doing good is based on the amount of effort put into the assignments. A great amount of feedback is given which makes redrafting and getting a better grade easier. Dr.Spracklen does check ins where you can discuss the feedback you got. A great section to pick for Jr. year writing.
reviews.rating_tags: Clear grading criteria--Gives good feedback--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Dr. Spracklen is an amazing professor. He is very invested in the growth and success of his students. He does multiple check ins with his students. The content is heavy and difficult but the class is set to go over the content multiple times. This class uses alternative grading which allows students to focus on learning instead of exam success.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Gives good feedback--Inspirational

reviews.comment: Very kind professor in the biology department. Tackles a tough course material and explains it very well. Ddemonstrates that he is trying to do his best for his students by doing in-person check-ins to go over how the course is going for you specifically. Uses inclass assignments more as a way to review. By far one my favorite professors at UMass!
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Gives good feedback--Caring

reviews.comment: (Biology 580) Dr. Spracklen is such a nice guy. He tries his best to provide an engaging and comfortable environment to all his students. He is very understanding and flexible with deadlines. He is also sympathetic and is willing to help in any way. All you have to do is read the assigned portions, answer pre-lecture questions, and attend class.

Dr. Spracklen is overall a great professor for writing! There are multiple assignments that are worth a good chunk of your grade, but I thought they were spaced out well. I was never overwhelmed by the work in the class, and smaller assignments are graded for effort. He gives clear rubrics which really help as well. Participation is also key.
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Clear grading criteria--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Sometimes the amount of feedback he gave was overwhelming, and even when I improved on the areas he specified and talked with him individually, the grade I got didn't reflect the work I put into my assignment.  The methods project was also not fun at all because you got bad grades unless you went ahead to see future steps in it. But still very kind
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Dr. Spracklen does a great job making a difficult topic like histology make sense. This was his first time through the course so there were some things that we had to pivot from that did not work. He is very willing to help if you just speak to him. If you want to really learn microscopic anatomy TAKE THIS COURSE. Prepare to work hard though!

Dr. Spracklen made bio 523 (a class for mainly seniors) overly difficult and expected us to study for hours upon end. He treats his class like its the only class students are taking, and like its the most important thing in the world. Making us memorize tiny useless details is not helpful to learning. Dr. Spracklen is arrogant and difficult.

The class itself wasn't too bad, but I didn't seem to enjoy Dr. Spracklen as much as other students on here say. He seems like a decent guy, but his style of teaching was hard for me to get used to and I felt that he took a different approach than other professors. Maybe because it is one of the few writing courses that I've taken?

Dr. Spracklen was easily one of my best teachers. Yes there was lots of assignments but none of them were unnecessarily difficult. Follow the rubric & watch the instructional videos it will be an easy course. He gives great feedback. Granted due to COVID this was not a typical course it was online and asynchronous but if anything it made it better.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Lots of homework--Participation matters

reviews.comment: Professor Spracklen is one of the nicest professors I've ever had! Writing in bio is not a super exciting class, but just going to office hours and hanging out with Spracklen made my weeks better. The assignments can be kind of annoying, but he gives clear feedback about exactly what you need to do to get an A. Wouldn't pick a different prof!
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Accessible outside class--Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: Dr. Spracklen really cares about his students, is always available to talk to, and provides really good feedback that actually feels relevant to writing in biology. 10/10 recommend taking 312 with him!

Dr. Spracklen is an amazing professor who truly cares about his students and gives honest, helpful feedback to help you improve on future papers. Although somewhat of a tough grader, he is always accessible and is extremely thorough in his lectures and expectations for each class. Make sure to attend each lecture since participation counts.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Skip class? You won't pass.--Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: Great professor, tough grader but very fair. Very responsive to emails and happy to help out.

Slides are chock-full of information and Kitto does read off of them, however it's all very clear and concise. He used to be an auditor but makes a great professor. Three exams, attendance mandatory, weekly homework's, frequently has extra credit opportunities. Super understanding when you email him about any issues too! I'd take him again.

Great professor. Lectures are actually pretty interesting and important for the students as many will go into the auditing profession. Lots of slides but keeps you engaged with discussions. Really cool dude, put in the work and you will get a good grade

Course material is dry but professor Kitto makes it as interesting as possible. Tests are difficult and hard to study for. A lot of group work that is more generously graded. Professor Kitto is a good dude and cares about his students.

Class sessions drown you in PowerPoint information, so reviewing for tests becomes difficult. Tests are often tricky and very specific, picking out details from one of many slides. Lots of group work, but graded fairly generously. A fairly easy class, just one that is hard to get through.

Very kind, helpful and easily accessible professor who teaches concepts super well. The course itself was the hardest I've taken and required a lot of effort and study on my end, however, the professor did a fantastic job accommodating my learning throughout the course.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Amazing lectures --Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Goated class, goated professor.

Taking my first graduate-level class (CS514) with McGregor was a great experience. While it really did feel like I was overwhelmed with the course material at times, he had very informative lectures that I could always go back to to clear up any doubt. Very challenging homeworks, but I thought his exams were easy.

He covered a lot of topics in the course but did make sure we all understood in the class. Homeworks were relatively difficult but they gave lot of practice. He answers almost all the questions in Piazza very clearly and as soon as possible. He also considers students' feedback posted in Piazza and implements accordingly.

I took CS 611 and I thought the class was very interesting and rigorous. The homeworks were challenging but we had 2 weeks to do them and we could do them in groups, so it wasn't so bad. Exams were pretty easy.

Professor Mcgregor is an amazing lecturer. His lectures are very clear and thorough. He makes sure everyone understands the material well.  On Piazza, he answers everyone's questions. He really is awesome and understanding of the students.

Nice guy, very helpful as a teacher, understanding. DON'T MISS CLASS! EVER! If you go to class and pay attention, you'll do relatively well. Course material is boring and it can be hard to focus in class on what's happening. Tests make or break the class for you. Homeworks: very long, don't procrastinate on these! TAs/Teacher are helpful.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--LOTS OF HOMEWORK--TEST HEAVY

reviews.comment: This class is very easy to do well in, but also just as easy to do poorly in. If you go to class and pay attention, you should do very well. Exams were not difficult, only 4 major homework assignments that we were given 10 days to do and weekly online quizzes. Good professor, cares about students and is quite funny.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Skip class? You won't pass.--ACCESSIBLE OUTSIDE CLASS

reviews.comment: Andrew McGregor is a fantastic lecturer. He's great at making sure everyone in the class understands what is going on without going too slowly, he's engaging, and he is good at making lecture interactive. I would take nearly any course if he was the professor and I would recommend anyone else to do the same.

Andrew is the best prof/person I have ever met. He listens to students, answers EVERY question with details. His class is very organized too. He posts all lecture slides and solution to every homework and exam (even practice exam). Don't hesitate to take his class or have a conversation with him about compsci or math! He's always there for you.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough Grader--LOTS OF HOMEWORK--Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: I have a lot of respect for Andrew because he actually cares very much about his students. He goes out of his way to answer questions in great detail and ensures you understand. The material can be somewhat abstract, but I don't see how anyone else can give better lectures. He is also a great guy, and structured the course very well. Pretty easy A
Great professor! Cares about students a lot and his lectures are very well organized.

Don't underestimate this course. It's relatively easy to do well but if you slack off you will do poorly. Mcgregor is a really nice guy and I loved him as a professor. My only complaint is that he has trouble controlling the lecture hall and would allow people to talk over him. His gentle personality is his biggest drawback. Gives perfect lectures.

McGregor is one of the few Comp Sci professor who actually seems to care about his students. He makes a concerted effort to learn people's names and makes sure you understand the material. The class itself is a little difficult as it is mostly math and very little programming.

You can navigate his personality and win his approval if you talk in all classes. But I will tell you it is fact: his 201H section is poorly run, artificially stressful, and not worth your time or sanity if you have more priority things to focus on.

201H with Bob Dow has its fair share of positive qualities like thought-provoking reading material and Dow having excellent taste in books and films, but the workload is heavy and his grudge issues make the learning environment artificially stressful.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Participation matters

reviews.comment: Bob Dow is a bright guy who picks interesting books and films. Unfortunately, his 201H section is a disorganized mess. He's better off being a literary scholar than a teacher. He is a really inspiring dude with good taste in literature, but the class setup drags everything down. Your call, I wouldn't recommend him if you like organized classes.

Getting on Bob Dow's good side isn't difficult but honestly it comes at the cost of your sanity. You have to participate in all classes, which is fine. However his section may not be ideal if your major is demanding like engineering or computer science. I recommend STEM majors against taking him for 201H as health is just as important as anything.

Do not take this class with Dow if your major is demanding like computer science. His 201H section is artificially harder than other sections for the following reasons: slow email responses, only 1 office hour, rude and narcissistic behavior, inability to admit to mistakes, and illegible feedback. Interesting readings, but discussions can suck.

Bob Dow is the only professor to avoid for 201H not because of the readings but because his 201H section is more artificially hard than that of the other professors. Unorganized, inaccessible (1 office hr, no Moodle). Grading based on agreement, not effort. Zero feedback. Hostile, dismissive, inflexible. If you have to take him, you're on your own.

This class was a bumpy ride. Class time was mostly Dow talking about the readings and trying to prompt discussion. Discussions weren't bad but he was not happy when discussions don't go in the directions he wants.Another issue I had was the disorganization. He gets upset when u ask questions about the syllabus. Assignments giving right before due.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Participation matters

reviews.comment: Interesting curriculum, knowledgeable and passionate professor.

201H with Professor Dow is an intense ride. Though passionate, his teaching style can be challenging. The workload is heavy, with frequent readings, papers, and a tough midterm. However, Unstuck study proved invaluable for exam prep, complementing the coursework well. Overall, a tough but rewarding experience.

Bob Dow is engaging, passionate, and a good guy but 201H under him is honestly a drag. Between 2 3+ hr movies/readings a week, 4-5 papers (up to 15 pages), and a take-home midterm, it is a lot to digest. Personally he liked me in the end, but fair warning: if you don't talk at least once in any of the discussions, he will hold a grudge against you.

I'm a quick reader and writer, yet this has been the most time-consuming class I've ever taken.  Bob Dow is engaging, incredibly smart, and an overall good person. You'll learn fascinating things, but the work is absurd. Between 2 3+ hr movies/readings a week, 3 papers (up to 15 pages), and a final presentation, it is a lot. Be careful.
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Lots of homework--So many papers

reviews.comment: Bob comes off as easygoing and views himself as chill, but he's really the opposite of empathetic towards struggles. No syllabus, passive-aggressive, won't offer written instructions for essays but grading is black box and depends on how much you agree with him. I did well in 201H but be warned he WILL hold grudges and make you be hard on yourself.

Bob Dow doesn't seem to care or want to stay in contact with his students. As a person who took 201H with him, I can safely confirm he is THE hardest 201H professor option out of all the other 201H sections. For example, I honestly found Orgo Lab and Biochem 423 much easier than this course. Take that into perspective, Orgo Lab and Biochem 423.

Rudest CHC professor ever. I'm convinced Dow ran 201H poorly with the ulterior motive to send students to therapy because he clearly thought all his students were lazy. Unlike what he thinks, this isn't true. I'm a CS major who's willing to put in thorough effort, but if he doesn't seem to listen to reasonable concerns, it's not a good look on him.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Lots of homework

reviews.comment: Bob Dow made 201H completely unbearable. The main issue is not the readings-it's the haphazard course management under Dow with zero willingness to take responsibility for his actions. Poor communication as he almost never responds to emails, refused to accept soft copies of papers (only hard copies were allowed), and had only 1 weekly office hour.

Bob Dow is insanely well-respected and knowledgeable, however, this doesn't excuse the way he ran 201H. He is an incredibly tough grader, and his criteria are impossible to decipher. He selects engaging reading material  but rarely checks his email. Overall, Dow has a wealth of knowledge but be ready to get roasted for your papers and read A LOT!

Bob Dow is hands down the worst choice for a 201H professor. If you take his class, be ready for harsh vibes. Don't expect reasonable workload, don't expect flexibility, don't expect to be understood, heard, or respected. The papers (worth 80%) are impossible with draconian grading policies. 201H with Dow is nothing but an exercise in self-torture.

Bob Dow is probably my least favorite professor at UMass. He's a very smart man who is generally respected and passionate about what he teaches, but he's a ridiculously hard grader, puts his students on the spot a lot, and doesn't give ample time to revise your papers. If you're late to class he'll call you out for it and hold grudges against you.

I probably wouldn't take him again. He was never really mean to me, he just put students like me on the spot A LOT. Main recommendation for surviving in 201H with Bob Dow is to do the readings, talk in every class, and expect a follow up question from him if you answer a question asked in discussions. Participation will get you through it.

Professor Dow is a genuine and kind man. He cares deeply about the subject matter and asks only for students to engage in the class discussions. The course is graded based on participation in class discussions, semi-weekly essays (1-2 pages double spaced), a midterm (a collection of writings, 4-6 pages one week deadline), and a final presentation.

Bob Dow seems like a nice man. To be honest, I personally have nothing against him and the readings he selects. But his 201H class was frustrating at times. Be prepared to bring hard copies of papers/notes to class because he doesn't like technology (eg: no phones while waiting for class to start or having laptops out for notes during class).
Bob Dow is by far the only professor you don't want to end up with for 201H and I would say that you should wait for a different semester if he is your only option left when selecting classes.
Really wonderful professor- stepped into a difficult situation and put his all into it!

Possibly the most irresponsible professor in CHC. Extremely belittling and rude, can't admit when he's wrong, email replies are always sporadic, only 1 office hour a week and hard to reach outside of class, doesn't care about student mental health, not open to helping students. Anyone can do a better job managing 201H.

No opportunities to get feedback and course structure was outdated. Drama creation is his priority, not mental health or student learning. Essay grading criteria were awful, and he's not warm or welcoming, so that doesn't help either. If you need to take 201H, save yourself the headache and just find an instructor who's more caring than Bob Dow.
Bob Dow selects interesting readings and films, but the workload of his classes obviously hits you like a truck.

Bob Dow is good at teaching the material and making boring classes interesting. However, his participation criteria are very, very harsh, so you have to talk in every class or he will not like that. Only take his class if your major isn't too demanding (this professor is not recommended for comp sci and engineering majors).
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Lots of homework

reviews.comment: Honestly, I don't understand a majority of these reviews. Bob Dow is honestly extremely friendly and passionate at teaching and he really is not a difficult grader. If you received a poor grade on an essay, he allowed extra attempts to redo the essay change the grade.

2 books, 2 essays and reports on them due almost every week (twice). Half grade deduction for even the most minor mistakes. Full of himself, doesn't respond to student concerns, turns an idea-building seminar into a hellish tortured 6-8 credit worthy workload. Apart from him and his unrealistic expectations, this is an excellent course.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Lots of homework

reviews.comment: Dow's ideas and commentary on what we read influenced me in many ways that I will take away from the class in years to come. While his lectures were intimidating and his style of teaching was different, the overall takeaway from the class was what made it a favorite of mine. His experience and insight is immeasurable yet unconventional.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Lecture heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: I usually try to avoid trash-talking professors, but some deserve it ngl. Bob Dow was just a character. He had his eccentricities (not in a funny way). Flipped out at class for not composting, frequently put students on the spot, opinions were the most lacking of all opinions, and didn't listen to students when they were feeling overwhelmed.

Do NOT take his class!!! His takes are the most biased of all takes, but if you disagree with him you will automatically get marked down. He doesn't seem to value diversity in opinions, he doesn't have a clear method of grading, and he's unorganized and lacks communication as well. Guy's a pretentious a$$hole!

Bob Dow is actively rude towards his students. Sits there and wastes a lot of class time putting students on the spot. Very boring, hates technology and will single people out and yell. Gets combative if you are too depressed and shows ZERO sympathy.

Bob Dow is the most repulsive, disrespectful, rudest man I'ver ever encountered. He wants to prove that his class is the best and gaslights those who think the opposite. My encounters with him made my blood boil just bc he is a bully. I consider myself to be able to handle almost any professor well but this class was just an automatic ego trip.
Inspirational in showing me exactly what I don't want out of a professor at Commonwealth Honors College. If you need to take 201H, wait for a more caring professor like Professor Yoder.
Dow doesn't care about the wellbeing or success of his students and definitely is one of the worst professors that I have had at UMass so far.

Bob Dow is NOT a human being and should no longer be employed in CHC. He frequently ignored complaints, gaslighted students who questioned his authority, regularly asked meaningless follow-up questions to force them to elaborate only to berate them. To top it off, his character literally reminds me of that of Billy Hargrove from Stranger Things.

This guy truly sucks. He is not a nice person, and he will not help you improve your grade if you are emotionally and mentally struggling. I would've given him a 0 but I have no choice. Get this guy out of UMass CHC.

I hope Robert Dow quits his job for good because he's got WAY TOO MUCH hate in his heart, and his close-minded attitude (always rejected opinions that don't match his) creates a dangerous environment unsuitable for learning. Poor communication as he won't respond to emails, and it's hard to get feedback from him. NEVER take his class!

Rude. Dismissive. Strict grader. No forgiveness. Doesn't believe in grade boost opportunities. Fully believes that everything he has done has been fair, but that's far from the truth. Workload higher than other 201H sections, feedback mostly consisted of roasts to berate students and less of how students can improve papers, and bad communication.

Do NOT take this class with Dow. Class was a nightmare and often felt more like a formal interview than a casual seminar. Course management was terrible, workload heavier than the other 201H sections, grading very arbitrary. Professor is very unorganized and lacks communication as well. The pain isn't worth DEMOLISHING your GPA.
He is extremely rude to students, and the rubric for grading papers don't make sense AT ALL.
His classes are really poorly managed. You have to stay on top of things because he won't give you an extension, and it's impossible to get feedback from him.

I'm not trying to be mean, but I didn't have a good experience w/ Robert Dow. Unorganized and lacks communication, creates a hostile learning environment, and doesn't listen to students when they're feeling burnt out. He's cruel and intimidating- I never wanted to interact with him. I was frustrated and always wanted to cry. Avoid all his classes.

Dow is the worst person I've ever met. He cares more about dismissing student perspectives and grades based on how much people agree with his false takes. The Commonwealth Honors College is a scam because they have clearly shown they don't care about their students in any capacity but rather grabbing money by allowing this guy to be a professor.

I've always had a Bob Dow do me wrong. I had him for a mandatory seminar class and not only were my sleep patterns messed up, but he was also very snobbish and demeaning and didn't care about his students AT ALL. Sure there was no final exam, but this was overshadowed by his subpar communication and lack of organization. Don't take, guys an a$$.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Participation matters

reviews.comment: Dow is the least inspiring professor in CHC. Extremely rude. Had no respect for any of our perspectives and constantly dismissed genuine concerns. Class was more of a "test" on how much you understood from the readings than discussions. Forced his students to find movies and readings outside of class instead of having movie days. I learned nothing.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Participation matters

reviews.comment: Bob Dow was downright horrid and did not create an engaging or welcoming learning environment. Avoid at all costs.
This is not a good professor to have for 201H. Grading criteria are incomprehensible and he's terrible at communication. Wait for a different professor.

I don't know why people are saying Bob Dow is an inspiring dude. He selects interesting readings, but boy bad things happen if you make an effort to get help from him. Not a very nice or empathetic human. He had no standardization and made the class impossible to do well on. DO NOT TAKE A CLASS WITH HIM IF YOU CAN AVOID IT.

The problem with Dow is that he won't admit to his mistakes, when he objectively is, and he is extremely rude to his students if he even gets a hint that they might think he's made a mistake. Never ever seen a professor act the way he does towards his students. Unless you're a sycophant, he's really just a pretentious dick who doesn't care at all.

I've never been treated with such blatant disrespect by a professor. Dow clearly has no regard for his students and is dismissive of their concerns. I was surprised to see all the bad reviews here, but they are deserved. I love writing papers, but having to deal with a close-minded fellow like Dow makes it a frustrating and unbearable endeavor.

If you have Dow for any class, you're automatically screwed because he's the type of teacher who expects students to agree with his flawed opinions, and he has a bunch of misconceptions about what "good writing" is. His Moodle page is disorganized, so as a result it is quite a headache for me to find the required readings for each discussions.

Don't ever take 201H with that man. My friend had Dow for 201H her freshman yr and once he went thru like war flashbacks in the middle of class and forced many, many, many of his students into uncomfortable situations (this isn't really his fault but omg). Also his takes are the most....uhhhhhhhhh....most........biased of takes.
This guy doesn't care at all about his students. Run away for your own good!!!
Pretentious ass who is strict and unfair as hell with his standardization and doesn't care about his students.

Dow has a massive ego. You learn nothing from his classes, even though he selects interesting films and readings. He would probably be a pretty good professor if he could admit to his own mistakes, fix the way he runs 201H, cut out some of the busy work, and check his ego at the door.

If you see Robert Dow's name, START RUNNING AND NEVER LOOK BACK. Simply put, he's unorganized and lacks communication. His feedback on papers is ILLEGIBLE, and he wastes a lot of time making an example out of students and putting them on the spot instead of driving an engaging discussion. You'd be better off taking 201H with someone else.

Bob Dow is akin to an absent yet powerful boomer whose true intentions are hidden behind a veil of a big ego. He cares about his students the same way a bird may take care of its' young, you are expected to start flying the moment you plummet out of the nest. If you can't, you fall, you fail.
Taking a class with Robert Dow left me braindead and shaved a decade off my already short life.

Robert Dow genuinely does not care if his students succeed or not. He is absolutely insane about his course standards and does not like to consider the mental health of students. I came to leave this review after a face-to-face interaction with him. I have never had a professor at UMass that cares less about his students than this man.
Very inconsistent grader! Grades do not reflect your effort if you have a professor like him or orgo professor Chris McDaniel.

I believe Bob Dow is an inspiring dude, but he's being super lazy. He had no idea how to run 201H because he didn't have a Moodle page set up, which is annoying because you have to find the required films and class readings on your own with no free PDFs of the readings provided. Overall, not a class I would take again, and I learned nothing.

Any class Bob Dow teaches automatically means that class is not a good class to take because while Dow is a big name in literature who selects interesting reading material, the structure of his classes is haphazard, he is boring, rude, sarcastic, disrespectful, and far from engaging, and communication from him is below average. Bad bad bad bad.

BobDow is an awful teacher. He's picky, monotone, disrespectful, and all-in-all a repulsive and disgusting human being who has no right to teach. I thought I'd like this class, but Dow made it more frustrating than it needed to be. I learned nothing from that useless fellow.

Never take a class with Bob Dow when you can take it with Professor Yoder. Bob Dow expects students to agree with his opinions and doesn't leave the floor open to multiple perspectives. He is rude and difficult to approach, and his discussions are super weird. Professor Yoder, on the other hand, is kind, caring, and easy to get help from.

Robert Dow is one of the least respectful professors the CHC has to offer. I don't normally complain against professors, but this guy is a real villain despite the interesting readings he selects - extremely rude and narrow-minded, terrible at communication, very poor course organization and structure, and uncomfortable and weird class discussions.

Robert Dow is a no-good, selfish, horrible professor who deserved to get his rating taken down by 2 points from his original rating because he's a real villain and bully who invalidates genuine student concerns and gaslights those who question anything on his courses. He has no right to be a professor anymore. Get this guy out of UMass!
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Participation matters

reviews.comment: Bob Dow has an unrivaled superiority complex that is quite proven in the way he takes pleasure in automatically failing those who make an effort to connect with him or disagree with his false opinions. He won't give you grade boost opportunities if you are struggling. I would've given him a 0 but couldn't. Get this man terminated from UMass CHC.

If you see Robert Dow's name, RUN THE OTHER DIRECTION AND NEVER LOOK BACK!! Dow is a prime example of a professor who doesn't value diversity in opinions, and it often feels like he's actively working against his students. Unorganized, lacks communication, no sympathy, berates you if your opinions don't match his false ideas. Never take his class!

It doesn't matter if you're a good student or not. The problem with Dow is he will do anything he can to give students a bad name, even if they're doing the right thing. You don't learn anything from taking his classes as his close-minded personality and disrespect towards literature novices creates a dangerous environment unsuitable for learning.
He is McDaniel Version 2.

Bro this guy doesn't help you. It's like trying to give a homeless man food, but the food is stale and dangerous to eat. Bob Dow makes you overthink and doubt yourself. Don't even take 201H with that man if you have the option. He is just awful at driving discussions and a very rude person who always feels like he's on a high horse.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Participation matters

reviews.comment: Jokes on you, Dow!! I passed 201H despite your disagreeable personality and willingness to set students up for automatic failure.

Do NOT take his class! Dow's 201H class had a much more frustrating workload than the other professors who taught 201H, and on top of that, he is very rude to students, lacks common sense and professionalism, is dismissive of genuine concerns, and makes no effort to connect with students. Truly obnoxious and horrible to have communication with.

Professor Dow was by far the worst professor I had during my time at UMass. He was rude, disrespectful, and impossible to get feedback from. The only opinions accepted in his class were those that aligned with his own. Your grade suffered if not, and class was a miserable experience. He has no business being a professor - shame on the UMass CHC.

Bob Dow may have a bright personality, but the way he sets up his classes darkens any form of inspiration he may give you. He doesn't use Moodle that often, and he has no organized syllabus or specific grading criteria for papers, which makes it hard to learn and get useful feedback on them. Overall he's an ok professor. Worst is an understatement.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: I would never take any class with Robert Dow. Took a class with him in the fall of 2021 and it destroyed my sanity, he is extremely mean to his students and wasn't flexible at all with the switch from COVID to face to face.
Worst 201H professor ever. Dow was a poor facilitator of discussions, and the workload was too depressing.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Participation matters

reviews.comment: I wouldn't take any classes with Robert Dow. In my honest opinion, his discussions are too formal and don't leave room for any opinions other than his.

It'd be unfair to comment on his character, but not on the way he handles his classes. Simply put, Robert Dow is unprofessional, disorganized, and incapable of structuring classes in a way that gives students enough time to improve their essay writing methodology. Use online resources like Sparknotes if you struggle.

NEVER take a class with Robert Dow. The general consensus is that he is not a nice or helpful human being, disorganized, very mean and unprofessional, inflexible, immature, harsh with communication, and disrespectful towards people going through a tough time. Unlike the other 201H professors, Dow is the only 201H professor to have an inflated ego.
Bob Dow is not a terrible teacher, but his inability to grow up or listen to valid complaints from others highly makes me question his professionalism as a professor overall.
Chill dude, but the way he structures 201H needs some serious overhauling.

201H is a frustrating class if Dow touches it as Dow was intolerant, overbearing, and mean, and he very clearly hated specific students for no reason. I thought Marius Minea was the most condescending professor I've had so far, but Robert Dow beats him to it.

Least respectful professor I have ever had period. Don't take any class with Robert Dow because he's going to make them more frustrating than they need to be as he shows no remorse for his overbearing personality, poor communication and ego.
No joke. My hair is graying so hard from taking a class with Robert Dow, and apart from that, he is disorganized, mean, unsympathetic, and he does not give students enough time to finish the essays.
Do not take classes with Robert Dow. He is unprofessional, disorganized, disrespectful, and has a reputation of making everything frustrating beyond practicality.

Robert Dow is an ok professor tbh. Not hard to do well, but not a good gen-ed. Technology policy is super unforgiving. Any instance of you being on a phone or another electric device WILL cause your participation grade to suffer. If you're a high energy morning person, take him. Otherwise, avoid.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Participation matters

reviews.comment: Robert Dow is a prime example of a mean and condescending professor with a lot of attitude. His feedback on essays is incomprehensible due to his messy handwriting, and he very clearly hated specific students for no reason. Be warned: if you voice any legit complaint on his poor course management, he WILL gaslight you like a big bully.

I would stay away from Bob Dow if you have a choice for a 201H professor. He's a chill dude who's trying to make the course fair, but 201H under him just has an outdated course structure. Basically, you don't get a lot of time to revise essays, and Dow is super unforgiving with due dates and participation.

Dow is a really inspiring teacher, I honestly like his class a lot but the workload is insane (and depressing). I read a lot a week (4-5ish hours) and we have hours of films to watch as well. You can get away with skipping a view readings and movies, but you have to talk in every class, so make sure you have something to say about the homework.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Lots of homework

reviews.comment: Robert Dow changed in the best way possible. Yes, he can be intimidating and strict at times, but it depends on whether you're on his good side or bad side. It's not hard to do well, and his 201H class has the best final outcome. Participation and patience will get you through it. Most importantly, he loves teaching.

Bob Dow is a very kind and understanding guy who cares a lot about the class he teaches, however he has high expectations. A typical week's assignment would be a 2-3 hour movie and then about 3-4 hours of reading (I'm not the fastest reader though). Something else is that this is NOT a history class even remotely. It's an English class.

Bob Dow is a super passionate professor. Although the out of class workload is a bit heavy, he selects pretty good reading and movie material (aside from a few foreign films which kinda suck). His discussions are lively and it is an open and friendly environment. He is very understanding and an overall fair grader.

Your class grade is based on 4 papers (20% each), a midterm (10%), and participation/reading journals (10%). Papers are graded fairly easily but no grading criteria was given. He has a few specific grammatical features that if you miss on your paper he deducts a whole letter grade. Movies/books assigned every class, many I didn't read/finish.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Participation matters--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Very good teacher, cares about the subject and wants you to engage in discussion.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Best professor i've had at umass. I was never bored because he always had something interesting thing to say. He really does care about his students, but you have to be present and not afraid to participate . In the end, he really just cares about growth and that you learned something. It's not hard to do well in and the work load isn't heavy.

For a class that is supposed to be discussing "ideas", there isn't a whole lot of ideas being discussed besides his. Grading policy is impossible to figure out and gives little to no feedback on assignments. Frequently calls out students for not participating, not showing up on time, etc. in front of whole class. Makes class awkward.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Skip class? You won't pass.

reviews.comment: doesn't like to be disagreed with. will twist your words. makes students uncomfortable, so no one talks in class. will then get mad at you for not being 'brave.' seems like he's only teaching his opinions. probably a very good, nice guy, but the only good part of this class is the readings.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--LOTS OF HOMEWORK

reviews.comment: Life-changing. It's "ideas that changed the world," so you should expect that the ideas you learn about are going to be complicated and difficult. I definitely put a lot of work in, but it made me a better student and ultimately a better human being. If you want to be inspired by an extremely intelligent and passionate prof, TAKE THIS CLASS.

Very intimidating professor who has no problem calling you out in front of the whole class.  Wants everyone to agree with his point of view and doesn't leave much room for others'.  If you don't get on his good side by frequently participating and agreeing with him, your grade WILL SUFFER.  Oh, and good luck asking him for an explanation or help.

Bob was an interesting professor. He desired for students to engage in discussion and it was usually terrifying if you came to class unprepared. He called on  students at random, but the conversations became very deep. Would take again, one of best professors for honors course

Bob Dow is a great man. He is forgiving, inspirational, and has a great outlook on life. He truly helps you to see the world in a new light. I recommend this class. I wish every one had the same outlook on life as him, the world would be a better place

Bob Dow was my favorite professor in the semester I took his class. Very cool guy. Assigns quite a bit of reading and writing homework. Journal entries (300+ words) due each week. 3 quizzes and 3 essay submissions in the semester. Quizzes were very easy. CLASS PARTICIPATION IS A MUST! You learn in his class by paying attention and participating!!

Definitely a great professor, really makes you think about life in a whole new way. Reading the books isn't hugely important (sparknotes can suffice), quizzes aren't bad, and only a couple 5-8 page "reading journals" which are not bad as long as you do the individual entries like he says. Fair professor and enjoyable class, take him!

He was a nice guy but for a teacher, he was unfair, mean, and critical.  If you had a bad class (aka a class that didn't participate as much as he wanted to), he would just be awful.  He gave so much more work than any of the other 291A classes too.

Bob Dow is the best professor I've had.  He was encouraging, inspiring, and made me want to do the work we were assigned.  We had great discussions in class on books, current events, life in general and everyone in my class loved him!
Interesting class, thought provoking discussions

Bob Dow is the worst prof at UMass. He's intolerant, overbearing, and mean.  Other english teachers told me I should be a professional writer. Dow HATED anything I had to say or write. He definitely DOES give D's, because I got them. If you don't agree w/ his ideas HE WILL FAIL YOU. If you think you can charm the devil, take the class, I dare you.

Bob is great! he will make you read and think differently than any other class. I really enjoyed it and reading is not my thing. Anyone will really benefit and be greatly rewarded if you take this class. Lots of books to read but they are great books! can be confrontational and scary at times but stick with it

Bob is the most inspiring teacher i have ever, and will ever, have. He sparked an understanding of literature that i had never touched on. Be ready to DEEPLY analyze really amazing readings. some readings were : old man and the sea, mrs. dalloway, a raisin in the sun. Best class i have ever taken, I nominated him for awards

Bob Dow is by far the best teacher at UMASS.  He's rediculously intelligent and his book choices are great. This was my favorite class, he allows students to explore novels in a way that may seem unnecessary, but the end result is a deeper understanding of the book.  Take this class!!

Professor Dow does incredible and possibly questionable things with literature. For some (like me) his class is an eye-opener, a challenge, and a blast. For others it is an exercise in frustration. Take it with an open mind. You might surprise yourself.

Bob Dow will force you to look into books like never before, and you'll never read the same way afterwards. He never disagrees with a students opinions, which creates an open atmosphere for discussion. His class really forces you to volunteer, put yourself out there. The discussions can be tedious, but are always purposeful.

One of the best professors I've ever had.  Perhaps THE best one.  I took 2 of his course and both were amazing.  He makes you look at things from a different angle which will probably stick with you and help you in the future! :)

Amazing class with stimulating and open discussions. You'll look at work in a very detailed and unique way. One of the best classes I've taken so far. If you go deep into the work he'll accept anything you come up with, you just have to be very detail orientated with your papers, but during class he'll try to run with anything you notice a& suggest

The most dissapointing class of my career. Despite the excellent readings and wonderful reccomendations, Bob turned out to be somewhat crazy. He flipped out at me for disagreeing with him, shamed students in class, and let us out thirty minutes every single class. If you agree with him he'll love you, if you don't you're in trouble
This class is not what I expected it was going to be and I think that it was falsely advertised on Spire.  If I knew what this class were going to be like I wouldn't have taken it.

Bob's class was an eye-opener.  Definately take him if you want more than your average professor.  Very opinionated, yes, but also very insightful and genuine.  Take his class if you want a class to look forward to.
Inspired and insightful

Dow, and his class, are a waste of time. He gives good grades to those who pursue the sycophant method, and remain docile to his unsubstantiated views on nearly everything; meanwhile, those who present alternative views are reprimanded severely in the most unjustified ways. He literally screamed at me on several occasions. One time: for commenting

While the material is interesting, Bob is very intimidating. He is hard to approach and often difficult grading wise. If you are afraid to participate, do not take the course, he REQUIRES CONSTANT PARTICIPATION. The subject and literature of war, however, is very insightful, opening up your eyes to the world of metaphor.

The topic is very interesting and Bob (since he doesn't like being called Prof. Dow) has experienced the horror of war first hand.  He gives a very insightful look into a world he hopes nobody ever has to experience again.

One of the best professors I've ever had.  Renewed my interest in reading.  Helped me to see the infinite number of possible connections in literature and film.  Excellent readings/films, excellent professor.
He was a great guy, very friendly and approachable.  He makes you think in new ways.  Class involves a lot of reading, make sure you have it done for class.  He grades tough, but fairly.
the most passionate teacher i've ever had, he will share his heart and sould with you, and you will learn from every bit of it. wonderful taste in books and films also.
One of the best professors I have ever had.  Demanding and tough course, and he expects a lot and is a very tough grader but you end up learning so much.

he's sort of a willy wonka. extremely excited about his trade, trying to enthuse everyone about the product. but like willy wonka, he's also inherently tragic, prone to moments of complete silence.  all in all a great class with great literature and film
He was honestly one of the worst teachers i've ever had. He was downright mean to students and did not create a very open and accepting work environment.
Excellent professor.
Emotionally draining course.  Really intense teacher.  Let yourself go.

Andy is super personable and really tries to get to know his students and their interests. He will tailor lecture topics to student interests regularly. If you're trying to decide who to choose for CNS junior year writing, I really recommend him. He also schedules the class differently than the other professors, with less work around finals week.
very lame >:(
Good prof., cares about and gets to know his students. He focused on things that are important in the fields we will be going into which makes it easy to care about this class. Fair grader.

Andrew is by far the best option for junior year writing.   I dropped another junior year writing course as the professor was a jumbled mess.  If you want a good junior year writing course try your best to get this professor.

Great, personable professor. He focused on topics that are actually useful and was an engaging lecturer. There is one group project, which takes up the majority of the semester. He grades fairly and gives great feedback, you can tell he really wants you to succeed.
reviews.rating_tags: Group projects--Clear grading criteria--Gives good feedback

reviews.comment: Great professor and would absolutely recommend for NatSci Junior year writing.

Super nice guy. The class is pretty easy and he is very accommodating to your needs. I thought junior writing was going to be terrible, but Dr. Farrar made it very manageable. Only 4 papers, two of them are group papers, and the other two are pretty short. The class itself can be boring, but it's not too bad.
No lectures, just slides and the book. That being said, this was online and during summer semester. Regardless , easy A.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: junior year writing is a dreaded class for many at umass, but while discussing topics like grammer which are usually like pulling teeth, Andy has a good sense of humor and is actually able to keep his class engaged. If you show up early to class he always had good things to chat about, and seems to actually care about getting to know students

Andy was the real reason I started to love Psych and his class was an earlier class but I literally would force myself to wake up and get to this class on time because lectures were a real treat. I ACTUALLY learned stuff and enjoyed it. Missing his class is like missing a party, his jokes and insight make class fun. I really feel Andy was human.

Andy is so passionate about psychology, and makes the class material so memorable. His examples leave the material imprinted in your mind. Only grades are exams are attendence, but show up and pay attention in class and it's an easy A. Andy is the best

Andy is the absolute best. The material for drugs & behavior is a little dense but super interesting. The lectures are clear and he is excellent about clearing up points of confusion. Andy clearly wants his students to succeed, and past that, he's a really fun professor. If you're thinking about taking this class, definitely go for it!

Amazing professor. Super funny guy who is very knowledgeable. The material is quite dense and neuroscience heavy for Drugs and Behavior, but super neat. He makes it very interesting and you learn something cool after every class. Tests are 60% of your grade though and there's only two, but if you study well then you'll have no problems.

Great guy, tries to be funny in class. Super interesting lectures and the exams are manageable. Dense information but definitely do-able. No homework! Only one group presentation. Overall fantastic class.

Andy meant well but was incredibly soft spoken and tried too hard to mix his humor into lecture content which became confusing. He often came off as rude and uncaring when contacted or approached with questions about the material. Wasted way too much time by calling attendance in our class, every single class, which had over 50 students in it.

Phenomenal professor, not only taught the most interesting class I've ever taken (Drugs and Behavior), but a very down to earth professor. The content in 535 is a bit dense, but he gives you every opportunity to succeed. Class is part lecture, part open discussion about fascinating aspects of pharmacology. Amazing class, amazing man, 10/10.

Andy is the best professor I've ever had. He's not only a very funny and enjoyable lecturer who connects well with the class, but is also very efficient in his lecture material and facilitates useful discussions. He is straightfoward in his criteria and wants everyone to do well. Andy is love. Andy is life.

Professor Drimmer is super kind and so beyond passionate about what she teaches and what she knows. She makes lectures fun and engaging (as someone who's never taken an art class). She is always very well prepared for class and always is open to questions and comments about art or things outside of it. Only 3 exams and two papers

One of the best professors I've ever had. She is the most interesting, funny, charismatic professor I have ever had. She is so cool and kind, and makes class genuinely enjoyable. She fosters engagement effortlessly, making the classroom laugh often and so many kids always raise their hands, which I have found is rare. 100000/10, highly recommend!

Drimmer's teaching style is utterly exhausting, I was criticized for a paper being "too well written" (I received a C), she did not respond to my email sharing I had a death in the family, and her grading felt subjective.  I had to attend a 5 hour lecture on rugs to get a decent grade with extra credit.  Still traumatized (in grad school now.)

Super nice professor and is very understanding and accommodating. Lectures are not manditory but go if you want to suceed in this class. Lecutres are very fast and it is very hard to take notes. 2 exams closed note and on paper and 3 essays. TA does most of the grading and grades essays very harshly. The exams are hard and require lots of studying

She always gives great lectures and uses class time very well! She is great with answering questions, and is forgiving if you communicate about needing an extension or other accommodation. There are opportunities for participation in class, but they are not required, and most of the class is spent listening to lectures.

Professor Drimmer did a great job of making art history accessible to anyone in the class! There are a lot of assignments that your grade is based on, so each one isn't weighted too heavily. There's quite a bit of writing on the exams, but only one paper for the semester. The class is mostly taught by other professors in the department.

She's a really good lecturer, enthusiastic about the material she teaches. She emphasizes the important stuff and makes really helpful reviews and sheets to follow along with. Discussion assignments were graded really easy. If you show up and take notes you'll do good.
Very great teacher, one of my favorites.

I was iffy about this class at first, but Sonja is such a nice woman and a great professor. I don't normally speak fondly of professors, but this class was very well organized and I actually learned a lot. It's not easy but not too bad, had no problem with the workload. The grading is very fair. The lectures are also very important to attend!
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Accessible outside class--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: To sum up, the professor is very good and professional, but as an undergraduate course, I think it is very difficult. I don't know what the professor's previous classes were like, but for me and the people around me. This class contains a lot of unnecessary content and professional difficulties.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Skip class? You won't pass.--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: There are multiple professors who teach specific areas in the course so it gets extremely difficult to follow the material, especially with online classes. However, Prof. Drimmer is super nice and funny and she gives notes for each class and test to make it easier to study. I didn't attend a lot of classes and still aced the class.

Because of CO-VID, taking classes online has been tough but Professor Drimmer is very understanding on remote learning and how everyone has a life going outside of class. Her classes are very educating, she shows how passionate she is in her field of studies which makes it easier to learn and understand.
Very friendly and nice but she goes really fast so come with open ears.
Great teacher. She loves what she's teaching which makes it easy to learn. If you put the work in, you can enjoy learning the material just as much as Sonja enjoys training.

Sonja Drimmer is the best professor I've had a UMASS. She takes her lectures and makes them incredibly engaging. Her excitement for the subject is apparent and makes classes that much more enjoyable. To be sure however, this class was in no way easy. Major work needs to be put in, especially for the papers.

This was one of my favorite classes. I learned a ton, and her class was actually very fun. I looked forward to going to her lectures. She is excellent at her job. I would highly recommend taking this course, or any course with Sonja.

Sonja is my favorite of all the professors I've ever had. She's super enthusiastic and into what she's teaching, because of her I declared a double major in art history. Exams are easy if you just put in the time to study and make flash cards. Get your essays done early and talk to your TA about your mistakes, change them and hand it in. Easy peasy

The thing I really like about this professor is she's actually really enthusiastic about what she's teaching. She's upbeat, hilarious, and also very informative. The hardest thing about her class is that it requires a lot of memorization, but if you go class and make flash cards you're good. She is by far my favorite professor. <3 you Sonja
She's the best professor I've ever had. Make me want to major in art histroy. She's very enthusiastic about the subject and very inspiring.
Would not recommend this class for an easy A. Prof Drimmer is nice but the exams are difficult as well as the papers.

She really cares about the subject, so if you are an art history major this class would be great for you. Otherwise, it's absolutely miserable. The work load is more than I've ever experienced in a GenEd and her tests require a ton of memorization and random yet specific knowledge. Would not recommend unless you're up for an insane amount of work.

Her enthusiasm is great and really helps to keep you engaged, but that doesn't totally make up for the workload. Her essays are really hard to BS and the exams require a ton of memorization. A great class if you're serious about learning Art History, but way too hard for a GenEd.

She's bright, witty, and makes coming to class tolerable even though not mandatory. Exams are a little tough due to the quantity of memorization but as long as you study, the class shouldn't be difficult whatsoever. Classes and assignments are well structured with clear expectations. I recommend this class to anyone.

Very nice professor, excited about her lectures and very clear. Uploads all lectures online, barely uses the textbook so don't bother buying it. Have to write a couple of papers and do a few assignments. Exams are fairly easy, memorizing paintings and short essays. Attendance not mandatory.
She is very intelligent, funny, and attractive. Really easy to listen to and follow. Extremely knowledgeable and learns names. Awesome professor.
peter is an awesome professor i love the way he sets up his classes. attendance is important bc he does quizzes every class! wonderful guy i would take any class by him ever.
reviews.rating_tags: Amazing lectures --Gives good feedback--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: This is a lecture class with a few assignments throughout the semester. Peter is a great teacher, although lecture could be a bit dry at times. I took this for my major, so I mostly enjoyed the material. I submitted a lot of work late but Peter was very understanding considering my circumstance.
Peter is a great lecturer and an easily likable person. I highly recommend taking his classes. Assignments for 232 were easy.

Not very difficult to get an A in this course, as there are no exams and the primary way to get points deducted is the essays, which he doesn't really give feedback on at all and also is pretty nitpicky about them, but it's fair. Lectures didn't feel engaging at all, but some of the topics were interesting. I'm an unrelated major, so maybe that's y

Lectures are kind of boring but oh well.  Regardless, he's an easily accessible professor, and the grading of assignments seems to be pretty lenient.  Just make sure to keep track of the graded online short quizzes and weekly activity assignments and you'll be fine.  There are 3 750-1000 word essays to be written but they were fairly doable.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Lecture heavy--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Extremely nice guy, easy grader, like others have said class is very structured in a good way. Not too difficult

I am really conflicted. This teacher is really nice and amazing but the content of the class is the most boring thing ever. The teacher is a little bit of a type A person but to the students benefit as the class is clearly structured. Despite him being a great person, the syllabus, slides, and lectures are painfully boring and uninteresting.

Three papers, graded very easily. For two of them, I wrote a draft, edited it in under 30 minutes, and got above a 90%. Weekly homework for completion, very fun. Two weekly quizzes w/ 4 attempts. Final is an easy group project. Groups are assigned. Casual lecture style. Make sure to do all the little assignments, you can miss a few, but not many.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: His class was fine, I learned some things. His assignments were alright. But he just gets on my nerves. No matter what excuse you give for being late/missing an assignment, he DOES NOT GIVE AF. I'm sure he's a nice guy but as a prof he displayed little compassion/flexibility. Very by-the-book.

Peter is an advisor and head of the SustComm department. He's very interested in his students success and what he teaches. Only three shorter essays that were pretty easy to write. Helpful with course registration as well, if you can take this class and you are interested in SCD you should.

Peter is honestly one of my favorite professors I have ever had. He is very knowledgeable, interesting, and wants to help his classes succeed. There is an average amount of work to do for the class, but he splits it up very nicely, so I never felt burdened by the readings or by the out of class assignments. 10/10 would recommend!

Don't buy the textbook. Those who bought it quit reading it after the third chapter. Attendance is mandatory but she is kind about students who come in late. I had the class split into two 1.5hr sessions at 8am. Professor DuBois LOVES politics, so you mostly talk about current events. It's a super easy class, interesting at times.

Don't buy the book. Her class is flipped and you are responsible for learning all of the info outside of class. The assignments are poorly outlined. Graded on exit tickets, 3 papers, 3 discussions, 1 presentation, 2 group projects, and final exam. She just yaps through the whole class.

Such a boring professor. Attendance is mandatory and she gives you scuff for not coming in when she doesn't do anything educational during class. She goes off topic and on random tangents all the time. She doesn't have structure for the class and her grading system is so confusing and never aligns with what she says.

Her final is beyond frustrating as it is "Lecture-Based"; however, our class is completely unstructured. She will put a couple of slides up with words and then go on tangents, of random stories and irrelevant conversations.
reviews.rating_tags: Group projects--Clear grading criteria--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Overall extremely poor professor. Multiple quizzes based on textbook alone with no lecture component (Lecture after the quiz, not before; very unhelpful!). Lack of actual teaching, overload of irrelevant personal stories. Being difficult to reach outside of class on top of rude (and late) email replies makes Lindsey a poor fit for this role.

The class was relatively interesting but the assignments were not explained very well, unclear. Also, not very reachable outside of class. It's not easy to make a 3hour lecture entertaining but does split it up with 2 breaks. The textbook is also reviewed in class by chapter so you really don't need to read it during the week.

His exams closely resemble exam review slides and TA review worksheets. Even if you skip lectures, attend the last class before each exam. Homework is graded based on effort and completion. The slides are clear and easy to understand. He is approachable, passionate about the subject, and does a great job explaining concepts!
Professor DuChene is kind, and quick to the point. The course material is fairly simple, but I would still advise showing up to lecture as his slides do not give much information on their own.

The course material can be made rigorous if one follows the textbook (Bard Electrochemical Methods) but this class was very easy, only going over rudimentary concepts. Some of our exam questions were taken straight from the practice problems. The class is fairly pleasant to listen in on.
Dr. DuChene is awesome! He really cares about his students. If you pay attention during lecture, you will be absolutely fine for the exams. There aren't many homework assignments.
reviews.rating_tags: Clear grading criteria--Gives good feedback--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Joe is a great guy, but I did not learn anything from his class. All the exams are recycled from previous years, and all hw can be found online so it is easy to do well, however you learn nothing. The lab is a completely different story- one of the worst labs ive taken here. Stay away from this class if you can.

unfortunately, it seems as though Joe is a professor who does not care too much at all about teaching. it may be possible that the department forced him into the role. he's a great guy and the class is easy to do well in but i didn't actually learn anything or gain any value from quant lecture. i shouldn't get an A in a class while learn nothing.

Really enjoyed quant lecture with professor DuChene. Homework wasn't required only suggested and he made course content very accessible and exams were not bad at all. Had a good flow during lecture and he made hard concepts easy to understand.
I start the day eager to learn but end up getting lost in his words. I had a better time reading the text. The class was fine and assessments were fair, but his lectures were hard to follow.

He made our class an experiment to implement AI. He decided that we can use Copilot on our exams, and in return made the exams super hard. Note that he did not teach us how to use Copilot. He does not listen to our concerns about how the exam was conducted, with no compensation for the troubles caused by online proctors and WiFi issues.
This class is basically my emotionally unavailable girlfriend—I give it everything I've got, it still says “not enough,” and then somehow I'm the one getting cheated on and graded for it.

the class had me feel like I was an image generation AI model generating an image thats exactly what was requested but they always had some minor problem with it so they require you to redo everything
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Lots of homework--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment:
What ever you do, do not take his class. 
He does not care about his students.

Marco is smart and to the point. Lectures are useful and he always posts notes that are basically solutions to the homework. He responds weirdly quickly on Piazza if you get confused. Homework and projects are very easy, so to make up for it, there's a lot of of them and the grading is very strict on format. Overall, easy class, mostly busy work.

Each assignment is accompanied by clear directions and an easily accessible rubric. Duarte is willing to answer questions in person after class or on Piazza. Strict grading but it follows professional code styling standards (to be consistent + readable). Lectures are useful + give extra credit for attendance. I actually enjoyed this class.

More a criticism of the class, I guess. For a 3 credit class, the amount of work required to do well in this course is absurd. The grading is inconsistent and confusing, so make sure to submit regrade requests. That said, the professor is short-tempered and a bit rude. He often complained about how hard it was to grade exams (he made it that way).

TA was bad, last year, the regrade after submission was within a day. WITHIN A DAY. Who has time to do the HW that is not even learned, two weeks before deadline? you gotta have no life bro 
I lost 20 points because of the technical issues, and dumass honorlock locked my screen and i couldnt do anything, and it is my fault??? Drop this class

As I kind man, ive never wanted to punch someone except him. Worst person and worst professor ill ever have. You are evil. You have no motive to teach, just to brutalize your students. We will hate you from bottom of the heart buddy. Dont take this class. Take with professor Leonard in spring. I hope you will lose your job.
save yourself the time and effort and take this with bill leonard he's way better
Wow. This class was a terrible experience. Monotone lectures that make you fall asleep. The TA's grade unfairly. I'm so happy I am done with this. Worst class I have taken so far.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Gives good feedback--Lots of homework

reviews.comment: Genuinely one of the hardest classes for a subject that is seemingly very simple in concept. The way everything was organized was the worst I've seen by far in any course I've taken. You're more likely to hit the lotto than getting good feedback on everything. Watch out for exams, because there WILL be things that were never mentioned.

A lot of students out there are complaining about how nitpicky he is, But maturity is when upon realizing how much precision and accuracy matters in this field later on. Would have given him a 5 only if the TA's were consistent with the grading. Examples in lecture help a lot for the homework. Try to finish the hw a week earlier and all is well.

Throughout my journey in university, I have never came across such a class and professor. Homeworks will receive terrible grades, regardless if you do them in office hours with the TA's. Awful experience in this class, DO NOT take this class with Duarte. Its clear that he's just doing this for the money and does not have passion for teaching.

Absolutely TERRIBLE class, assignments are graded with pure inconsistency and professor shows no understanding of the students' situations. TA graders are absolute nightmares and when brought to the professors attention, he does not do anything. Does not reply to 90% of emails.
This guy is geniunely the worst human being, people like this shouldn't be allowed to penalize students in a major as hard as ECE.
Crimes against humanity are committed when your assignments are graded

grading is incomprehensible and practically random. be prepared to do every assignment 2-3 times.

you learn nothing and the whole class is graded based on his random bs criteria, huge waste of time, take prof. leonard instead
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: This class is just bad and the professor does not care about his students succeeding. Homework directions can be vague but grading is overly harsh. Just skip taking this guy and take professor leonard, anyone but professor duarte!

One of the worst courses taken to date. Content is easy but the inconsistent grading makes it impossible to get a decent grade. MATLAB and excel code can work but somehow you still end up with an F for a hw. Code has to match the rubric exactly and sometimes still can end up with a low grade depending on TA grading your work. Nightmare of a class
Good midterm grade but I cant get a good grade in the class because the homeworks are impossible...
Absolute nut job of a professor

They find the tiniest mistake in the Answers, and take off 20% of the grade with it. 
I once forgot to add a single comment regarding a unit in a matlab exercise, and got 5 points off of 25.
I will drop out his class and take 202 with Bill Leonard during the winter.
He does not want to see students succeed

Does not care about his students. 
Does not account for wifi, or technical issues during online exams.
Makes us use functions we've never seen in lecture. 
Very passive aggressive as well.

This class was brutal. Takes away points on assignments for the most absurd things, like putting a space where there "shouldn't" be a space because it makes your code "unreadable". Didn't realize first graders were reading my code. Also get ready to spend 8 hours a week on a PDF combiner merging all your submissions into one file...

The problem with this course is the grading system. You lose points for like variable names, font size is off, no spaces around equals signs, etc. A clear rubric for assignments would be helpful but the rubric is split up over multiple docs and kind of a slog. You can resubmit, but they're slow to regrade. Not his grading system, so 202 is just bad
Homeworks are extremely long and difficult for no reason and professor won't give you clear feedback on assignments.
It was OK I guess.

Honestly if he provided a rubric of what an assignment should look like all his problems would be fixed. Extremely nit picky which I deem to be unfair as he will call out unnecessary errors(For example my final phase of a project won't be graded because I have extra parenthesis and only use a variable I created once in the previous phase).

Marco Duarte is the worst professor I have had yet. The class is so poorly structured and the assignments are beyond redundant and annoying. He does not teach anything in class and his grading is unbelievably harsh. This is by far the worst class I have taken, PLEASE take this class during winter/summer.

Boring lecturer, he expains matlab + excel topics very well through his examples. HW is generally straightforward, with the two projects being avaliable to do for months and only slightly tougher than the homeworks. Online exams with a screen recording software. Very nitpicky on grading, I wish he posted a clearer rubric for grading assignments.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Lots of homework

reviews.comment: Lectures are fine however grading for projects is abysmal. There is no one grading scheme that is publicly available. Even submitting a course survey led to 0/11 because my screenshot wasn't right. My friend sent the same type of screenshot and got 11/11.

Duarte is not a good teacher for this class and simply doesn't care. He has plenty of other issues that someone has posted on twitter check out the thread of how he was and what he did this semester!
@ECE202duarte
:( breaks promises

Absolutely do not take Marco Duarte for ECE 202. The conceptual concepts of the class are incredibly easy, but the grading system is exhausting and ruthless. The grading on assignments is painstakingly strict, so assignments that would ordinarily take a few hours can take 10+ because of the amount of revisions you will have to make. Very bad.

There are not words for how bad his grading is. You will submit a perfect assignment after 10 hours of making it flawless and he will still give you a D despite everything being objectively correct and easily understandable. Just try to get above a C on any assignment. Try, please. Take his class and see for yourself.

Marco seems like a good guy however the way 202 is taught and the rubric for the homework drove me insane to the point where I was on a 72Hr hold at the hospital on SW. It doesn't help that Marco really doesn't gaf about students and he probably hates teaching this course, so it just sucks for everyone. 3 Credit course taking up too much time.

He's pretty monotone but the lectures give you solid understanding if actually pay attention. The homework's were the worst part of the class. They took forever and were a lot harder than most examples we've seen causing a lot of headaches. Thankfully the midterms were pretty easy compared to them but the final was tough. He graded nicely though.

Duarte is a nice person but bad lecturer. His voice is so hard to listen to as he is very monotone. This becomes a big problem when you realize you can't read his horrible hand writing. 3 tests, first one hard, second one very easy, final was crazy hard and didn't match what we learned. Got good grades but felt like I learned nothing. SI saved me!
Very mid lectures and exam questions are out of this world. Although he grades leniently but don't feel like anyone learnt much from this course. Way too much work

Introductory Digital - Discrete Time Signal Processing course. Goes over conventional signal processing techniques like tranform theory/filter based techniques. Lays a pretty solid foundation for advanced signal processing and image processing courses. Duarte's explanation are really clear. If you pay attention in class you're unlikely to fail.
